The conclusion is a finite stratification, not local constancy on all
of $X$. For a closed point $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ of an
irreducible curve with open complement $j$, the sheaf
$j_!\mathbf F_\ell\oplus i_*\mathbf F_\ell$ has cardinality $\ell$
at every stalk, but its generization map from $Z$ to its complement
is zero. In the proof above, injectivity comes from lifting the
generic stalk; it is not assumed for arbitrary generization maps.

The formal development (`AlgebraicGeometry.StrictTransform`,
specialized to blow-ups as
`Scheme.IdealSheafData.strictTransform`) works with this
scheme-theoretic-closure definition directly, and proves the identification
over the preserved open ([lemma-nagata-strict-transform-over-complement])
by scheme-image flat base change for a quasi-compact flat monomorphism
(`Nagata.ker_comap_self`), not through the torsion-quotient chart
model. The chart-by-chart infrastructure below
([def-nagata-strict-transform-chart-ring] through
[prop-nagata-strict-transform-closed-fiber-product]) is accordingly
not formalized — with the exception of the chart surjectivity
([lemma-nagata-strict-chart-map-surjective]), which is proved in the
subring-generation form used by the formalized Tag 080E route; of the
power-torsion material only the affine algebraic layer
(`Submodule.powTorsion` and its localization/exactness lemmas) is.
The identification of the strict transform with the blow-up of the
extended ideal ([thm-nagata-strict-transform-is-blowup],
Stacks Tag 080E) *is* formalized, but by the universal-property route
recorded in [def-nagata-strict-transform-blowup-comparison] and the
revised proof of [thm-nagata-strict-transform-is-blowup] — a
comparison morphism into the fibre product which is a closed immersion by
a chart-wise surjectivity computation, together with schematic density of
the exceptional complement — rather than by gluing the chart-ring
isomorphisms.

The formal statement
(`exists_finiteDegree_center_le_blowup`) recasts Tag 0803 purely
in ideal-sheaf terms: $Z'$ is replaced by a finite-type ideal sheaf
$\mathcal J$ on the blow-up and the conclusion is the inverse-image
equality $\mathcal L\cdot\mathcal O_{X'}=\mathcal I_E^d\cdot\mathcal J$ for
a finite-type $\mathcal L\subseteq\mathcal I^d$; no relative-Proj quotient
is formed, and the support bound is recovered downstream
(`coe_support_eq_of_comap_pow_mul`). The choice-packaged
[def-nagata-proj-closed-center-finite-degree] is replaced by the bare
existential.

*Consequence for the sketch.* Because the layer is elementary apart from
the four points above, a proof sketch of the passage from the three abstract
inputs to the five Weil conjectures can be written once and for all, with the
four non-elementary points isolated as marked obligations: the alternating
middle pairing, the two endpoint computations, the embedding extension, and
the intrinsic-weight/integrality step. This is precisely what the present
document does, and it is why this layer can be stated over any coefficient
theory in which the three inputs hold.

The formal proof (`Nagata.schemeImageFlatBaseChange`) does not run
the affine kernel computations of
[lemma-nagata-dense-flat-pullback] and
[lemma-nagata-dense-flat-pullback]: it factors the base-changed
morphism through $\operatorname{SIm}(g)\times_YY'$ and applies Mathlib's
`IsSchemeTheoreticallyDominant.of_isPullback`, which encapsulates
those computations. Only quasi-compactness of $g$ is needed, and
[lemma-nagata-scheme-image-restrict-open] is obtained in Lean as the
special case of flat base change along an open immersion, reversing the
order of these two lemmas.

The formal proof (`isProper_blowupMap`) follows this target-local
reduction and settles the affine case
([lemma-nagata-affine-blowup-proper]) by identifying
$\operatorname{Bl}_I(A)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ with
`Proj.toSpecZero` of the Rees algebra and invoking Mathlib's
properness of $\operatorname{Proj}$ over its degree-zero part, fed by
[prop-nagata-rees-finite-generation]. Projectivity of the blow-up is therefore not needed.

The formal statement (`extendedToBlowup_isEffectiveCartier`) proves
the effective-Cartier form only, directly from
[lemma-nagata-chart-extended-ideal-principal] and
[lemma-nagata-chart-generator-regular]: being effective Cartier is a
local condition, so the gluing step through
[lemma-nagata-chart-generators-associated] and the invertible-sheaf
half ([def-nagata-invertible-ideal],
[lemma-nagata-effective-cartier-is-invertible],
[lemma-nagata-invertible-ideal-is-effective-cartier]) are not needed
and are not formalized. The Lean theorem also requires no finite-type
hypothesis on the center.

Let $j:U_0\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ be a dense open immersion and
let $\mathcal M$ be an irreducible
lisse Weil sheaf on
$U_0$, unramified at infinity,
punctually $\iota$-pure of weight
$w$, with irreducible geometric fundamental representation of
[def-wf-fundamental-representation] and
Fourier-nonexceptional
middle extension
$j_*\mathcal M$. Then
$H_c^1(\mathbf A^1_{k_0},j_*\mathcal M)$ has
weights at most $w+1$.

## Proof

*Step 1: the transform of the middle extension.* The hypothesis
[def-fd-nonexceptional] excludes, after geometric base change, a
constant sheaf up to a constant Weil twist; so $\mathcal M$ is not
geometrically constant. Being nonzero, irreducible and unramified at
infinity, $\mathcal M$ is therefore constituent-nonexceptional by
[lem-a1-unramified-nonexceptional], and
[prop-a1-fourier-middle-extension] supplies a dense open
$j':U'_0\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ of the dual line and a nonzero
irreducible lisse Weil sheaf $\mathcal M'$ on $U'_0$ with

$$
\operatorname{FT}_\psi\bigl((j_*\mathcal M)[1]\bigr)\cong(j'_*\mathcal M')[1].
$$

*Step 2: the weight of $\mathcal M'$.* Since $\mathcal M$ is moreover
punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$, the last assertion of
[cor-fd-l2-plancherel-middle-extension] shows that $\mathcal M'$ is
punctually $\iota$-pure of weight exactly $w+1$ on all of $U'_0$.

*Step 3: weights of the middle extension on the dual line.* The dual
line is a smooth geometrically connected affine curve, and
$\mathcal M'$ is a nonzero lisse Weil sheaf on the dense open $U'_0$
all of whose closed-point Frobenius eigenvalues satisfy
$|\iota(\alpha)|^2=q_x^{w+1}\le q_x^{w+1}$. Boundary semicontinuity
[lem-wf-boundary-semicontinuity], with $\beta=w+1$, shows that the
middle extension $j'_*\mathcal M'$ of [def-wf-middle-extension] has
punctual weights at most $w+1$ at every closed point of the dual line,
including the finitely many points outside $U'_0$, where it may be
singular.

*Step 4: the origin fibre.* By the stationary-phase identification
[cor-fd-origin-stationary-phase], whose hypotheses are those of the
present statement, there is a Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism

$$
H_c^1(\mathbf A^1_{k_0},j_*\mathcal M)\cong(j'_*\mathcal M')_{0'},
$$

the geometric Frobenius of $k_0$ on the left corresponding to the local
Frobenius $F_{0'}$ at the $k_0$-rational point $0'$ on the right. Hence
the eigenvalues of Frobenius on $H_c^1(\mathbf A^1_{k_0},j_*\mathcal M)$
are those of $F_{0'}$ on the stalk, and by Step 3 (with $q_{0'}=q$)
each of them satisfies $|\iota(\alpha)|^2\le q^{w+1}$. In the
convention of [def-weil-punctual-weights], this says that
$H_c^1(\mathbf A^1_{k_0},j_*\mathcal M)$ has weights at most $w+1$.
The irreducibility of the geometric fundamental representation of
[def-wf-fundamental-representation] is not needed for this argument.

For $p_d:\mathbf A^d_S\to S$, on the entire ordinary
derived categories of etale $A$-module sheaves,

$$
Rp_{d!}\dashv p_d^*(d)[2d].
$$

The notation refers to affine space, ordinary etale compact supports, and Tate twists.

## Proof

Let $j:\mathbf A^1_S\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^1_S$.
The definition in [def-amb-etale-compact-support]
is $Rp_{1!}=Rq_*j_!$. By
[thm-amb-p1-adjunction], [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality],
its right adjoint is $j^*q^*(1)[2]=p_1^*(1)[2]$.
For $d=0$ the assertion is the identity adjunction.
The composition of compact-support functors is
[lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons]. For $d>0$, factor the affine-space projection into
$d$ successive affine-line projections. The right
adjoint of the composite is the reversed composite of
their right adjoints, by their Hom adjunction bijections.
The twists add by [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], giving
$p_d^*(d)[2d]$.

Let $\square$ be an
open-immersion square and let
$\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. For every
$K\in D^+(U_{\Et},\Lambda)$ the map of
[lem-cbc-extension-zero-base-change] is an isomorphism

$$
g^{-1}j_!K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }j'_!g_U^{-1}K
$$

in $D^+(X'_{\Et},\Lambda)$, and the isomorphism is natural in $K$,
is the identity for $g=\operatorname{id}$, and is compatible with
pasting of open-immersion squares.

## Proof

Both $g^{-1}$, $g_U^{-1}$ are exact inverse images, and $j_!$,
$j'_!$ are exact by [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], so the
degreewise isomorphisms of [lem-cbc-extension-zero-base-change]
give a termwise isomorphism of complexes, i.e. an isomorphism in the
derived category; the
named compatibilities are the functoriality, identity, and pasting
properties of the construction in
[lem-cbc-extension-zero-base-change].

For a proper
$f:X\to Y$ and the canonical identification
$Rf_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*$ of
[def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] (the compactification
$j=\operatorname{id}$, $p=f$), the map $\operatorname{Ex}_!$
of [def-cbc-exchange-map] is the proper-base-change exchange map
of [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]; consequently the
compact-support base change of
[thm-cbc-finite-torsion] specializes to proper base change for
proper $f$.

## Proof

For $j=\operatorname{id}$ the extension-by-zero identification
of [def-cbc-exchange-map] is the identity, so
$\operatorname{Ex}_!$ is the exchange map of
[def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] for the proper $p=f$, by
[def-cbc-exchange-map] and the identification
$Rf_!=Rf_*$ of [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed].

attrs.title: Proper morphisms: compact supports equal direct image

objects.body:
Let $S$ be a noetherian scheme and let $f\colon X\to S$ be a proper morphism.
Then there are an integer $n\geq0$, a proper surjective morphism
$\pi\colon X'\to X$ and a *closed* immersion
$i\colon X'\to\mathbf P^n_S$ of $S$-schemes; moreover $\pi$ is an isomorphism
over a dense open subscheme of $X$. In particular every proper $S$-scheme is
dominated by a projective $S$-scheme through a proper surjective morphism.

## Proof

A proper morphism is separated and of finite type, so [thm-chow-lemma]
applies and yields $\pi\colon X'\to X$ and an immersion
$i\colon X'\to\mathbf P^n_S$ with the stated properties. Both $f$ and $\pi$
are proper, hence so is $f\circ\pi\colon X'\to S$. Since $\mathbf P^n_S\to S$
is separated, 01W6 shows that $i$ is universally closed; in
particular $i(X')\subseteq\mathbf P^n_S$ is closed, and an immersion with
closed image is a closed immersion by 01IQ. Thus $f\circ\pi$
is the composition of the closed immersion $i$ with the structure morphism
$\mathbf P^n_S\to S$, so $X'$ is projective over $S$.

## Detailed form

In the situation of [thm-chow-lemma], the
composite

$$
 i:X'\hookrightarrow\widetilde X\hookrightarrow Z
 \hookrightarrow\prod_{i=1}^m\mathbf P^{n_i}_Y
 \xrightarrow{\ s\ }\mathbf P^N_Y,\qquad N=\prod_{i=1}^m(n_i+1)-1,
$$

of the open immersion $X'\subseteq\widetilde X$, the closed immersion
$\widetilde X\hookrightarrow Z$ of
[lem-chow-graph], the product of the closed immersions
$Z_i\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^{n_i}_Y$, and the Segre embedding
([lem-chow-segre]) is a closed immersion, and
$f\circ\pi$ equals the composite of $i$ with $\mathbf P^N_Y\to Y$.

## Proof

By [thm-chow-lemma], $\pi$ is proper and
surjective and $\pi^{-1}(U)\xrightarrow{\sim}U$. The composite $i$ is a
composite of the open immersion $X'\subseteq\widetilde X$ with closed
immersions (the closed immersion $\widetilde X\hookrightarrow Z$, the product
of the closed immersions $Z_i\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^{n_i}_Y$, and the Segre
embedding), hence an immersion. Its source $X'$ is proper over $Y$: the
composite of the proper surjective $\pi$ with the proper $f$ is proper; its
target $\mathbf P^N_Y$ is separated over $Y$, so $i$ is proper, and a proper
immersion is a closed immersion. Finally $f\circ\pi$ and the composite of $i$
with $\mathbf P^N_Y\to Y$ are both the structure morphism of the $Y$-scheme
$X'$, since every morphism in the display is a morphism of $Y$-schemes, as in
the last paragraph of the proof of
[thm-chow-lemma].

For every $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, there is a natural isomorphism

$$
d_{K,A,B}:(D_{X,A}K)\otimes_A^LB
\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{X,B}(K_B).
$$

The maps form a cocycle under further coefficient change and
carry evaluation and the double-dual morphism to the corresponding
maps at $B$. If $\dim X\leq d$ and $K$ has Tor interval
$[a,b]$, both sides have Tor interval $[-b-2d,-a]$.

## Proof

Apply [thm-coef-finite-hom] with second argument
$\omega_{X,A}$, and then use
[lem-coef-finite-dualizing] on that argument. The resulting
map is $d_{K,A,B}$. Evaluation compatibility follows from
the two comparisons already proved, and transposing evaluation
as in [lem-weil-duality-pairing] gives double-dual
compatibility. The cocycle is their quotient cocycle. The Tor
bound is [lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata], together
with preservation of the Tor interval by scalar extension.

For $K,L\in D^b_c(X,R)$, the ambient
$R\mathcal Hom_R(K,L)$ lies in $D^b_c(X,R)$ and its
reductions are the corresponding finite internal Homs. If the
reduction Tor intervals of $K,L$ are $[a,b]$, $[c,e]$
and $\dim X\leq d$, one output interval is
$[c-b-2d,e-a+2d]$.

## Proof

Completeness and the canonical reductions follow from
[lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction]. The input reductions are
finite-Tor by [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor]. Their internal
Homs are constructible with the stated uniform bound by
[cor-weil-finite-constructible-hom]. These are exactly the
remaining conditions on the integral output.

For a scheme over $\mathbf F_q$, duality at $E$ and
$\Qlb$ preserves the category of Weil complexes on its
geometric fiber. Evaluation, biduality, the exceptional adjunction
data, and the finite scalar-extension comparisons are Weil
equivariant. This assertion does not require a
Frobenius-stable integral lattice for a rational Weil complex.

## Proof

The underlying operations now preserve the relevant constructible
categories by [thm-coef-rational-verdier], [lem-coef-rational-operations], [thm-coef-qbar-verdier].
Consequently the equivariance construction of
[lem-fix-weil-operations] applies, including to the
dualizing object supplied by the exceptional adjoint. Write
$g$ for geometric Frobenius and
$\theta_K:g^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ for a Weil structure in
[def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. The dual Weil structure is
the composite

$$
g^*DK\xrightarrow{\sim}D(g^*K)
\xrightarrow{D(\theta_K^{-1})}DK.
$$

The first map is the internal-Hom comparison for the equivalence
$g^*$, using the dualizing Weil structure. Naturality of
evaluation proves its equivariance, and transposition gives the
same conclusion for $\delta$. This works with a rational
$\theta_K$ itself; it is unnecessary to reduce that
automorphism on a chosen integral lattice. At $\Qlb$ the
finite diagram representing $K$, $\theta_K$, and its
inverse is realized at one common finite coefficient field.

The comparisons in [lem-coef-integral-finite-extension]
are built from scalar tensor, the dualizing counit, and evaluation.
Their finite-level comparisons commute with the Frobenius
automorphism square, and normalized tower transport preserves
that equality. Their rationalizations and common-stage images
therefore commute with the displayed dual Weil structure. The
same units and counits as in [lem-fix-weil-operations]
give the exceptional-adjunction assertion.

attrs.title: Weil equivariance of the completed coefficient duality

objects.body:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated finite type carrying the ambient exceptional
right adjoint datum of [def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint], and let
$g:Y'\hookrightarrow Y$ be an *open immersion*. Then the
base-change comparison $Lg'^*Rf^{\times}\to Rf'^{\times}Lg^*$ is an
isomorphism. In particular the base-change comparison holds for the
passage from an affine open of the base to the base, which is what an
assembly on affine charts requires. On the blueprint's coefficient class
[def-sf-fullcd-used-class] the ambient datum displayed as the hypothesis
is the theorem [cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge], so the comparison is
an isomorphism on that class without hypothesis, and it is on that class that
the assembly of [thm-pur-general-admissibility] consumes it.

## Proof

Choose a compactification $X\xrightarrow{j_0}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$
of [thm-nagata-compactification], with $p$ proper. By
[prop-exc-base-change-proper] the comparison holds for $p$ against
the open immersion $g$, and by
[cor-exc-base-change-reduces-to-proper] the comparison for $f$
follows from that for $p$.

attrs.title: Base change for an arbitrary morphism, against an open immersion

objects.body:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated finite type with a
compactification
$X\xrightarrow{j_0}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$, and let $g:Y'\to Y$
be arbitrary. If the base-change comparison
$L\overline g^*Rp^{\times}\to R(p')^{\times}Lg^*$ is an isomorphism for
the proper morphism $p$, then the base-change comparison
$Lg'^*Rf^{\times}\to Rf'^{\times}Lg^*$ is an isomorphism for $f$.
Consequently the comparison for a general separated finite-type morphism
is reduced to its proper part, the open part being free. The ambient
exceptional right adjoint datum that the identity $Rf^{\times}\cong j_0^*Rp^{\times}$ uses is, on the blueprint's coefficient class
[def-sf-fullcd-used-class], the theorem
[cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge], so the reduction is unconditional
there.

## Proof

The compact-support functor is $Rf_!=Rp_!j_{0!}=Rp_*j_{0!}$, so by
uniqueness of right adjoints — the uniqueness invoked in the ambient
datum of [def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint] — the ambient right
adjoint is
$Rf^{\times}\cong j_0^*Rp^{\times}$, and likewise
$Rf'^{\times}\cong j_0'^*R(p')^{\times}$ for the base change. The
base-change comparison for $f$ is therefore, by pullback composition
([def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]), the comparison for $p$ conjugated
by the isomorphisms $Lg'^*j_0^*\cong j_0'^*L\overline g^*$; it is an
isomorphism whenever the comparison for $p$ is.

attrs.title: Base change for a general morphism reduces to the proper part

objects.body:
Let $j:U_0\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ be a dense open immersion
with finite complement, and let $\mathcal M$ be a lisse Weil sheaf on
$U_0$, punctually $\iota$-pure
of weight $w$. Suppose that the Fourier–Deligne transform of its
middle extension has the
middle-extension shape

$$
\operatorname{FT}_\psi\bigl(j_*\mathcal M[1]\bigr)\cong j'_*\mathcal M'[1]
$$

with $\mathcal M'$ lisse on a dense open
$U_0'\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$, punctually $\iota$-pure of
weight $v$. Then

$$
v=w+1 .
$$

The middle-extension shape holds, with $\mathcal M'$ irreducible,
whenever $\mathcal M$ is irreducible and constituent-nonexceptional
([prop-a1-fourier-middle-extension]). In that case the purity of
$\mathcal M'$ is automatic as well: if $\mathcal M$ is nonzero,
irreducible, constituent-nonexceptional and punctually $\iota$-pure of
weight $w$, then the sheaf $\mathcal M'$ of
[prop-a1-fourier-middle-extension] is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight
exactly $w+1$.

## Proof

The trace function of [def-fd-trace-function] is unchanged in
absolute value by the shift $[1]$: the shift multiplies the
alternating trace by $-1$, of $\iota$-modulus one, so
$\|f_{j_*\mathcal M[1]}\|_m=\|f_{j_*\mathcal M}\|_m$ and likewise
$\|f_{j'_*\mathcal M'[1]}\|_m=\|f_{j'_*\mathcal M'}\|_m$ for every
$m$. The Plancherel shift [lem-fd-l2-plancherel-shift], applied
to the Weil complex $j_*\mathcal M[1]$, therefore reads

$$
\|j'_*\mathcal M'\|
=\bigl\|\operatorname{FT}_\psi(j_*\mathcal M[1])\bigr\|
=\|j_*\mathcal M\|+1 .
$$

By the middle-extension comparison [lem-fd-l2-middle-extension],
$\|j_*\mathcal M\|=\|\mathcal M\|=w$ and
$\|j'_*\mathcal M'\|=\|\mathcal M'\|=v$, the second equality in each
case being the rigidity [lem-wf-l2-purity-rigidity] applied to the
punctually pure lisse sheaf $\mathcal M$ respectively $\mathcal M'$.
Substituting, $v=w+1$.

For the last assertion, [prop-a1-fourier-middle-extension] supplies the
middle-extension shape with $\mathcal M'$ lisse on the dense open
$U'_0$, and [thm-fd-generic-fourier-sheaf-pure] shows that
$\mathcal M'$ is punctually $\iota$-pure of some real weight $v$ on all
of $U'_0$. All hypotheses of the first part are then met, so $v=w+1$.

attrs.title: Plancherel for a middle extension: the transform shifts the weight of a pure lisse sheaf by exactly one

objects.body:
Let $j:U_0\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ and let $\mathcal M$ be
irreducible and lisse on $U_0$, unramified at infinity, with
Fourier-nonexceptional middle
extension. Then the Fourier transform of [def-fd-transform] takes the
middle-extension shape
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi(j_{!*}\mathcal M[1])=j'_{!*}\mathcal M'[1]$,
and the degree $-1$ part of the fiber at
the origin of the dual line is the $H_c^1$-term of the local Fourier
exact sequence at the origin:

$$
\mathcal H^{-1}\Bigl(\operatorname{FT}_\psi(j_{!*}\mathcal M[1])_{0'}\Bigr)
\cong H_c^1(\mathbf A^1_{k_0},j_*\mathcal M)\;\cong\;(j'_*\mathcal M')_{0'}\;=\;\bigl(\mathcal M'_{\bar\eta}\bigr)^{I_{0'}},
$$

the last identification being the invariants of the local inertia
$I_{0'}$ at the origin of the dual line (trivial if $0'\in U'_0$): the
stationary phase term is therefore the origin part of the transformed
middle extension. Moreover $H_c^2(\mathbf A^1_{k_0},j_*\mathcal M)=0$.
All these identifications are *Frobenius-equivariant*: the origin $0'$
is a $k_0$-rational point, and the geometric Frobenius of $k_0$ acting
on $H_c^1(\mathbf A^1_{k_0},j_*\mathcal M)$ corresponds to the local
Frobenius $F_{0'}$ on the stalk $(j'_*\mathcal M')_{0'}$ of the Weil
sheaf $j'_*\mathcal M'$, and to the action of a Frobenius lift on
$(\mathcal M'_{\bar\eta})^{I_{0'}}$.

## Proof

The shape: Fourier-nonexceptionality says in particular that
$\mathcal M$ is not geometrically constant, so, being unramified at
infinity, $\mathcal M$ is constituent-nonexceptional by
[lem-a1-unramified-nonexceptional], and
[prop-a1-fourier-middle-extension] gives an isomorphism of Weil
complexes
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi(j_{!*}\mathcal M[1])\cong j'_{!*}\mathcal M'[1]=j'_*\mathcal M'[1]$
with $\mathcal M'$ nonzero, irreducible and lisse.

The first identification is [lem-fd-stalk-at-origin]: the fiber of
the transform at the origin is $R\Gamma_c(\mathbf A^1,j_*\mathcal M[1])[1]$,
whose degree $-1$ part is $H_c^1(\mathbf A^1_{k_0},j_*\mathcal M)$,
while its degree $0$ part is
$H_c^2(\mathbf A^1_{k_0},j_*\mathcal M)$. This identification is
Frobenius-equivariant. Indeed, the Weil structure of
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K_0)$ is the one transported from those of
$K_0$ and of the kernel of [def-fd-transform] through $p_1^*$,
$\otimes$ and $p_{2,!}$, and the isomorphism of
[lem-fd-stalk-at-origin] at the rational point $0'$ is composed of
the base change isomorphism for $p_{2,!}$ along
$0'\hookrightarrow V^\vee$ and the trivialisation of the kernel on
the fibre $\mathbf A^1\times\{0'\}$ (the kernel of the zero function
$x\cdot0$ is the constant Weil sheaf). Both are natural isomorphisms
defined over $k_0$, so they commute with the Weil descent data, and the
stalk Frobenius $F_{0'}$ of the transform corresponds to the geometric
Frobenius on $R\Gamma_c(\mathbf A^1_{k_0},j_*\mathcal M)$.

For the second identification, the transformed object has the shape
$j'_*\mathcal M'[1]$ of [def-wf-middle-extension], a single
sheaf placed in degree $-1$; its fiber at the point $0'$ of the dual
line is therefore concentrated in degree $-1$, where it is the stalk
$(j'_*\mathcal M')_{0'}$, and the isomorphism of Weil complexes above
induces a Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism of the fibres at the
rational point $0'$. Comparing the two descriptions of the same fiber
gives $H_c^1(\mathbf A^1_{k_0},j_*\mathcal M)\cong(j'_*\mathcal M')_{0'}$
equivariantly, and $H_c^2(\mathbf A^1_{k_0},j_*\mathcal M)=0$
because the degree $0$ part vanishes. If $0'\notin U'_0$, the
boundary-stalk description of
[lem-wf-boundary-stalk-invariants] gives
$(j'_*\mathcal M')_{0'}=\bigl(\mathcal M'_{\bar\eta}\bigr)^{I_{0'}}$,
Frobenius-equivariantly; if $0'\in U'_0$, the inertia $I_{0'}$ acts
trivially on the lisse sheaf $\mathcal M'$ and the stalk is
$\mathcal M'_{\bar\eta}=(\mathcal M'_{\bar\eta})^{I_{0'}}$. All
cohomology is in the compact-support convention of
[def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology].

attrs.title: The origin fiber is the stationary-phase contribution

objects.body:
Fix a field embedding $\iota:\Qlb\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$; the trace functions take values in $E\subset\Qlb$, and the absolute value and complex conjugation below are those of $\mathbf C$, read through $\iota$. Then for every $n\ge1$ and every Weil complex $K$ on $\mathbf A^1$,

$$
\sum_{y\in\mathbf F_{q^n}}
\left|\iota\,t_{\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K)}(y)\right|^2
=q^n\sum_{x\in\mathbf F_{q^n}}
\left|\iota\,t_K(x)\right|^2 .
$$

## Proof

Apply $\iota$ to the finite Fourier sum of [thm-fd-fourier-trace], multiply it by its complex conjugate, and sum over $y$; since $\iota\psi_n(z)$ is a complex root of unity, $\overline{\iota\psi_n(x'y)}=\iota\psi_n(-x'y)$, so

$$
\sum_{y}\Bigl|\sum_x \iota t_K(x)\,\iota\psi_n(xy)\Bigr|^2
=\sum_{y}\sum_{x,x'}\iota t_K(x)\,\overline{\iota t_K(x')}\ \iota\psi_n((x-x')y).
$$

The orthogonality relation [lem-fd-additive-orthogonality] (an identity in $\Qlb$, transported by $\iota$) makes the inner $y$-sum equal to $q^n$ when $x=x'$ and zero otherwise. The surviving diagonal sum is exactly the right-hand side written with the absolute values of the trace function of [def-fd-trace-function].

Let $k$ be a field, let $A$ be a finite ring annihilated by
an integer invertible in $k$, and let $j:X\hookrightarrow Y$
be an open immersion of finite-type $k$-schemes. For every
$K\in D^b_c(X,A)$, one has $Rj_*K\in D^b_c(Y,A)$.
The notation refers to bounded constructible complexes, and ordinary derived categories.

## Proof

First let $K=F$ be a sheaf. Decompose its underlying finite
torsion group into its finitely many primary parts, and filter
the $\ell$-primary part by
$F\supset\ell F\supset\ell^2F\supset\cdots\supset0$.
These subsheaves and quotients are constructible by
[thm-constructible-serre]; each quotient is
annihilated by $\ell$. Its derived direct image is computed
over $\mathbf F_\ell$ by
[lem-fin-coefficients-forgetful-direct-image], and is bounded
constructible by [cor-fin-deligne-open-over-field].
The finite sequence of long exact cohomology sequences proves
the same assertion for the underlying finite additive sheaf of
$Rj_*F$, with a finite cohomological range. Its inherited
$A$-action preserves constructibility: on any stratum where
the additive sheaf is finite locally constant, the finitely many
endomorphisms defining the $A$-action are locally constant
matrices after an etale trivialization. Refining those
trivializations makes it a locally constant finite $A$-module
sheaf. Thus the assertion holds with its original coefficients.
For bounded $K$, use its finitely many cohomology sheaves and
the finite truncation triangles, equivalently
[thm-sp-truncation-e2]. The finite union of their ranges
bounds $Rj_*K$; kernels, cokernels and extensions preserve
constructibility by [thm-constructible-serre].

attrs.title: Open direct images with arbitrary finite allowable coefficients

objects.body:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic different from $\ell$,
let $j:X\hookrightarrow Y$ be an open immersion of finite-type
$k$-schemes, and let $F$ be a constructible
$\mathbf F_\ell$-sheaf. Then $Rj_*F\in D^b_c(Y,\mathbf F_\ell)$.
The notation refers to ordinary derived categories.

## Proof

Apply [thm-fin-deligne-generic-open] with
$S=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Its only nonempty open is $S$
itself, so the generic conclusion is the assertion on all of $Y$.
No stratification of $Y$ and no closed-base-change assertion
for $Rj_*$ is needed here.

attrs.title: Higher open direct images over a field

objects.body:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a projective
morphism of finite-type
schemes over a field, with geometric fibre dimensions at most one.
If the order of a finite abelian group $M$ is invertible on $S$,
every higher direct image
$R^qf_*\underline M$ is
constructible.

## Proof

A finite abelian group has a finite filtration with successive
quotients $\mathbf F_\ell$, for primes $\ell$ dividing its order.
Taking constant sheaves is exact, as may be checked on every stalk.
Proceed by induction along this filtration, starting from
[thm-fin-projective-curve-constant].
For $0\to M'\to M\to M''\to0$, the long exact sequence identifies
$R^qf_*\underline M$ in a short exact sequence with left term

$$
\operatorname{coker}(R^{q-1}f_*\underline {M''}
\to R^qf_*\underline {M'})
\quad\hbox{and right term}\quad
\ker(R^qf_*\underline {M''}\to R^{q+1}f_*\underline {M'}).
$$

All four sheaves are constructible by induction, with the
negative-degree term zero. The kernel, cokernel and extension
clauses of [thm-constructible-serre] finish the induction.

attrs.title: Finite constant groups on projective curve families

objects.body:
Let $Y$ be connected with geometric point $\bar y$ and let $M$ be a
finite abelian group. Then there is a canonical bijection

$$
H^1(Y_{\Et},\underline M)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cont}}\bigl(\pi_1(Y,\bar y),M\bigr),
$$

given on torsors by choosing $p\in P_{\bar y}$ — a simply transitive
$M$-set — and sending $P$ to the continuous homomorphism $f_P$ with

$$
g\cdot p=p+f_P(g)\qquad(g\in\pi_1(Y,\bar y));
$$

the class of $P$ is independent of the choice of $p$ because $M$ is
abelian. (This is the identification used, without citation, in the proof
of the additive-character lemma of the monodromy chapter.)

## Proof

By [thm-galois-fundamental] an $M$-torsor $P$ in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-finite-torsors] is a finite
$\pi_1$-set with a simply transitive $M$-action commuting with the
$\pi_1$-action. For $p\in P_{\bar y}$, [sbc-prop-torsors-h1] shows that
$g\cdot p=p+f_P(g)$ defines a continuous homomorphism
$f_P:\pi_1(Y,\bar y)\to M$ that is independent of $p$ (as $M$ is abelian)
and depends only on the isomorphism class of $P$.
Conversely a continuous homomorphism $f$ makes $M$ into a finite
continuous $\pi_1$-set by $g\cdot a=f(g)+a$, commuting with
translations, hence corresponds to an $M$-torsor. The constructions are
inverse. The identification with $H^1$ is
[thm-galois-torsor-h1].

Let $Y$ be connected with geometric point $\bar y$, and let $\Lambda$ be
a finite ring. Then evaluation at $\bar y$ is an exact equivalence between
locally constant sheaves of finite $\Lambda$-modules on $Y_{\Et}$ and
continuous $\Lambda$-linear representations of $\pi_1(Y,\bar y)$ on
finite $\Lambda$-modules. It is a tensor equivalence: for commutative
$\Lambda$ it carries $\mathcal F\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal G$ to
$\mathcal F_{\bar y}\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal G_{\bar y}$ with the diagonal
action and the constant sheaf $\Lambda$ to the trivial representation
$\Lambda$. It is compatible with base change along a map
$\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ of finite rings: it carries
$\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F$ to
$\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F_{\bar y}$ with the induced action. For $\Lambda=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ the
same holds for lisse $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-sheaves with finite
stalks, by the coefficient conventions of
[def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes].

## Proof

Here $\pi_1=\pi_1(Y,\bar y)=\operatorname{Aut}(F_{\bar y})$ is the group
of [def-galois-fibre-functor]. A locally constant sheaf of finite
$\Lambda$-modules is, by
[thm-galois-lc-etale] applied to the underlying sheaf of sets together
with the module structure, a finite etale cover with a $\Lambda$-linear
action of its automorphism group; by [thm-galois-fundamental] such
objects correspond to finite continuous $\pi_1$-sets with $\Lambda$-linear
action, i.e. to continuous representations on finite $\Lambda$-modules.
The $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-statement follows by writing a lisse sheaf
with finite stalks as a filtered colimit of finite-level ones over the
coefficient stages of [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes].

*Exactness.* Let $u:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ be a map of locally
constant sheaves of finite $\Lambda$-modules. Choose an etale covering
$\{U_i\to Y\}$ on which both are constant, $\mathcal F|_{U_i}\cong
\underline M_i$ and $\mathcal G|_{U_i}\cong\underline N_i$. A map
$\underline M_i\to\underline N_i$ on $U_i$ is a locally constant function
$U_i\to\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(M_i,N_i)$, a finite set, so $U_i$ is a
finite disjoint union of open and closed pieces on each of which $u$ is
a constant map $M_i\to N_i$. Refining the covering by these pieces, the
kernel and cokernel of $u$ (taken in all sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules)
are constant on each piece with finite values, hence locally constant of
finite $\Lambda$-modules. So the locally constant sheaves form a full
abelian subcategory closed under kernels and cokernels, and the stalk
functor, being exact on all sheaves, is exact on it. On the
representation side kernels and cokernels are computed on the underlying
modules with the induced action, so evaluation at $\bar y$ is an exact
equivalence of abelian categories.

*Naturality of the action.* By [def-galois-fibre-functor] an element
$\sigma\in\pi_1$ is a natural automorphism of $F_{\bar y}$ on finite
locally constant sheaves of sets, so for every map
$\phi:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ of such sheaves
$\phi_{\bar y}\circ\sigma=\sigma\circ\phi_{\bar y}$; applied to the
two projections of $\mathcal A\times\mathcal B$ this shows that $\sigma$
acts diagonally on $(\mathcal A\times\mathcal B)_{\bar y}
=\mathcal A_{\bar y}\times\mathcal B_{\bar y}$.

*Tensor products.* Let $\Lambda$ be commutative. The sheaf
$\mathcal F\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal G$ (sheafified presheaf tensor product)
has stalk $\mathcal F_{\bar y}\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal G_{\bar y}$, and on a
common trivializing covering it is constant with finite value
$M_i\otimes_\Lambda N_i$, so it is locally constant of finite
$\Lambda$-modules. The canonical bilinear map
$\mathcal F\times\mathcal G\to\mathcal F\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal G$ is a
map of finite locally constant sheaves of sets, so by the previous
paragraph its stalk $\mathcal F_{\bar y}\times\mathcal G_{\bar y}\to
(\mathcal F\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal G)_{\bar y}$ is equivariant for the
diagonal action; hence the stalk isomorphism
$\mathcal F_{\bar y}\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal G_{\bar y}\cong
(\mathcal F\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal G)_{\bar y}$ is $\pi_1$-equivariant
for the diagonal action on the source. These isomorphisms are natural and
compatible with the associativity, commutativity and unit constraints,
since they are so on stalks. The constant sheaf $\underline\Lambda$ has a
section over $Y$ through every point of its stalk, and $\sigma$ fixes the
stalk of a global section (naturality applied to the map
$\underline{\{*\}}\to\underline\Lambda$), so it goes to the trivial
representation $\Lambda$.

*Base change of coefficients.* For $\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ a map of finite
rings, $\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F$ has stalk
$\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F_{\bar y}$, which is finite, and is
constant with value $\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda M_i$ on each $U_i$, hence
locally constant of finite $\Lambda'$-modules. For each $\lambda'\in\Lambda'$
the map $\mathcal F\to\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F$,
$s\mapsto\lambda'\otimes s$, is a map of finite locally constant sheaves of
sets, so its stalk commutes with every $\sigma$; since the elements
$\lambda'\otimes m$ generate $\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F_{\bar y}$
additively, $\sigma$ acts on this stalk by $\lambda'\otimes m\mapsto
\lambda'\otimes\sigma m$, the induced action. The isomorphism is natural
in $\mathcal F$ and, for $\Lambda\to\Lambda'\to\Lambda''$, compatible with
composition, so evaluation at $\bar y$ commutes with base change of
coefficients (and, trivially, with restriction of scalars along
$\Lambda\to\Lambda'$).

Let $Y$ be connected with geometric point $\bar y$. Assigning to a
connected finite etale cover $P$ the stabilizer in $\pi_1(Y,\bar y)$ of a
point of $P_{\bar y}$ is a bijection between the isomorphism classes of
connected finite etale covers of $Y$ and the open subgroups of
$\pi_1(Y,\bar y)$, and the degree of $P$ over $Y$ is the index of the
subgroup. (This is the form used without citation in the proof of the
finite-monodromy lemma of the smooth base change chapter.)

## Proof

Here $\pi_1=\pi_1(Y,\bar y)=\operatorname{Aut}(F_{\bar y})$ is the group
of [def-galois-fibre-functor] and the covers are the finite etale
covers of [def-galois-object]. Under [thm-galois-fundamental] connected finite etale covers of $Y$
correspond to transitive finite continuous $\pi_1$-sets — the
transitivity being that of [lem-galois-transitive] — i.e. to
$\pi_1/H$ with $H$ open: the stabilizer of a point of $P_{\bar y}$ is
that subgroup, and $\#F_{\bar y}(P)=\#\pi_1/H=[\pi_1:H]$ is the degree. A
morphism of connected covers corresponds to an equivariant map
$\pi_1/H\to\pi_1/H'$, which exists exactly when $H'$ is contained in
$H$ up to conjugacy, so the assignment is bijective on isomorphism
classes.

attrs.title: Open subgroups and finite etale covers

objects.body:
Let $k$ be a separably closed
field, let $X$ and $Y$ be schemes of finite type over $k$, let
$n\ge1$ be an integer invertible in $k$, and let
$E\in D(X_{\Et},\kunZn)$, $K\in D(Y_{\Et},\kunZn)$. Choose
compactifications $j_X:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$ and
$j_Y:Y\hookrightarrow\overline Y$ over $k$, with $\overline X,\overline Y$
proper over $k$, and put
$R\Gamma_c(X_{\Et},E)=R\Gamma(\overline X_{\Et},j_{X,!}E)$ and similarly
for $Y$. Then the composite

$$
\begin{gathered}
R\Gamma_c(X_{\Et},E)\kunotimes{\kunZn}R\Gamma_c(Y_{\Et},K)
\\
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
R\Gamma\bigl((X\times_kY)_{\Et},
\pr_1^{-1}j_{X,!}E\kunotimes{\kunZn}\pr_2^{-1}j_{Y,!}K\bigr)
\\
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
R\Gamma_c\bigl((X\times_kY)_{\Et},
\pr_1^{-1}E\kunotimes{\kunZn}\pr_2^{-1}K\bigr)
\end{gathered}
$$

of the Künneth map of [thm-kun-0f1p] applied to $j_{X,!}E$ and
$j_{Y,!}K$ with the identification of the second line is an isomorphism;
the second arrow identifies
$\pr_1^{-1}j_{X,!}E\kunotimes{\kunZn}\pr_2^{-1}j_{Y,!}K$ with
$j_{X\times_kY,!}(\pr_1^{-1}E\kunotimes{\kunZn}\pr_2^{-1}K)$ along the
compactification $j_X\times_kj_Y$.

## Proof

The first arrow is an isomorphism by [thm-kun-0f1p], applied to the
complexes $j_{X,!}E\in D(\overline X_{\Et},\kunZn)$ and
$j_{Y,!}K\in D(\overline Y_{\Et},\kunZn)$ and to the isomorphism
$R\Gamma(\overline X_{\Et},j_{X,!}E)\cong R\Gamma_c(X_{\Et},E)$ which is
the definition of compact support
([def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]). For the second arrow: the
product of the two open immersions $j_X,j_Y$ is the open immersion
$j_X\times_kj_Y$ of $X\times_kY$ into
$\overline X\times_k\overline Y$, which is proper over $k$ because
properness is stable under products, so
$j_{X\times_kY,!}=j_{X,!}\boxtimes j_{Y,!}$ is the extension by zero along
the compactification, and the identity
$\pr_1^{-1}j_{X,!}E\kunotimes{\kunZn}\pr_2^{-1}j_{Y,!}K\cong (j_X\times_kj_Y)_!(\pr_1^{-1}E\kunotimes{\kunZn}\pr_2^{-1}K)$ is the compatibility
of the extension by zero with the tensor product and the inverse image
([def-weil-extension-by-zero]). The independence of the two
isomorphisms of the chosen compactifications is the coherence recorded in
[def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed].

attrs.title: Künneth formula for compactly supported cohomology

objects.body:
Let $X_0$ be a normal geometrically connected curve over $k_0$, put
$|k_0|=q$, and fix a real weight character $\lambda$ ([d-weights]). Let
$\rho:W(X_0)\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$ be the representation of a lisse
Weil sheaf, with the monodromy data of [def-wf-monodromy-data], computed
with one fixed degree-one element $s$, and let
$z=(h,m)\in G^{[m]}(\Qlb)$ be an algebraic-monodromy element of positive
degree $m$ which is central in $G_{\mathrm{arith}}(\rho)$ (an element
furnished by [lem-mg-common-positive-central-element] when $\rho$ is
semisimple). Let $Q\neq0$ be a Weil-stable subquotient of $V$, or more
generally any of the tensor, exterior-power or iterated-subquotient
constructions of [lem-mg-degree-component-functoriality], of rank $r$,
with Weil representation $\rho_Q$, with finite geometric determinant,
i.e. $\det\rho_Q(\pi_1(X))$ finite, and with the homomorphism
$\Phi_Q:G_{\mathrm{arith}}(\rho)\to G_{\mathrm{arith}}(\rho_Q)$ of that
lemma. The representation $Q$ need not be irreducible or semisimple.
Say that $z$ *acts on $Q$ as a scalar* $c_Q\in\Qlb^\times$ if the matrix
of $\Phi_Q(z)$ under the matrix map $(h',n)\mapsto h'\rho_Q(s)^n$ of
[def-wf-arithmetic-monodromy-extension] is $c_Q\,1_Q$. If $z$ acts on
$Q$ as a scalar $c_Q$, then

$$
\dw_\lambda(Q)=\frac{\lambda(c_Q)}{m}.
$$

The scalar-action hypothesis holds whenever $Q$ is Weil-irreducible.
In particular, for an irreducible lisse Weil sheaf $\mathcal W_0$ of rank
$r$ with representation $\rho_{\mathcal W}$ and finite geometric
determinant, and $z\in G^{[m]}$ central in
$G_{\mathrm{arith}}(\rho_{\mathcal W})$ (the case $V=Q$, $\Phi_Q$ the
identity), $z$ acts by a scalar $c_W$ and

$$
\dw_\lambda(\mathcal W_0)=\frac{\lambda(c_W)}{m};
$$

for $\lambda=\lambda_\iota$ this reads

$$
\frac{2\log_q|\iota(\det\rho_{\mathcal W}(s))|}{r}=\frac{2\log_q|\iota(c_W)|}{m},
$$

where $\log_q$ is the base-$q$ logarithm. The determinant weight
$\dw_\lambda(Q)$ does not depend on the degree-one element used to
define it in [d-weights].

## Proof

*The matrix map is a homomorphism.* For $(h',n),(h'',p)$ in
$G_{\mathrm{arith}}(\rho_Q)$, the product
$(h'\alpha^n(h''),n+p)$ of [def-wf-arithmetic-monodromy-extension] has
matrix
$h'\rho_Q(s)^nh''\rho_Q(s)^{-n}\rho_Q(s)^{n+p}
=(h'\rho_Q(s)^n)(h''\rho_Q(s)^p)$. If $w\in W(X_0)$ has degree $n$,
then $ws^{-n}\in\pi_1(X)$, so $(\rho_Q(ws^{-n}),n)$ lies in
$G_{\mathrm{arith}}(\rho_Q)$ and its matrix is $\rho_Q(w)$.

*The general scalar case.* Let
$\chi_{\det}=\det\circ\rho_Q:W(X_0)\to\Qlb^\times$ be the character of
the determinant line of $Q$, and put $c=\chi_{\det}(s)$. Write
$\Phi_Q(z)=(h_Q,m)$ with $h_Q\in H_{\mathrm{geom}}(\rho_Q)$; the degree
is $m$ because $\Phi_Q$ preserves degrees
([lem-mg-degree-component-functoriality]). By hypothesis its matrix is
$h_Q\rho_Q(s)^m=c_Q1_Q$, and taking determinants on the $r$-dimensional
space $Q$ gives

$$
c_Q^r=\det(h_Q)\,c^m .
$$

The morphism $\Delta_{\rho_Q}$ of
[lem-mg-determinant-monodromy-morphism] sends $\Phi_Q(z)$ to
$(\det h_Q,m)$ in the arithmetic monodromy group of the rank-one
determinant line. The group $A=\chi_{\det}(\pi_1(X))$ is finite by
hypothesis, so [lem-wf-rank-one-algebraic-extension] applies: in the
notation of [def-wf-degree-components],
$H_{\mathrm{geom}}(\chi_{\det})=A$ and
$G_{\mathrm{arith}}(\chi_{\det})=A\times\mathbf Z$, so
$a:=\det h_Q\in A$. The element $a$ has finite order, and a real weight
character kills finite-order elements: if $a^e=1$ with $e>0$, then
$e\lambda(a)=\lambda(a^e)=0$. Applying $\lambda$ therefore gives
$r\lambda(c_Q)=m\lambda(c)$, that is,

$$
\frac{\lambda(c_Q)}{m}=\frac{\lambda(c)}{r}=\dw_\lambda(Q)
$$

by the definition in [d-weights]. Only the scalar action of $z$ on $Q$
was used here, not the irreducibility or semisimplicity of $Q$.

*Irreducible $Q$.* By [lem-mg-degree-component-functoriality],
$\Phi_Q(z)$ is central in $G_{\mathrm{arith}}(\rho_Q)$. By the first
paragraph its matrix commutes with the matrix $\rho_Q(w)$ of every
$(\rho_Q(ws^{-n}),n)$, i.e. with the whole Weil-group image. If $Q$ is
Weil-irreducible, [lem-wf-schur-scalar] makes this matrix a scalar
$c_Q$, nonzero because the matrix is invertible. Taking $V=Q$ and
$\Phi_Q$ the identity gives the stated case of $\mathcal W_0$, and the
case $\lambda=\lambda_\iota$ is the last display.

*Independence of the lift.* Replacing the degree-one element by $us$
with $u\in\pi_1(X)$ multiplies $\chi_{\det}(s)$ by the finite-order
element $\chi_{\det}(u)\in A$, which $\lambda$ kills; so
$\dw_\lambda(Q)$ does not depend on the degree-one lift.

attrs.title: Central element determines the determinant weight

objects.body:
Let $X_0$ be a normal geometrically connected curve over $k_0$, put
$|k_0|=q$, fix $\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$, and let
$\mathcal F_0$ be a nonzero lisse
Weil sheaf on $X_0$ with
semisimple geometric
representation. Choose a
composition series in the sense of
[def-mg-weil-composition-series], with simple factors
$A_1,\ldots,A_t$. Write $d_a=\dim A_a$ and let $\gamma_a$ be the
determinantal weight of $A_a$.
Let $R$ be the set of distinct values among the $\gamma_a$, and put

$$
r(\gamma):=\sum_{\gamma_a=\gamma}d_a,
$$

Thus $\dim V=\sum_{\gamma\in R}r(\gamma)$. For every
$0\le r\le\dim V$, every Jordan–Holder constituent of the exterior
power $\bigwedge^r\mathcal F_0$ (constituents and exterior powers of
Weil representations as in [def-real-weil-representation-operations])
has determinant weight

$$
\sum_{\gamma\in R}n_\gamma\gamma,
\qquad 0\le n_\gamma\le r(\gamma),
\qquad \sum_{\gamma\in R}n_\gamma=r.
$$

Conversely every admissible tuple $(n_\gamma)$ occurs as the
determinant weight of at least one
Jordan–Holder constituent. The input factors
$\gamma_a$ are counted with multiplicity as in
[def-mg-determinantal-weight-multiset]; the assertion concerns the
possible weights and their non-emptiness, not an equality of output
multiplicities for coincident sums.

## Proof

The factors $A_a$ are those of the chosen series of
[def-mg-weil-composition-series], counted as in
[def-mg-determinantal-weight-multiset], and $\gamma_a$ is their
determinantal weight in the sense of [def-wf-determinantal-weight] (the
geometric semisimplicity of [def-wf-geometric-semisimplicity] is not
needed for the argument). By [lem-rp-determinant-weights-agree], every
$A_a$ and every Jordan–Holder constituent of
$\bigwedge^r\mathcal F_0$ has finite geometric determinant, and for
each of them $\dw_\iota$ equals $\dw_{\lambda_\iota}$. Hence
[prop-ag-det-weight-exterior], applied with $\lambda=\lambda_\iota$, gives the assertion and
its converse.

attrs.title: Determinant weights of an exterior power

objects.body:
Let $\mathcal F_0$ be a nonzero lisse Weil sheaf with
semisimple geometric
representation on a normal geometrically connected curve $X_0$, and let
$\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n$ be its determinant weights, counted with
multiplicity in [def-mg-determinantal-weight-multiset]. For every
$k\ge1$, every Jordan–Holder constituent of the tensor power
$\mathcal F_0^{\otimes k}$ (constituents and tensor products of Weil
representations as in [def-real-weil-representation-operations]) has
determinant weight

$$
\alpha_{i_1}+\cdots+\alpha_{i_k}
$$

for some indices $i_1,\ldots,i_k$, and every such sum occurs for at
least one constituent. In particular, if $\beta=\max_i\alpha_i$, the
largest determinant weight of $\mathcal F_0^{\otimes k}$ is
$k\beta$.

## Proof

Choose a composition series of the Weil representation in the sense of
[def-mg-weil-composition-series], with simple factors $A_i$. By
[lem-mg-jordan-holder] and [def-mg-determinantal-weight-multiset], after
reindexing, $\alpha_i=\dw_\iota(A_i)$ (the geometric semisimplicity of
[def-wf-geometric-semisimplicity] is not needed for the argument). By
[lem-rp-determinant-weights-agree], every $A_i$ and every
Jordan–Holder constituent of $\mathcal F_0^{\otimes k}$ has finite
geometric determinant, and for each of them the determinant weight
$\dw_\iota$ of [def-wf-determinantal-weight] equals
$\dw_{\lambda_\iota}$. We prove both assertions by induction on $k$,
using the two-factor tensor rule [prop-ag-det-weight-two-factor-tensor]
with $\lambda=\lambda_\iota$. For $k=1$ the constituents of
$\mathcal F_0$ are the $A_i$ by [lem-mg-jordan-holder], with
determinant weights $\alpha_i$. For $k\ge2$ apply
[prop-ag-det-weight-two-factor-tensor] to $\mathcal V_0=\mathcal
F_0^{\otimes(k-1)}$ and $\mathcal E_0=\mathcal F_0$, both nonzero and
lisse on $X_0$, with composition series whose factors are the
constituents of $\mathcal F_0^{\otimes(k-1)}$, respectively the $A_j$;
all of these, and all constituents of $\mathcal F_0^{\otimes k}$, have
finite geometric determinant by the previous paragraph. Every
constituent $Q$ of $\mathcal F_0^{\otimes k}$ therefore has
$\dw(Q)=\dw(V_i)+\alpha_j$ for a constituent $V_i$ of
$\mathcal F_0^{\otimes(k-1)}$, which by induction has weight
$\alpha_{i_1}+\cdots+\alpha_{i_{k-1}}$. Conversely, by induction every
sum $\alpha_{i_1}+\cdots+\alpha_{i_{k-1}}$ is the weight of some
constituent $V_i$, and the converse half of
[prop-ag-det-weight-two-factor-tensor] gives a constituent of
$\mathcal F_0^{\otimes k}$ of weight $\dw(V_i)+\alpha_{i_k}$. The
statement about $\beta$ follows by taking all indices with
$\alpha_{i_r}=\beta$.

attrs.title: Determinant weights of a finite tensor power

objects.body:
Let $X_0$ be a normal geometrically connected curve over $k_0$, put
$|k_0|=q$, and let
$\mathcal L_0$ be a rank-one lisse
Weil sheaf on $X_0$ with Weil
character $\chi:\hyperref[def-wf-weil-group]{W(X_0)}\to E^\times$, with $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$
finite, such that $\chi(\pi_1(X))$ is finite, and fix
$\iota:E\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$. For $w\in\mathbf R$ the
sheaf $\mathcal L_0$ is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$ if
and only if there is (equivalently, for every) element
$\sigma\in W(X_0)$ of positive degree $d$ with

$$
|\iota(\chi(\sigma))|=q^{wd/2}.
$$

## Proof

Fix a degree-one lift $s\in W(X_0)$ as in
[def-wf-weil-group], and put $c=\chi(s)$. By
hypothesis the restriction of
$\chi$ to $\pi_1(X)$ has finite image, and by the modulus identity
of [lem-wf-rank-one-component-modulus] applied to the image of
the degree-$m$ coset of $W(X_0)$ in
$G^{[m]}\subseteq G_{\mathrm{arith}}(\rho)$ (an element
$w=\gamma s^m$ with $\gamma\in\pi_1(X)$ has matrix
$\rho(\gamma)\rho(s)^m$), one has

$$
|\iota(\chi(w))|=|\iota(c)|^{m}\qquad\text{for all }w\in W(X_0)
\text{ with }\deg(w)=m.
$$

If $\mathcal L_0$ is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$, then at
a closed point $x$ the eigenvalue $\chi(F_x)$ of the local
geometric Frobenius $F_x$ (of degree $d(x)$) has modulus
$q_x^{w/2}=q^{d(x)w/2}$ by [def-weil-punctual-weights], so the
identity above gives $|\iota(c)|^{d(x)}=q^{d(x)w/2}$, whence
$|\iota(c)|=q^{w/2}$ and
$|\iota(\chi(\sigma))|=|\iota(c)|^{d}=q^{wd/2}$ for every
positive-degree $\sigma$. Conversely, if the displayed equality
holds for one such $\sigma$, then $|\iota(c)|=q^{w/2}$ by the same
identity, and every closed point $x$ satisfies
$|\iota(\chi(F_x))|=|\iota(c)|^{d(x)}=q_x^{w/2}$, which is the
punctual purity of [def-weil-punctual-weights].

attrs.title: Rank-one weight from a positive-degree element

objects.body:
Let $X$ be a scheme. If $\mathcal I$ is an invertible ideal on $X$, then
$b_{X,\mathcal I}$ is an isomorphism.

## Proof

The identity of $X$ lifts to the blow-up by the universal property. Compose
this lift with the blow-up map in both orders and use uniqueness.

attrs.title: Blow-up of an effective Cartier center

objects.body:
The constructed $d_{\mathcal I}$ and $d_{\mathcal J}$ are morphisms over
$X$. If both ideals restrict to the unit ideal on an open $U$, the product
blow-up and both maps restrict to the identity over $U$.

## Proof

The maps are composites over $X$ by definition. On $U$, all three ideals
are the unit ideal, so all three blow-ups are identified with $U$ by the
complement theorem. The universal maps are unique over $U$, hence become
the identity under these identifications.

attrs.title: Common refinement by the product ideal

objects.body:
Let $S$ be qcqs, let $X$ be a qcqs $S$-scheme, let $U\subseteq X$ be a dense
quasi-compact open subscheme, and let $Y\to S$ be proper and of finite type.
Every $S$-morphism $f\colon U\to Y$ extends to an $S$-morphism
$\widetilde f\colon\widetilde X\to Y$ on some $U$-admissible blow-up
$\widetilde X\to X$.

## Proof

Take $V=U$. By
[lemma-nagata-conrad-morphism-is-quasi-domination], $(U,f)$ is a
quasi-domination of $U$ over $Y$, because a proper morphism is separated.
[thm-nagata-conrad-elimination] gives a $U$-admissible blow-up
$\widetilde X\to X$ and a quasi-domination $(W,\widetilde f)$ of
$\widetilde X$ over $Y$ extending $f$. Since $Y\to S$ is proper,
[lemma-nagata-conrad-quasi-domination-proper-target] forces $W$ to be
all of $\widetilde X$.

attrs.title: Extension of a rational map to a proper target (Conrad)

objects.body:
Let $k$ be a separably closed field and let $X$ be a scheme over $k$
which is smooth over $k$.

1. For every field extension $K/k$ put $X_K=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K$, and for
$x\in X(k)$ let $x_K=\operatorname{Spec}(K)\times_kx$ be the induced $K$-rational point of
$X_K$. Then the set $\{x_K : x\in X(k)\}$ is Zariski dense in $X_K$ (for $K=k$
this is the density of $X(k)$ in $X$).
1. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_{X_K}$-module and
$s\in H^0(X_K,\mathcal{L})$ a section which does not vanish identically, i.e.
$s(y)\neq0$ in $\mathcal{L}(y)=\mathcal{L}_y\otimes\kappa(y)$ for some $y\in X_K$.
Then there is an $x\in X(k)$ such that $s$ does not vanish at $x_K$.
1. If $X$ is a smooth projective curve over $k$, then $X(k)$ is infinite.
If moreover $K=k$, then every non-zero $s\in H^0(X,\mathcal{L})$, for $\mathcal{L}$ an
invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module, does not vanish identically, so (2) applies:
$s(x)\neq0$ for some $x\in X(k)$.

## Proof

(1) Let $p:X_K\to X$ be the projection. It is the base change of
$\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ along $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, and the structure morphism of any
scheme over a field is universally open (Morphisms of Schemes,
Lemma 29.23.4, Tag [0383](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0383));
hence $p$ is open. Let $Z\subseteq X_K$ be a closed subset containing every
$x_K$, and suppose $U:=X_K\setminus Z\neq\emptyset$. Then $p(U)\subseteq X$ is a
nonempty open subset, so by [lem-pc-rational-points-dense] it contains a
point $x\in X(k)$. The fibre of $p$ over $x$ is
$\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(x)\otimes_kK)=\operatorname{Spec}(k\otimes_kK)=\operatorname{Spec}K$, a single point, namely
$x_K$. Since $x\in p(U)$, some point of $U$ lies over $x$, so $x_K\in U$,
contradicting $x_K\in Z$. Hence $Z=X_K$, which is the asserted density.

(2) The set $W:=\{y\in X_K : s(y)\neq0\}$ is open: on an open
$V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X_K$ on which $\mathcal{L}$ is free on a generator $e$
([def-sc-invertible-module]) write $s|_V=a\cdot e$ with $a\in A$; then
$s(y)\neq0$ if and only if $a\notin\mathfrak p_y$, so $W\cap V=D(a)$. By
hypothesis $W\neq\emptyset$, so its complement is a closed subset not
containing all of $X_K$; by (1) it misses some $x_K$, i.e. $x_K\in W$.

(3) A smooth projective curve is in particular a curve over $k$
([def-pc-smooth-projective-curve]), hence an integral scheme of
dimension one ([def-pc-curve]); in particular $X\neq\emptyset$ and its
generic point $\eta$ is not closed. Every $x\in X(k)$ is a closed point
(its residue field is $k$). If $X(k)$ were finite, it would be a finite
union of closed points, hence a closed subset of $X$ not containing
$\eta$; but $X(k)$ is dense in $X$ by [lem-pc-rational-points-dense], so
its closure is $X\ni\eta$, a contradiction. Hence $X(k)$ is infinite.
For the last assertion let $0\neq s\in H^0(X,\mathcal{L})$. Since $X$ is
integral, restriction of sections of $\mathcal{L}$ to the generic point is
injective on every nonempty open (on an affine open
$\operatorname{Spec}A$ trivialising $\mathcal{L}$, with $A$ a domain, $s=a\cdot e$ and
$a\neq0$ in $A\subseteq\operatorname{Frac}A=\kappa(\eta)$), so $s_\eta\neq0$ in the
one-dimensional $\kappa(\eta)$-vector space $\mathcal{L}_\eta=\mathcal{L}(\eta)$; thus $s$ does not
vanish at $\eta$ and (2) (with $K=k$) gives $x\in X(k)$ with $s(x)\neq0$.

*Remark on base change.* For a general extension $K/k$ the hypothesis
of (2) holds for every non-zero $s$ as soon as $X_K$ is integral (by the
generic-point argument of (3) applied on $X_K$); for a smooth projective
curve with a rational point this integrality is established later in
the twist-lemma block, where this statement is used in exactly that
form.

attrs.title: Consequences of the density of rational points

objects.body:
Let $S$ be locally Noetherian, let $f:X\to S$ be
projective, and let
$\mathcal G$ be a coherent
$\mathcal O_X$-module flat over $S$.
For any morphism $g:T\to S$, without a Noetherian hypothesis on
$T$, the canonical base-change map

$$
Lg^*(Rf_*\mathcal G)\longrightarrow Rf_{T,*}\mathcal G_T
$$

is an isomorphism, and both sides are perfect.
The symbols $Lg^*$ and $Rf_*$ denote the
derived pullback and
derived direct image.

## Proof

The isomorphism is [lem-pc-rf-base-change-flat-module].
By [lem-pc-projective-noetherian-rf-perfect], the source
before pullback is perfect. Locally it is a bounded complex of
finite projective modules, as in [def-pc-perfect-complex].
Tensoring such a complex with any base algebra preserves this
description: a finite projective module is the image of an
idempotent on a finite free module, and tensoring preserves that
idempotent decomposition. Hence derived pullback is perfect,
and the isomorphic right side is perfect as well.

attrs.title: Arbitrary base change for a projective Noetherian family

objects.body:
Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be a smooth projective curve over $k$ with
a $k$-rational point $\sigma$. Then the functors
$\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}$ and
$\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k}$ on
$(\mathit{Sch}/k)_{fppf}$ are isomorphic. In particular
$\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}$ is an fppf sheaf (represented once $\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k}$ is;
and covariantly: if $\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}$ is representable, then so is
$\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k}$, by the group law of [thm-pc-pic-split]).

## Proof

By [lem-pc-rational-hyp] and [thm-pc-pic-split],
$\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k}$ is the fppf sheafification of the presheaf
$K(T)=\operatorname{Ker}(\sigma_T^*)$, and by [lem-pc-k-sheaf] the
presheaf $K$ is itself an fppf sheaf; since
$\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}=K$ ([def-pc-pic-sigma-functor]), the two functors
are naturally isomorphic. [The reference is the discussion in Stacks
Project, Picard Schemes of Curves, Section 44.6, after Lemma 44.6.1.]

Let $k$ be a field, let $C$ be a
smooth projective curve over $k$
which is geometrically integral,
and let $(J_s,\varphi)$ be the scheme with its
descent datum furnished by
[lem-pd-canonical-descent-datum] and [lem-pd-descent-cocycle]. Then
there are a finite separable extension $K/k$, a scheme $J_K$ of finite
presentation over $K$, and a descent datum
$\varphi_K$ on $J_K$ over $\Spec(K)/\Spec(k)$ such that
$J_K\times_KK_s\cong J_s$ and such that $\varphi_K$
base changes to $\varphi$; moreover $J_K$ may
be chosen projective over $K$.

## Proof

The datum $(J_s,\varphi)$ of [lem-pd-canonical-descent-datum] and
[lem-pd-descent-cocycle] is a
[def-pd-descent-datum] over $\Spec(k_s)/\Spec(k)$ with $k_s$ the
[def-pd-separable-closure]. Write
$k_s=\colim_{K/k\ \text{finite separable}}K$ and $S_i=\Spec(K_i)$ for the
finite separable subextensions, an inverse system with affine transition
morphisms and affine (hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated) terms, whose
limit is $S=\Spec(k_s)$; all fibre products below are the finite-presentation
ones of [def-pc-morphism-conventions]. The scheme $J_s$ is of finite
presentation over $k_s$: it is smooth over the field $k_s$ and of finite type,
by [thm-pd-geometric-pic0]. By
[thm-pd-spreading-out](1) there are $i$ and a scheme $J_i$ of finite
presentation over $K_i$ with $J_i\times_{K_i}k_s\cong J_s$; enlarge $i$ if
necessary so that the $\varphi$ and the cocycle equation, which are morphisms
and equalities of morphisms of finite presentation between finitely presented
schemes, spread out as well, using [thm-pd-spreading-out](2) and
[thm-pd-spreading-out](3); the spread-out isomorphism is the descent
datum $\varphi_K$ over $\Spec(K)/\Spec(k)$, whose base change to $\Spec(k_s)$
is $\varphi$ by the very form of [def-pc-base-change]. To obtain
projectivity, apply [thm-pd-spreading-out](2) to a closed immersion
$J_s\hookrightarrow\mathbf{P}^N_{k_s}$, which exists because $J_s$ is an
abelian variety by [thm-pd-geometric-pic0] and abelian varieties are
projective by [lem-sc-abelian-variety-projective]; the target
$\mathbf{P}^N_{k_s}$ is the base change of $\mathbf{P}^N_{K_i}$, so the
immersion descends to a closed immersion $J_{i'}\hookrightarrow \mathbf{P}^N_{K_{i'}}$ for some $i'\geq i$, exhibiting $J_{i'}$ as a
[def-pc-projective-morphism] over $K_{i'}$. Put
$K=K_{i'}$ and $J_K=J_{i'}$.

attrs.title: The descent datum is defined at a finite separable level

objects.body:
Let $k$ be a field, let $C$ be a
smooth projective curve over $k$
which is geometrically integral,
and let $k'/k$ be a field extension. Then the
base change of the
degree-zero part along
$\Spec(k')\to\Spec(k)$ is the degree-zero part of the base change:

$$
\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\times_k k'\;\cong\;\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C_{k'}/k'} .
$$

## Proof

By [lem-pd-picard-base-change] the functor
$\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}$ restricts to
$\operatorname{Pic}_{C_{k'}/k'}$ on the slice over $k'$, and the restriction of
a functor to a slice is the base change in the sense of
[def-pc-base-change]. The degree morphism of
[def-pd-degree-morphism] is defined through the fibrewise degree, and
[lem-pd-degree-locally-constant](3) says precisely that it is compatible
with this restriction: the restriction of
$\deg:\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\to\underline{\Z}$ is the degree morphism of
$C_{k'}$. Restricting the kernel of a morphism of sheaves to a slice gives
the kernel of the restricted morphism, so the two degree-zero parts agree after
base change, which is the displayed isomorphism.

attrs.title: The degree-zero part is compatible with base change

objects.body:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective curve ([def-pc-smooth-projective-curve])
which is geometrically irreducible, hence geometrically integral with
$H^0(X,\cO_X)=k$ (this is needed: for $X=\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf C}$ over
$k=\mathbf R$ and $K=\mathbf C$ the conclusion fails),
of genus $g$ and $\cL$ a line
bundle on $X_K$ ($K/k$ any field extension) with $h^0(X_K,\cL)=1$
and $H^q(X_K,\cL)=0$ for $q>0$. Then

$$
\deg(\cL)=\chi(\cL)-\chi(\cO_{X_K})=1-(1-g)=g.
$$

This is the exact instance of Riemann–Roch used in the
zero-scheme dictionary ([lem-pc-zero-scheme-recd]).

## Proof

The vanishing gives $\chi(\cL)=h^0=1$ ([def-pc-euler-characteristic]).
Riemann–Roch [lem-sc-riemann-roch], applied to $\cO$ after the flat
base change to $\bar K$ (which changes neither $\chi(\cO)$ nor the
genus, [lem-pc-genus-base-change], whose hypotheses "geometrically
irreducible with $H^0(X,\cO_X)=k$" are the ones assumed here; the
smooth projective curve
$X_{\bar K}$ over the algebraically closed field $\bar K$ is a proper
smooth connected curve in the sense of that lemma by
[lem-pc-curves-are-sc], $X_{\bar K}$ being integral because $X$ is
geometrically integral), gives $\chi(\cO_{X_K})=1-g$; and
$\deg\cL=\chi(\cL)-\chi(\cO_{X_K})$ by [def-pc-degree-line-bundle].
Hence $\deg\cL=g$.

Uses: [def-pc-degree-line-bundle], [def-pc-euler-characteristic], [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve], [lem-pc-curves-are-sc], [lem-pc-genus-base-change], [lem-sc-riemann-roch]

In the Poincare duality conventions of this chapter (the fixed setting; $X_0$ not necessarily proper), restrict to the field stage $\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$, and put $K=\Lambda _X$ (perfect, with canonical evaluation the unit identification). Poincare duality is the perfect pairing

$$
H_c^i(X,\Lambda )\times H^{2d-i}\bigl(X,\Lambda (d)\bigr) \longrightarrow \Lambda ,
$$

equivalently the line-valued pairing

$$
H_c^i(X,\Lambda )\times H^{2d-i}(X,\Lambda ) \longrightarrow \Lambda (-d),
$$

for every $i\in \mathbf Z$. Since $X$ is geometrically connected, the $i=2d$ case together with $H^0(X,\Lambda)\cong\Lambda$ (the connectedness clause of Proposition 1.58) gives

$$
H_c^{2d}\bigl(X,\Lambda (d)\bigr)\cong \Lambda , \qquad H_c^{2d}(X,\Lambda )\cong \Lambda (-d),
$$

with the first isomorphism induced by the trace map $\operatorname{tr}_X$; if $X_0$ is proper, the same holds with $H_c$ replaced by $H$.

## Proof

Step 1: the coefficient dual of the constant object. For $K=\Lambda _X$, $K^\vee =R\mathcal Hom_X(\Lambda _X,\Lambda _X)=\Lambda _X$ with the unit identification as the canonical evaluation, by the internal-Hom with the unit object of [def-pod-coefficient-dual-on-x]; therefore

$$
K^\vee (d)[2d]=\Lambda _X(d)[2d].
$$

Step 2: the pairings. By [thm-pod-derived-poincare-duality] the derived pairing is perfect, and by [thm-pod-degreewise-perfectness-over-a-field] the degreewise pairings

$$
H_c^i(X,\Lambda )\times H^{2d-i}\bigl(X,\Lambda (d)\bigr)\to \Lambda
$$

are perfect; the line-valued form is the twist elimination of [prop-pod-degree-of-the-pairing]. None of this uses properness. Step 3: the top degree. Perfectness at $i=2d$ gives $H_c^{2d}(X,\Lambda )\cong H^0(X,\Lambda (d))^\vee$. Since $X_0$ is geometrically connected, $X$ is connected and $H^0(X,\Lambda )\cong \Lambda$ with the geometric Frobenius acting as the identity, by the connectedness clause of [prop-cohomological-finiteness], which needs no properness; hence $H^0(X,\Lambda(d))\cong\Lambda(d)$ and $H_c^{2d}(X,\Lambda)\cong\Lambda(d)^\vee=\Lambda(-d)$, and twisting by $d$ ([prop-pod-degree-of-the-pairing]) gives $H_c^{2d}(X,\Lambda (d))\cong \Lambda$. Step 4: the identification with the trace. Under this duality, moved by the twist elimination of [prop-pod-degree-of-the-pairing] to $H_c^{2d}(X,\Lambda(d))\times H^0(X,\Lambda)\to\Lambda$, $x\in H_c^{2d}(X,\Lambda(d))$ corresponds to the functional $1\mapsto\beta(x\otimes 1)$ on $H^0(X,\Lambda)=\Lambda\cdot 1$. By [def-pod-derived-poincare-pairing], $\beta(x\otimes1)$ is the normalized smooth trace of $x\smile_c 1$, and $x\smile_c1=x$ by the unit clause of [prop-pod-cup-product-coherence]; so the isomorphism $H_c^{2d}(X,\Lambda(d))\cong\Lambda$ is $x\mapsto\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{a_X,\Lambda}(x)$, the counit of $Ra_{X!}\dashv Ra_X^!$ through $\eta_X$ with the normalization of [def-pur-smooth-trace], i.e. the trace map $\operatorname{tr}_X$ of [def-weil-poincare-trace-cup] (whose definition on $H_c^{2d}$ uses no properness); its untwisted form is $\operatorname {tr}^{(-d)}_X:H_c^{2d}(X,\Lambda)\to\Lambda(-d)$. The last assertion (for $X_0$ proper, $H_c$ replaced by $H$) is the proper comparison of [thm-pod-proper-poincare-duality].

In the Poincare duality conventions of this chapter (the fixed setting), strict Weil complex with $K$ perfect, at a *field* coefficient stage $\Lambda \in \{ E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell }\}$ (the hypothesis of [thm-pod-degreewise-perfectness-over-a-field]; the statement fails over $\mathcal O_E$, where the degreewise pairing need not be perfect). Relative to the perfect pairing of Theorem 9.23, the operator $F_{K^\vee }$ on $H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee )$ is conjugate to

$$
q^d\, \bigl(F_{c,K}^{-1}\bigr)^{\mathsf t}.
$$

Thus an eigenvalue $\alpha$ of $F_{c,K}$ on $H_c^i(X,K)$ with algebraic multiplicity $m$ corresponds, with the same multiplicity, to the eigenvalue $q^d/\alpha$ of $F_{K^\vee }$ on $H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee )$. If $X_0$ is proper, the first space is $H^i(X,K)$.

## Proof

Step 1: the adjoint identification. By [thm-pod-degreewise-perfectness-over-a-field] the degreewise pairing is perfect, so the bilinear form $b:H_c^i(X,K)\times H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee )\to \Lambda$ is nondegenerate and the map

$$
\Phi :H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee )\longrightarrow H_c^i(X,K)^\vee , \qquad \Phi (y)(x)=\langle x,y\rangle ^{\mathrm{untw}}_i,
$$

is an isomorphism of $\Lambda$-vector spaces, the field-stage dual being the ordinary dual, by [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Step 2: the similitude translates. The untwisted similitude of [cor-pod-untwisted-similitude], $b(F_{c,K}x,F_{K^\vee }y)=q^db(x,y)$, says precisely that

$$
\Phi \circ F_{K^\vee }=q^d\, \bigl(F_{c,K}^{-1}\bigr)^{\mathsf t}\circ \Phi ,
$$

where $\bigl(F_{c,K}^{-1}\bigr)^{\mathsf t}$ is the transpose of the inverse operator on the dual $H_c^i(X,K)^\vee$. Therefore $F_{K^\vee }=q^d\Phi ^{-1}\bigl(F_{c,K}^{-1}\bigr)^{\mathsf t}\Phi$, i.e. $F_{K^\vee }$ is conjugate to $q^d\bigl(F_{c,K}^{-1}\bigr)^{\mathsf t}$. Step 3: eigenvalues. A linear operator on a finite-dimensional vector space and its transpose have the same characteristic polynomial, and conjugation does not change it, so the eigenvalues of $F_{K^\vee }$ are the eigenvalues of $q^dF_{c,K}^{-1}$; on the finite-dimensional space $H_c^i(X,K)$ (Step 1 and the finite-dimensionality of [thm-pod-degreewise-perfectness-over-a-field]) the eigenvalues of an automorphism are the inverses of the eigenvalues of the operator, each with the same algebraic multiplicity, so the eigenvalues of $F_{K^\vee }$ are the $q^d/\alpha$ with the multiplicities of the eigenvalues $\alpha$ of $F_{c,K}$. Step 4: the last assertion is the proper comparison $H_c^i=H^i$ of [thm-pod-proper-poincare-duality], which requires $X_0$ proper.

In the Poincare duality conventions of this chapter (the fixed setting), strict Weil complex with $K$ perfect. The untwisted, line-valued pairing of Proposition 9.21 takes values in $A(-d)$, on which geometric Frobenius acts by $q^d$, and it satisfies

$$
\bigl\langle F_{c,K}x,\; F_{K^\vee }y\bigr\rangle _i^{\mathrm{untw}} =q^d\langle x,y\rangle _i^{\mathrm{untw}} \qquad \bigl(x\in H_c^i(X,K),\  y\in H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee )\bigr).
$$

In particular, for $K=K_X=\Lambda_X$ the constant sheaf with its canonical datum and $K^\vee \cong K_X$ canonically, applying the operator $F$ to both arguments gives

$$
\langle Fx,Fy\rangle _i=q^d\langle x,y\rangle _i.
$$

## Proof

Step 1: eliminate the twist. The second factor of the twisted pairing is $H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee (d))$, which is identified with $H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee )\otimes _A\Lambda (d)$ by the definition of the twist in [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] (twisting a complex commutes with global sections; this is the identification of [prop-pod-degree-of-the-pairing]), and the datum $\varphi _{K^\vee (d)}=\varphi _{K^\vee }\otimes \tau _d$ of [def-pod-dual-tate-datum] consists of the contragredient datum on $K^\vee$ together with the scalar $q^{-d}$ on the twist line by [def-pur-tate-datum]. Step 2: write $y=y_0\otimes \xi _d$ under that identification; then $F_{K^\vee (d)}y=F_{K^\vee }y_0\otimes q^{-d}\xi _d$, and the identity of [thm-pod-equivariance-of-the-twisted-pairing] reads

$$
\langle F_{c,K}x,\; F_{K^\vee }y_0\rangle _i^{\mathrm{untw}}\cdot (c_d) =q^d\, \langle x,y_0\rangle _i^{\mathrm{untw}}\cdot (c_d),
$$

where the untwisted pairing is the morphism into $A(-d)$ of [prop-pod-degree-of-the-pairing] and $\cdot (c_d)$ denotes evaluation of the $A(-d)$-line on a generator; the two sides are therefore equal in $A(-d)$. Step 3: by [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists] the geometric Frobenius acts on $A(-m)$ by $q^m$, so on $A(-d)$ it acts by $q^d$; this is the normalization of the value line and gives the identity of the statement. Step 4: for the constant sheaf $K=K_X$ with its canonical datum, $K^\vee \cong K_X$ canonically, the contragredient datum of the canonical datum is the canonical datum (the canonical structure is symmetric, by [def-pod-dual-tate-datum]), so both operators are the same global geometric Frobenius operator $F$ of [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius], on the constant sheaf, and the display specialises to the stated identity.

Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes (no hypothesis on $S$). If
$f$ is proper and quasi-finite, then $f$ is finite.
(*Stacks Project, More on Morphisms, a consequence of Zariski's main
theorem; the locally Noetherian case is Tag
[02OG](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02OG).*)

## Proof

*Step 0: reduction to an affine base.* By
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $f$ is finite if and only if it is
affine and $f_*\mathcal O_X$ is a finite $\mathcal O_S$-module. By
[pqf-lem-affine-local-target] (with [pqf-def-affine-morphism]) it
therefore suffices to find an affine open covering $S=\bigcup_iV_i$
such that each $f^{-1}(V_i)$ is affine with
$\Gamma(f^{-1}(V_i),\mathcal O_X)$ a finite
$\Gamma(V_i,\mathcal O_S)$-module: then $f$ is affine, $f_*\mathcal
O_X$ is the quasi-coherent sheaf whose sections over $V_i$ are these
modules, and it is of finite type on the covering $\{V_i\}$. Let
$V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ be any affine open and replace
$f$ by its restriction $f^{-1}(V)\to V$. This restriction is again
proper (it is the base change of $f$ along the open immersion
$V\hookrightarrow S$, and separatedness, finite type and universal
closedness are preserved, the last because a base change of the
restriction is a base change of $f$) and quasi-finite (it is of finite
type and its fibres are fibres of $f$, [pqf-def-quasifinite]). So we
may assume $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ is affine, and we must show that
$X$ is affine with $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ a finite $R$-module.

*Step 1: Zariski's main theorem.* By [pqf-lem-proper-basic], $f$ is
separated and of finite type; by [pqf-lem-qf-locqf-qc] it is locally
quasi-finite, i.e. quasi-finite at every point of $X$
([pqf-def-quasifinite]). The affine scheme $S$ is quasi-compact and
quasi-separated. Hence [thm-pqf-zmt-factorization] gives a scheme
$T$, a quasi-compact open immersion $j:X\hookrightarrow T$ and a
finite morphism $p:T\to S$ with $f=p\circ j$. Since $p$ is finite,
it is affine, so $T=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B=\Gamma(T,\mathcal
O_T)$ a finite $R$-algebra.

*Step 2: the image of $j$ is closed.* The morphism $p$ is affine,
hence separated (a morphism of affine schemes has closed-immersion
diagonal, as $B\otimes_RB\to B$ is surjective). Consider the graph
$\Gamma_j=(\mathrm{id}_X,j):X\to X\times_ST$. It is the base change of
the diagonal $\Delta_{T/S}:T\to T\times_ST$ along
$j\times\mathrm{id}_T:X\times_ST\to T\times_ST$, hence a closed
immersion, and in particular a closed map. The second projection
$\mathrm{pr}_2:X\times_ST\to T$ is the base change of $f$ along $p$;
since $f$ is universally closed ([pqf-lem-proper-basic]), it is a
closed map. Therefore $j=\mathrm{pr}_2\circ\Gamma_j$ is a closed map,
and $Z=j(X)$ is a subset of $T$ which is both open (as $j$ is an open
immersion) and closed.

*Step 3: conclusion.* An open and closed subset of the affine scheme
$\operatorname{Spec}B$ is of the form $Z=D(e)=V(1-e)$ for an
idempotent $e\in B$ (the standard correspondence between idempotents
of $B$ and open-and-closed subsets of $\operatorname{Spec}B$, via the
decomposition $B\cong eB\times(1-e)B$). Since $j$ identifies $X$ with
the open subscheme $Z=D(e)$ of $T$, we get

$$
X\cong\operatorname{Spec}B_e\cong\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(B/(1-e)B\bigr),
$$

using $B_e\cong eB\cong B/(1-e)B$ for an idempotent $e$. Thus $X$ is
affine and $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)\cong B/(1-e)B$ is a quotient of the
finite $R$-module $B$, hence a finite $R$-module. By Step 0, $f$ is
finite.

*Remark (the locally Noetherian case).* When $S$ is locally
Noetherian the statement also follows without Zariski's main theorem:
a quasi-finite morphism has finite fibres by
[pqf-lem-qf-finitefibres], so $f$ is proper with finite fibres in the
sense of [pqf-def-quasifinite], and
[thm-pqf-finite-iff-proper-finite-fibres] applies.

In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
$\Lambda\in\{\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$, and let $a_X:X\to\Spec k$ be a
separated finite-type smooth morphism of pure dimension $d$. The
dualizing complex

$$
\omega_{X,\Lambda}=Ra_X^!\Lambda
$$

has the canonical identification

$$
\omega_{X,\Lambda}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Lambda_X(d)[2d]
$$

obtained from [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity], and the counit
identifies with the transported normalized integration map

$$
R\Gamma_c(X,\Lambda_X(d)[2d])\longrightarrow\Lambda.
$$

## Proof

Apply [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity] to $f=a_X$ and the
coefficient $\Lambda$: the purity isomorphism identifies the dualizing
complex with $\Lambda_X(d)[2d]$, and the counit is the transported smooth
trace [def-pur-smooth-trace], whose normalization is the
coefficient transport of
[thm-pur-trace-normalization-transitivity].

attrs.title: Adic and rational smooth dualizing complexes

objects.body:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
$A=A_{E,n}$, let $d\geq0$, and let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$. The
comparison

$$
\gamma_{p_d,K}:Lp_d^*K(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rp_d^!K
$$

of [def-pur-affine-space-comparison] is an isomorphism.

## Proof

By induction on $d$: the case $d=0$ is the identity, and for
$d\geq1$ the composition law [prop-pur-affine-space-composition-law]
expresses $\gamma_{p_d,K}$ as the composite of the isomorphism
$\gamma_{p_{d-1},Rp_1^!K}$ (the induction hypothesis applied to the
$(d-1)$-fold affine space over the base-changed line) with the affine-line
purity isomorphism $\gamma_{p_1,K}$ of [thm-pur-affine-line-purity],
both conjugated by invertible reassociation isomorphisms; hence
$\gamma_{p_d,K}$ is an isomorphism.

In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
$A=A_{E,n}$, let $B$ be a
separated finite-type
$k$-scheme and let $z:B\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^c_B$ be the zero
section of the affine space of [def-sbc-affine-space]. The
$c$-fold exterior product of the normalized affine-line orientation of
[thm-pur-affine-line-orientation] is a canonical, base-change
compatible isomorphism

$$
\Lambda_B\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rz^!\Lambda_{\mathbf A^c_B}(c)[2c],
$$

i.e. $Rz^!\Lambda\cong\Lambda_B(-c)[-2c]$; the product of the Kummer
boundaries of the coordinates $t_1,\dots,t_c$ corresponds to $1$.
Moreover this isomorphism is the inverse of the composite
$Rz^!\Lambda_{\mathbf A^c_B}(c)[2c]\xrightarrow{Rz^!(\gamma_{p_c,\Lambda_B})}
Rz^!Rp_c^!\Lambda_B\cong\Lambda_B$, where $\gamma_{p_c,\Lambda_B}$ is the
affine-space purity comparison of [def-pur-affine-space-comparison]
(an isomorphism by [cor-pur-affine-space-purity]) and the last
identification is the composition law for $p_cz=\operatorname{id}_B$:
the affine-space purity comparison, restricted along the zero section,
is normalized by the product of the Kummer boundaries of the
coordinates. Equivalently, the integration map transposed from
$\gamma_{p_c,\Lambda_B}$ sends the class of the zero section,
$\partial\kappa(t_1)\cup\cdots\cup\partial\kappa(t_c)$, to $1$.

## Proof

First work on the ordinary etale site. The explicit adjunction of
[cor-amb-affine-space-adjunction] gives
$p_c^\times\Lambda_B=\Lambda_{\mathbf A^c_B}(c)[2c]$.
Composition of adjunctions, as in
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and
$p_cz=\operatorname{id}_B$ therefore identify
$Rz^!\Lambda_{\mathbf A^c_B}(c)[2c]$ with $\Lambda_B$.
In rank one this is the supported coordinate orientation: the
Cartier map of [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map] integrates to $1$
under [def-amb-p1-trace], which is the normalization of
[thm-pur-affine-line-orientation]. Iterating the affine-line
adjunctions, the corresponding section classes are the ordered
product of these Cartier maps; their residues multiply to $1$.
The even shifts and twists add by [def-coefficient-twists-detailed].
The comparison [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] transports the
composition and counits to the stated finite etale-origin objects.
Finally the rank-one orientations commute with base change by
