[prop-pur-affine-line-orientation-base-change], and all the Cartier maps
and the explicit affine-space counits commute with base change, by
[lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map], [prop-asd-smooth-base-change].
Hence the resulting zero-section isomorphism has the claimed
normalization and base-change compatibility. No general relative
Kunneth assertion with closed support is needed for this calculation.
Finally, $\gamma_{p_c,\Lambda_B}$ is the transpose of the composite
affine-line adjunction ([thm-pur-affine-line-purity] identifies each
affine-line comparison with the adjoint of the normalized trace, and
[def-pur-affine-space-comparison] composes them along the tower), so
the identification $Rz^!\Lambda_{\mathbf A^c_B}(c)[2c]\cong\Lambda_B$
obtained above from $p_c^\times\Lambda_B=\Lambda_{\mathbf A^c_B}(c)[2c]$
and $p_cz=\operatorname{id}_B$ is exactly $Rz^!(\gamma_{p_c,\Lambda_B})$
followed by the composition isomorphism, which is the stated
compatibility with the affine-space purity comparison.

In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d$
and let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$. Substituting the identification
of [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object] into the tensor formula of
[thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness] gives the canonical
isomorphism

$$
Lf^*K(d)[2d]\;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;Rf^!K.
$$

Every map involved was normalized by the Kummer generator, so the Tate
twist, shift, and trace normalization are fixed canonically; the
identification is compatible with arbitrary base change and
composition.

## Proof

The composite is the twist reassociation of
[def-coefficient-twists-detailed], the inverse of the identification of
[thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object], and the tensor formula of
[thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness]; each is an isomorphism.

In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
$A=A_{E,n}$, and let $a_X:X\to\Spec k$ be a
separated finite-type,
smooth morphism of pure dimension $d$. The dualizing complex

$$
\omega_X=Ra_X^!A
$$

has the canonical identification

$$
\omega_X\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }A_X(d)[2d],
$$

coming from [thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity], and the counit
$Ra_{X!}\omega_X\to A$ is the normalized integration map

$$
R\Gamma_c(X,A_X(d)[2d])\longrightarrow A
$$

of [thm-pur-trace-normalization-transitivity], sending the
fundamental class of the $d$-dimensional oriented fiber to $1$.

## Proof

Apply [thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity] to $f=a_X$ and
$K=A$: its source $La_X^*A(d)[2d]$ is $A_X(d)[2d]$, giving the
identification of the dualizing complex. Under this identification the
counit $Ra_{X!}Ra_X^!A\to A$ is, by [def-pur-smooth-trace], the
smooth trace
$\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{a_X,A}$, whose normalization is
[thm-pur-trace-normalization-transitivity] in the case
$Y=\Spec k$.

In the purity conventions of this chapter
([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting), let $f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type
morphism. The
ambient exceptional right
adjoint datum of [def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint] was the
hypothesis under which this corollary was formerly stated; on the bounded
constructible and finite-Tor coefficients of its two clauses it is the theorem
[cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge], so it is not assumed, and the two
clauses below hold without it. Then $f$
satisfies the two preservation clauses of
[def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility]: with the affine charts
$U\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$ and the integers $d_U$ of
[thm-pur-general-admissibility], put
$D=\max_Ud_U$ and $c_U=2\,(d_U+\dim Y)$. Then $Rf^!$ carries
$D_c^{[a,b]}(Y,A)$ into $D_c^{[a-2D,b-2D+c]}(X,A)$ for
$c=\max_U\bigl(c_U+1+2(D-d_U)\bigr)$, and it carries finite Tor
amplitude in $[a,b]$ to finite Tor amplitude in $[a-2D,b-2D+c]$.

## Proof

For each chart the target $\mathbf A^{d_U}_V$ of the chartwise
presentation is of finite type over $k$ of dimension
$d_U+\dim V\leq d_U+\dim Y$. The open complement $W_U$ of $U$ in it
therefore satisfies the open-complement condition with constant
$2(d_U+\dim V)$ by [lem-exc-open-complement-known], hence also with
the larger constant $c_U=2(d_U+\dim Y)$, the condition being monotone
in its constant. The hypothesis of
[thm-pur-general-admissibility] is thus satisfied with these
constants, and its conclusion is the assertion.

attrs.title: Preservation for a general separated finite-type morphism

objects.body:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d$.
The
ambient exceptional right
adjoint datum of [def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint] was the
hypothesis under which this corollary was formerly stated; it is not assumed
here, being on the bounded constructible and finite-Tor coefficients that the
two clauses below quantify over the theorem
[cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge]. Then $f$ satisfies the
two preservation clauses of
[def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility], with
$c_f^-=c_f^+=-2d$ in the signed convention of that definition:

1. *constructibility.* For all integers $a\leq b$,
$$
L\in D_c^{[a,b]}(Y,A)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
Rf^!L\in D_c^{[a-2d,b-2d]}(X,A).
$$
1. *finite Tor amplitude.* If $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ has
finite Tor amplitude in
$[a,b]$, then $Rf^!K$ has finite Tor amplitude in
$[a-2d,b-2d]$; in particular $Rf^!$ carries $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$
into $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$.

Thus every smooth morphism is
exceptional-adjoint admissible at $A=A_{E,n}$ in the constructible sense —
the three clauses of [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility] read on the
complexes of the blueprint's coefficient class that the two clauses below
quantify over; the unrestricted clause (1) of that definition, on all
pro-etale sheaves, is false in general and is not asserted —: the
preservation
clauses are consequences of purity, not hypotheses of it, and the ambient
datum that the earlier form of this corollary assumed is not an assumption
either, by [cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge]. The weaker statement
``admissible at $\Lambda\in\{\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$'' demands in addition the
uniformity of the two clauses over the finite stages and the
finite-reduction and scalar-extension compatibilities of the right adjoints;
those are the coefficient transport of the transport section at the end of
this chapter, and they are *not* asserted here.

## Proof

By [cor-pur-dualizing-object-purity] the right adjoint $Rf^!$, whose
existence on the coefficients used here is the theorem
[cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge], is
identified with $Lf^*(-)(d)[2d]$ on finite-Tor objects. For a
bounded constructible complex $L$ without finite Tor amplitude, use
the tensor formula on all ordinary etale complexes of
[thm-asd-smooth-tensor], the orientation at $\Lambda$ of
[thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object], and the comparison
[thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class]. They give the same identification
for $L$; no site-perfectness of $L$ is assumed. The criterion below is
applied at the finite etale level and transported to the small pro-etale
site along [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale], as elsewhere in this
chapter.
Step 1: (1). The inverse image of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact] is exact.
It preserves constructibility: pull back each finite stratification
and each finite locally constant sheaf on its strata, as in
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. Thus for
$L\in D_c^{[a,b]}(Y,A)$ the complex $Lf^*L$ is bounded constructible
with $\mathcal H^r(Lf^*L)\cong f^*\mathcal H^r(L)$, which vanishes for
$r\notin[a,b]$; the [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] twist preserves the
vanishing degrees by [prop-weil-twist-preserves], and the shift moves them, by the convention
$\mathcal H^r(C[2d])=\mathcal H^{r+2d}(C)$, to $[a-2d,b-2d]$.
Step 2: (2). Test the finite Tor amplitude of $Rf^!K$ by the residue
field criterion of [lem-exc-residue-tor-test]: it is equivalent to
the complex $\mathcal H^\bullet\bigl(Rf^!K\otimes^L_A\kappa\bigr)$ being
concentrated in $[a-2d,b-2d]$. Substituting the purity
identification and the associativity of the derived tensor product,

$$
Rf^!K\otimes^L_A\kappa
\;\cong\;\bigl(Lf^*K\otimes^L_A\kappa\bigr)(d)[2d]
\;\cong\;Lf^*\bigl(K\otimes^L_A\kappa\bigr)(d)[2d].
$$

By the same criterion applied to $K$, the complex
$K\otimes^L_A\kappa$ has cohomology in $[a,b]$; the inverse image
$Lf^*$ is exact, so $Lf^*(K\otimes^L_A\kappa)$ has cohomology in
$[a,b]$, and the twist by the locally constant free rank-one sheaf
$\Lambda(d)$ preserves the vanishing degrees. The shift therefore puts
the cohomology in $[a-2d,b-2d]$, which is the assertion. At field
coefficients the assertion is the case already recorded in
[lem-weil-field-tor-amplitude].

attrs.title: Smooth morphisms satisfy the preservation clauses

objects.body:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $\pi:E\to B$ be a vector bundle of constant rank $r$ with zero
section $z$. For every $K\in D^b_{ctf}(B,\Lambda)$ there is a
canonical isomorphism

$$
R\pi^!K\;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;L\pi^*K(r)[2r],
$$

compatible with base change, with direct sums of vector bundles, and
with the adjunctions; in particular

$$
\omega_\pi=R\pi^!\Lambda_B\;\cong\;\Lambda_E(r)[2r],
$$

and the identification is compatible with the finite reduction of the
coefficients.

## Proof

At finite coefficient level on the ordinary etale site,
[thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity] constructs exactly the adjoint
of integration against the globally defined trace of
[def-amb-vector-integration]. It is an isomorphism for every
complex, hence in particular for the coefficients here.
The comparison of actual right adjoints in
[thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class], together with
[thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], transports this isomorphism and
its counit to the stated etale-origin category.

The compatibility claims concern these specified maps. On a
trivializing open the integration is the ordered affine-space counit
of [cor-amb-affine-space-adjunction]. The explicit projective-line
trace [def-amb-p1-trace] and its diagonal Kummer class commute
with coefficient reduction and base change, and composition of their
adjunctions gives the corresponding compatibilities for affine space.
For a direct sum of bundles choose simultaneous trivializations; the
two integrations are the same iterated counit, with the additive
twists of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. These equalities descend as
equalities between degree-zero sheaves on the base, because
[lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace] identifies every local source
with $\Lambda$, and [lem-amb-linear-trace-invariance] gives
agreement on overlaps. Transposing these equalities proves all the
claimed compatibilities. The proof precedes general smooth purity.

Let $U_0$ be a smooth geometrically connected affine curve, let
$U=U_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $\mathcal G_0$ be a lisse
Weil sheaf on $U_0$. Then, as
power series in $t$ (the Euler series of [d-real-cohom]),

$$
\prod_{x\in|U_0|}\det\bigl(1-F_xt^{d(x)},\mathcal G_{0,\bar x}\bigr)^{-1}
=
\frac{\det(1-Ft,H_c^1(U,\mathcal G))}
{\det(1-Ft,H_c^2(U,\mathcal G))},
$$

where $|U_0|$ is the set of closed points, $d(x)$ the degree of
$x$, and the right-hand side is the graded form of the
Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula
[thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar] of the trace-formula chapter (summed
with the signs $(-1)^{i+1}$).

## Proof

This is the curve case of the Euler-product form of the trace formula
[thm-trf-l-function-euler-product], applied with $\Lambda=\Qlb$,
$X_0=U_0$ (separated of finite type, of dimension one) and
$K=\mathcal G_0$, a sheaf placed in degree zero, under the hypotheses
of [thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar] with which the trace formula
is applied to $\mathcal G_0$. The local factor of that theorem at a
closed point $x$ is $\det(1-F_xt^{e_x}\mid\mathcal G_{0,\bar x})$,
with $e_x=d(x)$ and $F_x$ the local geometric Frobenius at $x$ of
[def-weil-punctual-weights], so its $L(U_0,\mathcal G_0,t)$ is the
left-hand side; by its items (2) and (3) this equals

$$
\frac{\det(1-Ft,H_c^1(U,\mathcal G))}
{\det(1-Ft,H_c^0(U,\mathcal G))\,\det(1-Ft,H_c^2(U,\mathcal G))}.
$$

Finally $H_c^0(U,\mathcal G)=0$ by [lem-a1-affine-hc0], so the
factor $i=0$ is $1$, which gives the displayed identity.

attrs.title: Euler product of the $L$-function of a lisse sheaf

objects.body:
Let $K$ be a field. Then $H^1(\operatorname{Spec}K_{\Et},\mathbf G_m)=0$
(and also $H^1((\operatorname{Spec}K)_{\mathrm{Zar}},\mathcal O^{\times})=0$).

## Proof

By [thm-sc-hilbert-90] with $X=\operatorname{Spec}K$, both groups are
isomorphic to the group of isomorphism classes of invertible
$\mathcal O_X$-modules. The underlying space of $X$ is a point, so a
quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module is a $K$-vector space and an
invertible one is a one-dimensional $K$-vector space, i.e. isomorphic
to $K=\mathcal O_X$. Hence the group is trivial.

For the bounded constructible coefficient class at $A=A_{E,n}$, the
vanishing input is [thm-sf-fullcd-class] and the exceptional adjoint
relative to that class is [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class]. Thus the
bounded-class uses of clause (1) of
[def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility] have this concrete
interpretation. The unrestricted ambient datum of
[def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint] is not asserted here; it is false in
general (an elliptic curve over $\overline{\mathbf F}_p$ with
$A=\mathbf F_r$, rem:sf-ambient-counterexample in the six-functors chapter),
and the constructible exceptional adjoint of
def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image is what the blueprint uses.

## Proof

Combine [thm-sf-fullcd-class] and
[thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class]. The latter quantifies over
bounded-below inputs in the comparison class and bounded-below targets;
this includes the bounded constructible instances of
[def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility]. It does not supply
the all-object quantifiers of [def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint].

attrs.title: The ambient datum relative to the bounded comparison class

objects.body:
In the setting of [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-nonproper], let
$K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ be of étale origin: $K\cong\nu_X^*K'$
for the comparison morphism
of sites and a bounded constructible complex $K'$ of $A$-modules on
$X_{\Et}$ of finite Tor amplitude
in $[a,b]$. Then the pro-étale direct image $Rf_*K$ is bounded
constructible on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and has finite Tor amplitude in
$[a,b+2d]$; that is, clause (iii) of the finite-Tor preservation summary holds at
the finite coefficient stage $A$ for such $K$.

## Proof

The morphism $f$ is of finite type, hence quasi-compact and
quasi-separated, so the comparison direct image of
[prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] gives an isomorphism

$$
\nu_Y^*Rf_{\Et,*}K'\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{\mathrm{proet},*}\nu_X^*K'
\cong Rf_{\mathrm{proet},*}K .
$$

By [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-nonproper] the complex
$Rf_{\Et,*}K'$ is bounded constructible on $Y_{\Et}$ with finite Tor
amplitude in $[a,b+2d]$, and [lem-exc-comparison-tor-interval]
transfers that Tor amplitude to its pullback
$\nu_Y^*Rf_{\Et,*}K'$, which is the finite-Tor condition of
[def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] on the pro-étale site; bounded
constructibility of that pullback is
[lem-weil-pbc-pullback-preserves-bounded-constructible]. The
identification therefore exhibits $Rf_{\mathrm{proet},*}K$ as a bounded
constructible pro-étale object of finite Tor amplitude in $[a,b+2d]$.
By [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] the bounded constructible
pro-étale objects are the pullbacks of the bounded constructible étale
objects, a reading recorded in clause (3) of
[lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative]; for those objects the
corollary is exactly clause (iii) of the finite-Tor preservation summary at the
finite coefficient stage $A$.

attrs.title: The pro-étale direct image for objects of étale origin

objects.body:
Fix the global finite-field datum, a prime $\ell\ne p$, $n\geq1$,
$A=A_{E,n}$, and the algebraically closed field
$k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes with
$\dim X\leq d$, let $f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type
morphism, and let $K$ be a bounded constructible complex of
$A$-modules on the small étale site $X_{\Et}$ with finite
Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$. Then
$Rf_*K$ is bounded constructible on $Y_{\Et}$ and has finite Tor
amplitude in $[a,b+2d]$. No properness and no compactifiability of $f$
is assumed.

## Proof

By [lem-sf-etale-direct-image-vanishing] the hypothesis
$\operatorname{UDV}(f,A;2d)$ of
[def-sf-uniform-direct-image-vanishing] holds for $f$ on the
small étale sites, for every sheaf of
$A$-modules; [thm-sf-direct-image-tor-amplitude] with $N=2d$ then
gives the assertion.

attrs.title: The direct image on finite Tor amplitude for a non-proper morphism

objects.body:
Fix the global finite-field datum, a prime $\ell\ne p$, an integer
$n\geq1$, $A=A_{E,n}$, and the algebraically closed field
$k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes with
$\dim X\leq d$, let $f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type
morphism, and let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Proet},A)$ be a bounded
constructible complex of $A$-modules on the small pro-étale site with
finite Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, both notions being the intrinsic ones of
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] and
[def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Then $Rf_*K$ is bounded
constructible on $Y_{\Proet}$ and has finite Tor amplitude in
$[a,b+2d]$. That is, clause (iii) of the finite-Tor preservation summary holds at
the finite coefficient stage $A$ for *every* object of
$D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Proet},A)$, with no restriction to the objects of étale
origin.

## Proof

By [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] the object $K$ is of
étale origin: there are a bounded complex $K'$ with constructible
cohomology on $X_{\Et}$ and an isomorphism $K\cong\nu_X^*K'$, and by
[lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude](ii) the complex $K'$ has finite Tor
amplitude in $[a,b]$ on the étale site.
[cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-nonproper], whose two inputs are
[thm-sf-direct-image-tor-amplitude] and
[lem-sf-etale-direct-image-vanishing], therefore gives a bounded
constructible étale complex $Rf_{\Et,*}K'$ with finite Tor amplitude in
$[a,b+2d]$. The morphism $f$ is of finite type, hence quasi-compact and
quasi-separated, so the comparison direct image of
[prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] gives an isomorphism

$$
Rf_{\Proet,*}\nu_X^*K'\cong\nu_Y^*Rf_{\Et,*}K',
$$

and [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude](i) gives finite Tor amplitude in
$[a,b+2d]$ and bounded constructibility for the right-hand side. As in
[cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-etale-origin] this is clause (iii) of
the finite-Tor preservation summary at the finite coefficient stage $A$ for the
object $K$.

attrs.title: The pro-étale direct image for all finite-Tor objects

objects.body:
In the setting of [def-sf-datum], let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite
type. Then

$$
D_XLf^*\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf^!D_Y
$$

as functors $D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)\to D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$, naturally in $f$.
If an orientation datum is fixed and $f$ is smooth of pure relative
dimension $d$, this reads $D_XLf^*\cong Lf^*D_Y(d)[2d]$.

## Proof

The Verdier exchange $D_YRf_!\cong Rf_*D_X$ is [thm-sf-verdier-exchange],
proved in this chapter from the tensor–Hom exchange and the projection
formula; biduality, axiom (A6), is [def-sf-datum] of this chapter,
where its geometric input is [thm-fix-general-biduality]; and the adjunctions $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$ and
$Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$ are those of [fix-prop-adjunctions]. Since $D_Y$ is
an anti-equivalence with inverse $D_Y$ by biduality, its right adjoint is
$D_Y$ itself, so the right adjoint of $D_YRf_!$ is $Rf^!D_Y$ and that of
$Rf_*D_X$ is $D_XLf^*$; passing to right adjoints, which is again the mate
calculus of [lem-sf-mate], gives the displayed isomorphism. The second
assertion substitutes the orientation $Rf^!\cong Lf^*(-)(d)[2d]$, which is
the content of [def-sf-orientation] as constructed in the purity
chapter.

In the setting of [def-weil-full-cohomological-dimension] the
condition $\operatorname{FullCD}(p,A;c)$ is equivalent to the following:
for every sheaf $\mathcal F$ of $A$-modules on
$\overline X_{\Proet}$ and every affine weakly contractible object
$W\to Y$ of $Y_{\Proet}$ the evaluations
$\mathcal H^r(Rp_*\mathcal F)(W)$ vanish for $r>c$, and the same holds
after every pro-étale base change of $p$. In particular the test of
$\operatorname{FullCD}$ needs no computation of geometric-point stalks,
and the failure of conservativity of the geometric-point stalks recorded in
clause (4) of [lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative] does not obstruct
it.

## Proof

The cohomology sheaves $\mathcal H^r(Rp_*\mathcal F)$ vanish for $r>c$
if and only if their evaluations at all affine weakly contractible objects
of $Y_{\Proet}$ vanish, by
[lem-sf-proetale-vanishing-detection](i) applied on $Y_{\Proet}$;
this is the first equivalence. The relative clause is the same statement
applied to the base-changed morphisms $p_V$, with the same detection
device on $V_{\Proet}$, which is legitimate because the base change of a
proper finite-type morphism is proper of finite type. The last sentence
restates the detection device used.

attrs.title: FullCD tested on affine weakly contractible objects

objects.body:
Let $K',M'\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Et},A)$ have Tor amplitude $[a,b]$
and $[c,d]$, and assume $K'$ is site-perfect. Then
$R\mathcal Hom_A(\nu_X^*K',\nu_X^*M')$ is bounded constructible
with Tor amplitude in $[c-b,d-a]$.

## Proof

Apply [thm-sf-hom-ctf] on the étale site, identify its pullback
by [thm-sf-hom-comparison-constructible], and transport the Tor
bound by [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude].

attrs.title: The pro-'etale internal Hom for a site-perfect first variable

objects.body:
For the constant complex $K=A_X$ in degree zero and the canonical
map $u:Lh^*A_X\simeq A_X$, every fixed geometric stalk has
categorical trace equal to $1$.
The complex is site-perfect.

## Proof

The complex consists of a single free rank-one sheaf, so it satisfies
[def-weil-site-perfect-complex]. Pullback preserves the unit by
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]; its canonical map is the
identity on each rank-one stalk. The degree-zero chain trace in
[lem-trf-chain-supertrace] is therefore $1$.

attrs.title: Constant coefficients have unit stalk trace

objects.body:
Fix the global finite-field datum
$p,a,q,k_0,k$, where $q=p^a$, let $X_0$ be a
separated finite-type
$k_0$-scheme, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let
$K=(\Qlb)_X$ be the constant
Weil sheaf with its canonical
Weil structure, the geometric Frobenius acting trivially. Assume
the compactification admissibility of
[thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar] for the constant lattice
$(\mathcal O_E)_X$ of $E_X$ at every finite level (the etale-origin
witnesses required there are supplied in the proof). Then for every
$m\geq1$,

$$
\#X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})
=
\sum_{i\in\mathbf Z}(-1)^i
\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(F^m\mid H_c^i(X,\Qlb)\bigr),
$$

and, when $X_0$ is
proper,

$$
\#X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})
=
\sum_{i\in\mathbf Z}(-1)^i
\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(F^m\mid H^i(X,\Qlb)\bigr),
$$

compactly supported cohomology being the ordinary one.

## Proof

The constant finite-level sheaves $A_{E,n}$ on the etale sites,
with their identity identifications after comparison pullback,
give the explicit witnesses of
[def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness] for the reductions
$(A_{E,n})_X$ of the constant lattice $(\mathcal O_E)_X$ of $K_E=E_X$.
Thus the finite-level hypotheses of
[thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar] hold for this lattice, and that
theorem applies to $K$.
For the constant Weil sheaf, the local geometric Frobenius
[def-trf-frobenius-operators] is the identity of the one-dimensional
stalk
$(\Qlb)_{\bar y}$, so

$$
\sum_{j}(-1)^j\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(F_{y,m}\mid H^j(K_{\bar y})\bigr)=1
$$

for every rational point $y$ (the unit stalk trace of [cor-trf-constant-stalk-trace], read at the field stage), and the right-hand side of
[thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar] is the cardinality of
$X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$, which is finite because $X_0$ is of finite
type. This is the first identity; the second is the identification
$H_c^i\simeq H^i$ for proper $X_0$ of
[def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology].

The boundary duality input of [def-weil-boundary-duality-input]
holds for every separated finite-type $Y/k$ and every finite stage
$A=A_{E,n}$. In particular the canonical evaluation-defined map

$$
\beta_L:i^*D_TL\longrightarrow D_ZRi^!L
$$

is an isomorphism for every closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$
between the locally closed pieces in that definition.

## Proof

Preservation in the first clause of
[def-weil-boundary-duality-input] is part of
[thm-fix-general-biduality], applied to every piece.
The independently formal comparison
$\alpha_{D_TL}:Ri^!D_TD_TL\cong D_Zi^*D_TL$ of
[lem-weil-closed-costalk-duality], composed with $Ri^!\delta_L$,
identifies $Ri^!L$ with $D_Zi^*D_TL$.
In particular $Ri^!L$ is finite-Tor constructible. Apply $D_Z$
and use biduality on $Z$:

$$
D_ZRi^!L\cong D_ZD_Zi^*D_TL\cong i^*D_TL.
$$

The inverse of this composite is $\beta_L$. Indeed, adjointing
back through tensor–Hom and $i_*\dashv Ri^!$, both maps correspond
to the restriction of the evaluation
$D_TL\otimes^L L\to\omega_T$. The evaluation identities in
[lem-weil-duality-pairing] then also give exactly the compatibility
between $\beta_{D_TK}$, $\alpha_K$, and $i^*\delta_K$ required
in the second clause of the definition. Thus boundary exchange is
derived after biduality and was not used to prove it.

attrs.title: The finite-stage boundary input is a consequence

objects.body:
Let $\dim X\leq d$, and let $K,L\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A_{E,n})$,
on the etale or pro-etale site over $\overline{\mathbf F}_q$.
Then $R\mathcal Hom_A(K,L)$ is bounded constructible of finite
Tor amplitude. If the Tor intervals of $K,L$ are respectively
$[a,b]$, $[c,e]$, one valid interval for this internal Hom is
$[c-b-2d,e-a+2d]$.

## Proof

The tensor–Hom adjunction of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and biduality
[thm-fix-general-biduality] give the natural identity

$$
R\mathcal Hom_A(K,L)
\cong R\mathcal Hom_A(K,D_XD_XL)
\cong D_X(K\otimes_A^LD_XL).
$$

By [lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata], $D_XL$ has Tor
interval $[-e-2d,-c]$. Tensor preservation
[lem-sf-tensor-ctf] gives interval $[a-e-2d,b-c]$ for the
tensor inside the last dual. Apply the same duality bound again to
obtain $[c-b-2d,e-a+2d]$. All the objects are constructible by
the same two results. The argument on the pro-etale site is the
transport by [lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison]; it makes
no site-perfectness assumption on $K$ or $L$ on all of $X$.

attrs.title: Internal Hom for arbitrary finite-stage constructible complexes

objects.body:
Under the hypotheses of [prop-weil-pbc-preservation-constructible], the
theorem [thm-weil-pbc-complete-proetale] restricts to a natural isomorphism
of ordinary triangulated functors
$$
 Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rf_*K
 \xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_*Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K
 \quad\text{in }\Dbc(Y'_{\Proet},A)
$$
for every $K\in\Dbc(X_{\Proet},A)$.

*Source note:* the isomorphism is Stacks Project, Pro-etale Cohomology,
Theorem 61.30.1 ([Tag 09C9](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C9)) with
$K$ satisfying its conditions, and the category $\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)$ is that
of Definition 61.29.1 ([Tag
09C1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C1)); the blueprint adds the
restriction of the tower-level theorem to $\Dbc(X_{\Proet},A)$, with the
amplitude bookkeeping proved in
[prop-weil-pbc-preservation-constructible].

## Proof

The isomorphism of [thm-weil-pbc-complete-proetale] exists for every derived
complete $K$ with compatible witnesses; the preservation proposition
[prop-weil-pbc-preservation-constructible] shows that all four displayed
objects lie in the bounded constructible complete category of
[def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], so the isomorphism lands
there.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be proper, let $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ be
geometric, and let $i_{\bar y}:X_{\bar y}\to X$ and $a_{\bar y}:X_{\bar
y}\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ be the projections. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite
ring and let $K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$. The etale base-change morphism is
an isomorphism

$$
 \bar y^{-1}Rf_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}
 Ra_{\bar y,*}i_{\bar y}^{-1}K.
$$

For a finite $\Lambda$-module sheaf $F$ this gives, for every $q\geq0$,

$$
 (R^qf_*F)_{\bar y}\xrightarrow{\sim}
 H^q(X_{\bar y},F|_{X_{\bar y}}).
$$

## Proof

Specialize [prop-weil-proet-finite-proper-base-change] to the cartesian square
[def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] defined by the geometric point $\bar y$, whose
base change is $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$; the second formula is the
cohomological consequence for the sheaf $F$ placed in degree zero.

In the setup of the finite-level geometric-fiber corollary, let $E/\Ql$ be
finite and let $K\in\Dbc(X,E)$. The $E$-coefficient exchange morphism is an
isomorphism
$$
 L\bar y^*Rf_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}
 Ra_{\bar y,*}Li_{\bar y}^*K
 \quad\text{in }\Dbc(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega,E).
$$

## Proof

Specialize [thm-weil-pbc-finite-extension] to the geometric-point base
change.

In the setup of the finite-level geometric-fiber corollary, let
$K\in\Dbc(X,\Qlb)$. The descended exchange morphism is an isomorphism
$$
 L\bar y^*Rf_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}
 Ra_{\bar y,*}Li_{\bar y}^*K
 \quad\text{in }\Dbc(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega,\Qlb).
$$
For a representative $(E,K_E)$, this is represented over a finite overfield
by the finite-extension formula of
[cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-finite-extension] applied to $T_{M/E}K_E$.

## Proof

Specialize [thm-weil-pbc-qbar] to the geometric-point base change; the
representative statement is the displayed form in [thm-weil-pbc-qbar].

Let $U_0/\mathbf F_q$ be normal, geometrically connected,
separated and of finite type, pure of dimension one; put
$U=U_0\times_{\mathbf F_q}\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and
$\Pi=\pi_1(U,\bar u)$; let $\ell\nmid q$, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite, and let
$\chi:\hyperref[def-wf-weil-group]{W(U_0,\bar u)}\to E^\times$ be a
continuous character with finite geometric image $\chi(\Pi)$. Choose $s$ with $\deg(s)=1$ and put
$c=\chi(s)$. Then $(W(U_0,\bar u),\deg,s)$ is a degree datum in the sense
of [d-monodromy] with $P=\Pi$, and for it the function
$\varepsilon=\chi_{\mathrm{fin}}$ of [d-ab-rankone] (with $\gamma=s$ and
$z=c$), namely $\varepsilon(w)=\chi(w)c^{-\deg(w)}$, is a finite-order
character $\varepsilon:W(U_0,\bar u)\to E^\times$ with
$\varepsilon(s)=1$, $\varepsilon(W(U_0,\bar u))=\chi(\Pi)$, and

$$
\chi(w)=\varepsilon(w)c^{\deg(w)}
\qquad(w\in W(U_0,\bar u)).
$$

The scheme and Weil-group conventions are those of
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], [def-wf-weil-group].

## Proof

The degree homomorphism $\deg:W(U_0,\bar u)\to\mathbf Z$ of
[def-wf-weil-group] is surjective with kernel $\Pi$ by
[lem-wf-weil-group-exact-sequence], and $\deg(s)=1$, so
$(W(U_0,\bar u),\deg,s)$ is a degree datum of [d-monodromy] with
$P=\Pi$. In the notation of [d-ab-rankone], $z=\chi(s)=c$,
$\chi_z(w)=c^{\deg(w)}$ and $\varepsilon=\chi_{\mathrm{fin}}$.
Since $\deg$ is additive, $\chi_z$ is a character, and since
$E^\times$ is abelian, the quotient $\varepsilon=\chi\chi_z^{-1}$ is again a
character. If $n=\deg(w)$, then $g=ws^{-n}$ has degree zero and hence
lies in $\Pi$; multiplicativity gives

$$
\varepsilon(w)=\chi(g)\chi(s)^nc^{-n}=\chi(g)\in\chi(\Pi),
$$

and conversely $\varepsilon(g)=\chi(g)$ for $g\in\Pi$, so
$\varepsilon(W(U_0,\bar u))=\chi(\Pi)$, and $\varepsilon(s)=\chi(s)c^{-1}=1$.
The group $\chi(\Pi)$ is finite by hypothesis. Thus the image of
$\varepsilon$ is finite, so $\varepsilon$ is of finite order, and the
displayed factorization $\chi=\varepsilon\chi_z$ holds by the definition of
$\chi_{\mathrm{fin}}$ in [d-ab-rankone].

attrs.title: Finite-order part times a degree character

objects.body:
In the situation of
[thm-wf-rank-one-finite-geometric-image-curve], with $c$ and
$\varepsilon$ from [cor-wf-rank-one-degree-factorization-curve]
(applicable because $\chi(\Pi)$ is finite by that theorem), fix an embedding
$\iota:\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$, and use its
restriction to $E$ (equivalently, choose an embedding $E\hookrightarrow \mathbf C$ and an extension to $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$). The rank-one lisse Weil sheaf
associated with $\chi$ by the
fundamental representation
is punctually $\iota$-pure of the
real weight

$$
w_\iota(\chi)=2\log_q|\iota(c)|,
$$

where $c=\chi(s)$ for any
degree-one element $s$.
The sheaf, degree, and punctual-purity conventions are those of
[def-wf-fundamental-representation], [def-wf-weil-group], [def-weil-punctual-weights].

## Proof

Let $x\in|U_0|$ be closed and set
$d=[\kappa(x):\mathbf F_q]$. The local geometric-Frobenius operator of
[def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] is represented in the Weil group by
a conjugacy class $F_x$ of degree $d$ [p-real-operations], with degree as in
[def-wf-weil-group]. Because $\chi$ is one-dimensional, its value
on this class is well defined. The factorization of
[cor-wf-rank-one-degree-factorization-curve] gives its unique stalk
eigenvalue as

$$
\alpha_x=\chi(F_x)=\varepsilon(F_x)c^d.
$$

The character $\varepsilon$ has finite image, so
$\varepsilon(F_x)$ is a root of unity. By
[lem-tw-root-of-unity-modulus],
$|\iota(\varepsilon(F_x))|=1$. Therefore

$$
|\iota(\alpha_x)|=|\iota(c)|^d
=q^{d w_\iota(\chi)/2}
=|\kappa(x)|^{w_\iota(\chi)/2}.
$$

This is precisely the definition in [def-weil-punctual-weights].
If $s'=gs$ is another degree-one lift, then
$\chi(s')/\chi(s)=\chi(g)$ is a root of unity by
[thm-wf-rank-one-finite-geometric-image-curve]; hence its complex
modulus is one and the displayed weight does not depend on $s$.

attrs.title: Punctual purity of a rank-one Weil character on a curve

objects.body:
Let $\mathcal F$ be lisse and $\iota$-pure of weight $w$ on a
punctured smooth curve, and let $x$ be the missing point. If the
local inertia action at $x$ is trivial, then the extended stalk
$(j_*\mathcal F)_{\bar x}$ is pure of weight $w$.

Consequently, if $j:U_0\hookrightarrow C_0$ is a dense open in a curve
in the sense of [d-real-setup] and $\mathcal G$ is a lisse Weil sheaf
on $C_0$ whose restriction $j^*\mathcal G$ is punctually $\iota$-pure
of weight $w$ on $U_0$, then $\mathcal G$ is punctually $\iota$-pure
of weight $w$ on all of $C_0$.

## Proof

By [lem-wf-boundary-stalk-invariants], trivial inertia identifies
the boundary stalk with the full local representation.
Apply [lem-wf-boundary-semicontinuity] on an affine neighbourhood
of the missing point to $\mathcal F$, and then to
$\mathcal F^\vee$. The latter is punctually pure of weight $-w$,
since duality inverts local eigenvalues, by
[def-weil-punctual-weights].
Because inertia is trivial, the extended dual stalk is the linear dual
of the extended stalk. The two bounds are therefore
$|\iota(\alpha)|^2\leq q_x^w$ and
$|\iota(\alpha^{-1})|^2\leq q_x^{-w}$.
Together they give equality, namely purity in
[def-weil-frobenius-module-weights].

For the consequence, the closed points of $U_0$ are covered by the
hypothesis; let $x\in C_0\setminus U_0$ (a finite set, $U_0$ being
dense in the curve $C_0$). Since $\mathcal G$ is lisse on $C_0$, its
geometric generic stalk is a representation of the fundamental group
of $C_0$, so the local inertia $I_x$ acts trivially on
$(j^*\mathcal G)_{\bar\eta}$. Removing the other points of
$C_0\setminus U_0$ from $C_0$ does not change the stalk of
$j_*j^*\mathcal G$ at $\bar x$, so the first part, applied to the lisse
sheaf $j^*\mathcal G$, pure of weight $w$, shows that
$(j_*j^*\mathcal G)_{\bar x}$ is pure of weight $w$. By
[lem-a1-lisse-middle-extension] the adjunction
$\mathcal G\to j_*j^*\mathcal G$ is an isomorphism; being a morphism of
Weil sheaves, it identifies $\mathcal G_{\bar x}$ with
$(j_*j^*\mathcal G)_{\bar x}$ compatibly with $F_x$. Hence every
eigenvalue of $F_x$ on $\mathcal G_{\bar x}$ has $\iota$-weight $w$,
which is punctual purity of weight $w$ at $x$ in
[def-weil-punctual-weights].

attrs.title: Purity at an unramified boundary point

objects.body:
Fix the finite-field datum
$(p,a,q,k_0,k)$, where $q=p^a$, choose a prime $\ell\neq p$, fix an
isomorphism $\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$, and let
$C_0/k_0$ be a smooth, proper,
geometrically connected scheme of pure dimension $1$. Put
$C=C_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let

$$
g=g(C)=\dim_kH^1(C,\mathcal O_C)
$$

be the genus of the
smooth proper connected curve $C$ over the
algebraically closed field $k$. Then, for every integer $n\geq1$,

$$
\boxed{
\left|\#C_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})-(q^n+1)\right|\leq2g\,q^{n/2}}.
$$

## Proof

Step 1: the point-count identity. The scheme $C_0$ is proper, so by
[cor-trf-point-counting] applied to the constant Weil sheaf,

$$
N_n:=\#C_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})
=\sum_{i\in\mathbf Z}(-1)^i\Tr\bigl(F^n\mid H^i(C,\Qlb)\bigr),
$$

where $F$ is the global geometric Frobenius in the
geometric-Frobenius convention.

Step 2: the range and the degree zero. By
[prop-cohomological-finiteness] (the constant sheaf on a scheme of
dimension $1$), $H^i(C,\Qlb)=0$ for $i\notin[0,2]$, and
$H^0(C,\Qlb)\cong\Qlb$ with geometric Frobenius acting as the
identity; hence $\Tr(F^n\mid H^0(C,\Qlb))=1$ for every $n$.

Step 3: the top degree. By [prop-endpoints] with $d=1$,
$H^2(C,\Qlb)\cong\Qlb(-1)$ Frobenius-equivariantly, and by
[def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists] geometric Frobenius acts on
$\Qlb(-1)$ by $q$; hence $\Tr(F^n\mid H^2(C,\Qlb))=q^n$.

Step 4: the dimension of $H^1$. By
[thm-sc-proper-cohomology] (the Kummer computation for a smooth
proper curve of genus $g$ over the algebraically closed field $k$),
for every $n'=\ell^r$, $r\geq1$, prime to $\operatorname{char}k$,

$$
H^1(C,\mathbf F_{n'})\cong(\mathbf Z/n'\mathbf Z)^{2g},
$$

and $H^q(C,\mathbf F_{n'})=0$ for $q>2$. The coefficient
construction of the framework chapter is levelwise: the derived-complete
integral coefficients of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], the
rationalization of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and the
common-stage extension of
[def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] assemble these finite
levels, so

$$
\dim_{\Qlb}H^1(C,\Qlb)=2g.
$$

Step 5: the trace bound. By [prop-weight-purity-roots] with
$i=1$ and $d=1$, every eigenvalue $\alpha$ of $F$ on
$H^1(C,\Qlb)$ satisfies $|\iota(\alpha)|=q^{1/2}$. Let
$\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_{2g}$ be the eigenvalues with algebraic
multiplicity (Step 4). The trace equals the sum of the eigenvalues,
so, applying the field isomorphism $\iota$ and the triangle inequality
in $\mathbf C$,

$$
\left|\iota\bigl(\Tr(F^n\mid H^1(C,\Qlb))\bigr)\right|
\leq\sum_{j=1}^{2g}|\iota(\alpha_j)|^n=2g\,q^{n/2}.
$$

Step 6: assembly. Combining Steps 1, 2 and 3,

$$
N_n-1-q^n=-\Tr\bigl(F^n\mid H^1(C,\Qlb)\bigr)
\quad\text{in }\Qlb.
$$

The left-hand side is an integer, hence fixed by $\iota$, so by
Step 5,

$$
|N_n-(q^n+1)|=\left|\iota\bigl(\Tr(F^n\mid H^1(C,\Qlb))\bigr)\right|
\leq2g\,q^{n/2},
$$

which is the claimed bound.

Fix the finite-field datum
$(p,a,q,k_0,k)$, where $q=p^a$, and a prime $\ell\neq p$; write
$\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$,
fix an isomorphism $\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$, and interpret
the $\Qlb$-objects in the
algebraically closed
coefficient category. Let $X_0/k_0$ be
smooth, proper, geometrically
connected of pure dimension $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, put
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, let $F$ be the
global geometric Frobenius
in the geometric-Frobenius convention, and
let $(V_{i,\ell},F_{i,\ell},P_{i,\ell})_{0\leq i\leq2d}$ be the
smooth-proper
cohomological family extended to $\Qlb$, with
reciprocal roots taken in the
ordinary/reciprocal-root convention. Let
$b_i=\deg P_i=\dim_{\Qlb}H^i(X,\Qlb)$ be the
Betti numbers, and let
$N_n:=\#X_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$ in the
point-count convention. Then, for every
integer $n\geq1$,

$$
\boxed{
\bigl|N_n-(q^{dn}+1)\bigr|\;\le\;\sum_{i=1}^{2d-1}b_i\,q^{in/2}}.
$$

In particular, for $n=1$,
$|N_1-q^d|\leq1+\sum_{i=1}^{2d-1}b_iq^{i/2}$, and for a curve ($d=1$,
$b_1=2g$) the bound reads $|N_n-(q^n+1)|\leq2g\,q^{n/2}$.

The endpoint term $1$ coming from $H^0$ cannot be dropped: for
$X_0=\mathbf P^1_{k_0}$ one has $d=1$, $b_1=0$ and $N_1=q+1$, so
$|N_1-q^d|=1>0=\sum_{i=1}^{2d-1}b_iq^{i/2}$. For $d=0$ the scheme
$X_0$ is $\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ and $N_n=1=q^{dn}$; the endpoints
$i=0$ and $i=2d$ coincide, which is why $d\geq1$ is assumed above.

## Proof

Step 1: the point-count identity. The scheme $X_0$ is proper, so by
[cor-trf-point-counting] applied to the constant sheaf,

$$
N_n=\sum_{i=0}^{2d}(-1)^i\Tr\bigl(F_{i,\ell}^n\mid V_{i,\ell}\bigr)
\quad\text{in }\Qlb .
$$

Step 2: the endpoint terms. By [prop-endpoints],
$P_0(T)=1-T$ and $P_{2d}(T)=1-q^dT$, and $b_0=b_{2d}=1$. Since
$P_{i,\ell}(T)=\det(1-TF_{i,\ell}\mid V_{i,\ell})$ is the coefficient
extension of $P_i$ ([def-weil-smooth-proper-cohomological-family],
[def-weil-betti-numbers]), the one-dimensional space $V_{0,\ell}$ has
Frobenius eigenvalue $1$ and the one-dimensional space $V_{2d,\ell}$ has
Frobenius eigenvalue $q^d$. As $d\geq1$, the degrees $0$ and $2d$ are
distinct, and

$$
\Tr\bigl(F_{0,\ell}^n\mid V_{0,\ell}\bigr)=1,
\qquad
\Tr\bigl(F_{2d,\ell}^n\mid V_{2d,\ell}\bigr)=q^{dn}.
$$

Since $2d$ is even, Step 1 becomes

$$
N_n-(q^{dn}+1)=\sum_{i=1}^{2d-1}(-1)^i
\Tr\bigl(F_{i,\ell}^n\mid V_{i,\ell}\bigr).
$$

Step 3: the middle terms. Fix $1\leq i\leq2d-1$ and let
$\alpha_{i,1},\ldots,\alpha_{i,b_i}$ be the eigenvalues of $F_{i,\ell}$
on $V_{i,\ell}$ with algebraic multiplicity; they are the reciprocal
roots of $P_{i,\ell}$, and there are $b_i=\deg P_{i,\ell}$ of them
([def-weil-smooth-proper-cohomological-family]). By
[prop-weight-purity-roots], $|\iota(\alpha_{i,j})|=q^{i/2}$ for every
$j$. The trace of $F_{i,\ell}^n$ is $\sum_j\alpha_{i,j}^n$ and $\iota$
is a field isomorphism, so the triangle inequality in $\mathbf C$ gives

$$
\Bigl|\iota\Tr\bigl(F_{i,\ell}^n\mid V_{i,\ell}\bigr)\Bigr|
\leq\sum_{j=1}^{b_i}|\iota(\alpha_{i,j})|^n=b_i\,q^{in/2}.
$$

Step 4: assembly. The left-hand side of the last display of Step 2 is
an integer, hence fixed by $\iota$. Applying $\iota$, the triangle
inequality and Step 3,

$$
\bigl|N_n-(q^{dn}+1)\bigr|
\leq\sum_{i=1}^{2d-1}\Bigl|\iota\Tr\bigl(F_{i,\ell}^n\mid V_{i,\ell}\bigr)\Bigr|
\leq\sum_{i=1}^{2d-1}b_i\,q^{in/2}.
$$

The case $n=1$ together with $|N_1-q^d|\leq|N_1-(q^d+1)|+1$ gives the
first particular statement. For $d=1$, the identity $b_1=2g$
is the dimension count in the proof of [cor-zl-hasse-bound], and the
bound specializes to the curve bound stated there.

Fix the finite-field datum
$(p,a,q,k_0,k)$, where $q=p^a$, and a prime $\ell\neq p$; write
$\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$,
fix an isomorphism $\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$, and interpret
the $\Qlb$-objects in the
algebraically closed
coefficient category. Let $X_0/k_0$ be
smooth, proper, geometrically
connected of pure dimension $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, put
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, let $F$ be the
global geometric Frobenius
in the geometric-Frobenius convention, and
let $(\Qlb)_X$ be the constant
$\Qlb$-sheaf on
$X$; no admissibility hypothesis is imposed on the structure morphism
$a_X:X_0\to\Spec k_0$ (its exceptional inverse image is the constructible
one, defined for every separated finite-type morphism; the ambient notion of
[def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility] is not used). Then, for every $i\in\mathbf Z$, the Frobenius module

$$
(H^i(X,\Qlb),F)
$$

is $\iota$-pure of weight $i$ in the sense of
[def-weil-frobenius-module-weights]; the group
$H_c^i(X,\Qlb)=H^i(X,\Qlb)$ (proper coincidence,
[prop-weil-operations]) is $\iota$-mixed of weights at most $i$.

## Proof

This is the absolute case of [prop-zl-smooth-proper-relative-purity].
Take $Y_0=\Spec k_0$ and $f_0=a_X:X_0\to\Spec k_0$, the structure morphism of
[def-weil-finite-field-fiber]: it is smooth and proper of pure relative
dimension $d$, and [prop-zl-smooth-proper-relative-purity] imposes no
admissibility hypothesis on it or on the structure morphisms. Take
$\mathcal F_0=(\Qlb)_{X_0}$, the constant Weil sheaf. It is
lisse, and it is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $0$ in the sense of
[def-weil-punctual-weights]: at every closed point $x$ the local
Frobenius of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] is the identity of the
one-dimensional stalk, so its only eigenvalue is $1$ and
$|\iota(1)|=1=q_x^{0/2}$.

The base $\Spec k_0$ has a single closed point $y$, with $q_y=q$ and
geometric point $\bar y=\Spec k$; the geometric fibre of $a_X$ over it is
$X$. The stalk of $R^{i}a_{X*}(\Qlb)_{X_0}$ at $\bar y$ is
$H^{i}(X,\Qlb)$, and the Weil isomorphism on $Ra_{X*}$ of
[prop-weil-operations], iterated once ($y$ has degree $1$), is the action
on cohomology of the global geometric Frobenius of
[def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius]; hence the local operator $F_y$ is
$F$. Clause (b) of [prop-zl-smooth-proper-relative-purity] (with $w=0$)
therefore says that every eigenvalue $\alpha$ of $F$ on $H^{i}(X,\Qlb)$
satisfies $|\iota(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}$, which is $\iota$-purity of weight $i$
of $(H^{i}(X,\Qlb),F)$ in the sense of
[def-weil-frobenius-module-weights]. By clause (a) the canonical map
$H_c^{i}(X,\Qlb)\to H^{i}(X,\Qlb)$ is a Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism
(the proper coincidence of [prop-weil-operations]), and a pure Frobenius
module of weight $i$ is $\iota$-mixed of weights at most $i$ (take $m=1$,
$w_1=i$ in [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights]); this is the assertion on
$H_c^{i}(X,\Qlb)$.

If $f:X_0\to Y_0$ is separated and of finite type and a Weil sheaf
$\mathcal F$ is $\iota$-mixed of weights at most $w$, then
$R^if_!\mathcal F$ is $\iota$-mixed of weights at most $w+i$ for
every $i$.

## Proof

Regard $\mathcal F$ as a complex concentrated in degree zero. The
definition [def-weil-complex-weights] identifies its upper bound
with membership in $D_{\le w}$. Noetherian induction and the localization rule
[lem-zl-open-closed-weight], in its morphism-level form
[lem-zl-morphism-open-closed-reduction] (source strata, target strata
and coefficient filtrations), reduce to the source and target strata
of [thm-zl-relative-noether]. The finite first arrow
$\nu$ preserves the upper weight bound by
[lem-zl-finite-pushforward]; every subsequent affine-line
projection preserves it by [thm-zl-relative-line-step]. Repeated
use of the composition isomorphism [lem-zl-shriek-composition],
in the form of the inheritance of the weight bound under composition
[lem-zl-composition-weight-bound] (stated for sheaves; for a sheaf in
degree zero the bound $R^if_!\mathcal F$ of weights at most $w+i$ is
the same as $Rf_!\mathcal F\in D_{\le w}$ by
[def-weil-complex-weights], so the complex-level steps supply its
hypotheses),
gives the bound for the whole factorization. The same localization
induction glues all strata, so $Rf_!\mathcal F\in D_{\le w}(Y_0)$;
reading the $i$th cohomology
sheaf gives the asserted bound $w+i$ (in the punctual sense of
[def-weil-punctual-weights]).

attrs.title: Cohomology-sheaf form of the direct-image theorem

objects.body:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, an integer $a\ge1$, a field $k_0$ with
$q=p^a$ elements, and an algebraic closure $\bar k$.
Arithmetic Frobenius is $\sigma:x\mapsto x^q$ on $\bar k$; geometric
Frobenius is $F=\sigma^{-1}$. They act on geometric points by coordinates.
The group of automorphisms fixing $k_0$ is $\Gal(\bar k/k_0)$.
A scheme is a locally ringed space locally isomorphic to
$\operatorname{Spec}R$ for a commutative ring $R$, with the structure
sheaf given by localizations of $R$; a scheme over $k_0$ has a morphism
to $\operatorname{Spec}k_0$. Finite type means a finite affine cover
whose coordinate rings are finitely generated $k_0$-algebras.
A morphism is separated if its diagonal is a closed immersion, and is
proper if it is separated, of finite type, and universally closed
(every base change maps closed subsets to closed subsets).
For a finite-type scheme over the perfect field $k_0$, smoothness means
that after extension to $\bar k$ every local ring $R$ is regular:
$\dim_{R/\mathfrak m}(\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2)=\dim R$.
Here $\mathfrak m$ is its maximal ideal and $\dim R$ is the supremum
of lengths of strict chains of prime ideals.
A group scheme over $k_0$ is a scheme with multiplication, identity and
inverse morphisms satisfying the group identities; these induce a group
on its points over each $k_0$-algebra. An abelian variety $A_0/k_0$ is a
proper, smooth, geometrically connected, commutative group scheme of
finite type. Geometric connectedness means connectedness after extension
to $\bar k$. Write $A=A_0(\bar k)$ additively.

objects.body:
Let $(W,\deg,\gamma)$ be a degree datum in the sense of [d-monodromy],
with $P=\ker(\deg)$. Conjugation by $\gamma$ is an automorphism
$\alpha$ of $P$, and $(u,n)\mapsto u\gamma^n$ identifies $W$ with the
split cyclic extension $P\rtimes_\alpha\mathbf Z$, whose multiplication is

$$
(u,n)(v,m)=(u\alpha^n(v),n+m),\qquad
\gamma=(1,1),\qquad \deg(u,n)=n;
$$

conversely, for any group $P$ and automorphism $\alpha$ this formula
defines a degree datum $(P\rtimes_\alpha\mathbf Z,\deg,(1,1))$ with kernel
$P\times\{0\}$. Every element has a unique form $u\gamma^n$ with $u\in P$
and $n=\deg(u\gamma^n)$. For a field $E$, a rank-one character is a homomorphism
$\chi:W\to E^\times$. It has finite geometric image if $\chi(P)$ is
finite, and finite image if $\chi(W)$ is finite. These are distinct
conditions; no topology is needed for the following factorization.
For such a character, set $z=\chi(\gamma)$ and define the functions

$$
\chi_z(w)=z^{\deg(w)},\qquad
\chi_{\mathrm{fin}}(w)=\chi(w)z^{-\deg(w)}\qquad(w\in W),
$$

so that $\chi(w)=\chi_{\mathrm{fin}}(w)\chi_z(w)$ by construction.

objects.body:
For the monodromy data $(G,H,F)$ of a represented degree datum
([d-monodromy]), a positive central pair is
$(N,z)$ with $N\in\mathbf Z_{>0}$ and
$z\in Z(G)\cap HF^N$, where $Z(G)$ is the centre of $G$.
The coset condition does not assert that $G/H$ is infinite cyclic or
that the cosets $HF^N$ for different $N$ are distinct.

Uses: [d-monodromy]

Fix the coefficient conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions] and a
Weil complex $(K,\varphi)$ on $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, where $X_0$ is smooth of
pure dimension one. Fix $m\ge1$ and $x\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$, and on $X$
let $i:\{\bar x\}\hookrightarrow X$ and $j:U=X\setminus\{\bar x\}\hookrightarrow X$.
The *curve pieces* of $K$ at $x$ are

$$
K^Z=Ri_*i^*K,\qquad K^U=j_!j^*K,
$$

the outer terms of the open–closed triangle
$K^U\to K\to K^Z\xrightarrow{+1}$ of [prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages].
Let $\Phi_m$ be the $m$-th power of the Frobenius of
[def-trf-scheme-frobenius], $\varphi_m$ the iterated Weil map of
[def-trf-iterated-weil-map] (the scheme-Frobenius map
$u_m:\Phi_m^*K\to K$), and $F_{x,m}$ the stalk Frobenius at $\bar x$
of [def-trf-frobenius-operators], which is the stalk map of $\varphi_m$
at the fixed point $\bar x$. The morphism $\Phi_m$ is finite and a
universal homeomorphism fixing $\bar x$, so $\Phi_m^{-1}(U)=U$, the
square of $j$ over $\Phi_m$ is Cartesian with restriction
$\Phi_{m,U}:U\to U$, and $\Phi_mi=i$. The induced maps on the two
pieces are:

- on the graph correspondence $(1,\Phi_m)$ of [def-trf-graph-correspondence],
  $u^Z=[i,i]_!(F_{x,m})$, the proper pushforward of
  [def-trf-coefficient-pushforward] of the stalk map, along the proper
  pushforward diagram $(i,i)$ from the point correspondence
  $(\operatorname{id},\operatorname{id})$ on $\{\bar x\}$ with coefficient
  $F_{x,m}$ on $K_{\bar x}$ to the graph $(1,\Phi_m)$ (a diagram because
  $1\circ i=i\circ\operatorname{id}$ and $\Phi_mi=i\circ\operatorname{id}$).
  Both exceptional legs being identities, the exceptional half of
  [def-trf-coefficient-pushforward] is the identity, and
  $u^Z=Ri_*F_{x,m}\circ\gamma$, where
  $\gamma:\Phi_m^*Ri_*i^*K\to Ri_*i^*K$ is the ordinary half, the
  composite of the unit of $i^*\dashv Ri_*$ with $Ri_*$ of the counit,
  through $i^*\Phi_m^*=(\Phi_mi)^*=i^*$;
- $u^U$, the composite

$$
\Phi_m^*j_!j^*K\simeq j_!\Phi_{m,U}^*j^*K
\xrightarrow{j_!j^*\varphi_m}j_!j^*K,
$$

  whose first isomorphism is open $!$-base change for the Cartesian
  square of $j$ over $\Phi_m$ ([prop-functor-package], clause (4)).

The same construction applies verbatim when $\varphi_m$ is replaced by a
Frobenius coefficient morphism $v:\Phi_m^*K\to K$ in the sense of
[def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism] (no Weil structure and no
invertibility), with $F_{x,m}$ replaced by the stalk map
$v_{\bar x}:K_{\bar x}\cong(\Phi_m^*K)_{\bar x}\to K_{\bar x}$. It
uses neither smoothness nor dimension one: it applies verbatim to any
separated finite-type $X_0$, and the smooth-curve case is the one needed
for the trace formula.

Over a finite field $F$ from the coefficient setup,
put $\mathbf A^1_F=\operatorname{Spec}F[t]$.
Glue $\operatorname{Spec}F[t]$ to $\operatorname{Spec}F[z]$ along
$F[t,t^{-1}]=F[z,z^{-1}]$, with $z=t^{-1}$, to obtain $\mathbf P^1_F$.
The first chart is $\mathbf A^1_F$ and its complement is the point
$\infty$ defined by $z=0$. Frobenius acts by $t\mapsto t^{|F|}$ and
$z\mapsto z^{|F|}$ on these charts.

Uses: [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], [rem-ptr-trf-coefficient-conventions-1]

A degree datum consists of a group $W$, a surjective homomorphism
$\deg:W\to\mathbf Z$, and a chosen element $\gamma$ of degree $1$.
Put $P=\ker(\deg)$; every $w$ has the form $u\gamma^{\deg w}$ with
$u\in P$. A represented datum adds a representation
$\rho:W\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$. Its arithmetic and geometric monodromy groups are
the reduced Zariski closures

$$
G=\overline{\rho(W)},\qquad H=\overline{\rho(P)},\qquad F=\rho(\gamma).
$$

These names concern the degree datum only; no topology or sheaf is
required in this subsection. A semisimple datum means that $V$ is a
semisimple $W$-representation.

For the Weil representation $\rho$ of a lisse Weil sheaf
([def-wf-fundamental-representation]), $(W(X_0),\deg,s)$ with $s$ of
degree one ([def-wf-weil-group]) is a degree datum, $P=\Pi$, and $H$
is the geometric monodromy group $H_{\mathrm{geom}}$ of
[def-wf-geometric-monodromy-group]; both closures are closed subgroups
by [lem-wf-zariski-closure-subgroup]. To avoid a clash with the
arithmetic monodromy extension $G_{\mathrm{arith}}(\rho)$, the closure
$G$ is then written $G_{\mathrm{Zar}}$. The degree-$m$ part of
$\rho(W(X_0))$ has closure $H_{\mathrm{geom}}F^m$
([lem-wf-degree-component-image]), and $G_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ contains all
of these translates.

Let $j:U_0\hookrightarrow C_0$ be a nonempty open in a
curve in the sense of [d-real-setup], with finite complement $S_0$, and let
$\mathcal F$ be lisse Weil on $U_0$, with Weil fundamental representation
$\rho$ of [def-wf-fundamental-representation].
Write $J=j_*\mathcal F$ for ordinary sheaf direct image, defined by
sections over the inverse image of an etale neighborhood; use this
construction at finite coefficient levels for adic coefficients.
For $s\in S_0$, let $K_s$ be the fraction field of the henselization of
$\mathcal O_{C_0,s}$, and put

$$
I_s=\ker\bigl(\Gal(\overline K_s/K_s)\to
\Gal(\overline{k(s)}/k(s))\bigr).
$$

Henselization is the universal local henselian extension with unchanged
residue field; a henselian ring lifts simple roots of monic polynomials.
Choose a geometric point over $\operatorname{Spec}K_s\to U_0$ and a path
from it to the base point of $\rho$; this gives a
decomposition-group homomorphism $\Gal(\overline K_s/K_s)\to\pi_1(U_0)$
carrying $I_s$ into $\pi_1(U)$ and the inverse image $W(K_s)$ of the
integer powers of geometric Frobenius of $k(s)$ into the Weil group
$W(U_0)$ of [def-wf-weil-group].
The local generic stalk $V_s$ is the space of $\rho$ with $W(K_s)$ acting through $\rho$.
Residue Frobenius lifts in $W(K_s)$ differ by elements of $I_s$, so they act
unambiguously on the invariants $V_s^{I_s}$ in the sense of
[def-real-weil-representation-operations].
Another path changes the homomorphism by conjugation by some
$g\in\pi_1(U_0)$. Write $g=wd$ with $w\in W(U_0)$ and $d$ in the image
$D$ of $\Gal(\overline K_s/K_s)$: identify $\Gal(k/\Fq)$ with
$\widehat{\mathbf Z}$ by sending geometric Frobenius to $1$, so that the
degree of [def-wf-weil-group] extends to
$\pi_1(U_0)\to\widehat{\mathbf Z}$ with $W(U_0)=\deg^{-1}(\mathbf Z)$;
then $\deg(D)=e_s\widehat{\mathbf Z}$, because $\Gal(\overline K_s/K_s)$
maps onto $\Gal(\overline{k(s)}/k(s))=\Gal(k/k(s))$, and
$\widehat{\mathbf Z}=\mathbf Z+e_s\widehat{\mathbf Z}$, so some $d\in D$
has $\deg g-\deg d\in\mathbf Z$, and $w=gd^{-1}$ lies in $W(U_0)$.
Conjugation by $d$ preserves the image of the normal subgroup $I_s$, and
it changes the image of a residue Frobenius lift $\Phi$ only by an
element of $I_s$, because the residue Galois group
$\Gal(\overline{k(s)}/k(s))$ is abelian, so that
$\delta\Phi\delta^{-1}\Phi^{-1}\in I_s$ for every
$\delta\in\Gal(\overline K_s/K_s)$. Hence the invariant space for the
new homomorphism is $\rho(w)V_s^{I_s}$, and the map $\rho(w)$ identifies
the two invariant spaces Frobenius-equivariantly, so $V_s^{I_s}$ is
independent of the choice up to Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism.

Uses: [d-real-setup], [def-real-weil-representation-operations], [def-wf-fundamental-representation], [def-wf-weil-group]

For any abelian sheaf $A$ on the etale site, ordinary cohomology means
$H^i(C,A)=R^i\Gamma(C,A)$, computed by an injective resolution.
For a constructible Weil sheaf $\mathcal K$ of
[def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] on a
curve in the sense of [d-real-setup], $H^i(C,\mathcal K)$ and $H_c^i(C,\mathcal K)$
are the etale cohomology groups obtained from derived global sections
and derived sections with proper support. With an adic lattice, take
the derived inverse limit of its finite coefficient levels and then
invert $\ell$; extend the finite coefficient field as needed.
They carry geometric Frobenius $F$ in the convention of [d-real-setup],
with Tate twists the constant Weil twists of [def-wf-constant-weil-twist].
Using the local characteristic factors $P_x$ of [def-wf-iota-real], the
Euler series is
the locally finite formal product

$$
L_\iota(C_0,\mathcal K,T)
=\prod_{x\in|C_0|}\iota P_x(\mathcal K,T^{e_x})^{-1}
\in 1+T\mathbf C[[T]].
$$

Locally finite means that only finitely many factors contribute to any
fixed coefficient; there are finitely many closed points of bounded degree.

Uses: [d-real-setup], [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], [def-wf-constant-weil-twist], [def-wf-iota-real]

For $f(T)=\sum_{n\ge0}a_nT^n\in\mathbf C[[T]]$, let $R(f)$ be the
supremum of $r\ge0$ such that $\sum_n|a_n|t^n$ converges for every
$0\le t<r$. A nonnegative series has all $a_n\in\mathbf R_{\ge0}$.
Products and exponentials of series with the requisite constant terms
are defined coefficientwise; infinite products are required to be
locally finite in each degree.

Fix $q=p^a$, $a\ge1$, an algebraic closure $k=\overline{\Fq}$, a prime
$\ell\ne p$, and a field embedding $\iota:\Qlb\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$.
A curve $C_0/\Fq$ is a nonempty, separated, smooth scheme of finite type,
of pure dimension one, whose base change $C=C_0\times_{\Fq}k$ is connected.
For a closed point $x$, put $e_x=[k(x):\Fq]$ and $q_x=q^{e_x}$.
Throughout, Frobenius means *geometric* Frobenius, the inverse of
the field automorphism $t\mapsto t^q$. Its local version at $x$ is $F_x$.
An affine open means a nonempty open subscheme isomorphic to the spectrum
of a finitely generated $\Fq$-algebra.

Fix the global finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ and the coefficient
conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Let
$f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a morphism of separated finite-type
$k_0$-schemes, write $f:X\to Y$ for its base change to $k$, and let
$\Phi_X,\Phi_Y$ be the $q$-power scheme Frobenii of
[def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. For $m\geq1$ put

$$
X'_m=Y\times_{\Phi_Y^m,Y,f}X,
\quad p_m:X'_m\to X,\quad f'_m:X'_m\to Y,
\quad r_m=(f,\Phi_X^m):X\to X'_m,
$$

where $f'_m$ and $p_m$ are the first and second projections, so
that $\Phi_Y^mf'_m=fp_m$. The map $r_m$ is defined because
$\Phi_Y^mf=f\Phi_X^m$: with $Q=q^m$, the maps $\Phi^m$ are the base
changes $\Phi_0^m\times\operatorname{id}_k$ of the absolute
$Q$-power Frobenii of the $k_0$-schemes $X_0$, $Y_0$ (their affine
incarnation is $a\mapsto a^Q$), and absolute Frobenius commutes with
every morphism of $\mathbf F_p$-schemes. By construction

$$
p_mr_m=\Phi_X^m,\qquad f'_mr_m=f .
$$

*The relative Frobenius.* Write $F_{X_0},F_{Y_0}$ for the absolute
$Q$-power Frobenii of $X_0,Y_0$ and put
$X_0^{(Q)}=Y_0\times_{F_{Y_0},Y_0,f_0}X_0$. The *relative
$Q$-power Frobenius* of $X_0$ over $Y_0$ is
$F_{X_0/Y_0}=(f_0,F_{X_0}):X_0\to X_0^{(Q)}$. Since fibre products
commute with the base change $k_0\to k$ and
$\Phi=\Phi_0\times\operatorname{id}_k$,

$$
X'_m=X_0^{(Q)}\times_{k_0}k,\qquad
r_m=F_{X_0/Y_0}\times_{k_0}\operatorname{id}_k .
$$

Affine-locally, for $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq Y_0$ and
$\operatorname{Spec}S\subseteq f_0^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}R)$, the
scheme $X_0^{(Q)}$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(R\otimes_{F,R}S)$, the
tensor product along $F:R\to R$, $r\mapsto r^Q$, on the left factor,
and $F_{X_0/Y_0}$ is given by

$$
R\otimes_{F,R}S\longrightarrow S,\qquad r'\otimes s\longmapsto
f_0^\#(r')\,s^Q ,
$$

which is well defined because $r'r^Q\otimes s$ and $r'\otimes f_0^\#(r)s$
have the same image $f_0^\#(r')f_0^\#(r)^Qs^Q$.

Representations of the same degree datum ([d-monodromy]) have
diagonal tensor action and the induced action on exterior powers.
For rank $r$, the determinant representation is $\bigwedge^r V$
([def-mg-determinant-line]);
write $\delta_V(w)=\det(\rho_V(w))$ for its character.
A real weight character is a homomorphism
$\lambda:k^\times\to(\mathbf R,+)$, so
$\lambda(ab)=\lambda(a)+\lambda(b)$.
A nonzero representation $Q$ has finite geometric determinant if
$\delta_Q(P)$ is finite. Define its determinant weight by

$$
\dw_\lambda(Q)=\frac{\lambda(\delta_Q(\gamma))}{\dim Q}.
$$

For a composition series ([def-mg-weil-composition-series]), constituent weights
mean the weights of its simple quotients. For a chosen simple
decomposition $V=\bigoplus_j V_j$, the rank-counted list repeats
$\dw_\lambda(V_j)$ exactly $\dim V_j$ times.

For $k=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, an embedding
$\iota:k\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$ and $q>1$, the usual normalization is
$\lambda_\iota(a)=2\log|\iota(a)|/\log q$.

In the conventions of [rem-dl-a1-conventions], let
$j:U_0\hookrightarrow A_0=\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ be a dense open immersion
and let $\mathcal M$ be a nonzero irreducible lisse Weil sheaf on
$U_0$, with geometric fundamental representation
$\rho_{\mathrm{geom}}:\pi_1(U,\bar\eta)\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$,
$V=\mathcal M_{\bar\eta}$, as in
[def-wf-fundamental-representation]. The *geometric irreducible
constituents* of $\mathcal M$ are the Jordan–Hölder constituents of
the $\pi_1(U,\bar\eta)$-module $V$, viewed as irreducible lisse sheaves
on $U=U_0\otimes k$.

$\mathcal M$ is *constituent-nonexceptional* if none of its geometric
irreducible constituents is isomorphic to the restriction
$\mathcal L_{\psi(ax)}|_U$ of the Artin–Schreier sheaf of
[def-fd-artin-schreier-sheaf] for any $a\in k$, the value $a=0$
included; for $a=0$ the excluded constituent is the trivial rank-one
sheaf $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$.

For a compactification
$c=(j,r)$ of $f:X\to S$ between Noetherian schemes,
define the ordinary etale compact-support candidate by

$$
Rf_!^c=Rr_*j_!:D(X_{\rm et},A)\longrightarrow D(S_{\rm et},A).
$$

Here $j_!$ is the etale
extension by zero,
and $Rr_*$ is the ordinary
derived direct image.
For a proper refinement take the comparison which is the
identity over $X$; the comparison lemma below proves
that these maps give a compactification-independent
functor, denoted $Rf_!$. This definition concerns
the etale category; it does not identify it with a
functor on the pro-etale category.
The notation refers to ordinary derived categories.

attrs.title: Compact supports on the ordinary etale category

objects.body:
An $\mathcal O_S$-module $\mathcal E$ on a scheme $S$ is
*locally free of constant rank $d$* if $S$ has a Zariski
open cover $(V_a)$ with
$\mathcal E|_{V_a}\cong\mathcal O_{V_a}^{\oplus d}$.
In particular it is a
quasi-coherent module; this is the
module convention used in the following vector-bundle definition.

attrs.title: Locally free modules of constant finite rank

objects.body:
For $q:\mathbf P^1_S\to S$, define

$$
t_q:Rq_*A(1)[2]\longrightarrow A_S
$$

as the projection onto the second summand of
$Rq_*A(1)[2]\cong A_S(1)[2]\oplus A_S$.
Thus $t_q(h)=1$. For any complex $K$ put

$$
\epsilon_K:Rq_*q^*K(1)[2]
\cong K\otimes_A^LRq_*A(1)[2]
\xrightarrow{1\otimes t_q}K.
$$

The first isomorphism is the proper projection formula of
[lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection].
The notation refers to the proved projective-line decomposition, and Tate twists.

attrs.title: Projective-line trace before an exceptional adjoint

objects.body:
Let $\pi:E\to S$ be a vector bundle of constant
rank $d$, in the sense of
[def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section]. Its integration
map

$$
t_\pi:R\pi_!A_E(d)[2d]\longrightarrow A_S
$$

is the map which on a trivializing open set is the
affine-space integration of
[lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace]. These maps glue
as morphisms of sheaves: the source has cohomology
only in degree zero on a trivializing cover, and
[lem-amb-linear-trace-invariance] identifies the
maps on every overlap.
The notation refers to Tate twists.

A separated finite-type
morphism $f:X\to S$ is *compactifiable* if it admits a
factorization $f=rj$ with $j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$ an open
immersion and $r:\overline X\to S$ proper; such a factorization is a
compactification of
$f$. Every morphism occurring in this chapter is compactifiable:
for a separated finite-type morphism of finite-type schemes over a
field, a compactification exists by
[thm-nagata-compactification].

Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme and let $\mathcal E$ be a
locally free sheaf of
$\mathcal O_S$-modules of constant finite rank $d$.
Its vector bundle is the relative affine scheme

$$
\pi:E=\operatorname{Spec}_S(\operatorname{Sym}^{\bullet}\mathcal E)
\longrightarrow S.
$$

Here the symmetric algebra is formed on each open affine and the
associated affine schemes glue by restriction. The augmentation
$\operatorname{Sym}^{\bullet}\mathcal E\to\mathcal O_S$
defines its closed
zero section $z:S\hookrightarrow E$.
A trivialization on a Zariski open $V\subset S$ is a choice
$\mathcal E|_V\cong\mathcal O_V^d$, giving
$E|_V\cong\mathbf A^d_V$. Changes of trivialization are invertible
$d$-by-$d$ matrices of regular functions on overlaps.

For $C$ as in [def-sc-curves], the *Brauer group* of $C$ is
$\Br(C)=H^2(C_{\Et},\mathbb G_m)$, the cohomology of the sheaf
$\mathbb G_m$ of [def-sc-gm-torsor] on the small etale site
$C_{\Et}$ ([def-weil-pbc-etale-site]).

Uses: [def-sc-curves], [def-sc-gm-torsor], [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]

Let $S$ be a scheme and let

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y
\end{array}
$$

be a cartesian square of
$S$-schemes with $f:X\to Y$
separated and of finite
type; no hypothesis on $g$ is made. A
*compactification of $f$* is a factorization

$$
X\xrightarrow{\ j\ }\overline X\xrightarrow{\ p\ }Y
$$

with $j$ an open immersion and $p$ a
proper $S$-morphism and
$pj=f$, as in
[def-weil-compactifications-refinements]; write
$c=(j,p)$. For the base change $g:Y'\to Y$, put

$$
\overline X'=\overline X\times_YY',\qquad
X'=X\times_YY'
$$

with the projections $\bar g':\overline X'\to\overline X$,
$p':\overline X'\to Y'$, $j':X'\hookrightarrow\overline X'$
(the base change of the open immersion), and
$g':X'\to X$; by the base-change stability in
[thm-nagata-compactification] the data $c'=(j',p')$ form a
compactification of $f'$.

In the situation of [def-cbc-exchange-map], let $(A,I)$
satisfy [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and let
$K\in D(X_{\Proet},A)$ be derived $I$-complete. For a
compactification $c=(j,p)$ and its base change $c'$, define the
*completed compact-support exchange map*

$$
\Ex^{\mathrm{comp}}_!(K):
Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rf_!K\longrightarrow Rf'_!Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K
$$

as the composite of the completed proper-base-change exchange map of
[thm-weil-pbc-complete-proetale] applied to $p$ and
$j_!K$, with the completed extension-by-zero comparison
$Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}j_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K$
of [lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison]; this is the
coefficient-level form of the map of [def-cbc-exchange-map].

Let $\square$ be a
compact-support
base-change square with $f:X\to Y$ separated of finite type, let
$\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring, and let $K\in D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$.
Choose a compactification $c=(j,p)$ of $f$ and its base change
$c'$; the
compact-support direct
image satisfies

$$
Rf_!K=Rp_*j_!K,\qquad Rf'_!K=Rp'_*j'_!K.
$$

The *compact-support exchange map* is

$$
\operatorname{Ex}_!(K):g^{-1}Rf_!K\longrightarrow Rf'_!g'^{-1}K,
$$

the composite of the
derived exchange morphism
of [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] for the proper $p$ and the
cartesian square $(\bar g',p')$, applied to $j_!K$, with the
extension-by-zero identification
$g^{-1}j_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!g_U^{-1}K=j'_!g'^{-1}K$ of
[cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change]; this is the map
denoted $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ in [def-exchange-projection].

An *open-immersion square* is a pair consisting of a
cartesian square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
U'&\xrightarrow{g_U}&U\\
j'\downarrow&&\downarrow j\\
X'&\xrightarrow{g}&X
\end{array}
$$

in which $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ and $j':U'\hookrightarrow X'$ are
open immersions, so that
$U'=U\times_XX'$; no hypothesis on $g$ is made.

Let $S$ be a scheme and let $n$ and $m$ be index sets for the homogeneous
coordinates of $\mathbf P^{n}_S$ and $\mathbf P^{m}_S$. The *Segre
embedding* is the morphism of $S$-schemes

$$
s\colon\mathbf P^{n}_S\times_S\mathbf P^{m}_S
\longrightarrow\mathbf P^{n\times m}_S,
\qquad
\bigl((x_k)_{k\in n},(y_l)_{l\in m}\bigr)
\longmapsto
\bigl[x_k\,y_l\bigr]_{(k,l)\in n\times m} .
$$

In the classical indexing this is
$\mathbf P^{n_1}_S\times_S\mathbf P^{n_2}_S\to\mathbf P^{N}_S$ with
$N=(n_1+1)(n_2+1)-1$; iterating it $m-1$ times embeds an $m$-fold product
into $\mathbf P^{N}_S$ with $N=\prod_{i=1}^m(n_i+1)-1$.

## Detailed form

For integers $n_1,\dots,n_m\geq0$, let $N=\prod_{i=1}^m(n_i+1)-1$ and let the
coordinates of $\mathbf P^N_Y$ be $X_{e}$, indexed by tuples
$e=(e_1,\dots,e_m)$ with $0\leq e_i\leq n_i$. The *Segre embedding* is the
morphism of $Y$-schemes

$$
 s:\prod_{i=1}^m\mathbf P^{n_i}_Y\longrightarrow\mathbf P^N_Y,
$$

given by the multihomogeneous coordinates

$$
 x\longmapsto\bigl[\prod_{i=1}^m x_{i,e_i}\bigr]_{e},
 \qquad x=(x_{i,0}:\cdots:x_{i,n_i})_{i=1}^m.
$$

A normalized DVR tower on $X$ consists of complexes
$M_n\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_n)$, represented in the derived
tower category of [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit], with
coherent transition maps whose adjoints

$$
M_m\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n\longrightarrow M_n\qquad(m\geq n)
$$

are isomorphisms and satisfy the quotient cocycle. Restriction of
scalars uses [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients].
No common stratification or integral local model is part of this
definition. Such finiteness assertions must be proved separately.

Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$, an integer $n\in\mathbf
Z_{\geq1}$, and a scheme $S$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. Use the small
pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] of $S$ and the derived
tensor product [def-weil-derived-tensor]. For every integer $r\geq1$, define
the pro-etale sheaf $\mu_{\ell^r,S}$ by

$$
 \mu_{\ell^r,S}(U)=
 \{u\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U^\times):u^{\ell^r}=1\}
 \qquad(U\to S).
$$

With transition maps $u\mapsto u^\ell$, use the finite-torsion coefficient
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] $A_{E,n}$ from the global
coefficient notation, and define

$$
  \Zl(1)_S=\varprojlim_{r\geq1}\mu_{\ell^r,S},\qquad
  \mathcal O_E(1)_S=\Zl(1)_S\otimes_{\Zl}\mathcal O_E,
$$

and

$$
  A_{E,n}(1)_S=
  \mathcal O_E(1)_S\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n},
 \qquad E(1)_S=\mathcal O_E(1)_S\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E.
$$

The $\Qlb$-twist is represented by $E(1)_S$ at every finite stage and is
compatible with scalar extension. For each displayed coefficient ring
$\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$, let $\Lambda_S$ denote its
coefficient object on $S$: it is the finite-level constant sheaf
$(A_{E,n})_S$ for $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, the completed coefficient sheaf
$\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,S}$ from the derived-complete integral construction
[def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] for $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$, and
the scalar extensions of these objects for $\Lambda=E,\Qlb$, with $\Qlb$
interpreted at a common finite stage. Thus, for each coefficient ring,
$\Lambda(1)_S$ is respectively the finite-level object $A_{E,n}(1)_S$, the
integral object $\mathcal O_E(1)_S$, the rational object $E(1)_S$, or its
common-stage $\Qlb$-extension. Define the twist for every $m\in\mathbf Z$ by

$$
 \Lambda(m):=
 \begin{cases}
   \Lambda_S,&m=0,\\
   \Lambda(1)_S^{\otimes_{\Lambda_S}m},&m>0,\\
   \operatorname{Hom}_{\Lambda_S}\bigl(\Lambda(-m),\Lambda_S\bigr),&m<0.
 \end{cases}
$$

For every $m\in\mathbf Z$ and every $K\in D(S_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$, set

$$
 K(m)=K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_S}\Lambda(m).
$$

Let $K_0$ be a field, let $X,Y$ be finite-type
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] $K_0$-schemes, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type $K_0$-morphism. Fix a prime $\ell$, write
$\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and require that its image in $K_0$ is invertible.
Choose a finite extension $E/\Ql$, an integer $n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, and
put $A=A_{E,n}$. Use finite-torsion coefficients
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] and the compact-support candidate
[def-weil-compact-support-candidate]. Choose an object
$c\in\operatorname{Comp}(f)$ in the compactification category
[def-weil-compactifications-refinements] and define

$$
 Rf_{!,n}=Rf_{!,n}^{c}:
 D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})
 \longrightarrow D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n}),
$$

the functor of [def-weil-compact-support-candidate] attached to $c$. Its
independence of the chosen compactification, and every other property
asserted of it in this blueprint, are asserted on the subcategory $\mathcal
D^{+}_{\mathrm{et}}(X,A_{E,n})$ of that definition, namely on the complexes
that come from the etale site with an etale-origin witness; there the
superscript is dropped. For a refinement $u:c_1\to c_2$, use the natural
comparison isomorphism $Rf_{!,n}^{c_1}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{!,n}^{c_2}$
induced by proper composition and extension by zero. Require these
comparisons to be the identity for identity refinements and transitive under
composition. The independence of the resulting functor from the chosen object
$c$, and the cocycle condition for the comparisons through a common
refinement, are the compactification-coherence proposition; that $Rf_{!,n}$
is a triangulated functor is
[lem-compact-support-direct-image-triangulated].

A sheaf $\mathcal F\in\shv{\et X}$ is *constant* if it lies in the
essential image of the constant-sheaf functor
$\mathcal A\to\shv{\et X}$, $M\mapsto M_X$, the left adjoint of global
sections (sheafification of the constant presheaf).

A sheaf $\mathcal F\in\shv{\et X}$ is *constructible* if there is a
stratification $(\iota_k\colon Z_k\to X)_{k<n}$ of $X$ such that each
pullback $\iota_k^*\mathcal F$ is finite locally constant.

A sheaf $\mathcal F\in\shv{\et X}$ (with $\mathcal A$ concrete) is
*finite* if for every geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$ the underlying
set of the stalk $\mathcal F_{\bar x}$ is finite.

A sheaf is *finite locally constant* if it is locally constant and
finite.

A *trivialising datum* for $\mathcal F\in\shv{\et X}$ is an étale
cover $(U_i\to X)_{i\in I}$ — a jointly surjective family of étale
morphisms — such that for every $i$ the restriction of $\mathcal F$ to
$\et{U_i}$, that is, the sheaf induced by $\mathcal F$ on the site
$\et X$ localised at $U_i$, is constant. The sheaf $\mathcal F$ is
*locally constant* if a trivialising datum exists.

A stratification $(T_l)_{l<m}$ of $T$ *refines* a stratification
$(T_k)_{k<n}$ if every $T_l$ is contained in some $T_k$.

A *stratification* of a topological space $T$ is a finite family
$(T_k)_{k<n}$ of pairwise disjoint locally closed subsets covering $T$
(Stacks Project, Tag `09XZ`, with finiteness added). A
*stratification* of a scheme $X$ is a stratification $(X_k)_{k<n}$ of
its underlying space together with, for each $k$, a scheme $Z_k$ and an
immersion $\iota_k\colon Z_k\to X$ with set-theoretic image $X_k$.

For $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$, write
$u:\mathcal B_X\to\mathcal B_Z$ for base change. For
$V=\operatorname{Spec}\overline C$ in the basis of
[def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis], set
$$
 v(V)=\operatorname{Spec}H_A(\overline C),
$$
using [def-exc-ind-etale-closed-lift]. Maps are the opposites of the maps
supplied by that algebra construction.

attrs.title: Lifting affine objects of the closed site

objects.body:
For a profinite group $G$ and a finite ring $A$, a discrete
$A$-module with continuous $G$-action is an $A$-module $M$
with a $G$-action by $A$-linear automorphisms such that every
element has an open stabilizer. This is an abelian category.
Its invariant functor sends $M$ to
$M^G=\{m:gm=m\text{ for all }g\in G\}$.
The continuous cohomology $H^q(G,M)$ is its right derived functor,
formed in the ordinary
derived category.
Equivalently it is computed by the complex of continuous inhomogeneous
cochains $G^q\to M$, with the usual group-cochain differential.

attrs.title: Discrete modules and continuous group cohomology

objects.body:
Let $k$ be a field, let $N$ be an integer prime to
$\operatorname{char}(k)$, and let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative
ring annihilated by $N$. Say that the *direct-image finiteness
input over $k$* holds if the following two clauses hold.

1. (*finiteness of the direct image*) For every morphism
$u:S\to T$ of
finite type between
finite-type $k$-schemes, every
constructible
$\Lambda$-sheaf $F$ on
$S_{{\mathrm{et}}}$, and every $q\geq0$, the higher direct image
$R^qu_*F$ of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] is constructible on
$T_{{\mathrm{et}}}$.
1. (*cohomological dimension*) Let $K$ be a separably closed
field with $\operatorname{char}(K)$ prime to $N$, and let $W$
be a finite-type $K$-scheme of dimension at most $d$. Then
$H^q(W,M)=0$ for every $q>2d$ and every torsion sheaf of abelian
groups $M$ on $W_{{\mathrm{et}}}$.

Both clauses concern the ordinary direct image and the etale cohomology
of schemes only: neither of them mentions the exceptional inverse image,
the ambient exceptional right adjoint datum, purity, or base change. Both
clauses are proved in this blueprint, in the constructibility chapter and the Jacobian chapter
respectively; the classical sources of the two statements, and the way
they are used here, are recorded in the remark that follows.

Let $I\subset A$ be an ideal, and specify a square Jacobian presentation
[def-exc-jacobian-presentation]
$\overline B=(A/I)[x_1,\ldots,x_m]/(\overline f_1,\ldots,\overline f_m)$.
Choose coefficientwise lifts $f_i\in A[x_1,\ldots,x_m]$, put
$\Delta=\det(\partial f_i/\partial x_j)$, and define
$$
 B^{\mathrm{lift}}=
 A[x_1,\ldots,x_m,t]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m,t\Delta-1).
$$
Its map to $\overline B$ sends $t$ to $\overline\Delta^{-1}$.

For an ideal $I\subset A$ and an ind-etale $A/I$-algebra $\overline C$, let
$\mathcal N_A(\overline C)$ have objects factorizations
$A\to B\to\overline C$, with $B/A$ etale of finite presentation, and
morphisms the compatible $A$-algebra maps. Define the $A$-algebra
$$
 H_A(\overline C)=\varinjlim_{\mathcal N_A(\overline C)}B
$$
