and retain its map to $\overline C$. A map of the algebras $\overline C$
acts by postcomposition on the indexing categories, and hence defines the
maps of this construction.

attrs.title: The ind-etale lift along a closed subscheme

objects.body:
A square Jacobian presentation of an $R$-algebra $B$ is a specified
isomorphism
$$
 B=R[x_1,\ldots,x_m]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)
$$
such that $\Delta=\det(\partial f_i/\partial x_j)$ has invertible image in
$B$. Finite presentation and etaleness have the meanings fixed by the scheme
conventions.

For a reduced one-dimensional Noetherian local ring $R$,
let $\mathfrak p_1,\ldots,\mathfrak p_t$ be its minimal
primes. Put

$$
Q(R)=\prod_{a=1}^t\operatorname{Frac}(R/\mathfrak p_a),
\qquad
B(R)=\prod_{a=1}^t\overline{(R/\mathfrak p_a)}^{\,
\operatorname{Frac}(R/\mathfrak p_a)}.
$$

The factors are the integral closures used in
[def-sc-normalization], [def-fin-normalization-extension].
The map $R\to B(R)$ is the product of the quotient maps
followed by the inclusions in these integral closures.
This defines the branch algebra without assuming its
finiteness or a decomposition into local rings.

attrs.title: The normalization algebra of local curve branches

objects.body:
Let $A$ be a finite ring, let $j:V\hookrightarrow T$ be a
quasi-compact open immersion,
and let $c\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$. Say that the pair $(V,T)$
satisfies the *open-complement condition with constant $c$* if

$$
R^qj_*M=0\qquad(q>c)
$$

for every sheaf $M$ of $A$-modules on $V_{\mathrm{et}}$, and if
$R^qj_*$ carries constructible
sheaves to constructible sheaves in
every degree. This is exactly the hypothesis under which the closed-support
computations of [lem-exc-closed-amplitude] and
[prop-exc-closed-tor] run: those two statements are conditional on the
open-complement condition for the complement of the closed immersion they
treat, and are unconditional where that condition is known independently,
in dimension at most one and, for the chart complements, from the
classical direct-image finiteness input.

Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a
closed immersion
with complementary open immersion $j$, and let $A$ be a
finite commutative ring. For a
pro-etale module sheaf
$N$ on $T$, set

$$
i^!_0N=i^*\ker\bigl(N\longrightarrow j_*j^*N\bigr).
$$

The map in this formula is the unit of the open
inverse-image and
direct-image adjunction. A morphism of sheaves induces a
map of these kernels and then its closed inverse image;
this specifies the functor on morphisms. No adjunction or
constructibility property is part of this construction.

Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$, an integer $n\in\mathbf
Z_{\geq1}$, and put $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $S$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is
invertible, let $X,Y$ be finite-type
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] $S$-schemes, and let every morphism
below be an $S$-morphism. Let $\Lambda\in\{A,\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$, where
the finite-level coefficient category is the finite-torsion constructible
category [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]; the latter coefficient
categories are obtained by derived completion, rationalization, and the
common-stage construction. Use the derived pullback, tensor, and
internal-Hom operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the derived
direct image [def-weil-derived-direct-image], and the compact-support direct
image [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. The finite-Tor and
interval conditions are the finite-Tor
[def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] and constructible-interval
[def-weil-constructible-intervals] conditions. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated
and of finite type, let $Y'$ be a finite-type $S$-scheme and let $g:Y'\to Y$
be separated and of finite type, and set $X'=X\times_Y Y'$, with projections
$g':X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$. Consider the resulting Cartesian square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
 X' & \xrightarrow{g'} & X\\
 f'\downarrow && \downarrow f\\
 Y' & \xrightarrow{g} & Y
\end{array}
$$

The direct-image exchange transformation

$$
 \operatorname{Ex}_*:\;Lg^*Rf_*\longrightarrow Rf'_*Lg'^*
$$

is adjoint to the composite

$$
 Lf'^*Lg^*Rf_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lg'^*Lf^*Rf_*
 \longrightarrow Lg'^*,
$$

whose second arrow is the counit of $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$. If $f=\bar f\circ j$
is a compactification [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], the
compact-support exchange map

$$
 \operatorname{Ex}_!:\;Lg^*Rf_!\longrightarrow Rf'_!Lg'^*
$$

is represented by $\operatorname{Ex}_*$ for $\bar f$, followed by the
canonical identification $L\bar g'^*j_!\cong j'_!Lg'^*$, where $\bar f':\bar
X'\to Y'$ and $\bar g':\bar X'\to\bar X$ are the base changes of $\bar f$,
and $j':X'\hookrightarrow\bar X'$ is the base change of $j$; the independence
of this map from the compactification is the compactification-coherence
proposition.

For $K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ and $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$, the projection
transformation is

$$
 \operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}:Rf_!K\otimes^L L
 \longrightarrow Rf_!(K\otimes^L Lf^*L).
$$

For this compactification it is the direct-image projection transformation
for $\bar f$, followed by $j_!K\otimes^LL\bar f^*L\cong j_!(K\otimes^LLf^*L)$.
These are natural transformations with the displayed sources and targets.

Let $k$ be a finite field or an algebraic closure of one, and let
$p=\operatorname{char}k$. A *nondegenerate additive character*
of $k$ is a nontrivial homomorphism

$$
\psi:(k,+)\longrightarrow\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell^\times.
$$

For a finite field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ with trace
$\operatorname{Tr}:k_0\to\mathbf F_p$, the character
$\psi(x)=\Psi(\operatorname{Tr}(x))$, for a fixed nontrivial
$\Psi:\mathbf F_p\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell^\times$, is called
*the* nondegenerate additive character. For $a\in k_0^\times$ the scalings
$\psi_a(x)=\psi(ax)$ are again nondegenerate characters.

*Recorded in advance* from chapter *Fourier–Deligne transform* of the source.

Let $X_0$ be a separated scheme of finite type over $k_0=\mathbf F_q$
(conventions of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]), let
$f\in\Gamma(X_0,\mathcal O_{X_0})$, and let
$\psi=\Psi\circ\operatorname{Tr}_{k_0/\mathbf F_p}$ be the nondegenerate
additive character of [def-fd-additive-character], with $\Psi$ the fixed
nontrivial character of $\mathbf F_p$. The *Artin–Schreier covering*
attached to $f$ is

$$
\pi:Y\to X_0,\qquad
Y=\operatorname{Spec}_{X_0}\mathcal O_{X_0}[T]/(T^p-T-f),
$$

a finite étale morphism in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], with the
$\mathbf F_p$-action $\sigma_a:T\mapsto T+a$ ($a\in\mathbf F_p$), which makes
it an $\mathbf F_p$-torsor in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-finite-torsors];
the $\sigma_a$ act on $\pi_*\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ by pullback. The
*Artin–Schreier sheaf* $\mathcal L_{\psi,f}$ is the $\Psi$-isotypic
component

$$
\mathcal L_{\psi,f}:=e_\Psi\cdot\pi_*\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell
\;\subseteq\;\pi_*\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell,
\qquad
e_\Psi=\frac1p\sum_{a\in\mathbf F_p}\Psi(-a)\,\sigma_a ,
$$

i.e. the subsheaf on which each $\sigma_a$ acts by $\Psi(a)$ ($e_\Psi$ is
defined since $p\neq\ell$). The idempotent uses the character $\Psi$ of
$\mathbf F_p$, not $\psi|_{\mathbf F_p}$, which is trivial when
$p\mid[k_0:\mathbf F_p]$. The same construction for the character
$\psi^{-1}=\Psi^{-1}\circ\operatorname{Tr}_{k_0/\mathbf F_p}$ defines
$\mathcal L_{\psi^{-1},f}:=e_{\Psi^{-1}}\cdot\pi_*\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$.
For $a\in k_0$ put
$\mathcal L_{\psi(af)}:=\mathcal L_{\psi,af}$ (similarly
$\mathcal L_{\psi^{-1}(af)}:=\mathcal L_{\psi^{-1},af}$); on
$\mathbf A^1_{k_0}=\operatorname{Spec}k_0[x]$ one writes
$\mathcal L_\psi:=\mathcal L_{\psi,x}$ (the *Artin–Schreier*, or
*exponential*, sheaf) and $\mathcal L_{\psi(ax)}:=\mathcal L_{\psi,ax}$.

Let $S_0$ be a separated
scheme of finite type over $k_0$, let $V_0\to S_0$ be a vector
bundle of rank $r$ with dual $V_0^\vee$, and let

$$
b:V_0\times_{S_0}V_0^\vee\longrightarrow\mathbf A^1_{S_0},\qquad
(x,\xi)\longmapsto\langle x,\xi\rangle,
$$

be the evaluation pairing, a morphism of $S_0$-schemes; composed with
$\mathbf A^1_{S_0}\to\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ it is a global function
$b\in\Gamma(V_0\times_{S_0}V_0^\vee,\mathcal O)$. The
*Fourier kernel* is the Artin–Schreier sheaf of [def-fd-artin-schreier-sheaf]
attached to this function,

$$
\mathcal K_\psi:=\mathcal L_{\psi,b}=b^*\mathcal L_\psi,
\qquad \mathcal L_\psi=\mathcal L_{\psi,x}\ \text{on }\mathbf A^1_{k_0},
$$

on $V_0\times_{S_0}V_0^\vee$; the two descriptions agree because the
Artin–Schreier covering of $f\circ h$ is the pullback along $h$ of the
covering of $f$, so $h^*\mathcal L_{\psi,f}=\mathcal L_{\psi,f\circ h}$.
For $K\in D^b_c(V,E)$ (the
coefficient category of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]), the
*Fourier integrand* is

$$
\mathcal F_\psi(K):=p_1^*K\otimes^L_E\mathcal K_\psi\in D^b_c(V\times_SV^\vee,E),
$$

with $p_1:V\times_SV^\vee\to V$ the first projection; the Fourier–Deligne
transform is its compact-support direct image along the second projection
$p_2$. (The triple product $V\times_SV^\vee\times_SV'$ with its projections
$r_{ij}$ is introduced separately, for the composition of kernel transforms.)

Let $j:U_0\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ be a dense open immersion and
let $\mathcal M$ be irreducible and lisse on $U_0$ (in the lisse
convention of [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]). Its
middle extension is
*Fourier-nonexceptional* if, after geometric base change, it is
neither a constant sheaf (up to a constant
Weil twist) nor the restriction
of an Artin–Schreier sheaf
$\mathcal L_{\psi(ax)}$ for any $a$.

For a Weil complex $K$ on a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $X_0$
and an $\mathbf F_{q^n}$-point $x\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$, the
*trace function* of $K$ at $x$ is

$$
t_K(x)=\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(F_x^{(n)}\mid K_{\bar x}\bigr)
=\sum_{j\in\mathbf Z}(-1)^j\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(F_x^{(n)}\mid\mathcal H^j(K)_{\bar x}\bigr),
$$

computed with the local Frobenius operators of
[def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] in the
$\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-coefficient category of
[def-weil-pbc-qbar-category].

attrs.title: Trace function of a Weil complex

objects.body:
For $K\in D^b_c(V,E)$, $V_0\to S_0$ being the rank-$r$ vector
bundle of [def-fd-kernel], the *Fourier–Deligne transform*
of $K$ is

$$
\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K):=p_{2,!}\bigl(p_1^*K\otimes^L_E\mathcal K_\psi\bigr)[r],
\qquad p_1:V\times_SV^\vee\to V,\ p_2:V\times_SV^\vee\to V^\vee,
$$

in Laumon's normalization (the shift $[r]$ – the relative dimension
of $V_0/S_0$ – is part of the definition; it is the
normalization for which the transform of a perverse object is
perverse, and for which the inversion formula below holds without an
additional shift, up to the twist $(-r)$). It is an exact
triangulated functor on the ambient derived categories; on the bounded
constructible domains its well-definedness is asserted in the
well-definedness theorem below.

Let $X$ be an
integral scheme
with function field $K$, and let $L/K$ be finite.
The normalization of $X$ in $L$ is the relative
spectrum of the integral closure of $\mathcal O_X$ in
$L$, with its canonical map to $X$. On an
affine open
$\operatorname{Spec}B$, this is
$\operatorname{Spec}\overline B^{,L}$.
Integral closure commutes with localization, so these
affine constructions glue. For $L=K$, this is exactly
[def-sc-normalization]; finiteness is not included in
the definition.

Fix the finite coefficient ring $\Lambda$ of
[sbc-def-coefficient-conventions]. For a morphism $f:X\to S$
between the finite-type schemes of
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let $\mathcal C(f)$ denote
the assertion that $R^qf_*F$, with direct image as in
[def-weil-pbc-direct-image], is constructible for every $q\geq0$
and every constructible $\Lambda$-sheaf $F$ in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes].
This predicate includes no uniform vanishing assertion.

Fix the global finite-field datum
$(p,a,q,k_0,k)$, a prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite extension
$E/\Ql$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer
$\varpi_E$, and $n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$; put
$A=A_{E,n}$ and $\Lambda\in\{A,\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$, with the
finite-torsion
constructibility, derived
completion, rationalization,
and
common-stage scalar
extension conventions of the preceding sections. Let $X,Y$ be
finite-type $k$-schemes,
let $f:X\to Y$ be a
separated morphism of
finite type, and let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an
open immersion. On the
small pro-etale sites use the
bounded constructible categories $D^b_c(-,\Lambda)$ and the
finite-Tor subcategories
$D^b_{ctf}(-,\Lambda)$. The *six-functor operation datum* of the blueprint
consists of:

1. the derived pullback $Lf^*$, the derived tensor
$-\otimes^L_{\Lambda}-$, and the derived internal Hom
$R\mathcal Hom_{\Lambda}(-, -)$, as in
the derived pullback,
tensor, and internal Hom operations, and the derived direct image
$Rf_*$, as in
the derived direct image;
1. the extension-by-zero functor $j_!$, as in
extension by zero, and the
compact-support direct image $Rf_!$, as in
the compactification
independent compact-support direct image at the finite level and
the integral,
rational, and algebraically closed compact-support functors at the
higher levels, with the compactification-comparison isomorphisms and
the composition law
$R(g\circ f)_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg_!Rf_!$ recorded there (the
candidate-level verification of the comparisons for refinements is
[prop-compactification-coherence-detailed]); when $f$ is
proper, the
identification $Rf_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*$ is the one of
[def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] for the compactification
$j=\operatorname{id}$, $p=f$;
1. the exchange transformations $\operatorname{Ex}_*$ and
$\operatorname{Ex}_!$ and the projection transformation
$\operatorname{PF}$, as in
the exchange and projection
transformations;
1. the exceptional inverse image
$$
Rf^!:D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)\longrightarrow D^b_c(X,\Lambda),
$$
the right adjoint of $Rf_!$ on the bounded constructible categories, as in
the exceptional inverse
image notation [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]: the constructible
exceptional adjoint, transported from the etale one, whose existence and
adjunction, interval boundedness, finite-Tor preservation, and refinement
compatibility of units and counits are theorems for every separated
finite-type morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes (thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class,
thm-sf-preservation-class); the ambient notion
exceptional-adjoint
admissibility is not assumed, its clause (1) being false in general;
1. the dualizing objects $\omega_{X,\Lambda}=Ra_X^!\Lambda$ and
the Verdier dual $D_X(-)=R\mathcal Hom_{\Lambda}(-,\omega_{X,\Lambda})$,
formed from the exceptional adjoint and the derived internal Hom already
listed above, for every separated finite-type $X$.

This definition names operations and their construction data. It asserts
neither smooth purity nor Verdier biduality. Preservation of the displayed
constructible domains is established by the separate operation theorems;
the adjoint is the constructible one, available without hypothesis.

Fix a prime $p$, a power $q=p^a$, the fields $k_0=\Fq$ and $k=\bar k_0$, a
prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with algebraic closure
$\Qlb$. All schemes are separated of finite type over $k_0$. We use:
the bounded constructible derived category $D^b_c(-,E)$ — the adic
category, $\Dbc$ of the pro-étale $E$-sheaves of the six-functor package
(derived-complete $\mathcal O_E$-complexes of étale origin, rationalized),
*not* the derived category of discrete sheaves of $E$-modules on the small
étale site, on which the base-change isomorphisms fail — with the six operations $Lf^*,Rf_*,Rf_!,Rf^!,\otimes^L, R\mathcal H om$ in the form of the six-functor package, the
compact-support direct image $Rf_!=Rf_*\circ j_!$ read through a
compactification, ordinary and compact-support cohomology, and the Tate
twists. The additive character $\psi$ takes values in
$\mu_p\subset\Qlb^\times$, so the Artin–Schreier sheaf and the Fourier
kernel $\mathcal K_\psi$ are a priori $\Qlb$-sheaves; we assume throughout
that $\mu_p\subset E$, so that $\psi$ is $E$-valued, $\mathcal K_\psi$ is a
lisse $E$-sheaf of rank one, and the tensor product $\otimes^L_E$ in the
definition of the transform makes sense on $\Dbc(V,E)$. (Without this
assumption the transform is defined at the $\Qlb$-stage, or over $E(\mu_p)$
after extension of scalars.) No weight, no $L^2$-weight parameter and no purity notion is used
anywhere in this file; the Tate twist is a coefficient normalization (the
blueprint records its definition among the weight foundations, but no weight
statement of that chapter is used below). (Blueprint def:weil-pbc-qbar-category,
prop:functor-package, def:weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology,
def:wf-tate-twist.)

attrs.title: The coefficient setting: six operations only

objects.body:
Let $Y$ be a scheme with a geometric point $\bar y\to Y$. Write
$\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$ for the category of
finite etale $Y$-schemes,
with $Y$-morphisms, and $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$ for the category of
finite locally constant sheaves of
finite sets on $Y_{\Et}$, with morphisms of sheaves. For
$\mathcal F\in\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$ and $P\in\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$ write

$$
\mathcal F_{\bar y},\qquad |P_{\bar y}|
$$

for the fibre at $\bar y$; An $M$-torsor is as in
[def-weil-pbc-finite-torsors].

attrs.title: Finite etale covers and finite locally constant sheaves

objects.body:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a category and $F:\mathcal C\to\mathbf{Sets}$ a
functor. The pair $(\mathcal C,F)$ is a *Galois category* if

1. $\mathcal C$ has finite limits and finite colimits;
1. every object of $\mathcal C$ is a finite coproduct of
*connected* objects, where $X$ is connected if it is not initial and
every monomorphism $Y\to X$ is either an isomorphism or has initial
source;
1. $F(X)$ is finite for every object $X$;
1. $F$ is exact (it commutes with finite limits and finite colimits)
and reflects isomorphisms (if $F(f)$ is bijective then $f$ is an
isomorphism).

For a functor with all $F(X)$ finite, $\operatorname{Aut}(F)$ is
identified with the subgroup of
$\prod_X\operatorname{Aut}(F(X))$ formed by the tuples induced by the
natural automorphisms of $F$, and carries the topology induced from the
product of the discrete topologies;

In the situation of [def-galois-categories], the *fibre functor*
is

$$
F_{\bar y}:\mathrm{FLC}(Y)\longrightarrow(\text{finite sets}),\qquad
\mathcal F\longmapsto\mathcal F_{\bar y},
$$

and on $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$ the notation
$P\mapsto|P_{\bar y}|$ of [def-galois-categories] is used; that
the two functors correspond under the identification of
[thm-galois-lc-etale] is part of that theorem. Its
*automorphism group*

$$
\pi_1(Y,\bar y)=\operatorname{Aut}(F_{\bar y})
$$

is the group of natural automorphisms of $F_{\bar y}$, embedded into
$\prod_{\mathcal F}\operatorname{Aut}(F_{\bar y}(\mathcal F))$ by
evaluation and endowed with the topology induced from the product of the
discrete topologies; this is the *etale fundamental group* of $Y$ at
$\bar y$. A $\pi_1(Y,\bar y)$-set is a finite set with a continuous
action of $\pi_1(Y,\bar y)$, and such sets form the category
$\pi_1(Y,\bar y)\text{-}\mathbf{Set}$.

Let $Y$ be connected with geometric point $\bar y$. A finite etale
$P\to Y$, i.e. an object of $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$ as in
[def-galois-categories], is a *Galois cover* if $P$ is
connected over $Y$ and $\operatorname{Aut}_Y(P)$ acts simply
transitively on $P_{\bar y}$.

Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes, $n\ge1$, and
$q_0\ge0$. Say *$BC(f,n,q_0)$ holds* if for every
commutative diagram

$$
\begin{array}{ccccc}
X&\longleftarrow&X'&\longleftarrow&Y\\
\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle f}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle f'}&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle e}\\
S&\longleftarrow&S'&\longleftarrow&T
\end{array}
$$

with $X'=X\times_SS'$, $Y=X'\times_{S'}T$, $g:T\to S'$
quasi-compact and
quasi-separated, $X'\to T$ (resp. $h:Y\to X'$) the resulting
projection, $\Lambda=\kunZn$ coefficients, and every abelian sheaf
$F$ on $T_{\Et}$ annihilated by $n$, the exchange morphism of
[def-kun-unbounded-exchange] is an
isomorphism on $q$-th cohomology sheaves for all $q\le q_0$; those
cohomology sheaves of the exchange morphism are the ones computed in
[lem-kun-bc-map-on-cohomology]. The
cohomological-dimension predicate of [def-kun-cd] is understood
at finite coefficients. The predicate is related to the one of the
smooth-base-change chapter, [sbc-def-base-change-property], which is
defined with the derived exchange morphism of
[sbc-def-base-change-map] in a single degree $q$, for $n$ invertible
on $S$ and squares over $S$ itself: the present $BC(f,n,q_0)$ is the
cumulative form over all base changes, i.e. (for $n$ invertible on
$S$) the property $BC(f',n,q)$ of [sbc-def-base-change-property] for
every $q\le q_0$ and every base change $f':X'\to S'$ of $f$, read
with the unbounded exchange morphism of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange];
the two exchange morphisms agree on the bounded complexes to which both
apply. Here $n$ is not required to be invertible on $S$.

For a
quasi-compact
quasi-separated scheme $T$, the torsion etale
*cohomological dimension* $\kuncd(T)$ is the least
$d\in\mathbf Z_{\ge0}$ with $H^q(T_{\Et},F)=0$ for every
torsion etale sheaf $F$ and
every $q>d$; it is $+\infty$ if no such $d$ exists. For a
quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism $f:X\to Y$, $\kuncd(f)$ is
the least $d$ such that $R^qf_*F=0$ for every torsion etale sheaf
$F$ on $X_{\Et}$ and every $q>d$. The equivalent description of this
vanishing by the strict local test schemes over a geometric point of
$Y$, that is, by the corresponding filtered colimits of cohomology
groups over the pointed etale neighbourhoods, is
[lem-kun-cd-stalk-criterion].

For a scheme $T$, a commutative ring $\Lambda$ and a
$\Lambda$-module $M$, the *constant sheaf* $\underline{M}$ on
$T_{\Et}$ is the sheafification of the constant presheaf
$U\mapsto M$ on the small etale site
[def-weil-pbc-etale-site]; it is the sheaf
of $M$-valued functions associated with the locally constant sheaf
with value $M$. For a complex $\mathcal M^\bullet$ of
$\Lambda$-modules, $\underline{\mathcal M^\bullet}$ is the termwise
constant complex of sheaves, and the operations are compatible with
shifts and with quasi-isomorphisms in $\mathcal M^\bullet$.

Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and $T$ a scheme, and work on
the small etale site of $T$, [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], with
sheaves of $\Lambda_T$-modules. A complex $\mathcal E^\bullet$ of
$\Lambda_T$-modules is *K-flat* if
$\mathcal E^\bullet\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F^\bullet$ is acyclic for
every acyclic complex $\mathcal F^\bullet$. The *derived tensor
product* of $K_1,K_2\in D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ is

$$
K_1\kunotimes{\Lambda}K_2=P\otimes_\Lambda K_2
\in D(T_{\Et},\Lambda),
$$

where $P\to K_1$ is a quasi-isomorphism with $P$ K-flat; the
independence of the result of the chosen K-flat model is
recorded with the other properties of this construction. For $K\in D(T_{\Et})$ and a complex of $\mathbf Z$-modules
$\mathcal M^\bullet$, $K\kunotimes{\mathbf Z}\underline{\mathcal M^\bullet}$
denotes derived tensor with the constant complex of
[def-kun-constant-sheaf].

attrs.title: Derived tensor product of etale sheaves

objects.body:
The *Krull dimension* $\kundim X$ of a scheme is the supremum
of the integers $r$ such that there is a strict chain
$Z_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq Z_r$ of nonempty irreducible closed
subsets of $|X|$. For $x\in X$, the *dimension at $x$* is

$$
\kundim_xX=\min\{\kundim U:x\in U\subseteq X\text{ open}\}.
$$

For a scheme $X$ of finite type over a field $K$ the finiteness
$\kundim X<\infty$ is recorded with the other properties of this notion, and the
computation of the dimension at a point $x\in X$ in terms of the
transcendence degree of
[def-kun-support] is [lem-kun-dimension-formula].

Let $T$ be a scheme and $F$ a sheaf of $\Lambda_T$-modules on
$T_{\Et}$. The *evaluation morphism* of $F$ is

$$
\bigoplus_{s\in\Gamma(T_{\Et},F)}\underline{\Lambda}\longrightarrow F,
\qquad 1_s\longmapsto s,
$$

and $F$ is *globally generated* if this morphism is an
epimorphism of sheaves; the equivalent description by surjectivity of
the evaluation morphism on every geometric stalk is
recorded with the other properties of this notion. For abelian sheaves take
$\Lambda=\mathbf Z$.

Consider a
cartesian square in the
category of schemes

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X\times_SY&\xrightarrow{\;q\;}&Y\\
\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle p}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle g}\\
X&\xrightarrow{\;f\;}&S
\end{array}
$$

and set $c=f\circ p=g\circ q$. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring
and let $E\in D(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$, $K\in D(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$; here
derived direct images are computed by the K-injective resolutions of
[prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist], so they are defined
on the unbounded derived categories. The *Kunneth map* (or
*external product*) is the morphism

$$
\kappa_{E,K}:\quad
Rf_*E\kunotimes{\Lambda}Rg_*K\longrightarrow
Rc_*\bigl(p^{-1}E\kunotimes{\Lambda}q^{-1}K\bigr)
$$

in $D(S_{\Et},\Lambda)$ which is adjoint (under the adjunction
$c^{-1}\dashv Rc_*$ of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]) to the
composite

$$
c^{-1}\bigl(Rf_*E\kunotimes{\Lambda}Rg_*K\bigr)
\;\cong\;
p^{-1}f^{-1}Rf_*E\kunotimes{\Lambda}q^{-1}g^{-1}Rg_*K
\xrightarrow{\ \varepsilon_f\otimes\varepsilon_g\ }
p^{-1}E\kunotimes{\Lambda}q^{-1}K,
$$

where the first isomorphism is the monoidality isomorphism of
[lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal] for the inverse image functors
together with the canonical identifications
$c^{-1}\cong p^{-1}f^{-1}$ and $c^{-1}\cong q^{-1}g^{-1}$, and
$\varepsilon_f$, $\varepsilon_g$ are the derived counits of
[def-weil-pbc-inverse-image].

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes, $\Lambda$ a commutative
ring, $E\in D(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$, and $K\in D(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$.
The *projection-formula morphism* is the morphism

$$
\mathrm{PF}_f(E,K):\quad
Rf_*E\kunotimes{\Lambda}K\longrightarrow
Rf_*\bigl(E\kunotimes{\Lambda}f^{-1}K\bigr)
$$

in $D(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$ adjoint to the composite

$$
f^{-1}(Rf_*E\kunotimes{\Lambda}K)
\cong f^{-1}Rf_*E\kunotimes{\Lambda}f^{-1}K
\xrightarrow{\ \varepsilon_f\otimes1\ }E\kunotimes{\Lambda}f^{-1}K,
$$

where the first map is the monoidality isomorphism of
[lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal] for the
inverse image $f^{-1}$ and
$\varepsilon_f$ is the counit of the derived adjunction.

A morphism of schemes $f:X\to Y$ is *projective* if there are
an integer $N\ge0$ and a
closed immersion
$i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_Y$ such that $f$ is the composite
of $i$ with the structural projection $\mathbf P^N_Y\to Y$. A
scheme is projective over a field $k$ if its structure morphism is
projective.

For a scheme $T$, a commutative ring $\Lambda$ and
$K\in D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$, choose a K-injective resolution in the
sense of [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions],
$K\to I$ (which exists by
[prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist]) and put

$$
\RGamma(T_{\Et},K)=\Gamma(T_{\Et},I),
\qquad
H^q(T_{\Et},K)=\mathcal H^q(\RGamma(T_{\Et},K)).
$$

The independence of the result of the chosen resolution is
recorded with the other properties of this construction, and for
$K\in\Dplus(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ its agreement with the functor
$\RGamma(T_{\Et},-)$ of
[def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] is
also recorded with those properties.

A field $K$ is *separably closed* if it admits no nontrivial
finite separable extension. A *separable closure* of a field
$K$ is a separable algebraic extension $K^{\mathrm{sep}}/K$ whose
top field is separably closed.

*Implementation note.* Mathlib's `IsSepClosed K` is stated as "every separable
polynomial over $K$ splits", which is equivalent to the formulation above. The
picard-schemes chapter defines the same notion again in that polynomial form, as
[def-pc-separably-closed].

Let $X$ be a scheme of finite type over a field $K$ (the
scheme conventions of
the proper-base-change chapter; in particular $X$ is Noetherian, quasi-compact and
quasi-separated). A point $x\in X$ is *closed* if $\{x\}$ is
closed in $|X|$; write

$$
\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(x)
$$

for the transcendence degree of the residue field $\kappa(x)$ over
$K$, and for $a\ge0$ set

$$
E_a(X)=\{x\in X:\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(x)\le a\}.
$$

For an etale sheaf $F\in\Ab(X_{\Et})$, the *support*
$\kunsupp F$ is the set of $x\in X$ such that $F_{\bar x}\ne0$
for some geometric point
$\bar x$ over $x$; that this set does not depend on the choice of
the geometric point over $x$ is recorded with the other properties of
this notion. For
$K\in D(X_{\Et})$ put

$$
\kunsupp K=\bigcup_q\kunsupp\mathcal H^q(K)
$$

using the cohomology
sheaves of $K$.

Let $T$ be a scheme, $\Lambda$ a commutative ring, and
$E\in D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$, $a,b\in\mathbf Z$. The object $E$ has
*tor amplitude in $[a,b]$* (resp. $[a,\infty)$) if for every
sheaf $\mathcal M\in\Mod(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ placed in degree zero,

$$
H^i\bigl(E\kunotimes{\Lambda}\mathcal M\bigr)=0
\qquad\text{for all }i\notin[a,b]\ \ (\text{resp. }i<a).
$$

That a bounded complex of flat $\Lambda_T$-module sheaves supported in
degrees $[a,b]$ has tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ is recorded with the
other properties of this notion; boundedness alone
does not imply finite tor amplitude.

For an etale abelian sheaf $F$ and $n\ge1$ write
$F[n]=\ker(n:F\to F)$, so that a
torsion sheaf is a sheaf whose
local sections are killed by positive integers. Let $K$ be a field
and let

$$
I_K=\{n\ge1:n\cdot1_K\ne0\},
$$

ordered by divisibility; $n\in I_K$ is called *invertible in
$K$*. A torsion sheaf on the etale site of a $K$-scheme has
*orders invertible in $K$* if every element of every geometric
stalk is killed by some $n\in I_K$. For $K$ of
characteristic $p>0$ this says the stalks have no
$p$-primary torsion; for $\operatorname{char}K=0$ it is no
condition besides torsion. A complex $K\in D(T_{\Et})$ has
*torsion cohomology with orders invertible in $K$* if every
$\mathcal H^q(K)$ has that property.

attrs.title: Torsion objects and orders invertible in a field

objects.body:
For a complex $\mathcal E^\bullet$ of etale sheaves, the
*stupid truncations* $\sigma_{\ge n}$ and $\sigma_{\le n}$
are obtained by replacing the terms in degrees $<n$ (resp. $>n$)
by $0$. The *good (canonical) truncations* $\tau_{\ge n}$,
$\tau_{\le n}$ are the truncation functors of the standard
t-structure on $D(T_{\Et})$: they keep the cohomology objects in the
retained range and kill those outside it. The triangle

$$
\tau_{\le n-1}K\to\tau_{\le n}K\to\mathcal H^n(K)[-n]\to
$$

is the truncation couple of [def-sp-truncation-couple] in
the spectral-sequence chapter; these truncation triangles are the ones used for the
hypercohomology
filtrations of the spectral-sequence chapter.

In a triangulated category with countable direct sums, the
*homotopy colimit* of a sequence $E_0\to E_1\to\cdots$ is
specified by a distinguished triangle

$$
\bigoplus_nE_n\xrightarrow{\,1-\mathrm{shift}\,}\bigoplus_nE_n
\longrightarrow\operatorname{hocolim}_nE_n\longrightarrow
\bigl(\bigoplus_nE_n\bigr)[1].
$$

The colimit of etale sheaves is the sheafification of the objectwise
colimit of the underlying presheaves. Geometric stalks are computed
by filtered colimits of sections over
pointed etale
neighbourhoods; their commutation with colimits of sheaves, hence
with colimits of complexes of sheaves, is
[lem-kun-stalks-commute-colimits].

Let $\square=(f,f',g,g',\alpha)$ be a
cartesian square, let
$\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, and let
$K\in D(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$. The derived adjunction
$f'^{-1}\dashv Rf'_*$ extends to the unbounded derived categories by
[prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist], and the
*exchange morphism* of $K$ is the mate

$$
\Ex_{\square,K}:g^{-1}Rf_*K\longrightarrow Rf'_*g'^{-1}K
$$

of the composite

$$
f'^{-1}g^{-1}Rf_*K\xrightarrow{\theta_\square}
g'^{-1}f^{-1}Rf_*K\xrightarrow{g'^{-1}\varepsilon_f}g'^{-1}K,
$$

exactly as in [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange].

If $\mathcal V$ is a rank-$r$ lisse
Weil sheaf with
fundamental representation
$V$, its *determinant line* is the rank-one Weil representation

$$
\det(V):=\bigwedge\nolimits^r V,
\qquad
\det(\rho)(g)=\det(\rho(g)).
$$

The corresponding rank-one Weil sheaf is denoted $\det(\mathcal V)$.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional Weil representation on the preceding
normal geometrically connected curve $X_0$. Its *determinantal-weight
multiset* is

$$
\bigl\{\!\bigl\{\hyperref[def-wf-determinantal-weight]{\dw_\iota(S)}:
S\text{ a simple summand of }V^{\mathrm{ss}}\bigr\}\!\bigr\},
$$

with one entry for every occurrence of $S$. Its independence of the
chosen composition series is [lem-mg-semisimplification-independent].

Let $V$ be the finite-dimensional Weil representation in the
monodromy data of a lisse Weil sheaf.
A *composition series* is a finite filtration by Weil-stable
subspaces

$$
0=V_0\subsetneq V_1\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq V_t=V
$$

such that every quotient $V_i/V_{i-1}$ is a *simple Weil
representation*: it is nonzero and has no nonzero proper Weil-stable
subspace. These
quotients, with repetitions retained, are the *composition factors*
of the chosen series.

attrs.title: Composition series of a Weil representation

objects.body:
For a composition series
$V_\bullet$, the *semisimplification* is

$$
V^{\mathrm{ss}}:=\bigoplus_{i=1}^{t}V_i/V_{i-1}.
$$

That its isomorphism class does not depend on the chosen composition
series is recorded with the other properties of this construction; the
multiset of its simple summands is the composition-factor multiset of
[lem-mg-jordan-holder].

Let $U\hookrightarrow X$ be a quasi-compact open immersion. A
*$U$-admissible blow-up datum* consists of a finite type
quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ with
$\mathcal I|_U=\mathcal O_U$, a morphism
$\pi\colon X'\to X$, and a specified isomorphism
$X'\cong\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$ over $X$. A morphism equipped
with such data is called a $U$-admissible blow-up. The definition records
the ideal and the identification with its blow-up; the equivalent
finite-presentation closed-center formulation is stated separately once
the required ideal/closed-immersion comparison is available.

For an ideal $I\subseteq A$, define

$$
\operatorname{Bl}_I(\operatorname{Spec}A)
=\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal R_A(I)).
$$

Its structure morphism is induced by the canonical degree-zero map
$A\to\mathcal R_A(I)_0$.

Define

$$
\chi_a\colon \operatorname{Spec}(A[I/a])\longrightarrow D_+(at)
$$

to be the affine morphism induced contravariantly by $\theta_a$ after the
standard identification of $D_+(at)$ with the spectrum of the degree-zero
homogeneous localization.

Define

$$
r_s\colon
\operatorname{Bl}_{IA_s}(\operatorname{Spec}A_s)
\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Bl}_I(\operatorname{Spec}A)
\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}A_s
$$

by applying the relative-Proj morphism of
[prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality] to $\rho_s$ and the
canonical degree-zero identifications.

Let $U\to S$ be quasi-compact and of finite type and let
$\iota_U\colon U\to\mathbb A^n_S$ be an immersion over $S$, as supplied by
[def-nagata-quasi-affine-immersion-affine-space] when $U$ is
quasi-affine. Compose $\iota_U$ with the standard open immersion
$\mathbb A^n_S\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^n_S$ and define

$$
\mathsf C_{\mathrm{aff}}(U/S)
=\mathsf C\bigl(U\longrightarrow\mathbb P^n_S\bigr)
$$

using [def-nagata-immersion-compactification].

**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the finite-presentation and
Noetherian descent is done in one step by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_isPullback_of_finitePresentation_of_isSeparated`
and `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.nonempty_noetherianApproximation`, so
this stage-by-stage bookkeeping is never carried out.

Suppose $S_{\lambda_0}=\operatorname{Spec}(A_{\lambda_0})$,
$S=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$, and fix a finite presentation

$$
B=A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(r_1,\ldots,r_m).
$$

Select finite-stage lifts of every coefficient of every $r_j$, let
$\lambda_B$ be their selected common upper bound, let
$r_{j,\lambda_B}$ be the lifted polynomials, and define

$$
B_{\lambda_B}
=A_{\lambda_B}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/
(r_{1,\lambda_B},\ldots,r_{m,\lambda_B}).
$$

Define $\beta_B$ to be the comparison from
$B_{\lambda_B}\otimes_{A_{\lambda_B}}A$ to $B$ induced by the presentation.

attrs.title: Finite-stage model of a finitely presented affine algebra

objects.body:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the finite-presentation and
Noetherian descent is done in one step by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_isPullback_of_finitePresentation_of_isSeparated`
and `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.nonempty_noetherianApproximation`, so
this stage-by-stage bookkeeping is never carried out.

Start with the finite lists of basic-open elements in $\mathsf G_S$.
Close these lists under the finitely many overlap maps and proposed
inverses, recording the finitely many coefficients occurring when the
images are expressed in the selected localizations. The identity and
cocycle paths in the finite gluing groupoid show that one such finite
closure suffices. For each chart, take the finitely generated
$\mathbf Z$-subalgebra generated by its resulting finite list. Define
$\lambda_{\mathrm{coeff}}(S)$ to be the selected finite upper bound of all
chartwise coefficient indices, and denote the resulting finite-stage raw
gluing datum by
$\mathsf G_{S,\lambda_{\mathrm{coeff}}}^{\mathrm{raw}}$.

attrs.title: Coefficient stage of an affine gluing presentation

objects.body:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the finite-presentation and
Noetherian descent is done in one step by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_isPullback_of_finitePresentation_of_isSeparated`
and `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.nonempty_noetherianApproximation`, so
this stage-by-stage bookkeeping is never carried out.

For every identity, inverse, open-preservation, and triple-cocycle equation
in $\mathsf G_S$, select a finite stage at which that equation holds on the
chosen generators after localization. Define
$\lambda_{\mathrm{glue}}(S)$ to be the selected upper bound of
$\lambda_{\mathrm{coeff}}(S)$ and these finitely many witness stages. Let
$\mathsf G_{S,\lambda_{\mathrm{glue}}}$ be the pullback of the raw datum to
this stage.

attrs.title: Cocycle-valid stage of an affine gluing presentation

objects.body:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the affine cover meeting the
selected generic points is produced in one step by
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAffineOpen_iSup_eq_top_and_genericPoints_subset_iInter`
and `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.finiteAffineOpenCoverDenseIInter`.

Let $X$ be quasi-separated, let $x\in X$, and let
$\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_r$ be generic points of distinct irreducible
components. Choose one witness from
[lemma-nagata-affine-neighbourhood-generic-points-exists] and denote
its affine open by $A(x;\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_r)$.

attrs.title: Affine neighbourhood containing selected generic points

objects.body:
For an $\mathbb N$-graded commutative ring $R$, use the Mathlib scheme
$\operatorname{Proj}(R)$, with its structural morphism to the degree-zero
spectrum. On a homogeneous element $f$ of positive degree, its standard
open is identified with $\operatorname{Spec}(R_{(f),0})$ by
`Proj.basicOpenIsoSpec`; a homogeneous family generating the
irrelevant ideal gives the cover through
`AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.iSup_basicOpen_eq_top`.

**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the finite-presentation and
Noetherian descent is done in one step by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_isPullback_of_finitePresentation_of_isSeparated`
and `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.nonempty_noetherianApproximation`, so
this stage-by-stage bookkeeping is never carried out.

Fix $\lambda_0\in I$ and a scheme $Y_{\lambda_0}$ equipped with a morphism
to $S_{\lambda_0}$. On the cofinal directed subsystem
$I_{\lambda_0}=\{\lambda\mid\lambda_0\leq\lambda\}$, define

$$
Y_\lambda=Y_{\lambda_0}\times_{S_{\lambda_0}}S_\lambda,
\qquad
Y=Y_{\lambda_0}\times_{S_{\lambda_0}}S.
$$

The transition morphisms $Y_\mu\to Y_\lambda$ for
$\lambda\leq\mu$ are the canonical base changes of the inverse-system
transitions $S_\mu\to S_\lambda$, and the maps $Y\to Y_\lambda$ are the
projections induced by $S\to S_\lambda$.

attrs.title: Base-changed system over a chosen stage

objects.body:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the affine blow-up and its
charts are the construction `AlgebraicGeometry.AffineBlowup`, with
`AffineBlowup.chart` and
`AffineBlowup.isLocalization_away_map` supplying the chart algebra
and its localization coherence, so neither is rebuilt by hand.

Let $a\in I$. Define $A[I/a]$ to be the $A$-subalgebra of $A_a$
generated by the fractions $x/a$ with $x\in I$.

**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: blow-ups are never
base-changed along a flat morphism. Every base-change step the route takes
goes through the universal property
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.exists_lift_blowup` and
the chart pullback squares
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.isPullback_blowup$\iota$`
instead.

Let $g\colon Y\to X$ be flat and let
$\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be a quasi-coherent ideal. With
$\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y$ defined in
[def-nagata-extended-ideal], define

$$
\operatorname{bc}_g\colon
\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y}(Y)
\longrightarrow
Y\times_X\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)
$$

by applying relative Proj to $\beta_g$ on affine opens and gluing. The
degreewise graded equivalence used in this construction is
[lemma-nagata-flat-pullback-rees].

Let $X$ be a scheme and let $\mathcal I,\mathcal J$ be finite-type
quasi-coherent ideals on $X$. Let $X_{\mathcal I,\mathcal J}$ be the
scheme obtained by first blowing up $\mathcal I$ and then the extended
ideal $\mathcal J\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)}$ from
[def-nagata-extended-ideal].
The first exceptional ideal is Cartier after the first blow-up. Applying
[lemma-nagata-cartier-total-transform-blowup] on the second blow-up
(chartwise, where the pulled-back local equation remains regular) shows
that its total transform is invertible. This is the special total-transform
input; no assertion about arbitrary images of invertible ideals is used.
On this iterated blow-up, the total transform
of the first exceptional ideal is invertible, and the second exceptional
ideal is invertible by [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center].
Hence their product, which is the extension of
$\mathcal I\mathcal J$, is invertible by
[lemma-nagata-invertible-ideal-mul]; define

$$
\Phi_{\mathcal I,\mathcal J}\colon
X_{\mathcal I,\mathcal J}
\longrightarrow\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal J}(X)
$$

by the universal-lift construction for their product. On
$\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal J}(X)$, factor the invertible
product first through the $\mathcal I$-blow-up. The extension of
$\mathcal I\mathcal J$ is an effective Cartier ideal, so
[lemma-nagata-invertible-product-factor] and
[lemma-nagata-effective-cartier-is-invertible] make the extensions
of both factors invertible. The universal lift for $\mathcal I$, followed
by the universal lift for the extended $\mathcal J$, defines the resulting
map

$$
\Psi_{\mathcal I,\mathcal J}\colon
\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal J}(X)
\longrightarrow X_{\mathcal I,\mathcal J}.
$$

attrs.title: Comparison maps for the product-ideal blow-up

objects.body:
Define

$$
d_{\mathcal I}\colon\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal J}(X)
\longrightarrow\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)
$$

as $\Psi_{\mathcal I,\mathcal J}$ followed by the first blow-up
projection. Define $d_{\mathcal J}$ symmetrically after interchanging
$\mathcal I$ and $\mathcal J$.

attrs.title: Domination maps from the product blow-up

objects.body:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the finite-presentation and
Noetherian descent is done in one step by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_isPullback_of_finitePresentation_of_isSeparated`
and `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.nonempty_noetherianApproximation`, so
this stage-by-stage bookkeeping is never carried out.

Let $g_\lambda\colon Z_\lambda\to Y_\lambda$ be of finite presentation
between finite-presentation $S_\lambda$-schemes, and assume its base change
to $S$ is a closed immersion. Define $\mu_{\mathrm{cl}}(g)$ by classical
choice from the witness type supplied by
[lemma-nagata-closed-immersion-stage-exists]. Only the index component
is part of this definition; its eventual property is stated below.

attrs.title: Stage at which a finite-presentation map is closed

objects.body:
Let $i\colon X\hookrightarrow X'$ be closed over $S$ and fix a
compactification $C'=(X'\to\overline X'\to S)$. Define
$\mathsf{Closed}(i,C')$ by taking the scheme-theoretic image
$\overline X=\operatorname{SIm}(X\to\overline X')$ and the factorization

$$
X\longrightarrow\overline X\hookrightarrow\overline X'\longrightarrow S.
$$

Let $X=V(\mathcal I)\hookrightarrow Y$ be closed with $Y$ qcqs. Let
$A_{X/Y}$ be the directed set of finite type quasi-coherent subideals
$\mathcal I_\alpha\subseteq\mathcal I$, ordered by inclusion. Define

$$
X_\alpha=V(\mathcal I_\alpha)\hookrightarrow Y,
$$

and for $\alpha\leq\beta$ define the transition
$X_\beta\hookrightarrow X_\alpha$ from
$\mathcal I_\alpha\subseteq\mathcal I_\beta$.

Let $U\hookrightarrow X_i$ be open immersions over $S$, with
$U,X_1,X_2$ separated and of finite type over the qcqs scheme $S$.
Construct the following objects in order.

1. Let
$$
X_{12}=\operatorname{SIm}
\bigl(U\longrightarrow X_1\times_SX_2\bigr)
$$
and write $p_i\colon X_{12}\to X_i$ for the projections.
1. Apply [def-nagata-elimination-indeterminacy] to $(p_i,U)$.
Denote the resulting blow-ups by
$X_i^i= X^{\mathrm{el}}(p_i,U)$, their center ideals by
$\mathcal I_i$, and the open strict transforms by
$X_{12}^i\subseteq X_i^i$.
1. On $X_{12}$ define
$$
\mathcal K_{12}
=p_1^{-1}\mathcal I_1\mathcal O_{X_{12}}\,
p_2^{-1}\mathcal I_2\mathcal O_{X_{12}},
\qquad
X'_{12}=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K_{12}}(X_{12}).
$$
1. The product-center blow-up maps to each $X_{12}^i$. Extend
$X'_{12}\to X_{12}^i$ across the open
$X_{12}^i\subseteq X_i^i$ by
[def-nagata-extended-admissible-blowup]; call the resulting
ambient schemes $X'_i$.
1. Define
$$
\mathsf{CM}(X_1,X_2;U)=X'_1\amalg_{X'_{12}}X'_2
$$
using the two constructed open immersions of $X'_{12}$.

The construction includes the maps $X'_i\to X_i$, the two open maps
$X'_i\to\mathsf{CM}(X_1,X_2;U)$, and the identified copy of $U$.

*Packaged interface.* What is recorded as data — and what the
formalised structure `CommonModification` carries — is only: the two
$U$-admissible blow-ups $X'_i\to X_i$, the two open immersions
$X'_i\to\mathsf{CM}(X_1,X_2;U)$ together with the fact that they cover
$\mathsf{CM}(X_1,X_2;U)$, the two lifted copies of $U$ and their agreement in
the glued scheme, and separatedness and finite type of
$\mathsf{CM}(X_1,X_2;U)\to S$. The stronger overlap identification of step 5
— that the two opens glue along *exactly* $X'_{12}$ and not merely along
their topological intersection — is an internal step of the construction: it is
used in the proof of [lemma-nagata-common-modification] to obtain
separatedness of the glued scheme, and separatedness is part of the packaged
interface. The downstream consumers
([def-nagata-two-open-final-modification] and
[lemma-nagata-two-open-density-transport]) use only the packaged
interface: density transport needs the two charts to cover and the copies of
$U$ to agree, and the valuative lifting argument needs only separatedness of
$\mathsf{CM}(X_1,X_2;U)\to S$.

A morphism $f\colon X\to S$ is *compactifiable* if the type of
compactifications of $f$ is nonempty.

Let $f\colon X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes. A *compactification*
of $f$ consists of a scheme $\overline X$, morphisms

$$
X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}S,
$$

and an equality $j;p=f$, such that $j$ is a quasi-compact open immersion and
$p$ is proper.

Given a compactification $C=(X\to\overline X\to S)$ and $S'\to S$, define
$C_{S'}$ to be

$$
X\times_SS'\longrightarrow\overline X\times_SS'\longrightarrow S'.
$$

Let $X$, $\mathcal I$, $X'$, $b$, $Z'$, $d$, and $\mathcal J(Z')$ be as in
[lemma-nagata-composition-center-ideal], and let the second blow-up be
centred at $Z'\hookrightarrow X'$. Let $E$ be the exceptional divisor of
$b$ and let $\mathcal I_E$ be its invertible ideal; write
$\mathcal I_{Z'}$ for the ideal defining $Z'$. Form the explicit ideal
$\mathcal K(Z')=\mathcal I\mathcal J(Z')$ on $X$. The extended ideal on
$X'$ is $\mathcal I_E^d\mathcal I_{Z'}$. Define

$$
\Omega_{Z,Z'}\colon
\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I_{Z'}}(X')
\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K(Z')}(X)
$$

as the product-blow-up comparison followed by the comparison which removes
the invertible factor $\mathcal I_E^d$. Define the reverse map by the
corresponding universal lifts.

attrs.title: Comparison for a composite of arbitrary blow-ups

objects.body:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: Deligne's disjointness blow-up
is formalized as the single statement
`AlgebraicGeometry.disjoint_closure_range_of_blowupMap_sup`,
which absorbs this step.

Consider open immersions $i\colon U\to V$ and $j\colon V\to X$, a morphism
$p\colon Z\to X$, a scheme $Y$ over $U$, and a quasi-compact immersion
$f\colon Y\to Z$ over $X$, so that the square

$$
(Y\xrightarrow{f}Z\xrightarrow{p}X)
\;=\;(Y\to U\xrightarrow{j\circ i}X)
$$

commutes; in particular $Y$ lies over $U$. Write $\overline Y$ for the scheme-theoretic image of $Y$ in $Z$
under $f$. Fix the following data.

1. A quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I_1$ on $X$ with
$\overline{V\setminus U}\subseteq V(\mathcal I_1)\subseteq X\setminus U$
as sets, and $T_1=V(\mathcal I_1^2)$, a square-zero thickening of
$V(\mathcal I_1)$.
1. A quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I_2$ on $X$ whose zero scheme
$T_2=V(\mathcal I_2)$ satisfies $T_2\subseteq T_1\cap(X\setminus V)$ as
sets.
1. The hypothesis that the closed subscheme
$p^{-1}(T_1)\cap\overline Y$ of $Z$ factors through the closed
subscheme $p^{-1}(T_2)$. Loosely: $p(p^{-1}(T_1)\cap\overline Y) \subseteq T_2\subseteq T_1\cap(X\setminus V)$, the first inclusion as
schemes and the second as sets.

Let $q\colon X'\to X$ be the blow-up of $X$ along $\mathcal I_1+\mathcal I_2$
and let $Y',Z',p'$ denote the base changes of $Y,Z,p$ along $q$.

**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: quasi-dominations are not
introduced in Lean. The extension statements are proved directly from
scheme-theoretic dominance and separatedness, through
`AlgebraicGeometry.ext_of_isSchemeTheoreticallyDominant_of_isSeparated`.

Let $X$ and $Y$ be $S$-schemes with $Y\to S$ separated. A
*quasi-domination of $X$ over $Y$* is a pair $(U,f)$ consisting of a
dense open subscheme $U\subseteq X$ and an $S$-morphism $f\colon U\to Y$
whose graph subscheme

$$
\Gamma_f\hookrightarrow U\times_SY
$$

is closed when viewed as a subscheme of $X\times_SY$. If $U'\subseteq X$ is
an open subscheme and $f'\colon U'\to Y$ an $S$-morphism, a
*quasi-domination of $X$ over $Y$ extending $f'$* is a quasi-domination
$(U,f)$ with $U'\subseteq U\subseteq X$ and $f|_{U'}=f'$.

Let $T\subseteq U$ be constructible and closed, with $U$ qcqs. Its
complement $W=U\setminus T$ is a quasi-compact open. Define

$$
\mathcal J_U(T)=\mathcal I_U(W).
$$

attrs.title: Ideal whose support is a constructible closed subset

objects.body:
Under the hypotheses of
[lemma-nagata-dense-affine-cover-exists], choose one witness and denote
its finite family and its total intersection by

$$
\mathcal U_X=(U_1,\ldots,U_n),
\qquad D_X=\bigcap_{i=1}^nU_i.
$$

attrs.title: Finite affine cover with selected dense intersection

objects.body:
A compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\to S$ is
*scheme-theoretically dense* when its first map has the predicate
introduced in [def-nagata-scheme-theoretically-dense-open]; explicitly,
this means that

$$
\mathcal O_{\overline X}\longrightarrow j_*\mathcal O_X
$$

is injective.

For a compactification $C=(X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\to S)$, define
$\mathsf{Dense}(C)$ by replacing $\overline X$ with
$\operatorname{SIm}(j)$ and using $j^{\mathrm{im}}$ as its first map.

Let $h\colon T\to P$ be quasi-compact, assume its image
inclusion $\operatorname{SIm}(h)\hookrightarrow P$ is an isomorphism, assume
$P$ is affine, and let $z\in P$.
Select a witness from
[def-nagata-dense-valuation-probe] and denote it by

$$
\mathsf{VP}(h,z)=
(A'_{h,z},K'_{h,z},\eta_{h,z},\alpha_{h,z}),
$$

where $A'_{h,z}$ is the selected valuation ring, $K'_{h,z}$ its fraction
field, $\eta_{h,z}\colon\operatorname{Spec}(K'_{h,z})\to T$ the selected
generic lift, and
$\alpha_{h,z}\colon\operatorname{Spec}(A'_{h,z})\to P$ the selected centred
valuation map.

## Existence of a valuation probe through a dense source

Let $h\colon T\to P$ be quasi-compact, assume its image
inclusion $\operatorname{SIm}(h)\hookrightarrow P$ is an isomorphism, assume
$P$ is affine, and let $z\in P$. There
exist a valuation ring $A'$ with fraction field $K'$, a morphism
$\eta\colon\operatorname{Spec}(K')\to T$, and a morphism
$\alpha\colon\operatorname{Spec}(A')\to P$ such that the generic square
commutes and the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}(A')$ maps to $z$.

*Proof.*
Let $Z=\operatorname{SIm}(h)$. The assumed image isomorphism identifies
$z$ with a point of $Z$. Stacks Project, Tag 02JQ (Lemma 29.6.5),
applied to the quasi-compact morphism $h$ and the point $z\in Z$, supplies
a valuation ring $A'$, its fraction field $K'$, a map
$\operatorname{Spec}(K')\to T$, and a map
$\operatorname{Spec}(A')\to Z$ whose generic restriction is the supplied
map and whose closed point is $z$. Composing the latter map with the image
closed immersion $Z\hookrightarrow P$ gives $\alpha$, and the generic
commutativity supplied by the theorem is exactly the displayed square.

Let $I$ be a nonempty directed preorder. Fix a base point $i_\varnothing$
and, for each pair $(i,j)$, fix a selected common upper bound $d(i,j)$
together with proofs $i\leq d(i,j)$ and $j\leq d(i,j)$. Define
$u(F)\in I$ by Finset induction, inserting only an element $i\notin F$:

$$
u(\varnothing)=i_\varnothing,
\qquad
u(F\cup\{i\})=d(u(F),i)\quad(i\notin F).

attrs.title: Selected upper bound of a finite set

objects.body:
A quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ is an
*effective Cartier ideal* if, on an open cover, it has a generator
which is a non-zero-divisor in the corresponding ring. Invertibility is
a consequence recorded separately below.

Let $q\colon Z\to X$ be separated and of finite type, let $X$ be qcqs, and
let $U\subseteq X$ be quasi-compact. Fix an isomorphism
$e_U\colon q^{-1}(U)\xrightarrow{\sim}U$ over $U$. The construction is the
bridge of [the-general-case-via-zariski-s-main-theorem--remark-2], with each
choice labelled.

1. By [lemma-nagata-conrad-schematically-dense-blowup], select a finite type
ideal $\mathcal I_0$ with $V(\mathcal I_0)=X\setminus U$ and put
$X_1=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I_0}(X)$, a $U$-admissible blow-up in which
$U$ is scheme-theoretically dense. Let $q_1\colon Z_1\to X_1$ be the strict
transform of $Z$; it is separated, of finite type, and an isomorphism over
$U$.
1. The section $s\colon U\cong q_1^{-1}(U)\hookrightarrow Z_1$ induced by
$e_U$ is a quasi-domination $(U,s)$ of $U$ over $Z_1$
([def-nagata-conrad-quasi-domination]). Apply
[thm-nagata-conrad-elimination] over the base $X_1$ with $V=U$, and select
the resulting $U$-admissible centre $\mathcal I$ on $X_1$ together with the
quasi-domination $(W,\widetilde s)$ of $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X_1)$
over $Z_1$ extending $s$.
1. Let $\mathcal I_1=\mathcal I_0\mathcal O_{X_1}$, so that
$V(\mathcal I_1)=X_1\setminus U$. Define

$$
X^{\mathrm{el}}(q,U)=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal I_1}(X_1),
\qquad
Z^{\mathrm{el}}(q,U)=\operatorname{ST}_{X^{\mathrm{el}}/X}(Z),
$$

together with the strict-transform projection
$q^{\mathrm{el}}\colon Z^{\mathrm{el}}(q,U)\to X^{\mathrm{el}}(q,U)$ and
the transported open identification induced by $e_U$. By
[cor-nagata-blowup-product-common-refinement], $X^{\mathrm{el}}(q,U)$
dominates $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X_1)$ over $X_1$, and by
[lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-comp] the composite
$X^{\mathrm{el}}(q,U)\to X_1\to X$ is a $U$-admissible blow-up of $X$
([def-nagata-admissible-blowup]).

The centres $\mathcal I_0$ and $\mathcal I$ are labelled selections, so
$X^{\mathrm{el}}(q,U)$ is a named object rather than an unspecified
existential variable.

Let $X$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated and let $U,W\subseteq X$ be
quasi-compact opens. Write a given $(U\cap W)$-admissible blow-up of $W$
as $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J}(W)\to W$. Its center ideal restricts
to the unit ideal on $U\cap W$, so glue $\mathcal J$ on $W$ with the unit
ideal on $U$ to an ideal $\mathcal J^+$ on $U\cup W$ using
[lemma-nagata-glue-finite-type-ideals], and set

$$
\mathcal I_{X}(\mathcal J)
=\operatorname{Ext}_{X,U\cup W}(\mathcal J^+),
$$

and define

$$
\mathsf{ExtBl}_{X,W,U}(\mathcal J)
=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I_X(\mathcal J)}(X)\longrightarrow X.
$$

attrs.title: Flat pullback map for Rees algebras

objects.body:
Let $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$ be the scheme produced by applying
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.GlueData.glued` to the valid datum of
[def-nagata-global-blowup-glue-data].

Fix an affine cover $(V_i)_i$ of $X$. Define
$\mathsf G(X,\mathcal I,(V_i))$ to consist of the local schemes
$\mathsf B_{V_i}(\mathcal I)$, their inverse images of $V_i\cap V_j$, and
the overlap maps obtained by gluing the maps $\omega_{ij,s}$ on a chosen
basic affine cover of every intersection. The equality on intersections
required to glue these local maps is
[lemma-nagata-global-blowup-overlap-independent].

## Validity of the global blow-up gluing datum

The raw datum $\mathsf G(X,\mathcal I,(V_i))$ has isomorphism-valued
overlap maps satisfying the identity, symmetry, and triple-overlap cocycle
axioms; hence it is a scheme gluing datum.

*Proof.*
The overlap maps are isomorphisms by
[lemma-nagata-global-blowup-overlap-basic]; independence of refinements,
identity, symmetry, and the triple cocycle are given by the cited coherence
lemmas. Hence the hypotheses of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.GlueData.glued` are satisfied.

Let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be quasi-coherent and let
$V=\operatorname{Spec}(A)\subseteq X$ be affine. Put
$I_V=\Gamma(V,\mathcal I)\subseteq A$ and define the local model

$$
\mathsf B_V(\mathcal I)=\operatorname{Bl}_{I_V}(V)\longrightarrow V.
$$

attrs.title: Local blow-up model on an affine open

objects.body:

\omega_{ij,s}\colon
\mathsf B_{V_i}(\mathcal I)|_{D(s)}
\longrightarrow
\mathsf B_{V_j}(\mathcal I)|_{D(s)}
$$

as $r_{j,s}\circ r_{i,s}^{-1}$: first use the inverse of the restriction
isomorphism $r_{i,s}$ to move from the first local model to the blow-up of
the localized ideal, and then use $r_{j,s}$ to reach the second local model.
Both restriction maps have the blow-up of the same localized ideal as their
common source.

Z_V=\operatorname{SIm}

V^{\mathrm{gr}}\subseteq Y^{\mathrm{gr}}
\quad\text{to be the represented open subscheme }Z_V^{\mathrm{st}},
\qquad
\psi^{\mathrm{gr}}\colon V^{\mathrm{gr}}\longrightarrow U

attrs.title: Quasi-compact open on which an immersion is closed

objects.body:
A quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ is
*invertible* if it is locally free of rank one as an
$\mathcal O_X$-module. The inclusion $\mathcal I\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_X$
is part of the ideal data; regularity of a local generator is not included
in this definition.

Let $X$ be qcqs, let $q\colon Z\to X$ be proper, let $V\subseteq X$ be a
quasi-compact open, set
$U=q^{-1}(V)$, and let $T\subseteq V$ be closed. Assume $U\to V$ is an
isomorphism over an open neighbourhood of $T$. Let $E\subseteq V$ be
the complement of $\operatorname{IsoOpen}(U\to V)$ from
[def-nagata-maximal-isomorphism-open].
Apply [def-nagata-spectral-constructible-separation] to $(T,E)$ and
denote the output by $(T_c,E_c)$. Perform the explicitly constructed
$V$-admissible separation blow-up

$$
X_1=\mathsf{CSepBl}_V(T_c,E_c).
$$

Let $\overline E_c$ denote the topological closure of the underlying subset
of $E_c$ in $X_1$, and let
$X_0=X_1\setminus\overline E_c$ and let $q_0\colon Z_0\to X_0$ be the
restriction of the strict transform of $q$. Form
$X_0^{\mathrm{el}}(q_0,V\setminus E_c)$ and extend this admissible blow-up
to $X_1$ by [def-nagata-extended-admissible-blowup]. Define
$\mathsf{IsoBl}_{V,T}(q)\to X$ to be the composite of these two
$V$-admissible blow-ups, represented as one blow-up by the composition
construction.

objects.body:

attrs.title: Stage of equality for two descended morphisms

objects.body:
Let $S$ be Noetherian and let $X\to S$ be separated and of finite type.
Then $X$ is Noetherian, hence qcqs, and the finite generic-point argument
supplies the selected dense affine cover
$\mathcal U_X=(U_1,\ldots,U_n)$ from
[def-nagata-dense-affine-cover]. Define pairs $(\mathsf C_r,h_r)$
recursively along the partial unions of
[def-nagata-partial-affine-unions], where $h_r$ is an explicit proof
that $\mathsf C_r$ is a compactification of $X_r\to S$. Since
$X_0=\emptyset$, the morphism $X_0\to S$ is proper, so set

$$
(\mathsf C_0,h_0)
=\bigl(\emptyset\hookrightarrow\emptyset\to S,
\text{the witness that a proper morphism compactifies itself}\bigr).
$$

Given $(\mathsf C_{r-1},h_{r-1})$, the next stage is $X_r=X_{r-1}\cup U_r$.
If $r>n$ there is nothing to add and $X_r=X_{r-1}$. If $r=1$ then
$X_1=U_1$ is affine and
[prop-nagata-affine-compactification] supplies $(\mathsf C_1,h_1)$.
Otherwise apply [thm-nagata-two-open] to the open cover
$X_r=X_{r-1}\cup U_r$, using $h_{r-1}$, the affine compactification witness
for $U_r$ from [prop-nagata-affine-compactification], and the dense
overlap from [lemma-nagata-partial-union-overlap-dense]. Choose the
resulting candidate and its compactification proof as
$(\mathsf C_r,h_r)$, and finally define

$$
\mathsf C_{\mathrm{Noeth}}(X/S)=\mathsf C_n,
\qquad h_{\mathrm{Noeth}}=h_n.
$$

The recursive datum is therefore a dependent finite sequence of pairs, not
an unproved sequence of candidates. At every stage also record that
$X_r\to S$ is separated and of finite type, as follows by restricting the
corresponding properties of $X\to S$ to the open $X_r\subseteq X$; these
are the hypotheses used at the next application of the two-open theorem.

A *Noetherian approximation* of a scheme $S$ consists of a cofiltered
index category $I_S$, a diagram $\lambda\mapsto S_\lambda$ of schemes of
finite type over $\mathbf Z$ whose transition morphisms
$t_{\mu\lambda}\colon S_\mu\to S_\lambda$ are affine, together with a limit
cone over that diagram with vertex $S$, so that

$$
S=\varprojlim_{\lambda\in I_S}S_\lambda .
$$

We write $\mathsf N(S)=(I_S,(S_\lambda)_\lambda, (t_{\mu\lambda})_{\lambda\leq\mu})$ for such a system. Each stage
$S_\lambda$ is then a Noetherian scheme, by the Hilbert basis theorem. The
construction of the following subsection produces such a system for every
quasi-compact quasi-separated $S$, by gluing the affine case
([lemma-nagata-noetherian-inverse-system-affine]) over a finite affine
cover.

**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the finite-presentation and
Noetherian descent is done in one step by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_isPullback_of_finitePresentation_of_isSeparated`
and `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.nonempty_noetherianApproximation`, so
this stage-by-stage bookkeeping is never carried out.

Define $S_{\lambda_{\mathrm{glue}}}$ to be the scheme obtained by gluing
$\mathsf G_{S,\lambda_{\mathrm{glue}}}$. More generally, for every finite
refinement $\lambda$ of the coefficient system satisfying the same finite
equations, define $S_\lambda$ by gluing the corresponding datum.

For $0\leq r\leq n$, define

$$
X_r=U_1\cup\cdots\cup U_r,
$$

so that $X_0=\emptyset$ and $X_n=X$.

attrs.title: Partial unions of the selected affine cover

objects.body:
Let $R$ be a ring, let $M$ be an $R$-module, and let $a\in R$. Define

$$
\Gamma_{(a)}(M)
=\{m\in M\mid \text{there is }n\geq0\text{ with }a^nm=0\}.
$$

Let $\mathcal I$ be a finite type quasi-coherent ideal on a qcqs scheme
$X$, let $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal I^n$, let
$X'=\operatorname{Proj}_X(\mathcal A)$, and let
$Z'\hookrightarrow X'$ be of finite presentation. Select, by classical
choice from the nonempty witness type supplied by
[lemma-nagata-proj-closed-center-finite-degree-exists], a pair
$(d,\mathcal F)$. No property of the selected pair is built into this
definition. Denote it by
$\mathsf{FD}(Z')=(d(Z'),\mathcal F(Z'))$.

## Properties of the finite-degree center data

The selected integer $d(Z')$ is positive, $\mathcal F(Z')$ is a finite
type submodule of $\mathcal I^{d(Z')}$, and

$$
Z'=\operatorname{Proj}_X
\bigl(\mathcal A/\mathcal F(Z')\mathcal A\bigr).
$$

Moreover the support of
$\mathcal I^{d(Z')}/\mathcal F(Z')$ lies over the underlying topological
image $b(|Z'|)$ together with the first center.

*Proof.*
These are the properties required of the witness selected in
[def-nagata-proj-closed-center-finite-degree]; existence of such a
witness is
[lemma-nagata-proj-closed-center-finite-degree-exists].

attrs.title: Finite-degree data attached to a closed center in Proj

objects.body:
Let $n$ be a finite index set and $S$ a scheme. Put

$$
\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}
=\operatorname{Proj}\bigl(\mathbf Z[T_i:i\in n]\bigr),
\qquad
\mathbf P(n;S)
=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z},
$$

where the polynomial ring carries its total-degree grading, and take for the
structural morphism $\mathbf P(n;S)\to S$ the first projection. Here $n$
indexes the *homogeneous* coordinates, so the classical
$\mathbf P^r_S$ is $\mathbf P(\{0,\dots,r\};S)$.

This is the same scheme over $S$ as
[def-nagata-relative-projective-space], but obtained without any
gluing, so it does not come with the standard-chart interface required
there; only the properties of $\mathbf P(n;S)$ as a scheme over $S$ are
available from it. In particular it gives no way to construct morphisms
*into* $\mathbf P(n;S)$; the route does not need such morphisms.

attrs.title: Projective space over a base scheme, by base change

objects.body:
Let $W\subseteq Y$ be a quasi-compact open in a qcqs scheme. Choose one
witness supplied by
[lemma-nagata-qc-open-complement-ideal-exists] and define
$\mathcal I_Y(W)$ to be its ideal component. Finiteness, quasi-coherence,
and the vanishing-set identity are specification fields, not additional
assertions in this definition.

attrs.title: Finite-type ideal attached to a quasi-compact open

objects.body:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the finite-presentation and
Noetherian descent is done in one step by

and `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.nonempty_noetherianApproximation`, so

Fix $\lambda_0$, assume $Y_{\lambda_0}$ is qcqs, and put
$Y=S\times_{S_{\lambda_0}}Y_{\lambda_0}$, and let $W\subseteq Y$ be a
quasi-compact open. Select finitely many affine opens of
$Y_{\lambda_0}$ meeting the image of $W$. On their inverse limits, write
$W$ as a finite union of basic opens $D(f_{ak})$. Choose finite-stage
lifts $f_{ak,\lambda_{ak}}$ and define

$$
\lambda_W=u(\{\lambda_0\}\cup\{\lambda_{ak}\}_{a,k}),
\qquad
W_{\lambda_W}=\bigcup_{a,k}D(f_{ak,\lambda_W})
\subseteq Y_{\lambda_W}.
$$

Quasi-compactness supplies a finite affine cover; on each chart the inverse
limit identifies the coordinate ring with the filtered colimit, so the open
has a finite basic-open presentation. Record those functions and lifts in
the witness before taking the common upper bound.

quasi-compact opens whose inverse images in $Y$ agree. On a finite affine

and its finitely many coefficients. Define

attrs.title: Affine-space immersion attached to a quasi-affine scheme

objects.body:
A morphism of schemes $p\colon Y\to X$ is *quasi-affine* if for every
affine open $X'\subseteq X$ the open subscheme $p^{-1}(X')\subseteq Y$ is a
quasi-affine scheme.

Let $A$ be a ring and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal. The Rees algebra is

$$
\mathcal R_A(I)=\bigoplus_{n\geq 0}I^nt^n\subseteq A[t].
$$

Its underlying ring is the subring of $A[t]$ consisting of polynomials whose
coefficient of $t^n$ belongs to $I^n$.

*Implementation note.* The current Mathlib object is the subalgebra
`reesAlgebra I` of the polynomial ring. The declarations
`mem_reesAlgebra_iff`, `reesAlgebra.monomial_mem`,
`adjoin_monomial_eq_reesAlgebra`, and
`reesAlgebra.fg` provide the membership and finite-generation facts
used below. The grading and the pieces in the next blocks are blueprint
data and must be defined explicitly.

Define

$$
\rho_s\colon A_s\otimes_A\mathcal R_A(I)
\longrightarrow\mathcal R_{A_s}(IA_s)
$$

degreewise by sending a coefficient $x\in I^n$ to $x/1\in(IA_s)^n$.

For $n\in\mathbb N$, let $\mathcal R_A(I)_n$ be the $A$-submodule of Rees
elements whose underlying polynomial is supported in degree $n$.

attrs.title: Homogeneous piece of the Rees algebra

objects.body:
For a scheme $S$ and $n\in\mathbb N$, define

$$
\mathbb A^n_S=\operatorname{Spec}_S
\bigl(\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_S}(\mathcal O_S^{\oplus n})\bigr).
$$

Concretely, on an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ of $S$ this is
$\operatorname{Spec}(R[T_1,\ldots,T_n])$; for a principal restriction
$D(a)\subseteq V$ the transition map is induced by
$R[T_1,\ldots,T_n]\to R_a[T_1,\ldots,T_n]$.

and `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.nonempty_noetherianApproximation`, so
this stage-by-stage bookkeeping is never carried out.

Let $S$ be qcqs and let $X\to S$ be of finite presentation. Select a
finite affine cover of
$S$, finite affine covers of its inverse images in $X$, finite
presentations of all chart algebras over the base chart algebras, finite
basic-open presentations of the overlaps, and the two directions of every
overlap isomorphism. Record these data and their finite identity, inverse,
and cocycle equations as $\mathsf R_X$.
Quasi-compactness gives finite affine covers and quasi-separatedness makes
overlaps quasi-compact. Finite presentation supplies finite generators and
relations; record both overlap directions and the finite identity and
cocycle equations as $\mathsf R_X$.

Descend every chart algebra in $\mathsf R_X$ using
[lemma-nagata-affine-fp-descends], every quasi-compact overlap open
using [lemma-nagata-qc-open-descends], and both directions of every
overlap isomorphism using [lemma-nagata-morphism-descends]. Define
$\lambda_{\mathrm{raw}}(X/S)$ to be the selected
upper bound of their finitely many stages, and denote the resulting raw
datum over $S_{\lambda_{\mathrm{raw}}}$ by
$\mathsf R_{X,\lambda_{\mathrm{raw}}}^{\mathrm{raw}}$.
Each object is transported by the canonical base-change map to the selected
upper bound. Functoriality supplies the comparison maps and coherence, so
the raw datum is well typed.

For the raw datum, form the finite list of required equalities of overlap
opens, inverse identities, and triple-overlap cocycles. Attach to each the

$\lambda_{\mathrm{rel}}(X/S)$ to be their common upper bound together with

$\mathsf R_{X,\lambda_{\mathrm{rel}}}$ be the raw datum transported to this
stage.
Canonical comparison maps identify the source and target of each later-stage
equality. Transporting its witness preserves the equation, so the finite
upper-bound list is well typed.

objects.body:

Let $X$ be a scheme and
$\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal A_n$ a quasi-coherent graded
$\mathcal O_X$-algebra. On every affine open $V\subseteq X$, form

$$
\operatorname{Proj}(\Gamma(V,\mathcal A)).
$$

Quasi-coherence identifies the graded algebra on a basic affine restriction
with coefficientwise localization. The intended relative Proj is the scheme
obtained by gluing these affine Proj schemes along the induced standard-chart
equivalences, with structural map to $X$ glued from the degree-zero maps.
The construction includes the chosen affine cover, all overlap
isomorphisms, their cocycle equalities, and the resulting universal
restriction isomorphisms.

$$
\mathbf P^r_X
=\operatorname{Proj}_X
\bigl(\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal O_X^{r+1})\bigr),
$$

with the symmetric-algebra generators placed in degree one. Its standard
opens are required to be the relative affine schemes of the degree-zero
homogeneous localizations at those generators. The existence and
compatibility of this object are supplied by
[lemma-nagata-relative-proj-exists].

This node is not formalized: it presupposes relative Proj, which is not
formalized either. Everything that needs only the scheme
$\mathbf P^r_X\to X$, and not its standard charts, uses
[def-nagata-projective-space-base-change] instead.

and `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.nonempty_noetherianApproximation`, so

Let $X\to S$ be a morphism and choose the inverse systems
$\mathsf N(X)$ and $\mathsf N(S)$ together with their comparison maps to
$X$ and $S$. A finite-stage datum for this morphism consists of indices
$\lambda_X$ and $\lambda_S$, a morphism
$\varphi_{\lambda_X,\lambda_S}\colon X_{\lambda_X}\to S_{\lambda_S}$,
and an equality after composing with the two limit projections: the map
$X\to S\to S_{\lambda_S}$ equals
$X\to X_{\lambda_X}\to S_{\lambda_S}$. The datum also records the finite
affine charts and generator-and-relation lists used to construct
$\varphi_{\lambda_X,\lambda_S}$. Finally it records a finite affine cover
of $X$, compatible opens in
$X_{\lambda_X}\times_{S_{\lambda_S}}S$, and chartwise surjections of
coordinate rings showing that the induced comparison
$X\to X_{\lambda_X}\times_{S_{\lambda_S}}S$ is an immersion; all overlap
equalities are included in the datum.

Suppose $g$ is supplied with a factorization
$T\xrightarrow{h}Z\xrightarrow{z}Y$, where $z$ is a closed immersion.
Define

$$
c_{g,Z}\colon\operatorname{SIm}(g)\longrightarrow Z
$$

from the containment of the ideal defining $Z$ in the kernel ideal defining
$\operatorname{SIm}(g)$.

attrs.title: Comparison map for a closed factorization

objects.body:

g^{\mathrm{im}}\colon T\longrightarrow\operatorname{SIm}(g)
$$

to be `Scheme.Hom.toImage g`. Its factorization equality is the

attrs.title: Canonical factor through a scheme-theoretic image

objects.body:
Let $a\colon T\to Y$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated immersion.
Define the scheme-theoretic closure of $T$ in $Y$ to be the closed
subscheme $\operatorname{SIm}(a)\hookrightarrow Y$.

Let $g\colon T\to Y$ be a morphism. Define
$\operatorname{SIm}(g)$ to mean the Mathlib scheme-theoretic image
`Scheme.Hom.image g`, with inclusion $g_{\mathrm{im}}$ and factor map
$g^{\mathrm{im}}$ supplied by
[lemma-nagata-scheme-image-ideal-qc]. Whenever a later argument needs
quasi-compactness, it must state that hypothesis explicitly.

## Detailed form

For a morphism $u:W\to X$ of schemes, the *scheme-theoretic image* of $u$ is
the largest closed subscheme $X'$ of $X$ through which $u$ factors, i.e. the
closed subscheme defined by $\ker(\mathcal O_X\to u_*\mathcal O_W)$. A
subscheme $W\subseteq X$ is *scheme-theoretically dense* if its
scheme-theoretic image in $X$ is $X$ itself. The scheme-theoretic closure of a
locally closed subscheme is the scheme-theoretic image of its immersion.

**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: scheme-theoretic density is
the predicate `AlgebraicGeometry.IsSchemeTheoreticallyDominant`,
which [def-nagata-dense-compactification] uses directly.

For a quasi-compact open immersion $j\colon U\hookrightarrow X$, say that
$U$ is scheme-theoretically dense in $X$ if the sheaf morphism

$$
\mathcal O_X\longrightarrow j_*\mathcal O_U
$$

is injective. This predicate is independent of whether the ambient scheme
is presented as part of a compactification.

Under the hypotheses of
[lemma-nagata-separate-closed-data-exists], choose its center
$C\hookrightarrow Z$. Compose it with the finite-presentation closed
immersion $Z\hookrightarrow X$, and define
$\mathsf{SepBl}_U(Z_1,Z_2)\to X$ to be the blow-up of $X$ along the
resulting center $C\hookrightarrow Z\hookrightarrow X$.

Let $X$ be qcqs, let $U\subseteq X$ be a quasi-compact open, and let
$T_1,T_2\subseteq U$ be disjoint constructible subsets closed in $U$.
Define

$$
\mathcal J_i=\mathcal J_U(T_i),\qquad
\mathcal I_i=\operatorname{Ext}_{X,U}(\mathcal J_i),\qquad
Z_i=V(\mathcal I_i),
$$

and set

$$
\mathsf{CSepBl}_U(T_1,T_2)
=\mathsf{SepBl}_U(Z_1,Z_2).
$$

**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the finite-presentation and
Noetherian descent is done in one step by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_isPullback_of_finitePresentation_of_isSeparated`
and `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.nonempty_noetherianApproximation`, so
this stage-by-stage bookkeeping is never carried out.

Let $X\to S$ be separated and of finite presentation, and start from its
constructed finite-stage model
$X^{\mathrm{desc}}_{\lambda_{\mathrm{rel}}}\to S_{\lambda_{\mathrm{rel}}}$. Choose one witness from
[lemma-nagata-separated-descent-stage-exists] and define
$\lambda_{\mathrm{sep}}(X/S)$ and
$X^{\mathrm{sep}}_{\lambda_{\mathrm{sep}}(X/S)}$ to be the index and model
recorded by that witness. The eventual separatedness and comparison
properties are stated separately below.

objects.body:

Let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf. Define
its sheaf Rees algebra by

$$
\mathcal R_X(\mathcal I)=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal I^n,
$$

with multiplication induced by the canonical multiplication maps
$\mathcal I^m\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal I^n\to \mathcal I^{m+n}$ and unit the degree-zero copy of $\mathcal O_X$.
The direct sum is taken in sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules. Define
multiplication on homogeneous summands by the displayed maps and extend it
by the universal property of the direct sum; the degree-zero inclusion is
the unit. Associativity and the unit laws are exactly
[lemma-nagata-sheaf-ideal-powers-assoc], so this is a graded
quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-algebra. The multiplication maps need not be
injective, and no such hypothesis is used.

attrs.title: Map to the blow-up chart of the extended ideal

objects.body:
Let $Z\to X$ be a morphism and let $X'\to X$ be the blow-up of a
finite-presentation center $C\subseteq X$. Put $U=X\setminus C$; then
$U\hookrightarrow X$ is quasi-compact. The *strict transform* of $Z$
is the scheme-theoretic closure of

$$
(Z\times_XU)\times_U(X'\times_XU)
$$

in $Z\times_XX'$, in the sense of
[def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-closure]. It is not enough to use only
the topological closure.

**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the strict transform is
supplied by the API of
`WeilConjectures/Compactification/StrictTransform.lean` —
`AlgebraicGeometry.strictTransform`, its closed immersion
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.isClosedImmersion_pullbackLift_blowup_comap`,
