`AlgebraicGeometry.isPullback_strictTransformOpen` — so the
strict-transform chart rings and their cocycle are never assembled by hand.

Let $A\to B$ be a ring map, let $I\subseteq A$, and let $a\in I$.
Define

$$
C_a(A,B,I)=B\otimes_A A[I/a].
$$

We regard $a$ as an element of $C_a(A,B,I)$ through the structural map
$A\to C_a(A,B,I)$.

Let $f\colon Y\to X$, let $\mathcal I$ be a quasi-coherent ideal on $X$,
and put $X'=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$. The pullback of
$\mathcal I$ to $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y}(Y)$ is the
invertible exceptional ideal of $\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y$, so the universal
property of the blow-up ([thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property],
Stacks Tag 0806) provides a unique lift
$\rho\colon\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y}(Y)\to X'$ of the
composite to $X$. Define the *comparison morphism*

$$
\psi_{f,\mathcal I}\colon
\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y}(Y)\longrightarrow
Y\times_XX'
$$

with components the structure morphism of
$\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y}(Y)$ and the lift $\rho$.
The morphism $\psi_{f,\mathcal I}$ is a closed immersion: this is
Zariski-local on $Y\times_XX'$, and over an affine open
$V=\operatorname{Spec}(B)\subseteq Y$ lying over an affine open
$\operatorname{Spec}(A)\subseteq X$ and a standard chart of $X'$ at
$a\in I$, it is the $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the canonical ring map
$B\otimes_AA[I/a]\to B[IB/\varphi(a)]$, which is surjective because a
fraction $y/\varphi(a)^n$ with $y\in I^nB$ is a $B$-linear combination of
fractions $\varphi(z)/\varphi(a)^n$ with $z\in I^n$.

ideal, and put $X'=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$. Choose an affine
cover $V_i=\operatorname{Spec}(A_i)$ of $X$, finite generating sets for
$\mathcal I|_{V_i}$, and affine covers
$W_{ij}=\operatorname{Spec}(B_{ij})$ of $f^{-1}(V_i)$. Define
$Y^{\mathrm{st}}_{\mathrm{chart}}$ by gluing the affine schemes
$\operatorname{Spec}(C_{i,j,a}^{\mathrm{st}})$ and their quotient closed
immersions into the corresponding affine pieces of $Y\times_XX'$.
On an overlap, refine to basic opens in the chosen $W_{ij}$ and in the
blow-up chart. The transition maps are the localizations of
[lemma-nagata-strict-transform-chart-localization-data]; they preserve
the quotient ideals and satisfy the double- and triple-overlap identities.
These maps, together with the affine closed immersions, are the specified
scheme-glue datum. No affineness of an unchosen fibre product is used.

attrs.title: Closed chart model of the global strict transform

objects.body:
For $\{i,j\}=\{1,2\}$, define

$$
Z_i=(U\setminus U_j)_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow U_i,
\qquad
Z_{i,k}=V_i\times_U Z_k\hookrightarrow V_i
\quad(k=1,2).
$$

Thus $Z_i$ is the canonical reduced closed subscheme on the indicated
complement, and $Z_{i,k}$ carries the scheme-theoretic inverse-image
structure rather than only its underlying closed set.

Define $\mathsf C_{12}(U/S)$ to be the constructed factorization

$$
U\xrightarrow{j_W}W\longrightarrow S.
$$

Define

$$
V_{12}=V_1\times_UV_2.
$$

The separatedness of $U\to S$ gives a closed immersion
$V_{12}\to V_1\times_SV_2$, hence an immersion
$V_{12}\to X_1\times_SX_2$. Define

$$
X_{12}=\operatorname{SIm}
\bigl(V_{12}\longrightarrow X_1\times_SX_2\bigr)
$$

and let $p_i\colon X_{12}\to X_i$ be the restrictions of the two product
projections.

Let $C_i^0$ be the compactification selected by classical choice from the
nonempty type witnessing compactifiability of $U_i\to S$. Define

$$
C_i=\mathsf{Dense}(C_i^0)
=\bigl(U_i\hookrightarrow X_i\longrightarrow S\bigr).
$$

attrs.title: Chosen dense compactifications of the two opens

objects.body:
Apply the common-modification construction to the two open immersions
$U\hookrightarrow W_1$ and $U\hookrightarrow W_2$. Denote its output by

$$
W'_i\longrightarrow W_i,
\qquad
W=\mathsf{CM}(W_1,W_2;U),
$$

with the two constructed open immersions $W'_i\hookrightarrow W$ and their
common open subscheme $U$.

*Implementation note.* There is no separate Lean declaration for this
construction. The proof of `AlgebraicGeometry.HasCompactification.of_two_open_cover`
([thm-nagata-two-open]) obtains it inline, as
`obtain ⟨cm⟩ := nonempty_commonModification ...` applied to the two intermediate
schemes; its type is the structure `AlgebraicGeometry.CommonModification` of
[def-nagata-common-modification].

attrs.title: Final common modification for the two-open construction

objects.body:
Apply the graph-extension construction to
$U_i\subseteq U$ and $C_i$. Denote its output by

$$
X_i^{\mathrm{gr}}\longrightarrow X_i,\qquad
U_i\subseteq V_i\subseteq X_i^{\mathrm{gr}},\qquad
\psi_i\colon V_i\longrightarrow U.
$$

From now on replace $X_i$ by $X_i^{\mathrm{gr}}$ and retain the notation
$X_i$ for the resulting proper ambient scheme.

For $\{i,j\}=\{1,2\}$, define

$$
X_i^\circ=X_i\setminus\overline Z_{i,j}
$$

and glue the open subschemes $U_i\subseteq U$ and
$U_i\subseteq X_i^\circ$ by the identity. Denote the result by

$$
W_i=U\amalg_{U_i}X_i^\circ.
$$

The construction includes the two open immersions
$U\hookrightarrow W_i$ and $X_i^\circ\hookrightarrow W_i$ and the induced
structural map $W_i\to S$.

For $\{i,j\}=\{1,2\}$, define

$$
X_i^{\mathrm{prep}}
=\mathsf{CSepBl}_{V_i}(Z_{i,i},Z_{i,j})
$$

and transport $V_i$, $U_i$, and $\psi_i$ along the chosen isomorphism over
$V_i$. Replace $X_i$ by $X_i^{\mathrm{prep}}$ and let
$\overline Z_{i,k}$ denote the closure of the transported $Z_{i,k}$ in the
new $X_i$.

attrs.title: Prepared ambient schemes with separated boundary closures

objects.body:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes and let $T$ be a scheme over
$S$. The *base change* is

$$
X_T:=X\times_ST,\qquad
\mathrm{pr}_T:X_T\longrightarrow T,\qquad
f_T:X_T\longrightarrow X,
$$

with the projections; for $g:T'\to T$ the *base change of a
module* $\mathcal{F}$ on $X_T$ is $\mathcal{F}_{T'}=g_X^*\mathcal{F}$ where
$g_X:X_{T'}\to X_T$. For a point $t\in T$ the *fibre*
$X_t=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(t))$ and the *geometric fibre* $X_{\bar t}$ are as in
Definition def:weil-pbc-scheme-conventions.
If $f$ has a section $\sigma:S\to X$ and $T$ is over $S$, then
$\sigma_T:=(\mathrm{id}_T\times\sigma):T\to X_T$ is the induced section.

Let $F:(\mathit{Sch})^{\mathrm{op}}\to\textit{Sets}$ be a functor and
let $(H_i)_{i\in I}$ be a family of
subfunctors of $F$. The family
*covers* $F$ if for every $\xi\in F(T)$ there is an open covering
$T=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ with $\xi|_{U_i}\in H_i(U_i)$ (Schemes,
Definition 26.15.3, Tag
[01JI](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01JI)).

Let $k$ be a field. A *variety over $k$* is a scheme $X$ over $k$
which is integral and whose structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ is
separated and of finite type
(Varieties, Definition 33.3.1, Tag
[020D](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/020D)). A
*curve over $k$* is a scheme over $k$ which is a variety of
dimension $1$ ([def-pc-dimension]; Varieties, Definition 33.43.1,
Tag [0A23](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A23)).
*Terminology.* This is the curve notion of the Stacks
Project (integral variety of dimension one over an arbitrary base
field), and it differs from the smooth-curve convention of
the curve-calculation chapter ([def-sc-curves]: a separated
scheme of finite type of dimension at most one over an
*algebraically closed* field);

Let $k$ be a field, $X$ a proper scheme over $k$ and $\mathcal{L}$ an
invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module. The
*degree* of $\mathcal{L}$ is

$$
\deg(\mathcal{L}):=\chi(X,\mathcal{L})-\chi(X,\mathcal{O}_X)\in\Z
$$

(Varieties, Definition 33.44.1, Tag
[0AYR](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AYR)). For an
effective Cartier divisor $D$ on $X$ the degree of $D$ is
$\deg(D):=\deg(\mathcal{O}_X(D))$.

attrs.title: The degree of an invertible module

objects.body:
Let $X$ be a scheme. Apply the
derived-category construction
to the abelian category of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules; denote
the result by $D(\mathcal O_X)$. The category
$D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ is the full subcategory consisting
of objects whose cohomology sheaves are quasi-coherent.

Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes. The *derived direct
image* is the total derived functor
$Rf_*:D(\mathcal{O}_X)\to D(\mathcal{O}_S)$; its cohomology sheaves
$H^i(Rf_*E)=R^if_*E$ are the *higher direct images*. (The
definition via injective resolutions (or the $K$-injective resolution
criterion of file 02, the standard $K$-injective-resolution criterion) is the
standard one; the relevant admissibility statements are in Derived
Categories of Schemes, Section 36.30, Tag
[0A1G](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A1G).)

For a morphism $g:T\to S$ of schemes,
let $Lg^*:D(\mathcal O_S)\to D(\mathcal O_T)$ be the left derived
functor of module pullback. Explicitly it is

$$
Lg^*E=\mathcal O_T\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{g^{-1}\mathcal O_S}g^{-1}E.
$$

The derived tensor product
is computed by a K-flat resolution.

attrs.title: Derived pullback of modules on schemes

objects.body:
The *dimension* $\dim X$ of a nonempty scheme $X$ is the supremum
of the Krull dimensions of the local rings of $X$, and the
*relative dimension* of a morphism $f:X\to S$ of finite type at a
point $s\in S$ is $\dim X_s$ (the dimension of the fibre); $f$ is
*of relative dimension $d$* if all nonempty fibres have dimension
$d$.

Let $S$ be a scheme and let $D\subset S$ be an
effective Cartier divisor
with ideal sheaf $\mathcal{I}_D$. The *associated invertible module* is

$$
\mathcal{O}_S(D):=\mathcal{H}om_{\mathcal{O}_S}(\mathcal{I}_D,\mathcal{O}_S)=\mathcal{I}_D^\vee .
$$

attrs.title: The module $\mathcal{O}_X(D)$ of an effective Cartier divisor

objects.body:
Let $k$ be a field, $X$ a proper scheme over $k$ and $\mathcal{F}$ a coherent
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module. The *Euler characteristic* of $\mathcal{F}$ is

$$
\chi(X,\mathcal{F}):=\sum_i(-1)^i\dim_kH^i(X,\mathcal{F})\in\Z ,
$$

where $H^i(X,\mathcal{F})$ are the
higher direct images of
$\mathcal{F}$ for the structure morphism.

Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category (for a scheme $X$: the category
of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules, or any abelian subcategory of it closed under the
operations below) and let $F,G$ be objects of $\mathcal A$ and
$i\ge0$. The *$i$-th Ext group* is

$$
\operatorname{Ext}^{i}_{\mathcal A}(F,G)
\;:=\;\Hom_{D(\mathcal A)}\bigl(F,\;G[i]\bigr),
$$

the group of morphisms from $F$ to the $i$-fold shift of $G$ in the
derived category ([def-pc-derived-category]); equivalently
(i.e. by the standard identification of the two descriptions, the
classical one via an injective resolution of $G$) it is the $i$-th
cohomology of the derived $\mathbf R\Hom(F,G)$. For sheaves on a
scheme $X$ one writes $\operatorname{Ext}^{i}_{\mathcal{O}_X}(-,-)$ (or
$\operatorname{Ext}^{i}_X(-,-)$) for the case
$\mathcal A$ the category of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules, and

$$
\mathcal{E}xt^{i}_{\mathcal{O}_X}(F,G):=H^i\mathcal{H}om^{\bullet}_{\mathcal{O}_X}(F,G)
$$

denotes the associated sheaf ($\mathcal{H}om^{\bullet}$ the derived
inner hom of sheaves).

Let $k$ be a field, $X$ a scheme over $k$ and $\sigma\in X(k)$. For a
scheme $T$ over $k$, let $F(T)\subseteq\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}(T)$ be the
subset of those $\mathcal{L}$ such that $Rf_{T,*}\mathcal{L}$ ($f_T:X_T\to T$,
$Rf_{T,*}$ as in [def-pc-derived-direct-image]) is an object of
$D(\mathcal{O}_T)$ isomorphic to an
invertible
$\mathcal{O}_T$-module placed in degree $0$; this is the subfunctor $F$ of
Stacks Project, Picard Schemes of Curves, Lemma 44.6.2 (the fact that it
is a subfunctor, and the open-immersion property, are
recorded with the other properties of this construction).

Let $K/k$ be a field extension. It is *finite* if $[K:k]<\infty$,
*algebraic* if every element of $K$ is algebraic over $k$,
*finite separable* if it is finite and every element has a separable
minimal polynomial over $k$, and *purely inseparable* if every
element $\alpha\in K$ satisfies $\alpha^{p^n}\in k$ for some $n$ (in
characteristic $0$ this means $K=k$). An *algebraic closure*
$\bar k$ of $k$ is an algebraically closed extension of $k$ which is
algebraic over $k$.

Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Then $f$ is *finite locally
free* if $f$ is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation. For an
integer $d\geq0$, $f$ is *finite locally free of degree $d$* if it is
finite locally free and for every $s\in S$ the fibre
$X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ (a finite set of points)
satisfies

$$
\dim_{\kappa(s)}\Gamma(X_s,\mathcal{O}_{X_s})=d .
$$

Let $S$ be a scheme and $\mathit{Sch}_{fppf}$ a big fppf site containing
$S$ (Topologies, Definition 34.7.8, Tag
[021S](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/021S)). The
*big fppf site of $S$* is $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$, whose coverings
are the families $\{T_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ of
flat morphisms locally of finite
presentation; an *fppf covering* is such a family.

Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be a
smooth projective curve over
$k$ which is geometrically
irreducible. The *genus* of $X$ is

$$
g(X):=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal{O}_X)\in\Z_{\geq0}
$$

(Stacks Project, Picard Schemes of Curves, Definition 44.6.3, Tag
[0B9W](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B9W)).

Let $k$ be a field and $X$ a scheme over $k$. $X$ is
*geometrically irreducible* (resp. *geometrically reduced*,
*geometrically connected*, *geometrically integral*) over $k$
if $X_{k'}$ is irreducible (resp. reduced, connected, integral) for
every field extension $k'/k$, where $X_{k'}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec} k}\operatorname{Spec}(k')$
([def-pc-base-change]).

Let $X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes and $d\geq0$. For a scheme $T$
over $S$ put

$$
\operatorname{Hilb}^d_{X/S}(T):=\bigl\{Z\subset X_T\ \text{a closed subscheme}:\
Z\to T\text{ is finite locally free of degree }d\bigr\},
$$

where ``finite locally free of degree $d$'' is
Definition [def-pc-finite-locally-free] and $X_T$ is the base change of
[def-pc-base-change]. If this functor is representable
([def-pc-representable-functor]), the representing scheme is
$\underline{\operatorname{Hilb}}^d_{X/S}$ (Stacks Project, Picard Schemes of Curves,
Chapter 44, Section 44.2, Tag
[0B94](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B94)).

Let $X$ be a scheme. An object $M\in D(\mathcal{O}_X)$ is an
*invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module placed in degree $0$* if $M\cong\mathcal{N}[0]$
for an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{N}$: $M$ is quasi-isomorphic to the
complex $\mathcal{N}$ concentrated in degree $0$. It is a
*finite locally free rank $r$ module placed in degree $i$* if
$M\cong E[-i]$ with $E$ finite locally free of rank $r$
([def-pc-finite-locally-free]). The structure of the cohomology of
$M$ in this situation is [lem-pc-degree-zero-properties].

Let $S$ be a standard graded
$k$-algebra, and let $l_0,l_1\in S_1$ satisfy
$D_+(l_0)\cup D_+(l_1)=\operatorname{Proj}(S)$.
The morphism $\pi_{l_0,l_1}:\operatorname{Proj}(S)\to \hyperref[def-sc-p1-standard]{\mathbf P^1_k}$
is obtained on $D_+(l_0)$ from the ring map
$k[t]\to S_{(l_0)}$, $t\mapsto l_1/l_0$, and on $D_+(l_1)$ from
$k[t^{-1}]\to S_{(l_1)}$, $t^{-1}\mapsto l_0/l_1$.

attrs.title: The morphism determined by two linear forms

objects.body:
All morphism-theoretic notions used below are the ones already introduced
in file 02: *quasi-compact*, *quasi-separated*,
*separated*, *locally of finite type* and *of finite
type*, *locally of finite presentation* and *of finite
presentation*, *surjective*, *open immersion*,
*closed immersion*, *immersion*, *universally closed*,
*proper*, *finite*, *integral*, *flat*,
*unramified*, *etale*, *geometric fibre* and
*geometric point* (see
Definition [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]).
One further notion is fixed here: *projective*
([def-pc-projective-morphism]).

Let $F:(\mathit{Sch})^{\mathrm{op}}\to\textit{Sets}$ be a functor and
$H\subseteq F$ a subfunctor. $H\subseteq F$ is *representable by open immersions* if for all pairs
$(T,\xi)$ with $T$ a scheme and $\xi\in F(T)$ there is an open
subscheme $U_\xi\subseteq T$ such that a morphism $f:T'\to T$ factors
through $U_\xi$ if and only if $f^*\xi\in H(T')$ (Schemes,
Definition 26.15.3, Tag
[01JI](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01JI)).

Let $X$ be a scheme and $E\in D(\mathcal{O}_X)$. $E$ is *perfect* if it is
locally (on an affine open cover of $X$) isomorphic to a bounded complex
of finite projective modules (Derived Categories of Schemes,
Section 36.31, Tag
[0BDH](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BDH)); the subcategory
is $D_{\mathrm{perf}}(\mathcal{O}_X)$.

Let $k$ be a field, $X$ a scheme over $k$, and $\sigma\in X(k)$ a
$k$-rational point. For a scheme $T$
over $k$ put

$$
\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}(T):=\operatorname{Ker}\Bigl(\sigma_T^*:\operatorname{Pic}(X_T)
\longrightarrow\operatorname{Pic}(T)\Bigr),
$$

i.e. the set of isomorphism classes $[\mathcal L]$ for which
$\sigma_T^*\mathcal L$ is isomorphic to $\mathcal O_T$.
A trivialization is not part of an element of this kernel; when a
proof chooses one, that choice is auxiliary. Its value at
$T=\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ is computed in [lem-pc-sigma-k-points].

Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes as in
[def-pc-picard-presheaf]. The *Picard functor*
$\operatorname{Pic}_{X/S}$ is the fppf sheafification of the
Picard presheaf on
$(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ ([def-pc-fppf-site]); if it is
representable ([def-pc-representable-functor]), the representing
scheme is $\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}_{X/S}$ (Stacks Project, Picard Schemes of
Curves, Definition 44.4.1, Tag
[0B9L](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B9L)). For $S=\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ we write
$\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k}$.

Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes. The *Picard presheaf* is

$$
(\mathit{Sch}/S)^{\mathrm{op}}\longrightarrow\textit{Sets},\qquad
T\longmapsto\operatorname{Pic}(X_T),
$$

with $\operatorname{Pic}$ of [def-sc-picard-group] (in the generality of
[rem-pc-sc-modules]) and $X_T$ of [def-pc-base-change].

For a nonnegatively graded commutative ring $S$, the scheme
$\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ has as points the homogeneous prime ideals
not containing $S_+$. Its standard open
$D_+(f)=\{\mathfrak p:f\notin\mathfrak p\}$, for homogeneous $f$
of positive degree, is the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}(S_{(f)})$;
the restriction maps are the graded localization maps.
Write $V_+(I)$ for the closed set of homogeneous primes containing $I$.
Here $\mathbf P^n_k=\operatorname{Proj}(k[x_0,\ldots,x_n])$, with
each $x_i$ of degree one.

*Mathlib:* `AlgebraicGeometry.Proj`, `AlgebraicGeometry.projIsoSpec`, `ProjectiveSpectrum.basicOpen`. These are basic Mathlib notions used throughout, so they are not mapped as the Lean declarations of this object.

attrs.title: Projective spectrum and its standard opens

objects.body:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes. $f$ is *H-projective*, or
*relatively projective*, if there is a closed immersion
$i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_S$ over $S$ with $f=\pi\circ i$
($\pi:\mathbf P^n_S\to S$ the structure morphism); $f$ is
*projective* if it is H-projective and quasi-compact (Morphisms of
Schemes, Definition 29.44.1, Tag
[01W8](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01W8); the Stacks
Project's *projective* is the form ``closed subscheme of a projective
bundle $\mathbf P(\mathcal E)$ over $S$'', while H-projective is the form
``closed immersion into some $\mathbf P^n_S$'', so the convention used here
is the H-projective one together with quasi-compactness). A scheme $X$
over a field $k$ is *projective over $k$* if the structure morphism
$X\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ is projective.

For a commutative ring $A$ and $n\ge0$, put
$P=\operatorname{Proj}(A[x_0,\ldots,x_n])$, using the
projective spectrum construction. Write
$U_i=D_+(x_i)$ for its standard affine opens. For $d\in\mathbf Z$,
the invertible module
$\mathcal O_P(d)$ is obtained by gluing free rank-one modules on
the $U_i$ with bases $e_i^{(d)}$ and transition rule
$e_i^{(d)}=(x_i/x_j)^d e_j^{(d)}$;

attrs.title: Twists on projective space over a ring

objects.body:
Let $k$ be a field and $X$ a scheme over $k$. A *$k$-rational
point* of $X$ is a section $\sigma:\operatorname{Spec}(k)\to X$ of the structure
morphism; for a scheme $T$ over $k$ the induced section is
$\sigma_T:T\to X_T$ ([def-pc-base-change]).

Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes. A *relative effective
Cartier divisor on $X/S$* is an effective Cartier divisor $D\subset X$
such that $D\to S$ is flat (Divisors, Definition 31.19.2, Tag
[062T](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/062T)).

Let $F:(\mathit{Sch}/S)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\textit{Sets}$ be a functor. The
*functor of points* of a scheme $X$ over $S$ is
$h_X=\operatorname{Hom}_S(\bullet,X)$; $F$ is *representable by a
scheme* if $F\cong h_P$ for some scheme $P$ over $S$
(Schemes, Section 26.15; Categories, Lemma 4.3.5, Tag
[001P](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/001P)). A scheme
representing a functor is denoted $\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}$,
$\underline{\operatorname{Hilb}}$ etc.; uniqueness of the representing scheme is
[lem-pc-representable-unique].

A *scheme* is a locally ringed space in the sense of Stacks
Project, Schemes, Definition 26.9.1 (Tag
[01IJ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01IJ)); $\mathit{Sch}$ denotes
the category of schemes, and a *morphism of schemes* is a morphism
in $\mathit{Sch}$. A scheme is *affine* if it is isomorphic to
$\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ for a commutative ring $A$; an *open subscheme* of $X$
is a subscheme whose underlying topological space is open in $X$.

*Mathlib:* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme`, `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom`. These are basic Mathlib notions used throughout, so they are not mapped as the Lean declarations of this object.

A field $k$ is *separably closed* if every nonconstant separable
polynomial $f\in k[T]$ has a root in $k$ (equivalently, $k$ has no
nontrivial finite separable field extension; the equivalence of the two
formulations is [lem-pc-sepclosed-finite-sep-trivial]).

*Implementation note.* This is the same notion as [def-kun-separably-closed],
which carries the Lean name `IsSepClosed`. Mathlib's `IsSepClosed k` is stated in
the polynomial form used here: every separable polynomial over $k$ splits. The source
attached `\lean{IsSepClosed}` to the pointer remark
[rem-ptr-pc-separably-closed-1], a fragment left over from splitting this
definition.

Let $k$ be a field. A *smooth projective curve over $k$* is a
curve $X$ over $k$ such that $X\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ is
smooth and
projective. In Stacks Project,
Chapter 44 (Picard Schemes of Curves) the phrase *smooth projective
curve over $k$* is used in exactly this sense;

Let $k$ be a field. A standard graded $k$-algebra is a commutative
$k$-algebra with a direct-sum decomposition $S=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}S_n$
such that $S_0=k$, $S_aS_b\subseteq S_{a+b}$, and $S$ is generated
as a $k$-algebra by finitely many elements of $S_1$.
An element of $S_n$ is homogeneous of degree $n$.
An ideal $I$ is homogeneous if every homogeneous component of each
of its elements is again in $I$. The ideal
$S_+=\bigoplus_{n>0}S_n$ is called the irrelevant ideal.
For a homogeneous element $f$, write $S_{(f)}$ for the degree-zero
subring of the graded localization $S[f^{-1}]$.

Let $F:(\mathit{Sch})^{\mathrm{op}}\to\textit{Sets}$ be a functor. A
*subfunctor* $H\subseteq F$ is an assignment
$T\mapsto H(T)\subseteq F(T)$ such that the maps $F(f):F(T)\to F(T')$
send $H(T)$ into $H(T')$ for all morphisms $f:T'\to T$ (Schemes,
Definition 26.15.3, Tag
[01JI](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01JI)).

Let $F:(\mathit{Sch})^{\mathrm{op}}\to\textit{Sets}$ be a functor. $F$
*satisfies the sheaf property for the Zariski topology* if for every
scheme $T$, every open covering $T=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ and every
collection $\xi_i\in F(U_i)$ with
$\xi_i|_{U_i\cap U_j}=\xi_j|_{U_i\cap U_j}$ there is a unique
$\xi\in F(T)$ with $\xi|_{U_i}=\xi_i$ (Schemes, Definition 26.15.3, Tag
[01JI](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01JI)).

attrs.title: Zariski sheaf property of a functor

objects.body:
Let $X$ be a scheme, $\mathcal{M}$ an
invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module and
$s\in H^0(X,\mathcal{M})$. The *zero scheme* $Z(s)\subseteq X$ of $s$ is
the closed subscheme defined by the ideal sheaf

$$
\mathcal{I}_{Z(s)}:=\operatorname{im}\Bigl(s^\vee:\mathcal{M}^\vee
\;\longrightarrow\;\mathcal{O}_X\Bigr).
$$

Its basic properties (well-definedness, local form
$\operatorname{Spec}(A/(a))$, compatibility with flat base change, $Z(s)=X \Leftrightarrow s=0$) are [lem-pc-zero-scheme-properties].

attrs.title: The zero scheme of a section

objects.body:
Let $k$ be a field. The *constant sheaf* $\underline{\Z}$ on the fppf
site $(\mathit{Sch}/k)_{fppf}$ of [def-pc-fppf-site] is the sheaf
associated with the constant presheaf $T\mapsto\Z$; its value on $T$ is the
group of locally constant functions $T\to\Z$.

Let now $C$ be a smooth projective
curve over $k$ which is
geometrically integral and let
$\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}$ be the
Picard functor. The *degree morphism*

$$
\deg:\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\longrightarrow\underline{\Z}
$$

is the morphism of fppf sheaves defined as follows: for $T$ over $k$ and a
class in $\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}(T)$ choose an fppf covering $\{T_i\to T\}$
and invertible $\mathcal{O}_{C_{T_i}}$-modules $\mathcal{L}_i$ representing the
pullbacks of the class along the
Picard presheaf; the locally constant
functions $t\mapsto\deg_{T_i}(\mathcal{L}_i)(t)$ of
[def-pd-fibrewise-degree] agree on the overlaps by
[lem-pd-degree-locally-constant](2–3) and glue to a locally constant
function $T\to\Z$, giving an element of $\underline{\Z}(T)$; the result is
independent of all choices by [lem-pd-degree-locally-constant].
The *degree-zero part* of the Picard functor is the subfunctor

$$
\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}:=\ker(\deg)\subseteq\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}
$$

in the sense of [def-pc-subfunctor]: its value on $T$ consists of the
classes whose fibrewise degree function is identically zero.

attrs.title: The constant integers sheaf and the degree morphism

objects.body:
Let $X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes and let $V$ be a scheme over $X$. Write
$X_2=X\times_YX$ and $X_3=X\times_YX\times_YX$ for the
fibre products over $Y$, with the projections
$\mathrm{pr}_0,\mathrm{pr}_1:X_2\to X$ and
$\mathrm{pr}_{01},\mathrm{pr}_{02},\mathrm{pr}_{12}:X_3\to X_2$. A
*descent datum on $V$ over $X/Y$* is an isomorphism
$\varphi:\mathrm{pr}_0^*V\to\mathrm{pr}_1^*V$ of schemes over $X_2$ satisfying
the cocycle condition
$\mathrm{pr}_{02}^*\varphi =\mathrm{pr}_{12}^*\varphi\circ\mathrm{pr}_{01}^*\varphi$
over $X_3$ (Stacks Project, Descent, Definition 35.34.1, Tag
[023V](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/023V)). The datum is
*effective* if there are a scheme $V_0$ over $Y$ and an isomorphism
$V\cong V_0\times_YX$ over $X$ whose pullback to $X_2$ recovers $\varphi$.

attrs.title: Descent datum for a scheme along a morphism

objects.body:
Let $k$ be a field and let $C$ be a
smooth projective curve over $k$
which is geometrically integral.
Let $T$ be a $k$-scheme (in the fppf site of
[def-pc-fppf-site]) and let $\mathcal{L}$ be an
invertible $\mathcal{O}_{C_T}$-module,
with $C_T$ the base change of $C$ along
$T\to\Spec(k)$. For a point $t\in T$ with residue field $\kappa(t)$, the
*fibre* $\mathcal{L}_t$ is an invertible module on the proper curve
$C_{\kappa(t)}$ over the field $\kappa(t)$, and the
*fibrewise degree* of $\mathcal{L}$ at $t$ is the integer

$$
\deg_T(\mathcal{L})(t):=\deg_{C_{\kappa(t)}}\bigl(\mathcal{L}_t\bigr)
:=\chi\bigl(C_{\kappa(t)},\mathcal{L}_t\bigr)
-\chi\bigl(C_{\kappa(t)},\mathcal{O}_{C_{\kappa(t)}}\bigr),
$$

with $\chi$ the Euler characteristic and
$\deg$ the degree of an invertible module
on a proper curve over a field.

attrs.title: Fibrewise degree of an invertible module on a curve

objects.body:
Let $k$ be a field. A *separable closure* of $k$ is a field $k_s$
together with a $k$-embedding $k\hookrightarrow k_s$ such that $k_s$ is
separably closed and algebraic and
separable over $k$; it is the compositum of the finite separable subextensions
$K/k$ of $k_s$, so that

$$
k_s=\colim_{K/k\ \text{finite separable}}K
$$

as a filtered colimit of $k$-algebras, and $\Spec(k_s)\to\Spec(k)$ is
faithfully flat. We fix one such $k_s$ for each field $k$ and write $C_{k_s}$
for the base change of a $k$-scheme $C$ along
$\Spec(k_s)\to\Spec(k)$.

In the setting of [def-per-support-condition], put

$$
\begin{aligned}
{}^pD^{\le0}(X)&:=\bigl\{K:\ \operatorname{SuppCon}(K)\bigr\},\\
{}^pD^{\ge0}(X)&:=\bigl\{K:\ \operatorname{CosuppCon}(K)\bigr\},
\end{aligned}
$$

and, for every $n\in\mathbf Z$,

$$
{}^pD^{\le n}(X):={}^pD^{\le0}(X)[-n],\qquad
{}^pD^{\ge n}(X):={}^pD^{\ge0}(X)[-n].
$$

The *perverse heart candidate* is

$$
\mathrm{Perv}^{\mathrm{cand}}(X):={}^pD^{\le0}(X)\cap{}^pD^{\ge0}(X).
$$

attrs.title: Perverse subcategories of the first kind

objects.body:
Let $X$ be a
separated scheme of finite
type over a field $k$, and work in the bounded constructible
$\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-coefficient categories of
[def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] on the etale site of $X$, with the
constructible conventions of
[def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] and the cohomology sheaves
$\mathcal H^i$ of [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. For
$K\in D^b_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ write

$$
\operatorname{SuppCon}(K)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\dim\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal H^{-i}(K)\le i\qquad(i\in\mathbf Z),
$$

with the convention that the empty support has dimension $-\infty$, and

$$
\operatorname{CosuppCon}(K)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{SuppCon}\bigl(D_XK\bigr),
$$

where $D_X$ is the Verdier dual of [def-trf-dualizing-complex].

In the Poincare duality conventions of this chapter (the fixed setting),
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$. The *coefficient dual* is

$$
K^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_X\bigl(K,\Lambda_X\bigr),
$$

with the canonical evaluation

$$
\operatorname{ev}_K:K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}K^\vee\longrightarrow\Lambda_X
$$

of the tensor–internal-Hom adjunction.

Fix the global finite-field datum
$p,a,q,k_0,k$, where $q=p^a$, a prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite
extension $E/\Ql$ contained in a fixed algebraic closure $\Qlb$, with
valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and an
integer $n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$. Put $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $X_0$ be a
smooth, separated finite-type, geometrically
connected $k_0$-scheme of pure dimension $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ (not
necessarily proper), put
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, set $s=\Spec k$, and let
$a_X:X\to s$ be the structure morphism, assumed
exceptional-adjoint
admissible at every finite coefficient stage. On the
small pro-etale site of $X$,
use

$$
D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)\qquad(\Lambda\in\{A,\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}),
$$

the bounded
constructible and finite-Tor
categories, the
derived pullback, tensor,
and internal Hom, the
derived direct image, the
compact-support direct image,
and the exceptional inverse
image, with the constructions and adjunctions of those definitions;
in particular

$$
\omega_{X,\Lambda}=Ra_X^!\Lambda
$$

with $Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$, and the
ordinary and
compact-support cohomology are

$$
R\Gamma(X,K),\ \ R\Gamma_c(X,K),\ \ H^i(X,K),\ \ H_c^i(X,K).
$$

Use the coefficient twists
$K(m)=K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}\Lambda(m)$ and the
Frobenius normalization
on them ($q^{-m}$ on $\Lambda(m)$, $q^m$ on $\Lambda(-m)$). At the
point $s$, the finite
coefficient categories are $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A_{E,n})$,
$D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(\mathcal O_E)$, $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)$, and the
common-stage category of
algebraically
closed coefficients; write $A$ for the coefficient ring of the point.
For $C$ in such a category put

$$
C^\vee=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,A).
$$

The $F$-operators are the
global geometric Frobenius operators of [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius] on the
global sections, with the
strict Weil structures of [def-pur-tate-datum] and the iterates of
[def-trf-frobenius-operators]. The canonical orientation is the one
of the smooth
dualizing complex supplied by the purity chapter ([thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object]; see
the interface record [rem-sf-orientation-pointer]): the canonical choice

$$
\eta_X:\omega_{X,\Lambda}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Lambda_X(d)[2d].
$$

For
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ put

$$
\mathbb D_XK=R\mathcal Hom_X\bigl(K,\omega_{X,\Lambda}\bigr),
\qquad
K^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_X\bigl(K,\Lambda_X\bigr),
$$

the *Verdier dual* and the *coefficient dual*.

Properness of $X_0$ is not part of this setting: the duality statements
formulated in it use compact supports $R\Gamma_c$ against ordinary
cohomology $R\Gamma$ and never compare the two. Properness is imposed
explicitly, and only, in the statements that need
$Ra_{X!}\cong Ra_{X*}$ (the untwisted trace on $H^{2d}$, the trace–cup
pairing on ordinary cohomology, and proper Poincare duality).

In the Poincare duality conventions of this chapter (the fixed setting), let $\Lambda\in\{A,\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell}\}$ and let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ be perfect over $\Lambda_X$ (the case $\Lambda=A$ is the finite stage; the other coefficients are its transports). The *derived Poincare pairing* is the composite

$$
\beta _K:\   R\Gamma _c(X,K)\otimes _\Lambda ^LR\Gamma \bigl(X,K^\vee (d)\bigr)[2d] \longrightarrow \Lambda,
$$

$$
\begin{array}{lll} R\Gamma _c(X,K)\otimes _\Lambda ^LR\Gamma \bigl(X,K^\vee (d)\bigr)[2d] & \xrightarrow {\  \smile _c\  }&  R\Gamma _c\bigl(X,K\otimes ^L_{\Lambda _X}K^\vee (d)\bigr)[2d]\\ & \xrightarrow {R\Gamma _c(\operatorname {ev}_K(d))[2d]}&  R\Gamma _c\bigl(X,\Lambda _X(d)\bigr)[2d]\\ & \xrightarrow {\  \operatorname {Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{a_X,\Lambda }\  }&  \Lambda, \end{array}
$$

where $\smile _c$ is the mixed-support cup product, $\operatorname {ev}_K$ is the evaluation of Definition 9.5, and $\operatorname {Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{a_X,\Lambda }$ is the normalized smooth trace of the purity chapter for the structure morphism $a_X$, i.e. the counit of $Ra_{X!}\dashv Ra_X^!$ through the canonical orientation $\eta _X$. None of these ingredients uses properness: the cup product and the trace only involve $Ra_{X!}$, $Ra_{X*}$ and $Ra_X^!$ for the separated finite-type smooth morphism $a_X$.

In the Poincare duality conventions of this chapter (the fixed setting), strict Weil complex: a perfect $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ with $\varphi _K:Lg_\gamma ^*K\xrightarrow {\sim }K$, in the notation of Definition 7.2 and of the geometric-Frobenius datum of the purity chapter. Let $\varphi _A:Lg_\gamma ^*A_X\xrightarrow {\sim } A_X$ be the canonical Weil structure on the constant coefficient object, and let $\tau _r:Lg_\gamma ^*A_X(r)\xrightarrow {\sim }A_X(r)$ be the Tate datum of the purity chapter, on which geometric Frobenius acts by the scalar $q^{-r}$. The *contragredient datum* on the coefficient dual is the typed composite

$$
\begin{gathered}
\varphi _{K^\vee }:\   Lg_\gamma ^*R\mathcal Hom_X(K,A_X) \\
\xrightarrow {\  \sim \  } R\mathcal Hom_X\bigl(Lg_\gamma ^*K,Lg_\gamma ^*A_X\bigr) \\
\xrightarrow {R\mathcal Hom(\operatorname {id},\varphi _A)} R\mathcal Hom_X\bigl(Lg_\gamma ^*K,A_X\bigr) \\
\xrightarrow {R\mathcal Hom(\varphi _K^{-1},\operatorname {id})} R\mathcal Hom_X(K,A_X),
\end{gathered}
$$

and the datum on the twisted dual is $\varphi _{K^\vee (r)}=\varphi _{K^\vee }\otimes \tau _r$, with the scalar $q^{-r}$ on $A_X(r)$ (hence $q^r$ on $A_X(-r)$). For $K=\Lambda_X$ the constant sheaf with its canonical datum, the contragredient datum corresponds to the canonical datum under the canonical identification $(\Lambda_X)^\vee\cong\Lambda_X$, and the resulting $F$-operators are the iterated global geometric Frobenius operators of chap:trace-formula.

In the Poincare duality conventions of this chapter (the fixed setting), $K,L\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$. The *mixed-support cup product* is the canonical map

$$
\smile _c:\  R\Gamma _c(X,K)\otimes _A^LR\Gamma (X,L) \longrightarrow R\Gamma _c\bigl(X,K\otimes ^L_{A_X}L\bigr)
$$

obtained as the composite of the projection transformation for $Rf_!$, applied to the pair $K,\; L'=Ra_{X*}L\in D^b_{ctf}(s,A)$,

$$
Ra_{X!}K\otimes _A^LRa_{X*}L \longrightarrow Ra_{X!}\bigl(K\otimes ^L_{A_X}La_X^*Ra_{X*}L\bigr),
$$

and the map induced by the counit $La_X^*Ra_{X*}L\to L$. The same construction at the $\mathcal O_E$-, $E$-, and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell }$-stages is obtained by levelwise application and transport. The cup product is associative and unital, graded-commutative, and compatible with finite reduction and base change of the coefficient ring.

In the Poincare duality conventions of this chapter (the fixed setting),
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$. Then $K$ is *perfect over
$\Lambda_X$* if it is quasi-isomorphic, locally on the
small pro-etale site of $X$,
to a bounded complex of finite projective $\Lambda_X$-modules.

attrs.title: Perfect complex over the coefficient ring on $X$

objects.body:
In the Poincare duality conventions of this chapter, let
$\Lambda\in\{A,\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$, and let $C,D$ be
perfect point complexes
over $\Lambda$. A morphism

$$
b:C\otimes _\Lambda^LD\longrightarrow \Lambda
$$

is *perfect* if its tensor–internal-Hom adjoint

$$
D\longrightarrow R\operatorname {Hom}_\Lambda(C,\Lambda)=C^\vee
$$

is an isomorphism.

In the Poincare duality conventions of this chapter (the fixed setting),
object $C$ of the
category at the point is
*perfect* if it is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite
projective $A$-modules. The *derived dual* is
$C^\vee=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,A)$, and the canonical evaluation and
coevaluation are the maps of the tensor–internal-Hom adjunction.

In the conventions of [def-pod-conventions] ($X_0$ not necessarily
proper), the trace map of [def-weil-poincare-trace-cup] is read through the
canonical orientation $\eta_X$ as the counit of $Ra_{X!}\dashv Ra_X^!$,

$$
\operatorname{tr}_X:H_c^{2d}(X,\Lambda(d))\longrightarrow\Lambda,
\qquad
\operatorname{tr}^{(-d)}_X:H_c^{2d}(X,\Lambda)\longrightarrow\Lambda(-d),
$$

the second being its untwisted form; neither uses properness (compare
[def-pur-smooth-trace], where the same trace is realized as the normalized
smooth trace $\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{a_X,\Lambda}$). If $X_0$ is
proper, then $Ra_{X!}\cong Ra_{X*}$ by [cor-cbc-proper-coincidence], so
$H_c^{2d}=H^{2d}$ and $\operatorname{tr}^{(-d)}_X$ is the map
$H^{2d}(X,\Lambda)\to\Lambda(-d)$ of [def-weil-poincare-trace-cup]; only
in this case is the trace–cup pairing
$\langle x,y\rangle_i=\operatorname{tr}^{(-d)}_X(x\smile y)$ on
$H^i(X,\Lambda)\times H^{2d-i}(X,\Lambda)$ of that definition read in
these conventions.

attrs.title: Poincare duality conventions: trace and trace-cup pairing

objects.body:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
$A=A_{E,n}$, and let $Y$ be a
separated finite-type
$k$-scheme. Put

$$
\mathbf A^1_Y=\mathbf A^1_{\mathbf Z}\times_{\mathbf Z}Y
$$

for the affine line of [def-sbc-affine-space], with projection
$p:\mathbf A^1_Y\to Y$, zero section $s:Y\to\mathbf A^1_Y$ (the closed
immersion defined by the vanishing of the coordinate), and open complement

$$
j:\mathbf G_{m,Y}=\mathbf A^1_Y\setminus s(Y)\longrightarrow\mathbf A^1_Y.
$$

Let $t$ denote the global coordinate function on $\mathbf A^1_Y$, viewed
as a global unit on $\mathbf G_{m,Y}$. With
$N=n\cdot v_\ell(\varpi_E)$ as in [lem-pur-finite-kummer-level]
(whose hypothesis $e(E/\Ql)\mid n$ is assumed from now on), the
finite-level twist is

$$
A(1)_{\mathbf A^1_Y}
=\mu_{\ell^N,\mathbf A^1_Y}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^N}A,
$$

and the *Kummer class of $t$* is the class

$$
\kappa(t)\in H^1(\mathbf G_{m,Y},A(1))
$$

obtained from the Kummer sequence of etale sheaves of units
on $\mathbf G_{m,Y}$,

$$
0\longrightarrow\mu_{\ell^N}\longrightarrow\mathbf G_m
\xrightarrow{\ \ell^N\ }\mathbf G_m\longrightarrow0,
$$

whose boundary map $\mathbf G_m(Y)\cong H^0(\mathbf G_{m,Y},\mathbf G_m) \to H^1(\mathbf G_{m,Y},\mu_{\ell^N})$ is applied to the global unit
$t\in\Gamma(\mathbf G_{m,Y},\mathbf G_m)$, followed by the coefficient
extension $H^1(-,\mu_{\ell^N})\to H^1(-,A(1))$ induced by the canonical
isomorphism $A(1)\cong\mu_{\ell^N}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^N}A$ of
[lem-pur-finite-kummer-level]. (The naive tensor
$\mathbf G_m\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^N}A$ of the Kummer sequence is not
defined at the level of sheaves: $\mathbf G_m$ is not a sheaf of
$\mathbf Z/\ell^N$-modules, as it contains elements of order not
dividing $\ell^N$; the $A$-coefficient form of the sequence is the
one obtained by extending coefficients on the $\mu_{\ell^N}$-term and
taking the connecting map, as above.) Equivalently, in *torsor
form*: the $\ell^N$-th root of the coordinate defines the finite etale
scheme

$$
\mathcal T_t=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{\mathbf G_{m,Y}}[T_0]
\bigm/\bigl(T_0^{\ell^N}-t\bigr),
$$

whose structure map $\mathcal T_t\to\mathbf G_{m,Y}$ is finite etale of
degree $\ell^N$ – the quotient is of finite presentation; $T_0$ is a
unit (the relation $T_0^{\ell^N}=t$ with $t$ a unit); and the
derivative $\ell^N T_0^{\ell^N-1}$ is a unit because $\ell^N$ is
invertible in the base field $k$ of [def-pur-conventions]
($\ell\neq p$ there) and $T_0$ is a unit, so the monogenic etale
criterion applies – and the multiplication of
$T_0$ by an $\ell^N$-th root of unity makes $\mathcal T_t$ a right
$\mu_{\ell^N,\mathbf G_{m,Y}}$-torsor; with $A$-coefficients,
$\mathcal T_t\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^N}A$ is a right
$A(1)_{\mathbf G_{m,Y}}$-torsor, and $\kappa(t)$ is the class of this
torsor in $H^1(\mathbf G_{m,Y},A(1))$, the two descriptions being related
by the standard identification of the boundary of the Kummer sequence
with the torsor class. On the small pro-etale site,
the [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] cohomology sheaves of
the exceptional inverse
image along the zero section are written $R^r s^!(-)$, and the
supported cohomology of the pair $(s(Y),\mathbf A^1_Y)$ is that of
[def-pur-support-cohomology].

In the finite-coefficient purity conventions,
let $p:\mathbf A^1_Y\to Y$ be the projection and
$j:\mathbf A^1_Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^1_Y$, $q:\mathbf P^1_Y\to Y$
its standard compactification, as in
the affine-line datum.
Define integration by restriction of the already constructed
projective-line trace:

$$
\int_p:Rp_!\Lambda(1)[2]=Rq_*j_!\Lambda(1)[2]
\longrightarrow Rq_*\Lambda(1)[2]
\xrightarrow{t_q}\Lambda_Y.
$$

For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$, define $\gamma_{p,K}$ to be the
exceptional adjoint of

$$
Rp_!Lp^*K(1)[2]
\xrightarrow{\sim}K\otimes^L Rp_!\Lambda(1)[2]
\xrightarrow{1_K\otimes\int_p}K,
$$

using the compact-support projection map
and Tate twists.
Thus $\gamma_{p,K}:Lp^*K(1)[2]\to Rp^!K$ is defined in the ambient
category; its isomorphy and bounded constructibility are conclusions.

In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
$A=A_{E,n}$, and write $p_d:\mathbf A^d_Y\to Y$ for the projection of
[def-sbc-affine-space], $d\geq0$, obtained as the iterated composite
of $d$ affine-line projections. For every $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$
define

$$
\gamma_{p_d,K}:Lp_d^*K(d)[2d]\longrightarrow Rp_d^!K
$$

as the ordered composite of the $d$ affine-line purity comparisons
[def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison], the composition isomorphisms
for the (coherently associative) exceptional inverse image of a composite
morphism, and the additivity isomorphisms for the
Tate twists. For $d=0$,
$\gamma_{p_0,K}$ is the identity of $K$.

In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
a separated finite-type
morphism $f:X\to Y$ is *cohomologically smooth* if:

1. $\omega_f=Rf^!\Lambda_Y$ is tensor-invertible;
1. for every $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ the canonical map
(the mate of the projection formula of
[def-exchange-projection] with the adjunction counit)
$$
\theta_{f,K}:Lf^*K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}\omega_f
\longrightarrow Rf^!K
$$
is an isomorphism;
1. for every Cartesian square
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X'&\xrightarrow{\ g'\ }&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{\ g\ }&Y,
\end{array}
$$
the canonical base-change map
$Lg'^*\omega_f\to\omega_{f'}$ is an isomorphism.

At this stage no isomorphism $\omega_f\simeq\Lambda_X(d)[2d]$ is part
of the definition.

In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
geometric-Frobenius datum,
and let $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ carry a strict Weil datum
$\varphi_M:Lg_{X,\gamma}^*M\cong M$. The compact-support transport of the
datum is

$$
\varphi_{f_!M}:Lg_{Y,\gamma}^*Rf_!M
\xrightarrow{\ \operatorname{Ex}_!\ }
Rf_!Lg_{X,\gamma}^*M
\xrightarrow{\ Rf_!(\varphi_M)\ }Rf_!M,
$$

the first arrow being the compact-support base change of
[def-exchange-projection] for the first Cartesian square of
[def-pur-scheme-geometric-frobenius]. Its scheme-Frobenius form is

$$
u_N=\varphi_N\circ\kappa_{T,N}:L\Phi_T^*N\longrightarrow N
$$

for every object $N$ on $T=X$ or $Y$ carrying a datum, as in
[def-pur-scheme-geometric-frobenius].

attrs.title: Compact-support transport of a Weil datum

objects.body:
Fix the global finite-field datum
$p,a,q,k_0,k$, where $q=p^a$, a prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite
extension $E/\Ql$ contained in a fixed algebraic closure $\Qlb$, with
valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and an
integer $n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$. Put $A=A_{E,n}$. On the
small pro-etale site, use the
bounded constructible
finite-torsion coefficient category $D^b_c(-,A)$, the
finite-Tor subcategories
$D^b_{ctf}(-,\Lambda)$ for $\Lambda\in\{A,\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$, the
derived pullback, tensor,
and internal Hom, the
[def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] cohomology sheaves
$\mathcal H^r$, the
compact-support direct image
$Rf_!$, and the
exceptional inverse image
$Rf^!$, with $Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$ and the
exchange and projection and [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]). Use the
coefficient twists of degree
$m\in\mathbf Z$,

$$
K(m)=K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_Y}\Lambda(m),
$$

and the terminology
smooth of relative dimension
$d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$. For $\Lambda=A$ all statements and
constructions below are made; the
derived-complete integral,
rationalized, and
common-stage
algebraically closed versions for $\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb$ are the
coefficient transports described in the transport section at the end of
this blueprint. Geometric Frobenius acts on the
twists with the specified
twist normalization of the framework chapter: by $q^{-1}$ on $\Lambda(1)$, by
$q^{-m}$ on $\Lambda(m)$, and by $q^{m}$ on $\Lambda(-m)$ for
$m\geq0$. For $a:Y\to\Spec k$ write

$$
\omega_{Y,\Lambda}=Ra^!\Lambda.
$$

In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting), in the situation of
[def-pur-section-invariant], the *deformation to the normal
cone* of the section is

$$
D_sV=
\operatorname{Bl}_{s(B)\times\{0\}}
\bigl(V\times_B\mathbf A^1_B\bigr)
\setminus\widetilde{V\times_B\{0\}},
$$

the tilde denoting the strict transform. It carries the maps and the
section

$$
\widetilde g:D_sV\longrightarrow\mathbf A^1_B,
\qquad
\widetilde s:\mathbf A^1_B\longrightarrow D_sV.
$$

The *family object* is

$$
F=L\widetilde s^*\omega_{\widetilde g}
\in\operatorname{Pic}\bigl(D^b_{ctf}(\mathbf A^1_B,\Lambda)\bigr).
$$

attrs.title: Deformation space of a closed section

objects.body:
Let $s:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a
closed immersion, and
let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be its open complement. Work with
$\Lambda$-module sheaves on the
small pro-etale sites in the
finite coefficient conventions.
For a sheaf $M$ define its subsheaf of sections supported on $Z$ by

$$
\mathcal G_ZM=\ker(M\longrightarrow j_*j^*M).
$$

Regarded as a sheaf on $Z$, it is
$s^!M:=s^{-1}\mathcal G_ZM$; thus $s_*s^!M=\mathcal G_ZM$.
Here $s^!$ is a left exact functor, distinct from the ordinary
restriction $s^{-1}$. A sheaf $I$ is *flasque for this pair*
if $I\to j_*j^*I$ is an epimorphism.

In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
$A=A_{E,n}$, let $V\to B$ be smooth of relative dimension $n$ and
let $Z\hookrightarrow V$ be a closed subfamily of pure codimension $c$
with $Z\to B$ smooth. A *frame at $Z$* is an etale open
$U\to V$ together with functions $f_1,\dots,f_c\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O)$
generating the ideal of $Z\cap U$. Put $D_j=V(f_j)$; the function
$f_j$ is a unit on $U\setminus D_j$. Use the boundary for this
individual closed–open pair from [thm-pur-with-support-exactness]
to define $\alpha_j=\partial_j\kappa(f_j)\in H^2_{D_j}(U,\Lambda(1))$.
The *class of the frame* is their
supported cup product

$$
\operatorname{cl}(f)
\;=\;\alpha_1\cup\cdots\cup\alpha_c
\;\in\;H^{2c}_{Z\cap U}\bigl(U,\Lambda(c)\bigr),
$$

where the Kummer classes are those of
[def-pur-affine-line-datum]. Each factor has degree two and
twist one; their supports intersect in $Z\cap U$, giving degree
$2c$ and twist $c$.

In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion with ideal sheaf
$\mathcal I$. The *normal cone* is
$N_{Z/X}=\operatorname{Spec}_Z\bigl(\bigoplus_{r\geq0}\mathcal I^r/ \mathcal I^{r+1}\bigr)$; if $i$ is a
regular immersion of pure
codimension $c$, the conormal sheaf
$\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ is locally free of rank $c$, and
$N_{Z/X}\to Z$ is a *vector bundle* of rank $c$ with a canonical
*zero section* $z:Z\hookrightarrow N_{Z/X}$.

In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $X$ be a separated
finite-type $k$-scheme and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a
closed immersion with
$Z$ separated of finite type and *pure codimension* $c\in \mathbf Z_{\geq1}$ in the sense that for every $z\in Z$ the local ring
$\mathcal O_{X,z}$ has Krull dimension $\dim\mathcal O_{Z,z}+c$. The
immersion is *regular* if for every $z\in Z$ the ideal of $Z$ in
$\mathcal O_{X,z}$ is generated by a regular sequence of length $c$
(equivalently, by the *linearization lemma* below, a pair of smooth
schemes with a regular immersion is etale-locally the linear pair; in
the proofs below we use the linearization lemma).

attrs.title: Regular closed immersion of pure codimension

objects.body:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
global finite-field datum
$(p,a,q,k_0,k)$, and let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a
finite-type separated
morphism of $k_0$-schemes whose base change to $k$ is smooth of relative
dimension $d$. Put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, and
let $f:X\to Y$ be the base change of $f_0$. With
$\gamma=\operatorname{Frob}_q=\sigma^{-1}$ in the
geometric Frobenius convention of
the framework chapter, write

$$
g_{X,\gamma}=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\Spec(\gamma),\
g_{Y,\gamma}=\operatorname{id}_{Y_0}\times\Spec(\gamma),
$$

for the semilinear (geometric-Galois) automorphisms, and let $\Phi_X$,
$\Phi_Y$ be the $q$-power scheme Frobenius endomorphisms of $X_0$
resp. $Y_0$, base-changed to $X$ and $Y$, in the notation of
[def-trf-scheme-frobenius]; they form the following commutative squares

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X & \xrightarrow{\ g_{X,\gamma}\ } & X\\
f\downarrow & & \downarrow f\\
Y & \xrightarrow{\ g_{Y,\gamma}\ } & Y,
\end{array}
\qquad
\begin{array}{ccc}
X & \xrightarrow{\ \Phi_X\ } & X\\
f\downarrow & & \downarrow f\\
Y & \xrightarrow{\ \Phi_Y\ } & Y,
\end{array}
$$

The first square is Cartesian, since its horizontal arrows are the
compatible semilinear automorphisms. The second is commutative by
the affine description of scheme Frobenius in
[def-trf-scheme-frobenius]; it is not asserted to be Cartesian.
The scheme-Frobenius forms below are transported from the first square
using the comparison isomorphisms, not by applying Cartesian base change
to the second square. The comparison
isomorphisms $\kappa_X,\kappa_Y$ are those of
[prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison]: the absolute Frobenius
factorizes as

$$
\operatorname{Fr}^{(q)}_{Y/k}=g_{Y,\sigma}\Phi_Y=\Phi_Yg_{Y,\sigma}
$$

([prop-trf-frobenius-factorization], with $\sigma:z\mapsto z^q$ the
arithmetic Frobenius), so the scheme Frobenius and the geometric-Galois
automorphism $g_{Y,\gamma}=g_{Y,\sigma}^{-1}$ differ by the universal
homeomorphism $\operatorname{Fr}^{(q)}_{Y/k}$, under which the etale site
is invariant by [thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance].
The isomorphisms are compatible with the pullback-composition
identifications and with $f$:

$$
Lf^*\kappa_Y=\kappa_XLf^*.
$$

attrs.title: Scheme and geometric Frobenius of the purity datum

objects.body:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting), let $g:V\to B$ be
smooth and let
$s:B\hookrightarrow V$ be a closed section. The
*section invariant* is the invertible object of
$\operatorname{Pic}\bigl(D^b_{ctf}(B,\Lambda)\bigr)$

$$
C(g,s)\;=\;Ls^*\omega_g\;=\;Ls^*Rg^!\Lambda_B,
$$

invertible by [def-pur-co-smoothness].

In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
$A=A_{E,n}$, and let

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X'&\xrightarrow{\ u\ }&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{\ v\ }&Y
\end{array}
$$

be a Cartesian square with $f$ smooth of relative dimension $d$ and
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$. The *smooth pullback exchange* for the
exceptional inverse image is the isomorphism

$$
\operatorname{Ex}^{!,\mathrm{sm}}_{f,v,K}:
Lu^*Rf^!K\longrightarrow Rf'^!Lv^*K
$$

defined as the typed composite

$$
Lu^*Rf^!K
\xrightarrow{(Lu^*\gamma_{f,K})^{-1}}
Lu^*Lf^*K(d)[2d]
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
Lf'^*Lv^*K(d)[2d]
\xrightarrow{\ \gamma_{f',Lv^*K}\ }
Rf'^!Lv^*K.
$$

This is distinct from the right-adjoint mate $\operatorname{BC}^!_*$ of
the compact-support base change; both source and target are fixed
explicitly by the definitions.

attrs.title: Smooth pullback exchange for exceptional inverse image

objects.body:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
$A=A_{E,n}$, let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth,
separated, of pure
relative dimension $d$, and let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$. The
*smooth purity map* is the composite

$$
\gamma_{f,K}:\;
Lf^*K(d)[2d]
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
Lf^*K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}\Lambda_X(d)[2d]
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
Lf^*K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}\omega_f
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
Rf^!K,
$$

the first isomorphism being the canonical twist reassociation of
[def-coefficient-twists-detailed], and the
third the tensor formula of [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness].

In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
$A=A_{E,n}$, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a smooth separated morphism of
relative dimension $d$. The *smooth trace* is the composite

$$
\operatorname{Tr}_f^{\mathrm{sm}}:
Rf_!\Lambda_X(d)[2d]
\xrightarrow{\ Rf_!(\gamma_{f,\Lambda_Y})\ }
Rf_!Rf^!\Lambda_Y
\xrightarrow{\ \operatorname{Tr}_f\ }\Lambda_Y,
$$

where $\operatorname{Tr}_f$ is the counit of the adjunction
$Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$ of
[def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility]; for
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ the coefficient-valued smooth trace is

$$
\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{f,K}:
Rf_!Lf^*K(d)[2d]
\xrightarrow{\ Rf_!(\gamma_{f,K})\ }
Rf_!Rf^!K
\xrightarrow{\ \operatorname{Tr}_{f,K}\ }K.
$$

For $K=\Lambda_Y$ this is the preceding normalized trace; the projection
formula identifies it with $K\otimes^L\operatorname{Tr}_f^{\mathrm{sm}}$.

Let $X$ be a scheme, let
$i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed subscheme with open complement
$j:U\hookrightarrow X$, and let $F$ be a torsion etale sheaf on the
small etale site of $X$. For
$q\geq0$, write $H^q_Z(X,F)$ for the $q$-th right derived functor of
the functor of sections with support in $Z$. The same notation is used
for bounded-below complexes with torsion cohomology in the
derived categories, and on
the small pro-etale site for finite-torsion coefficients, with the
functor of sections with support understood in the corresponding
topology.

Fix the closed–open pair of
supported sections. For a bounded
below complex $K$, choose the specified
K-injective resolution
$K\to I(K)$, with injective terms. Put

$$
A(K)=s_*s^!I(K),\quad B(K)=I(K),\quad C(K)=j_*j^*I(K).
$$

Let $u:A(K)\to B(K)$ be the inclusion. The cone complex is
$\operatorname{Cone}(u)^m=B(K)^m\oplus A(K)^{m+1}$, with differential
$d(b,a)=(d_Bb+u(a),-d_Aa)$. This construction specifies the maps; it does not identify
ordinary restriction $s^{-1}$ with the derived functor $Rs^!$.

attrs.title: The support-localization triangle of a complex: the construction

objects.body:
Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ and $j:W\hookrightarrow X$ be
closed immersions, and
write $h:Z\times_XW\hookrightarrow X$. For classes
$\alpha\in H_Z^a(X,F)$ and $\beta\in H_W^b(X,G)$ in
supported cohomology, represent
them by morphisms as in [lem-pur-supported-hom].
Their *supported cup product* is the morphism

$$
h_*\Lambda_{Z\times_XW}
\cong i_*\Lambda_Z\otimes^L_\Lambda j_*\Lambda_W
\xrightarrow{\alpha\otimes\beta}(F\otimes^L_\Lambda G)[a+b],
$$

read as an element of $H_{Z\cap W}^{a+b}(X,F\otimes^L_\Lambda G)$.
The first identification is the stalkwise identification of the
coefficient sheaves: each stalk is either $0$ or the free module
$\Lambda$, so these sheaves are flat and their tensor is the
coefficient sheaf on the intersection. Tensor and shifts are those
of derived tensor.

Let $Z\subset X,W\subset Y$ be closed subschemes of
separated finite-type
schemes over an algebraically closed field $k$. Fix a finite
commutative coefficient ring $A$, and let $K,L$ be bounded-below
complexes of $A$-module sheaves on their etale sites whose
derived exterior product
is bounded below. The *supported exterior product* is the map

$$
\kappa^{Z,W}_{K,L}:
R\Gamma_Z(X,K)\otimes_A^LR\Gamma_W(Y,L)
\longrightarrow
R\Gamma_{Z\times W}(X\times_kY,K\boxtimes_A^L L).
$$

It is obtained by pulling back sections in the two factors and
tensoring them: their supports meet in $Z\times W$.
Derive this pairing with K-flat tensor and injective support
resolutions. Thus its composition with the map forgetting support
is the ordinary exterior product,
and its cohomology uses the
support functors.

attrs.title: Exterior product in cohomology with closed support

objects.body:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
geometric-Frobenius datum,
and a coefficient ring $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$. A
*strict geometric-Weil datum* on $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ is a
specified isomorphism in the ordinary triangulated category

$$
\varphi_K:Lg_{Y,\gamma}^*K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }K;
$$

for $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ such a datum is a normalized system of
finite-stage data compatible with the reductions, for $\Lambda=E$ an
object obtained from an $\mathcal O_E$-datum by inverting $\varpi$,
and for
$\Lambda=\Qlb$ a datum over some finite $E/\Ql$,
modulo further finite coefficient extension (as in
[def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], with the
rationalized common-stage
conventions). In every case the forgetful object lies in
$D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ and $\varphi_K$ denotes the resulting typed
isomorphism; its scheme-Frobenius form is

$$
u_K=\varphi_K\circ\kappa_{Y,K}:L\Phi_Y^*K\longrightarrow K.
$$

The Tate line carries its canonical
datum, the twist normalization of
[def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists],

$$
\tau_1:Lg_{Y,\gamma}^*\Lambda_Y(1)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Lambda_Y(1),
\quad
\tau_r:Lg_{Y,\gamma}^*\Lambda_Y(r)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Lambda_Y(r),
$$

on which geometric Frobenius acts by $q^{-1}$ on $\Lambda(1)$ and by
$q^{-r}$ on $\Lambda(r)$. The induced datum on the source of smooth
purity is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\varphi^{\mathrm{pur}}_{f,K}:
Lg_{X,\gamma}^*\bigl(Lf^*K(d)[2d]\bigr)
&\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
Lf^*Lg_{Y,\gamma}^*K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}
Lg_{X,\gamma}^*\Lambda_X(d)[2d]\\
&\xrightarrow{\ Lf^*\varphi_K\otimes\tau_d\ }
Lf^*K(d)[2d],
\end{aligned}
$$

and the datum on the exceptional inverse image is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\varphi^!_{f,K}:Lg_{X,\gamma}^*Rf^!K
&\xrightarrow{\ \operatorname{Ex}^{!,\mathrm{sm}}_{f,g_{Y,\gamma},K}\ }
Rf^!Lg_{Y,\gamma}^*K
\xrightarrow{\ Rf^!(\varphi_K)\ }Rf^!K,
\end{aligned}
$$

using the smooth pullback exchange of [def-pur-smooth-pullback-exchange]
for the first Cartesian square of [def-pur-scheme-geometric-frobenius].

attrs.title: Strict Weil data and the Tate datum

objects.body:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $f:X\to Y$ be separated finite type; Put
$W=X\times_YX$ with projections $p_1,p_2$ and
diagonal $\Delta$, and let $L\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ be
tensor-invertible. A *trace–diagonal datum* for $(f,L)$ is a
pair

$$
\operatorname{tr}_f:Rf_!L\longrightarrow\Lambda_Y,
\qquad
\operatorname{cl}_\Delta:\Delta_!\Lambda_X\longrightarrow p_2^*L.
$$

The *induced functor* (a functor by [lem-weil-derived-tensor-functorial]) is

$$
G_L:D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)\longrightarrow D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda),
\qquad G_L(K)=Lf^*K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}L,
$$

and $\operatorname{tr}_f$ defines, via the projection formula, the
*counit*

$$
\epsilon_K:Rf_!G_L(K)\cong K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_Y}Rf_!L
\xrightarrow{\ \operatorname{id}\otimes\operatorname{tr}_f\ }K;
$$

$\operatorname{cl}_\Delta$ defines, the *unit*

$$
\eta_A:A\cong Rp_{2!}\bigl(p_1^*A\otimes^L_{\Lambda_W}\Delta_!\Lambda_X\bigr)
\xrightarrow{\ \operatorname{id}\otimes\operatorname{cl}_\Delta\ }
Rp_{2!}\bigl(p_1^*A\otimes^L_{\Lambda_W}p_2^*L\bigr)
\cong G_L(Rf_!A).
$$

The two *triangular composites* are the composites

$$
Rf_!A\xrightarrow{\ Rf_!\eta_A\ }Rf_!G_LRf_!A
\xrightarrow{\ \epsilon_{Rf_!A}\ }Rf_!A
$$

and

$$
G_LK\xrightarrow{\ \eta_{G_LK}\ }G_LRf_!G_LK
\xrightarrow{\ G_L\epsilon_K\ }G_LK,
$$

natural in $A\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ and
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$.

For the support-localization triangle,
*canonicality* means independence of the chosen injective resolution
under the derived comparison maps. *Functoriality* means that a
morphism of input complexes induces the specified morphism of triangles,
compatible with composition in the derived category. *Etale
base-change compatibility* means that, for an
etale map $v:X'\to X$,
pullback identifies this triangle with the triangle for
$Z'=Z\times_XX'$, $U'=U\times_XX'$ and $v^*K$.

attrs.title: Canonicality, functoriality and etale base change of the triangle

objects.body:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $E\to B$ be a
vector bundle of constant
rank $r$, with zero section $z$ and projection $\pi$. The
tautological section of $\pi^*E$ has zero scheme $z(B)$; its
localized top Chern class of [thm-pur-localized-top-chern] is the
supported class

$$
\operatorname{thom}(E):z_*\Lambda_B\longrightarrow\Lambda_E(r)[2r].
$$

Applying $R\pi_!$ defines

$$
\tau_E:\Lambda_B\longrightarrow R\pi_!\Lambda_E(r)[2r].
$$

Explicitly, with $\overline E=\mathbf P_B(E\oplus\mathcal O_B)$ and
the localization triangle of the open $E=\overline E\setminus \mathbf P_B(E)$ of def:weil-open-closed-recollement, the two
[thm-pur-projective-bundle-formula] decompositions for the
$\mathbf P^r$-bundle $\overline E\to B$ and the $\mathbf P^{r-1}$-bundle $\mathbf P_B(E)\to B$ identify the fiber of the
restriction map with

$$
R\pi_!\Lambda_E\;\cong\;\Lambda_B(-r)[-2r].
$$

Under a local decomposition $E\simeq L_1\oplus\cdots\oplus L_r$ the
supported class is $\operatorname{thom}(L_1)\smile\cdots\smile \operatorname{thom}(L_r)$.

attrs.title: Thom class of a vector bundle

objects.body:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
a *vector bundle of constant rank* $c$ over a
separated finite-type
$k$-scheme $Z$ is a morphism $p:E\to Z$ together with a
locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $c$ and an isomorphism
$E\cong\operatorname{Spec}_Z\bigl(\mathrm{Sym}^{\bullet}\mathcal E\bigr)$
over $Z$; the *zero section* is the closed immersion
$z:Z\hookrightarrow E$ defined by the augmentation. A
*trivialization* of $E$ is an etale open $Z'\to Z$ together with
an isomorphism $E|_{Z'}\cong\mathbf A^c_{Z'}$ over $Z'$.

Let $X_0$ be as in [def-wf-fundamental-representation], with Weil group
$W=W(X_0)$ and degree map $\deg:W\to\mathbf Z$ of [def-wf-weil-group]. A
*Weil representation* is a finite-dimensional $\Qlb$-vector space $V$ with a
homomorphism $\rho:W\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$ whose restriction to the
geometric subgroup $\pi_1(X)$ is continuous; the Weil fundamental
representation of [def-wf-fundamental-representation] is one. For Weil
representations $V,V'$:

- the *direct sum* $V\oplus V'$ and the *tensor product* $V\otimes V'$
  carry the actions $g(v,v')=(gv,gv')$ and $g(v\otimes v')=gv\otimes gv'$;
- the *exterior power* $\bigwedge^rV$ carries
  $g(v_1\wedge\cdots\wedge v_r)=gv_1\wedge\cdots\wedge gv_r$; the top
  exterior power is the determinant line $\det V$ of [def-mg-determinant-line];
- the *dual* $V^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}(V,\Qlb)$ carries
  $(g\lambda)(v)=\lambda(g^{-1}v)$.

A Weil representation is *irreducible* if it is simple in the sense of
[def-mg-weil-composition-series]. Its *constituents* are the composition
factors of a composition series of [def-mg-weil-composition-series], counted
with multiplicity, and their direct sum is the semisimplification $V^{\mathrm{ss}}$
of [def-mg-weil-semisimplification]. For a
subgroup $I\subseteq W$ the *invariants* and *coinvariants* are

$$
V^I=\{v\in V:gv=v\text{ for all }g\in I\},\qquad
V_I=V/\langle gv-v:g\in I,\ v\in V\rangle .
$$

Uses: [def-mg-determinant-line], [def-mg-weil-composition-series], [def-mg-weil-semisimplification], [def-wf-fundamental-representation], [def-wf-weil-group]

Let $X_0$ be a normal geometrically connected curve over $k_0$, fix
$\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$, and let $\mathcal F_0$ be a
nonzero lisse Weil sheaf on $X_0$. Choose a composition series of
$\mathcal F_0$ in the sense of [def-mg-weil-composition-series], with
irreducible factors $V_1,\ldots,V_t$, and put
$r_a=\operatorname{rank}V_a$.

1. The *constituent determinant weights* of $\mathcal F_0$ are the
   numbers $\dw_\iota(V_a)$ of [def-wf-determinantal-weight], counted
   once for each factor; this is the determinantal-weight multiset of
   [def-mg-determinantal-weight-multiset].
2. The *rank-counted list* of determinant weights of $\mathcal F_0$ is
   the multiset in which $\dw_\iota(V_a)$ is repeated exactly $r_a$
   times, for $a=1,\ldots,t$. It has $\operatorname{rank}\mathcal F_0$
   entries.
3. Suppose $\mathcal S$ is semisimple, $\mathcal S=\bigoplus_aV_a$ with
   $V_a$ irreducible of rank $r_a$ (direct sums and irreducibility of
   Weil representations as in [def-real-weil-representation-operations]). For $\gamma\in\mathbf R$ the
   *weight block* of weight $\gamma$ of $\mathcal S$, and the rank and
   weight sum above it, are

$$
\mathcal S(\gamma)=\bigoplus_{\dw_\iota(V_a)=\gamma}V_a,\qquad
N_\gamma=\sum_{\dw_\iota(V_a)>\gamma}r_a,\qquad
B_\gamma=\sum_{\dw_\iota(V_a)>\gamma}r_a\,\dw_\iota(V_a).
$$

These notions do not depend on the choices made. By
[lem-mg-jordan-holder] the factors $V_a$ are determined up to
permutation, isomorphism and multiplicity by $\mathcal F_0$; for a
semisimple $\mathcal S=\bigoplus_aV_a$ the partial sums
$V_1\oplus\cdots\oplus V_b$ form a composition series, so the same
applies to any two decompositions into irreducible summands. Moreover
$\dw_\iota$ is an isomorphism invariant, since isomorphic sheaves have
isomorphic determinant lines; so the lists in 1 and 2, and the numbers
$N_\gamma$ and $B_\gamma$, depend only on $\mathcal F_0$ resp.
$\mathcal S$. In terms of the rank-counted list, $N_\gamma$ is the
number of entries $>\gamma$ and $B_\gamma$ is their sum. Finally
$\mathcal S(\gamma)$ is the sum inside $\mathcal S$ of all irreducible
subsheaves $W$ with $\dw_\iota(W)=\gamma$, hence a well-defined
subsheaf: each $V_a$ with $\dw_\iota(V_a)=\gamma$ is such a $W$;
conversely, for such a $W$ the projection $W\to V_a$ is zero unless
$W\cong V_a$ (Schur's lemma, both being irreducible), so $W$ lies in
the sum of the $V_a$ isomorphic to $W$, all of which have
$\dw_\iota(V_a)=\dw_\iota(W)=\gamma$. In particular
$\mathcal S=\bigoplus_{\gamma}\mathcal S(\gamma)$, the sum running over
the finitely many distinct constituent determinant weights, and
$\operatorname{rank}\mathcal S(\gamma)$ is the number of entries equal
to $\gamma$ in the rank-counted list.

attrs.title: Rank-counted determinant weights and weight blocks

objects.body:
For a scheme $S$ and an integer $n\geq0$, the *affine $n$-space*
over $S$ is

$$
\mathbf A^n_S=\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(\mathcal O_S[x_1,\dots,x_n]\bigr)
$$

with its structure morphism $\mathbf A^n_S\to S$; for $n=0$ one has
$\mathbf A^0_S=S$. The smoothness of the projection is
the corresponding statement below.

A scheme $S$ is *integral* if it is nonempty, reduced, and
irreducible; it is *normal* if it is integral and the local ring at
every point is a normal domain (a domain integrally closed in its
fraction field). A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is *dominant* if $f(X)$
is dense in $Y$. A finite etale morphism $\pi:Z\to C$ is a
*Galois cover with group $G$* if $G$ acts on $Z$ over $C$
by finite etale
automorphisms, the quotient is $Z/G\cong C$, and $Z\to C$ is a
$G$-torsor (the action is simply transitive on every geometric fibre);
the *deck group* of a Galois cover is the group of its
automorphisms over $C$; for a Galois cover with connected total space
this group is $G$, as the deck-group lemma below records. A morphism $f:X\to S$ has
*geometrically connected fibres* if for every point $s\in S$ the
fibre $X_s$ is geometrically connected over $\kappa(s)$ (its base
change to every separably closed extension of $\kappa(s)$ is connected).
A morphism $f:X\to S$ has *geometrically reduced fibres* if for
every point $s\in S$ the fibre $X_s$ is reduced after every separably
closed extension of $\kappa(s)$; it has *geometrically connected,
resp. reduced, fibres* if the corresponding property holds for every
geometric point.

attrs.title: Integral, normal, dominant, Galois covers, and geometrical connectedness

objects.body:
A morphism of schemes $f:X\to Y$ is *smooth* if it is locally of
finite presentation and formally smooth, the latter meaning that every
morphism $T\to X$ over $Y$ from a closed subscheme $T\subset T'$
defined by a nilpotent ideal sheaf extends, Zariski locally on $T'$,
to a morphism $T'\to X$ over $Y$
([Stacks Project,
Definition 37.11.1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02H0)); by
[Lemma 37.11.7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02H6) this is
the notion of a smooth morphism of
[Stacks Project,
Section 29.35](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01V4). The description of
smooth morphisms by flatness and smooth fibres is
smooth morphisms by flatness and smooth fibres is a criterion stated
below. A
fibre through that point has dimension $n$; it has relative dimension
$n$ if this holds at every point, the local constancy of this function
being
being a consequence of that criterion. An
*etale* morphism is a smooth
morphism of relative dimension zero.

Let $k$ be a field. An *abelian variety* over $k$ is a
group scheme $A$ over $k$ which
is proper, smooth and connected over $k$. A group scheme with
these three properties is also called a *complete group
variety*;

Let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$ and $\mathcal L$ a line
bundle on $X$. $\mathcal L$ is *very ample* if the complete
linear system $|\mathcal L|=\mathbf P(H^0(X,\mathcal L)^{\vee})$
gives a closed immersion $i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_k$ with
$i^*\mathcal O(1)\cong\mathcal L$ (so that every global section of
$\mathcal L$ is pulled back from a linear form on $\mathbf P^N$)
(*reference: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes, Definition
29.39.1, [Tag 01VM](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01VM) (very ample) and Properties of Schemes, Section
28.27, [Tag 01PR](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01PR) (ample invertible sheaves)*). $\mathcal L$ is
*ample* if
$\mathcal L^{\otimes m}$ is very ample for some $m\geq1$ (the
standard characterization for proper schemes; *reference:
Stacks Project, Properties of Schemes, Proposition 28.27.13, [Tag 01Q3](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01Q3)*).

attrs.title: Very ample and ample line bundles

objects.body:
Let $C$ be a curve and let $n\geq1$.
The *constant etale sheaf* $\mathbf F_n$ on $C_{\Et}$ is the
sheaf $\underline{\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z}$ associated to the constant
presheaf $U\mapsto\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$ (see
[def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]); its geometric stalks are
$\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$.

attrs.title: Constant etale sheaves on a curve

objects.body:
Let $r\geq0$. A field $K$ is *$C_r$* if every
homogeneous polynomial form $F\in K[x_1,\dots,x_N]$ of degree
$d>0$ in $N>d^r$ variables has a nontrivial zero in $K^N$.

Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field. A *curve over
$k$* is a separated scheme of finite
type over $k$ of dimension at most one; it is
*smooth* if it is smooth over $k$, *proper* if it is
proper over $k$, and *affine* if it is an affine scheme.
A *connected curve* is a curve that is nonempty, connected (as a
topological space) and of dimension one.
$\mathcal C$ denotes the category of smooth separated connected curves over
$k$.
(Here $k$ is required to be algebraically closed. A curve may be empty,
disconnected, or have zero-dimensional components; a statement that needs
a nonempty connected curve of dimension one says *connected curve*.
The Picard chapter also uses curves over arbitrary fields; its smooth
connected curves over algebraically closed fields are connected curves in
the present sense.)

Let $C$ be a connected curve over $k$. A
*divisor* on $C$ is a finite formal sum
$D=\sum_Pn_P[P]$ of closed points $P$ of $C$ with integer
coefficients; $\operatorname{Div}(C)$ is the free abelian group on
the closed points of $C$. For $f\in k(C)^*$
([def-sc-function-field]), its *divisor* is

$$
\operatorname{div}(f)=\sum_P v_P(f)\,[P],
$$

where $v_P$ is the normalized valuation of the local ring
$\mathcal O_{C,P}$; such divisors are *principal*. That
$\mathcal O_{C,P}$ is a discrete valuation ring when $C$ is
smooth, so that $v_P$ is defined, is
[lem-sc-smooth-regular] together with
[lem-sc-regular-dim1-dvr], and it is not part of the
definition.
The *divisor class group* is

$$
\operatorname{Cl}(C):=\operatorname{Div}(C)/\{\operatorname{div}(f):f\in k(C)^*\}.
$$

For $D=\sum n_P[P]$ the associated sub-$\mathcal O_C$-module of
the constant sheaf $k(C)$ is

$$
\mathcal O_C(D)(U):=\{f\in k(C):\operatorname{div}(f)|_U+D|_U\geq0\};
$$

that it is invertible for $C$ smooth, i.e. that
$D\mapsto[\mathcal O_C(D)]$ identifies
$\operatorname{Cl}(C)$ with $\operatorname{Pic}(C)$, is
recorded with the other properties of this construction, and it is not part of the
definition. The
*degree* of $D$ is

$$
\deg D:=\sum_Pn_P.
$$

(For reducible $C$ all objects above are defined componentwise.)

Let $C$ be a curve. An *effective Cartier divisor* on $C$ is a closed
subscheme $D\subseteq C$ which is locally defined by a single
non-zero-divisor: every point of $D$ has an open neighbourhood
$U$ and a non-zero-divisor $f\in\mathcal O_C(U)$ with
$D\cap U=V(f)$.

Let $X$ be a scheme and $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent
$\mathcal O_X$-module. The associated sheaf $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{et}}$
on the small etale site assigns to
$u:U\to X$ the group $\Gamma(U,u^*\mathcal F)$, with the usual
pullback restrictions. Here $u^*\mathcal F$ is pullback as a module
on a ringed space. That this presheaf is already a sheaf – so that
the assignment defines a sheaf and not merely a presheaf – is the
descent property of quasi-coherent modules,
[lem-sc-etale-qcoherent-descent], and it is not part of the
definition.

attrs.title: The etale sheaf associated with a quasi-coherent module

objects.body:
For a scheme $X$ and an integer $c\geq0$, write
$\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(X)\leq c$ if
$H^q(X,F)=0$ for every torsion
abelian etale sheaf
$F$ and every $q>c$, where cohomology is the ordinary
derived section functor of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].
For a field $K$, write $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(K)\leq c$
for this condition on $\operatorname{Spec}K$.

Let $X$ be a scheme and $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ be
$\mathcal O_X$-modules. The *Ext groups* are the right derived
functors of the contravariant functor
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(-,\mathcal G)$:

$$
\operatorname{Ext}^i_X(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)
:=R^i\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(-,\mathcal G)(\mathcal F)
$$

on the abelian category of $\mathcal O_X$-modules; in particular
$\operatorname{Ext}^0_X(\mathcal F,\mathcal G) =\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$.

Let $k\subseteq k'$ be an extension of algebraically closed fields
and let $C$ be a curve over $k$. Put

$$
\pi_{k'}:C_{k'}:=C\times_kk'\longrightarrow C,
\qquad
F_{k'}:=\pi_{k'}^{-1}F
$$

for an etale sheaf $F$ on $C_{\Et}$, and let

$$
\rho^q_{k'/k}(C,F):H^q(C_{\Et},F)\longrightarrow
H^q((C_{k'})_{\Et},F_{k'})
$$

be the pullback map.

attrs.title: Field extensions, base change, pullback maps

objects.body:
Let $C$ be a curve over $k$. The
*function field* $k(C)$ is the product of the stalks of the
structure sheaf at the generic points of the irreducible components
of $C$; equivalently the ring of rational functions on $C$. For
an integral curve it is the field of fractions of
$\mathcal O_C(U)$ for any nonempty affine open $U\subseteq C$.

attrs.title: The function field of a curve

objects.body:
Let $k$ be a field. A *geometrically integral smooth projective curve
over $k$* is a scheme $C$ over $k$ which is
smooth and projective over $k$
and geometrically integral over
$k$. Its *genus* is

$$
g(C):=\dim_kH^1(C,\mathcal O_C),
$$

finite because coherent cohomology of a proper scheme over a field is
finite-dimensional, and invariant under base change,
$g(C_{k'})=g(C)$ for every field extension $k'/k$, by flat base change
along the base change of [def-pc-base-change]. For an algebraically
closed extension $k'/k$ the base change $C_{k'}$ is a
proper smooth connected curve in the sense of the
algebraically closed conventions of the smooth-curve chapter, and
$g(C)=g(C_{k'})$ with the genus of [def-sc-genus]; in particular the
degree and $\operatorname{Pic}^0$ conventions of [def-sc-pic0] apply to
$C_{k'}$. The statements of the present chapter that are formulated over an
arbitrary field use this definition; the algebraically closed statements use
[def-sc-curves].

Let $k$ be a field and $c\geq1$. The *general linear group
scheme* is the affine scheme

$$
\mathrm{GL}_{c,k}:=\Spec k[x_{ij}:1\leq i,j\leq c]\bigl[1/\det\bigr],
\qquad
\det:=\sum_{\sigma\in\mathfrak S_c}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)
\prod_{i=1}^{c}x_{i\sigma(i)},
$$

with comultiplication $m^*(x_{ij})=\sum_{r=1}^{c}x_{ir}\otimes x_{rj}$,
counit $\varepsilon(x_{ij})=\delta_{ij}$ and antipode
$i^*(x_{ij})=(-1)^{i+j}M_{ji}/\det$, where $M_{ji}$ is the
determinant of the matrix obtained from $(x_{kl})$ by deleting row
$j$ and column $i$; the group-scheme axioms of
[def-sc-group-scheme] hold because matrix multiplication is
associative, $1$ is a unit and $A\cdot A^{\mathrm{adj}}=\det(A)\cdot1$
with $A^{\mathrm{adj}}=(M_{kl})$. Its $R$-points are
$\mathrm{GL}_c(R)$, the group of invertible $c\times c$ matrices over
$R$. The *special linear group scheme* is the closed
subgroup scheme

$$
\mathrm{SL}_{c,k}:=\Spec k[x_{ij}]/(\det-1)\subseteq\mathrm{GL}_{c,k}.
$$

The determinant defines a homomorphism
$\det:\mathrm{GL}_{c,k}\to\mathbf G_m$ with
[def-sc-gm-ga], dual to $t\mapsto\det$; it is multiplicative
because $\det(AB)=\det(A)\det(B)$.

attrs.title: The general and special linear group schemes

objects.body:
Let $C$ be a proper smooth connected curve over
an algebraically closed field $k$. The *genus* of $C$ is

$$
g(C):=\dim_kH^1(C,\mathcal O_C),
$$

finite because coherent cohomology of a proper scheme over a field
is finite-dimensional (coherent higher direct images of a proper
morphism are coherent: *reference: Stacks Project, Cohomology
of Schemes, Proposition 30.19.1, [Tag 02O5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02O5)*; this is the genus of
Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves, Definition 53.8.1,
[Tag 0BY7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BY7), which
