defines $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$ for a proper scheme $X$ of
dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, the present $C$).
Equivalently, by duality
$g=\dim_kH^0(C,\Omega^1_{C/k})$ (*reference: Stacks Project,
Algebraic Curves, Lemma 53.4.1, [Tag 0BS2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BS2), parts (5) and
(6)*). (For a smooth separated, not necessarily proper, connected curve the
genus used in this blueprint is the genus of a compactification
$\overline C$ of $C$, i.e. of a proper smooth connected curve containing
$C$ as an open subscheme with finite complement; this convention is
fixed explicitly at the single place where it is used, and it is the
compactification lemma below that provides the compactification.)

Let $k$ be a field. The *multiplicative group* is the
group scheme
$\mathbf G_m=\Spec k[t,t^{-1}]$, with comultiplication, counit and
antipode the $k$-algebra maps $m^*(t)=t\otimes t$,
$\varepsilon(t)=1$, $i^*(t)=t^{-1}$; the group-scheme axioms of
[def-sc-group-scheme] hold because the identities
$(t_1t_2)t_3=t_1(t_2t_3)$, $1\cdot t=t=t\cdot1$ and $t^{-1}t=1$
hold in the Laurent polynomial ring. The *additive group* is
$\mathbf G_a=\Spec k[y]$, with $m^*(y)=y\otimes1+1\otimes y$,
$\varepsilon(y)=0$, $i^*(y)=-y$; here the axioms are the
corresponding identities for addition. For $n\geq1$,

$$
\mu_n:=\Spec k[t]/(t^n-1)\subseteq\mathbf G_m
$$

is the *group scheme of $n$-th roots of unity*, and, when
$\operatorname{char}k=p>0$,

$$
\alpha_p:=\Spec k[y]/(y^p)\subseteq\mathbf G_a
$$

is the *Frobenius kernel* of $\mathbf G_a$; both are closed
subgroup schemes, the closed
immersion being the one induced by the displayed surjections of
coordinate rings. The group schemes $\mathbf G_m$ and $\mu_n$ are
the ones occurring in the
$\mathbf G_m$-torsors and in the
Kummer sequence of the smooth-curve chapter.

attrs.title: The multiplicative group, the additive group, and their finite subgroups

objects.body:
Let $X$ be a scheme (for instance a curve $C$ as in
[def-sc-curves]), and let $\mathbf G_m$ be the sheaf
$U\mapsto\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)^{\times}$ on the small etale site
$X_{\Et}$. A
$\mathbf G_m$-*torsor* on $X_{\Et}$ is an etale sheaf $T$
on $X_{\Et}$ together with an action
$\mathbf G_m\times T\to T$ which is free and transitive, such that
$T$ is locally isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m$ with its translation
action: there is an etale covering $\{U_i\to X\}$ with
$T|_{U_i}\cong\mathbf G_m|_{U_i}$. A torsor is *trivial* if
it is isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m$. More generally, for an abelian
sheaf $G$ on $X_{\Et}$ a $G$-*torsor* is defined in the same way
with $G$ in place of $\mathbf G_m$; replacing the etale site by the
Zariski site $X_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ and $\mathbf G_m$ by
$\mathcal O_X^{\times}$ gives the notion of a *Zariski*
$\mathcal O_X^{\times}$-torsor.

Let $k$ be a field. A $k$-*group scheme* is a $k$-scheme
$G$ together with morphisms $m:G\times_kG\to G$ (multiplication),
$i:G\to G$ (inverse) and $e:\operatorname{Spec}k\to G$ (identity)
such that the usual associativity, unit and inverse diagrams
commute; equivalently, the functor of points
$R\mapsto G(R)$ takes values in groups. The group scheme is
*commutative* if $m\circ s=m$, where $s$ swaps the two
factors. A *homomorphism* $f:G\to H$ of group schemes is a
morphism of schemes compatible with the multiplications; the
*kernel* of $f$ is the closed subgroup scheme

$$
\ker f:=G\times_{H,f,e_H}\operatorname{Spec}k.
$$

(That this fibre product is a closed subgroup scheme is
[lem-sc-kernel-subgroup].) The group scheme $G$ is *finite* if its
structure morphism $G\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is finite in the sense
of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]; then $G=\operatorname{Spec}A$
with $A=\Gamma(G,\mathcal O_G)$ a finite-dimensional $k$-algebra, and
the *order* of $G$ is

$$
\lvert G\rvert:=\dim_k\Gamma(G,\mathcal O_G).
$$

The group scheme $G$ is *étale* over $k$ if its structure morphism is
étale in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. A finite
$k$-algebra $A$ is a *finite étale $k$-algebra* if it is isomorphic to
a finite product $L_1\times\dots\times L_r$ of finite separable field
extensions $L_j$ of $k$. For finite $G$, the group scheme $G$ is étale
over $k$ if and only if $\Gamma(G,\mathcal O_G)$ is a finite étale
$k$-algebra ([lem-sc-finite-etale-algebra-criterion]).

Let $G$ be a group scheme over a
field $k$. A *closed subgroup scheme* of $G$ is a closed
subscheme $Z\subseteq G$ such that for every $k$-algebra $R$ the
subset $Z(R)\subseteq G(R)$ is a subgroup of the group $G(R)$. A
*subgroup scheme* of $G$ is a $k$-group scheme $Z$ together
with a homomorphism $i:Z\to G$ whose
induced maps $i(R):Z(R)\to G(R)$ are injective for every $k$-algebra
$R$. The subgroup scheme is *normal* if $i(R)(Z(R))$ is a
normal subgroup of $G(R)$ for every $R$.

Let $G$ be a group scheme over a field
$k$ with multiplication $m$, inverse $i$, unit $e$ and structure
morphism $p:G\to\Spec k$, and let $g\in G(k)$ be a $k$-point. The
*left translation* by $g$ is the composite

$$
L_g:G\xrightarrow{\ (g\circ p,\ \mathrm{id}_G)\ }G\times_kG
\xrightarrow{\ m\ }G,
$$

the *right translation* by $g$ is
$R_g=m\circ(\mathrm{id}_G,g\circ p)$, and *conjugation* by $g$
is $c_g=L_g\circ R_{g^{-1}}$. For a closed
subgroup scheme
$Z\subseteq G$ the *translate* $gZ$ is the image of the
composite $L_g\circ j$, where $j:Z\hookrightarrow G$ is the closed
immersion.

Let $X$ be a proper scheme of dimension $g$ over a field $k$
and $\mathcal M$ an ample invertible
$\mathcal O_X$-module. The *degree* of $X$ with respect to
$\mathcal M$ is

$$
\deg_{\mathcal M}(X):=g!\cdot
\bigl(\text{leading coefficient of }m\mapsto\chi(X,\mathcal
M^{\otimes m})\bigr),
$$

the leading coefficient being taken for the function
$m\mapsto\chi(X,\mathcal M^{\otimes m})$ of $m$. That this
function is a numerical polynomial in $m$ of total degree at most
$g$ – the Hilbert polynomial of $\mathcal M$ – so that the
leading coefficient, and hence the degree, is well defined, is
[lem-sc-hilbert-polynomial], and it is not part of the
definition.

attrs.title: The Hilbert degree of an ample line bundle

objects.body:
Let $X$ be a scheme (for instance a curve $C$ as in [def-sc-curves],
in which case one speaks of invertible $\mathcal O_C$-modules). An
*invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module* is a quasi-coherent
$\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal L$ which is locally free of rank
one for the Zariski topology (equivalently: there is an
$\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal L^{-1}$ with
$\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal L^{-1}\cong\mathcal O_X$). Its
*dual* is

$$
\mathcal L^{\vee}:=\mathcal{H}om_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal L,\mathcal O_X).
$$

Let $A,B$ be abelian varieties
over $k$. An *isogeny* $f:A\to B$ is a surjective
homomorphism with finite kernel; the
*degree* of an isogeny is the order of its kernel.

Let $C$ be a geometrically integral smooth
projective curve over a field $k$, of genus $g=g(C)$
([def-sc-general-curve]). A
*Jacobian of $C$* is a pair $(J,\varphi)$ consisting of an
abelian variety $J$ over $k$
of dimension $g$ together with an isomorphism of group-valued
functors

$$
\varphi:\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }h_J,
$$

where $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$ is the degree-zero part of the
Picard functor
([def-sc-pic0], [def-sc-picard-functor]); that is, a
Jacobian of $C$ is a representing object of
$\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$ in the category of abelian varieties
of dimension $g$ over $k$, together with the representing
isomorphism. Whether such a pair exists, and which properties it
has, is not part of this definition. When a Jacobian
$(J,\varphi)$ of $C$ is fixed, we write $J_C:=J$ and call
$J_C$ the *Jacobian* of $C$, so that $\varphi$ is the
canonical identification $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\cong h_{J_C}$.

Let $C$ be a smooth curve over $k$.
The *sheaf of Kähler differentials* of $C$ over $k$ is

$$
\Omega^1_{C/k}:=\Delta^*\bigl(\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2\bigr),
$$

where $\Delta:C\to C\times_kC$ is the diagonal immersion and
$\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_{C\times_kC}$ the ideal sheaf of the
diagonal; equivalently, on an affine open
$U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq C$, $\Omega^1_{C/k}|_U$ is the
sheaf associated with the $A$-module $\Omega^1_{A/k}$ of Kähler
differentials of the $k$-algebra $A$ with its universal
derivation $d:A\to\Omega^1_{A/k}$, the standard affine description.
The *canonical sheaf* of $C$ is

$$
\omega_C:=\Omega^1_{C/k}.
$$

attrs.title: Kähler differentials and the canonical sheaf of a smooth curve

objects.body:
Let $C$ be a curve over $k$ and let
$n$ be prime to $\operatorname{char}k$. The
*Kummer sequence* is the sequence of etale sheaves on
$C_{\Et}$

$$
1\longrightarrow\mu_n\longrightarrow\mathbf G_m
\xrightarrow{\ t\mapsto t^n\ }\mathbf G_m\longrightarrow1.
$$

Let $k$ be algebraically closed, let $C$ be a
curve over $k$, let $n\geq1$ be prime
to $\operatorname{char}k$, and let

$$
\mu_n(U):=\{x\in\mathcal O_U(U):x^n=1\},\qquad U\to C\text{ etale},
$$

be the etale sheaf of $n$-th roots of unity. Given a root of unity
$\zeta\in\mu_n(k)$, the *canonical trivialization associated
to $\zeta$* is the isomorphism of etale sheaves

$$
\theta_\zeta:\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\mu_n,
\qquad a\longmapsto\zeta^a.
$$

attrs.title: The canonical trivialization of the constant sheaf

objects.body:
Let $A$ be an abelian variety
over $k$ and $n\geq1$. The $n$-th *multiplication map*
$[n]:A\to A$ is the
homomorphism given on points by
$a\mapsto a+\cdots+a$ ($n$ summands). The $n$-*torsion
subgroup scheme* is the kernel

$$
A[n]:=\ker([n]),
$$

a closed subgroup scheme of $A$ ([def-sc-group-scheme], [lem-sc-kernel-subgroup]).

Let $X$ be an integral scheme with function field
$K=k(X)$ ([def-sc-function-field]). The *normalization
of $X$ in $K$* is

$$
X^{\nu}:=\operatorname{\underline{Spec}}_X\bigl(\widetilde{\mathcal O_X}\bigr),
$$

where $\widetilde{\mathcal O_X}$ is the integral closure of
$\mathcal O_X$ in the constant sheaf $K$, together with the
canonical morphism $\nu:X^{\nu}\to X$. Finiteness is a
separate property of this morphism; it is not part of the definition.

Let $k$ be a field and
$\mathbf P^1_k=\operatorname{Proj}k[x_0,x_1]$. The
*standard affine cover* is

$$
U_0:=D(x_0)=\operatorname{Spec}k[t],\quad t:=x_1/x_0,
\qquad
U_1:=D(x_1)=\operatorname{Spec}k[s],\quad s:=x_0/x_1,
$$

$$
U_{01}:=U_0\cap U_1=\operatorname{Spec}k[t,t^{-1}].
$$

For $d\in\mathbf Z$, a *twisted structure sheaf*
$\mathcal O(d)$ on $\mathbf P^1_k$ is an
$\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1_k}$-module together with generating
sections $g_0\in\Gamma(U_0,\mathcal O(d))$ and
$g_1\in\Gamma(U_1,\mathcal O(d))$ that trivialize it over $U_0$
and over $U_1$ and satisfy the glueing relation

$$
g_0=t^{-d}g_1\qquad\text{over }U_{01}.
$$

For $d=1$ we take $g_0=x_0$ and $g_1=x_1$, so that
$\mathcal O(1)$ is the tautological bundle with the glueing
$x_0=t^{-1}x_1$.

attrs.title: The standard affine cover and the twists on $\mathbf P^1_k$

objects.body:
Let $C$ be a proper smooth connected curve over
algebraically closed $k$. The *degree* is the homomorphism

$$
\deg:\operatorname{Pic}(C)\to\mathbf Z,\qquad
\deg[\mathcal O(D)]=\deg D,
$$

of the divisor class group of [def-sc-divisor], transported
across the identification $\operatorname{Cl}(C)\cong \operatorname{Pic}(C)$ of [lem-sc-divisor-class-curve]; it
sends the class of a $k$-rational point
to $1$. That it is well defined, i.e. that it vanishes on
principal divisors, is [lem-sc-deg-principal-zero], and it is
not part of the definition. Put

$$
\operatorname{Pic}^0(C):=\ker(\deg).
$$

Let $C$ be a proper smooth connected curve over a
field $k$. The *Picard functor*

$$
\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}:(k\text{-algebras})\longrightarrow\mathbf{Ab},
\qquad \operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}:=
\bigl(R\longmapsto\operatorname{Pic}(C\times_k\operatorname{Spec}R)\bigr)^{\#}_{\mathrm{fppf}},
$$

is the fppf sheafification of the presheaf of
invertible modules; for
$d\in\mathbf Z$, $\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}$ is the subfunctor
of $\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}$ of invertible modules of fibrewise
degree $d$ (degree $d$ on every geometric fibre). This
definition fixes the fppf sheafification and its subfunctors
$\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}$, and nothing else: no
representability of $\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}$, and no openness
or closedness of the subfunctors $\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}$, is
assumed here.

attrs.title: The Picard functor of a proper curve

objects.body:
Let $C$ be a curve. The
*Picard group* $\operatorname{Pic}(C)$ is the set of
isomorphism classes of
invertible $\mathcal O_C$-modules, with the group law induced by tensor product: the
unit is $\mathcal O_C$ and the inverse of an invertible module
$\mathcal L$ is its dual $\mathcal L^{\vee}$. That
$\mathcal L^{\vee}$ is invertible and that this law satisfies
the group axioms is [lem-sc-pic-group], and it is not part of
the definition. (*Stacks Project, Definition 18.32.6, Tag
[040C](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/040C)*.)

A curve $C$ over $k$ is
*quasi-projective* if it admits an open immersion into a closed
subscheme of some projective space, equivalently a locally closed
immersion $C\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_k$.

For an abelian sheaf $F$ on the
small Zariski site of $X$,
let $H^q(X_{\rm Zar},F)$ be the $q$-th right derived
functor of $F\mapsto F(X)$. Equivalently take the
cohomology of the section complex of an injective resolution,
using the ordinary resolution convention of
[def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions].

An abelian sheaf $F$ on a topological space $X$ is
*flasque* if $F(V)\to F(U)$ is surjective for every
inclusion of open subsets $U\subset V\subset X$.

attrs.title: Flasque sheaves on the Zariski site

objects.body:
For a scheme $X$,
the site $X_{\rm Zar}$ has its open subschemes as objects,
inclusions as morphisms, and jointly surjective open families
as coverings. An abelian sheaf on this site assigns abelian
groups to opens and satisfies the usual gluing and uniqueness
axioms for an open covering.

Fix a scheme $T$ carrying a coefficient stage $\Lambda$ and a site — the
*small étale* or the *small pro-étale* site of
def:weil-pbc-etale-site and def:weil-pbc-proetale-site. The
*ambient* categories are the ordinary derived categories of
$\Lambda_T$-modules

$$
D(T,\Lambda),\quad D^+(T,\Lambda),\quad D^-(T,\Lambda),\quad D^b(T,\Lambda),
$$

together with, for a set of primes $P$ invertible on $T$, the full
subcategory $D^+_{P\text{-tor}}(T,\Lambda)$ of complexes whose geometric
stalks are torsion with prime divisors in $P$
(sbc-def-derived-categories-with-allowable-torsion). The *small*
categories are the full subcategories

$$
\Dbc(T,\Lambda)\subseteq D^b(T,\Lambda),\qquad
\Dctf(T,\Lambda)\subseteq\Dbc(T,\Lambda),\qquad
D_c^{[a,b]}(T,\Lambda)\subseteq\Dbc(T,\Lambda)
$$

of bounded constructible complexes, of bounded constructible complexes of
finite Tor amplitude, and of bounded constructible complexes with cohomology
concentrated in $[a,b]$
(def:weil-finite-torsion-constructibility,
def:weil-finite-tor-amplitude,
def:weil-constructible-intervals); at the field stages
$\Dctf=\Dbc$ by definition.

In the setting of [def-sf-datum], let $K,L\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$.
The *mixed-support cup product* is the composite

$$
\smile_c:R\Gamma_c(X,K)\otimes^L_\Lambda R\Gamma(X,L)\longrightarrow
R\Gamma_c\bigl(X,K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}L\bigr)
$$

of the projection transformation for $Ra_{X!}$ applied to the pair $(K,L)$
and the map induced by the counit $La_X^*Ra_{X*}L\to L$; the same
construction at the other coefficient stages is obtained by levelwise
application and transport, and it is associative, unital and
graded-commutative.

Fix the global finite-field datum
$(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a
finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and
uniformizer $\varpi_E$, an integer $n\ge1$, and put
$A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and
$\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ as in
def:weil-derived-complete-integral,
def:weil-rationalization-karoubi,
def:weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients. A *six-functor
datum* is the datum of the
six-functor datum of [thm-weil-six-operations] —
the categories $D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$, the functors $Lf^*,Rf_*,Rf_!, Rf^!$, $-\otimes^L_\Lambda-$, $R\mathcal H om_\Lambda(-,-)$, the
exchange and projection
transformations, the compact-support
direct image $Rf_!=R\bar f_*j_!$ for a compactification, and the
exceptional inverse image
— subject to the following axioms, for all composable separated
finite-type morphisms and all $K,L$ in the stated finite-Tor domains:

1. ****(A1)**** $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$ and $Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$, with the
pasted units and counits for composites;
1. ****(A2)**** base change: $Lg^*Rf_!\cong Rf'_!Lg'^*$ for every
Cartesian square, and $Lg^*Rf_*\cong Rf'_*Lg'^*$ for proper $f$ or smooth
$g$;
1. ****(A3)**** the projection transformation is an isomorphism
([def-sf-pf]);
1. ****(A4)**** the composition law $R(g\circ f)_!\cong Rg_!Rf_!$
with its pentagon, and $Rf_!\cong Rf_*$ for proper $f$;
1. ****(A5)**** compatibility of all of the above with finite
reduction, scalar extension, and the pro-étale realization;
1. ****(A6)**** the dualizing functor
$D_X=R\mathcal H om_X(-,\omega_X)$ is a contravariant exact anti-equivalence
of $D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ with $K\to D_XD_XK$ an isomorphism (Verdier
biduality).

This is an axiomatized framework: a formal consequence may use only
the clauses explicitly invoked in its proof. For the concrete coefficient
system each clause needs its own verification on the stated domain; the
definition itself does not discharge those verification obligations.

Fix the global finite-field datum, a prime $\ell\ne p$, an integer
$n\geq1$, $A=A_{E,n}$ with the
finite-torsion
coefficient convention, $k=\Fbar$, finite-type $k$-schemes $Y$ and
$\overline X$, and a proper
finite-type $k$-morphism $p:\overline X\to Y$. Use the
small pro-étale sites, the
derived direct image $Rp_*$, and
the cohomology-sheaf
functor $\mathcal H^r$. Call a sheaf $\mathcal F$ of $A$-modules on
$\overline X_{\Proet}$ a *coefficient sheaf of the blueprint's class*
if it is of étale origin,
$\mathcal F\cong\nu_{\overline X}^*\mathcal G$ for a sheaf $\mathcal G$
of $A$-modules on $\overline X_{\Et}$ in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], the comparison morphism
$\nu_{\overline X}$ being that of
[def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]; this is the class of
[def-sf-fullcd-used-class], read on the source $\overline X$, and by
[lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] it is also the class of
constructible pro-étale coefficient sheaves. For an integer
$c\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, write
$\operatorname{FullCD}_{\mathrm{cls}}(p,A;c)$ if

$$
\mathcal H^r(Rp_*\mathcal F)=0\qquad(r\in\mathbf Z,\ r>c)
$$

for every coefficient sheaf $\mathcal F$ of that class on
$\overline X_{\Proet}$, and if, for every object $V\to Y$ of
$Y_{\Proet}$ and every such $\mathcal F$, the base change
$p_V:\overline X\times_YV\to V$ of $p$ satisfies

$$
\mathcal H^r\bigl(R(p_V)_*(\mathcal F|_{\overline X\times_YV})\bigr)=0
\qquad(r\in\mathbf Z,\ r>c),
$$

the restriction $\mathcal F|_{\overline X\times_YV}$ being the pullback
along the projection $\overline X\times_YV\to\overline X$, which is again
of étale origin on the base-changed source by
[lem-sf-fullcd-class-restriction]. The two displayed clauses are the
two clauses of [def-weil-full-cohomological-dimension] with the
quantifier over *all* sheaves of $A$-modules replaced by the
quantifier over this class, and nothing else is changed: in particular
$\operatorname{FullCD}(p,A;c)$ implies
$\operatorname{FullCD}_{\mathrm{cls}}(p,A;c)$ for every $c$, the class
being a class of sheaves. The class-restricted datum is the form
the blueprint uses, and it is the form referred to as the class form below.

Fix the global finite-field datum, a prime $\ell\ne p$, $n\geq1$,
$A=A_{E,n}$, the algebraically closed field $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$,
and a finite-type $k$-scheme $\overline X$. Call a sheaf
$\mathcal F$ of $A$-modules on the small pro-étale site
$\overline X_{\Proet}$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] a
*coefficient sheaf of the blueprint's class* if it is of étale
origin: $\mathcal F\cong\nu_{\overline X}^*\mathcal G$ for a sheaf
$\mathcal G$ of $A$-modules on the small étale site, the comparison
morphism $\nu_{\overline X}$ being that of
[def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Equivalent descriptions of
this class are the constructible sheaves in the intrinsic sense of
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] and the complexes of
[def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] on the étale side, by
[lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]; the description by étale
origin is the one used below.

attrs.title: The coefficient class of the blueprint

objects.body:
For $i=1,2$ let $f_i:X_i\to Y_i$ be separated of finite type between
finite-type $k$-schemes, exceptionally admissible in the sense of
[def-trf-admissibility] where $Rf^!$ occurs — which every such morphism is,
no ambient datum being assumed — (with $Rf^!$ the exceptional
inverse image of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] and $Rf_!$ the
compact-support direct image of [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed],
[def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]), put $f=f_1\times f_2$, and let
$L_i\in\Dctf(Y_i,\Lambda)$, $B_i\in\Dctf(X_i,\Lambda)$.

3pt
1. **(i)** The $!$-Künneth
$\mathrm{Ku}_!:Rf_!(B_1\boxtimes B_2)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } Rf_{1!}B_1\boxtimes Rf_{2!}B_2$ is [thm-sf-kunneth-relative] for the base
$B=Y_1\times Y_2$, using
$X_1\times X_2=(X_1\times Y_2)\times_B(Y_1\times X_2)$. It is an isomorphism.
1. **(ii)** The *exceptional Künneth*
$\alpha:Rf_1^!L_1\boxtimes Rf_2^!L_2\to Rf^!(L_1\boxtimes L_2)$ is the
exceptional adjoint of
$$
Rf_!\bigl(Rf_1^!L_1\boxtimes Rf_2^!L_2\bigr)
\xrightarrow{\ \mathrm{Ku}_!\ }
Rf_{1!}Rf_1^!L_1\boxtimes Rf_{2!}Rf_2^!L_2
\xrightarrow{\ \varepsilon_1\boxtimes\varepsilon_2\ }
L_1\boxtimes L_2 ,
$$
where the $\varepsilon_i$ are the counits of $Rf_{i!}\dashv Rf_i^!$
(axiom (A1) of [def-sf-datum]).
1. **(iii)** For $E_i\in\Dctf(Y_i,\Lambda)$, on the same scheme $Y_i$ as
$L_i$, the *external Hom* map
$$
\beta:\RHom(E_1,L_1)\boxtimes\RHom(E_2,L_2)
\longrightarrow\RHom\bigl(E_1\boxtimes E_2,L_1\boxtimes L_2\bigr)
$$
is the tensor–Hom transpose of the two evaluations, with the tensor symmetry
and its Koszul signs.
1. **(iv)** For separated finite-type $k$-schemes $X,Y$ whose structure
morphism $a_Y$ and product projection
$p_X=\operatorname{id}_X\times a_Y:X\times Y\to X$ satisfy the
exceptional-adjoint admissibility of [def-trf-admissibility] (the inputs
for $\omega_Y$ and $\mathbb D_Y$, for $Rp_X^!$, and for
$\alpha_{\operatorname{id}_X,a_Y}$), for
$M\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ and $N\in\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$, with
$p_X,p_Y$ the projections of $X\times Y$, and with the Verdier dual
$\mathbb D_Y$ and dualizing complex $\omega_Y=Ra_Y^!\Lambda$ of [def-sf-pf], the
*Künneth–Verdier* map is
$$
\begin{aligned}
\kappa_{M,N}:M\boxtimes\mathbb D_YN
&\xrightarrow{\ \beta\ }\RHom\bigl(p_Y^*N,M\boxtimes\omega_Y\bigr)\\
&\xrightarrow{\ \RHom(1,\alpha_{\operatorname{id}_X,a_Y})\ }
\RHom\bigl(p_Y^*N,Rp_X^!M\bigr),
\end{aligned}
$$
using the unit identifications $\RHom(\Lambda_X,M)=M$ and
$\Lambda_X\boxtimes N=p_Y^*N$; here $\beta$ is applied to the pairs
$(E_1,L_1)=(\Lambda_X,M)$ on $X$ and $(E_2,L_2)=(N,\omega_Y)$ on $Y$.

Only $\mathrm{Ku}_!$ is built from isomorphisms; invertibility of
$\alpha,\beta,\kappa$ is the content of [prop-trf-exceptional-kunneth], [prop-trf-external-hom]
and [thm-trf-kunneth-verdier].

Uses: [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], [def-sf-datum], [def-sf-pf], [def-trf-admissibility], [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], [thm-sf-kunneth-relative]

In the setting of [def-sf-datum], an *orientation datum* consists
of, for every smooth separated finite-type $f:X\to Y$ of pure relative
dimension $d$, an isomorphism

$$
\gamma_{f,\Lambda_Y}:\ Lf^*\Lambda_Y(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf^!\Lambda_Y,
$$

natural in $Y$, compatible with composition, with étale base change,
with finite reduction, scalar extension, and the pro-étale realization,
and equal to the canonical orientation of the affine line
$\mathbf A^1_Y\to Y$ on the projection; for $f=a_X$ it reads
$\omega_{X,\Lambda}\cong\Lambda_X(d)[2d]$.

In the setting of [def-sf-datum] and [def-sf-orientation], let
$X$ be smooth, separated of finite type and geometrically connected of pure
dimension $d$ over $k$, with structure morphism
$a_X:X\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ (whose exceptional inverse image is the
constructible one of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]; no admissibility
hypothesis is imposed), and assume either that $X$ is
proper, or that $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ for a smooth, separated finite-type,
geometrically connected $k_0$-scheme $X_0$ (in the latter case no
properness is required); these are the hypotheses of global Verdier
duality. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ be such that $K^\vee$ is perfect
on $X$. The
*derived Poincare pairing* is the composite

$$
\beta_K:\ R\Gamma_c(X,K)\otimes^L_\Lambda
R\Gamma\bigl(X,K^\vee(d)\bigr)[2d]\longrightarrow\Lambda,
$$

$$
\begin{array}{lll}
R\Gamma_c(X,K)\otimes^L_\Lambda R\Gamma(X,K^\vee(d))[2d]
&\xrightarrow{\ \smile_c\ }&
R\Gamma_c\bigl(X,K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}K^\vee(d)\bigr)[2d]\\[2pt]
&\xrightarrow{\ R\Gamma_c(\operatorname{ev}_K(d))[2d]\ }&
R\Gamma_c\bigl(X,\Lambda_X(d)\bigr)[2d]\\[2pt]
&\xrightarrow{\ \operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{a_X,\Lambda}\ }&
\Lambda,
\end{array}
$$

where $\smile_c$ is the mixed-support cup product of
[def-sf-cup], $\operatorname{ev}_K$ is the
evaluation of [def-sf-pf], and
$\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{a_X,\Lambda}$ is the normalized smooth
trace, i.e. the counit of $Ra_{X!}\dashv Ra_X^!$ read through the
orientation of [def-sf-orientation]. A morphism
$b:C\otimes^L_\Lambda D\to\Lambda$ of point complexes is *perfect* if
its tensor–internal-Hom adjoint $D\to C^\vee$ is an isomorphism.

In the setting of [def-sf-datum], let $a_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be
the structure morphism of a separated finite-type $k$-scheme and put
$\omega_X=Ra_X^!\Lambda$. For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ the
*Verdier dual* and the *coefficient dual* are

$$
\mathbb D_XK=R\mathcal H om_X(K,\omega_X),\qquad
K^\vee=R\mathcal H om_X(K,\Lambda_X),
$$

and for a separated finite-type $f:X\to Y$ the *projection
transformation* is

$$
\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}:Rf_!K\otimes^L_\Lambda L\longrightarrow
Rf_!\bigl(K\otimes^L_\Lambda Lf^*L\bigr)
$$

of [def-exchange-projection]; axiom (A3) is the assertion
that it is an isomorphism, and it is verified for the concrete
compact-support direct image in [thm-sf-pf-finite], [prop-sf-pf-reduction], [thm-sf-pf-adic], [thm-sf-pf-field], [thm-sf-pf-proetale] and [prop-sf-pf-coherence].

attrs.title: Coefficient dual, Verdier dual, and the projection formula

objects.body:
Fix the global finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with valuation ring
$\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, an integer $n\ge1$, and put
$A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. The *coefficient stages* are
$\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$, with constructibility, finite Tor
amplitude, constructible intervals and Tate twists as in
def:weil-finite-torsion-constructibility,
def:weil-finite-tor-amplitude,
def:weil-constructible-intervals and def:coefficient-twists.
Morphisms are separated of finite type.

Fix the global finite-field datum, a prime $\ell\ne p$, an integer
$n\geq1$, and put $A=A_{E,n}$, a finite local ring; every sheaf of
$A$-modules is then a torsion sheaf of abelian groups. Let
$k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes and
let $f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type
morphism. For $N\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, write
$\operatorname{UDV}(f,A;N)$ if

$$
R^qf_*M=0\qquad(q>N)
$$

for the higher direct images of
$f$ on the small étale sites and for
every sheaf $M$ of $A$-modules on $X_{\Et}$. This is the vanishing
clause of the finiteness predicate $\mathrm{FIN}$ of
[def-weil-pbc-constructible-direct-image-finiteness], read on the
étale site and imposed on all module sheaves rather than on the
constructible ones only.

attrs.title: Uniform vanishing of the higher direct images

objects.body:
An *abelian category* is a preadditive category with a zero object and finite
biproducts, which admits kernels and cokernels, in which every monomorphism
is a kernel and every epimorphism is a cokernel.

Let $v:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a left exact additive
[def-sp-left-exact-additive] functor. An object $X\in\mathcal A$ is
$v$-*acyclic* if $R^nv(X)=0$ for every $n>0$, where $R^nv$ is the right
derived functor [def-sp-left-exact-additive] of $v$. In the sheaf case
relevant to the proper-base-change chapter: for the etale direct image
$v=f_*$, $f_*$-acyclic means $R^qf_*(X)=0$ for $q>0$.

attrs.title: Acyclic objects for a left exact functor

objects.body:
A *composable pair* $(F,G)$ consists of left exact additive
[def-sp-left-exact-additive] functors

$$
 \mathcal A\xrightarrow{\ F\ }\mathcal B\xrightarrow{\ G\ }\mathcal C
$$

between Grothendieck abelian categories
[def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. $F$ *sends injectives to $G$-acyclics* if
$F(I)$ is $G$-acyclic [def-sp-acyclic] for every injective
[def-sp-injective-resolutions] object $I\in\mathcal A$.

attrs.title: Composable pairs with an acyclicity condition

objects.body:
In the situation of [def-sp-exact-couple], regard all cycle and boundary
objects as subobjects of the initial page $E_2$. Set $Z_2=E_2$, $B_2=0$.
Given $E_r=Z_r/B_r$, define $Z_{r+1}\subseteq Z_r$ as the inverse image of
$\ker d_r$, and $B_{r+1}\subseteq Z_r$ as the inverse image of
$\operatorname{im}d_r$ under $Z_r\twoheadrightarrow E_r$, component by
component. Thus $E_{r+1}=Z_{r+1}/B_{r+1}$, the $Z_r$ decrease, and the $B_r$
increase inside $E_2$. When these limits exist, put
$Z_\infty=\bigcap_rZ_r$, $B_\infty=\bigcup_rB_r$, and
$E_\infty=Z_\infty/B_\infty$. The couple is *regular* if each
$B_r^{p,q}\subseteq E_2^{p,q}$ is eventually constant. It is *complete* if
the subobjects $\operatorname{im}(\alpha^r:D^{p+r,q-r}\to D^{p,q})$ have zero
intersection for every $(p,q)$. It *converges to the filtration
[def-sp-filtration] of an object $A$* if

$$
 E_\infty^{p,q}\cong\operatorname{gr}^pA^{p+q}
$$

compatibly with the structure maps (the *abutment*).

Let $\mathcal C$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. A *double complex*
$D^{\bullet,\bullet}$ in $\mathcal C$ is a family of objects $D^{p,q}$
($p,q\in\mathbb Z$) with morphisms

$$
 d_I:D^{p,q}\to D^{p+1,q},\qquad d_{II}:D^{p,q}\to D^{p,q+1}
$$

such that $d_I\circ d_I=0$, $d_{II}\circ d_{II}=0$ and
$d_I\circ d_{II}=d_{II}\circ d_I$. It is *first-quadrant* if $D^{p,q}=0$
unless $p\geq0$ and $q\geq0$. For each $p$ the *$p$-th column*
$(D^{p,\bullet},d_{II})$ and for each $q$ the *$q$-th row*
$(D^{\bullet,q},d_I)$ are complexes; their cohomology objects are written

$$
 H^q_{II}(D^{p,\bullet}):=H^q(D^{p,\bullet},d_{II}),\qquad
 H^p_{I}(D^{\bullet,q}):=H^p(D^{\bullet,q},d_I).
$$

Since $d_I$ commutes with $d_{II}$, it induces morphisms
$H^q_{II}(D^{p,\bullet})\to H^q_{II}(D^{p+1,\bullet})$, making
$H^q_{II}(D)$ a complex in the first index, with cohomology
$H^p_IH^q_{II}(D)$; symmetrically $d_{II}$ makes $H^p_I(D)$ a complex in the
second index, with cohomology $H^q_{II}H^p_I(D)$.

For a first-quadrant double complex the *total complex*
$\operatorname{Tot}(D)$ is

$$
 \operatorname{Tot}(D)^n:=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}D^{p,q},\qquad
 d|_{D^{p,q}}:=d_I+(-1)^pd_{II}:D^{p,q}\to D^{p+1,q}\oplus D^{p,q+1};
$$

the sum is finite (only $0\leq p\leq n$ contribute, and
$\operatorname{Tot}(D)^n=0$ for $n<0$), and $d\circ d=0$ because
$d_I^2=d_{II}^2=0$ and the two cross terms $(-1)^{p+1}d_{II}d_I$ and
$(-1)^pd_Id_{II}$ cancel.

The *first* and *second filtrations* of $\operatorname{Tot}(D)$ are the
decreasing filtrations [def-sp-filtration]

$$
 {}'F^p\operatorname{Tot}(D)^n:=\bigoplus_{i\geq p}D^{i,n-i},\qquad
 {}''F^q\operatorname{Tot}(D)^n:=\bigoplus_{j\geq q}D^{n-j,j}
$$

(filtration by the first, resp. the second, degree). Both are filtrations by
subcomplexes, since $d_I$ raises the first degree by one and preserves the
second, while $d_{II}$ preserves the first and raises the second. In total
degree $n$ both satisfy $F^0\operatorname{Tot}(D)^n=\operatorname{Tot}(D)^n$
and $F^{n+1}\operatorname{Tot}(D)^n=0$, so they are finite in each degree.
Their graded pieces are the complexes

$$
 \operatorname{gr}^p_{'F}\operatorname{Tot}(D)=D^{p,\bullet-p}
 \ \text{with differential }(-1)^pd_{II},\qquad
 \operatorname{gr}^q_{''F}\operatorname{Tot}(D)=D^{\bullet-q,q}
 \ \text{with differential }d_I .
$$

(Stacks Project, Homological Algebra: double complexes and their associated
total complexes, and the two filtrations used for the spectral sequences of
a double complex.)

attrs.title: First-quadrant double complexes, total complex and the two filtrations

objects.body:
The spectral sequence statements used in the proper-base-change chapter are
obtained from the statements above by the substitutions: the abelian category
[def-sp-abelian] $\mathcal A$ is $\operatorname{Ab}(X_{\mathrm{et}})$
(Grothendieck abelian [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]), the left exact additive
[def-sp-left-exact-additive] functor $v$ is the etale direct image $f_*$ with
right derived functors $R^nf_*$, $K\in\operatorname{Ch}^+(\mathcal A)$ is
$K\in\Dplus(X_{\mathrm{et}})$ (with the K-injective resolution
[def-sp-kinjective-bridge] presentation of the proper-base-change chapter),
the homological functors $\Phi$ are $Rf_*$, $Rf'_*g'^{-1}$, $g^{-1}Rf_*$, the
natural transformation $\eta$ of couples is the derived exchange morphism
$\Ex_{\square,K}$ (introduced in the conventions of the proper-base-change
chapter), and the composite pair $(F,G)$ is $(f_*,h_*)$ for $X\to Y\to Z$.

Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. An *exact couple*
$(D,E,\alpha,f,g)$ inside the bigraded objects $D=\bigoplus D^{p,q}$,
$E=\bigoplus E^{p,q}$ consists of maps of bidegrees

$$
 \alpha:D^{p,q}\to D^{p-1,q+1}\quad(-1,+1),\qquad
 f:E^{p,q}\to D^{p+2,q-1}\quad(+2,-1),\qquad
 g:D^{p,q}\to E^{p,q}\quad(0,0)
$$

such that the composite of two consecutive structure maps is zero and at
every $(p,q)$ the following exactness conditions hold (each comparing
subobjects of one single object):

$$
 \ker\!\Bigl(\alpha:D^{p,q}\to D^{p-1,q+1}\Bigr)
  =\operatorname{im}\!\Bigl(f:E^{p-2,q+1}\to D^{p,q}\Bigr),
$$

$$
 \ker\!\Bigl(f:E^{p,q}\to D^{p+2,q-1}\Bigr)
  =\operatorname{im}\!\Bigl(g:D^{p,q}\to E^{p,q}\Bigr),
$$

$$
  \ker\!\Bigl(g:D^{p,q}\to E^{p,q}\Bigr)
   =\operatorname{im}\!\Bigl(\alpha:D^{p+1,q-1}\to D^{p,q}\Bigr).
$$

(The bidegrees are those of the truncation couple of a t-structure
filtration, with the abutment in total degree $p+q$; they are the convention
in which the hypercohomology spectral sequence has $E_2^{p,q}\Rightarrow
\mathcal H^{p+q}$.) Setting $d:=g\circ f:E^{p,q}\to E^{p+2,q-1}$ (bidegree
$(+2,-1)$), the identity $f\circ g=0$ gives $d\circ d=0$, and the *derived
couple* is

$$
 D'^{p,q}:=\operatorname{im}\!\bigl(\alpha:D^{p+1,q-1}\to D^{p,q}\bigr),
 \qquad
 E'^{p,q}:=\frac{\ker\!\bigl(d:E^{p,q}\to E^{p+2,q-1}\bigr)}
                    {\operatorname{im}\!\bigl(d:E^{p-2,q+1}\to E^{p,q}\bigr)},
$$

with

$$
 \alpha':=\alpha|_{D'},\qquad
 f'(x):=f(x)\ \ (x\in\ker d),\qquad
 g'(y):=\overline{g(y')}\ \ (y=\alpha(y')\in D'^{p,q}),
$$

which is well defined because $f(\ker
d)\subseteq\ker g=\operatorname{im}\alpha$, because $d(g(y'))=g\circ f\circ
g\,(y')=0$, and because changing $y'$ by
$\ker\alpha=\operatorname{im}f$ changes $g(y')$ by $\operatorname{im}d$. The
*spectral sequence of the couple* is $E_2=E$, $d_2=d$, $E_3=E'$,
$d_3=g'\circ f'$ (bidegree $(+3,-2)$), and recursively $E_{r+1}=E'_r$, so
that $d_r$ has bidegree $(+r,1-r)$ for $r\geq2$.

(Stacks Project: Definitions 12.21.1 and 12.21.3 (Tags
[011Q](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/011Q),
[011S](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/011S)), Lemma 12.21.2 (Tag
[011R](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/011R)), and the shift-functor
variant Remark 12.21.5 (Tag
[011U](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/011U)).)

Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. A *decreasing
filtration* $F^\bullet$ of an object $A\in\mathcal A$ is a family of
subobjects $F^nA\subseteq A$ ($n\in\mathbb Z$) with
$A\supseteq\cdots\supseteq F^nA\supseteq F^{n+1}A$; a *filtered object* is a
pair $(A,F)$. The *graded pieces* are
$\operatorname{gr}^nA:=F^nA/F^{n+1}A$. The filtration is *finite and
separated* on $A$ if $F^0A=A$, $F^NA=0$ for some $N$, and $\bigcap_nF^nA=0$.
(*Stacks Project: Definition 12.19.1, Tag
[0121](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0121).*)

A Grothendieck abelian category is an *abelian category* [def-sp-abelian]
which has small colimits, a generator, and exact filtered colimits.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a pretriangulated category (with shift $[1]$,
distinguished triangles and rotation), and let $\mathcal A$ be abelian
[def-sp-abelian]. An additive functor $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal A$ is
*homological* if for every distinguished triangle $K_1\to K_2\to K_3\to
K_1[1]$ the sequences $F(K_1)\to F(K_2)\to F(K_3)$ and $F(K_3)\to F(K_1[1])$
are exact at the middle spots.

Let $(A,F)$ be a filtered object [def-sp-filtration] and let $A\to B$ be a
morphism in the abelian category [def-sp-abelian] $\mathcal A$. The *image
filtration* on $B$ is the filtration

$$
 F^nB:=\operatorname{im}\bigl(F^nA\to B\bigr).
$$

(*Stacks Project:* the case of this construction used below is the induced
filtration on the homology of a filtered differential object, Definition
12.23.4, Tag [012E](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/012E)
($F^pH(K,d)=\operatorname{im}(H(F^pK,d)\to H(K,d))$); the definition above is
the same recipe for an arbitrary morphism $A\to B$.)

An object $I$ of an *abelian category* is *injective* if for every
monomorphism $M\hookrightarrow N$, the restriction
$\operatorname{Hom}(N,I)\to\operatorname{Hom}(M,I)$ is surjective. Here
$\operatorname{Hom}(-,I)$ is contravariant. An *injective resolution* of an
object $X$ of an abelian category with enough injectives is a bounded-below
cochain complex $X\longrightarrow I^\bullet$ of injective objects whose
cohomology is concentrated in degree zero, where it equals $X$.

A *K-injective resolution* of a complex $K$ is a quasi-isomorphism $K\to I$
with $I$ K-injective: for every acyclic complex $A$ the complex
$\operatorname{Hom}(A,I)$ is acyclic. In a Grothendieck abelian category
[def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] every bounded-below complex admits a
K-injective resolution.

This is what carries a left exact additive functor
[def-sp-left-exact-additive] from objects to complexes, and it is the bridge
the name refers to. For $v:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ left exact additive and
$K\in\operatorname{Ch}^+(\mathcal A)$, choose a K-injective resolution $K\to
I$ and set

$$
 RvK:=v(I),\qquad R^pv(K):=\mathcal H^p(RvK).
$$

That the choice of resolution does not matter, and that for an object $X$
placed in degree zero this agrees with the derived functors $R^pv(X)$ defined
by injective resolutions, is [lem-sp-kinjective-computes]; until that lemma
the notation is read as depending on the chosen resolution. This is the only
meaning $Rv$ has on complexes anywhere in the chapter.

**Status.** The source defines $Rv$ only on objects, in
[def-sp-left-exact-additive], and then uses $RvK$ for complexes in the
truncation couple, in the shift rule and in both hypercohomology spectral
sequences without ever saying what it is. Each of the two statements that
could have fixed it — the Cartan--Eilenberg theorem [thm-sp-if-e1] and the
comparison lemma [lem-sp-kinjective-computes] — was left appealing to the
other, which is what made their proofs circular. The definition is stated
here instead, and both proofs now rest on it.

Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian]. A functor
$v:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ is *additive* if it preserves finite products
(equivalently finite biproducts); it is *left exact* if it is additive and
preserves kernels. Suppose that $\mathcal A$ has enough injectives. For a
left exact additive functor $v$ and an object $X\in\mathcal A$, the *right
derived functors* $R^nv$ ($n\geq0$) are defined via injective resolutions
[def-sp-injective-resolutions]: for an injective resolution $X\to I^\bullet$,

$$
 R^nv(X):=\mathcal H^n(v(I^\bullet)),
$$

the independence of the choice and the identification $R^0v=v$ being the
well-definedness lemma below.

attrs.title: Additive left exact functors and right derived functors

objects.body:
Let $\mathcal C$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], let $\kappa$ be a
set, let $c:\mathbb Z\to\operatorname{ComplexShape}\kappa$ be a family of
complex shapes, and let $r_0\in\mathbb Z$ be a starting page. A *spectral
sequence* $E$ consists of a complex $E(r)$ of shape $c(r)$ (the $r$-th
*page*, with differentials $d_r$) for every $r\geq r_0$, together with
isomorphisms $\mathcal H(E(r))_{pq}\xrightarrow{\sim}E(r+1)_{pq}$ for every
$r\geq r_0$ and every index $pq$; a *morphism* of spectral sequences is a
compatible family of morphisms of pages.

Let $v:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be left exact and additive
[def-sp-left-exact-additive] between Grothendieck abelian categories
[def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], and let $K\in\operatorname{Ch}^+(\mathcal A)$
be bounded below with $\mathcal H^q(K)=0$ for $q<a$. The *truncation couple*
of $K$ is the pair of bigraded objects

$$
 D^{p,q}=\mathcal H^{p+q}\bigl(Rv(\tau_{\leq q}K)\bigr),\qquad
 E^{p,q}=\mathcal H^{p+q}\bigl(Rv(\mathcal H^q(K)[-q])\bigr),
$$

obtained from the triangles

$$
 \tau_{\leq q-1}K\to\tau_{\leq q}K\to\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]\to
$$

by applying $Rv$ — the derived functor on $\operatorname{Ch}^+$ of
[def-sp-kinjective-bridge], the truncations $\tau_{\leq q}K$ and the shifted
cohomology sheaves being complexes and not objects — and taking cohomology,
with the structure maps $\alpha$,
$f$, $g$ of bidegrees $(-1,+1)$, $(+2,-1)$, $(0,0)$ as in
[def-sp-exact-couple] (the map $f:E^{p,q}\to D^{p+2,q-1}$ is the boundary
$\mathcal H^{p+q}(Rv\mathcal H^q(K)[-q])\to\mathcal H^{p+q+1}(Rv\,\tau_{\le
q-1}K)$ of the triangle).

attrs.title: The truncation couple of a bounded-below complex

objects.body:
For the prime $\ell$ and an abelian group $M$, put

$$
M[\ell^n]=\{x:\ell^nx=0\},\qquad
T_\ell M=\{(t_n)_{n\ge1}:t_n\in M[\ell^n],\ \ell t_{n+1}=t_n\}.
$$

The ring $\Zell$ consists of compatible residues
$c_n\in\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$ under reduction.
It acts by $(ct)_n=c_nt_n$, independently of the integer representative
of $c_n$. Define $\Qell=\Zell[1/\ell]$ and
$V_\ell M=T_\ell M[1/\ell]$. A fraction is written $\ell^{-b}t$;
the equality of fractions $\ell^{-b}t=\ell^{-c}u$ means that
$\ell^d(\ell^ct-\ell^bu)=0$ for some $d\ge0$.
An automorphism $s$ of $M$ acts coordinatewise and on fractions, and
$(V_\ell M)^s$ denotes its fixed submodule.

attrs.title: Tate module of an abelian group

objects.body:
Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions, with $A_n=A_{E,n}$. An
*$A_\bullet$-system* on $X$ is a family

$$
K_\bullet=\bigl(K_n,t_{n+1,n}\bigr)_{n\geq1},\qquad
K_n\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A_n),
$$

with transition morphisms compatible with the quotients
$A_{n+1}\twoheadrightarrow A_n$; it is *normalized* if
$K_n\otimes_{A_n}^LA_j\xrightarrow{\sim}K_j$ for $j\leq n$. Using the
adic coefficient datum of
the proper-base-change chapter and the
derived inverse limit,
define

$$
K_{\mathcal O_E}:=R\!\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_{n,X}K_n,
$$

and let $\mathcal D^b_{ctf,\mathrm W,adic}(X,\mathcal O_E)$ be the
category of normalized systems with a strict Weil structure at every
level, compatible with the transitions; the resulting realizations are
the derived-complete bounded
constructible $\mathcal O_E$-complexes of the framework chapter with finite
Tor amplitude, by the reconstruction of the proper-base-change chapter (the levelwise
statements below).

Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions, $A=A_{E,n}$, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type
morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes. Say that $f$ is
*exceptionally admissible at $A$* when the compact-support direct image
$Rf_!:D^b_{ctf}(X,A)\to D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ has a specified right adjoint
$Rf^!:D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)\to D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, with unit
$\operatorname{id}\to Rf^!Rf_!$ and counit
$Rf_!Rf^!\to\operatorname{id}$ (i.e. the adjunction $Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$),
and the composition and base-change exchange isomorphisms used below; and
*exceptionally admissible* when this holds at every finite coefficient stage
$A=A_{E,n}$ with constants independent of $n$. The functor in question is
the constructible exceptional inverse image of
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and the condition is a *theorem*, not a
restriction: every separated finite-type morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes
is exceptionally admissible, the adjunction on $D^b_{ctf}$ being
thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class, the preservation
$Rf^!D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)\subseteq D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ with stage-independent constants
being thm-sf-preservation-class, and the composition and base-change
isomorphisms being the mates of those of $Rf_!$. The trace-formula chapter
names the condition only to make explicit which functor each statement uses.
Nothing of the strong ambient notion of
[def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility] — the ambient datum
$\operatorname{FullCD}$ on every pro-etale sheaf together with an ambient
right adjoint — is assumed: that datum fails in general (for an elliptic
curve over $\overline{\mathbf F}_p$ with $A=\mathbf F_r$;
rem:sf-ambient-counterexample in the six-functors chapter), and no
preservation clause is assumed either.

*Recorded in advance* from chapter *The trace formula* of the source.

Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions, $A=A_{E,n}$, $s=\Spec k$. Let $T$ be a
separated finite-type
$k$-scheme whose structure morphism $a_T:T\to s$ is
exceptionally admissible, with
dualizing complex $\omega_T=\omega_{T,A}=Ra_T^!A_s$ of
[def-trf-dualizing-complex]. A *Borel–Moore section* on $T$ is a
morphism

$$
\alpha:A_T\longrightarrow\omega_T
$$

in $D(T,A)$; they form the $A$-module
$\Hom_{D(T,A)}(A_T,\omega_T)$.

Let $h:T\to T'$ be a proper
morphism of such $k$-schemes, with $h$, $a_T$ and $a_{T'}$
exceptionally admissible (so $a_T=a_{T'}\circ h$). For a
Borel–Moore section $\alpha$ on $T$, its *pushforward*
$h_*\alpha:A_{T'}\to\omega_{T'}$ is the composite

$$
A_{T'}\xrightarrow{\ \eta_h\ }Rh_*A_T
\xrightarrow{\ Rh_*\alpha\ }Rh_*\omega_T
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rh_!Rh^!\omega_{T'}
\xrightarrow{\ \varepsilon_h\ }\omega_{T'},
$$

where:

- $\eta_h$ is the unit of the adjunction $Lh^*\dashv Rh_*$ of the
  derived direct image at
  $A_{T'}$, using $Lh^*A_{T'}=A_T$;
- the isomorphism is the identification $Rh_*\cong Rh_!$ for the
  proper $h$ of [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed],
  followed by $Rh_!$ applied to the inverse of the canonical
  isomorphism $Rh^!\omega_{T'}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_T$ of
  [thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition] (applied with $d=h$,
  $X=T'$, $F=T$);
- $\varepsilon_h$ is the counit of the adjunction
  $Rh_!\dashv Rh^!$ of [def-trf-admissibility] at $\omega_{T'}$.

Since each arrow other than $Rh_*\alpha$ is independent of
$\alpha$ and $Rh_*$ is an additive $A$-linear functor, the map
$\alpha\mapsto h_*\alpha$ is $A$-linear.

attrs.title: Borel–Moore sections and their proper pushforward

objects.body:
Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions, with $A=A_{E,n}$, and define
$D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$ to be the category of *perfect*
$A$-complexes, realized explicitly as the category of bounded
complexes of finitely generated projective $A$-modules, (The
perfect form is the one needed here: only perfect complexes are
dualizable with respect to the derived tensor, so only for them does
the coevaluation of the display below exist.)
For $P\in D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$ put
$P^\vee=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,A)$. The coevaluation and evaluation
are

$$
\operatorname{coev}_P:A\longrightarrow P\otimes_A^LP^\vee,\qquad
\operatorname{ev}_P:P^\vee\otimes_A^LP\longrightarrow A,
$$

the triangle identities for which are
[lem-trf-chain-supertrace]; here $\otimes^L_A$ is the
derived tensor over $A$. For an
endomorphism $v:P\to P$, the *categorical trace* is

$$
\operatorname{tr}_A(v\mid P):=
\operatorname{ev}_P\circ\operatorname{sym}\circ
\bigl(v\otimes_A^L1\bigr)\circ\operatorname{coev}_P
\in\operatorname{End}_{D(A)}(A)\cong A.
$$

The identification $\operatorname{End}_{D(A)}(A)\cong A$ is the
classical one (a bounded complex concentrated in degree $0$ with
zero differentials: the quasi-isomorphism class of an endomorphism of
$A$ is its degree-$0$ scalar).

*Recorded in advance* from chapter *The trace formula* of the source.

attrs.title: Perfect complex and its categorical trace

objects.body:
Fix the global finite-field datum
$p,a,q,k_0,k$, where $q=p^a$, a prime $\ell\neq p$, and a finite
extension $E/\Ql$ contained in a fixed algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of
$\Ql$, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer
$\varpi_E$, and an integer $n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$. Put
$A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $X_0$ be a
separated finite-type
$k_0$-scheme, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and write
$a_X:X\to\Spec k$ for its structure morphism. On the
small pro-etale site of $X$,
use the bounded
constructible finite-torsion coefficient category $D^b_c(X,A)$ and
the finite-Tor subcategory
$D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, the
derived pullback, tensor
and internal Hom, the
cohomology sheaves, and
the compact-support
cohomology construction; in particular

$$
R\Gamma_c(X,K)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{X!}K),\qquad
H_c^i(X,K)=\mathrm H^i\bigl(R\Gamma_c(X,K)\bigr)
$$

with the finite-coefficient
categories over a point.

*Recorded in advance* from chapter *The trace formula* of the source.

Fix the global finite-field datum and the coefficient conventions,
$A=A_{E,n}$, $s=\Spec k$; all functors are derived, and we write
$c_2^*$, $c_1^!$ for $Lc_2^*$, $Rc_1^!$. Let
$c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times_sX$ be an admissible cohomological
correspondence of [def-trf-correspondence], let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$
and let $u:c_2^*K\to c_1^!K$ be a correspondence. Let
$b=(b_1,b_2):D\to Y\times_sY$ be a second admissible correspondence. A
*proper pushforward diagram* $(f,g):(C,c)\to(D,b)$ consists of proper
morphisms

$$
f:X\longrightarrow Y,\qquad g:C\longrightarrow D,
\qquad b_ig=fc_i\quad(i=1,2).
$$

No Cartesian condition is imposed on either leg square
$(c_i,g,b_i,f)$, and $X,Y,C,D$ need not be proper over $s$. Put
$K'=Rf_*K$. Write $\eta_g:\operatorname{id}\to Rg_*g^*$ and
$\varepsilon_f:f^*Rf_*\to\operatorname{id}$ for the unit and counit of
the ordinary adjunctions, and $\varepsilon_{c_1}:Rc_{1!}c_1^!\to\operatorname{id}$
for the counit of $Rc_{1!}\dashv c_1^!$, all as in [fix-prop-adjunctions].

1. *The ordinary half.* Let
$$
\begin{aligned}
\gamma:b_2^*K'
&\xrightarrow{\ \eta_g\ }Rg_*g^*b_2^*Rf_*K
= Rg_*c_2^*f^*Rf_*K\\
&\xrightarrow{\ Rg_*c_2^*\varepsilon_f\ }Rg_*c_2^*K,
\end{aligned}
$$
the equality being the pullback composition $g^*b_2^*=(b_2g)^*=(fc_2)^*=c_2^*f^*$.
1. *The exceptional half.* Since $f$ and $g$ are proper,
$Rf_*=Rf_!$ and $Rg_*=Rg_!$ ([prop-functor-package], clause (3)), and the
composition law of [thm-sf-comp-composition] applied to $b_1g=fc_1$ gives
$\Xi_1:Rb_{1!}Rg_*\cong R(b_1g)_!=R(fc_1)_!\cong Rf_!Rc_{1!}$. Let
$$
\delta:Rg_*c_1^!K\longrightarrow b_1^!K'
$$
be the exceptional adjoint (for $Rb_{1!}\dashv b_1^!$) of
$$
Rb_{1!}Rg_*c_1^!K\xrightarrow{\ \Xi_1\ }Rf_!Rc_{1!}c_1^!K
\xrightarrow{\ Rf_!\varepsilon_{c_1}\ }Rf_!K=K'.
$$
1. The *coefficient pushforward* of $u$ is
$$
[f,g]_!u:=\delta\circ Rg_*u\circ\gamma:\
b_2^*K'\longrightarrow b_1^!K',
$$
a correspondence on $(Y,K')$ supported on $b$ (Varshavsky, loc. cit.,
1.2.4).
1. *The induced map of fixed schemes.* Let $F_c=\operatorname{Fix}(c)$
and $F_b=\operatorname{Fix}(b)$ be the fixed schemes of
[def-trf-fixed-scheme], with projections $i_c:F_c\to C$, $d_c:F_c\to X$
and $i_b:F_b\to D$, $d_b:F_b\to Y$. Since
$b\,g\,i_c=(f\times f)\,c\,i_c=(f\times f)\Delta_Xd_c=\Delta_Y\,f\,d_c$,
the universal property of $F_b=D\times_{Y\times_sY,\Delta_Y}Y$ gives a
unique morphism
$$
h:F_c\longrightarrow F_b,\qquad i_bh=g\,i_c,\qquad d_bh=f\,d_c .
$$
Its properness, and hence the Borel–Moore pushforward of the trace
class along $h$, are established in the next lemma of this block.

*The Cartesian case.* Neither construction uses a Cartesian
square, but they reduce to the familiar maps when the squares are
Cartesian. The recipe for $\gamma$ is the recipe of the exchange
$\operatorname{Ex}_*$ of [def-exchange-projection] (the adjoint of the
counit composed with the identification of pullbacks); so if
$(c_2,g,b_2,f)$ is Cartesian, $\gamma=\operatorname{Ex}_*$ is the proper
base-change isomorphism $b_2^*Rf_*\cong Rg_*c_2^*$ of
[prop-functor-package], clause (4). The map $\delta$ is the exchange map
of [def-trf-admissibility] formed from the composition law and the
exceptional counits; if $(c_1,g,b_1,f)$ is Cartesian, it is inverse to the
dual base-change isomorphism $b_1^!Rf_*\cong Rg_*c_1^!$ of
[thm-sf-dual-base-change] (applied with $b_1$ as the exceptional map and
$f$ as the proper map). Indeed, the latter is the mate of
$\operatorname{Ex}_!$, and $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ is compatible with the
composition law ([fix-lem-exchanges], item 4) and with the adjunctions
([fix-prop-adjunctions], item 4), so the two mates are mutually inverse.

Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions, $A=A_{E,n}$, put $s=\Spec k$, and let $X$ be
separated of finite type
over $k$. A *cohomological correspondence* consists of a
separated finite-type
scheme $C$ with a morphism

$$
c=(c_1,c_2):C\longrightarrow X\times_sX,
$$

and, for $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, a morphism

$$
u:Lc_2^*K\longrightarrow Rc_1^!K
$$

in $D(C,A)$, where $Lc_2^*$ is the
derived pullback and
$Rc_1^!$ is the
exceptional inverse image
of [def-trf-admissibility]; $c_2$ is the ordinary pullback leg
and $c_1$ the exceptional leg. The correspondence is
*admissible* if $c_1$ and every base change of $c_1$ occurring
below are exceptionally admissible at $A$.

*Recorded in advance* from chapter *The trace formula* of the source.

Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions, $A=A_{E,n}$, put $s=\Spec k$, and let $X,Y,C,D$ be
separated finite-type $k$-schemes, with $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ and
$L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$. Products are taken over $s$.

1. A *correspondence from $(X,K)$ to $(Y,L)$* consists of a morphism
$$
c=(c_1,c_2):C\longrightarrow Y\times_sX
$$
and a morphism
$$
u:Lc_2^*K\longrightarrow Rc_1^!L
$$
in $D(C,A)$, where $Lc_2^*$ is the derived pullback and $Rc_1^!$ the
exceptional inverse image of [def-trf-admissibility]. The
ordinary-pullback leg is $c_2$ and the exceptional leg is $c_1$; the
correspondence is *admissible* if $c_1$ and every base change of $c_1$
used below are exceptionally admissible at $A$. An
*endocorrespondence* of $(X,K)$ is the case $Y=X$, $L=K$; it is exactly
a cohomological correspondence of [def-trf-correspondence].
1. An *opposite correspondence* is a correspondence from $(Y,L)$ to
$(X,K)$, i.e. a morphism $d=(d_1,d_2):D\to X\times_sY$ together with
$v:Ld_2^*L\to Rd_1^!K$ in $D(D,A)$.
1. For such a pair put
$$
Z=Y\times_sX,\qquad \bar d=\tau d:D\longrightarrow Z,\qquad
E(C,D)=C\times_{Z,c,\bar d}D,
$$
where $\tau:X\times_sY\xrightarrow{\sim}Y\times_sX$ exchanges the
factors, so that $\bar d=(d_2,d_1)$. Write $p_1:Z\to Y$ and
$p_2:Z\to X$ for the two projections, so that $c_1=p_1c$ and
$c_2=p_2c$.

All supports $C,D,E(C,D)$ and all structure maps $c,d,\bar d$ and the
projections of $E(C,D)$ remain specified data; nothing is identified
up to non-specified isomorphism.

For an endocorrespondence $c$ of $(X,K)$ and the identity
correspondence $d=\Delta_X:X\to X\times_sX$, $v=1_K$ (here $d_1=d_2=\operatorname{id}_X$, so $Rd_1^!K=K=Ld_2^*K$), one has
$\bar d=\tau\Delta_X=\Delta_X$, hence
$E(C,X)=C\times_{X\times_sX,c,\Delta_X}X=\operatorname{Fix}(c)$ is the
fixed scheme of [def-trf-fixed-scheme].

attrs.title: Correspondences between pairs and opposite correspondences

objects.body:
Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions, $A=A_{E,n}$, put $s=\Spec k$, and let $Y$ be a
separated finite-type
$k$-scheme whose
structure morphism
$a_Y:Y\to s$ is
exceptionally admissible in the sense of [def-trf-admissibility] (which
holds for every such $Y$; no ambient datum is assumed). Put

$$
\omega_{Y,A}:=Ra_Y^!A_s,\qquad
D_YM:=R\mathcal Hom_A\bigl(M,\omega_{Y,A}\bigr)
\qquad
\bigl(M\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)\bigr),
$$

using the exceptional inverse
image of $a_Y$ and the
derived internal Hom and
tensor; here $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ is the
finite-Tor subcategory of the
bounded constructible
derived category. The *evaluation* is the canonical map

$$
\operatorname{ev}_M:D_YM\otimes_A^LM\longrightarrow\omega_{Y,A}
$$

obtained from the tensor–internal-Hom adjunction: it is the transpose of
the identity of $D_YM$ under the
adjunction isomorphism

$$
\Hom_{D(Y,A)}
\bigl(D_YM\otimes_A^LM,\omega_{Y,A}\bigr)
\cong
\Hom_{D(Y,A)}
\bigl(D_YM,R\mathcal Hom_A(M,\omega_{Y,A})\bigr).
$$

Here $\omega_{Y,A}$ is the *dualizing complex* of $Y$ over $A$
and $D_Y$ the *Verdier dual* functor.

Use the finite coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$. For finite-type $k$-schemes $X_1,X_2$, projections
$p_i:X_1\times_kX_2\to X_i$, and complexes
$M_i$ in the finite-Tor constructible category $D^b_{ctf}(X_i,A)$, define

$$
M_1\boxtimes_A^L M_2:=Lp_1^*M_1\otimes_A^L Lp_2^*M_2.
$$

This notation includes the order of the factors and uses only the derived
pullback and tensor of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and
[def-weil-derived-tensor].

Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions, and let $c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times_sX$ be a
cohomological correspondence with
$s=\Spec k$. Let

$$
\Delta_X:X\longrightarrow X\times_sX
$$

be the diagonal. The *fixed scheme* is

$$
F=\operatorname{Fix}(c):=C\times_{X\times_sX,c,\Delta_X}X,
$$

the scheme-theoretic intersection of the image of $c$ with the
diagonal, with first projection $i_F:F\to C$ and second projection
$d:F\to X$, so that $c_1i_F=d=c_2i_F$. For $h:X\to X$ a
morphism,
$\operatorname{Fix}(h):= \operatorname{Fix}((\operatorname{id}_X,h))$ is the scheme-theoretic
equalizer of $h$ and the identity. We say that $F$ has
*finitely many open-and-closed components* when the set
$\pi_0(F)$ of open-and-closed connected components of $F$ is finite;
in that case

$$
F=\coprod_{\beta\in\pi_0(F)}\beta,
$$

with each $\beta$ an open-and-closed
subscheme of $F$.

*Recorded in advance* from chapter *The trace formula* of the source.

Fix the global finite-field datum and the coefficient conventions of
[def-trf-coefficient-conventions], let $X_0$ be a separated
finite-type $k_0$-scheme, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $\Phi$ be
the $q$-power scheme Frobenius of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius], with
iterates $\Phi^m$. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$.

1. A *Frobenius coefficient morphism* on $K$ is an arbitrary morphism
$$
\psi:L\Phi^*K\longrightarrow K
$$
in the derived category of $X$; no invertibility is required.
1. Its *iterates* $\psi_m:L\Phi^{m*}K\to K$, $m\geq1$, are defined
recursively by $\psi_1=\psi$ and
$$
\psi_m:\;L\Phi^{m*}K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
L\Phi^*L\Phi^{(m-1)*}K
\xrightarrow{\ L\Phi^*\psi_{m-1}\ }L\Phi^*K
\xrightarrow{\ \psi\ }K,
$$
where the first arrow is the composition isomorphism of derived
pullback for $\Phi^m=\Phi^{m-1}\circ\Phi$; thus $\psi_m$ is the
composite of the pulled-back copies $L\Phi^{i*}\psi$,
$0\leq i\leq m-1$, exactly as for the iterated Weil isomorphism of
[def-trf-iterated-weil-map].
1. Its *graph map* in degree $m$ is the graph correspondence of
[def-trf-graph-correspondence] attached to $(h,v)=(\Phi^m,\psi_m)$:
$$
c_m=(c_1,c_2)=(\operatorname{id}_X,\Phi^m),\qquad u=\psi_m:
Lc_2^*K=L\Phi^{m*}K\longrightarrow K=Rc_1^!K .
$$
1. Its *global operator* in degree $m$ is
$$
F_{c,m}(\psi)=T_{c_m}(\psi_m):R\Gamma_c(X,K)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_c(X,K),
$$
the global operator of [def-trf-global-operator] of the graph map. It
is defined because the ordinary leg $c_2=\Phi^m$ is finite
([def-trf-scheme-frobenius]), hence proper
([def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]), and the exceptional leg
$c_1=\operatorname{id}_X$ is admissible with $Rc_1^!=\operatorname{id}$.

*Example.* For a strict Weil complex $(K,\varphi)$ of
[def-trf-strict-weil-complex], the scheme-Frobenius map
$u_1=\varphi\circ\kappa_K:L\Phi^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ of
[def-trf-iterated-weil-map] is an (invertible) Frobenius coefficient
morphism; the notion above drops the invertibility, and the iterates,
graph map and global operator are given by the same composites.

Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions, and let $(K,\varphi)\in D^b_{ctf,\mathrm W}(X,A)$.

1. The *$m$-th iterate of the global geometric Frobenius* is
$$
F_{c,K}^{\,m}:
R\Gamma_c(X,K)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_c(X,K),
$$
the composite of the canonical
direct-image identification
with the compact-support
global geometric
Frobenius action constructed in the trace-formula chapter applied to
$\varphi^{[m]}$. Its description as
$R\Gamma_c(X,\varphi^{[m]})\circ g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}$, where
$g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}$ is the compact-support base-change isomorphism
along the automorphism $g_\gamma^m$, is
`lem-trf-frobenius-operator-compact-description` of the trace-formula chapter. It is the
endomorphism of the
compact-support
cohomology $H_c^i(X,K)$ in the finite coefficient stage.
1. For a point $x\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ with geometric point
$\bar x:\Spec k\to X$ lying over $x$, define the *local
geometric Frobenius*
$$
F_{x,m}:K_{\bar x}\longrightarrow K_{\bar x},
\qquad
F_{x,m}=\varphi^{[m]}_{\bar x}\circ\tau_{x,m},
$$
where $\tau_{x,m}:K_{\bar x}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \bigl(Lg_\gamma^{m*}K\bigr)_{\bar x}$ is the canonical stalk
transport and $K_{\bar x}=L\bar x^*\operatorname{For}(K)$ is the
stalk complex of the
derived pullback.
The dependence of $F_{x,m}$ on the lift and, through a closed point
below, on the degree, is recorded in
[lem-trf-local-frobenius-conjugacy] and
[lem-trf-frobenius-degree-formula]; that the transport
$\tau_{x,m}$ is defined for every point
$x\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ is the fixed-point statement
[thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points].

*Recorded in advance* from chapter *The trace formula* of the source.

attrs.title: Global and local geometric Frobenius operators

objects.body:
In the setting of [def-trf-correspondence], assume that the
ordinary leg $c_2$ is
proper. The
*global operator* of a correspondence $u$ is

$$
T_c(u):R\Gamma_c(X,K)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_c(X,K),
$$

the composite

$$
\begin{aligned}
R\Gamma_c(X,K)&\xrightarrow{\eta^*_{c_2}}
R\Gamma_c(X,Rc_{2*}Lc_2^*K)
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }R\Gamma_c(C,Lc_2^*K)\\
&\xrightarrow{R\Gamma_c(C,u)}
R\Gamma_c(C,Rc_1^!K)
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }R\Gamma_c(X,Rc_{1!}Rc_1^!K)\\
&\xrightarrow{R\Gamma_c(X,\varepsilon_{c_1})}R\Gamma_c(X,K),
\end{aligned}
$$

where $R\Gamma_c$ is the compact-support cohomology of the
coefficient conventions
(computed with the
compact-support direct
image, and:

1. the first arrow is the unit of the adjunction
$Lc_2^*\dashv Rc_{2*}$ of the
derived direct image, applied
to $K$ on $X$: this is the canonical arrow $K\to Rc_{2*}Lc_2^*K$;
1. the first isomorphism is the identification $Rc_{2*}\simeq Rc_{2!}$ for the
proper $c_2$ (the
proper-coincidence clause of the six-operations package,
[prop-functor-package], item (3)), applied to $Lc_2^*K$ and
composed with the identity naturality of the compact-support
construction;
1. the second isomorphism is the *composition law* of the
compact-support direct image for the composite
$a_X\circ c_1=a_C$ ([prop-functor-package], item (3)),
$$
Ra_{X!}Rc_{1!}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }R(a_X\circ c_1)_!=Ra_{C!},
$$
which is correctly an isomorphism of functors with the associativity
compatibility: this arrow transports the compact-support cohomology of
$C$ to that of $X$ along the exceptional leg (it is *not* the
projection formula; the projection formula is not used here, and the
coinage of the terminology in earlier drafts was a slip);
1. the last arrow is the counit
$\varepsilon_{c_1}:Rc_{1!}Rc_1^!\to\operatorname{id}$ of the
adjunction $Rc_{1!}\dashv Rc_1^!$ of [def-trf-admissibility],
applied to $K$ and then to
$R\Gamma_c(X,-)$ (exact, so it maps the counit to an arrow in the
derived category).

The composite is a morphism of $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$
by [lem-trf-global-operator-perfect], and

Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions, and let $h:X\to X$ be a
separated finite-type
$k$-endomorphism and $v:Lh^*K\to K$ for
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$. The *graph correspondence* of $(h,v)$ is

$$
C=X,\qquad c_1=\operatorname{id}_X,\qquad c_2=h,\qquad u=v,
$$

a cohomological correspondence whose
fixed scheme, in the sense of [def-trf-fixed-scheme], is
$\operatorname{Fix}(c)=\operatorname{Fix}(h)$, the scheme-theoretic
equalizer of $h$ and $\operatorname{id}_X$.

*Recorded in advance* from chapter *The trace formula* of the source.

Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions, $A=A_{E,n}$, $s=\Spec k$, and let $\beta$ be
separated finite type
and proper over $s$,
with structure morphism
$a_\beta:\beta\to s$ is exceptionally
admissible and $\omega_{\beta,A}$ the
dualizing complex of
[def-trf-dualizing-complex]. The *integration* (the
``trace along $a_\beta$'') is the map

$$
\int_\beta:
\Hom_{D(\beta,A)}\bigl(A_\beta,\omega_{\beta,A}\bigr)\longrightarrow A
$$

sending $\tau:A_\beta\to\omega_{\beta,A}$ to the composite

$$
A\xrightarrow{\ \eta^*\ }
R\Gamma(\beta,A_\beta)
\xrightarrow{R\Gamma(\tau)}
R\Gamma(\beta,\omega_{\beta,A})
\xrightarrow{\ \varepsilon_{a_\beta}\ }A,
$$

where the first arrow is the composite

$$
A=R\Gamma(s,A_s)
\xrightarrow{\ R\Gamma(s,\eta_\beta)\ }
R\Gamma(s,Ra_{\beta*}A_\beta)
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
R\Gamma(s,Ra_{\beta!}A_\beta)=R\Gamma(\beta,A_\beta),
$$

whose first map is $R\Gamma(s,-)$ applied to the unit of the
adjunction $La_\beta^*\dashv Ra_{\beta*}$ of the
derived direct image, and
whose second is the identification $Ra_{\beta*}\cong Ra_{\beta!}$ for
the proper $a_\beta$
of [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] (so that
$R\Gamma(\beta,-)=R\Gamma(s,Ra_{\beta!}-)$); and the last arrow is
the composite

$$
R\Gamma(\beta,\omega_{\beta,A})
=R\Gamma(s,Ra_{\beta!}Ra_\beta^!A_s)
\xrightarrow{\ R\Gamma(s,\varepsilon_{a_\beta})\ }
R\Gamma(s,A_s)=A,
$$

where $\varepsilon_{a_\beta}$ is the counit of the adjunction
$Ra_{\beta!}\dashv Ra_\beta^!$ of
[def-trf-admissibility], applied to
$\omega_{\beta,A}=Ra_\beta^!A_s$ of
[def-trf-dualizing-complex].

Let $(K,\varphi)\in D^b_{ctf,\mathrm W}(X,A)$ under the conventions of
[def-trf-strict-weil-complex]. For $m\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$ define
the iterated Weil isomorphism

$$
\varphi^{[m]}:Lg_\gamma^{m*}K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }K,
\qquad
\varphi^{[m]}=\varphi\circ Lg_\gamma^*\varphi\circ\cdots\circ
L(g_\gamma^{m-1})^*\varphi,
$$

and, with $\kappa^{(m)}$ of [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison],
the scheme-Frobenius map

$$
u_m=\varphi^{[m]}\circ\kappa^{(m)}_K:
L\Phi^m{}^*K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }K.
$$

The cocycle identity satisfied by the $\varphi^{[m]}$ is
[lem-trf-iterated-weil-cocycle].

attrs.title: Iterated Weil isomorphism and scheme-Frobenius map

objects.body:
Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions. In the
common-stage
algebraically closed coefficient category of the framework chapter, an object
of $D^b_c(X,\Qlb)$ is represented by a finite-stage pair $(E,K_E)$
with $E/\Ql$ finite in $\Qlb$; the category is idempotent complete,
so no idempotent appears in the presentation (in the classical
presentation of the
$\Qlb$ coefficient category of
the proper-base-change chapter the object was a pair $((E,K_E),e)$ with $e^2=e$ in
the common-stage category). The *trace of an endomorphism $v$ on the
summand* $e$ of a perfect complex $P$ is the
categorical trace

$$
\operatorname{tr}_E\bigl(v\circ e\mid P\bigr),
$$

which depends only on the summand $(eP,ev)$: the decomposition
$P\simeq eP\oplus(1-e)P$ splits $v\circ e$ as $ev|eP$ on the
summand and $0$ on the complement.

Let $(f,g):(C,c)\to(D,b)$ be a proper pushforward diagram of
[def-trf-coefficient-pushforward], with $K$, $u$, $K'=Rf_*K$,
$F_c,F_b$, $i_c,d_c,i_b,d_b$ and the proper $h:F_c\to F_b$ as there and in
[lem-trf-fixed-map-proper]. Assume the exceptional admissibility of every
morphism below that carries an exceptional inverse image (the
correspondences $c,b$ as total maps, the structure maps of $X,Y,F_c,F_b$,
and $f,g,h,i_c,i_b,d_c,d_b$). Put $q=f\times f$, which is proper by
[lem-trf-fixed-map-proper], so that $bg=qc$ and
$q\Delta_X=\Delta_Yf$. Write $\omega$ for the dualizing complexes and $D$
for the Verdier duals of [def-trf-dualizing-complex], and use the
identifications $Rf_*=Rf_!$, $Rg_*=Rg_!$, $Rq_*=Rq_!$, $Rh_*=Rh_!$ for the
proper maps ([prop-functor-package], clause (3)), the units $\eta$ and
counits $\varepsilon$ of [fix-prop-adjunctions], and the external product
of [def-trf-external-product]. Define:

1. *Kernels.* $P_X=K\boxtimes D_XK$ on $X\times_sX$ and
$P_Y=K'\boxtimes D_YK'$ on $Y\times_sY$.
1. *Trace along $f$.* $\tau_f:Rf_*\omega_X\cong Rf_!Rf^!\omega_Y
\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}\omega_Y$, using
$\omega_X\cong Rf^!\omega_Y$ of [thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition]
and the counit of $Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$. The same recipe defines
$\tau_h:Rh_*\omega_{F_c}\to\omega_{F_b}$.
1. *Multiplication.* $\mu_f:Rf_*M\otimes Rf_*N\to Rf_*(M\otimes N)$ is the
ordinary adjoint of $f^*(Rf_*M\otimes Rf_*N)=f^*Rf_*M\otimes f^*Rf_*N
\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_f\otimes\varepsilon_f}M\otimes N$.
1. *Dual pushforward.* $\chi_f:Rf_*D_XK\to D_YK'=R\mathcal Hom(K',\omega_Y)$
is the tensor–Hom adjoint of
$$
Rf_*D_XK\otimes Rf_*K\xrightarrow{\ \mu_f\ }Rf_*(D_XK\otimes K)
\xrightarrow{\ Rf_*\mathrm{ev}_K\ }Rf_*\omega_X\xrightarrow{\ \tau_f\ }\omega_Y .
$$
1. *Kernel pushforward.* With the $!$-Künneth isomorphism of
[def-sf-kv-maps] (i) for $f\times f$, put
$$
\Pi_f=\mathrm{Ku}_!(f,f;K,D_XK)^{-1}:K'\boxtimes Rf_*D_XK
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rq_*P_X,
\qquad
\rho_f=(1\boxtimes\chi_f)\circ\Pi_f^{-1}:Rq_*P_X\longrightarrow P_Y .
$$
1. *Evaluation kernels.* $\delta_K:P_X\to R\Delta_{X*}\omega_X$ is the map
$e_K$ of [lem-trf-trace-map-from-external-duality] (adjoint to evaluation
preceded by the tensor symmetry), and $\delta_{K'}=e_{K'}$ likewise.
1. *Kernel class.* The kernel class of $u$ is the exceptional adjoint
$$
[u]_P:Rc_!A_C\longrightarrow P_X
$$
of $A_C\xrightarrow{\widetilde u}\mathcal H_c(K)\cong Rc^!P_X$, where
$\widetilde u$ is the mate of [def-trf-trace-class-source] and the
isomorphism is the external duality of [thm-trf-verdier-duality]. The
same recipe gives $[v]_P:Rb_!A_D\to P_Y$ for a correspondence $v$ on
$(Y,K')$ supported on $b$.
1. *Support isomorphisms.* $\zeta_c:Ri_{c*}\omega_{F_c}\xrightarrow{\sim}
Rc^!R\Delta_{X*}\omega_X$ is the inverse of the composite
$Rc^!R\Delta_{X*}\omega_X\cong Ri_{c*}Rd_c^!\omega_X\cong Ri_{c*}\omega_{F_c}$
of the right-adjoint form of fixed-square base change
([thm-trf-fixed-point-base-change]) and
[thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition]; $\zeta_b$ likewise.
1. *Composition and exchange.* $\Xi:Rb_!Rg_*\cong Rq_*Rc_!$ is the
composition law of [thm-sf-comp-composition] for $bg=qc$, and
$$
\mathsf E:Rg_*Rc^!\longrightarrow Rb^!Rq_*
$$
is the exceptional adjoint of
$Rb_!Rg_*Rc^!\xrightarrow{\Xi}Rq_*Rc_!Rc^!\xrightarrow{Rq_*\varepsilon_c}Rq_*$.
We identify $Rq_*R\Delta_{X*}=R\Delta_{Y*}Rf_*$ by $q\Delta_X=\Delta_Yf$.

By construction ([lem-trf-trace-map-from-external-duality]) the trace map
$\mathfrak t_{c,K}$ is $R\Gamma(C,-)$ of
$\zeta_c^{-1}\circ Rc^!\delta_K\circ(\mathcal H_c(K)\cong Rc^!P_X)$.

attrs.title: Kernel, evaluation and support maps of a proper pushforward diagram

objects.body:
Fix the global finite-field datum
$p,a,q,k_0,k$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] (so $k$ is an algebraic
closure of $k_0$) and the coefficient
conventions, put $s=\Spec k$, and let $E$ be a separated finite-type
$s$-scheme. Throughout, the structure morphisms of $E$ and of the
open-and-closed subschemes of $E$ considered below are assumed
exceptionally admissible in the sense of [def-trf-admissibility], so
that their dualizing complexes of [def-trf-dualizing-complex] are
defined.

*Restricted sections.* Let $\sigma:A_E\to\omega_{E,A}$ be a section
(a morphism in $D(E,A)$), and let $j_B:B\hookrightarrow E$ be the
inclusion of an open-and-closed subscheme. The *restriction* of
$\sigma$ to $B$ is

$$
j_B^*\sigma:\;
A_B\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
Lj_B^*A_E
\xrightarrow{Lj_B^*\sigma}
Lj_B^*\omega_{E,A}
\longrightarrow\omega_{B,A},
$$

the last arrow being the canonical identification
$Lj_B^*\omega_{E,A}\cong Rj_B^!\omega_{E,A}\cong\omega_{B,A}$
obtained from the equality $Rj_B^!\cong Lj_B^*$ for the open immersion
$j_B$ (the purity clause of the six-operations package
[prop-functor-package], item (6), in relative dimension $0$) and the
composition isomorphism of [thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition]
applied to $j_B$. This restricted section is defined for every
open-and-closed $B$, whether or not $B$ (or $E$) is proper over $s$.

*Local terms.* If moreover $B$ is proper over $s$, the *local term*
of $\sigma$ on $B$ is

$$
\operatorname{LT}_B(\sigma):=\int_B j_B^*\sigma\in A,
$$

the integral of [def-trf-integration]; properness of $B$ is needed
only for this scalar integral, and the ambient $E$ need not be proper.

*Endocorrespondences.* Let $c$ be an admissible correspondence in the
sense of [def-trf-correspondence], with
$u:Lc_2^*K\to Rc_1^!K$ and fixed scheme
$F=\operatorname{Fix}(c)$ of [def-trf-fixed-scheme], and let
$\operatorname{Tr}_c(u):A_F\to\omega_{F,A}$ be its trace class of
[def-trf-trace-class]. For an open-and-closed $B\subseteq F$, proper
over $s$, put

$$
\operatorname{LT}_B(u):=\operatorname{LT}_B\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)\bigr)
=\int_B j_B^*\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)\in A;
$$

$F$ itself need not be proper. In particular, when $F$ is proper over
$s$ and has finitely many open-and-closed components
$\beta\in\pi_0(F)$ in the sense of [def-trf-fixed-scheme], each $\beta$
is open-and-closed in $F$ and proper over $s$, and we write

$$
\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)|_\beta:=j_\beta^*\operatorname{Tr}_c(u):
A_\beta\longrightarrow\omega_{\beta,A},
\qquad
\operatorname{LT}_\beta(u):=
\int_\beta\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)|_\beta\bigr)\in A
$$

for the *local term* of $u$ at $\beta$.

*Point components.* If $\bar x$ is a point of $F$ such that $\{\bar x\}$
is open in $F$ and the open-and-closed subscheme $B_{\bar x}\subseteq F$
with underlying set $\{\bar x\}$ is reduced, then
$B_{\bar x}\simeq\Spec k$ ($k$ being algebraically closed and
$B_{\bar x}$ of finite type over $k$), so $B_{\bar x}$ is proper over
$s$, and we write
$\operatorname{LT}_{\bar x}(u):=\operatorname{LT}_{B_{\bar x}}(u)$,
the local term on the reduced open-and-closed point component of
$\bar x$. This applies to every Frobenius fixed point: for the
Frobenius correspondence $c=(\operatorname{id}_X,\Phi^m)$ on
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, with $X_0$ of finite type over $k_0$ and $\Phi$
the $q$-power scheme Frobenius, the fixed
scheme is the disjoint union of reduced points $\Spec k$, one for each
$y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$, by [thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points], and
$\operatorname{LT}_{\bar y}(u)=\operatorname{LT}_y(u)$ denotes the local
term on the component indexed by $y$.

Fix the coefficient conventions, put $s=\Spec k$, and let
$(C,c,u)$, $(D,d,v)$ be an opposite pair between $(X,K)$ and
$(Y,L)$, with $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ and $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$, in the
notation of [def-trf-correspondence-between-pairs] and
[def-trf-supported-pairing]. Put $E=E(C,D)$, the fiber product of the
two supports of [def-trf-correspondence-between-pairs], and let
$\langle u,v\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}:A_E\to\omega_E$ be the
Borel–Moore section of [def-trf-supported-pairing]. For an
open-and-closed subscheme $j_B:B\hookrightarrow E$, the *restricted
pairing* is the restricted section of [def-trf-local-term]

$$
A_B\simeq j_B^*A_E\xrightarrow{j_B^*\langle u,v\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}}
j_B^*\omega_E\simeq\omega_B,
$$

where the last identification uses open purity and the composition
isomorphism for dualizing complexes, as in [def-trf-local-term]. It
is defined for every open-and-closed $B$, proper or not. If $B$ is
proper over $s$, the *local term* of the pair on $B$ is

$$
\operatorname{LT}_B(u,v):=
\operatorname{LT}_B\bigl(\langle u,v\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}\bigr)
=\int_B j_B^*\langle u,v\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}\in A,
$$

the integral of [def-trf-integration]; the ambient $E$ need not be
proper. For an endocorrespondence $(C,c,u)$ of $(X,K)$ ([def-trf-correspondence]),
i.e. $(Y,L)=(X,K)$, paired with the diagonal $(X,\Delta,1_K)$, so that $E=\operatorname{Fix}(c)$ and
$\langle u,1_K\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}=\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)$ by
[lem-trf-trace-class-diagonal-pairing], this gives, for
open-and-closed $B\subseteq\operatorname{Fix}(c)$ proper over $s$,

$$
\operatorname{LT}_B(u):=\operatorname{LT}_B(u,1_K)
=\int_B j_B^*\operatorname{Tr}_c(u),
$$

which is the local term $\operatorname{LT}_B(u)$ of
[def-trf-local-term]. At a Frobenius fixed point $\bar x$,
$\operatorname{LT}_{\bar x}$ means the local term on the reduced
open-and-closed point component $B_{\bar x}\simeq\Spec k$ of
$\bar x$, as in [def-trf-local-term].

attrs.title: Local terms of an opposite pair

objects.body:
Fix the global finite-field datum
$p,a,q,k_0,k$, where $q=p^a$, let $X_0$ be a
finite-type
$k_0$-scheme, and put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. Let
$\sigma:k\to k$, $z\mapsto z^q$, be the arithmetic Frobenius and put
$\gamma=\sigma^{-1}=\operatorname{Frob}_q$, so that
$g_\gamma=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\Spec(\gamma):X\to X$ is the
geometric-Frobenius automorphism. The
$q$-power scheme Frobenius of $X_0$ is the $k_0$-morphism
$\Phi_0:X_0\to X_0$ whose affine incarnation is $a\mapsto a^q$; its
base change

$$
\Phi:=\Phi_0\times_{k_0}\operatorname{id}_k:X\longrightarrow X
$$

is a $k$-morphism with affine incarnation
$a\otimes b\mapsto a^q\otimes b$ on $A_0\otimes_{k_0}k$, and is
finite and radicial.
For $m\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ write $\Phi^m$ for the $m$-fold
iterate, and write

$$
g_\sigma=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\Spec(\sigma):X\longrightarrow X
$$

for the arithmetic Galois automorphism. On the
small pro-etale site, the
derived pullback functors $L\Phi^m{}^*$ and $Lg_\gamma^{m*}$ are the
pullbacks along these endomorphisms.

*Recorded in advance* from chapter *The trace formula* of the source.

attrs.title: Scheme and Galois Frobenius of the geometric fiber

objects.body:
Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions of this trace-formula blueprint: $A=A_{E,n}$, $X_0$
separated finite type over $k_0$, $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, on the
small pro-etale site. A
*strict Weil complex at $A$* is a pair $(K,\varphi)$ with
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ and an isomorphism formed using the
derived pullback

$$
\varphi:Lg_\gamma^*K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }K,
$$

where $g_\gamma=g_X$ is the
geometric-Frobenius
automorphism of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]; morphisms are morphisms
of $K$ commuting with $\varphi$. Write
$D^b_{ctf,\mathrm W}(X,A)$ for the resulting category, the finite
coefficient stage of the
Weil-complex category of
the trace-formula chapter, with its forgetful functor $\operatorname{For}$.
This is a category of pairs over $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, not a triangulated
(derived) category of Weil sheaves such as $D^b_{c,\mathrm W}$ of
[def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]: its Hom-groups are not Ext groups of Weil
sheaves (a nonsplit Frobenius extension of $A$ by $A$, a Jordan block, gives
no nonzero map $A\to A[1]$ of pairs). Only traces, stalk Frobenius maps,
