weights of cohomology sheaves, equivariant maps and functorial triangles are
used.

*Recorded in advance* from chapter *The trace formula* of the source.

attrs.title: Strict Weil complex at finite coefficients

objects.body:
In the setting of [def-trf-correspondence-between-pairs], let
$P\in D(Z,A)$ and let $i:T\to Z$ be a separated finite-type morphism of
separated finite-type $k$-schemes, with compact-support direct image
$Ri_!$ as in the coefficient conventions. A *class supported on $i$*
with values in $P$ is an element of

$$
H_T^0(Z,P):=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(Z,A)}\bigl(Ri_!A_T,P\bigr),
$$

where $A_T$ is the constant sheaf. The map $i$ is part of the data of
the class: it need not be an immersion, and different specified maps
with the same image give different groups.

Fix the coefficient conventions of
[def-trf-coefficient-conventions], $A=A_{E,n}$, $s=\Spec k$. Let
$X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes whose structure morphisms
$a_X,a_Y$ are exceptionally admissible
([def-trf-admissibility]), with the dualizing data
$\omega_X,\omega_Y$, $D_X,D_Y$ and evaluations of
[def-trf-dualizing-complex], and let
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$. Put

$$
Z:=Y\times_sX,\qquad p_1:Z\to Y,\quad p_2:Z\to X,
$$

and let $\tau:X\times_sY\xrightarrow{\sim}Y\times_sX$ exchange the
factors. External products are
$M\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}N:=Lp_1^*M\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}Lp_2^*N$
([def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]).

*Opposite pairs.* Let $(C,c,u)$ be a correspondence from $(X,K)$ to
$(Y,L)$ and $(D,d,v)$ an opposite correspondence, in the sense of
[def-trf-correspondence-between-pairs] (which generalizes
[def-trf-correspondence], the case $(Y,L)=(X,K)$); such a pair is an
*opposite pair*. With $\bar d=\tau d:D\to Z$ and
$E=E(C,D)=C\times_{c,Z,\bar d}D$ as there, write $e_C:E\to C$,
$e_D:E\to D$ for the projections and
$e:=c\,e_C=\bar d\,e_D:E\to Z$ (all maps separated of finite type, and
exceptionally admissible where an exceptional functor is applied; in
particular $c$, $\bar d$, $e$ and $p_1$ are exceptionally admissible).

*Step 1: the supported classes.* Let
$[u]\in H^0_C\bigl(Z,\RHom_A(Lp_2^*K,Rp_1^!L)\bigr)$ be the class of
$u$ given by [lem-trf-correspondence-class], a class supported on $c$
in the sense of [def-trf-supported-class].
The Künneth–Verdier
isomorphism of [thm-trf-kunneth-verdier] for the product $Y\times_sX$,
with $M=L$ and $N=K$,
$\kappa_{L,K}:L\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}D_XK\xrightarrow{\sim}
\RHom_A(Lp_2^*K,Rp_1^!L)$, gives the class supported on $c$

$$
\widetilde u:=\kappa_{L,K}^{-1}\circ[u]:
Rc_!A_C\longrightarrow P:=L\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}D_XK .
$$

The same construction applied to $(D,d,v)$ on $X\times_sY$ gives
$\kappa_{K,L}^{-1}\circ[v]:Rd_!A_D\to K\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}D_YL$;
applying the isomorphism $R\tau_!=R\tau_*$ (with
$R\tau_!Rd_!\simeq R\bar d_!$ by [prop-functor-package], item (3))
and the symmetry of $\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}$, which identifies
$R\tau_*(K\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}D_YL)$ with
$D_YL\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}K$ on $Z$, gives

$$
\widetilde v:R\bar d_!A_D\longrightarrow Q:=D_YL\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}K .
$$

*Step 2: the support of the product.* The projection formula
([prop-functor-package], item (5)), the base change
$Lc^*R\bar d_!\simeq Re_{C!}Le_D^*$ in the Cartesian square defining
$E$ ([prop-functor-package], item (4)), and the composition
$Rc_!Re_{C!}\simeq Re_!$ ([prop-functor-package], item (3)) give the
canonical isomorphism

$$
\mu:Re_!A_E\simeq Rc_!Re_{C!}Le_D^*A_D
\simeq Rc_!\bigl(Lc^*R\bar d_!A_D\bigr)
\simeq Rc_!A_C\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}R\bar d_!A_D .
$$

*Step 3: the pairing.* Using the symmetry of
$\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}$ and the monoidality of $Lp_i^*$,
$P\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}Q\simeq
Lp_1^*(D_YL\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}L)\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}
Lp_2^*(D_XK\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}K)$; the two Verdier evaluations
$\operatorname{ev}_L$, $\operatorname{ev}_K$ of
[def-trf-dualizing-complex] map this to
$\omega_Y\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}\omega_X$, and the exceptional
Künneth isomorphism $\alpha$ of [prop-trf-exceptional-kunneth] for
$f_1=a_Y$, $f_2=a_X$, $L_1=L_2=A_s$ (note $a_Y\times a_X=a_Z$ and
$A_s\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}A_s=A_s$ on $s\times_ss=s$) is the product
comparison $\omega_Y\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}\omega_X\simeq\omega_Z$.
Composing,

$$
\sigma_{u,v}:
Re_!A_E\xrightarrow{\ \mu\ }
Rc_!A_C\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}R\bar d_!A_D
\xrightarrow{\widetilde u\otimes\widetilde v}
P\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}Q
\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_L\boxtimes\operatorname{ev}_K}
\omega_Y\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}\omega_X
\xrightarrow{\ \alpha\ }\omega_Z .
$$

The *Borel–Moore section* (of [def-trf-integration])

$$
\langle u,v\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}:A_E\longrightarrow\omega_E
$$

is the exceptional adjoint of $\sigma_{u,v}$: its image under
$\Hom_Z(Re_!A_E,\omega_Z)\cong\Hom_E(A_E,Re^!\omega_Z)$, followed by
the identification $Re^!\omega_Z\simeq\omega_E$ of
[thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition].

*The diagonal case.* For $(Y,L)=(X,K)$ take the opposite
correspondence $D=X$, $d=\Delta_X$, $v=1_K$ (both legs are
$\operatorname{id}_X$); then $\bar d=\Delta_X$ and
$E=C\times_{X\times_sX,c,\Delta_X}X=\Fix(c)$ is the fixed scheme of
[def-trf-fixed-scheme]. Abbreviate
$\LT_B(u,v)=\LT_B(\langle u,v\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}})$, the local term of
[def-trf-local-term] (for $B$ a proper open-and-closed component). That
$\langle u,1_K\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}$ is the trace class of
[def-trf-trace-class] is [lem-trf-trace-class-diagonal-pairing].

That this construction is unconditional is
[prop-trf-trace-class-unconditional].

Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions, $A=A_{E,n}$, $s=\Spec k$, and let
$c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times_sX$ be an admissible
cohomological correspondence with
fixed scheme
$F=\operatorname{Fix}(c)$ of [def-trf-fixed-scheme]. A
correspondence $u:Lc_2^*K\to Rc_1^!K$ is equivalently a section
$\widetilde u:A_C\to\mathcal H_c(K)$ of the
trace-class source of
[def-trf-trace-class-source]; its *Verdier trace class* is

$$
\operatorname{Tr}_c(u):
A\xrightarrow{\widetilde u}
R\Gamma(C,\mathcal H_c(K))
\xrightarrow{\mathfrak t_{c,K}}
R\Gamma(F,\omega_{F,A})
$$

where the displayed morphism is identified with an element of
$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(F,A)}(A_F,\omega_{F,A})$ by the
global-sections adjunction, and $\mathfrak t_{c,K}$ is
the morphism of [lem-trf-trace-map-from-external-duality]. Here
$\omega_{F,A}$ is the
dualizing complex of
[def-trf-dualizing-complex].

attrs.title: Trace-class notation conditional on its construction

objects.body:
In the setting of [def-trf-correspondence], for an admissible
cohomological correspondence
$u:Lc_2^*K\to Rc_1^!K$ put

$$
\mathcal H_c(K):=
R\mathcal Hom_A\bigl(Lc_2^*K,Rc_1^!K\bigr)\in D(C,A).
$$

By the tensor–internal-Hom
adjunction, the correspondence $u$ is equivalently a section (the
*mate*) $\widetilde u:A_C\to\mathcal H_c(K)$, i.e. an element of
$\Hom_{D(C,A)}(A_C,\mathcal H_c(K))$: the adjunction isomorphism

$$
\Hom_{D(C,A)}(A_C,R\mathcal Hom_A(Lc_2^*K,Rc_1^!K))
\cong
\Hom_{D(C,A)}(Lc_2^*K,Rc_1^!K)
$$

identifies $\widetilde u$ with $u$.

Let $j_0:X_0\hookrightarrow Y_0$ be an
open immersion of
separated finite-type schemes over the
finite field $k_0$, with
base change $j:X\hookrightarrow Y$. For a
strict Weil complex
$(K,\varphi)$ on $X$, set

$$
\bar K=j_!K,\qquad
\bar\varphi:
Lg_Y^*j_!K\xrightarrow{b_{g_Y}}
j_!Lg_X^*K\xrightarrow{j_!\varphi}j_!K.
$$

Here $j_!$ is extension by
zero ([def-weil-extension-by-zero]), and $b_{g_Y}$ is the comparison
isomorphism of [lem-trf-open-square-exchange] for the Cartesian square
of [lem-trf-frobenius-open-square].

Fix the global finite-field datum and the coefficient ring
$A=A_{E,n}$. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a separated morphism of
separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes, with geometric base change
$f:X\to Y$, and write $\Phi_X,\Phi_Y$ for the $q$-power scheme
Frobenii of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. For $m\geq1$ use the
relative Frobenius factorization of [d-relative-frob]:

$$
X'_m=Y\times_{\Phi_Y^m,Y,f}X,\qquad
p_m:X'_m\to X,\quad f'_m:X'_m\to Y,\qquad
r_m=(f,\Phi_X^m):X\to X'_m,
$$

so that $p_mr_m=\Phi_X^m$ and $f'_mr_m=f$; this uses
$f\Phi_X^m=\Phi_Y^mf$, which holds because $\Phi^m$ is the base
change of the $q^m$-power Frobenius of $k_0$-schemes, which commutes
with every $k_0$-morphism.

1. For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ the *Frobenius comparison*
$\theta_{f,m}=\theta_{f,m,K}$ is the composite
$$
L\Phi_Y^{m*}Rf_!K
\xrightarrow[\sim]{\operatorname{Ex}_!}Rf'_{m!}Lp_m^*K
\xrightarrow{Rf'_{m!}(\eta_{r_m})}
Rf'_{m!}Rr_{m*}Lr_m^*Lp_m^*K
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf_!L\Phi_X^{m*}K .
$$
The first arrow is the compact-support exchange of
[def-exchange-projection] for the Cartesian square defining $X'_m$,
an isomorphism by arbitrary base change ([prop-functor-package],
clause (4)). The second arrow is $Rf'_{m!}$ applied to the unit of
$Lr_m^*\dashv Rr_{m*}$ of [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. The last
arrow is $Rr_{m*}\simeq Rr_{m!}$ for the finite, hence proper, map
$r_m$, the composition law
$Rf'_{m!}Rr_{m!}\simeq R(f'_mr_m)_!=Rf_!$ ([prop-functor-package],
clause (3)), and $Lr_m^*Lp_m^*\simeq L(p_mr_m)^*=L\Phi_X^{m*}$
([def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]).
The middle unit is invertible: $r_m$ is a finite universal
homeomorphism by [i-relative-frob], so $Lr_m^*$ is an equivalence
on $D^b_{ctf}$ with invertible unit by [i-topology], applied to
$Lp_m^*K\in D^b_{ctf}(X'_m,A)$. Hence $\theta_{f,m}$ is an
isomorphism, natural in $K$ because each of its three arrows is
([fix-lem-exchanges], clause (1)).
1. For a Frobenius coefficient morphism $u:L\Phi_X^*K\to K$ of
[def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism] (no invertibility
assumed), the *Weil $!$-pushforward* of $(K,u)$ along $f$ is the
pair $(Rf_!K,\psi)$ with
$$
\psi=Rf_!u\circ\theta_{f,1}:\;
L\Phi_Y^*Rf_!K\xrightarrow{\ \theta_{f,1}\ }Rf_!L\Phi_X^*K
\xrightarrow{\ Rf_!u\ }Rf_!K .
$$
It lies in $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ by [prop-functor-package], and $\psi$
is a Frobenius coefficient morphism on $Rf_!K$.
1. In particular, for a strict Weil complex $(K,\varphi)$ of
[def-trf-strict-weil-complex], take $u=u_1=\varphi\circ\kappa_K$,
its scheme-Frobenius map of [def-trf-iterated-weil-map], with
$\kappa$ of [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison]. Then $\psi$ is a
composite of two isomorphisms, so $(Rf_!K,\psi)$ is a pushforward
with invertible scheme-Frobenius structure.

Let $q=p^r$ be a prime power, let $k=\mathbf F_q$, and let
$\overline k$ be an algebraic closure. Let $X$ be a
separated scheme of finite type
over $k$. The $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-coefficient derived categories
on $X_{\overline k}$ are those of
[def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], with
$H^i_c(X_{\overline k},\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ the compactly supported
cohomology of 02.

*Recorded in advance* from chapter *Weight foundations and monodromy groups* of the source.

Let $\alpha\in\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ be an eigenvalue of the
$\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-linear automorphism $\Phi_X^*$ of
[def-tw-frobenius-action]. The $q$-adic absolute value of
$\alpha$, in the *weight normalization*, is

$$
|\alpha|:=q^{v(\alpha)},\qquad|q|=q,
$$

where $v$ is the $\mathbf Q_\ell$-adic valuation normalized by
$v(q)=1$ (equivalently:
$|\alpha|=|\alpha|_{\mathbf Q_\ell\text{-adic}}^{-1}$ for the usual
normalized absolute value on $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with
$|\ell|=\ell^{-1}$), extended to each finite extension of
$\mathbf Q_\ell$ by the usual
$(|\alpha|)^{[K:\mathbf Q_\ell]}= |N_{K/\mathbf Q_\ell}(\alpha)|$ rule (the absolute value
$|\cdot|_{\mathbf Q_\ell\text{-adic}}$ alone would give
$|q|=q^{-1}$, so the reciprocal normalization is what makes
$|q|=q$ and hence the weight convention below). The
eigenvalue $\alpha$ has *weight* $w\in\mathbf Z$ if
$|\alpha|=q^{w/2}$.

Let $\Phi_X$ be the geometric Frobenius endomorphism of
$X_{\overline k}$ (the inverse of the $q$-power map, extended by base
change from $X$; the scheme-theoretic Frobenius is described in the
trace-formula chapter, 09). It induces, for every
$i$, a $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-linear automorphism

$$
\Phi_X^*:H^i(X_{\overline k},\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)
\longrightarrow H^i(X_{\overline k},\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell),
$$

and similarly on compactly supported cohomology; the same notation is used
after any base change.

*Recorded in advance* from chapter *Weight foundations and monodromy groups* of the source.

For an abelian category $\mathcal A$, a cochain complex consists of objects
$K^r$, $r\in\mathbf Z$, and differentials $d^r:K^r\to K^{r+1}$ satisfying
$d^{r+1}d^r=0$. Its cohomology is $\ker d^r/\operatorname{im}d^{r-1}$. A
quasi-isomorphism is a morphism of complexes inducing an isomorphism on every
cohomology object. The derived category $D(\mathcal A)$ is the localization
of the category of cochain complexes at these quasi-isomorphisms, with
morphism sizes taken in the chosen universe. See
[Stacks Project, Section 13.11](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05RR).

attrs.title: Derived category of an abelian category

objects.body:
Fix a prime $p$, $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, put $q=p^a$, and set
$k_0=\Fq$, and let $k=\Fbar$ be the fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$.
Fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, write
$\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and use
the finite-field datum.
Set

$$
\overline{\mathbf Q}^{(\ell)}=
\{z\in\Qlb:z\text{ is algebraic over }\mathbf Q\}.
$$

This is an algebraically closed subfield of $\Qlb$. Fix an algebraic
closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}$ of $\mathbf Q$. A $\mathbf Q$-embedding
$\jmath:\overline{\mathbf Q}\xrightarrow{\sim} \overline{\mathbf Q}^{(\ell)}$ is an ell-adic realization of algebraic
numbers.

attrs.title: The algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q$ inside $\Qlb$

objects.body:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]
$(p,a,q,k_0,k)$, a prime $\ell\neq p$, and a scheme $Y$. Set
$\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and use
the rationalized category [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] for every finite
coefficient field. Let $\mathcal E_\ell$ be the directed set of finite
extensions $E/\Ql$ contained in $\Qlb$. For $E\subset L$, the transition
functor is $K\mapsto K\otimes_E L$. Form a triangulated category $\mathcal
C_Y$ whose objects are pairs $(E,K)$ with $E\in\mathcal E_\ell$ and $K\in
D^b_c(Y,E)$, and whose morphisms between $(E,K)$ and $(E',K')$ are

$$
 \Hom_{\mathcal C_Y}((E,K),(E',K'))
 =\varinjlim_{\substack{L\in\mathcal E_\ell\\L\supset E,E'}}
 \Hom_{D^b_c(Y,L)}
 \bigl(K\otimes_E L,K'\otimes_{E'}L\bigr).
$$

Composition and distinguished triangles are represented over one common
finite extension. Define

$$
 D^b_c(Y,\Qlb)=\mathcal C_Y.
$$

No Karoubi completion is taken: the notation $\mathcal C_Y$ denotes the
common-stage category displayed above, in which no idempotent is formally
adjoined. Every object, morphism, and distinguished triangle has a finite
coefficient field of definition, after enlarging that field if necessary.

Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$, an integer $n\in\mathbf
Z_{\geq1}$, and put $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $S$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is
invertible, let $X,Y$ be finite-type
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] $S$-schemes, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type $S$-morphism, with a compactification
[def-weil-compactifications-refinements] $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline
X\xrightarrow{p}Y$. Say that $f$ carries the *ambient exceptional right
adjoint datum at $A$* if clause (1) of
[def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility] holds: the full
cohomological-dimension condition [def-weil-full-cohomological-dimension]
$\operatorname{FullCD}(p,A;c_{\mathrm{cd}})$ holds for some
$c_{\mathrm{cd}}\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, the compact-support direct image
[def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] $Rf_{!,n}$ has a right adjoint
$Rf_n^{\times}$ on the *ordinary* derived categories of the small pro-etale
sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site],

$$
 \operatorname{Hom}_Y\bigl(Rf_{!,n}K,L\bigr)\cong
 \operatorname{Hom}_X\bigl(K,Rf_n^{\times}L\bigr),
$$

and for every refinement of the compactification the units, counits and
comparison maps agree. This datum asserts the *existence* of the ambient
right adjoint and nothing about its values; it says nothing about
constructibility or finite Tor amplitude.

*Warning.* This datum is not satisfied in general. Its $\operatorname{FullCD}$ clause quantifies over *every* pro-etale sheaf of $A$-modules, and that fails already for the structure morphism of an elliptic curve $E$ over $\overline{\mathbf F}_p$ with $A=\mathbf F_r$, $r\neq p$: there is a pro-etale $A$-module sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $E$, not of etale origin, with $H^n(E_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal F)\neq0$ for every $n\geq1$, so $Rf_*=Rf_!$ does not preserve the coproduct $\bigoplus_n\mathcal F[n]$ and has no right adjoint on $D(E_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ nor on $D^+$ (rem:sf-ambient-counterexample in the six-functors chapter). The datum is therefore never assumed on the proof chain of this blueprint; what is used is the constructible exceptional adjoint of def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image, whose existence and adjunction on the bounded-below complexes of etale origin is the theorem thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class and whose preservation clauses are thm-sf-preservation-class.

Let $p$ be prime, let $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, put $q=p^a$ and
$k_0=\Fq$, and let $k=\Fbar$ be the
fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$.
Let $X_0/k_0$ be
smooth, proper, and geometrically
connected of pure dimension $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, and put
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. Fix an indeterminate $T$. For every prime
$\ell\neq p$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and for
$P(T)=\sum_r c_rT^r\in\mathbf Z[T]$ write
$P^{(\ell)}(T)=\sum_r(c_r\cdot1_{\Ql})T^r$, and let
$(V_{i,\ell},F_{i,\ell},P_{i,\ell})_{0\leq i\leq2d}$ be the
smooth-proper
cohomological family, and let $P_i(T)\in\mathbf Z[T]$ be the
integral Frobenius factor
with $P_i(0)=1$ and $P_i^{(\ell)}=P_{i,\ell}$ for every $\ell\neq p$.
For
$0\leq i\leq2d$, define

$$
b_i=\deg P_i.
$$

For every integer $i<0$ or $i>2d$, put $b_i=0$.

Fix $A=A_{E,n}$ and a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $Y$, where
$k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$. The *boundary duality input* for
$(Y,A)$ consists of the following assertions, on the chosen finite-stage
coefficient categories.

1. For every locally closed $T\subseteq Y$, the exceptional
adjoints and their composition laws define
$\omega_T=Ra_T^!A$ and
$D_T=R\mathcal Hom_T(-,\omega_T)$, and $D_T$ carries
$D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$ into itself.
1. For every closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ between such
pieces, the canonical boundary exchange
$$
\beta_L:i^*D_TL\longrightarrow D_ZRi^!L
\qquad(L\in D^b_{ctf}(T,A))
$$
is an isomorphism. It is the adjoint of the pairing
$$
i^*D_TL\otimes^L Ri^!L\longrightarrow
Ri^!(D_TL\otimes^L L)\longrightarrow Ri^!\omega_T=\omega_Z.
$$
These comparisons are compatible with evaluation: using $\beta_{D_TK}$
and the inverse of $D_Z\alpha_K$ from
[lem-weil-closed-costalk-duality], the restriction $i^*\delta_K$
identifies with $\delta_{i^*K}$.

The first clause includes preservation as a separate condition. The second
clause interchanges ordinary and exceptional restriction; it does not
identify $i^*$ with $Ri^!$.

For a complex $K$ of sheaves on the small pro-etale site
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] with cohomology sheaves
[def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] $\mathcal H^r(K)$, the *cohomological
support* is the set of degrees in which the cohomology does not vanish:

$$
 \operatorname{Supp}_{\mathrm{coh}}(K)
 =\{r\in\mathbf Z:\mathcal H^r(K)\neq0\}.
$$

Let $K_0$ be a field, let $X,Y$ be finite-type
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] $K_0$-schemes, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type $K_0$-morphism. Fix a prime $\ell$, write
$\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and require that its image in $K_0$ is invertible.
Choose a finite extension $E/\Ql$, an integer $n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, and
put $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $c=(j,\bar f)$ be an object of the compactification
category [def-weil-compactifications-refinements] $\operatorname{Comp}(f)$.
Using the finite-torsion coefficient sheaves
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] $A$, the derived direct image
[def-weil-derived-direct-image] $R\bar f_{*,n}$, and the extension-by-zero
functor [def-weil-extension-by-zero] $j_!$, set

$$
 Rf_{!,n}^{c}=R\bar f_{*,n}\,j_!:
 D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)
 \longrightarrow D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A),
$$

a functor attached to the chosen compactification $c$. Every property
asserted of it in this blueprint — independence of the chosen
compactification, base-change compatibility, coherence and the finite-level
comparisons — is asserted on the full subcategory $\mathcal
D^{+}_{\mathrm{et}}(X,A)\subseteq D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ of complexes that
*come from the etale site* in the sense of the etale-origin witness of the
proper-base-change chapter, a forward reference since the comparison morphism
of sites is introduced there; that subcategory contains the finite-torsion
constructible complexes of [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]
together with their witnesses. On $\mathcal D^{+}_{\mathrm{et}}(X,A)$ the
functor is independent of $c$, so there the superscript may be dropped; off
that subcategory nothing beyond the displayed formula is asserted, and in
particular no independence, base-change or constructibility claim is made.
Here $R\bar f_{*,n}$ is computed by a K-injective resolution and $j_!$ is
exact.

attrs.title: Compact-support candidate attached to a compactification

objects.body:
Let $S$ be a scheme; when $S$ is a finite-field scheme, impose the geometric
hypotheses [def-weil-geometric-hypotheses]. Let $X$ and $Y$ be finite-type
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] $S$-schemes, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type $S$-morphism. A *compactification* $c=(j,\bar f)$ of
$f$ is a factorization

$$
 X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y
$$

with $j$ an open immersion, $\bar f$ a proper $S$-morphism, and $\bar f\circ
j=f$. A *refinement* $u:c_1\to c_2$ is a proper $Y$-morphism

$$
 u:\overline X_1\longrightarrow\overline X_2
$$

such that $u\circ j_1=j_2$. Compactifications and refinements form a category
$\operatorname{Comp}(f)$.

For the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], fix a prime
$\ell\neq p$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$, a scheme $Y$, and a uniformizer
$\varpi_E$ of the valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$. For each $n\in\mathbf
Z_{\geq1}$, set $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ as in the finite-torsion
constructibility condition [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], and
use the derived tensor product [def-weil-derived-tensor] on the small
pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] of $Y$. The completed
coefficient sheaf is

$$
 \widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}=\varprojlim_n(A_{E,n})_Y
$$

in the abelian category of sheaves of rings. Let
$\Sh(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ be the category of modules over
$\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$, and let $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ be
its localization at quasi-isomorphisms; this notation does not mean modules
over the discrete constant sheaf $(\mathcal O_E)_Y$. Cohomology sheaves of
complexes on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ are those of the standard $t$-structure on
this derived category, as in [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. For every
$n$ the surjection $\widehat{\mathcal
O}_{E,Y}\twoheadrightarrow(A_{E,n})_Y$ makes every $A_{E,n}$-module a module
over $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$, and

$$
 \operatorname{Res}_n:
 \Sh(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})
 \longrightarrow\Sh(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)
$$

denotes the resulting *restriction of scalars*; its exactness is recorded
with the other properties of this construction. The reduction morphisms
$A_{E,n+1}\twoheadrightarrow A_{E,n}$ are the maps
$(A_{E,n+1})_Y\twoheadrightarrow(A_{E,n})_Y$ between constant sheaves.

Fix a prime $p$, an integer $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, put $q=p^a$, $k_0=\Fq$,
and let $k=\Fbar$ be the fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$. Fix a prime
$\ell\neq p$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$
of $\Ql$, a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $Y_0$, and
$Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$. Put

$$
 g_Y=\operatorname{id}_{Y_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{Frob}_q):
 Y\longrightarrow Y
$$

for the geometric-Frobenius automorphism [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. Fix
$\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$, $w\in\mathbf R$, and let $K\in
D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(Y,\Qlb)$ be a Weil complex. Let $a_Y:Y\to\Spec k$ be the structure morphism, with $Ra_Y^!$ its
constructible exceptional inverse image [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]
at $\Qlb$ (defined for every separated finite-type morphism; no admissibility
hypothesis in the ambient sense of
[def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility] is imposed). Choose a
dualizing Weil complex $(\omega_Y,\theta_{\omega_Y})$ and require

$$
 \operatorname{For}(\omega_Y)=Ra_Y^!\Qlb,
$$

where $Ra_Y^!$ denotes the exceptional inverse image for the structure
morphism. Require
$\theta_{\omega_Y}:Lg_Y^*\operatorname{For}(\omega_Y)
\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{For}(\omega_Y)$ to be the canonical
functorial Weil lift induced by geometric-Frobenius base change and the
adjunction units and counits, rather than an arbitrary Weil lift. The
internal derived Hom is the derived pullback/tensor/Hom operation. Define
$D_YK$ to be the Weil complex whose underlying complex is

$$
 \operatorname{For}(D_YK)=
 R\mathcal Hom_{\Qlb}\bigl(\operatorname{For}(K),\operatorname{For}(\omega_Y)\bigr),
$$

with the Weil structure induced by $\theta_K$ and $\theta_{\omega_Y}$. For
every $j\in\mathbf Z$, the cohomology sheaf $\mathcal
H^j(\operatorname{For}K)$ is assigned the punctual-weight notion
[def-weil-punctual-weights]. Define

$$
 \Wt_{\iota,\leq w}(K)
 \Longleftrightarrow
 \bigl(\mathcal H^j(\operatorname{For}K)
 \text{ is \(\iota\)-mixed of weights at most \(w+j\) for every }
 j\in\mathbf Z\bigr),
$$

$$
 \Wt_{\iota,\geq w}(K)\Longleftrightarrow
 \Wt_{\iota,\leq-w}(D_YK).
$$

The complex $K$ is $\iota$-pure of weight $w$ if both predicates hold.

Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] $p,a,q,k_0,k$, a
prime $\ell\neq p$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic closure
$\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and choose a finite-type
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] $k$-scheme $Y$ and a finite extension
$E/\Ql$ contained in $\Qlb$. Let $\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$. For $\Lambda=E$, use
the rationalized coefficient category
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]; its integral representatives have
finite-level reductions satisfying the finite-torsion constructibility
condition [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. For $\Lambda=\Qlb$, use
the common-stage category
[def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. For every $m\in\mathbf Z$,
write $\tau^{\leq m}$ and $\tau^{\geq m}$ for the constructible truncation
functors obtained from the standard $t$-structure. For $\Lambda=E$ or
$\Qlb$, define

$$
\begin{aligned}
 D^{\leq0}_c(Y,\Lambda)&=
 \{K:\tau^{\geq1}K=0\},\\
 D^{\geq0}_c(Y,\Lambda)&=
 \{K:\tau^{\leq-1}K=0\}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Their intersection is the abelian category $\Sh_c(Y,\Lambda)$, called the
*constructible heart*; its objects are constructible $\Lambda$-adic sheaves
whose finite-level reductions satisfy the finite-torsion constructibility
condition [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], with the rationalized
and common-stage interpretations supplied by the coefficient constructions.

Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$, an integer $n\in\mathbf
Z_{\geq1}$, and a scheme $Y$ on which $\ell$ is invertible, as well as
integers $a,b\in\mathbf Z$ with $a\leq b$. Put $A=A_{E,n}$, and use the
derived cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] $\mathcal
H^r$. Define

$$
D_c^{[a,b]}(Y,A)=
\{K\in D^b_c(Y,A):
\mathcal H^r(K)=0\text{ for every }
r\in\mathbf Z\setminus[a,b]\}.
$$

Here $D^b_c(Y,A)$ is the bounded category with the finite-torsion
constructibility condition [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility].

Fix a scheme $Y$, a commutative ring $A$, a complex $K\in
D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, and an integer $r\in\mathbf Z$. Let

$$
 \mathcal H^r(K)
$$

denote the $r$-th cohomology sheaf for the standard t-structure on the
derived category of sheaves of $A_Y$-modules on the small pro-etale site
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. The nonpositive part of this
t-structure consists of complexes with vanishing cohomology in positive
degrees, and the nonnegative part consists of complexes with vanishing
cohomology in negative degrees. The notation is invariant under
quasi-isomorphism.

attrs.title: Cohomology sheaves of a derived complex

objects.body:
Use the completed integral coefficient sheaf
[def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$, its
reductions $(A_{E,n})_Y$, the derived category $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal
O_E)$, and the restriction of scalars $\operatorname{Res}_n$ attached to
them, exact by [lem-weil-restriction-of-scalars-exact]. For a complex $K\in
D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ put

$$
 K_n:=K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n},
$$

the derived tensor product [def-weil-derived-tensor] with the constant
$(A_{E,n})_Y$-module. The reduction morphisms $A_{E,n+1}\twoheadrightarrow
A_{E,n}$ make $(K_n)_{n\geq1}$ an inverse system in the single triangulated
category $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$, with transition maps
$\operatorname{Res}_{n+1}K_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_nK_n$. Write

$$
 R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nK_n
$$

for the derived limit [def-weil-derived-limit] of this inverse system, formed
inside the single triangulated category $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$
by its Roos triangle; no strict-tower model and no resolution of the system
is chosen, and the transition maps above are already maps in
$D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$. The compatible maps $K\to
\operatorname{Res}_nK_n$ induce a canonical map

$$
 K\longrightarrow R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nK_n,
$$

and $K$ is *derived complete* if this canonical map is an isomorphism. This
is the coefficient-sheaf form of Definition 15.93.4 of the Stacks Project,
Tag [091S](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/091S); the equivalent
description of derived completeness by a derived limit over the Koszul tower
$K_\bullet(A,f_1^n,\dots,f_r^n)$ of the generators of the ideal (in Situation
15.93.15 of the Stacks Project) is Lemma 15.93.17, Tag
[091Z](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/091Z).

Let $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ be the full triangulated subcategory of
$D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$, the derived category of the completed
integral coefficient sheaf [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], whose
objects $K$ are derived complete [def-weil-derived-complete] and satisfy

$$
 K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}\in D^b_c(Y,A_{E,n})
$$

for every $n\geq1$, where $D^b_c(Y,A_{E,n})$ is the category of bounded
complexes satisfying the finite-torsion constructibility condition
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], the derived tensor product
[def-weil-derived-tensor] being that of the derived tensor notation. In
addition we require that the cohomological supports
[def-weil-cohomological-support]

$$
 \operatorname{Supp}_{\mathrm{coh}}
 \bigl(K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}\bigr)
$$

are contained in a single interval $[r,s]$ of $\mathbf Z$ with $r\leq s$
independent of $n$. This uniform amplitude of the reductions is part of the
definition of $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$, and it is the only boundedness
condition imposed on them.

Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$, an integer $n\in\mathbf
Z_{\geq1}$, and put $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $X,Y$ be schemes on which $\ell$ is
invertible, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]; write $f_n$ for this morphism at
coefficient level $A_{E,n}$. On the small pro-etale sites
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with derived pullback and internal
Hom notation [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and derived tensor
notation [def-weil-derived-tensor], the functor
$f_*:\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)\to\Sh(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ is left exact. At
finite level, choose a K-injective resolution and define its total
right-derived functor by

$$
 Rf_{*,n}=R(f_n)_*:D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})
 \longrightarrow D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n}).
$$

For a derived-complete integral [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]
complex $K\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$, define

$$
 Rf_*K=
 R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_n Rf_{*,n}
 \bigl(K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}\bigr).
$$

The tower maps are induced by $A_{E,n+1}\twoheadrightarrow A_{E,n}$. The
finite-reduction comparison is the natural map

$$
 (Rf_*K)\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}
 \longrightarrow
 Rf_{*,n}\bigl(K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}\bigr);
$$

its being an isomorphism, and its compatibility with composition and scalar
extension, are separate comparison assertions, not part of this definition of
the derived direct image. Here $A_{E,n}$ and finite-level constructibility
are the finite-torsion coefficient data
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], and $\mathcal H^r$ is the
cohomology-sheaf functor [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. For
$\Lambda=E$ use the rationalized category
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]; for $\Lambda=\Qlb$ use the common-stage
category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients].

Let $\mathcal D$ be a triangulated category and let $(K_n,f_n)_{n\in\mathbf
Z_{\geq1}}$ be an inverse system of objects of $\mathcal D$, with transition
maps $f_n:K_{n+1}\to K_n$. Assume that the countable product $\prod_nK_n$
exists in $\mathcal D$, and let

$$
 1-s:\prod_nK_n\longrightarrow\prod_nK_n,\qquad
 (k_n)_{n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}}\longmapsto
 \bigl(k_n-f_{n+1}(k_{n+1})\bigr)_{n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}}
$$

be the *transition endomorphism* of the system. An object $K\in\mathcal D$ is
a *derived limit*, or *homotopy limit*, of $(K_n,f_n)$ if it is the first
term of a distinguished triangle

$$
 K\longrightarrow\prod_nK_n\xrightarrow{\ 1-s\ }\prod_nK_n
 \longrightarrow K[1],
$$

and one then writes $K=R\varprojlim_nK_n$. The displayed triangle is the
*Roos triangle* of the system. The definition is made inside the triangulated
category $\mathcal D$, for an inverse system of objects *of* $\mathcal D$: no
resolution of the system is chosen and no model for $\mathcal D$ is fixed. It
is Definition 13.34.1 of the Stacks Project, Tag
[08TC](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08TC).

attrs.title: Derived limit of an inverse system

objects.body:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$, an integer $n\in\mathbf
Z_{\geq1}$, and put $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $X,Y$ be schemes on which $\ell$ is
invertible, let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and, for every coefficient level, let
$f_n$ denote the morphism $f$ equipped with coefficients in $A_{E,n}$. Use
the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] on $X$ and
$Y$. The symbol $A$ denotes the constant coefficient sheaf on each such site,
and $D(-,A)$ is its ambient derived category. For $K\in
D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, and for every scheme $W\in\{X,Y\}$ and $M,N\in
D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, define

$$
 Lf^*K=f^{-1}K\otimes^L_{f^{-1}A}A,
 \qquad
 M\otimes_A^L N,
 \qquad
 R\mathcal Hom_A(M,N)
$$

using K-flat resolutions for the derived tensor products
[def-weil-derived-tensor] and a K-injective resolution of the second variable
for derived internal Hom. Finite-torsion coefficients use finite-torsion
constructibility [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. For integral
coefficients, the K-flat and K-injective resolutions are taken in the ambient
derived category of modules over the completed coefficient sheaf. The
derived-complete integral category
[def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] is the specified full
subcategory; a resolution is not required to remain in that subcategory term
by term. Write

$$
 Lf_n^*=L(f_n)^*.
$$

For $\Lambda\in\{\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$, define the operation by the
compatible finite reductions, the derived inverse limit for $\mathcal O_E$,
the rationalization for $E$, and the common-stage coefficient construction
for $\Qlb$, using the rationalized coefficient category
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and the algebraically closed coefficient
category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients].

attrs.title: Derived pullback, tensor product, and internal Hom

objects.body:
Fix a scheme $Y$ and a commutative ring $A$, and use the small pro-etale site
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$. A complex $P$
of $A_Y$-modules is *K-flat* if tensoring it with every acyclic complex
preserves acyclicity. For complexes $K_1,K_2$ of $A_Y$-modules, choose a
quasi-isomorphism $P\to K_1$ with $P$ K-flat and define

$$
 K_1\otimes_A^L K_2=P\otimes_A K_2
$$

in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$. For a ring map $A\to B$ and a complex $K_1$,
write $K_1\otimes_A^L B$ for derived tensor with the constant $B_Y$-module.

Let $p$ be prime, let $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, put $q=p^a$, and set
$k_0=\Fq$; let $k=\Fbar$ be the
fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$.
Fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and fix an
indeterminate $T$. For $P(T)=\sum_r c_rT^r\in\mathbf Z[T]$, write
$P^{(\ell)}(T)=\sum_r(c_r\cdot1_{\Ql})T^r$ for coefficientwise extension.
Let
$X_0/k_0$ be smooth,
proper, and geometrically connected of pure dimension
$d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, and put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. Let $F$ be
geometric Frobenius. For each integer $i$
with $0\leq i\leq2d$, let

$$
V_{i,\ell}=H^i(X,\Ql),\qquad
F_{i,\ell}=F\vert_{V_{i,\ell}},\qquad
P_{i,\ell}(T)=\det(1-TF_{i,\ell}\mid V_{i,\ell}).
$$

These data form the
smooth-proper
cohomological family, where $H^i(X,\Ql)$ is
ordinary cohomology. Let
$P_i(T)\in\mathbf Z[T]$ be an
integral Frobenius factor
with $P_i(0)=1$ and $P_i^{(\ell)}(T)=P_{i,\ell}(T)$, and define the
Betti number
$b_i=\deg P_i=\dim_{\Ql}V_{i,\ell}$.
For a polynomial $P(T)=\sum_{r\geq0}c_rT^r$, with coefficients
$c_r$ indexed by integers $r\geq0$, and an integer $m\geq0$, write
$[T^m]P(T)=c_m$ for its coefficient of $T^m$.
For $0\leq i\leq2d$, set

$$
D_i=(-1)^{b_i}[T^{b_i}]P_i(T)\in\mathbf Z\setminus\{0\}.
$$

The image of $D_i$ in $\Ql$ is
$\det(F_{i,\ell}\mid H^i(X,\Ql))$. Define

$$
\chi=\sum_{i=0}^{2d}(-1)^ib_i.
$$

Define also the alternating determinant scalar

$$
\Delta=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}D_i^{(-1)^i}\in\mathbf Q^\times.
$$

Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$, an integer $n\in\mathbf
Z_{\geq1}$, and put $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $S$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is
invertible, let $X,Y$ be finite-type
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] $S$-schemes, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type $S$-morphism. Choose a compactification
[def-weil-compactifications-refinements] $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline
X\xrightarrow{p}Y$, so $j$ is an open immersion and $p$ is proper. Use
finite-torsion constructibility
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. Say that $f$ is
*exceptional-adjoint admissible at $A$* if:

1. the full cohomological-dimension condition
   [def-weil-full-cohomological-dimension]
   $\operatorname{FullCD}(p,A;c_{\mathrm{cd}})$ holds for some
   $c_{\mathrm{cd}}\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, and $Rf_n^{\times}$ is a right
   adjoint to $Rf_{!,n}$ on the ambient derived categories, and for every
   refinement its units, counits, and comparison maps agree;
2. there are *signed* integers $c_f^-,c_f^+\in\mathbf Z$ such that, for every
   pair of integers $a\leq b$, with $D_c^{[a,b]}$ the constructible
   cohomological interval subcategory
   [def-weil-constructible-intervals],
   $$
    L\in D_c^{[a,b]}(Y,A)\Longrightarrow
    Rf_n^{\times}L\in D_c^{[a+c_f^-,b+c_f^+]}(X,A);
   $$
   the constants record the cohomological bounds of the right adjoint. Their
   signs allow shifts in either direction; proving these bounds for a
   particular geometric morphism is a separate obligation.
3. for the finite-Tor subcategory [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]
   $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$, one has
   $$
    L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)
   \Longrightarrow
    Rf_n^{\times}L\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A).
   $$

For $\Lambda\in\{\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$, call $f$ admissible at $\Lambda$
when the three displayed conditions hold at every finite coefficient stage
with uniform bounds and when the finite-reduction and scalar-extension maps
for the corresponding right adjoints are isomorphisms. These are proof
obligations for restriction of an ambient right adjoint, not consequences of
the definition of a separated finite-type morphism.

*Warning.* Clause (1) is not satisfied in general: its
$\operatorname{FullCD}$ condition fails for the structure morphism of an
elliptic curve over $\overline{\mathbf F}_p$ with $A=\mathbf F_r$, $r\neq p$,
and for that morphism $Rf_!=Rf_*$ has no right adjoint on the ambient derived
category, nor on $D^+$ (rem:sf-ambient-counterexample in the six-functors
chapter). Hence the structure morphism of a smooth proper variety may *not*
be presupposed exceptional-adjoint admissible in this sense, and no statement
on the proof chain of this blueprint assumes it. What the blueprint uses is
the constructible exceptional adjoint of def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image,
defined without clause (1) from the etale adjoint; for it the analogues of
(1)–(3) on $D^b_c$ and $D^b_{ctf}$ are theorems for every separated
finite-type morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes (thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class
for the adjunction, thm-sf-preservation-class for the two preservation
clauses with the constants $c_f^-=-2D$, $c_f^+=2\dim Y+1$). The present
definition is retained only to name the stronger, optional, ambient notion.

Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with valuation ring $\mathcal
O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and an integer $n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, with
$A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $S$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is
invertible, let $X,Y$ be finite-type
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] $S$-schemes, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type $S$-morphism; in every use of this blueprint $S=\Spec k$
with $k$ a field, so that $X$ and $Y$ are Noetherian. *No ambient datum is
assumed.* Let $f^{\times}:D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)\to D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ be the
right adjoint of the etale compact-support functor
$Rf^{\mathrm{et}}_!=Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}j^{\mathrm{et}}_!$ attached to a
compactification, which exists unconditionally by Brown representability on
the ordinary etale derived categories of the Noetherian schemes $X,Y$ (the
etale exceptional adjoint, thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint of the smooth
duality chapter). Use finite-torsion constructibility
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] and the compact-support direct image
[def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. On the small pro-etale sites
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with $\nu_X,\nu_Y$ the comparison morphisms
[def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], *define*

$$
 Rf_n^!:=\nu_X^*\,f^{\times}\,R\nu_{Y,*}:
 D^+(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})\longrightarrow D^+(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n}),
$$

the etale right adjoint transported along the etale/pro-etale comparison;
on $D^b_c(Y,A_{E,n})$, every object of which is of etale origin,
$L\cong\nu_Y^*G$, this is $Rf_n^!L=\nu_X^*f^{\times}G$, and one restricts to

$$
 Rf_n^!:D^b_c(Y,A_{E,n})\longrightarrow D^b_c(X,A_{E,n}).
$$

For $\Lambda\in\{\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$, use respectively derived inverse
limits, rationalization, and the common-stage construction
[def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] of the compatible finite-level
functors, and define

$$
 Rf^!:D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)\longrightarrow D^b_c(X,\Lambda).
$$

For $K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ and $L\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$, characterize the
resulting functor by the natural adjunction isomorphisms

$$
 \Hom_Y(Rf_!K,L)\cong\Hom_X(K,Rf^!L).
$$

The two defining properties of this functor are theorems, not hypotheses.
The adjunction isomorphism holds for every bounded-below $K$ of etale origin
(in particular every $K\in D^b_c(X,A_{E,n})$) and every bounded-below $L$,
with units and counits compatible with refinements of the compactification:
this is thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class (the etale adjunction transported by the
compact-support comparison and the full faithfulness of $\nu^*$ on $D^+$).
The displayed typing — that $Rf_n^!$ carries $D^b_c(Y,A_{E,n})$ into
$D^b_c(X,A_{E,n})$, and finite-Tor objects
[def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] into finite-Tor objects, with explicit bounds
$[a,b]\mapsto[a-2D,b+2\dim Y+1]$ independent of $n$ — is
thm-sf-preservation-class, proved by localizing on affine charts and composing
the closed-immersion and smooth cases; the primary source for the
preservation of constructibility and of finite Tor dimension with the
non-regular coefficient rings $\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ is Zheng,
arXiv:1006.3810, Prop. 2.29(2), 3.16, 3.21 and Lemma 3.18. These are the
analogues, for the constructible functor, of clauses (2) and (3) of
[def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility], and the stage-independence of the
constants is what makes the normalized systems of the integral stage well
defined.

*Relation to the ambient datum.* The ambient exceptional right adjoint datum
[def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint] is *not* assumed anywhere in this
definition, and it is false in general: for the structure morphism of an
elliptic curve over $\overline{\mathbf F}_p$ with $A=\mathbf F_r$ the functor
$Rf_*=Rf_!$ has no right adjoint on $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, nor on $D^+$
(rem:sf-ambient-counterexample in the six-functors chapter). When the datum
happens to hold together with the preservation clauses of
[def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility], the restriction of the ambient
$Rf_n^{\times}$ to $D^b_c(Y,A_{E,n})$ agrees with $Rf_n^!$ by uniqueness of
adjoints; no statement of this blueprint needs this.

Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, let $U$ and $\overline X$ be schemes,
and let $j:U\hookrightarrow\overline X$ be an open immersion
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] of schemes, and use the small pro-etale
sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use the constant coefficient
sheaf $A$. This includes the rings $A_{E,n}$ of the finite-torsion
coefficient construction [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. For a
module sheaf $M$ on $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$, define extension by zero by
sheafifying the module presheaf

$$
 P_M(V)=
 \begin{cases}
 M(V\to U),&\text{if }V\to\overline X\text{ factors through }U,\\
 0,&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
$$

Such a factorization is unique because $j$ is an open immersion. Restriction
is the restriction in $M$ whenever the source factors through $U$, and is the
zero map otherwise. This defines the functor

$$
 j_!: \Sh(U_{\mathrm{proet}},A)
 \longrightarrow \Sh(\overline X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)
$$

by its action on sections and sheafification; no conservativity of ordinary
geometric stalks is part of the definition.

A field is a commutative ring $K$ with $0\neq1$ in which
every nonzero element has a multiplicative inverse.

*Mathlib:* `Field`. A basic Mathlib notion, used throughout, so it is not mapped as the Lean declaration of this object.

Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] $p,a,q,k_0,k$,
and fix a prime $\ell\neq p$. Write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic
closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and fix a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with valuation
ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$. Put
$A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. The finite-torsion constructibility
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] and derived-complete integral
[def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] conventions give the ordinary
derived categories $D(A_{E,n})$ and $D(\mathcal O_E)$. The
$\Qlb$-coefficient category uses the common finite-stage construction
[def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Let $\mathcal E_\ell$ denote
the directed set of finite extensions $E'/\Ql$ contained in $\Qlb$. Let
$D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A_{E,n})$ be the full subcategory of $D(A_{E,n})$
consisting of bounded complexes with finite cohomology modules. Let
$D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(\mathcal O_E)$ be the full subcategory of $D(\mathcal
O_E)$ consisting of bounded derived-complete complexes with finitely
generated cohomology modules, and let $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)$ be the bounded
derived category of finite-dimensional $E$-vector spaces. Put

$$
D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(\Qlb)=
 \underset{E\in\mathcal E_\ell}{\operatorname{2-colim}}
 D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E).
$$

For $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, evaluation at its geometric point defines
equivalences

$$
\operatorname{Fib}_s:D^b_c(s,A_{E,n})\xrightarrow{\sim}
D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A_{E,n}),\qquad
\operatorname{Fib}_s:D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)\xrightarrow{\sim}
D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(\mathcal O_E),\qquad
\operatorname{Fib}_s:D^b_c(s,E)\xrightarrow{\sim}D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E).
$$

At the algebraically closed coefficient, the same functor is obtained
stagewise and then passed to the finite-stage colimit:

$$
\operatorname{Fib}_s:D^b_c(s,\Qlb)\xrightarrow{\sim}
D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(\Qlb).
$$

attrs.title: Finite coefficient categories over a point

objects.body:
A vector subspace $V$ over
a field $K$ is finite-dimensional if
there are finitely many elements $v_1,\ldots,v_r\in V$ such that
every element of $V$ is a $K$-linear combination of them.

*Mathlib:* `FiniteDimensional`. A basic Mathlib notion, used throughout, so it is not mapped as the Lean declaration of this object.

Throughout this blueprint, fix a prime $p$ and an integer $a\in\mathbf
Z_{\geq1}$, and put $q=p^a$. Set

$$
 k_0=\Fq,
 \qquad
 k=\Fbar\text{ (a fixed algebraic closure of }k_0\text{)}.
$$

The tuple $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ is the *global finite-field datum* used throughout.
For every integer $n\geq1$, let $\mathbf F_{q^n}\subset k$ be the unique
subfield with $q^n$ elements. For any scheme $S$, write $|S|$ for its set of
closed points and, for $s\in|S|$, write $\kappa(s)$ for the residue field at
$s$. For a $k_0$-scheme $Y_0$ whose structure morphism is of finite type
[def-weil-finite-type-morphism], write

$$
 Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k,
 \qquad
 a_Y:Y\longrightarrow\Spec k
$$

for its geometric fiber and structure morphism. For every finite-type
$k_0$-scheme $Y_0$ and every $n\geq1$, define

$$
 Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})
 =\operatorname{Hom}_{k_0}\bigl(\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf F_{q^n},Y_0\bigr),
 \qquad
 \#Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})=\#\operatorname{Hom}_{k_0}
 \bigl(\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf F_{q^n},Y_0\bigr).
$$

For each prime $\ell\neq p$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic
closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and write $\Zl$ for the valuation ring of $\Ql$.
Thus $\Qlb$ is algebraically closed over $\Ql$, and $\Zl$ consists of the
elements of nonnegative $\ell$-adic valuation. A single choice of $\ell$ and
its coefficient fields is understood whenever they occur without a subscript.
For every finite extension $E/\Ql$, write $\mathcal O_E$ for its valuation
ring, choose a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and, for every $n\geq1$, set

$$
 A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n.
$$

Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$, an integer $n\in\mathbf
Z_{\geq1}$, and a scheme $Y$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. Put $A=A_{E,n}$
and use the derived cohomology sheaves
[def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] and the derived tensor product
[def-weil-derived-tensor]. For an object $K\in D^b_c(Y,A)$ satisfying the
finite-torsion constructibility condition
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], say that $K$ has *finite Tor
amplitude* if there are integers $a\leq b$ such that, for every sheaf $M$ of
$A$-modules placed in degree zero,

$$
 \mathcal H^r(K\otimes^L_A M)=0
 \qquad\text{for every }r\in\mathbf Z\setminus[a,b].
$$

Define $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ as the full triangulated subcategory of such objects.
For $K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$, a derived-complete bounded constructible
complex [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], say that $K$ has
finite Tor amplitude if every reduction $K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,j}$,
$j\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, has finite Tor amplitude with one interval
independent of $j$, and define $D^b_{ctf}(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ accordingly. At
field coefficients the finite-Tor subcategories are, by definition, the
bounded constructible rationalized category
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and its common-stage algebraically closed
coefficient category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]:

$$
 D^b_{ctf}(Y,E):=D^b_c(Y,E),
 \qquad
 D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Qlb):=D^b_c(Y,\Qlb).
$$

The second equality is interpreted in the finite-stage triangulated
2-colimit. For $A_{E,n}$, finite Tor amplitude is an additional condition and
does not follow from bounded constructibility. At the integral stage it is
imposed by the displayed definition; the separate residue-field argument
below proves that every object of the derived-complete constructible category
in fact satisfies it. This conclusion uses the compatibility of all
reductions of one integral object.

For the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], fix a prime
$\ell\neq p$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$ of its
valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, an integer $n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, and a
scheme $Y$. On the small pro-etale site
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$, put

$$
  A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n.
$$

A sheaf of $A_{E,n}$-modules on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is *constructible* if
there is a finite disjoint partition $Y=\bigsqcup_{\nu=1}^N Y_\nu$ by locally
closed constructible subschemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and
the restriction to each $Y_\nu$ is locally constant with finite
$A_{E,n}$-module stalks. For a derived complex, for every $i\in\mathbf Z$,
write $\mathcal H^i$ for its cohomology sheaves
[def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Define

$$
 D^b_c(Y,A_{E,n})\subset D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})
$$

to be the full triangulated subcategory of complexes with finitely many
nonzero cohomology sheaves, all constructible.

A morphism of schemes $f:X\to Y$ is *locally of finite type* if, for every
affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $Y$, the preimage $f^{-1}(V)$ has an
affine open cover by $\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ a finitely generated
$A$-algebra. It is *quasi-compact* if every such preimage is quasi-compact.
It is *of finite type* if both conditions hold; equivalently, the affine
cover of each $f^{-1}(V)$ can be chosen finite. For a scheme over a field,
finite type refers to its structure morphism. See
[Stacks Project, Section 29.15](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01T0).

For a commutative ring $R$, an element of $R[[T]]$ is a sequence
$(c_n)_{n\geq0}$ in $R$, written $\sum_{n\geq0}c_nT^n$.
Addition is coefficientwise, and the coefficient of $T^n$ in a
product is $\sum_{i=0}^n c_i d_{n-i}$.

*Mathlib:* `PowerSeries`. A basic Mathlib notion, used throughout, so it is not mapped as the Lean declaration of this object.

Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] $p,a,q,k_0,k$, where
$q=p^a$, and a prime $\ell\neq p$. Write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an
algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and choose a finite extension $E/\Ql$
contained in $\Qlb$. On $\Spec k_0$ and its geometric fiber
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], use the Tate-twist construction
[def-coefficient-twists-detailed]; its natural Weil isomorphism is induced by
the geometric Frobenius convention [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. Geometric
Frobenius acts on $E(1)$ by $q^{-1}$, on $E(m)$ by $q^{-m}$, and on $E(-m)$
by $q^m$, for every $m\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$. These actions commute with
finite reduction and scalar extension to $\Qlb$; in particular, the action on
$E(-d)$ is multiplication by $q^d$ for every $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$.

For the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], the
arithmetic Frobenius of $k$ is

$$
 \varphi_q:k\longrightarrow k,
 \qquad z\longmapsto z^q.
$$

Put $\gamma=\operatorname{Frob}_q=\varphi_q^{-1}$. For a finite-type
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] $k_0$-scheme $Y_0$, set
$Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$ and define the associated semilinear automorphism

$$
 g_Y=\operatorname{id}_{Y_0}\times\Spec(\gamma):Y\longrightarrow Y.
$$

This is distinct from the absolute $q$-power morphism of $Y$; every Frobenius
operator in this blueprint is induced by $g_Y$ and is geometric.

Fix a prime $p$, an integer $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, and let $q=p^a$ be the
fixed prime power. Fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$,
choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and fix an isomorphism
$\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$. For a finite-dimensional
$\Qlb$-vector space $V$, an automorphism $F$, and $w\in\mathbf R$, call
$(V,F)$ $\iota$-pure of weight $w$ if every eigenvalue $\alpha$ of $F$
satisfies $|\iota(\alpha)|=q^{w/2}$. Call $(V,F)$ $\iota$-mixed of weights at
most $w$ if there are an integer $m\geq0$, an $F$-stable filtration

$$
 0=V_0\subset V_1\subset\cdots\subset V_m=V
$$

and real numbers $w_1,\ldots,w_m\leq w$ such that each $(V_r/V_{r-1},F)$ is
$\iota$-pure of weight $w_r$.

Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$, an integer $n\in\mathbf
Z_{\geq1}$, and put $A=A_{E,n}$, with the finite-torsion coefficient
convention [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. Let $S$ be a scheme on
which $\ell$ is invertible, let $Y$ and $\overline X$ be finite-type
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] $S$-schemes, and let $p:\overline X\to
Y$ be a proper $S$-morphism. Use finite-torsion $A$-coefficients and the
derived direct image [def-weil-derived-direct-image] $Rp_*$. On the small
pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $\mathcal H^r$
denote the cohomology-sheaf functor
[def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. For an integer $c\in\mathbf
Z_{\geq0}$, write $\operatorname{FullCD}(p,A;c)$ if

$$
 \mathcal H^r(Rp_*\mathcal F)=0\qquad(r\in\mathbf Z,\ r>c)
$$

for every sheaf $\mathcal F$ of $A$-modules on $\overline
X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, and, for every object $V\to Y$ of
$Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$, if $p_V:\overline X\times_YV\to V$ is the base change
of $p$, then

$$
 \mathcal H^r\bigl(R(p_V)_*(\mathcal F|_{\overline X\times_YV})\bigr)=0
 \qquad(r\in\mathbf Z,\ r>c).
$$

*Warning.* Because the quantifier ranges over *every* pro-etale sheaf of
$A$-modules, $\operatorname{FullCD}(p,A;c)$ fails in general, even for $p$
proper and smooth of dimension one over an algebraically closed field: for an
elliptic curve $E$ over $\overline{\mathbf F}_p$, $A=\mathbf F_r$ with
$r\neq p$, there is a pro-etale $A$-module sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $E$ with
$H^n(E_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal F)\neq0$ for every $n\geq1$
(rem:sf-ambient-counterexample in the six-functors chapter; the sheaf is not
of etale origin). What does hold, with $c=2\dim\overline X$, is the
restriction of the condition to the coefficient sheaves of etale origin,
def-sf-fullcd-class and thm-sf-fullcd-class, and this restricted form is the
only one the blueprint uses.

Let $p$ be prime, let $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, and let
$q=p^a$ be the fixed prime power.
Fix $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ and an indeterminate $T$. For each integer
$i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$, let $P_i(T)\in\mathbf Z[T]$ satisfy
$P_i(0)=1$, put $b_i=\deg P_i$, and define the
determinant constant

$$
D_i=(-1)^{b_i}[T^{b_i}]P_i(T).
$$

Set

$$
\chi=\sum_{i=0}^{2d}(-1)^ib_i,
\qquad
\Delta=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}D_i^{(-1)^i}.
$$

Assume $d\chi$ is even; in geometric applications this follows from the
duality relations $b_i=b_{2d-i}$, $D_iD_{2d-i}=q^{db_i}$, and the
evenness of the middle degree when $d$ is odd. Define

$$
h=\frac{d\chi}{2}\in\mathbf Z
$$

and

$$
\varepsilon=
(-1)^\chi q^{-h}\Delta
\in\mathbf Q^\times.
$$

Negative exponents in $\Delta$ denote multiplicative inverses in
$\mathbf Q^\times$.

For the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]
$(p,a,q,k_0,k)$, let $Y_0$ be a finite-type
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] $k_0$-scheme. It is *smooth of pure
dimension $d$* if $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, the structure morphism $Y_0\to\Spec
k_0$ is a smooth morphism, and every irreducible component of
$Y_0\times_{k_0}k$ has Krull dimension $d$. It is *proper* if its structure
morphism is separated, of finite type, and universally closed, i.e. it is a
proper morphism. It is *geometrically connected* if it is nonempty and
$Y_0\times_{k_0}k'$ is connected for every field extension $k'/k_0$,
equivalently if its geometric fiber $Y_0\times_{k_0}k$ is nonempty and
connected.

Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] $p,a,q,k_0,k$, a
prime $\ell\neq p$. Write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic closure
$\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and choose a finite extension $E/\Ql$ contained in $\Qlb$.
Let $Y_0$ be a separated finite-type
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] $k_0$-scheme, put
$Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, set $\gamma=\operatorname{Frob}_q$, the geometric
Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-detailed], and
$g_Y=\operatorname{id}_{Y_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma):Y\to Y$, and
choose $(K,\theta_K)\in D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(Y,E)$. The Weil structure
[def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] is the isomorphism formed with the derived
pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]
$Lg_Y^*\operatorname{For}(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{For}(K)$, and the
ordinary cohomology [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] endomorphism is
induced by

$$
 \RGamma(Y,\operatorname{For}K)\xrightarrow{\sim}
 \RGamma(Y,Lg_Y^*\operatorname{For}K)
 \xrightarrow{\RGamma(\theta_K)}\RGamma(Y,\operatorname{For}K).
$$

The compactly supported endomorphism is the explicitly defined composite

$$
\RGammac(Y,\operatorname{For}K)\xrightarrow{\sim}
\RGammac(Y,Lg_Y^*\operatorname{For}K)
 \xrightarrow{\RGammac(\theta_K)}\RGammac(Y,\operatorname{For}K),
$$

where $s=\operatorname{Spec} k$ and
$\RGammac(Y,-)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{Y!}(-))$. Both operators, and their
actions on cohomology [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], are denoted
$F$.

Let $K$ be a field, let
$C(T)=\sum_{n\geq0}c_nT^n\in K[[T]]$ be a
formal power series, and let
$r,s\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$. The Hankel matrix of $C$ is the infinite
matrix

$$
\mathcal H(C)=(c_{r+s})_{r,s\geq0}.
$$

Its rank is the supremum of the ranks of its finite square submatrices.

attrs.title: Hankel matrix of a power series

objects.body:
Fix a prime $p$, $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, put $q=p^a$,
$k_0=\Fq$, and let $k=\Fbar$ be the
fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$.
Let $X_0/k_0$ be
smooth, proper, geometrically
connected of pure dimension $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, with
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. Fix an indeterminate $T$. For every prime
$\ell\neq p$, write
$\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and let
$P_{i,\ell}\in\Ql[T]$, $0\leq i\leq2d$, be the determinant factors in the
smooth-proper
cohomological family.
For $P(T)=\sum_{r\geq0}a_rT^r\in\mathbf Z[T]$, write

$$
P^{(\ell)}(T)=\sum_{r\geq0}(a_r\cdot1_{\Ql})T^r\in\Ql[T].
$$

For an integer $i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$, an integral
realization-independent factor in degree
$i$ is a polynomial
$P_i\in\mathbf Z[T]$ such that

$$
P_i^{(\ell)}=P_{i,\ell}
$$

for every prime $\ell\neq p$.

attrs.title: Integral realization of a Frobenius factor

objects.body:
Let $K_0$ be a field, let $X,Y$ be finite-type
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] $K_0$-schemes, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type $K_0$-morphism. Fix a prime $\ell$, write
$\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and
require that its image in $K_0$ is invertible. Choose a finite extension
$E/\Ql$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, and a uniformizer $\varpi_E$. For
every $n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, set $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. The
categories $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$, $D^b_c(X,E)$, and $D^b_c(X,\Qlb)$ use,
respectively, the derived-complete integral
[def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], rationalized
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and common-stage algebraically closed
[def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] constructions. The finite levels
use finite-torsion constructibility
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. For $K\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal
O_E)$, put $K_n=K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$ and define

$$
 Rf_!K=
 R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_n Rf_{!,n}K_n.
$$

This is the compactification-independent direct image
[def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. If $K_E\in D^b_c(X,E)$ is
represented by $K$, define

$$
 Rf_!K_E=(Rf_!K)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}^L E
$$

in the rationalized category. If $K_{\Qlb}\in D^b_c(X,\Qlb)$ is represented
at a finite stage by $K_E$ for some $E\subset\Qlb$, define

$$
 Rf_!K_{\Qlb}=Rf_!K_E\otimes_E\Qlb
$$

in the common-stage category.

attrs.title: Integral, rational, and algebraically closed compact-support functors

objects.body:
For an additive category $\mathcal T$, the *Karoubi envelope*
$\Kar(\mathcal T)$ has objects $(K,e)$, where $K\in\mathcal T$ and
$e\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal T}(K)$ satisfies $e^2=e$, and morphisms
$u:(K,e)\to(L,d)$ the morphisms $u\in\Hom_{\mathcal T}(K,L)$ satisfying
$u=d\,u\,e$. The identity of $(K,e)$ is $e$, and composition is inherited
from $\mathcal T$. The canonical functor

$$
 \mathcal T\longrightarrow\Kar(\mathcal T),\qquad
 K\longmapsto(K,\operatorname{id}_K),\qquad f\longmapsto f,
$$

is the *inclusion of $\mathcal T$ in its Karoubi envelope*.

*Difference:* Stacks states neither the construction of the Karoubi envelope
nor its inclusion functor, and its splitting criterion is one of three
equivalent characterizations of Karoubianity rather than a construction
applied to a given category; the request on that section page to add the
construction of the Karoubi envelope stands as an open comment (Comment
5787), and the addition of the explicit section--retraction form of an
idempotent to Lemma 12.4.2 was declined.

Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$, a prime $\ell\neq p$. Write
$\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and choose
a finite extension $E/\Ql$ contained in $\Qlb$. Let $Y_0$ be a finite-type
$k_0$-scheme, put $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, and choose $K\in D^b_{c,\mathrm
W}(Y,E)$, a Weil complex. For a closed point $y\in|Y_0|$, with $|Y_0|$ and
$\kappa(y)$ the closed-point and residue-field notation, let $y$ have degree
$r=[\kappa(y):\Fq]$. Choose an embedding $\kappa(y)\hookrightarrow k$ and the
associated geometric point $\bar y\to Y$. Iterating the Weil isomorphism $r$
times and using the resulting return to $\bar y$ defines, for every
$j\in\mathbf Z$, the local operator $F_y$ associated with the global
geometric-Frobenius action on the stalk of the cohomology sheaf $\mathcal
H^j(\operatorname{For}K)_{\bar y}$.

More generally, for every $n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$ and $x\in Y_0(\mathbf
F_{q^n})$ in the finite-field point set, choose an associated geometric point
$\bar x\to Y$; the $n$-fold iterate at $\bar x$ defines $F_x^{(n)}$. Put

$$
  K_{\bar x}:=
  L\bar x^*\operatorname{For}(K),\qquad
  \Tr(F_x^{(n)}\mid K_{\bar x})=
 \sum_{j\in\mathbf Z}(-1)^j
 \Tr\bigl(F_x^{(n)}\mid
 \mathcal H^j(\operatorname{For}K)_{\bar x}\bigr).
$$

Here $L\bar x^*$ is the derived pullback.

attrs.title: Local Frobenius and local alternating trace

objects.body:
Fix an indeterminate $T$, and let
$Z(T)\in1+T\mathbf Z[[T]]\cap\mathbf Q(T)$ be any rational series
with integer coefficients and constant coefficient one, in the
formal power series convention.
A normalized reduced integral presentation
of $Z$ is a pair $A,B\in\mathbf Z[T]$ such that

$$
A(0)=B(0)=1,
\qquad
\gcd(A,B)=1\text{ in }\mathbf Q[T],
\qquad
Z(T)=\frac{A(T)}{B(T)}
$$

as a Taylor series at $T=0$.

Fix a prime $p$, an integer $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, and let
$q=p^a$ be the fixed prime power.
Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}$ of $\mathbf Q$. For every number field
$L\subset\overline{\mathbf Q}$, define

$$
\operatorname{Emb}_{\mathbf Q}(L,\mathbf C)=
\{\tau:L\longrightarrow\mathbf C:
\tau\text{ is a field homomorphism and }\tau|_{\mathbf Q}
=\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf Q}\}.
$$

For $\alpha\in\overline{\mathbf Q}^{\times}$, let
$\mathbf Q(\alpha)$ be the smallest subfield of $\overline{\mathbf Q}$
containing $\mathbf Q$ and $\alpha$. For $w\in\mathbf R$, call
$\alpha$ a
*$q$-Weil number of weight $w$* if

$$
\forall\tau\in
\operatorname{Emb}_{\mathbf Q}(\mathbf Q(\alpha),\mathbf C),
\qquad |\tau(\alpha)|=q^{w/2}.
$$

It is an *algebraic integer* if there are an integer $m\geq1$ and
integers $a_0,\ldots,a_{m-1}$ such that

$$
\alpha^m+a_{m-1}\alpha^{m-1}+\cdots+a_1\alpha+a_0=0.
$$

Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$, an integer $n\in\mathbf
Z_{\geq1}$, and put $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $Z,U,X$ be schemes on which $\ell$ is
invertible. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] and let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be its
complementary open immersion. Write $i^*,j^*$ for the derived pullbacks
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and use the exact
extension-by-zero functor [def-weil-extension-by-zero] $j_!$ and the derived
direct image [def-weil-derived-direct-image] $Ri_*$ on the small pro-etale
sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For $K\in D^b_c(X,A)$, a
bounded complex with the finite-torsion constructibility condition
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], the canonical open--closed pair
of maps is

$$
 j_!j^*K\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow Ri_*i^*K,
$$

given by the open counit and the closed unit. An *open--closed recollement
triangle* means a distinguished triangle extending this specified pair. This
names the data and the required property; existence of this triangle is not
assumed in the definition. It will follow from the sheaf-level exact sequence
when the complementary open immersion is quasi-compact, in particular for the
Noetherian schemes used in the finite-field applications.

Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] $p,a,q,k_0,k$, where
$q=p^a$, and a prime $\ell\neq p$. Write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an
algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and choose a finite extension $E/\Ql$
contained in $\Qlb$, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer
$\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$. Put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and
$\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$. Let $Y$ be a separated
finite-type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] $k$-scheme and $a_Y:Y\to
s=\Spec k$ its structure morphism. Use the finite coefficient categories
[def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], Weil complexes
[def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], derived direct image
[def-weil-derived-direct-image], compact-support direct image
[def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], and Tate twists
[def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Evaluation at the geometric point of $s$
gives equivalences

$$
\begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Fib}_s:D^b_c(s,A_{E,n})&\xrightarrow{\sim}
 D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A_{E,n}),\\
 \operatorname{Fib}_s:D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)&\xrightarrow{\sim}
 D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(\mathcal O_E),\\
 \operatorname{Fib}_s:D^b_c(s,E)&\xrightarrow{\sim}D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E).
\end{aligned}
$$

For $\Qlb$, the target is the stagewise $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(\Qlb)$ defined in
the finite-coefficient construction
[def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. For $K\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$, define the
coefficient complexes

$$
 \RGamma(Y,K)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{Y*}K),
 \qquad
 \RGammac(Y,K)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{Y!}K),
$$

and

$$
H^i(Y,K)=\mathrm H^i\bigl(\RGamma(Y,K)\bigr),
\qquad
H_c^i(Y,K)=\mathrm H^i\bigl(\RGammac(Y,K)\bigr).
$$

For a coefficient ring $\Lambda$ in the displayed list, let $\Lambda_Y$
denote its coefficient object on the small pro-etale site
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]: it is the finite-level constant
sheaf $(A_{E,n})_Y$ for $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, the completed coefficient sheaf
$\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$ from the derived-complete integral construction
[def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] for $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$, and
the scalar extensions supplied by the rationalized coefficient construction
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and the algebraically closed coefficient
construction [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] for
$\Lambda=E,\Qlb$. When $\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$, equip it with the canonical
Weil structure from the Weil-sheaf structure
[def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Abbreviate

$$
 H^i(Y,\Lambda)=H^i(Y,\Lambda_Y),\qquad
 H_c^i(Y,\Lambda)=H_c^i(Y,\Lambda_Y).
$$

For every integer $m$, the notation with a Tate twist means

$$
 H^i(Y,\Lambda(m))=H^i\bigl(Y,\Lambda_Y(m)\bigr),\qquad
 H_c^i(Y,\Lambda(m))=H_c^i\bigl(Y,\Lambda_Y(m)\bigr),
$$

where $\Lambda_Y(m)=\Lambda_Y\otimes^L_\Lambda\Lambda(m)_Y$ uses the
coefficient-twist construction [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. In
particular, $(\Ql)_Y(m)$ denotes the twisted constant coefficient object and
$\Ql(m)$ is its coefficient-space notation in these abbreviations. If $K$ is
a Weil complex [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], each of these four symbols is
obtained by applying the displayed construction to $\operatorname{For}(K)$.
Whenever one of these coefficient spaces is finite-dimensional over its
field, its dimension, trace, and determinant have their ordinary
linear-algebraic meanings.

Fix the finite-field datum $p$, $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\Fq$, and let
$k=\Fbar$ be the fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$, and a prime $\ell\neq p$,
and choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $X_0/k_0$
be smooth, proper, geometrically connected of pure dimension $d\in\mathbf
Z_{\geq0}$, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, fix an indeterminate $T$, and, for
every integer $i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$, set $V_{i,\ell}=H^i(X,\Ql)$, the
ordinary cohomology group, and let $F_{i,\ell}$ be the geometric-Frobenius
[def-weil-frobenius-detailed] operator on this space, and set
$P_{i,\ell}(T)=\det(1-TF_{i,\ell}\mid V_{i,\ell})$ to be the determinant
family in the smooth-proper cohomological family
[def-weil-smooth-proper-cohomological-family]. All roots are taken in this
chosen algebraically closed field $\Qlb$.

Let $P(T)\in\Ql[T]$ be a polynomial with $P(0)=1$. An *ordinary root* is a
scalar $\beta\in\Qlb$ satisfying $P(\beta)=0$. It is nonzero. A *reciprocal
root* is a scalar $\alpha\in\Qlb^\times$ satisfying $P(\alpha^{-1})=0$. Over
an algebraic closure one has

$$
 P(T)=\prod_j(1-\alpha_jT),
$$

where the $\alpha_j$, counted with algebraic multiplicity, are the reciprocal
roots.

Fix a prime $p$, an integer $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, put $q=p^a$,
$k_0=\Fq$, and let $k=\Fbar$ be the
fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$.
Fix an indeterminate $T$.
Let $X_0/k_0$ be
smooth, proper, geometrically
connected of pure dimension
$d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, with $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. For every prime
$\ell\neq p$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and let
$P_{i,\ell}\in\Ql[T]$ for
$0\leq i\leq2d$ be the determinant factors in the
smooth-proper
cohomological family. Define

$$
N_\ell(T)=\prod_{\substack{0\leq i\leq2d\\ i\text{ odd}}}P_{i,\ell}(T),
\qquad
D_\ell(T)=\prod_{\substack{0\leq i\leq2d\\ i\text{ even}}}P_{i,\ell}(T).
$$

For every curve coefficient pair [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting] $(C,F)$: for
every integer $q>2$, $H^q(C_{\Et},F)=0$.

For every curve coefficient pair [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting] $(C,F)$ with $C$
affine: for every integer $q>1$, $H^q(C_{\Et},F)=0$.

attrs.title: Assertion (C2): vanishing on an affine curve

objects.body:
For every curve coefficient pair [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting] $(C,F)$ with
$\operatorname{char}k=p>0$ and $F$ $p$-primary
[def-weil-pbc-primary-torsion]: for every integer $q>1$,
$H^q(C_{\Et},F)=0$.

For every curve coefficient pair [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting] $(C,F)$ with $F$
constructible [def-weil-pbc-constructible-torsion] and prime to
$\operatorname{char}k$ [def-weil-pbc-primary-torsion]: for every integer
$q\geq0$, $H^q(C_{\Et},F)$ is a finite abelian group.

attrs.title: Assertion (C4): finiteness for a coefficient prime to the characteristic

objects.body:
For every curve coefficient pair [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting] $(C,F)$ with $C$
proper over $k$ and $F$ constructible [def-weil-pbc-constructible-torsion]:
for every integer $q\geq0$, $H^q(C_{\Et},F)$ is a finite abelian group.

attrs.title: Assertion (C5): finiteness for a proper curve

objects.body:
For every curve coefficient pair [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting] $(C,F)$ with $F$
prime to $\operatorname{char}k$ [def-weil-pbc-primary-torsion]: for every
algebraically closed extension $k'/k$ and every integer $q\geq0$, the pullback
map [def-weil-pbc-extension-pullback] $\rho^q_{k'/k}(C,F)$ is an isomorphism.

attrs.title: Assertion (C6): invariance under algebraically closed extension, coefficient prime to the characteristic

objects.body:
For every curve coefficient pair [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting] $(C,F)$ with $C$
proper over $k$: for every algebraically closed extension $k'/k$ and every
integer $q\geq0$, the pullback map [def-weil-pbc-extension-pullback]
$\rho^q_{k'/k}(C,F)$ is an isomorphism, without a restriction on the torsion
of $F$.

attrs.title: Assertion (C7): invariance under algebraically closed extension for a proper curve

objects.body:
For every curve coefficient pair [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting] $(C,F)$ and
every open immersion $a:U\hookrightarrow C$, the restriction map

$$
 a^*:H^2(C_{\Et},F)\longrightarrow H^2(U_{\Et},a^{-1}F)
$$

is surjective.

attrs.title: Assertion (C8): surjectivity of restriction to an open curve

objects.body:
For a sheaf of rings $B_T$ on $T_{\Proet}$, define the Grothendieck abelian
category

$$
 \operatorname{Tow}_{B}(T)=
 \operatorname{Fun}\bigl(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}},
              \Mod(T_{\Proet},B_T)\bigr).
$$

Its objects are strict inverse sequences $M_1\leftarrow M_2\leftarrow\cdots$,
and kernels, cokernels, and exactness are computed levelwise. Write
$\operatorname{ev}_n:\operatorname{Tow}_{B}(T)\to\Mod(T_{\Proet},B_T)$ for
the exact evaluation functor.

Let $A$ be noetherian, let $I=(a_1,\dots,a_r)$, assume $A/I$ is torsion, and
put $P_n=A/I^n$. Give $P_n$ the discrete topology and let $(P_n)_T$ be the
sheafification of

$$
 U\longmapsto\operatorname{Cont}(\pi_0(|U|),P_n)
$$

on $T_{\Proet}$. Define

$$
 A_T=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_T,
 \qquad
 D(T_{\Proet},A)=D(\Mod(T_{\Proet},A_T)),
$$

and assume each $P_n$ is finite as a set and perfect as an $A$-module. For
$K\in D(T_{\Proet},A)$ choose a functorial K-flat representative $QK$ (in the
sense of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]). The strict complexes

$$
 QK\otimes_{A_T}(P_n)_T
$$

and the quotient maps $P_{n+1}\to P_n$ define an object $K_\bullet\in
D(\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T))$. Its $n$-th evaluation is canonically

$$
 K_n=K\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_n)_T,
$$

and it carries functorial normalization isomorphisms

$$
 K_{n+1}\otimes^L_{P_{n+1}}P_n\xrightarrow{\sim}K_n
$$

satisfying the quotient cocycle.

The reduction tower $K_n=K\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_n)_T$ with $P_n=A/I^n$, and the
derived completeness tested by it, are the constant Noetherian case of Stacks
Project, Section 61.20 (Tag
[099L](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099L)) and Lemma 61.20.1 (Tag
[099M](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099M)), which for a Noetherian
ring $\Lambda$ and an ideal $I\subset\Lambda$ on an arbitrary site states
$K^\wedge=\Rlim(K\otimes^L_\Lambda\underline{\Lambda/I^n})$; the Stacks entry
assumes a Noetherian ring and an ideal, while the form used here is the
decomposed datum of the tower category $\operatorname{Tow}_A(T)$ over
$T_{\Proet}$, with each $P_n$ required to be perfect.

attrs.title: Tower category and adic coefficient datum

objects.body:
For a tower $M_\bullet=(M_n,t_{n+1,n})$, put

$$
s((x_n)_n)=(t_{n+1,n}(x_{n+1}))_n,
\qquad
R\varprojlim_nM_n:=\operatorname{Cone}
\left(1-s:\prod_nM_n\longrightarrow\prod_nM_n\right)[-1].
$$

Thus there is a functorial distinguished triangle

$$
R\varprojlim_nM_n\longrightarrow\prod_nM_n
\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_nM_n\longrightarrow .
$$

Maps of towers act componentwise on the two products and hence on the cone.

For a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with its chosen
identification, and a coefficient sheaf $R$, define the ambient pro-etale
exchange transformation

$$
 \Ex^R_{\square}:Lg^*Rf_*\longrightarrow Rf'_*Lg'^*
$$

to be the mate, under $Lf'^*\dashv Rf'_*$, of

$$
 Lf'^*Lg^*Rf_*\xrightarrow{\sim}
 Lg'^*Lf^*Rf_*\xrightarrow{Lg'^*\varepsilon_f}Lg'^*,
$$

using the derived operations on ringed pro-etale topoi. It is defined before
any completeness or constructibility condition.

Assume $T$ is noetherian of finite dimension and the torsion orders are
