invertible on $T$. Define $\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)$ to be the full subcategory of
derived $I$-complete objects, in the sense of the intrinsic completion,
whose reduction tower has compatible etale origins
[def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness] and is uniformly bounded constructible
in the sense of the bounded constructible tower.

This is the category $D_{cons}(X,\Lambda)$ of Stacks Project, Definition
61.29.1 ([Tag 09C1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C1), Section
61.29, [Tag 09C0](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C0)): the Stacks
definition assumes a Noetherian ring $\Lambda$ with an ideal $I$ and calls
$K\in D(X_{\Proet},\Lambda)$ constructible if $K$ is derived complete and
$K\otimes^L_\Lambda\underline{\Lambda/I}$ has constructible cohomology
sheaves and locally finite tor dimension, whereas the form used here
requires, over $A=\mathcal O_E$ and $I=(\varpi)$, a uniformly bounded
constructible reduction tower with compatible etale origins.

An adic tower is an object $M_\bullet\in D(\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T))$
equipped with normalization isomorphisms
$M_{n+1}\otimes^L_{P_{n+1}}P_n\simeq M_n$ satisfying the quotient cocycle of
[def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. It is *uniformly bounded
constructible* if there are integers $d_0\leq d_1$, one finite
stratification $T=\coprod_\alpha T_\alpha$, and, on each stratum, a pro-etale
covering $\{U_{\alpha j}\to T_\alpha\}_j$ with the following datum. For each
$U_{\alpha j}$ there is a bounded complex $L_{\alpha j}$, supported in
$[d_0,d_1]$, whose terms are finite locally constant $A_T|_{U_{\alpha
j}}$-modules and whose reductions have finite lisse cohomology, together with
isomorphisms

$$
 M_n|_{U_{\alpha j}}\xrightarrow{\sim}
 L_{\alpha j}\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_n)_T|_{U_{\alpha j}}
$$

for every $n$. These isomorphisms intertwine the normalization maps of
$M_\bullet$ with the quotient transition maps of the local reduction tower.

The finite-level constructibility of the local models is the notion of Stacks
Project, Section 61.27 (Tag
[09AI](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09AI)) and Definition 61.28.1
(Tag [09BT](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09BT), Section 61.28, Tag
[09BS](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09BS)): the Stacks entries define
constructibility, lissity and adic lissity of a single sheaf $\mathcal
F=\lim\mathcal F/I^n\mathcal F$ for a Noetherian ring $\Lambda$ with an ideal
$I$, the adic lisse case by local isomorphism to $\underline M^\wedge$, and
state no tower-level assertion; the form used here is a uniform tower with
bounded local models and finite lisse reductions.

For schemes and morphisms

$$
\begin{CD}
X' @>{g'}>> X\\
@V{f'}VV       @VV{f}V\\
Y' @>{g}>> Y,
\end{CD}
$$

we write $\square=(f,f',g,g',\alpha)$ when
$\alpha:X'\xrightarrow{\sim}X\times_Y Y'$ is a specified isomorphism and
$f\circ g'=g\circ f'$ as maps to $Y$. The notation
$g'^{-1}F$ always means inverse image using this specified identification.

## Detailed form

A *cartesian square* $\square=(f,f',g,g',\alpha)$ is a diagram

$$
 \begin{array}{ccc}
 X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
 f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
 Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y
 \end{array}
$$

of scheme morphisms [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] together with a chosen
identification $\alpha:X'\xrightarrow{\sim}X\times_YY'$ and the corresponding
equality $fg'=gf'$. This choice gives a specified natural isomorphism

$$
 \theta_\square:f'^{-1}g^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}g'^{-1}f^{-1}
$$

of inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] functors, compatible with
identities and pasted squares.

attrs.title: Cartesian square and chosen pullback identification

objects.body:
Let $f=[M,u]:(E,K)\to(F,L)$ be a morphism of the finite-stage pair category
[def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category], represented over the finite field
$M$. Choose in $\mathcal C_M(T)$ a distinguished cone triangle
$$
 T_{M/E}K\xrightarrow{u}T_{M/F}L
 \xrightarrow{i_u}C(u)\xrightarrow{p_u}(T_{M/E}K)[1].
$$
Its image in $\mathcal P_T$ is the triangle with cone object $(M,C(u))$,
second arrow represented by $i_u$, and third arrow represented by
$$
 \sigma_{M/E,K}^{-1}\circ p_u:
 C(u)\longrightarrow T_{M/E}(K[1]).
$$
A triangle in $\mathcal P_T$ is distinguished if it is isomorphic to such a
common-stage cone triangle.

*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this construction: the
blueprint adds the common-stage cone triangles of the pair category,
together with the shift comparisons of
[prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus]. The axioms to be met are Stacks':
Derived Categories, Definition 13.3.1 ([Tag
0144](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0144), triangle and morphism of
triangles for an additive auto-equivalence $[1]$) and Definition 13.3.2
([Tag 0145](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0145), triangulated
category: TR1--TR4, TR4 being the octahedral axiom), both fetched and
quoted, and the pattern "distinguished means isomorphic to a triangle coming
from a given category" is the one used in Proposition 13.5.6 ([Tag
05R6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05R6)) for a localization
$S^{-1}\mathcal D$. Difference: Stacks fixes one additive category, its
shift and its set of distinguished triangles, while here the triangles are
generated by the cone triangles of the finite stages of a filtered pair
category; the ledger's verified derived-category entries (08TC, 07KC, 0BK6,
0BK7, 070M) likewise concern a fixed derived category.

Let $\Lambda$ be Noetherian, let $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\subseteq\Lambda$ have
$\Lambda/I$ torsion, and suppose every $P_n:=\Lambda/I^n$ is perfect over
$\Lambda$. For $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$ put

$$
K_n:=K\otimes^L_\Lambda P_n.
$$

For $b\geq a$, let $q_{b,a}:K_b\to K_a$ be induced by
$P_b\to P_a$. The quotient identities give
$q_{a,a}=1$ and $q_{c,a}=q_{b,a}q_{c,b}$. Associativity also gives the
normalization isomorphisms

$$
K_b\otimes^L_{P_b}P_a\xrightarrow{\sim}K_a,
$$

and these obey the same cocycle.

attrs.title: Adic coefficient datum and reduction tower

objects.body:
Let $K$ be derived complete and let every $K_n$ have a displayed witness
$\epsilon_X^{-1}L_n\simeq K_n$ with
$L_n\in D_c^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda/I^n)$. Define

$$
\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{comp}}_{\square,K}:
Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rf_*K\longrightarrow
Rf'_*L(g')^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K
$$

to be the ordered composite

$$
\begin{aligned}
Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rf_*K
&\xrightarrow{\sim}R\varprojlim_n Lg^*Rf_*K_n\\
&\xrightarrow{R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Ex}_{\square,K_n}}
R\varprojlim_nRf'_*L(g')^*K_n\\
&\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_*R\varprojlim_nL(g')^*K_n
=Rf'_*L(g')^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K.
\end{aligned}
$$

In the notation above, the first two arrows are $H$ followed by $V'$.
The first isomorphism uses reconstruction and the perfect projection formula;
the second displayed isomorphism is the inverse of direct-image/limit
commutation. This definition fills the map-construction omission in Tag
`09C9`.

## Detailed form

Assume that every $K_n$ carries a specified etale-origin witness
[def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]. Define
$$
 \Ex^{\mathrm{comp}}_{\square,K}:
 Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rf_*K
 \longrightarrow Rf'_*Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K
$$
as the ordered composite
$$
 \begin{aligned}
  Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rf_*K
  &\xrightarrow{\sim}\Rlim B_\bullet\\
  &\xrightarrow{\Rlim(v'_\bullet)}\Rlim D_\bullet\\
  &\xrightarrow{\sim}
  Rf'_*\Rlim\bigl(Lg'^*_{\operatorname{Tow}}K_\bullet\bigr)
  =Rf'_*Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K.
 \end{aligned}
$$
The first isomorphism is reconstruction followed by the projection formula
for the finite quotients, and the last is the inverse of the canonical
direct-image/derived-limit comparison. These choices are part of the
displayed ordered composite.

The completeness of $Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}$ and the
direct-image/derived-limit comparison used here are clauses (2) and (4) of
Stacks Project, Lemma 61.20.2 ([Tag
099N](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099N), Section 61.20, [Tag
099L](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099L)): the Stacks entry assumes
a Noetherian ring $\Lambda$, an ideal $I$ and a morphism of topoi, and
states $Rf_*K=\Rlim Rf_*(K\otimes^L_\Lambda\underline{\Lambda/I^n})$ and
$Lf^*_{comp}M=\Rlim Lf^*(M\otimes^L_\Lambda\underline{\Lambda/I^n})$, while
the form used here is the ordered composite assembled from the tower
category and the per-level witnesses of
[def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness].

This identifier carries a `-detailed` suffix: the sketch import already uses
`def-weil-pbc-completed-base-change-map` for the corresponding statement.

Write

$$
S=Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rf_*K,
\qquad T=Rf'_*L(g')^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K.
$$

Let $s:S\xrightarrow{\sim}A_\infty$ be the pullback/tensor comparison in the
first part of the completed construction, and let
$t:D_\infty\xrightarrow{\sim}T$ be the inverse of direct-image/limit
commutation. Define genuine completed Weil structures by

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Theta_S&:=s^{-1}\Theta_{A,\infty}\Phi_{Y'}(s):
\Phi_{Y'}S\xrightarrow{\sim}S,\\
\Theta_T&:=t\Theta_{D,\infty}\Phi_{Y'}(t^{-1}):
\Phi_{Y'}T\xrightarrow{\sim}T.
\end{aligned}
$$

Under these identifications the completed base-change map is the ordered
composite

$$
\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{comp}}_{\square,K}=tWs,
\qquad W=V'H=H'V.
$$

attrs.title: Weil structures on the completed source and target

objects.body:
For $g:Y'\to Y$ define

$$
Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K:=
R\varprojlim_n\bigl(Lg^*K\otimes^L_\Lambda\Lambda/I^n\bigr).
$$

The comparison from ordinary pullback is the completion map of $Lg^*K$.

## Detailed form

For $g:T'\to T$, levelwise inverse image on strict tower complexes has a
total left derived functor

$$
 Lg^*_{\operatorname{Tow}}:
 D(\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T))
 \longrightarrow D(\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T')).
$$

Its $n$-th evaluation on the reduction tower $K_\bullet$ of
[def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] is $Lg_n^*K_n$. For a derived complete
$K$, define

$$
 Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K
   =\Rlim\bigl(Lg^*_{\operatorname{Tow}}K_\bullet\bigr)
 \quad\text{in }D(T'_{\Proet},A).
$$

The object $Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K$ is the $Lf^*_{comp}$ of Stacks Project,
Lemma 61.20.2 (2) and (5) (Tag
[099N](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099N), Section 61.20, Tag
[099L](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099L)), namely $Lf^*$ followed by
derived completion, computed as
$R\lim Lf^*(M\otimes^L_\Lambda\underline{\Lambda/I^n})$: the Stacks entry
assumes a Noetherian ring $\Lambda$, an ideal $I$ and a morphism of topoi,
and characterizes $Lf^*_{comp}$ as the left adjoint of $Rf_*$ on derived
complete objects, while the form used here defines it by the derived limit of
the levelwise pullback tower of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum].

Put

$$
S=Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rf_*K,
\qquad T=Rf'_*L(g')^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K.
$$

Let

$$
\sigma_n:S\otimes^LP_n\xrightarrow{\sim}A_n
$$

be finite reduction of completed pullback. For $E=L(g')^*K$, let

$$
\tau_n:T\otimes^LP_n\xrightarrow{\sim}C_n
$$

be the inverse of
$\widehat{Rf'_*E}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_*\widehat E=T$, tensored with
$P_n$, followed by finite reduction of $\widehat{Rf'_*E}$. Define

$$
\alpha_n=h_n\sigma_n:S\otimes^LP_n\to B_n,
\qquad
\delta_n=h'_n\tau_n:T\otimes^LP_n\to D_n,
$$

and let

$$
\overline\xi_n=
\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{comp}}_{\square,K}\otimes^L1_{P_n}:
S\otimes^LP_n\longrightarrow T\otimes^LP_n.
$$

Thus every arrow in the completed reduction square is named, typed, and
expressed as an ordered composite of reduction, direct-image, projection-
formula, or base-change maps.

attrs.title: The four edges of the completed reduction square

objects.body:
Define

$$
\operatorname{comp}_K:K\longrightarrow R\varprojlim_nK_n
$$

as the map induced by the compatible quotient arrows $K\to K_n$.

Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. A sheaf of $\Lambda_T$-modules on
the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] $T_{\Et}$ is *lisse* if it is
locally constant with finite stalks [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], and
*constructible* if $T$ admits a finite partition by locally closed
constructible subschemes on each of which the restriction is lisse. A complex
$K\in D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ is *bounded constructible* if every $\mathcal
H^i(K)$ is constructible and there are integers $a\leq b$ with $\mathcal
H^i(K)=0$ for $i\notin[a,b]$. The corresponding full subcategory
is denoted

$$
 \Dbc(T_{\Et},\Lambda)\subset D(T_{\Et},\Lambda).
$$

For the adic coefficient datum, write $\Lambda=P_n=A/I^n$, and assume $T$
noetherian of finite dimension with the orders of the torsion ring $P_n$
invertible on $T$. A sheaf $F$ of $\Lambda_{T,\Proet}$-modules on
$T_{\Proet}$ is *constructible* if $F\cong\nu_T^*F_{\Et}$ for the comparison
morphism of sites [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]
$\nu_T:T_{\Proet}\to T_{\Et}$ and a constructible $\Lambda$-module sheaf
$F_{\Et}$ on $T_{\Et}$. For a morphism $u:S\to T$, write
$\mathrm{FIN}(u,\Lambda;c)$ if:

1. *constructibility of direct images:* for every constructible sheaf $F$ of
   $\Lambda_{S,\Proet}$-modules on $S_{\Proet}$ and every $q\geq0$, the
   sheaf $R^qu_*F$ on $T_{\Proet}$ is constructible;
2. *amplitude:* there is an integer $c\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ such that
   $R^qu_*F=0$ for every $q>c$ and every constructible sheaf $F$ of
   $\Lambda_{S,\Proet}$-modules on $S_{\Proet}$.

The identification of constructible sheaves on $T_{\Proet}$ with the
pullbacks $\nu_T^*F_{\Et}$ of constructible etale sheaves is the equivalence
of Stacks Project, Section 61.27 ([Tag
09AI](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09AI)), whose coefficient ring is
assumed Noetherian; the finiteness condition $\mathrm{FIN}(u,\Lambda;c)$
itself, in particular its finite-level form for $\Lambda=P_n=A/I^n$, is a
hypothesis of this blueprint rather than a quoted statement.

Let $(C,F)$ be a curve coefficient pair [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting]. The
torsion sheaf $F$ is *constructible* if $C$ has a finite partition by locally
closed constructible subschemes on each of which its restriction is locally
constant with finite stalks.

attrs.title: Constructible torsion sheaves on a curve

objects.body:
For a finite covering $\mathcal V=\{V_a\to U\}_{a=1}^m$ on either site and a
module sheaf $M$, its Cech cochain complex has

$$
 \check C^p(\mathcal V,M)=
 \prod_{a_0,\ldots,a_p}M(V_{a_0}\times_U\cdots\times_UV_{a_p}),
 \qquad \delta=\sum_{j=0}^{p+1}(-1)^j d_j^*.
$$

Its cohomology is denoted $\check H^p(\mathcal V,M)$. The augmentation is
restriction from $M(U)$. Here module sheaves have the meanings of the etale
and pro-etale sheaf conventions.

Let $k$ be algebraically closed, let $C$ be separated of finite type over $k$
with $\dim C\leq1$, and let $F\in\Ab(C_{\Et})$ be a torsion sheaf. A pair
$(C,F)$ of this form is a *curve coefficient pair*.

attrs.title: The curve setting of the eight assertions

objects.body:
For a scheme $T$ and a commutative ring $R$, let
$\mathsf{Cpx}(\Mod(T_{\Et},R))$ be the abelian category of cochain complexes
of $R_T$-module sheaves and let

$$
 D(T_{\Et},R)=\mathsf{Cpx}(\Mod(T_{\Et},R))
 [\{\text{quasi-isomorphisms}\}^{-1}]
$$

be its Verdier localization at quasi-isomorphisms; the notation without $R$
refers to sheaves of abelian groups. The triangulated category
$\Dplus(T_{\Et},R)$ is the full subcategory of objects whose cohomology
sheaves vanish below some integer, and $D^b(T_{\Et},R)$ is the full
subcategory of objects with only finitely many nonzero cohomology sheaves.
For $K\in D(T_{\Et},R)$ write $\mathcal H^i(K)$ for its $i$-th cohomology
sheaf (with respect to the standard t-structure). An object has *torsion
cohomology* if every $\mathcal H^i(K)$ is a torsion sheaf
[def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves].

For $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}})$ choose an injective resolution
$K\xrightarrow{\simeq}I^\bullet$. Apply
$\operatorname{Ex}_{\square,I^r}$ in every degree and use the naturality
lemma to obtain a morphism of complexes

$$
g^{-1}f_*I^\bullet\longrightarrow f'_*g'^{-1}I^\bullet.
$$

Choose a K-injective replacement
$g'^{-1}I^\bullet\xrightarrow{\simeq}J^\bullet$ in the Grothendieck
category of etale abelian sheaves on $X'$. Compose the displayed map with
$f'_*g'^{-1}I^\bullet\to f'_*J^\bullet$ and define

$$
\operatorname{Ex}_{\square,K}:g^{-1}f_*I^\bullet\longrightarrow f'_*J^\bullet
$$

to be its class in $D^+(Y'_{\mathrm{et}})$. The target complex is a model
for $Rf'_*g'^{-1}K$, since $J^\bullet$ is K-injective; the source is a model
for $g^{-1}Rf_*K$ because $g^{-1}$ is exact.
Its class in $D^+(Y'_{\mathrm{et}})$ is

$$
\operatorname{Ex}_{\square,K}:g^{-1}Rf_*K\longrightarrow
Rf'_*g'^{-1}K.
$$

## Detailed form

For $K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$, the *derived exchange morphism* is the adjoint
mate

$$
 \Ex_{\square,K}:g^{-1}Rf_*K\longrightarrow Rf'_*g'^{-1}K
$$

of the composite

$$
 f'^{-1}g^{-1}Rf_*K\xrightarrow{\theta_\square}
 g'^{-1}f^{-1}Rf_*K\xrightarrow{g'^{-1}\varepsilon_f}g'^{-1}K,
$$

using the derived adjunction of the inverse-image adjunction
[def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and the specified isomorphism $\theta_\square$
of the cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square].
Equivalently, choose a K-injective resolution
[def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions] $K\to I$, apply the underived exchange
morphism [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] $\Ex^0_{\square,I}$ term
by term, and compare $g'^{-1}I$ with a K-injective resolution on $X'$.

Let $\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T)$ be the tower category of
[def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], with its evaluation functors
$\operatorname{ev}_n$, and let $M_\bullet\in
D(\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T))$. The evaluations $\operatorname{ev}_nM_\bullet$,
together with the transition maps they carry, exhibit
$(\operatorname{ev}_nM_\bullet)_{n\geq1}$ as an inverse system in the single
triangulated category $D(T_{\Proet},A)$. Its *sequential derived inverse
limit*

$$
 \Rlim M_\bullet
$$

is its derived limit in the sense of the conventions chapter; it is defined
by the Roos triangle applied to $(\operatorname{ev}_nM_\bullet)$. The derived
product $R\!\prod_nM_n$ is the product in $D(T_{\Proet},A)$, computed
termwise by Lemma 13.34.2 (Tag
[07KC](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07KC): for $\mathcal A$ abelian
with exact countable products, $D(\mathcal A)$ has countable products,
represented by termwise products of any representatives, with
$H^p(\prod_iK_i)=\prod_iH^p(K_i)$). Both entries are stated for an inverse
system in one triangulated category $D(\mathcal A)$; the form used here is
the system $(\operatorname{ev}_nM_\bullet)$ read off an object of the tower
category $\operatorname{Tow}_A(T)$ over $T_{\Proet}$, and no further
construction is made: the Roos triangle is exactly the triangle recalled
above.

For a morphism [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] $u:U\to V$, direct image is
the left exact functor

$$
 u_*:\Ab(U_{\Et})\longrightarrow\Ab(V_{\Et}),
 \qquad (u_*F)(W)=F(W\times_VU),
$$

where $W\to V$ runs over the objects of the small etale site
[def-weil-pbc-etale-site] $V_{\Et}$. If $K\to I(K)$ is a K-injective
resolution [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions], set

$$
 Ru_*K=u_*I(K),\qquad
 Ru_*:\Dplus(U_{\Et})\longrightarrow\Dplus(V_{\Et}),
$$

with $R^qu_*F=\mathcal H^q(Ru_*F)$ for a sheaf $F$. With a fixed coefficient
ring whose pullback is canonically identified with itself, the same functors
act on module sheaves.

attrs.title: Direct image and its derived functor

objects.body:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed, let $X$ be separated of finite type over
$k$ with $\dim X\leq1$, and let $F$ be a torsion sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$.
Write $\mathcal C_r(X,F)$, $1\leq r\leq8$, for the following assertions:

1. $H^q(X,F)=0$ for $q>2$;
1. $H^q(X,F)=0$ for $q>1$ when $X$ is affine;
1. $H^q(X,F)=0$ for $q>1$ when $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$ and $F$ is
$p$-power torsion;
1. every $H^q(X,F)$ is finite when $F$ is constructible and its torsion
is prime to $\operatorname{char}k$;
1. every $H^q(X,F)$ is finite when $X$ is proper and $F$ is
constructible;
1. for every algebraically closed extension $k'/k$, the restriction
$H^q(X,F)\to H^q(X_{k'},F|_{X_{k'}})$ is an isomorphism when the torsion
of $F$ is prime to $\operatorname{char}k$;
1. the map in (6) is an isomorphism when $X$ is proper, without a
restriction on the torsion;
1. for every open $a:W\hookrightarrow X$, the restriction
$H^2(X,F)\to H^2(W,a^{-1}F)$ is surjective.

## Detailed form

For a curve coefficient pair [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting] $(C,F)$, write
$\mathcal C(C,F)$ for the conjunction of the eight assertions

$$
 \mathcal C(C,F)=\bigwedge_{j=1}^{8}\mathcal C_j(C,F),
$$

namely [def-weil-pbc-C1], [def-weil-pbc-C2], [def-weil-pbc-C3],
[def-weil-pbc-C4], [def-weil-pbc-C5], [def-weil-pbc-C6], [def-weil-pbc-C7]
and [def-weil-pbc-C8].

Let $T$ be a scheme and let $F$ be an etale abelian sheaf on the small etale
site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] of $T$. The *(etale) cohomology groups* of $F$
are

$$
 H^q(T_{\Et},F)=\mathcal H^q\bigl(\Gamma(T,I^\bullet)\bigr)
 \qquad(q\geq0),
$$

where $F\to I^\bullet$ is a K-injective resolution
[def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions] and $\Gamma(T,-)$ is the functor of
global sections. For $K\in\Dplus(T_{\Et})$, write

$$
 \RGamma(T_{\Et},K)=\Gamma(T,\operatorname{Kinj}(K)),\qquad
 H^q(T_{\Et},K)=\mathcal H^q\bigl(\RGamma(T_{\Et},K)\bigr)
$$

for the derived global sections and the derived cohomology groups.

Starting with $R_0=R$, let $R_{n+1}$ be the tensor product over $R_n$ of one
representative of every faithfully flat etale $R_n$-algebra of finite
presentation. An arbitrary tensor product here means the filtered colimit of
its finite tensor products, including the empty tensor product $R_n$. Set
$R^{\mathrm e}=\varinjlim_nR_n$. Representatives are chosen in a fixed
universe throughout.

An object $K\in\Dplus(T_{\Proet},\Lambda)$ *comes from the etale site* if it
is equipped with a pair

$$
 (L,\alpha),\qquad
 L\in\Dplus(T_{\Et},\Lambda),\quad
 \alpha:\nu_T^*L\xrightarrow{\sim}K,
$$

where $\nu_T^*$ is the inverse image of the comparison morphism of sites
[def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. The pair $(L,\alpha)$, rather than
only its existence, is retained when maps are transported.

For a scheme $T$, let $\Ab(T_{\Et})$ be the abelian category of sheaves of
abelian groups on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] $T_{\Et}$;
it is a Grothendieck abelian category. For a commutative ring $R$, let $R_T$
be the constant sheaf of rings on $T_{\Et}$ and write $\Mod(T_{\Et},R)$ for
the abelian category of sheaves of $R_T$-modules. A sheaf $F\in\Ab(T_{\Et})$
is *torsion* if every local section of $F$ is locally killed by a positive
integer: for $s\in F(U)$ there are an etale covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ and
integers $n_i>0$ with $n_is|_{U_i}=0$. Equivalently every geometric stalk of
$F$ is torsion. This is weaker than asking every group $F(U)$ to be torsion:
the constant sheaf $\mathbf Q/\mathbf Z$ is torsion, while its sections over
$U=\coprod_{n\ge1}T$ contain $(1/2^n)_n$, of infinite order. A
sheaf of sets on $T_{\Et}$ is *locally constant* if it is locally isomorphic
to a constant sheaf, and *lisse* if it is locally constant with finite
stalks. It is *constructible* if $T$ admits a finite partition into locally
closed constructible subschemes on each of which it is finite locally
constant. A sheaf has *torsion cohomology* if every cohomology sheaf is
torsion.

attrs.title: Sheaves of abelian groups and of modules

objects.body:
For a scheme $T$, the *small etale site* $T_{\Et}$ has as objects the etale
morphisms [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] $U\to T$, as morphisms the
$T$-morphisms between them, and as covering families the finite or arbitrary
jointly surjective families $\{U_i\to U\}$ of etale morphisms. Fibre products
exist in $T_{\Et}$ and are computed as scheme-theoretic fibre products, so
$T_{\Et}$ is a site with finite limits.

Let $v:W\to X$ be etale [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] and let $M$ be a sheaf of
modules over a constant ring $A$ on $W_{\Et}$, as in
[def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Define $v_!M$ by sheafifying the presheaf

$$
 V\longmapsto\bigoplus_{s\in\operatorname{Hom}_X(V,W)}M(V,s).
$$

Here $(V,s)$ denotes $V$ as an etale $W$-scheme, and restriction sends the
summand indexed by $s$ to the summand indexed by its restriction. When $v$ is
an open immersion this is the usual extension by zero: there is at most one
such lift.

attrs.title: Extension by zero along an etale map

objects.body:
For an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, extension by zero is the exact
functor

$$
 j_!:\Ab(U_{\Et})\longrightarrow\Ab(X_{\Et})
$$

left adjoint to $j^{-1}$. It is characterized on geometric stalks by

$$
 (j_!F)_{\bar x}=
 \begin{cases}
 F_{\bar x},&\bar x\text{ lies in }U,\\
 0,&\bar x\text{ lies in }X\setminus U.
 \end{cases}
$$

## Detailed form

For an open immersion
$j:U\hookrightarrow X$, *extension by zero* is the

$$
j_!:\Ab(U_{\Et})\longrightarrow\Ab(X_{\Et})
$$

of [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]: the exact functor left
adjoint to $j^{-1}$, acting by

$$
(j_!F)_{\bar x}=
\begin{cases}
F_{\bar x_U},&\bar x\text{ lies in }U,\\
0,&\bar x\text{ lies in }X\setminus U,
\end{cases}
$$

on geometric stalks, and
exact, hence acting degreewise on complexes. For a finite
commutative ring $\Lambda$ the same construction is used for sheaves
of $\Lambda$-modules.

attrs.title: Extension by zero for open immersions

objects.body:
For a curve coefficient pair [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting] $(C,F)$ and an
algebraically closed extension $k'/k$, write

$$
 \pi_{k'}:C_{k'}=C\times_k k'\longrightarrow C,
 \qquad F_{k'}=\pi_{k'}^{-1}F,
$$

and let

$$
 \rho^q_{k'/k}(C,F):H^q(C_{\Et},F)\longrightarrow
 H^q((C_{k'})_{\Et},F_{k'})
$$

be the *pullback map* in degree $q$.

attrs.title: Base change of the coefficient and the pullback map

objects.body:
For a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] $\square$ with
$\Lambda$-coefficient data as in the adic coefficient datum, write
$\mathrm{AMP}(\square;c)$ if, for every $n\geq1$, with $P_n=A/I^n$ and
$\Lambda=P_n$:

1. the finite-level direct images satisfy the finiteness conditions
   [def-weil-pbc-constructible-direct-image-finiteness]
   $\mathrm{FIN}(f,P_n;c)$ and $\mathrm{FIN}(f',P_n;c)$;
2. the finite-level pullbacks $Lg_n^*,Lg_n'^*$ restrict to exact
   triangulated functors
   $$
    \begin{aligned}
     Lg_n^* &:D^b_c(Y_{\Proet},P_n)\longrightarrow
              D^b_c(Y'_{\Proet},P_n),\\
     Lg_n'^* &:D^b_c(X_{\Proet},P_n)\longrightarrow
               D^b_c(X'_{\Proet},P_n)
    \end{aligned}
   $$
   which carry objects with cohomology in $[a,b]$ into objects with
   cohomology in $[a,b]$.

Here $D^b_c(Z_{\Proet},P_n)^{[a,b]}$ denotes the full class of objects of
$D^b_c(Z_{\Proet},P_n)$ whose cohomology vanishes outside $[a,b]$. That the
conditions (i)--(ii) imply the amplitude containments for
$Rf_*,Rf'_*,Lg_n^*,Lg_n'^*$ is recorded with the other properties of this
predicate.

*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this predicate: its first
clause is the finiteness condition of the blueprint, whose etale inputs are
Lemma 59.92.2 ([Tag 095U](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/095U),
amplitude) and Theorem 63.14.5 ([Tag
0GL0](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0GL0), constructibility),
transferred to the pro-etale sites below, and its second clause is the
restriction of the finite-level pullbacks to bounded constructibles, for
which the nearest entries are Definition 61.29.1 ([Tag
09C1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C1)), Proposition 61.29.7 ([Tag
09C7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C7)) and the pullback
compatibility of Lemmas 61.27.2 and 61.27.4 ([Tag
09AK](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09AK), [Tag
09AL](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09AL)); the blueprint adds the
predicate that lets the amplification hypotheses be stated for one square
and one level $n$.

Consider a Cartesian square

$$
\begin{CD}
U @>{j_X}>> X\\
@V{v}VV @VV{\bar v}V\\
V @>{j_Y}>> Y
\end{CD}
$$

with $j_X,j_Y$ open immersions and $\bar v$ finite. For an abelian sheaf
$G$ on $U_{\mathrm{et}}$, define

$$
\beta_{\bar v,j_Y,G}:(j_Y)_!v_*G\longrightarrow
\bar v_*(j_X)_!G
$$

as the morphism adjoint to

$$
v_*G\xrightarrow{\sim}
j_Y^{-1}\bar v_*(j_X)_!G.
$$

The displayed isomorphism is finite base change
$j_Y^{-1}\bar v_*\cong v_*j_X^{-1}$ followed by
$j_X^{-1}(j_X)_!G\cong G$.

## Detailed form

For a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]

$$
 \begin{array}{ccc}
 U&\xrightarrow{j_U}&X\\
 v\downarrow&&\downarrow\bar v\\
 V&\xrightarrow{j_V}&Y,
 \end{array}
$$

with $j_U,j_V$ open immersions and $\bar v$ finite, define

$$
 \beta_{\bar v,j_V,G}:(j_V)_!v_*G
 \longrightarrow\bar v_*(j_U)_!G
$$

as the adjoint of the finite-base-change identification after restriction to
$V$.

Let $u:T'\to T$ be finite and $F$ an etale sheaf on $T$. For an etale
$V\to T$ and $s\in F(V)$, define

$$
u_V^\sharp(s)\in(u^{-1}F)(V\times_TT')
$$

to be the image of $s$ under the unit from the presheaf inverse image to its
sheafification.

## Detailed form

For a finite morphism [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] $h:V\to Y$ and
$a\in\Gamma(Y,F)$, define $h^\sharp a\in\Gamma(V,h^{-1}F)$ by the unit of the
inverse-image adjunction [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image].

attrs.title: Pullback of a section along a finite morphism

objects.body:
Let $X$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. An augmented simplicial $X$-scheme
consists of schemes $U_n$, face maps $d_i:U_n\to U_{n-1}$, degeneracy maps
$s_i:U_n\to U_{n+1}$, and $U_0\to X$, satisfying the simplicial identities.
Its *matching scheme* $M_n(U)$ is the finite limit specifying all compatible
proper faces of an $n$-simplex; $M_0(U)=X$ and $M_1(U)=U_0\times_XU_0$. It is
a *split etale hypercover* if every $U_n\to M_n(U)$ is an etale covering
[def-weil-pbc-etale-site] and there are specified nondegenerate summands
$N_m$ with

$$
 U_n=\coprod_{[n]\twoheadrightarrow[m]}N_m.
$$

Here $[n]=\{0,\ldots,n\}$, and the index runs over order-preserving
surjections. We call it *finite in each degree* if every $N_m$ is a finite
disjoint union of quasi-compact quasi-separated etale $X$-schemes of finite
presentation. A *truncation through degree $r$* retains all these data for
$n\leq r$. A refinement is a morphism of augmented simplicial schemes over
$X$; two refinements are identified when they are simplicially homotopic. For
an abelian sheaf $F$, set

$$
 C^n(U,F)=F(U_n),\qquad
 \delta=\sum_{i=0}^{n+1}(-1)^i d_i^*:C^n(U,F)\longrightarrow C^{n+1}(U,F).
$$

In particular, computing $H^q(C^\bullet(U,F))$ requires degrees through
$q+1$, even though a cocycle itself has degree $q$.

Let $\mathsf{FinExt}_\ell$ be the poset of finite intermediate fields
$\Ql\subset E\subset\Qlb$; it is filtered because the compositum of two
finite fields is finite. Put
$$
 \mathcal C_E(T)=\Dbc(T,E),
 \qquad T_{F/E}=F\otimes_E^L-:\mathcal C_E(T)\to\mathcal C_F(T),
$$
the categories $\Dbc(T,E)$ being those of
[def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. The normalized units
$T_{E/E}=\operatorname{id}$, the associators $a_{G,F,E}$, and the shift
comparisons $\sigma_{F/E}$ used below are the data constructed in
[prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension].

Define an object of $\mathcal P_T$ to be a pair $(E,K)$ with
$K\in\mathcal C_E(T)$. A morphism representative
$(M,u):(E,K)\to(F,L)$ consists of a finite field $M\supset E,F$ and a map
$$
 u:T_{M/E}K\longrightarrow T_{M/F}L
 \quad\text{in }\mathcal C_M(T).
$$
For $M\subset N$, transport it to
$$
 u_N=
 a_{N,M,F,L}\circ T_{N/M}(u)\circ a_{N,M,E,K}^{-1}.
$$
Representatives $(M,u)$ and $(N,v)$ are equivalent if $u_P=v_P$ in
$\mathcal C_P(T)$ for some finite $P\supset M,N$. Define
$$
 \Hom_{\mathcal P_T}((E,K),(F,L))
 =\varinjlim_{M\supset E,F}
 \Hom_{\mathcal C_M(T)}(T_{M/E}K,T_{M/F}L)
$$
as the resulting equivalence classes. Addition, identities, negatives, and
composition are computed after transporting all representatives to one
common finite overfield.

*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this construction: the
ledger's verified entries contain no filtered-colimit or Karoubi
construction of coefficient categories, and the blueprint adds the pair
category $\mathcal P_T$ of finite stages, whose morphism sets are filtered
colimits over the finite extensions $E/\Ql$. The nearest entries, each
fetched and quoted, are Categories, Definition 4.21.1 ([Tag
00D3](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00D3), directed set) and Lemma
4.21.5 ([Tag 0032](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0032), a filtered
index category may be replaced by a directed set without changing colimits)
with Remark 4.21.6 ([Tag
09P8](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09P8), a colimit indexed by a
finite filtered category need not be trivial), and Definition 61.29.1 ([Tag
09C1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C1)), which fixes one
Noetherian coefficient ring $\Lambda$ and forms no colimit over coefficient
fields. Difference: those entries take colimits of diagrams inside a fixed
category and keep the coefficient ring fixed, whereas the blueprint adds
both the filtered poset $\mathsf{FinExt}_\ell$ and the category
$\mathcal P_T$ built from it.

For a finite abelian group $M$, an $M$-torsor on $Y_{\Et}$ is a finite locally
constant sheaf $P$ with an $M$-action such that $M\times P\to P\times_YP$ is
an isomorphism. Write

$$
 \operatorname{Tor}^1(Y,M)
$$

for the pointed set of isomorphism classes of $M$-torsors on $Y_{\Et}$.

Let
$$
 h_n:A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}B_n,
 \qquad h'_n:C_n\xrightarrow{\sim}D_n
$$
be the isomorphisms supplied by the projection-formula maps on the corners
of the four-corners construction [def-weil-pbc-four-corners]. Let
$$
 v_n:A_n\to C_n
$$
be the tensor reduction of the ambient ringed exchange map
$$
 \Ex^A_{\square,K}:Lg^*Rf_*K\longrightarrow Rf'_*Lg'^*K
$$
of [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange], transported through the canonical
isomorphism
$Lg_n^*((Rf_*K)\otimes_A^LP_n)\simeq(Lg^*Rf_*K)\otimes_A^LP_n$. Let
$$
 v'_n:B_n\xrightarrow{\sim}D_n
$$
be the finite-level pro-etale exchange isomorphism for $K_n$, obtained from
its specified finite-coefficient etale-origin witness.

*Source:* the four arrows are Stacks entries. The exchange morphisms are the
canonical base change map $Lg^*Rf_*K\to Rf'_*L(g')^*K$ of Cohomology on
Sites, Remark 21.19.3 ([Tag
07A7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07A7)), constructed there in full
generality for a commutative diagram of ringed topoi as the adjoint of
$L(g')^*$ of the adjunction map $Lf^*Rf_*K\to K$; $v_n$ is its tensor
reduction along $P_n$, and $v'_n$ is its finite-level form, an isomorphism
by Theorem 61.30.1 ([Tag 09C9](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C9))
applied to $K_n$ with its etale-origin witness. The projection-formula
companions $h_n,h'_n$ are the map of Equation 21.50.0.1 ([Tag
0B56](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B56)) and its
perfect-coefficient form, Lemma 21.50.1 ([Tag
0944](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0944)). Difference of generality:
Stacks' base change map is stated for ringed topoi with no completeness
hypothesis and no coefficient tower, and is not asserted to be an
isomorphism — the isomorphism is Stacks' proper base change theorem 61.30.1,
which states no construction of the map; the required identification of
$v'_n$ with the finite-level form of the specified etale-origin witness, and
the assembly of the two exchange arrows with their two projection-formula
companions on the corners of one square, are the blueprint's presentation at
the finite coefficient rings $P_n=A/I^n$.

Let $\square$ be cartesian [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with $f$ proper,
let $K$ be derived $I$-complete in the sense of the adic coefficient datum,
put $K_n=K\otimes_A^LP_n$, and put
$$
 E=Lg'^*K,
 \qquad E_n=Lg_n'^*K_n
       \xleftarrow{\sim}E\otimes_A^LP_n.
$$
Define four objects of $D(Y'_{\Proet},P_n)$:
$$
 \begin{aligned}
  A_n&=Lg_n^*((Rf_*K)\otimes_A^LP_n),&
  B_n&=Lg_n^*Rf_*K_n,\\
  C_n&=(Rf'_*E)\otimes_A^LP_n,&
  D_n&=Rf'_*E_n.
 \end{aligned}
$$

*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this four-corner datum: its
inputs are given separately by the completed pullback and its finite
reduction (Lemma 61.20.2, [Tag
099N](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099N)), the proper base-change
isomorphism (Theorem 61.30.1, [Tag
09C9](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C9)) and the projection formula
that identifies $A_n$ with $B_n$ and $C_n$ with $D_n$ after tensoring with
the perfect coefficient $P_n$ (Equation 21.50.0.1, [Tag
0B56](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B56), with Lemma 21.50.1, [Tag
0944](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0944)), but no entry assembles
the four finite-level corners $A_n,B_n,C_n,D_n$ of one square; the blueprint
adds that assembly, at the finite coefficient rings $P_n=A/I^n$.

For $E_n=L(g')^*K_n$, define

$$
\vartheta_{E,n}:=
L(g')^*(\vartheta_n)\,\kappa_{g',K_n}:
\Phi_{X'}E_n\xrightarrow{\sim}E_n.
$$

The Weil structures on $B_n$ and $D_n$ are the typed composites

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Theta_{B,n}:\Phi_{Y'}B_n
&\xrightarrow{\kappa_g}Lg^*\Phi_YRf_*K_n
\xrightarrow{Lg^*\beta_{f,n}}Lg^*Rf_*\Phi_XK_n
\xrightarrow{Lg^*Rf_*\vartheta_n}B_n,\\
\Theta_{D,n}:\Phi_{Y'}D_n
&\xrightarrow{\beta_{f',E_n}}Rf'_*\Phi_{X'}E_n
\xrightarrow{Rf'_*\vartheta_{E,n}}D_n.
\end{aligned}
$$

Transport these structures across the two projection-formula isomorphisms:

$$
\Theta_{A,n}:=h_n^{-1}\Theta_{B,n}\Phi_{Y'}(h_n),
\qquad
\Theta_{C,n}:=(h'_n)^{-1}\Theta_{D,n}\Phi_{Y'}(h'_n).
$$

Thus every $\Theta_{Z,n}$ has the genuine Weil type
$\Phi_{Y'}Z_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Z_n$ for
$Z=A,B,C,D$.

attrs.title: Weil structures on the four finite corners

objects.body:
A Frobenius-equivariant datum for the proper Cartesian square $\square$ and
the tower $K_\bullet$ includes displayed witnesses

$$
\epsilon_X^{-1}L_n\xrightarrow{\sim}K_n,
\qquad L_n\in D_c^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},P_n),
$$

compatible with the tower transitions. Pullback supplies the corresponding
etale-origin witnesses for $E_n=L(g')^*K_n$. The datum then consists of
automorphisms

$$
\operatorname{Fr}_X,\quad \operatorname{Fr}_Y,\quad
\operatorname{Fr}_{X'},\quad \operatorname{Fr}_{Y'}
$$

such that

$$
\begin{aligned}
f\operatorname{Fr}_X&=\operatorname{Fr}_Yf,&
g\operatorname{Fr}_{Y'}&=\operatorname{Fr}_Yg,\\
g'\operatorname{Fr}_{X'}&=\operatorname{Fr}_Xg',&
f'\operatorname{Fr}_{X'}&=\operatorname{Fr}_{Y'}f'.
\end{aligned}
$$

The four resulting Frobenius faces are equipped with their Cartesian
identifications, and these identifications make the resulting cube commute
with the chosen Cartesian identification for $\square$. Put
$\Phi_Z=L\operatorname{Fr}_Z^*$. Since every $\operatorname{Fr}_Z$ is an
automorphism, every $\Phi_Z$ is an exact equivalence and preserves products
and fibres.

The pullback faces give canonical isomorphisms

$$
\kappa_g:\Phi_{Y'}Lg^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lg^*\Phi_Y,
\qquad
\kappa_{g'}:\Phi_{X'}L(g')^*\xrightarrow{\sim}L(g')^*\Phi_X.
$$

The proper Frobenius faces give finite-level exchange isomorphisms

$$
\beta_{f,n}:\Phi_YRf_*K_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*\Phi_XK_n,
\qquad
\beta_{f',M}:\Phi_{Y'}Rf'_*M\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_*\Phi_{X'}M.
$$

Finally the datum contains isomorphisms

$$
\vartheta_n:\Phi_XK_n\xrightarrow{\sim}K_n
$$

such that, for $r_{n+1,n}:K_{n+1}\to K_n$,

$$
r_{n+1,n}\vartheta_{n+1}
=\vartheta_n\Phi_X(r_{n+1,n}).
$$

The constant coefficient quotients carry their identity Frobenius
structures, and all displayed comparisons are required to respect their
normalizations and cocycles.

Let $h:W\to V$ be a morphism and let $\bar v:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V$ be a
geometric point with $\Omega$ algebraically closed. The *geometric fibre* of $h$
over $\bar v$ is the set of morphisms $\bar w:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to W$ with
$h\circ\bar w=\bar v$; equivalently, the set of $\Omega$-points of the scheme-theoretic
fibre $W\times_V\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. It is finite when $h$ is finite.

attrs.title: Geometric fibre of a finite morphism

objects.body:
Let $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ be a geometric point
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. A *pointed etale neighbourhood* of $\bar
t$ is a pair $(U,\bar u)$ with $U\to T$ an object of the small etale site
[def-weil-pbc-etale-site] and $\bar u:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$ a lift
of $\bar t$. For a sheaf $F$ on $T_{\Et}$, define its *stalk at $\bar t$* by

$$
 F_{\bar t}=\varinjlim_{(U,\bar u)}F(U),
$$

where the colimit runs over pointed etale neighbourhoods with the opposite
index category.

A pair $(A,I)$ consisting of a commutative ring and an ideal is *henselian*
if, for every finite $A$-algebra $B$, every idempotent of $B/IB$ lifts
uniquely to an idempotent of $B$. A local ring is *henselian* when its
maximal-ideal pair is henselian, and *strictly henselian* when it is
henselian and its residue field is separably closed. For
$T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and an ideal $I$, write
$T_0=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ for the closed subscheme.

Let $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}})$ have torsion cohomology sheaves and choose
$a$ with $\mathcal H^q(K)=0$ for $q<a$. The canonical truncation tower
$\tau_{\leq q}K$ defines spectral sequences

$$
E_2^{p,q}=R^pf_*\mathcal H^q(K)\Longrightarrow
\mathcal H^{p+q}(Rf_*K),
$$

and

$$
{E'}_2^{p,q}=R^pf'_*g'^{-1}\mathcal H^q(K)\Longrightarrow
\mathcal H^{p+q}(Rf'_*g'^{-1}K).
$$

Their filtration in total degree $n$ is the image filtration induced by
$\mathcal H^n(Rf_*\tau_{\leq q}K)\to\mathcal H^n(Rf_*K)$; the second
filtration is induced by
$\mathcal H^n(Rf'_*g'^{-1}\tau_{\leq q}K)\to \mathcal H^n(Rf'_*g'^{-1}K)$.

## Detailed form

Let $K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ have torsion cohomology and choose $a$ with
$\mathcal H^q(K)=0$ for $q<a$. Canonical truncations define spectral sequences

$$
 E_2^{p,q}=R^pf_*\mathcal H^q(K)
 \Longrightarrow\mathcal H^{p+q}(Rf_*K)
$$

and

$$
 E_2'{}^{p,q}=R^pf'_*g'^{-1}\mathcal H^q(K)
 \Longrightarrow\mathcal H^{p+q}(Rf'_*g'^{-1}K),
$$

whose filtration in degree $n$ is the image filtration obtained from
$\tau_{\leq q}K\to K$.

## Proof

The truncation triangles $\tau_{\leq q-1}K\to\tau_{\leq q}K\to\mathcal
H^q(K)[-q]\to$ are the truncation couple of the spectral-sequence chapter, so
its truncation spectral sequence, applied in the dictionary of that chapter to
the left exact functor $f_*$, supplies the first displayed spectral sequence
with the image filtration, its $E_2$-page being $E_2^{p,q}=R^pf_*\mathcal
H^q(K)$ by the shift identification and the finite-filtration induction. The
second sequence is the same theorem applied to $g'^{-1}K$, exactness of
$g'^{-1}$ giving $\mathcal H^q(g'^{-1}K)=g'^{-1}\mathcal H^q(K)$ and hence the
displayed $E_2'$-page.

An $A$-algebra is *ind-etale* if it is a filtered colimit of etale algebras
of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. It is *ind-Zariski*
if such a presentation can be chosen with terms finite products of
localizations $A_f$. The corresponding affine scheme is an inverse limit of
affine etale schemes, with affine transition maps. A ring map is *weakly
etale* when its map on spectra is weakly etale in
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]; equivalently, $B$ is flat over $A$ and
over $B\otimes_A B$ by multiplication.

For affine $X$, let $\mathcal B_X$ be the full subcategory of $X_{\Proet}$
consisting of affine schemes ind-etale over $X$. Give it the coverings
induced from the small pro-etale site.

For a proper $f:X\to Y$, define $\mathsf{IA}(f)$ to mean: for every prime
$\ell$, every $g:Y'\to Y$, every square $\square$, and every injective sheaf
$I$ of $\mathbf F_\ell$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$, the sheaf
$g'^{-1}I$ is $f'_*$-acyclic, i.e.
$R^qf'_*g'^{-1}I=0$ for all $q>0$.

## Detailed form

For a proper morphism [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] $f:X\to Y$ and a
prime $r$, write $\mathrm{IA}_r(f)$ if, after every base change $g:Y'\to Y$,
every injective sheaf $I$ of $\mathbf F_r$-modules on $X_{\Et}$ satisfies

$$
 R^qf'_*g'^{-1}I=0\qquad(q>0),
$$

where $f'$ and $g'$ are the maps of the associated cartesian square
[def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] and $R^q$ is the higher direct image
[def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Write $\mathrm{IA}(f)$ if this holds for every
prime $r$.

For $m\geq1$, let

$$
 Q_m=K(A_T;a_1^m,\dots,a_r^m)
   =\bigotimes_{j=1}^r[A_T\xrightarrow{a_j^m}A_T]
$$

in cohomological degrees $[-r,0]$. For each factor define a chain map

$$
 [A_T\xrightarrow{a_j^{m+1}}A_T]
 \longrightarrow[A_T\xrightarrow{a_j^m}A_T]
$$

whose degree $-1$ component is multiplication by $a_j$ and whose degree $0$
component is the identity. Their tensor product is a chain map
$q_{m+1,m}:Q_{m+1}\to Q_m$; the composites $q_{m+2,m}=q_{m+1,m}q_{m+2,m+1}$
make $(Q_m)_m$ a strict tower.

For a functorial K-flat representative $QK$, the complexes
$QK\otimes_{A_T}Q_m$ form an object of $D(\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T))$. Define

$$
 K^{\wedge}_{\mathrm{Kos}}
   =\Rlim_m(QK\otimes_{A_T}Q_m).
$$

The compatible degree-zero maps $A_T\to Q_m$ define $K\to
K^{\wedge}_{\mathrm{Kos}}$. The object $K$ is derived $I$-complete if this
map is an isomorphism.

Derived completeness here is the condition
$K\xrightarrow{\sim}\Rlim(K\otimes^L_\Lambda\underline{\Lambda/I^n})$ of
Stacks Project, Lemma 61.20.1 (Tag
[099M](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099M), Section 61.20, Tag
[099L](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099L)): the Stacks entry assumes
a Noetherian ring $\Lambda$ and an ideal $I$, and presents the completion as
the left adjoint of $D_{comp}(\mathcal C,\Lambda)\subset D(\mathcal
C,\Lambda)$, whereas the form used here is the Koszul model $Q_m$ over
$A=\mathcal O_E$, $I=(\varpi)$, whose agreement with the quotient-tower form
of 61.20.1 is [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction].

Let

$$
Q_m:=K(\Lambda;f_1^m,\ldots,f_r^m)
$$

be the Koszul complex in degrees $[-r,0]$. Its map $Q_{m+1}\to Q_m$ is
the tensor product, over $j$, of the two-term chain maps whose degree-zero
component is the identity and whose degree-minus-one component is
multiplication by $f_j$. Define

$$
K^{\wedge,\mathrm{Kos}}:=
R\varprojlim_m(K\otimes^L_\Lambda Q_m).
$$

The augmentations $\Lambda\to Q_m$ give
$\kappa_K:K\to K^{\wedge,\mathrm{Kos}}$. Call $K$ intrinsically derived
$I$-complete when $\kappa_K$ is an isomorphism; below, ``derived
$I$-complete'' always means this intrinsic condition.

For a morphism [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] $u:U\to V$, inverse image

$$
 u^{-1}:\Ab(V_{\Et})\longrightarrow\Ab(U_{\Et})
$$

is the left adjoint of the direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] $u_*$,
defined by sheafifying the presheaf inverse image along the functor
$U_{\Et}\to V_{\Et}$. Its unit and counit are denoted $\eta_u$ and
$\varepsilon_u$. With a fixed coefficient ring whose pullback is canonically
identified with itself, the same functors act on module sheaves.

attrs.title: Inverse image and the derived adjunction

objects.body:
A complex $I$ of sheaves on an etale site is *K-injective* if for every
acyclic complex $A$ the complex $\operatorname{Hom}(A,I)$ is acyclic. A
*K-injective resolution* of a complex $K$ is a quasi-isomorphism $K\to I$
with $I$ K-injective.

Let $\xi_K:Lg^*Rf_*K\to Rf'_*E$ be the unit–counit exchange map

$$
Lg^*Rf_*K\longrightarrow
Rf'_*L(f')^*Lg^*Rf_*K
\simeq Rf'_*L(g')^*Lf^*Rf_*K
\xrightarrow{Rf'_*L(g')^*\epsilon_K}Rf'_*E.
$$

Define the four edges

$$
\begin{aligned}
h_n&:=Lg^*(\pi_{f,K,n}):A_n\longrightarrow B_n,\\
v_n&:=\xi_K\otimes^L1_{P_n}:A_n\longrightarrow C_n,\\
h'_n&:=\pi_{f',E,n}:C_n\longrightarrow D_n,\\
v'_n&:=\xi_{K_n}:B_n\longrightarrow D_n.
\end{aligned}
$$

For $v_n$ use
$Lg^*((Rf_*K)\otimes P_n)\simeq(Lg^*Rf_*K)\otimes P_n$.
The transported S8 map is $v'_n$, because its construction was identified
there with this unit–counit exchange map.

For the proper Cartesian square $\square$, put $E=L(g')^*K$ and, for every
$n\geq1$, define

$$
\begin{aligned}
A_n&:=Lg^*((Rf_*K)\otimes^LP_n),&
B_n&:=Lg^*Rf_*K_n,\\
C_n&:=(Rf'_*E)\otimes^LP_n,&
D_n&:=Rf'_*E_n,
\end{aligned}
$$

where $E_n=L(g')^*K_n=E\otimes^LP_n$. The chosen Cartesian
identification supplies
$L(g')^*Lf^*=L(f')^*Lg^*$ throughout.

Let $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ be a geometric point. Define
$\mathcal N_{\bar s}$ to have objects pairs $(V,\bar v)$ with $V\to S$
etale and $\bar v:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V$ above $\bar s$.
A morphism $(V,\bar v)\to(W,\bar w)$ is an $S$-map $V\to W$ carrying
$\bar v$ to $\bar w$. We index stalk colimits by
$\mathcal N_{\bar s}^{\mathrm{op}}$ so that restriction maps point forward.

## Detailed form

For a geometric point [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] $\bar
s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$, let $\mathcal N_{\bar s}$ be the category
whose objects are pairs $(V,\bar v)$ with $V\to S$ etale
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and $\bar v\to V$ above $\bar s$. A
morphism preserves the chosen geometric points. Stalk colimits are indexed by
$\mathcal N_{\bar s}^{\mathrm{op}}$.

Let $(C,F)$ be a curve coefficient pair [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting], and let
$\operatorname{char}k=p>0$. The sheaf $F$ is *$p$-primary* if every element of
every geometric stalk $F_{\bar c}$ is killed by a power of $p$, and *prime to
$p$* if every such element has finite order coprime to $p$. In characteristic
zero, "prime to the characteristic" imposes no condition.

For a finite discrete ring $\Lambda$, let $\Lambda_{T,\Proet}$ be the
sheafification of

$$
 U\longmapsto\operatorname{Cont}(\pi_0(|U|),\Lambda)
$$

on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let
$\Mod(T_{\Proet},\Lambda)$ be its abelian category of module sheaves and
define

$$
 D(T_{\Proet},\Lambda)=
 \mathsf{Cpx}(\Mod(T_{\Proet},\Lambda))
 [\{\text{quasi-isomorphisms}\}^{-1}].
$$

The subcategories $\Dplus(T_{\Proet},\Lambda)$ and
$\Dbc(T_{\Proet},\Lambda)$ are defined by lower boundedness and by pullback
of the bounded constructible etale objects of
[def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], respectively.

attrs.title: Finite coefficients on the pro-etale site

objects.body:
Let $u:U\to V$ be a morphism and let $R_V$ be a coefficient sheaf whose
inverse image is identified with $R_U$. The module inverse image is

$$
 u^*F=u^{-1}F\otimes_{u^{-1}R_V}R_U.
$$

Using a functorial K-flat and K-injective resolution
[def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions] defines ordinary triangulated functors

$$
 Lu^*:D(V_{\Proet},R_V)\longrightarrow D(U_{\Proet},R_U),
 \qquad
 Ru_*:D(U_{\Proet},R_U)\longrightarrow D(V_{\Proet},R_V),
$$

with $Lu^*\dashv Ru_*$.

attrs.title: Derived operations on ringed pro-etale topoi

objects.body:
For a scheme $T$, the *small pro-etale site* $T_{\Proet}$ has as objects the
weakly etale [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] morphisms $U\to T$, and as
covering families the jointly surjective fpqc covering families, i.e.
families $\{U_i\to U\}$ of weakly etale maps such that for every affine open
$V\subset U$, finitely many affine opens $V_j\subset U_{i_j}$ have images
covering $V$.

## Detailed form

Fix a scheme $Y$. Choose Grothendieck universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal V$ and
a $\mathcal V$-small skeleton, as required by the size convention
[def-weil-size-convention], and form all categories below inside $\mathcal
V$. The site $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ has as objects the $\mathcal U$-bounded
weakly etale maps $U\to Y$, where a weakly etale map
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] is flat with flat diagonal. A family
$\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ is a covering if every arrow is weakly etale and, for
every affine open $V\subset U$, finitely many affine opens $V_j\subset
U_{i_j}$ have images covering $V$.

For a commutative ring $A$, let $A_Y$ be the sheafification of the constant
presheaf $U\mapsto A$ on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Let
$\Sh(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ be the abelian category of sheaves of
$A_Y$-modules, and set

$$
 D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)=D\bigl(\Sh(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)\bigr),
$$

using the derived category of cochain complexes
[def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

Let $f:X\to Y$ admit a chosen compactification

$$
X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y,
\qquad f=pj,
$$

with $j$ a quasi-compact open immersion and $p$ proper. For this datum set

$$
Rf_!^{(j,p)}E:=Rp_*j_!E.
$$

For proper $f$, its identity compactification is $(j,p)=(1_X,f)$.

For a morphism of ringed topoi $h:\mathcal T\to\mathcal S$, an object
$E\in D(\mathcal T,\Lambda)$, and a strict-perfect package $F^\bullet$ on
$\mathcal S$, define

$$
\pi_{h,E,F}:Rh_*E\otimes^L_\Lambda F^\bullet
\longrightarrow Rh_*(E\otimes^L_\Lambda Lh^*F^\bullet)
$$

to be adjoint to

$$
Lh^*(Rh_*E\otimes^LF^\bullet)
\simeq Lh^*Rh_*E\otimes^LLh^*F^\bullet
\xrightarrow{\epsilon_E\otimes1}
E\otimes^LLh^*F^\bullet.
$$

For $F^r=\Lambda^{N_r}$, let $\rho_r$ be the inverse of the finite-sum
identification

$$
(Rh_*E)^{N_r}\xrightarrow{\pi_r}Rh_*(E^{N_r}).
$$

For a projective term with the displayed splitting, define

$$
\rho_{F^r}:=
(Rh_*E\otimes p_r)\,\rho_r\,
Rh_*(1_E\otimes h^*i_r).
$$

The bounded totalization of the $\rho_{F^r}$ is denoted
$\rho_{h,E,F}$.

For $f:X\to Y$, $K\in D(X_{\Proet},A)$, and $P\in D(Y_{\Proet},A)$, define

$$
 \pi_{f,K,P}:(Rf_*K)\otimes_A^LP
 \longrightarrow Rf_*(K\otimes_A^LLf^*P)
$$

as the adjoint of the tensor product of the counit $Lf^*Rf_*K\to K$ with
$Lf^*P$, using the operations of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations].

(*Source:* the morphism is Stacks Project, Cohomology on Sites, Equation
21.50.0.1 (Tag [0B56](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B56)), the map
$Rf_*E\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_{\mathcal D}}K\to Rf_*(E\otimes^L_{\mathcal
O_{\mathcal C}}Lf^*K)$ of Section 21.50 (Tag
[0943](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0943), Projection formula), which
is defined there as the adjoint of the canonical map $Lf^*(Rf_*E\otimes^L_{
\mathcal O_{\mathcal D}}K)= Lf^*Rf_*E\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_{\mathcal
C}}Lf^*K\to E\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}}Lf^*K$ coming from the map
$Lf^*Rf_*E\to E$. The blueprint's $\pi_{f,K,P}$ is this map for the ambient
pro-etale ringed topoi with $E=K$ and $K=P$, and its description as the
adjoint of the tensor product of the counit $Lf^*Rf_*K\to K$ with $Lf^*P$ is
Stacks' description. Difference of generality: Stacks states the map for a
morphism of ringed topoi with coefficients in the structure sheaves $\mathcal
O_{\mathcal C}$, $\mathcal O_{\mathcal D}$, with no completeness hypothesis
and no coefficient tower, whereas the blueprint forms it for the operations
of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] inside the adic coefficient datum of
[def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]; no statement about the map itself
differs.)

Let $u:T_1\to T_2$ be
proper, and let
$j_i:X\hookrightarrow T_i$ be
open immersions with
$u j_1=j_2$. Fix a finite ring $\Lambda$ and
$K\in\hyperref[def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]{D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)}$.
Set $V=T_1\times_{T_2}X$, with projections $b:V\to T_1$ and
$p:V\to X$, and let $s:X\to V$ be the morphism induced by $j_1$,
so that $b s=j_1$ and $p s=\operatorname{id}_X$. Define

$$
\alpha_{u,K}:j_{2!}K\longrightarrow Ru_*j_{1!}K
$$

to be the adjoint, under $j_{2!}\dashv j_2^{-1}$, of
$\theta_{u,K}^{-1}$. The functor $Ru_*$ here is the
derived direct image.

attrs.title: Comparison map for a proper map fixing an open

objects.body:
For a proper morphism $f:X\to Y$, define $\mathsf{PBC}(f)$ to mean that for
every morphism $g:Y'\to Y$, every associated Cartesian square $\square$, and
every torsion sheaf $F$ on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$, the map
$\operatorname{Ex}_{\square,F}$ is an isomorphism in the derived category.
The assertion includes the specified map of Definition
[def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange], not an unnamed isomorphism.

## Detailed form

For a proper morphism [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] $f:X\to Y$, write
$\mathrm{PBC}(f)$ if, for every morphism $g:Y'\to Y$, every associated
cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] $\square$, and
every torsion sheaf [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] $F\in\Ab(X_{\Et})$, the
specified map

$$
 \Ex_{\square,F}:g^{-1}Rf_*F\longrightarrow Rf'_*g'^{-1}F
$$

of the derived exchange morphism [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] is
an isomorphism in $\Dplus(Y'_{\Et})$. Here *torsion* means that the
canonical map $\varinjlim_nF[n]\to F$, $F[n]=\ker(n:F\to F)$, is an
isomorphism, equivalently that every geometric stalk $F_{\bar x}$ is a
torsion group (each local section is, locally on $X_{\Et}$, killed by a
positive integer); it is not required that every group $F(U)$ be torsion.

For $\alpha\in\Qlb$ and $f=[M,u]$ in $\mathcal P_T$, choose a finite field
$N\supset M,\Ql(\alpha)$ and define
$$
 \alpha f=[N,\alpha u_N].
$$
Define
$$
 \Dbc(T,\Qlb)=\mathcal P_T:
$$
an object is a pair $(E,K)$ with $K\in\Dbc(T,E)$ at a finite stage $E$, and
a morphism is a class $[M,u]$ of
[def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]. The shift is that of
[def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones] and the distinguished triangles are the
common-stage cone triangles of [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones]; that these
data satisfy the Verdier axioms and give an ordinary triangulated category
is [thm-weil-pbc-verdier-axioms]. No Karoubi envelope is taken in this
definition: that the category is idempotent complete, and that the envelope
$\Kar(\mathcal P_T)$ is canonically equivalent to it, is recorded with the
other properties of this construction.

*Source note:* the verified Chapter 61 coefficient entries, Section 61.28
([Tag 09BS](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09BS)) and Definition
61.28.1 ([Tag 09BT](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09BT)), keep a
fixed Noetherian ring $\Lambda$ with an ideal $I$ and define constructible,
lisse and adic lisse $\Lambda$-sheaves on $X_{\Proet}$; Definition 61.29.1
([Tag 09C1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C1), fetched and quoted)
fixes the category $D_{cons}(X,\Lambda)$ of those $K$ that are derived
complete with respect to $I$ and have
$K\otimes^L_\Lambda\underline{\Lambda/I}$ of constructible cohomology and
locally of finite tor dimension, and Proposition 61.29.7 ([Tag
09C7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C7), on a Noetherian scheme the
constructible objects are the adic constructible ones) identifies the two
descriptions; all of them keep $\Lambda$ fixed, whereas the form used here
is the filtered colimit of the finite-stage categories $\Dbc(T,E)$ over the
finite extensions $E/\Ql$; the blueprint adds that colimit construction,
with its scalar action and its shift.

Let $E/\Ql$ be finite, let $\mathcal O_E$ be its ring of integers, and let
$\varpi$ be a uniformizer. Define
$$
 \Dbc(T,E)=
 \Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)[1/\varpi],
$$
the *rationalization* (raw scalar localization) of the integral category
[def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]: it has the same objects as
$\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)$, and morphisms
$$
 \Hom(K,L)[1/\varpi]
 =\Hom_{\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)}(K,L)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E.
$$
No Karoubi envelope is taken in this definition. That the category is
idempotent complete, and that the canonical functor into the Karoubi
envelope is consequently an exact equivalence, is recorded with the other
properties of this construction.

attrs.title: Rational category from an integral category

objects.body:
Let $T$ be a closed subset of $\operatorname{Spec}R$. For a constructible
neighbourhood $E\supset T$, let $e_E$ be the idempotent of $R^w$ selecting
the parts in $E$ in [def-weil-pbc-w-localization]. Define

$$
 R_{[T]}=\varinjlim_{E\supset T}(R^w)_{e_E},
$$

where neighbourhoods are ordered by reverse inclusion. Their finite
intersections are again such neighbourhoods.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes. It is *quasi-compact* if the
preimage of every affine open of $Y$ is quasi-compact, and *quasi-separated*
if its diagonal $X\to X\times_YX$ is quasi-compact. A scheme is *affine* if
it is isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}A$ for a commutative ring $A$. The
morphism $f$ is *separated* if its diagonal is a closed immersion, of *finite
type* if it is quasi-compact and every affine open of $Y$ is covered by
finitely many affine opens of $X$ whose coordinate rings are finitely
generated over the coordinate ring of the corresponding affine open of $Y$,
and of *finite presentation* if the same holds with finitely presented
algebras. It is *surjective* if it is surjective on underlying topological
spaces, an *open immersion* if it identifies $X$ with an open subscheme of
$Y$, and a *closed immersion* if it is affine and is induced locally by a
surjective ring homomorphism. It is an *immersion* if it factors as a closed
immersion followed by an open immersion (equivalently, as an open immersion
followed by a closed immersion). It is *universally closed* if every base
change of $f$ is a closed map, and *proper* if it is separated, of finite
type, and universally closed. It is *finite* if it is affine and
$f_*\mathcal O_X$ is a finite $\mathcal O_Y$-algebra, and *integral* if it is
affine and $f_*\mathcal O_X$ is integral over $\mathcal O_Y$. It is
*radicial* if for every field $K$ the map $X(K)\to Y(K)$ is injective, and a
*universal homeomorphism* if every base change of $f$ is a homeomorphism of
underlying spaces. It is *flat* if every induced local-ring map is flat, and
*unramified* if it is locally of finite type and its diagonal is an open
immersion. It is *etale* if it is locally of finite presentation, flat, and
unramified, and *weakly etale* if it is flat and its diagonal is flat.

For $y\in|Y|$, the *geometric fiber* over $y$ is

$$
 X_{\bar y}=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(y)},
$$

where $\overline{\kappa(y)}$ is a chosen algebraic closure of the residue
field $\kappa(y)$. A *geometric point* of $Y$ is a morphism $\bar
y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ with $\Omega$ algebraically closed. A
subset of a scheme is *locally closed* if it is the intersection of an open
and a closed subset, and *constructible* if it is a finite union of locally
closed subsets; a *locally closed constructible subscheme* is a subscheme
whose underlying set is locally closed and constructible. A topological space
is *spectral* if it is quasi-compact, quasi-separated, sober, and has a basis
of quasi-compact opens.

For a scheme $T$, the inclusion of etale $T$-schemes into weakly etale
$T$-schemes is continuous and preserves finite limits. It defines a geometric
morphism

$$
 \nu_T:T_{\Proet}\longrightarrow T_{\Et},
 \qquad
 \nu_T^*:\Sh(T_{\Et})\rightleftarrows
 \Sh(T_{\Proet}):\nu_{T,*}.
$$

For a finite discrete ring $\Lambda$, the same adjunction acts on sheaves of
$\Lambda$-modules.

Let $p:Y\to S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a proper
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] morphism with $A$ a commutative ring. Put
$B=H^0(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$, a ring under the $A$-algebra structure induced by
$p$, and let $q:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ be the canonical morphism and
$s:\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ the morphism of the algebra
structure, so that $p=s\circ q$. The factorization

$$
 Y\xrightarrow{\ q\ }\operatorname{Spec}B\xrightarrow{\ s\ }\operatorname{Spec}A
$$

is the *Stein factorization* of $p$ (*source: Stacks Project, More on
Morphisms, Section 37.53, Tag
[03GX](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03GX)*).

Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be strictly henselian local, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$,
$s=\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak m)$, $X=\mathbf P^1_S$, and
$X_0=\mathbf P^1_s$. For a sheaf $F$ on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ write
$F_0$ for its inverse image on $(X_0)_{\mathrm{et}}$.

## Detailed form

Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be strictly henselian local, put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$,
$s=\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak m)$, $X=\mathbf P^1_S$, and $X_0=\mathbf
P^1_s$. For an etale sheaf $F$ on $X$, write $F_0$ for its inverse image on
$X_0$ and let

$$
 \operatorname{res}_F:\Gamma(X,F)\longrightarrow\Gamma(X_0,F_0)
$$

be restriction.

Let

$$
\mathcal I_{\bar s}:=
(\mathcal N^{\mathrm{aff}}_{\bar s})^{\mathrm{op}}.
$$

For $V=\operatorname{Spec}A_V$, define
$D_{\bar s}:\mathcal I_{\bar s}\to\mathbf{CRing}$ by
$D_{\bar s}(V,\bar v)=A_V$. An arrow
$(W,\bar w)\to(V,\bar v)$ in $\mathcal I_{\bar s}$ represented by a pointed
map $a:(V,\bar v)\to(W,\bar w)$ is sent to
$a^\#:A_W\to A_V$. Put

$$
A^{\mathrm{sh}}_{S,\bar s}:=\varinjlim_{\mathcal I_{\bar s}}D_{\bar s},
\qquad
S_{(\bar s)}:=\operatorname{Spec}A^{\mathrm{sh}}_{S,\bar s}.
$$

The affine scheme–ring anti-equivalence carries the colimit cocone to the
canonical limit cone

$$
S_{(\bar s)}\xrightarrow{\sim}
\varprojlim_{(V,\bar v)\in\mathcal N^{\mathrm{aff}}_{\bar s}}V.
$$

## Detailed form

For affine $(V,\bar v)$ with $V=\operatorname{Spec}A_V$, put

$$
 \mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{S,\bar s}
   =\varinjlim_{(V,\bar v)}A_V,
 \qquad
 S_{(\bar s)}=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{S,\bar s}.
$$

The canonical maps from $S_{(\bar s)}$ to the affine pointed etale
neighborhoods identify it with their inverse limit; these affine
neighborhoods form the indexing subcategory used in the displayed colimit.

On a localization of a ringed topos, let $Q$ be represented by a bounded
complex $F^\bullet$ of finite projective $\Lambda$-modules. A strict-perfect
package for this representation consists, for every $r$, of an integer
$N_r$ and maps

$$
F^r\xrightarrow{i_r}\Lambda^{N_r}
\xrightarrow{p_r}F^r,\qquad p_ri_r=1.
$$

Write $e_r=i_rp_r$; then $e_r^2=e_r$, $p_re_r=p_r$, and $e_ri_r=i_r$.
Perfectness means that such packages exist after a covering. When
$Q\in D(\Lambda)$ is a perfect coefficient complex, one global package and
its associated constant sheaf may be used.

For a ring $A$, put $W=A^w$, let $I$ be the radical ideal defining its closed
point subset, whose closedness is proved in
[lem-weil-pbc-w-localization-points], and set

$$
 E=W^{\mathrm e},\qquad C_A=E_{[V(IE)]}.
$$

The operations are those of [def-weil-pbc-w-localization],
[def-weil-pbc-etale-contraction] and [def-weil-pbc-retained-localization].

For $n\geq1$ and a scheme $S$, define polynomials $F_0,\dots,F_n$ by

$$
 \prod_{i=1}^n(x_it+y_i)=\sum_{j=0}^nF_jt^j.
$$

Each $F_j$ is multihomogeneous of degree one in every pair $(x_i,y_i)$. The
associated rational formula is

$$
 ((x_1:y_1),\dots,(x_n:y_n))\longmapsto[F_0:\cdots:F_n].
$$

For such a cartesian square $\square$, write $\mathrm{TOW}(\square)$ if the
levelwise tower functors of [def-weil-pbc-finite-level-amplification] carry
every uniformly bounded constructible tower to a tower of the same kind,
with local finite-locally-constant models compatible with the amplitude
containments of [def-weil-pbc-finite-level-amplification].

*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this predicate: that direct
images and pullbacks of a bounded constructible tower remain one is the
tower-level form of the constructibility and amplitude conditions of Lemma
59.92.2 ([Tag 095U](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/095U)), Theorem
63.14.5 ([Tag 0GL0](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0GL0)), Definition
61.29.1 ([Tag 09C1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C1)) and
Proposition 61.29.7 ([Tag 09C7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C7)),
which are stated for a single complex on a Noetherian scheme; the closest
tower-level entry is Lemma 61.29.2 ([Tag
09C2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C2)), which bounds the
reduction tower of one constructible object but does not carry it through a
functor. The blueprint adds the preservation predicate
$\mathrm{TOW}(\square)$ together with the local finite-locally-constant
models.

For every $q\geq a$, set

$$
\begin{aligned}
A_q&=g^{-1}Rf_*\tau_{\leq q}K,&
G_q&=g^{-1}Rf_*\mathcal H^q(K)[-q],\\
B_q&=Rf'_*g'^{-1}\tau_{\leq q}K,&
H_q&=Rf'_*g'^{-1}\mathcal H^q(K)[-q].
\end{aligned}
$$

The canonical truncation triangle and its exchanged image are

$$
\begin{CD}
A_{q-1}@>{i_q}>>A_q@>{j_q}>>G_q@>{k_q}>>A_{q-1}[1]\\
@V{e_{q-1}}VV@V{e_q}VV@V{\bar e_q}VV@VV{e_{q-1}[1]}V\\
B_{q-1}@>{i'_q}>>B_q@>{j'_q}>>H_q@>{k'_q}>>B_{q-1}[1].
\end{CD}
$$

For total degree $n$, define

$$
\begin{aligned}
D_A^{q,n}&=\mathcal H^n(A_q),&
\mathcal E_A^{p,q}&=\mathcal H^{p+q}(G_q)
=g^{-1}R^pf_*\mathcal H^q(K),\\
D_B^{q,n}&=\mathcal H^n(B_q),&
\mathcal E_B^{p,q}&=\mathcal H^{p+q}(H_q)
=R^pf'_*g'^{-1}\mathcal H^q(K).
\end{aligned}
$$

The exact-couple differential is

$$
d_1=(j_{q-1})_*\circ(k_q)_*:
\mathcal E_A^{p,q}\longrightarrow\mathcal E_A^{p+2,q-1},
$$

and likewise $d'_1=(j'_{q-1})_*(k'_q)_*$. This first
exact-couple page is the page conventionally denoted $E_2$ in the
hypercohomology indexing.

## Detailed form

For $q\geq a$, apply $g^{-1}Rf_*$ and $Rf'_*g'^{-1}$ to the truncation
triangle

$$
 \tau_{\leq q-1}K\to\tau_{\leq q}K
 \to\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]\to.
$$

The exchange morphisms [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] on its three terms give
a morphism between the resulting exact couples. Its first graded component in
bidegree $(p,q)$ is

$$
 g^{-1}R^pf_*\mathcal H^q(K)\longrightarrow
 R^pf'_*g'^{-1}\mathcal H^q(K).
$$

Let $F$ be a sheaf of abelian groups on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$. The chosen
Cartesian identification gives a canonical isomorphism of inverse-image
functors

$$
f'^{-1}g^{-1}\;\xrightarrow{\sim}\;g'^{-1}f^{-1}.
$$

Define $\operatorname{Ex}_{\square,F}$ to be the adjoint of the composite

$$
f'^{-1}g^{-1}f_*F
\xrightarrow{\sim}g'^{-1}f^{-1}f_*F
\xrightarrow{g'^{-1}\varepsilon_f}g'^{-1}F.
$$

Thus

$$
\operatorname{Ex}_{\square,F}:g^{-1}f_*F\longrightarrow
f'_*g'^{-1}F
$$

is a globally constructed morphism of sheaves. Naturality, identity, and
pasting are properties of this fixed mate; no family of stalk maps is used to
construct it.

## Detailed form

For $F\in\Ab(X_{\Et})$ and a cartesian square
[def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] $\square$, define the *underived
exchange morphism*

$$
 \Ex^0_{\square,F}:g^{-1}f_*F\longrightarrow f'_*g'^{-1}F
$$

to be the adjoint, under $f'^{-1}\dashv f'_*$, of the composite

$$
 f'^{-1}g^{-1}f_*F\xrightarrow{\theta_\square}
 g'^{-1}f^{-1}f_*F\xrightarrow{g'^{-1}\varepsilon_f}g'^{-1}F,
$$

where $\theta_\square$ is the specified isomorphism of the cartesian-square
identification [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] and $\varepsilon_f$
is the counit of the inverse-image adjunction
[def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], and where $f_*$, $f'_*$ are the direct image
[def-weil-pbc-direct-image] functors. For an etale $V\to Y'$, a
representative of a section of $g^{-1}f_*F$ on $V$ consists of an etale $W\to
Y$, a map $V\to W\times_YY'$, and a section of $F$ on $X\times_YW$; its image
is the restriction of that section along

$$
 X'\times_{Y'}V\longrightarrow X\times_YW,
$$

followed by sheafification.

attrs.title: Underived exchange map: corrected categorical construction

objects.body:
For an affine scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]
$X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, its *patch topology* is generated by the subsets
$D(f)$ and $V(f)$, for $f\in A$. A subset is *constructible* here if it is a
finite Boolean combination of these subsets. We call $X$ *w-local* if its
closed points form a closed subset and every connected component has exactly
one closed point.

attrs.title: Patch topology and w-local affine schemes

objects.body:
For a ring $A$, consider finite partitions $\mathcal P$ of
$\operatorname{Spec}A$ into nonempty constructible
[def-weil-pbc-w-local] sets. For each part $E$, choose $f_E\in A$ with
$E\subset D(f_E)$. Refining a partition and multiplying its denominators
gives a directed system of algebras $\prod_{E\in\mathcal P}A_{f_E}$. Define

$$
 A^w=\varinjlim_{(\mathcal P,(f_E))}
          \prod_{E\in\mathcal P}A_{f_E}.
$$

The transition maps are the componentwise localization maps; common
refinements use intersections of parts and products of denominators. This
specifies an ind-Zariski [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra] algebra, without
asserting its geometric properties in the definition.

For a weakly etale [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra] map $A\to B$, take
$C=C_A$ from [def-weil-pbc-strict-w-cover], and let $J$ be the radical ideal
of its closed point subset, supplied by
[lem-weil-pbc-strict-w-cover]. Define

$$
 D_0=B\otimes_AC,\qquad
 B'= (D_0)_{[V(JD_0)]}
$$

using [def-weil-pbc-retained-localization].

attrs.title: An affine refinement of a weakly etale algebra

objects.body:
For such a cartesian square $\square$, write $\mathrm{WIT}(\square)$ if the
four finite-level functors of [def-weil-pbc-finite-level-amplification]
commute with the normalization isomorphisms for $P_{n+1}\to P_n$ and carry
compatible etale-origin witnesses [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness] to
compatible etale-origin witnesses.

*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this predicate: the
etale-origin witnesses are the blueprint's device for Stacks' hypothesis in
Theorem 61.30.1 ([Tag 09C9](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C9)) that
$K\otimes^L_\Lambda\underline{\Lambda/I^n}$ be bounded below with cohomology
sheaves coming from the etale site. The per-level existence of such an
origin is Stacks' Lemma 61.29.2 ([Tag
09C2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C2)) (4): for a constructible
$K$ on a quasi-compact $X$ there are $a,b$ with $K=\Rlim K_n$, each $K_n$ of
tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ with constructible cohomology sheaves, and
$K_n=\epsilon^{-1}L_n$ for some $L_n\in D_{ctf}(X_{\Et},\Lambda/I^n)$.
Difference: Stacks states this for a single object, and neither asserts that
the $L_n$ are compatible over $n$ nor tracks maps $\alpha_n$ as in
[def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]; the blueprint adds the compatibility
predicate $\mathrm{WIT}(\square)$.

Let $p$ be prime, let $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, put $q=p^a$, and set
$k_0=\Fq$, and let $k=\Fbar$ be the fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$. Fix a
prime $\ell\neq p$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and choose an algebraic
closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$. Let $X_0/k_0$ be smooth, proper, and geometrically
connected of pure dimension $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$. Put
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $a_X:X\to\Spec k$ be its structure morphism.
Write $H^i(X,-)$ and $H_c^i(X,-)$ for the ordinary and compactly supported
cohomology groups, and, for every integer $m$, write $\Ql(m)$ for the Tate
twist [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] of degree $m$. Write $Ra_X^!$ for
the constructible exceptional inverse image of
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] at $\Ql$ and $\Qlb$ — defined for every
separated finite-type morphism, so no admissibility hypothesis on $a_X$ is
imposed (the ambient notion of [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility]
is not used) — and $\otimes^L$ for the derived tensor product, using the
derived pullback/tensor/Hom notation. Choose an
orientation isomorphism for the smooth structure morphism $a_X:X\to\Spec k$,

$$
 \eta_X:Ra_X^!\Ql\xrightarrow{\sim}(\Ql)_X(d)[2d],
$$

where $\Ql(d)$ uses the Tate twist [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] of degree $d$. We
use $Ra_{X*}$ and $Ra_{X!}$ for the derived direct image and the
compact-support direct image [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed],
respectively. Through $\eta_X$, the counit $Ra_{X!}Ra_X^!\Ql\to\Ql$ defines
the trace map

$$
 \operatorname{tr}_X:H_c^{2d}(X,\Ql(d))\longrightarrow\Ql.
$$

For the proper structure morphism, use the compact-support direct image
[def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] comparison and, after untwisting, write

$$
 \operatorname{tr}^{(-d)}_X:H^{2d}(X,\Ql)\longrightarrow\Ql(-d).
$$

The multiplication $(\Ql)_X\otimes^L(\Ql)_X\to(\Ql)_X$ defines, for all
integers $i,j$, cup products

$$
\smile:H^i(X,\Ql)\otimes_{\Ql}H^j(X,\Ql)
 \longrightarrow H^{i+j}(X,\Ql).
$$

For $x\in H^i(X,\Ql)$ and $y\in H^j(X,\Ql)$, the cup product is
graded-commutative:

$$
 y\smile x=(-1)^{ij}x\smile y
 \qquad
 (x\in H^i(X,\Ql),\ y\in H^j(X,\Ql)).
$$

For every integer $i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$, and for every $x\in H^i(X,\Ql)$
and $y\in H^{2d-i}(X,\Ql)$, define

$$
 \langle x,y\rangle_i=
 \operatorname{tr}^{(-d)}_X(x\smile y):
 H^i(X,\Ql)\times H^{2d-i}(X,\Ql)
 \longrightarrow\Ql(-d).
$$

Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$, where $q=p^a$, and use geometric
Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]; let $Y_0$ be a finite-type $k_0$-scheme. Fix
an indeterminate $T$. For every integer $n\geq1$, put

$$
 Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})=\operatorname{Hom}_{k_0}
 (\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf F_{q^n},Y_0),
 \qquad
 N_n(Y_0)=\#Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^n}).
$$

Write $|Y_0|$ for the set of closed points of $Y_0$. For a closed point
$x\in|Y_0|$, let $\kappa(x)$ be its residue field and set
$\deg(x)=[\kappa(x):\Fq]$. For every integer $r\geq1$, put

$$
 c_r=\#\{x\in|Y_0|:\deg(x)=r\}.
$$

Define the Hasse--Weil zeta series by

$$
 Z(Y_0,T)=
 \exp\left(\sum_{n\geq1}N_n(Y_0)\frac{T^n}{n}\right)
 \in1+T\mathbf Q[[T]].
$$

The exponential is the formal power-series exponential.

Fix a prime $p$, an integer $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, put $q=p^a$, $k_0=\Fq$,
and let $k=\Fbar$ be the fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$. Fix a prime
$\ell\neq p$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$
of $\Ql$, and fix an isomorphism $\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$. Let
$Y_0$ be a finite-type $k_0$-scheme, put $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let
$\mathcal F$ be a constructible $\Qlb$-sheaf in the constructible heart,
carrying the Weil-sheaf structure. For each closed point $y\in|Y_0|$, use the
closed-point notation [def-weil-point-counts-zeta], set $q_y=\#\kappa(y)$,
choose an embedding $\kappa(y)\hookrightarrow k$, and choose a geometric
point $\bar y\to Y$ above $y$ (the eigenvalues of $F_y$ do not depend on these choices, by [lem-weil-local-frobenius-conjugacy-class]). Let $F_y$ be the local geometric-Frobenius
operator [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] on $\mathcal F_{\bar y}$. For
$w\in\mathbf R$, call $\mathcal F$ punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$ if
every eigenvalue $\alpha$ of every $F_y$ satisfies

$$
 |\iota(\alpha)|=q_y^{w/2}.
$$

Call $\mathcal F$ $\iota$-mixed of weights at most $w$ if there are an
integer $m\geq0$, constructible $\Qlb$-Weil subsheaves

$$
 0=\mathcal F_0\subset\mathcal F_1\subset\cdots\subset\mathcal F_m=\mathcal F,
 \qquad w_1,\ldots,w_m\in\mathbf R,\quad w_r\leq w,
$$

such that each quotient $\mathcal F_r/\mathcal F_{r-1}$ is punctually
$\iota$-pure of weight $w_r$.

For the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], fix a prime
$\ell\neq p$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$, a scheme $Y$, and a uniformizer
$\varpi_E$ of its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$. The derived-complete
integral category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] is
$D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$, built from the finite-torsion coefficients
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] $A_{E,n}=\mathcal
O_E/\varpi_E^n$. If $\mathcal C$ is an $\mathcal O_E$-linear triangulated
category, its rationalization $\mathcal C[1/\varpi_E]$ has the same objects
and, for $K,L\in\mathcal C$,

$$
 \Hom_{\mathcal C[1/\varpi_E]}(K,L)
 =\Hom_{\mathcal C}(K,L)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E.
$$

Set

$$
 D^b_c(Y,E)=
 D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)[1/\varpi_E].
$$

No Karoubi (idempotent) completion is taken in this definition: the notation
$\mathcal C[1/\varpi_E]$ denotes the raw scalar localization displayed above,
in which no idempotent is formally adjoined. For $E=\Ql$, this uses $\mathcal
O_E=\Zl$ and $\varpi_E=\ell$.

If $E\subset L$ is a finite extension, the scalar-extension functor is

$$
 -\otimes_E L:D^b_c(Y,E)\longrightarrow D^b_c(Y,L),
$$

defined on integral representatives by completed derived tensor product
[def-weil-derived-tensor] with $\mathcal O_L$, levelwise modulo powers of the
two uniformizers, followed by rationalization.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism. Write $|Y|$ for the set of closed points of
$Y$, and, for $y\in|Y|$, write $\kappa(y)$ for its residue field. The phrase
of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] has the preceding meaning. It
is *of finite presentation* if every affine open $V\subseteq Y$ has a finite
affine cover of $f^{-1}(V)$ by $\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ a finitely
presented algebra over the coordinate ring of $V$. A ring is *regular* if
each localization at a prime has Krull dimension equal to the minimal number
of generators of its maximal ideal; a scheme is regular if all its local
rings are regular. The morphism $f$ is *flat* if every induced local-ring map
is flat, and *smooth* if it is locally of finite presentation and flat with
regular geometric fibers. It is a *closed immersion* if it is affine and is
induced locally by a surjective ring homomorphism. It is *separated* if its
diagonal $X\to X\times_YX$ is a closed immersion, and *universally closed* if
