## Proof

Test the projection map of
[def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-map] at a geometric point
$\bar t$. It becomes the constant-coefficient map

$$
K_{\bar t}\otimes_A^LR\Gamma(V_{\bar t},L|_{V_{\bar t}})
\longrightarrow
R\Gamma(V_{\bar t},\underline{K_{\bar t}}\otimes_A^LL|_{V_{\bar t}}).
$$

Both sides, as functors of $K_{\bar t}\in D(A)$, are exact
and preserve coproducts. This follows on the right from the coproduct result
[lem-amb-proper-coproducts] applied over the geometric point. The comparison is the
identity for $K_{\bar t}=A$. The shifts of $A$ generate
$D(A)$ under coproducts and cones: free resolutions and their
truncations give the usual explicit construction. Hence the map
is an isomorphism for every $K_{\bar t}$. [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] proves the assertion on $T$.

attrs.title: The proper projection formula on the ambient category

objects.body:
Let $S$ be integral and of finite type over a field $k$, let
$\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, let $f:X\to S$ be a
separated smooth morphism of
finite type, and let $L$ be a finite locally constant
$\mathbf F_\ell$-sheaf. There is a nonempty open $U\subset S$
such that $Rf_{U,*}L|_{X_U}$ is bounded with finite locally
constant cohomology, and for every $v:T\to U$ with Noetherian $T$ the ordinary
base-change morphism

$$
v^*Rf_{U,*}L|_{X_U}\longrightarrow Rf_{T,*}L|_{X_T}
$$

is an isomorphism.
The notation refers to ordinary derived categories.

## Proof

Write $\lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$. The relative dimension is
locally constant by
[sbc-lem-smooth-relative-dimension-locally-constant]; the
finitely many occurring dimensions give a finite disjoint open
decomposition, so we may treat one dimension at a time.
Put $\omega_f=f^\times\lambda_S$. The ambient smooth theorem
[thm-asd-smooth-tensor] says that $\omega_f$ is locally an
invertible sheaf in degree $-2d$, that
$f^\times M=\omega_f\otimes f^*M$. Its compatibility with
Noetherian base change is [prop-asd-smooth-base-change]. In particular
$N=L^\vee\otimes\omega_f$ is bounded constructible and the
finite-dimensional evaluation isomorphism gives

$$
R\mathcal Hom_X(N,\omega_f)=L.
$$

The internal adjunction proved on the ambient categories in
[prop-asd-internal-adjunction] therefore identifies

$$
Rf_*L
=R\mathcal Hom_S(Rf_!N,\lambda_S).
\tag{\(\ast\)}
$$

This invokes neither preservation of a constructible subcategory
by $f^!$ nor ordinary direct-image finiteness.

By [lem-fin-compact-bounded-and-base-change], $C=Rf_!N$
is bounded constructible. Each of its finitely many nonzero
cohomology sheaves is finite locally constant on some nonempty
open of the integral scheme $S$: take the stratum containing
the generic point in the constructible stratification of
[def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], and then its open
neighborhood. Intersect these finitely many opens to obtain $U$.
Apply [lem-fin-lisse-field-dual] to $C|_U$; equation
$(\ast)$ gives the claimed bounded locally constant cohomology.

For $v:T\to U$ with Noetherian $T$, the ambient smooth theorem identifies
$v_X^*N$ with the coefficient complex used for $f_T$.
Compact-support base change identifies
$v^*C$ with $Rf_{T,!}v_X^*N$, and
[lem-fin-lisse-field-dual] permits pullback through its
internal dual. Thus the pullback of $(\ast)$ is the same
isomorphism $(\ast)$ for $f_T$. Naturality of internal
adjunction with respect to its unit and counit identifies this
composite with the ordinary base-change morphism. Hence the
specified morphism, and not merely two abstract objects, is an
isomorphism. Intersect the opens obtained for the finitely many
relative dimensions to finish.

attrs.title: A smooth source with locally constant coefficients

objects.body:
Let $(A,I)$ satisfy [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], let

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
U'&\xrightarrow{g_U}&U\\
j'\downarrow&&\downarrow j\\
X'&\xrightarrow{g}&X
\end{array}
$$

be an open-immersion square,
and let $K\in D(U_{\Proet},A)$ be derived $I$-complete. Then the
canonical map

$$
Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}j_!K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }j'_!Lg_{U,\mathrm{comp}}^*K
$$

is an isomorphism, natural in $K$.

## Proof

The functor $j_!$ is exact
([def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] on the pro-etale site,
[lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]), so the reduction tower of
$j_!K$ is $j_!K_\bullet$ (reductions commute with $j_!$ by
exactness and [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]). By
[def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] its reduction maps are
$Lg_n^*j_!K_n$, which
[lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change] identifies
with $j'_!Lg_{U,n}^*K_n$, the reductions of
$j'_!Lg_{U,\mathrm{comp}}^*K$ (with the reduction compatibilities of
[lemma-weil-pbc-completed-pullback-reduction] for the map
$g_U$). Applying the exactness of $j'_!$ and
[lem-cbc-exact-functor-rlim] to the defining derived limits of
[def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] gives the asserted
isomorphism (the countable-product hypothesis of
[lem-cbc-exact-functor-rlim] holds for $j'_!$: extension by
zero for an open immersion is exact and, being the stalk- and
sectionwise extension by the zero functor
$V\mapsto V\cap U'$, it is computed levelwise and preserves the
countable products of the derived-product representation).

Let $F$ be a triangulated functor between the derived categories of
pro-etale module sheaves which is exact, commutes with the
levelwise evaluation of
[def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit], and commutes with the
*countable* derived products of the tower category, i.e. the
canonical maps
$F(R\prod_nM_n)\to R\prod_nF(M_n)$ are isomorphisms for every
family $(M_n)_n$ (a triangulated functor preserves finite
products, hence only finite, not countable, products in general).
Then for every tower $M_\bullet\in D(\operatorname{Tow}(T))$ the
canonical map

$$
F\bigl(\Rlim M_\bullet\bigr)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Rlim F(M_\bullet)
$$

is an isomorphism.

## Proof

By [prop-weil-pbc-roos-triangle], $M_\bullet$ sits in the
distinguished triangle

$$
\Rlim M_\bullet\to R\!\prod_nM_n\xrightarrow{1-s}R\!\prod_nM_n
\to(\Rlim M_\bullet)[1].
$$

The functor $F$ is exact, so applying $F$ produces a
distinguished triangle with third vertex $F(\Rlim M_\bullet)$;
on the two derived products $F$ is computed levelwise, because
$F$ commutes with the evaluations of
[def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit] and with the countable
products of the Roos triangle representation, so the image of
$1-s$ is $1-F(s)$. Hence $F(\Rlim M_\bullet)$ is a cone of
$1-F(s)$ over the tower $F(M_\bullet)$; and
[prop-weil-pbc-roos-triangle] applied to $F(M_\bullet)$
exhibits $\Rlim F(M_\bullet)$ as a cone of $1-F(s)$ as well.
Cones of a fixed morphism in a triangulated category are
canonically isomorphic, and the canonical map of the statement is
that comparison, so it is an isomorphism.

attrs.title: Exact functors commute with derived limits of towers

objects.body:
Let

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
U'&\xrightarrow{g_U}&U\\
j'\downarrow&&\downarrow j\\
X'&\xrightarrow{g}&X
\end{array}
$$

be an open-immersion square.
For every abelian sheaf $F$ on $U_{\Et}$ the canonical map

$$
g^{-1}j_!F\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }j'_!g_U^{-1}F
$$

u
identification $j'^{-1}g^{-1}=g_U^{-1}j^{-1}$ (the square commutes)
composed with the counit of
[def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. For a finite commutative ring
$\Lambda$ and a complex of $\Lambda$-module sheaves the isomorphism
holds degreewise.

## Proof

Fix a geometric point $\bar x'$ of $X'$ with image
$\bar x=g(\bar x')$. By the stalk characterization of
[def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], whose underived form is
[def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero],

$$
(g^{-1}j_!F)_{\bar x'}=(j_!F)_{\bar x}=
\begin{cases}
F_{\bar x},& \bar x\in U,\\
0,&\bar x\in X\setminus U,
\end{cases}
\qquad
(j'_!g_U^{-1}F)_{\bar x'}=
\begin{cases}
(g_U^{-1}F)_{\bar x'}=F_{\bar x},&\bar x'\in U',\\
0,&\bar x'\in X'\setminus U',
\end{cases}
$$

and $\bar x\in U$ if and only if $\bar x'\in U'$ because the square
is cartesian. Under these identifications the two stalks of the map
agree (the adjoint construction of the map is precisely the
corresponding restriction of sections); the inverse image functors
are exact, and
[lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] makes the map an
isomorphism. For complexes the argument applies termwise, exactness
of $j_!$ giving the derived statement.

attrs.title: Extension by zero commutes with arbitrary base change

objects.body:
For composable
open immersions
$U\hookrightarrow V\hookrightarrow X$, the canonical comparison

$$
(j_2)_!(j_1)_!F\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }(j_2j_1)_!F
$$

is an isomorphism, natural in $F$ and compatible with the identity
open immersion and the two ways of composing three open immersions.

## Proof

All three functors are left adjoint to the corresponding inverse
image functors, and the two candidates are the left adjoints of the
same functor $((j_2j_1)^{-1}=(j_1)^{-1}(j_2)^{-1})$, so they are
canonically isomorphic (the comparison being the mate of the
identification of inverse images); naturality and the coherence
equations follow from the adjunction calculus, as in
[def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero].

For an open immersion
$j:U\hookrightarrow X$, a finite coefficient ring $\Lambda$, a
complex $K$ of $\Lambda$-modules on $U_{\Proet}$, and a complex
$L$ of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\Proet}$, the canonical map (with the derived tensor product of
[def-weil-derived-tensor])

$$
(j_!K)\otimes^L_\Lambda L\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
j_!\bigl(K\otimes^L_\Lambda j^{-1}L\bigr)
$$

is an isomorphism in $D(X_{\Proet},\Lambda)$.

## Proof

The canonical map is the adjoint of the projection morphism for
$j^{-1}$, the functors $j^{-1}$ and $-\otimes^L_\Lambda$
commuting by [def-weil-derived-tensor]. We verify the map by the
tensor–internal-Hom adjunction of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. For a test complex $M$
on $X_{\Proet}$,

$$
\operatorname{Hom}\bigl((j_!K)\otimes^L_\Lambda L,M\bigr)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}\bigl(j_!K,R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(L,M)\bigr)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}\bigl(K,j^{-1}R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(L,M)\bigr),
$$

the first isomorphism being the tensor–internal-Hom adjunction and
the second the adjunction $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$ of
[lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. Formation of the internal Hom
commutes with inverse image,
$j^{-1}R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(L,M)\cong R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(j^{-1}L,j^{-1}M)$, by the same definition; the
last group is therefore
$\operatorname{Hom}\bigl(K\otimes^L_\Lambda j^{-1}L,j^{-1}M\bigr)$,
which by $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$ again is

$$
\operatorname{Hom}\bigl(j_!\bigl(K\otimes^L_\Lambda j^{-1}L\bigr),M\bigr).
$$

The two Hom-functors in $M$ are thus isomorphic, so by Yoneda the
two complexes are canonically isomorphic, and the isomorphism is the
displayed canonical map because it is induced by the units and counits
of the two adjunctions. No constructibility, no stalk computation,
and no conservativity enters: the statement is the projection formula
for the exact left adjoint $j_!$, in the pro-etale site.

attrs.title: Projection formula for extension by zero

objects.body:
Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a
closed immersion with
complementary
open immersion
$j:U\hookrightarrow X$, and let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative
ring. For every $K\in D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ there is a functorial
distinguished triangle

$$
j_!j^{-1}K\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow i_*i^{-1}K
\longrightarrow j_!j^{-1}K[1],
$$

where $i_*$ is the (exact) direct image of the closed immersion, and
the triangle is compatible with the adjunctions
$j_!\dashv j^{-1}$, $i^{-1}\dashv i_*$ of
[prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions].

## Proof

The closed immersion $i$ is finite,
so $i_*$ is exact by [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact].
A short exact sequence of sheaves
$0\to j_!j^{-1}F\to F\to i_*i^{-1}F\to0$ is obtained from the
stalkwise description of [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]: on $U$
the first map is the counit of $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$, an isomorphism
by the identity $j^*j_!\cong\operatorname{id}$ of
[prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions], and the third map is
$0$ there; on $Z$ the first term already has stalk $0$, the
spaces of the first two terms at a point of $Z$ agree, and the
third map is the (inverse-image) unit of
[prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions], an isomorphism.
The exact
kernel–cokernel description at every stalk gives the short exact
sequence, and taking the associated distinguished triangle in the
derived category gives the assertion; functoriality and the
adjunction compatibilities are those of the short exact sequence and
of [def-weil-open-closed-recollement].

For an open immersion
$j:U\hookrightarrow X$, extension by zero on the small pro-etale
site (the functor $j_!$ of [def-weil-extension-by-zero])
is the exact left adjoint of $j^{-1}$, acts degreewise, and is
characterized by the same stalk prescription as the etale one,

$$
(j_!K)_{\bar x}=
\begin{cases}
K_{\bar x},&\bar x\text{ lies in }U,\\
0,&\bar x\text{ lies in }X\setminus U,
\end{cases}
$$

for a complex $K$ of pro-etale sheaves and a geometric point
$\bar x$ of $X$; it is compatible with restriction of scalars
along a finite coefficient ring.

## Proof

The exactness and the left-adjoint property are part of
[def-weil-extension-by-zero], which is stated on the pro-etale
site. For the stalk description, the category of weak etale
neighbourhoods of $\bar x$ in
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] is filtered, and the
subcategory of the neighbourhoods that factor through the open
subscheme $U$ is cofinal in the neighbourhoods of $\bar x$ when
$\bar x\in U$, and empty otherwise; hence the stalk formula, and
the degreewise property of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]
follows from the explicit cofinality, the compatibility with
restriction of scalars being the naturality of the construction in
the coefficient ring.

attrs.title: Extension by zero on the pro-etale site

objects.body:
Let

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
U'&\xrightarrow{g_U}&U\\
j'\downarrow&&\downarrow j\\
X'&\xrightarrow{g}&X
\end{array}
$$

be an open-immersion square
and let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. For every complex
$K$ of $\Lambda$-module sheaves on $U_{\Proet}$ the canonical map

$$
g^{-1}j_!K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }j'_!g_U^{-1}K
$$

is an isomorphism, natural in $K$; here all functors are the
pro-etale ones of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero].

## Proof

Both sides are left adjoints, and we identify their right adjoints.
By [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero] the functor $j_!$ is left
adjoint to $j^{-1}$ and is exact, and by
[def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] the same adjunction is available on
the primed square. For a complex $M$ on $X'_{\Proet}$ the two
Hom-functors in $K$ are therefore

$$
\operatorname{Hom}\bigl(g^{-1}j_!K,M\bigr)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}\bigl(j_!K,g_*M\bigr)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}\bigl(K,j^{-1}g_*M\bigr),
$$

$$
\operatorname{Hom}\bigl(j'_!g_U^{-1}K,M\bigr)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}\bigl(g_U^{-1}K,j'^{-1}M\bigr)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}\bigl(K,g_{U*}j'^{-1}M\bigr).
$$

The two right adjoints agree. For $V\to U$ the under-category of
$X$-objects under $V$ has $V$ itself as initial object, so the
value of $j^{-1}g_*M$ at $V$ is $M(V\times_XX')$; and the value
of $g_{U*}j'^{-1}M$ at $V$ is $j'^{-1}M(V\times_UU')= M(V\times_XX')$, the open-immersion square of
[def-cbc-open-immersion-square] being cartesian and $V\times_UU'$
being the same weakly etale $X'$-object as $V\times_XX'$. Both
identifications are restriction of sections along an open immersion,
so the two right adjoints are equal, not merely isomorphic. The two
Hom-functors in $K$ are therefore isomorphic, and by Yoneda the two
left adjoints are canonically isomorphic. The isomorphism is natural
in $K$, being induced by the naturality of the adjunction
isomorphisms, and it is the canonical map of the statement because
both sides of the comparison are assembled from the units and counits
of the displayed adjunctions.

Let $\nu_X:X_{\Proet}\to X_{\Et}$ be the comparison morphism of
[def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. For an open immersion
$j:U\hookrightarrow X$ and a finite commutative ring $\Lambda$ the
canonical comparison

$$
\nu_X^*j^{\mathrm{et}}_!F\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }j^{\mathrm{proet}}_!\nu_U^*F
$$

is an isomorphism for every sheaf $F$ of $\Lambda$-modules on
$U_{\Et}$, naturally in $F$ and compatible with composition of
open immersions; here the two $j_!$ are those of
[def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] and
[def-weil-extension-by-zero].

## Proof

Both sides are left adjoints of functors to the sheaves on
$U_{\Proet}$, and we identify their right adjoints.
By [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] the inverse image
$\nu_X^*$ is left adjoint to $\nu_{X*}$, and it is computed on the
objects common to the two sites; by
[def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] and
[def-weil-extension-by-zero] the functors
$j^{\mathrm{et}}_!$ and $j^{\mathrm{proet}}_!$ are left adjoint to
the corresponding restriction along $j$. For a sheaf $M$ on
$X_{\Proet}$ the two Hom-functors in $F$ are therefore

$$
\operatorname{Hom}\bigl(\nu_X^*j^{\mathrm{et}}_!F,M\bigr)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}\bigl(j^{\mathrm{et}}_!F,\nu_{X*}M\bigr)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}\bigl(F,j^{\mathrm{et},-1}\nu_{X*}M\bigr),
$$

$$
\operatorname{Hom}\bigl(j^{\mathrm{proet}}_!\nu_U^*F,M\bigr)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}\bigl(\nu_U^*F,j^{-1}M\bigr)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}\bigl(F,\nu_{U*}j^{-1}M\bigr).
$$

The two right adjoints agree as functors to sheaves on $U_{\Et}$.
Indeed, for an etale $W\to U$ the under-category of etale
$X$-schemes under $W$ has $W$ itself as initial object, because
$W$ is etale over $X$ as a composite of etale morphisms; hence
both $j^{\mathrm{et},-1}\nu_{X*}M$ and $\nu_{U*}j^{-1}M$ evaluate
at $W$ to $M(W)$, the identification being the restriction of
sections along the open immersion $U\hookrightarrow X$. The two
Hom-functors in $F$ are therefore isomorphic, and by Yoneda the two
left adjoints are canonically isomorphic: this is the displayed
comparison. Naturality in $F$ and compatibility with a composite of
open immersions follow from the same identification of right
adjoints, which is the restriction of sections along an open
immersion and is natural and transitive, as in
[lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition].

attrs.title: Comparison of extension by zero with the site morphism

objects.body:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite discrete ring and let $T$ be a scheme.

1. *locality for covering families.* A morphism
$F\to G$ of complexes of $\Lambda$-module sheaves on
$T_{\Proet}$ is an isomorphism if and only if its inverse image
along every member of one
pro-etale covering family
of $T$ is an isomorphism. Equivalently: a complex on
$T_{\Proet}$ is acyclic if and only if its cohomology sheaves
vanish, and a sheaf on $T_{\Proet}$ vanishes if and only if it
vanishes after inverse image along the members of a covering family.
1. *detection on the affine ind-etale basis.* For affine
$T$, a sheaf on $T_{\Proet}$ vanishes if and only if its sections
on every object of the affine ind-etale basis
[def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis] vanish; consequently a morphism
of complexes on $T_{\Proet}$ is an isomorphism if and only if it
induces a quasi-isomorphism of sections on every object of that
basis. For general $T$ the same holds with the bases of the
members of an affine open cover.
1. *complexes of etale origin.* Let
$\nu_T:T_{\Proet}\to T_{\Et}$ be the comparison morphism of
[def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] and let
$F'\to G'$ be a morphism of bounded-below complexes of etale
$\Lambda$-sheaves. Then $\nu_T^*F'\to\nu_T^*G'$ is an
isomorphism if and only if it is an isomorphism at every geometric
point of $T$. In particular the geometric-point stalks are
jointly conservative on the bounded constructible objects
$\Dbc(T_{\Proet},\Lambda)$, which are of etale origin by
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules].
1. *warning.* None of this extends to arbitrary pro-etale
sheaves: the collection of geometric-point stalks is *not*
conservative on $\Sh(T_{\Proet})$. For
$T=\operatorname{Spec}k$ with $k$ algebraically closed and a
nonzero abelian group $A$, the sheafified quotient of functions
modulo locally constant functions, $\mathcal F(U)=\{\text{functions } U\to A\}/\{\text{locally constant functions}\}$, has
$\mathcal F(T)=0$ while $\mathcal F\neq0$, the site
$T_{\Proet}$ containing affine objects with infinitely many points
(Stacks Project, Pro-étale Cohomology, Section 61.18,
[Tag 0991](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0991)).

## Proof

*Step 1 (clause (1)).* A morphism of complexes is an
isomorphism if and only if its cone is acyclic, and a complex is
acyclic if and only if all its cohomology sheaves vanish: this is the
definition of the derived category of
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] as the localization at the
quasi-isomorphisms. Vanishing of a sheaf is a local condition for the
topology. Indeed, if $\mathcal H$ is a sheaf on $T_{\Proet}$ whose
inverse images along the members of a covering family vanish, then for
every object $V$ the sheaf axiom presents $\mathcal H(V)$ as the
equalizer of two maps between products of groups
$\mathcal H(V\times_TU_i)$ that are zero, the family being a
covering; hence $\mathcal H(V)=0$, and the converse is functoriality
of inverse image. Applying this to the cohomology sheaves of the cone
gives the equivalence of the first sentence.

*Step 2 (clause (2)).* This is
[lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]: restriction to the affine
ind-etale basis of [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis] determines a
sheaf and its morphisms uniquely and detects isomorphisms of sheaves.
Restriction of a complex is exact and degreewise, so a morphism of
complexes is a quasi-isomorphism if and only if its restriction is
one. A general $T$ is covered by its affine opens, and clause (1)
reduces the statement to the affine case.

*Step 3 (clause (3)).* Let $\mathcal G'$ be a bounded-below
complex of etale $\Lambda$-sheaves. The etale neighbourhoods of a
geometric point $\bar t$ of $T$ are cofinal among its weakly etale
neighbourhoods, by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and
[def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], the inverse image of the
comparison morphism being computed on the common objects; hence
$(\nu_T^*\mathcal G')_{\bar t}=\mathcal G'_{\bar t}$, naturally in
$\mathcal G'$. If $\nu_T^*F'\to\nu_T^*G'$ is an isomorphism at
every geometric point, then $F'\to G'$ is an isomorphism at every
geometric point, hence an isomorphism by
[lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]; applying the functor
$\nu_T^*$ exhibits $\nu_T^*F'\to\nu_T^*G'$ as an isomorphism. The
converse follows from functoriality. For bounded-below complexes one
applies this degreewise to the cohomology sheaves, inverse image being
exact and the identification of stalks being natural. The final
assertion of the clause is the definition: the bounded constructible
objects of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] are by definition the
pullbacks of the bounded constructible etale objects. Full
faithfulness of $\nu_T^*$ on bounded-below complexes,
[thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], is not needed for this argument,
but it shows that the etale model of a morphism of etale origin is
unique.

*Step 4 (clause (4)).* The replacement for the false general
statement is the displayed reference. Concretely, on
$T=\operatorname{Spec}k$ the single geometric point of $T$ is the
only point of the small pro-etale site that comes from a strictly
henselian local ring, while the site contains the affine objects
$U=\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{colim}\operatorname{Map}(E_n,k))$
for $E=\varprojlim E_n$ an inverse limit of finite sets with
surjective transition maps; such a $U$ is ind-Zariski, hence weakly
etale, over $k$ and has infinitely many points, so the sheaf
$\mathcal F$ of the statement has a nonzero value there while
$\mathcal F(T)=0$. No clause of this lemma asserts conservativity
of geometric-point stalks beyond clause (3), and clause (3) confines
the failure to complexes that are not of etale origin.

attrs.title: Detecting isomorphisms on the pro-etale site

objects.body:
Let $S$ be a scheme and let $V$ be an affine scheme equipped with a morphism
$g\colon V\to S$ that is locally of finite type. Then there are a finite index
set $n$ and an immersion $j\colon V\to\mathbf P^n_S$ with
$j$ followed by $\mathbf P^n_S\to S$ equal to $g$. Here the homogeneous
coordinates $T_i$ of $\mathbf P^n_S$ are indexed by the finite set $n$.

## Proof

Write $B=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$, so that $V=\Spec B$. We give an elementary
construction; it does not use ample invertible sheaves.

*Step 1: a cover adapted to $g$.* Every point of $V$ has a basic open
neighbourhood $D(b)$ with $g(D(b))$ contained in an affine open of $S$: pick an
affine open $W\subseteq S$ around the image point and then a basic open of $V$
inside $g^{-1}(W)$. Since $V$ is quasi-compact, finitely many of these cover
$V$: there are a finite set $\Lambda$, sections $b_\lambda\in B$ and affine
opens $W_\lambda\subseteq S$ with $D(b_\lambda)\subseteq g^{-1}(W_\lambda)$ and
$V=\bigcup_{\lambda}D(b_\lambda)$.

*Step 2: generators with a common denominator.* Fix $\lambda$ and put
$A_\lambda=\Gamma(W_\lambda,\mathcal O_S)$. The induced morphism
$D(b_\lambda)\to W_\lambda$ is a morphism of affine schemes that is locally of
finite type, so $B_{b_\lambda}=\Gamma(D(b_\lambda),\mathcal O_V)$ is a finitely
generated $A_\lambda$-algebra. Clearing denominators, we may choose the
generators of the shape $c_\mu/b_\lambda^{N}$ with $c_\mu\in B$ and a single
exponent $N$, indexed by a finite set $M_\lambda$. Put

$$
t_{\lambda,\ast}=1,\qquad t_{\lambda,\mu}=c_\mu b_\lambda
\quad(\mu\in M_\lambda),
$$

a family indexed by the finite set $M_\lambda^{+}=M_\lambda\sqcup\{\ast\}$.
In $B_{b_\lambda}$ we have $t_{\lambda,\ast}/b_\lambda=1/b_\lambda$ and
$t_{\lambda,\mu}/b_\lambda=c_\mu$, hence
$c_\mu/b_\lambda^{N}=(1/b_\lambda)^{N}\cdot c_\mu$ lies in the subring
generated by $A_\lambda$ and the quotients $t_{\lambda,\bullet}/b_\lambda$.
Therefore $B_{b_\lambda}$ is generated as a ring by the image of $A_\lambda$
together with the quotients $t_{\lambda,\bullet}/b_\lambda$.

*Step 3: the morphism.* Let
$n=\Lambda\sqcup\coprod_{\lambda\in\Lambda}M_\lambda^{+}$, a finite set, and
let $s\colon n\to B$ be the family given by $s_\lambda=b_\lambda$ for
$\lambda\in\Lambda$ and $s_{(\lambda,\mu)}=t_{\lambda,\mu}$. The
$D(b_\lambda)$ cover $V$, so the $s_i$ generate the unit ideal of $B$, and
therefore they define a morphism $j\colon V\to\mathbf P^n_S$ over $S$ with
$j^{-1}\bigl(D_+(T_i)\bigr)=D(s_i)$.

*Step 4: $j$ is an immersion.* The opens $D_+(T_{\lambda})$ for
$\lambda\in\Lambda$ have preimages $D(b_\lambda)$, which cover $V$; hence the
image of $j$ is contained in $U=\bigcup_{\lambda\in\Lambda}D_+(T_\lambda)$.
Being an immersion is local on the target, so it suffices to show that the
restriction of $j$ over each $D_+(T_\lambda)$ is an immersion. On the standard
chart $D_+(T_\lambda)\cong\mathbf A^{\,n\setminus\{\lambda\}}_S$ this
restriction is the morphism

$$
D(b_\lambda)\longrightarrow\mathbf A^{\,n\setminus\{\lambda\}}_S,
\qquad Y_i\longmapsto s_i/b_\lambda .
$$

Since $D(b_\lambda)\subseteq g^{-1}(W_\lambda)$, it factors through the open
subscheme $\mathbf A^{\,n\setminus\{\lambda\}}_{W_\lambda}$, and the resulting
morphism
$D(b_\lambda)\to\mathbf A^{\,n\setminus\{\lambda\}}_{W_\lambda} =\Spec A_\lambda[Y_i]$ is $\Spec$ of the $A_\lambda$-algebra map
$Y_i\mapsto s_i/b_\lambda$. That map is surjective by Step 2, because its
image already contains the quotients $t_{\lambda,\bullet}/b_\lambda$. Hence
$D(b_\lambda)\to\mathbf A^{\,n\setminus\{\lambda\}}_{W_\lambda}$ is a closed
immersion, and composing with the open immersion
$\mathbf A^{\,n\setminus\{\lambda\}}_{W_\lambda}\to \mathbf A^{\,n\setminus\{\lambda\}}_S$ shows that the restriction of $j$ over
$D_+(T_\lambda)$ is an immersion.

## Detailed form

Let $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be affine and let $U$ be an affine scheme of
finite type over $Y$, say $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ generated as an
$A$-algebra by $b_1,\dots,b_m$. Then the $A$-algebra surjection
$A[x_1,\dots,x_m]\twoheadrightarrow B$, $x_j\mapsto b_j$, defines a closed
immersion

$$
 U\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^m_Y,
$$

and composing with the open immersion $\mathbf A^m_Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf
P^m_Y$ (where $\mathbf A^m_Y=D_+(x_0)\subseteq\mathbf P^m_Y$) gives an
immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^m_Y$.

## Proof

The surjection $A[x_1,\dots,x_m]\twoheadrightarrow B$ is a surjective ring
homomorphism between the coordinate rings of affine schemes, so it induces a
closed immersion of affine schemes (on affines, closed immersions are exactly
those induced by surjective ring homomorphisms). The composite with the open
immersion $\mathbf A^m_Y=D_+(x_0)\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^m_Y$ is an
immersion, since a composite of an open and a closed immersion is an
immersion.

attrs.title: An affine scheme of finite type immerses into projective space

objects.body:
Let $X$ be a quasi-separated scheme, let $Z_1,\dots,Z_n$ be pairwise distinct
irreducible components of $X$ with generic points $\eta_i$, and let $x\in X$.
Then there is an affine open $U\subseteq X$ containing $x$ and all the
$\eta_i$.

## Proof

After renumbering we may assume $x\in Z_i$ for $i\leq r$ and $x\notin Z_k$ for
$k>r$. Then $\bigcap_{k>r}(X\setminus Z_k)$ is an open neighbourhood of $x$,
so there is an affine open $W$ with
$x\in W\subseteq\bigcap_{k>r}(X\setminus Z_k)$; thus $W\cap Z_k=\emptyset$ for
$k>r$. For $i\leq r$ the set $W\cap Z_i$ is a nonempty open subset of the
irreducible space $Z_i$, hence contains its generic point, so $\eta_i\in W$.

By [lem-chow-disjoint-affines] applied to $Z_{r+1},\dots,Z_n$ there are
pairwise disjoint affine opens $U_k\ni\eta_k$ for $k>r$. Fix $k>r$. Since $X$
is quasi-separated, $W\cap U_k$ is a quasi-compact open of $U_k$, and it does
not contain $\eta_k$ because $\eta_k\in Z_k$ while $W\cap Z_k=\emptyset$. As
in the proof of [lem-chow-disjoint-affines], $\eta_k$ is a minimal prime
of the affine scheme $U_k$, so 00EV provides a standard affine
open $U_k'\subseteq U_k$ with $\eta_k\in U_k'$ and $U_k'\cap W=\emptyset$.

The opens $W$ and $U_k'$ for $k>r$ are pairwise disjoint and affine, so

$$
U:=W\cup\bigcup_{k>r}U_k'
$$

is affine by 01I5, and it contains $x$ and all the $\eta_i$.

## Detailed form

Let $X$ be quasi-separated, let $Z_1,\dots,Z_n$ be pairwise distinct
irreducible components of $X$ with generic points $\eta_i$, and let $x\in X$.
Then there is an affine open $U\subseteq X$ containing $x$ and all the
$\eta_i$.
(Stacks Project, Properties, Tag
[01ZX](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01ZX) = Lemma 28.30.4.)

## Proof

After renumbering, let $x\in Z_i$ precisely for $i\leq r$, so that $x\notin
Z_k$ for $k>r$.

*Step 1: an affine open $W$ around $x$ avoiding the components not through
$x$.* For $k>r$, the complement $X\setminus Z_k$ is an open neighbourhood of
$x$, hence so is the finite intersection $O:=\bigcap_{k>r}(X\setminus Z_k)$.
Since the affine open subschemes form a basis of the topology, we may choose
an affine open $W$ with $x\in W\subseteq O$; then $W\cap Z_k=\emptyset$ for
$k>r$.

*Step 2: the generic points $\eta_i$, $i\leq r$, lie in $W$.* For $i\leq r$
the intersection $W\cap Z_i$ is nonempty (it contains $x$) and is an open
subset of the irreducible space $Z_i$; every nonempty open subset of an
irreducible space contains its generic point, so $\eta_i\in W\cap Z_i\subseteq
W$.

*Step 3: disjoint affine opens around $\eta_{r+1},\dots,\eta_n$.* Apply
[lem-chow-disjoint-affines] to the components
$Z_{r+1},\dots,Z_n$: for every $k>r$ there is an affine open $V_k\ni\eta_k$
with $V_k\cap Z_l=\emptyset$ for $l>r,\ l\neq k$, and the $V_k$ are pairwise
disjoint.

*Step 4: shrinking the $V_k$ away from $W$.* Let $k>r$. Quasi-separatedness of
$X$ means that the diagonal $X\to X\times_{\mathbf Z}X$ is quasi-compact; the
open $W\cap V_k$ is the base change of the diagonal along $W\times_{\mathbf
Z}V_k\to X\times_{\mathbf Z}X$, so $W\cap V_k\to W\times_{\mathbf Z}V_k$ is
quasi-compact, and the target is affine, whence $W\cap V_k$ is quasi-compact.
Writing $V_k=\operatorname{Spec}R_k$, the point $\eta_k$ corresponds to a
minimal prime $\mathfrak p_k$ of $R_k$: indeed $Z_k\cap V_k$ is an irreducible
component of $V_k$ (otherwise its closure in $X$ would contain a closed
irreducible subset strictly larger than $Z_k$), and it is the closure of
$\{\eta_k\}$, so $\mathfrak p_k$ is a minimal prime. By Algebra, Lemma 10.26.4
(Stacks Project, Tag [00EV](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00EV)),
applied to $R:=R_k$, the minimal prime $\mathfrak p_k$, and the quasi-compact
open $W\cap V_k\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}R_k$ which does not contain
$\mathfrak p_k$ (as $W\cap Z_k=\emptyset$), there is $f_k\in
R_k\setminus\mathfrak p_k$ with $D(f_k)\cap(W\cap V_k)=\emptyset$. Put
$V_k':=D(f_k)\subseteq V_k$: this is an affine open containing $\eta_k$ and
disjoint from $W$.

*Step 5: the union.* The opens $W$ and $V_k'$ ($k>r$) are pairwise disjoint
and each is affine, so their union

$$
 U:=W\cup\bigcup_{k>r}V_k'
$$

is affine: by Schemes, Lemma 26.6.8 (Tag
[01I5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01I5)) a disjoint union of two
affine opens is affine, and we iterate. It contains $x$ and all
$\eta_1,\dots,\eta_n$, as required.

attrs.title: An affine open containing a point and all generic points

objects.body:
Let $T$ and $Y$ be schemes over $S$ with $Y\to S$ separated, let
$a,b\colon T\to Y$ be morphisms of $S$-schemes and let $V\subseteq T$ be a
scheme-theoretically dense open subscheme with $a|_V=b|_V$. Then $a=b$.

## Proof

This is 01RH. Concretely, the equaliser of $a$ and $b$ is the
base change of the diagonal $Y\to Y\times_S Y$ along
$(a,b)\colon T\to Y\times_S Y$, hence a closed subscheme of $T$ because
$Y\to S$ is separated; it contains $V$, which is scheme-theoretically dense, so
it is all of $T$.

## Detailed form

Let $Z$ be a scheme, $U\subseteq Z$ a scheme-theoretically dense
([def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image]) open subscheme, and $f,g:Z\to
X$ two morphisms into a separated scheme $X$ with $f|_U=g|_U$. Then $f=g$.

## Proof

The equalizer $E$ of $f$ and $g$ is the inverse image of the diagonal of $X$
under $(f,g):Z\to X\times X$; as $X$ is separated, the diagonal is a closed
immersion, and closed immersions are stable under base change, so $E\subseteq
Z$ is a closed subscheme. It contains $U$, which is scheme-theoretically dense
in $Z$ by [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image]; hence $E=Z$, i.e.
$f=g$. (This is Stacks Project, Morphisms, Lemma 29.7.10, Tag
[01RH](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01RH).)

attrs.title: Two morphisms agreeing on a scheme-theoretically dense open

objects.body:
Let $S$ be a scheme and let $j\colon V\to\mathbf P^n_S$ be a quasi-compact
immersion. Let $Z\subseteq\mathbf P^n_S$ be the scheme-theoretic image of $j$.
Then $Z$ is a closed subscheme of $\mathbf P^n_S$, the induced morphism
$V\to Z$ is an open immersion identifying $V$ with a scheme-theoretically dense
open subscheme of $Z$, and $Z\to S$ is proper.

The formalisation packages this data as a structure
`ProperClosedModel`, in the case in which it is used below: $S$ is
noetherian and $g\colon V\to S$ is locally of finite type with $V$ affine, so
that $j$ is supplied by [lem-chow-affine-immersion] and is automatically
quasi-compact because $V$ is then noetherian.

## Proof

The first two assertions are 01RG applied to the quasi-compact
immersion $j$. For the last one, $\mathbf P^n_S\to S$ is proper by
01WC, a closed immersion is proper by 01W5, and
a composition of proper morphisms is proper; hence $Z\to S$ is proper.

## Detailed form

Let $Y$ be affine and let $j:U\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_Y$ be an immersion of
a quasi-compact scheme $U$. Let $Z\subseteq\mathbf P^n_Y$ be the
scheme-theoretic closure of the image of $j$, in the sense of
[def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image]. Then $j$ factors as

$$
 U\hookrightarrow Z\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_Y,
$$

where $U\hookrightarrow Z$ is a scheme-theoretically dense open immersion and
$Z\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_Y$ is the closed immersion; in particular $Z\to
Y$ is proper, as the composite of the closed immersion
$Z\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_Y$ with the proper $\mathbf P^n_Y\to Y$.

## Proof

By [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image], $Z$ is the largest closed
subscheme of $\mathbf P^n_Y$ through which $j$ factors, so the factorization
into the closed immersion $Z\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_Y$ and the induced
morphism $U\to Z$ exists. The latter is an open immersion with $U$
scheme-theoretically dense in $Z$: this is exactly Stacks Project, Morphisms,
Lemma 29.7.7 (Tag [01RG](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01RG)), applied
to the immersion $j$ (which is quasi-compact because $U$ is quasi-compact),
whose conclusion is that the scheme-theoretic image $Z$ of an immersion
contains $U$ as a scheme-theoretically dense open subscheme (and
topologically dense). Finally: a closed immersion is proper; the
projective-space morphism is proper (Stacks Project, Morphisms, Lemma 29.44.5,
Tag [01WC](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01WC), applied to $\mathbf
P^n_Y\to Y$); composites of proper morphisms are proper. Hence $Z\to Y$ is the
composite of two proper morphisms, hence proper.

attrs.title: Closed model of a quasi-compact immersion

objects.body:
Let $X$ be a quasi-separated scheme, let $Z_1,\dots,Z_n$ be pairwise distinct
irreducible components of $X$ and let $\eta_i\in Z_i$ be their generic points.
Then there are affine opens $U_i\subseteq X$ with $\eta_i\in U_i$ and
$U_i\cap U_j=\emptyset$ for $i\neq j$. Consequently
$U_1\cup\dots\cup U_n$ is an affine open containing all the $\eta_i$.

## Proof

For $k\neq i$ we have $\eta_i\notin Z_k$: otherwise
$Z_i=\overline{\{\eta_i\}}\subseteq Z_k$, contradicting that $Z_i$ and $Z_k$
are distinct irreducible components. Hence
$\bigcap_{k\neq i}(X\setminus Z_k)$ is an open neighbourhood of $\eta_i$, and
since the affine opens form a basis of the topology we may choose an affine
open $V_i$ with

$$
\eta_i\in V_i\subseteq\bigcap_{k\neq i}(X\setminus Z_k).
$$

In particular $V_i\cap Z_k=\emptyset$, and a fortiori $\eta_k\notin V_i$, for
all $k\neq i$.

Fix $i$ and put $W_i:=\bigcup_{j\neq i}(V_i\cap V_j)$. Each $V_i\cap V_j$ is
quasi-compact because $X$ is quasi-separated, so $W_i$ is a quasi-compact open
subset of $V_i$, and $\eta_i\notin W_i$ because $\eta_i\notin V_j$ for
$j\neq i$. Write $V_i=\Spec R_i$. The irreducible components of the open
subscheme $V_i$ are the nonempty intersections $C\cap V_i$ with $C$ an
irreducible component of $X$, so $Z_i\cap V_i$ is an irreducible component of
$V_i$ with generic point $\eta_i$; equivalently $\eta_i$ corresponds to a
minimal prime $\mathfrak p_i\subseteq R_i$. By 00EV applied to
$R_i$, the minimal prime $\mathfrak p_i$ and the quasi-compact open
$W_i\subseteq\Spec R_i$, there is $f_i\in R_i\setminus\mathfrak p_i$ with
$D(f_i)\cap W_i=\emptyset$. Put $U_i:=D(f_i)$. Then $U_i$ is an affine open
containing $\eta_i$, and for $j\neq i$ we have
$U_i\cap V_j\subseteq V_i\cap V_j\subseteq W_i$, whence
$U_i\cap V_j=\emptyset$ and in particular $U_i\cap U_j=\emptyset$.

Finally, a scheme that is the disjoint union of two affine opens is affine by
01I5; iterating, $U_1\cup\dots\cup U_n$ is affine.

## Detailed form

Let $X$ be quasi-separated, let $Z_1,\dots,Z_n$ be pairwise distinct
irreducible components of $X$, and let $\eta_i\in Z_i$ be their generic
points. Then for every $i$ there is an affine open $V_i\subseteq X$ containing
$\eta_i$ such that $V_i\cap Z_k=\emptyset$ for $k\neq i$; in particular the
$V_i$ are pairwise disjoint.
(Stacks Project, Properties, Tag
[01ZV](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01ZV) = Lemma 28.30.1.)

## Proof

For $k\neq i$ the point $\eta_i$ does not lie in the closed set $Z_k$, since
the $Z_l$ are pairwise distinct irreducible components and $\eta_i\in Z_i$;
hence $X\setminus Z_k$ is an open neighbourhood of $\eta_i$, as is the finite
intersection

$$
 W_i:=\bigcap_{k\neq i}(X\setminus Z_k),
$$

which satisfies $W_i\cap Z_k=\emptyset$ for all $k\neq i$. The affine open
subschemes of a scheme form a basis for its topology (every scheme is locally
$\operatorname{Spec}$ of a ring, in which the distinguished opens form a
basis), so there is an affine open $V_i$ with $\eta_i\in V_i\subseteq W_i$;
this gives $V_i\cap Z_k=\emptyset$ for $k\neq i$. For $i\neq j$ the open set
$V_i$ avoids $Z_j$, whereas $V_j\ni\eta_j\in Z_j$, so $V_i\cap V_j=\emptyset$,
i.e. the $V_i$ are pairwise disjoint.

attrs.title: Disjoint affine neighbourhoods of generic points

objects.body:
In the situation of [lem-chow-graph] put $V_i:=p_i^{-1}(U_i)$ and
$X':=V_1\cup\dots\cup V_m$, an open subscheme of $Z$. Then the morphisms
$p_i|_{V_i}\colon V_i\to U_i\subseteq X$ glue to a morphism of $S$-schemes

$$
\pi\colon X'\longrightarrow X
$$

with $\pi|_{V_i}=p_i|_{V_i}$, and $\pi|_U=\mathrm{id}_U$.

In the formalisation $V_i$ is the preimage under $p_i$ of the image of $U_i$ in
$Z_i$, and $V_i$, $U$ and $X'$ are all opens of $Z$; the last assertion reads
that the composition of the open immersion $U\to X'$ with $\pi$ is the inclusion
$U\to X$.

## Proof

By [lem-chow-graph](3) we have $U\subseteq V_i$ for every $i$, and
$p_i|_U\colon U\to U_i\subseteq X$ is the inclusion. Since $U$ is
scheme-theoretically dense in $Z$ and $V_i\cap V_j\subseteq Z$ is open, $U$ is
scheme-theoretically dense in $V_i\cap V_j$. The two morphisms
$p_i|_{V_i\cap V_j}$ and $p_j|_{V_i\cap V_j}$ into $X$ agree on $U$, and
$X\to S$ is separated, so they are equal by
[lem-chow-agree-on-dense-open]. Hence the $p_i|_{V_i}$ glue to
$\pi\colon X'\to X$, and $\pi|_U=\mathrm{id}_U$.

## Detailed form

In the situation of [lem-chow-graph], put

$$
 V_i:=p_i^{-1}(U_i)\subseteq\widetilde X
$$

and $X':=V_1\cup\dots\cup V_m$. Then for all $i,j$, $U\subseteq V_i\cap V_j$
is scheme-theoretically dense, and the morphisms $p_i|_{V_i}:V_i\to U_i$ glue
to a morphism

$$
 \pi:X'\longrightarrow X
$$

over $Y$. (Here $X$ is identified with the separated scheme in which the
affine opens $U_i\subseteq X$ sit; $X$ is separated over $Y$ since $X\to Y$ is
proper.) One has $\pi|_U=\operatorname{id}_U$.

## Proof

Since $U\subseteq\widetilde X$ is scheme-theoretically dense by
[lem-chow-graph] (i), and $V_i\cap V_j$ is an open
subscheme of $\widetilde X$, the open $U\subseteq V_i\cap V_j$ is
scheme-theoretically dense in $V_i\cap V_j$ (restriction of density to opens).
The two morphisms $p_i|_{V_i\cap V_j}$ and $p_j|_{V_i\cap V_j}$ take values in
$U_i\cap U_j\subseteq X$ and agree on $U$; by
[lem-chow-agree-on-dense-open] (whose hypotheses hold: $X$ is
separated over $Y$ because it is proper over $Y$), they agree. Hence the
morphisms $p_i|_{V_i}$ are compatible on overlaps and glue to a morphism
$\pi:X'\to X$ (gluing of schemes coincides with gluing of morphisms), and to
see $\pi|_U=\operatorname{id}_U$: each $p_i|_{V_i}$ restricts on $U\subseteq
V_i$ to the identity on $U$ (the open immersion $U\hookrightarrow U_i$ and the
composite $U\hookrightarrow\widetilde X\hookrightarrow Z_i$ are the same
morphism by construction of the diagonal morphism $j$ in
[lem-chow-graph]).

Let $S$ be noetherian, let $X\to S$ be separated of finite type and let
$X=U_1\cup\dots\cup U_m$ be a finite affine open covering such that
$U:=U_1\cap\dots\cap U_m$ is scheme-theoretically dense in $X$. Choose, by
[lem-chow-affine-immersion], immersions
$j_i\colon U_i\to\mathbf P^{n_i}_S$ and, by [lem-chow-closed-model],
closed subschemes $Z_i\subseteq\mathbf P^{n_i}_S$ with $U_i\to Z_i$ a
scheme-theoretically dense open immersion and $Z_i\to S$ proper. Let
$Z\subseteq\mathbf P^{n_1}_S\times_S\dots\times_S\mathbf P^{n_m}_S$ be the
scheme-theoretic image of

$$
j=(j_1|_U,\dots,j_m|_U)\colon U
\longrightarrow\mathbf P^{n_1}_S\times_S\dots\times_S\mathbf P^{n_m}_S .
$$

Then:

1. $Z\to\mathbf P^{n_1}_S\times_S\dots\times_S\mathbf P^{n_m}_S$ is a
closed immersion, $j$ induces an open immersion $U\to Z$ identifying $U$ with
a scheme-theoretically dense open subscheme of $Z$, and $Z\to S$ is proper;
1. for every $i$ the projection $\mathrm{pr}_i|_Z\colon Z\to\mathbf P^{n_i}_S$ factors through $Z_i$, and the induced morphism
$p_i\colon Z\to Z_i$ is proper;
1. $p_i|_U$ is the open immersion $U\to U_i\to Z_i$; in particular
$U\subseteq p_i^{-1}(U_i)$.

The formalisation takes the $m$-fold fibre product
$\mathbf P^{n_1}_S\times_S\dots\times_S\mathbf P^{n_m}_S$ to be the categorical
product in the category of $S$-schemes, so that (1) is a closed immersion into
that product rather than into a single projective space; the composition with
the Segre embedding of [lem-chow-segre], giving a closed immersion
$Z\to\mathbf P^N_S$ over $S$ as used in Step 7 of the proof of
[thm-chow-lemma], is the separate statement
`ChowGraph.exists_isClosedImmersion_over` listed above. It also
weakens the hypotheses to what the proof uses:
the members of the cover need not be affine and need not cover $X$, only $X$
needs to be a noetherian space, and $U$ need not be dense in $X$.

## Proof

Each $j_i|_U$ is an immersion, being the composition of the open immersion
$U\to U_i$ with the immersion $j_i$. Hence $j$ is an immersion by
[lem-chow-tuple-immersion], and it is quasi-compact because $U$ is
noetherian. Part (1) now follows from 01RG for the first two
assertions; for the third, $\mathbf P^{n_1}_S\times_S\dots\times_S \mathbf P^{n_m}_S\to S$ is proper, being a finite fibre product of proper
$S$-schemes, and $Z$ is a closed subscheme of it, so $Z\to S$ is proper by
01W5.

For (2), the open immersion $U\to Z$ is quasi-compact and scheme-theoretically
dominant, so $\mathrm{pr}_i|_Z\colon Z\to\mathbf P^{n_i}_S$ and its restriction
$\mathrm{pr}_i\circ j=j_i|_U$ to $U$ have the same kernel. That kernel
contains the ideal sheaf of $Z_i$, because $j_i|_U$ factors through $Z_i$ by
construction; so the universal property of the closed immersion
$Z_i\to\mathbf P^{n_i}_S$ produces the morphism $p_i\colon Z\to Z_i$ with
$p_i$ followed by $Z_i\to\mathbf P^{n_i}_S$ equal to $\mathrm{pr}_i|_Z$. (This
is 01R9 in the case in which $Z_i$ is presented as the
scheme-theoretic image of $j_i|_U$, which it is: formation of the
scheme-theoretic image commutes with restriction to the open $U_i\subseteq X$.)
It is proper: $Z\to S$ is proper by (1) and $Z_i\to S$ is separated, so $p_i$
is proper by 01W6.

Part (3) is immediate from $\mathrm{pr}_i\circ j=j_i|_U$ and the fact that
$j_i$ identifies $U_i$ with an open subscheme of $Z_i$.

## Detailed form

Let $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be affine, let $X\to Y$ be of finite type, and
let $X=U_1\cup\dots\cup U_m$ be the affine open cover of
[lemma-nagata-dense-affine-cover-exists], with its dense open $U:=\bigcap_iU_i$.
Applying [lem-chow-scheme-theoretic-closure] (which keeps $X$ proper
if it was, and keeps each $U_i$ affine and of finite type over $Y$), we assume
from now on that $U$ is scheme-theoretically dense in $X$. For each $i$, let
$U_i\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^{n_i}_Y$ be the immersion of
[lem-chow-affine-immersion], and let
$Z_i\subseteq\mathbf P^{n_i}_Y$ be the closed model of
[lem-chow-closed-model], so that $U_i\hookrightarrow Z_i$ is a
scheme-theoretically dense open immersion. Put

$$
 Z:=\prod_{i=1}^mZ_i,
$$

and let $\widetilde X\subseteq Z$ be the scheme-theoretic image
([def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image]) of the diagonal morphism

$$
 j=(j_1|_U,\dots,j_m|_U):U\longrightarrow Z.
$$

Then:

- (i) $U\hookrightarrow\widetilde X$ is a scheme-theoretically dense open
  immersion, and $\widetilde X\to Y$ is proper;
- (ii) the projections $\mathrm{pr}_i|_{\widetilde X}:\widetilde
  X\to\mathbf P^{n_i}_Y$ factor through $Z_i$, i.e. there are morphisms
  $p_i:\widetilde X\to Z_i$ with
  $p_i=(\mathrm{pr}_i|_{\widetilde X}\text{ co-restricted})$, and each $p_i$
  is proper;
- (iii) the composite

  $$
   \widetilde X\hookrightarrow Z\hookrightarrow\prod_{i=1}^m\mathbf P^{n_i}_Y
   \xrightarrow{\ s\ }\mathbf P^N_Y,\qquad N=\prod_{i=1}^m(n_i+1)-1,
  $$

  of the closed immersion $\widetilde X\hookrightarrow Z$, the product of the
  closed immersions $Z_i\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^{n_i}_Y$, and the Segre
  embedding ([def-chow-segre],
  [lem-chow-segre]) is a closed immersion.

## Proof

*The reduction step is legitimate.* By
[lem-chow-scheme-theoretic-closure], $X^{*}\to X$ is a surjective
closed immersion and $U\subseteq X^{*}$ is scheme-theoretically dense;
$\pi:X^{*}\to X$ is proper whenever $X\to Y$ is (a closed immersion followed
by a proper morphism is proper), so conclusions about properness pass from
$X^{*}$ to $X$, and the $U_i^{*}=X^{*}\cap U_i$ are affine, of finite type
over $Y$, with $U=\bigcap_iU_i^{*}$. Hence we may replace $X$ by $X^{*}$ and
$U_i$ by $U_i^{*}$.

*$j$ is an immersion.* By [lem-chow-affine-immersion] each
$j_i|_U$ factors as the closed immersion $U\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^{n_i}_Y$
followed by the open immersion $\mathbf A^{n_i}_Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf
P^{n_i}_Y$. The induced morphism $U\to\prod_i\mathbf A^{n_i}_Y$ is a closed
immersion: the target is affine with coordinate ring the tensor product over
$A$ of the coordinate rings of the $\mathbf A^{n_i}_Y$, and each of the
coordinate ring maps onto $B=\mathcal O_U(U)$ is surjective, hence so is the
tensor product map. Composing with the open immersion $\prod_i\mathbf
A^{n_i}_Y\hookrightarrow\prod_i\mathbf P^{n_i}_Y$ and using that
$\prod_iZ_i\subseteq\prod_i\mathbf P^{n_i}_Y$ is closed, we get that $j:U\to
Z$ is an immersion.

*Proof of (i).* Stacks Project, Morphisms, Lemma 29.7.7 (Tag
[01RG](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01RG)) applied to the
quasi-compact immersion $j$ (its source $U$ is quasi-compact) shows that the
scheme-theoretic image $\widetilde X$ of $j$ contains $U$ as a
scheme-theoretically dense open subscheme. For properness: each $Z_i\to Y$ is
proper by [lem-chow-closed-model]; $Z=\prod_iZ_i$ is closed in
$\prod_i\mathbf P^{n_i}_Y$ (a product of closed immersions is a closed
immersion), and $\prod_i\mathbf P^{n_i}_Y$ is proper over $Y$ by
[lem-chow-segre] and
[def-chow-segre] (its structure morphism is the composite
of the closed Segre immersion $\prod_i\mathbf P^{n_i}_Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf
P^N_Y$ with the proper $\mathbf P^N_Y\to Y$); hence $Z\to Y$ is proper, and
the closed subscheme $\widetilde X\subseteq Z$ is proper over $Y$ too
(`closed subscheme` means the composite of the closed immersion with the
proper morphism is proper).

*Proof of (ii).* The morphism $\mathrm{pr}_i\circ j$ equals $j_i|_U:\ U\to
Z_i\subseteq\mathbf P^{n_i}_Y$, i.e. it factors through the closed subscheme
$Z_i$; by the universal property of the scheme-theoretic image
([def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image]; equivalently Stacks Project,
Morphisms, Lemma 29.6.6, Tag
[01R9](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01R9)), the induced morphism
$\mathrm{pr}_i|_{\widetilde X}:\widetilde X\to\mathbf P^{n_i}_Y$ thus factors
through $Z_i$, giving $p_i$. The morphism $p_i$ is proper by Stacks Project,
Morphisms, Lemma 29.42.7 (Tag
[01W6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01W6)): $\widetilde X\to Y$ is
proper by (i), the target $Z_i$ is separated over $Y$ (it is a closed
subscheme of the projective $Y$-scheme $\mathbf P^{n_i}_Y$, which is separated
over $Y$), and a morphism from a $Y$-proper scheme to a $Y$-separated scheme
is proper.

*Proof of (iii).* $\widetilde X\hookrightarrow Z$ is a closed immersion by the
definition of the scheme-theoretic image
([def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image]); the product of the closed
immersions $Z_i\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^{n_i}_Y$ is a closed immersion; and
$s$ is a closed immersion by [lem-chow-segre].
Compositions of closed immersions are closed immersions, which proves (iii).

In the situation of [lem-chow-glue] one has $\pi^{-1}(U_i)=V_i$ for every
$i$. Consequently $\pi^{-1}(U_i)\to U_i$ is the proper morphism
$p_i|_{V_i}$.

## Proof

The inclusion $V_i\subseteq\pi^{-1}(U_i)$ holds because $\pi|_{V_i}=p_i|_{V_i}$
takes values in $U_i$. The morphism $p_i|_{V_i}\colon V_i\to U_i$ is proper,
being the base change of the proper morphism $p_i$ along the open immersion
$U_i\to Z_i$. The open subscheme $\pi^{-1}(U_i)\subseteq Z$ is separated over
$S$, hence $\pi^{-1}(U_i)\to U_i$ is separated. Applying 01W6
to the commutative triangle formed by $V_i\to\pi^{-1}(U_i)$ and the two
morphisms to $U_i$, we conclude that $V_i\to\pi^{-1}(U_i)$ is universally
closed; in particular $V_i$ is closed in $\pi^{-1}(U_i)$. On the other hand
$U\subseteq V_i$ and $U$ is dense in the open subscheme
$\pi^{-1}(U_i)\subseteq Z$, so $V_i$ is dense in $\pi^{-1}(U_i)$. Being closed
and dense, $V_i=\pi^{-1}(U_i)$.

## Detailed form

In the situation of [lem-chow-glue],

$$
 \pi^{-1}(U_i)=V_i
$$

for every $i$; consequently the restriction $\pi^{-1}(U_i)\to U_i$ is the
morphism $p_i|_{V_i}$, which is proper by
[lem-chow-graph] (ii) and the stability of properness
under base change.

## Proof

The inclusion $V_i\subseteq\pi^{-1}(U_i)$ holds because $\pi|_{V_i}=p_i|_{V_i}$
maps $V_i$ into $U_i$ ([lem-chow-glue]).

*Step 1: $\pi$ is separated.* Each $p_i|_{V_i}:V_i\to U_i$ is proper by
[lem-chow-graph] (ii) (its properness is stable under
the base change along the open immersion $U_i\to Z_i$, Stacks Project,
Morphisms, Lemma 29.42.5, Tag
[01W4](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01W4)), hence separated; since
separatedness is local on the source and the $V_i$ cover $X'$, the morphism
$\pi$ is separated. Hence its base change
$\pi^{-1}(U_i)=X'\times_XU_i\to U_i$ along the open immersion $U_i\to X$ is
separated.

*Step 2: $V_i$ is closed in $\pi^{-1}(U_i)$.* Apply Stacks Project,
Morphisms, Lemma 29.42.7 (Tag
[01W6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01W6)) to the diagram whose
composite $V_i\to\pi^{-1}(U_i)\to U_i$ is the proper morphism $p_i|_{V_i}$ and
whose second member $\pi^{-1}(U_i)\to U_i$ is separated: the lemma says that
the morphism $V_i\to\pi^{-1}(U_i)$ is proper, hence closed, so its image
(which is $V_i$ itself) is closed in $\pi^{-1}(U_i)$.

*Step 3: $V_i$ is dense in $\pi^{-1}(U_i)$.* By
[lem-chow-graph] (i), $U$ is scheme-theoretically dense
in $\widetilde X$; since $U\subseteq V_i$ and
$\pi^{-1}(U_i)\subseteq\widetilde X$ is open, the closure of $V_i$ in
$\pi^{-1}(U_i)$ is all of $\pi^{-1}(U_i)$. Steps 2 and 3 give
$V_i=\pi^{-1}(U_i)$.

attrs.title: The preimages of the members of the cover

objects.body:
Let $X$ be a scheme and let $U\subseteq X$ be a dense open subscheme such that
the inclusion $u\colon U\to X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let
$X^{*}\subseteq X$ be the scheme-theoretic image of $u$. Then:

1. $X^{*}\to X$ is a surjective closed immersion which is an isomorphism
over $U$;
1. $U\subseteq X^{*}$ is a scheme-theoretically dense open subscheme;
1. if $X=U_1\cup\dots\cup U_m$ is a finite affine open covering, then the
opens $U_i^{*}:=X^{*}\cap U_i$ are affine, cover $X^{*}$, and satisfy
$U_1^{*}\cap\dots\cap U_m^{*}=U$.

## Proof

By construction $X^{*}\to X$ is a closed immersion, and $U$ factors through it.
Its image is a closed subset containing the dense subset $U$, hence is all of
$X$, so $X^{*}\to X$ is surjective. The quasi-coherent ideal sheaf of $X^{*}$
is $\ker(\mathcal O_X\to u_*\mathcal O_U)$, whose restriction to $U$ is
$\ker(\mathcal O_U\to\mathcal O_U)=0$; hence $X^{*}\cap U=U$ and $X^{*}\to X$
is an isomorphism over $U$. This proves (1). Since formation of the
scheme-theoretic image commutes with restriction to opens, the
scheme-theoretic image of $U\to X^{*}$ is $X^{*}$, which is (2). For (3), each
$U_i^{*}$ is a closed subscheme of the affine scheme $U_i$, hence affine, and
$U_1^{*}\cap\dots\cap U_m^{*}=X^{*}\cap U=U$.

In Lean, $X^{*}$ is `U.ι.image`, the scheme-theoretic image of the
inclusion `U.ι`, and $U_i^{*}$ is the open
`U.ι.imageι ⁻¹ᵁ Uᵢ` of $X^{*}$; the copy of $U$ in $X^{*}$ is
`U.ι.imageι ⁻¹ᵁ U`. Surjectivity comes from the identification of the
underlying set of a scheme-theoretic image with the closure of the set-theoretic image
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.range_imageι`), and being an isomorphism
over $U$ is expressed as `IsIso (U.ι.imageι ∣_ U)`. Only
quasi-compactness of $u$ is used: quasi-separatedness is automatic for an open immersion, and
Mathlib's kernel ideal sheaf theory needs only quasi-compactness.

## Detailed form

Let $X$ be quasi-compact and let $U\subseteq X$ be a dense open subscheme. Let
$X^{*}\subseteq X$ be the scheme-theoretic closure of $U\to X$ in the sense of
[def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image]. Then $X^{*}\to X$ is a
surjective closed immersion, an isomorphism over $U$, and $U$ is
scheme-theoretically dense in $X^{*}$. If moreover $X=U_1\cup\dots\cup U_m$ is
a finite affine open cover and $U_i^{*}:=X^{*}\cap U_i$, then each $U_i^{*}$
is affine and $U_1^{*}\cap\dots\cap U_m^{*}=U$.

## Proof

By [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image], $X^{*}\to X$ is a closed
immersion. Its image is a closed subset containing $U$, whose underlying set
is dense in $X$; hence the image is all of $X$, i.e. $X^{*}\to X$ is
surjective. The ideal sheaf of $X^{*}$ in $X$ is $\ker(\mathcal O_X\to
u_*\mathcal O_U)$ where $u:U\to X$; its restriction to the open $U$ is
$\ker(\mathcal O_U\to\mathcal O_U)=0$, so $X^{*}\cap U=U$: the closed
immersion is an isomorphism over $U$. By definition the scheme-theoretic image
of $U\to X^{*}$ is $X^{*}$, i.e. $U$ is scheme-theoretically dense in $X^{*}$.
Each $U_i^{*}$ is a closed subscheme of the affine scheme $U_i$, and a closed
subscheme of an affine scheme is affine, so $U_i^{*}$ is affine; and

$$
 U_1^{*}\cap\dots\cap U_m^{*}=X^{*}\cap U_1\cap\dots\cap U_m
 =X^{*}\cap U=U,
$$

the last equality because $U\subseteq X^{*}$.

attrs.title: Scheme-theoretic closure of a dense open

objects.body:
The morphism $s$ of [def-chow-segre] is a closed immersion. Consequently,
for index sets $n_1,\dots,n_m$ there are an index set $N$ and a closed
immersion of $S$-schemes

$$
\mathbf P^{n_1}_S\times_S\dots\times_S\mathbf P^{n_m}_S
\longrightarrow\mathbf P^{N}_S ;
$$

one may take $N=n_1\times\dots\times n_m$. Moreover, if all the $n_i$ are
finite, then $\mathbf P^{n_1}_S\times_S\dots\times_S\mathbf P^{n_m}_S\to S$ is
proper.

## Proof

Being a closed immersion is local on the target and on $S$, so we may assume
$S=\Spec A$ is affine and check the assertion on the standard affine charts
$D_+(X_e)\subseteq\mathbf P^N_S$, which cover $\mathbf P^N_S$. For a
multi-index $e$ one has

$$
s^{-1}\bigl(D_+(X_e)\bigr)=\prod_{i=1}^m D_+(x_{i,e_i}),
$$

which is affine, being a finite fibre product of affine schemes over the affine
base. On these charts $s$ is induced by the $A$-algebra homomorphism

$$
\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^N_S}\bigl(D_+(X_e)\bigr)
\longrightarrow
\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^{n_1}_S}\bigl(D_+(x_{1,e_1})\bigr)\otimes_A\dots
\otimes_A\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^{n_m}_S}\bigl(D_+(x_{m,e_m})\bigr),
\qquad
\frac{X_f}{X_e}\longmapsto\prod_{i=1}^m\frac{x_{i,f_i}}{x_{i,e_i}}.
$$

This homomorphism is surjective: for each $i$ and each $0\leq f_i\leq n_i$ the
multi-index $f=(e_1,\dots,e_{i-1},f_i,e_{i+1},\dots,e_m)$ satisfies
$X_f/X_e\mapsto x_{i,f_i}/x_{i,e_i}$, and these ratios generate the target as
an $A$-algebra. Hence $s$ is, locally on the target, the morphism of affine
schemes attached to a surjective ring homomorphism, i.e. a closed immersion.
Compare 01WD. (The argument above is written for a general
$m$; the formalisation carries it out for the binary case $m=2$ over
$\Spec\mathbf Z$, obtains a general base $S$ by base change, and reduces the
general $m$ to the binary case by the induction below.)

The $m$-fold statement follows by induction on the index set of the product.
For the empty product the fibre product is $S$ itself, which is
$\mathbf P^{N}_S$ for a one-element index set $N$; and if
$\mathbf P^{n_2}_S\times_S\dots\times_S\mathbf P^{n_m}_S\to\mathbf P^{N}_S$ is
a closed immersion, then so is

$$
\mathbf P^{n_1}_S\times_S\bigl(\mathbf P^{n_2}_S\times_S\dots\times_S
\mathbf P^{n_m}_S\bigr)
\longrightarrow\mathbf P^{n_1}_S\times_S\mathbf P^{N}_S
\longrightarrow\mathbf P^{n_1\times N}_S,
$$

the first morphism because closed immersions are stable under base change and
the second by the binary case.

The last assertion does not use the Segre embedding: a finite fibre product of
proper $S$-schemes is proper over $S$, because properness is stable under base
change and under composition, and $\mathbf P^{n_i}_S\to S$ is proper by
01WC.

## Detailed form

The Segre embedding of [def-chow-segre] is a closed
immersion.

## Proof

We check the criterion for a closed immersion on the distinguished affine
charts of the target, which cover $\mathbf P^N_Y$. Let $e=(e_1,\dots,e_m)$,
$0\leq e_i\leq n_i$, and let $D_+(X_e)\subseteq\mathbf P^N_Y$ be the
corresponding distinguished chart. Its preimage under $s$ is

$$
 s^{-1}(D_+(X_e))=\prod_{i=1}^m D_+(x_{i,e_i}),
$$

an affine $Y$-scheme: the chart $D_+(x_{i,e_i})$ of $\mathbf P^{n_i}_Y$ is
affine, and a finite product of affine schemes over an affine base is affine.
On these charts, after normalizing $X_e=1$ and $x_{i,e_i}=1$, the morphism $s$
is given by the ring homomorphism of polynomial rings

$$
 \mathcal O_{\mathbf P^N_Y}(D_+(X_e))
 \longrightarrow\bigotimes_{i=1}^m\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^{n_i}_Y}
 \bigl(D_+(x_{i,e_i})\bigr),
 \qquad
 \frac{X_f}{X_e}\longmapsto\prod_{i=1}^m\frac{x_{i,f_i}}{x_{i,e_i}},
$$

which sends the coordinate $\frac{X_f}{X_e}$ to the corresponding monomial.
This map is surjective: for each $i$ and each $0\leq f_i\leq n_i$, the
monomial for the multi-index $f=(e_1,\dots,e_{i-1},f_i,e_{i+1},\dots,e_m)$
equals the single ratio $x_{i,f_i}/x_{i,e_i}$, so the image contains every
generator of the target polynomial ring. Hence $s$ is affine-locally (on the
target) the morphism of affine schemes induced by a surjective ring
homomorphism, i.e. a closed immersion. Since being a closed immersion is local
on the target, $s$ is a closed immersion (cf. Stacks Project, Constructions,
Tag [01WD](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01WD) = Lemma 27.13.6).

## Detailed form

The Segre embedding

$$
\mathbf P^m_S\times_S\mathbf P^n_S\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^{(m+1)(n+1)-1}_S
$$

is a closed immersion (over every base scheme $S$). Consequently
the tensor product $\mathcal O(1)\boxtimes\mathcal O(1)$ of very
ample modules is very ample, and the composite of a closed immersion
into $\mathbf P^N_S\times_S\mathbf P^M_S$ with the Segre embedding is
a closed immersion into a single projective space.
(*Stacks Project, Constructions of Schemes, Lemma 27.13.6,
[Tag 01WD](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01WD).*)

## Proof

This is the recorded classical input of the statement, Stacks Project,
Constructions of Schemes, Lemma 27.13.6, [Tag
01WD](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01WD). The two recorded consequences are immediate from it: very
ampleness is tested after a closed immersion into a projective space, and
the displayed composite of closed immersions is a closed immersion. No
separate proof is given.

attrs.title: The Segre embedding is a closed immersion

objects.body:
Let $S$ be a scheme, let $Y_1,\dots,Y_m$ be schemes over $S$ and let
$f_i\colon T\to Y_i$ be morphisms of $S$-schemes. If some $f_k$ is an
immersion, then

$$
(f_1,\dots,f_m)\colon T\longrightarrow Y_1\times_S\dots\times_S Y_m
$$

is an immersion.

## Proof

Composing $(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ with the projection $\mathrm{pr}_k$ gives back
$f_k$, which is an immersion; hence $(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ is an immersion, because
if a composition $h\circ g$ is an immersion then so is $g$.

(The blueprint originally deduced this from 01KR by factoring
$(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ through $T\times_S Y_2\times_S\dots\times_S Y_m$, which also
requires the $Y_i$ to be separated over $S$. The argument above needs neither.)

attrs.title: Tuples of morphisms with one immersion

objects.body:
For a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ and
$M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, the canonical comparison

$$
b_{i,M}:(Ri_A^!M)\otimes_A^LB
\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri_B^!(M_B)
$$

is an isomorphism. It is the adjoint of

$$
i_*((Ri_A^!M)\otimes_A^LB)
\cong(i_*Ri_A^!M)\otimes_A^LB
\longrightarrow M_B,
$$

where the last map is the tensor product of the closed exceptional
counit. The comparison commutes with the exceptional counit,
composition of closed immersions, and successive coefficient changes.
The analogous assertion holds for a locally closed immersion,
using its factorization into an open and a closed immersion.

## Proof

Let $j$ be the open complement. Tensor the triangle of
[lem-exc-closed-support-triangle] by $B$:

$$
(i_*Ri_A^!M)\otimes_A^LB\longrightarrow M_B
\longrightarrow(Rj_{*,A}j^*M)\otimes_A^LB\longrightarrow.
$$

Closed direct image is exact, commutes with sums, and is extension
by zero on stalks; hence it commutes with derived tensor by the
constant coefficient complex. Open restriction also commutes
with that tensor. The third term is
$Rj_{*,B}j^*(M_B)$ by [lem-coef-finite-direct-image].
The resulting triangle is therefore the closed-support triangle
for $M_B$. Its map on the first term is obtained from the
displayed exceptional counit, so it is $i_*b_{i,M}$.
The full faithfulness of $i_*$, as in
[def-weil-open-closed-recollement], shows that $b_{i,M}$
is an isomorphism.

All the finite-Tor domains used here are justified: the previously
proved finite boundary exchange
[cor-weil-boundary-duality-discharge] and finite biduality
[thm-fix-general-biduality] identify
$Ri_A^!M\cong D_Zi^*D_XM$, so it is finite-Tor constructible.
The assertion on the $B$-side is the same finite theorem.
This use of finite biduality introduces no integral-duality input.
For composition or successive coefficient changes, transpose
both composites to the same composite of exceptional counits.
Their equality proves the required coherence. Open exceptional
inverse image is ordinary restriction, whose coefficient
comparison is reassociation of tensor product. Factoring a
locally closed immersion proves its version with the same
evaluation and counit compatibilities.

attrs.title: Finite coefficient change for closed support

objects.body:
Let $f:T\to X$ be separated of finite type, and let
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$. The canonical projection map is an
isomorphism

$$
c_{f,K}:(Rf_{*,A}K)\otimes_A^LB
\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{*,B}(K_B).
$$

It is natural in $K$, compatible with composition of morphisms
and successive coefficient quotients, and has the same assertion
on finite constructible pro-etale realizations.

## Proof

The bound $R^qf_*M=0$ for all etale $A$-module sheaves and
$q>2\dim T$ is [lem-sf-etale-direct-image-vanishing].
The module $B$ is finite over the Noetherian ring $A$.
Consequently [lem-sf-projection-finite-constant] applies to
this constant module and gives the asserted map as an isomorphism.
Here is the relevant truncation estimate from that proof.
Choose a resolution $P\to B$ by finite free $A$-modules in
nonpositive degrees, and set $P_t=\sigma_{\geq-t}P$.
Its error $C_t=\operatorname{Cone}(P_t\to B)$ lies in
$D^{\leq-t-1}(A)$. If $K\in D^{\leq b}$ and
$N=2\dim T$, then uniform cohomological dimension gives
$Rf_*D^{\leq r}\subseteq D^{\leq r+N}$ on bounded-above
complexes. The two error terms

$$
(Rf_*K)\otimes_A^LC_t,
\qquad Rf_*(K\otimes_A^LC_t)
$$

therefore lie in $D^{\leq b+N-t-1}$. For each fixed degree,
take $t$ large enough; the coefficient comparison for $P_t$
is an isomorphism by finite sums, shifts and cones from $A$,
and the error terms no longer affect that degree. This is an
argument in $D^-$ with a fixed cohomological-dimension bound;
finite length of the resolution of $B$ is not asserted. Both outputs are bounded
constructible of finite Tor amplitude by
[thm-sf-direct-image-tor-amplitude] and by derived scalar
extension. Direct image computed with $B$-module coefficients
has the same underlying $A$-module derived object: the usual
etale sections, acyclic resolutions, or hypercover computation of
sheaf cohomology do not change when the coefficient action is
forgotten. This identifies the projection formula with the
displayed comparison between the two coefficient categories.

The map is the projection transformation defined by tensor
adjunction and the pullback counit. In a successive quotient
$A\to B\to C$, reassociating the threefold tensor product makes
the one-step and two-step maps have the same transpose. The same
argument with the composite pullback counit proves compatibility
with composition of $f$'s. These identities hold before a
free resolution is chosen, hence also after the truncation proof.
Finally [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] and
[lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] transport the objects and
these specified maps to the finite pro-etale categories.

attrs.title: Finite coefficient change for ordinary direct image

objects.body:
Let $a_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and
$\omega_{X,A}=Ra_{X,A}^{\times}A$. There is a canonical
isomorphism

$$
u_{X,A,B}:\omega_{X,A}\otimes_A^LB
\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{X,B}.
$$

It is the adjoint, for $Ra_{X,B!}\dashv Ra_{X,B}^{\times}$, of

$$
Ra_{X,B!}(\omega_{X,A}\otimes_A^LB)
\cong(Ra_{X,A!}\omega_{X,A})\otimes_A^LB
\longrightarrow A\otimes_A^LB=B.
$$

These maps satisfy the quotient cocycle and carry the reduction
of the dualizing counit to the dualizing counit.

## Proof

The object $\omega_{X,A}$ is finite-Tor constructible by
[lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata], applied to $A_X$.
Thus compact-support coefficient comparison
[lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change] constructs the
displayed adjoint map without any coefficient compatibility
assumption on an exceptional right adjoint.

By [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality], the assertion is local
on $X$. Choose an affine open and a closed embedding
$i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^r_k$. Composition of ambient
right adjoints and [cor-amb-affine-space-adjunction] give

$$
\omega_{X,A}=Ri_A^!A(r)[2r],\qquad
\omega_{X,B}=Ri_B^!B(r)[2r].
$$

The Tate rank-one object at $A$ reduces to the one at $B$,
and shifts commute with coefficient tensor. Applying
[lem-coef-finite-closed-shriek] therefore proves the displayed
map is an isomorphism. The local map is the global map defined
above: transposing it under the composite adjunction yields the
closed-immersion counit followed by the affine-space counit,
which is the structure-morphism counit. In particular these
maps agree on overlaps. The same adjoint calculation proves
the quotient cocycle and compatibility with the counit.
The dualizing-object comparison of
[lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison] transports this
canonical map to the finite pro-etale realization.

attrs.title: Finite coefficient change for the dualizing object

objects.body:
For a separated finite-type $f:X\to Y$, on the finite-Tor
constructible categories one has canonically

$$
Rf_n^!L\cong D_{X,n}f^*D_{Y,n}L.
$$

For $m\geq n$, coefficient reduction gives a canonical isomorphism

$$
(Rf_m^!L)\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n
\cong Rf_n^!(L\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n).
$$

These maps satisfy the quotient cocycle and identify the units and
counits under the compact-support coefficient comparison.

## Proof

Finite exceptional preservation is [thm-sf-preservation-class].
The finite anti-equivalences of [thm-fix-general-biduality],
ordinary pullback–direct-image adjunction, and the formal exchange
[fix-cor-verdier-exchange] give natural adjunction bijections

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,D_Xf^*D_YL)
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(f^*D_YL,D_XK)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(D_YL,Rf_*D_XK)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(D_YL,D_YRf_!K)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_!K,L).
\end{aligned}
$$

Here every object is in the finite-Tor constructible domain.
Uniqueness of the right adjoint identifies this functor with the
already constructed $Rf^!$, together with its unit and counit.
The internal-Hom adjunction [fix-lem-tensor-adjunction], followed
by derived global sections, gives the corresponding canonical
isomorphism of derived mapping complexes. This supplies the enriched
adjunction independently of taking degree-zero Hom groups.

Apply the coherent duality comparisons
[cor-coef-finite-verdier] to the two duals in this formula;
coefficient tensor commutes with ordinary pullback. This constructs
the stated coefficient isomorphism and its cocycle. To identify
its adjunction maps, transpose under the displayed bijections.
Every arrow is either evaluation, a tensor associativity map, or
an adjunction counit. The duality comparison preserves evaluation,
and [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change] preserves the
compact-support counit and projection construction. The transposes
are consequently the same compact-support coefficient comparison.
Thus the maps identify the units and counits, before any tower is
reconstructed.

attrs.title: Finite exceptional adjoints and coefficient change

objects.body:
Let $E\subset L$ be a finite extension of coefficient fields,
with ramification index $e$. For every $n\geq1$, put

$$
A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n,\qquad
B=\mathcal O_L/\varpi_E^n\mathcal O_L
=\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^{en}=A_{L,en}.
$$

Equality here is equality of ideals; a unit relating the chosen
uniformizers does not change the quotient. The coefficient ring
$B$ is finite free over $A$. For finite-Tor constructible
complexes the canonical maps give isomorphisms

$$
\begin{aligned}
(Rf_{*,A}K)\otimes_A B&\cong Rf_{*,B}(K\otimes_A B),\\
(Ri_A^!M)\otimes_A B&\cong Ri_B^!(M\otimes_A B),\\
\omega_{X,A}\otimes_A B&\cong\omega_{X,B},\\
R\mathcal Hom_A(K,M)\otimes_A B
&\cong R\mathcal Hom_B(K\otimes_A B,M\otimes_A B),\\
(D_{X,A}K)\otimes_A B&\cong D_{X,B}(K\otimes_A B).
\end{aligned}
$$

They respect evaluation, double-dual maps and the adjunction
counits, are compatible with further finite coefficient-field
extension, and commute with coefficient reduction. Their formation
is natural under scheme isomorphisms, in particular Frobenius.
Thus the levels $en$ give the coefficient comparisons on a
cofinal subsystem of the $\mathcal O_L$-adic tower.

## Proof

The module $\mathcal O_L$ is finite and torsion free over the
DVR $\mathcal O_E$, hence finite free; reducing a free basis
modulo $\varpi_E^n$ proves the assertion about $B/A$.
The ordinary direct-image projection comparison is an isomorphism
for a finite free coefficient module by additivity; this is the
finite-free starting case of [lem-coef-finite-direct-image].
Apply it to the closed-support triangle exactly as in
[lem-coef-finite-closed-shriek]. This proves the closed
exceptional comparison with the same counit-defined map.
The local closed-embedding computation of
[lem-coef-finite-dualizing] then proves the comparison for
$\omega_X$. The Tate twists of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]
commute with coefficient extension: they are the tensor extensions
of the same prime-to-characteristic root-of-unity sheaves, and
the affine-space trace uses their coefficient-linear counit.

For internal Hom one can either repeat the strata argument of
[thm-coef-finite-hom], or use finite freeness directly.
The tensor–Hom adjunction in
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] identifies the
underlying $A$-object of the target with
$R\mathcal Hom_A(K,M\otimes_A B)$.
For a finite free coefficient module, additivity identifies this
with $R\mathcal Hom_A(K,M)\otimes_A B$. The canonical
identification is independent of the temporary choice of a
free basis, since it is the map adjoint to evaluation. Combining
this with the dualizing comparison gives the Verdier comparison
by precisely the construction of [cor-coef-finite-verdier].

For two field extensions, or a quotient followed by extension,
transpose both proposed composite comparisons under the same
adjunction. Both are tensor reassociation followed by the same
evaluation or counit. This proves their equality, as well as
evaluation and double-dual compatibility. The constructions use
only pullback, tensor, evaluation, and natural adjunction maps,
so they are unchanged by transporting along a scheme
isomorphism. Finally the positive multiples $en$ are cofinal
among the positive integers, and
$(\varpi_E^n)\mathcal O_L=(\varpi_L^{en})$. These are exactly
the finite levels needed when reconstructing after scalar extension;
one does not identify equal numerical indices for the two different
uniformizers.

attrs.title: Finite free coefficient extensions and cofinal levels

objects.body:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type, with
$\dim X\leq d$. For $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ with reduction
Tor interval $[a,b]$, the functor defined in
[def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] satisfies

$$
Rf_!K\in D^b_c(Y,R),\qquad
(Rf_!K)\otimes_R^L A_n\cong Rf_{!,n}K_n.
$$

One uniform reduction Tor interval is $[a,b+2d]$. These are the
canonical compact-support coefficient comparisons.

## Proof

The input reductions have a common Tor interval by
[lem-coef-integral-residue-tor]. On a compactification
$f=\bar f j$, replace the compactifying scheme by the
scheme-theoretic closure of $X$. Its dimension is at most
$d$. Extension by zero preserves constructibility and the
Tor interval. The proper direct-image theorem
[thm-sf-direct-image-tor-amplitude], with the bound of
[lem-sf-etale-direct-image-vanishing], therefore gives
$[a,b+2d]$ for $R\bar f_*j_!K_n$.
The finite compact-support site comparison is
[thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale].

The coefficient maps of
[lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change] make these objects
a normalized tower. Apply
[lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity]: its limit has exactly
the stated reductions, with their constructibility and uniform
bound. That limit is the definition in
[def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. Both its
counit comparison and the maps used above are induced by the same
coefficient maps, so the isomorphisms are the specified comparisons.

attrs.title: Integral compact supports have the prescribed reductions

objects.body:
Let $E\subset L$ be finite extensions of $\Ql$, put
$R=\mathcal O_E$, $S=\mathcal O_L$, and write
$T_{S/R}K=S\widehat\otimes_R^LK$. This exact functor preserves
the integral bounded constructible categories. There are canonical
isomorphisms

$$
u_{L/E}:T_{S/R}\omega_{X,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{X,S},
\qquad
v_{K,M}:T_{S/R}R\mathcal Hom_R(K,M)
\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_S(T_{S/R}K,T_{S/R}M),
$$

and consequently

$$
\beta_{L/E,K}:T_{S/R}D_{X,R}K
\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{X,S}(T_{S/R}K)
\qquad(K,M\in D^b_c(X,R)).
$$

They commute with evaluation and with the canonical map
$K\to D_{X,R}D_{X,R}K$. They are compatible with finite
coefficient quotients, the identity extension, and composition of
finite field extensions, including the tensor associators.

## Proof

The $R$-module $S$ is finite free. On completed coefficient
sheaves it is therefore still finite free; its tensor functor is
exact and commutes with derived inverse limits. In particular the
completed tensor of a derived-complete complex is the ordinary
derived tensor with this finite free coefficient sheaf. If $e$
is the ramification index, the ideals
$\varpi_E^nS=\varpi_L^{en}S$ are a cofinal system of powers of
the maximal ideal of $S$. The reductions of $T_{S/R}K$ along
this system are

$$
(S/\varpi_E^nS)\otimes_{R/\varpi_E^n}^LK_n,
\qquad K_n=K\otimes_R^L R/\varpi_E^n.
$$

They are constructible and have a uniform Tor interval, since
[lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] supplies that interval for
$K_n$ and finite free extension preserves it. The normalized
tower reconstruction of [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity]
therefore gives an object of $D^b_c(X,S)$. The intervening
$\varpi_L$-reductions are recovered by derived tensor from
any larger cofinal level, so they have the same Tor bound.

By [prop-coef-integral-dualizing], the reductions of the
integral dualizing objects are the finite dualizing objects.
At the cofinal levels [lem-coef-finite-free-extension] gives
the specified maps

$$
(S/\varpi_E^nS)\otimes_{R/\varpi_E^n}^L\omega_{X,R/\varpi_E^n}
\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{X,S/\varpi_E^nS}.
$$

Their quotient compatibility makes them a map of normalized
derived towers. Taking the derived limit, and using the
finite-free tensor comparison above, gives
