$E_r^{0,n}$; hence $E_\infty^{0,n}\hookrightarrow E_2^{0,n}$. Composing with
$H^n\twoheadrightarrow H^n/F^1H^n=E_\infty^{0,n}$ gives the left edge. These
associated graded identifications are the convergence data of
[def-sp-convergence]. The constructions commute with morphisms of filtered
abutments and of pages, so they are functorial.

attrs.title: Edge maps of the Grothendieck spectral sequence

objects.body:
Every Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] has enough
injectives.
(*Source: the classical input; the sites used in this blueprint are
Grothendieck topoi, cf. Stacks Project, Cohomology on Sites, Section 12.24.*)

## Proof

The assertion is the input recorded in the source note; the blueprint uses it
throughout for injective resolutions in the sheaf categories of the etale and
pro-etale sites; it is not discharged here.

attrs.title: Grothendieck abelian categories have enough injectives

objects.body:
Let $v:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a left exact additive
[def-sp-left-exact-additive] functor between Grothendieck abelian categories
[def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] and let $K\in\operatorname{Ch}^+(\mathcal A)$.
Then:

1. **(Well-definedness.)** Any two K-injective resolutions
[def-sp-kinjective-bridge] $f:K\to I$ and $g:K\to J$ are homotopy equivalent
under $K$, by a homotopy equivalence unique up to homotopy. Hence
$v(I)\cong v(J)$ by a canonical isomorphism in the homotopy category, the
object $RvK$ of [def-sp-kinjective-bridge] is well defined up to canonical
isomorphism, and it is functorial in $K$.

2. **(Agreement on objects.)** A bounded-below complex of injective objects
is K-injective. In particular an injective resolution
[def-sp-injective-resolutions] $X\to I^\bullet$ of an object $X$ is a
K-injective resolution of $X[0]$, and

$$
 \mathcal H^p\bigl(Rv(X[0])\bigr)\cong R^pv(X)
$$

for every $p$, the right-hand side being the derived functor of
[def-sp-left-exact-additive].

3. **(Shift.)** $Rv(K[n])\cong(RvK)[n]$ for every $n\in\mathbb Z$.

**Status.** The source proved the agreement in (2) by saying that a
Cartan--Eilenberg resolution refines both routes, which made this lemma and
the Cartan--Eilenberg theorem [thm-sp-if-e1] depend on each other. Nothing
below uses a Cartan--Eilenberg resolution: (1) and (3) are formal
consequences of K-injectivity, and (2) needs only that an injective
resolution of an object is a bounded-below complex of injectives. The
theorem now cites this lemma and not the other way round.

## Proof

*The comparison principle.* Let $I$ be K-injective and let $s:A\to B$ be a
quasi-isomorphism. Then

$$
 s^*:\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(B,I)\longrightarrow
 \operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(A,I)
$$

is bijective. Indeed, complete $s$ to a distinguished triangle $A\to B\to
C(s)\to A[1]$ in the homotopy category; $C(s)$ is acyclic because $s$ is a
quasi-isomorphism. The functor $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(-,I)$ is
homological, so it turns that triangle into a long exact sequence, and

$$
 \operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(C(s),I[n])
 =\mathcal H^n\bigl(\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(C(s),I)\bigr)=0
$$

for every $n$, since $C(s)$ is acyclic and $I$ is K-injective
[def-sp-kinjective-bridge]. The two outer terms of the long exact sequence
vanish, so $s^*$ is bijective.

*(1).* Apply the principle to the quasi-isomorphism $f:K\to I$ and the
K-injective complex $J$: there is $u:I\to J$, unique up to homotopy, with
$uf\simeq g$. Symmetrically there is $w:J\to I$, unique up to homotopy, with
$wg\simeq f$. Then $(wu)f\simeq wg\simeq f=\operatorname{id}_I\circ f$, and
the principle applied to $f$ and $I$ says that a morphism $I\to I$ is
determined up to homotopy by its composite with $f$; hence
$wu\simeq\operatorname{id}_I$, and symmetrically
$uw\simeq\operatorname{id}_J$. An additive functor carries homotopies to
homotopies, so $v(u)$ and $v(w)$ are mutually inverse in the homotopy
category and give the canonical isomorphism $v(I)\cong v(J)$. Uniqueness up
to homotopy makes the isomorphism independent of the choices and compatible
with composition. The same principle lifts a morphism $K\to K'$ to a morphism
between chosen resolutions, uniquely up to homotopy, which is functoriality of
$RvK$ in $K$.

*(2).* Let $I^\bullet$ be a bounded-below complex of injectives, say $I^n=0$
for $n<n_0$, let $A$ be acyclic and let $\varphi:A\to I^\bullet$ be a chain
map. We build a homotopy $h^n:A^n\to I^{n-1}$ with
$\varphi^n=d\,h^n+h^{n+1}d_A^{\,n}$ by induction on $n$, taking $h^n=0$ for
$n\leq n_0$, which is legitimate because $I^{n-1}=0$ there and $\varphi^n=0$
for $n<n_0$. Assume $h^m$ is built for $m\leq n$ and the identity holds below
$n$, and put $\psi=\varphi^n-d\,h^n:A^n\to I^n$. Then

$$
 \psi\,d_A^{\,n-1}
 =\varphi^nd_A^{\,n-1}-d\,h^nd_A^{\,n-1}
 =d\,\varphi^{n-1}-d\bigl(\varphi^{n-1}-d\,h^{n-1}\bigr)=0 ,
$$

so $\psi$ kills $\operatorname{im}d_A^{\,n-1}$, which is $\ker d_A^{\,n}$
because $A$ is acyclic. Hence $\psi$ factors through
$A^n/\ker d_A^{\,n}\cong\operatorname{im}d_A^{\,n}$, and since $I^n$ is
injective the resulting map $\operatorname{im}d_A^{\,n}\to I^n$ extends along
the monomorphism $\operatorname{im}d_A^{\,n}\hookrightarrow A^{n+1}$ to a map
$h^{n+1}:A^{n+1}\to I^n$ with $h^{n+1}d_A^{\,n}=\psi$, which is the required
identity in degree $n$. So every chain map from an acyclic complex to
$I^\bullet$ is null-homotopic. A shift $I^\bullet[n]$ is again a
bounded-below complex of injectives, so the same holds for it, and therefore
$\mathcal H^n(\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(A,I^\bullet))
=\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(A,I^\bullet[n])=0$ for every $n$: the
complex $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(A,I^\bullet)$ is acyclic and
$I^\bullet$ is K-injective.

An injective resolution $X\to I^\bullet$ of an object is a bounded-below
complex of injectives which is a quasi-isomorphism from $X[0]$
[def-sp-injective-resolutions], so it is a K-injective resolution of $X[0]$.
By part (1) and [def-sp-kinjective-bridge], $Rv(X[0])\cong v(I^\bullet)$, and
$\mathcal H^p(v(I^\bullet))=R^pv(X)$ is the definition of the derived functor
in [def-sp-left-exact-additive].

*(3).* If $I$ is K-injective then so is $I[n]$, because
$\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(A,I[n])$ is $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(A,I)[n]$
and a shift of an acyclic complex is acyclic. So $K[n]\to I[n]$ is a
K-injective resolution of $K[n]$, and $v$, being additive, commutes with the
shift of a complex: $Rv(K[n])=v(I[n])=v(I)[n]=(RvK)[n]$.

Let $\Phi:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a homological functor
[def-sp-homological-functor] with $\mathcal D$ abelian
[def-sp-abelian]. For every distinguished triangle $K_1\to K_2\to K_3\to
K_1[1]$ there is a long exact sequence

$$
 \cdots\to\Phi(K_1)\to\Phi(K_2)\to\Phi(K_3)
 \xrightarrow{\ \delta\ }\Phi(K_1[1])\to\cdots
$$

whose connecting map $\delta$ is natural in the triangle.

## Proof

This is the definition of [def-sp-homological-functor] applied to $F=\Phi$:
the exactness at the middle spots of the two halves of the triangle (the
rotation of a distinguished triangle is distinguished) iterates to the
infinite long exact sequence, and the connecting map is obtained by applying
$\Phi$ to the rotation morphism $K_3\to K_1[1]$ of the triangle.

attrs.title: Long exact sequences of distinguished triangles

objects.body:
Let $\varphi:E\to E'$ be a morphism of spectral sequences
[def-sp-spectral-sequence]. If $\varphi$ is an isomorphism on the
$E_2$-page in every bidegree, then it is an isomorphism on all pages $E_r$,
$2\leq r\leq\infty$.

## Proof

Each $E_{r+1}$ is the homology of the page $E_r$
([def-sp-spectral-sequence]); a morphism of complexes which is a
quasi-isomorphism induces a homology isomorphism, and the page
identifications are compatible with the morphism. Hence the
$E_2$-isomorphism gives the $E_3$-isomorphism, induction gives all $E_r$, and
the intersection and union formulas in [def-sp-convergence] give
$E_\infty\cong E'_\infty$.

Let $u:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be an exact functor between abelian
categories [def-sp-abelian] admitting a right adjoint $u_*:\mathcal
B\to\mathcal A$. Then $u_*$ sends injective
[def-sp-injective-resolutions] objects to injective objects.

## Proof

By [def-sp-injective-resolutions], $I\in\mathcal B$ is injective iff for
every monomorphism $N\hookrightarrow N'$ in $\mathcal B$ the map

$$
 \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(N',I)\longrightarrow
 \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(N,I)
$$

is surjective. By the adjunction

$$
 \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(uM,N)\cong
 \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(M,u_*N),
$$

the injectivity of $u_*I$ is equivalent to the surjectivity of
$\operatorname{Hom}(uM',I)\to\operatorname{Hom}(uM,I)$ for every monomorphism
$M\hookrightarrow M'$ in $\mathcal A$; this holds because $u$ is exact, hence
preserves monomorphisms, and $I$ is injective.

attrs.title: Right adjoints of exact functors preserve injectives

objects.body:
Let $v$ be a left exact additive [def-sp-left-exact-additive] functor, let
$K\in\operatorname{Ch}^+(\mathcal A)$ and let $q\in\mathbb Z$. Then the
derived functor commutes with the shift and the cohomology of a shifted
complex is the shifted cohomology:

$$
 \mathcal H^{p+q}\bigl(Rv(\mathcal H^qK[-q])\bigr)
 =\mathcal H^{p}\bigl(Rv(\mathcal H^qK)\bigr)
 =R^pv(\mathcal H^qK).
$$

## Proof

The derived functor of a left exact additive functor
[def-sp-left-exact-additive] on $\operatorname{Ch}^+$ is the functor applied
to a K-injective resolution, by the definition in
[def-sp-kinjective-bridge]. It commutes with the shift by part (3) of
[lem-sp-kinjective-computes], so the cohomology of the shifted complex is the
shifted cohomology, which is the first displayed identity. The second is the
definition $R^pv=\mathcal H^p\circ Rv$ of [def-sp-kinjective-bridge],
together with part (2) of [lem-sp-kinjective-computes] identifying it, on an
object, with the derived functor of [def-sp-left-exact-additive].

Let $v:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be left exact and additive
[def-sp-left-exact-additive] between Grothendieck abelian categories
[def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], and let $K\in\operatorname{Ch}^+(\mathcal A)$
be bounded below with $\mathcal H^q(K)=0$ for $q<a$. Then the truncation
couple [def-sp-truncation-couple] of $K$, with the structure maps $\alpha$,
$f$, $g$ of bidegrees $(-1,+1)$, $(+2,-1)$, $(0,0)$ of
[def-sp-truncation-couple], is an exact couple [def-sp-exact-couple].

## Proof

Exactness of a couple means the three identities of subobjects of
[def-sp-exact-couple] in every bidegree. Fix $q$ and apply the homological
functor $\mathcal H^{p+q}\circ Rv$ to the distinguished triangle $\tau_{\leq
q-1}K\to\tau_{\leq q}K\to\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]\to$ of
[def-sp-truncation-couple]; by [lem-sp-long-exact-of-triangle] the result is
the long exact sequence

$$
 \cdots\to D^{p+1,q-1}\xrightarrow{\ \alpha\ }D^{p,q}
 \xrightarrow{\ g\ }E^{p,q}\xrightarrow{\ f\ }D^{p+2,q-1}\to\cdots,
$$

where the three maps are the ones recorded in
[def-sp-truncation-couple], and the exactness of this sequence at its three
displayed spots is precisely $\ker\alpha=\operatorname{im}f$,
$\ker f=\operatorname{im}g$ and $\ker g=\operatorname{im}\alpha$ in the
bidegree $(p,q)$. As $q$ and $p$ are arbitrary this is the assertion.

attrs.title: The truncation couple is an exact couple

objects.body:
Let $M$ be an abelian group, $\ell$ a prime, and $\sigma$ an automorphism of $M$
whose fixed subgroup $M^\sigma$ is finite. Then $T_\ell M$ has no $\ell$-power
torsion, $(T_\ell M)^\sigma=0$, and $(V_\ell M)^\sigma=0$ (in the notation of
[def-tate-module-abelian-group]); the same holds for $\sigma^{-1}$.

## Proof

$T_\ell M$ has no $\ell$-torsion:
$\ell t=0$ implies $t_n=\ell t_{n+1}=0$; iteration excludes all
$\ell$-power torsion. Thus its map into the localization is injective.
If $\ell^{-b}t$ is fixed, this injectivity gives $\sigma t=t$.
All $t_n$ lie in the finite group $M^\sigma$, whose $\ell$-primary
subgroup is killed by a uniform $\ell^e$. Compatibility then gives
$t_n=\ell^et_{n+e}=0$. Finally an automorphism and its inverse have the
same fixed vectors, so the assertion holds for $\sigma^{-1}$.

attrs.title: No fixed vectors on the Tate module when the fixed subgroup is finite

objects.body:
Let $X$ be a scheme in characteristic $p>0$. On its
small pro-etale site, the
derived pullback
along absolute $p$-power Frobenius $F_X$ has a canonical
trivialization $LF_X^*\simeq\operatorname{id}$. It commutes with
restriction to open subschemes and with its multiplicative iterates.
(Source for the input: [Stacks,
Tag 0F6W](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F6W), Lemma 37.64.15 – for a weakly etale $U\to X$ the relative
Frobenius $F_{U/X}:U\to U\times_{X,F_X}X$ is an isomorphism; the
trivialization of the derived pullback and its compatibilities with
restriction and with the iterates are the content of the proof below.)

## Proof

An object $v:V\to X$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] is weakly
etale. Its relative Frobenius is

$$
r_V=(F_V,v):V\longrightarrow V\times_{X,F_X}X.
$$

It is integral and universally bijective. For an affine ring map
$R\to B$, the corresponding map
$B\otimes_{R,F_R}R\to B$ sends $b\otimes a$ to $b^pv(a)$.
Every $b\in B$ satisfies the monic equation $T^p-b^p=0$ over the
image, proving integrality. For an algebraically closed field
$\Omega$, a homomorphism from the tensor product to $\Omega$
specifies maps $\beta:B\to\Omega$, $\alpha:R\to\Omega$ satisfying
$\beta(v(a))=\alpha(a)^p$. The unique lift to $B$ is
$b\mapsto\beta(b)^{1/p}$: it is a ring map and its restriction to
$R$ is $\alpha$. This proves universal bijectivity. The argument
is local on $X$ and $V$, so $r_V$ is a universal homeomorphism.

Its source and target are weakly etale over $X$; the target is a
base change of $v$. Thus [lem-trf-weakly-etale-between-objects]
shows that $r_V$ is weakly etale. For clarity, the geometric
factorization behind this Mathlib result is as follows. If
$f:U\to W$ is a map between weakly etale $X$-schemes, its graph
$\Gamma_f:U\to U\times_XW$ is the base change of
$\Delta_{W/X}$ along
$(f\circ\operatorname{pr}_U,\operatorname{pr}_W)$, so is flat.
The projection $U\times_XW\to W$ is flat as a base change of
$U\to X$. Their composite $f$ is flat. Moreover the square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
U&\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}}&U\\
{\scriptstyle\Delta_f}\downarrow&&
\downarrow{\scriptstyle\Delta_{U/X}}\\
U\times_WU&\longrightarrow&U\times_XU
\end{array}
$$

is Cartesian: on a test scheme a point of its fiber product is
$(u,(u_1,u_2))$ with $(u,u)=(u_1,u_2)$, hence is uniquely
$(u,(u,u))$. Therefore $\Delta_f$ is flat as well. These are
exactly the flatness conditions in
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties].
Applying [lem-trf-weakly-etale-homeomorphism] now makes
$r_V$ an isomorphism.

The $r_V$ commute with all morphisms of site objects. Consequently
the base-change functor $V\mapsto V\times_{X,F_X}X$ is naturally
isomorphic to the identity and preserves its coverings. On sheaves,
the inverses of the restriction maps along $r_V$ give
$\mathcal F(V)\simeq(F_{X*}\mathcal F)(V)$. Taking left adjoints
gives $F_X^*\simeq\operatorname{id}$. Both functors are exact,
so the same maps on complexes give the derived assertion with
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Restricting the maps
$r_V$ to an open gives the same relative Frobenius there.
Composing them gives relative $p^m$-power Frobenius, proving the
restriction and iteration assertions.

*Recorded in advance* from chapter *The trace formula* of the source.

attrs.title: Canonical trivialization of absolute Frobenius pullback

objects.body:
Let $(\mathcal C_i,\mathcal T_i)$ be triangulated categories with
$T_i:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C_i$ the shifts, and let
$F_i:\mathcal C_1\to\mathcal C_2$, $G_i:\mathcal C_2\to\mathcal C_1$
be exact functors with adjunctions
$F_1\dashv G_1$ (unit $\eta_1$, counit $\varepsilon_1$) and
$F_2\dashv G_2$ (unit $\eta_2$, counit $\varepsilon_2$), and let
$\alpha:F_1\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }F_2$ be a natural isomorphism.

1. There is a unique natural isomorphism
$\beta:G_1\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }G_2$ compatible with the adjunctions,
given explicitly by the composite
$$
\beta:\quad G_1
\xrightarrow{\ \eta_2G_1\ }
G_2F_2G_1
\xrightarrow{\ G_2\alpha^{-1}G_1\ }
G_2F_1G_1
\xrightarrow{\ G_2\varepsilon_1\ }
G_2
$$
and its inverse
$$
\beta^{-1}:\quad G_2
\xrightarrow{\ \eta_1G_2\ }
G_1F_1G_2
\xrightarrow{\ G_1\alpha G_2\ }
G_1F_2G_2
\xrightarrow{\ G_1\varepsilon_2\ }
G_1.
$$
1. The units and counits are carried to each other: the two
composite morphisms
$$
\operatorname{id}\xrightarrow{\ \eta_1\ }G_1F_1
\xrightarrow{\ \beta F_1\ }G_2F_1
\xrightarrow{\ G_2\alpha\ }G_2F_2,
\qquad
\operatorname{id}\xrightarrow{\ \eta_2\ }G_2F_2,
$$
are equal, and the two composites
$$
F_1G_1\xrightarrow{\ F_1\beta\ }F_1G_2
\xrightarrow{\ \alpha G_2\ }F_2G_2
\xrightarrow{\ \varepsilon_2\ }\operatorname{id},
\qquad
F_1G_1\xrightarrow{\ \varepsilon_1\ }\operatorname{id},
$$
are equal; the analogous identities hold with the roles of the two
adjunctions exchanged. In particular the unit-compatibility reads
$$
G_2\alpha\circ\beta F_1\circ\eta_1=\eta_2,
$$
as morphisms $\operatorname{id}\to G_2F_2$ after the canonical
identification $G_2F_1\xrightarrow{G_2\alpha}G_2F_2$.
1. *Uniqueness.* Any natural isomorphism
$\beta':G_1\xrightarrow{\sim}G_2$ satisfying the unit compatibility
of (2) together with its counit analogue is equal to $\beta$; in
particular the identification of $G_1$ with $G_2$ is canonical
once $\alpha$ is.

All functors and natural transformations are in the
classical framework.

## Proof

In the framework of [rem-trf-classical-framework], for every
$x\in\mathcal C_1$, $y\in\mathcal C_2$, the adjunctions give
natural bijections

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}(x,G_1y)
&\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(F_1x,y)\\
&\xrightarrow{\ h\mapsto h\circ\alpha_x^{-1}\ }
\operatorname{Hom}(F_2x,y)
\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(x,G_2y).
\end{aligned}
$$

Yoneda gives a unique natural isomorphism $\beta:G_1\to G_2$.
Applying the bijection to $x=G_1y$ and
$\operatorname{id}_{G_1y}$ gives exactly the formula for $\beta_y$
in (1). Replacing $\alpha^{-1}$ with $\alpha$ in the reversed
bijection gives the displayed formula for $\beta^{-1}$; these maps
are inverse because the two Hom-bijections are inverse.

The unit $\eta_{1,x}$ corresponds to
$\operatorname{id}_{F_1x}$. The displayed bijection sends it to the
adjoint of $\alpha_x^{-1}:F_2x\to F_1x$, namely
$G_2(\alpha_x^{-1})\eta_{2,x}$.
Consequently $\beta_{F_1x}\eta_{1,x} =G_2(\alpha_x^{-1})\eta_{2,x}$, which proves the unit formula.
The counit corresponds to the identity of $G_1y$. Hence
$\beta_y$ is adjoint to
$\varepsilon_{1,y}\alpha_{G_1y}^{-1}$, giving

$$
\varepsilon_{2,y}F_2(\beta_y)
=\varepsilon_{1,y}\alpha_{G_1y}^{-1}.
$$

Precompose with $\alpha_{G_1y}$ and use naturality of $\alpha$ to
obtain
$\varepsilon_{2,y}\alpha_{G_2y}F_1(\beta_y)=\varepsilon_{1,y}$,
the counit formula of (2). The reversed bijections give the analogous
identities for the inverse. Finally, either adjunction compatibility
forces the displayed Hom-bijection, so Yoneda proves uniqueness.

attrs.title: Mates along an isomorphism of left adjoints

objects.body:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let
$P^\bullet=(P^i,d^i)_{i\in\mathbf Z}$ be a bounded complex of finite
projective $A$-modules, and let $v:P^\bullet\to P^\bullet$ be a chain
map. On the model category of bounded complexes of finite projective
$A$-modules use the following *strict* symmetric monoidal
structure (the Koszul convention of
the categorical trace):

1. the tensor product of complexes is the total complex of the
double complex $(P^i\otimes_AQ^j)$, with the differential
$d(p\otimes q)=dp\otimes q+(-1)^{|p|}p\otimes dq$, the unit is
$A$ concentrated in degree $0$, and the associator and unit
isomorphisms are the identity maps;
1. the braiding is
$\operatorname{sym}_{P,Q}(p\otimes q)=(-1)^{|p||q|}q\otimes p$;
1. the dual complex $P^\vee$ is
$(P^\vee)^n=\operatorname{Hom}_A(P^{-n},A)$ with the differential
$$
(d^\vee\varphi)(x):=(-1)^{|\varphi|+1}\varphi(dx),
$$
so that $|e^\vee|=-|e|$ for the dual basis element $e^\vee$ of a
basis element $e$;
1. the evaluation and the coevaluation are
$$
\operatorname{ev}_P(\varphi\otimes p):=\varphi(p),\qquad
\operatorname{coev}_P(1):=\sum_{\alpha}e_\alpha\otimes e_\alpha^\vee,
$$
where $(e_\alpha)$ is a basis of the finite projective $A$-module
$\oplus_iP^i$ (the sum is finite because $P^\bullet$ is bounded, and
is independent of the basis).

Then:

1. **(a)** $\operatorname{ev}_P$ and $\operatorname{coev}_P$ are
chain maps of degree $0$;
1. **(b)** the triangle identities hold:
$$
(\operatorname{ev}_P\otimes1)\circ(1\otimes\operatorname{coev}_P)=1_{P^\vee},\qquad
(1\otimes\operatorname{ev}_P)\circ(\operatorname{coev}_P\otimes1)=1_P;
$$
1. **(c)** the categorical
trace of $v$ is the supertrace of its components,
$$
\operatorname{tr}_A(v\mid P)=
\sum_{i\in\mathbf Z}(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(v^i\mid P^i\bigr),
$$
the sum of the ordinary traces of the components; in particular
$\operatorname{tr}_A(\operatorname{id}_P)=\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{rank}_AP^i$,
the Euler characteristic.

Consequently the value depends only on the homotopy, hence the
quasi-isomorphism, class of $v$: it is a well-defined function

$$
\operatorname{tr}_A:\operatorname{End}_{D(A)}(P)\longrightarrow A
$$

on the derived category, which is the categorical trace of
Definition
[def-trf-categorical-trace].

## Proof

The conventions being explicit, all four assertions are direct
computations in the model category; by
[def-trf-coefficient-conventions] (and the local projectivity of
a bounded complex of finite projective modules) the derived tensor
products of [def-trf-categorical-trace] are computed by these
strict tensor products, and

$$
\operatorname{End}_{D(A)}(A,A)=
\operatorname{Hom}_{K(A)}(A,A)=\operatorname{Hom}_A(A,A)\cong A
$$

(the only chain maps $A\to A$ are the degree-$0$ scalars, and there
are no homotopies, as $A$ is concentrated in degree $0$), so the
composite of [def-trf-categorical-trace] is an element of $A$.

*Step 1: $\operatorname{ev}_P$ is a chain map of degree $0$.*
For $\varphi\in(P^\vee)^n$ and $p\in P^m$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{ev}\bigl(d(\varphi\otimes p)\bigr)
&=\operatorname{ev}\bigl(d^\vee\varphi\otimes p+(-1)^{|\varphi|}
\varphi\otimes dp\bigr)\\
&=(d^\vee\varphi)(p)+(-1)^{|\varphi|}\varphi(dp)
=(-1)^{|\varphi|+1}\varphi(dp)+(-1)^{|\varphi|}\varphi(dp)=0,
\end{aligned}
$$

and $d\operatorname{ev}(\varphi\otimes p)=0$ since $A$ has zero
differential; the degree count
$|\varphi|+|p|=n+m$ is unchanged, so $\operatorname{ev}_P$ is a
chain map of degree $0$. (By the same computation the dual
differential is a differential: $(d^\vee)^2\varphi(x)= (-1)^{|\varphi|+2}(d^\vee\varphi)(dx)= (-1)^{|\varphi|+2}(-1)^{|\varphi|+1}\varphi(d^2x)=0$.)

*Step 2: $\operatorname{coev}_P$ is a chain map.* Write
$d e_\alpha=\sum_\beta d_{\beta\alpha}e_\beta$ with
$d_{\beta\alpha}=e_\beta^\vee(de_\alpha)$, so that
$d^\vee e_\alpha^\vee=\sum_\beta(-1)^{|e_\alpha^\vee|+1}d_{\alpha\beta} e_\beta^\vee$ by the rule of item (3). Then

$$
\begin{aligned}
d\bigl(\operatorname{coev}_P(1)\bigr)
&=\sum_\alpha\Bigl(de_\alpha\otimes e_\alpha^\vee+
(-1)^{|e_\alpha|}e_\alpha\otimes d^\vee e_\alpha^\vee\Bigr)\\
&=\sum_{\alpha,\beta}d_{\beta\alpha}\,e_\beta\otimes e_\alpha^\vee
+\sum_{\alpha,\beta}
(-1)^{|e_\alpha|}(-1)^{|e_\alpha^\vee|+1}d_{\alpha\beta}\,
e_\alpha\otimes e_\beta^\vee\\
&=\sum_{\alpha,\beta}\Bigl(d_{\alpha\beta}
+(-1)^{|\alpha|+(-|\alpha|)+1}d_{\alpha\beta}\Bigr)
e_\alpha\otimes e_\beta^\vee=0,
\end{aligned}
$$

where in the last line the summation indices of the first sum were
swapped ($\alpha\leftrightarrow\beta$) and the identities
$|e_\alpha^\vee|=-|e_\alpha|$ and
$(-1)^{|\alpha|-|\alpha|+1}=-1$ were used. Hence
$\operatorname{coev}_P$ is a chain map of degree $0$.

*Step 3: the triangle identities.* The associator and the unit
isomorphisms are the identity maps, so

$$
\begin{aligned}
(\operatorname{ev}_P\otimes1_P)(1_{P^\vee}\otimes
\operatorname{coev}_P)(\psi)
&=\sum_\alpha
\operatorname{ev}_P(\psi\otimes e_\alpha)\,e_\alpha^\vee
=\sum_\alpha\psi(e_\alpha)e_\alpha^\vee=\psi,\\
(1_P\otimes\operatorname{ev}_P)(\operatorname{coev}_P\otimes1_P)(p)
&=\sum_\alpha
e_\alpha\,\operatorname{ev}_P(e_\alpha^\vee\otimes p)
=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha\,e_\alpha^\vee(p)=p,
\end{aligned}
$$

for all $p\in\oplus_iP^i$ and $\psi\in\oplus_i(P^\vee)^i$; both
identities are degreewise and are the two triangle identities (a)
and (b) of the statement. (The braiding $\operatorname{sym}$ is
not used in these two identities; it is the Koszul sign
$(-1)^{|p||q|}$ that produces the alternating signs in Step 4.)

*Step 4: the trace of the composite.* Let
$(e_{i,a})_{a}$ be a basis of $P^i$ for each $i$ and
$e_{i,a}^\vee$ the dual basis of $(P^\vee)^{-i}$ (so
$|e_{i,a}^\vee|=-i$). The composite of
[def-trf-categorical-trace] is

$$
\begin{aligned}
1&\longmapsto\sum_{i,a}e_{i,a}\otimes e_{i,a}^\vee
\longmapsto\sum_{i,a}v\,e_{i,a}\otimes e_{i,a}^\vee\\
&\longmapsto\sum_{i,a}(-1)^{|v e_{i,a}||e_{i,a}^\vee|}
e_{i,a}^\vee\otimes v\,e_{i,a}
=\sum_{i,a}(-1)^{i(-i)}e_{i,a}^\vee\otimes v\,e_{i,a}\\
&\longmapsto\sum_{i,a}(-1)^{i(-i)}e_{i,a}^\vee(v\,e_{i,a})
=\sum_{i,a}(-1)^i e_{i,a}^\vee(v^i e_{i,a})
=\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(v^i\mid P^i),
\end{aligned}
$$

because $i(-i)=-i^2\equiv i^2\equiv i\pmod 2$, so
$(-1)^{i(-i)}=(-1)^i$. This is (c). (The second arrow uses that
$v$ is a chain map of degree $0$, whence
$|v\,e_{i,a}|=i$.)

*Step 5: independence of the representative.* The sum of Step 4
is visibly independent of the chosen bases (a change of basis
$e'_\alpha=\sum_\beta c_{\alpha\beta}e_\beta$ with inverse matrix $c^{-1}$
substitutes $\sum e'_\alpha\otimes e'^\vee_\alpha=\sum e_\alpha\otimes e_\alpha^\vee$, as $\sum_\alpha c_{\alpha\beta} (c^{-1})_{\gamma\alpha}=\delta_{\beta\gamma}$). It is invariant under
homotopy: if $v-v'=ds+sd$ with $s:P^i\to P^{i-1}$ of degree $-1$,
then, using the cyclicity of the trace,

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(d^{i-1}s^i\mid P^i)
+\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(s^{i+1}d^i\mid P^i)\\
&=\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(d^{i-1}s^i)
-\sum_i(-1)^{i-1}\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(s^{i}d^{i-1}\bigr)=0,
\end{aligned}
$$

the two sums cancelling term by term after the index shift
$i\mapsto i+1$ in the second. Hence $\operatorname{tr}_A(v\mid P)$
depends only on the homotopy class, i.e. on the morphism
$v\in\operatorname{End}_{D(A)}(P)$; this is precisely the value of the
composite of [def-trf-categorical-trace] (its tensor products are
the strict ones of this model, its
$\operatorname{coev}_P,\operatorname{ev}_P$ the maps of steps 1–3,
and $\operatorname{End}_{D(A)}(A)\cong A$), so the derived-level
categorical trace of a quasi-isomorphism class of endomorphisms equals
the supertrace of any projective representative, as stated.

attrs.title: Chain-level supertrace computation, with explicit conventions

objects.body:
Use the finite coefficient
ring $A$, and let $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ be a
compactification
of $a_X:X\to s=\Spec k$, with proper map $\bar a:\bar X\to s$.
For a bounded
constructible complex $K$ equipped with an
explicit etale-origin
witness, there is a canonical natural isomorphism

$$
C_{j,K}:R\Gamma_c(X,K)\xrightarrow{\sim}
R\Gamma(\bar X,j_!K).
$$

Here $j_!K$ is extension by
zero, and the ordinary
and compact-support cohomology use the
fiber over $s$.
The comparison respects changes of compactification.

## Proof

For the chosen compactification,
[def-weil-compact-support-candidate] gives
$Ra_{X!}^{\,j}K=R\bar a_*j_!K$. The comparison in
[def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], with the cocycle identity
of [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed], identifies $Ra_{X!}K$
with this candidate. The witness $K\simeq\nu_X^*L$, with
$L\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, from
[def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness] puts $K$ in precisely
the domain on which compactification coherence has been proved.
Neither etale descent of all constructible pro-etale complexes nor
coherence for arbitrary pro-etale objects is asserted here.
Apply the fiber functor of
[def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. By
[def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], the source becomes
$R\Gamma_c(X,K)$ and the target becomes
$R\Gamma(\bar X,j_!K)$. This is $C_{j,K}$.
Naturality is the naturality of the candidate comparisons.
Their cocycle identity proves the asserted compatibility when the
compactification is changed.

Fix the global finite-field datum and the coefficient ring
$A=A_{E,n}$. Let $j_0:X_0\hookrightarrow\bar X_0$ be a
compactification over $k_0$ of a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme,
with base change $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ to $k$, and write
$\Phi=\Phi_X$, $\bar\Phi=\Phi_{\bar X}$ for the $q$-power scheme
Frobenii of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. For $m\geq0$ let

$$
b_m:L\bar\Phi^{m*}j_!\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }j_!L\Phi^{m*}
$$

be the comparison isomorphism of [lem-trf-open-square-exchange] for the
Cartesian square of [lem-trf-frobenius-open-square] with
$(h,\bar h)=(\Phi^m,\bar\Phi^m)$. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ carry an
explicit etale-origin witness.

1. *Extension of coefficient morphisms.* For every morphism
$v:L\Phi^{m*}K\to K$ put
$$
\bar v=j_!v\circ b_m:\;L\bar\Phi^{m*}j_!K\longrightarrow j_!K .
$$
If $\psi:L\Phi^*K\to K$ is a Frobenius coefficient morphism of
[def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism] (no invertibility assumed),
then $\bar\psi$ is a Frobenius coefficient morphism on
$j_!K\in D^b_{ctf}(\bar X,A)$, and its iterates are the extensions of
the iterates of $\psi$:
$$
(\bar\psi)_m=\overline{\psi_m}=j_!\psi_m\circ b_m\qquad(m\geq1).
$$
1. *Stalks.* Let $\bar y$ be a geometric point of $\bar X$ with
$\bar\Phi^m\bar y=\bar y$, and let $\bar v_{\bar y}$, $v_{\bar y}$ be
the induced stalk endomorphisms (through
$(L\bar\Phi^{m*}M)_{\bar y}\cong M_{\bar y}$). If $\bar y$ lies in
$X$, then $(j_!K)_{\bar y}=K_{\bar y}$ and $\bar v_{\bar y}=v_{\bar y}$;
otherwise $(j_!K)_{\bar y}=0$.
1. *Global operators.* For the graph correspondences
$c=(\operatorname{id}_X,\Phi^m)$ and
$\bar c=(\operatorname{id}_{\bar X},\bar\Phi^m)$ of
[def-trf-graph-correspondence], the comparison
$C_{j,K}:R\Gamma_c(X,K)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(\bar X,j_!K)$ of
[lem-trf-compactification-cohomology] intertwines the global
operators of [def-trf-global-operator]:
$$
C_{j,K}\circ T_c(v)=T_{\bar c}(\bar v)\circ C_{j,K}.
$$

## Proof

*(1).* The complex $j_!K$ lies in $D^b_{ctf}(\bar X,A)$ by
[lem-trf-open-ctf], so $\bar\psi$ is a Frobenius coefficient morphism
on it. For the iterates, argue by induction on $m$, the case $m=1$
being the definition. The squares of [lem-trf-frobenius-open-square]
for $\bar\Phi$ and $\bar\Phi^{m-1}$ paste to the square for
$\bar\Phi^m$, so by the pasting clause of
[lem-trf-open-square-exchange], after the pullback composition
identifications,
$b_m=b_{1,L\Phi^{(m-1)*}K}\circ L\bar\Phi^*b_{m-1}$. Using the
recursion of [def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism], the induction
hypothesis, and the naturality of $b_1$,

$$
(\bar\psi)_m=\bar\psi\circ L\bar\Phi^*(\bar\psi)_{m-1}
=j_!\psi\circ b_1\circ L\bar\Phi^*j_!\psi_{m-1}\circ
L\bar\Phi^*b_{m-1}
=j_!\psi\circ j_!L\Phi^*\psi_{m-1}\circ b_{1}\circ L\bar\Phi^*b_{m-1}
=j_!\psi_m\circ b_m .
$$

*(2).* Stalks of $j_!K$ are $K_{\bar y}$ on $X$ and $0$ off $X$ by
[def-weil-extension-by-zero]. For $\bar y$ in $X$ the stalk functor
factors through restriction to the open $X$; there
$j^*j_!=\operatorname{id}$ and $j^*b_m$ is the identity after the
pullback identifications (the normalization clause of
[lem-trf-open-square-exchange]), so $j^*\bar v=v$ and hence
$\bar v_{\bar y}=v_{\bar y}$.

*(3).* Write $M=L\Phi^{m*}K$, which again carries an explicit
etale-origin witness by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], so that
$C_{j,M}$ is defined. By [prop-trf-graph-operator],

$$
T_c(v)=R\Gamma_c(X,v)\circ\iota_X\circ R\Gamma_c(X,\eta),\qquad
T_{\bar c}(\bar v)=R\Gamma(\bar X,\bar v)\circ\iota_{\bar X}\circ
R\Gamma(\bar X,\bar\eta),
$$

where $\eta:K\to R\Phi^m_*M$ and
$\bar\eta:j_!K\to R\bar\Phi^m_*L\bar\Phi^{m*}j_!K$ are the units, and
$\iota_X$, $\iota_{\bar X}$ are the identifications
$R\Phi^m_*\simeq R\Phi^m_!$ followed by the composition law for
$a_X\Phi^m=a_X$, respectively $a_{\bar X}\bar\Phi^m=a_{\bar X}$ (the
scheme Frobenius is a $k$-morphism). Let
$\gamma:j_!R\Phi^m_*M\xrightarrow{\sim}R\bar\Phi^m_*j_!M$ be the
composition isomorphism of the compact-support direct image for
$j\Phi^m=\bar\Phi^mj$ ([prop-functor-package], item (3), with
$R\Phi^m_*=R\Phi^m_!$ for the finite maps $\Phi^m$, $\bar\Phi^m$).

*Step A: the units.* We claim
$$
\gamma\circ j_!\eta=R\bar\Phi^m_*b_m\circ\bar\eta:\quad
j_!K\longrightarrow R\bar\Phi^m_*j_!M .
$$
By the adjunction $j_!\dashv j^*$ of [def-weil-extension-by-zero] it
suffices to compare the adjoint maps
$K\to j^*R\bar\Phi^m_*j_!M$. By the proof of
[lem-trf-open-square-exchange], $j^*R\bar\Phi^m_*=R\Phi^m_*j^*$ with
the comparison given by the identity on sections, and
$j^*j_!=\operatorname{id}$; under these identifications $j^*\gamma$ is
the identity of $R\Phi^m_*M$, both sides being computed by the same
section formula over objects of the site of $X$. Hence the adjoint
of the left-hand side is $\eta$. On the other hand, $b_m$ is, by its
construction in [lem-trf-open-square-exchange], the left-adjoint mate
of the equality $j^*R\bar\Phi^m_*=R\Phi^m_*j^*$ for the composite
adjunctions $L\bar\Phi^{m*}j_!\dashv j^*R\bar\Phi^m_*$ and
$j_!L\Phi^{m*}\dashv R\Phi^m_*j^*$; the unit compatibility of
[lem-trf-adjoint-mate], item (2), for this pair of adjunctions says
exactly that the adjoint of the right-hand side is also $\eta$. This
proves the claim.

*Step B: transport to cohomology.* The comparisons $C_{j,-}$ are
natural in the witnessed complex ([lem-trf-compactification-cohomology]),
so $C_{j,K}\circ R\Gamma_c(X,v)=R\Gamma(\bar X,j_!v)\circ C_{j,M}$.
They are compatible with the composition law of the compact-support
direct image ([prop-compactification-coherence-detailed]: the
comparison with the candidate $R\bar a_*j_!$ respects composition), which
gives
$$
C_{j,M}\circ\iota_X\circ R\Gamma_c(X,\eta)
=\iota_{\bar X}\circ R\Gamma(\bar X,\gamma\circ j_!\eta)\circ C_{j,K}.
$$
Substituting Step A and $j_!v\circ b_m=\bar v$ (naturality of
$\iota_{\bar X}$ moves $R\bar\Phi^m_*b_m$ past it), one obtains
$C_{j,K}\circ T_c(v)=R\Gamma(\bar X,\bar v)\circ\iota_{\bar X}\circ
R\Gamma(\bar X,\bar\eta)\circ C_{j,K}=T_{\bar c}(\bar v)\circ C_{j,K}$.
No invertibility of $v$ is used anywhere.

attrs.title: Extension by zero of a Frobenius coefficient morphism

objects.body:
In the setting of [def-trf-correspondence-between-pairs], let
$c=(c_1,c_2):C\to Z=Y\times_sX$ be the support of a correspondence from
$(X,K)$ to $(Y,L)$, and assume that $c$ and the projection
$p_1:Z\to Y$ are exceptionally admissible at $A$
([def-trf-admissibility]). Then tensor–Hom adjunction, the projection
formula and exceptional adjunction give a canonical isomorphism

$$
\operatorname{Hom}_{D(Z,A)}\bigl(Rc_!A_C,
R\mathcal Hom_A(Lp_2^*K,Rp_1^!L)\bigr)
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
\operatorname{Hom}_{D(C,A)}\bigl(Lc_2^*K,Rc_1^!L\bigr),
$$

natural in $K$ and $L$. For a correspondence
$u:Lc_2^*K\to Rc_1^!L$, its *class* $[u]$ is the inverse image of $u$
under this isomorphism; it is a class supported on $c$ with values in
$R\mathcal Hom_A(Lp_2^*K,Rp_1^!L)$ in the sense of
[def-trf-supported-class], i.e. $[u]\in
H^0_C\bigl(Z,R\mathcal Hom_A(Lp_2^*K,Rp_1^!L)\bigr)$.

## Proof

Put $M=Lp_2^*K$ and $N=Rp_1^!L$; both lie in the bounded constructible
finite-Tor category on $Z$, the first by the pullback clause of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the second because $p_1$ is
exceptionally admissible. Then

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_Z\bigl(Rc_!A_C,R\mathcal Hom_A(M,N)\bigr)
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z\bigl(Rc_!A_C\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}M,N\bigr)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z\bigl(Rc_!(A_C\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}Lc^*M),N\bigr)
=\operatorname{Hom}_Z\bigl(Rc_!Lc^*M,N\bigr)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_C\bigl(Lc^*M,Rc^!N\bigr)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_C\bigl(Lc_2^*K,Rc_1^!L\bigr).
\end{aligned}
$$

The first arrow is the tensor–internal-Hom adjunction of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. The second is the
compact-support projection formula of [prop-functor-package] (clause
five) for $c$, applied with the constant sheaf $A_C$ in the first
variable and the finite-Tor complex $M$ in the second, and
$A_C\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}(-)$ is the identity. The third is the
exceptional adjunction $Rc_!\dashv Rc^!$ of [def-trf-admissibility]
for the admissible $c$. The last uses the pullback composition
$Lc^*Lp_2^*\cong L(p_2c)^*=Lc_2^*$ of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and the composition isomorphism
$Rc^!Rp_1^!\cong R(p_1c)^!=Rc_1^!$ of the exceptional inverse image
supplied with the admissibility datum of [def-trf-admissibility]. Every
arrow is a bijection natural in $K$ and $L$, so the composite is the
asserted isomorphism and $[u]$ is well defined. The final assertion is
the definition of $H^0_C$ in [def-trf-supported-class] with $i=c$,
$T=C$ and $P=R\mathcal Hom_A(M,N)$.

Let $X$ be a separated finite-type scheme over $k$ and $A$ a
finite coefficient ring as in [def-trf-coefficient-conventions].
The triangulated category $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ is the thick subcategory of
$D(X,A)$ generated by the objects

$$
Rg_*j_!L ,
$$

where $U$ is a locally closed stratum of $X$,
$j:U\hookrightarrow\overline U$ is the open immersion into its closure,
$g:\overline U\hookrightarrow X$ is the closed immersion, and $L$ is a lisse
sheaf of $A$-modules on $U$ with flat stalks. Constant coefficients
$L=A_U$ do not suffice in general.

## Proof

Step 0 (the generators are in $D^b_{ctf}$). A lisse sheaf with flat
stalks has Tor amplitude $[0,0]$; extension by zero along $j$ and the
exact pushforward along the closed immersion $g$ preserve
constructibility and Tor amplitude.

Step 1 (flat model). The truncations
$\tau_{\leq q}K$ of an object $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ need not have finite
Tor amplitude when $A$ is not a field (e.g. $A=\mathbf Z/4$,
$K=[A\xrightarrow{2}A]$, whose cohomology sheaves $\mathbf Z/2$ have
infinite Tor dimension), so the cohomology sheaves cannot be used. Instead,
apply the constructible variant of [lem-sf-flat-model] on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$:
its input is that every constructible sheaf of $A$-modules is a quotient of a
finite direct sum of the flat constructible sheaves $j_{V!}A_V$, $V\to X$
affine étale (Stacks 095M; SGA $4\frac12$, Rapport, 4.6), that the
cohomology sheaves of $K$ are constructible
([def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]), and that kernels and cokernels of
maps of constructible sheaves are constructible; its conclusion is that $K$
is isomorphic to a bounded complex $P$ of flat constructible sheaves, the
flat truncation $Q$ in that proof being constructible as well. The
stupid-truncation triangles
$\sigma_{\geq q+1}P\to\sigma_{\geq q}P\to P^q[-q]\xrightarrow{+1}$
reduce the claim to a single flat constructible sheaf $F$: a thick
subcategory containing two terms of a distinguished triangle contains the
third, the two-out-of-three step for triangles of
[lem-sf-triangle-two-out-of-three].

Step 2 (extension across the strata). As in
[lem-fin-constructible-devissage], choose a dense open
$j_U:U\hookrightarrow X$ on which $F$ is lisse, with closed complement
$i:Z\hookrightarrow X$. The exact sequence

$$
0\longrightarrow j_{U!}(F|_U)\longrightarrow F
\longrightarrow i_*i^*F\longrightarrow0
$$

has $F|_U$ lisse with flat stalks and $i^*F$ flat constructible on $Z$,
of smaller dimension. By induction on dimension, pushing the resulting
filtration forward along the exact functor $i_*$, $F$ is a finite iterated
extension of objects $Rg_*j_!L$ as in the statement, with $L$ the
restriction of $F$ to a locally closed stratum; each extension is a
distinguished triangle, so $F$ lies in the thick closure.

Step 3 (why lisse coefficients). The lisse coefficients are not reduced
further. The abelian category of constructible sheaves is not of finite
length, and its simple objects are punctual
([lem-trf-simple-constructible]), so a lisse sheaf on a positive-dimensional
stratum is not a finite extension of simple constructible sheaves. Nor is
$L$ in general a direct summand of $\pi_*\pi^*L$ for a finite étale Galois
cover $\pi$ trivializing it, when $\ell$ divides the order of the
monodromy. And constant coefficients do not generate: on
$X=\mathbf G_m$ over $k$ with $p\neq2$ and $A=\mathbf F_3$, the complexes
whose generic-stalk cohomology has only trivial $\pi_1$-composition
factors form a thick subcategory containing every $Rg_*j_!A_U$ but not
the order-$2$ Kummer sheaf. A statement checked on the generators may,
when it is étale-local on $U$, still be reduced to constant coefficients
by passing to a trivializing finite étale cover.

Fix the coefficient
conventions, $A=A_{E,n}$, and let $c:C\to Z$ be a separated
finite-type morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes which is admissible at
$A$ ([def-trf-admissibility]). For
$M,N\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$ the canonical comparison

$$
R\mathcal Hom_A\bigl(c^*M,c^!N\bigr)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
c^!R\mathcal Hom_A(M,N)
$$

is an isomorphism, natural in $M$ and $N$. Its first variable is
required to be an ordinary pullback and its second an exceptional one;
the analogous statement with $c^!$ in the first variable is false, as
recorded in [def-trf-admissibility].

## Proof

Let $P\in D^b_{ctf}(C,A)$ be a test object. The exceptional adjunction
of [def-trf-admissibility] and the tensor–internal-Hom adjunction of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] give the chain

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_C\bigl(P,R\mathcal Hom_A(c^*M,c^!N)\bigr)
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_C\bigl(P\otimes_A^Lc^*M,c^!N\bigr)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z\bigl(c_!\bigl(P\otimes_A^Lc^*M\bigr),N\bigr)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z\bigl(c_!P\otimes_A^LM,N\bigr)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z\bigl(c_!P,R\mathcal Hom_A(M,N)\bigr)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_C\bigl(P,c^!R\mathcal Hom_A(M,N)\bigr),
\end{aligned}
$$

in which the third arrow is the projection formula of
[prop-functor-package] for the admissible $c$, applied to the
first tensor factor, and the remaining arrows are the two adjunctions.
Every arrow is natural in $P$, so the Yoneda lemma identifies the two
representable functors of $P$ and produces the canonical comparison of
the statement. Naturality in $M$ and $N$, and compatibility with
shifts and distinguished triangles, are the corresponding properties of
the adjunctions and of the projection formula.

attrs.title: Exceptional internal Hom versus exceptional pullback

objects.body:
Let $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ be the
finite coefficient ring,
so that $A$ is a local Artinian ring with maximal ideal
$(\varpi_E)$, and let $C$ be a bounded complex of $A$-modules
whose cohomology modules are finite, i.e. an object of the
finite-coefficient
category over a point of the trace-formula chapter. Then $C$ has
finite Tor amplitude if and
only if $C$ lies in $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$ in the sense of
[def-trf-categorical-trace], i.e. if and only if $C$ is
quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finitely generated free
$A$-modules.

## Proof

Write $A=A_{E,n}$ for the finite coefficient ring of
[def-trf-coefficient-conventions]: it is a local ring with
maximal ideal $(\varpi_E)$.

*(If.)* Suppose that $C$ is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded
complex $P^\bullet$ of finite free $A$-modules with $P^i=0$ for
$i\notin[a,b]$. For every $A$-module $M$ the derived tensor
$C\otimes_A^LM\cong P^\bullet\otimes_AM$ is concentrated in degrees
$[a,b]$, so that $\operatorname{Tor}_i^A(C,M)=0$ for
$i\notin[a,b]$: in the notation of
[def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] the complex $C$ has finite Tor
amplitude, and it is perfect in the sense of
[def-trf-categorical-trace] by construction.

*(Only if.)* Suppose that $C$ has finite Tor amplitude, i.e. finite tor dimension in the sense of
[Stacks, Tag 0652](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0652)
(Definition 15.68.1, in Section 15.68, Tor dimension).
Each cohomology module $H^i(C)$ is finite by hypothesis, hence
$0$-pseudo-coherent as an $A$-module by
[Stacks, Tag 064T](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/064T);
since $C$ is bounded it lies in $D^-(A)$, so
[Stacks, Tag 066B](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/066B)
shows that the complex $C$ itself is pseudo-coherent. By
[Stacks, Tag 0658](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0658) a
pseudo-coherent complex of finite tor dimension over a ring is
perfect, and if it has tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ it is
quasi-isomorphic to a complex $E^\bullet$ of finite projective
$A$-modules with $E^i=0$ for $i\notin[a,b]$. Since $A$ is a
local ring, a finite projective $A$-module is free
([Stacks, Tag 00NZ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00NZ),
Lemma 10.78.5: a finite flat module over a local ring is finite free;
equivalently
[Tag 00NX](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00NX), Lemma 10.78.2,
parts (2) and (5), together with Nakayama's lemma), so that
$E^\bullet$ is a bounded
complex of finitely generated free $A$-modules quasi-isomorphic to
$C$: $C$ lies in the category $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$ of
[def-trf-categorical-trace].

The finite-Tor-amplitude hypothesis cannot be dropped in the second
direction: the module $A/(\varpi_E)$, viewed as a complex
concentrated in degree $0$, has finite cohomology modules, while its
minimal free resolution

$$
\cdots\to A\xrightarrow{\varpi_E}A\xrightarrow{\varpi_E}A\to
A/(\varpi_E)\to0
$$

is infinite, so that $\operatorname{Tor}_i^A(A/(\varpi_E), A/(\varpi_E))\cong A/(\varpi_E)\neq0$ for all $i\geq0$ and
$A/(\varpi_E)$ is not quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of
finite free $A$-modules.

*Recorded in advance* from chapter *The trace formula* of the source.

attrs.title: Finite Tor amplitude and perfectness over the finite coefficient ring

objects.body:
Let $(f,g):(C,c)\to(D,b)$ be a proper pushforward diagram of
[def-trf-coefficient-pushforward], with induced map
$h:F_c=\operatorname{Fix}(c)\to F_b=\operatorname{Fix}(b)$. Then:

1. $h$ factors as
$$
h:\ F_c\xrightarrow{\ \kappa\ }C\times_DF_b\xrightarrow{\ \pi\ }F_b,
$$
where $\pi$ is the base change of $g$ along $i_b:F_b\to D$, and
$\kappa$ is a base change of the relative diagonal
$\Delta_{X/Y}:X\to X\times_YX$, hence a closed immersion;
1. $h$ and $q=f\times f:X\times_sX\to Y\times_sY$ are proper.

Consequently, for a correspondence $u$ on $(X,K)$ supported on $c$, with
the exceptional admissibility of $h$ and of the structure morphisms of
$F_c,F_b$, the *proper pushforward of the trace class*

$$
h_*\operatorname{Tr}_c(u):A_{F_b}\longrightarrow\omega_{F_b}
$$

is defined: it is the Borel–Moore pushforward of
[def-trf-borel-moore-pushforward] of the Borel–Moore section
$\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)$ of [def-trf-trace-class].

## Proof

Put $G=C\times_DF_b$, with projections $\pi:G\to F_b$ and
$j:G\to C$. By [def-trf-fixed-scheme],
$F_b=D\times_{Y\times_sY,\Delta_Y}Y$, so a $T$-point of $G$ is a pair
$(t,y)$ of $t\in C(T)$ and $y\in Y(T)$ with $b(g(t))=(y,y)$, i.e. with
$fc_1(t)=y=fc_2(t)$. Hence $(c_1,c_2)\circ j$ factors through
$X\times_YX\subset X\times_sX$, giving a morphism $\lambda:G\to X\times_YX$.
The morphism $X\times_YX\to X\times_sX$ is a monomorphism (it is the base
change of the monomorphism $\Delta_Y$). Therefore a $T$-point of
$G\times_{X\times_YX,\lambda,\Delta_{X/Y}}X$ is a pair $((t,y),x)$ with
$(c_1t,c_2t)=(x,x)$, and then $y=fx$ is determined; that is, exactly a
pair $(t,x)$ with $c(t)=\Delta_X(x)$, which is a $T$-point of
$F_c=C\times_{X\times_sX,c,\Delta_X}X$. These identifications are natural
in $T$, so

$$
F_c\cong G\times_{X\times_YX,\Delta_{X/Y}}X,
$$

and the first projection $\kappa:F_c\to G$, $\kappa=(i_c,f d_c)$, is the
base change of $\Delta_{X/Y}$. Since $\pi\kappa=(g i_c,fd_c)$ as a map to
$D\times_{Y\times_sY}Y$, the identities $i_bh=gi_c$, $d_bh=fd_c$ of
[def-trf-coefficient-pushforward] give $\pi\kappa=h$. This is (1),
except for the closed immersion claim.

The proper $f$ is separated, so $\Delta_{X/Y}$ is a closed immersion
([def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]), and so is its base change
$\kappa$. Closed immersions are proper
([lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]); $\pi$ is proper as a base change
of the proper $g$, and $h=\pi\kappa$ is proper as a composite
([lem-kun-proper-stability]). Finally
$q=(f\times\operatorname{id}_Y)\circ(\operatorname{id}_X\times f)$ is a
composite of base changes of $f$, hence proper by
[lem-kun-proper-stability]. This proves (2). The last assertion is the
definition of [def-trf-borel-moore-pushforward] applied to the proper $h$,
$T=F_c$, $T'=F_b$ and $\alpha=\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)$.

attrs.title: The induced map of fixed schemes is proper

objects.body:
Let $x\in|X_0|$ be a closed point with degree
$d_x=[\kappa(x):\Fq]$, let $m$ be divisible by $d_x$, let
$x_m\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^{d_x}})$ be a point above $x$, and put
$F_x=F_{x_m,d_x}$, the *one-circuit local Frobenius* (well
defined up to conjugation by
[lem-trf-local-frobenius-conjugacy]). Then for every
$y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ above $x$,

$$
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(F_{y,m}\mid K_{\bar y}\bigr)
=
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(F_x^{\,m/d_x}\mid K_{\bar x}\bigr)
$$

in $A$.

## Proof

*Step 1: iteration at one lift.* Let $\bar x$ be the geometric
point of the lift $x_m$, and suppose first that
$m=r\cdot d_x$. For a fixed point $\bar z$ of $\Phi^d$ the
transport $\tau_{z,d}$ of [def-trf-frobenius-operators] is the
canonical identification $K_{\bar z}\cong K_{g_\gamma^d\bar z}\cong K_{\bar z}$ of [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison] and the
fixed-point property (the same two identifications and the universal
homeomorphism invariance used in the proof of
[lem-trf-local-frobenius-conjugacy]); the same holds for
$\tau_{z,m}$, and the composite identification for $m=rd$ is the
$r$-fold iteration of the one for $d$ (the functoriality of the
pullback under $g_\gamma^{d}$-iterates, i.e. $g_\gamma^{m}=g_\gamma^{d}\circ\cdots\circ g_\gamma^{d}$). Hence,
with the iterated Weil isomorphisms $\varphi^{[m]}$ of
[def-trf-iterated-weil-map],

$$
\begin{aligned}
F_{z,m}
&=\varphi^{[m]}_{\bar z}\circ\tau_{z,m}
=\varphi^{[d]}_{\bar z}\circ
Lg_\gamma^{d*}\bigl(\varphi^{[(r-1)d]}\bigr)_{\bar z}
\circ\tau_{z,d}\circ\tau_{z,(r-1)d}\\
&=\bigl(\varphi^{[d]}_{\bar z}\circ\tau_{z,d}\bigr)
\circ\bigl(\varphi^{[(r-1)d]}_{\bar z}\circ\tau_{z,(r-1)d}\bigr)
=F_{z,d}\circ F_{z,(r-1)d},
\end{aligned}
$$

where the second equality is the cocycle identity
$\varphi^{[rd]}=\varphi^{[d]}\circ Lg_\gamma^{d*}\varphi^{[(r-1)d]}$
of [lem-trf-iterated-weil-cocycle] together with the naturality of the
canonical stalk identifications (the two ways around the fixed-point
identifications agree, exactly as in the proof of
[lem-trf-local-frobenius-conjugacy], (3)); induction on $r$
gives

$$
F_{z,m}=F_{z,d}^{\,r}
$$

as endomorphisms of $K_{\bar z}$.

*Step 2: changing the lift.* For a general
$y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ above $x$, let
$\bar y=\bar z_i=g_\gamma^i(\bar x)$ ($i$ well defined modulo
$d_x$) and let $T_i:K_{\bar y}\xrightarrow{\sim}K_{\bar x}$ be the
canonical transport of
[lem-trf-local-frobenius-conjugacy], (2). By the conjugacy part
(3) of [lem-trf-local-frobenius-conjugacy] and Step 1,

$$
F_{y,m}=T_i^{-1}F_{z,m}T_i=T_i^{-1}F_{z,d}^{\,r}T_i
=\bigl(T_i^{-1}F_{z,d}T_i\bigr)^{r},
$$

and by the same conjugacy $T_i^{-1}F_{z,d}T_i=F_{x_m,d_x}$ (the
one-circuit operator at the lift $x_m$); this holds for every
$y$ above $x$, so

$$
\operatorname{tr}_A(F_{y,m}\mid K_{\bar y})
=\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(F_{x_m,d_x}^{\,r}\mid K_{\bar x}\bigr),
$$

the traces being equal because the conjugating isomorphisms are
isomorphisms of the perfect complexes
([prop-trf-trace-formal-laws], (1)), and
$K_{\bar y}\in D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$. This is the displayed
identity with $r=m/d_x$.

attrs.title: Degree formula for the local Frobenius

objects.body:
Fix the finite-field datum.
Let $j_0:X_0\hookrightarrow Y_0$ be an
open immersion
over $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, and let $j:X\hookrightarrow Y$
be its base change to $k$. For the
scheme and Galois Frobenii,
each square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X&\xrightarrow{h}&X\\
{\scriptstyle j}\downarrow&&\downarrow{\scriptstyle j}\\
Y&\xrightarrow{\bar h}&Y
\end{array}
$$

is Cartesian, where $(h,\bar h)=(\Phi_X^m,\Phi_Y^m)$ or
$(g_X^m,g_Y^m)$, and $m\geq0$. With
$s=\Spec k$, $g_s=\Spec(\gamma)$, and structure maps $a_X,a_Y$,

$$
a_Xg_X^m=g_s^ma_X,\qquad a_Yg_Y^m=g_s^ma_Y.
$$

In particular these Galois maps are not asserted to be $k$-morphisms.

## Proof

The absolute $q^m$-power map on a characteristic-$p$ ring sends
each prime ideal to itself. Hence the scheme Frobenius of $Y_0$
has inverse image $X_0$ on the underlying open subset, and its
restriction is the Frobenius of $X_0$. For open immersions,
pullback is exactly the inverse-image open with the restricted
structure sheaf ([def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]).
Thus the open square over $k_0$ is Cartesian. Base changing gives
the scheme-Frobenius square in the statement, with the definitions
of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius].

The maps $g_Y^m=\operatorname{id}_{Y_0}\times\Spec(\gamma^m)$
preserve $X_0\times_{k_0}k$; their restrictions there are $g_X^m$.
They are isomorphisms, so the same inverse-image description of
opens gives the second Cartesian square. Finally, the structure
map of the geometric fiber of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]
is the second projection. Composing it with the displayed product
automorphism gives $\Spec(\gamma^m)a_Y$, and the same computation
applies to $X$. This proves the two asserted equalities.

attrs.title: Frobenius preserves an open subscheme defined over the finite field

objects.body:
Fix the global finite-field
datum and the coefficient
conventions, and let $(K,\varphi)\in D^b_{ctf,\mathrm W}(X,A)$. Then
the $m$-th iterate $F_{c,K}^{\,m}$ of the global geometric
Frobenius of [def-trf-frobenius-operators] is the composite

$$
F_{c,K}^{\,m}=R\Gamma_c(X,\varphi^{[m]})\circ g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*},
$$

where $\varphi^{[m]}$ is the iterated Weil isomorphism of
[def-trf-iterated-weil-map] and $g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}$ is the
compact-support base-change isomorphism along the automorphism
$g_\gamma^m$ of the
global geometric
Frobenius action.

## Proof

By [def-trf-frobenius-operators] the operator $F_{c,K}^{\,m}$ is
the composite of the canonical direct-image identification of
[def-weil-derived-direct-image] with the compact-support global
geometric Frobenius action of
[def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius] applied to
$\varphi^{[m]}$ of [def-trf-iterated-weil-map]. That action
transports the pair $(g_\gamma^m,Lg_\gamma^{m*}\varphi^{[m]})$ along
the compact-support base-change identification for the finite
automorphism $g_\gamma^m$: on the coefficient complex the transport
is $R\Gamma_c(X,\varphi^{[m]})$ by
[def-trf-coefficient-conventions], and on the scheme variable it is
the base-change isomorphism $g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}$. The comparison
between the scheme Frobenius and the geometric Frobenius that underlies
this transport is [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison], whose input
is the invariance of the site under the universal homeomorphism
$\Phi^m$ between them, [thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance];
no further choice enters. The composite is therefore the displayed
one.

attrs.title: Compact-support description of the global Frobenius

objects.body:
Fix the coefficient
conventions and an
admissible cohomological
correspondence $c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times_sX$ whose ordinary leg
$c_2$ is proper, and let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$. Then the global
operator $T_c(u)$ of [def-trf-global-operator] is natural in
the pair $(u,K)$: a morphism of correspondences
$u\to u'$ over a morphism $K\to K'$ in $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ induces
a commutative square relating $T_c(u)$ and $T_c(u')$.

## Proof

By [def-trf-global-operator] the operator $T_c(u)$ is the
composite of the five arrows displayed there. Each of them is
natural in $u$ and $K$: the unit of the adjunction
$Lc_2^*\dashv Rc_{2*}$ and the counit of the adjunction
$Rc_{1!}\dashv Rc_1^!$ of [def-trf-admissibility] are natural
transformations, the two comparison isomorphisms are the specified
structure isomorphisms of the six-operations package and are natural
in the coefficient object, and $R\Gamma_c(C,-)$ is a functor, so
that $R\Gamma_c(C,u)$ is natural in $u$ and in $K$ by
[def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. A composite of natural
arrows is natural, which is the displayed commutativity.

Fix the coefficient
conventions, let $c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times_sX$ be an
admissible cohomological
correspondence whose ordinary leg $c_2$ is
proper, and let
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ with correspondence
$u:Lc_2^*K\to Rc_1^!K$. Then the global operator $T_c(u)$ of
[def-trf-global-operator] is a morphism of
$D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$ in the sense of
[def-trf-categorical-trace]: every intermediate complex of the
composite defining $T_c(u)$ is compact-support cohomology of a
finite-Tor constructible
complex.

## Proof

By [def-trf-coefficient-conventions] the source and the target of
$T_c(u)$ are $R\Gamma_c(X,K)$, which lies in
$D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$ by
[prop-trf-compact-support-perfectness], and
$D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$ of [def-trf-categorical-trace] is a
full subcategory of $D(A)$, so it
suffices to see that the composite of
[def-trf-global-operator] is formed in
$D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$, i.e. that its intermediate complexes are
compact-support cohomology of finite-Tor constructible complexes in
the sense of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]:
$Lc_2^*K$ is finite-Tor constructible, so
$R\Gamma_c(C,Lc_2^*K)\in D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$; the identification
$Rc_{2*}\cong Rc_{2!}$ for the proper $c_2$ shows that
$Rc_{2*}Lc_2^*K\cong Rc_{2!}Lc_2^*K$ is finite-Tor constructible as
well, so $R\Gamma_c(X,Rc_{2*}Lc_2^*K)\in D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$;
finally $Rc_1^!K$ is finite-Tor constructible by item (3) of
[def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility], as required by the
admissibility of
[def-trf-admissibility], so that $R\Gamma_c(C,Rc_1^!K)$ and,
by the identification
$R\Gamma_c(X,Rc_{1!}Rc_1^!K)\cong R\Gamma_c(C,Rc_1^!K)$ of
[def-trf-global-operator] composed with
[def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed],
$R\Gamma_c(X,Rc_{1!}Rc_1^!K)$ are compact-support cohomology of
finite-Tor constructible complexes. Each of these four complexes is
therefore an object of $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$, which is the
assertion.

attrs.title: The global operator is an endomorphism of a perfect complex

objects.body:
In the setting of [def-trf-global-operator], let
$K'\to K\to K''\to K'[1]$ be a distinguished triangle in
$D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ and let $(u',u,u'')$ be a morphism of the
corresponding triangles of the functors $Lc_2^*$ and $Rc_1^!$.
Then the global operators of [def-trf-global-operator] fit into a
morphism of distinguished triangles

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
R\Gamma_c(X,K')&\xrightarrow{\ T_c(u')\ }&R\Gamma_c(X,K')\\
\Big\downarrow&&\Big\downarrow\\
R\Gamma_c(X,K)&\xrightarrow{\ T_c(u)\ }&R\Gamma_c(X,K)\\
\Big\downarrow&&\Big\downarrow\\
R\Gamma_c(X,K'')&\xrightarrow{\ T_c(u'')\ }&R\Gamma_c(X,K'').
\end{array}
$$

## Proof

By [def-trf-global-operator] the global operator is the composite
of the counit of the adjunction $Rc_{2,!}\dashv Rc_2^!$, the
identification $R\Gamma_c(X,Rc_{2,*}Lc_2^*K)\cong R\Gamma_c(C,Lc_2^*K)$, the map $R\Gamma_c(C,u)$ and the
identification $R\Gamma_c(C,Rc_1^!K)\cong R\Gamma_c(X,Rc_{1,!}Rc_1^!K)$
with its counit. Each of these constructions is a natural
transformation of exact functors in the coefficient object: the
functors $Lc_2^*$, $Rc_1^!$, $Rc_{i,*}$, $Rc_{i,!}$,
$R\Gamma_c$ are exact (the admissibility of
[def-trf-admissibility] supplies the adjunctions and
[prop-trf-compact-support-perfectness] the perfectness needed for
the compact-support identifications), the units and counits of
adjunctions are natural, and the exchange identifications are
compatible with base change. Hence, the squares commuting by [lem-trf-global-operator-naturality], the composite is compatible with
distinguished triangles, which is the assertion.

attrs.title: The global operator is triangulated in the coefficient

objects.body:
Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions, $A=A_{E,n}$, $s=\Spec k$, and let $T$ be
separated finite type
and proper over $s$
with exceptionally admissible
structure morphism $a_T:T\to s$. Identify
$\omega_s=Ra_s^!A_s=A_s$ ($a_s=\operatorname{id}_s$) and
$\End_{D(s,A)}(A_s)=\End_{D(A)}(A)=A$ via $R\Gamma(s,-)$. Then for
every Borel–Moore section $\alpha:A_T\to\omega_T$ of
[def-trf-borel-moore-pushforward],

$$
\int_T\alpha=(a_T)_*\alpha\in A,
$$

where $\int_T$ is the integration of [def-trf-integration] and
$(a_T)_*$ the pushforward of [def-trf-borel-moore-pushforward]
along the proper morphism $h=a_T:T\to T'=s$.

## Proof

Take $h=a_T$, $T'=s$ in [def-trf-borel-moore-pushforward]. Then
$\omega_{T'}=Ra_s^!A_s=A_s$ by [def-trf-dualizing-complex], and the
isomorphism $Ra_T^!\omega_s\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_T$ of
[thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition] (with $d=a_T$, $X=s$) is the
identity of $Ra_T^!A_s=\omega_T$, since the composition isomorphism
$Ra_T^!R\operatorname{id}_s^!\cong Ra_T^!$ for the identity is the
identity by the unit coherence of the exchange data. Hence
$(a_T)_*\alpha$ is the composite

$$
A_s\xrightarrow{\eta_{a_T}}Ra_{T*}A_T
\xrightarrow{Ra_{T*}\alpha}Ra_{T*}\omega_T
\cong Ra_{T!}Ra_T^!A_s\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{a_T}}A_s .
$$

Applying the $A$-linear equivalence
$R\Gamma(s,-):D(s,A)\to D(A)$ ($k$ algebraically closed) term by
term, the first arrow becomes the map $\eta^*$ of
[def-trf-integration] (composed with $Ra_{T*}\cong Ra_{T!}$, which
commutes with $Ra_{T*}\alpha\leftrightarrow Ra_{T!}\alpha$ by
naturality of that identification), the second becomes
$R\Gamma(\tau)$ with $\tau=\alpha$, and the last becomes
$\varepsilon_{a_\beta}$ with $\beta=T$. So the two composites
$A\to A$ agree, i.e. $\int_T\alpha=(a_T)_*\alpha$ under
$\End_{D(A)}(A)=A$.

attrs.title: Integration is pushforward to the point

objects.body:
Fix the coefficient
conventions, $A=A_{E,n}$, $s=\Spec k$, and let $T$ be a
separated finite-type scheme over $s$ which is a finite disjoint union

$$
T=\coprod_{\beta\in B}\beta
$$

of open-and-closed subschemes $j_\beta:\beta\hookrightarrow T$, each
proper over $s$. Then $T$ is proper over $s$. For
$\tau:A_T\to\omega_{T,A}$ and $\beta\in B$ define the *restriction*

$$
\tau|_\beta:
A_\beta\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Lj_\beta^*A_T
\xrightarrow{Lj_\beta^*\tau}Lj_\beta^*\omega_{T,A}
\cong Rj_\beta^!\omega_{T,A}\cong\omega_{\beta,A},
$$

using the equality $Rj_\beta^!\cong Lj_\beta^*$ for the open immersion
$j_\beta$ ([prop-functor-package], item (6), relative dimension $0$)
and the identification of [thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition]
(this restriction makes sense without any properness). Then

$$
\int_T\tau=\sum_{\beta\in B}\int_\beta(\tau|_\beta),
$$

where $\int_T,\int_\beta$ are the integrations of
[def-trf-integration] and $\omega_{T,A}$ is the
dualizing complex of
[def-trf-dualizing-complex]; for $B=\emptyset$ both sides are $0$.
In particular, if $c$ is an admissible correspondence whose fixed
scheme $F=\operatorname{Fix}(c)$ of [def-trf-fixed-scheme] has
finitely many open-and-closed components $\beta\in\pi_0(F)$, each
proper over $s$, then $F$ is proper and
$\int_F\tau=\sum_{\beta\in\pi_0(F)}\int_\beta(\tau|_\beta)$, the
restrictions being those of [def-trf-local-term].

## Proof

*Properness.* The morphism $a_T:T\to s$ is separated and of finite
type. It is universally closed: for any $s'\to s$ the base change
$T_{s'}=\coprod_\beta\beta_{s'}$ is a finite disjoint union of
open-and-closed pieces, a closed subset $Z\subseteq T_{s'}$ is the
finite union of the closed subsets $Z\cap\beta_{s'}$ of the
$\beta_{s'}$, and its image in $s'$ is the finite union of their
images, which are closed because each $\beta\to s$ is universally
closed. Hence $T$ is proper over $s$ and $\int_T$ of
[def-trf-integration] is defined.

*Splitting.* The pro-etale site of a disjoint union of schemes is the
disjoint union of the sites ([def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]), so
$D(T,A)\cong\prod_{\beta}D(\beta,A)$ via $(Lj_\beta^*)_\beta$, and the
six operations decompose
accordingly: in particular
$R\Gamma(T,-)\cong\prod_\beta R\Gamma(\beta,-)$ (the product is a direct
sum over the finite set $B$),
the unit $A\to R\Gamma(T,A_T)$ of [def-trf-integration] is the
tuple of the units of the components, and the counit
$\varepsilon_{a_T}$ is the tuple of the counits
$\varepsilon_{a_\beta}$ (the adjunctions of [def-trf-integration]
decompose with the products, by the compatibility of the six-functor
formalism with disjoint unions; here $a_\beta=a_Tj_\beta$ and
$Rj_\beta^!=Lj_\beta^*$). Under this decomposition $\omega_{T,A}$
corresponds to the tuple of the $Lj_\beta^*\omega_{T,A}\cong
\omega_{\beta,A}$ of [thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition], and
$\tau$ to the tuple of its restrictions $\tau|_\beta$ defined above.
Hence the composite displayed in
[def-trf-integration] for $\int_T\tau$ is the tuple of the
composites defining the $\int_\beta(\tau|_\beta)$; the unit
$A\to\bigoplus_\beta R\Gamma(\beta,A_\beta)$ is the diagonal and the
counit $\bigoplus_\beta R\Gamma(\beta,\omega_{\beta,A})\to A$ is the sum
map, so the composite is the sum of the component composites, which is
the displayed identity. If $B=\emptyset$ then $T=\emptyset$,
$R\Gamma(T,-)=0$ and both sides vanish.

*The fixed-scheme case.* For $T=F$ and $B=\pi_0(F)$, finite by
hypothesis ([def-trf-fixed-scheme]), the restriction $\tau|_\beta$
above is literally the composite used in [def-trf-local-term], so the
last assertion is the special case just proved.

attrs.title: Integration splits over the open–closed components

objects.body:
Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions, $A=A_{E,n}$, $s=\Spec k$, and let $\beta$ be
separated finite type
and proper over $s$
with exceptionally admissible
structure morphism $a_\beta:\beta\to s$. Then the integration
$\int_\beta$ of [def-trf-integration] is $A$-linear: for
$\tau,\tau'\in\Hom_{D(\beta,A)}(A_\beta,\omega_{\beta,A})$ and
$a\in A$,

$$
\int_\beta(\tau+a\tau')=\int_\beta(\tau)+a\int_\beta(\tau').
$$

## Proof

The integration is the composite
$A\xrightarrow{\eta^*}R\Gamma(\beta,A_\beta) \xrightarrow{R\Gamma(\tau)}R\Gamma(\beta,\omega_{\beta,A}) \xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{a_\beta}}A$ of
[def-trf-integration]. The first arrow is built from the unit of
the adjunction $La_\beta^*\dashv Ra_{\beta*}$ of
[def-weil-derived-direct-image] and the identification
$Ra_{\beta*}\cong Ra_{\beta!}$ of
[def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]: it does not depend on
$\tau$. The last arrow is $R\Gamma(s,-)$ applied to the counit of
the adjunction $Ra_{\beta!}\dashv Ra_\beta^!$ of
[def-trf-admissibility] at $\omega_{\beta,A}=Ra_\beta^!A_s$ of
[def-trf-dualizing-complex], and $R\Gamma(s,-)$ is an
$A$-linear functor, so this arrow is $A$-linear; it also does not
depend on $\tau$. The middle arrow is $R\Gamma(\beta,-)$ applied
to $\tau$, and $A$-linearity of the compact-support cohomology of
[def-trf-coefficient-conventions] gives
$R\Gamma(\beta,\tau+a\tau')=R\Gamma(\beta,\tau)+aR\Gamma(\beta,\tau')$;
the exceptional inverse image enters only through
$\omega_{\beta,A}=Ra_\beta^!A_s$, by the dualizing-complex
construction of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Composing
the three $A$-linear arrows gives the displayed identity.

Let $(K,\varphi)\in D^b_{ctf,\mathrm W}(X,A)$ be a
strict Weil complex under the
conventions of [def-trf-strict-weil-complex], with
$g_\gamma=g_X$ the
geometric-Frobenius automorphism
of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius], and let

$$
\varphi^{[m]}:Lg_\gamma^{m*}K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }K
\qquad(m\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1})
$$

be the iterated Weil isomorphism
of [def-trf-iterated-weil-map]. Then for all
$m,n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$ the identity

$$
\varphi^{[m+n]}=\varphi^{[m]}\circ Lg_\gamma^{m*}\varphi^{[n]}
$$

holds after the canonical pullback identifications
$Lg_\gamma^{m*}Lg_\gamma^{n*}K\cong L(g_\gamma^m\circ g_\gamma^n)^*K=Lg_\gamma^{m+n*}K$.

## Proof

By [def-trf-strict-weil-complex], $\varphi$ is an isomorphism
$Lg_\gamma^*K\to K$ with $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$; by
[def-trf-scheme-frobenius], $g_\gamma$ is an automorphism of
$X$ satisfying $g_\gamma^{m+n}=g_\gamma^m\circ g_\gamma^n$, so that
the derived pullbacks satisfy $Lg_\gamma^{m+n*}\cong Lg_\gamma^{m*}Lg_\gamma^{n*}$ under the canonical identification
displayed in the statement. Under this identification both sides of
the identity are the composite of the $m+n$ maps

$$
Lg_\gamma^{m+n*}K\xrightarrow{Lg_\gamma^{m+n-1*}\varphi}\cdots
\xrightarrow{Lg_\gamma^*\varphi}K
$$

of [def-trf-strict-weil-complex]: the left-hand side is the
composite defining $\varphi^{[m+n]}$ in
[def-trf-iterated-weil-map], while the right-hand side is the
concatenation of the composites defining $\varphi^{[m]}$ and
$\varphi^{[n]}$ in [def-trf-iterated-weil-map]; the
concatenation is identified with the composite of the $m+n$ maps by
the associativity of composition and the naturality of the canonical
pullback identifications.

attrs.title: Cocycle identity for the iterated Weil isomorphism

objects.body:
Fix the coefficient
conventions and a strict Weil complex $(K,\varphi)$, and let
$x\in|X_0|$ be a closed point of degree $d=d_x=[\kappa(x):\Fq]$.

1. *The lifts above $x$.* The geometric points of $X$
above $x$ are exactly the $d_x$ distinct points
$$
\bar z_i:=g_\gamma^{\,i}(\bar z_0)\qquad(i\in\mathbf Z/d_x\mathbf Z),
$$
for any one such point $\bar z_0$; the cyclic group generated by
$g_\gamma$ permutes them transitively. (For $d_x\mid m$, every
$\bar z_i$ is a fixed point of the $m$-th iterate $\Phi^m$, by
[thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points], so the local Frobenius
$F_{y,m}$ of [def-trf-frobenius-operators] is defined at every
rational point $y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ above $x$.)
1. *The canonical transports.* For $i\geq0$, write
$T_i:K_{\bar z_i}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }K_{\bar z_0}$ for the composite
$$
K_{\bar z_i}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
\bigl(Lg_\gamma^{i*}K\bigr)_{\bar z_0}
\xrightarrow{\ \varphi^{[i]}_{\bar z_0}\ }
K_{\bar z_0},
$$
whose first arrow is the canonical identification of the pro-etale
stalk of the pullback with the stalk at the translated point
($\bigl(Lg_\gamma^{i*}K\bigr)_{\bar z_0}\cong K_{g_\gamma^i\bar z_0} =K_{\bar z_i}$). The $T_i$ depend on the choice of $\bar z_0$
(they are canonical *for the given cyclic ordering*), and satisfy
the cocycle identities
$$
T_{i+j}=T_i\circ\bigl(\text{the transport }T_j
\text{ computed at }\bar z_i\bigr)
$$
transported from the cocycle identity
$\varphi^{[i+j]}=\varphi^{[i]}\circ Lg_\gamma^{i*}\varphi^{[j]}$ of
[lem-trf-iterated-weil-cocycle] through the canonical stalk
identifications.
1. *Conjugacy.* Let $m\geq1$ be a multiple of $d_x$, and
let $y_0,y_1,\ldots,y_{d_x-1}\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ be the
rational points above $x$, numbered so that
$\bar y_i=\bar z_i$. Then
$$
F_{y_i,m}=T_i^{-1}\circ F_{y_0,m}\circ T_i
\qquad\text{on }K_{\bar y_i},
$$
in particular the operators at the various lifts are conjugate, the
traces $\operatorname{tr}_A(F_{y_i,m}\mid K_{\bar y_i})$ are equal,
and the conjugacy class of the one-circuit operator $F_{y_0,d_x}$ is
independent of the lift $\bar z_0$ (the numbering and the class are
fixed by the orbit).

## Proof

*(1)* A geometric point above $x$ is a morphism
$\bar z:\Spec k\to X$ with image the closed point $x$ and is given
by a homomorphism $\sigma_z:\kappa(x)=\Fq[t]/(\mu_x)\to k$, i.e. by the choice of a root $\sigma_z(t)\in k$ of the minimal polynomial
$\mu_x$. All roots of $\mu_x$ lie in the fixed finite subfield
$\mathbb F_{q^{d_x}}\subset k$ (the unique one), so the geometric
points above $x$ correspond to the $d_x$ roots, i.e. to the
$d_x$ embeddings; they are permuted transitively by the cyclic group
generated by the geometric Frobenius $g_\gamma$ (the $q^{-1}$-power
map on the roots), for the same reason the Frobenius permutes the
roots of an irreducible polynomial over a finite field transitively;
the distinct points in the orbit are $g_\gamma^i(\bar z_0)$,
$0\leq i<d_x$, because the stabilizer of a root of $\mu_x$ in the
cyclic group of $g_\gamma$ equals the Galois group of
$\Fq[t]/(\mu_x)$ acting on it and the orbit has exactly
$d_x=[\kappa(x):\Fq]$ elements. This is the first assertion; the
fixed-point assertion for $d_x\mid m$ is
[thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points] (the $k$-point $\bar z_i$ is
a $k$-rational point of $\operatorname{Fix}(\Phi^m)$).

*(2)* The canonical identification of the first arrow is the
standard colimit description of the pro-etale stalk functor composed
with the morphism of sites induced by $g_\gamma^i$ (for a geometric
point $\bar z$, $L\bar y^*(Lf^*K)\cong K_{f\bar y}$ canonically,
natural in $K$); $\varphi^{[i]}$ is that of
[def-trf-iterated-weil-map]. The cocycle identity of
[lem-trf-iterated-weil-cocycle] is the
stalkwise form of

$$
\varphi^{[i+j]}=\varphi^{[i]}\circ Lg_\gamma^{i*}\varphi^{[j]}
$$

under the canonical identifications
$(Lg_\gamma^{i*}Lg_\gamma^{j*}K)_{\bar z_0}\cong (Lg_\gamma^{i+j*}K)_{\bar z_0}\cong K_{\bar z_{i+j}}$ (the second is
the naturality of the stalk identification in the functoriality
$g_\gamma^{i+j}=g_\gamma^i\circ g_\gamma^j$).

*(3)* For a fixed point $\bar z$ of $\Phi^m$ the transport
$\tau_{z,m}$ of [def-trf-frobenius-operators] is the composite

$$
K_{\bar z}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
\bigl(Lg_\gamma^{m*}K\bigr)_{\bar z}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
K_{\bar z}
$$

of the canonical pullback-stalk identification with the canonical
identification $K_{g_\gamma^m\bar z}\cong K_{\bar z}$ supplied by
$\kappa^{(m)}$ of [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison] and the
fixed-point property $\Phi^m\bar z=\bar z$; hence, on the orbit,
the composite $T_{i}\circ F_{y_0,m}\circ T_i^{-1}$ and the operator
$F_{y_i,m}$ are the same morphism $K_{\bar z_i}\to K_{\bar z_i}$:
both are the stalkwise transport of the composite

$$
\varphi^{[m]}\circ Lg_\gamma^{m*}\varphi^{[i]}
\ \longleftrightarrow\ \varphi^{[i]}\circ Lg_\gamma^{i*}\varphi^{[m]}
\xrightarrow{\ \text{cocycle}\ }
\varphi^{[i+m]}
$$

around the loop $\bar z_i\xrightarrow{g_\gamma^i}\bar z_0\cong g_\gamma^m\bar z_0\xrightarrow{g_\gamma^i}\bar z_i$ (the two
routes around it give the same morphism since the canonical
identifications compose and the two factorizations of
$\varphi^{[i+m]}$ are the same by the cocycle identity of (2)).
This gives the displayed conjugacy; the equality of the traces uses
the conjugacy-invariance (1) of
[prop-trf-trace-formal-laws] applied to the perfect complex
$K_{\bar y_i}\in D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$
([prop-trf-compact-support-perfectness]), and the independence
for $m=d_x$ follows likewise, as every choice of $\bar z_0$ is
among the orbit points and the operators are conjugate.

attrs.title: Conjugacy of the local Frobenius along the Frobenius orbit

objects.body:
Let $c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times X$ be an admissible correspondence with
$\operatorname{Fix}(c)=F$, coefficient $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ and
$u:c_2^*K\to c_1^!K$ ([def-trf-correspondence]), and let $y\in F(k)$ be a
geometric fixed point which is an open-and-closed component of $F$. Say
that $c$ is *contracting at $y$* if $c_1^{-1}(y)$ is the reduced point $y$,
$c_2(y)=y$, and the ideal sheaves on $C$ satisfy

$$
c_2^{\cdot}(\mathcal I_y)^n\subset\mathcal I_{y,C}^{\,n+1}\qquad\text{for some }n\geq1,
$$

where $\mathcal I_{y,C}=c_1^{\cdot}(\mathcal I_y)\mathcal O_C$ is the ideal of
the reduced point $y\subset C$. This is Varshavsky's "$c$ stabilizes
$Z=\{y\}$ and is contracting near $Z$"
([Def. 2.1.1](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0505564)), with the two legs
interchanged to match the convention $u:c_2^*K\to c_1^!K$; the stabilizing
inclusion $c_2^{\cdot}(\mathcal I_y)\subset\mathcal I_{y,C}$ follows from
$c_2(y)=y$, and the condition holds with $n=1$ whenever the map induced by
$c_2$ on the cotangent space at $y$ is zero.

1. (Contracting local terms.) If $c$ is contracting at $y$, then the
restriction $\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)|_y$, and hence the local term
$\operatorname{LT}_y(u)$ of [def-trf-local-term], depend only on the stalk
$K_{\bar y}$ and on the stalk map $u_{\bar y}:K_{\bar y}\to K_{\bar y}$
induced by $u$ (via $c_2(y)=y=c_1(y)$):
$\operatorname{LT}_y(u)=\operatorname{tr}_A(u_{\bar y}\mid K_{\bar y})$.
No invertibility of $u$ is required.
1. (Zero-stalk vanishing.) If $c$ is contracting at $y$ and $K_{\bar y}=0$,
then $\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)|_y=0$ and $\operatorname{LT}_y(u)=0$, for
every coefficient morphism $u$.
1. (Smooth-curve form.) In the smooth-curve setting of
[d-curve-pieces] — $X_0$ smooth of pure dimension one, $m\ge1$,
$x\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ with geometric point $\bar x$ — let
$v:L\Phi^{m*}K\to K$ be either the scheme-Frobenius map
$u_m=\varphi^{[m]}\circ\kappa^{(m)}_K$ of [def-trf-iterated-weil-map]
(the map written $\varphi_m$ in [d-curve-pieces]) or an arbitrary,
not necessarily invertible, Frobenius coefficient morphism
$L\Phi^{m*}K\to K$ (in the sense of
[def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism] for $\Phi^m$, the
$q^m$-power Frobenius of $X_0\times_{k_0}\mathbf F_{q^m}$; for
instance the iterate $\psi_m$ of a Frobenius coefficient morphism
$\psi$), and consider the graph correspondence of
$(\Phi^m,v)$ of [def-trf-graph-correspondence], assumed admissible
as throughout so that its trace class is defined. If $K_{\bar x}=0$,
then the local term $\operatorname{LT}_{\bar x}(v)$ at the fixed
point $\bar x$ is zero.

## Proof

*The stalk of the trace-class source.* By [def-trf-trace-class-source]
the source is $\mathcal H_c(K)=R\mathcal Hom_A(c_2^*K,c_1^!K)$. Its stalk
at $y$ is **not** $R\mathcal Hom_A(K_{\bar y},K_{\bar y})$: restriction to
a point commutes with $i^!$ on internal Hom, but not with $i^*$. For
$X=\mathbf A^1$, $j:\mathbf G_m\hookrightarrow X$, $K=j_!A$ and the graph
of a Frobenius (so that $c_2^*K\simeq K$ and $c_1^!K=K$), internal-Hom
adjunction gives $R\mathcal Hom_A(j_!A,j_!A)\simeq Rj_*A$, whose
degree-zero stalk at $0$ is $A$ (the punctured strictly henselian curve is
connected), although $K_0=0$. Hence (1) and (2) cannot be read off from
the stalk: the trace map of [lem-trf-trace-map-from-external-duality] is
local on $F$, but its source at $y$ sees more than $(K_{\bar y},u_{\bar y})$.
A nonzero source can still map to zero, and for contracting correspondences
it does; this is the content of (1) and (2).

*(1) and (2).* These are the contracting-correspondence theorem of
Varshavsky, [Thm. 2.1.3](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0505564), translated
into the present conventions. In Varshavsky's convention a $c$-morphism is
$c_1^*\mathcal F\to c_2^!\mathcal F$; interchanging the legs, his
hypothesis "$c$ stabilizes $Z$ and is contracting near $Z$" for
$Z=\{y\}$ reads
$c_2^{\cdot}(\mathcal I_y)\subset c_1^{\cdot}(\mathcal I_y)\mathcal O_C$ and
$c_2^{\cdot}(\mathcal I_y)^n\subset(c_1^{\cdot}(\mathcal I_y)\mathcal O_C)^{n+1}$,
which is the hypothesis above. His conclusion, for the open-and-closed
component $\beta=\{y\}$ of $F$, which meets $Z$, is
$\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)|_y=\operatorname{Tr}_{c|_Z}(u|_Z)|_y$ and
$\operatorname{LT}_y(u)=\operatorname{LT}_y(u|_Z)$, where
$c|_Z:c_1^{-1}(Z)_{\mathrm{red}}\to Z\times Z$ is the correspondence
induced on $Z$ and $u|_Z$ the restricted coefficient morphism (his 1.5.6).
Since $c_1^{-1}(y)=y$ is reduced, $c|_Z$ is the identity correspondence of
the point $y\cong\Spec k$, with coefficient $K_{\bar y}$ and morphism the
stalk map $u_{\bar y}$; its local term is
$\operatorname{tr}_A(u_{\bar y}\mid K_{\bar y})$ by
[lem-trf-local-term-point]. This proves (1), and (2) is the case
$K_{\bar y}=0$, where $\operatorname{tr}_A(0\mid0)=0$. Varshavsky's theorem
is proved by specialization to the normal cone of $Z$ (his §§1.3–1.4 and
2.1); it holds for every $c$-morphism and for the finite coefficient rings
$A=A_{E,n}$ (his §1.1), and nothing is inverted. Its proof reduces, via
the additivity of trace classes along the open–closed decomposition
