$X=Z\sqcup U$ and proper pushforward from $Z$, precisely to the vanishing
(2) for $j_!j^*K$, which is then shown by the normal-cone argument; the
blueprint quotes this argument and does not reprove it.

*(3).* The graph correspondence of $(\Phi^m,v)$ has
$C=X$, $c_1=\operatorname{id}_X$, $c_2=\Phi^m$ and fixed scheme
$\operatorname{Fix}(\Phi^m)$ by [def-trf-graph-correspondence]. By
[thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points] this fixed scheme is the disjoint
union of copies of $\Spec k$, one for each point of
$X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$; in particular it is finite over $k$, hence
proper with finitely many open-and-closed components, so the local
terms of [def-trf-local-term] are defined, and the geometric point
$\bar x$ over $x$ is one of these components, an isolated reduced fixed
point. The graph is contracting at $\bar x$: $c_1^{-1}(\bar x)=\bar x$,
$\Phi^m(\bar x)=\bar x$, and if $t_i$ are affine coordinates with
$a_i=t_i(x)\in\mathbf F_{q^m}$, then
$\Phi^{m\cdot}(t_i-a_i)=t_i^{q^m}-a_i=(t_i-a_i)^{q^m}$, so
$\Phi^{m\cdot}(\mathcal I_{\bar x})\mathcal O_X\subset\mathcal I_{\bar x}^{\,q^m}\subset\mathcal I_{\bar x}^{\,2}$
as $q^m\geq2$; this holds for every separated finite-type $X_0$, not only
for curves. Its stalk map is
$v_{\bar x}:K_{\bar x}=(L\Phi^{m*}K)_{\bar x}\to K_{\bar x}$, using
$\Phi^m(\bar x)=\bar x$. Applying (2) with $y=\bar x$ and $u=v$ gives
$\operatorname{LT}_{\bar x}(v)=0$ when $K_{\bar x}=0$; since (1) and
(2) use no invertibility of $u$, this holds both for the
scheme-Frobenius map $u_m$ and for an arbitrary Frobenius coefficient
morphism.

attrs.title: Locality and zero-stalk vanishing of the local term

objects.body:
Fix the coefficient
conventions, let $c$ be an
admissible correspondence with
fixed scheme $F$ over $s=\Spec k$ (not necessarily proper), and let
$\beta\subseteq F$ be an open-and-closed subscheme with
$\beta\simeq\Spec k$, finite etale over $s$ in relative dimension
$0$ (for instance a component $\beta\in\pi_0(F)$ of this form when
$F$ is proper with finitely many open-and-closed components, or the
reduced point component $B_{\bar x}$ of a point $\bar x$ of $F$). Then
the local term
$\operatorname{LT}_\beta(u)=\int_\beta(\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)|_\beta)$
of [def-trf-local-term], where
$\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)|_\beta=j_\beta^*\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)$, is
the element of $A$ corresponding to
the trace class
$\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)|_\beta$ under the canonical identification

$$
\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\beta,A)}\bigl(A_\beta,\omega_{\beta,A}\bigr)
\cong\operatorname{End}_{D(A)}(A)\cong A
$$

of the point case $\beta\simeq\Spec k$. In particular this computes
$\operatorname{LT}_{\bar x}(u)=\operatorname{LT}_{B_{\bar x}}(u)$ at
every point $\bar x$ with reduced open-and-closed point component
$B_{\bar x}$.

## Proof

The trace class
$\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)$ and hence its restriction
$\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)|_\beta$ of [def-trf-local-term] are
defined for the admissible $c$ by
[prop-trf-trace-class-unconditional]. Being isomorphic to $\Spec k$, the open-and-closed subscheme $\beta$
of the fixed scheme of [def-trf-fixed-scheme] is a
separated finite-type
proper $s$-scheme, and (as in [def-trf-local-term]) it is taken with structure morphism $a_\beta$ admissible in
the sense of [def-trf-admissibility], and the purity clause of
[prop-functor-package] in relative dimension $0$ identifies
$\omega_{\beta,A}=Ra_\beta^!A_s$ of
[def-trf-dualizing-complex] with $A_\beta$, so that
$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\beta,A)}(A_\beta,\omega_{\beta,A})\cong \operatorname{End}_{D(A)}(A)\cong A$.
For $\tau:A_\beta\to\omega_{\beta,A}$ the integration is the
composite $A\xrightarrow{\eta^*}R\Gamma(\beta,A_\beta) \xrightarrow{R\Gamma(\tau)}R\Gamma(\beta,\omega_{\beta,A}) \xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{a_\beta}}A$ of
[def-trf-integration]. For $\tau=\operatorname{id}_{A_\beta}$
under the identification $\omega_{\beta,A}\cong A_\beta$, the middle
arrow is the identity of $R\Gamma(\beta,A_\beta)$ and the composite
of the first and last arrows is the composite of the unit and the
counit of the adjunction $Ra_{\beta!}\dashv Ra_\beta^!$ of
[def-trf-admissibility], which is the identity of $A$ by the
triangle identity of the adjunction; since the integration is
$A$-linear by [lem-trf-integration-linear], it is the identity
map on all of $A$. Applying this to
$\tau=\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)|_\beta$ gives the last assertion, by the
definition of the local term in [def-trf-local-term].

attrs.title: The local term at a point component

objects.body:
Let $j:U\hookrightarrow Y$ be an
open immersion of
finite-type $k$-schemes, and use the
finite coefficient ring $A$.
For a bounded
constructible complex $K$ of
finite Tor amplitude, its
extension by zero
$j_!K$ belongs to $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$. Its
cohomological range
and Tor amplitude may be taken to be those of $K$.

## Proof

Exactness in [def-weil-extension-by-zero] gives
$\mathcal H^r(j_!K)=j_!\mathcal H^r(K)$, so the range does not grow.
Take a common finite locally closed stratification of $U$
witnessing constructibility of the finitely many nonzero
$\mathcal H^r(K)$ in [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility].
Each stratum is locally closed in $Y$, and adding the closed
complement $Y\setminus U$ gives a finite stratification of $Y$.
The restrictions of the extended cohomology sheaves are the same
finite locally constant sheaves on these strata and the zero sheaf
on the complement. This proves constructibility.

If the Tor amplitude in [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] is
$[a,b]$, apply [lem-trf-open-tensor] with an arbitrary sheaf
$M$ of $A$-modules on $Y$, in degree zero. Its restriction
$j^*M$ is in degree zero, so $K\otimes_A^Lj^*M$ has no
cohomology outside $[a,b]$. Exact extension by zero preserves
that vanishing, giving the same Tor bound for $j_!K$.

attrs.title: Extension by zero preserves constructibility and Tor amplitude

objects.body:
Use the finite coefficient ring
$A=A_{E,n}$. Let

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
U'&\xrightarrow{g_U}&U\\
{\scriptstyle j'}\downarrow&&\downarrow{\scriptstyle j}\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y
\end{array}
$$

be a Cartesian square with $j,j'$
open immersions.
On the small pro-etale sites,
the extension-by-zero functors
and derived pullbacks
admit a canonical natural isomorphism

$$
b_g:Lg^*j_!\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!Lg_U^*.
$$

Its restriction to $U'$ is the identity, after the pullback
identifications. These isomorphisms respect identity squares and
pasting of Cartesian squares.
(Source for the etale version:
[Stacks, Tag 03S6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03S6),
Lemma 59.70.5, the underived statement $j'_!f'^{-1}=f^{-1}j_!$ on
sheaves; the derived form and the compatibilities are proved below.)

## Proof

Restriction along an open immersion is localization of the site:
an object $V\to U$ is also an object over $Y$.
For a sheaf $Q$ on $Y'$, the direct-image formula gives

$$
(j^*g_*Q)(V)=Q(V\times_Y Y')
=(g_{U*}j'^*Q)(V).
$$

The equality respects restrictions and coverings on the site of
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Thus $j^*g_*=g_{U*}j'^*$,
with all comparison maps specified on sections.

The exact functor $j'^*$ preserves injectives and K-injectives:
its left adjoint $j'_!$ is exact by
[def-weil-extension-by-zero]. For K-injectives this follows
directly by applying the adjunction to Hom complexes against an
acyclic complex. Thus a K-injective resolution of $Q$ computes
both sides of

$$
j^*Rg_*Q\simeq Rg_{U*}j'^*Q,
$$

using [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. Taking left adjoints,
with the exact inverse-image pullbacks of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], gives
$Lg^*j_!\simeq j'_!Lg_U^*$. This defines $b_g$.
On $U'$ the section equality is the identity, so its mate has the
stated normalization. The section equalities for two pasted squares
compose to the equality for the outer square. The uniqueness of
left adjoints with their adjunction data proves the pasting and
identity assertions. This proof uses no claim that ordinary
geometric stalks detect arbitrary pro-etale sheaves.

attrs.title: Open-square exchange from restriction of direct image

objects.body:
Let $j:U\hookrightarrow Y$ be an
open immersion, and use
the finite coefficient ring
$A$. For $K\in D(U,A)$ and $M\in D(Y,A)$, there is a natural
isomorphism

$$
(j_!K)\otimes_A^LM\simeq j_!(K\otimes_A^Lj^*M),
$$

where $j_!$ is extension by
zero, tensor is the derived
tensor product, and $j^*$ is the
derived pullback.

## Proof

For sheaves, internal Hom restricts to internal Hom on an open
localized site: on any object over $U$, both are morphisms on the
same slice site. Tensor–Hom adjunction and $j_!\dashv j^*$ of
[def-weil-extension-by-zero] give, for sheaves $P,M,N$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}(j_!P\otimes_A M,N)
&\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(P,j^*\mathcal Hom_A(M,N))\\
&\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(P,\mathcal Hom_A(j^*M,j^*N))\\
&\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(j_!(P\otimes_Aj^*M),N).
\end{aligned}
$$

Yoneda gives the underived tensor identity and its naturality.

Choose a K-flat representative $P^\bullet$ for $K$ as in
[def-weil-derived-tensor]. The same identity on complexes
shows that $j_!P^\bullet$ is K-flat. Indeed, for an acyclic
$Q^\bullet$, $j^*Q^\bullet$ is acyclic because inverse image is
exact ([def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]), so
$P^\bullet\otimes_Aj^*Q^\bullet$ and its exact extension by zero
are acyclic. Extension by zero commutes with direct sums, being a
left adjoint, and therefore commutes with the direct-sum
totalization of the tensor complex. The underived identity on
these representatives is the required derived identity.

Use the finite coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$ of
[def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of
separated finite-type
schemes, let $Z$ be an auxiliary such scheme, and let $L\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, $Q\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$ in the
finite-Tor constructible
category. Then the canonical comparison

$$
Rf_*L\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L} Q
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
R(f\times\operatorname{id}_Z)_*\bigl(L\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L} Q\bigr)
$$

is an isomorphism, natural in $L$ and $Q$.

## Proof

Consider the Cartesian square

$$
\begin{gathered}
X\times Z \xrightarrow{f\times\operatorname{id}_Z} Y\times Z,\\
p_X:X\times Z\to X,\qquad p_Y:Y\times Z\to Y,\qquad
p_Z:X\times Z\to Z,\qquad p'_Z:Y\times Z\to Z,
\end{gathered}
$$

with $p_Z=p'_Z\circ(f\times\operatorname{id}_Z)$. Writing the external
product as
$L\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}Q=p_X^*L\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}p_Z^*Q =p_X^*L\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}(f\times\operatorname{id}_Z)^*\bigl(p'_Z{}^*Q\bigr)$,
the canonical comparison is the composite

$$
\begin{aligned}
Rf_*L\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}Q
= p_Y^*Rf_*L\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}p'_Z{}^*Q
&\longrightarrow
R(f\times\operatorname{id}_Z)_*\bigl(p_X^*L\bigr)
\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}p'_Z{}^*Q\\
&\longrightarrow
R(f\times\operatorname{id}_Z)_*\bigl(L\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}Q\bigr)
\end{aligned}
$$

of the base-change map along $p_Y$ and the projection map for the ordinary
direct image $R(f\times\operatorname{id}_Z)_*$. Neither map is an isomorphism
by a general theorem: $Z$ is an arbitrary finite-type scheme, so $p_Y$ is
smooth only when $Z$ is and smooth base change does not apply, and the
projection formula for $Rf_*$ (as opposed to $Rf_!$) is not an isomorphism in
general.

*Step 1: $\mathbf Z/N$-coefficients.* Put $N=\ell^n$, so that $A$ is a
$\mathbf Z/N$-algebra. With $K=k$, $X\leftarrow X'\leftarrow Y$ and
$\Spec K\leftarrow S'\leftarrow T$ of [lem-kun-0f1n] taken to be
$Z\leftarrow Z\times Y\leftarrow Z\times X$ and
$\Spec k\leftarrow Y\xleftarrow{f}X$, that lemma says precisely that for
every $E\in D(Z_{\Et},\mathbf Z/N)$ and $F\in D(X_{\Et},\mathbf Z/N)$ the
canonical map

$$
p'_Z{}^{*}E\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{\mathbf Z/N}p_Y^*Rf_*F
\longrightarrow
R(f\times\operatorname{id}_Z)_*\bigl(p_Z^*E\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{\mathbf Z/N}p_X^*F\bigr)
$$

is an isomorphism (its bounded form is [lem-kun-0f1j]). This is the
assertion for $\mathbf Z/N$-coefficients, up to the symmetry of the tensor
product.

*Step 2: coefficient transport to $A$.* Let $P$ be the bounded flat
$A$-model of $L$ given by [lem-sf-flat-model]. Both sides of the
comparison are exact in $Q$, so the finite $\varpi_E$-adic filtration
$Q\supseteq\varpi_EQ\supseteq\dots$ of a bounded complex (equivalently, the
triangles $\varpi_E^{i+1}\mathcal H^q\to\varpi_E^{i}\mathcal H^q\to
\varpi_E^{i}\mathcal H^q/\varpi_E^{i+1}\mathcal H^q$ on the cohomology
sheaves, together with the truncation triangles) reduces the assertion to
the case where $Q$ is a single sheaf of $\kappa$-modules,
$\kappa=A/(\varpi_E)$. For such $Q$,
$P\otimes_A Q=(P\otimes_A\kappa)\otimes_\kappa Q$ with $P\otimes_A\kappa$ a
complex of flat $\kappa$-module sheaves, and the comparison for
$(L,Q)$ over $A$ is the comparison for $(P\otimes_A\kappa,Q)$ over the
finite field $\kappa$. Step 1 and the proof of [lem-kun-0f1j] are linear
over the coefficient field — truncations, flat resolutions, filtered colimits
of constructible sheaves, the embedding of a constructible sheaf into a
finite sum of $\pi_{i*}$ of constant sheaves for finite $\pi_i$, and dimension
shifting — and apply verbatim with the finite field $\kappa$ in place of
$\mathbf F_\ell$; alternatively, $\kappa$ is a finite free
$\mathbf F_\ell$-module, so $\kappa$-linear constructible sheaves are
$\mathbf F_\ell$-constructible sheaves with a $\kappa$-action and the
$\kappa$-linear comparison is a direct summand of the $\mathbf F_\ell$-linear
one.

The composite is the canonical comparison, since both maps are natural in
their variables; naturality in $L$ and $Q$ follows from the functoriality of
the base-change and projection maps.
(*Provenance:* Stacks Project, Étale Cohomology, Lemma 59.97.8,
[Tag `0F1N`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F1N), which is
[lem-kun-0f1n] here, together with SGA 5, III, 1.1 and 1.6.4 for the
coefficient and site generality used here.)

attrs.title: Ordinary Kunneth for a general morphism

objects.body:
Let $p:C'\to C$ be proper, $c_i'=c_i p$, and let
$u':Lc_2'^*K\to Rc_1'^!K$ be a correspondence on $C'$. Then
$(\operatorname{id}_X,p):(C',c')\to(C,c)$ is a proper pushforward diagram
in the sense of [def-trf-coefficient-pushforward], with pushforward
correspondence $p_!u':=[\operatorname{id}_X,p]_!u'$, and the induced map of
fixed schemes is the proper base change $p_F:F'\to F$ of
[lem-trf-fixed-map-proper]. The compatibility

$$
\operatorname{Tr}_c(p_!u')=(p_F)_*\operatorname{Tr}_{c'}(u')
$$

(with $(p_F)_*$ the pushforward of Borel–Moore sections along the
proper $p_F$ of [def-trf-borel-moore-pushforward], sometimes written
$(p_F)_!$) is therefore the special case $f=\operatorname{id}_X$, $g=p$ of
[thm-trf-trace-proper-compatibility] (Varshavsky,
[loc. cit.](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0505564), 1.2.5); neither a
properness hypothesis over $s$ nor a Cartesian condition is needed. The
former open interface is therefore retired and is no longer listed among
the unresolved inputs of this chapter.

attrs.title: Proper pushforward compatibility of trace maps: discharged

objects.body:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme and $\Lambda$ a finite ring. Every
simple object of the abelian category of constructible $\Lambda$-sheaves on
$X_{\Et}$ is of the form $i_{x!}M$, where $x\in X$ is a point with
$\{x\}$ locally closed, $i_x:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$ is the
induced immersion, and $M$ is a simple finite $\Lambda$-module with a
continuous action of $\operatorname{Gal}(\kappa(x)^{\mathrm{sep}}/\kappa(x))$,
viewed as a sheaf on $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$. If $X$ is of finite type
over a field, $x$ is a closed point and $i_{x!}=i_{x*}$. In particular a
nonzero lisse sheaf on a scheme of positive dimension is not a finite
extension of simple constructible sheaves.

## Proof

Let $F$ be simple, and let $\eta$ be the generic point of an irreducible
component $V$ of the closure of the support of $F$. Choose an open
$U\subset V$ containing $\eta$, disjoint from the other components, on
which $F|_U$ is locally constant and nonzero, and an open $W\subset X$ with
$W\cap\overline{\operatorname{supp}F}=U$. Extension by zero gives a nonzero
subsheaf $j_{W!}(F|_W)\subset F$, so it equals $F$ and
$\operatorname{supp}F\subset U$. If $U\neq\{\eta\}$, pick a point
$y\in U$ closed in $U$, $y\neq\eta$, and put
$W'=W\setminus\overline{\{y\}}$; then $j_{W'!}(F|_{W'})$ is a nonzero
subsheaf of $F$ (it is nonzero at $\eta$) with zero stalk at $y$, where $F$
is nonzero, contradicting simplicity. Hence $U=\{\eta\}$, so $\{\eta\}$ is
locally closed and $F=i_{\eta!}M$ with $M=i_\eta^*F$. Subsheaves of
$i_{\eta!}M$ are supported in $\{\eta\}$, hence of the form $i_{\eta!}N$ for
a Galois-stable submodule $N\subset M$, so $M$ is simple. Conversely each
such $i_{x!}M$ is simple by the same correspondence. On a scheme of finite
type over a field a locally closed point is closed (Jacobson property). For
the last assertion: a finite extension of punctual sheaves has finite
support, while a nonzero lisse sheaf on a positive-dimensional scheme does
not.

Fix the coefficient conventions, $A=A_{E,n}$, $s=\Spec k$, let
$c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times_sX$ be an admissible correspondence
([def-trf-correspondence]) with fixed scheme $F=\Fix(c)$ and fixed-square
maps $i_F:F\to C$, $d:F\to X$ ([def-trf-fixed-scheme]), let
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ and $u:Lc_2^*K\to Rc_1^!K$. Assume the exceptional
admissibility ([def-trf-admissibility]) required by
[def-trf-supported-pairing] for the diagonal opposite pair
$(C,c,u)$, $(X,\Delta_X,1_K)$ and by
[lem-trf-trace-map-from-external-duality]. Then the Borel–Moore section
of the diagonal pair ([def-trf-supported-pairing]) is the Verdier trace
class of [def-trf-trace-class]:

$$
\langle u,1_K\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}=\Tr_c(u)
\qquad\text{in }\Hom_{D(F,A)}(A_F,\omega_{F,A}).
$$

The equality holds exactly, with no sign and no twist: both sides are
the exceptional adjoint, along $d$, of the class of $u$ read through the
Künneth–Verdier isomorphism, base changed to the diagonal and evaluated.

## Proof

*Notation.* Put $Z=X\times_sX$ with projections $p_1,p_2$, diagonal
$\Delta=\Delta_X$ (a closed immersion, $X$ being separated), factor
exchange $\tau$ (so $\tau\Delta=\Delta$, $p_i\tau=p_{3-i}$), and
$e:=c\,i_F=\Delta d:F\to Z$. All pullbacks and tensor products are
derived ([def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]). Put $D:=D_XK$,
$\omega=\omega_{X,A}$, and

$$
P:=K\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}D=Lp_1^*K\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}Lp_2^*D,
\qquad
e':L\Delta^*P=K\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}D\xrightarrow{\ \mathrm{sym}\ }
D\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}K\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_K}\omega ,
$$

with $\operatorname{ev}_K$ the evaluation of [def-trf-dualizing-complex]
and $\mathrm{sym}$ the symmetry with its Koszul signs; the map
$e_K:P\to R\Delta_*\omega$ of
[lem-trf-trace-map-from-external-duality] is the
$L\Delta^*\dashv R\Delta_*$ adjoint of $e'$. For an exceptionally
admissible $f$ write
$\operatorname{adj}_f:\Hom(Rf_!M,N)\cong\Hom(M,Rf^!N)$. The
identifications $\omega\cong R\Delta^!\omega_Z$,
$\omega_{F,A}\cong Rd^!\omega$ and $\omega_{F,A}\cong Re^!\omega_Z$ are
those of [thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition]; by its compatibility
with further compositions, the last is the composite of the first two
with $Re^!\cong Rd^!R\Delta^!$. In the diagonal case of
[def-trf-supported-pairing] one has $(Y,L)=(X,K)$, $\bar d=\Delta$,
$E=F$, $e_C=i_F$, $e_D=d$, and the Künneth–Verdier isomorphism used there
is $\kappa:=\kappa_{K,K}:P\xrightarrow{\sim}\RHom_A(Lp_2^*K,Rp_1^!K)$ of
[thm-trf-kunneth-verdier]. Let

$$
\widetilde u:=\kappa^{-1}\circ[u]:Rc_!A_C\longrightarrow P
$$

be the supported class of $u$ (Step 1 there, with $[u]$ from
[lem-trf-correspondence-class]), and let $\widetilde u_{\mathrm{tr}}:A_C\to
\mathcal H_c(K)$ be the mate of $u$ from
[def-trf-trace-class-source].

*Step 1 (both constructions start from $\widetilde u$).* Let
$\xi:\mathcal H_c(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rc^!P$ be the comparison of
[thm-trf-verdier-duality]: the exchange
$\mathcal H_c(K)=\RHom_A(Lc^*Lp_2^*K,Rc^!Rp_1^!K)\cong
Rc^!\RHom_A(Lp_2^*K,Rp_1^!K)$ of
[lem-trf-exceptional-internal-hom-exchange], followed by
$Rc^!\kappa^{-1}$. We claim

$$
\xi\circ\widetilde u_{\mathrm{tr}}=\operatorname{adj}_c(\widetilde u).
\tag{1}
$$

The exchange is defined by the Yoneda chain of
[lem-trf-exceptional-internal-hom-exchange]; evaluated on the test
object $A_C$ that chain reads
$\Hom_C(A_C,\mathcal H_c(K))\cong\Hom_C(Lc^*M,Rc^!N)\cong
\Hom_Z(Rc_!A_C\otimes M,N)\cong\Hom_Z(Rc_!A_C,\RHom_A(M,N))\cong
\Hom_C(A_C,Rc^!\RHom_A(M,N))$ with $M=Lp_2^*K$, $N=Rp_1^!K$, using
$A_C\otimes Lc^*M=Lc^*M$. Its first arrow is the mate bijection of
[def-trf-trace-class-source], and its middle arrows are, in reverse,
exactly the tensor–Hom, projection-formula and exceptional-adjunction
steps whose composite defines $[u]$ in [lem-trf-correspondence-class]
(with the same identifications $Lc_2^*=Lc^*Lp_2^*$,
$Rc_1^!=Rc^!Rp_1^!$). Hence the exchange sends $\widetilde u_{\mathrm{tr}}$
to $\operatorname{adj}_c([u])$, and by naturality of $\operatorname{adj}_c$
in its target, $Rc^!\kappa^{-1}\circ\operatorname{adj}_c([u])
=\operatorname{adj}_c(\kappa^{-1}[u])$, which is (1).

*Step 2 (the trace class).* Let
$bc:L\Delta^*Rc_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rd_!Li_F^*$ be the base change of
[thm-trf-fixed-point-base-change] (2), and put

$$
h:\;Rd_!A_F=Rd_!Li_F^*A_C\xrightarrow{\ bc^{-1}\ }
L\Delta^*Rc_!A_C\xrightarrow{\ L\Delta^*\widetilde u\ }L\Delta^*P
\xrightarrow{\ e'\ }\omega .
$$

We claim $\Tr_c(u)=\operatorname{adj}_d(h)$, read through
$Rd^!\omega\cong\omega_{F,A}$. By [def-trf-trace-class] and naturality of
the global-sections adjunction (with
$R\Gamma(C,Ri_{F*}-)=R\Gamma(F,-)$), $\Tr_c(u)$ is the
$Li_F^*\dashv Ri_{F*}$ adjoint of $\varphi\circ\widetilde u_{\mathrm{tr}}:
A_C\to Ri_{F*}\omega_{F,A}$, where $\varphi$ is the objectwise map of
[lem-trf-trace-map-from-external-duality]:
$\varphi=(\text{composition})\circ BC\circ Rc^!e_K\circ\xi$, with
$BC:Rc^!R\Delta_*\cong Ri_{F*}Rd^!$ the right-adjoint form of $bc$. By
(1), $Rc^!e_K\circ\xi\circ\widetilde u_{\mathrm{tr}}
=\operatorname{adj}_c(g)$ with $g:=e_K\circ\widetilde u:Rc_!A_C\to
R\Delta_*\omega$. That $BC$ is the right-adjoint form of $bc$ (its
compatibility with the adjunction data, [thm-trf-fixed-point-base-change])
means precisely: for every $g:Rc_!M\to R\Delta_*N$, the $i_F$-adjoint of
$BC\circ\operatorname{adj}_c(g)$ is
$\operatorname{adj}_d(g^\flat\circ bc^{-1}):Li_F^*M\to Rd^!N$, where
$g^\flat:L\Delta^*Rc_!M\to N$ is the $L\Delta^*\dashv R\Delta_*$ adjoint
of $g$. Here $g^\flat=e'\circ L\Delta^*\widetilde u$, since $e_K$ is the
adjoint of $e'$; so $g^\flat\circ bc^{-1}=h$, which is the claim.

*Step 3 (pairing with the diagonal class).* Let
$\widetilde v:R\Delta_!A_X\to Q=D\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}K$ be the
supported class of $(X,\Delta,1_K)$ in [def-trf-supported-pairing]: it is
$\widetilde v=s\circ\tau_*\widetilde v'$ with
$\widetilde v':=\kappa^{-1}\circ[1_K]:R\Delta_!A_X\to P$ and
$s:\tau_*P\cong Q$ the symmetry. Let
$\gamma=\alpha\circ(\operatorname{ev}_K\boxtimes\operatorname{ev}_K)\circ
\mathrm{rearr}:P\otimes Q\to\omega_Z$ be the contraction of Step 3 there.
We claim

$$
\gamma\circ(1_P\otimes\widetilde v)
=\varepsilon_\Delta\circ R\Delta_!(e')\circ\pi_P,
\tag{2}
$$

where $\pi_P:P\otimes R\Delta_!A_X\cong R\Delta_!L\Delta^*P$ is the
projection formula ([prop-functor-package] (5), after the symmetry, which
is sign-free because $R\Delta_!A_X$ is a sheaf in degree $0$) and
$\varepsilon_\Delta:R\Delta_!\omega\cong R\Delta_!R\Delta^!\omega_Z\to
\omega_Z$ is the counit. Equivalently (by projection formula and
$\operatorname{adj}_\Delta$), the $\Delta$-adjoint
$L\Delta^*P\to R\Delta^!\omega_Z\cong\omega$ of the left side is $e'$.

(3a) By [lem-trf-correspondence-class] for $c=\Delta$ (both legs
$\operatorname{id}_X$), the tensor–Hom transpose
$[1_K]^T:R\Delta_!A_X\otimes Lp_2^*K\to Rp_1^!K$ is, after
$R\Delta_!A_X\otimes Lp_2^*K\cong R\Delta_!K$, the $\Delta$-adjoint of the
composition isomorphism $K\cong R\Delta^!Rp_1^!K$; equivalently, under
the adjunction for $p_1\Delta=\operatorname{id}_X$, it corresponds to
$1_K$, i.e. $\varepsilon_{p_1}\circ Rp_{1!}[1_K]^T=1_K$ on
$Rp_{1!}R\Delta_!K=K$.

(3b) By [def-sf-kv-maps] (iii), (iv), the transpose
$\kappa^T:P\otimes Lp_2^*K\to Rp_1^!K$ of $\kappa$ is
$Lp_1^*K\otimes Lp_2^*(D\otimes K)\xrightarrow{1\otimes Lp_2^*\operatorname{ev}_K}
K\boxtimes\omega\xrightarrow{\alpha_{\operatorname{id},a_X}}Rp_1^!K$ (the
other evaluation is the unit identification $\RHom_A(A_X,K)=K$, and moving
the unit $A_X$ costs no sign), with $\alpha_{\operatorname{id},a_X}$ the
exceptional Künneth map of [prop-trf-exceptional-kunneth] for
$p_1=\operatorname{id}_X\times a_X$. So $\kappa\circ\widetilde v'=[1_K]$
transposes to

$$
\alpha_{\operatorname{id},a_X}\circ(1\otimes Lp_2^*\operatorname{ev}_K)
\circ(\widetilde v'\otimes 1_{Lp_2^*K})=[1_K]^T .
\tag{3}
$$

(3c) Let $\varpi:Lp_1^*D\otimes Rp_1^!K\to Rp_1^!\omega\cong\omega_Z$ be
the $p_1$-adjoint of
$Rp_{1!}(Lp_1^*D\otimes Rp_1^!K)\cong D\otimes Rp_{1!}Rp_1^!K
\xrightarrow{1\otimes\varepsilon_{p_1}}D\otimes K
\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_K}\omega$. Apply the autoequivalence
$\tau^*$ ($\tau^*R\Delta_!A_X=R\Delta_!A_X$,
$\tau^*\omega_Z\cong\omega_Z$): the left side of (2) becomes
$\gamma^\tau\circ(1\otimes\widetilde v')$ with
$\gamma^\tau:=\tau^*\gamma\circ(1\otimes\tau^*s):\tau^*P\otimes P\to
\omega_Z$, where $\tau^*P=Lp_2^*K\otimes Lp_1^*D$. Then

$$
\gamma^\tau=\varpi\circ(1_{Lp_1^*D}\otimes\kappa^T)\circ r,
\qquad
r:\tau^*P\otimes P\cong Lp_1^*D\otimes(P\otimes Lp_2^*K)
$$

the symmetry-constraint permutation. Both sides contract the factor-one
$D$ with the factor-one $K$ and the factor-two $D$ with the factor-two
$K$ by $\operatorname{ev}_K$, and then identify the result with
$\omega_Z$; they agree because $\alpha_{a_X,a_X}$ factors as
$\alpha_{\operatorname{id},a_X}$ (for $L_1=\omega$) followed by
$Rp_1^!\omega=Rp_1^!Ra_X^!A_s\cong Ra_Z^!A_s$ (both are exceptional
adjoints of $\mathrm{Ku}_!$ followed by counits, [def-sf-kv-maps] (i),
(ii), and $\mathrm{Ku}_!$ is compatible with composition and with the
exchange of factors), because $\alpha_{\operatorname{id},a_X}$ is natural
in $L_1$ and compatible with $Lp_1^*D\otimes(-)$ through the projection
formula (which is how $\varpi$ is built), and because all permutations
used are symmetry constraints with Koszul signs, so two composites
inducing the same permutation of the same factors coincide (coherence of
the symmetric monoidal structure, [prop-functor-package], final clause).

(3d) By (3c), naturality of $r$, and (3),

$$
\gamma^\tau\circ(1\otimes\widetilde v')
=\varpi\circ(1_{Lp_1^*D}\otimes[1_K]^T)\circ r',
\qquad
r':\tau^*P\otimes R\Delta_!A_X\cong
Lp_1^*D\otimes(R\Delta_!A_X\otimes Lp_2^*K).
$$

Take $\Delta$-adjoints. Since $\tau\Delta=\Delta$ and $p_i\Delta=\operatorname{id}$,
$L\Delta^*\tau^*P=K\otimes D$ and $L\Delta^*r'$ is $\mathrm{sym}:K\otimes
D\cong D\otimes K$. The map
$\varpi\circ(1\otimes[1_K]^T):R\Delta_!(D\otimes K)\cong
Lp_1^*D\otimes R\Delta_!K\to\omega_Z\cong Rp_1^!\omega$ corresponds, under
the adjunction for $p_1\Delta=\operatorname{id}_X$, to
$D\otimes K\xrightarrow{1\otimes\varepsilon_{p_1}Rp_{1!}[1_K]^T}D\otimes K
\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_K}\omega$ (definition of $\varpi$ and
naturality of the projection formula), which is $\operatorname{ev}_K$ by
(3a). Hence the $\Delta$-adjoint of $\tau^*$ of the left side of (2) is
$\operatorname{ev}_K\circ\mathrm{sym}=e'$; as $\tau^*$ commutes with the
$\Delta$-adjunction ($\tau$ an automorphism with $\tau\Delta=\Delta$), so
is that of the left side itself. This proves (2).

*Step 4 (the supported pairing).* By [def-trf-supported-pairing], with
$\mu:Re_!A_F\cong Rc_!A_C\otimes R\Delta_!A_X$,

$$
\sigma_{u,1_K}=\gamma\circ(\widetilde u\otimes\widetilde v)\circ\mu
=\gamma\circ(1_P\otimes\widetilde v)\circ(\widetilde u\otimes1)\circ\mu
=\varepsilon_\Delta\circ R\Delta_!\bigl(e'\circ L\Delta^*\widetilde u\bigr)
\circ\pi_{Rc_!A_C}\circ\mu
$$

by (2) and naturality of the projection formula. The isomorphism $\mu$
is built from the projection formula for $c$ and the base change along
$c$ in the fixed square; the isomorphism
$R\Delta_!(bc^{-1})\circ(Re_!\cong R\Delta_!Rd_!):Re_!A_F\cong
R\Delta_!L\Delta^*Rc_!A_C$ is built from the base change along $\Delta$
in the same Cartesian square. By the coherence of the composition,
base-change and projection-formula isomorphisms ([prop-functor-package]
(3)–(5) and its final clause) the isomorphism
$Re_!A_F\cong Rc_!A_C\otimes R\Delta_!A_X$ does not depend on which leg
of the square is used, i.e.
$\pi_{Rc_!A_C}\circ\mu=R\Delta_!(bc^{-1})\circ(Re_!\cong R\Delta_!Rd_!)$.
Therefore

$$
\sigma_{u,1_K}=\varepsilon_\Delta\circ R\Delta_!(h)\circ
(Re_!A_F\cong R\Delta_!Rd_!A_F).
$$

The adjunction $Re_!\dashv Re^!$ is the composite of those for $\Delta$
and $d$ (this is how $Re^!\cong Rd^!R\Delta^!$ is defined), and
$\operatorname{adj}_\Delta(\varepsilon_\Delta\circ R\Delta_!h)=h$
(followed by $\omega\cong R\Delta^!\omega_Z$). Hence
$\operatorname{adj}_e(\sigma_{u,1_K})=\operatorname{adj}_d(h)$ under
$Re^!\omega_Z\cong Rd^!R\Delta^!\omega_Z\cong Rd^!\omega$, and by the
compatibility recalled in the notation paragraph,
$\langle u,1_K\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}=\operatorname{adj}_d(h)$ read through
$Rd^!\omega\cong\omega_{F,A}$. By Step 2 this is $\Tr_c(u)$.

attrs.title: The trace class is the diagonal supported pairing

objects.body:
Let $(f,g):(C,c)\to(D,b)$ be a proper pushforward diagram of
[def-trf-coefficient-pushforward] (no Cartesian leg square, no properness
over $s$), with the notation and admissibility of
[def-trf-kernel-pushforward-maps]. Then:

1. *(evaluation)* as maps $Rq_*P_X\to R\Delta_{Y*}\omega_Y$,
$$
\delta_{K'}\circ\rho_f=R\Delta_{Y*}\tau_f\circ Rq_*\delta_K ;
$$
1. *(support)* as maps
$Rg_*Ri_{c*}\omega_{F_c}=Ri_{b*}Rh_*\omega_{F_c}\to Rb^!R\Delta_{Y*}\omega_Y$,
$$
Rb^!\bigl(R\Delta_{Y*}\tau_f\bigr)\circ\mathsf E\circ Rg_*\zeta_c
=\zeta_b\circ Ri_{b*}\tau_h ,
$$
where the source identification is $gi_c=i_bh$.

Moreover, for a Cartesian square $(\beta',\alpha',\beta,\alpha)$
($\beta:V\to W$, $\alpha:U\to W$ proper, $V'=V\times_WU$) the exceptional
adjoint of the right-adjoint base-change isomorphism
$R\alpha'_*R\beta'^!\cong R\beta^!R\alpha_*$ (the mate of
$\operatorname{Ex}_!$) is
$R\beta_!R\alpha'_*R\beta'^!\cong R\alpha_!R\beta'_!R\beta'^!
\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}R\alpha_*$, the composition law followed by the
counit of $\beta'$.

## Proof

*The last assertion.* The base-change isomorphism is the mate of
$\operatorname{Ex}_!:\alpha^*R\beta_!\cong R\beta'_!\alpha'^*$ under the four
adjunctions ([fix-prop-adjunctions], item 4). Taking the exceptional adjoint
of a mate and using the triangle identities (the mate calculus of
[lem-sf-mate]) expresses it through $\operatorname{Ex}_!$, the unit of
$\alpha$ and the counits of $\alpha'$ and $\beta'$; since $\alpha,\alpha'$ are
proper, $\operatorname{Ex}_!=\operatorname{Ex}_*$ is compatible with the
composition law $R\beta_!R\alpha'_!\cong R\alpha_!R\beta'_!$
([fix-lem-exchanges], items 1 and 4; [thm-sf-comp-composition]), and the
unit–counit pair of $\alpha'$ cancels. What remains is the displayed
composite.

*Evaluation (1).* Both sides are maps into $R\Delta_{Y*}\omega_Y$, so it
suffices to compare their adjoints for $\Delta_Y^*\dashv R\Delta_{Y*}$. The
adjoint of $\delta_{K'}$ is $\mathrm{ev}_{K'}\circ\mathrm{sym}:K'\otimes
D_YK'\to\omega_Y$, so the left side has adjoint
$\mathrm{ev}_{K'}\circ\mathrm{sym}\circ(1\otimes\chi_f)\circ\Delta_Y^*\Pi_f^{-1}$.
The adjoint of the right side is
$\tau_f\circ Rf_*(\mathrm{ev}_K\circ\mathrm{sym})\circ\mathrm{Ex}$, where
$\mathrm{Ex}:\Delta_Y^*Rq_*\to Rf_*\Delta_X^*$ is the exchange map of the
commutative square $q\Delta_X=\Delta_Yf$ (adjoint to
$f^*\Delta_Y^*Rq_*=\Delta_X^*q^*Rq_*\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_q}\Delta_X^*$, as in
[def-exchange-projection]). We claim

$$
\mathrm{Ex}\circ\Delta_Y^*\Pi_f=\mu_f:
Rf_*K\otimes Rf_*D_XK\longrightarrow Rf_*(K\otimes D_XK).
$$

Indeed $\mathrm{Ku}_!$ of [def-sf-kv-maps] (i) is the composite of
[thm-sf-kunneth-relative], built from the composition law, two projection
formulas and one base change; for proper maps these are the direct-image
projection maps and $\operatorname{Ex}_*$ (compatibility with $Rf_!\cong Rf_*$,
[thm-sf-kunneth-relative], with the projection formula,
[lem-sf-kunneth-coherence] (iv), [fix-prop-projection-formula]), each adjoint to a
counit ([def-exchange-projection]). By naturality and the triangle
identities ([fix-prop-adjunctions]) the inverse $\Pi_f$ is therefore the
adjoint of $q^*(K'\boxtimes Rf_*D_XK)=f^*Rf_*K\boxtimes f^*Rf_*D_XK
\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_f\boxtimes\varepsilon_f}K\boxtimes D_XK$, i.e.
$\varepsilon_q\circ q^*\Pi_f=\varepsilon_f\boxtimes\varepsilon_f$. Then
$\mathrm{Ex}\circ\Delta_Y^*\Pi_f$ is adjoint to
$\Delta_X^*(\varepsilon_q\circ q^*\Pi_f)=\varepsilon_f\otimes\varepsilon_f$,
which is the defining adjoint of $\mu_f$. With the claim, the adjoint of
the right side composed with $\Delta_Y^*\Pi_f$ is
$\tau_f\circ Rf_*(\mathrm{ev}_K\circ\mathrm{sym})\circ\mu_f$, and by the
definition of $\chi_f$ (after the symmetry, which commutes with $\mu_f$) this
is $\mathrm{ev}_{K'}\circ\mathrm{sym}\circ(1\otimes\chi_f)$. Since $\Pi_f$ is
an isomorphism, the two adjoints agree, proving (1).

*Support (2).* Both sides are maps into $Rb^!(-)$; compare their exceptional
adjoints for $Rb_!\dashv Rb^!$, which are maps
$Rb_!Ri_{b*}Rh_*\omega_{F_c}\to R\Delta_{Y*}\omega_Y$. The fixed squares of $c$
and $b$ are Cartesian ([prop-trf-fixed-square-cartesian]), $i_c,i_b$ are closed
immersions (base changes of the diagonals of the separated $X$, $Y$), and
$\zeta_c,\zeta_b$ are built from the right-adjoint base change of
[thm-trf-fixed-point-base-change] and
[thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition]. By the last assertion, the exceptional
adjoint of $\zeta_c$ is
$Rc_!Ri_{c*}\omega_{F_c}\cong Rc_!Ri_{c!}Rd_c^!\omega_X\cong R\Delta_{X*}Rd_{c!}Rd_c^!\omega_X
\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{d_c}}R\Delta_{X*}\omega_X$, and likewise for
$\zeta_b$.

For the left side, the definition of $\mathsf E$ gives
$\varepsilon_b\circ Rb_!\mathsf E=Rq_*\varepsilon_c\circ\Xi$, so its adjoint is

$$
R\Delta_{Y*}\tau_f\circ Rq_*\bigl(\varepsilon_c\circ Rc_!\zeta_c\bigr)\circ\Xi
=R\Delta_{Y*}\bigl(\tau_f\circ Rf_*\varepsilon_{d_c}\bigr)
$$

after the composition-law identifications, and
$\tau_f\circ Rf_*\varepsilon_{d_c}$ is the counit of $R(fd_c)_!\dashv R(fd_c)^!$
at $\omega_Y$ ([fix-prop-adjunctions], item 3), with
$\omega_{F_c}\cong R(fd_c)^!\omega_Y$ by
[thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition]. For the right side, its adjoint is
$R\Delta_{Y*}\bigl(\varepsilon_{d_b}\circ Rd_{b*}\tau_h\bigr)$, and
$\varepsilon_{d_b}\circ Rd_{b*}\tau_h$ is the counit for $d_bh$ at $\omega_Y$
by the same pasting. Since $fd_c=d_bh$ ([def-trf-coefficient-pushforward]),
these are the counit for one and the same morphism, and the two
composition-law identifications of the source with
$R\Delta_{Y*}R(fd_c)_!\omega_{F_c}$ agree by the associativity of
[thm-sf-comp-composition] (the maps $h$, $q$, $g$ being proper by
[lem-trf-fixed-map-proper]). Hence the adjoints agree, proving (2). Only the
two fixed squares are used as Cartesian squares.

attrs.title: Exchange of the trace maps: evaluation and support

objects.body:
Let
$F=\operatorname{Fix}(c)$, $i_F:F\to C$, and $d:F\to X$ be the
fixed-square maps, all with the
exceptional admissibility required
below. There is then a morphism

$$
\mathfrak t_{c,K}:R\Gamma(C,\mathcal H_c(K))
\longrightarrow R\Gamma(F,\omega_{F,A}),
$$

where the source and target use the
trace-class source and
dualizing complex.

## Proof

Let $\Delta:X\to X\times_sX$ be the diagonal. The external product
of [def-trf-external-product] pulls back to
$K\otimes_A^LD_XK$. The definition of the Verdier dual in
[def-trf-dualizing-complex], evaluation for internal Hom, and the
symmetry of the derived tensor in [def-weil-derived-tensor] give
$K\otimes_A^LD_XK\to\omega_{X,A}$.
By the pullback/direct-image adjunction of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], its adjoint is

$$
e_K:K\boxtimes_A^LD_XK\longrightarrow R\Delta_*\omega_{X,A}.
$$

Assuming the comparison requested in [thm-trf-verdier-duality],
apply $Rc^!$ to this map and form

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal H_c(K)&\xrightarrow{\sim}Rc^!(K\boxtimes_A^LD_XK)\\
&\xrightarrow{Rc^!e_K}Rc^!R\Delta_*\omega_{X,A}\\
&\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri_{F*}Rd^!\omega_{X,A}\\
&\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri_{F*}\omega_{F,A}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The last two arrows are the exceptional form of fixed-square base
change in [thm-trf-fixed-point-base-change] and the composition
of dualizing complexes in [thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition].
Taking derived global sections gives $\mathfrak t_{c,K}$.
Equivalently, adjunction along $i_F$ gives
$\theta_{c,K}:Li_F^*\mathcal H_c(K)\to\omega_{F,A}$.
Thus this objectwise map is a consequence of the external duality
[thm-trf-verdier-duality], which is proved; the construction is
unconditional.

Let $(f,g):(C,c)\to(D,b)$ be a proper pushforward diagram of
[def-trf-coefficient-pushforward] (no Cartesian leg square, no properness
over $s$), with the notation and admissibility of
[def-trf-kernel-pushforward-maps]. Then the kernel class of the coefficient
pushforward $[f,g]_!u$ is the transported kernel class of $u$:

$$
[\,[f,g]_!u\,]_P
=\rho_f\circ Rq_*[u]_P\circ\Xi\circ Rb_!\eta_g
\quad:\ Rb_!A_D\longrightarrow P_Y ,
$$

where $\eta_g:A_D\to Rg_*A_C$ is the unit.

## Proof

Throughout, $p_1,p_2$ and $p'_1,p'_2$ are the projections of
$X\times_sX$ and $Y\times_sY$, so that $p'_iq=fp_i$; put
$H_X=R\mathcal Hom(p_2^*K,p_1^!K)$ and $H_Y=R\mathcal Hom(p'^*_2K',p'^!_1K')$,
and let $\kappa_X=\kappa_{K,K}:P_X\xrightarrow{\sim}H_X$,
$\kappa_Y=\kappa_{K',K'}:P_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}H_Y$ be the Künneth–Verdier
isomorphisms of [thm-trf-kunneth-verdier].

*Step 0: kernel class versus class.* For a correspondence $v$ on
$(X,K)$ supported on $c$, let $[v]:Rc_!A_C\to H_X$ be its class of
[lem-trf-correspondence-class]. The external duality of
[thm-trf-verdier-duality] is the exchange
$\mathcal H_c(K)\cong Rc^!H_X$ of [lem-trf-exceptional-internal-hom-exchange]
followed by $Rc^!\kappa_X^{-1}$, and that exchange is built from the
tensor–Hom adjunction, the projection formula and $Rc_!\dashv Rc^!$ in
the same order as the bijection of [lem-trf-correspondence-class]. Hence
the exceptional adjoint of $A_C\to\mathcal H_c(K)\cong Rc^!H_X$ is $[v]$,
and $[v]_P=\kappa_X^{-1}[v]$. Likewise $[w]_P=\kappa_Y^{-1}[w]$ on $D$.

*Step 1: the transport map.* Let $\delta_1:Rq_*p_1^!\to p'^!_1Rf_*$ be the
exceptional adjoint of
$Rp'_{1!}Rq_!p_1^!\cong Rf_!Rp_{1!}p_1^!\xrightarrow{Rf_!\varepsilon}Rf_!$
(the recipe of $\delta$ in [def-trf-coefficient-pushforward] for the square
$p'_1q=fp_1$). Let $\Phi:Rq_*H_X\to H_Y$ be the tensor–Hom adjoint of

$$
\begin{aligned}
Rq_*H_X\otimes p'^*_2K'
&\xrightarrow{\ \mathrm{PF}\ }Rq_*\bigl(H_X\otimes p_2^*f^*Rf_*K\bigr)
\xrightarrow{\ \varepsilon_f\ }Rq_*\bigl(H_X\otimes p_2^*K\bigr)\\
&\xrightarrow{\ \mathrm{ev}\ }Rq_*p_1^!K
\xrightarrow{\ \delta_1\ }p'^!_1K',
\end{aligned}
$$

with $\mathrm{PF}$ the projection map of [fix-prop-projection-formula] for
the proper $q$ and $q^*p'^*_2=p_2^*f^*$. The lemma follows from the two
identities

$$
\text{(a)}\quad \kappa_Y\circ\rho_f=\Phi\circ Rq_*\kappa_X,
\qquad
\text{(b)}\quad [\delta\circ Rg_*v\circ\gamma]
=\Phi\circ Rq_*[v]\circ\Xi\circ Rb_!\eta_g ,
$$

since with $v=u$, Step 0 turns (b) into
$[\,[f,g]_!u\,]_P=\kappa_Y^{-1}\Phi\,Rq_*(\kappa_X[u]_P)\,\Xi\,Rb_!\eta_g$,
and (a) turns this into the assertion.

*Step 2: proof of (b).* A map $Rb_!A_D\to H_Y$ is determined by its
image under the bijection of [lem-trf-correspondence-class], and further
by the adjoint of that image along $Rb_{1!}\dashv b_1^!$, a map
$Rb_{1!}b_2^*K'\to K'$ (using $Rb_{1!}=Rp'_{1!}Rb_!$ and
$b^!p'^!_1=b_1^!$). For the left side of (b), the definition of $\delta$
gives the adjoint

$$
Rb_{1!}b_2^*K'\xrightarrow{Rb_{1!}\gamma}Rb_{1!}Rg_*c_2^*K
\xrightarrow{\Xi_1}Rf_!Rc_{1!}c_2^*K
\xrightarrow{Rf_!v^\flat}Rf_!K=K',
$$

where $v^\flat=\varepsilon_{c_1}\circ Rc_{1!}v$ is the adjoint of $v$. For the right
side, unwind the bijection: tensor with $p'^*_2K'$, apply the projection
formula for $b$, then $\Phi$, then the counit of $p'_1$. By the definition
of $\delta_1$, the counit of $p'_1$ after $Rp'_{1!}\delta_1$ is
$Rf_!$ of the counit of $p_1$; by the naturality of $\mathrm{PF}$ and its
compatibility with the composition law ([fix-prop-projection-formula],
[fix-prop-coherence]), the projection formulas for $b$, $q$ and $c$
combine into the projection formula for $bg=qc$, and the class $[v]$ is
turned back into $v^\flat$. The right side thus becomes

$$
Rb_{1!}b_2^*K'\xrightarrow{\eta_g}Rb_{1!}Rg_*g^*b_2^*K'
=Rb_{1!}Rg_*c_2^*f^*K'
\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_f}Rb_{1!}Rg_*c_2^*K
\xrightarrow{\Xi_1}Rf_!Rc_{1!}c_2^*K\xrightarrow{Rf_!v^\flat}K' .
$$

Its first two arrows are $Rb_{1!}\gamma$ by the definition of $\gamma$,
so the two adjoints coincide, proving (b).

*Step 3: proof of (a).* Both sides are maps $Rq_*P_X\to H_Y$; compare
their adjoints $Rp'_{1!}(Rq_*P_X\otimes p'^*_2K')\to K'$ as in Step 2. By
[def-sf-kv-maps] (iv), $\kappa_X$ is $\beta$ followed by the exceptional
Künneth $\alpha_{\operatorname{id},a_X}$, whose exceptional adjoint is the
counit $\varepsilon_{a_X}$ of $Ra_{X!}\dashv Ra_X^!$ after $\mathrm{Ku}_!$
([def-sf-kv-maps] (ii)). Hence the adjoint of $\kappa_X$ evaluates the
factor $D_XK$ of $P_X$ against the $p_2^*K$-variable and then applies
$\varepsilon_{a_X}$ to $\omega_X$ in the second factor; similarly for
$\kappa_Y$. On the left side, $\rho_f$ first undoes $\Pi_f$, and the
defining evaluation of $\chi_f$ turns the evaluation of $D_YK'$ against
$K'$ into $\tau_f\circ Rf_*\mathrm{ev}_K\circ\mu_f$; since
$\varepsilon_{a_Y}\circ Ra_{Y!}\tau_f=\varepsilon_{a_X}$ (the counit of
$a_X=a_Yf$ is the pasted counit, [fix-prop-adjunctions], item 3), and
$\mu_f$ and $\Pi_f$ are adjoint to $\varepsilon_f\otimes\varepsilon_f$
(the projection maps and the exchange $\operatorname{Ex}_*$ entering
$\mathrm{Ku}_!$ are adjoint to counits, [def-exchange-projection],
[fix-prop-projection-formula]), the left side becomes: apply
$\varepsilon_f:f^*K'\to K$ to the $p_2^*K'$-variable, evaluate $D_XK$
against it, and apply $\varepsilon_{a_X}$. On the right side, $\Phi$ applies
the same $\varepsilon_f$ and then the adjoint of $\kappa_X$, followed by
$\delta_1$ and the counit of $p'_1$, which together are $Rf_!$ of the
counit of $p_1$; this is the same composite. Hence (a) holds, and with it
the lemma.

attrs.title: Exchange of the trace-class sources: the kernel of the coefficient pushforward

objects.body:
Let $c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times X$ be an admissible correspondence with
coefficient $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ and $u:c_2^*K\to c_1^!K$
([def-trf-correspondence]), with fixed scheme $F$, and let
$i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed subscheme with open complement
$j:U\hookrightarrow X$ which is *$c$-invariant*: $c_2(c_1^{-1}(Z))\subset Z$
set-theoretically, so that $c_1^{-1}(Z)\subset c_2^{-1}(Z)$ and
$c_2^{-1}(U)\subset c_1^{-1}(U)$. Then $u$ induces coefficient morphisms
$u^U$ on $K'=j_!j^*K$ and $u^Z$ on $K''=Ri_*i^*K$: $u^U=[j]_!(u|_U)$ is
the extension by zero of the restriction of $u$ to the open correspondence
$c|_U$ on $c^{-1}(U\times U)=c_2^{-1}(U)$, and $u^Z=[i]_!(u|_Z)$ is the
pushforward of the restriction of $u$ to the closed correspondence
$c|_Z:c_1^{-1}(Z)_{\mathrm{red}}\to Z\times Z$ (in the Frobenius case
these are the pieces $u^U,u^Z$ of [d-curve-pieces]). The triple
$(u^U,u,u^Z)$ is a morphism of the open–closed triangles
$K'\to K\to K''\to K'[1]$ of the functors $Lc_2^*$ and $Rc_1^!$, and the
Verdier trace classes of [def-trf-trace-class] satisfy

$$
\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)=\operatorname{Tr}_c(u^U)+\operatorname{Tr}_c(u^Z)
$$

in $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(F,A)}(A_F,\omega_{F,A})$.
This is the additivity of the Verdier trace class along a $c$-invariant
open–closed decomposition
([Varshavsky, Prop. 1.5.10](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0505564), proved in
his §5.3 by filtered trace maps; classically SGA 5, Exposé III, 4.13). It
is *not* asserted for an arbitrary morphism $(u',u,u'')$ of distinguished
triangles in $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$: for the identity correspondence of a point
that assertion is the additivity of the categorical trace on arbitrary
endomorphisms of distinguished triangles of perfect complexes, which fails
([prop-trf-trace-formal-laws], item (2)).

## Proof

*The induced morphisms.* Restriction of $u$ to the open correspondence
$c|_U$ uses only $j^*=j^!$ and the inclusions $c_2^{-1}(U)\subset c_1^{-1}(U)$;
the extension by zero $[j]_!(u|_U):c_2^*j_!j^*K\to c_1^!j_!j^*K$ is the
composite of the open $!$-base change $c_2^*j_!\cong j_!(c_2|_U)^*$, of
$j_!(u|_U)$ and of the canonical map $j_!(c_1|_U)^!\to c_1^!j_!$. The
restriction $u|_Z$ exists because $Z$ is $c$-invariant ($c|_Z$ is the
correspondence induced on $c_1^{-1}(Z)_{\mathrm{red}}$, and $u$ pulls back
along the closed immersion of correspondences), and $[i]_!(u|_Z)$ is its
coefficient pushforward along the proper morphism $[i]$ of correspondences,
as in [thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition] and the proper pushforward
of this chapter. That $(u^U,u,u^Z)$ is a morphism of the open–closed
triangles is checked by adjunction exactly as in the Frobenius case treated
in the proof of item (2) of the trace-class additivity proposition of this
block, the third square following from the first two and the vanishing
$\operatorname{Hom}(j_!N[1],Ri_*M)=0$.

*Additivity.* The identity of trace classes is
[Varshavsky, Prop. 1.5.10](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0505564) in our leg
convention (his $c$-morphisms are $c_1^*\mathcal F\to c_2^!\mathcal F$, so
his $c_2^{-1}(Z)$ is our $c_1^{-1}(Z)$ and his $c$-invariance
$c_1(c_2^{-1}(Z))\subset Z$ is our $c_2(c_1^{-1}(Z))\subset Z$). His proof
(§5.3, Lemma 5.3.2, after Illusie, SGA 5 III 4.13) lifts the trace map to
the filtered derived category $D^bF_{ctf}(X,A)$: the two-step filtration
$j_!j^*K\subset K$ makes $(K,u)$ a filtered $c$-morphism whose graded
pieces are $(j_!j^*K,u^U)$ and $(Ri_*i^*K,u^Z)$, the trace map is a
morphism of filtered bifunctors, and the trace of a filtered $c$-morphism
is the sum of the traces of its graded pieces. The argument needs the
filtered origin of the triple: it is not a consequence of the three squares
commuting in the derived category.

*What the previous argument got wrong.* An earlier proof of this lemma
restricted the trace classes to the geometric points $\bar y$ of $F$ and
claimed $Li_{\bar y}^*\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)=\operatorname{tr}_A(u_{\bar y}\mid K_{\bar y})$
in general. This is false: the stalk at $\bar y$ of the trace-class source
$R\mathcal Hom_A(c_2^*K,c_1^!K)$ is not $R\mathcal Hom_A(K_{\bar y},K_{\bar y})$
(for $K=j_!A$ on $\mathbf A^1$ the source is $Rj_*A$, with nonzero stalk at
$0$ although $K_0=0$), and the equality of the local term with the stalk
trace holds only under a contracting hypothesis
([lem-trf-local-term-locality], item (1)). The reduction to the point
normalization is therefore not available, and the filtered argument above
replaces it.

attrs.title: Triangle compatibility of the trace class

objects.body:
Let $U\to S$ and $V\to S$ be weakly etale morphisms.
Every $S$-morphism $f:U\to V$ is weakly etale.
(Source: [Stacks, Tag 0951](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0951).)

## Proof

Omitted.

*Recorded in advance* from chapter *The trace formula* of the source.

Let $f:V\to W$ be a
weakly etale morphism
and a universal homeomorphism.
Then $f$ is an isomorphism.
(Source: [Stacks, Tag 0F6V](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F6V).)

## Proof

By [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], $f$ is integral,
surjective and universally injective, and both $f$ and its diagonal
are flat. The diagonal is a closed immersion, since an integral map is
separated; it is surjective on underlying points by universal
injectivity. A flat surjective closed immersion is an isomorphism.
Indeed, on affines its ring map is $R\to R/I$, where $I$ is a nil
ideal and $R/I$ is flat. Tensoring the injection $(x)\to R$ with
$R/I$, for $x\in I$, gives $(x)/I(x)=0$; hence $x=ax$ for some
$a\in I$. Since $a$ is nilpotent, $1-a$ is a unit and $x=0$.
Thus $I=0$.

The diagonal of $f$ is therefore an isomorphism, so $f$ is a
monomorphism. On an affine open of $W$, integrality makes its
inverse image affine. The resulting ring map $R\to B$ is faithfully
flat and multiplication $B\otimes_R B\to B$ is an isomorphism.
The faithfully flat equalizer
$R\to B\rightrightarrows B\otimes_R B$ identifies $R$ with all of
$B$, because the two arrows both become the identity under
multiplication. Hence $R\to B$ is an isomorphism. These affine
identifications prove the assertion.

*Recorded in advance* from chapter *The trace formula* of the source.

attrs.title: A weakly etale universal homeomorphism is an isomorphism

objects.body:
In the setting of [def-trf-weil-shriek-pushforward], let
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ and $m,n\geq1$.

1. *Base-change composition.* After the pullback composition
identifications $L\Phi^{(m+n)*}\simeq L\Phi^{m*}L\Phi^{n*}$ on $X$
and on $Y$,
$$
\theta_{f,m+n,K}=\theta_{f,m,L\Phi_X^{n*}K}\circ
L\Phi_Y^{m*}\theta_{f,n,K}:
L\Phi_Y^{(m+n)*}Rf_!K\longrightarrow Rf_!L\Phi_X^{(m+n)*}K .
$$
1. *Iterates.* Let $u:L\Phi_X^*K\to K$ be a Frobenius coefficient
morphism, with iterates $u_m$ of
[def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism], and let
$\psi=Rf_!u\circ\theta_{f,1}$ be the Weil $!$-pushforward. Then the
iterates $\psi_m$ of the Frobenius coefficient morphism $\psi$ on
$Rf_!K$ satisfy
$$
\psi_m=Rf_!u_m\circ\theta_{f,m}\qquad(m\geq1).
$$

Neither statement uses invertibility of $u$.

## Proof

*Step 1: factorizing the relative Frobenius.* Paste the Cartesian
square defining $X'_n$ of [d-relative-frob] with the Cartesian
square obtained by pulling $f'_n:X'_n\to Y$ back along $\Phi_Y^m$.
Since $\Phi_Y^n\Phi_Y^m=\Phi_Y^{m+n}$, the outer rectangle identifies
$$
X'_{m+n}=Y\times_{\Phi_Y^m,Y,f'_n}X'_n,
\qquad f'_{m+n}=\text{first projection},\qquad
p_{m+n}=p_nq,
$$
where $q:X'_{m+n}\to X'_n$ is the second projection. On test points,
$(y,x)\in X'_m$ means $\Phi_Y^my=f(x)$, and
$t(y,x)=(y,r_n(x))=(y,(f(x),\Phi_X^nx))$ defines a map
$t:X'_m\to X'_{m+n}$. The square
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X'_m&\xrightarrow{\ p_m\ }&X\\
{\scriptstyle t}\downarrow&&\downarrow{\scriptstyle r_n}\\
X'_{m+n}&\xrightarrow{\ q\ }&X'_n
\end{array}
$$
is Cartesian: a point of the fiber product is $(y,(y',x'),x)$ with
$(y',x')=(f(x),\Phi_X^nx)$, which is exactly a point $(y,x)$ of
$X'_m$. Moreover $f'_{m+n}t=f'_m$, and
$$
tr_m(x)=(f(x),(f(x),\Phi_X^{m+n}x))=r_{m+n}(x),
$$
so $r_{m+n}=t\circ r_m$, with $t$ finite as a base change of $r_n$.

*Step 2: the comparison.* Put $M=L\Phi_X^{n*}K=Lr_n^*Lp_n^*K$.
Expand the right-hand side of (1) using the three arrows of
[def-trf-weil-shriek-pushforward]. The second factor is
$L\Phi_Y^{m*}$ of $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ for the $\Phi_Y^n$-square,
followed by $L\Phi_Y^{m*}Rf'_{n!}(\eta_{r_n})$ and the composition
identification $Rf'_{n!}Rr_{n*}\simeq Rf_!$. For the first factor,
write the Cartesian square of $f$ along $\Phi_Y^m$ as the vertical
pasting of the $t$-square above and the square of $f'_n$ along
$\Phi_Y^m$. By the pasting identity and the compatibility with the
composition law of [fix-lem-exchanges], clauses (2) and (4), its
$\operatorname{Ex}_!$ is the $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ for $f'_n$ followed
by the exchange for $r_n$ along $q$. The latter is the ordinary
exchange $\operatorname{Ex}_*:Lq^*Rr_{n*}\to Rt_*Lp_m^*$ of
[def-exchange-projection], because $r_n$ is proper and one may use
the trivial compactification; it is invertible by proper base change
([prop-functor-package], clause (4)).

By naturality of $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ in the coefficient complex
([fix-lem-exchanges], clause (1)), move
$\operatorname{Ex}_!$ for $f'_n$ past $\eta_{r_n}$. The two
exchanges for the $\Phi_Y^n$- and $\Phi_Y^m$-squares then paste, by
[fix-lem-exchanges], clause (2), to the exchange for the outer
rectangle, which is the first arrow of $\theta_{f,m+n}$. What remains
on $N=Lp_{m+n}^*K=Lq^*Lp_n^*K$ is
$$
N\xrightarrow{Lq^*\eta_{r_n}}Lq^*Rr_{n*}Lr_n^*Lp_n^*K
\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Ex}_*}Rt_*Lp_m^*Lr_n^*Lp_n^*K
\simeq Rt_*Lt^*N
\xrightarrow{Rt_*\eta_{r_m}Lt^*}Rt_*Rr_{m*}Lr_m^*Lt^*N .
$$
By the definition of $\operatorname{Ex}_*$ as the adjoint of the
counit composite in [def-exchange-projection], and the triangle
identities of $Lr_n^*\dashv Rr_{n*}$ of
[def-weil-derived-direct-image], the composite of the first two
arrows is the unit $\eta_t$ at $N$, after $Lp_m^*Lr_n^*\simeq
Lt^*Lq^*$ from $r_np_m=qt$
([def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]). The unit of the composite
adjunction for $r_{m+n}=tr_m$ is $Rt_*\eta_{r_m}Lt^*\circ\eta_t$.
Hence the displayed composite is $\eta_{r_{m+n}}$ at $N$. Finally,
all remaining arrows are composition identifications for $Rh_!$ and
$Lh^*$ ([prop-functor-package], clause (3), and
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]), which are coherent for
$f'_{m+n}tr_m=f$ and $p_nqtr_m=\Phi_X^{m+n}$. Therefore the
right-hand side of (1) equals the defining composite of
$\theta_{f,m+n,K}$, proving (1).

*Step 3: iterates.* For $m=1$, $\psi_1=\psi=Rf_!u\circ\theta_{f,1}$
is the definition. Assume the formula for $m$. By
[def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism],
$\psi_{m+1}=\psi\circ L\Phi_Y^*\psi_m$ after the pullback
composition identification. Thus
$$
\psi_{m+1}=Rf_!u\circ\theta_{f,1,K}\circ L\Phi_Y^*Rf_!u_m
\circ L\Phi_Y^*\theta_{f,m,K}.
$$
Naturality of $\theta_{f,1}$ in $K$
([def-trf-weil-shriek-pushforward]) gives
$\theta_{f,1,K}\circ L\Phi_Y^*Rf_!u_m
=Rf_!L\Phi_X^*u_m\circ\theta_{f,1,L\Phi_X^{m*}K}$. Hence
$$
\psi_{m+1}=Rf_!(u\circ L\Phi_X^*u_m)\circ
\theta_{f,1,L\Phi_X^{m*}K}\circ L\Phi_Y^*\theta_{f,m,K}
=Rf_!u_{m+1}\circ\theta_{f,m+1,K},
$$
using the recursive definition of $u_{m+1}$ in
[def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism] and (1) with the pair
$(1,m)$. This proves (2) by induction.

In the setting of [def-trf-weil-shriek-pushforward], let
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, let $u:L\Phi_X^*K\to K$ be a Frobenius
coefficient morphism of [def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism] (no
invertibility assumed), and let $(L,\psi)=(Rf_!K,Rf_!u\circ\theta_{f,1})$
be its Weil $!$-pushforward, with iterates
$\psi_m=Rf_!u_m\circ\theta_{f,m}$ ([lem-trf-weil-shriek-iterates]).

1. *Global operators.* Let
$c_f:R\Gamma_c(Y,Rf_!K)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_c(X,K)$ be the
composition isomorphism for $a_Yf=a_X$ ([prop-functor-package],
clause (3)). For every $m\geq1$ the global operators of
[def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism] satisfy
$$
c_f\circ F_{c,m}(\psi)=F_{c,m}(u)\circ c_f .
$$
1. *Fibres.* Let $m\geq1$, $y\in Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$, and let
$\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}k\to Y$ be the geometric point over $y$, so
that $\Phi_Y^m\bar y=\bar y$. Put $X_{\bar y}=X\times_{f,Y,\bar y}\operatorname{Spec}k$,
with $i_{\bar y}:X_{\bar y}\to X$, and $K|_{\bar y}=Li_{\bar y}^*K$.
Then $X_{\bar y}=X_{0,y}\times_{\mathbf F_{q^m}}k$ for the separated
finite-type $\mathbf F_{q^m}$-scheme $X_{0,y}=X_0\times_{Y_0,y}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf F_{q^m}$,
and for the finite-field datum with $q$ replaced by $q^m$
([def-weil-finite-field-fiber]) the $q^m$-power scheme Frobenius of
$X_{0,y}$ is the restriction $\Phi_{X_{\bar y}}$ of $\Phi_X^m$. The
composite
$$
u_m|_{\bar y}:L\Phi_{X_{\bar y}}^*K|_{\bar y}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
Li_{\bar y}^*L\Phi_X^{m*}K\xrightarrow{\ Li_{\bar y}^*u_m\ }K|_{\bar y}
$$
is a Frobenius coefficient morphism for this datum, and the proper
base-change isomorphism
$\beta_{\bar y}:L_{\bar y}=\bar y^*Rf_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_c(X_{\bar y},K|_{\bar y})$
([prop-functor-package], clause (4)) satisfies
$$
\beta_{\bar y}\circ\psi_{m,\bar y}=F_{c,1}\bigl(u_m|_{\bar y}\bigr)\circ\beta_{\bar y},
$$
where $\psi_{m,\bar y}:L_{\bar y}\cong(L\Phi_Y^{m*}L)_{\bar y}\to L_{\bar y}$
is the stalk map of $\psi_m$ at the fixed point $\bar y$ and $F_{c,1}$ is
the degree-one global operator over $\mathbf F_{q^m}$.
1. *Points and stalks.* $X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ is the disjoint union of
the sets $X_{0,y}(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ over $y\in Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$, and
for $x\in X_{0,y}(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ with geometric point $\bar x$ the
stalk map of $u_m|_{\bar y}$ at $\bar x$ is the stalk map $u_{m,\bar x}$.

Invertibility of $u$ is used nowhere.

## Proof

For a finite $k$-morphism $h:T'\to T$ of separated finite-type
$k$-schemes and $M\in D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$ write
$$
h^\sharp_M:R\Gamma_c(T,M)\xrightarrow{\ \eta_h\ }R\Gamma_c(T,Rh_*Lh^*M)
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }R\Gamma_c(T',Lh^*M)
$$
for the map induced by the unit of $Lh^*\dashv Rh_*$
([def-weil-derived-direct-image]), followed by $Rh_*\simeq Rh_!$ and
the composition law for $a_Th=a_{T'}$ ([prop-functor-package],
clause (3)). By [prop-trf-graph-operator], the global operator of the
graph correspondence of an endomorphism $h$ with coefficient
$w:Lh^*M\to M$ is $R\Gamma_c(T,w)\circ h^\sharp_M$; in particular
$F_{c,m}(u)=R\Gamma_c(X,u_m)\circ(\Phi_X^m)^\sharp_K$ and
$F_{c,m}(\psi)=R\Gamma_c(Y,\psi_m)\circ(\Phi_Y^m)^\sharp_L$. Two formal
properties are used.

(α) *Composition.* For finite $h':T''\to T'$ and $h:T'\to T$,
$(hh')^\sharp_M=h'^\sharp_{Lh^*M}\circ h^\sharp_M$ after
$Lh'^*Lh^*\simeq L(hh')^*$ ([def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]):
the unit of the composite adjunction is the composite of the units, and
the composition law is associative ([prop-functor-package],
clause (3)).

(β) *Base change.* In the Cartesian square of [d-relative-frob]
defining $X'_m$, the maps $\Phi_Y^m$ and $p_m$ are finite
([def-trf-scheme-frobenius]; $p_m$ is a base change of $\Phi_Y^m$). The
exchange $\operatorname{Ex}_!:L\Phi_Y^{m*}Rf_!\to Rf'_{m!}Lp_m^*$ of
[def-exchange-projection] is the mate, for the adjunctions
$L\Phi_Y^{m*}\dashv R\Phi^m_{Y*}$ and $Lp_m^*\dashv Rp_{m*}$, of the
composition isomorphism
$Rf_!Rp_{m!}\simeq R(fp_m)_!=R(\Phi_Y^mf'_m)_!\simeq R\Phi^m_{Y!}Rf'_{m!}$
([fix-lem-exchanges], item (4)). The unit compatibility of mates
([lem-trf-adjoint-mate], item (2)) says that $R\Phi^m_{Y*}\operatorname{Ex}_!$
after the unit $\eta_{\Phi_Y^m}$ at $Rf_!K$ equals $Rf_!\eta_{p_m}$ followed
by that composition isomorphism. Applying $R\Gamma_c(Y,-)$ and the
composition laws, which are coherent ([fix-lem-exchanges], items (2)
and (4)), gives
$$
c_{f'_m}\circ R\Gamma_c(Y,\operatorname{Ex}_!)\circ(\Phi_Y^m)^\sharp_L
=(p_m)^\sharp_K\circ c_f,
$$
with $c_{f'_m}:R\Gamma_c(Y,Rf'_{m!}-)\simeq R\Gamma_c(X'_m,-)$.

*(1).* By [def-trf-weil-shriek-pushforward], $\theta_{f,m}$ is
$\operatorname{Ex}_!$, then $Rf'_{m!}(\eta_{r_m})$, then the
identifications $Rf'_{m!}Rr_{m*}\simeq Rf_!$ and
$Lr_m^*Lp_m^*\simeq L\Phi_X^{m*}$; here $r_m$ is finite by
[i-relative-frob]. Under $c_{f'_m}$ and $c_f$, the second and third arrows
become $(r_m)^\sharp_{Lp_m^*K}$, by the definition of $\sharp$ and the
associativity of the composition law. Hence, by (β) and then (α) for
$p_mr_m=\Phi_X^m$,
$$
c_f\circ R\Gamma_c(Y,\theta_{f,m})\circ(\Phi_Y^m)^\sharp_L
=(r_m)^\sharp\circ(p_m)^\sharp_K\circ c_f=(\Phi_X^m)^\sharp_K\circ c_f .
$$
Naturality of $c_f$ gives
$c_f\circ R\Gamma_c(Y,Rf_!u_m)=R\Gamma_c(X,u_m)\circ c_f$. Composing,
$c_f\circ F_{c,m}(\psi)=R\Gamma_c(X,u_m)\circ(\Phi_X^m)^\sharp_K\circ c_f
=F_{c,m}(u)\circ c_f$.

*(2).* The identification $X_{\bar y}=X_{0,y}\times_{\mathbf F_{q^m}}k$
holds because both are $X_0\times_{Y_0}\operatorname{Spec}k$, with
$\operatorname{Spec}k\to Y_0$ the composite of $\bar y$ and the
projection. Since $y$ is rational over $\mathbf F_{q^m}$, the absolute
$q^m$-power Frobenius of $Y_0$ fixes it, so $\Phi_Y^m\bar y=\bar y$, and
$f\Phi_X^m=\Phi_Y^mf$ shows that $\Phi_X^m$ maps $X_{\bar y}$ to itself.
The restriction is the base change to $k$ of the absolute $q^m$-power
Frobenius of $X_{0,y}$, which is the $q^m$-power scheme Frobenius of the
$\mathbf F_{q^m}$-scheme $X_{0,y}$ of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. Hence
$u_m|_{\bar y}$ is a morphism of the required shape.

Pull the Cartesian square of [d-relative-frob] back along
$\bar y$ through $f'_m$. Because $\Phi_Y^m\bar y=\bar y$, its fibre is
$(X'_m)_{\bar y}=\operatorname{Spec}k\times_{\bar y,Y,f}X=X_{\bar y}$,
the base change of $p_m$ is $i_{\bar y}$, and since $r_m$ is a morphism
over $Y$ ($f'_mr_m=f$) with $p_mr_m=\Phi_X^m$, its base change is
$\Phi_{X_{\bar y}}$. By the pasting law for $\operatorname{Ex}_!$
([fix-lem-exchanges], item (2)), $\bar y^*\operatorname{Ex}_!$ for the
square of $f$ along $\Phi_Y^m$, followed by the base-change isomorphism
for $f'_m$ along $\bar y$, is the base-change isomorphism for $f$ along
$\Phi_Y^m\bar y=\bar y$, that is $\beta_{\bar y}$. The finite map $r_m$
satisfies proper base change, and its exchange
$\operatorname{Ex}_*$ along the fibre inclusion is compatible with the
units by the triangle identities, as in Step 2 of
[lem-trf-weil-shriek-iterates]; thus the base change of
$Rf'_{m!}(\eta_{r_m})$ along $\bar y$ is, under $\beta_{\bar y}$,
the map induced by the unit $\eta_{\Phi_{X_{\bar y}}}$, and the
remaining composition identifications become those defining
$(\Phi_{X_{\bar y}})^\sharp$. Hence
$\beta_{\bar y}\circ\bar y^*\theta_{f,m}=(\Phi_{X_{\bar y}})^\sharp_{K|_{\bar y}}\circ\beta_{\bar y}$
after the identification $\bar y^*L\Phi_Y^{m*}=\bar y^*$. By naturality
of the base-change isomorphism,
$\beta_{\bar y}\circ\bar y^*Rf_!u_m=R\Gamma_c(X_{\bar y},u_m|_{\bar y})\circ\beta_{\bar y}$.
Since $\psi_{m,\bar y}=\bar y^*Rf_!u_m\circ\bar y^*\theta_{f,m}$ under
$\bar y^*L\Phi_Y^{m*}=\bar y^*$, composing and using
[prop-trf-graph-operator] for $h=\Phi_{X_{\bar y}}$ gives
$\beta_{\bar y}\circ\psi_{m,\bar y}=F_{c,1}(u_m|_{\bar y})\circ\beta_{\bar y}$.

*(3).* An $\mathbf F_{q^m}$-point $x$ of $X_0$ lies over the
$\mathbf F_{q^m}$-point $y=f_0\circ x$ of $Y_0$, and the points of
$X_0$ over $y$ are exactly the $\mathbf F_{q^m}$-points of the fibre
$X_{0,y}$; this gives the disjoint union. The stalk of
$Li_{\bar y}^*M$ at $\bar x\in X_{\bar y}$ is $M_{\bar x}$, compatibly
with pullback identifications, so the stalk of $u_m|_{\bar y}$ at
$\bar x$ is $u_{m,\bar x}$.

attrs.title: Global operator and fibres of the Weil $!$-pushforward

objects.body:
In the setting of [def-weil-punctual-weights], if a lisse
Weil sheaf $\mathcal F$ is
punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$, then its linear dual
$\mathcal F^\vee$ ([def-real-weil-representation-operations]) is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $-w$.

## Proof

The Frobenius eigenvalues on the dual stalk at a closed point $y$ are
the inverses of the eigenvalues of $F_y$ on $\mathcal F_{\bar y}$ ([p-linear-spectra])
(the dual representation), so the complex moduli are
$q_y^{-w/2}$ by [lem-tw-multiplicativity], which is weight $-w$
in [def-weil-punctual-weights].

If $\alpha,\beta$ are eigenvalues of weights $w_1,w_2$ (as in
[def-tw-eigenvalue]), then $\alpha\beta$ has weight
$w_1+w_2$, and $\alpha^{-1}$ has weight $-w_1$ when
$\alpha\neq0$.

## Proof

In the absolute-value convention of [def-tw-eigenvalue] the
absolute value is multiplicative:
$|\alpha\beta|=|\alpha||\beta|=q^{(w_1+w_2)/2}$, and
$|\alpha^{-1}|=|\alpha|^{-1}$; the same holds in every finite extension
and every embedding.

Fix the finite-field datum
$(p,a,q,k_0,k)$, and let $h:X_0\to Y_0$ be a
finite-type morphism
of finite-type $k_0$-schemes.
Let $\mathcal F$ be a
Weil sheaf on $X_0$,
punctually pure of weight $w$.
For a closed point $y\in Y_0$, write
$m=[\kappa(y):k_0]$, so $\kappa(y)\cong\mathbf F_{q^m}$, and set

$$
X_y:=X_0\times_{Y_0}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y).
$$

Then the restriction $\mathcal F|_{X_y}$, with its induced Weil
structure, is punctually pure of weight $w$ relative to
$\kappa(y)$.

## Proof

The inclusion $X_y\hookrightarrow X_0$ is a closed immersion.
Thus a closed point $z$ of $X_y$ is the same closed point on
$X_0$, with the same residue field and the same local Frobenius
operator on the restricted stalk.
If $r=[\kappa(z):\kappa(y)]$, the tower of finite residue fields gives

$$
[\kappa(z):k_0]=mr,\qquad q_z=q^{mr}=(q^m)^r .
$$

Consequently an eigenvalue $\alpha$ on that stalk satisfies

$$
|\iota(\alpha)|=q_z^{w/2}=(q^m)^{rw/2},
$$

by [def-weil-punctual-weights] on $X_0$.
This is the same punctual weight condition over $\kappa(y)$.
No identification between the stalk at $z$ and a stalk at $y$
is involved.

attrs.title: Punctual purity on a closed fibre

objects.body:
Every root of unity $\zeta\in\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell^\times$ has
absolute value $|\zeta|=1$ with respect to the absolute value of
[def-tw-eigenvalue]; in particular every root of unity is of weight
$0$. Moreover, for every field isomorphism
$\iota:\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$, the
complex number $\iota(\zeta)$ also has modulus one.

## Proof

If $\zeta^m=1$ for some $m\geq1$, then multiplicativity of the
absolute value gives $|\zeta|^m=1$, hence $|\zeta|=1$; the same
argument applies to the complex modulus of $\iota(\zeta)$. Weight zero
is the case $w=0$ of [def-tw-eigenvalue].

attrs.title: Modulus of a root of unity

objects.body:
Fix the finite-field datum
$(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ and an isomorphism
$\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$ as in
[def-weil-punctual-weights]. If a lisse
Weil sheaf $\mathcal F$ is
punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$, then its
Tate twist $\mathcal F(n)$ is
punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w-2n$, for every
$n\in\mathbf Z$. The same shift holds for upper weight bounds: if
$\mathcal F$ is $\iota$-mixed of weights at most $w$, then
$\mathcal F(n)$ is $\iota$-mixed of weights at most $w-2n$.

## Proof

At a closed point $y$ of degree $m$, the local Frobenius operator
$F_y$ of [def-weil-punctual-weights] acts on the twist
stalk $\mathcal F(n)_{\bar y}$ as $q^{-mn}$ times the operator on
$\mathcal F_{\bar y}$, by the Frobenius-on-twists normalization of
[def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists] (the local operator is the
$m$-fold iterate of the global geometric Frobenius). Hence the
eigenvalues of $\mathcal F(n)_{\bar y}$ are the
$q^{-mn}\alpha$, $\alpha$ running over the eigenvalues of
$F_y$ on $\mathcal F_{\bar y}$, and by
[lem-tw-multiplicativity] and $q_y=q^m$,

$$
|\iota(q^{-mn}\alpha)|=q^{-mn}q^{mw/2}=q_y^{(w-2n)/2},
$$

which is the punctual purity of weight $w-2n$ of
[def-weil-punctual-weights]. For the mixed statement, apply the
pure statement to the graded pieces of a weight filtration of
$\mathcal F$ (the twist is exact and preserves the filtration by
[def-weil-frobenius-module-weights] at the level of stalk modules)
and use the same shift on each piece.

attrs.title: Weight shift under a Tate twist

objects.body:
Let $K$ be a field with $\operatorname{char}(K)\neq2$, $V$ a
finite-dimensional $K$-vector space, and $\beta:V\times V\to K$ a
nondegenerate alternating bilinear form. Then $\dim_K V$ is even.

## Proof

With $B$ the Gram matrix of $\beta$ one has $B^\top=-B$; hence
$\det(B)=\det(-B^\top)=(-1)^n\det(B)$, and $\det(B)\neq0$
(nondegenerate, $K$ a field) with $\operatorname{char}(K)\neq2$ gives
$(-1)^n=1$, i.e. $n=\dim_K V$ is even.

Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring and let $K$ be a bounded complex of finite
$R$-modules with finite Tor amplitude in the sense of
[def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]: there are integers $a\le b$ with
$\mathcal H^i(K\otimes^L_RM)=0$ for every $i\notin[a,b]$ and every
$R$-module $M$. Then $K$ is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of
finite projective $R$-modules concentrated in degrees $[a,b]$. If
$R$ is local, projective is free, so $K$ is then site-perfect in the
sense of [def-weil-site-perfect-complex].

## Proof

This is the criterion of the Stacks Project, More on Algebra,
Lemma 15.76.2, [Tag 0658](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0658),
with the definition of a perfect complex, Definition 15.76.1,
[Tag 0657](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0657): an object of
$D(R)$ is perfect, that is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of
finite projective $R$-modules, if and only if it is pseudo-coherent and of
finite Tor dimension, and a perfect complex of Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$
is quasi-isomorphic to a complex of finite projective modules vanishing
outside $[a,b]$.

Both hypotheses are available here. *Finite Tor dimension* is the
hypothesis of the statement. *Pseudo-coherence:* each term $K^i$ of
the bounded complex is a finite module over the Noetherian ring $R$, hence
finitely presented; resolving the terms by finite free modules and taking
the total complex of the resulting double complex, with the usual signs,
gives a bounded-above complex of finite free $R$-modules together with a
quasi-isomorphism onto $K$, which is precisely the condition that $K$ is
pseudo-coherent. Finally, over a local ring a finite projective module is
free: a finitely generated projective module is a direct summand of a finite
free module, and over a local ring such a summand has constant rank, hence
is free. A finite module over the Noetherian ring $R$ is perfect if and
only if it admits a finite resolution by finite projective modules, which is
the case at hand; this is Stacks Project, More on Algebra, Lemma 15.76.3,
[Tag 066Q](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/066Q).

attrs.title: Bounded complexes of finite Tor amplitude are perfect

objects.body:
Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion and suppose the
ambient exceptional adjoints are defined, with
$\omega_Z=Ri^!\omega_T$. Put
$D_T=R\mathcal Hom_T(-,\omega_T)$ and
$D_Z=R\mathcal Hom_Z(-,\omega_Z)$. Then there is a natural
isomorphism

$$
\alpha_K:Ri^!D_TK\xrightarrow{\sim}D_Zi^*K.
$$

This assertion does not use biduality.

## Proof

For any test complex $N$ on $Z$, the tensor adjunction of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and the closed exceptional
adjunction of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] give

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_Z(N,Ri^!D_TK)
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_T(i_*N\otimes^L K,\omega_T)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_T(i_*(N\otimes^L i^*K),\omega_T)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z(N\otimes^L i^*K,\omega_Z)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z(N,D_Zi^*K).
\end{aligned}
$$

The middle projection identity holds for a closed immersion in the
recollement of [def-weil-open-closed-recollement] because
$i_*$ is exact and fully faithful, and its stalkwise extension by
zero commutes with tensor product; flat resolutions give the derived
identity. The calculation localizes on every etale test object, so it
identifies the internal Hom objects. Yoneda proves the isomorphism.
Every arrow is defined by adjunction and evaluation, giving naturality.

attrs.title: Exceptional restriction of a Verdier dual

objects.body:
For the coefficient stages of
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] and
[def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], the following distinctions hold.

1. If $\Lambda=A_{E,n},E$, or
$\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, then $\Lambda$ is self-injective and
quasi-Frobenius. Ordinary duality $\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(-,\Lambda)$
is exact, preserves finite modules, and for every finite
$\Lambda$-module $M$ the evaluation map
$$
M\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda\bigl(\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(M,\Lambda),\Lambda\bigr)
$$
is an isomorphism. Consequently derived coefficient duality is an
anti-equivalence on bounded complexes with finite cohomology.
1. The discrete valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ is not
quasi-Frobenius. Ordinary evaluation is an isomorphism for finite
projective $R$-modules, but not for all finite $R$-modules.
Every $K\in D^b(R)$ with finite cohomology is perfect, and the
*derived* evaluation
$$
K\longrightarrow
R\operatorname{Hom}_R\bigl(R\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,R),R\bigr)
$$
is an isomorphism.
1. More generally, derived evaluation into the coefficient double dual
is an isomorphism for every perfect complex over any ring. In particular,
the finite-Tor point case does not require self-injectivity of the
coefficient ring.

## Proof

The field cases are finite-dimensional vector-space duality. For
$A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, every ideal is
$\varpi^iA$. A homomorphism $u:\varpi^iA\to A$ satisfies
$\varpi^{n-i}u(\varpi^i)=0$, hence
$u(\varpi^i)\in\varpi^iA$. Write
$u(\varpi^i)=\varpi^ib$; multiplication by $b$ extends $u$ to
$A$. Baer's criterion, Stacks Project,
[Tag 0AVF](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AVF), now gives
self-injectivity. Since $A$ is Artinian, it is quasi-Frobenius.
A finite $A$-module is a finite direct sum of cyclic modules
$A/\varpi^i$, so it suffices to check evaluation on these. A functional
$A/\varpi^i\to A$ is determined by its value at $1$, which lies in
$\operatorname{Ann}_A(\varpi^i)=\varpi^{n-i}A/\varpi^n$, so that

$$
\operatorname{Hom}_A(A/\varpi^i,A)\cong\varpi^{n-i}A/\varpi^n
\cong A/\varpi^i ;
$$

the evaluation map at $1$ is a generator of the double dual, hence an
isomorphism. Exactness of $\operatorname{Hom}_A(-,A)$ and bounded
truncation give derived biduality for bounded finite cohomology.

Over $R=\mathcal O_E$, the finite module $T=R/\varpi_E R$ is
nonzero but $\operatorname{Hom}_R(T,R)=0$. In particular ordinary
duality is not exact: applying it to
$0\to R\xrightarrow{\varpi_E}R\to T\to0$ leaves the nonsurjective
map $R\xrightarrow{\varpi_E}R$. Thus $R$ is not self-injective.
It is a regular ring, so bounded complexes with finite cohomology are
perfect by Stacks Project,
[Tag 066Z](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/066Z).
For a perfect complex over any ring, a bounded finite projective model
computes its derived dual, and termwise evaluation computes the derived
double dual; this is Stacks Project,
[Tag 07VI](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07VI).
It proves both the integral assertion and the last clause.

attrs.title: Coefficient biduality at finite and integral stages

objects.body:
Let $K_0$ be a field, let $X,Y$ be finite-type
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] $K_0$-schemes, let $f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type $K_0$-morphism, fix a prime $\ell$ whose image in $K_0$
is invertible, and fix an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$. Let
$K_{\Qlb}\in D^b_c(X,\Qlb)$ be an object of the common-stage category of
[def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] represented at the finite
coefficient stages $E\subset L\subset\Qlb$ by $K_E\in D^b_c(X,E)$ and $K_L\in
D^b_c(X,L)$ of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Then the two objects

$$
 Rf_!K_E\otimes_E\Qlb,\qquad Rf_!K_L\otimes_L\Qlb
$$

of $D^b_c(Y,\Qlb)$, formed from the compact-support functor
[def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], are canonically
isomorphic.

## Proof

The scalar-extension functors between the finite stages of
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] are exact and compatible with composition
by [lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition], and the finite-stage
compact-support functors of
[def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] carry the scalar-extension
isomorphisms supplied by the common-stage construction of
[def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. By the descent-of-functors
proposition of the proper-base-change chapter the compatible family therefore
descends to a single exact functor on the common-stage category, so its value
on the object $K_{\Qlb}$ is computed indifferently at the stage $E$ or at the
larger stage $L$.

attrs.title: Independence of the finite coefficient field

objects.body:
Let $K_0$ be a field, let $X,Y$ be finite-type
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] $K_0$-schemes, let $f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type $K_0$-morphism, fix a prime $\ell$ whose image in $K_0$
is invertible, and choose a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with valuation ring
$\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$. Let $K,K'\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal
O_E)$ be integral complexes of the derived-complete integral category
[def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] representing the same object of
the rationalized category $D^b_c(X,E)$ of
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Then the two objects

$$
 (Rf_!K)\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}E,\qquad
 (Rf_!K')\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}E
$$

of $D^b_c(Y,E)$, formed from the compact-support direct image
[def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], are canonically
isomorphic.

## Proof

The integral compact-support functor $K\mapsto
R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nRf_{!,n}K_n$ of
[def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] is $\mathcal O_E$-linear
and exact on the derived-complete integral constructible category
$D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]: it
is built from the finite-level functors $Rf_{!,n}$ of
[def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], each triangulated by
[lem-compact-support-direct-image-triangulated], and from the derived limit
[def-weil-derived-limit], which is triangulated by its defining triangle. By
the rational-transport proposition of the proper-base-change chapter every
exact $\mathcal O_E$-linear functor on the integral constructible category
extends uniquely to its rationalization $D^b_c(X,E)$ of
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]; a uniquely determined extension takes the
same value on any two integral representatives $K,K'$ of one object, and that
identification is the canonical isomorphism asserted.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism of separated finite-type
schemes over a field, and use finite coefficients invertible there.
On the ambient etale derived categories let
$\omega_T=Ra_T^{\times}A$ and
$D_T=R\mathcal Hom_A(-,\omega_T)$. For every complex $K$,
the ambient exchange $D_YRf_*\cong Rf_*D_X$ identifies
$Rf_*\delta_K$ with $\delta_{Rf_*K}$. In particular, if the
latter is an isomorphism then so is the former.
Neither exceptional-adjoint admissibility on a constructible
subcategory nor geometric biduality is assumed.

## Proof

Composition of the ambient right adjoints of
[thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] gives
$f^{\times}\omega_Y=\omega_X$. As $f$ is proper,
$Rf_!=Rf_*$; the ambient internal adjunction of
[prop-asd-internal-adjunction], valid for arbitrary complexes,
therefore gives $D_YRf_*\cong Rf_*D_X$.

Push forward the evaluation of [lem-weil-duality-pairing] and
compose with the projection morphism of
[lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] and the exceptional counit.
The resulting pairing is

$$
Rf_*K\otimes_A^LRf_*D_XK
\longrightarrow Rf_*(K\otimes_A^LD_XK)
\longrightarrow Rf_*\omega_X\longrightarrow\omega_Y.
$$

The isomorphism of [prop-asd-internal-adjunction] is exactly the
adjoint of this pairing. Transpose evaluation twice. Its first
transpose is the double-dual arrow by definition, while its second
transpose is evaluation for the dual precomposed with that arrow.
Tensor symmetry includes its Koszul signs. Naturality of the
projection morphism and counit therefore identifies the two
transposes after push-forward with the same transposes of the
displayed pairing. Equivalently, the canonical composite

$$
Rf_*D_XD_XK\cong D_YRf_*D_XK
\cong D_YD_YRf_*K
$$

carries $Rf_*\delta_K$ to $\delta_{Rf_*K}$. Both comparison
maps are isomorphisms independently of biduality, proving the last
assertion as well.

attrs.title: The double-dual morphism under a proper push-forward

objects.body:
Let $j:W\to Y$ be etale between separated finite-type schemes over
a field, with finite coefficients invertible there. For the ambient
etale dualizing objects, the canonical identifications
$j^*\omega_Y=\omega_W$ and $j^*D_Y=D_Wj^*$ identify
$j^*\delta_K$ with $\delta_{j^*K}$. Thus biduality is local
for the etale topology. The same restriction calculation applies
to the finite pro-etale realization.

## Proof

Etale locality of the ambient adjoint,
[lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality], identifies
$j^*\omega_Y$ with $\omega_W$. Restriction to the etale
slice commutes with derived internal Hom. Indeed, its left adjoint
is exact etale extension by zero, so restriction preserves injective
resolutions, and ordinary internal Hom restricts to the internal Hom
on that slice. Applying exact monoidal restriction to the evaluation
of [lem-weil-duality-pairing] therefore gives evaluation for
$j^*K$. Transpose with the tensor–Hom adjunction of
