[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]; this gives the claimed
identity of double-dual maps. An isomorphism is detected by a covering
family. The proof is a slice-site argument and also applies on the
pro-etale realization; it does not apply to ordinary restriction
along a closed immersion.

Let $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}Z$ be morphisms of schemes on which
$\ell$ is invertible, and use the derived direct images of
[def-weil-derived-direct-image]. There is a canonical isomorphism

$$
 c_{g,f}:R(g\circ f)_*\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rg_*\circ Rf_*
$$

at each coefficient stage of that definition:

1. at finite level $A_{E,n}$, as functors
$D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})\to D(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})$;
1. for $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$, on those $K\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ with
$Rf_*K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ (so that the right side is defined);
1. for $\Lambda=E$, on the rationalized category of
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], for the same $K$;
1. for $\Lambda=\Qlb$, on the common-stage category of
[def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], for objects $(E,K)$ with $K$
as in (3);
1. on the small étale site, for any ring $A$, as functors
$D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)\to D(Z_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ between the ordinary
derived categories of étale sheaves of $A$-modules.

The isomorphism $c_{g,f}$ is natural in $K$, is the identity when $f$ or $g$
is an identity, and is associative: for a further morphism $h:Z\to W$ the
two isomorphisms $R(hgf)_*\cong Rh_*Rg_*Rf_*$ built from $c$ agree. In
particular it is compatible with transport of structure along automorphisms
of $X,Y,Z$ commuting with $f$ and $g$ (such as Frobenius), since the direct
image along an automorphism $\sigma$ is the inverse image along
$\sigma^{-1}$.

## Proof

*Finite level.* Put $A=A_{E,n}$. The constant sheaves satisfy
$f^{-1}A_Y=A_X$, so the sheaf-level inverse image $f^{-1}$ of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] is an exact left adjoint of
$f_*:\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)\to\Sh(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$. Hence $f_*$
carries K-injective complexes [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions] to
K-injective complexes: for an acyclic $B$ one has
$\operatorname{Hom}(B,f_*I)=\operatorname{Hom}(f^{-1}B,I)$, and $f^{-1}B$ is
acyclic. This is the argument of
[lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-preserves-injectives], applied to complexes and
on the pro-etale site. If $K\to I$ is a K-injective resolution, then $f_*I$
is a K-injective complex computing $Rf_{*,n}K$, so
$Rg_{*,n}Rf_{*,n}K=g_*f_*I=(gf)_*I=R(gf)_{*,n}K$. By the well-definedness
and functoriality of K-injective resolutions
([lem-sp-kinjective-computes], part (1)), the resulting isomorphism does not
depend on $I$ and is natural in $K$. Identity and associativity hold because
$(hg)f=h(gf)$ already holds for the sheaf-level functors on the same
representative $I$. The same argument applies verbatim on the small étale site with any
coefficient ring (item (5)) and to sheaves of abelian groups, and for $\widehat{\mathcal O}_E$-modules it gives the composition
isomorphism for the derived functor $Rh^{\wedge}_*$ of
$h_*:\Sh(-,\mathcal O_E)\to\Sh(-,\mathcal O_E)$ in the following form. The
derived direct image of modules over a sheaf of rings is computed on the
underlying abelian sheaves, since a K-injective complex of modules is K-limp
and so acyclic for the direct image of abelian sheaves. The canonical map
$R(gf)^{\wedge}_*\to Rg^{\wedge}_*Rf^{\wedge}_*$ given by the universal
property of right derived functors therefore becomes the abelian-sheaf
isomorphism after the forgetful functor to abelian sheaves. That functor
reflects isomorphisms, so the map is an isomorphism.

*Integral stage.* Let $h$ be any of $f,g,gf$ and let $K$ be derived complete
[def-weil-derived-complete]. First, $Rh^{\wedge}_*$ commutes with
$\operatorname{Res}_n$: the functor $\operatorname{Res}_n$ is exact
([lem-weil-restriction-of-scalars-exact]) and commutes with $h_*$ on sheaves.
Both $\operatorname{Res}_nRh_{*,n}$ and $Rh^{\wedge}_*\operatorname{Res}_n$
are computed on underlying abelian sheaves by the previous paragraph, so the
canonical comparison
$\operatorname{Res}_nRh_{*,n}\to Rh^{\wedge}_*\operatorname{Res}_n$ is an
isomorphism. Second, $Rh^{\wedge}_*$ commutes with countable products,
because a product of K-injective complexes is K-injective and $h_*$
commutes with products termwise. It is also exact, so it carries the Roos
triangle of [def-weil-derived-limit] for the system
$(\operatorname{Res}_nK_n)$ to a Roos triangle for
$(Rh^{\wedge}_*\operatorname{Res}_nK_n)$. Combining these facts with
derived completeness $K\xrightarrow{\sim}R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nK_n$
gives

$$
 Rh_*K=R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nRh_{*,n}K_n
 \cong R\varprojlim_nRh^{\wedge}_*\operatorname{Res}_nK_n
 \cong Rh^{\wedge}_*R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nK_n
 \cong Rh^{\wedge}_*K ,
$$

so the direct image of [def-weil-derived-direct-image] is the derived functor
$Rh^{\wedge}_*$ on derived-complete objects. For $K\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$
with $Rf_*K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$, both $K$ and $Rf_*K$ are derived
complete ([def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]). Applying this
identification for $h=gf$, $f$ and $g$ therefore gives

$$
 R(gf)_*K\cong R(gf)^{\wedge}_*K\cong Rg^{\wedge}_*Rf^{\wedge}_*K
 \cong Rg_*Rf_*K,
$$

the middle step being the composition isomorphism for $\widehat{\mathcal
O}_E$-modules. Naturality, identity and associativity are inherited from the
module level.

*Rational stage.* By [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], $D^b_c(-,E)$ has the
same objects as $D^b_c(-,\mathcal O_E)$ and
$\operatorname{Hom}\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$ as morphisms, and $Rf_*$ on it is
the $\mathcal O_E$-linear integral functor followed by $-\otimes_{\mathcal
O_E}E$ on morphisms. The integral isomorphism $c_{g,f}$ is a natural
isomorphism of $\mathcal O_E$-linear functors, so its image is a natural
isomorphism of the rationalized functors. The identity and associativity
equations are preserved.

*Algebraically closed stage.* In the common-stage category of
[def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], an object $(E,K)$ has direct
image $(E,Rf_*K)$, and a morphism is represented at some finite $L\supset E$
after scalar extension. Take $c_{g,f}$ at stage $E$ on objects. It is
compatible with scalar extension to $L$, which is what naturality for
morphisms represented at $L$ requires. Indeed, on integral representatives
$-\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$ is, as an $\widehat{\mathcal
O}_E$-module, a finite direct sum of copies of the identity ($\mathcal O_L$
being finite free over $\mathcal O_E$). The derived functors $Rh^{\wedge}_*$
and the composition isomorphism commute with finite direct sums and with the
forgetful functors along $\widehat{\mathcal O}_E\to\widehat{\mathcal O}_L$,
since all of them are computed on underlying abelian sheaves. The iterated
extensions agree by [lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition]. Hence $c_{g,f}$
at stage $E$ and at stage $L$ correspond under scalar extension, giving a
natural isomorphism in $D^b_c(Z,\Qlb)$ with the stated identity and
associativity properties.

Finally, for an automorphism $\sigma$ the direct image $R\sigma_*$ is
inverse to $R(\sigma^{-1})_*$ by the identity and associativity properties.
An automorphism of the diagram $X\to Y\to Z$ therefore transports $c_{g,f}$
to itself by associativity, which is the asserted compatibility with
transport of structure.

Let $\mathcal D$ be a triangulated category and let $(K_n,f_n)$ be an inverse
system of objects of $\mathcal D$.

1. If $\prod_nK_n$ exists in $\mathcal D$, then a derived limit
   [def-weil-derived-limit] $R\varprojlim_nK_n$ exists, and any two derived
   limits of the system are isomorphic, although not canonically so.
2. Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category with exact countable products and
   let $\mathcal D=D(\mathcal A)$. Then countable products exist in $\mathcal
   D$, are represented by termwise products of any representatives, and
   satisfy $H^p\bigl(\prod_iK_i\bigr)\cong\prod_iH^p(K_i)$ for all $p$.
3. In the situation of (2), assume in addition that $\mathcal A$ has enough
   injectives. If $I_\bullet$ is a K-injective representative, in the abelian
   category of towers in $\mathcal A$, of the system $(K_n,f_n)$, then
   $\varprojlim_nI_n$ represents $R\varprojlim_nK_n$. Consequently "choosing
   a K-injective replacement of the tower" and "taking the first term of the
   Roos triangle" [def-weil-derived-limit] produce isomorphic objects.

## Proof

Assertion (1) is axiom TR1 applied to the defining triangle of
[def-weil-derived-limit], together with TR3 for the uniqueness of a cone;
this is Definition 13.34.1 of the Stacks Project, Tag
[08TC](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08TC) and the remarks following
it, and it also explains why a derived limit is determined only up to a
non-unique isomorphism. Assertion (2) is Lemma 13.34.2 of the Stacks Project,
Tag [07KC](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07KC): since countable
products are exact in $\mathcal A$, the termwise product of representatives
represents the product in $D(\mathcal A)$, and its cohomology is the product
of the cohomologies. Assertion (3) is the K-injective presentation of the
right derived functor of $\varprojlim$. The Stacks Project form of the model
statement is Lemma 13.34.6, Tag
[070M](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/070M), which treats the
truncation tower $I_n$ built from a single complex $K^\bullet$ by the
construction of Lemma 13.29.3 and concludes that $\varprojlim_nI_n$ exists,
is K-injective, and represents $R\varprojlim_n\tau_{\ge-n}K^\bullet$; the
general-tower form used here is the same argument applied to a K-injective
replacement of the given tower. Its inputs are that a product of K-injective
complexes is K-injective (Tag
[0BK6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BK6), Lemma 13.31.5, stated
there without a bounded-below hypothesis, only that the termwise products
exist) and that every complex of the ambient category admits a K-injective
resolution: for a Grothendieck abelian category this is Tag
[079P](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/079P), Theorem 19.12.6, and the
ambient categories occurring in this blueprint are categories of sheaves of
modules, which are Grothendieck; the general form for an abelian category
with exact countable products and enough injectives is Spaltenstein's
theorem. The existence of the products used is Lemma 13.34.3, Tag
[0BK7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BK7).

attrs.title: Existence and computation of derived limits

objects.body:
Fix a scheme $Y$ and a commutative ring $A$, and use the small pro-etale site
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$. For complexes
$K_1,K_2,K_1',K_2'$ of $A_Y$-modules, every pair of morphisms $K_1\to K_1'$
and $K_2\to K_2'$ in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ induces a morphism

$$
 K_1\otimes_A^LK_2\longrightarrow K_1'\otimes_A^LK_2'
$$

between the objects of [def-weil-derived-tensor], and the assignment carries
identities to identities and composites to composites in each variable.

## Proof

On the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], choose
K-flat resolutions $P\to K_1$ and $P'\to K_1'$, so that
$K_1\otimes_A^LK_2=P\otimes_AK_2$ and $K_1'\otimes_A^LK_2'=P'\otimes_AK_2'$
by [def-weil-derived-tensor]. For a morphism $K_2\to K_2'$ the ordinary
tensor product $P\otimes_A-$ is functorial and the result is independent of
the resolution $P\to K_1$ by
[lem-weil-derived-tensor-resolution-independent]. For a morphism $K_1\to
K_1'$, the composite $P\to K_1\to K_1'$ factors, up to homotopy, through a
morphism of complexes $P\to P'$ which is well defined in the homotopy
category (Lemma 15.60.16 of the Stacks Project, Tag
[0G6M](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0G6M)); tensoring it with $K_2$
and applying [lem-weil-derived-tensor-resolution-independent] once more gives
the induced morphism, again independently of the resolutions. Compatibility
with identities and composition is inherited from the ordinary tensor product
together with the uniqueness of the lifted maps in the homotopy category, and
the two constructions agree up to the canonical commutativity constraint of
Lemma 15.60.14 of the Stacks Project, Tag
[0BYI](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BYI), which is functorial in
both complexes; hence the object is functorial in both variables at once.

attrs.title: Functoriality of the derived tensor product

objects.body:
Fix a scheme $Y$, a commutative ring $A$, and complexes $K_1,K_2$ of
$A_Y$-modules on the small pro-etale site
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Let $P\to K_1$
and $P'\to K_1$ be quasi-isomorphisms of complexes of $A_Y$-modules whose
sources are K-flat [def-weil-derived-tensor]. Then the induced map

$$
 P\otimes_AK_2\longrightarrow P'\otimes_AK_2
$$

is a quasi-isomorphism. Consequently the object $K_1\otimes_A^LK_2$ of
[def-weil-derived-tensor] is independent of the chosen K-flat resolution, up
to canonical isomorphism in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$.

## Proof

Over a ring, a quasi-isomorphism $\alpha:P\to Q$ between K-flat complexes
induces a quasi-isomorphism
$\operatorname{id}_L\otimes\alpha:\operatorname{Tot}(L\otimes P)\to
\operatorname{Tot}(L\otimes Q)$ for every complex $L$: this is Lemma 15.60.12
of the Stacks Project, Tag
[064L](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/064L), whose proof uses only the
K-flatness [def-weil-derived-tensor] of the two complexes, the existence of
K-flat resolutions (Tag
[06Y4](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06Y4)) and the behaviour of
K-flatness under tensoring (Tag
[06Y0](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06Y0)). For complexes of
$A_Y$-modules on the small pro-etale site
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] the same argument applies: tensor
products, total complexes and truncations are formed termwise in the abelian
category of sheaves of $A_Y$-modules, in which filtered colimits are exact,
and K-flat resolutions exist by the functorial flat-resolution construction.
Since $P$ and $P'$ are both K-flat resolutions of $K_1$, the identity of
$K_1$ lifts to a morphism $P\to P'$ in the homotopy category of complexes
(Tag [0G6M](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0G6M)), and the resulting
map $P\otimes_AK_2\to P'\otimes_AK_2$ is a quasi-isomorphism by the first
part. This is the assertion recorded for modules in Definition 15.60.13 of
the Stacks Project, Tag
[064M](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/064M) (the category of K-flat
resolutions of $K_1$ is cofiltered and Lemma 15.60.12 shows that the functor
obtained is independent of the choice).

attrs.title: Resolution independence of the derived tensor product

objects.body:
Let $X$ be a separated finite-type scheme over a field, with finite
coefficients invertible on that field. On the ambient etale derived
category put $\omega_X=Ra_X^{\times}A$, using the right adjoint of
[thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], and let
$D_X=R\mathcal Hom_A(-,\omega_X)$. For every complex $K$, the
evaluation of internal Hom is a natural pairing

$$
\mathrm{ev}_K:D_XK\otimes_A^LK\longrightarrow\omega_X.
$$

Its transpose is the natural double-dual morphism
$\delta_K:K\to D_XD_XK$. It is compatible with shifts and is a
morphism of distinguished triangles. The same formal construction
applies on the pro-etale site whenever its ambient dualizing object is
specified; it does not assume that $D_XK$ is constructible.

## Proof

The tensor–internal-Hom adjunction of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] has evaluation as its
counit. Compose that evaluation with tensor symmetry, and transpose
under the same adjunction, obtaining $\delta_K$. Naturality of the
counit gives naturality of this map. Internal Hom is triangulated in
each variable, with the standard shift and Koszul-sign conventions, by
[lem-sf-hom-triangulated] (on the pro-etale site by the same Hom-complex
argument);
the natural transformation to its double application therefore
commutes with shifts and gives a morphism of triangles. This
construction takes place in the ambient categories, before any
preservation assertion.

attrs.title: The duality pairing and the double-dual morphism

objects.body:
Let $\mathcal T$ be a triangulated category with a t-structure $(\mathcal
T^{\le0},\mathcal T^{\ge0})$, and let $(\Kar\mathcal T)^{\le0}$ and
$(\Kar\mathcal T)^{\ge0}$ be the closures under retracts of the images of
$\mathcal T^{\le0}$ and $\mathcal T^{\ge0}$ in the Karoubi envelope $\mathcal
T^\natural=\Kar(\mathcal T)$ of [def-weil-karoubi-envelope]. These form a
t-structure on $\mathcal T^\natural$, the truncation triangle of an object
$(K,e)$ being

$$
 (\tau^{\le0}K,e_{\le0})\longrightarrow(K,e)\longrightarrow
 (\tau^{\ge1}K,e_{\ge1})\longrightarrow(\tau^{\le0}K,e_{\le0})[1],
$$

where $e_{\le0}=\tau^{\le0}(e)$ and $e_{\ge1}=\tau^{\ge1}(e)$. Its heart is
canonically equivalent to the Karoubi envelope $\Kar(\mathcal
T^{\le0}\cap\mathcal T^{\ge0})$ of the heart of $\mathcal T$.

(*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this form: it would require a
t-structure on $\mathcal T$, which Stacks does not define (see the pages
listed at [def-weil-t-structure]; the truncation triangle itself is Remark
13.12.4, Tag [08J5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08J5)), and an
idempotent completion of a triangulated category, which Stacks does not
construct (Homological Algebra, Section 12.4, Tag
[09SF](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09SF)). The blueprint adds the
retract-closure t-structure on the Karoubi envelope, functoriality of the
truncation triangle under an idempotent endomorphism, and the identification
of its heart with the envelope of the heart.)

## Proof

The shift conditions of [def-weil-t-structure] and the orthogonality are
preserved by retracts: the shift is an equivalence, and a morphism from a
retract of an object of $\mathcal T^{\le0}$ to a retract of an object of
$\mathcal T^{\ge1}$ is a retract of an element of the zero group
$\Hom_{\mathcal T}(A,B[-1])$, hence zero. For the truncation axiom,
functoriality of the truncation triangle $A(K)\to K\to C(K)\to A(K)[1]$ in
$K\in\mathcal T$ (with $A(K)=\tau^{\le0}K$, $C(K)=\tau^{\ge1}K$) applied to
the idempotent endomorphism $e:K\to K$ produces an idempotent endomorphism
$(e_{\le0},e,e_{\ge1})$ of the triangle; its components are idempotent
because the square of the endomorphism is the endomorphism induced by
$e^2=e$. Its image triangle in $\mathcal T^\natural$ is a retract of the
image of the truncation triangle, hence distinguished by
[lem-weil-karoubi-envelope-triangulated]; since $\tau^{\le0}K\in\mathcal
T^{\le0}$ and $\tau^{\ge1}K\in\mathcal T^{\ge1}$, the image triangle has the
requisite retract-factors $(\tau^{\le0}K,e_{\le0})\in(\mathcal
T^\natural)^{\le0}$ and $(\tau^{\ge1}K,e_{\ge1})\in(\mathcal
T^\natural)^{\ge1}$, and the image over all $K$ and $e$ gives the truncation
triangle axiom. For the heart: an object $(K,e)$ of the heart has zero
$\tau^{\le-1}$-part in the extended t-structure, so its truncation triangle
exhibits $(K,e)\cong H^0((K,e))$ $=(\mathcal H^0K,\mathcal H^0(e))$, with
$\mathcal H^0K\in\mathcal H(\mathcal T)$; conversely, for $A\in\mathcal
H(\mathcal T)$ and an idempotent $e$ of $A$, the object $(A,e)$ of $\mathcal
T^\natural$ is a retract of the image $(A,\operatorname{id}_A)$ of $A$, hence
lies in the heart. The two constructions are inverse up to the canonical
functor of [def-weil-karoubi-envelope], so the heart is exactly $\Kar(\mathcal
H(\mathcal T))$.

The functor $j_!$ of [def-weil-extension-by-zero] is left adjoint to
restriction $j^*$ on pro-etale module sheaves.

## Proof

For an open immersion the site over $U$ is the slice of
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] over $U$: maps into $U$ are unique
when they exist, and the coverings are the same coverings over the larger
scheme. A morphism from the presheaf $P_M$ of [def-weil-extension-by-zero] to
a sheaf $N$ is therefore precisely a compatible family $M(V)\to N(V)$ on
objects over $U$; on all other objects the source is zero. This is a morphism
$M\to j^*N$. Sheafification preserves maps to sheaves, so it gives
$\operatorname{Hom}(j_!M,N)=\operatorname{Hom}(M,j^*N)$, naturally in both
arguments.

Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow\overline X$ be
an open immersion [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] of schemes and use
the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] with the
constant coefficient sheaf $A$, including the finite-torsion coefficient
rings [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] $A_{E,n}$. Then the
extension-by-zero functor [def-weil-extension-by-zero] $j_!$ is exact.

## Proof

In the presheaf construction of [def-weil-extension-by-zero], kernels are
computed objectwise: on an object over $U$ this is the kernel of the
corresponding section map, and on other objects it is zero. Sheafification of
module presheaves is exact, so $j_!$ preserves kernels on the module sheaves
of [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. For an epimorphism $M\to N$, a
section of $P_N(V)$ is either zero or a section of $N(V)$ with $V$ over $U$.
In the latter case it lifts on a covering of $V$ in $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$.
This is also a covering in the ambient site of
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Thus $P_M\to P_N$ is locally
surjective; after sheafification it is an epimorphism. Preservation of
kernels and epimorphisms proves exactness.

Let $F$ be a field, let $Y$ be a scheme, and let $K$ be a bounded
constructible complex at a field coefficient stage: an object of the
rationalized category $D^b_c(Y,E)$ of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] with
$F=E$, or an object of the common-stage category $D^b_c(Y,\Qlb)$ of
[def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] with $F=\Qlb$. Then $K$ has
finite Tor amplitude in the sense of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]: there
are integers $a\leq b$ such that

$$
 \mathcal H^r\bigl(K\otimes^L_FM\bigr)=0
 \qquad(r\in\mathbf Z\setminus[a,b])
$$

for every sheaf $M$ of $F$-modules placed in degree zero, the derived tensor
product being that of [def-weil-derived-tensor].

## Proof

Over a field $F$ every $F$-module is flat, so a sheaf $M$ of $F$-modules
placed in degree zero is K-flat and the derived tensor product of
[def-weil-derived-tensor] is computed by the ordinary tensor product; hence
$\mathcal H^r(K\otimes^L_FM)\cong\mathcal H^r(K)\otimes_FM$ for every
$r\in\mathbf Z$. The bounded constructibility imposed in
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and in
[def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] gives integers $a\leq b$ with
$\mathcal H^r(K)=0$ for $r\notin[a,b]$; on this interval the vanishing
required by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] holds vacuously in the remaining
degrees, and off it both sides vanish. Such a pair $a\leq b$ is therefore a
finite Tor amplitude interval for $K$.

attrs.title: Finite Tor amplitude at field coefficients

objects.body:
Fix the finite-field datum
and finite coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$.
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type
morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes.
On the small etale sites, let
$K\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and
$L\in D^b_c(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, in the
derived categories of
bounded complexes with constructible cohomology.
Assume $L$ has
finite Tor amplitude,
using the same tensor-vanishing definition on the etale site.
The projection transformation,
formed with the
derived tensor and pullback
and the compact-support
direct image, is an isomorphism:

$$
Rf_!K\otimes_A^L L
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } Rf_!(K\otimes_A^L Lf^*L).
$$

It is natural in $K,L$.
The same assertion holds for their pro-etale realizations equipped
with etale-origin witnesses,
where the representatives satisfy the displayed hypotheses.

## Proof

First work on the etale site. Choose a compactification
$f=p\circ j$. By [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed],
$Rf_!=Rp_*j_!$. The map of [def-exchange-projection]
is the composite of the direct-image projection map for $p$
and

$$
j_!K\otimes_A^L p^*L
\cong j_!(K\otimes_A^L f^*L).
$$

The latter isomorphism can be checked on etale stalks: on the open
subset both maps are the identity, and off it both terms are zero.
The same calculation works with K-flat representatives for the
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] derived tensor product.

Let $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ be a geometric point,
let $X_{\bar y}=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, and write
$K_{\bar y}^{\mathrm{fib}}$ for the pullback of $K$ to this fiber
and $P=L_{\bar y}\in D(A)$.
Compact-support base change [thm-cbc-finite-torsion]
and exactness of geometric stalks identify the stalk of the
displayed projection map with

$$
R\Gamma_c(X_{\bar y},K_{\bar y}^{\mathrm{fib}})\otimes_A^L P
\longrightarrow
R\Gamma_c(X_{\bar y},
K_{\bar y}^{\mathrm{fib}}\otimes_A^L\underline P).
$$

Here $\underline P$ is the pullback of the complex of $A$-modules
$P$ from $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$.
Both base-change applications are legitimate: finite Tor amplitude
of $L$ makes $K\otimes_A^L f^*L$ bounded below.

This identification concerns the actual projection map.
Indeed the exchange map in [def-cbc-exchange-map] is obtained
from proper base change and the open-immersion base-change map.
For the proper part, transposing either order of exchange and
projection gives the same composite: pull back
$Rp_*j_!K\otimes L$, apply the counit
$p^*Rp_*j_!K\to j_!K$ to the first factor, and retain the
pullback of $L$ in the second factor.
For the open part, both composites are the identity on the open
stalks and zero on the complementary stalks. Thus the exchange
identifications carry the chosen projection map to the fiber map.

The stalk-perfectness lemma [fix-lem-finite-tor-perfect]
gives a bounded finite-free representative of $P$.
For fixed $K_{\bar y}^{\mathrm{fib}}$, the two sides of the fiber
map are exact functors of $P$ on bounded complexes of finite
projective $A$-modules, and the displayed map is a natural
transformation of these functors.
For $P=A$ it is the unit identification, hence an isomorphism.
It remains an isomorphism after finite direct sums, shifts,
mapping cones, and direct summands: for cones use the long exact
cohomology sequences, and for summands restrict the inverse along
the splitting maps.
Successive truncation by terms builds every bounded finite-free
complex from finite sums of shifts of $A$.
It follows that the fiber map is an isomorphism for this $P$.
Every geometric stalk of the cone of the original projection map
therefore vanishes. Conservativity on the etale site,
[lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative], proves that its
cone is zero. Naturality follows from the construction.

For the pro-etale assertion, use the specified representatives in
[def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness].
The exact comparison inverse image of
[thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] commutes with tensor and
pullback, while the compact-support comparison used in
[thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale] identifies the transported
$Rp_*j_!$ and its exchange maps.
The same counit computation above identifies the transported
projection map with the pro-etale one. Transporting the etale
isomorphism proves the assertion for these realizations.

Let $K$ be a field and
$V\subseteq K^{\mathbf Z_{\geq0}}$ a
finite-dimensional
vector subspace.
There is a finite set of indices
$J\subseteq\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ such that
$v\mapsto(v_j)_{j\in J}$ is injective on $V$.

## Proof

The finite-dimensionality in
[def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace] permits induction on
the nonnegative integer $\dim_K V$.
Start with $W=V$ and $J=\varnothing$. If $W\neq0$, choose
$v\in W\setminus\{0\}$ and an index $j$ with $v_j\neq0$.
Replace $W$ by the kernel of the nonzero coordinate functional
$w\mapsto w_j$ on $W$, and add $j$ to $J$.
The dimension strictly decreases. After at most $\dim_K V$ steps,
the intersection of the selected coordinate kernels is zero.
This is exactly the injectivity asserted.

attrs.title: Finite coordinates detect a finite-dimensional sequence space

objects.body:
Let $X$ be a separated finite-type scheme over
$k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, and let
$\nu_X:X_{\mathrm{proet}}\to X_{\Et}$ be the comparison morphism.
For finite coefficients $A$, $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Et},A)$, and
$M\in D^b_c(X_{\Et},A)$, the canonical map

$$
\nu_X^*R\mathcal Hom_A(K,M)
\longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom_A(\nu_X^*K,\nu_X^*M)
$$

is an isomorphism. Moreover
$\nu_X^*\omega_{X,\Et}\cong\omega_{X,\mathrm{proet}}$, and these
comparisons identify evaluations and double-dual maps. In particular
finite-stage Verdier duality on the pro-etale constructible category
is transported from etale Verdier duality.

## Proof

The comparison for $Rj_*$, including a quasi-compact open immersion
$j$, is [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image]. The exact
comparison pullback commutes with the open restrictions and closed
direct images, as their stalk and extension-by-zero descriptions show.
Apply it to the closed-support triangle of
[lem-exc-closed-support-triangle]; the first comparison identifies
the third term with the pro-etale $Rj_*j^*$ term. Full faithfulness
of closed direct image then gives
$\nu_Z^*Ri_{\Et}^!M\cong Ri_{\mathrm{proet}}^!\nu_X^*M$.
This establishes the required closed exceptional comparison directly
from recollement, without an assertion that closed ordinary restriction
commutes with internal Hom.

The finite stratification in
[lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata], and the triangles of
[def-weil-open-closed-recollement], reduce internal-Hom comparison
to $K=Rs_!P$, with $P$ site-perfect: internal Hom is triangulated in
the first variable by [lem-sf-hom-triangulated] (the same Hom-complex
argument applies on the pro-etale site), and the exact $\nu^*$ carries
triangles to triangles, so the comparison maps form morphisms of
triangles. On both sites the identity
of [lem-weil-stratum-ambient-hom] reads

$$
R\mathcal Hom(Rs_!P,M)
=Rs_*R\mathcal Hom(P,Rs^!M).
$$

The locally closed $Rs^!$ commutes with $\nu^*$ by the open and
closed comparisons above. The site-perfect complex $P$ of
[def-weil-site-perfect-complex] is locally a bounded complex of finite
free modules, and for such a first variable and a bounded constructible
second variable the internal Hom commutes with $\nu^*$ by
[lem-sf-hom-comparison-finite-free]; the question being local, this
applies to $R\mathcal Hom(P,Rs^!M)$. Finally $Rs_*$ commutes with comparison by
[prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image]. Hence the specified
internal-Hom map is an isomorphism on every stratum generator and then
on $K$.

Locally embed $X$ as a closed subscheme of a smooth affine space.
On both sites its dualizing object is the closed exceptional inverse
image of the smooth dualizing object. Smooth purity
[thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity] and the closed comparison
just proved identify these objects; uniqueness of the adjunction
comparisons makes the local identifications agree on overlaps.
The Hom comparisons are defined by evaluation, so they identify its
transpose, the double-dual map, as well. Finally the equivalence of
bounded constructible categories is
[lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], and finite Tor intervals
are preserved and detected by [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude].

attrs.title: Finite-stage duality under the site comparison

objects.body:
Let $X$ be separated of finite type over $k$, let
$p:X\to\mathbf A^1_k$ be a morphism, and let $g$
be pullback to $X_{\bar\eta}$, where
$\bar\eta=\operatorname{Spec}\overline{k(t)}$.
Then, Zariski locally on $X$,

$$
g^*\omega_X\cong\omega_{X_{\bar\eta}}(1)[2].
$$

For every $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Et},A)$, this comparison identifies
$g^*\delta_K$ with $\delta_{g^*K}$; the displayed invertible
twist and shift cancel after taking the dual twice.

## Proof

On an affine open of $X$, choose a closed immersion
$i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^r_{\mathbf A^1_k}$ over
$\mathbf A^1_k$. Composition of the ambient adjunctions of
[thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] and the explicit affine-space
adjunction [cor-amb-affine-space-adjunction] compute

$$
\omega_X=Ri^!A(r+1)[2r+2],\qquad
\omega_{X_{\bar\eta}}=Ri_{\bar\eta}^!A(r)[2r].
$$

Apply closed-support generic exchange from
[lem-weil-geometric-generic-exchange]; an invertible constant
twist and shift commute with this right adjoint by tensor adjunction.
This gives the first comparison. It is compatible with the
evaluations defining duality, since it was obtained from composition
and the adjunction counits.

Both $K$ and $D_XK$ are bounded constructible of finite Tor
amplitude by [lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata].
The internal-Hom comparison in
[lem-weil-geometric-generic-exchange] can therefore be applied
twice. Writing $L=A(1)[2]$, the first application gives
$g^*D_XK=D_{X_{\bar\eta}}(g^*K)\otimes L$; the second gives

$$
g^*D_XD_XK
=D_{X_{\bar\eta}}D_{X_{\bar\eta}}(g^*K),
$$

because $D(Q\otimes L)=D(Q)\otimes L^{-1}$.
Evaluation compatibility and [lem-weil-duality-pairing]
identify the pulled-back double-dual arrow with the one on the
generic fibre. The construction is needed only locally for checking
the arrow on geometric stalks; its compatibility with open restriction
is [lem-weil-delta-restriction].

attrs.title: The double dual on a geometric generic fibre

objects.body:
Let $B$ be a smooth integral curve over $k$, let
$\bar\eta=\operatorname{Spec}\overline{k(B)}$, and let $g$
denote geometric generic pullback on a finite-type $B$-scheme.
For a separated finite-type $B$-morphism $h:T\to X$, a closed
immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$, and bounded constructible
complexes in the expressions below, the natural comparisons are
isomorphisms:

$$
g_X^*Rh_*L\cong Rh_{\bar\eta,*}g_T^*L,
\qquad
g_Z^*Ri^!M\cong Ri_{\bar\eta}^!g_X^*M.
$$

For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Et},A)$ and
$M\in D^b_c(X_{\Et},A)$, one also has

$$
g_X^*R\mathcal Hom_A(K,M)
\cong R\mathcal Hom_A(g_X^*K,g_X^*M).
$$

The comparisons preserve evaluation and tensor adjunction.

## Proof

First replace $\overline{k(B)}$ by a separable closure of $k(B)$.
It is the inverse limit of nonempty opens in the normalizations of
$B$ in finite separable extensions of its function field, after
removing their branch loci. These are etale over opens of $B$;
one may choose affine opens, so all transition maps are affine.
At every such stage the first comparison is smooth base change,
[sbc-thm-bounded-below-derived-smooth-base-change].
Every affine etale test object over the generic fibre descends to a
stage. On it, [lem-weil-pbc-derived-cohomology-continuity]
identifies the filtered colimit of the stagewise cohomology groups
with the cohomology on the generic fibre. Exactness of filtered
colimits thus passes the canonical comparison to the limit in each
degree. Passing from the separable closure to the algebraic closure
is a purely inseparable extension; its base changes are universal
homeomorphisms and induce equivalences of etale topoi by
[thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance]. This proves
the first assertion, with no properness assumption on $h$.

Let $j$ be the open complement of $i$. Pull back the triangle

$$
i_*Ri^!M\longrightarrow M\longrightarrow Rj_*j^*M\longrightarrow
$$

of [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle]. Inverse image is exact,
commutes with closed direct image by its stalkwise description, and
commutes with $Rj_*$ by the first assertion. The resulting triangle
is the corresponding closed-support triangle on the generic fibre.
The full faithfulness of $i_{\bar\eta,*}$ gives the second comparison.
Only the closed-support formula is used here, not boundary duality.

For the internal-Hom comparison, use the finite smooth stratification
and the site-perfect restrictions of $K$ from the argument of
[lem-weil-bounded-finite-tor-perfect] and the definitions in
[def-weil-site-perfect-complex]. The open–closed triangles
[def-weil-open-closed-recollement] reduce the assertion to
$K=Rs_!P$, for a locally closed immersion $s:S\hookrightarrow X$
and site-perfect $P$. The ambient identity

$$
R\mathcal Hom_X(Rs_!P,M)
\cong Rs_*R\mathcal Hom_S(P,Rs^!M)
$$

is [lem-weil-stratum-ambient-hom]. Factor $s$ into an open
and a closed immersion. Its exceptional inverse image is a composite
of ordinary open restriction and the closed-support functor just
treated. Hence it commutes with $g^*$. Internal Hom from $P$
is $P^\vee\otimes^L-$, which commutes with inverse image, and
$Rs_*$ commutes with $g^*$ by the first assertion. This proves
the comparison on each generator and therefore on $K$.
All intermediate complexes are bounded constructible: this follows
for $Rj_*$ from [thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility], for
closed $Ri^!$ from the same closed-support triangle or
[lem-exc-closed-amplitude], and for internal Hom from $P$
from its bounded finite-projective model. Thus each preceding
bounded-below comparison is applied in its proved domain.
All maps are the maps obtained by tensor adjunction from evaluation;
the smooth, limit, and closed-support comparisons used above are
natural in those maps. Thus these are the specified canonical
comparisons, compatible with evaluation, rather than merely
isomorphisms between the underlying objects.

attrs.title: Geometric generic restriction and the boundary operations

objects.body:
Let $(\mathcal T^{\le0},\mathcal T^{\ge0})$ be a t-structure on a
triangulated category $\mathcal T$ in the sense of [def-weil-t-structure]
(not necessarily bounded), and let $\mathcal A=\mathcal
T^{\le0}\cap\mathcal T^{\ge0}$ be its heart, which is abelian by
[prop-weil-heart-abelian].

1. (*Truncations.*) For every $K\in\mathcal T$ and $n\in\mathbf Z$ the
   triangle $\tau^{\le n}K\to K\to\tau^{\ge n+1}K\to\tau^{\le n}K[1]$ with
   $\tau^{\le n}K\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$ and $\tau^{\ge n+1}K\in\mathcal
   T^{\ge n+1}$ is unique up to unique isomorphism, and $\tau^{\le n}$,
   $\tau^{\ge n+1}$ are functors, right, respectively left, adjoint to the
   inclusions of $\mathcal T^{\le n}$ and $\mathcal T^{\ge n+1}$. There is
   a canonical isomorphism $\tau^{\ge0}\tau^{\le0}\cong\tau^{\le0}\tau^{\ge0}$,
   and $H^0:=\tau^{\ge0}\tau^{\le0}:\mathcal T\to\mathcal A$; put
   $H^i(K):=H^0(K[i])$.
2. (*Extensions.*) $\mathcal T^{\le n}$, $\mathcal T^{\ge n}$ and
   $\mathcal A$ are closed under extensions: if $X\to Y\to Z\to X[1]$ is
   distinguished and $X,Z$ lie in one of them, so does $Y$.
3. (*Kernels and cokernels.*) Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of $\mathcal A$
   and complete it to a distinguished triangle $X\xrightarrow fY\to S\to
   X[1]$. Then $S\in\mathcal T^{\le0}\cap\mathcal T^{\ge-1}$,
   $$
   \ker f\cong H^{-1}(S)=(\tau^{\le-1}S)[-1],\qquad
   \operatorname{coker}f\cong H^0(S)=\tau^{\ge0}S,
   $$
   with the kernel map $(\tau^{\le-1}S)[-1]\to S[-1]\to X$ and the
   cokernel map $Y\to S\to\tau^{\ge0}S$.
4. (*Short exact sequences.*) A sequence $0\to X\xrightarrow fY
   \xrightarrow gZ\to0$ of $\mathcal A$ is short exact if and only if
   there is a morphism $\delta:Z\to X[1]$ such that $X\xrightarrow fY
   \xrightarrow gZ\xrightarrow\delta X[1]$ is distinguished, and then
   $\delta$ is unique. In particular a distinguished triangle whose three
   terms lie in $\mathcal A$ is a short exact sequence of $\mathcal A$.
5. (*Cohomological functor.*) $H^0$ is cohomological: a distinguished
   triangle $X\to Y\to Z\to X[1]$ gives a long exact sequence in
   $\mathcal A$
   $$
   \cdots\to H^{i}(X)\to H^{i}(Y)\to H^{i}(Z)\to H^{i+1}(X)\to\cdots .
   $$

(*Source: Beilinson--Bernstein--Deligne, Faisceaux pervers, 1.3.3--1.3.6
and 1.1.9--1.1.10; no Stacks Project entry states this form, for the
reasons recorded at [def-weil-t-structure].*)

## Proof

Throughout, axiom 1 of [def-weil-t-structure] gives $\mathcal T^{\le
n-1}\subseteq\mathcal T^{\le n}$ and $\mathcal T^{\ge n+1}\subseteq
\mathcal T^{\ge n}$, and axiom 2, shifted, gives $\Hom(A,B)=0$ for
$A\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$, $B\in\mathcal T^{\ge n+1}$. We use the long exact
$\Hom$ sequences of distinguished triangles freely.

*(1).* Let $A\to K\to B\to A[1]$ be a triangle as in axiom 3 (shifted to
level $n$). For $A'\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$ the sequence
$\Hom(A',B[-1])\to\Hom(A',A)\to\Hom(A',K)\to\Hom(A',B)$ has both outer
terms zero ($B[-1],B\in\mathcal T^{\ge n+1}$), so $A$ represents
$\Hom(-,K)$ on $\mathcal T^{\le n}$. Hence $A=:\tau^{\le n}K$ is unique up
to unique isomorphism and functorial in $K$, right adjoint to the
inclusion; dually $B=:\tau^{\ge n+1}K$ represents $\Hom(K,-)$ on $\mathcal
T^{\ge n+1}$. The third morphism is unique because $\Hom(A[1],B)=0$ (the
argument of (4) below). Two consequences: $K\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$ iff
$\tau^{\ge n+1}K=0$, and $K\in\mathcal T^{\ge n+1}$ iff $\Hom(A',K)=0$ for
all $A'\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$ (then $\tau^{\le n}K\to K$ is zero, so
$\tau^{\le n}K=0$); dually $\mathcal T^{\le n}$ is the left orthogonal of
$\mathcal T^{\ge n+1}$. For $K\in\mathcal T^{\le0}$ the object
$\tau^{\ge0}K$ is an extension of $K$ and $(\tau^{\le-1}K)[1]$, so it lies
in $\mathcal T^{\le0}$ by (2) (whose proof uses only the orthogonality just
shown); dually $\tau^{\le0}$ preserves $\mathcal T^{\ge0}$. So $H^0$ takes
values in $\mathcal A$. For the commutation, the octahedral axiom applied
to $\tau^{\le-1}K\to\tau^{\le0}K\to K$ (the first map is the truncation of
$\tau^{\le0}K$, since both represent $\Hom(-,K)$ on $\mathcal T^{\le-1}$)
gives a distinguished triangle
$\tau^{\ge0}\tau^{\le0}K\to\tau^{\ge0}K\to\tau^{\ge1}K\to$, whose first
term lies in $\mathcal T^{\le0}$ and whose third lies in $\mathcal
T^{\ge1}$. By uniqueness it is the truncation triangle of $\tau^{\ge0}K$,
so $\tau^{\ge0}\tau^{\le0}K\cong\tau^{\le0}\tau^{\ge0}K$.

*(2).* By (1), $\mathcal T^{\ge n+1}$ is the right orthogonal of $\mathcal
T^{\le n}$, and a right orthogonal is closed under extensions: for
$A'\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$ the sequence
$\Hom(A',X)\to\Hom(A',Y)\to\Hom(A',Z)$ is exact with zero outer terms.
Dually for $\mathcal T^{\le n}$, and $\mathcal A$ is the intersection.

*(3).* The object $S$ is an extension of $Y$ and $X[1]$, both in
$\mathcal T^{\le0}\cap\mathcal T^{\ge-1}$, so $S$ lies there by (2);
consequently $\tau^{\le-1}S\in\mathcal T^{\le-1}\cap\mathcal T^{\ge-1}$
and $\tau^{\ge0}S\in\mathcal A$ by (1), and these are $H^{-1}(S)[1]$ and
$H^0(S)$. Let $T\in\mathcal A$. The sequence
$\Hom(X[1],T)\to\Hom(S,T)\to\Hom(Y,T)\to\Hom(X,T)$ is exact with
$\Hom(X[1],T)=0$, and $\Hom(\tau^{\ge0}S,T)=\Hom(S,T)$ by adjunction. So
$\Hom(\tau^{\ge0}S,T)$ is the set of $h:Y\to T$ with $hf=0$, that is,
$Y\to\tau^{\ge0}S$ is a cokernel of $f$. Dually, $\Hom(T,Y[-1])=0$ and
$\Hom(T,(\tau^{\le-1}S)[-1])=\Hom(T,\tau^{\le0}(S[-1]))=\Hom(T,S[-1])$, so
$\Hom(T,(\tau^{\le-1}S)[-1])$ is the set of $h:T\to X$ with $fh=0$, and
$(\tau^{\le-1}S)[-1]\to X$ is a kernel of $f$.

*(4).* Keep the triangle of (3). If $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ
\xrightarrow\delta X[1]$ is distinguished with $Z\in\mathcal A$, then
$S\cong Z\in\mathcal T^{\ge0}$, so $\tau^{\le-1}S=0$ and $\ker f=0$, while
$\tau^{\ge0}S=S$, so $g$ is a cokernel of $f$ by (3); the sequence is short
exact. Conversely, let $0\to X\to Y\to Z\to0$ be short exact. Then $\ker
f=0$ gives $\tau^{\le-1}S=0$ by (3), so $S\in\mathcal A$ and $Y\to S$ is a
cokernel of $f$. The unique isomorphism $S\cong Z$ under $Y$ carries the
triangle of (3) to a distinguished triangle $X\to Y\to Z\to X[1]$. If
$\delta,\delta'$ both complete $(f,g)$, the morphism axiom gives
$h:Z\to Z$ with $hg=g$ and $\delta'h=\delta$. Then $(h-1)g=0$, so
$h-1$ factors through $\delta$ via some $X[1]\to Z$; but
$\Hom(X[1],Z)=0$ because $X[1]\in\mathcal T^{\le-1}$ and $Z\in\mathcal
T^{\ge0}$. So $h=1$ and $\delta'=\delta$.

*(5).* Rotating triangles, it suffices to show that $H^0X\to H^0Y\to H^0Z$
is exact at $H^0Y$ for every distinguished $X\to Y\to Z\to X[1]$.

(a) If $X,Y,Z\in\mathcal T^{\ge0}$, then $0\to H^0X\to H^0Y\to H^0Z$ is
exact: for $K\in\mathcal T^{\ge0}$ and $T\in\mathcal A$, (1) gives
$H^0K=\tau^{\le0}K$ and $\Hom(T,H^0K)=\Hom(T,K)$, and
$0=\Hom(T,Z[-1])\to\Hom(T,X)\to\Hom(T,Y)\to\Hom(T,Z)$ is exact; conclude by
Yoneda in the abelian category $\mathcal A$. Dually, if $X,Y,Z\in\mathcal
T^{\le0}$, then $H^0X\to H^0Y\to H^0Z\to0$ is exact, using
$\Hom(H^0K,T)=\Hom(K,T)$ for $K\in\mathcal T^{\le0}$.

(b) If $Z\in\mathcal T^{\ge0}$, the octahedral axiom applied to
$\tau^{\le-1}X\to X\to Y$ gives distinguished triangles
$\tau^{\le-1}X\to Y\to Y''\to$ and $\tau^{\ge0}X\to Y''\to Z\to$. By (2)
$Y''\in\mathcal T^{\ge0}$, so the first is the truncation triangle and
$Y''\cong\tau^{\ge0}Y$. Since $H^0\tau^{\ge0}=H^0$ by the commutation in
(1), (a) applied to $\tau^{\ge0}X\to\tau^{\ge0}Y\to Z$ gives the exact
sequence $0\to H^0X\to H^0Y\to H^0Z$. Dually, if $X\in\mathcal T^{\le0}$,
applying the octahedral axiom to $Y\to Z\to\tau^{\ge1}Z$ gives a
triangle $X\to\tau^{\le0}Y\to\tau^{\le0}Z\to$ and an exact sequence
$H^0X\to H^0Y\to H^0Z\to0$.

(c) In general, apply the octahedral axiom to $\tau^{\le0}X\to X\to Y$.
It gives distinguished triangles $\tau^{\le0}X\to Y\to W\to$ and
$\tau^{\ge1}X\to W\to Z\to$, with $Y\to W\to Z$ equal to the given map
$Y\to Z$. By the second half of (b), $H^0X=H^0\tau^{\le0}X\to H^0Y\to
H^0W\to0$ is exact. Rotating the second triangle to $W\to Z\to
(\tau^{\ge1}X)[1]\to W[1]$, whose third term lies in $\mathcal T^{\ge0}$,
the first half of (b) shows that $H^0W\to H^0Z$ is a monomorphism. Hence
$\ker(H^0Y\to H^0Z)=\ker(H^0Y\to H^0W)=\operatorname{im}(H^0X\to H^0Y)$.

attrs.title: Short exact sequences in the heart are triangles

objects.body:
Let $\mathcal T$ be an additive category and let $\Kar(\mathcal T)$ be its
Karoubi envelope [def-weil-karoubi-envelope]. The canonical functor

$$
 \mathcal T\longrightarrow\Kar(\mathcal T),\qquad
 K\longmapsto(K,\operatorname{id}_K),\qquad f\longmapsto f,
$$

is fully faithful.

(*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this form: Stacks does not
construct the Karoubi envelope (Homological Algebra, Section 12.4, Tag
[09SF](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09SF), states the Karoubian
property in Definition 12.4.1, Tag
[09SG](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09SG), and characterizes it in
Lemma 12.4.2, Tag [09SH](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09SH)), hence
states no full faithfulness for the inclusion of a category in its envelope;
the blueprint adds the elementary verification that the canonical functor is
bijective on morphism sets, which is what the bounded-t-structure argument
below uses to read an equivalence off full faithfulness.)

## Proof

By [def-weil-karoubi-envelope] the objects of $\Kar(\mathcal T)$ are the
pairs $(K,e)$ with $e^2=e$, the morphisms $(K,e)\to(L,d)$ are the morphisms
$u:K\to L$ of $\mathcal T$ satisfying $u=d\,u\,e$, and composition and
identities are those of $\mathcal T$. For $f:K\to L$ the condition is
$\operatorname{id}_L\,f\,\operatorname{id}_K=f$, which every morphism $f$
satisfies, so the map

$$
 \Hom_{\mathcal T}(K,L)\longrightarrow
 \Hom_{\Kar(\mathcal T)}\bigl((K,\operatorname{id}_K),
 (L,\operatorname{id}_L)\bigr),\qquad f\longmapsto f,
$$

is bijective; it is the identity on underlying morphisms, so it preserves
composition and identities. Hence the canonical functor is full and faithful.

attrs.title: The inclusion of a category in its Karoubi envelope is fully faithful

objects.body:
Let $\mathcal T$ be an additive category and let $\Kar(\mathcal T)$ be its
Karoubi envelope [def-weil-karoubi-envelope]. Every idempotent endomorphism
of an object of $\Kar(\mathcal T)$ splits.

(*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this form for the envelope:
Lemma 12.4.2 (Tag [09SH](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09SH))
characterizes the splitting of idempotents — an idempotent endomorphism
$p:z\to z$ of a Karoubian preadditive category admits a direct sum
decomposition $z=x\oplus y$ with $p$ the projection onto $y$ — but states it
as one of three equivalent characterizations of Karoubianity (Definition
12.4.1, Tag [09SG](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09SG)), so it cannot
be applied to $\Kar(\mathcal T)$ before the envelope is known to be
Karoubian; the explicit splitting $i=p=f$ of an idempotent of $\Kar(\mathcal
T)$ by the pair of morphisms of $\mathcal T$ is the blueprint's addition, and
it is what makes the envelope a model for the idempotent completion used
below.)

## Proof

Let $(K,e)$ be an object of $\Kar(\mathcal T)$ and let $f:(K,e)\to(K,e)$ be
an idempotent endomorphism. By [def-weil-karoubi-envelope] the endomorphism
$f$ is a morphism $f:K\to K$ of $\mathcal T$ with $f=e\,f\,e$ and $f^2=f$.
Then $e f=e(e f e)=e^2fe=efe=f$ and $f e=(e f e)e=e f e^2=e f e=f$.
Consequently $f^2=f$ makes $(K,f)$ an object of $\Kar(\mathcal T)$, and the
morphisms

$$
 i=f:(K,f)\longrightarrow(K,e),\qquad
 p=f:(K,e)\longrightarrow(K,f)
$$

of $\mathcal T$ are morphisms of $\Kar(\mathcal T)$: for $i$ the condition
$i=e\,i\,f$ reads $f=eff=ef=f$, and for $p$ the condition $p=f\,p\,e$ reads
$f=ffe=fe=f$. Their composite $p\circ i=f\circ f=f$ is the identity of
$(K,f)$, whose identity is $f$ itself, and $i\circ p=f\circ f=f$, so
$f=i\circ p$ exhibits $f$ as the composite of a section and a retraction.
Hence every idempotent of $\Kar(\mathcal T)$ splits.

attrs.title: The Karoubi envelope is idempotent complete

objects.body:
Let $\mathcal T$ be a triangulated category. With the shift
$(K,e)[1]=(K[1],e[1])$ and with distinguished triangles the triangles
isomorphic to direct summands, in the category of triangles, of images of
distinguished triangles of $\mathcal T$, the category $\Kar(\mathcal T)$ of
[def-weil-karoubi-envelope] is an ordinary triangulated category, and the
canonical functor of [def-weil-karoubi-envelope] is exact.

(*Source: the classical Balmer--Schlichting idempotent completion of
triangulated categories; retained here as the auxiliary model used in the
proof of the bounded-t-structure theorem below, after which the envelope is
shown to be redundant; no Stacks Project entry states this form: Stacks' only
entries on idempotents are the definition of a Karoubian preadditive category
(Definition 12.4.1, Tag
[09SG](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09SG)), its characterization by
the splitting of idempotents (Lemma 12.4.2, Tag
[09SH](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09SH)) and the Karoubianity
criteria of Lemma 12.4.3 (Tag
[05QV](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05QV): countable products and
kernels of maps which have a right inverse, or dually countable coproducts
and cokernels of maps which have a left inverse), all in Homological Algebra,
Section 12.4 (Tag [09SF](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09SF)); Chapter
13 contains no idempotent completion of a triangulated category, and the
derived-limit and K-injective entries 08TC, 07KC, 0BK6, 0BK7, 070M, 079P
concern a fixed triangulated category rather than its idempotent completion;
the blueprint adds the description of the distinguished triangles of
$\Kar(\mathcal T)$ as retracts of images of distinguished triangles of
$\mathcal T$.*)

## Proof

The assertion is the idempotent-completion input recorded in the source note.
It is not discharged here: it enters the blueprint only through the auxiliary
model $\Kar(\mathcal T)$ of [def-weil-karoubi-envelope] in the
bounded-t-structure theorem below, whose finite-stage and $\Qlb$-stage
conclusions make the envelope redundant for the coefficient categories.

Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$, a prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite
extension $E/\Ql$, a finite-type $k_0$-scheme $Y_0$ with
$Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, a Weil complex $K\in D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(Y,E)$, a closed
point $y\in|Y_0|$ of degree $r=[\kappa(y):\Fq]$, and an integer $j\in\mathbf
Z$. For two embeddings $\kappa(y)\hookrightarrow k$ with associated geometric
points $\bar y,\bar y'\to Y$, the local operators $F_y$ and $F'_y$ on the
stalks of the cohomology sheaf $\mathcal H^j(\operatorname{For}K)$
constructed in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] are conjugate: there is an
isomorphism $\mathcal H^j(\operatorname{For}K)_{\bar y}\cong \mathcal
H^j(\operatorname{For}K)_{\bar y'}$ carrying $F_y$ to $F'_y$.

## Proof

Two embeddings $\kappa(y)\hookrightarrow k$ differ by an element of
$\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)$, because $k$ is the fixed algebraic closure of the
finite field $k_0$ and $\kappa(y)$ is a finite field; the associated
geometric points $\bar y$ and $\bar y'$ of $Y$ are therefore related by a
power of the geometric-Frobenius automorphism $g_Y$ of
[def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. That automorphism induces an isomorphism between the
stalks of the cohomology sheaf $\mathcal H^j(\operatorname{For}K)$ at the two
points, and the Weil isomorphism is an isomorphism
$Lg_Y^*\operatorname{For}(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{For}(K)$, which
intertwines the local operator built at $\bar y$ with the one built at its
translate. Iterating this and using the $r$-fold return prescribed in
[def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] transports $F_y$ to $F'_y$, which is the
conjugacy asserted.

attrs.title: Independence of the local Frobenius operator from the embedding

objects.body:
Let $X$ be affine. A morphism between bounded-below complexes of pro-etale
module sheaves is an isomorphism if its derived sections on every
$W\in\mathcal B_X$ are isomorphisms.

## Proof

Take the cone in the ordinary derived category and represent it by a
bounded-below injective complex $J^\bullet$. By
[lem-weil-pbc-proetale-restriction-injectives], $\Gamma(W,J^\bullet)$
computes its derived sections on $W$. Its cohomology sheaf in degree $n$ is
the sheafification of the presheaf $W\mapsto H^n\Gamma(W,J^\bullet)$: kernels
are computed objectwise, and cokernels are then sheafified. All these groups
are zero on the basis by hypothesis, so [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis] makes
every cohomology sheaf zero. The cone is zero and the morphism is an
isomorphism.

attrs.title: Derived sections on the basis detect isomorphisms

objects.body:
On a site with a basis closed under fibre products, suppose every covering of
a basis object has a finite basis refinement. An injective module sheaf has
vanishing positive Cech cohomology [def-weil-pbc-cover-cech] for every finite
basis covering. If a module sheaf $M$ has this same vanishing for every such
covering, then $H^q(U,M)=0$ for every basis object $U$ and $q>0$, where
cohomology is derived sections.

## Proof

For a covering $V=\coprod_aV_a\to U$, form the augmented complex of free
module sheaves on $V^{p+1}_U$, ending in the free module sheaf on $U$. It is
exact: locally on a test object mapping to $U$, the cover has a lift to $V$.
Insert that lift as first coordinate. The alternating-face differential
satisfies $\partial h+h\partial=1$, since adjacent inserted faces cancel. A
local chain has finite support, so one common cover suffices for all its
generators. Applying $\operatorname{Hom}(-,I)$ for an injective sheaf $I$
gives the augmented complex of [def-weil-pbc-cover-cech], which is
consequently exact. This argument uses local lifts, not a choice of points of
the topos.

Embed $M$ into an injective $I$ and put $Q=I/M$. A section of $Q(U)$ lifts to
$I$ on a finite basis cover. Differences of these lifts form a Cech
one-cocycle in $M$. Its vanishing in $\check H^1$ lets us adjust the lifts by
sections of $M$ so that they agree. They then glue in $I$. Thus $I(U)\to
Q(U)$ is surjective for every basis object. This yields a short exact
sequence of Cech complexes on every basis covering, including all its
intersections. The first paragraph and the assumed vanishing for $M$ imply
the same positive Cech vanishing for $Q$. Repeat with an injective embedding
of $Q$. The long exact sequences for derived sections give $H^1(U,M)=0$ and
$H^q(U,M)=H^{q-1}(U,Q)$ for $q>1$. Iteration proves the assertion in every
finite degree. This is the Cech acyclicity criterion of
[Stacks Project, Tag 03F9](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03F9), with
its dimension-shifting proof included.

attrs.title: Injectives and the Cech acyclicity criterion

objects.body:
Let $p:V\to X$ be a scheme morphism and
$s:X\hookrightarrow V$ an
open immersion with
closed image and $p s=\operatorname{id}_X$.
For a finite ring $\Lambda$ and
$K\in\hyperref[def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]{D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)}$,
restriction to this component gives a canonical isomorphism

$$
Rp_*s_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}K,
$$

where $Rp_*$ and $s_!$ are the
derived direct image and
extension by zero.

## Proof

The disjoint open cover
$V=s(X)\amalg(V\setminus s(X))$ identifies sheaves on $V_{\Et}$
with pairs of sheaves on its components, by the sheaf gluing axiom.
In this product description the functor $s_!$ of
[def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] is $F\mapsto(F,0)$.
It is also right adjoint to the exact restriction to the first
component, and hence preserves injectives. For every etale $W\to X$,
the direct image in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] has

$$
(p_*s_!F)(W)
=\Gamma(V\times_XW,s_!F)
=\Gamma(W,F),
$$

because $p s=\operatorname{id}_X$ and the other component contributes
zero. Apply this identity to a bounded-below injective resolution
from [prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist]; its extension
by zero is still an injective resolution. The identity in each
degree is the asserted derived isomorphism.

attrs.title: Direct image from an open and closed section

objects.body:
Let $r:T\to V$ and $p:V\to S$ be scheme morphisms. If $p$ is
separated and $p\circ r$ is a closed immersion, then $r$ is a
closed immersion.

## Proof

Omitted.

attrs.title: Closed immersion detected after separated composition

objects.body:
The composite of closed immersions [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] is a
closed immersion, and a product (over a common base) of closed immersions is
a closed immersion. An open immersion is of finite type.

## Proof

A composite of closed immersions is affine and is induced locally by a
composite of surjective ring homomorphisms, hence a closed immersion. The
base change of a closed immersion is a closed immersion, since tensoring a
surjective ring homomorphism is surjective (right exactness of tensor), and
the product over a common base of closed immersions $Z_i\hookrightarrow W_i$
is the composite of two such base changes (the closed subscheme
$Z_1\times_YZ_2\subseteq W_1\times_YW_2$ is the intersection of the two
base-changed subschemes). An open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow Y$ is locally
of finite type: around $x\in U$ choose an affine $V\subseteq Y$ and a
principal affine $D(f)\subseteq U\cap V$ containing $x$, which is affine of
finite type over $V$; with quasi-compact source it is therefore of finite
type by [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], which is the case used in this
blueprint (the open subschemes in question are quasi-compact).

attrs.title: Closure of the closed-immersion and finite-type properties

objects.body:
A closed immersion [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] is proper, and so is the
composite of a closed immersion followed by a proper morphism; in particular,
a closed subscheme of a proper scheme is proper over the base.

## Proof

A closed immersion is affine, hence separated, is of finite type (a
surjective ring homomorphism makes the target a finitely generated algebra
over the source), and is universally closed, since closed immersions are
closed maps and are stable under base change; all these notions are those of
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Hence a closed immersion is proper, and
the composite of a closed immersion followed by a proper morphism is proper
by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]; in particular a closed subscheme of a
scheme proper over the base is proper over the base.

Let $Y$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $(F_a)$ be a filtered system of
abelian etale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Then

$$
 \varinjlim_a H^q(Y_{\Et},F_a)\xrightarrow{\sim}
 H^q(Y_{\Et},\varinjlim_a F_a)\qquad(q\geq0).
$$

Here cohomology is the derived functor of
[def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]; no torsion assumption is needed. The
assertion also holds in sheaves of modules over a fixed constant ring.

## Proof

On the basis of quasi-compact quasi-separated etale objects, every cover has
a finite refinement by basis objects, and their pairwise fibre products stay
in the basis. Hence the objectwise filtered colimit of the $F_a$ satisfies
the sheaf equalizer axiom on this basis: filtered colimits of abelian groups
commute with finite products and kernels. It therefore computes the sheaf
colimit of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] on every basis object.

For a hypercover finite in each degree, as in
[def-weil-pbc-finite-split-hypercover], this gives
$C^n(U,\varinjlim_aF_a)=\varinjlim_a C^n(U,F_a)$ in each degree. Exactness of
filtered colimits gives the same identity on $H^q$. Now take the colimit over
hypercover refinements and use [thm-weil-pbc-hypercover-cohomology] on both
sides. The two colimits commute, by their universal properties. Every
identification is induced by maps of sheaves and restriction of sections, so
it is the canonical map of the statement. See also
[Stacks Project, Tag 09Z1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09Z1), whose
cohomological input is proved here by refinement. For module sheaves, use the
module version of [thm-weil-pbc-hypercover-cohomology]; filtered colimits of
modules have the same exactness and finite-limit properties.

For finite $\Lambda$ and $K\in\Dplus(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$, the derived unit
induces a natural isomorphism

$$
 R\Gamma(T_{\Et},K)\xrightarrow{\sim}
 R\Gamma(T_{\Proet},\nu_T^*K).
$$

Both functors are ordinary derived sections.

## Proof

Since $\nu_T^*$ is exact by
[prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level], its right adjoint $\nu_{T,*}$
in [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] preserves injectives. For an
injective pro-etale resolution $J^\bullet$ of a bounded-below complex,
$\nu_{T,*}J^\bullet$ therefore computes its derived direct image and the
subsequent derived sections. Underived evaluation on the final object gives
$\Gamma(T_{\Et},\nu_{T,*}J^r)=\Gamma(T_{\Proet},J^r)$. Thus
$R\Gamma_{\Et}R\nu_{T,*}=R\Gamma_{\Proet}$. Apply this identity to the
derived unit, which is an isomorphism by [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison].

If $X$ is affine and $I$ is injective in etale module sheaves on $X$, then

$$
 H^q(U_{\Proet},(\nu_X^*I)|_U)=0
 \quad(U\in\mathcal B_X,\ q>0).
$$

Here the left side is derived evaluation on the basis object $U$.

## Proof

By [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis] and [lem-weil-pbc-cech-criterion], it
suffices to prove positive Cech vanishing on every finite basis covering
$\{V_a\to U\}$. There are two separate limits in this calculation.

First write each $V_a$ as a limit of affine etale finite-presentation
$U$-schemes, using the stability lemma for ind-etale algebras. Every finite
choice of stages still covers $U$. As in the proof of
[lem-weil-pbc-comparison-sections], section continuity on all finite
intersections writes the Cech complex of [def-weil-pbc-cover-cech] as the
filtered colimit of those for these etale coverings of $U$. Exactness of
filtered colimits gives the same identity on Cech cohomology.

Second, fix one such finite etale covering $\{W_a\to U\}$, and write
$U=\varprojlim_iU_i$ with $U_i$ affine etale over $X$. The covering descends
to a finite etale covering $\{W_{a,i}\to U_i\}$ at a sufficiently late stage,
by the descent of finite-presentation data at an inverse limit; all its
finite intersections descend by base change. The same section continuity and
exactness of filtered colimits give

$$
 \check H^q(\{W_a\to U\},\nu_X^*I)
 =\varinjlim_i\check H^q(\{W_{a,i}\to U_i\},I).
$$

On the right every term is an etale object over $X$; the identification of
its sections with those of $I$ is [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-sections].
Injectivity of $I$ and the first assertion of
[lem-weil-pbc-cech-criterion] make the right side zero for $q>0$. Both limits
therefore give zero, and the criterion proves the claimed derived vanishing.
The identification with cohomology on $U_{\Proet}$ is
[lem-weil-pbc-proetale-restriction-injectives]. This supplies the geometric
step in [Stacks Project, Tag
099U](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099U) without assuming it as part
of the site comparison.

attrs.title: Acyclicity of the pulled-back etale injectives

objects.body:
For $u:U\to V$ there is a natural isomorphism

$$
 \nu_U^*u_{\Et}^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}
 u_{\Proet}^{-1}\nu_V^*.
$$

It is compatible with identity maps, composites, and the cartesian
identification in [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square].

## Proof

On a representable etale sheaf $h_W$, both inverse-image composites give the
pro-etale sheaf represented by $W\times_VU$. To check the comparison inverse
image in this assertion, work on affine charts and write a basis object as a
limit of affine etale schemes. Maps from this limit into an affine etale
scheme of finite presentation descend to a stage, so the formula of
[lem-weil-pbc-comparison-sections] is exactly the representable sheaf of the
base change. General etale $W$ follows by its affine covering and sheaf
gluing. Scheme inverse image on a representable is its base change by the
defining base-change functor on sites.

Every sheaf is a colimit of representable sheaves over its sections.
Explicitly, the coproduct of these representables maps epimorphically to the
sheaf, and the two projections from its relation sheaf give a coequalizer
presentation. In module sheaves use free modules on those representables and
a cokernel presentation instead. Inverse images preserve these colimits. Thus
the just specified identifications extend uniquely to an isomorphism on every
sheaf for the morphism of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. On
representables the identity and composition equations are the identity and
associativity of scheme base change, including the chosen cartesian
identification in [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. The colimit presentations
extend these equations to all sheaves. Exactness gives the same coherent
isomorphisms on complexes.

attrs.title: Comparison inverse image commutes with scheme pullback

objects.body:
Let $X$ be affine, let $F$ be an etale module sheaf, and write a basis object
as $U=\varprojlim_i U_i$ with $U_i/X$ affine etale of finite presentation.
Then naturally

$$
 (\nu_X^*F)(U)=\Gamma(U_{\Et},F|_U)
             =\varinjlim_i F(U_i).
$$

The restriction $F|_U$ is the scheme inverse image. The same section formula
holds for sheaves of sets.

## Proof

Define $P_F(U)=\Gamma(U_{\Et},F|_U)$ on the basis. The second equality in the
statement is the continuity of sections at an inverse limit; restriction of
an etale sheaf to an etale object is evaluation on its slice. We verify that
$P_F$ is already a sheaf for the finer topology. Let $\{V_a\to U\}$ be a
finite basis covering. By the stability lemma for ind-etale algebras write
$V_a=\varprojlim_\lambda V_{a,\lambda}$, with each $V_{a,\lambda}\to U$
affine etale of finite presentation. Every finite choice of stages still
covers $U$, because its images contain the images of the covering $V_a$'s.
The fibre products in each degree of [def-weil-pbc-cover-cech] commute with
these inverse limits. Section continuity, applied on these fibre products to
$F|_U$, therefore writes their section groups as the filtered colimit of the
finite-stage section groups. Finite products and kernels commute with
filtered colimits of modules. The etale sheaf equalizer at each finite stage
consequently proves the covering equalizer for $P_F$. By
[lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis], it extends to the full site.

We identify it with the inverse image by its adjunction, so no comparison of
derived categories is being assumed here. Given $F\to\nu_{X,*}G$, each
presentation gives compatible maps $F(U_i)\to G(U_i)\to G(U)$, hence
$P_F(U)\to G(U)$. These maps are natural on the basis: a map from a limit to
a finite-presentation affine object factors through a stage, and equalities
of factorizations hold later, by the descent of finite-presentation data at
an inverse limit. Conversely a map $P_F\to G$ restricts to $F\to\nu_{X,*}G$,
since $P_F(U_i)=F(U_i)$ on etale objects. These constructions are inverse, as
every section of $P_F(U)$ is represented at a stage. They give precisely the
adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], proving the formula.
The sheaf and adjunction arguments use only finite products, equalizers, and
filtered colimits, and hence apply to sets too.

attrs.title: Sections of the comparison inverse image

objects.body:
Let $U$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $C$ a constructible torsion
abelian sheaf on $U_{\Et}$. There is an affine inverse-system $U\cong\varprojlim
U_\lambda$ with Noetherian quasi-compact quasi-separated $U_\lambda$ and
affine transition maps, an index $\lambda$, a constructible torsion sheaf
$C_\lambda$ on $U_\lambda$ pulling back to $C$, and a finite-pushforward
embedding of $C_\lambda$ whose pullback is an embedding of $C$.

## Proof

*Step 1: the approximation.* A quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme is the
inverse limit $U=\varprojlim_\lambda U_\lambda$ of Noetherian quasi-compact
quasi-separated schemes with affine transition maps (absolute Noetherian
approximation, Stacks Project, Limits of Schemes, Tag
[01ZA](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01ZA), Proposition 32.5.4).

*Step 2: the sheaf descends.* Constructibility of $C$ means that $U$ carries a
finite partition into locally closed constructible subschemes on each of which
$C$ is finite locally constant; a finite locally constant sheaf with finite
stalks is specified by finitely many etale finite-presentation objects,
finitely many sections and finitely many equalities expressing the
trivializations and the compatibility on the overlaps. By descent of
finite-presentation data at an inverse limit all of this datum descends: there
are an index $\lambda$, a finite family of etale finite-presentation objects
of $U_\lambda$, finitely many sections and equalities over $U_\lambda$, and a
covering condition, whose pullbacks to $U$ present $C$. This gives a
constructible torsion sheaf $C_\lambda$ on $U_\lambda$ with
$\nu_\lambda^*C_\lambda=C$.

*Step 3: the embedding descends.* Applying
[lem-weil-pbc-constructible-finite-pushforward-noetherian] to $C_\lambda$ on
the Noetherian $U_\lambda$ produces finite morphisms
$h_{\lambda,i}:V_{\lambda,i}\to U_\lambda$ and finite abelian groups $M_i$
with a monomorphism
$C_\lambda\hookrightarrow\bigoplus_i(h_{\lambda,i})_*\underline{M_i}$. A
finite morphism between finitely presented schemes is finitely presented, so
the source and target of this morphism are finite-presentation data; the same
descent lemma therefore applies a second time, and after increasing $\lambda$
there are finite morphisms $h_i:V_i\to U_\lambda$ and a morphism of sheaves
$C_\lambda\to\bigoplus_i(h_i)_*\underline{M_i}$ over $U_\lambda$ whose
pullback to $U$ is the embedding; since pullback is exact and reflects
monomorphisms, and since a monomorphism over $U_\lambda$ already holds there,
the descended map is a monomorphism.

*Step 4: the pullback is a monomorphism of $C$.* Pullback along $U\to
U_\lambda$ is exact, and for a finite morphism the formation of direct image
commutes with the affine base change $U\to U_\lambda$:
$\nu_\lambda^*(h_i)_*\underline{M_i}=(\nu_\lambda^*h_i)_*\underline{M_i}$,
which is the finite-base-change compatibility of the direct image applied to
the finite $h_i$. Hence the pullback of the descended monomorphism is the
required $C\hookrightarrow\bigoplus_i(h_i)_*\underline{M_i}$ on $U$, where
each $h_i$ is finite and finitely presented as the pullback of a finite
morphism between finitely presented schemes.

*Remark on the limits input.* Step 2 uses only the descent of
finite-presentation data at an inverse limit, and the identification
$h_*\underline M=\varinjlim_i(h_i)_*\underline M$ used in the Noetherian case
is the section formula $\varinjlim_i\underline M\bigl(W\times_UV_i\bigr)
=\underline M\bigl(W\times_UV\bigr)$ over the etale finite-presentation
objects $W\to U$. No separate limits statement is assumed.

Let $U$ be Noetherian and let $C$ be a constructible torsion abelian sheaf on
$U_{\Et}$. There are finite morphisms $h_i:V_i\to U$ and finite abelian groups
$M_i$ with a monomorphism
$C\hookrightarrow\bigoplus_i(h_i)_*\underline{M_i}$.

**Status.** The two sub-gaps this statement used to carry are closed. (a) The
extension of the generic map is valid because the normalization $V$ is normal:
the extension lemma is [lem-weil-pbc-normal-constant-generic]; no locally
constant sheaf is extended across a boundary, the sheaf extended is the
constant sheaf. (b) The factorization of $C\to h_*\underline M$ through one
finite stage is the finite-presentation property of constructible sheaves in
the category of sheaves, [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-finitely-presented],
recorded as the classical input Tag 09Z4.

## Proof

*Step 1: the local model at a point.* For every geometric point $\bar x\to U$,
constructibility gives a finite separable extension $K/\kappa(x)$ and a finite
abelian group $M$ for which $C$ is constant with value $M$ over
$\operatorname{Spec}K$. Let $Z\subset U$ be the reduced closure of $x$, let
$V\to Z$ be the normalization of $Z$ in $K$, and let
$\operatorname{Spec}K\to V$ be the generic inclusion. The scheme $V$ is
integral and normal with function field $K$; this is the classical
normalization of an integral scheme in a finite extension of its function
field (Stacks Project, Morphisms, Lemma 29.54.13, Tag
[035L](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/035L)).

*Step 2: the generic map.* The identification
$C|_{\operatorname{Spec}K}\cong\underline M$ is a map
$C|_{\operatorname{Spec}K}\to\underline M$, and
[lem-weil-pbc-normal-constant-generic], applied to the normal integral $V$ and
the inclusion $g:\operatorname{Spec}K\to V$ of its generic point, identifies
$g_*\underline M$ with $\underline M$. Hence that map adjoints to
$C|_V\to\underline M$, and adjoints again to a map

$$
 C\longrightarrow h_*\underline M,\qquad h:V\to U
$$

of sheaves on $U$, the morphism $h$ being the composite of the normalization
with $V\to Z\hookrightarrow U$. This is the step that the former pending note
recorded as unjustified: the justification is exactly the normality of $V$,
and no locally constant sheaf is extended across a boundary.

*Step 3: the stalk map at $\bar x$.* Choose a lift $\bar y$ of $\bar x$ to
$V$. The diagram

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
C_{\bar x}&\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }&(C|_V)_{\bar y}\\
\downarrow&&\downarrow\\
(h_*\underline M)_{\bar x}&\longrightarrow&\underline M_{\bar y}
\end{array}
$$

is commutative, and $\underline M_{\bar y}=M$, so the stalk map of Step 2 is
injective at $\bar x$.

*Step 4: the finite approximation of $h_*\underline M$.* The normalization map
is integral, not finite in general: writing its affine coordinate algebra as
the filtered union of its finite $\mathcal O_Z$-subalgebras, the induced
direct image is the filtered colimit of the corresponding finite pushforwards,

$$
 h_*\underline M=\varinjlim_i(h_i)_*\underline M,
$$

which over an etale finite-presentation object $W\to U$ is the section formula
$\varinjlim_i\underline M(W\times_UV_i)=\underline M(W\times_UV)$ applied to
the affine limit $V=\varprojlim_iV_i$.

*Step 5: factorization through one finite stage.* The map $C\to h_*\underline
M$ of Step 2 is a morphism from a constructible sheaf into a filtered colimit
of sheaves, so by [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-finitely-presented] it factors
through one stage: there are an index $i$ and a map $C\to(h_i)_*\underline M$
whose composite with the transition map is the given map. Hence $\bar x$
admits a finite pushforward $h_i:V_i\to U$, the morphism $V_i\to Z$ being
finite by construction, detecting its stalk.

*Step 6: finite selection.* The finite-selection statement
[lem-weil-pbc-constructible-noetherian-finite-selection] now produces a finite
set of indices for which the direct sum of the maps of Step 5 is injective on
every geometric stalk; a map of sheaves injective on every geometric stalk is
a monomorphism by conservativity of geometric stalks. This is the Noetherian
construction of Stacks Project, Lemma 59.74.3 (Tag
[09Z6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09Z6)).

*Remark (the Nagata case).* If $U$ is Nagata, for instance of finite type over
a field, the normalization $V\to Z$ is finite already, so Step 4 is
unnecessary and the embedding is produced by Steps 1 to 3 and 6 directly. This
is the case used in the applications below.

Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, let $\Lambda$ be a
Noetherian ring, let $F$ be a constructible sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on
$X_{\Et}$, and let $G=\varinjlim_iG_i$ be a filtered colimit of sheaves of
$\Lambda$-modules. Then the canonical map

$$
 \varinjlim_i\operatorname{Mor}(F,G_i)\longrightarrow
 \operatorname{Mor}(F,G)
$$

is a bijection; equivalently, every morphism $F\to G$ factors through one of
the $G_i$, and any two such factorizations agree after passing to a common
refinement of the index.
(*Stacks Project, Etale Cohomology, Lemma 59.73.8, Tag
[09Z4](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09Z4).*)

## Proof

Two recorded inputs are used. First, a constructible sheaf of
$\Lambda$-modules is a finite colimit of representable sheaves $h_W$ with
$W\to X$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated (Stacks Project, Etale Cohomology,
Lemma 59.73.5, Tag [09Y9](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09Y9), whose
proof argues by a finite stratification of $X$ and induction on the number of
strata). Second, for such a $W$ the sections $\mathcal
G(W)=\operatorname{Mor}(h_W,\mathcal G)$ of a sheaf commute with filtered
colimits of sheaves (Stacks Project, Sites, Lemma 7.17.7, Tag
[0738](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0738): a quasi-compact
quasi-separated object of a site is coherent). Colimits in the first variable
are computed on the presentation, and the two assertions of the statement are
respectively the existence and the uniqueness of the factorization, so the two
inputs give the bijection.

attrs.title: Constructible sheaves are finitely presented in the category of sheaves

objects.body:
Let $X$ be Noetherian, let $F$ be a constructible abelian etale sheaf, and let
$(\phi_\lambda:F\to G_\lambda)_{\lambda\in L}$ be a family of maps to
arbitrary abelian etale sheaves. Assume that for every geometric point $\bar
x$ and every $0\neq v\in F_{\bar x}$, some $\lambda$ satisfies
$(\phi_\lambda)_{\bar x}(v)\neq0$. Then a finite subset $L_0\subset L$ makes

$$
 (\phi_\lambda)_{\lambda\in L_0}:
 F\longrightarrow\bigoplus_{\lambda\in L_0}G_\lambda
$$

a monomorphism. In particular, the conclusion holds if at each geometric point
some single $\phi_\lambda$ is injective.

## Proof

Choose the finite partition of [lem-weil-pbc-irreducible-lisse-strata], and a
geometric generic point $\bar\eta_i$ of each $S_i$. The group
$F_{\bar\eta_i}$ is finite. For each of its nonzero elements choose one
$\phi_\lambda$ detecting it, and let $L_i$ be the resulting finite set of
indices. The map

$$
 F|_{S_i}\longrightarrow
 \bigoplus_{\lambda\in L_i}G_\lambda|_{S_i}
$$

is injective at $\bar\eta_i$, hence is a monomorphism on all of $S_i$ by
[lem-weil-pbc-lisse-generic-kernel]. Take $L_0=\bigcup_iL_i$. At any geometric
point of $X$, projection to the summands indexed by its stratum's $L_i$ shows
that the $L_0$-map is injective. Exactness of the geometric stalk functors
makes every stalk of its kernel zero; conservativity of geometric stalks then
makes the kernel zero. No finiteness or constructibility of the target sheaves
is needed.

attrs.title: Noetherian finite selection of stalk tests

objects.body:
Let $T$ be Noetherian and $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring. Every
subsheaf of a constructible $\Lambda$-module sheaf on the small etale site
is constructible.

*Source note:* this is Stacks Project, Section 59.74, Constructible sheaves
on Noetherian schemes ([Tag 03RY](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03RY)),
whose Proposition 59.74.1 (3) states that for a Noetherian scheme $X$ and a
Noetherian ring $\Lambda$ every submodule and quotient module of a
