constructible sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\Et}$ is constructible (the
weak Serre input being Lemma 59.71.6, [Tag
03RZ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03RZ)). The blueprint's statement
is the same assertion for a finite commutative ring $\Lambda$, which is
Noetherian, on the small etale site of a Noetherian $T$, and it adds a
self-contained proof by Noetherian induction on geometric stalks in place of
Stacks' proof through a finite partition into locally constant pieces.

## Proof

Let $G\subset F$, with $F$ constructible. For a constant finite module sheaf
$\underline M$ on an irreducible scheme $W$, and a subsheaf
$H\subset\underline M$, put
$$
 W_m=\{w:\ m\text{ belongs to }H_{\bar w}\subset M\}
 \qquad(m\in M).
$$
This is independent of the choice of geometric point above $w$. It is open.
Indeed, membership is represented by a section of $H$ on an etale
neighbourhood whose image in $\underline M$, after refinement, is the
constant section $m$. Its image in $W$ is open because a flat, locally
finitely presented morphism is open. Such images cover exactly $W_m$. The
local lifts of $m$ glue uniquely, because $H\to\underline M$ is injective.

Every nonempty $W_m$ contains the generic point of $W$. The finite
intersection $W^\circ$ of the nonempty $W_m$'s is therefore nonempty and
open. On it membership in $H$ is the fixed submodule
$M'=H_{\bar\eta}\subset M$. The glued sections give
$\underline{M'}\to H|_{W^\circ}$, and this is an isomorphism on all stalks,
hence an isomorphism by conservativity of geometric stalks.

We now use Noetherian induction on closed subsets of $T$. Pullback to any
such subset preserves the injection, by exactness of geometric stalks, and
preserves the finite partition defining constructibility. Reducible closed
subsets are handled by their finitely many components, using the
finitely-many-components lemma for Noetherian schemes and removing the
preceding components from each partition. For a reduced irreducible closed
subset, choose a nonempty open on which $F$ is lisse, and an etale
trivialization near its generic point. Removing the other irreducible
components of this Noetherian trivializing scheme gives a nonempty
irreducible open $W$. It still dominates the chosen base open: the image of
a nonempty etale open is open and contains its generic point. The preceding
calculation gives $W^\circ$ on which $G$ is constant. Its image $O$ in the
base is nonempty and open; $W^\circ\to O$ is an etale cover, so $G|_O$ is
finite locally constant. Induction supplies a finite lisse partition on the
proper closed complement. Adjoin $O$ to obtain a partition of the whole
subset. At $T$ this proves the assertion. This is the strong subobject
assertion of [Stacks Project, Section
59.74](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03RY), with its Noetherian
hypothesis retained.

attrs.title: Subsheaves of a constructible sheaf on a Noetherian scheme

objects.body:
For a proper finite-type curve $C$ and a torsion sheaf $F$, assertion
$\mathcal C_7(C,F)$ of [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions] follows
from its instances for reduced curves with constructible $\mathbf
F_r$-coefficients, for every prime $r$. The intervening coefficient passage is
governed by constructible subsheaves, finite primary decomposition, and the
exact sequence

$$
 0\to F[r]\to F\to F/F[r]\to0.
$$

## Proof

Let $C$ be a proper finite-type curve and $F$ a torsion sheaf. The reduction
$C_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow C$ is a universal homeomorphism, so by
invariance of the etale site under universal homeomorphisms we may replace $C$
by its reduction. The sheaf $F$ is the filtered colimit of its constructible
torsion subsheaves (the constructible approximation on a quasi-compact
quasi-separated scheme), so [lemma-weil-pbc-curve-filtered-cohomology] and the
naturality of the maps $\rho^q_{k'/k}$ reduce $\mathcal C_7(C,F)$ to its
instances for constructible $F$; the finite primary decomposition and the
exact sequence $0\to F[r]\to F\to F/F[r]\to0$ (iterated over the prime factors
of the torsion orders) reduce constructible $F$ by
[lemma-weil-pbc-eight-curve-devissage] to the instances with $\mathbf
F_r$-coefficients.

Let $C$ be a reduced curve and $F$ a constructible $\mathbf F_r$-sheaf. There
is a dense open $j:U\hookrightarrow C$, a finite disjoint union of irreducible
curves, on which $F$ is finite locally constant. For $i:Z=C\setminus
U\hookrightarrow C$ there is a natural exact sequence

$$
 0\to j_!j^{-1}F\to F\to i_*i^{-1}F\to0,
$$

and $Z$ is zero-dimensional. Write $U=\coprod_aU_a$ and let
$j_a:U_a\hookrightarrow C$ be the composite open immersion. Then

$$
 \mathcal C(C,F)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \mathcal C(C,j_{a,!}(F|_{U_a}))\text{ for every }a.
$$

## Proof

The finite partition of $C$ into locally closed constructible subschemes on
which the constructible $\mathbf F_r$-sheaf $F$ is lisse (locally constant with
finite stalks) is a stratification in the sense of
[def-constructible-stratification] whose pullbacks of $F$ are finite locally
constant, so $F$ is constructible in the sense of
[def-constructible-constructible]. By [prop-constructible-generic-constancy]
there is a dense open $U'\subseteq C$ with $F|_{U'}$ finite locally constant.
Remove from $U'$ the finitely many closed points at which two distinct
irreducible components of $C$ meet; the result is a dense open
$j:U\hookrightarrow C$ on which $F$ is still finite locally constant, a reduced
curve whose irreducible components are disjoint, hence a finite disjoint union
$U=\coprod_aU_a$ of irreducible curves. Its complement $i:Z\hookrightarrow C$
contains no generic point of $C$, so it is zero-dimensional. The sequence
$0\to j_!j^{-1}F\to F\to i_*i^{-1}F\to0$ is exact, since at geometric points
of $U$ the middle and left terms agree and the right term vanishes, and at
geometric points of $Z$ the left term vanishes and the sequence is the
identity of the right term. For the equivalence: $j_!j^{-1}F$ decomposes as
the finite direct sum of the $j_{a,!}(F|_{U_a})$ (the $U_a$ are open and
closed in $U$), the terms $i_*i^{-1}F$ are constructible on the
zero-dimensional $Z$, where all $\mathcal C_j$
([def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions]) hold: the vanishing and
finite-stalk finiteness statements follow from
[lem-weil-pbc-zero-dimensional-cohomology], field-extension invariance follows
from [lem-weil-pbc-zero-dimensional-field-extension], and (C8) is a map
between zero groups. Moreover, $\mathcal C(-,G_1\oplus G_2)$ is equivalent to
$\mathcal C(-,G_1)\wedge\mathcal C(-,G_2)$ for the finite direct sums;
together with [lemma-weil-pbc-eight-curve-devissage] this gives the displayed
equivalence.

Let $X=\varprojlim_jX_j$ be a cofiltered system of quasi-compact
quasi-separated schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with affine
transition maps. For a finite ring $\Lambda$, let $K_i\in\Dplus(X_{i,\Et},
\Lambda)$ and let $K_j,K$ be its inverse images
[def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Then the canonical restriction map is an
isomorphism

$$
 \varinjlim_{j\geq i}H^nR\Gamma(X_{j,\Et},K_j)
 \xrightarrow{\sim}H^nR\Gamma(X_{\Et},K)
 \qquad(n\in\mathbb Z).
$$

## Proof

Choose $a$ below the cohomological support of $K_i$, in
[def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Exact inverse image in
[prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact] preserves this bound and commutes with
truncations and cohomology sheaves. To calculate degree $n$, one may replace
all these complexes by their truncations in degrees $[a,n]$. Indeed the
complementary truncation starts in degree $n+1$, and its injective resolution
and derived sections have no cohomology in degrees at most $n$.

For a single sheaf in one degree, the assertion is
[lemma-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology-continuity]. Its proof works in
$\Lambda$-module sheaves by the module version of
[thm-weil-pbc-hypercover-cohomology]; its cochains and refinements are
unchanged. Build a bounded truncation by its finite sequence of triangles

$$
 \tau_{\leq b-1}K_i\longrightarrow\tau_{\leq b}K_i
 \longrightarrow\mathcal H^b(K_i)[-b]\longrightarrow .
$$

Apply derived sections at all stages and at the limit. Filtered colimits of
modules are exact, so their long exact cohomology sequences remain exact
after taking the colimit. The five lemma, inductively in $b-a$, proves the
comparison in all degrees for every finite truncation. The preceding
truncation argument then gives the assertion for $K_i$. All arrows used are
the restriction arrows, so this proves the named map, naturally in the
complex and in the inverse system.

Let $\square$ be a cartesian square
[def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] and let $K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$. If
$K\to I$ is a K-injective resolution
[def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions] of $K$ and $g'^{-1}I\to J$ is a
K-injective resolution of $g'^{-1}I$ on $X'$, then the morphism

$$
 g^{-1}Rf_*K\longrightarrow Rf'_*g'^{-1}K
$$

of the derived category [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] obtained by
applying the underived exchange morphism
[def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] $\Ex^0_{\square,I}$ term by term
to $I$ and comparing $g'^{-1}I$ with $J$ is the derived exchange morphism
$\Ex_{\square,K}$ of [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange].

## Proof

By [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] the morphism $\Ex_{\square,K}$ is
the mate, under the derived adjunction $f'^{-1}\dashv Rf'_*$, of the
composite $g'^{-1}\varepsilon_f\circ\theta_\square$ of the identification
$\theta_\square$ of [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with the counit
of the adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. The termwise construction
applies to $I$ the mate of the same composite in the underived adjunction
$f'^{-1}\dashv f'_*$, namely the underived exchange morphism
$\Ex^0_{\square,I}$ of [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange]; its source
$g^{-1}Rf_*K$ is computed by $g^{-1}I$ and its target $Rf'_*g'^{-1}K$ by the
K-injective resolution $J$ of $g'^{-1}I$, both resolutions existing by
[prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist] and being K-injective in the
sense of [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions]. Since the derived direct
image of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] is computed by K-injective resolutions,
forming mates commutes with the passage from the underived adjunction to the
derived one, so the two procedures produce the same morphism of the derived
category, namely $\Ex_{\square,K}$ as defined in
[def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange].

attrs.title: The termwise construction of the derived exchange morphism

objects.body:
Let $f:T\to S$ be a scheme morphism and
$a:U\hookrightarrow S$ an
open immersion. In the
cartesian square
put $V=T\times_SU$, $b:V\hookrightarrow T$, and $f_U:V\to U$.
For a finite ring $\Lambda$ and
$L\in\hyperref[def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]{D^+(T_{\Et},\Lambda)}$,
restriction gives a natural isomorphism

$$
a^{-1}Rf_*L \xrightarrow{\sim} Rf_{U,*}b^{-1}L,
$$

using the
derived direct image and
inverse image functors.

## Proof

For an etale $W\to U$, also viewed as etale over $S$, the direct
image of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] satisfies

$$
(a^{-1}f_*F)(W)=F(T\times_SW)
=(f_{U,*}b^{-1}F)(W).
$$

Here restriction along an open is the inverse image of
[def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], which is exact by
[prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact]. The extension-by-zero functor
$b_!$ of [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] is exact and left
adjoint to $b^{-1}$. Consequently, if $I$ is injective on
$T_{\Et}$, the identity

$$
\operatorname{Hom}_{V_{\Et}}(-,b^{-1}I)
\simeq \operatorname{Hom}_{T_{\Et}}(b_!(-),I)
$$

is an exact contravariant functor: $b_!$ preserves short exact
sequences, and $\operatorname{Hom}(-,I)$ is exact. Thus $b^{-1}I$
is injective.

Choose a bounded-below injective resolution $L\to I^\bullet$ as in
[prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Exactness of
$b^{-1}$ and the preceding injectivity calculation make
$b^{-1}I^\bullet$ an injective resolution of $b^{-1}L$.
The displayed identity of sections applied in every degree identifies
$a^{-1}f_*I^\bullet$ with $f_{U,*}b^{-1}I^\bullet$.
Since $a^{-1}$ is exact, these represent the two derived functors
in the statement. This proves the derived isomorphism.
These identifications are restrictions of the same sections, so they
commute with successive restrictions and composition of direct images.

attrs.title: Derived direct image restricted to an open

objects.body:
Let $T$ be a scheme and let $K\to L$ be a morphism of complexes in
$\Dplus(T_{\Et})$ of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Then $K\to L$ is an
isomorphism of $\Dplus(T_{\Et})$ if and only if for every geometric point
[def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] $\bar t$ of $T$ and every integer $i$ the
induced map

$$
 \mathcal H^i(K)_{\bar t}\longrightarrow\mathcal H^i(L)_{\bar t}
$$

of geometric stalks is an isomorphism.

## Proof

By [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] the category $\Dplus(T_{\Et})$ is the
full subcategory of the Verdier localization of the complex category at the
quasi-isomorphisms consisting of the bounded-below complexes, so a morphism
of complexes is an isomorphism of $\Dplus(T_{\Et})$ precisely when it is a
quasi-isomorphism, that is, precisely when it induces an isomorphism on every
cohomology sheaf.

Assume that $\mathcal H^i(K)_{\bar t}\to\mathcal H^i(L)_{\bar t}$ is an
isomorphism for every geometric point $\bar t$ and every $i$. By
[prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] the stalk functor is exact, so it
commutes with the formation of cohomology sheaves and the stalk of the
morphism $\mathcal H^i(K)\to\mathcal H^i(L)$ of sheaves of
[def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] at $\bar t$ is the displayed isomorphism. By
[lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] each $\mathcal H^i(K)\to\mathcal
H^i(L)$ is therefore an isomorphism of sheaves, so $K\to L$ is a
quasi-isomorphism, hence an isomorphism of $\Dplus(T_{\Et})$.

Conversely, an isomorphism of $\Dplus(T_{\Et})$ is a quasi-isomorphism, so it
induces isomorphisms $\mathcal H^i(K)\to\mathcal H^i(L)$ for all $i$;
applying the exact stalk functor of
[prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] gives the asserted isomorphisms on
geometric stalks.

attrs.title: Conservativity of geometric stalks on the derived category

objects.body:
For every morphism $u:U\to V$, the functor $u_*$ sends injective etale sheaves
to injective etale sheaves. The relevant adjunction is $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$, and
$u^{-1}$ is exact.

## Proof

By the elementary criterion for injective objects ([lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives]), a right adjoint to an exact
functor preserves injectives; the exact functor is $u^{-1}$ and the right
adjoint is $u_*$.

The map $R\to R^{\mathrm e}$ is faithfully flat and ind-etale
[def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Every faithfully flat etale algebra of
finite presentation over $R^{\mathrm e}$ has a section. Every maximal
localization of $R^{\mathrm e}$ is strictly henselian
[def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology].

## Proof

Finite tensor products in [def-weil-pbc-etale-contraction] are faithfully
flat and etale. Their transition maps are faithfully flat, so tensoring a
nonzero module into their filtered colimit never kills a nonzero element.
Consequently all the stated colimit maps are faithfully flat; they are
ind-etale by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability]. An etale algebra of finite
presentation over $R^{\mathrm e}$ descends to some $R_n$, and a surjective
etale covering of finite presentation descends after increasing $n$, by
[lem-weil-pbc-etale-finite-data-descent]. Its algebra occurs as a tensor
factor in $R_{n+1}$. The resulting map from that algebra to $R^{\mathrm e}$
is the required section.

Put $S=R^{\mathrm e}$ and let $\mathfrak m$ be maximal. An affine etale
neighbourhood of the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}S_{\mathfrak m}$
descends, after clearing finitely many denominators, to an affine etale map
$E\to\operatorname{Spec}S$ whose image contains $D(f)$ for some
$f\notin\mathfrak m$. Choose $a\in S$ with $g=1-af\in\mathfrak m$. The finite
etale family $E\amalg\operatorname{Spec}S_g\to\operatorname{Spec}S$ is
surjective and has a section by the preceding paragraph. After localization
at $\mathfrak m$, a section lands in a single summand, since a local ring has
no nontrivial idempotent. It cannot land in $S_g$, since $g\in\mathfrak m$.
Thus every such etale neighbourhood has a local section.

For clarity, the elementary local-ring criterion just used to recognize
strict henselianity consists of two tests. A finite separable residue
extension can be lifted by a monic polynomial with invertible derivative to
an etale neighbourhood. Its section forces that residue extension to be
trivial. Similarly an approximate simple root of a monic polynomial defines
an etale neighbourhood after inverting its derivative. Shrink this
neighbourhood to exclude the other points of its finite closed fibre; its
section then lifts the specified root. The simple-root Hensel criterion,
equivalently lifting idempotents of finite algebras, is the henselian
condition of [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Together these tests prove
strict henselianity.

attrs.title: Strict henselian local rings in the etale contraction

objects.body:
Let $X=\varprojlim_iX_i$, where the $X_i$ are quasi-compact and
quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and the transition maps are
affine. Quasi-compact quasi-separated etale $X$-schemes of finite
presentation, finite diagrams of these schemes, and equalities of their
morphisms descend to some $X_i$. A finite family that is a covering
[def-weil-pbc-etale-site] at the limit is a covering at every sufficiently
late stage of a descended diagram.

## Proof

First suppose the schemes are affine. An algebra of finite presentation is
specified by finitely many generators and relations. Every coefficient in
these expressions occurs at one common stage of the filtered colimit of
coordinate rings. A morphism is specified by finitely many images of
generators; its relations and an equality of two such morphisms hold at a
later common stage. Etaleness descends by a finite standard-etale affine
presentation: the equations, the inverse of the relevant Jacobian
determinant, and the finitely many identities asserting that the chosen opens
cover are all finite algebraic data. These are elementary finite-presentation
and localization calculations.

In the quasi-compact quasi-separated case of
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], choose finitely many affine opens at a
fixed base stage and pull them back. Choose finitely many affine presentation
charts of the object above them. Their overlaps have finite affine covers, by
quasi-separatedness. Descend the gluing maps and their inverses on these
covers by the affine calculation. The cocycle identities on triple overlaps
hold at a common later stage, again by a finite affine cover and the equality
calculation. Gluing gives the required descended scheme and morphisms. This
proves the finite-diagram assertion.

For the covering assertion, the images of finitely many quasi-compact etale
maps form a quasi-compact open, and their union commutes with base change: a
nonempty fibre remains nonempty after extension of its residue field. The
complement is constructible. If its pullback to every later stage were
nonempty, these constructible complements, with their constructible
topologies, would form a system of nonempty compact Hausdorff spaces. An
inverse system of such spaces has nonempty limit: the finitely many
compatibility conditions on a finite product can always be met at a common
later stage, so compactness applies. A compatible family of scheme points
gives a point of the inverse-limit scheme for affine transition maps, as
follows locally by taking the union of the compatible prime ideals in the
colimit ring. This would give a point outside the covering at the limit, a
contradiction. Thus the complement is empty at some stage. This is precisely
surjectivity of the family in [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. For comparison with
the usual finite-presentation formulation, see
[Stacks Project, Tag 01ZM](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01ZM); the
finite data and the covering argument have been specified above.

attrs.title: Finite-presentation data at an inverse limit

objects.body:
For an etale map $v:W\to X$, the functor $v_!$
[def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension] is exact and left adjoint to $v^*$
[def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] on sheaves of modules over a constant ring.
Consequently $v^*$ sends injective module sheaves to injective module
sheaves.

## Proof

A morphism from the presheaf in [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension] to a sheaf
$N$ is a compatible family of maps $M(V,s)\to N(V)$. Such a family is exactly
a morphism $M\to v^*N$: on the slice etale site, the inverse image of
[def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] is restriction. Sheafification has the same maps
to $N$, so this proves adjunction.

At a geometric point $\bar x$, the defining direct sums give

$$
 (v_!M)_{\bar x}=\bigoplus_{\bar w\in W_{\bar x}} M_{\bar w}.
$$

Indeed, a point of the etale fibre is a lift on an etale neighbourhood of
$\bar x$. Finitely many lifts and germs can be represented on a common
neighbourhood by taking fibre products. Equality of finitely many germs holds
on a further neighbourhood. Thus taking the colimit over neighbourhoods gives
exactly the displayed direct sum, whose elements have finite support.
Geometric stalks are exact by
[prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact]; direct sums of modules are exact.
Conservativity in [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] proves
exactness of $v_!$. Finally
$\operatorname{Hom}(-,v^*I)=\operatorname{Hom}(v_!(-),I)$ is exact when $I$
is injective, proving the last assertion.

Let $X=\varprojlim_jX_j$ be as in the quasi-compact quasi-separated
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] setting above. Let $F_i$ be an abelian
etale sheaf on $X_i$, and let $F_j,F$ be its inverse images
[def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Then

$$
 \varinjlim_{j\geq i}F_j(X_j)\xrightarrow{\sim}F(X).
$$

The same formula holds on every etale finite-presentation object $W_j\to X_j$,
with $W=X\times_{X_j}W_j$.

## Proof

Work on the basis of quasi-compact quasi-separated etale objects of finite
presentation. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-finite-data-descent], every basis object
and every finite covering diagram descend to a stage. Define on this basis

$$
 G(W)=\varinjlim_{k\geq j}F_k(W_k)
 \quad\text{if }W=W_j\times_{X_j}X.
$$

This is independent of the chosen presentation: an isomorphism between two
presentations and its inverse descend at a later stage, and so do the
identities and any equality of morphisms. The restriction maps are defined by
descending the relevant morphisms in the same way.

This presheaf is a sheaf. Indeed, a covering of a basis object has a finite
refinement by basis objects. Its equalizer diagram involves only finitely
many section groups, including the pairwise intersections. Descend that
finite covering diagram; filtered colimits commute with its finite products
and equalizer. The sheaf axiom for every $F_k$, in
[def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], is therefore the sheaf axiom for $G$.

To identify $G$, first fix a stage $j$. The inverse image of $F_i$ on $X_j$
is, by [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], the sheafification of the presheaf of
sections on objects mapping to etale objects of $X_i$. Thus a section of
$F_j(W_j)$ is locally represented by such sections; equality of
representatives is also local. Only finite coverings are needed when $W_j$ is
quasi-compact. It follows that a section of $G(W)$ is locally represented by
the same inverse-image presheaf for $X\to X_i$. Conversely, the finitely many
objects, morphisms and equalities in any such local representation on $X$
descend by the cited finite-data lemma. They consequently define a section in
some $F_j(W_j)$; equality descends by the same argument. These two local
constructions give inverse morphisms between $G$ and the sheafified inverse
image $F$. Evaluating on $X$, or on $W$, gives the asserted formula.

attrs.title: Continuity of sections at an inverse limit

objects.body:
Using the standard cohomological cone convention, the morphism of
[def-weil-pbc-truncation-exact-couples] commutes with the connecting
maps and with every differential of the two spectral sequences. Its $E_2$ map
is the derived exchange morphism for the torsion cohomology sheaf $\mathcal
H^q(K)$; explicitly, in bidegree $(p,q)$ it is

$$
 g^{-1}R^pf_*\mathcal H^q(K)\longrightarrow
 R^pf'_*g'^{-1}\mathcal H^q(K).
$$

## Proof

The datum of [def-weil-pbc-truncation-exact-couples] is a morphism of
exact couples: the exchange morphisms of [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] on
the three terms of each truncation triangle commute with the connecting maps
by naturality, so the structure maps $\alpha,f,g$ are preserved. A morphism of
exact couples therefore induces morphisms of the two spectral sequences
compatible with every differential, and the connecting maps being part of the
exact-couple structure, the compatibility covers them. The $E_2$-map in
bidegree $(p,q)$ is the first graded component of the couple morphism, namely
the derived exchange morphism of [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] for the
torsion cohomology sheaf $\mathcal H^q(K)$, as displayed.

The transformation $\Ex_{\square}$ of the derived exchange morphism
[def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] is the identity for an identity
square. For horizontally or vertically pasted cartesian squares
[def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], the exchange morphism of the outer
rectangle equals the composite of the exchange morphisms of the two inner
squares after inserting the canonical associativity isomorphisms for inverse
and derived direct images.

## Proof

Both equations are the mate versions of the identity and pasting laws for
$\theta_\square$ recorded in [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square],
transported through the adjunction calculus for the adjunctions
$f'^{-1}\dashv Rf'_*$ and $f^{-1}\dashv Rf_*$ of the squares involved. By
[lemma-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-replacement] every displayed map is the
specified derived exchange morphism of
[def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange].

attrs.title: Identity and pasting equations for exchange

objects.body:
For every $n$, the diagram
$$
 \begin{array}{ccc}
  A_n&\xrightarrow{h_n}&B_n\\
  v_n\downarrow&&\downarrow v'_n\\
  C_n&\xrightarrow{h'_n}&D_n
 \end{array}
$$
commutes. Equivalently, $v'_nh_n=h'_nv_n$.

*Source:* the commutativity is Stacks Project, Cohomology on Sites, Remark
21.50.2 ([Tag 0E48](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0E48)): the
projection-formula map (21.50.0.1, [Tag
0B56](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B56)) is compatible with the
base change map of Remark 21.19.3 ([Tag
07A7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07A7)), i.e. for a commutative
diagram of ringed topoi and $E\in D(\mathcal O_{\mathcal C})$,
$K\in D(\mathcal O_{\mathcal D})$ the square formed by
$Lg^*(Rf_*E\otimes^LK)\to Lg^*Rf_*(E\otimes^LLf^*K)$ (projection formula),
$Lg^*(Rf_*E\otimes^LK)\to Lg^*Rf_*E\otimes^LLg^*K$ (base change),
$Rf'_*L(g')^*E\otimes^LLg^*K\to Rf'_*(L(g')^*E\otimes^LL(f')^*Lg^*K)$
(projection formula) and
$Lg^*Rf_*(E\otimes^LLf^*K)\to Rf'_*L(g')^*(E\otimes^LLf^*K)$ (base change)
commutes; this is exactly the rectangle $v'_nh_n=h'_nv_n$ at the level of
the four corners of [def-weil-pbc-four-corners]. Difference of generality:
Stacks states the commutativity for arbitrary $E,K$ over ringed topoi, with
no completeness hypothesis, no coefficient tower and no finite coefficient
ring, and omits the verification ("we omit the verification"); the rectangle
is the finite-level instance at the perfect coefficient $P_n=A/I^n$ of the
adic coefficient datum, and it is this finite-level form that the completed
exchange below reduces to.

## Proof

The two routes around the rectangle are both the level-$n$ reduction of the
base-change mate, computed through the projection-formula isomorphisms on
the two sides; naturality of the perfect-coefficient projection-formula map
with respect to the base-change mate makes them equal, with the arrows of
[def-weil-pbc-four-arrows].

A finite [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] morphism is proper.

## Proof

A finite morphism is affine, hence separated, since the diagonal of an affine
morphism is a closed immersion in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]; it is of finite type because an
$A$-algebra that is a finite $A$-module is finitely generated as an
$A$-algebra. It is universally closed: a finite ring map is integral ([pqf-lem-finite-integral-lft]), hence has going-up, hence
a finite morphism is closed, and finite morphisms are stable under base
change, so every base change of a finite morphism is closed. These are
exactly the defining properties of properness in
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions].

Finite pullback of sections, in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-finite-section-pullback], satisfies the following four
equations: identity pullback fixes a section; pullback along a composite
equals the composite pullback; pullback commutes with restriction to the
closed fiber; and a section descended from a finite surjective refinement
pulls back to the chosen local section on that refinement.

## Proof

The first three equations are the functoriality of the inverse-image unit of
[def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], applied to the identities $V\times_YY=V$, to
composites, and to the cartesian square defining the closed fiber of
[def-weil-pbc-finite-section-pullback]. The fourth is the uniqueness
statement in finite descent, applied to the local sections selected on the
refinement.

Let $U$ be Noetherian, let $h:V\to U$ be finite, and let $E$ be a
constructible abelian etale sheaf on $V$. Then its direct image $h_*E$ is
constructible on $U$.

## Proof

Pullback preserves constructibility: pull back the finite locally closed
partition and each of its finite constant etale trivializations. For every
closed subset $T\subset U$, give $T$ its reduced scheme structure and put
$V_T=V\times_UT$. [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-exchange] identifies $(h_*E)|_T$ with
the direct image of the constructible pullback of $E$ along the finite map
$V_T\to T$.

We prove that $(h_*E)|_T$ has a finite lisse partition by Noetherian
induction on these closed subsets. The empty subset is immediate. If $T$ is
reducible, its finitely many irreducible components $T_1,\ldots,T_r$ from
[lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-components] are proper closed subsets. Apply
induction to each and restrict its partition to
$T_i\setminus\bigcup_{j<i}T_j$. These restricted pieces are locally closed,
disjoint and cover $T$.

If $T$ is irreducible, its reduced structure is integral. Choose a nonempty
affine open $Q\subset T$ and apply
[lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-generic-constructible] to $V_Q\to Q$. It
supplies a dense open $Q^\circ\subset T$ on which $(h_*E)|_T$ is lisse. The
proper closed complement $T\setminus Q^\circ$ has a finite lisse partition by
induction. Adjoining $Q^\circ$ gives the required partition of $T$. At
$T=U_{\mathrm{red}}$, its locally closed pieces, composed with
$U_{\mathrm{red}}\to U$, are locally closed subschemes partitioning $U$, which
proves constructibility on $U$. No finite bound on the Krull dimension is
used.

attrs.title: Finite pushforward preserves constructibility on Noetherian schemes

objects.body:
Let $S$ be an integral Noetherian affine scheme, let $g:Z\to S$ be finite, and
let $E$ be a constructible abelian etale sheaf on $Z$. There is a dense open
$S^\circ\subset S$ on which the direct image $g_*E$ is lisse.

## Proof

Write $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, with $A$ a Noetherian domain and fraction
field $K$. A finite algebra is integral ([pqf-lem-finite-integral-lft]). Lying over, applied also after every
base change, shows that a finite map is closed: the image of $V(I)$ is the
closed set defined by the contraction of $I$. We use this elementary
finite-algebra fact to shrink the base below.

The nilpotent closed immersion $Z_{\mathrm{red}}\to Z$ is a universal
homeomorphism, so invariance of the etale site under universal homeomorphisms
permits us to replace $Z$ by $Z_{\mathrm{red}}$, pulling back $E$. By
[lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-components], $Z$ has finitely many irreducible
components $C_i$. The points of its generic fibre are exactly the generic
points of the components dominating $S$: in a finite algebra over a domain,
primes over $(0)$ become primes of an Artinian $K$-algebra, hence are minimal.
If there are none, $g(Z)$ is a proper closed subset and $g_*E$ is zero on its
open complement.

For each dominating $C_i$, the finite lisse partition of $E$ has a locally
closed stratum containing its generic point. That stratum contains an open
neighbourhood of the generic point inside $C_i$. Shrink this neighbourhood
further to avoid every other component. It is then open in the reduced scheme
$Z$, and $E$ is lisse there. The union $W$ of these finitely many
neighbourhoods contains the whole generic fibre. The closed subset $g(Z\setminus
W)$ misses the generic point of $S$. Choose a nonempty principal open in its
complement and replace $S$ by it. Now $E$ is lisse on all of $Z$.

Here is the finite-algebra calculation needed for the remaining step. Put
$B=\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$. The reduced finite $K$-algebra $B\otimes_AK$ is a
finite product of finite extensions $L_i/K$. In each $L_i$, the elements
separable over $K$ form its maximal separable subextension, over which $L_i$
is purely inseparable. Choose a finite Galois extension $K'/K$ containing
every conjugate of these finitely many separable subextensions. Consequently

$$
 \bigl(B\otimes_AK'\bigr)_{\mathrm{red}}
       =\prod_j L'_j
$$

with each $L'_j/K'$ purely inseparable. Indeed, tensoring each separable
subextension with $K'$ splits it into a product of copies of $K'$; the
remaining purely inseparable extension has, after any field base change and
reduction, a single purely inseparable residue field.

A primitive element for $K'/K$ has a monic separable minimal polynomial $P\in
K[t]$. Invert its finitely many coefficient denominators and its nonzero
discriminant in $A$. Then

$$
 A'=A[t]/(P)\subset K',\qquad \operatorname{Frac}(A')=K'
$$

is a finite free etale domain over $A$, of positive rank. The basis
$1,t,\ldots,t^{\deg P-1}$ proves injectivity into $K'$; invertibility of $P'$
in the quotient proves the etale condition. Positive rank and lying over make
$\operatorname{Spec}A'\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ surjective.

Put $D=(B\otimes_AA')_{\mathrm{red}}$. Its $A'$-torsion is a finitely
generated module, so one nonzero element annihilates it. After inverting that
element,

$$
 D\hookrightarrow D\otimes_{A'}K'=\prod_jL'_j .
$$

Each idempotent of this finite product is a fraction $d/c$ with $d\in D$ and
$0\neq c\in A'$. Inverting these finitely many denominators places all the
idempotents in $D$; their relations hold because of the displayed injection.
Hence $D=\prod_jD_j$, with each $D_j$ a finite $A'$-algebra embedded in
$L'_j$, and thus a domain.

In characteristic $p>0$, choose finite algebra generators of the $D_j$. Pure
inseparability supplies one common $q=p^e$ such that every generator $b$ has
$b^q\in K'$. Clear these finitely many denominators to put all $b^q$ in $A'$.
In a field of characteristic $p$, a $q$-th root is unique if it exists. Thus
at most one homomorphism from each $D_j$ to any field can extend a given
homomorphism from $A'$. This is precisely the radicial condition. Each $A'\to
D_j$ is injective and integral, so lying over gives surjectivity, also after
base change. After any base change the map is therefore a bijective finite
closed map, hence a homeomorphism. In characteristic zero the fields $L'_j$
equal $K'$; clearing denominators in the finite generators directly gives
$D_j=A'$. In both cases every $\operatorname{Spec}D_j\to\operatorname{Spec}A'$
is a finite surjective universal homeomorphism.

All the localizations just made in $A'$ come from shrinking
$\operatorname{Spec}A$. Combine their denominators into a single nonzero $c$
in the original finite free algebra $A'$, clearing any previous denominators
first. The determinant $N(c)\in A$ of multiplication by $c$ is nonzero, as is
seen after tensoring with $K$. The adjugate matrix shows that inverting $N(c)$
makes $c$ a unit in $A'$. Thus the final cover
$S'=\operatorname{Spec}A'\to S^\circ$ is still finite surjective etale. Only
the reduction of $Z\times_SS'$ has been decomposed into the
$\operatorname{Spec}D_j$; its nilpotent thickening is handled by invariance
under universal homeomorphisms.

Under that same site equivalence, a finite locally constant sheaf descends to
a finite locally constant sheaf: a trivializing etale covering descends and
the equivalence identifies constant sheaves. Therefore the direct image on
$S'$ is a finite product of lisse sheaves, hence lisse by a common refinement
of their finitely many trivializing covers. [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-exchange]
identifies it with the pullback of $g_*E|_{S^\circ}$. The cover $S'\to
S^\circ$ is itself etale and surjective, so its trivializing covers form a
trivializing etale cover of $S^\circ$, proving the assertion.

For every $a\geq1$, the derived counit from inverse limit to evaluation
induces a functorial isomorphism

$$
 (\Rlim K_\bullet)\otimes_A^LP_a\xrightarrow{\sim}K_a.
$$

Moreover, $(-)\otimes_A^LP_a$ commutes with the two derived countable
products occurring in the Roos triangle attached to the derived inverse-limit
construction.

(*Source note:* the reduction isomorphism is the finite-level form of derived
completeness in Stacks Project, Lemma 61.20.1 (Tag
[099M](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099M):
$K=\Rlim(K\otimes^L_\Lambda\underline{\Lambda/I^n})$ for a derived complete
$K$, for a Noetherian ring $\Lambda$ with an ideal $I$ on an arbitrary site)
and of the Koszul form of Lemma 15.93.17 (Tag
[091Z](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/091Z): $K$ is derived complete if
and only if $K\to\Rlim(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}K_n^\bullet)$ is an
isomorphism). Those entries concern a single derived complete object of
$D(\mathcal C,\Lambda)$; the form used here is tower-level, being stated for
the strict quotient tower of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], and it
adds the commutation of $(-)\otimes_A^LP_a$ with the two derived products of
the Roos triangle, which the verified entries do not state.)

## Proof

By [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction] the Koszul completion is identified
with $\Rlim K_\bullet$, so we verify the statement for the Koszul completion:
tensoring the strict Koszul tower with the bounded finite-projective
representative of $P_a$ and evaluating at the $a$-th stage gives the
canonical isomorphism. The commutation with the two derived products is the
compatibility of tensor with products in the Roos triangle of
[prop-weil-pbc-roos-triangle].

A flat morphism locally of finite presentation is an open map, and the same
holds after every base change.

## Proof

Omitted; the statement is already in Mathlib.

Let $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{h}Z$ be morphisms of schemes and let $F$ be
a sheaf on $X_{\Et}$. There is a functorial first-quadrant spectral sequence

$$
 E_2^{p,q}=R^ph_*R^qf_*F
 \Longrightarrow R^{p+q}(hf)_*F.
$$

No acyclicity hypothesis on $F$ is needed: the construction is via an
injective resolution of $F$, and $f_*$ preserves injectives because $f^{-1}$
is exact (the standard Grothendieck spectral sequence for the left exact
functors $f_*$, $h_*$; for bounded-below complexes with torsion cohomology the
same statement holds for the derived pushforwards by the same argument). It is
compatible with inverse image in a cartesian base change.

## Proof

The pair $(f_*,h_*)$ is a composable pair, with the hypothesis of the
statement asserting that $f_*F$ is $h_*$-acyclic; for $F$ injective this
hypothesis holds by [lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-preserves-injectives].
Therefore the Grothendieck spectral sequence theorem of the spectral-sequence
chapter supplies the functorial first-quadrant spectral sequence
$E_2^{p,q}=R^ph_*R^qf_*F\Longrightarrow R^{p+q}(hf)_*F$, whose $E_2$-page,
edge maps and convergence are those of the composite of left exact functors;
the compatibility with inverse image in a cartesian base change is the
naturality of its base-change form, in the dictionary of the
spectral-sequence chapter.

attrs.title: Grothendieck spectral sequence for a composite

objects.body:
Let $U\to X$ be a split etale hypercover
[def-weil-pbc-finite-split-hypercover]. Write $\mathbb Z[V]$ for the
sheafification of the free abelian presheaf on the sheaf represented by an
etale $X$-scheme $V$. Then the alternating-face augmented complex

$$
 \cdots\longrightarrow\mathbb Z[U_2]\longrightarrow
 \mathbb Z[U_1]\longrightarrow\mathbb Z[U_0]
 \longrightarrow\mathbb Z[X]\longrightarrow0
$$

is exact. For an injective abelian sheaf $I$, its complex of sections
consequently satisfies $H^0(C^\bullet(U,I))=I(X)$ and
$H^p(C^\bullet(U,I))=0$ for $p>0$. The same assertions hold with free modules
over a constant ring.

## Proof

Exactness is a local assertion about the sheaves of
[def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. A local chain has finite support. Choose
locally a vertex in $U_0$, using its covering of $X$. For each of the
finitely many simplices in a given chain, including its faces, construct a
cone to this vertex. Inductively, the cone on the boundary of a simplex has
already been specified. The matching-cover condition in
[def-weil-pbc-finite-split-hypercover] supplies a simplex with exactly those
faces after an etale cover. Take a common refinement for the finitely many
choices. Denote this cone operation by $h$. The alternating-face formula
gives $\partial h+h\partial=1$ on the augmented finite collection of chains:
the faces through the new vertex cancel and the remaining face is the
original simplex. Thus every cycle is locally a boundary. In degree zero the
same construction uses the augmentation, and proves its surjectivity as well.

The defining free-sheaf adjunction gives $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb
Z[V],I)=I(V)$. Applying $\operatorname{Hom}(-,I)$ to the exact augmented
complex is exact because $I$ is injective, which proves the assertions about
$C^\bullet(U,I)$. Replacing free abelian groups by free modules gives the
identical proof for a constant coefficient ring.

attrs.title: The augmented free complex of a hypercover

objects.body:
For a quasi-compact quasi-separated $X$, split etale hypercovers finite in
each degree [def-weil-pbc-finite-split-hypercover] exist. Their homotopy
category is cofiltered. A finite collection of local lifting requirements on
their terms in finitely many degrees can be satisfied after refinement,
provided each requirement is locally solvable for the etale topology.
Consequently an arbitrary etale hypercover can, through any specified finite
degree, be refined by one finite in each degree.

## Proof

Use the quasi-compact etale objects of the site in
[def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Their fibre products and the finite limits
defining matching schemes are quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Any etale
covering of such an object admits a finite refinement by affine opens of its
members: etale maps have open images, and finitely many of those images cover
the target. Each selected affine is of finite presentation over the target.

Construct a split hypercover successively. In degree $n$, retain the finitely
many degeneracy summands already prescribed, choose a finite cover of
$M_n(U)$ as the new summand $N_n$, and use its projections for the face maps.
The matching equations give the simplicial identities. This is precisely the
split construction in [def-weil-pbc-finite-split-hypercover]. For a
refinement $V\to U$, the corresponding target for the new nondegenerate
summand is

$$
 M_n(V)\times_{M_n(U)} U_n.
$$

Its map to $M_n(V)$ is a cover, so the same construction works. If local
lifts have also been prescribed, intersect this cover with the finitely many
covering families on which the lifts exist. Before constructing degree $n$,
impose also the pullbacks of the requirements in higher specified degrees
along every degeneracy from degree $n$. There are only finitely many such
degeneracies up to the specified degree. Thus the already prescribed
degenerate summands have the required lifts as well. Epimorphisms of the
sheaves in [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] are locally surjective, so lifting
finitely many sections through epimorphisms is one such requirement.
Continuing above the specified degree needs no new requirements. This also
constructs a refinement of an arbitrary hypercover: only finitely many affine
pieces of the covering of each matching scheme are selected at each step.

For two hypercovers, perform this construction with the product of their
matching covers; the result maps to both. For parallel maps $f,g:V\to U$,
construct a homotopy after refining $V$. In degree zero choose, locally, a
$1$-simplex of $U$ with endpoints $f(v),g(v)$. In subsequent degrees
triangulate $\Delta^n\times\Delta^1$ into its $n+1$ standard simplices.
Previously chosen faces prescribe compatible boundaries; the matching covers
of $U$ lift those boundaries after finite refinement. Induction supplies a
simplicial homotopy in every degree. On cochains the alternating sum of these
prism maps is a chain homotopy: internal faces cancel in pairs, leaving
$g^*-f^*$. This proves cofilteredness after identifying homotopic maps.

Every pro-etale object over an affine $X$ has a cover by objects of $\mathcal
B_X$. Every covering of a basis object has a refinement by a finite covering
of basis objects. Fibre products of basis objects over a basis object remain
in the basis. Restriction to this basis determines a sheaf and its morphisms
uniquely and detects isomorphisms of sheaves.

## Proof

Cover an object by affine opens. On each of them apply the ind-etale
refinement theorem over the affine base $X$. Its faithfully flat affine
refinement is a covering in the small pro-etale site and belongs to
[def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]. For a covering of an affine basis object, the
definition of a pro-etale covering first selects finitely many affine pieces
of its members. Apply the same refinement theorem over that basis object to
these pieces. Their composites with $X$ are ind-etale by the stability lemma
for ind-etale algebras. The relative-map and base-change assertions of that
lemma prove stability under the required fibre products.

For completeness, the extension of a sheaf on this basis is explicit: a
section on an arbitrary object is a compatible family of sections on a basis
covering, with equality imposed on basis coverings of the pairwise
intersections. Two choices are compared on a common refinement, which exists
by the preceding covering and fibre-product assertions. The basis sheaf axiom
makes this comparison independent of refinements and permits gluing. This
constructs a sheaf on the full site inverse to restriction, on objects and
morphisms. It also proves the asserted detection of isomorphisms.

attrs.title: The ind-etale subsite is a basis

objects.body:
The classes of ind-etale [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra] and ind-Zariski
maps are stable under base change, composition, and filtered colimits. An
ind-etale map is weakly etale. If $B,C$ are ind-etale over $A$, every
$A$-algebra map $B\to C$ is ind-etale. Weakly etale maps are stable under
composition and base change.

## Proof

Base change preserves finite products of localizations and etale
finite-presentation algebras. A finite presentation and its relations descend
through a filtered colimit. In a composite of ind-etale maps, descend each
finite-presentation algebra at the second step to a sufficiently late stage
at the first step, using [lem-weil-pbc-etale-finite-data-descent] on affines.
Taking all such stages gives the presentation required by
[def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. For ind-Zariski maps the same calculation
just descends the finitely many elements being inverted and the finitely many
product idempotents. It also proves the filtered-colimit assertion.

For a finite-presentation etale algebra $E/A$, its diagonal is both open and
closed in $\operatorname{Spec}(E\otimes_AE)$: it is open by the etale
condition and closed because the map is affine. Thus the kernel of
multiplication is generated by an idempotent. If $B=\varinjlim E_i$, an
element in the kernel of $B\otimes_AB\to B$ descends to an element whose
multiplication is zero at a sufficiently late stage. The kernel is therefore
generated by idempotents. The quotient by this kernel is the localization
inverting their complements. Consequently $B\otimes_AB\to B$ is ind-Zariski
and flat. Also $B/A$ is flat, as a filtered colimit of flat algebras. This
proves weak etaleness.

Given $B\to C$ as in the statement, factor it as $B\to B\otimes_AC\to C$. The
first map is ind-etale by base change. The second is the base change of the
just computed diagonal of $B/A$, hence ind-Zariski. This proves the relative
assertion. Finally, for a composite of weakly etale maps $A\to B\to C$, the
factorization

$$
 C\otimes_AC\longrightarrow C\otimes_BC\longrightarrow C
$$

has first arrow a base change of the multiplication of $B/A$ and second arrow
the multiplication of $C/B$. Both are flat. Together with transitivity of
flatness this proves the assertion about composites; the base-change
assertion follows directly from the two flatness conditions.

attrs.title: Stability and diagonal of an ind-etale algebra

objects.body:
Let $X$ be Noetherian and $F$ a constructible abelian etale sheaf on $X$.
There is a finite partition $X=\coprod_{i=1}^m S_i$ into nonempty irreducible
locally closed subschemes such that each $F|_{S_i}$ is locally constant with
finite stalks.

## Proof

Start with the finite lisse partition supplied by constructibility. A part $S$
is Noetherian, so [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-components] lists its
irreducible components as $C_1,\ldots,C_r$. Put

$$
 S_i=C_i\setminus\bigcup_{j<i}C_j.
$$

Each $S_i$ is open in $C_i$, and contains its generic point: an irreducible
component is not contained in the union of the other finitely many
components. Thus $S_i$ is nonempty and irreducible. These sets are disjoint
and cover $S$; they are locally closed in $S$, hence in $X$. Give them their
reduced locally closed scheme structures. Restriction of an etale
trivialization shows that $F|_{S_i}$ is still locally constant with finite
stalks. Performing this construction for the finitely many original parts
gives the required partition.

A morphism in $D(\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T))$ whose evaluation at every $n$ is
an isomorphism is itself an isomorphism and remains an isomorphism after
$\Rlim$. If a derived complete object $C$ satisfies $C\otimes_A^LP_n=0$ for
every $n$, then $C=0$. Consequently a morphism between derived complete
objects is an isomorphism once every finite reduction is an isomorphism.

The vanishing criterion is the characterization
$K=\Rlim(K\otimes^L_\Lambda\underline{\Lambda/I^n})$ of Stacks Project, Lemma
61.20.1 (Tag [099M](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099M)): the Stacks
entry assumes a Noetherian ring $\Lambda$ and an ideal $I$ and concerns one
object of $D(\mathcal C,\Lambda)$, while the conservativity of the levelwise
evaluations on $\operatorname{Tow}_A(T)$ used here is a property of the tower
category of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] that 61.20 does not state.
The closure of the derived complete objects under cones, used at the end of
the statement, is clause (1) of Stacks Project, Proposition 61.21.1 (Tag
[099Q](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099Q), Section 61.21, Tag
[099P](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099P)), which states that the
derived complete sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules form a weak Serre subcategory,
together with clause (5) (an object is derived complete if and only if every
cohomology sheaf is): the Stacks entry assumes a Noetherian ring $\Lambda$
with an ideal $I$ and a site with enough weakly contractible objects, and the
form used here is the tower-category statement over $T_{\Proet}$.

## Proof

The evaluation functors of [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit] are jointly
conservative on the tower category, and $\Rlim$ is a triangulated functor ([prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality]), so
the first assertion holds. For a derived complete $C$,
[prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction] identifies $C$ with $\Rlim C_\bullet$,
and the vanishing of every finite reduction kills the tower $C_\bullet$
levelwise, hence $C=0$; the cone of a morphism between derived complete
objects is again derived complete, so the last assertion follows from the
second.

Let $S$ be a nonempty irreducible scheme with generic point $\eta$, and fix a
geometric point $\bar\eta$ over $\eta$. Let $F$ be a locally constant abelian
etale sheaf, let $G$ be any abelian etale sheaf, and let $\phi:F\to G$ be a
morphism. If $\phi_{\bar\eta}$ is injective, then $\phi$ is a monomorphism.

## Proof

Let $N=\ker(\phi)$; exactness of the geometric stalk functors gives
$N_{\bar\eta}=0$. Suppose $N\neq0$. By conservativity of geometric stalks,
there is a nonzero geometric germ of $N$, represented by a local section. Use
a common etale refinement on which $F$ is constant. The image of that section
in $F$ can, after another neighbourhood restriction, be taken to be one fixed
nonzero element $m$ of the constant group. We have thus obtained a nonempty
etale $W\to S$ and a section of $N|_W$ whose image is constantly $m\neq0$.

Etale morphisms are flat and locally of finite presentation, so
[lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open] makes the image of $W$ a nonempty open in $S$. It
contains $\eta$, hence $W_{\bar\eta}$ is a nonempty etale scheme over an
algebraically closed field. Choose one of its geometric points. The displayed
section then has nonzero image $m$ in the stalk of $F|_W$, while its stalk in
$N|_W$ is $N_{\bar\eta}=0$, a contradiction. Therefore $N=0$ and $\phi$ is a
monomorphism.

attrs.title: A generic stalk detects kernels in a locally constant sheaf

objects.body:
Suppose $A\to B$ identifies every local ring: for every prime $q\subset B$,
the map $A_{q\cap A}\to B_q$ is an isomorphism. If $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is
w-local [def-weil-pbc-w-local], then $B/A$ is ind-Zariski
[def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra].

## Proof

Consider an arbitrary finitely presented algebra $P/A$ with a map $P\to B$.
At a maximal ideal $q$ of $B$, its finitely many generators become fractions
in $A_{q\cap A}$. Choose a common denominator and then clear the finitely
many defining relations. This gives $f\notin q\cap A$ and $P\to A_f$ inducing
the given local map. Equality with $P\to B$, and invertibility of $f$, hold
on an open neighbourhood $O_q$ of $q$, since only finitely many equalities
must be checked.

By [lem-weil-pbc-w-local-partition], the closed points of
$\operatorname{Spec}B$ have a finite clopen partition subordinate to finitely
many $O_q$'s. Its extension to $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is still subordinate to
these opens. Write $B=\prod_{j=1}^mB_j$ for the corresponding idempotent
decomposition. The local factorizations give

$$
 P\longrightarrow\prod_{j=1}^mA_{f_j}
 \longrightarrow\prod_{j=1}^mB_j=B.
$$

Here is the finite-presentation argument turning this into the claimed
colimit, rather than merely a supply of local maps. Take all finite products
of principal localizations equipped with an $A$-map to $B$. Two have a common
successor by applying the displayed factorization to their tensor product.
For two parallel maps, impose equality on finitely many algebra generators in
their target; the resulting finitely presented quotient still maps to $B$,
and the displayed factorization equalizes the two maps at a successor. Thus
this category is filtered. Polynomial algebras show that its colimit surjects
onto $B$; imposing one equation shows injectivity. This is the ind-Zariski
presentation of [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra].

A tower of finite abelian groups satisfies the Mittag--Leffler condition and
has $\varprojlim{}^1=0$. Consequently, for the derived inverse-limit
construction of [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit], the canonical Milnor
map is an isomorphism for such a tower.

(*Source note:* the vanishing is Stacks Project, More on Algebra, Lemma
15.88.1 (3) (Tag [07KW](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07KW): if
$(A_n)$ is Mittag--Leffler then $R^1\lim A_n=0$, i.e. the system is right
acyclic for $\lim$), and the identification of the Milnor map is Lemma
15.88.10 (Tag [07KY](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07KY)). Stacks
states these for towers of abelian groups; the form used here is a tower of
finite abelian groups in the tower category over $T_{\Proet}$, finiteness
being what forces the Mittag--Leffler condition, and the conclusion is stated
for the canonical Milnor map of [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit].)

## Proof

Descending chains of subgroups of a finite group stabilize, so the tower is
Mittag--Leffler and $\varprojlim{}^1=0$ by the product-cokernel description
of $\varprojlim{}^1$; the exact sequence of
[prop-weil-pbc-roos-triangle] then identifies the Milnor map.

A Noetherian scheme has finitely many irreducible components.

## Proof

Omitted; the statement is already in Mathlib.

Let $Y$ be an integral normal scheme with function field $K$, let
$g:\operatorname{Spec}K\to Y$ be the inclusion of the generic point, and let
$\underline E$ be the constant etale sheaf with value a finite abelian group
$E$. Then the canonical map $\underline E\to g_*\underline E$ is an
isomorphism. The same holds for the inclusion $j:U\hookrightarrow Y$ of a
nonempty open subscheme.
(*Stacks Project, Etale Cohomology, Lemma 59.73.13, Tag
[09Z5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09Z5).*)

## Proof

Let $\bar y\to Y$ be a geometric point and let $Y_{(\bar
y)}=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O^{sh}_{Y,\bar y}$ be the strict
henselization limit [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. By
[def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] the stalk $(g_*\underline E)_{\bar y}$ is the
filtered colimit of $\underline E(\operatorname{Spec}K\times_YV)$ over the
pointed etale neighbourhoods $V$ of $\bar y$, and
[lemma-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology-continuity] in degree zero identifies this
colimit with

$$
 (g_*\underline E)_{\bar y}
 =\underline E\bigl(\operatorname{Spec}K\times_YY_{(\bar y)}\bigr).
$$

Now $\mathcal O^{sh}_{Y,\bar y}$ is a normal domain: it is a strict
henselization of the local ring of the normal scheme $Y$ at $y$, and the
strict henselization of a normal local ring is normal (Stacks Project, More on
Algebra, Lemma 15.46.6, Tag
[06DI](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06DI)). Its fraction field is a
finite extension of $K$, so $K\otimes_{\mathcal O_{Y,y}}\mathcal
O^{sh}_{Y,\bar y}$, the localization of that domain at the nonzero elements of
$\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, is a domain as well. Hence $\operatorname{Spec}K\times_YY_{(\bar
y)}$ is irreducible, and a locally constant function on an irreducible scheme
with values in a discrete set is constant, by the description of the constant
sheaf in [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]; therefore $\underline
E(\operatorname{Spec}K\times_YY_{(\bar y)})=E=\underline E_{\bar y}$ and the
canonical map is an isomorphism on the stalk at $\bar y$. This holds at every
geometric point, so the map is an isomorphism by
[lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]. For a nonempty open
$j:U\hookrightarrow Y$ the same computation applies, the fibre product
$U\times_YY_{(\bar y)}$ being nonempty and irreducible over each affine open of
$Y$ because $U$ contains the generic point.

attrs.title: Constant sheaves on a normal scheme and the generic point

objects.body:
Let $p:V\to S$ be a
separated morphism and
$s:S\hookrightarrow V$ an
open immersion satisfying
$p\circ s=\operatorname{id}_S$. Its image is open and closed in
$V$, and the decomposition
$V=s(S)\amalg(V\setminus s(S))$ is a decomposition into open
subschemes.

## Proof

The identity of $S$ is a closed immersion, so
[lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-from-composite] makes $s$ a
closed immersion. It is already an open immersion; the two immersion
notions of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] therefore identify
$S$ with an open and closed subscheme of $V$. Its complement is
open, and the two disjoint opens cover $V$.

attrs.title: An open section is also closed

objects.body:
Let $n>1$, choose a prime $r\mid n$, and let $F$ be killed by $n$. There is a
natural exact sequence

$$
 0\longrightarrow F[r]\longrightarrow F
 \xrightarrow{r} rF\longrightarrow0,
$$

where $F[r]$ is killed by $r$ and $rF$ is killed by $n/r$. Thus a property of
torsion sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] stable under short exact
sequences and known for prime-torsion sheaves holds for every sheaf killed by
a positive integer.

## Proof

The displayed sequence is the kernel--image sequence for multiplication by
$r$ in the abelian category of etale sheaves, whose kernels and images are
computed sectionwise as in [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. The claims about the
orders follow from $r\cdot F[r]=0$ and $n/r\cdot rF=0$. The induction on the
number $\sum_\ell v_\ell(n)$ of prime factors of $n$, using this sequence at
each step, proves the stability assertion.

For a weakly etale $v:W\to X$, the site $W_{\Proet}$ is the slice of
$X_{\Proet}$ over $W$. The restriction functor on constant-coefficient module
sheaves is exact and preserves injectives. Consequently derived evaluation on
$W$, computed in sheaves on $X_{\Proet}$, agrees with derived global sections
on $W_{\Proet}$.

## Proof

Composition and base change preserve weak etaleness by the stability lemma
for ind-etale algebras. A morphism between two weakly etale $X$-schemes is
weakly etale as well. On rings, factor $B\to C$ as $B\to B\otimes_AC\to C$.
The first arrow is weakly etale by base change; the second is a base change
of the flat diagonal of $B/A$. This second map is a flat ring epimorphism,
whose own diagonal is an isomorphism, so is weakly etale. The scheme
assertion follows on affine opens. Objects, morphisms, and coverings of the
small pro-etale site therefore identify the slice with $W_{\Proet}$.

The construction of extension by zero along an etale map applies on this
slice with exactly the same formula: sheafify

$$
 V\longmapsto\bigoplus_{s:V\to W\text{ over }X}M(V,s).
$$

A map from this presheaf to $N$ is precisely a family of maps $M(V,s)\to
N(V)$ compatible with restrictions, hence a map to the restriction of $N$.
This proves its left adjunction to restriction. The constructed functor is
exact. Kernels are computed summand by summand before sheafification, which
is exact for module presheaves. For an epimorphism of sheaves on the slice, a
local section of the displayed direct sum has finite support. Lift its
finitely many summands on coverings in the slice and take a common covering
of $V$. Thus its sheafification is locally surjective and hence an
epimorphism. This proves exactness without a claim about ordinary geometric
stalks on the pro-etale site.

The adjunction now makes restriction preserve injectives. Restriction itself
is exact by the exactness of the pro-etale inverse image for constant
coefficients; it is the inverse image of the pro-etale operations for this
localization. Restricting an injective resolution therefore computes both
versions of derived sections in the statement.

With the notation of [lemma-weil-pbc-chow-factorization], the map

$$
 i_X=(\pi,i_Y):\widetilde X\longrightarrow
 X\times_Y\mathbf P^n_Y\simeq\mathbf P^n_X
$$

is a closed immersion over $X$.

## Proof

The map $i_X$ is an immersion by the graph construction applied to the two
maps supplied by [lemma-weil-pbc-chow-factorization]. Its source is proper over $X$ and its
target is separated over $X$, so $i_X$ is proper; a proper immersion is a
closed immersion.

If $f:X\to Y$ is proper [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and $g:Y'\to Y$ is
arbitrary, then the base change $f':X\times_YY'\to Y'$ is proper.

## Proof

For $f$ separated or of finite type, the base change $f'$ has the same
property by the corresponding stability of closed diagonals and of finite
generation under base change, in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]; and $f'$ is universally closed because
every base change of $f'$ is a base change of $f$, which is a closed map by
the universal closedness of $f$. Hence $f'$ is proper by
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions].

attrs.title: Properness is stable under base change

objects.body:
The image of a proper [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] morphism $f:X\to Y$
is closed in $Y$ (a proper morphism is universally closed, hence closed, and
its image is a closed subset carrying an induced $Y$-scheme structure).

## Proof

A proper morphism is universally closed, hence closed: by
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] every base change of a proper morphism is a
closed map, so $f$ itself is a closed map, and the identity base change gives
the asserted closedness. Its image is therefore a closed subset of $Y$,
carrying the induced closed subscheme structure of the scheme-theoretic
image, and $f$ restricted to its image is a proper surjection.

attrs.title: A proper morphism has closed image

objects.body:
The composite of proper [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] morphisms is
proper.

## Proof

Separatedness, finite type and universal closedness are each stable under
composition in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]: the diagonal
of a composite is the composite of diagonals (hence a closed immersion), the
finite-type property passes through composites (finiteness of the generation
is transitive), and the composite of universally closed morphisms is
universally closed, since the base changes of the composite are composites of
base changes and composites of closed maps are closed. Hence the composite of
proper morphisms is proper.

A proper [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] morphism which is an immersion is
a closed immersion, and the image of a proper immersion is closed.

## Proof

Write $f=i\circ j$ with $j:U\hookrightarrow W$ an open immersion and
$i:W\hookrightarrow Y$ a closed immersion, as in the definition of an
immersion of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. By
[lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image], $f(U)=i(j(U))$ is closed in $Y$, so
$j(U)=i^{-1}(f(U))$ is closed in $W$ as the inverse image of a closed subset
along the closed immersion $i$; being also open in $W$, $j(U)$ is an
open-and-closed subscheme of $W$, and such a subscheme is a closed subscheme
of $W$. Therefore $U\hookrightarrow W\hookrightarrow Y$ is a composite of
closed immersions, so $f$ is a closed immersion, and the image of a proper
immersion is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image].

Let $u:T_1\to T_2$ and $v:T_2\to T_3$ be proper maps with
open immersions $j_i:X\hookrightarrow T_i$ satisfying
$u j_1=j_2$ and $v j_2=j_3$. For $K\in D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$
with finite $\Lambda$, the maps of
the comparison-map
construction satisfy

$$
\alpha_{vu,K}
= (Rv_*\alpha_{u,K})\circ\alpha_{v,K},
$$

under the canonical identification $R(vu)_*=Rv_*Ru_*$.
For the identity map the comparison is the identity.

## Proof

Both sides have source $j_{3!}K$. By the adjunction in
[def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], it suffices to compare their
restrictions to $X$. Apply
[lem-weil-pbc-derived-open-restriction] successively along
$v$ and $u$. In each inverse image of $X$, the distinguished
component $X$ is open and closed by
[lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-section], and all the complexes
$j_{i!}K$ vanish on the complementary components. Restriction of the
two composites to this component is therefore the identity of $K$.
The same is true for $\alpha_{vu,K}$, whose comparison isomorphism is
the one of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-identification] for the
composite proper map, by
[def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison]. The section identifications
in the open-restriction lemma agree for composite maps, so these are
the same adjoint morphism. This proves the displayed identity.
For $u=\operatorname{id}$, that adjoint morphism is already the
identity; uniqueness under the adjunction proves the last assertion.

For every datum in
the comparison-map
construction, the specified map $\alpha_{u,K}$ is an isomorphism.

## Proof

On the open $j_2(X)$, the section described in
[lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-section] exhibits $X$ as an open and
closed subscheme of the relevant inverse image, and the comparison
isomorphism $\theta_{u,K}$ of
[lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-identification] is built from the
identity of $K$ on that component; hence $\alpha_{u,K}$ of
[def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison], being the adjoint of
$\theta_{u,K}^{-1}$, restricts to the identity of $K$. In
particular this holds at every geometric point of that open, including
points over generic points.

Let $\bar z:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T_2$ instead lie outside
$j_2(X)$, and write $i:T_{1,\bar z}\to T_1$ for the geometric
fibre. The fibre has empty intersection with $j_1(X)$, since
$u j_1=j_2$. Extension by zero in
[def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] therefore gives
$i^{-1}j_{1!}K=0$, degree by degree. The geometric-fibre formula
[cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-finite] gives

$$
(Ru_*j_{1!}K)_{\bar z}
\simeq R\Gamma(T_{1,\bar z},i^{-1}j_{1!}K)=0.
$$

The source $j_{2!}K$ also has zero stalk there. Thus the map is a
quasi-isomorphism on every geometric stalk.
[lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative], applied to the
cohomology sheaves of its cone, proves the assertion.

attrs.title: Proper pushforward of extension by zero

objects.body:
Let $u:T_1\to T_2$ be a
proper morphism between
Noetherian schemes, and $j_i:X\hookrightarrow T_i$
open immersions with
$u j_1=j_2$. Fix a finite coefficient ring
$\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, and a
bounded-below etale complex
$L\in D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$.
Writing $K=\nu_X^*L$ for pullback along
the comparison
morphism, there is a canonical isomorphism on the pro-etale site

$$
j_{2!}K\xrightarrow{\sim}Ru_*j_{1!}K.
$$

Here $j_!$ is
extension by zero and
$Ru_*$ is the
derived direct image.
These maps are the identity for the identity proper map and commute
with composition of proper maps fixing $X$.

## Proof

Apply the exact functor $\nu^*$ from
[thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] to the etale isomorphism
[lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison-iso].
The right side is identified with the pro-etale direct image by
[prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image]; properness gives its
quasi-compact and quasi-separated hypothesis.

For the left side, the comparison morphism in
[def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] satisfies
$j_{\Et}^{-1}\nu_{T,*}G=\nu_{X,*}j_{\Proet}^{-1}G$:
both evaluate a pro-etale sheaf $G$ on the same etale objects over
the open $X$. Taking left adjoints, using the adjunctions in
[def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], [def-weil-extension-by-zero], gives

$$
\nu_T^*j_{\Et,!}\simeq j_{\Proet,!}\nu_X^*.
$$

All these functors are exact, so the identity holds on complexes.
It transports the etale comparison map to the displayed map.
The identifications are natural and commute with composition;
thus [lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison-composition] transports
its identity and composition law as well.

attrs.title: Proper-open comparison for complexes from the etale site

objects.body:
Let $u:T_1\to T_2$ be proper, let $j_i:X\hookrightarrow T_i$ be
open immersions with $u j_1=j_2$, let $\Lambda$ be a finite ring and
let $K\in D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$, as in
[def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison], with $V=T_1\times_{T_2}X$,
projections $b:V\to T_1$, $p:V\to X$ and section $s:X\to V$.
Then restriction of
extension by zero along the
clopen section identifies $b^{-1}j_{1!}K$ with $s_!K$, and
restriction of the
derived direct image identifies
$j_2^{-1}Ru_*j_{1!}K$ with $Rp_*b^{-1}j_{1!}K$; consequently the
composite

$$
\theta_{u,K}:j_2^{-1}Ru_*j_{1!}K\xrightarrow{\sim}K
$$

is a specified isomorphism, namely the one used in
[def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison].

## Proof

By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-section] the morphism $s$ is an
open immersion with $ps=\operatorname{id}_X$ and closed image in
$V$, and $b s=j_1$; hence $j_{1!}=b_!s_!$, and the restriction
$b^{-1}b_!$ being the identity for the open immersion $b$, the
restriction of the extension by zero of
[def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] gives
$b^{-1}j_{1!}K=s_!K$. Applying
[lem-weil-pbc-derived-open-restriction] to the morphism
$u:T_1\to T_2$, the open immersion $j_2:X\hookrightarrow T_2$ and
the object $j_{1!}K$ of the derived category, the fibre product
there being $V=T_1\times_{T_2}X$ with maps $b$ and $p$,
identifies $j_2^{-1}Ru_*j_{1!}K$ with $Rp_*b^{-1}j_{1!}K$, the
derived direct image being that of
[def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Substituting the previous
identification gives $j_2^{-1}Ru_*j_{1!}K\cong Rp_*s_!K$, and
[lem-weil-pbc-clopen-section-direct-image] gives
$Rp_*s_!K\cong K$; the composite of these identifications is the
specified isomorphism $\theta_{u,K}$ named in
[def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison].

Let $u:T_1\to T_2$ be
proper and let
$j_2:X\hookrightarrow T_2$ be an open immersion. For the fibre
product $V=T_1\times_{T_2}X$ with projection $p:V\to X$ of
[def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison], the morphism $p$ is
proper and therefore
separated.

## Proof

By construction in [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison] the square
with sides $u:T_1\to T_2$, $j_2:X\to T_2$, $b:V\to T_1$ and
$p:V\to X$ is cartesian, so $p:V\to X$ is the base change of the
proper morphism $u$ along $j_2$. By
[lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change] a base change of a proper
morphism is proper, so $p$ is proper, and a proper morphism is
separated by the definition of properness in
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions].

attrs.title: Properness of the projection of the comparison square

objects.body:
Let $u:T_1\to T_2$ be
proper and let
$j_i:X\hookrightarrow T_i$ be
open immersions with
$u j_1=j_2$. For $V=T_1\times_{T_2}X$, with projections
$b:V\to T_1$, $p:V\to X$ and the morphism $s:X\to V$ induced by
$j_1$ of [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison], the morphism
$s$ is an
open immersion with
$p\circ s=\operatorname{id}_X$ whose image is open and closed in
$V$, and $s$ identifies $X$ with the open subscheme $j_1(X)$
of $V$, the projection $b$ identifying $V$ with the open
subscheme $u^{-1}(j_2(X))$ of $T_1$.

## Proof

The projection $b:V\to T_1$ is the base change of the open immersion
$j_2$ along $u$; a base change of an open immersion is an open
immersion, and its image is $u^{-1}(j_2(X))$, so $b$ identifies
$V$ with the open subscheme $u^{-1}(j_2(X))$ of $T_1$. Since
$u j_1=j_2$, the morphism $j_1$ maps $X$ into
$u^{-1}(j_2(X))=b(V)$, so the pair $(j_1,\operatorname{id}_X)$
factors through the fibre product $V=T_1\times_{T_2}X$: there is a
morphism $s:X\to V$ with $bs=j_1$ and $ps=\operatorname{id}_X$,
the one named in [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison]. Being
the restriction of the open immersion $j_1$ to the open subscheme
$b(V)$, the morphism $s$ is an open immersion, and it identifies
$X$ with the open subscheme $j_1(X)$ of $V$. By
[lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-p-proper] the morphism $p$ is proper,
hence separated, and $s$ is an open immersion with
$ps=\operatorname{id}_X$; the criterion of
[lem-weil-pbc-open-section-clopen] therefore makes the image of
$s$ open and closed in $V$, with
$V=s(X)\amalg(V\setminus s(X))$ a decomposition into open
subschemes. All schemes and morphisms here are those of
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions].

attrs.title: The section of the comparison square and the open it fixes

objects.body:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be proper and let $g:X\to W$ be a $Y$-morphism with $W$
separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] over $Y$. Then $g$ is proper.

## Proof

Write $g=\mathrm{pr}_W\circ\Gamma_g$ with $\Gamma_g=(1,g):X\to X\times_YW$
the graph. Since $W$ is separated over $Y$, its diagonal is a closed
immersion, and the graph is a base change of this diagonal along
$X\times_YW\to W\times_YW$, hence again a closed immersion (a base change is
a product of the type handled by
[lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-products], in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]); it is proper by
[lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. The projection $X\times_YW\to W$ is a
base change of the proper $f$, hence proper by
[lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], and the composite $g$ is therefore proper
by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition].

Let $\Lambda=P_n$ be as in
[def-weil-pbc-constructible-direct-image-finiteness] and let $g:V'\to V$ be
a morphism of schemes. The derived pullback $Lg^*=g^{-1}$ restricts to an
exact triangulated functor
$$
 Lg^*:\Dbc(V_{\Proet},\Lambda)\longrightarrow\Dbc(V'_{\Proet},\Lambda),
$$
and carries the class of objects with cohomology in $[a,b]$ into the same
class.

*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this form. Stacks' nearest
entries are the equivalence defined by $\epsilon^{-1}$ between constructible
sheaves on $X_{\Et}$ and on $X_{\Proet}$, Lemma 61.27.2 ([Tag
09AK](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09AK)), its complex-level form
for bounded below complexes, Lemma 61.27.4 ([Tag
09AL](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09AL)), and the weak Serre
property of the constructible category, Lemma 61.27.3 ([Tag
09B5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09B5)); the constructibility
entries Definition 61.29.1 ([Tag
09C1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C1)) and Proposition 61.29.7
([Tag 09C7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C7)) are stated for a
Noetherian scheme and a Noetherian coefficient ring and concern adic
constructibility, and no entry states that a pullback preserves a
cohomological interval. Difference: the blueprint adds the exactness of
$Lg^*=g^{-1}$ on the finite coefficient rings $P_n$ and the preservation of
the interval $[a,b]$, for the bounded constructible categories of
[def-weil-pbc-constructible-direct-image-finiteness].

## Proof

On the etale site, inverse image is exact and takes a constructible
$\Lambda$-module sheaf to a constructible one: in the partition description
of a constructible complex the restriction to each piece is lisse with
finite stalks, the inverse image of a lisse sheaf is lisse, and the inverse
image of a locally closed constructible subscheme is locally closed
constructible, the preimage of a finite partition being a finite partition.
Hence the bounded constructible etale complexes are preserved, with the
cohomological interval preserved by exactness. For finite constant
coefficients, the pro-etale operations identify the pro-etale inverse image
with the sheaf inverse image, and [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]
transports the etale statement to the pro-etale site.

Let $u:U\to V$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] of schemes and let $F$ be an etale abelian
sheaf on $U$. Then for every $q\geq0$ the sheaf $R^qu_*F$ of
[def-weil-pbc-direct-image] is the sheafification of the presheaf on the
small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] of $V$

$$
 W\longmapsto H^q(W\times_VU,F|)
 \qquad(W\to V\text{ etale}),
$$

and on $\Dplus(U_{\Et})$ the derived direct image $Ru_*$ is computed in each
degree by the same description, applied to a K-injective resolution
[def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions].

## Proof

Choose a K-injective resolution $F\to I^\bullet$ of the sheaf
[def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] $F$, which exists by
[prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. By
[def-weil-pbc-direct-image] one has $Ru_*F=u_*I^\bullet$, so $R^qu_*F$ is the
$q$-th cohomology sheaf of the complex of sheaves $u_*I^\bullet$. For an
etale $W\to V$ the definition of the direct image gives
$(u_*I^\bullet)(W)=I^\bullet(W\times_VU)$, so the presheaf underlying
$u_*I^\bullet$ assigns to $W$ the complex $\Gamma(W\times_VU,I^\bullet)$;
restriction to the etale $U$-scheme $W\times_VU$ preserves K-injective
complexes, because this restriction functor is exact and has the exact left
adjoint given by extension by zero of
[def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension] (injective sheaves being preserved by
[lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives], and exact functors with an exact
left adjoint preserving K-injective complexes by the K-injective formalism,
Stacks Project, Lemma 13.31.9, Tag
