[08BJ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08BJ)), so the $q$-th cohomology
of that complex is $H^q(W\times_VU,F|)$, the cohomology groups of
[def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] being independent of the chosen K-injective
resolution by [prop-weil-pbc-cohomology-resolution-independent]. The presheaf
$W\mapsto H^q(W\times_VU,F|)$ on the small etale site
[def-weil-pbc-etale-site] of $V$ therefore has sheafification equal to the
$q$-th cohomology sheaf of $u_*I^\bullet$, because sheafification is exact
(Stacks Project, Lemma 7.10.15, Tag
[00WJ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00WJ)) and so commutes with the
formation of cohomology of a complex of presheaves; this is the first
assertion. Applying the same computation in every degree to a K-injective
resolution of a bounded-below complex $K\in\Dplus(U_{\Et})$ in place of $F$,
which is legitimate by [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions], gives the
second assertion.

attrs.title: Higher direct images for quasi-compact quasi-separated morphisms

objects.body:
Let $M_\bullet$ be a uniformly bounded constructible adic tower in the sense
of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower] and put $M=\Rlim M_\bullet$.
For every local model in [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower],
restriction of the derived-limit projections gives a functorial isomorphism

$$
 L_{\alpha j}\xrightarrow{\sim}M|_{U_{\alpha j}}.
$$

Consequently $M$ is derived $I$-complete, the canonical maps

$$
 M\otimes_A^LP_n\xrightarrow{\sim}M_n
$$

are isomorphisms compatible with normalization, and $M$ has no cohomology
outside $[d_0,d_1]$. No finiteness assertion about the groups of sections on
$U_{\alpha j}$ is required.

That a derived limit of such a tower is derived $I$-complete is the criterion
of Stacks Project, Lemma 61.20.1 (Tag
[099M](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099M), Section 61.20, Tag
[099L](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099L)): the Stacks entry assumes
a Noetherian ring $\Lambda$ with an ideal $I$ and states the criterion
$K=\Rlim(K\otimes^L_\Lambda\underline{\Lambda/I^n})$ for a single object,
whereas the form used here reconstructs a uniform local tower from its models
$L_{\alpha j}$. The corresponding statement for the derived category is
Stacks Project, Proposition 61.29.7 (Tag
[09C7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C7), Section 61.29, Tag
[09C0](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C0)): there an object of
$D_{cons}(X,\Lambda)$ on a Noetherian scheme is adic constructible. The
Stacks entry assumes a Noetherian ring $\Lambda$ with an ideal $I$ and a
Noetherian scheme, whereas the form used here is the tower-level local model
$L_{\alpha j}$, a bounded complex of finite locally constant $A_T$-modules.

## Proof

Restricted to the local model $U_{\alpha j}$ of
[def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower], the tower $M_\bullet$ is the
reduction tower $L_{\alpha j}\otimes^L(P_n)_T|_{U_{\alpha j}}$ of the local
finite-free model $L_{\alpha j}$ with the quotient transition maps; its
derived limit (in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit]) is
$L_{\alpha j}\otimes^L_{A_T}\Rlim(P_n)_T|_{U_{\alpha j}} =L_{\alpha j}$,
since $L_{\alpha j}$ is a bounded complex of finite locally free modules and
$\Rlim(P_n)_T=A_T$ by [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]; the
derived-limit projections realize the displayed isomorphism $L_{\alpha
j}\xrightarrow{\sim}M|_{U_{\alpha j}}$. Applying
[prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction] to the tower $M_\bullet$ gives that $M$
is derived $I$-complete in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion], and
[lem-weil-pbc-finite-reduction-reconstruction] applied to the local towers
gives the isomorphisms $M\otimes_A^LP_n\xrightarrow{\sim}M_n$, compatible
with the normalization maps; the bounds $[d_0,d_1]$ and the absence of any
finiteness assertion on section groups are properties of the local models.

attrs.title: Reconstruction of a uniform local tower

objects.body:
Put
$$
 A_\infty=\Rlim A_\bullet,\quad
 B_\infty=\Rlim B_\bullet,\quad
 C_\infty=\Rlim C_\bullet,\quad
 D_\infty=\Rlim D_\bullet,
$$
and let $H,V,H',V'$ be the images under the triangulated functor $\Rlim$ ([prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality]) of
the four compatible tower morphisms $h,v,h',v'$. Then
$$
 V'H=H'V:A_\infty\longrightarrow D_\infty.
$$
The $n$-th component of both sides is the equality $v'_nh_n=h'_nv_n$ at
level $n$.

*Source note:* the assertion is the functoriality of the derived limit of
Stacks Project, Derived Categories, Definition 13.34.1 ([Tag
08TC](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08TC)), whose triangle is natural
in the system, so that a functorial model of $\Rlim$ carries compatible
tower morphisms to morphisms and preserves composition. The Stacks entry
states the triangle for one system; the blueprint adds the assembly over the
tower category, the functoriality of the sequential derived inverse limit
proved above, and the identification of the $n$-th components of both sides
with the finite-level equations $v'_nh_n=h'_nv_n$.

## Proof

The triangle functor $\Rlim$ of the derived inverse limit preserves the
rectangle commutation of [lem-weil-pbc-tower-compatibility], and evaluation
at $n$ recovers the finite-level equality.

attrs.title: The rectangle passes to the derived limit

objects.body:
Assume that for every scheme $S$ the projection $\mathbf P^1_S\to S$ satisfies
$\mathrm{PBC}$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-property]. Then, for every scheme
$T$ and every $n\geq0$, the product projection $(\mathbf P^1_T)^n\to T$
satisfies $\mathrm{PBC}$ by repeated base change and composition (over the
successive bases $T,\mathbf P^1_T,\dots$), and $\mathbf P^n_T\to T$ satisfies
$\mathrm{PBC}$ by cancellation along $\sigma_n$.

## Proof

The product projection $(\mathbf P^1_T)^n\to T$ is a composite of $n$
projective-line projections over successive bases, so it has $\mathrm{PBC}$ by
[prop-weil-pbc-composition-stability] applied stepwise. The morphism
$\sigma_n$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-finite], hence has
$\mathrm{PBC}$ by [prop-weil-pbc-finite-morphism], and is surjective by
[lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-surjective]. Since $(\mathbf
P^1_T)^n\to\mathbf P^n_T\to T$ composes to the product projection,
[lemma-weil-pbc-cancellation] gives $\mathrm{PBC}$ for $\mathbf P^n_T\to T$.

attrs.title: Reduction of projective space to products of lines

objects.body:
The map $R\to R_{[T]}$ is ind-Zariski [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], and
its points are the pairs $(x,y)$ with $x\in T$, $y\subset x$, with local ring
$R_y$. If all points of $T$ are closed in $\operatorname{Spec}R$, then
$\operatorname{Spec}R_{[T]}$ is w-local [def-weil-pbc-w-local] with closed
point set $T$. If moreover $T=V(J)$, its quotient by $J$ is canonically
$R/J$.

## Proof

The construction in [def-weil-pbc-retained-localization] is a filtered
sequence of idempotent localizations. Such localizations are ind-Zariski, so
[lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability] proves the first assertion. A closed
subset is patch closed. Compactness in
[lem-weil-pbc-w-local-partition] says that the intersection of its
constructible neighbourhoods is exactly itself. Thus
[lem-weil-pbc-w-localization-points] gives precisely the listed pairs and
local rings. The same fibre calculation gives the components
$\operatorname{Spec}R_x$; their closed points $(x,x)$ form the closed subset
obtained by base change from the closed point subset of
$\operatorname{Spec}R^w$.

If $T=V(J)$ consists of maximal ideals, a prime of $R_{[T]}/JR_{[T]}$ has
$J\subset y\subset x$ with $x\in T$. Maximality of every prime containing $J$
forces $y=x$. Both spectra in the quotient map are zero-dimensional affine
spectra, hence compact Hausdorff, and the map is a continuous bijection,
hence a homeomorphism. At every prime the map on local rings is the identity
of $R_x/JR_x$. It is therefore an isomorphism of locally ringed spaces, and
the asserted ring isomorphism follows.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be proper and surjective, let $I$ be injective on $Y_{\Et}$,
and choose a monomorphism $f^{-1}I\hookrightarrow J$ with $J$ injective on
$X_{\Et}$. The adjoint map

$$
 I\longrightarrow f_*J
$$

of the direct image adjunction is a monomorphism. Injectivity of $I$ supplies
a retraction $f_*J\to I$, so $I$ is a direct summand of $f_*J$.

## Proof

At a geometric point $\bar y\to Y$, choose a geometric point $\bar x\to X$
above it, possible by surjectivity on geometric points. Composing the stalk
map $I_{\bar y}\to(f_*J)_{\bar y}$ with restriction to $J_{\bar x}$ gives the
inclusion $I_{\bar y}=(f^{-1}I)_{\bar x}\hookrightarrow J_{\bar x}$, so the
stalk map is a monomorphism; by conservativity of geometric stalks, the map
itself is a monomorphism. Since $I$ is injective, the monomorphism splits,
which is the assertion.

attrs.title: Retract supplied by a proper surjection

objects.body:
For $A=\Zl$ and $I=(\ell)$, the quotient $P_n=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$ is
perfect over $\Zl$, represented by

$$
 [\Zl\xrightarrow{\ell^n}\Zl]
$$

in degrees $-1$ and $0$, in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. The analogous two-term resolution
holds for $\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$ over the ring of integers $\mathcal O_E$ of
a finite extension $E/\Ql$.

(*Source note:* perfectness is that of Stacks Project, More on Algebra,
Definition 15.76.1 (Tag
[0657](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0657)): an object of $D(R)$ is
perfect if it is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite projective
$R$-modules, so the displayed two-term complex of finite free $A$-modules
presents $P_n$ as a perfect complex. Stacks states the definition for a ring
$R$; the form used here is the same notion for $A=\Zl$ and $A=\mathcal O_E$
with $P_n=A/I^n$, and [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] additionally
requires each $P_n$ to be finite as a set.)

## Proof

A uniformizer is a non-zero-divisor in a complete discrete valuation ring, so
the displayed two-term complex is a finite free resolution of the quotient,
which is therefore perfect as required by
[def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum].

The algebra $C_A$ is faithfully flat and ind-etale
[def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra] over $A$. Its spectrum is w-local
[def-weil-pbc-w-local], its maximal local rings are strictly henselian
[def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], and its closed points surject onto
$\operatorname{Spec}A$.

## Proof

Use the notation of [def-weil-pbc-strict-w-cover]. The map $W\to E$ is
faithfully flat and ind-etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-contraction]. Its fibre
over a maximal ideal of $W$ is an algebraic algebra over a field, by
[lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-field]; all its primes are maximal also in $E$.
Hence $T=V(IE)$ consists of closed points.
[lem-weil-pbc-retained-localization] makes $C_A$ w-local with these closed
points and unchanged local rings there. Those rings are strictly henselian by
[lem-weil-pbc-etale-contraction]. Faithful flatness of $E/W$ shows that $T$
surjects onto the closed points of $W$, which surject onto
$\operatorname{Spec}A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-w-localization-points]. The composite
$A\to C_A$ is ind-etale by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability], and hence
flat. The just proved surjectivity makes it faithfully flat.

attrs.title: Properties of the strict w-local cover

objects.body:
A finite-type morphism whose geometric fibres are all nonempty is surjective.

## Proof

Let $y\in|Y|$ and let $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ be a geometric
point over $y$, with $\Omega$ an algebraic closure of $\kappa(y)$. The
geometric fibre $X_{\bar y}$ is nonempty, so some point of $X_{\bar y}$ maps
to a point $x\in X$; under the projection $X_{\bar y}\to X$, the image of
$X_{\bar y}$ maps to the point of $Y$ image of the closed point of
$\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, namely $y$. Hence $f(x)=y$ for some $x$, so $f$
is surjective on underlying points (the finite-type hypothesis is not needed
for this argument).

attrs.title: Surjectivity criterion via nonempty geometric fibres

objects.body:
The morphism $\sigma_n$ of [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-properties] is
finite. More precisely, on the chart where all $y_i$ are nonzero, the induced
affine ring extension is integral: each $z_i=x_i/y_i$ satisfies

$$
 T^n-e_1T^{n-1}+\cdots+(-1)^ne_n=0.
$$

The corresponding reversed equations give integral affine ring extensions on
the charts at infinity, and these charts cover $(\mathbf P^1_S)^n$.

## Proof

On the displayed chart the ring extension is generated by the $z_i$, each of
which is integral over the elementary-symmetric subring because it is a root
of the monic polynomial with coefficients $e_j=F_j/F_0$; the same argument
with $x_i$ and $y_i$ interchanged covers the charts at infinity. These charts
cover $(\mathbf P^1_S)^n$, so the affine criterion shows that the morphism
built in [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-properties] is finite.

The polynomials $F_0,\dots,F_n$ of [def-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-morphism]
have no common zero on $(\mathbf P^1_S)^n$ and are invariant under the action
of the symmetric group $S_n$. Hence
[def-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-morphism] gives an $S_n$-invariant morphism

$$
 \sigma_n:(\mathbf P^1_S)^n\longrightarrow\mathbf P^n_S.
$$

## Proof

A common zero of all $F_j$ would make the product $\prod_{i=1}^n(x_it+y_i)$
the zero polynomial in $t$, forcing some pair $(x_i,y_i)$ to vanish, which is
impossible in $\mathbf P^1$. Permuting the factors fixes every $F_j$, so
$\sigma_n$ is $S_n$-invariant.

attrs.title: No common zero and permutation invariance

objects.body:
Let $\sigma_n:(\mathbf P^1_S)^n\to\mathbf P^n_S$ be the symmetric-product
morphism [def-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-morphism]. It is finite and
surjective. Equivalently, over every algebraically closed geometric point of
$S$, every binary form of degree $n$ factors as a product of $n$ linear forms,
including factors at infinity.

## Proof

Over an algebraically closed geometric point, every binary form of degree $n$
factors as a product of $n$ linear forms, so every geometric fibre of the
morphism constructed in [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-finite] is nonempty; a
finite-type morphism with nonempty geometric fibres is surjective
([lem-weil-pbc-surjective-nonempty-fibres]).

The transition morphisms $P_{n+1}\to P_n$ make each of the four corner
families an object
$$
 A_\bullet,B_\bullet,C_\bullet,D_\bullet
 \in D(\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(Y'))
$$
after restriction of scalars, and make $h,h',v,v'$ morphisms in this derived
tower category. Evaluation at $n$ recovers the four displayed corners and
arrows. The rectangle equation commutes with every transition and with every
compatible endomorphism of $K$.

*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this tower-level datum. Stacks
describes the completed pullback and its reductions for a single object
(Lemma 61.20.2, [Tag 099N](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099N)), the
proper base-change isomorphism (Theorem 61.30.1, [Tag
09C9](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C9)) and, for a constructible
$K$, the structure of its reduction tower: Lemma 61.29.2 ([Tag
09C2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C2)) gives $K=\Rlim K_n$ with
$K_n=K\otimes^L_\Lambda\underline{\Lambda/I^n}$ of tor amplitude in a fixed
interval $[a,b]$, with constructible cohomology sheaves and of the form
$K_n=\epsilon^{-1}L_n$ for $L_n\in D_{ctf}(X_{\Et},\Lambda/I^n)$. The
derived-tower bookkeeping itself is the blueprint's (the derived inverse
limit and the bounded constructible tower), and no entry makes the four
corner families objects of the derived tower category; the blueprint adds
the transition data, the compatibility of the rectangle with every
transition and with compatible endomorphisms of $K$, and the identification
of the $n$-th evaluations with the finite-level corners.

## Proof

The normalization isomorphisms of [def-weil-pbc-four-arrows] make the four
families strict towers, and the reduction compatibilities of the projection
formula and of the finite-level exchange map make the four arrows tower
morphisms; the rectangle equation of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-level-rectangle]
is then compatible with the transitions by construction.

For a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] and
$L\in\Dplus(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$, use the natural comparison isomorphisms

$$
 \nu_{X'}^*g'_{\Et}{}^{-1}\simeq
 g'_{\Proet}{}^{-1}\nu_X^*,
 \qquad
 \nu_Y^*Rf_{\Et,*}L\simeq Rf_{\Proet,*}\nu_X^*L,
$$

and their analogues for the other sides. Conjugating the etale exchange map
[def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] by these isomorphisms gives the pro-etale
unit--counit exchange map

$$
 g_{\Proet}^{-1}Rf_{\Proet,*}\nu_X^*L
 \longrightarrow
 Rf'_{\Proet,*}g_{\Proet}'{}^{-1}\nu_X^*L
$$

of [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange].

## Proof

Expanding the unit--$\theta_\square$--counit composite of
[def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] and conjugating each arrow through the
comparison isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] and
[prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] gives exactly the mate of the ambient
ringed exchange; naturality of the two comparison adjunctions makes the
resulting square commute.

Let $\square$ be a cartesian square
[def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], let $F\in\Ab(X_{\Et})$, and let
$V\to Y'$ be etale. For a representative of a section of $g^{-1}f_*F$ over
$V$, consisting of an etale $W\to Y$, a map $V\to W\times_YY'$, and a section
of $F$ on $X\times_YW$, restrict that section along $X'\times_{Y'}V\to
X\times_YW$ and sheafify. The resulting section of $f'_*g'^{-1}F$ over $V$
depends only on the class of that representative in $(g^{-1}f_*F)(V)$, and it
is the section corresponding to the underived exchange morphism
$\Ex^0_{\square,F}$ of [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] under the
adjunction $f'^{-1}\dashv f'_*$.

## Proof

By [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] the morphism
$\Ex^0_{\square,F}$ is the adjoint, under the adjunction $f'^{-1}\dashv
f'_*$ of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], of the composite
$g'^{-1}\varepsilon_f\circ\theta_\square$, where $\theta_\square$ is the
natural isomorphism attached to the chosen identification of the cartesian
square of [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] and $\varepsilon_f$ is the
counit of the adjunction $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$. Evaluating that composite on
sections gives the displayed sectionwise rule: the counit
$\varepsilon_f:f^{-1}f_*F\to F$ sends the section of $f^{-1}f_*F$ over $W$
represented by a section of $F$ over $X\times_YW$ to that section, the
isomorphism $\theta_\square$ transports it along the identification $X'\cong
X\times_YY'$ to the section over $X'\times_{Y'}V$, and taking the adjoint of
the composite with respect to $f'^{-1}\dashv f'_*$ is the identity on
sections of the direct image of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Two
representatives of one class in $(g^{-1}f_*F)(V)$, a filtered colimit of
sections over etale $W\to Y$ by [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], agree over a
common refinement, and the restriction maps of $F$ are compatible with that
refinement, so the resulting section of $f'_*g'^{-1}F$ over $V$ is
independent of the representative.

attrs.title: Well-definedness of the sectionwise exchange rule

objects.body:
Base changes of universal homeomorphisms
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] are universal homeomorphisms.

## Proof

By [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], a universal homeomorphism $u$ is a
morphism every base change of which is a homeomorphism of underlying
topological spaces. If $v$ is a base change of $u$, then every base change of
$v$ is, by associativity of fibre products, also a base change of $u$, hence
a homeomorphism; so $v$ is a universal homeomorphism.

If $I$ is a direct summand of $M$ and $R^qh_*M=0$ for $q>0$, then
$R^qh_*I=0$ for $q>0$. This remains true after arbitrary base change.

## Proof

The higher direct image functors are additive, and additive functors preserve
retracts, so the direct summand structure on $I$ is preserved by $R^qh_*$; the
asserted vanishing follows from the vanishing on $M$. The argument is
insensitive to base change.

The patch topology of an affine scheme is compact Hausdorff. For a w-local
[def-weil-pbc-w-local] affine scheme $X$, its closed point set $X^c$ is a
profinite space, and restriction identifies clopen partitions of $X$ with
clopen partitions of $X^c$. An open subset containing a part of $X^c$
contains the corresponding components of $X$.

## Proof

Embed $\operatorname{Spec}A$ in $\{0,1\}^A$ by recording membership in a
prime ideal. The conditions for a subset to be a proper prime ideal are
closed conditions, each involving finitely many coordinates. Its image is
therefore closed in this compact Hausdorff product. The induced topology is
exactly the patch topology of [def-weil-pbc-w-local].

We recall explicitly the affine component fact being used. The intersection
of all clopen neighbourhoods of a point is its connected component. Indeed
this intersection is the spectrum of the localization obtained by inverting
all idempotents equal to one at the point. A nontrivial idempotent in that
localization would descend, together with its idempotent equation, to a
finite stage, and then give a smaller clopen neighbourhood. Thus its spectrum
is connected. Every point of an affine scheme specializes to a maximal ideal.
In the w-local case that maximal ideal is consequently the unique closed
point in its component.

Write $X^c=V(J)$. The ring $A/J$ has all primes maximal. Its spectrum is
compact Hausdorff with a basis of clopen sets: after quotienting by its
nilradical, every localization at a prime is a field, so for each $a$ the
ideals $(a)$ and its annihilator generate the unit ideal; this produces an
idempotent with the same basic open as $a$. This proves the assertion about
profiniteness. Distinct closed points belong to distinct components, hence
are separated by clopen subsets of $X$, by the component fact. If $E\subset
X^c$ is clopen, compactness first separates each point of $E$ from all of
$X^c\setminus E$ by finitely many clopen subsets of $X$, and then covers $E$
by finitely many such subsets. Their union extends $E$. It is unique, because
every nonempty clopen subset contains a closed point. Finally an open set is
stable under generalization, so it contains the whole component of each
closed point it contains.

attrs.title: Clopen partitions on a w-local affine scheme

objects.body:
The points of $\operatorname{Spec}A^w$ are pairs $(x,y)$ of primes of $A$
with $y\subset x$; their local rings are $A_y$. Its connected components are
the fibres over $x$, each isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}A_x$. Its closed
points $(x,x)$ form a closed subset identified with $\operatorname{Spec}A$ in
the patch topology. In particular, $A\to A^w$ is faithfully flat and
$\operatorname{Spec}A^w$ is w-local [def-weil-pbc-w-local].

## Proof

A prime of the colimit in [def-weil-pbc-w-localization] chooses one part in
each finite constructible partition. These choices form an ultrafilter of
constructible subsets and therefore give a unique patch point $x$, by
compactness in [lem-weil-pbc-w-local-partition]. Its contraction $y$ to $A$
avoids every $f\notin x$: use the partition by $D(f),V(f)$, and invert $f$ on
the first part. Thus $y\subset x$. Conversely such a pair specifies the prime
at every stage, so gives a unique prime of the colimit. The local ring is the
colimit of the stage local rings $A_y$, whose transition maps are identities;
it is $A_y$.

The idempotents of the constructible partitions give a continuous map to the
patch space of $x$'s. The fibre over $x$ is obtained by localizing at all the
idempotents selecting parts containing $x$. In this localization every
element is a fraction from $A$ with denominator outside $x$, and every such
fraction occurs. Equality of two fractions is likewise detected after one
further localization. Its ring is therefore $A_x$. These fibres are
connected, while different fibres are separated by those idempotents, so they
are the components.

A point $(x,y)$ is closed precisely when $y=x$. The complement of these
points is open: if $f\in x\setminus y$, the intersection of the idempotent
part labelled $V(f)$ with the ordinary basic open $D(f)$ contains $(x,y)$ and
no diagonal pair. The topology on diagonal pairs is generated by
constructible subsets of $\operatorname{Spec}A$, so is the patch topology.
This proves w-locality in [def-weil-pbc-w-local]. Finally the map is flat by
[lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability], and every prime $x$ is the image of
$(x,x)$. Flatness and surjectivity on spectra give faithful flatness.

If $k$ is a field and $B/k$ is weakly etale
[def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], every finitely generated $k$-subalgebra of
$B$ is finite etale. In particular $B$ is ind-etale, is reduced, and all its
residue fields are separable algebraic over $k$.

## Proof

By [lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-tor], every $B$-module is flat. For a local ring
with this property, flatness of the quotient by $(b)$ gives $b=bc$ for some
$c\in(b)$. If $b$ is a nonunit, $1-c$ is a unit, so $b=0$. All local rings of
$B$ are therefore fields; in particular $B$ is reduced.

We first treat a weakly etale field extension $k\subset L$. By
[lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability] and the Tor formula, $L\otimes_kL$ also
has every module flat. For any subfield $E\subset L$ containing $k$, the map
$E\otimes_kE\to L\otimes_kL$ is faithfully flat. Flatness of every module
descends along a faithfully flat ring map, by the tensor criterion for
injectivity. Thus $E\otimes_kE$ has every module flat. If $t\in L$ were
transcendental, take $E=k(t)$. Then $E\otimes_kE$ is a domain with the
nonzero nonunit $t\otimes1-1\otimes t$, and its localization at the diagonal
prime is not a field, a contradiction. Hence $L/k$ is algebraic. An
inseparable element would instead give a finite subextension $E/k$ for which
$E\otimes_kE$ is nonreduced: its presentation by the minimal polynomial has a
repeated factor at the root already in $E$. This is the same contradiction.
Thus $L/k$ is separable algebraic.

Apply this result to the fields $B_{\mathfrak q}$. They are weakly etale over
$k$, since localization is ind-Zariski and weak etaleness is preserved by
composition. Given $b\in B$, at each prime choose a monic separable
polynomial annihilating its germ. This relation holds on a basic open
neighbourhood. Finitely many such neighbourhoods cover $\operatorname{Spec}B$;
the product of their polynomials annihilates $b$ in every local ring, hence
in $B$. Thus every element of $B$ is integral over $k$. A finitely generated
subalgebra is consequently finite-dimensional and reduced, hence a product of
finite field extensions. Each factor embeds into some $B_{\mathfrak q}$, so
each extension is separable. These finite etale subalgebras form the filtered
presentation of [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. This proves the field
calculation also recorded in
[Stacks Project, Tag 092Q](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/092Q).

attrs.title: Weakly etale algebras over a field

objects.body:
Let $A$ be an integrally closed domain with fraction field $K$, and let $B/A$
be weakly etale [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Then $B$ is integrally
closed in $B\otimes_AK$.

## Proof

We give the reduction to elementary flat-module algebra. For each $x\in
K\setminus A$, choose a valuation overring $V_x\subset K$ containing $A$ but
not $x$. This is the valuation criterion for integral dependence. Set
$V=\prod_xV_x$, $L=\prod_xK$. The diagonal map of $K$ makes $A=K\times_LV$.
The map $V\to L$ is localization at tuples with all coordinates nonzero:
denominators can be chosen coordinatewise. Every finitely generated ideal of
$V$ is generated by one tuple, by choosing in each valuation ring a generator
of smallest valuation among the given finite list. Its annihilator is
generated by the idempotent of the coordinates where that tuple is zero. Thus
each such ideal is projective; every ideal is flat by filtered colimits.
Submodules of finite free modules are flat by induction on the number of
coordinates, using the image ideal in the last coordinate; arbitrary free
modules follow by filtered colimits. Hence all modules over $V$ have flat
resolutions of length at most one.

Flatness of $B/A$ preserves the exact equalizer sequence defining the
pullback square, and gives

$$
 B=(B\otimes_AK)\times_{B\otimes_AL}(B\otimes_AV).
$$

Put $C=B\otimes_AV$. It is weakly etale over $V$ by
[lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability], so [lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-tor] bounds
its flat dimensions by one. Its localization $C'=B\otimes_AL$ is injective,
since $B/A$ is flat and $V\to L$ is injective.

If $z\in C'$ is integral over $C$, the subalgebra $D=C[z]$ is finite over
$C$. It is flat: from $D\subset C'$, the Tor exact sequence identifies
$\operatorname{Tor}_1^C(D,M)$ with a subquotient of
$\operatorname{Tor}_2^C(C'/D,M)=0$. Flatness of $D$ and $C'$ makes the
composite

$$
 D\otimes_CD\longrightarrow C'\otimes_CD
 \longrightarrow C'\otimes_CC'=C'
$$

injective. Its image is $D$, so multiplication on $D\otimes_CD$ is an
isomorphism. Also $C\to D$ is faithfully flat: it is flat and injective
integral, and lying over gives surjectivity on spectra. The faithfully flat
equalizer $C\to D\rightrightarrows D\otimes_CD$ then gives $C=D$. Thus $C$ is
integrally closed in $C'$. An element of $B\otimes_AK$ integral over $B$
consequently lies in $C$, hence in $B$ by the displayed pullback. If $A=K$,
the assertion is immediate and the empty product construction is
unnecessary. This expands the reductions in
[Stacks Project, Tag 092W](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/092W) and
[Tag 092V](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/092V).

attrs.title: Integral closure after weakly etale base change

objects.body:
If $A\to B$ is weakly etale [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], then for
$B$-modules $M,N$ there are natural identifications

$$
 \operatorname{Tor}^B_i(M,N)=
 B\otimes_{B\otimes_AB}\operatorname{Tor}^A_i(M,N).
$$

In particular, a common bound on the flat resolution lengths of all
$A$-modules is also such a bound for $B$-modules.

## Proof

Take free $B$-module resolutions $P\to M$, $Q\to N$, in nonnegative
homological degrees. They are flat resolutions over $A$, by the flatness
condition in [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. The double complex
$P\otimes_AQ$ therefore computes $\operatorname{Tor}^A(M,N)$. The two factors
give it an action of $B\otimes_AB$. Tensoring over that ring with $B$ is
exact, by the other flatness condition. It commutes with homology and
identifies the double complex with $P\otimes_BQ$, which computes the left
side. This proves the formula. The bound follows from the usual
characterization of flat dimension by vanishing of Tor.

Let $k$ be algebraically closed and let $C$ be a separated finite-type
$k$-scheme of dimension at most zero, as allowed in
[def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions]. For an abelian etale sheaf
$F$, its etale cohomology is canonically

$$
 H^q(C,F)=
 \begin{cases}
  \displaystyle\prod_{c\in|C|}F_{\bar c},&q=0,\\
  0,&q>0,
 \end{cases}
$$

where the product is finite and $F_{\bar c}$ denotes the geometric stalk at
$c$.

## Proof

Finite type in the setup of [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting] gives a finite affine
cover by spectra of finite-type zero-dimensional $k$-algebras. Such rings are
Artinian; their prime ideals are finite in number and maximal, and their
residue fields are finite over $k$, hence equal to $k$. Consequently $|C|$ is
finite discrete and $C_{\mathrm{red}}=\coprod_{c\in|C|}\operatorname{Spec}k$.
The reduction is a universal homeomorphism, so invariance of the etale site
under universal homeomorphisms identifies the cohomology with that of this
finite disjoint union.

Every etale scheme over an algebraically closed field is a disjoint union of
copies of its spectrum: an affine etale neighbourhood is zero-dimensional and
reduced, and its residue fields are finite separable extensions of $k$. Thus
the small etale site on $\operatorname{Spec}k$ has sheaf category equal to the
category of sets, and abelian sheaves equal to abelian groups. Global sections
on each point are its stalk, and are exact. Global sections on the finite
disjoint union are the finite product of these exact functors. Taking their
right derived functors gives the formula.

Let $k\subset k'$ be algebraically closed fields, let $C$ be a separated
finite-type $k$-scheme of dimension at most zero, and let $F$ be a torsion
etale sheaf. The pullback map $\rho^q_{k'/k}(C,F)$ of the curve coefficient
pair [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting] is an isomorphism for every $q\geq0$.

## Proof

By [lem-weil-pbc-zero-dimensional-cohomology], both sides vanish for $q>0$. In
degree zero, reduce by invariance under universal homeomorphisms to the finite
disjoint union $C_{\mathrm{red}}=\coprod_c\operatorname{Spec}k$; its base
change is $\coprod_c\operatorname{Spec}k'$. On each point the pullback of a
sheaf of abelian groups is the same group, and its map on sections is the
identity. The map $\rho^0_{k'/k}(C,F)$ of
[def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions] is therefore the product of
these identity maps, hence an isomorphism.

Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime
$\ell\neq p$, a scheme $Y$, and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and let
$\mathcal C_Y=D^b_c(Y,\Qlb)$ be the common-stage coefficient category of
[def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], whose finite stages are the
rationalized categories $D^b_c(Y,E)$ of
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Then $\mathcal C_Y$ is idempotent
complete, and the canonical functor

$$
 \mathcal C_Y\longrightarrow\Kar(\mathcal C_Y)
$$

into its Karoubi envelope is an exact equivalence.

## Proof

Every finite stage $D^b_c(Y,E)$ of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] is
idempotent complete by the finite-stage Karoubian theorem of the
proper-base-change chapter. The category $\mathcal C_Y$ of
[def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] is the common-stage category of
the filtered system of these stages, so the filtered retract-descent
proposition applies: every idempotent of the common-stage category splits,
and a splitting may be represented over a single finite coefficient field.
The canonical functor into the Karoubi envelope is fully faithful by
definition of the envelope and essentially surjective because every
idempotent splits, hence it is an exact equivalence.

attrs.title: Idempotent completeness of the common-stage category

objects.body:
Let $E/\Ql$ be a finite extension with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, let $Y$
be a scheme, and let $D^b_c(Y,E)$ be the rationalized category of
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Then $D^b_c(Y,E)$ is idempotent
complete, and the canonical functor

$$
 D^b_c(Y,E)\longrightarrow\Kar\bigl(D^b_c(Y,E)\bigr)
$$

into its Karoubi envelope is an exact equivalence.

## Proof

The rationalization $D^b_c(Y,E)$ of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] is the
scalar localization of the derived-complete integral category
$D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] at
the central endomorphism given by $\varpi_E$, and it carries the rationalized
standard bounded $t$-structure, whose restriction to the integral category is
given by the levelwise truncations on the reduction tower. By the
finite-stage Karoubian theorem the rationalization of the integral
constructible category at a finite coefficient field is idempotent complete,
and the canonical functor into the Karoubi envelope is an exact equivalence.
The same conclusion follows from the bounded $t$-structure alone, every
idempotent of a triangulated category with a bounded $t$-structure splitting
by the Karoubian bounded-$t$ theorem. Both displayed assertions are therefore
established.

attrs.title: Idempotent completeness of the rationalized category

objects.body:
Fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with valuation ring
$\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, a scheme $Y$, and an integer
$n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, and let $\widehat{\mathcal
O}_{E,Y}\twoheadrightarrow(A_{E,n})_Y$ be the reduction of the completed
coefficient sheaf [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Then the
restriction of scalars $\operatorname{Res}_n$ is an exact functor

$$
 \operatorname{Res}_n:
 \Sh(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})
 \longrightarrow\Sh(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)
$$

between the categories of sheaves on the small pro-etale site
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].

## Proof

Kernels, images and cokernels of morphisms of sheaves of modules on the small
pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] are formed termwise on
the underlying sheaves of abelian groups, and $\operatorname{Res}_n$ of
[def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] is the identity on underlying
sheaves of abelian groups: the $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$-module structure
it uses is the one induced by the ring surjection $\widehat{\mathcal
O}_{E,Y}\twoheadrightarrow(A_{E,n})_Y$. A short exact sequence of
$A_{E,n}$-modules therefore remains short exact after restriction of scalars,
which is the exactness asserted.

Let $E\subset L\subset M$ be finite extensions of $\Ql$ and let $Y$ be a
scheme. For every object $K$ of the rationalized category $D^b_c(Y,E)$ of
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
 (K\otimes_EL)\otimes_LM\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }K\otimes_EM
$$

in $D^b_c(Y,M)$, natural in $K$ and compatible with the identity extension;
that is, the scalar-extension functors of
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] are compatible with composition of finite
extensions.

## Proof

On integral representatives the two composites are both computed, in the two
possible orders, from the completed derived tensor product with $\mathcal
O_M$; the associativity isomorphism of the derived tensor product identifies

$$
 (K\widehat\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L)
 \widehat\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_L}\mathcal O_M
 \cong K\widehat\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_M.
$$

The second tensor product is over $\mathcal O_L$, as required by the tower of
finite free coefficient extensions. The levelwise reductions and the
rationalization of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] commute with this
identification. After rationalization the comparison is the composite of
associators recorded in the scalar-extension proposition of the
proper-base-change chapter, which also supplies naturality in the object and
the unit and pentagon equations. All categories and functors involved are
those of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi].

Let $E\subset L$ be a finite extension of $\Ql$ and let $Y$ be a scheme. The
scalar-extension functor

$$
 -\otimes_E L:D^b_c(Y,E)\longrightarrow D^b_c(Y,L)
$$

of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] is an exact triangulated functor: it
preserves shifts and carries distinguished triangles of $D^b_c(Y,E)$ to
distinguished triangles of $D^b_c(Y,L)$.

## Proof

The functor is well defined by [lem-weil-scalar-extension-well-defined]. On
integral representatives it is the derived tensor product
$-\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$ of [def-weil-derived-tensor] composed
with the levelwise reductions of
[def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] and the rationalization of
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]; being a composite of exact functors of
triangulated categories it preserves shifts and distinguished triangles. The
same statements, with the associators, shift comparisons and unit equations
of the normalized system, are recorded in the scalar-extension proposition of
the proper-base-change chapter, to which the present functor is the transport
along the identification of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] with the raw
scalar localization there.

attrs.title: Scalar extension is an exact triangulated functor

objects.body:
Let $E\subset L$ be a finite extension of $\Ql$, with rings of integers
$\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$ and uniformizers $\varpi_E,\varpi_L$, and
let $Y$ be a scheme. For an object of the rationalized category $D^b_c(Y,E)$
of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] represented by an integral complex
$K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$, the object

$$
 \bigl(K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L\bigr)
 \otimes_{\mathcal O_L}L
$$

of $D^b_c(Y,L)$, formed with the derived tensor product
[def-weil-derived-tensor], levelwise modulo powers of the two uniformizers
and followed by rationalization, is independent of the chosen integral
representative $K$, up to canonical isomorphism.

## Proof

The composite of the functor $-\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$, the
levelwise reductions and the rationalization is $\mathcal O_E$-linear and
exact on the derived-complete integral constructible category
$D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]:
$\mathcal O_L$ is finite free over $\mathcal O_E$, so tensoring with it
preserves the boundedness and the derived completeness of the objects, and
the derived tensor product used at each stage is that of
[def-weil-derived-tensor]. By the rational-transport proposition of the
proper-base-change chapter every exact $\mathcal O_E$-linear functor on the
integral constructible category extends uniquely to its rationalization
$D^b_c(Y,E)$ of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and a uniquely determined
extension is computed indifferently from any integral representative of its
argument.

Let $s:S\hookrightarrow X$ be a locally closed immersion. On either
of the two finite-coefficient sites, and on the ambient derived
categories, there is a natural isomorphism

$$
R\mathcal Hom_X(Rs_!P,M)
\cong Rs_*R\mathcal Hom_S(P,Rs^!M).
$$

No constructible-preservation or biduality assertion is assumed.

## Proof

Factor $s$ into an open and a closed immersion. The adjunctions of
[def-weil-open-closed-recollement], [lem-exc-closed-ambient] construct
$Rs^!$ as their composite. Extension by zero for an open or closed
immersion is exact, and its stalkwise description gives, for all
complexes, $Q\otimes^LRs_!P=Rs_!(s^*Q\otimes^LP)$; use flat
resolutions to derive the tensor product. For every test complex
$Q$ on $X$, the adjunctions and the internal Hom of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] give

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_X(Q,R\mathcal Hom_X(Rs_!P,M))
&=\operatorname{Hom}_X(Rs_!(s^*Q\otimes^LP),M)\\
&=\operatorname{Hom}_S(s^*Q\otimes^LP,Rs^!M)\\
&=\operatorname{Hom}_X(Q,Rs_*R\mathcal Hom_S(P,Rs^!M)).
\end{aligned}
$$

Yoneda proves the assertion. The maps are defined by evaluation and
the adjunction counits, so the identity is compatible with both.

attrs.title: Internal Hom from extension along a stratum

objects.body:
Let $X$ be separated of finite type over $k$.
Its ambient dualizing object is $\omega_X=Ra_X^{\times}A$.
Write $D_X=R\mathcal Hom_A(-,\omega_X)$.
Then $D_X$ carries $D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Et},A)$ into itself.
More precisely, if $\dim X\leq d$ and $K$ has Tor amplitude
in $[a,b]$, then $D_XK$ has Tor amplitude in
$[-b-2d,-a]$. This bound is independent of the exponent $n$.
This conclusion is independent of Verdier biduality and of the boundary
exchange $i^*D_X\to D_ZRi^!$.

## Proof

Choose a finite stratification of $X_{\mathrm{red}}$ by smooth
locally closed subschemes $s:S\hookrightarrow X$ on which the
cohomology of $K$ is finite locally constant. Such a stratification
exists by constructibility, Noetherian induction, and the fact that a
reduced scheme over the perfect field $k$ has a dense smooth open in
each irreducible component. Nilpotent thickenings leave the etale site
unchanged. The finite-Tor restriction $P=s^*K$ is site-perfect:
successive local finite-free presentations give a bounded-above free
resolution, and truncation below the Tor bound leaves a finitely
presented flat last syzygy. This is the sheaf-local argument of
[lem-weil-bounded-finite-tor-perfect], with the notion of
[def-weil-site-perfect-complex]; it does not claim that each
cohomology module separately has finite projective dimension.

The open–closed triangles of
[def-weil-open-closed-recollement] build $K$, by finitely many
cones, from the objects $Rs_!P$. Ambient tensor adjunction gives

$$
D_XRs_!P\cong
Rs_*R\mathcal Hom_A(P,Rs^{\times}\omega_X)
=Rs_*D_SP.
$$

This is [lem-weil-stratum-ambient-hom] for the locally closed
immersion, using composition of right adjoints. It is an ambient
identity, so it assumes no constructible preservation by $D_X$.
On a stratum of dimension $r$, the ambient smooth theorem
[thm-asd-smooth-tensor] makes $\omega_S$ an invertible sheaf
shifted by $[2r]$. Thus $D_SP=P^\vee\otimes\omega_S$ is
a site-perfect complex of Tor amplitude
$[-b-2r,-a-2r]$. The direct-image
theorem [thm-sf-direct-image-tor-amplitude], with the uniform
vanishing bound of [lem-sf-etale-direct-image-vanishing], makes
$Rs_*D_SP$ bounded constructible of Tor amplitude
$[-b-2r,-a]$, contained in $[-b-2d,-a]$.
The localization triangles assemble these pieces by extensions;
tensoring such a triangle with any module sheaf preserves the common
vanishing interval. Exactness of internal Hom in its first variable
therefore gives the stated bound for $D_XK$. Taking $K=A_X$ also proves that
$\omega_X$ is bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude.

Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] $p,a,q,k_0,k$, a
prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite-type $k_0$-scheme $Y_0$ with
$Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and let
$D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(Y,\Qlb)$ be the common-stage Weil category of
[def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Then $D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(Y,\Qlb)$ is idempotent
complete, and the canonical functor

$$
 D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(Y,\Qlb)\longrightarrow
 \Kar\bigl(D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(Y,\Qlb)\bigr)
$$

into its Karoubi envelope is an exact equivalence.

## Proof

At a finite coefficient field $E$, the category $D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(Y,E)$ of
[def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] is the localization of bounded complexes of
constructible $E$-Weil sheaves at equivariant quasi-isomorphisms, and its
heart is the category of constructible $E$-Weil sheaves, which is abelian:
kernels and cokernels of morphisms of Weil sheaves are computed in the
constructible heart [def-weil-constructible-heart], and the Frobenius
isomorphism $\theta$ is carried along. The equivariant standard
$t$-structure is therefore bounded with abelian heart, so by the Karoubian
bounded-$t$ theorem every finite stage $D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(Y,E)$ is idempotent
complete and its canonical functor into the Karoubi envelope is an exact
equivalence. The category $D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(Y,\Qlb)$ is the 2-colimit of
these stages over the directed set of finite extensions of $\Ql$, as recorded
in the common-stage construction of
[def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]; by the filtered retract-descent
proposition it is idempotent complete, an idempotent of the colimit
descending to a finite stage and splitting there, and its canonical functor
into the Karoubi envelope is again an exact equivalence.

attrs.title: Idempotent completeness of the common-stage Weil category

objects.body:
Let $U_0/k_0$ be geometrically connected and separated of finite type,
put $U=U_0\times_{k_0}\overline{k}_0$, and choose a geometric point
$\bar u\to U$. Put $A_n=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. There is a
natural Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism

$$
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cont}}(\pi_1(U,\bar u),\mathbf Z_\ell)
\xrightarrow{\sim}
\varprojlim_n H^1_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(U,A_n).
\tag{3.2}
$$

Under the Weil-group action determined by a
degree-one lift $s$, Frobenius on the left is

$$
f\longmapsto\bigl[g\longmapsto f(s^{-1}gs)\bigr].
$$

The cohomology and Weil-group conventions are those of
[def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], [def-wf-weil-group].

## Proof

At level $n$, [lem-wf-finite-constant-h1-pi1] gives

$$
H^1(U,A_n)\cong
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cont}}(\pi_1(U,\bar u),A_n).
\tag{3.3}
$$

Its naturality shows that the transition map is reduction modulo
$\ell^n$. A compatible family on the right of (3.3) gives, point by
point, a homomorphism to
$\varprojlim_nA_n=\mathbf Z_\ell$. It is continuous because the inverse
image of $\ell^n\mathbf Z_\ell$ is the open kernel of its level-$n$
reduction. Conversely, reducing a continuous $\mathbf Z_\ell$-valued
homomorphism gives such a family. This proves (3.2). The explicit
Weil-descent computation in [lem-wf-finite-constant-h1-pi1], together
with [def-wf-weil-group], gives precomposition by
$g\mapsto s^{-1}gs$, which is the asserted Frobenius action.

attrs.title: Continuous $\mathbf Z_\ell$-characters are compatible finite-level classes

objects.body:
Let $k$ be a field.

1. (Chevalley.) If $f:X\to Y$ is a morphism of affine schemes of
   finite type over $k$, then the image of every constructible subset of
   $X$ is a constructible subset of $Y$. In particular $f(X)$ is
   constructible.
2. If $S$ is a nonempty constructible subset of an affine scheme $Y$ of
   finite type over $k$, then $S$ contains a nonempty open subset of its
   closure $\overline S$. In particular, a dense constructible subset of
   $Y$ contains a nonempty open subset of $Y$.

## Proof

(1) The coordinate map $k[Y]\to k[X]$ is of finite type, hence of
finite presentation because $k[Y]$ is Noetherian
([lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components]). Chevalley's theorem says that
for a ring map of finite presentation the induced map on spectra sends
constructible subsets to constructible subsets (in Mathlib:
`PrimeSpectrum.isConstructible_comap_image`). On the Noetherian space
$Y$, constructible in this sense is the same as a finite union of
intersections of an open and a closed subset.

(2) Write $S=\bigcup_{i=1}^rS_i$ with $S_i=U_i\cap F_i$, $U_i$ open and
$F_i$ closed, all $S_i$ nonempty. Put $Z=\overline S$; then
$Z=\bigcup_i\overline{S_i}$. The space $Z$ is a closed subset of $Y$,
hence has finitely many irreducible components
([lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components], applied to
$\operatorname{Spec}$ of the corresponding quotient of $k[Y]$), and it
is nonempty. Choose one, $C$. Since $C=\bigcup_i(C\cap\overline{S_i})$
is irreducible, $C\subseteq\overline{S_i}$ for some $i$. Let $\Omega$ be
the complement in $Z$ of the union of the other irreducible components.
It is open in $Z$, contained in $C$, and nonempty because $C$ is not
contained in the union of finitely many other components (it would lie
in one of them, contradicting maximality). So $\Omega$ is a nonempty
open subset of $Z$ with $\Omega\subseteq\overline{S_i}$; in particular
it is open in $\overline{S_i}$ and therefore meets the dense subset
$S_i$ of $\overline{S_i}$.

As $\overline{S_i}\subseteq F_i$, we have
$S_i=U_i\cap\overline{S_i}$, so
$S_i\cap\Omega=U_i\cap\Omega$, which is open in $Z$. It is nonempty by
the previous paragraph and contained in $S$. This is the required
nonempty open subset of $\overline S$. When $S$ is dense, $\overline
S=Y$.

attrs.title: Chevalley constructibility and open pieces of constructible sets

objects.body:
Let $X$ be an irreducible affine variety over a field $k$, with
coordinate algebra $k[X]$ (finitely generated and reduced). Then $k[X]$
is a domain, and every closed subset $Y\subsetneq X$ satisfies
$\dim Y\le\dim X-1$ (with the convention $\dim\varnothing=-1$), where
dimension is the supremum of lengths of strict chains of prime ideals of
the coordinate algebra.

## Proof

*Domain.* The closure of a point $\mathfrak p$ of
$X=\operatorname{Spec}k[X]$ is $V(\mathfrak p)$, and $X=\bigcup V(\mathfrak p)$
over the minimal primes. If $ab=0$ in $k[X]$, then every prime contains
$a$ or $b$, so $X=V(a)\cup V(b)$; by irreducibility $X=V(a)$, say, so
$a$ lies in every prime ideal, hence in the nilradical, which is $0$
because $k[X]$ is reduced. Thus $k[X]$ is a domain ($X$ is nonempty, so
$k[X]\neq0$).

*Finiteness of the dimension.* By Noether normalization there is a
finite injective $k$-algebra map $k[t_1,\ldots,t_d]\to k[X]$, and for
an integral extension the Krull dimensions agree (lying over, going up
and incomparability); the polynomial ring has dimension $d$. So
$\dim X=d$ is a finite integer.

*Strict drop.* Write $Y=V(I)$ with $I$ radical, so that $k[Y]=k[X]/I$.
If $Y=\varnothing$ there is nothing to prove, as $\dim X\ge0$. Otherwise
$I$ is a proper ideal, and $I\neq0$: radical ideals correspond
bijectively to closed subsets and $V(0)=X\neq Y$. A strict chain
$\mathfrak q_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak q_r$ of primes of
$k[X]/I$ pulls back to a strict chain of primes of $k[X]$ containing
$I$; all of them are nonzero, so prepending the prime $(0)$ of the
domain $k[X]$ yields a strict chain of length $r+1$. Hence
$\dim Y+1\le\dim X$, and $\dim Y$ is finite since $\dim X$ is.

attrs.title: Proper closed subsets have strictly smaller dimension

objects.body:
Let $A$ be a finitely generated commutative algebra over a field $k$ and
$X=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Then $A$ is Noetherian, every descending chain
of closed subsets of $X$ stabilizes, and $X$ has only finitely many
irreducible components.

## Proof

*Noetherianity.* Choose a surjection $k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\to A$. The
polynomial ring is Noetherian by the Hilbert basis theorem, and a
quotient of a Noetherian ring is Noetherian, because ideals of $A$
correspond to ideals of $k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ containing the kernel,
compatibly with inclusions; so $A$ satisfies the ascending chain
condition on ideals.

*Descending chains of closed sets.* Every closed subset of $X$ is
$V(I)$ for an ideal $I$, and $V(I)=V(\sqrt I)$. For radical ideals
$I,J$ one has $V(I)\subseteq V(J)$ if and only if $J\subseteq I$, since
$\sqrt I$ is the intersection of the primes containing $I$. Thus
$Z\mapsto I(Z)$, the intersection of the primes in $Z$, is an
inclusion-reversing bijection from closed subsets to radical ideals. A
descending chain $Z_1\supseteq Z_2\supseteq\cdots$ of closed sets gives
an ascending chain $I(Z_1)\subseteq I(Z_2)\subseteq\cdots$, which
stabilizes because $A$ is Noetherian; hence so does the chain of closed
sets.

*Finitely many components.* Call a closed subset *good* if it is a
finite union of irreducible closed subsets (the empty set being the
empty union). Suppose some closed subset is not good. By the descending
chain condition the set of such closed subsets has a minimal element
$Z$. Then $Z$ is nonempty and not irreducible, so $Z=Z_1\cup Z_2$ with
$Z_1,Z_2\subsetneq Z$ closed. By minimality $Z_1$ and $Z_2$ are good,
hence so is $Z$, a contradiction. Write
$X=C_1\cup\cdots\cup C_m$ with irreducible closed $C_j$ and discard
every $C_j$ contained in another. If $C$ is any irreducible closed
subset, then $C=\bigcup_j(C\cap C_j)$ forces $C\subseteq C_j$ for some
$j$, because an irreducible space is not a finite union of proper
closed subsets. Hence the maximal irreducible closed subsets, that is
the irreducible components, are exactly the remaining $C_j$, and there
are finitely many of them.

attrs.title: Affine schemes of finite type are Noetherian with finitely many components

objects.body:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and $A$ a finitely generated
commutative $k$-algebra, $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$.

1. Every closed point $x\in X$, i.e. every maximal ideal
   $\mathfrak m_x\subset A$, has residue field $A/\mathfrak m_x=k$;
   thus closed points are the same as $k$-points, i.e. $k$-algebra
   homomorphisms $A\to k$.
2. (Vanishing principle.) If $A$ is reduced, a function $f\in A$ whose
   value $f(x)\in k$ vanishes at every $k$-point $x$ is zero.
3. Consequently, if $\varphi:X\to Y$ is a regular map of affine
   varieties and $Z\subseteq Y$ is a closed subvariety with
   $\varphi(x)\in Z$ for every $k$-point $x$ of $X$, then $\varphi$
   factors uniquely through $Z$.

## Proof

(1) For a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, the field $A/\mathfrak m$ is a
finitely generated $k$-algebra, hence a finite extension of $k$ by
Zariski's lemma. As $k$ is algebraically closed, the structure map
$k\to A/\mathfrak m$ is an isomorphism, so evaluation at $x$ is a
surjection $A\to k$ with kernel $\mathfrak m_x$. Conversely, the kernel
of a $k$-algebra homomorphism $A\to k$ is a maximal ideal, and the two
constructions are mutually inverse.

(2) By (1), $f(x)=0$ means $f\in\mathfrak m_x$. So $f$ lies in every
maximal ideal of $A$. By the Nullstellensatz (in the form: a finitely
generated algebra over a field is a Jacobson ring, so every prime ideal
is an intersection of maximal ideals), the intersection of the maximal
ideals of $A$ equals the intersection of its prime ideals, which is the
nilradical $\sqrt0$. Since $A$ is reduced, $\sqrt0=0$, hence $f=0$.
Equivalently, for any ideal $I\subseteq A$ the functions vanishing on the
$k$-points of $V(I)$ form $\sqrt I$; this is the form
$I(V(I))=\sqrt I$ of the Nullstellensatz.

(3) Write $Z=V(J)$ with $J\subseteq k[Y]$ radical, so that
$k[Z]=k[Y]/J$. For $g\in J$ and a $k$-point $x$ of $X$, one has
$(\varphi^*g)(x)=g(\varphi(x))=0$ because $\varphi(x)\in Z$. The
coordinate algebra $k[X]$ is reduced, so $\varphi^*g=0$ by (2). Thus
$\varphi^*:k[Y]\to k[X]$ kills $J$ and factors through $k[Y]/J$; the
factorization is unique because $k[Y]\to k[Y]/J$ is surjective.

attrs.title: Residue fields of closed points and the vanishing principle

objects.body:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed and let $X,Y$ be affine varieties over
$k$, with reduced finitely generated coordinate algebras $A=k[X]$ and
$B=k[Y]$. Then $A\otimes_kB$ is a reduced finitely generated
$k$-algebra, so $X\times Y=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_kB)$ is an
affine variety whose $k$-points are the pairs $(x,y)$ of $k$-points.
In particular the vanishing principle of
[lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing] applies to it: a regular
function on $X\times Y$ vanishing at all $k$-points $(x,y)$ is zero.
Thus an identity between regular maps defined on $X\times Y$ (such as a
commutator map) may be checked on $k$-points, one variable at a time.

## Proof

The algebra $A\otimes_kB$ is generated by the tensors of generators of
$A$ and of $B$, so it is finitely generated. A $k$-algebra homomorphism
$A\otimes_kB\to k$ is the same as a pair of $k$-algebra homomorphisms
$A\to k$, $B\to k$, so by part (1) of
[lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing] the $k$-points of $X\times Y$
are the pairs $(x,y)$, and the value of $a\otimes b$ at $(x,y)$ is
$a(x)b(y)$.

Let $0\neq t\in A\otimes_kB$. Write $t=\sum_{i=1}^ra_i\otimes b_i$ with
$b_1,\ldots,b_r$ linearly independent over $k$; then some $a_i\neq0$.
By the vanishing principle for the reduced algebra $A$ there is a
$k$-point $x$ with $a_i(x)\neq0$. Applying evaluation at $x$ in the first
factor gives $\sum_ia_i(x)b_i\in B$, which is nonzero by linear
independence. By the vanishing principle for $B$ there is a $k$-point
$y$ where it does not vanish, i.e.
$t(x,y)=\sum_ia_i(x)b_i(y)\neq0$.

So a nonzero element of $A\otimes_kB$ has a nonzero value at some
$k$-point. If $t$ were nilpotent, $t^n=0$, then $t(x,y)^n=0$ in the
field $k$ for all $(x,y)$, so $t$ would vanish at every $k$-point and
hence $t=0$. Thus $A\otimes_kB$ is reduced, and the argument just given
is precisely the vanishing principle on $X\times Y$. For the last
sentence: two regular maps $\varphi,\psi:X\times Y\to Z$ into an affine
variety agree if $\varphi^*g-\psi^*g$ vanishes at all $k$-points for
every $g\in k[Z]$, that is, if $\varphi(x,y)=\psi(x,y)$ for all
$k$-points; and this may be checked by fixing $x$ and varying $y$, then
varying $x$.

attrs.title: Products of reduced affine varieties are reduced

objects.body:
For a closed algebraic subgroup $H\subseteq\operatorname{GL}(V)$,
the identity component $H^\circ$ is a closed, open, normal subgroup.
The connected components are exactly the pairwise disjoint cosets
$hH^\circ$. There are finitely many of them, and multiplication of
cosets makes

$$
\pi_0(H)=H/H^\circ
$$

a finite group.

## Proof

A finite-type algebraic variety has finitely many irreducible
components ([lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components]). Every connected component is a union of irreducible
components: if an irreducible component meets a connected component,
their union is connected, so maximality of the connected component
contains that irreducible component. Hence there are finitely many
connected components. Each is closed, and its complement, being a
finite union of the other closed components, is closed; thus each
component is also open.

The image of the connected space
$H^\circ\times H^\circ$ under multiplication is connected and
contains the identity. By the definition of $H^\circ$ in
[def-wf-algebraic-components], that image lies in $H^\circ$.
The image of $H^\circ$ under inversion is connected and contains
the identity as well, so it too lies in $H^\circ$. Therefore
$H^\circ$ is a subgroup. Conjugation by any $h\in H$ is a
homeomorphism fixing the identity, so it preserves $H^\circ$;
thus this subgroup is normal.

Translation by $h$ is a homeomorphism and carries $H^\circ$
onto a connected open-and-closed subset containing $h$. It is
therefore exactly the connected component of $h$. The components
are consequently the disjoint cosets $hH^\circ$. Normality makes
coset multiplication well defined, and the already proved finiteness
of the component set makes $H/H^\circ$ a finite group.

attrs.title: Identity component, cosets, and the finite component group

objects.body:
In the situation of [def-wf-arithmetic-monodromy-extension], the
multiplication $(h,m)(h',n)=(h\alpha^m(h'),m+n)$ makes
$G_{\mathrm{arith}}(\rho)$ a group with identity $(1,0)$ and inverses
$(h,m)^{-1}=(\alpha^{-m}(h^{-1}),-m)$, and the degree map $\deg_G$
of [def-wf-arithmetic-monodromy-extension] is a surjective group
homomorphism with kernel $H_{\mathrm{geom}}\times\{0\}$, where
$H_{\mathrm{geom}}$ is the geometric monodromy group of
[def-wf-geometric-monodromy-group].

## Proof

By [lem-wf-conjugation-geometric-monodromy], $\alpha$ is an
automorphism of the group $H_{\mathrm{geom}}$ of
[def-wf-geometric-monodromy-group], so each power $\alpha^m$ is a
group automorphism and $\alpha^{m+n}=\alpha^m\circ\alpha^n$. The
displayed product is therefore associative:

$$
(h,m)\bigl((h',n)(h'',p)\bigr)
=(h\alpha^m(h')\alpha^{m+n}(h''),m+n+p)
=\bigl((h,m)(h',n)\bigr)(h'',p).
$$

The element $(1,0)$ is a two-sided identity because
$\alpha^m(1)=1$, and the displayed formula for $(h,m)^{-1}$ is a
two-sided inverse because $\alpha^{-m}(\alpha^m(h'))=h'$. Finally
$\deg_G\bigl((h,m)(h',n)\bigr)=m+n =\deg_G(h,m)+\deg_G(h',n)$, so $\deg_G$ is a homomorphism; it is
surjective since $\deg_G(1,m)=m$, and its kernel is the set of pairs
$(h,0)$, namely $H_{\mathrm{geom}}\times\{0\}$, as in
[def-wf-arithmetic-monodromy-extension].

attrs.title: The arithmetic monodromy extension is a group

objects.body:
Let $X_0$ be a curve over $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ in the sense of
[d-real-setup] (smooth, separated, geometrically connected; it need
not be affine, e.g. it may be proper), let $j:U_0\hookrightarrow X_0$ be a dense open
immersion with finite complement $S_0$, and let $\mathcal F$ be a
lisse Weil sheaf of rank $r\ge1$ on $U_0$. Assume that for every
closed point $x\in|U_0|$ and every eigenvalue $\alpha$ of the local
Frobenius $F_x$ on $\mathcal F_{\bar x}$ the inequality

$$
|\iota(\alpha)|^2\le q_x^{\beta}
$$

holds for a real number $\beta$ (i.e. $\mathcal F$ is punctually
$\iota$-mixed of weights at most $\beta$ in the punctual weight
convention of [def-weil-punctual-weights]). Then the same
inequality holds at every boundary point: for every $s\in S_0$ and
every eigenvalue $\alpha$ of $F_s$ on the middle-extension stalk
$(j_*\mathcal F)_{\bar s}$ of
[def-wf-middle-extension],

$$
|\iota(\alpha)|^2\le q_s^{\beta}.
$$

Since $j_*\mathcal F$ restricts to $\mathcal F$ on $U_0$, this says
that $j_*\mathcal F$ has punctual weights at most $\beta$ on all of
$X_0$.

## Proof

Step 0 (reduction to an affine curve). Fix $s\in S_0$. Since $X_0$
is of finite type over $k_0$, the point $s$ has an affine open
neighbourhood $X'_0\subseteq X_0$. The scheme $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$
is smooth and connected, hence irreducible (a connected noetherian
normal scheme is integral), so the nonempty open
$X'=X'_0\times_{k_0}k$ is irreducible, in particular connected; thus
$X'_0$ is a smooth geometrically connected affine curve. Put
$U'_0=U_0\cap X'_0$, a dense open of $X'_0$ with finite complement
$S'_0=S_0\cap X'_0\ni s$, with inclusion $j':U'_0\hookrightarrow X'_0$.
The restriction $\mathcal F|_{U'_0}$ is lisse of rank $r$ and
satisfies the hypothesis at every closed point of $U'_0\subseteq U_0$.
Formation of the direct image along an open immersion commutes with
restriction to an open: for $V\to X'_0$ étale, sections of
$(j_*\mathcal F)|_{X'_0}$ and of $j'_*(\mathcal F|_{U'_0})$ over $V$
are both the sections of $\mathcal F$ over
$V\times_{X_0}U_0=V\times_{X'_0}U'_0$. Hence
$(j_*\mathcal F)|_{X'_0}=j'_*(\mathcal F|_{U'_0})$ as Weil sheaves, and
the stalks at $\bar s$ agree together with their Frobenius $F_s$
(equivalently, both are $\mathcal F_{\bar\eta}^{I_s}$ by
[lem-wf-boundary-stalk-invariants], and $I_s$ depends only on the
henselization at $s$). So the bound at $s$ follows from the affine
case applied to $j'$. From now on we assume $X_0$ affine.

Step 1 (the pole-free region of the open part). Let
$L(U,t):=\prod_{x\in|U_0|}\det(1-F_xt^{d(x)},\mathcal F_{\bar x})^{-1}$
be the open-part $L$-series of [d-real-cohom]. In the punctual weight convention of
[def-weil-punctual-weights], its logarithmic derivative has the
coefficient series

$$
c_m:=\sum_{d\mid m}d\sum_{\substack{x\in|U_0|\\d(x)=d}}
\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(F_x^{m/d}\mid\mathcal F_{\bar x}\bigr),
$$

and by the hypothesis the summands have modulus at most
$r q^{m\beta/2}$ (an eigenvalue of $F_x^{m/d}$ has $\iota$-modulus
$q_x^{\beta/2}$ to the power $m/d$, i.e. $q^{m\beta/2}$). Since
the points over $k_m$ regroup as
$\#U_0(k_m)=\sum_{d\mid m}d\cdot\#\{x\in|U_0|:d(x)=d\}$, the estimate
of [lem-wf-point-count-linear-growth], applied over all base
extensions $k_n$, gives $|c_m|\le r\,d\,q^{m(\beta/2+1)}$ for a
constant $d$. Hence the series $\sum_m c_m t^{m-1}$ converges for
$|t|<R$ with $R:=q^{-\beta/2-1}$, the power series
$\log L(U,t)=\sum_m c_m t^m/m$ converges there, and
$L(U,t)=\exp(\log L(U,t))$ is holomorphic and nonzero on
$|t|<R$.

Step 2 (the poles of the graded form). By
[lem-wf-euler-product-middle-extension] the full $L$-series
$L(X,t):=\prod_{x\in|X_0|}\det(1-F_xt^{d(x)},(j_*\mathcal F)_{\bar x})^{-1}$
equals $\det(1-Ft,H_c^1)/\det(1-Ft,H_c^2)$ with $H_c^i$ the
compact-support cohomology of the middle extension
$j_*\mathcal F$ of [def-wf-middle-extension] in the convention of
[def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] on $X_0$. The
$H_c^2$-factor: the boundary corrections at $S$ are concentrated in
degree zero (the recollement triangle
$j_!\mathcal F\to j_*\mathcal F\to i_*i^*j_*\mathcal F\to$ of [prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages], with
$H_c^i(X,i_*B)=0$ for $i\ge1$ on the zero-dimensional
$B$), so $H_c^2(X,j_*\mathcal F)\cong H_c^2(U,\mathcal F)$, and
[lem-a1-affine-hc2] describes
$H_c^2(U,\mathcal F)$ as the coinvariants $V_{\pi_1(U)}(-1)$ of the
local geometric generic stalk $V=\mathcal F_{\bar\eta}$ twisted by
$(-1)$. The quotient $Q=V_{\pi_1(U)}$ is a Weil subquotient on
which the geometric fundamental group acts trivially. Thus a closed
point Frobenius of degree $d(x)$ acts on $Q$ as the $d(x)$-th
power of its degree-one operator. For every eigenvalue $\lambda$
of that operator, $\lambda^{d(x)}$ is therefore a closed-point
eigenvalue of this quotient, and hence of the original sheaf.
The hypothesis gives $|\iota(\lambda)|\le q^{\beta/2}$.
This argument concerns only the geometrically constant quotient;
it makes no assertion about an arbitrary Frobenius lift on $V$.
Hence an eigenvalue $\alpha$ of the
global $F$ on $H_c^2(X,j_*\mathcal F)$ satisfies
$|\iota(\alpha)|\le q^{\beta/2+1}$, i.e. the roots of the
denominator polynomial, the inverses $\alpha^{-1}$, lie outside the
disc $|t|<R$. The numerator is a polynomial and the rational function
is therefore holomorphic on $|t|<R$.

Step 3 (each boundary factor is pole-free). The identity of
[lem-wf-euler-product-middle-extension] reads
$L(X,t)=L(U,t)\cdot\prod_{s\in S_0}B_s(t)$ with
$B_s(t):=\det(1-F_st^{d(s)},(j_*\mathcal F)_{\bar s})^{-1}$; by
Steps 1–2 the left-hand side is holomorphic and $L(U,t)$ is
holomorphic and nonzero on $|t|<R$, so the finite product
$\prod_s B_s(t)$ has a pole at no point of the disc. A pole of the
product at $t_0$ is a pole of one of the factors, so every
$B_s$ is holomorphic on the disc: no root of
$\det(1-F_st^{d(s)},(j_*\mathcal F)_{\bar s})$ lies in $|t|<R$.
For an eigenvalue $\alpha$ of $F_s$ on the boundary stalk, the
number $t_0$ with $t_0^{d(s)}=\alpha^{-1}$ is such a root, whence
$|\iota(\alpha)|^{-1}\ge q^{-d(s)(\beta/2+1)}$, i.e.

$$
|\iota(\alpha)|^2\le q^{d(s)(\beta+2)}=q_s^{\beta+2}.
$$

Step 4 (sharpening by tensor powers). Apply Steps 1–3 to the $k$-fold
tensor power $\mathcal F^{\otimes k}$, lisse of rank $r^k$ on
$U$, whose punctual bounds are $q_x^{k\beta}$. For an eigenvalue
$\alpha$ of $F_s$ on $(j_*\mathcal F)_{\bar s} =\mathcal F_{\bar\eta}^{I_s}$ (the boundary stalk description
[lem-wf-boundary-stalk-invariants]), choose an eigenvector
$v\in\mathcal F_{\bar\eta}^{I_s}$; then $v^{\otimes k}$ is an
$I_s$-invariant eigenvector of $F_s$ on
$\mathcal F_{\bar\eta}^{\otimes k}$ with eigenvalue $\alpha^k$ (an instance of [p-linear-spectra]), so
$\alpha^k$ is an eigenvalue of $F_s$ on the boundary stalk of
$\mathcal F^{\otimes k}$ and the $\beta+2$ bound of Step 3 for that
sheaf gives
$|\iota(\alpha)|^{2k}\le q_s^{k\beta+2}$, hence
$|\iota(\alpha)|^2\le q_s^{\beta+2/k}$. Letting $k\to\infty$
gives the asserted bound.

attrs.title: Boundary semicontinuity of weights on a curve

objects.body:
Let $j:U_0\hookrightarrow C_0$ be a dense open immersion of smooth
curves over $k_0$, let $\mathcal F$ be lisse on $U_0$, and let
$x\in C_0\setminus U_0$ be a closed boundary point with local residue
field $\kappa(x)$ and inertia group $I_x$ of [d-real-boundary] inside the local
fundamental group of the
fundamental representation.
Then the boundary stalk of the
middle extension is

$$
(j_*\mathcal F)_{\bar x}\simeq\mathcal F_{\bar\eta}^{I_x},
$$

where $\mathcal F_{\bar\eta}$ is the
geometric generic stalk of
$\mathcal F$ at $x$ and the invariants are formed for the inertia
action. The identification is equivariant for Frobenius: the geometric
Frobenius of $\kappa(x)$ acting on the stalk of the Weil sheaf
$j_*\mathcal F$ at $\bar x$ corresponds to the action of a residue
Frobenius lift on $\mathcal F_{\bar\eta}^{I_x}$ of [d-real-boundary]
(which is independent of the lift).

## Proof

The strict-henselization stalk formula of
[prop-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-stalk-formula] is a statement about
torsion sheaves, and a lisse $\Qlb$-sheaf is in general not trivialized
by any finite etale cover (the unipotent Kummer extension on
$\mathbf G_m$ has infinite geometric monodromy), so the formula is
applied at the finite levels $\mathcal F_n$ of an $\mathcal O_E$-model
of $\mathcal F$, which are locally constant sheaves of finite
$\mathcal O_E/\mathfrak m_E^n$-modules. For each $n$ the stalk of
$j_*\mathcal F_n$ at the geometric point $\bar x$ is computed on the
punctured strict henselian trait
$\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{C_0,\bar x}\setminus\{x\}$,
the spectrum of a field with absolute Galois group the inertia group
$I_x=\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\kappa(\eta_x)}/\kappa(\eta_x))$: the
sections of the locally constant sheaf $\mathcal F_n$ over it are the
invariants $M_n^{I_x}$ of the finite-level geometric generic stalk
$M_n$. The geometric stalk of the adic sheaf $j_*\mathcal F$ (in the
sense of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], formed levelwise) is
$(\varprojlim_nM_n^{I_x})\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$. Invariants commute
with inverse limits, so $\varprojlim_nM_n^{I_x}=M^{I_x}$ for the lattice
$M=\varprojlim_nM_n$ of $\mathcal F_{\bar\eta}$, and
$M^{I_x}=M\cap\mathcal F_{\bar\eta}^{I_x}$ is saturated in $M$, so
$M^{I_x}\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E=\mathcal F_{\bar\eta}^{I_x}$; the tower
$(M_n^{I_x})_n$ need not be adic, but only its limit enters. This is the
displayed identification.

For the Frobenius equivariance, let $D_x=\operatorname{Gal}(\overline K_x/K_x)$
be the decomposition group of [d-real-boundary], $K_x$ the fraction
field of the henselization $\mathcal O^{\mathrm h}_{C_0,x}$, so that
$D_x/I_x=\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\kappa(x)}/\kappa(x))$ and
$\overline K_x^{I_x}$ is the fraction field of
$\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{C_0,\bar x}$. The identification above is
the restriction of sections of $\mathcal F$ from the punctured strict
henselian trait to its geometric generic point, which is natural in
automorphisms of $\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{C_0,\bar x}$ over
$\mathcal O^{\mathrm h}_{C_0,x}$. An element $\sigma\in D_x$ induces
such an automorphism, acting on $(j_*\mathcal F)_{\bar x}$ through its
image in $\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\kappa(x)}/\kappa(x))$ and on
$\mathcal F_{\bar\eta}$ through the Weil fundamental representation of
[def-wf-fundamental-representation]; naturality says that these actions
correspond on $\mathcal F_{\bar\eta}^{I_x}$. Taking $\sigma$ a lift of
the geometric Frobenius of $\kappa(x)$ (in the local Weil group, so that
the action on $\mathcal F_{\bar\eta}$ is defined for a Weil sheaf) gives
the stated equivariance; two lifts differ by an element of $I_x$, which
acts trivially on the invariants.

Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $\Qlb$, and let
$\mathfrak a\subseteq\operatorname{End}(M)$ be a
finite-dimensional Lie algebra. If

$$
\operatorname{tr}(XY)=0
\quad\text{for all }X\in[\mathfrak a,\mathfrak a]
\text{ and }Y\in\mathfrak a,
$$

then $\mathfrak a$ is solvable.

## Proof

Let $\mathfrak d=[\mathfrak a,\mathfrak a]$. We first show that
every $X\in\mathfrak d$ is nilpotent. Write the ordinary Jordan
decomposition of the matrix $X$ as $X=S+N$, where $S$ is
diagonalizable, $N$ is nilpotent, and $SN=NS$. In a basis which
diagonalizes $S$, the operator
$\operatorname{ad}X:Y\mapsto XY-YX$ on $\operatorname{End}(M)$
has Jordan decomposition
$\operatorname{ad}S+\operatorname{ad}N$: the first summand is
diagonalizable, the second nilpotent, and they commute. For each
eigenvalue $\delta$ of $\operatorname{ad}X$, let $e_\delta$ be
the size of its largest Jordan block. Hermite interpolation gives a
polynomial $P$ such that

$$
P(t)\equiv0\pmod{t^{e_0}},\qquad
P(t)\equiv\delta\pmod{(t-\delta)^{e_\delta}}
\quad(\delta\ne0).
$$

Here $e_0$ is the size of the largest Jordan block for the zero
eigenvalue. On the generalized zero-eigenspace this polynomial kills
the whole nilpotent block, while on a generalized
$\delta$-eigenspace with $\delta\ne0$ it retains the scalar
$\delta$ and kills its nilpotent part; hence
$\operatorname{ad}S=P(\operatorname{ad}X)$. Since $\mathfrak d$ is
an ideal of $\mathfrak a$, $\operatorname{ad}X$ carries
$\mathfrak a$ into $\mathfrak d$, and hence
$[S,\mathfrak a]\subseteq\mathfrak d$. The same calculation with
commutators shows that $\operatorname{ad}S$ preserves $\mathfrak d$.

Let $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_N$ be the eigenvalues of $S$, with
algebraic multiplicity, and let $E$ be their finite-dimensional
$\mathbf Q$-linear span. For a $\mathbf Q$-linear map
$f:E\to\Qlb$, define $Z_f$ to act by $f(\lambda)$ on the
$\lambda$-eigenspace of $S$. Choose a polynomial $R_f$ satisfying

$$
R_f(\lambda_i-\lambda_j)=f(\lambda_i-\lambda_j)
\quad\text{for all }i,j,\qquad R_f(0)=0.
$$

This is ordinary interpolation on the finite set of differences (the
value at $0$ is already $f(0)=0$). On
$\operatorname{Hom}(M_{\lambda_i},M_{\lambda_j})$, both sides have
the same scalar action, so
$\operatorname{ad}Z_f=R_f(\operatorname{ad}S)$. Thus
$[Z_f,\mathfrak a]\subseteq\mathfrak d$.

Write $X=\sum_j[A_j,B_j]$. Cyclicity of trace and the preceding
containment give

$$
\operatorname{tr}(XZ_f)
=\sum_j\operatorname{tr}([Z_f,A_j]B_j)=0.
$$

Because $N$ preserves every $S$-eigenspace and is nilpotent there,
$\operatorname{tr}(NZ_f)=0$; hence

$$
\sum_{i=1}^N f(\lambda_i)\lambda_i
=\operatorname{tr}(SZ_f)=0. \tag{*}
$$

Choose a $\mathbf Q$-basis $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ of $E$, write
$\lambda_i=\sum_j a_{ij}e_j$ with $a_{ij}\in\mathbf Q$, and put
$f_j(e_k)=\delta_{jk}$. Comparing the coefficient of $e_j$ in
$(*)$ for $f=f_j$ gives $\sum_i a_{ij}^2=0$. A sum of squares
of rational numbers is zero only when every summand is zero. Thus all
$\lambda_i$ vanish and $X$ is nilpotent. Hence every element of
$\mathfrak d$ is nilpotent; by [lem-wf-engel-matrix],
$\mathfrak d$ is nilpotent and hence solvable. The quotient
$\mathfrak a/\mathfrak d$ is abelian. Appending the derived series
of $\mathfrak d$ to the first step
$\mathfrak a\supseteq\mathfrak d$ therefore gives a terminating
derived series for $\mathfrak a$, so $\mathfrak a$ is solvable.

Let $U_0/k_0$ be as in
[def-wf-weil-group], put
$\Pi=\pi_1(U_0\times_{k_0}\overline{k}_0,\bar u)$, and let
$\chi:W(U_0,\bar u)\to E^\times$
be continuous, where $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite. Choose
$s\in W(U_0,\bar u)$ with $\deg(s)=1$. There are integers
$N,r\geq1$ for which

$$
\lambda:\Pi\longrightarrow E,
\qquad
\lambda(g)=\log(\chi(g)^N),
$$

is a continuous additive character and satisfies

$$
\lambda(sgs^{-1})=\lambda(g)=\lambda(s^{-1}gs)
\qquad(g\in\Pi).
$$

## Proof

The exact sequence of [def-wf-weil-group] makes $\Pi$ a profinite,
hence compact, group, since $\Pi$ is the kernel of the degree map by
[lem-wf-weil-group-exact-sequence]. Therefore
$B=\chi(\Pi)$ is a compact subgroup of
$E^\times$. The normalized valuation
$v_E:E^\times\to\mathbf Z$ is continuous and $\mathbf Z$ is discrete,
so $v_E(B)$ is a finite subgroup of the torsion-free additive group
$\mathbf Z$. Hence $v_E(B)=0$ and
$B\subseteq\mathcal O_E^\times$.

Choose $r$ and $N$ from
[lem-wf-deep-principal-unit-log]. Then
$\chi(g)^N\in1+\mathfrak m_E^r$ for every $g\in\Pi$, so $\lambda$
is defined and continuous. Since the target of $\chi$ is abelian and
the logarithm is a homomorphism on the chosen principal-unit group,

$$
\lambda(gh)=\log(\chi(g)^N\chi(h)^N)
=\lambda(g)+\lambda(h).
$$

Moreover

$$
\chi(sgs^{-1})=\chi(s)\chi(g)\chi(s)^{-1}=\chi(g),
$$

which gives the first invariance identity. Replacing $g$ by
$s^{-1}gs$ gives the second one.

attrs.title: A multiplicative curve character produces an invariant additive character

objects.body:
Let $X_0$ be a smooth geometrically connected affine curve over
$k_0=\mathbf F_q$ (the separated finite-type conventions of
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]), let $\mathcal F$ be a lisse
Weil sheaf in the coefficient category of
[def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], and let
$\bar{\mathcal F}$ be the sheaf of the complex-conjugate
($\iota$-conjugate) local Frobenius eigenvalues. Then for every
$y\in X_0(k_m)$,

$$
\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(F_y\mid
(\mathcal F\otimes\bar{\mathcal F})_{\bar y}\bigr)
=
\bigl|\iota\operatorname{Tr}(F_y\mid\mathcal F_{\bar y})\bigr|^2
\in\mathbf R_{\ge0},
$$

and consequently the $L^2$-series of the trace function,

$$
\varphi_{\mathcal F}(t):=\sum_{m\ge1}\Bigl(\sum_{y\in X_0(k_m)}
\bigl|\iota\operatorname{Tr}(F_y\mid\mathcal F_{\bar y})\bigr|^2\Bigr)t^{m-1},
$$

is the logarithmic derivative $L'/L$ of the $L$-series

$$
L(t):=L(X_0,\mathcal F\otimes\bar{\mathcal F},t)
=\prod_{x\in|X_0|}
\det\bigl(1-F_xt^{d(x)},(\mathcal F\otimes\bar{\mathcal F})_{\bar x}\bigr)^{-1},
$$

the factorization being the Euler-product form of the
Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula on the affine curve.

## Proof

At a closed point $x$ the eigenvalue multiset of
$\mathcal F\otimes\bar{\mathcal F}$ in the coefficient category of
[def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] at $\bar x$ is the set of
products $\alpha_i\bar\alpha_j$ of the $\iota$-images of the
eigenvalues of $F_x$ on $\mathcal F_{\bar x}$, hence at a point
$y\in X_0(k_m)$ the trace of the tensor is
$\sum_i|\iota(\alpha_i^m)|^2=|\iota\operatorname{Tr}(F_y)|^2\ge0$.
The regrouping of the closed points over the $k_m$-points therefore
gives the logarithmic derivative of the Euler product: the coefficient
of $t^{m-1}$ in $L'/L$ is
$\sum_{y\in X_0(k_m)}\operatorname{Tr}(F_y\mid(\mathcal F\otimes\bar{\mathcal F})_{\bar y})$,
