$\mathbf F_q\subseteq\mathbf F_{q^m}$, and descending it along the finite
Galois action. Consequently the induced arithmetic fundamental group is
the inverse image of
$\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathbf F}_q/\mathbf F_{q^m})$ inside the
arithmetic fundamental group of $X_0$. The geometric kernel is unchanged,
because both geometric fibres equal $X$.

The geometric Frobenius over $\mathbf F_{q^m}$ is the $m$-th power of
the geometric Frobenius over $\mathbf F_q$, by the convention of
[def-tw-frobenius-action]. Taking the inverse image of the cyclic
group it generates in the exact sequence of [def-wf-weil-group],
whose degree-zero part is the geometric subgroup $\pi_1(X)$ by
[lem-wf-weil-group-exact-sequence], therefore gives exactly
$\deg^{-1}(m\mathbf Z)$. Dividing the old degree by $m$ sends this
Frobenius, and hence $s^m$, to one, which proves the normalized-degree
formula.

attrs.title: Weil group after a finite constant-field extension

objects.body:
Let $X_0$ be a geometrically connected separated finite-type
$k_0$-scheme with $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $\Phi_X$ be the
geometric Frobenius of [def-tw-frobenius-action]. For the Weil
group
$W(X_0)=\pi_1(X_0,\bar x)\times_{\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)} \langle\Phi_X\rangle$ of [def-wf-fundamental-representation] and
its degree map $\deg$ of
[def-wf-weil-group], the map $\deg$ is a surjective group
homomorphism whose kernel is the geometric fundamental group
$\pi_1(X)$, and it sends every lift of $\Phi_X$ to $1$;
equivalently, the sequence

$$
1\longrightarrow\pi_1(X)\longrightarrow W(X_0)
\xrightarrow{\deg}\mathbf Z\longrightarrow0
$$

is exact.

## Proof

By [def-wf-fundamental-representation], $W(X_0)$ is the fibre
product of $\pi_1(X_0,\bar x)\to\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)$ with the
cyclic subgroup $\langle\Phi_X\rangle$ generated by the geometric
Frobenius of [def-tw-frobenius-action]; the second projection,
composed with the isomorphism $\langle\Phi_X\rangle\cong\mathbf Z$ that
sends $\Phi_X$ to $1$, is the degree map of
[def-wf-weil-group], so it is a group homomorphism, it is surjective
(the element $(\Phi_X,\Phi_X)$ of the fibre product maps to $1$, and
$\langle\Phi_X\rangle$ is cyclic), and it sends the lifts of $\Phi_X$,
which are the elements of the fibre over $\Phi_X$, to $1$. Its kernel
consists of the pairs $(\gamma,1)$, and $\gamma$ ranges over the
kernel of $\pi_1(X_0,\bar x)\to\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)$, i.e. over
the geometric fundamental group $\pi_1(X)$; the map
$\gamma\mapsto(\gamma,1)$ is injective with this image, which is the
exactness assertion.

Let $\Gamma$ be a subgroup of $\operatorname{GL}(V)$ over
$\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and let $H$ be its Zariski closure
inside $\operatorname{GL}(V)$. Then $H$ is a closed algebraic
subgroup.

## Proof

Let $f$ be a regular function on $\operatorname{GL}(V)$ vanishing
on $\Gamma$. The function $F(g,h)=f(gh)$ is regular on
$\operatorname{GL}(V)\times\operatorname{GL}(V)$. For fixed
$h\in\Gamma$, the function $g\mapsto F(g,h)$ vanishes on
$\Gamma$, since $\Gamma$ is a subgroup, and hence vanishes on $H$
by the definition of Zariski closure. Now fix $g\in H$; the function
$h\mapsto F(g,h)$ vanishes on $\Gamma$, so it vanishes on $H$.
Thus $f(gh)=0$ for all $g,h\in H$, and $HH\subseteq H$.
Likewise $g\mapsto f(g^{-1})$ is regular, vanishes on $\Gamma$,
and therefore vanishes on $H$; hence $H^{-1}\subseteq H$.
The identity belongs to $H$, so $H$ is a subgroup.

attrs.title: Zariski closure of a matrix subgroup

objects.body:
Let $C_0$ be a smooth affine curve and let $\mathcal E$ be lisse and
punctually $\iota$-pure of weight zero. Every nonzero Frobenius
eigenvalue on $H_c^2(C,\mathcal E)$ has weight two.

## Proof

First assume that $C_0$ is geometrically connected. Then
[lem-a1-affine-hc2-pure], applied with $w=0$, shows that
$H_c^2(C,\mathcal E)$ is $\iota$-pure of weight two in
[def-weil-frobenius-module-weights]: every Frobenius eigenvalue on it
has $\iota$-modulus $q$.

For a general smooth affine curve, choose a finite extension
$\mathbf F_{q^e}/\mathbf F_q$ over which all its finitely many
geometric connected components are defined. This is possible because
each open and closed component is specified by an idempotent in its
affine coordinate ring after base change to $\overline{\mathbf F}_q$,
and the finitely many coefficients of these idempotents lie in a
finite extension. Over $\mathbf F_{q^e}$ the curve is a finite
disjoint union of geometrically connected smooth affine curves.
The restricted sheaves remain punctually pure of weight zero:
if a closed point $z$ of the base change maps to $x\in C_0$,
the Frobenius on its stalk is $F_x^{[\kappa(z):\kappa(x)]}$.
Every eigenvalue is therefore a positive integral power of an
eigenvalue of $F_x$, and still has modulus one, as required by
[def-weil-punctual-weights]. Apply the preceding argument to
each component and take the direct sum of their compactly supported
cohomology. Every eigenvalue of $F^e$ on this sum has modulus
$q^e$. If $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $F$, then
$\lambda^e$ is an eigenvalue of $F^e$, so
$\lvert\iota(\lambda)\rvert^e=q^e$, and
$\lvert\iota(\lambda)\rvert=q$. The empty curve has zero
cohomology, so its assertion is vacuous.

attrs.title: Purity of the top affine-curve factor

objects.body:
If $C_0$ is a smooth affine curve and $\mathcal F$ is constructible
in the coefficients of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], then
$H_c^i(C,\mathcal F)=0$ for $i\notin\{0,1,2\}$.

## Proof

Choose a smooth proper completion $j:C\hookrightarrow\overline C$
by [lem-sc-compactification]. At finite coefficient level,

$$
R\Gamma_c(C,\mathcal F_n)
=R\Gamma(\overline C,j_!\mathcal F_n)
$$

by [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. The object
$j_!\mathcal F_n$ is a sheaf in degree zero.
The cohomological-dimension bound
[lem-sc-cohomological-dimension](a), applied to this sheaf,
therefore gives vanishing outside degrees $0,1,2$.

For a constructible integral lattice and its finite reductions,
the groups $H^r(\overline C,j_!\mathcal F_n)$ are finite by
[sbc-thm-finiteness-finite-type] applied to the proper
structure morphism of $\overline C$.
The inverse-limit computation
[prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits] has Milnor exact sequence

$$
0\longrightarrow\varprojlim\nolimits^1
H^{r-1}(\overline C,j_!\mathcal F_n)
\longrightarrow H_c^r(C,\mathcal F_{\mathcal O_E})
\longrightarrow\varprojlim H^r(\overline C,j_!\mathcal F_n)
\longrightarrow0.
$$

The first term vanishes by [lem-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler];
thus passage to the integral lattice introduces no degree $3$
term. Rationalizing, and then making the finite scalar extensions
of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], preserves this vanishing and
gives the assertion for $\mathcal F$.
The argument concerns sheaves in degree zero: an arbitrary shift
of such a sheaf would shift the cohomological range.

attrs.title: Cohomological range of an affine curve

objects.body:
A Noetherian scheme $X$ has a finite partition by
locally closed reduced
affine subschemes.

## Proof

Choose a finite affine open cover $U_1,\ldots,U_m$.
Set $S_i=U_i\setminus\bigcup_{j<i}U_j$, with its reduced
closed subscheme structure inside $U_i$.
Each $S_i$ is affine, since it is closed in an affine scheme,
and is locally closed in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Every point belongs
to the piece indexed by the first $U_i$ containing it.
Hence these finitely many pieces are disjoint and cover $X$.

Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $X$ be a smooth
connected affine $k$-scheme of dimension $d\geq2$, let
$T\to X$ be a connected finite etale cover, and let $S\subset X(k)$
be a nonempty finite set. There is a smooth connected closed affine
curve $C\subset X$ containing $S$ such that $T\times_X C$ is
connected. If $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, the curve and its inclusion
are defined over a finite extension of $\mathbf F_q$.

## Proof

We spell out the geometric input. We use the ordinary Bertini lemmas
[Stacks Project, Tag 0FD5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FD5)
(sections vanishing on a prescribed closed subscheme),
[Tag 0FD6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FD6)
(smoothness), and
[Tag 0G4F](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0G4F)
(geometric irreducibility of a linear system).
These are statements about schemes and linear systems, with no weight
or monodromy hypothesis.

Embed $X$ in projective space and let $\overline X$ be its
projective closure. For a sufficiently large $n$, let $V$ be
the space of sections of $\mathcal O_{\overline X}(n)$ vanishing
on the reduced finite subscheme $S$. Tag 0FD5 makes its base locus
on $X$ exactly $S$, and makes its associated map an immersion on
$X\setminus S$. Increasing $n$ if necessary makes

$$
V\longrightarrow\bigoplus_{s\in S}
(\mathfrak m_s/\mathfrak m_s^2)\otimes
\mathcal O_{\overline X}(n)|_s
$$

surjective. Indeed, apply the usual eventual vanishing of coherent
$H^1$ for an ample twist to the ideal of the union of the first
infinitesimal neighborhoods of these finitely many points. Thus
nonzero first derivative at each $s$ is a nonempty open condition
on $V$. Tag 0FD6 on $X\setminus S$, together with these finitely
many derivative conditions, makes a general member smooth everywhere
on $X$.

For completeness, the hypotheses of Tag 0G4F hold both on $X$ and
for the pulled-back linear system on $T$. Both schemes are smooth
and connected over $k$, hence irreducible. The respective base
loci are $S$ and its finite inverse image, of codimension at least
two. Choose $x\in X\setminus S$. Since the linear system induces
an immersion there, choose two sections vanishing at $x$ with
independent differentials, and a third section nonzero at $x$.
The common zero locus of the first two has a codimension-two component
through $x$ not contained in the third divisor. At any point of
$T$ above $x$, etaleness gives the same assertion for the
pulled-back sections. These verify the remaining hypothesis of
Tag 0G4F. A general member therefore cuts both $X$ and $T$
in irreducible subschemes. Intersect the finitely many nonempty open
conditions on the irreducible parameter space $V$, and choose a
$k$-point in their intersection.

The resulting $X_1$ is a smooth connected closed affine subscheme
of dimension $d-1$, contains $S$, and its inverse image $T_1$
is connected and finite etale over it. Repeat this construction until
dimension one. In dimension two the same argument applies, since
the finite base locus still has codimension two. This proves the
claim about $C$. Over $\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ all the finitely
many defining equations and morphisms involve only finitely many
coefficients, so descend to one finite constant-field extension.
Geometric smoothness and connectedness are the properties just proved
after base change to $k$.

attrs.title: Curves through prescribed points preserving a finite cover

objects.body:
Let $K'\to K\to K''\to K'[1]$ be a distinguished triangle in the
constructible $\Qlb$-Weil categories of
[def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]. If $K'$ and $K''$ belong to

$$
D_{\le w}(X_0):=\{K:\Wt_{\iota,\leq w}(K)\}
$$

in the sense of [def-weil-complex-weights], then so does $K$.

## Proof

The long exact sequence of [lem-sp-long-exact-of-triangle] for the
distinguished triangle, read in the cohomology sheaves of
[def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], contains, for every $j$,
the exact sequence

$$
\mathcal H^j(K')\to\mathcal H^j(K)\to\mathcal H^j(K'')\to
\mathcal H^{j+1}(K')\to\cdots .
$$

By [def-weil-complex-weights]-plus-[def-weil-punctual-weights],
$\mathcal H^j(K')$ and $\mathcal H^j(K'')$ are $\iota$-mixed of weights
at most $w+j$. The exact sequence exhibits $\mathcal H^j(K)$ as an
extension of a subobject of $\mathcal H^j(K'')$ by a quotient of
$\mathcal H^j(K')$: the image of $\mathcal H^j(K')\to\mathcal H^j(K)$
is a Weil quotient sheaf of $\mathcal H^j(K')$, and the image of
$\mathcal H^j(K)\to\mathcal H^j(K'')$ is a Weil subsheaf of
$\mathcal H^j(K'')$ (all maps in the long exact sequence are morphisms
of Weil sheaves). By the sheaf-level stability of mixedness under
subsheaves, quotients and extensions,
[lem-a1-mixed-direct-summand] (1) and (2), both are $\iota$-mixed of
weights at most $w+j$, and hence so is $\mathcal H^j(K)$. (The
Frobenius-module bounds [lem-a1-subquotient-extension-bounds],
[lem-a1-extension-bounds] of [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights] are the
stalkwise shadow of this.) Since $j$ was arbitrary, $K\in D_{\le w}(X_0)$,
which is [def-weil-complex-weights].

Every direct summand of an object of $D_{\le w}(X_0)$ again belongs to
$D_{\le w}(X_0)$.

## Proof

If $K=K'\oplus K''$, then
$\mathcal H^j(K)=\mathcal H^j(K')\oplus\mathcal H^j(K'')$ (cohomology
of a direct sum), so each cohomology sheaf of the summand is a direct
summand of a cohomology sheaf of $K$, which is $\iota$-mixed of
weights at most $w+j$ by [def-weil-complex-weights]; by the
mixedness for direct summands of [lem-a1-mixed-direct-summand],
$\mathcal H^j(K')$ is $\iota$-mixed of weights at most $w+j$ in the
sense of [def-weil-punctual-weights], i.e. $K'\in D_{\le w}(X_0)$.

Let $h:X_0\to Z_0$ and $g:Z_0\to Y_0$ be separated finite-type
morphisms of separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes. Suppose the
direct-image weight assertion holds for $h$ and for $g$: for every
real $v$, every $\iota$-mixed Weil sheaf of weights at most $v$ on the
source has its $i$th higher direct image with compact support
$\iota$-mixed of weights at most $v+i$, for every $i$. Then the same
assertion holds for $gh$: if $\mathcal F$ is an $\iota$-mixed Weil
sheaf on $X_0$ of weights at most $w$, then $R^n(gh)_!\mathcal F$ is
$\iota$-mixed of weights at most $w+n$ for every $n$.

## Proof

By [lem-zl-shriek-composition] there is a Frobenius-compatible
isomorphism $R(gh)_!\mathcal F\simeq Rg_!(Rh_!\mathcal F)$. Apply the
hypercohomology spectral sequence of the truncation construction
[def-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-filtrations] to the exact functor $Rg_!$
and the bounded complex $K=Rh_!\mathcal F$, whose cohomology sheaves
are $\mathcal H^b(K)=R^bh_!\mathcal F$. This is the compact-support
Leray spectral sequence

$$
E_2^{a,b}=R^ag_!\bigl(R^bh_!\mathcal F\bigr)
\ \Longrightarrow\ R^{a+b}(gh)_!\mathcal F,
$$

a spectral sequence of Weil sheaves (all maps are Frobenius-compatible,
[def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]), with only finitely many nonzero terms
and a finite abutment filtration
([lemma-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-convergence]).

By the assertion for $h$, the sheaf $R^bh_!\mathcal F$ is $\iota$-mixed
of weights at most $w+b$. By the assertion for $g$, applied with
$v=w+b$, the term $E_2^{a,b}$ is $\iota$-mixed of weights at most
$w+a+b$. Each later page $E_{r+1}^{a,b}$ is a subquotient of
$E_r^{a,b}$, so $E_\infty^{a,b}$ is a subquotient of $E_2^{a,b}$, and
the abutment $R^n(gh)_!\mathcal F$ carries a finite filtration whose
graded pieces are the $E_\infty^{a,b}$ with $a+b=n$; all of these are
constructible Weil sheaves and all maps are maps of Weil sheaves. For
$a+b=n$ the sheaf $E_2^{a,b}$ is $\iota$-mixed of weights at most
$w+n$, so by the sheaf-level stability of mixedness under Weil
subsheaves and quotients, [lem-a1-mixed-direct-summand](1), applied
page by page, so is $E_\infty^{a,b}$. Stability under extensions,
[lem-a1-mixed-direct-summand](2), applied along the finite filtration,
gives the same bound for $R^n(gh)_!\mathcal F$, in the sense of
[def-weil-punctual-weights].

attrs.title: Composition preserves the direct-image weight bound

objects.body:
On every separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, the constant
Weil sheaf $\Qlb$ is
punctually $\iota$-pure of weight zero.

## Proof

At a degree-$n$ closed point, the local Frobenius operator of
[def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] acts on the constant stalk by
identity (the $n$-fold iterate of the geometric Frobenius of
[def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius] fixes the constant section
$1$), whose complex absolute value is $1=q^{n\cdot0/2}=q_y^{0/2}$
as required by [def-weil-punctual-weights].

attrs.title: Weight zero of the constant sheaf

objects.body:
Let $X_0$ be a smooth geometrically connected affine scheme over a
finite field, and let $\mathcal S_1,\ldots,\mathcal S_r$ be lisse
$\Qlb$-Weil sheaves whose geometric restrictions are irreducible.
Given a nonempty finite set of geometric points of $X_0$ over
closed points, if $\dim X_0\geq1$, there is, after a finite
constant-field extension, a smooth geometrically connected affine
curve in $X_0$ through these points on which every
$\mathcal S_j$ remains geometrically irreducible.

## Proof

Use the geometric representations of
[def-wf-fundamental-representation], and choose finite coefficient
fields for them as allowed in [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category].
By [lem-zl-finite-matrix-irreducibility], each has a finite
reduction quotient detecting absolute irreducibility. Intersect
their open normal kernels in $\pi_1(X)$, where
$X=X_0\times\overline{\mathbf F}_q$. The resulting finite quotient
$Q$ corresponds to a connected finite etale Galois cover $T\to X$.
For $\dim X\geq2$, apply
[lem-zl-bertini-finite-cover-curve]. Connectedness of the
restricted $Q$-torsor means that the image of $\pi_1(C)$ acts
transitively on $Q$, hence is all of $Q$. It surjects onto each
chosen reduction quotient. The finite matrix witnesses show that
all the restricted geometric representations remain irreducible.
The curve and inclusion descend to a finite constant extension;
the restrictions inherit their Weil structures over that field.
For dimension one take $C=X$, with its given finite-field model.

Let $(V,F)$ be a Frobenius module, as in
the trace-series definition,
and put $N_n=\Tr(F^n\mid V)$ for every $n\geq1$. Then

$$
\exp\left(\sum_{n\geq1}N_n\frac{T^n}{n}\right)
=\det(1-TF\mid V)^{-1}
\quad\text{in }\Qlb[[T]].
$$

## Proof

By [lem-zl-log-det-identity],

$$
\log\det(1-TF\mid V)=-\sum_{n\geq1}N_n\frac{T^n}{n}.
$$

The exponential of a series in $T\Qlb[[T]]$ lies in
$1+T\Qlb[[T]]$, the determinant has constant coefficient $1$ and
hence a multiplicative inverse in $\Qlb[[T]]$, and on these two sets
the formal exponential and the formal logarithm are mutually inverse
bijections. Exponentiating the displayed identity therefore gives

$$
\exp\left(\sum_{n\geq1}N_n\frac{T^n}{n}\right)
=\exp\bigl(-\log\det(1-TF\mid V)\bigr)
=\det(1-TF\mid V)^{-1}.
$$

attrs.title: Euler-product identity for a Frobenius module

objects.body:
Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite, let $V$ be an $n$-dimensional
$E$-vector space, and let $\rho:\Pi\to\operatorname{GL}_E(V)$
be a continuous representation of a profinite group. Assume that
$V\otimes_E\Qlb$ is irreducible. There exist a stable
$\mathcal O_E$-lattice $L$ and $N\geq1$ such that any subgroup
$\Pi'\subset\Pi$ with the same image as $\Pi$ on
$L/\varpi_E^N L$ still acts absolutely irreducibly on $V$.

## Proof

First recall the elementary matrix-algebra argument behind Burnside's
lemma. If a unital algebra $A\subset\operatorname{End}_k(W)$ acts
irreducibly on a finite-dimensional vector space over an algebraically
closed field, Schur's lemma [lem-wf-schur-scalar] says
$\operatorname{End}_A(W)=k$. For linearly independent
$w_1,\ldots,w_r$, induction on $r$ shows that
$A\to W^r$, $a\mapsto(aw_1,\ldots,aw_r)$, is onto.
For the induction, its image projects onto $W^{r-1}$. The kernel
in the last copy of $W$ is an $A$-submodule, hence is either
$W$ or zero. In the latter case the image is the graph of an
$A$-linear map $W^{r-1}\to W$; Schur's lemma makes that map
$(v_i)\mapsto\sum c_i v_i$. Applying it to the tuple furnished by
$1\in A$ contradicts the independence of the $w_i$.
Taking a basis of $W$ proves $A=\operatorname{End}_k(W)$.

Apply this to the span of $\rho(\Pi)$ after extending scalars from
$E$ to $\Qlb$. The $E$-span already has dimension $n^2$,
so choose $g_1,\ldots,g_{n^2}\in\Pi$ whose matrices form an
$E$-basis of $\operatorname{End}_E(V)$.
Compactness of $\rho(\Pi)$ supplies a stable lattice (as in [p-real-integral]): for an initial
lattice $L_0$, all its translates lie in $\varpi_E^{-a}L_0$
for some $a$; their $\mathcal O_E$-span is a finitely generated
torsion-free module containing $L_0$, and hence is a lattice $L$.
It is stable under the whole group.

Write the matrices in a basis of $L$. The determinant $\Delta$
of their $n^2$ vectorized columns is a nonzero element of
$\mathcal O_E$. Choose $N>v_{\varpi_E}(\Delta)$.
If $\Pi'$ has the same finite reduction image, choose
$h_j\in\Pi'$ with
$\rho(h_j)\equiv\rho(g_j)\pmod{\varpi_E^N}$.
Their column determinant is congruent to $\Delta$ modulo
$\varpi_E^N$, so is nonzero. Thus the $E$-span of
$\rho(\Pi')$ is again the whole matrix algebra. The same is true
after extending scalars to $\Qlb$, which excludes any nonzero
proper invariant subspace. Continuity ensures that the reduction
image is a finite quotient of $\Pi$.

attrs.title: Absolute irreducibility has a finite matrix witness

objects.body:
If $g:Z_0\to Y_0$ is finite and
$K\in D_{\le w}(Z_0)$, then $Rg_*K=Rg_!K$ belongs to
$D_{\le w}(Y_0)$.

## Proof

A finite morphism is proper, so $Rg_!=Rg_*$ by the properness law of
[prop-functor-package], and $g_*$ is exact by
[lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact]; hence
$\mathcal H^j(Rg_*K)=g_*\mathcal H^j(K)$. Fix $j$ and choose a
finite Weil filtration of $\mathcal H^j(K)$ whose nonzero quotients
$\mathcal Q_i$ are punctually pure in the sense of
[def-weil-punctual-weights], of weights $u_i\le w+j$, as
provided by [def-weil-complex-weights]. Exactness pushes this
filtration forward. It remains to check that $g_*\mathcal Q_i$ is
punctually pure of weight $u_i$. Let $y$ be closed and use the finite
stalk formula of [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula]. The geometric
Frobenius permutes the finitely many points $x$ over $y$; on an orbit
of length $f$, its $f$-th power on the corresponding summand is the
local Frobenius $F_x$. If $\mu$ is an eigenvalue on that orbit, then
$\mu^f$ is an eigenvalue of $F_x$. Since $\mathcal Q_i$ is pure,

$$
|\iota(\mu)|^f=|\iota(\mu^f)|
=q_x^{u_i/2}=(q_y^f)^{u_i/2},
$$

so $|\iota(\mu)|=q_y^{u_i/2}$. Thus each $g_*\mathcal Q_i$ is
punctually pure of weight $u_i$, and the pushed-forward filtration makes
$g_*\mathcal H^j(K)$ mixed of weights at most $w+j$. This holds for
every $j$, hence $Rg_*K\in D_{\le w}(Y_0)$ by
[def-weil-complex-weights].

Let $X_0$ be smooth and geometrically connected over a finite field,
and let $\mathcal G$ be a lisse $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf. After a finite
constant extension it has a finite filtration by lisse Weil subsheaves
with geometrically irreducible nonzero quotients.

## Proof

The rank gives finite length for representations of the Weil group
of [def-wf-weil-group]. Treat an irreducible factor $V$ and
write $\Pi=\pi_1(X)$.
Its restriction to this normal subgroup is semisimple by
[lem-mg-normal-restriction-semisimple]. A Frobenius lift permutes
the finitely many geometric isotypic components. Choose $m$ fixing
them all. The subgroup generated by $\Pi$ and $F^m$ is the Weil
group after a degree-$m$ constant extension, by the group calculation
of [lem-wf-weil-group-constant-extension].
Restriction to this finite-index normal subgroup is semisimple by
[lem-wf-finite-index-restriction-semisimple].

Each irreducible summand is geometrically isotypic, of the form
$S\otimes M$, with $\Pi$ acting irreducibly on $S$ and trivially
on $M$. Choose an intertwiner $T$ on $S$ for conjugation by
$F^m$. Schur's lemma [lem-wf-schur-scalar] identifies the
action of $F^m$ with $T\otimes B$ for an invertible operator
$B$ on $M$. The operator $B$ has an eigenline over $\Qlb$;
its tensor product with $S$ is Weil-stable. Irreducibility forces
$\dim M=1$. Thus every such summand is geometrically irreducible.
Taking a common multiple of the extension degrees for the finitely
many original factors and refining their filtration proves the claim.
These subrepresentations are objects of the finite-stage coefficient
category.
Indeed, start with a finite coefficient field defining the original
representation and its Frobenius map, as in
[def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]. Choose bases for the finitely many
subspaces in the resulting filtration. Their finitely many coordinates
belong to one finite extension $E'$ of that field. The subspaces
they span over $E'$ are stable: this can be checked after the faithful
scalar extension $E'\subset\Qlb$, where stability has already been
proved. Their subspace and quotient representations are continuous
for the geometric fundamental group and inherit the $F^m$-action.
Thus they give lisse Weil subsheaves and quotients at the finite stage
$E'$, which also justifies applying the finite matrix witnesses to
these constituents.
This argument concerns the extension $\Pi\rtimes\mathbf Z$ only
and does not use a rank-one weight theorem on $X_0$.

attrs.title: Geometric constituents after a constant extension on any base

objects.body:
Let $(V,F)$ be a Frobenius module, as in
the trace-series definition.
Then, as formal power series in $\Qlb[[T]]$,

$$
\log\det(1-TF\mid V)
=-\sum_{n\geq1}\Tr(F^n\mid V)\frac{T^n}{n}
=-\operatorname{tr}_F(T).
$$

No semisimplicity assumption is imposed on $F$.

## Proof

The field $\Qlb$ is algebraically closed, so by [p-linear-triangular] choose a basis of $V$ in
which the matrix of $F$ is upper triangular; let

$$
\lambda=(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_m),\qquad m=\dim_{\Qlb}V,
$$

be its diagonal entries, i.e. the eigenvalues of $F$ with algebraic
multiplicity. The matrix of $F^n$ is upper triangular with diagonal
$(\lambda_1^n,\ldots,\lambda_m^n)$, so

$$
\Tr(F^n\mid V)=\sum_{j=1}^{m}\lambda_j^n,
$$

and the matrix of $1-TF$ is upper triangular with diagonal
$(1-\lambda_1T,\ldots,1-\lambda_mT)$, so

$$
\det(1-TF\mid V)=\prod_{j=1}^{m}(1-\lambda_jT).
$$

Every factor lies in $1+T\Qlb[[T]]$, where the formal logarithm is a
homomorphism for finite products: for
$A,B\in1+T\Qlb[[T]]$ the derivative of $\log(AB)$ is
$(AB)'/(AB)=A'/A+B'/B$, the derivative of $\log A+\log B$, and both
sides have constant term $0$. For a single factor, the definition of
the formal logarithm gives

$$
\log(1-\lambda T)=-\sum_{n\geq1}\frac{\lambda^nT^n}{n}.
$$

Summing over $j=1,\ldots,m$, interchanging the two finite index ranges,

$$
\log\det(1-TF\mid V)
=-\sum_{n\geq1}\left(\sum_{j=1}^{m}\lambda_j^n\right)\frac{T^n}{n}
=-\sum_{n\geq1}\Tr(F^n\mid V)\frac{T^n}{n},
$$

which is the negative of the trace series of
[def-zl-frobenius-trace-series].

Fix the finite field, coefficient field and embedding $\iota$ of
[def-weil-punctual-weights].
Let $\mathcal G$ be a
constructible
$\Qlb$-Weil sheaf on a
separated finite-type
$k_0$-scheme $Y_0$. Assume that for some $u\in\mathbf R$
it is $\iota$-mixed of weights
at most $u$. Let $v\in\mathbf R$, and suppose that at every
closed point $y$ every eigenvalue $\alpha$ of local Frobenius
on $\mathcal G_{\bar y}$ satisfies
$|\iota(\alpha)|\leq q_y^{v/2}$.
Then $\mathcal G$ is $\iota$-mixed of weights at most $v$.

## Proof

Take a finite filtration by constructible Weil subsheaves supplied
by the mixedness hypothesis in [def-weil-punctual-weights].
Write $\mathcal Q_r$ for its punctually pure quotients and $u_r$
for their weights. Remove zero quotients.

A nonzero $\mathcal Q_r$ has a nonzero stalk on some lisse stratum
of a constructible stratification
([def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]). The locus where the
lisse rank is nonzero contains a nonempty locally closed piece.
It contains a closed geometric point of $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$:
on a nonempty affine open of that piece, take a maximal ideal;
the weak Nullstellensatz gives residue field $k$.
Its coordinates lie in a finite extension of the finite field
$k_0$, so its image $y$ in $Y_0$ is a closed point.
Thus $(\mathcal Q_r)_{\bar y}\neq0$ for some such $y$.

Taking stalks of the filtration is exact and respects local
Frobenius. Choose a basis adapted to it. The Frobenius matrix is
block triangular, so its characteristic polynomial is the product ([p-linear-filtration])
of those on the successive quotients. Each eigenvalue on
$(\mathcal Q_r)_{\bar y}$ is therefore an eigenvalue on
$\mathcal G_{\bar y}$. Choose one; it is nonzero since Frobenius
acts invertibly. Purity and the assumed bound give

$$
q_y^{u_r/2}=|\iota(\alpha)|\leq q_y^{v/2}.
$$

Since $q_y>1$, this implies $u_r\leq v$.
The original finite filtration now has all nonzero quotient weights
at most $v$, which is precisely the required mixedness bound.

attrs.title: Punctual cutoff for an already mixed sheaf

objects.body:
For a separated finite-type morphism $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ of separated
finite-type $k_0$-schemes, say that $f_0$ satisfies the
*direct-image assertion* if, for every $w\in\mathbf R$ and every
constructible Weil sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $X_0$ which is $\iota$-mixed of
weights at most $w$ ([def-weil-punctual-weights]), the sheaf
$R^rf_{0!}\mathcal F$ is $\iota$-mixed of weights at most $w+r$ for
every $r$; say that $f_0$ satisfies the *complex form* of the assertion
if $Rf_{0!}$ carries $D_{\le w}(X_0)$ into $D_{\le w}(Y_0)$ for every
$w$ ([def-weil-complex-weights]).

1. *(Source.)* Let $j_0:U_0\hookrightarrow X_0$ be open with closed
   complement $i_0:Z_0\hookrightarrow X_0$. If the direct-image
   assertion (resp. its complex form) holds for $f_0j_0$ and $f_0i_0$,
   it holds for $f_0$.
1. *(Target.)* Let $j'_0:V_0\hookrightarrow Y_0$ be open with closed
   complement $i'_0:T_0\hookrightarrow Y_0$, and let
   $f_{V}:f_0^{-1}(V_0)\to V_0$, $f_T:f_0^{-1}(T_0)\to T_0$ be the
   restrictions of $f_0$. If the direct-image assertion (resp. its
   complex form) holds for $f_V$ and $f_T$, it holds for $f_0$.
   By induction, the same holds for any finite stratification of $Y_0$
   by locally closed pieces built from successive open–closed
   decompositions.
1. *(Coefficients.)* Fix $f_0$ and $w$, and let
   $0\to\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal F''\to0$ be an exact
   sequence of constructible Weil sheaves on $X_0$. If
   $R^rf_{0!}\mathcal F'$ and $R^rf_{0!}\mathcal F''$ are $\iota$-mixed
   of weights at most $w+r$ for every $r$, so is $R^rf_{0!}\mathcal F$.
   By induction on the length, the same holds for a finite filtration of
   $\mathcal F$ by Weil subsheaves.

## Proof

*Step 0: exact sequences of sheaves.* Let $A\xrightarrow{a}B
\xrightarrow{b}C$ be an exact sequence of constructible Weil sheaves on
$Y_0$ with $A$ and $C$ $\iota$-mixed of weights at most $u$. Then $B$ is
$\iota$-mixed of weights at most $u$. Indeed, put
$B'=\operatorname{im}(a)$, a Weil quotient of $A$, and note that $B/B'$
is a Weil subsheaf of $C$ by exactness. Both are $\iota$-mixed of
weights at most $u$ by [lem-a1-mixed-direct-summand](1), and then so is
the extension $0\to B'\to B\to B/B'\to0$ by
[lem-a1-mixed-direct-summand](2).

*Restriction.* If $h:W_0\hookrightarrow X_0$ is a locally closed
immersion and $\mathcal F$ is mixed of weights at most $w$, then so is
$h^*\mathcal F$: restrict the filtration; a closed point of $W_0$ is a
closed point of $X_0$ with the same residue field, stalk and local
Frobenius. Applied to cohomology sheaves, $h^*$ carries
$D_{\le w}(X_0)$ into $D_{\le w}(W_0)$.

*Part 1.* For a Weil complex $K$ on $X_0$ take the open–closed
recollement triangle $j_{0!}j_0^*K\to K\to i_{0*}i_0^*K\to$ of
[def-weil-open-closed-recollement], which exists and is
Weil-equivariant by [prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages]. Applying
$Rf_{0!}$ and the composition constraint of item (3) of
[prop-functor-package] (with its Weil descent, item (1)) gives the
distinguished triangle

$$
R(f_0j_0)_!\,j_0^*K\longrightarrow Rf_{0!}K\longrightarrow
R(f_0i_0)_!\,i_0^*K\longrightarrow .
$$

Complex form: if $K\in D_{\le w}(X_0)$, then $j_0^*K$ and $i_0^*K$ lie
in $D_{\le w}$ by the restriction remark, so the outer terms lie in
$D_{\le w}(Y_0)$ by hypothesis, and
[lem-zl-complex-extension] gives $Rf_{0!}K\in D_{\le w}(Y_0)$.
Sheaf form: take $K=\mathcal F$ in degree zero. The long exact
sequence of cohomology sheaves ([lem-sp-long-exact-of-triangle])
contains the exact sequence

$$
R^r(f_0j_0)_!\,j_0^*\mathcal F\longrightarrow R^rf_{0!}\mathcal F
\longrightarrow R^r(f_0i_0)_!\,i_0^*\mathcal F
$$

of Weil sheaves. The restrictions $j_0^*\mathcal F$, $i_0^*\mathcal F$
are mixed of weights at most $w$, so the outer terms are mixed of
weights at most $w+r$ by hypothesis, and Step 0 gives the claim for the
middle term.

*Part 2.* By arbitrary base change for compact-support direct images,
item (4) of [prop-functor-package], applied to the Cartesian squares
over $j'_0$ and $i'_0$,

$$
j_0'^{*}Rf_{0!}K\simeq Rf_{V!}\bigl(K|_{f_0^{-1}V_0}\bigr),
\qquad
i_0'^{*}Rf_{0!}K\simeq Rf_{T!}\bigl(K|_{f_0^{-1}T_0}\bigr),
$$

Weil-equivariantly. Complex form: for $K\in D_{\le w}(X_0)$ the
restrictions of $K$ lie in $D_{\le w}$, so the right sides lie in
$D_{\le w}(V_0)$ and $D_{\le w}(T_0)$. Extension by zero $j'_{0!}$ has
the same stalks at points of $V_0$ and zero stalks elsewhere, and
extends filtrations by zero, so
$j'_{0!}j_0'^{*}Rf_{0!}K\in D_{\le w}(Y_0)$; the finite pushforward
bound [lem-zl-finite-pushforward] gives
$i'_{0*}i_0'^{*}Rf_{0!}K\in D_{\le w}(Y_0)$. The target devissage
[lem-zl-open-closed-weight] then gives $Rf_{0!}K\in D_{\le w}(Y_0)$.
Sheaf form: the pullbacks $j_0'^*$, $i_0'^*$ are exact, so taking
$\mathcal H^r$ in the displayed isomorphisms for $K=\mathcal F$ shows
that $G=R^rf_{0!}\mathcal F$ has $j_0'^*G$ and $i_0'^*G$ mixed of weights
at most $w+r$. Applying the same argument to $G$ in degree zero gives
$G[0]\in D_{\le w+r}(Y_0)$, i.e. $G$ is mixed of weights at most $w+r$.
The stratified version follows by induction on the number of
open–closed steps.

*Part 3.* The short exact sequence is a distinguished triangle ([lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles])
$\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal F''\to$; applying the exact functor
$Rf_{0!}$ and taking cohomology sheaves
([lem-sp-long-exact-of-triangle]) gives exact sequences
$R^rf_{0!}\mathcal F'\to R^rf_{0!}\mathcal F\to R^rf_{0!}\mathcal F''$,
and Step 0 applies. For a finite filtration, induct on its length using
the sequences $0\to\mathcal F_{i-1}\to\mathcal F_i\to
\mathcal F_i/\mathcal F_{i-1}\to0$.

attrs.title: Open–closed reduction for the direct-image assertion

objects.body:
Let $K$ be a field, $B\neq0$ a finitely generated commutative
$K$-algebra, and $K[T_1,\ldots,T_d]\to B$ an injective $K$-algebra
homomorphism over which $B$ is a finitely generated module (such a
map exists by [lem-zl-noether-normalization-field]). Then
$d=\dim B$, the Krull dimension of $B$; in particular
$\dim B<\infty$.

In particular, if $B$ has Krull dimension one, there is an injective
$K$-algebra homomorphism $K[T]\to B$ making $B$ a finite
$K[T]$-module. This holds in particular over finite fields $K$, and
applies to the coordinate rings of affine charts of the curves over
$\mathbf F_q$ considered in this part.

## Proof

Put $A=K[T_1,\ldots,T_d]$ and regard $A\subseteq B$. A finite
extension is integral, since each element of $B$ acts on the finite
$A$-module $B$ and satisfies the monic characteristic polynomial of that
action (determinant trick). We show $\dim B=\dim A$ and then
$\dim A=d$.

*Step 1 ($\dim B\le\dim A$; incomparability, [pqf-lem-incomparability]).* Let
$\mathfrak q\subsetneq\mathfrak q'$ be primes of $B$; we claim
$\mathfrak q\cap A\neq\mathfrak q'\cap A$. Suppose both contract to
$\mathfrak p$. Then $A/\mathfrak p\hookrightarrow B/\mathfrak q$ is
injective and integral, $B/\mathfrak q$ is a domain, and
$\mathfrak q'/\mathfrak q$ is a nonzero prime contracting to $0$. Pick
$0\neq b\in\mathfrak q'/\mathfrak q$ and a monic equation
$b^n+a_{n-1}b^{n-1}+\cdots+a_0=0$ over $A/\mathfrak p$ of minimal
degree $n$. Then $a_0\neq0$: otherwise
$b(b^{n-1}+\cdots+a_1)=0$ in the domain $B/\mathfrak q$ with $b\ne0$
gives an equation of smaller degree. But
$a_0=-b(b^{n-1}+\cdots+a_1)\in(\mathfrak q'/\mathfrak q)\cap
(A/\mathfrak p)=0$, a contradiction. Hence a strict chain
$\mathfrak q_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak q_r$ in $B$ contracts
to a strict chain of primes of $A$ of the same length, so
$\dim B\le\dim A$.

*Step 2 ($\dim B\ge\dim A$; lifting chains).* Let
$\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_r$ be a chain of
primes of $A$. By lying over [pqf-lem-lying-over] (the map $A\to B$ is
injective and integral) there is a prime $\mathfrak q_0$ of $B$ over
$\mathfrak p_0$, and by going up [pqf-lem-going-up], inductively, primes
$\mathfrak q_0\subseteq\mathfrak q_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\mathfrak q_r$
with $\mathfrak q_i\cap A=\mathfrak p_i$. These inclusions are strict
because the contractions are distinct. Hence $\dim B\ge\dim A$.

*Step 3 ($\dim A=d$).* The chain
$0\subsetneq(T_1)\subsetneq(T_1,T_2)\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq
(T_1,\ldots,T_d)$ of primes of $A$ shows $\dim A\ge d$. That
$\dim K[T_1,\ldots,T_d]\le d$, hence $=d$, is the standard
computation of the dimension of a polynomial ring over a field (for
instance: a strict chain of primes of a finitely generated domain over
$K$ strictly decreases the transcendence degree of the fraction fields
of the successive quotients, and
$\operatorname{Frac}A=K(T_1,\ldots,T_d)$ has transcendence degree $d$;
see Stacks Project, Commutative Algebra, the section on dimension of
finite type algebras over fields).

Combining the three steps, $\dim B=\dim A=d$. For the final
assertion, apply [lem-zl-noether-normalization-field] to $B$ with
$\dim B=1$: it gives some $K[T_1,\ldots,T_d]\to B$ injective and finite,
and the first part forces $d=1$; put $T=T_1$. This is Stacks Project,
Lemma 10.115.4 ([Tag 00OY](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00OY)),
together with the equality of dimensions along an integral injective
map ([Tag 00OK](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00OK)),
specialized to $\dim B=1$.

attrs.title: The number of Noether coordinates is the Krull dimension

objects.body:
Let $K$ be a field and $B\neq0$ a finitely generated commutative
$K$-algebra. There exist an integer $d\geq0$ and an injective
$K$-algebra homomorphism $K[T_1,\ldots,T_d]\to B$ over which
$B$ is a finitely generated module.
The reference formulation is
[Stacks Project,
Lemma 10.115.4](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00OY).

## Proof

Omitted.

Let $j:U_0\hookrightarrow X_0$ be open with closed complement
$i:Z_0\hookrightarrow X_0$. If the two outer terms
$j_!j^*K$ and $i_*i^*K$ of the localization triangle
$j_!j^*K\to K\to i_*i^*K\to$ belong to $D_{\le w}(X_0)$, then so
does $K$.

## Proof

The localization triangle is the open–closed recollement triangle of
[def-weil-open-closed-recollement], which exists for $\Qlb$-Weil complexes by [prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages]; by hypothesis its two outer
terms lie in $D_{\le w}(X_0)$, so the extension stability of complex
weights [lem-zl-complex-extension] gives $K\in D_{\le w}(X_0)$.
(The closed-immersion term $i_*i^*K$ is a finite-pushforward, hence
has the same weights as $i^*K$ by [lem-zl-finite-pushforward].)

Let $g:Z_0\to Y_0$ be a separated quasi-finite morphism of separated
finite-type $k_0$-schemes.

1. For a $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $Z_0$ (a Weil complex
concentrated in degree $0$) one has $R^ig_!\mathcal F=0$ for $i>0$.
Hence $g_!=\mathcal H^0Rg_!$ is exact on $\Qlb$-Weil sheaves, and
$\mathcal H^j(Rg_!K)=g_!\mathcal H^j(K)$ for every Weil complex $K$
and every $j$.
1. If $K\in D_{\le w}(Z_0)$, then $Rg_!K\in D_{\le w}(Y_0)$.

In particular $g_!$ preserves mixedness and upper weight bounds: if
$\mathcal F$ is a mixed $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf (of weights $\le w$), then so
is $g_!\mathcal F=Rg_!\mathcal F$.

## Proof

Since $Y_0$ is of finite type over a field, it is quasi-compact and
quasi-separated, so Zariski's main theorem in the form of the
quasi-finite factorization [thm-pqf-zmt-factorization] factors $g$
globally as

$$
Z_0\xrightarrow{\ j_0\ }\overline Z_0\xrightarrow{\ \bar g\ }Y_0
$$

with $j_0$ a quasi-compact open immersion and $\bar g$ finite; in
particular $\overline Z_0$ is again a separated finite-type
$k_0$-scheme. The factorization is defined over $k_0$, so it base
changes to $k$ and is compatible with the geometric Frobenius
automorphisms; all functors below therefore carry Weil structures. By
the composition isomorphism and the properness law of
[prop-functor-package] (clause 3), and since a finite morphism is
proper,

$$
Rg_!\simeq R\bar g_!\,j_{0!}\simeq R\bar g_*\,j_{0!}.
$$

*(1).* Extension by zero [def-weil-extension-by-zero] is exact: its
stalk at a geometric point of $Z$ is the stalk of the input, and at a
geometric point of the complement it is $0$. The finite direct image
$\bar g_*$ is exact by [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact], so
$R\bar g_*=\bar g_*$. Both statements hold at every finite coefficient
stage and hence, by the common-stage construction of
[def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], for $\Qlb$-coefficients. Thus for a Weil
sheaf $\mathcal F$ we get $Rg_!\mathcal F\simeq\bar g_*j_{0!}\mathcal F$,
a complex concentrated in degree $0$, i.e. $R^ig_!\mathcal F=0$ for
$i\neq0$. Applying the exact functor $\bar g_*j_{0!}$ termwise gives
$\mathcal H^j(Rg_!K)=\bar g_*j_{0!}\mathcal H^j(K)=g_!\mathcal H^j(K)$.

*(2).* By (1) and the composition isomorphism it suffices to treat the
two pieces. For $j_0$: a closed point of $\overline Z_0$ either lies in
$Z_0$, where $j_{0!}K$ has the same stalk with the same local
Frobenius as $K$, or lies outside, where the stalk is $0$; so each
$\mathcal H^j(j_{0!}K)=j_{0!}\mathcal H^j(K)$ receives, from a
filtration of $\mathcal H^j(K)$ with punctually pure quotients of
weights $\le w+j$ as in [def-weil-complex-weights], the filtration
by the (exact) extensions by zero, whose quotients are again punctually
pure of the same weights. Hence $j_{0!}K\in D_{\le w}(\overline Z_0)$.
For $\bar g$: the finite pushforward bound [lem-zl-finite-pushforward]
gives $R\bar g_*j_{0!}K\in D_{\le w}(Y_0)$.

*In particular.* A mixed Weil sheaf $\mathcal F$ has a finite
filtration with punctually pure quotients; if $w$ is the largest of
their weights, then $\mathcal F\in D_{\le w}(Z_0)$ by
[def-weil-complex-weights]. By (2), $Rg_!\mathcal F\in D_{\le w}(Y_0)$,
and by (1) this complex is the sheaf $g_!\mathcal F$ in degree $0$;
so $g_!\mathcal F$ is mixed of weights $\le w$.

attrs.title: Quasi-finite morphisms: exactness and upper-weight bound

objects.body:
Let $A,B\in1+T\mathbf C[T]$ be coprime. If $A/B\in\mathbf R(T)$, then
$A,B\in\mathbf R[T]$.

## Proof

Complex conjugation gives $A/B=\overline A/\overline B$, hence
$A\overline B=\overline A B$. Unique factorization and coprimality show
that $A$ is a scalar multiple of $\overline A$ and $B$ the same scalar
multiple of $\overline B$. All four constant terms are one, so the
scalar is one. Thus both polynomials are fixed by conjugation.

Fix the coefficient and weight conventions of
[def-weil-punctual-weights]. Let $h:U_0\to Y_0$ be a
smooth separated morphism
between separated finite-type
$k_0$-schemes, with every nonempty geometric fiber a smooth affine curve,
and let $\mathcal F$ be a
lisse
$\Qlb$-Weil sheaf that is
punctually $\iota$-pure of weight
$w$. Then for every $i$ there is a real number $u_i$ such that
$R^ih_!\mathcal F$ is
$\iota$-mixed of weights at most
$u_i$.
The proof follows the reduction in Kiehl–Weissauer I.7, pp. 53–54:
the curve bound separates the two cohomological root radii, and
[thm-zl-real-mixed-by-curves] supplies mixedness on the base by
geometric reduction to the already proved real-sheaf theorem on curves.
No instance of the general direct-image weight theorem is imported.

## Proof

Normalize $\mathcal F$ as in
[def-wf-normalized-real-envelope]: put
$b=\iota^{-1}(q^{-w/2})$,
$\mathcal F^0=\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal B_b$, and
$\mathcal E=\mathcal F^0\oplus(\mathcal F^0)^\vee$.
It is lisse, pure of weight zero and real by
[lem-wf-envelope-real]. The relative factor calculation
[lem-zl-relative-envelope-factor-reality], which uses only the
proved curve estimate, shows that $R^ih_!\mathcal E$ is real for
every $i$. These are constructible sheaves: the finite-level
finiteness theorem [sbc-thm-finiteness-finite-type] supplies the
constructible landing hypotheses in the coefficient passage of
[thm-cbc-qbar].

Apply [thm-zl-real-mixed-by-curves] on $Y_0$, obtaining a
finite mixed filtration of $R^ih_!\mathcal E$.
Additivity makes $R^ih_!\mathcal F^0$ a direct summand, so it is
mixed by [lem-a1-mixed-direct-summand]. The constant-twist
projection formula [lem-wf-constant-twist-cohomology] identifies

$$
R^ih_!\mathcal F
\cong R^ih_!\mathcal F^0\otimes\mathcal B_{b^{-1}}.
$$

Tensoring the finite filtration with this rank-one sheaf is exact.
At a closed point of degree $m$, the twist multiplies each
eigenvalue by $b^{-m}$, of $\iota$-modulus $q^{mw/2}$, by
[def-wf-constant-weil-twist]. Thus every pure quotient of weight
$v$ becomes pure of weight $v+w$, including where its stalk is
zero. This gives the required finite mixed filtration without a
lissity assumption on the direct image. Its finitely many
weights have a maximum $u_i$; for the zero sheaf take any $u_i$.

attrs.title: Mixedness of the direct images over a relative affine curve

objects.body:
Let $h:U_0\to Y_0$ be smooth and separated with every nonempty
geometric fiber a smooth affine curve, and let $\mathcal F$ be lisse
and punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$. Then every Frobenius
eigenvalue on the stalk of $R^ih_!\mathcal F$ at a closed point $y$
of degree $m$ has absolute value at most
$(q^m)^{(w+i)/2}$, i.e. the punctual weight of
$R^ih_!\mathcal F$ at $y$ is at most $w+i$.

## Proof

Compact-support base change [thm-cbc-qbar], applied to the
cartesian square formed by the fiber $U_y\to U_0$ and the point
$y\to Y_0$, identifies the stalk of $R^ih_!\mathcal F$ at a
geometric point over $y$ with
$H_c^i(U_{\bar y},\mathcal F|_{U_{\bar y}})$. The restricted sheaf has
weight $w$ relative to $q^m$ by the rescaling lemma
[lem-tw-punctual-rescaling]. After a finite extension of
$\kappa(y)$, all geometric components of the affine fiber are
defined and geometrically connected. Apply the curve estimate
[thm-a1-curve-upper] (the upper bound on a smooth geometrically
connected curve, with no condition at infinity) to each component.
The direct sum has the same bound, and
[lem-a1-weight-bound-constant-extension] reflects it back to
$\kappa(y)$. This obtains the displayed bound.

attrs.title: Punctual upper bound in a relative affine curve

objects.body:
Let $h:U_0\to Y_0$ be as in [lem-zl-relative-curve-punctual], and
let $\mathcal E$ be lisse, $\iota$-real, and punctually $\iota$-pure
of weight zero. Then every $R^ih_!\mathcal E$ is $\iota$-real.

## Proof

Fix a closed point $y$ of the base. By [thm-cbc-qbar], the
local polynomials of $R^ih_!\mathcal E$ at $y$ are the polynomials
$P_i$ of the compactly supported cohomology of the fiber
$U_{\bar y}$ (the local Frobenius eigenvalues of the stalk). The
group in degree zero vanishes by (the affine-line form of) the
$H_c^0$-vanishing of lisse sheaves on nonproper curves,
[lem-a1-affine-hc0]; the roots of $P_1$ have modulus
at most $q_y^{1/2}$ by [lem-zl-relative-curve-punctual] (weight
zero, $i=1$), while every nonzero root of $P_2$ has modulus $q_y$
by the top-factor purity [lem-zl-affine-curve-hc2-purity].

The trace formula [cor-trf-point-counting] identifies the fiber
$L$-function, i.e. the exponential of the point-count series of the
fiber with coefficients $\mathcal E$, with
$P_1(T)/P_2(T)$ (the cohomological factorization over the finite
field $\kappa(y)$, with $H_c^0=0$): exponentiating the alternating
trace sum degree by degree, the Euler-product identity
[lem-zl-euler-product-identity] turns the exponential of the trace
series of $F$ on $H_c^i$ into $P_i(T)^{-1}$. Its Euler factors have real
coefficients by the $\iota$-reality of $\mathcal E$
([def-wf-iota-real] applied to the restriction to the fiber), so
this quotient lies in $\mathbf R(T)$. The radii are disjoint
($|z|\leq q_y^{1/2}$ for $P_1$, $|z|=q_y$ for the roots of
$P_2$), and [lem-zl-root-radius-separation] therefore makes the
fraction reduced with denominator $P_2$ in the reduced form; now
[lem-zl-real-reduced-factors] gives
$P_1,P_2\in\mathbf R[T]$. This holds for every $y$; degree zero is
trivial ($P_0=1$ by the vanishing), and all other degrees vanish or
are captured by [lem-zl-affine-curve-range]. This proves the
asserted $\iota$-reality.

attrs.title: Reality of relative factors for an envelope

objects.body:
Let $A(T),B(T)\in1+T\mathbf C[T]$. If every reciprocal root of $A$ has
modulus at most $R$ and every reciprocal root of $B$ has modulus exactly
$S>R$, then the modulus-$S$ reciprocal poles of the reduced rational
function $A(T)/B(T)$ are exactly the reciprocal roots of $B$, with
multiplicity.

## Proof

Cancellation in a quotient can occur only between equal roots of its
numerator and its denominator. Equal complex numbers have equal
modulus. Since the two allowed modulus sets are disjoint, no root of
$B$ can be a root of $A$; hence every denominator root survives as a
pole with its original multiplicity.

Suppose that, for a separated finite-type map $f:X_0\to Y_0$, every
mixed Weil sheaf $\mathcal F$ of weights at most $v$ has
$R^af_!\mathcal F$ mixed of weights at most $v+a$, for every $a$.
Then $Rf_!$ carries $D_{\le w}(X_0)$ into $D_{\le w}(Y_0)$.

## Proof

Apply the hypercohomology spectral sequence provided by the truncation
construction of [def-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-filtrations] and the
exact triangulated functor $Rf_!$ of [prop-functor-package]:

$$
E_2^{a,b}=R^af_!\bigl(\mathcal H^b(K)\bigr)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \mathcal H^{a+b}\bigl(Rf_!K\bigr),
$$

with the finite image filtration of
[lemma-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-convergence]. By
[def-weil-complex-weights], each $\mathcal H^b(K)$ is
$\iota$-mixed of weights at most $w+b$; by the hypothesis of the
lemma every $E_2^{a,b}$ is mixed of weights at most $w+a+b$. Every
later page $E_{r+1}^{a,b}$ is a subquotient of $E_r^{a,b}$, and the
abutment $\mathcal H^n(Rf_!K)$ is filtered with graded pieces
$E_\infty^{a,b}$, $a+b=n$; the subquotient and extension bounds of
[lem-a1-subquotient-extension-bounds], [lem-a1-extension-bounds]
(stalkwise, with the
punctual weight convention of
[def-weil-punctual-weights]) show that $\mathcal H^n(Rf_!K)$ is
$\iota$-mixed of weights at most $w+n$, i.e. $Rf_!K\in D_{\le w}(Y_0)$
by [def-weil-complex-weights].

For composable separated finite-type morphisms
$X_0\xrightarrow fY_0\xrightarrow gZ_0$ of separated finite-type
$k_0$-schemes, the exceptional direct images satisfy a functorial
isomorphism $R(gf)_!\simeq Rg_!Rf_!$ compatible with Frobenius.

## Proof

This is the composition constraint in the six-operation formalism,
item (3) of [prop-functor-package] of the framework chapter.

Let $A$ be a domain and $B$ a finitely generated commutative
$A$-algebra. There are $0\neq s\in A$, $d\geq0$, and
coordinates
$t\in B_s^d$ for which $\nu_t$ is
finite.

## Proof

Put $K=\operatorname{Frac}A$ and fix algebra generators
$b_1,\ldots,b_m$ of $B$ over $A$.
If $B\otimes_AK=0$, the equality $1=0$ in the localization
means $s\cdot1=0$ in $B$ for some $0\neq s\in A$.
Then $B_s=0$, a finite $A_s$-module, and $d=0$ works.

Otherwise [lem-zl-noether-normalization-field] supplies
$t_1,\ldots,t_d\in B\otimes_AK$ such that $B\otimes_AK$
is finite over $K[t_1,\ldots,t_d]$.
Each $b_j$ therefore satisfies a monic equation

$$
b_j^{e_j}+\sum_{r<e_j}c_{jr}(t_1,\ldots,t_d)b_j^r=0,
\qquad c_{jr}\in K[T_1,\ldots,T_d].
$$

This uses the elementary determinant argument for an element acting
on a finite module. Choose a nonzero product $s_0\in A$ of
denominators so that all $t_i$ lie in $B_{s_0}$ and every
coefficient of every $c_{jr}$ lies in $A_{s_0}$.
The finitely many displayed equations hold after localization to
$K$; each of their left-hand sides is consequently killed by some
nonzero element of $A$. Enlarge $s_0$ by the product of these
elements, obtaining $s$, so the equations already hold in $B_s$.
Reducing powers with the monic equations shows that the finitely
many monomials

$$
b_1^{r_1}\cdots b_m^{r_m},\qquad 0\leq r_j<e_j,
$$

generate $B_s=A_s[b_1,\ldots,b_m]$ as an
$A_s[t_1,\ldots,t_d]$-module. Thus the map $\nu_t$
of [def-zl-localized-coordinates] is finite.

attrs.title: Spreading affine normalization to a principal open

objects.body:
Two stratifications $(\iota_k\colon Z_k\to X)_{k<n}$ and
$(\kappa_l\colon W_l\to X)_{l<m}$ of a scheme $X$ have a common refinement.

## Proof

Index the pairs $(k,l)$ by $k+nl<nm$. The intersections $X_k\cap X'_l$ are
locally closed (an intersection of two locally closed sets is locally
closed), pairwise disjoint, and cover $X$. Take as scheme on the stratum
$X_k\cap X'_l$ the fibre product $Z_k\times_XW_l$ with the immersion
$Z_k\times_XW_l\to X$; it is an immersion, as a composite of the base
change of $\kappa_l$ with $\iota_k$, and its image is
$\iota_k(\iota_k^{-1}(X'_l))=X_k\cap X'_l$. This stratification refines
both given ones.

Finite direct sums of finite locally constant sheaves are finite locally
constant; the same holds for locally constant sheaves and for finite
sheaves.

## Proof

For two sheaves with trivialising data $(U_i\to X)_i$ and $(V_j\to X)_j$,
the family $(U_i\times_XV_j\to X)_{i,j}$ is an étale cover trivialising
both. Restriction to a localised site is exact and preserves finite direct
sums, and a finite direct sum $M_X\oplus N_X$ of constant sheaves is the
constant sheaf $(M\oplus N)_X$, because sheafification and the constant
presheaf functor are additive. Stalks commute with finite direct sums,
and a finite direct sum of finite sets is finite.

Let $\mathcal A=\mathrm{Mod}_\Lambda$ with $\Lambda$ a finite ring. The
kernel and the cokernel of a morphism between finite locally constant
sheaves, and the middle term of a short exact sequence whose outer terms
are finite locally constant, are finite locally constant. (The kernel and
cokernel statements are formalised, for any ring $\Lambda$; the extension
statement is not.)

## Proof

Restricting to an étale cover trivialising both sheaves
([lemma-constructible-flc-biproduct]), we may assume the morphism is
$\varphi\colon M_X\to N_X$ with $M$, $N$ finite (the stalks of the constant
sheaf $M_X$ are $M$). By [lemma-constructible-hom-constant-locally]
kernel and cokernel are locally constant with finite stalks.

For an extension $0\to M_X\to\mathcal E\to N_X\to0$, again on a
trivialising cover, consider the sheaf $P$ of sections of
$\mathcal E\to N_X$: over $U\to X$ its sections are the morphisms
$s\colon N_U\to\mathcal E|_U$ with $\pi\circ s=\mathrm{id}$. It is a torsor
under the sheaf $\mathcal{H}om(N_X,M_X)=\Hom_\Lambda(N,M)_X$ (two sections
differ by a morphism $N_U\to M_U$, and locally sections exist since the
sequence is locally split in the étale topology: the stalks are finite
modules and a surjection of sheaves is locally surjective on sections).
The group $\Hom_\Lambda(N,M)$ is finite, so by
[lemma-constructible-torsor-trivialises] $P$ has a section over an
étale cover $(U_i\to X)$, and over $U_i$ the sequence splits:
$\mathcal E|_{U_i}\cong M_{U_i}\oplus N_{U_i}=(M\oplus N)_{U_i}$. Hence
$\mathcal E$ is locally constant, with finite stalks $M\oplus N$.

attrs.title: Kernels, cokernels and extensions of finite locally constant sheaves

objects.body:
Let $\mathcal A=\mathrm{Mod}_\Lambda$ with $\Lambda$ a ring, let $M$ be a finite
$\Lambda$-module, let $N$ be a $\Lambda$-module and let $\varphi\colon M_X\to N_X$ be a
morphism of constant sheaves on $\et X$. Then there is an étale cover
$(U_i\to X)_i$ such that $\varphi|_{U_i}$ is induced by a $\Lambda$-linear
map $f_i\colon M\to N$, i.e. equals $(f_i)_{U_i}\colon M_{U_i}\to N_{U_i}$.
Consequently the kernel and the cokernel of $\varphi$ are locally constant,
with restrictions $(\ker f_i)_{U_i}$ and $(\operatorname{coker}f_i)_{U_i}$.

## Proof

By the adjunction between constant sheaves and global sections,
$\Hom(M_X,N_X)=\Hom_\Lambda(M,\Gamma(X,N_X))$. A global section of $N_X$
over $X$ is, on an étale cover, a section of the constant presheaf, that
is, an element of $N$; hence, on an étale cover $(U_i\to X)_i$ obtained by
intersecting the covering sieves for the finitely many sections $\varphi(m)$,
$m\in M$, every $\varphi(m)$ is the constant section $n_{i,m}$ over $U_i$.
Over a nonempty $U_i$ the map $N\to\Gamma(U_i,N_X)$ is injective (a
section of the constant presheaf which becomes zero in the sheafification
vanishes on a covering sieve, whose members are nonempty), so
$m\mapsto n_{i,m}$ is $\Lambda$-linear, giving $f_i\colon M\to N$ with
$\varphi|_{U_i}$ the morphism of constant sheaves induced by $f_i$ (both
morphisms out of the constant sheaf $M_{U_i}$ have the same adjoint
$M\to\Gamma(U_i,N_X)$; here one uses that the restriction of a constant
sheaf to $\et{U_i}$ is the constant sheaf, compatibly with the unit maps).
Empty $U_i$ are discarded from the cover.
Since restriction to $\et{U_i}$ is exact and the constant sheaf functor is
exact (a composite of the exact constant presheaf functor and
sheafification), the kernel and cokernel of $\varphi|_{U_i}$ are the
constant sheaves on $\ker f_i$ and $\operatorname{coker}f_i$.

Let $a\colon Z\to X$ and $b\colon Z'\to X$ be immersions with the same
image. Then $a^*\mathcal F$ is finite locally constant if and only if
$b^*\mathcal F$ is.

## Proof

Let $W=Z\times_XZ'$ with projections $p\colon W\to Z$ and $q\colon W\to Z'$.
The projection $p$ is an immersion, as a base change of $b$, and it is
surjective, its image being $a^{-1}(b(Z'))=a^{-1}(a(Z))=Z$. A surjective
immersion is a surjective closed immersion (an immersion is a closed
immersion into an open subscheme, and surjectivity forces that open to be
everything), hence a universal homeomorphism. The same holds for $q$. Now
$p^*a^*\mathcal F\cong q^*b^*\mathcal F$, both being the pullback along
$a\circ p=b\circ q$, so by
[lemma-constructible-universal-homeomorphism-invariance] applied to
$p$ and to $q$, $a^*\mathcal F$ is finite locally constant if and only if
$p^*a^*\mathcal F$ is, if and only if $q^*b^*\mathcal F$ is, if and only if
$b^*\mathcal F$ is.

If $\mathcal F\cong\mathcal F'$ in $\shv{\et X}$, then $\mathcal F$ is
locally constant (finite, finite locally constant, constructible) if and
only if $\mathcal F'$ is.

## Proof

An isomorphism of sheaves induces isomorphisms of the restrictions to every
localised site, of all stalks, and of all pullbacks, and each of the four
notions is a condition on these. A trivialising datum, respectively a
stratification, for $\mathcal F$ is therefore one for $\mathcal F'$.

Let $(\iota_k\colon Z_k\to X)_k$ be a stratification with all
$\iota_k^*\mathcal F$ finite locally constant, and let
$(\kappa_l\colon W_l\to X)_l$ refine it. Then all $\kappa_l^*\mathcal F$
are finite locally constant.

## Proof

Fix $l$ and choose $k$ with $X'_l\subseteq X_k$. The base change
$\kappa'_l\colon W_l\times_XZ_k\to Z_k$ of $\kappa_l$ is an immersion, and
the composite $\iota_k\circ\kappa'_l\colon W_l\times_XZ_k\to X$ is an
immersion with image $\iota_k(\iota_k^{-1}(X'_l))=X'_l$, the same image as
$\kappa_l$. Its pullback of $\mathcal F$ is
$\kappa_l'^*\iota_k^*\mathcal F$, finite locally constant by
[prop-constructible-pullback] (its lemmas for locally constant and
finite sheaves). By [lemma-constructible-immersion-independence],
$\kappa_l^*\mathcal F$ is finite locally constant.

For $g\colon Y\to X$ and $M\in\mathcal A$ there is a natural isomorphism
$g^*(M_X)\cong M_Y$. In particular $g^*$ sends constant sheaves to constant
sheaves.

## Proof

Both $M\mapsto g^*(M_X)$ and $M\mapsto M_Y$ are left adjoint to
$\mathcal G\mapsto\Gamma(Y,\mathcal G)=\Gamma(X,g_*\mathcal G)$, because
base change along $g$ preserves the terminal object of the site
($Y\times_XX\cong Y$); left adjoints are unique up to unique isomorphism.

Let $g\colon Y\to X$ be a morphism and let $\mathcal F\in\shv{\et X}$ be
finite. Then $g^*\mathcal F$ is finite.

## Proof

For a geometric point $\bar y$ of $Y$, the stalk $(g^*\mathcal F)_{\bar y}$
is the stalk $\mathcal F_{g\circ\bar y}$ by
[lemma-openclosed-stalk-upperstar], which is finite by hypothesis.

Let $g\colon Y\to X$ be a morphism and let $\mathcal F\in\shv{\et X}$ be
locally constant. Then $g^*\mathcal F$ is locally constant.

## Proof

Let $(U_i\to X)_i$ be a trivialising datum for $\mathcal F$. The base
change $(U_i\times_XY\to Y)_i$ is an étale cover of $Y$, since étale
morphisms and jointly surjective families are stable under base change.
The restriction of $g^*\mathcal F$ to $\et{U_i\times_XY}$ is the pullback,
along the projection $g_i\colon U_i\times_XY\to U_i$, of the restriction
of $\mathcal F$ to $\et{U_i}$: pullback along $g$ followed by restriction to
the localised site equals restriction followed by pullback along $g_i$,
because both are the sheaf pullback along the composite of the base change
functors, which agree. The restriction of $\mathcal F$ to $\et{U_i}$ is
constant, and pullbacks of constant sheaves are constant by
[lemma-constructible-pullback-constant]. Hence
$(U_i\times_XY\to Y)_i$ is a trivialising datum for $g^*\mathcal F$.

Let $g\colon Y\to X$ be a morphism and let $(\iota_k\colon Z_k\to X)_{k<n}$
be a stratification of $X$. Then the base changes
$(\iota'_k\colon Z_k\times_XY\to Y)_{k<n}$ form a stratification of $Y$,
with strata $g^{-1}(X_k)$.

## Proof

Immersions are stable under base change, and the image of the base change
$Z_k\times_XY\to Y$ of $\iota_k$ is the preimage $g^{-1}(\iota_k(Z_k))$:
the underlying set of a fibre product of schemes surjects onto the
set-theoretic fibre product, so the image of the projection to $Y$ is
exactly the set of points of $Y$ whose image in $X$ lies in the image of
$\iota_k$. The sets $g^{-1}(X_k)$ are locally closed, pairwise disjoint and
cover $Y$, as preimages of the locally closed, pairwise disjoint sets $X_k$
covering $X$.

Let $\mathcal G$ be a finite locally constant sheaf of groups on $\et X$
and let $P$ be a $\mathcal G$-torsor. Then $P$ is trivial on an étale
cover of $X$.

## Proof

Working on the members of a trivialising cover of $\mathcal G$ we may
assume $\mathcal G=G_X$ for a finite group $G$. A $G_X$-torsor is
representable by a scheme $P\to X$ finite étale (locally on $X$ it is
$\bigsqcup_{g\in G}X$, and the transition functions are locally constant
permutations; see SGA 4); since $P\to X$ is étale and
surjective it is an étale cover, and $P$ restricted to $P$ has the
tautological section, so it is trivial there.

attrs.title: Torsors under finite locally constant sheaves

objects.body:
Let $u\colon Z'\to Z$ be a universal homeomorphism. Then
$\mathcal G\in\shv{\et Z}$ is constant (locally constant) if and only if
$u^*\mathcal G$ is. If moreover $u$ is a surjective closed immersion, then
$\mathcal G$ is finite (finite locally constant) if and only if
$u^*\mathcal G$ is.

## Proof

The direction ``only if'' is
[lemma-constructible-pullback-locally-constant], [lemma-constructible-pullback-finite].
For the converse, base change along $u$ is an equivalence of sites
$\et Z\simeq\et{Z'}$ (Stacks Project, Tag `04DZ`), hence $u^*$ is an
equivalence of categories of sheaves
([thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance]). Constancy: $u^*$ is
fully faithful and carries constant sheaves to constant sheaves, so from
$u^*\mathcal G\cong u^*M_{Z}$ we get $\mathcal G\cong M_Z$. Local
constancy: let $(V'_i\to Z')_i$ be a trivialising étale cover of
$u^*\mathcal G$. Each $V'_i$ is isomorphic over $Z'$ to $V_i\times_ZZ'$
for an étale $V_i\to Z$, and the $V_i$ cover $Z$ since $u$ is
surjective. The projection $u_i\colon V_i\times_ZZ'\to V_i$ is a
universal homeomorphism, and $u_i^*(\mathcal G|_{V_i})\cong (u^*\mathcal G)|_{V'_i}$ is constant, so $\mathcal G|_{V_i}$ is constant
by the first part applied to $u_i$. Finiteness, for $u$ a surjective closed
immersion: the residue field maps of a closed immersion are surjective,
hence isomorphisms, so every geometric point $\bar z$ of $Z$ lifts to a
geometric point $\bar z'$ of $Z'$ with $u\circ\bar z'=\bar z$, and the
stalk of $\mathcal G$ at $\bar z$ is the stalk of $u^*\mathcal G$ at
$\bar z'$.

Let $X$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated and let $U\subseteq X$ be
quasi-compact. A composition of two $U$-admissible blow-ups is a
$U$-admissible blow-up. The chosen isomorphism over $U$ is the composite of
the chosen pullback isomorphisms.

## Proof

Apply [thm-nagata-composition-of-blowups]. It writes the composite as
the blow-up of a finite-presentation center $Y\hookrightarrow X$ whose
support is the union of the first center and the image of the second center.
Both sets are disjoint from $U$, because the first blow-up is the identity
over $U$ by [lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-over-open], and the second
center is disjoint from its inverse image. Thus $Y\cap U=\varnothing$,
equivalently its defining ideal restricts to the unit ideal on $U$, so the
resulting blow-up is $U$-admissible. The isomorphism supplied by the
composition theorem is over $X$. Pulling it back to $U$ identifies the
composite with the composite of the two specified pullback isomorphisms;
the equality follows after composing with the structure maps, where it is
the associativity equality for fibre products.

If $\pi\colon X'\to X$ is $U$-admissible, then its center ideal restricts to
the unit ideal on $U$, and the induced morphism
$X'\times_XU\to U$ is an isomorphism. The inverse and the equality over
$U$ are part of the resulting specified isomorphism.

## Proof

Choose the ideal and blow-up identification from
[def-nagata-admissible-blowup]. The unit-ideal restriction is the
disjointness condition on the center. Apply
[thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement] to identify the blow-up over $U$
with $U$, then transport that isomorphism across the chosen identification
with $X'$.

attrs.title: An admissible blow-up is unchanged over the preserved open

objects.body:
Let $U\hookrightarrow X$ be a quasi-compact scheme-theoretically dense open
immersion, and let $\mathcal I$ be a finite type quasi-coherent ideal with
$\mathcal I|_U=\mathcal O_U$. Then the inverse image of $U$ is
scheme-theoretically dense in $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$.
Consequently the same assertion holds after any finite composite of
$U$-admissible blow-ups.

## Proof

First, the complement of the support of an invertible ideal is
scheme-theoretically dense: on an affine open where the ideal is generated
by a single non-zero-divisor $a$, the restriction map to the complement of
the support is the localization away from $a$, which is injective.
Applying this on $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$ to the extended ideal
$\mathcal I\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)}$, which is
invertible by [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center], shows that the
inverse image of the complement $W$ of the center is scheme-theoretically
dense in the blow-up. Density now descends along the partial isomorphism:
the blow-up map $\pi$ is an isomorphism over $W$ by
[thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement], hence also over the smaller
open $U\subseteq W$; since $U$ is quasi-compact and scheme-theoretically
dense in $X$, the inclusion $U\hookrightarrow W$ is scheme-theoretically
dominant, and transporting it across the isomorphism over $W$ and composing
with the dense open immersion $\pi^{-1}(W)\hookrightarrow \operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$ shows that $\pi^{-1}(U)$ is
scheme-theoretically dense. For a finite composite, the inverse image of
$U$ at each stage is again a quasi-compact scheme-theoretically dense open,
so induction on the length of the composite applies the one-step lemma at
each stage.

attrs.title: Density is preserved by an admissible blow-up

objects.body:
For $Z=V(I)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}(A)$, the affine blow-up morphism
restricts to an isomorphism over $\operatorname{Spec}(A)\setminus Z$.

## Proof

The complement is covered by the basic opens $D(a)$, $a\in I$. On $D(a)$
the localized ideal is the unit ideal, so
[prop-nagata-affine-blowup-restrict] and
[lemma-nagata-affine-blowup-top] identify the blow-up with $D(a)$.
The identifications agree on overlaps by
[lemma-nagata-affine-blowup-restrict-cocycle], and hence glue.

If $I$ is finitely generated, the affine blow-up morphism is proper.

## Proof

By [def-nagata-affine-blowup], the affine blow-up is
$\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal R_A(I))\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, the
structural morphism of Proj followed by the isomorphism
$\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal R_A(I)_0\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$ induced by
$\mathcal R_A(I)_0\cong A$ ([lemma-nagata-rees-degree-zero]), with the grading of [prop-nagata-rees-graded].
Since $I$ is finitely generated, the Rees algebra is of finite type over
its degree-zero part ([prop-nagata-rees-finite-generation]). The
verified properness instance for $\operatorname{Proj}$ of a graded ring of
finite type over its degree-zero part ([def-nagata-affine-proj]) makes the
structural morphism proper, and composing with an isomorphism keeps it
proper.

The restriction isomorphism is the identity for $s=1$, and its two possible
composites on an iterated basic open $D(st)$ agree literally after the
chosen canonical associativity isomorphisms.

## Proof

On each standard chart, the map for $s=1$ is induced by the identity of the
Rees algebra, hence is the identity. For $s,t$, both composites send a
homogeneous fraction to its image in the localization at $st$; the two
coefficient maps are equal by [lemma-nagata-rees-localization-one]
and [lemma-nagata-rees-localization-mul].
The chart maps therefore agree on a cover, proving the asserted identity
and cocycle equalities globally.

attrs.title: Identity and cocycle laws for affine restriction

objects.body:
The blow-up of $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ in the unit ideal is canonically
isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ over $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$.

## Proof

The Rees algebra of the unit ideal is $A[t]$. The single standard open
$D_+(t)$ covers Proj, and its chart algebra $A[A/1]$ is $A$.

If $U$ is affine, then $U$ is quasi-affine in the sense used in
[lemma-nagata-quasi-affine-immersion-affine-space-exists]; in
particular that lemma applies to any $U\to S$ of finite type with $U$
affine.

## Proof

The identity of $U$ realizes the canonical map
$U\to\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ as an open immersion, and
$U$ is quasi-compact. This is the defining quasi-affine property, and a
finite-type structure morphism is in particular locally of finite type.

**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the finite-presentation and
Noetherian descent is done in one step by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_isPullback_of_finitePresentation_of_isSeparated`
and `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.nonempty_noetherianApproximation`, so
this stage-by-stage bookkeeping is never carried out.

The algebra $B_{\lambda_B}$ is finitely presented over
$A_{\lambda_B}$, and the constructed map $\beta_B$ is an isomorphism.

## Proof

The displayed quotient is a finite presentation by construction. Tensoring
it with $A$ sends every lifted relation to the original $r_j$ and preserves
the finite polynomial presentation. Thus the base-changed presentation is
the chosen presentation of $B$, with $\beta_B$ and its generatorwise inverse
mutually inverse.

**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the finite-presentation and
Noetherian descent is done in one step by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_isPullback_of_finitePresentation_of_isSeparated`
and `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.nonempty_noetherianApproximation`, so
this stage-by-stage bookkeeping is never carried out.

Every selected finite coefficient subalgebra, basic-open element, restricted
overlap map, and proposed inverse is defined at
$\lambda_{\mathrm{coeff}}$. Under base change to the original chart rings,
these objects are the corresponding restrictions of the data in
$\mathsf G_S$.

## Proof

Each finite coefficient list lies in one finitely generated
$\mathbf Z$-subalgebra by
[lemma-nagata-ring-finite-type-subalgebras]. The selected upper bound
dominates every such stage by
[lemma-nagata-directed-finite-upper-bound]. Hence all selected
coefficients and restricted maps are simultaneously defined at the named
common stage, and base change returns the original finite lists. The full
chart rings are recovered only after taking the filtered colimit over all
finite refinements; no single stage is asserted to contain every coefficient
of an arbitrary chart ring.

attrs.title: All gluing coefficients occur at the selected stage

objects.body:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the finite-presentation and
Noetherian descent is done in one step by

The overlap maps in $\mathsf G_{S,\lambda_{\mathrm{glue}}}$ preserve the
selected opens, are mutually inverse, and satisfy all identity and
triple-overlap cocycle equations.

## Proof

Every required equality is determined by finitely many generators after
localization. Equality in the colimit is witnessed at a finite stage.
The definition includes all those witness stages in one finite set, and the
selected upper-bound lemma makes every equation hold simultaneously at
$\lambda_{\mathrm{glue}}(S)$.

attrs.title: Property of the selected affine neighbourhood, [stacks-project]

objects.body:
