attrs.title: Property of the descended finite affine presentation

objects.body:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: no separate relative-Proj
primitive was formalized. The blow-up is glued from the affine Proj charts
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.basicOpenIsoSpec`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.iSup_basicOpen_eq_top`) with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Cover.RelativeGluingData`.

For any morphism $g\colon Y\to X$ and graded quasi-coherent algebra
$\mathcal A$ on $X$, coefficientwise pullback gives a canonical isomorphism

$$
\operatorname{Proj}_Y(g^*\mathcal A)
\cong Y\times_X\operatorname{Proj}_X(\mathcal A).
$$

## Proof

Cover $X$ by affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ and cover each affine
inverse image in $Y$ by $W=\operatorname{Spec}(B)$, with structure map
$A\to B$. Put $C=\Gamma(V,\mathcal A)$. For every positive-degree
homogeneous $f\in C$, the two standard charts in the asserted comparison
have coordinate rings

$$
B\otimes_A C_{(f),0}\quad\text{and}\quad
(B\otimes_A C)_{(f\otimes1),0}.
$$

For fixed $f$, the degree-zero homogeneous localization is the filtered
colimit of the modules $C_{m\deg(f)}$ under multiplication by $f$.
Since tensor product commutes with filtered colimits, there is a canonical
isomorphism

$$
B\otimes_A C_{(f),0}\;\xrightarrow{\sim}\;
(B\otimes_A C)_{(f\otimes1),0}.
$$

On pure fractions this isomorphism and its inverse are given by

$$
(b\otimes x/f^m)\longmapsto (b\otimes x)/(f\otimes1)^m,
\qquad
(b\otimes x)/(f\otimes1)^m\longmapsto b\otimes x/f^m
$$

and extend additively. The filtered-colimit description, rather than
injectivity after tensoring, proves that these formulas are well-defined and
mutually inverse for an arbitrary $A\to B$. They are compatible with
localization at a second homogeneous element, so the affine chart
isomorphisms agree on all overlaps. The standard opens cover both Proj
schemes, and `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.GlueData.glued` therefore
produces an
isomorphism

$$
\operatorname{Proj}_Y(g^*\mathcal A)\cong
Y\times_X\operatorname{Proj}_X(\mathcal A).
$$

The construction is natural in $g$ and in maps of graded algebras because
every displayed map is induced by tensor product and localization; hence it
is the required canonical arbitrary-base-change comparison.

attrs.title: Relative Proj base change for an arbitrary morphism

objects.body:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: no separate relative-Proj
primitive was formalized. The blow-up is glued from the affine Proj charts
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.basicOpenIsoSpec`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.iSup_basicOpen_eq_top`) with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Cover.RelativeGluingData`.

The relative Proj construction in
[def-nagata-relative-proj] exists as a scheme, is independent up to a
unique isomorphism compatible with the chosen affine-chart
identifications, and restricts over every affine open $V\subseteq X$ to
$\operatorname{Proj}(\Gamma(V,\mathcal A))$. These restriction
isomorphisms commute with further restriction and with the structural maps.

## Proof

Choose the index set of all affine opens $V\subseteq X$. For each $V$ put
$P_V=\operatorname{Proj}(\Gamma(V,\mathcal A))$. If $W\subseteq V$ is a
principal affine open, quasi-coherence gives the coefficientwise graded
localization

$$
\Gamma(V,\mathcal A)[s^{-1}]\;\xrightarrow{\sim}\;
\Gamma(W,\mathcal A),
$$

and the affine Proj construction gives an isomorphism from $P_W$ onto the
inverse image of $W$ in $P_V$. To cover an arbitrary overlap $V\cap V'$,
index the gluing datum by triples $(V,V',W)$ with $W$ affine and
$W\subseteq V\cap V'$, together with a principal refinement inside $W$.
The associated isomorphism is the map on each standard chart induced by the
displayed localization. Every overlap is covered by such indices, and the
maps are isomorphisms because localization is transitive.

The identity and inverse axioms are the cases $V=V'$ and exchange of the two
affine indices. On a triple overlap all routes send a fraction
$x/s^m$ to its image in the localization at the product of the three
denominators; hence the cocycle axiom is exactly
[lemma-nagata-proj-chart-ring-cocycle]. The datum therefore satisfies
the scheme-gluing axioms, so the Mathlib
construction `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.GlueData.glued` produces a
scheme $P$ and a morphism $P\to X$ (the degree-zero maps agree on every
overlap). Its restriction to $V$ is the specified $P_V$ by the restriction
field of the same gluing construction. A second affine cover produces the
same overlap datum after passing to the common refinement by affine opens;
the uniqueness field of `Scheme.GlueData.glued` gives a unique
isomorphism over $X$ that
respects all the local identifications. (No uniqueness among arbitrary
automorphisms over $X$ is asserted.) The same argument on a third
refinement proves compatibility with further restrictions.

attrs.title: Existence and affine compatibility of relative Proj

objects.body:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: no separate relative-Proj
primitive was formalized. The blow-up is glued from the affine Proj charts
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.basicOpenIsoSpec`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.iSup_basicOpen_eq_top`) with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Cover.RelativeGluingData`.

If $\mathcal L$ is an invertible ideal on $Y$, the relative Proj of
$\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$ is canonically isomorphic to $Y$.
Under this isomorphism $\mathcal O(1)$ identifies with $\mathcal L$, and
the universal degree-one map $\mathcal L\to\mathcal O(1)$ is the identity
of $\mathcal L$. The inclusion
$\mathcal L\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_Y$ is a separate effective-Cartier
inclusion and is not the tautological quotient.

## Proof

Cover $Y$ by affine opens $V$ on which $\mathcal L$ has a generator $a$.
By [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-invertible-tensor-powers-affine], the
relative Proj restricts over each such $V$ to $V$, with the identification
induced by the degree-zero localization map. On an overlap $V\cap W$, if
$b=ua$ for a unit $u$, the two chart identifications send a fraction
$(r a^n)/a^n$ (respectively $(r u^{-n}b^n)/b^n$) to the same coefficient $r$.
Hence they agree on overlaps and glue, by the relative-Proj gluing
compatibility, to a canonical isomorphism with $Y$. The degree-one
localization identifies the tautological section with the chosen generator;
these local identifications glue to $\mathcal O(1)\cong\mathcal L$, and the
resulting universal degree-one map is the identity on $\mathcal L$. The
inclusion $\mathcal L\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_Y$ is independent of this
tautological quotient and remains the specified effective-Cartier inclusion.

attrs.title: Proj of the tensor powers of an invertible ideal

objects.body:
Let $V=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ be an affine open on which the invertible
ideal $\mathcal L$ is generated by one element $a$. Then the graded
algebra $\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal L(V)^{\otimes n}$ is generated by the
single degree-one element $a$, and its degree-zero homogeneous localization
at $a$ is canonically $A$. Consequently the standard open $D_+(a)$ is all
of $\operatorname{Proj}_A(\bigoplus_n\mathcal L(V)^{\otimes n})$, and the
resulting affine Proj is canonically $V$ over $V$.

## Proof

Choose the basis $a$ of the rank-one $A$-module $\mathcal L(V)$. Tensoring
this basis identifies $\mathcal L(V)^{\otimes n}$ with $A\,a^{\otimes n}$,
and multiplication sends $a^{\otimes m}\otimes a^{\otimes n}$ to
$a^{\otimes(m+n)}$. Thus every homogeneous element is uniquely $r a^n$
and the algebra is the polynomial algebra $A[a]$ with $a$ in degree one.
A degree-zero fraction has the form $(r a^n)/a^n$ and is sent to $r$;
this gives mutually inverse ring maps between the homogeneous localization
and $A$. Since $a$ generates the irrelevant ideal, the standard-open cover
lemma makes $D_+(a)$ the whole Proj, proving the asserted affine
identification and its compatibility with the degree-zero structure map.

If $S$ is qcqs and $X\to S$ is locally of finite type with $X$
quasi-compact and quasi-separated, then a finite-stage datum exists after enlarging both
indices. Its chart maps use only finitely many coefficients and relations,
and their base change to $S$ is the original morphism.

## Proof

Choose finite affine presentations of source and target charts. Their
finitely many coefficients, structural maps, and overlap identities occur
at one common stage by the finite-data lemma; enlarging both indices gives
the required compatible datum and immersion charts.

attrs.title: Existence of finite-stage data for a finite-type morphism

objects.body:
For every ring $A$, its finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-subalgebras form a
directed system and the canonical map

$$
\varinjlim_{A_0\subseteq A,\;A_0/\mathbf Z\ \mathrm{finite\ type}}A_0
\longrightarrow A
$$

is an isomorphism. In particular every finite set of elements of $A$ is
contained in one such subalgebra.

## Proof

The subalgebra generated by the union of two finite generating sets contains
both corresponding subalgebras. Every element of $A$ lies in the
subalgebra generated by that element, proving surjectivity. Since all
transition maps are inclusions, two representatives with equal image agree
in a common over-algebra, proving injectivity. A finite set is contained in
the subalgebra it generates.

attrs.title: A ring is the filtered colimit of its finite-type $\mathbf Z$-subalgebras

objects.body:
Let $C\to B$ be a ring map, let $K=\ker(C\to B)$, and let $a\in C$ map
to a unit of $B$. Put $C_a=C[1/a]$. If $C/K\to B$ is injective, then

$$
\ker(C\longrightarrow C_a\longrightarrow B)
=\{c\in C\mid \exists n,\ a^nc\in K\},
$$

and this kernel is the inverse image of
$\Gamma_{(a)}(C/K)$ under $C\to C/K$.
Consequently the scheme-theoretic image of the induced map from $B$ on an
$a$-chart is the quotient by the $a$-power torsion, i.e. the strict-transform
chart of the scheme-theoretic image of $\operatorname{Spec}(B)\to \operatorname{Spec}(C)$.

## Proof

If $c$ maps to zero in $B$, then its image in $C_a/KC_a$ is zero because
$C/K\to B$ is injective. The localization criterion gives
$a^nc\in K$ for some $n$. Conversely, such an equality maps to zero in $B$
because $a$ is a unit there. This proves the displayed kernel equality.
On a standard blow-up chart replace $C$ by $C_a(A,B,I)$ and $a$ by the
chart equation. The quotient by the displayed kernel is exactly the
quotient by $\Gamma_{(a)}$; the affine strict-transform formula and the
closure characterization identify it with the strict-transform chart.

For a morphism $g\colon T\to Y$, Mathlib defines its scheme-theoretic image
as the closed subscheme cut out by the ideal sheaf $\operatorname{ker}(g)$.
It also supplies the closed immersion
$g_{\mathrm{im}}\colon\operatorname{SIm}(g)\hookrightarrow Y$ and the
factor map $g^{\mathrm{im}}\colon T\to\operatorname{SIm}(g)$.
When $g$ is quasi-compact, the stalk maps of $g^{\mathrm{im}}$ are
injective and the support of $\operatorname{ker}(g)$ is the closure of the
topological range of $g$.

*Implementation note.* The verified declarations are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.image`, `Scheme.Hom.imageι`,
`Scheme.Hom.toImage`, `Scheme.Hom.toImage_imageι`,
`Scheme.Hom.toImage_app_injective` (under quasi-compactness), and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.support_map` together with
`Scheme.IdealSheafData.map_bot` (under quasi-compactness). No
invented `Scheme.Hom.support_ker` or
`schemeTheoreticImageIdeal_isQuasiCoherent` declaration is assumed.

## Proof

This block records the existing Mathlib construction. The closed
subscheme is `Scheme.Hom.image g`, its inclusion is the declaration
`Scheme.Hom.imageι g`, and the factor map is
`Scheme.Hom.toImage g`; the displayed composite is the theorem
`Scheme.Hom.toImage_imageι`. The additional quasi-compact
assertions are exactly the two declarations named in the implementation
note, so no direct-image calculation is silently imported here.

If $i\colon Z\hookrightarrow Y$ is a closed immersion, then the factor map
$i^{\mathrm{im}}\colon Z\to\operatorname{SIm}(i)$ is an isomorphism. Thus
the scheme-theoretic image of a closed immersion is canonically its source,
compatibly with the maps to $Y$.

## Proof

The current Mathlib instance
`AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion.instIsIsoSchemeToImage`
supplies the isomorphism for every morphism carrying the
`IsClosedImmersion` property. Its compatibility with the inclusion
is the factorization equality
`Scheme.Hom.toImage_imageι`.

attrs.title: Scheme-theoretic image of a closed immersion

objects.body:
Let $U\hookrightarrow X$ be a quasi-compact open immersion, let
$Y\to S$ be separated, and let
$U\to X\times_SY$ be a morphism whose first projection is the given open
immersion. If $Z$ is its scheme-theoretic image, then the projection
$Z\to X$ has inverse image $U$ over the open $U\subseteq X$, and this
inverse image maps isomorphically to $U$.

## Proof

By [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-restrict-open], restriction to
$U\times_SY$ commutes with taking the scheme-theoretic image. On this
open target the original map is a section of
$U\times_SY\to U$. That projection is separated, so its section is a
closed immersion. By
[lemma-nagata-scheme-image-of-closed-immersion], its
scheme-theoretic image is canonically its source, compatibly with the
projection to $U$.

attrs.title: Scheme-theoretic image of a partial section

objects.body:
Let $g\colon T\to Y$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, let
$W\subseteq Y$ be open, let $T_W=T\times_YW$, and let
$g_W\colon T_W\to W$ be the base change of $g$. Then

$$
\operatorname{SIm}(g_W)
\cong\operatorname{SIm}(g)\times_YW
$$

as closed subschemes of $W$, compatibly with their inclusions into $W$.

## Proof

On an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}(A)\subseteq Y$, the image ideal is
the kernel of
$A\to\Gamma(T\times_YV,\mathcal O)$. On every principal open
$D(s)\subseteq V\cap W$,
[lemma-nagata-dense-flat-pullback] identifies the image
kernel of the restricted morphism with the localization of this ideal.
The declaration
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.ideal_comap_of_isOpenImmersion`
identifies that localized ideal with the comap of the original image ideal,
and `Scheme.IdealSheafData.comapIso` identifies the closed
subscheme it defines with the fibre product. Functoriality under further
localization makes these affine isomorphisms agree on overlaps. They glue
to the displayed canonical isomorphism, and the construction from equal
ideal sheaves makes it compatible with the two inclusions into $W$.

attrs.title: Restriction of a scheme-theoretic image to an open target

objects.body:
Let $V\to X\times_SY$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and assume its
projection to $X$ factors through an open $U\subseteq X$. Let $Z$ be its
scheme-theoretic image. If $X'\to X$ is a $U$-admissible blow-up, then the scheme-theoretic
image of the lifted map $V\to X'\times_SY$ is the strict transform of $Z$.
More precisely, use the canonical isomorphism
$\varepsilon\colon X'\times_XU\cong U$ from
[thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement]; the lift is the map whose
$X'$-component is obtained from $V\to U$ by
$\varepsilon^{-1}\colon U\to X'\times_XU\to X'$ and whose $Y$-component is
the given projection $V\to Y$.

## Proof

Apply [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-transport-strict-transform] to the
given map $V\to X\times_SY$. Its lifted map is exactly the map specified in
the statement through $\varepsilon^{-1}$, so the resulting image equality is
the claimed identification with the strict transform.

Let $h\colon T\to X\times_SY$ be quasi-compact, with
first projection factoring through a quasi-compact open $U\subseteq X$.
(The Stacks Project assumes $h$ quasi-separated as well; the formalised
statement drops it, since the kernel ideal sheaf theory used here only needs
quasi-compactness, exactly as recorded for
[lemma-nagata-dense-flat-pullback].)
Let $Z=\operatorname{SIm}(h)$ and let $\pi\colon X'\to X$ be a
$U$-admissible blow-up. Via the canonical identity
$X'\times_XU\cong U$, let $h'$ be the lifted map to $X'\times_SY$. Then

$$
\operatorname{SIm}(h')
\;=\;\operatorname{ST}_{X'/X}(Z)
$$

as closed subschemes of $X'\times_SY$, compatibly with their maps to $X'$.

## Proof

Restriction of scheme-theoretic image to $U\times_SY$ identifies the image
there with the image of $h|_U$ by
[lemma-nagata-scheme-image-restrict-open]. Work on an affine chart of
$X'\times_SY$ on which the pulled-back center has principal equation $a$.
Write its coordinate ring as $C$ and refine the source by affine opens
$\operatorname{Spec}(B_j)$. The image ideal on this chart is
$K=\bigcap_j\ker(C\to B_j)$, so $C/K\to\prod_jB_j$ is injective; the image
of $a$ is a unit in every $B_j$ because $h$ factors through $U$. Applying
[lemma-nagata-scheme-image-affine-saturation] to the product ring
identifies the kernel on this chart with the $a$-saturation of the pulled
back image ideal. By
[prop-nagata-strict-transform-closed-fiber-product] and
[lemma-nagata-strict-transform-closure-characterization], that
quotient is precisely the strict-transform chart. The identifications are
unchanged after localization, so they agree on overlaps and glue to the
claimed global equality.

attrs.title: Scheme-image transport to a strict transform

objects.body:
The composite of $g^{\mathrm{im}}$ with
$\operatorname{SIm}(g)\hookrightarrow Y$ is $g$. For every closed
factorization through $Z$, the constructed map $c_{g,Z}$ is a closed
immersion compatible with the maps to $Y$, and it is the unique compatible
morphism $\operatorname{SIm}(g)\to Z$.

## Proof

The factorization equality is `Scheme.Hom.toImage_imageι`.
Let $\mathcal I_Z$ be the ideal of $Z$. From
$z\circ h=g$ every local section of $\mathcal I_Z$ maps to zero under $g$,
so $\mathcal I_Z\subseteq\operatorname{ker}(g)$. The induced quotient map
therefore gives a closed immersion
$c_{g,Z}\colon\operatorname{SIm}(g)\to Z$; its composite with $z$ is the
image inclusion by construction. If $c'$ is another compatible map, then
composing both $c'$ and $c_{g,Z}$ with the closed immersion $z$ gives the
same image inclusion

$$
z\circ c'=g_{\mathrm{im}}=z\circ c_{g,Z}.
$$

A closed immersion is a monomorphism, so cancellation of $z$ gives
$c'=c_{g,Z}$.

attrs.title: Universal property of the scheme-theoretic image

objects.body:
The scheme-theoretic closure is the smallest closed subscheme of $Y$
through which $a$ factors: it factors through every such closed subscheme,
and the comparison is unique over $Y$.

## Proof

This is [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-universal] applied to the immersion
$a$, together with
[def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-closure].

**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: boundary separation is
`AlgebraicGeometry.separationBlowup` with
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_admissibleBlowup_disjoint_closures`,
proved from Deligne's disjointness blow-up rather than from this
preparation.

Let $X$ be qcqs, let $U\subseteq X$ be quasi-compact open, and let
$Z_i=V(\mathcal I_i)\hookrightarrow X$ be finite-presentation closed
immersions with $Z_1\cap Z_2\cap U=\varnothing$. Put
$Z=V(\mathcal I_1\mathcal I_2)$, $U_Z=Z\times_XU$, and
$P_i=Z_i\times_XU$. The two closed subschemes $P_i$ are the disjoint
open-and-closed components of $U_Z=P_1\amalg P_2$. There is a finite
presentation closed center $C\hookrightarrow Z$, disjoint from $U_Z$, such
that the blow-up $Z' = \operatorname{Bl}_C(Z)\to Z$ is $U_Z$-admissible
and the strict transforms of $Z_1$ and $Z_2$ in $Z'$ are disjoint.

## Proof

Put $K_i=\mathcal I_Z(P_i)$, the finite-type ideal whose vanishing set is
$Z\setminus P_i$ ([def-nagata-qc-open-complement-ideal]). Since
$P_1$ and $P_2$ are disjoint, $V(K_1K_2)=Z$; finite type and
quasi-compactness therefore give $N>0$ with $(K_1K_2)^N=0$ by
[lemma-nagata-finite-type-nil-ideal-nilpotent]. The restrictions of
both $K_i$ to the quasi-compact closed boundary $Z\setminus U_Z$ are finite
type nil ideals, so enlarge $N$ until those restrictions are also killed by
the $N$th power. Replace $K_i$ by $K_i^N$; their vanishing sets are
unchanged, now $K_1K_2=0$, and both ideals vanish on $Z\setminus U_Z$. Let
$J=K_1+K_2$ and $C=V(J)$. On $U_Z=P_1\amalg P_2$, $K_1$ is the unit ideal
on $P_1$ and zero on $P_2$, while $K_2$ has the opposite behaviour. Hence
$J|_{U_Z}=\mathcal O_{U_Z}$ and $J$ vanishes on $Z\setminus U_Z$. Thus
$Z\setminus C=U_Z$ and $C\cap U_Z=\varnothing$. The closed
immersion $C\hookrightarrow Z$ is finite presentation because $J$ is finite
type.

Work on an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}(A)\subseteq Z$, with generators
$(a_\alpha)$ of $K_1$ and $(b_\beta)$ of $K_2$. The blow-up of $J$ is
covered by $A[J/a_\alpha]$ and $A[J/b_\beta]$. In
$A[J/a_\alpha]$, the element $a_\alpha$ is a nonzerodivisor by
[lemma-nagata-chart-generator-regular]; since
$a_\alpha K_2=0$, it follows that $K_2A[J/a_\alpha]=0$. Interchanging
the roles of $K_1$ and $K_2$ gives $K_1A[J/b_\beta]=0$. An
$a_\alpha$-chart and a $b_\beta$-chart have empty
intersection: on their overlap $a_\alpha b_\beta$ is both zero and a
nonzerodivisor, so the overlap ring is zero. Consequently the blow-up is a
disjoint union of the open-and-closed union $Z'_1$ of the $a_\alpha$-charts
and the open-and-closed union $Z'_2$ of the $b_\beta$-charts; the construction
is intrinsic in the extended ideals $K_i\mathcal O_{Z'}$, so these local
decompositions glue.

Over $U_Z$, the inverse image of $P_i$ lies in $Z'_i$. The strict transform
of $Z_i\to Z$ is the scheme-theoretic closure of that inverse image. Since
$Z'_i$ is closed as well as open, this closure remains in $Z'_i$. The two
strict transforms are therefore disjoint.

attrs.title: Preparation data for separating two closed boundaries, [stacks-project]

objects.body:
The morphism $\mathsf{SepBl}_U(Z_1,Z_2)\to X$ is $U$-admissible, and the
strict transforms of $Z_1$ and $Z_2$ in it are disjoint.

## Proof

The selected center is disjoint from $U_Z$, hence its image in $X$ is
disjoint from $U$. A composite of finite-presentation closed immersions is
finite presentation, so the ambient center is finite presentation and its
blow-up is $U$-admissible. By
[lemma-nagata-strict-transform-ambient-closed], the strict transforms
of $Z_1$ and $Z_2$ in this ambient blow-up agree with their strict
transforms in $\operatorname{Bl}_C(Z)$, which are disjoint by the selected
preparation witness.

attrs.title: Properties of the closed-boundary separation blow-up, [stacks-project]

objects.body:
The constructed blow-up $\mathsf{CSepBl}_U(T_1,T_2)\to X$ is
$U$-admissible, and the closures of the inverse images of $T_1$ and $T_2$
are disjoint.

## Proof

By [lemma-nagata-constructible-closed-support],
$V(\mathcal J_i)=T_i$ in $U$. The restriction equality from
[lemma-nagata-extend-finite-type-ideal] consequently gives
$|Z_i\cap U|=T_i$, so $Z_1\cap Z_2\cap U=\varnothing$. Apply
[lemma-nagata-separate-closed-subschemes]. In the resulting
$U$-admissible blow-up $\pi\colon X'\to X$, the closure of
$\pi^{-1}(T_i)$ is contained in the underlying set of the strict transform
of $Z_i$: the strict transform is closed in $X'$, and it contains every
point lying both over the preserved open and over $Z_i$ — in particular
every point of $\pi^{-1}(T_i)$. The two strict transforms are disjoint,
so these two closures are disjoint as claimed.

Let $X\to S$ be separated and of finite presentation, and let
$X^{\mathrm{desc}}_{\lambda_{\mathrm{rel}}}\to S_{\lambda_{\mathrm{rel}}}$ be the finite-presentation descent model.
There is a later index $\lambda_{\mathrm{sep}}$ for which the descended
model is separated, remains of finite presentation, and has base change
canonically isomorphic to $X\to S$.

## Proof

Let $D$ be the diagonal of the finite-presentation descended model over
$S_{\lambda_{\mathrm{rel}}}$. It is of finite presentation by
[lemma-nagata-diagonal-finite-presentation]. By
[lemma-nagata-finite-presentation-descends], base change identifies
the source model with $X$. Under this identification,
[lemma-nagata-diagonal-base-change] identifies the base change of
$D$ with $\Delta_{X/S}$, which is a closed immersion because $X\to S$ is
separated. Apply
[lemma-nagata-closed-immersion-stage-exists] to $D$ and choose the
resulting index $\lambda_{\mathrm{sep}}$. The diagonal at that stage is
closed, so the corresponding descended morphism is separated. Its finite
presentation and its comparison isomorphism with $X$ are obtained by base
changing the finite-presentation descent data to this later stage.

attrs.title: Existence of a separated descent stage

objects.body:
The constructed morphism
$X^{\mathrm{sep}}_{\lambda_{\mathrm{sep}}(X/S)} \to S_{\lambda_{\mathrm{sep}}(X/S)}$ is
separated and of finite presentation, and its base change to $S$ is
canonically $X\to S$.

## Proof

The initial descended model is finite presentation and has base change $X$.
The diagonal base-change lemma identifies the base change of its diagonal
with the closed immersion $\Delta_{X/S}$. At the explicitly selected
closed-immersion stage, the actual diagonal is closed, hence the model is
separated. Finite presentation and the base-change identification persist
under increasing the stage.

attrs.title: Property of the selected separated descent stage, [stacks-project]

objects.body:
Let $Y=\varprojlim_\alpha Y_\alpha$ be a cofiltered limit of qcqs schemes with
affine transition maps. If $Y$ is separated, then there is an index
$\alpha_0$ such that $Y_\alpha$ is separated for every $\alpha\geq\alpha_0$.

## Proof

Choose a finite affine open cover $U_1,\dots,U_m$ of one stage
$Y_{\alpha_1}$ and let $U_{\alpha,k}$, $U_k$ denote the inverse images in
$Y_\alpha$ and in $Y$; these are affine because the transition maps are
affine. A scheme covered by affine opens whose pairwise intersections are
affine, and for which the sections over such an intersection are generated by
the sections of the two members, is separated; so two things must be
descended.
First, $U_{k_1}\cap U_{k_2}$ is affine because $Y$ is separated, hence
$U_{\alpha,k_1}\cap U_{\alpha,k_2}$ is affine for all $\alpha$ past some
stage by Stacks [Tag 01Z6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01Z6).
Second, the sections over $U_{\alpha,k_1}\cap U_{\alpha,k_2}$ are generated
over the sections of $U_{\alpha,k_1}$ by finitely many elements, because that
intersection is a quasi-compact open of the affine $U_{\alpha,k_1}$; and the
elements of $\Gamma(U_{k_1}\cap U_{k_2})$ that already come from a stage,
inside the subring generated there by the sections of the two members, form a
subring, which by separatedness of $Y$ is everything. So those finitely many
generators are reached at a common stage, and the generation statement then
persists at every later stage because the sections over the intersection at a
later stage are generated by those of the earlier stage together with those of
the corresponding member of the cover.

attrs.title: Existence of a separated stage, absolute case, [stacks-project]

objects.body:
Let $X=U\cup V$ be an open cover over $S$. Assume that $U\to S$ and
$V\to S$ are separated and that

$$
U\cap V\longrightarrow U\times_SV
$$

is a closed immersion. Then $X\to S$ is separated.

## Proof

The target of $\Delta_{X/S}$ is covered by

$$
U\times_SU,\quad U\times_SV,\quad
V\times_SU,\quad V\times_SV.
$$

On the two unmixed pieces the diagonal is closed by separatedness of $U/S$
and $V/S$. On the mixed pieces use
[lemma-nagata-diagonal-mixed-open]. Closed immersions are local on the
target, so $\Delta_{X/S}$ is closed.

Let $f\colon Y\to S$ be separated, let $A$ be a valuation ring with
fraction field $K$, and let $h_1,h_2\colon\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to Y$ be
$S$-morphisms whose restrictions to $\operatorname{Spec}(K)$ coincide.
Then $h_1=h_2$.

## Proof

The equalizer of $h_1$ and $h_2$ is the inverse image of the diagonal
$\Delta_f\colon Y\hookrightarrow Y\times_S Y$. Since $f$ is separated,
this is a closed subscheme of $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$. It contains the
generic point because the two restrictions to $\operatorname{Spec}(K)$ are
equal. A valuation ring is a domain, so its generic point is the prime
$(0)$, whose closure is all of $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$. Hence the closed
equalizer is the whole spectrum, and the two morphisms are equal.

attrs.title: Uniqueness of a valuation lift for a separated morphism

objects.body:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: no separate relative-Proj
primitive was formalized. The blow-up is glued from the affine Proj charts
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.basicOpenIsoSpec`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.iSup_basicOpen_eq_top`) with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Cover.RelativeGluingData`.

For a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$, the canonical
maps $\mathcal I^m\otimes\mathcal I^n\to\mathcal I^{m+n}$ are associative
and have $\mathcal I^0=\mathcal O_X$ as a two-sided unit.

## Proof

On an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ these maps are induced by
multiplication of the ideals $I^m$ and $I^n$ in $A$. Associativity and the
unit law are therefore the corresponding ring identities. Localization
preserves these identities, and equality of morphisms of quasi-coherent
sheaves can be checked on an affine cover, so the identities glue on $X$.

**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the existence statement
`PrespectralSpace.exists_isCompact_isOpen_disjoint_union_eq_univ`
is used directly, so no selected separation datum and specification lemma
are introduced.

The constructed subsets $T_c,T'_c$ are constructible and closed in $V$,
and they satisfy

$$
T\subseteq T_c,\qquad T'\subseteq T'_c,\qquad
T_c\cap T'_c=\varnothing.
$$

## Proof

Complements of quasi-compact opens in a spectral space are constructible
closed subsets. The choice of $W$ gives $T\subseteq T_c$, the choice of
$W'$ gives $T'\subseteq T'_c$, and $V\setminus W\subseteq W'$ gives
$T_c\cap T'_c=\varnothing$.

attrs.title: Properties of the constructible separation data

objects.body:
If $T,T'$ are disjoint closed subsets of a spectral space $V$, there exist
quasi-compact opens $W,W'\subseteq V$ such that

$$
T'\subseteq W,\quad W\cap T=\varnothing,\quad
V\setminus W\subseteq W',\quad W'\cap T'=\varnothing.
$$

## Proof

Quasi-compact opens form a basis of a spectral space. For each $x\in T'$,
choose a quasi-compact open neighbourhood contained in $V\setminus T$.
The closed subset $T'$ is quasi-compact, so finitely many suffice; their
union is a quasi-compact open $W$ containing $T'$ and disjoint from $T$.
The closed subset $V\setminus W$ is quasi-compact and lies in the open
$V\setminus T'$. Cover it by finitely many quasi-compact opens contained
in $V\setminus T'$ and let $W'$ be their union.

attrs.title: Existence of constructible closed separators in a spectral space

objects.body:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the strict transform is
supplied by the API of
`WeilConjectures/Compactification/StrictTransform.lean` —
`AlgebraicGeometry.strictTransform`, its closed immersion

The kernel of $\sigma_a$ is exactly
$\Gamma_{(a)}(C_a(A,B,I))$.

## Proof

Both source and target map to $B_b$. The target $B[J/b]$ is the subalgebra
generated there by the fractions from $J$, and $\sigma_a$ has exactly that
image by [lemma-nagata-strict-chart-map-surjective]. Thus its kernel
is the kernel of localization at $b$. Under the $A$-action this is the
kernel of localization at $a$, which equals the $a$-power torsion by
[lemma-nagata-power-torsion-kernel-localization].

attrs.title: Kernel of the map to the extended-ideal chart

objects.body:
The constructed homomorphism $\sigma_a$ is surjective.

## Proof

By [lemma-nagata-chart-ring-normal-form], the target is generated as a
$B$-algebra by the fractions $z/b$ with $z\in J$. Write
$z=\sum_k y_k\overline{x_k}$ with $x_k\in I$. Then

$$
z/b=\sum_k\sigma_a\bigl(y_k\otimes(x_k/a)\bigr),
$$

proving surjectivity.

**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the strict transform is
supplied by the API of
`WeilConjectures/Compactification/StrictTransform.lean` —
`AlgebraicGeometry.strictTransform`, its closed immersion
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.isClosedImmersion_pullbackLift_blowup_comap`,
and the pullback square
`AlgebraicGeometry.isPullback_strictTransformOpen` — so the
strict-transform chart rings and their cocycle are never assembled by hand.

The assignment defining $\sigma_a$ respects addition, multiplication, the
localization relations in $A[I/a]$, and the two $A$-algebra structures.
Consequently $\sigma_a$ is a well-defined $B$-algebra homomorphism.

## Proof

For $x,x'\in I$, the relations

$$
\frac{x+x'}a=\frac xa+\frac{x'}a,
\qquad
\frac xa\frac{x'}a=\frac{xx'}{a^2}
$$

have the same images in $B_b$. The image of $A$ through the left tensor
factor equals its image through the chart factor. The universal properties
of $A[I/a]$ and of $B\otimes_AA[I/a]$ therefore give the stated map, and
its displayed formula determines it uniquely.

attrs.title: Well-definedness of the extended-ideal chart map

objects.body:
Let $Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion and let $X'\to X$ be a
blow-up. Blowing up $Z$ in the pulled-back center gives the strict transform
of $Z$ in $X'$. Strict transforms computed inside $Z$ and inside $X$ agree
under the induced closed immersion.

## Proof

By [thm-nagata-strict-transform-is-blowup], the strict transform is the
blow-up of $Z$ in the extended center ideal. On an affine chart
$X=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ with $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(B)$, the induced
map to $Z\times_XX'$ is the quotient map
$B\otimes_AA[I/a]\twoheadrightarrow B\otimes_AA[I/a]/\Gamma_{(a)}$. The target chart of the blow-up of $Z$ is
identified with this quotient by
[prop-nagata-strict-transform-chart-iso]. It is therefore precisely
the closed immersion of the closed chart model. These identifications
commute with localization and agree on overlaps by
[prop-nagata-strict-transform-closed-fiber-product]; gluing proves
equality of the two global closed subschemes, as well as the claimed
compatibility with the induced closed immersion.

**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the strict transform is
supplied by the API of
`WeilConjectures/Compactification/StrictTransform.lean` —
`AlgebraicGeometry.strictTransform`, its closed immersion
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.isClosedImmersion_pullbackLift_blowup_comap`,
and the pullback square
`AlgebraicGeometry.isPullback_strictTransformOpen` — so the
strict-transform chart rings and their cocycle are never assembled by hand.

The quotient map
$C_a(A,B,I)\to C_a^{\mathrm{st}}(A,B,I)$ defines a closed immersion of
the strict-transform chart into the ordinary base-change chart.

## Proof

The power-torsion subset is an ideal by
[lemma-nagata-power-torsion-submodule], applied to the regular module
$C_a(A,B,I)$. The spectrum of a quotient ring is a closed subscheme.

**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the strict transform is
supplied by the API of
`WeilConjectures/Compactification/StrictTransform.lean` —
`AlgebraicGeometry.strictTransform`, its closed immersion
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.isClosedImmersion_pullbackLift_blowup_comap`,
and the pullback square
`AlgebraicGeometry.isPullback_strictTransformOpen` — so the
strict-transform chart rings and their cocycle are never assembled by hand.

The localized strict-transform chart comparisons agree on double
localizations and satisfy the cocycle equality on triple chart overlaps.

## Proof

On an intersection of the $a$- and $a'$-charts, choose a basic affine
refinement on which both chart restrictions are defined. The ordinary
blow-up transition is the specified localization isomorphism; by
[lemma-nagata-affine-blowup-restrict-cocycle] its two composites on a
triple refinement agree. Localizing the quotient map
$C_a\twoheadrightarrow C_a^{\mathrm{st}}$ gives the quotient by the
localized power-torsion ideal, by
[lemma-nagata-strict-transform-chart-localization-data]. Thus the
ordinary transition descends uniquely to a transition of strict-transform
chart rings. The descended maps agree with the comparisons constructed
after localization by
[lemma-nagata-strict-transform-chart-localization]. On a triple
refinement their two composites become the same ordinary transition before
quotienting, hence are equal after quotienting. This proves both the
double-overlap compatibility and the cocycle.

The constructed localized comparison $(\overline\sigma_a)_s$ equals the
strict-transform chart comparison constructed directly from the localized
data.

## Proof

Localization commutes with the tensor product and with the power-torsion
quotient by [lemma-nagata-power-torsion-localization]. Both maps send
every pure tensor and every generator $x/a$ to the same fraction. Ring-map
extensionality gives the equality, and
[prop-nagata-strict-transform-chart-iso] supplies the equivalence
property on both sides.

For $s\in B$, the canonical map

$$
(C_a(A,B,I)/\Gamma_{(a)}C_a(A,B,I))_s
\longrightarrow
C_a(A,B_s,I)/\Gamma_{(a/1)}C_a(A,B_s,I)
$$

is an isomorphism. These isomorphisms are compatible with further
localization: the maps obtained by localizing successively at $s$ and $t$
agree with localization at $st$.

## Proof

Localization commutes with tensor products, so
$(B\otimes_A A[I/a])_s\cong B_s\otimes_A A[I/a]$. By
[lemma-nagata-power-torsion-localization], the image of the
$a$-power-torsion submodule is exactly the $a/1$-power-torsion submodule.
The universal property of quotients gives the displayed isomorphism.
Compatibility for $s,t$ follows because both composites send pure tensors
and chart fractions to the same elements of the $st$-localization.

attrs.title: Localization data for strict-transform chart quotients

objects.body:
Let $f\colon Y\to X$, let $\mathcal I$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent
ideal on $X$, put $X'=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$, and let
$U=X\setminus V(\mathcal I)$. The strict transform is the smallest
closed subscheme of $Y\times_XX'$ through which

$$
Y\times_XU\longrightarrow Y\times_XX'
$$

factors. In particular it is the scheme-theoretic closure of this open
part.

## Proof

On an $a$-chart put $C=C_a(A,B,I)$. A closed subscheme containing the
preserved open is given by a quotient $C\twoheadrightarrow C/K$ for which
$K_a=0$. By
[lemma-nagata-power-torsion-kernel-localization], this says exactly
that $K\subseteq\Gamma_{(a)}(C)$. Therefore the quotient
$C\twoheadrightarrow C/\Gamma_{(a)}(C)$ factors through every such
quotient, which is precisely the containment of the corresponding closed
subschemes in the required direction. It becomes an isomorphism after
inverting $a$, again by the kernel description. The quotient has no
residual $a$-power torsion by
[lemma-nagata-power-torsion-quotient-torsionfree], so this local
characterization is stable under further restriction. The chart
descriptions glue by
[prop-nagata-strict-transform-closed-fiber-product], proving the
asserted minimality globally.

Let $f\colon Y\to X$, let $\mathcal I$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent
ideal, and put $X'=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$. Over
$U=X\setminus V(\mathcal I)$, the strict transform is canonically
$Y\times_XU$, and its map to $Y$ is the ordinary pullback isomorphism.

## Proof

The blow-up is the identity over $U$ by
[thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement]. Under this specified
isomorphism the open whose closure defines the strict transform is all of
$Y\times_XU$. It is already a closed subscheme of itself, so the minimal
closed-subscheme characterization of
[lemma-nagata-strict-transform-closure-characterization] identifies
the restriction with $Y\times_XU$. On charts this is the quotient by the
zero torsion ideal after $a$ is inverted; these identifications agree on
overlaps by the closed chart model in
[prop-nagata-strict-transform-closed-fiber-product]. The projection
equality is the one induced by the fibre-product square.

attrs.title: Strict transform on the preserved open

objects.body:
Let $X'\to X$ be the blow-up of a center $C\hookrightarrow X$. Over
$X\setminus C$, the strict transform is canonically the ordinary pullback.
This identification is compatible with the projection to the original
scheme.

## Proof

This is exactly
[lemma-nagata-strict-transform-over-complement], applied to the ideal
defining $C$. The compatibility with the projection is part of that
canonical identification.

attrs.title: Strict transform over the complement of the center

objects.body:
The constructed structural morphism $W\to S$ is proper.

## Proof

The morphism $U_1\cap U_2\to W$ is quasi-compact and dense by
[lemma-nagata-final-density], and its valuation diagrams admit unique
lifts by [lemma-nagata-two-open-valuative-lifting]. The dense-source
valuative criterion makes $W\to S$ universally closed. It is separated
and of finite type by
[lemma-nagata-two-open-final-modification]; hence it is proper.

For $i=1,2$, the constructed $C_i$ is a scheme-theoretically dense
compactification of $U_i\to S$; in particular $X_i\to S$ is proper and
$U_i\hookrightarrow X_i$ is a quasi-compact open immersion.

## Proof

This is exactly [prop-nagata-dense-refinement], applied to each selected
compactification $C_i^0$.

attrs.title: Properties of the chosen dense compactifications

objects.body:
In the finite diagram defining $W'_1,W'_2$ and $W$, assume that $U$ is
scheme-theoretically dense in each initial ambient piece and that every
intervening blow-up is $U$-admissible. Then the induced map
$U_1\cap U_2\to W$ is quasi-compact with dense image.

## Proof

The initial copies of $U$ are scheme-theoretically dense by hypothesis.
Every graph, boundary-separation, and final modification in the displayed
diagram is $U$-admissible, so
[lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-preserves-density] identifies the
inverse image of $U$ at each stage as a scheme-theoretically dense open.
The compatibility of the chosen copies of $U$ through a finite composite is
the conclusion of
[lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-comp]. Therefore the common copy of
$U$ is dense in each of the final chart opens $W'_1$ and $W'_2$.

Let $F\subseteq W$ be closed and contain the image of
$U_1\cap U_2$. Its inverse image in each open chart $W'_i$ is closed and
contains the dense image of $U_1\cap U_2$, hence equals $W'_i$. Since the
two charts cover $W$ by
[lemma-nagata-two-open-final-modification], $F=W$, proving density.
The source $U_1\cap U_2$ is quasi-compact because $S$ is Noetherian,
$U\to S$ is of finite type, and every open subscheme of the resulting
Noetherian scheme $U$ is quasi-compact. Each map to $W'_i$ is a composite
of a quasi-compact open
immersion with finitely many blow-ups, which are quasi-compact; the finite
open cover then proves that $U_1\cap U_2\to W$ is quasi-compact.

attrs.title: Density and quasi-compactness under the finite modification diagram

objects.body:
Each $W'_i\to W_i$ is $U$-admissible; the maps $W'_i\hookrightarrow W$
are open immersions covering $W$; their copies of $U$ agree; and $W\to S$
is separated and of finite type. In particular the induced map
$j_W\colon U\to W$ is an open immersion.

*Implementation note.* There is no separate Lean declaration for this
lemma. Inside the proof of `AlgebraicGeometry.HasCompactification.of_two_open_cover`
([thm-nagata-two-open]) the assertions are read off the output of
`AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_commonModification`
([lemma-nagata-common-modification]); the open immersion $j_W$ is the local
`jW := cm.u₁ ≫ cm.k₁` there.

## Proof

The schemes $W_i$ are separated and of finite type by
[lemma-nagata-intermediate-separated]. Thus all hypotheses of the
common-modification property apply, and
[lemma-nagata-common-modification] gives every stated assertion.
The map $j_W$ is the composite of $U\hookrightarrow W'_i$ with either open
immersion $W'_i\hookrightarrow W$; the two composites coincide by the
gluing construction.

attrs.title: Structural properties of the final common modification

objects.body:
Let $A$ be a valuation ring with fraction field $K$. Every commutative
diagram whose generic map
$\operatorname{Spec}(K)\to W$ factors through $U_1\cap U_2$ has a unique
lift $\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to W$ over $S$.

## Proof

By
[lemma-nagata-proper-separated-valuation-extension], properness and
separatedness of $X_i\to S$ extend the generic map to maps
$g_i\colon\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to X_i$. By
[lemma-nagata-one-valuation-avoids-boundary], one extension factors
through $X_i\setminus\overline Z_{i,j}$ and hence through $W_i$. The
generic map already lifts to the preserved open $U\subseteq W'_i$.
The admissible blow-up $W'_i\to W_i$ is proper, hence separated, so
[lemma-nagata-proper-separated-valuation-extension] supplies a lift
to $W'_i$; its open map to $W$ gives the desired lift. Any two branch
choices have the same generic restriction. Since $W\to S$ is separated by
[lemma-nagata-two-open-final-modification],
[lemma-nagata-separated-valuation-lift-unique] makes the two maps
equal.

attrs.title: Valuative lifting for the two-open candidate

objects.body:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the finite-presentation and
Noetherian descent is done in one step by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_isPullback_of_finitePresentation_of_isSeparated`
and `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.nonempty_noetherianApproximation`, so
this stage-by-stage bookkeeping is never carried out.

The valid finite coefficient refinements occurring in
[def-nagata-noetherian-stage] are nonempty and directed under
inclusion. If $\lambda\leq\mu$, inclusion of coefficient algebras induces
compatible affine chart maps $S_\mu\to S_\lambda$; these maps satisfy the
identity and composition laws.

## Proof

The selected valid stage is one object. Given two valid refinements, take
the union of their finite coefficient lists and then a common upper bound of
the finitely many stages witnessing their gluing equations. The finite-data
lemma makes the resulting refinement valid and above both inputs. Inclusion
of coefficient rings induces the affine maps on every chart. Their
restrictions agree on overlaps by the gluing equations, so they glue; the
identity and composition laws hold chartwise and therefore globally.

attrs.title: Valid finite coefficient refinements form a directed set

objects.body:
Let $A$ be a valuation ring with fraction field $K$, let $Z\hookrightarrow Y$
be a closed immersion, and let $g\colon\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to Y$. If the
restriction of $g$ to $\operatorname{Spec}(K)$ factors through $Z$, then
$g$ factors through $Z$.

## Proof

Pull the defining ideal of $Z$ back to $A$. It becomes zero after applying
the injective map $A\hookrightarrow K$, so it was already zero in $A$.

attrs.title: Factorization through a closed subscheme over a valuation ring

objects.body:
Let $A$ be a valuation ring with fraction field $K$, let
$K\hookrightarrow L$ be a field extension, and let $B\subseteq L$ be a
valuation ring dominating the image of $A$. Then

$$
K\cap B=A
$$

inside $L$.

## Proof

The inclusion $A\subseteq K\cap B$ follows because $B$ contains the image
of $A$. Conversely, let $x\in K\cap B$. If $x\notin A$, the valuation-ring
property of $A$ gives $x^{-1}\in A$, and in fact
$x^{-1}\in\mathfrak m_A$: otherwise $x^{-1}$ would be a unit of $A$ and
$x$ would belong to $A$. Since $B$ dominates $A$, the image of
$\mathfrak m_A$ lies in $\mathfrak m_B$. But $x\in B$ and
$x^{-1}\in\mathfrak m_B$ would imply
$1=xx^{-1}\in\mathfrak m_B$, a contradiction. Thus $x\in A$, proving
$K\cap B\subseteq A$ and hence the asserted equality.

attrs.title: Intersection with a dominating valuation ring

objects.body:
Let $A$ be a valuation ring and let $O\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ be
open. If the closed point $\mathfrak m_A$ belongs to $O$, then
$O=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$.

## Proof

Choose a basic open $D(a)$ with $\mathfrak m_A\in D(a)\subseteq O$.
Then $a\notin\mathfrak m_A$, hence $a$ is a unit of the local ring $A$ and
$D(a)=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$.

attrs.title: An open containing the closed point of a valuation spectrum is total

objects.body:
Let $A$ be a valuation ring with fraction field $K$. Suppose
$\operatorname{Spec}(K)\to U_1\cap U_2$ is an $S$-morphism and let
$g_i\colon\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to X_i$ be extensions. Then the pair

$$
(g_1,g_2)\colon\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to X_1\times_SX_2
$$

factors through $X_{12}$.

## Proof

The two generic maps have the same image in $U$, so their pair lands in
$V_1\times_UV_2=V_{12}$. Composing with the canonical image-factor map
gives a factorization of the generic pair through $X_{12}$. The map
$A\to K$ is injective because a valuation ring is a domain. Apply
[lemma-nagata-valuation-factor-closed] to the closed immersion
$X_{12}\hookrightarrow X_1\times_SX_2$ and the morphism
$(g_1,g_2)\colon\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to X_1\times_SX_2$. It extends the
generic factorization to all of $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$.

attrs.title: The pair of valuation extensions factors through $X_{12}$

objects.body:
Let $A$ be a valuation ring with fraction field $K$, and let
$K\hookrightarrow L$ be a field extension. There exists a valuation ring
$B\subseteq L$ with fraction field $L$ which dominates $A$. In Lean the
conclusion is recorded in the combined form $K\cap B=A$ of
[lemma-nagata-valuation-intersection], from which the domination is
recovered.

## Proof

Apply Stacks Project, Tag 00IA (Lemma 10.50.2), to the inclusion
$K\hookrightarrow L$. Its proof considers the partially ordered set of
local subrings of $L$ containing $A$ and dominating $A$; a chain union is
again such a local subring, so Zorn gives a maximal one. If its fraction
field is smaller than $L$, choose $t$ outside that fraction field. In the
transcendental case, localizing $A[t]$ at the prime generated by $t$ and
$\mathfrak m_A$ gives a strictly larger dominating local subring. In the
algebraic case, choose $0\ne a\in A$ with $at$ integral over $A$, choose a
prime over $\mathfrak m_A$ in the finite algebra $A[at]$, and localize
there; this again contradicts maximality. Hence the maximal subring has
fraction field $L$. The same maximality argument applied to $x$ and
$x^{-1}$ for every $0\ne x\in L$ proves that it is a valuation ring, and
its maximal ideal contracts to $\mathfrak m_A$, so it dominates $A$.

attrs.title: Extension of a valuation ring to a field extension, [stacks-project]

objects.body:
Let $f\colon X\to Y$ be separated, quasi-compact, locally quasi-finite and
locally of finite type. Then $f$ factors as

$$
X\xrightarrow{\;j\;}W\xrightarrow{\;g\;}Y,\qquad g\circ j=f,
$$

with $j$ an open immersion and $g$ an affine morphism.

## Proof

This is Grothendieck's form of Zariski's Main Theorem, available in Mathlib
as `Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/ZariskisMainTheorem.lean`. Take $W$ to
be the relative normalization of $Y$ in $X$, $j$ the canonical morphism
$X\to W$ and $g$ the structure morphism $W\to Y$. Zariski's Main Theorem
says that $j$ is an open immersion under exactly these hypotheses, and $g$ is
integral, hence affine, by construction of the relative normalization.

attrs.title: Zariski's Main Theorem as a factorization

objects.body:
Let $f\colon X\to Y$ be separated, quasi-compact, locally quasi-finite and
locally of finite type, and suppose $Y$ is quasi-affine. Then $X$ is
quasi-affine.

## Proof

Write $f=g\circ j$ with $j\colon X\to W$ an open immersion and $g\colon W\to Y$ affine, using
[lemma-nagata-zmt-open-immersion-affine-factorization]. An affine
morphism to a quasi-affine scheme has quasi-affine source, so $W$ is
quasi-affine. Moreover $X$ is quasi-compact, since $f$ is quasi-compact and
$Y$ is quasi-compact. So $X$ is a quasi-compact locally closed subscheme of
the quasi-affine scheme $W$, and such a subscheme is quasi-affine (Stacks Tag
0BCK).

attrs.title: A quasi-finite scheme over a quasi-affine base is quasi-affine

objects.body:
Let $i\colon Z\to X$ be a closed immersion, let $q\colon W\to Z$ be étale
and let $w\in W$. Then there are an open subscheme $W_0\subseteq W$
containing $w$, a scheme $V$ étale over $X$, and an isomorphism of
$Z$-schemes

$$
W_0\cong V\times_XZ.
$$

In the pointed form used below, if $\bar w\colon\Spec\Omega\to W$ is a point
of $W$ with values in a field, then there are a scheme $V$ étale over $X$
and a morphism $V\times_XZ\to W$ of $Z$-schemes through which $\bar w$
factors: apply the above at the image point of $\bar w$ and compose the
isomorphism with the open immersion $W_0\subseteq W$.

## Proof

The assertion is local at $w$, so we may shrink $X$, $Z$ and $W$ around
$i(q(w))$ and $w$. Choose an affine open $\Spec R\subseteq X$ containing
$i(q(w))$; then $Z$ meets it in $\Spec R/I$, and we may choose an affine open
$\Spec B\subseteq W$ containing $w$ and lying over $\Spec R/I$, so that $B$
is an étale $R/I$-algebra.

By the local structure of étale algebras, after replacing $\Spec B$ by a
basic open subscheme containing $w$ we may assume that $B$ is a standard
étale $R/I$-algebra. By
[lemma-openclosed-standard-etale-lift] there is a standard étale
$R$-algebra $A$ with $(R/I)\otimes_RA\cong B$. Put
$V:=\Spec A$, mapping to $X$ through $\Spec A\to\Spec R\subseteq X$; this is
étale, being an étale morphism followed by an open immersion. Finally

$$
V\times_XZ=\Spec A\times_{\Spec R}\Spec R/I=\Spec\bigl((R/I)\otimes_RA\bigr)
\cong\Spec B=:W_0,
$$

which is an open subscheme of $W$ containing $w$.

attrs.title: Étale morphisms lift locally along a closed immersion

objects.body:
Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a site and let $p$ be a point of it: a stalk functor
$\shv{\mathcal C}\to\mathrm{Type}\,w$ that preserves finite limits and all
colimits. Then composing the fibre functor with the universe-raising
equivalence $\mathrm{Type}\,w\to\mathrm{Type}\,\max(w,w')$ is again a point of
$(\mathcal C,J)$, and its stalks are the old ones up to that equivalence.

Applied to $\et X$: the raised family of geometric points of $\et X$ is a
conservative family of points at the universe of the coefficients. Concretely,
a morphism of sheaves on $\et X$ with values in $\mathcal A$ is an
isomorphism as soon as it is an isomorphism on the stalk at every geometric
point of $X$.

## Proof

Universe raising is an equivalence of categories which preserves and reflects
all limits and colimits, so composing with it preserves every property in the
definition of a point. The stalk functors of the raised point are the old
ones followed by an equivalence, hence detect exactly the same
isomorphisms.

For the second statement, conservativity of a family of points is checked
against a covering-sieve criterion: a family is conservative as soon as every
sieve $S$ on an object $V$ whose associated subobject of the sheaf represented
by $V$ has full stalk at every point of the family is a covering sieve. That
criterion mentions no fibre universe, so the proof of
conservativity for the geometric points of $\et X$ at the universe of schemes
transcribes verbatim to the raised family. What is used about $\et X$ is
that for a scheme $V$ étale over $X$ and a point $v\in V$ there is a
geometric point of $X$ through which $v$ is visible; this is the existence of
enough geometric points on the small étale site.

Let $i\colon Z\to X$ be a closed immersion, let $\bar z$ be a geometric point
of $Z$ and write $\bar x:=i\circ\bar z$ for the corresponding geometric point
of $X$. Then the base-change functor

$$
\Phi\colon\mathrm N(\bar x)\to\mathrm N(\bar z),
\qquad(V,\bar v)\mapsto(V\times_XZ,\bar z),
$$

on the categories $\mathrm N(\bar x)$, $\mathrm N(\bar z)$ of pointed étale
neighbourhoods is initial. Consequently, for every
$\mathcal H\in\shv{\et Z}$,

$$
(i_*\mathcal H)_{\bar x}\cong\mathcal H_{\bar z},
$$

naturally in $\mathcal H$.

## Proof

Write $\mathrm N(\bar x)$ for the cofiltered category of étale
neighbourhoods $(V,\bar v)$ of $\bar x$ in $\et X$ and $\mathrm N(\bar z)$
for that of $\bar z$ in $\et Z$. By the formula for $i_*$,

$$
(i_*\mathcal H)_{\bar x}
=\colim_{(V,\bar v)\in\mathrm N(\bar x)^{\mathrm{op}}}(i_*\mathcal H)(V)
=\colim_{(V,\bar v)\in\mathrm N(\bar x)^{\mathrm{op}}}
\mathcal H(V\times_XZ),
$$

so the displayed isomorphism is the comparison of colimits induced by
$\Phi$, and it suffices to prove that $\Phi$ is initial.

No connectedness argument is written by hand. Both $\mathrm N(\bar x)$ and
$\mathrm N(\bar z)$ are cofiltered, being categories of étale
neighbourhoods of a point, and for a functor between cofiltered categories
initiality follows from the two conditions:

1. every object $d$ of $\mathrm N(\bar z)$ is dominated: there is an object
$c$ of $\mathrm N(\bar x)$ and a morphism $\Phi(c)\to d$;
1. any two morphisms $\sigma,\sigma'\colon\Phi(c)\to d$ are equalised
after precomposing with $\Phi(\tau)$ for some
$\tau\colon c'\to c$ in $\mathrm N(\bar x)$.

Only these two are proved.

*Domination.* This is [lemma-openclosed-etale-lifts-locally] in its
pointed form, applied to $W\to Z$ and $\bar w$ for $d=(W,\bar w)$: it produces
$V$ étale over $X$ and a $Z$-morphism $V\times_XZ\to W$ through which
$\bar w$ factors. The factorisation supplies the lift $\bar v$ of $\bar x$ to
$V$, so $c=(V,\bar v)$ is an object of $\mathrm N(\bar x)$ and the morphism is
one of pointed étale neighbourhoods $\Phi(c)\to d$.

*Equalisation.* Let $\sigma,\sigma'\colon\Phi(V,\bar v)=V\times_XZ\to W$
be two morphisms of pointed étale neighbourhoods; both send the marked point
$p$ of $V\times_XZ$ to the marked point of $W$, and both are morphisms over
$Z$. Now $W\to Z$ is étale, hence unramified, so its diagonal is an open
immersion and the locus in $V\times_XZ$ where two $Z$-morphisms into $W$ agree
is open; it contains $p$ because $\sigma$ and $\sigma'$ agree there. Finally
$V\times_XZ\to V$ is a closed immersion, hence inducing on the underlying
spaces, so that agreement locus is the trace of an open subscheme
$V_0\subseteq V$, which contains the marked point of $V$. Then
$c'=(V_0,\bar v)$ is again an object of $\mathrm N(\bar x)$ and the inclusion
$\tau\colon c'\to c$ has $\Phi(\tau)$ landing in the agreement locus, so
$\Phi(\tau)\circ\sigma=\Phi(\tau)\circ\sigma'$.

The second condition is precisely where the shrinking that
[rmk-openclosed-no-dense-subsite] says is unavailable to the
dense-subsite argument is harmless: in a colimit over neighbourhoods one is
allowed to pass to $V_0$. Note also that the fibre product $V_1\times_XV_2$ of
two neighbourhoods, which a hand-written connectedness argument would have to
construct, is exactly what the cofilteredness of $\mathrm N(\bar x)$ supplies.

Let $f\colon Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes, let $\bar y$ be a geometric
point of $Y$ and let $\mathcal F\in\shv{\et X}$. Then

$$
(f^*\mathcal F)_{\bar y}\cong\mathcal F_{f\circ\bar y},
$$

naturally in $\mathcal F$.

## Proof

The functor $f^*$ is the pullback of sheaves along the morphism of sites
given by base change $\et X\to\et Y$, $V\mapsto V\times_XY$. Pulling a point
of $\et Y$ back along a morphism of sites gives a point of $\et X$, and the
stalk of a pulled-back sheaf at a point is by construction the stalk of the
sheaf at the transported point. It remains to identify the transport of the
geometric point $\bar y$ along base change with the geometric point
$f\circ\bar y$ of $X$. This is the universal property of the fibre product:
for $V\in\et X$, lifting $\bar y$ to $V\times_XY$ is the same as lifting
$f\circ\bar y$ to $V$, so the two points have the same étale neighbourhoods
and hence the same stalk functor.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $I\subseteq R$ an ideal. Recall that a
*standard étale pair* over a ring $S$ is a pair of polynomials
$(f,g)$ in $S[T]$ with $f$ monic and $g^n\in(f',f)$ for some $n$, and that
its algebra is $S[T][1/g]/(f)$, which is étale over $S$.

Let $(\bar f,\bar g)$ be a standard étale pair over $R/I$. Then there is a
standard étale pair $(F,H)$ over $R$ and an isomorphism of $R/I$-algebras

$$
(R/I)\otimes_R\bigl(R[T][1/H]/(F)\bigr)
\cong(R/I)[T][1/\bar g]/(\bar f).
$$

In words: every standard étale algebra over $R/I$ is the base change of a
standard étale algebra over $R$.

## Proof

No witness of the standard-étale condition is lifted; lifting one naively
does not work, since a lift of the identity witnessing the condition only
holds modulo $I$. Instead the pair over $R$ is chosen so that the condition
holds for free, using two observations.

*For a monic $f$ and an arbitrary $g$, the pair $(f,g\cdot f')$ is
standard étale.* Indeed $f'$ divides $(g f')^1$, so the condition
$g^n\in(f',f)$ holds with $n=1$ and the witness $(g,0)$.

*Replacing $g$ by $g\cdot f'$ does not change the algebra:*

$$
S[T][1/(g f')]/(f)\cong S[T][1/g]/(f),
$$

because $f'$ is already invertible in $S[T][1/g]/(f)$ — that is exactly the
standard-étale condition for $(f,g)$ — so inverting it again changes
nothing. Formally, the image of $T$ on either side satisfies the universal
property of the other standard étale algebra, and the two induced maps are
mutually inverse.

Now lift $\bar f$ to a monic $F\in R[T]$ of the same degree, lift $\bar g$ to
an *arbitrary* $G\in R[T]$, and put $H:=G\cdot F'$. By the first
observation $(F,H)$ is a standard étale pair over $R$, and the algebra of a
standard étale pair base changes to the algebra of the pair with reduced
coefficients. The reduction of $(F,H)$ along $R\to R/I$ is
$(\bar f,\bar g\cdot\bar f')$, whose algebra is $(R/I)[T][1/\bar g]/(\bar f)$
by the second observation. That is the asserted isomorphism.

attrs.title: Lifting a standard étale algebra along a quotient

objects.body:
In the situation of [lemma-openclosed-vanishing-lowerstar],
$i^*j_!\mathcal G=0$ for every $\mathcal G\in\shv{\et U}$.

## Proof

The point of the argument is that no section of $j_!\mathcal G$ is computed:
$j_!$ is a sheafification and its sections are not accessible. Instead one
uses only adjunctions. For every $\mathcal H\in\shv{\et Z}$,

$$
\Hom(i^*j_!\mathcal G,\mathcal H)
\cong\Hom(j_!\mathcal G,i_*\mathcal H)
\cong\Hom(\mathcal G,j^*i_*\mathcal H)=0
$$

by [lemma-openclosed-vanishing-lowerstar]. Taking
$\mathcal H=i^*j_!\mathcal G$ shows that the identity of
$i^*j_!\mathcal G$ is zero, that is, $i^*j_!\mathcal G=0$.

Let $j\colon U\to X$ and $i\colon Z\to X$ have disjoint ranges, with $j$ an
open immersion. Then $j^*i_*\mathcal H=0$ for every
$\mathcal H\in\shv{\et Z}$.

## Proof

For an open immersion $j$ the functor $j^*$ is restriction along the
base-change functor $\et X\to\et U$, so for $T\in\et U$, regarded as an
object of $\et X$ through $j$,

$$
(j^*i_*\mathcal H)(T)=(i_*\mathcal H)(T)=\mathcal H(T\times_XZ).
$$

The structure morphism $T\to X$ factors through $j$, so its range is
contained in that of $j$ and hence disjoint from that of $i$; a fibre product
of two morphisms with disjoint ranges is empty
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isEmpty_pullback` in Mathlib: a point of
$V\times_XW$ gives a point of $X$ in both ranges), so $T\times_XZ$ is empty.
The
sheaf condition for the empty covering of the empty scheme says that
$\mathcal H(\emptyset)$ is a terminal object, and in an additive category a
terminal object is a zero object. A sheaf all of whose sections are zero is
a zero object of $\shv{\et U}$.

For every $a\geq1$, projection to level $a$ induces a functorial
isomorphism

$$
\left(R\varprojlim_nK_n\right)\otimes^L_\Lambda P_a
\xrightarrow{\sim}K_a.
$$

## Proof

Use the preceding comparison to replace the quotient tower by
$K\otimes^LQ_m$. Since $P_a$ is perfect, tensoring with $P_a$ commutes
with both products in the product-cone model. For $m\geq a$, the
differential of $Q_m\otimes^L P_a$ is zero. Its degree-zero transition is
the identity, whereas every composite of $a$ successive transitions in a
negative degree contains a factor $f_j^a\in I^a$ and is zero over $P_a$.
Thus the negative-degree towers are pro-zero and the degree-zero tower is
the constant tower $P_a$. After tensoring with $K$, its product-cone limit
is $K\otimes^LP_a=K_a$. The surviving degree-zero projection is precisely
the displayed map. This also exposes the finite Tor-amplitude input: the
bounded finite-projective complex representing $P_a$ is what permits it to
pass through the two countable products.

The full subcategory $\mathcal N^{\mathrm{aff}}_{\bar s}$ of affine pointed
etale neighbourhoods is initial in $\mathcal N_{\bar s}$ and hence cofinal
for the opposite-indexed stalk colimit.

## Proof

Given $(V,\bar v)$, choose an affine open $V_0\subseteq V$ containing the
image of $\bar v$; then $(V_0,\bar v)\to(V,\bar v)$ is a morphism. Given two
affine refinements, their fibre product over $V$ contains the lifted geometric
point; an affine open around that point refines both. These two facts give
nonemptiness and connectedness of every comma category required for
initiality.

## Detailed form

The full subcategory of affine [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] pointed
etale neighborhoods is initial in $\mathcal N_{\bar s}$ of
[def-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods], hence cofinal for the
opposite-indexed stalk colimit.

## Proof

Given $(V,\bar v)$, an affine open $V_0\subseteq V$ containing the image of
$\bar v$ gives a morphism $(V_0,\bar v)\to(V,\bar v)$; given two affine
refinements, an affine open of their fibre product around the lifted point
refines both. These two facts are exactly the nonemptiness and connectedness
of the comma categories required for initiality in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods].

Let $f:X\to Y$ be proper and surjective and $h:Y\to Z$ proper. If $f$ and
$hf$ satisfy $\mathsf{IA}$, then $h$ satisfies $\mathsf{IA}$.

## Proof

Fix a base change $a:Z'\to Z$ and an injective $\mathbf F_\ell$-module sheaf
$I$ on $Y$. Choose a
monomorphism $f^{-1}I\hookrightarrow J$ with $J$ injective on $X$. Applying
$f_*$ gives $\iota:I\to f_*J$. If a germ $a\in I_{\bar y}$ maps to zero,
choose a geometric $\bar x\to X$ above $\bar y$ (surjectivity). The canonical
stalk identification $(f^{-1}I)_{\bar x}\cong I_{\bar y}$ sends $a$ to the
germ of $a$ at $\bar x$; the monomorphism into $J$ makes that germ zero. The
definition of the direct-image stalk then says that $a$ vanishes on an etale
neighbourhood of $\bar y$, so $a=0$. Thus $\iota$ is monic. Injectivity of $I$ supplies a retraction
$r:f_*J\to I$ with $r\circ\iota=\mathrm{id}_I$, making $I$ a direct summand.
After base change, proper underived exchange gives
$b^{-1}f_*J\cong f'_*a_X^{-1}J$. The spectral sequence

$$
R^ph'_*R^qf'_*a_Y^{-1}I\Longrightarrow R^{p+q}(h'f')_*a_X^{-1}I
$$

is computed using the injective $J$ and the assumed acyclicity of $hf$.
The $q>0$ terms vanish for $J$ by $\mathsf{IA}(f)$, and total-degree
vanishing for $hf$ forces $R^ph'_*a_Y^{-1}(f_*J)=0$ for $p>0$. Derived
direct image preserves finite direct sums and retracts, so the same vanishing
holds for the direct summand $a_Y^{-1}I$. This is Tag `0A4C`; the
stalk injectivity argument is written here because surjectivity is essential.

## Detailed form

Let $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{h}Z$ be proper, with $f$ surjective. If
$\mathrm{PBC}(f)$ and $\mathrm{PBC}(hf)$ hold, then $\mathrm{PBC}(h)$ holds.

## Proof

$\mathrm{PBC}(h)$ is equivalent to $\mathrm{IA}(h)$, so we prove
$\mathrm{IA}(h)$. Fix a base change $c:Z'\to Z$, write $Y'=Y\times_ZZ'$,
$X'=X\times_ZZ'$ with projections $b$, $a$, and base-changed maps $f'$, $h'$,
and fix a prime $r$ and an injective $\mathbf F_r$-module sheaf $I$ on $Y$. By
[lem-weil-pbc-retract-supplied], $b^{-1}I$ is a direct summand of
$b^{-1}f_*J$ for a suitable injective $J$ on $X$. The underived proper
exchange identifies $b^{-1}f_*J$ with $f'_*a^{-1}J$; $\mathrm{IA}_r(f)$ and
$\mathrm{IA}_r(hf)$ kill the higher direct images of $a^{-1}J$ along $f'$ and
$h'f'$, so the spectral sequence of
[lem-weil-pbc-grothendieck-spectral-sequence] collapses to the $q=0$ row and
yields $R^ph'_*(f'_*a^{-1}J)=0$ for $p>0$. Via the exchange identification
this is the vanishing for $b^{-1}f_*J$, and
[lem-weil-pbc-vanishing-descends-retract] descends it to the retract
$b^{-1}I$, proving $\mathrm{IA}_r(h)$.

Let $\iota_Y:X'\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_Y$ be the closed immersion and
$\pi:X'\to X$ the Chow modification. Then

$$
\iota_X=(\pi,\iota_Y):X'\longrightarrow
X\times_Y\mathbf P^n_Y=\mathbf P^n_X
$$

is a closed immersion over $X$.

## Proof

The identification $\mathbf P^n_X=X\times_Y\mathbf P^n_Y$ is the defining fibre-product
identity ([lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-pullback]), so the pair $\iota_X=(\pi,\iota_Y)$ is a morphism over $X$ by construction, and
composing it with the base change $\mathbf P^n_X\to\mathbf P^n_Y$ of $f$ gives back
$\iota_Y$. That base change is separated, because $f$ is separated and separatedness is
stable under base change. A morphism whose composite with a separated morphism is a closed
immersion is itself a closed immersion; hence $\iota_X$ is a closed immersion.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] morphism with
$Y$ affine. There exist a proper surjection $\pi:\widetilde X\to X$, an
integer $n\geq0$, and a closed immersion

$$
 i:\widetilde X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_Y
$$

with $f\circ\pi=p\circ i$, where $p:\mathbf P^n_Y\to Y$ is the structure
morphism. No noetherian or finite-presentation hypothesis is imposed on $Y$ or
$f$. The assertion is stable under base change on $Y$: for any morphism
$Y'\to Y$ the pulled-back data are such data for $X\times_YY'\to Y'$.

(For $Y$ noetherian this is also [cor-chow-lemma-proper], which moreover makes
$\pi$ an isomorphism over a dense open subscheme of $X$.)

## Proof

Here $\mathbf P^n_S$ denotes $\mathbf P(\{0,\dots,n\};S)$ of
[def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Since it is defined as
$S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$, associativity
of fibre products gives, for every morphism $S'\to S$, a canonical isomorphism
$\mathbf P^n_S\times_SS'=\mathbf P^n_{S'}$ over $S'$; and
$\mathbf P^n_S\to S$ is proper, in particular separated, by
[lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper]. We also use freely that
proper morphisms, surjective morphisms, immersions and closed immersions are
stable under base change (for properness this is
[lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]), and that a closed immersion followed by an
immersion is an immersion.

*Step 1: a separated finitely presented envelope.* The scheme $Y$ is affine,
hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and $f$ is separated and of finite
type. By [prop-nagata-finite-type-closed-in-fp] the envelope
$\mathsf{Env}_{\mathrm{fp}}(X/Y)=(X^{\mathrm{fp}},i^{\mathrm{fp}})$ of
[def-nagata-finite-type-closed-in-fp] consists of a separated $Y$-scheme
$g:X^{\mathrm{fp}}\to Y$ of finite presentation and a closed immersion
$i^{\mathrm{fp}}:X\hookrightarrow X^{\mathrm{fp}}$ over $Y$, so
$g\circ i^{\mathrm{fp}}=f$. (The scheme $X^{\mathrm{fp}}$ need not be proper
over $Y$; only $X$ is.)

*Step 2: a noetherian model of the envelope.* Apply the descended model of
[def-nagata-final-descended-model] to the separated finitely presented
morphism $g$. By [lemma-nagata-final-descended-model] this gives a noetherian
scheme $Y_0$ (a member of the noetherian approximation system of $Y$), a
morphism $Y\to Y_0$, a separated morphism of finite presentation
$g_0:X^{\mathrm{fp}}_0\to Y_0$, and an isomorphism of $Y$-schemes

$$
 \epsilon:X^{\mathrm{fp}}_0\times_{Y_0}Y\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }X^{\mathrm{fp}}.
$$

*Step 3: Chow's lemma on the model.* The morphism $g_0$ is separated and of
finite type over the noetherian scheme $Y_0$, so [thm-chow-lemma] supplies an
integer $n\geq0$, a proper surjective morphism
$\pi_0:X'_0\to X^{\mathrm{fp}}_0$ and an immersion
$i_0:X'_0\to\mathbf P^n_{Y_0}$ of $Y_0$-schemes, i.e.
$g_0\circ\pi_0=p_0\circ i_0$ with $p_0:\mathbf P^n_{Y_0}\to Y_0$.

*Step 4: base change to $Y$.* Put $X'':=X'_0\times_{Y_0}Y$ and let
$\pi'':=\epsilon\circ(\pi_0\times_{Y_0}\operatorname{id}_Y):X''\to
X^{\mathrm{fp}}$ and
$i'':=i_0\times_{Y_0}\operatorname{id}_Y:X''\to\mathbf P^n_{Y_0}\times_{Y_0}Y
=\mathbf P^n_Y$. Then $\pi''$ is proper and surjective, $i''$ is an
immersion, and both are morphisms over $Y$, so that
$g\circ\pi''=p\circ i''$ (base change of the identity of Step 3).

*Step 5: restriction to $X$.* Define $\widetilde X$ as the preimage of the
closed subscheme $X$ under $\pi''$:

$$
 \widetilde X:=X''\times_{X^{\mathrm{fp}}}X,
 \qquad \pi:=\operatorname{pr}_2:\widetilde X\to X,
 \qquad k:=\operatorname{pr}_1:\widetilde X\hookrightarrow X'',
$$

the fibre product being formed with $\pi''$ and $i^{\mathrm{fp}}$. Then $\pi$
is the base change of $\pi''$ along $i^{\mathrm{fp}}$, hence proper and
surjective, and $k$ is the base change of the closed immersion
$i^{\mathrm{fp}}$ along $\pi''$, hence a closed immersion. Set
$i:=i''\circ k:\widetilde X\to\mathbf P^n_Y$, an immersion. It is a morphism
over $Y$ with

$$
 p\circ i=p\circ i''\circ k=g\circ\pi''\circ k
 =g\circ i^{\mathrm{fp}}\circ\pi=f\circ\pi,
$$

using the cartesian square $\pi''\circ k=i^{\mathrm{fp}}\circ\pi$.

*Step 6: $i$ is a closed immersion.* The composite $f\circ\pi$ is proper by
[lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition], since $\pi$ and $f$ are proper. So
$\widetilde X$ is proper over $Y$, and $i$ is a $Y$-morphism to the separated
$Y$-scheme $\mathbf P^n_Y$; by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-to-separated] the morphism
$i$ is proper. A proper immersion is a closed immersion
[lem-weil-pbc-proper-immersion-closed]. Hence $(\pi,n,i)$ has all the required
properties.

*Step 7: base-change stability.* Given such data $(\pi,n,i)$ for $f$ and any
morphism $Y'\to Y$, the base changes
$\pi\times_Y Y':\widetilde X\times_YY'\to X\times_YY'$ and
$i\times_YY':\widetilde X\times_YY'\to\mathbf P^n_Y\times_YY'=\mathbf
P^n_{Y'}$ are a proper surjection and a closed immersion, and the identity
$f\circ\pi=p\circ i$ of morphisms over $Y$ base changes to the corresponding
identity over $Y'$. $\square$

## Remark

The proof never descends $X$ itself: when $f$ is not of finite presentation
no descent $X=X_0\times_{Y_0}Y$ need exist. Only the separated finitely presented
envelope $X^{\mathrm{fp}}$ is descended, Chow's lemma is applied to its
noetherian model, which is merely separated of finite type, and properness of
the resulting closed immersion is recovered on $X$ in Step 6.

The completed exchange map is natural in $K$, is the identity for identity
squares, and commutes with horizontal and vertical pasting.

## Proof

At every finite level these equations are the S0/S8 equations. They commute
with the tower transitions by naturality of coefficient reduction. Apply
$R\varprojlim$ to each equality and conjugate by the same reconstruction,
projection-formula, and direct-image/limit isomorphisms used in the definition.
The resulting equations are precisely the completed equations.

## Detailed form

Completed exchange of [def-weil-pbc-completed-base-change-map] is
natural in $K$, equals the identity for identity squares, and satisfies
horizontal and vertical pasting after the canonical associativity
isomorphisms.

*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states these coherence properties of
the completed exchange: Theorem 61.30.1 ([Tag
09C9](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C9)) asserts only that the
base-change map is an isomorphism, Lemma 61.20.2 ([Tag
099N](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099N)) gives the functoriality of
$Lf^*_{comp}$ and of $Rf_*$ alone, and the nearest recorded coherence of the
two ingredients is the commutativity of the projection formula with the base
change map, Remark 21.50.2 ([Tag
0E48](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0E48)), stated for a single
square of ringed topoi without coefficients or completion. The blueprint
adds naturality in $K$, the identity-square statement and horizontal and
vertical pasting for the completed exchange.

## Proof

The finite-level reductions of [lemma-weil-pbc-completed-map-reduction]
satisfy the identity and pasting laws of the exchange identity-and-pasting
lemma levelwise, and the tower morphisms preserve these compatible
equalities, so the completed map of
[def-weil-pbc-completed-base-change-map] inherits them.

For every Frobenius-equivariant square and Weil tower datum,

$$
\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{comp}}_{\square,K}\Theta_S
=\Theta_T\Phi_{Y'}
(\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{comp}}_{\square,K}):
\Phi_{Y'}S\longrightarrow T.
$$

If all four Frobenius automorphisms and all pullback/exchange comparisons are
identities, then $\vartheta_n$ is an ordinary compatible endomorphism and
this equation specializes exactly to the operator naturality of the finite
rectangle and its product-cone limit. For nonidentity Frobenius, no
identification of $\Phi_XK_n\to K_n$ with an endomorphism $K_n\to K_n$ is
made.

## Proof

Using the displayed definitions and cancelling $s^{-1}s$ and $t^{-1}t$,
the left side is

$$
tW\Theta_{A,\infty}\Phi_{Y'}(s),
$$

whereas the right side is

$$
t\Theta_{D,\infty}\Phi_{Y'}(W)\Phi_{Y'}(s).
$$

They are equal by the product-cone Frobenius equation. When every
$\Phi_Z$ is the identity, the four formulas defining $\Theta_{Z,n}$ become
the endomorphisms induced from $\vartheta_n$ and the equation just proved is
the fibrewise limit of the equations in operator naturality. This proves
the specialization statement without using it to type the genuine
Frobenius case.

attrs.title: Completed proper base change is Frobenius-equivariant

objects.body:
For every $n$, the diagram

$$
\begin{CD}
S\otimes^LP_n @>{\overline\xi_n}>> T\otimes^LP_n\\
@V{\alpha_n}V{\sim}V @VV{\delta_n}V{\sim}\\
B_n @>{v'_n}>> D_n
\end{CD}
$$

commutes. Hence reduction of
$\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{comp}}_{\square,K}$ modulo $I^n$, conjugated
by the displayed canonical reduction isomorphisms, is exactly the S8
transported finite-level exchange map $v'_n=\operatorname{Ex}_{\square,K_n}$.
The squares for $n+1\to n$ commute, and the assertion is natural for
compatible tower endomorphisms. Under a Frobenius-equivariant datum, use
$\Phi_{Y'}P_n=P_n$ to give the two reductions their induced Weil structures.
Then

$$
\begin{aligned}
\alpha_n(\Theta_S\otimes1)
&=\Theta_{B,n}\Phi_{Y'}(\alpha_n),\\
\delta_n(\Theta_T\otimes1)
&=\Theta_{D,n}\Phi_{Y'}(\delta_n),
\end{aligned}
$$

and the displayed reduction square is a square of Weil objects.

## Proof

Under $S=A_\infty$ and the direct-image completion identification
$T\simeq C_\infty$, the completed exchange map is both limit composites

$$
V'H=H'V:A_\infty\longrightarrow D_\infty,
$$

followed by the inverse of direct-image/limit commutation. More explicitly,
if $d:T\to D_\infty$ is direct-image/limit commutation and
$c:C_\infty\to T$ is direct-image completion, then its construction gives
$dc=H'$. Functorial finite
reduction and the component equations of the limit rectangle give

$$
\tau_n\overline\xi_n=v_n\sigma_n.
$$

Consequently the two composites around the completed reduction square are

$$
\delta_n\overline\xi_n
=h'_n\tau_n\overline\xi_n=h'_nv_n\sigma_n
$$

and

$$
v'_n\alpha_n=v'_nh_n\sigma_n.
$$

They are equal term by term because $h'_nv_n=v'_nh_n$ in the finite-level
rectangle. Naturality of finite reduction makes $\sigma_n$ and $\tau_n$
commute with $n+1\to n$, and functoriality of tensor reduction does the same
for $\overline\xi_n$. Together with the four transition equations, this
shows that the completed squares commute with $K_{n+1}\to K_n$ on every
corner. The limit construction and all four reduction edges are
operator-equivariant, so the conjugated equality is operator-natural as well.

For Frobenius, the definition of $\Theta_S$ transports
$\Theta_{A,\infty}$ across $s$, and the $n$th product-cone component followed
by $h_n$ is $\alpha_n$. This gives the first displayed Weil equation. The
definition of $\Theta_T$ transports $\Theta_{D,\infty}$ across $t$, and its
$n$th component is $\delta_n$, giving the second. The completed Frobenius
equation for $\overline\xi_n$, together with finite-level equivariance of
$v'_n$, now says that every arrow of the reduction square is a Weil morphism.

## Detailed form

For every $n$, reduction of $\Ex^{\mathrm{comp}}_{\square,K}$ of
