objects.body:
If $S$ is
locally Noetherian and $f:X\to S$ is
locally of finite type, then $X$ is locally Noetherian.
(*Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes, Lemma 29.15.6, Tag
[01T6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01T6).*)

## Proof

Let $x\in X$ and put $s=f(x)$. Since $S$ is locally Noetherian
([pqf-def-locnoeth]) there
is an affine open neighbourhood $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $s$ with
$R$ Noetherian, and since $f$ is locally of finite type there is an
affine open neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $x$ with
$f(U)\subset V$ and such that $A$ is a finite type $R$-algebra,
i.e. $A=R[y_1,\dots,y_n]/I$ for some ideal $I$ (the ring-level
existence of such a pair $(U,V)$ is the content of the local finite
type condition in [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]; shrinking
$U$ around $x$ preserves it). By the Hilbert basis theorem, $R$
Noetherian implies the polynomial ring $R[y_1,\dots,y_n]$ Noetherian,
hence its quotient $A$ is Noetherian; the localization $A_{\mathfrak p}$ at the prime $\mathfrak p$ of $x$ is Noetherian (ideals of
$S^{-1}A$ are extended ideals: $\mathfrak b\mapsto S^{-1}\mathfrak b$ is a bijection onto the ideals of $S^{-1}A$, so a
chain of ideals in $S^{-1}A$ lifts to a finite chain in $A$). Hence
$\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is Noetherian for every $x$, i.e. $X$ is locally
Noetherian.

attrs.title: Finite type over a locally Noetherian base

objects.body:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes and $s\in S$. If $f$ is
locally of finite type and $f^{-1}(\{s\})$ is a finite set, then $X_s$
is a finite discrete space and $f$ is quasi-finite at each point of
$X$ lying over $s$.

## Proof

The fibre $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is locally of
finite type over the field $\kappa(s)$ and has finitely many points;
as in the proof of [pqf-lem-qf-finitefibres], restricting to an
affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A$ over an affine open
$\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$, the finite type
$\kappa(s)$-algebra $A\otimes_R\kappa(s)$ has finitely many prime
ideals, hence is Artinian, all its primes maximal, and its spectrum is
a finite discrete set. Hence $X_s$ is a finite discrete space, each of
its points is isolated, and at every point the ring map is quasi-finite
at the corresponding prime in the sense of
[pqf-def-quasifinite], i.e. $f$ is quasi-finite at each point
over $s$.

Let $A\hookrightarrow B$ be an injective integral map of rings. Then
every prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$ is the contraction of a prime of
$B$.
(*Classical: this is the lying-over theorem; Stacks Project,
Algebra, Lemma 10.36.22, Tag
[00GU](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00GU), is the going-up
companion of it, and its proof invokes lying over as Algebra Lemma
10.36.17.*)

## Proof

Put $S=A\setminus\mathfrak p$. Localization gives an injective integral
map $A_{\mathfrak p}\hookrightarrow S^{-1}B$; the target is nonzero
because the map is injective. Choose a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of
$S^{-1}B$. Its contraction is maximal in $A_{\mathfrak p}$: after
quotienting, $S^{-1}B/\mathfrak m$ is a field integral over the
contracted domain, and a domain over which a field is integral is
itself a field (an integral equation for $a^{-1}$ expresses $a^{-1}$ in
the domain for each nonzero $a$). The only maximal ideal of
$A_{\mathfrak p}$ is $\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}$. Pulling
$\mathfrak m$ back to $B$ therefore gives a prime whose contraction is
$\mathfrak p$.

attrs.title: Lying over for an injective integral extension

objects.body:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a
proper morphism of schemes.
Then $f$ is separated, universally closed, of finite type,
quasi-compact and quasi-separated. In
particular, if $S$ is affine then $X$ is separated and quasi-compact.

## Proof

The first three assertions are part of the definition of properness in
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]; quasi-compactness is part of
the finiteness condition there, and quasi-separatedness follows from
separatedness (the diagonal is an affine closed immersion, hence
quasi-compact). If $S$ is
affine then $X$ is quasi-compact and separated because $f$ is
quasi-compact and separated.

Let $f:X\to S$ be a
proper morphism of schemes.
Then $f$ is a closed map.

## Proof

This is [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image] of the ambient-foundations chapter.

Let $f:X\to S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of
schemes. Then $f_*$ transforms quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules
into quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-modules.
(*Stacks Project, Schemes, Lemma 26.24.1, Tag
[01LC](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01LC).*)

## Proof

Work over an affine open $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset S$ and put
$X_0=f^{-1}(S_0)$. By quasi-compactness in
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], choose finitely many affine
opens $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ covering $X_0$, small enough that
$\mathcal F|_{U_i}=\widetilde{M_i}$ as in
[pqf-def-coherent]. For each pair $i,j$, the intersection
$U_i\cap U_j$ is quasi-compact: it is the inverse image of the affine
$U_i\times_{S_0}U_j$ under the quasi-compact diagonal of $f$.
Choose a finite affine cover $W_{ijk}=\operatorname{Spec}C_{ijk}$
of this intersection, again with
$\mathcal F|_{W_{ijk}}=\widetilde{N_{ijk}}$.

The sheaf gluing axiom gives an exact sequence at its first two terms

$$
0\longrightarrow\Gamma(X_0,\mathcal F)
\longrightarrow\prod_i M_i
\xrightarrow{\delta}\prod_{i,j,k}N_{ijk},
$$

where $\delta$ is the difference of the two restrictions.
Indeed, a tuple of sections on the $U_i$ glues precisely when its
restrictions agree on every member $W_{ijk}$ covering every overlap.

For $a\in A$, pull these two finite covers back to $D(a)$. The same
gluing axiom computes $\Gamma(f^{-1}(D(a)),\mathcal F)$ as the kernel
of the resulting restriction-difference map. By
[pqf-lem-associated-sections-localize], its two terms and its
map are obtained from the displayed sequence by $-\otimes_AA_a$.
Localization is exact and commutes with finite products, hence

$$
\Gamma(f^{-1}(D(a)),\mathcal F)
\cong\Gamma(X_0,\mathcal F)\otimes_AA_a.
$$

These isomorphisms commute with further principal localization,
since every map used is restriction of sections. Thus on the basis
of principal opens of $S_0$, the sheaf $f_*\mathcal F$ agrees with
$\widetilde{\Gamma(X_0,\mathcal F)}$. It is quasi-coherent on $S_0$
by [pqf-def-coherent]; varying $S_0$ proves the assertion.

Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Then $f$ is
quasi-finite if and only if $f$ is
locally of finite type, of finite type, quasi-compact and has finite
fibres.
(*Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes, Lemma 29.21.10, Tag
[02NH](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02NH).*)

## Proof

*($\Rightarrow$).* Quasi-finite means: of finite type and every
point of $X$ is isolated in its fibre, by
[pqf-def-quasifinite]. Finite type in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] is quasi-compact plus locally of
finite type, so only the finiteness of the fibres remains. Let $s\in S$
and put $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$, a scheme
locally of finite type over the field $\kappa(s)$ ($f$ is locally of
finite type). Every point of $X_s$ is isolated, so the open
$X_s$ has dimension zero, and a locally finite type, quasi-compact,
zero-dimensional scheme over a field is the spectrum of an Artinian
$\kappa(s)$-algebra, a finite ring; its spectrum is a finite discrete
set (classical commutative algebra: finite type over a field with
dimension zero is Artinian, and Artinian rings have finitely many
prime ideals, all maximal). Hence $f^{-1}(\{s\})=|X_s|$ is finite.
*($\Leftarrow$).* Assume $f$ is locally of finite type and
quasi-compact (so of finite type by
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]) and has finite fibres. For
$x\in X$, with $s=f(x)$, the fibre $X_s$ is locally of finite type
over $\kappa(s)$ with finitely many points; restricting to an affine
open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$ around $x$ with
$f(\operatorname{Spec}A)\subset\operatorname{Spec}R$ (which exists
because $f$ is locally of finite type, by
[pqf-def-quasifinite]), the ring
$A\otimes_R\kappa(s)$ has finitely many prime ideals; being of
finite type over the field $\kappa(s)$ it is Artinian, so all its
primes are maximal and $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_R\kappa(s))$ is a
finite discrete set. Thus $x$ is an isolated point of its fibre, and
$R\to A$ is quasi-finite at the prime of $x$ in the sense of
[pqf-def-quasifinite]; hence $f$ is quasi-finite at every point,
which together with finite type is the definition of quasi-finite.

attrs.title: Quasi-finite = finite type + quasi-compact + finite fibres

objects.body:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Then $f$ is quasi-finite if
and only if $f$ is locally quasi-finite and quasi-compact.

## Proof

A quasi-finite morphism is of finite type, hence locally of finite type
and quasi-compact, by [pqf-def-quasifinite] and
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and each of its points is
isolated in its fibre, which is exactly quasi-finiteness at that point,
so it is locally quasi-finite. Conversely, if $f$ is locally
quasi-finite and quasi-compact, then it is locally of finite type by
[pqf-def-quasifinite] and hence of finite type by
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]; the points of $X$ are isolated
in their fibres because quasi-finiteness at a point is the isolation
condition of the definition, so $f$ is quasi-finite.

Let $X$ be a
quasi-separated scheme and
let $U,V\subset X$ be quasi-compact open subschemes. Then
$U\cap V$ is a quasi-compact open subscheme.

## Proof

The affine opens form a basis of the topology of a scheme, so the
quasi-compact opens $U$ and $V$ are finite unions of affine opens,
$U=U_1\cup\dots\cup U_m$ and $V=V_1\cup\dots\cup V_n$. Then
$U\cap V=\bigcup_{i,j}(U_i\cap V_j)$ is a finite union, so it suffices
to treat the case that $U$ and $V$ are affine. In the product
$X\times X$ the rectangle $U\times V$ is affine, hence
quasi-compact, and the diagonal $\Delta:X\to X\times X$ is a
quasi-compact morphism, because $X$ is quasi-separated
([def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]). By the definition of a
quasi-compact morphism in [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] the
preimage of the affine open $U\times V$ under $\Delta$ is
quasi-compact. The diagonal is the identity on points, so that preimage
is $U\cap V$.

Let $X$ be a scheme. Assume that $X$ is quasi-compact, that $X$ is
quasi-separated, and that $\mathrm H^1(X,\mathcal I)=0$ for every
quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals $\mathcal I\subset\mathcal O_X$ of
finite type. Then $X$ is affine.
(*Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 30.3.2, Tag
[01XG](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01XG).*)

## Proof

This is the recorded classical input named in the statement, Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 30.3.2 ([Tag 01XG](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01XG)): Serre's criterion, that a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme is affine as soon as the first cohomology of every quasi-coherent sheaf of finite type ideals vanishes. No separate proof is given.

Let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of modules on a scheme $X$. If
$\mathcal F_x=0$ for all $x\in X$, then $\mathcal F=0$.

## Proof

A local section of $\mathcal F$ is zero in its stalk at every point,
hence zero in a neighbourhood of every point, hence zero globally by
the sheaf axioms and the definition of the stalks.

attrs.title: A sheaf with vanishing stalks is zero

objects.body:
The conclusion is a finite stratification, not local constancy on all
of $X$. For a closed point $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ of an
irreducible curve with open complement $j$, the sheaf
$j_!\mathbf F_\ell\oplus i_*\mathbf F_\ell$ has cardinality $\ell$
at every stalk, but its generization map from $Z$ to its complement
is zero. In the proof above, injectivity comes from lifting the
generic stalk; it is not assumed for arbitrary generization maps.

Let $j:U_0\hookrightarrow C_0$ be a dense open immersion of smooth
curves, let $i:Z_0=C_0\setminus U_0\hookrightarrow C_0$, and let
$\mathcal F$ be lisse on $U_0$. The open–closed localization
triangle, with the middle extension of [def-wf-middle-extension],
gives

$$
R\Gamma_c(U,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow
R\Gamma_c(C,j_*\mathcal F)\longrightarrow
R\Gamma_c(Z,i^*j_*\mathcal F)\longrightarrow\ .
$$

In particular, because the finite-boundary term is concentrated in
degree zero, the degree-one segment is

$$
H_c^0(Z,i^*j_*\mathcal F)\longrightarrow H_c^1(U,\mathcal F)
\longrightarrow H_c^1(C,j_*\mathcal F)\longrightarrow0
$$

and the degree-zero injection
$H_c^0(U,\mathcal F)\hookrightarrow H_c^0(C,j_*\mathcal F)$.

## Proof

The boundary triangle $j_!\mathcal F\to j_*\mathcal F\to i_*i^*j_*\mathcal F\to$ (whose boundary term is supported on the finite closed subscheme $Z$) is the open–closed recollement triangle of [def-weil-open-closed-recollement] of the framework chapter, which exists for Qlb-Weil complexes by [prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages], applied to $K=j_*\mathcal F$, with the extension-by-zero and derived-direct-image conventions of that definition. The last term
$R\Gamma_c(Z,i^*j_*\mathcal F)$ is concentrated in degree zero by the
finite-boundary computation [lem-a1-finite-boundary-cohomology]
(applicable since $i^*j_*\mathcal F$ is constructible by [lem-fin-boundary-sheaf]),
so the long exact cohomology sequence of the triangle gives the
displayed degree-one segment and the stated injections.

attrs.title: Boundary localization triangle for a curve

objects.body:
In the setting and with the conventions of [thm-a1-curve-perverse-heart],
the simple objects of the abelian category $\mathrm{Perv}(C)$ are the
following:

- the *punctual* objects $i_{x*}E$ (in degree $0$), where $x$ is a closed
  point of $C$ and $E$ is an irreducible sheaf on $x$, that is, an
  irreducible Weil module at $x$ in the Weil case;
- the *middle extensions* $(j_*\mathcal N)[1]$ of [def-wf-middle-extension],
  where $j:U\hookrightarrow C$ is a dense open immersion and $\mathcal N$
  is a nonzero irreducible lisse sheaf on $U$. Here irreducible means that
  $\mathcal N$ has no lisse subsheaf other than $0$ and $\mathcal N$.

Every object of either kind is simple, and every simple object is of one
of these kinds.

## Proof

We use the parts (1)–(5) of [thm-a1-curve-perverse-heart] freely.
"Punctual" and "no punctual subsheaf" are meant as there. We also use [lem-wf-dense-open-pi1-surjective] (SGA 1, Exposé V,
Proposition 8.2): for a dense open $k:U'\hookrightarrow U$ of a smooth
curve, the maps of fundamental groups and of Weil groups are surjective,
and consequently, for a lisse sheaf $\mathcal N$ on $U$, the unit
$\mathcal N\to k_*k^*\mathcal N$ is an isomorphism (part (3)) and, if
$\mathcal N$ is irreducible, so is $k^*\mathcal N$ (part (4)).

*Punctual objects are simple.* Let $E$ be irreducible, so $E\neq0$, and
let $0\to Q\to i_{x*}E\to R\to0$ be exact in $\mathrm{Perv}(C)$. Part (5)
gives $\mathcal H^{-1}Q=0$ and an exact sequence
$0\to\mathcal H^{-1}R\to\mathcal H^0Q\to i_{x*}E\to\mathcal H^0R\to0$.
Here $\mathcal H^{-1}R$ is a subsheaf of the punctual sheaf
$\mathcal H^0Q$, so it is punctual, and by (3) it is zero. So
$\mathcal H^0Q$ is a subsheaf of $i_{x*}E$. Subsheaves of $i_{x*}E$
correspond to submodules of $E$, since $i_{x*}$ is exact and fully
faithful with inverse $i_x^*$ on sheaves supported at $x$. Hence either
$\mathcal H^0Q=0$, and then $Q=0$, or $\mathcal H^0Q=i_{x*}E$, and then
$R=0$.

*Middle extensions are simple.* Let $P=(j_*\mathcal N)[1]$ with
$\mathcal N$ nonzero and irreducible, so $P\neq0$, and let
$0\to Q\to P\to R\to0$ be exact in $\mathrm{Perv}(C)$. Part (5) gives
$\mathcal H^0R=0$ and an exact sequence
$$
0\to\mathcal H^{-1}Q\to j_*\mathcal N\to\mathcal H^{-1}R\to
\mathcal H^0Q\to0 .
$$
Choose a dense open $k:U'\hookrightarrow U$ on which $\mathcal H^{-1}Q$
and $\mathcal H^{-1}R$ are lisse and the punctual sheaf $\mathcal H^0Q$
vanishes, and write $j'=j\circ k$. On $U'$ we get an exact sequence of
lisse sheaves $0\to\mathcal H^{-1}Q|_{U'}\to\mathcal N|_{U'}\to
\mathcal H^{-1}R|_{U'}\to0$. Since $\mathcal N|_{U'}$ is irreducible,
there are two cases.

(a) Suppose $\mathcal H^{-1}Q|_{U'}=0$. Then $\mathcal H^{-1}Q$ is a
punctual subsheaf of $j_*\mathcal N$, so it is zero by (3) and (4), and
$\mathcal N|_{U'}\cong\mathcal H^{-1}R|_{U'}$. Put
$\mathcal H:=\mathcal H^{-1}R$. By (3) it has no punctual subsheaf, so
the unit $\mathcal H\to j'_*j'^*\mathcal H$ is injective, because its
kernel is punctual. The composite
$$
j_*\mathcal N\to\mathcal H\to j'_*j'^*\mathcal H
\cong j'_*(\mathcal N|_{U'})=j_*k_*k^*\mathcal N
$$
is $j_*$ of the unit $\mathcal N\to k_*k^*\mathcal N$, which is an
isomorphism. Hence the injective second map is also surjective, and so
$j_*\mathcal N\to\mathcal H$ is an isomorphism. Its cokernel
$\mathcal H^0Q$ therefore vanishes, and $Q=0$. This is the step that
excludes a punctual subobject of the middle extension.

(b) Suppose $\mathcal H^{-1}Q|_{U'}=\mathcal N|_{U'}$. Then
$\mathcal H^{-1}R$ vanishes on $U'$, so it is punctual, hence zero by
(3). Then $R=0$, and $Q\to P$ is an isomorphism.

*Every simple object is of one of the two kinds.* Let $P$ be simple. The
exact sequence $0\to(\mathcal H^{-1}P)[1]\to P\to(\mathcal H^0P)[0]\to0$
of (5) forces either $\mathcal H^{-1}P=0$ or $\mathcal H^0P=0$.

If $\mathcal H^{-1}P=0$, then $P=\mathcal G[0]$ with $\mathcal G$
punctual, supported on a finite set of closed points, so
$\mathcal G\cong\bigoplus_xi_{x*}\mathcal G_x$. Every subsheaf
$\mathcal G'\subset\mathcal G$ gives a short exact sequence
$0\to\mathcal G'[0]\to\mathcal G[0]\to(\mathcal G/\mathcal G')[0]\to0$ in
the heart. This holds because the three terms are punctual, hence in the
heart by (3), and they form a distinguished triangle, so part (4)
of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles] applies. By simplicity
$\mathcal G$ has no subsheaves other than $0$ and $\mathcal G$. So
$\mathcal G=i_{x*}E$ for a single closed point $x$ and an irreducible $E$.

If $\mathcal H^0P=0$, then $P=\mathcal F[1]$ with $\mathcal F\neq0$
having no punctual subsheaf. Choose a dense open $j:U\hookrightarrow C$
on which $\mathcal F$ is lisse, and put $\mathcal N:=j^*\mathcal F$. The
unit $\mathcal F\to j_*\mathcal N$ is injective, because its kernel is
punctual. In particular $\mathcal N\neq0$. Let $\mathcal Q$ be its
cokernel. It vanishes on $U$, so it is punctual. The sheaf sequence
$0\to\mathcal F\to j_*\mathcal N\to\mathcal Q\to0$ gives a distinguished
triangle $\mathcal Q[0]\to\mathcal F[1]\to(j_*\mathcal N)[1]\to$ whose
three terms lie in the heart by (3) and (4). So it is a short exact
sequence in $\mathrm{Perv}(C)$ by part (4) of
[lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles]. Its quotient $(j_*\mathcal N)[1]$ is
nonzero, so simplicity forces $\mathcal Q=0$, and hence
$P\cong(j_*\mathcal N)[1]$.

It remains to show that $\mathcal N$ is irreducible. Let
$0\neq\mathcal N'\subsetneq\mathcal N$ be a lisse subsheaf, and let
$\mathcal C$ be the cokernel of $j_*\mathcal N'\to j_*\mathcal N$. Let
$\mathcal C'' := \mathcal C/\mathcal C_{\mathrm p}$ be its quotient by
its largest punctual subsheaf, and let
$\mathcal F':=\ker(j_*\mathcal N\to\mathcal C'')$. The sequence
$0\to\mathcal F'\to j_*\mathcal N\to\mathcal C''\to0$ has no punctual
subsheaf in any of its terms: $\mathcal F'$ is a subsheaf of
$j_*\mathcal N$, and $\mathcal C''$ has none by construction. So, as
above, it gives a short exact sequence
$0\to\mathcal F'[1]\to P\to\mathcal C''[1]\to0$ in $\mathrm{Perv}(C)$.
On $U$ the sheaf $\mathcal C|_U=\mathcal N/\mathcal N'$ is lisse, so
$\mathcal C_{\mathrm p}|_U=0$ and $\mathcal F'|_U=\mathcal N'$. Both
$\mathcal F'$ and $\mathcal C''$ are therefore nonzero, and this
contradicts the simplicity of $P$. Hence $\mathcal N$ is irreducible, and
$P$ is a middle extension of the second kind.

attrs.title: Simple perverse sheaves on a smooth curve

objects.body:
In the conventions of [rem-dl-a1-conventions], let
$j:U_0\hookrightarrow A_0$ be a dense open immersion and let
$\mathcal M$ be a nonzero irreducible lisse Weil sheaf on $U_0$ which is
constituent-nonexceptional in the sense of
[def-a1-constituent-nonexceptional]. Then there are a dense open
immersion $j':U'_0\hookrightarrow A'_0$ into the dual line and a nonzero
irreducible lisse Weil sheaf $\mathcal M'$ on $U'_0$ such that the
Fourier–Deligne transform of [def-fd-transform] of the middle extension
of [def-wf-middle-extension] satisfies

$$
\operatorname{FT}_\psi\bigl((j_*\mathcal M)[1]\bigr)\cong
(j'_*\mathcal M')[1].
$$

## Proof

Write $\mathrm{Perv}(A_0)$ and $\mathrm{Perv}(A'_0)$ for the perverse
hearts of [def-per-perverse-subcategories] on the two lines. We use three
facts about these hearts.

- **(H1)** The two perverse classes form a t-structure whose heart is
  abelian, with the sheaf-level description on a curve
  ([thm-a1-curve-perverse-heart]).
- **(H2)** $\operatorname{FT}_\psi$ is t-exact: it sends
  $\mathrm{Perv}(A_0)$ into $\mathrm{Perv}(A'_0)$, and
  $\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}$ sends $\mathrm{Perv}(A'_0)$ into
  $\mathrm{Perv}(A_0)$ ([thm-a1-fourier-t-exact]).
- **(H3)** The simple objects of the curve heart are the punctual
  $i_{x*}E$, with $x$ a closed point and $E$ an irreducible Weil module
  at $x$ placed in degree $0$, and the $(j_*\mathcal N)[1]$, with
  $\mathcal N$ a nonzero irreducible lisse Weil sheaf on a dense open;
  each of these is simple ([prop-a1-curve-perverse-simples]).

*Step 1: the transform is simple.* By (H3),
$P:=(j_*\mathcal M)[1]$ is a simple object of $\mathrm{Perv}(A_0)$, and
by (H2) $\operatorname{FT}_\psi(P)$ lies in $\mathrm{Perv}(A'_0)$. Put
$G:=\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}(-)(1)$, using the Tate twist of
[def-wf-tate-twist]. Fourier inversion [lem-fd-inversion] with $r=1$
gives $\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K)\cong K(-1)$,
hence $G\circ\operatorname{FT}_\psi\cong\operatorname{id}$. Applied to the
character $\psi^{-1}$ it gives
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}(M)\cong M(-1)$, and
the Tate-twist clause of base linearity [prop-base-linear] (the twist
being the pullback of the twisting object of the base) gives
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi\bigl(\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}(M)(1)\bigr)\cong
\operatorname{FT}_\psi\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}(M)(1)\cong M$, i.e.
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi\circ G\cong\operatorname{id}$. Hence
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi(P)\neq0$.

By (H2) both functors are exact functors between the abelian hearts of
(H1). Let $0\neq Q\subsetneq\operatorname{FT}_\psi(P)$ be a proper
nonzero subobject. Then $G(Q)\to G\operatorname{FT}_\psi(P)\cong P$ is a
monomorphism. Its source $G(Q)$ is nonzero, and its cokernel
$G\bigl(\operatorname{FT}_\psi(P)/Q\bigr)$ is nonzero, because
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi\circ G\cong\operatorname{id}$ detects zero
objects. This contradicts the simplicity of $P$. So
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi(P)$ is simple, and by (H3) it is either
punctual or of the form $(j'_*\mathcal M')[1]$, with $\mathcal M'$
nonzero, irreducible and lisse on a dense open $U'_0$.

*Step 2: transforms of punctual objects.* Let $\xi\in k$ and let
$\delta_\xi$ be the skyscraper sheaf $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ at
$\xi$ on the geometric dual line $A'$, in degree $0$. We claim

$$
\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}(\delta_\xi)\cong\mathcal L_{\psi(-\xi x)}[1]
\quad\text{on }A.
$$

The case $\xi=0$ is the second formula of [lem-fd-first-formula], and
the general case uses the same computation. In the transform from $A'$
to $A$, the pullback of $\delta_\xi$ along the first projection is
supported on $\{\xi\}\times A$. The second projection restricts to an
isomorphism from this line onto $A$. On the line, the kernel of
[def-fd-kernel] for the character $\psi^{-1}$ restricts to
$\mathcal L_{\psi^{-1}(\xi x)}$. By [lem-fd-as-characters] this is
$\mathcal L_{\psi^{-1},\xi x}\cong\mathcal L_{\psi,-\xi x}
=\mathcal L_{\psi(-\xi x)}$. The compactly supported direct image
along an isomorphism is the sheaf itself, and the shift $[1]$ of
[def-fd-transform] gives the claim.

*Step 3: the punctual case is excluded.* Suppose
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi(P)\cong i_{x*}E$ is punctual. Apply $G$ and use
Step 1:

$$
(j_*\mathcal M)[1]\cong\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}(i_{x*}E)(1).
$$

Pass to the geometric base change, which commutes with the transform by
[lem-fd-base-change]. After this base change, $i_{x*}E$ becomes a
finite direct sum of copies of skyscrapers $\delta_\xi$ at the geometric
points $\xi$ over $x$. The Tate twist becomes trivial. So Step 2 gives

$$
(j_*\mathcal M)_{\bar k}[1]\cong
\bigoplus_{\xi}\mathcal L_{\psi(-\xi x)}^{\oplus n_\xi}[1],
\qquad\text{hence}\qquad
\mathcal M_{\bar k}\cong\bigoplus_\xi
\bigl(\mathcal L_{\psi(-\xi x)}|_U\bigr)^{\oplus n_\xi}
$$

after restriction to $U$, using $j^*j_*\mathcal M=\mathcal M$. Since
$\mathcal M\neq0$, some $n_\xi>0$. Every geometric irreducible
constituent of $\mathcal M$ is then some $\mathcal L_{\psi(ax)}|_U$
with $a=-\xi\in k$, where $a=0$ is allowed. This contradicts
constituent-nonexceptionality in [def-a1-constituent-nonexceptional].

Therefore $\operatorname{FT}_\psi\bigl((j_*\mathcal M)[1]\bigr)$ is a
simple object of the second kind in (H3), which is the assertion.

The hypothesis is needed. Conversely, the transform of a linear
character is punctual: for $a=0$, $\operatorname{FT}_\psi$ of the
constant sheaf is $\delta_0(-1)[-1]$ by [lem-fd-first-formula]. Hence
an input with an exceptional geometric constituent can have a punctual
simple constituent in its transform.

attrs.title: Fourier transform of an irreducible middle extension

objects.body:
Let $j:U_0\hookrightarrow C_0$ be a dense open immersion of smooth
geometrically connected curves, and let $\mathcal F$ be lisse and
punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$ on $U_0$. Then

$$
H_c^r(C,j_*\mathcal F)\quad\text{has weights at most }w+r
$$

for every $r$, where $j_*\mathcal F$ is the
middle extension.

## Proof

Choose a dense affine $v:V_0\hookrightarrow U_0$ by
[lem-a1-affine-core-of-curve]. The recovery lemma
[lem-a1-lisse-middle-extension] identifies
$v_*\mathcal F|_V$ with $\mathcal F$, so by transitivity of ordinary
direct image, $j_*\mathcal F$ is the middle extension of
$\mathcal F|_{V_0}$ directly from $V_0$ to $C_0$.

The affine estimate [thm-a1-affine-curve-upper] bounds
$H_c^r(V,\mathcal F)$ by $w+r$. The boundary stalk at a point of
the finite complement $C\setminus V$ is the inertia invariants of the
local geometric generic stalk, of weights at most $w$ by the
weights-of-inertia-invariants corollary [lem-wf-boundary-semicontinuity]
(with the boundary stalk description of
[lem-wf-boundary-stalk-invariants]), and the finite-boundary
calculation [lem-a1-finite-boundary-cohomology] then shows that
the boundary term of
the localization triangle [prop-a1-curve-boundary-sequence] for
$V\hookrightarrow C$ is concentrated in degree zero, and
[lem-a1-finite-boundary-weights] gives its weights at
most $w$. Thus each middle cohomology group $H_c^r(C,j_*\mathcal F)$
is an extension of a quotient of $H_c^r(V,\mathcal F)$ by a subobject
of the (degree-zero) boundary group; when $r=0$ it is an injection.
Subquotients preserve the stated bounds by
[lem-a1-subquotient-extension-bounds], and extensions preserve
them by [lem-a1-extension-bounds]; since $r\geq0$, the boundary bound $w$ is at
most $w+r$.

attrs.title: Upper bound for a curve middle extension

objects.body:
Let $X_0$ be a normal geometrically connected curve over $k_0$, put
$|k_0|=q$, fix a real weight character $\lambda$ as in [d-weights], and let
$\mathcal F_0$ be a nonzero lisse
Weil sheaf on $X_0$. Choose a
composition series in the sense of
[def-mg-weil-composition-series], with simple factors
$A_1,\ldots,A_t$. Write $d_a=\dim A_a$ and let
$\gamma_a=\dw_\lambda(A_a)$.
Let $R$ be the set of distinct values among the $\gamma_a$, and put

$$
r(\gamma):=\sum_{\gamma_a=\gamma}d_a,
$$

Thus $\dim V=\sum_{\gamma\in R}r(\gamma)$. Let
$0\le r\le\dim V$, and assume that every $A_a$ and every
Jordan–Holder constituent of $\bigwedge^r\mathcal F_0$ has finite
geometric determinant. Then every Jordan–Holder constituent of
$\bigwedge^r\mathcal F_0$ has
determinant weight

$$
\sum_{\gamma\in R}n_\gamma\gamma,
\qquad 0\le n_\gamma\le r(\gamma),
\qquad \sum_{\gamma\in R}n_\gamma=r.
$$

Conversely every admissible tuple $(n_\gamma)$ occurs as the
determinant weight of at least one
Jordan–Holder constituent. The input factors
$\gamma_a$ are counted with multiplicity; the assertion concerns the
possible weights and their non-emptiness, not an equality of output
multiplicities for coincident sums.

## Proof

Write $V$ for the Weil representation. The factors and their weights
are those of
[def-mg-weil-composition-series] and [d-weights]. The Weil
semisimplification $V^{\mathrm{ss}}=\bigoplus_aA_a$ of
[def-mg-weil-semisimplification] is a semisimple Weil representation,
so [lem-mg-common-positive-central-element] applies to it, giving
a central element $z$ of degree $d>0$ (in the monodromy data of
[def-wf-monodromy-data]). For each simple
factor $A_a$, its image is
central by [lem-mg-degree-component-functoriality]. Its matrix
commutes with the Weil-group image on $A_a$, so
[lem-wf-schur-scalar] applies to this Weil-simple representation and
gives a scalar $c_a$. The central-element formula
[cor-mg-central-determinant-weight], applicable because $A_a$ has
finite geometric determinant, gives

$$
\gamma_a=\frac{\lambda(c_a)}{d}.
$$

By [lem-mg-filtered-exterior-power], $\bigwedge^rV$ has a finite
Weil-stable filtration with nonzero successive quotients

$$
Q_{\boldsymbol n}=\bigotimes_{a=1}^t\bigwedge^{n_a}A_a,
\qquad 0\le n_a\le d_a,
\qquad \sum_a n_a=r,
$$

each a tensor construction on subquotients of $V^{\mathrm{ss}}$.
The refinement lemma [lem-mg-filtration-refinement] reduces all
composition factors to these quotients. On $Q_{\boldsymbol n}$, the
central element acts by $c_{\boldsymbol n}:=\prod_a c_a^{n_a}$. Every
simple factor $C$ of this quotient receives a central degree-$d$ element
by [lem-mg-degree-component-functoriality]; its matrix commutes with
the Weil-group image on $C$, and therefore is scalar by Schur's lemma.
Since $C$ has finite geometric determinant by assumption,
[cor-mg-central-determinant-weight] gives

$$
\dw_\lambda(C)=\frac{\lambda(c_{\boldsymbol n})}{d}
=\sum_a n_a\gamma_a.
$$

Grouping equal $\gamma_a$'s gives the asserted aggregate tuple and its
capacity bounds. Conversely, for an admissible tuple $(n_\gamma)$,
distribute each $n_\gamma$ among the indices with $\gamma_a=\gamma$,
never exceeding $d_a$. The resulting $Q_{\boldsymbol n}$ is nonzero,
so [lem-mg-composition-series-exists] gives a simple factor, whose
weight is the required sum. This proves the converse.

attrs.title: Determinant weights of an exterior power (conditional)

objects.body:
Fix a real weight character $\lambda$ as in [d-weights]. Let
$\mathcal V_0$ and $\mathcal E_0$ be nonzero lisse Weil sheaves on the
same normal geometrically connected curve $X_0$, with Weil
representations $V$ and $E$. Choose composition series in the sense of
[def-mg-weil-composition-series], with simple factors
$V_1,\ldots,V_t$ of $V$ and $E_1,\ldots,E_u$ of $E$. Assume that every
$V_i$, every $E_j$, and every Jordan–Holder constituent of
$V\otimes E$ has finite geometric determinant. Then for every
Jordan–Holder constituent $Q$ of $V\otimes E$ there is a pair $(i,j)$
with

$$
\dw_\lambda(Q)=\dw_\lambda(V_i)+\dw_\lambda(E_j).
$$

Conversely, every such sum occurs for at least one constituent. Neither
$V$, $E$ nor $V\otimes E$ is assumed semisimple.

## Proof

The multisets $\{V_i\}$ and $\{E_j\}$ do not depend on the chosen
series by [lem-mg-jordan-holder]. Form the Weil semisimplifications
$V^{\mathrm{ss}}=\bigoplus_iV_i$ and $E^{\mathrm{ss}}=\bigoplus_jE_j$
of [def-mg-weil-semisimplification]; both are semisimple Weil
representations on the same curve. Apply
[lem-mg-common-positive-central-element] to the pair
$V^{\mathrm{ss}},E^{\mathrm{ss}}$, i.e. to
$\rho=V^{\mathrm{ss}}\oplus E^{\mathrm{ss}}$, and let $z$ be the
resulting central element of degree $m>0$. Each $V_i$ and each $E_j$
is a Weil-stable direct summand, hence a subquotient, of $\rho$, so by
[lem-mg-degree-component-functoriality] the image of $z$ on it is
central of degree $m$; by [lem-wf-schur-scalar] it acts on $V_i$ by a
scalar $c_i$ and on $E_j$ by a scalar $d_j$. Since $V_i$ and $E_j$
have finite geometric determinant, [cor-mg-central-determinant-weight]
gives

$$
\dw_\lambda(V_i)=\frac{\lambda(c_i)}{m},\qquad
\dw_\lambda(E_j)=\frac{\lambda(d_j)}{m}.
$$

By [lem-mg-filtered-tensor-product], $V\otimes E$ has a Weil-stable
filtration whose successive quotients are the representations
$V_i\otimes E_j$, each pair $(i,j)$ occurring once. Each
$V_i\otimes E_j$ is a tensor product of two subquotients of $\rho$, so
[lem-mg-degree-component-functoriality] applies to it and to its
iterated subquotients, and the image of $z$ acts on $V_i\otimes E_j$
by $c_id_j$. By [lem-mg-filtration-refinement], every constituent $Q$
of $V\otimes E$ is a composition factor of some $V_i\otimes E_j$. The
image of $z$ on $Q$ is central of degree $m$ by the same
functoriality, acts by the scalar $c_id_j$, and $Q$ has finite
geometric determinant by hypothesis; therefore
[cor-mg-central-determinant-weight] and the fact that $\lambda$ is a
homomorphism give

$$
\dw_\lambda(Q)=\frac{\lambda(c_id_j)}{m}
=\frac{\lambda(c_i)}{m}+\frac{\lambda(d_j)}{m}
=\dw_\lambda(V_i)+\dw_\lambda(E_j).
$$

Conversely, each $V_i\otimes E_j$ is nonzero, so it has a composition
series by [lem-mg-composition-series-exists]; its factors are
constituents of $V\otimes E$ by [lem-mg-filtration-refinement], and
each has determinant weight $\dw_\lambda(V_i)+\dw_\lambda(E_j)$.

attrs.title: Determinant weights of a tensor product of two sheaves (conditional)

objects.body:
Let $p$ be prime, let $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, put $q=p^a$ and
$k_0=\Fq$, and let $k=\Fbar$ be the
fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$.
Let $X_0/k_0$ be
smooth, proper, and geometrically
connected of pure dimension $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, and put
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. Fix indeterminates $T$ and $U$. For every
prime $\ell\neq p$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and, for
$P(T)=\sum_r c_rT^r\in\mathbf Z[T]$, write
$P^{(\ell)}(T)=\sum_r(c_r\cdot1_{\Ql})T^r$ for coefficientwise extension, and let
$(V_{i,\ell},F_{i,\ell},P_{i,\ell})_{0\leq i\leq2d}$ be the
smooth-proper
cohomological family. Fix an integer $i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$. Let
$P_i(T)\in\mathbf Z[T]$ be the
integral Frobenius factor
with $P_i(0)=1$ and $P_i^{(\ell)}=P_{i,\ell}$ for every $\ell\neq p$,
and put $r_i=\deg P_i$. Fix an algebraic closure
$\overline{\mathbf Q}$ of $\mathbf Q$. A
reciprocal root
$\alpha\in\overline{\mathbf Q}$ of $P_i$ means a root of
$P_i^\#(U)=U^{r_i}P_i(U^{-1})$; its inverse $\beta=\alpha^{-1}$ is the
corresponding ordinary root.
The reciprocal polynomial

$$
P_i^\#(U)=U^{r_i}P_i(U^{-1})\in\mathbf Z[U]
$$

is monic, and every reciprocal root $\alpha$ is an
algebraic integer. For every embedding
$\tau:\mathbf Q(\alpha)\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$,

$$
|\tau(\alpha)|=q^{i/2};
$$

and $\alpha$ is a
$q$-Weil number of weight $i$. More
explicitly, for every prime $\ell'\neq p$, let
$\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell'}$ be an algebraic closure of
$\mathbf Q_{\ell'}$, set

$$
\overline{\mathbf Q}^{(\ell')}=
\{z\in\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell'}:z\text{ is algebraic over }\mathbf Q\},
$$

and choose an
ell-adic realization
$\jmath_{\ell'}:\overline{\mathbf Q}\xrightarrow{\sim} \overline{\mathbf Q}^{(\ell')}$. Then $\jmath_{\ell'}(\alpha)$ is a reciprocal root
of $P_{i,\ell'}$, hence an eigenvalue of $F_{i,\ell'}$ on
$H^i(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell'})$, the
ordinary cohomology group
after scalar extension.
Every ordinary root $\beta$
satisfies,
for every $\tau:\mathbf Q(\beta)\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$,

$$
|\tau(\beta)|=q^{-i/2}.
$$

## Proof

By [prop-integral-recovery], the polynomial $P_i$ is integral and its
scalar extension is $P_{i,\ell}$. The reciprocal-root convention is the
one in [def-weil-ordinary-reciprocal-roots], so the reversed polynomial
is monic and its roots are algebraic integers. The weight assertion follows
from [prop-weight-purity-roots], while [lem-embedding-extension] extends
an arbitrary complex embedding of the number field generated by a root to
an isomorphism of algebraic closures. Thus every complex conjugate has
absolute value $q^{i/2}$, and inversion gives the ordinary-root statement.
The terminology and algebraic-integer criterion are those of
[def-weil-numbers].

attrs.title: Arithmetic roots of the integral factors

objects.body:
For a compactifiable morphism $f:X\to S$ between
Noetherian schemes, and arbitrary complexes $M$ on
$X$ and $K$ on $S$, there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
Rf_*R\mathcal Hom_A(M,f^\times K)
\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_A(Rf_!M,K).
$$

The notation refers to derived pullback and internal Hom, and ordinary etale compact supports.

## Proof

For every test complex $Q$ on $S$, the ordinary
derived pullback, tensor, and internal-Hom adjunctions of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] give

$$
\begin{split}
\operatorname{Hom}_S(Q,Rf_*R\mathcal Hom_A(M,f^\times K))
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(f^*Q\otimes_A^LM,f^\times K)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S(Rf_!(f^*Q\otimes_A^LM),K)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S(Q\otimes_A^LRf_!M,K)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S(Q,R\mathcal Hom_A(Rf_!M,K)).
\end{split}
$$

The second bijection is
[thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]; the third is the
projection formula of
[lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection], applied on a
compactification and preceded by exact extension by zero.
These bijections are natural in all three complexes.
Yoneda therefore gives the asserted canonical isomorphism.
It is the map obtained by applying $Rf_!$ to evaluation
and then composing with the counit, since the displayed
bijections transpose precisely those maps.

Let $f:X\to S$ be as in
[thm-asd-smooth-tensor], and let $g:S'\to S$
be any morphism of Noetherian schemes. Denote its base
change by $f':X'\to S'$, with $g':X'\to X$.
The canonical morphism

$$
g'^*f^\times K\longrightarrow f'^\times g^*K
$$

is an isomorphism for every complex $K$. At $K=A$
it identifies $g'^*\omega_f$ with $\omega_{f'}$,
and it respects the tensor isomorphism of
[thm-asd-smooth-tensor].
The notation refers to smooth morphisms, and derived pullback and internal Hom.

## Proof

Proper base change on a compactification, followed by the
stalkwise base-change identity for extension by zero, gives
$Rf'_!g'^*\cong g^*Rf_!$, for bounded-below complexes by the
finite-amplitude argument in
[lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection]. Define the
displayed map by the adjunction of
[thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], transposing

$$
Rf'_!g'^*f^\times K\cong g^*Rf_!f^\times K
\longrightarrow g^*K.
$$

For a projective-line projection its unit and counit are
those explicitly constructed in
[thm-amb-p1-adjunction]. Both commute with base change:
the supported diagonal class does so by
[lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map], and the trace does so
by [thm-amb-p1-decomposition]. Hence the displayed
map in that case is the ordinary inverse-image and twist
base-change isomorphism. The same holds for an affine-line
projection by restricting its projective compactification,
and for affine space by composing those adjunctions.

It remains to verify the three coherences on which the identification
rests; each is a statement about the canonical maps, not merely about
their sources and targets.
*(i) The underlying base-change map in the model case.*
For the affine-space projection $\mathbf A^d_{S_0}\to S_0$
over a Zariski open $S_0\subseteq S$, the identification
$Rf'_!g'^*\cong g^*Rf_!$ of the first paragraph is the composite of
proper base change for the compactification
$\mathbf A^d\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^d$ with the stalkwise identity
$g^*j_!=j'_!g'^*$ for the extension by zero; both are comparisons of
the two diagrams obtained by base changing one diagram along $g$,
so the composite restricts to the chart $S'_0=S'\times_SS_0$.
*(ii) Unit and counit on the chart.* There the adjunction of
[thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] is the affine-space adjunction
[cor-amb-affine-space-adjunction], whose unit and counit are built
from the trace and the supported diagonal class; these commute with
base change by [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map] and
[thm-amb-p1-decomposition]. The displayed map is the transpose of
the counit composite, so the base-change isomorphism of (i) carries it
to the corresponding transpose over $S'_0$, which is the map defined
by the same recipe there.
*(iii) Descent to $X'$.* On the etale chart of $f$ used in
the proof of [thm-asd-smooth-tensor],
[lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality] identifies the map under
consideration with the base-change isomorphism of (ii) preceded by
etale inverse image, the sum over the finite fibre commuting with base
change; it is therefore an isomorphism on an etale cover of $X'$,
hence everywhere. Finally the tensor maps of
[thm-asd-smooth-tensor] were transposed from the projection
formula and the counit, and applying the same transposition to the
commuting base-change diagram of those two maps gives their base-change
compatibility. This proves all the claimed identifications.

attrs.title: Arbitrary base change for smooth ambient duality

objects.body:
Let $A_0$ be an abelian variety over the finite field $k_0$ of [d-ab-field],
$A=A_0(\bar k)$, and $\ell\ne p$. Its rational Tate module has no nonzero
vector fixed by geometric Frobenius:

$$
(V_\ell A)^F=0.
$$

More precisely, with $T_\ell A$, $V_\ell A$ the Tate modules of the abelian
group $A$ ([def-tate-module-abelian-group]), on which the arithmetic
Frobenius $\sigma$ and $F=\sigma^{-1}$ act coordinatewise, one has
$(T_\ell A)^\sigma=(T_\ell A)^F=0$ and $(V_\ell A)^\sigma=(V_\ell A)^F=0$.

## Proof

In the finite-field setting of [d-ab-field], the fixed points of
$x\mapsto x^q$ in $\bar k$ are exactly $k_0$: every element of $k_0$ is a
root of $T^q-T$ (as $k_0^\times$ has order $q-1$), and this polynomial has
at most $q$ roots. Now let $P\in A=A_0(\bar k)$ with $\sigma P=P$. Choose
one of the finitely many affine charts $\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $A_0$,
$R=k_0[x_1,\dots,x_m]/I$, containing the image of $P$; since $\sigma$ acts
by coordinates over $k_0$, the point $\sigma P$ has the same image, and in
this chart $P$ is a $k_0$-algebra map $\varphi:R\to\bar k$ with
$\sigma\circ\varphi=\varphi$. Hence every $\varphi(x_i)$ lies in $k_0$, so
$P\in A_0(k_0)$ and there are at most $q^m$ such points in the chart.
Thus $A^\sigma=A_0(k_0)$ is a finite group.
Apply [lem-tate-module-no-fixed] to the abelian group $A$ and the automorphism
$\sigma$; it gives $(T_\ell A)^\sigma=0$ and $(V_\ell A)^\sigma=0$, and the
same for $F=\sigma^{-1}$.

attrs.title: No Frobenius-fixed vectors on the Tate module of an abelian variety

objects.body:
Let $A$ be an abelian variety ([def-sc-abelian-variety]) of dimension $g$ over an algebraically
closed field $k$ and let $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$. Then

$$
T_\ell A\cong\Z_\ell^{2g},\qquad V_\ell A\cong\Q_\ell^{2g}.
$$

## Proof

By [lem-sc-ntorsion-etale] each level is
$A[\ell^n](k)\cong(\Z/\ell^n\Z)^{2g}$, and the transition map $[\ell]:A[\ell^{n+1}](k)\to A[\ell^n](k)$ is
surjective, since $A(k)$ is divisible by [lem-sc-isogeny-surjective]
(an $\ell$-th root of a point of $A[\ell^n](k)$ lies in $A[\ell^{n+1}](k)$). Choosing compatible bases through these surjections
identifies the inverse system defining $T_\ell A$
([def-wf-abelian-tate-module]) with the system
$(\Z/\ell^n\Z)^{2g}$ under reduction, whose limit is $\Z_\ell^{2g}$;
tensoring with $\Q_\ell$ gives $V_\ell A\cong\Q_\ell^{2g}$.

Uses: [def-sc-abelian-variety], [def-wf-abelian-tate-module], [lem-sc-isogeny-surjective], [lem-sc-ntorsion-etale]

attrs.title: The $\ell$-adic Tate module is free of rank $2g$

objects.body:
Let $V_0\to S_0$ be the rank-$r$ vector bundle of [def-fd-kernel], let
$p:V\to S$ and $p':V^\vee\to S$ be the structure morphisms, and let
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi$ be the transform of [def-fd-transform]. For
$K\in D^b_c(V,E)$ and $N\in D^b_c(S,E)$ there is an isomorphism, natural
in $K$ and $N$,

$$
\operatorname{FT}_\psi\bigl(K\otimes^L_Ep^*N\bigr)\cong
\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K)\otimes^L_E{p'}^*N .
$$

In particular:

1. for $N$ from the base,
   $\operatorname{FT}_\psi(p^*N)\cong\operatorname{FT}_\psi(\underline{E})\otimes^L_E{p'}^*N$,
   so the transform of a base-changed sheaf is the base change of the
   transform of the unit;
2. (*Tate twists*) for every $m\in\mathbf Z$ and every $K$,
   $$
   \operatorname{FT}_\psi\bigl(K(m)\bigr)\cong\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K)(m),
   $$
   with the Tate twist of [def-wf-tate-twist]; if $K$ carries a Weil
   structure, this isomorphism is one of Weil complexes.

## Proof

Write $\pi:V\times_SV^\vee\to S$ for the structure morphism of the Fourier
square, so that $p\circ p_1=\pi=p'\circ p_2$. Pullback is monoidal and
compatible with composition, hence

$$
p_1^*\bigl(K\otimes^L_Ep^*N\bigr)\cong p_1^*K\otimes^L_Ep_1^*p^*N
\cong p_1^*K\otimes^L_E\pi^*N\cong p_1^*K\otimes^L_Ep_2^*{p'}^*N .
$$

Tensoring with the kernel $\mathcal K_\psi$ of [def-fd-kernel] and using
the associativity and commutativity constraints of $\otimes^L_E$ gives

$$
p_1^*\bigl(K\otimes^L_Ep^*N\bigr)\otimes^L_E\mathcal K_\psi\cong
\bigl(p_1^*K\otimes^L_E\mathcal K_\psi\bigr)\otimes^L_Ep_2^*\bigl({p'}^*N\bigr).
$$

The first factor $A:=p_1^*K\otimes^L_E\mathcal K_\psi$ lies in
$D^b_c(V\times_SV^\vee,E)$ ($\mathcal K_\psi$ being lisse of rank one),
and $L:={p'}^*N\in D^b_c(V^\vee,E)$ has finite Tor amplitude because
$E$ is a field. The morphism $p_2$ is separated of finite type, so the
compact-support projection formula, clause (5) of
[prop-functor-package], gives

$$
p_{2,!}\bigl(A\otimes^L_Ep_2^*L\bigr)\cong p_{2,!}(A)\otimes^L_EL .
$$

Finally the shift commutes with tensoring by $L$,
$(X\otimes^L_EL)[r]\cong X[r]\otimes^L_EL$, and by the definition
[def-fd-transform] the two sides are
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K\otimes^L_Ep^*N)$ and
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K)\otimes^L_E{p'}^*N$. Each isomorphism used is a
natural transformation, whence naturality in $K$ and $N$.

(1) is the case $K=\underline E=E_V$, since $E_V\otimes^L_Ep^*N\cong p^*N$.

(2) Let $E_S(m)$, $E_V(m)$, $E_{V^\vee}(m)$ be the twisting objects of
[def-wf-tate-twist] on $S$, $V$, $V^\vee$. For any morphism $f:X\to Y$
the canonical isomorphisms $f^*\mu_{\ell^n,Y}\cong\mu_{\ell^n,X}$
(both being the sheaf represented by the group scheme $\mu_{\ell^n}$)
are compatible with the $\ell$-th power transition maps; since
$\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_Y$ is pro-etale locally isomorphic to the constant
sheaf $\mathbf Z_\ell$, whose pullback is again $\mathbf Z_\ell$, the
pullback commutes with this limit, and they give
$f^*E_Y(1)\cong E_X(1)$; since $f^*$ is monoidal, this gives
$f^*E_Y(m)\cong E_X(m)$ for $m\ge0$, and, $E_Y(m)$ being invertible
(lisse of rank one) with inverse $E_Y(-m)=R\mathcal Hom_E(E_Y(m),E_Y)$,
pullback commutes with this dual, which gives the case $m<0$. Hence
$K(m)=K\otimes^L_EE_V(m)\cong K\otimes^L_Ep^*E_S(m)$ and
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K)(m)\cong\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K)\otimes^L_E{p'}^*E_S(m)$,
and the main isomorphism with $N=E_S(m)$ gives (2). The Frobenius
pullbacks commute with all the canonical isomorphisms used (monoidality
of pullback, the projection-formula map, the pullback of roots of
unity), so a Weil structure on $K$ is carried to the Weil structure on
both sides.

attrs.title: P7: the transform is linear over the base

objects.body:
Write $a:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, $\dim X\leq d$, and
$\omega_{X,n}=Ra_n^!A_n$. There is a canonical derived-complete
object

$$
\omega_{X,R}=R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_n\omega_{X,n},
\qquad \omega_{X,R}\otimes_R^L A_n\cong\omega_{X,n}.
$$

It is in $D^b_c(X,R)$, with uniform reduction Tor interval
$[-2d,0]$. For $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ there is a natural
isomorphism of derived mapping complexes

$$
R\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,\omega_{X,R})
\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_R(Ra_!K,R).
$$

Thus $\omega_{X,R}$ is the value at $R$ of the exceptional
right adjoint on the constructible coefficient category.

## Proof

The coherent comparisons of [lem-coef-finite-dualizing] make
$(\omega_{X,n})_n$ a normalized tower. Effectivity
[lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity] gives the displayed
reductions and completeness. The finite preservation bound of
[lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata], transported by
[lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison], gives
$[-2d,0]$ by taking the constant input. Thus all finiteness
conditions of the integral category are checked on these identified
reductions.

For the adjunction, use the finite exceptional adjoints of
[thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] on bounded constructible inputs
and the compact-support reduction
[lem-coef-integral-compact-support]. At finite level the
adjunction on derived mapping complexes follows by applying derived
global sections to [prop-asd-internal-adjunction] on the etale site
and transporting it by the already stated finite site comparisons.
Thus this is an adjunction of mapping complexes before taking limits.
Derived extension–restriction of scalars and preservation of limits in the
second mapping variable give

$$
\begin{aligned}
R\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,\omega_{X,R})
&\cong R\varprojlim_n R\operatorname{Hom}_{X,A_n}(K_n,\omega_{X,n})\\
&\cong R\varprojlim_n R\operatorname{Hom}_{A_n}(Ra_{!,n}K_n,A_n)\\
&\cong R\varprojlim_n R\operatorname{Hom}_R(Ra_!K,A_n)\\
&\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_R(Ra_!K,R).
\end{aligned}
$$

The last equality uses the complete coefficient object
$R=R\varprojlim A_n$. The transition maps in the second line
are those of the finite adjunctions: the dualizing comparisons are
defined by their counits. Hence all four lines identify the specified
natural maps. Taking degree zero gives the claimed adjunction,
without interchanging $H^0$ and an ordinary inverse limit.

attrs.title: The integral dualizing object and its adjunction

objects.body:
For a separated finite-type $f:X\to Y$, define

$$
G_fL=R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_n Rf_n^!L_n.
$$

Then $G_f$ maps $D^b_c(Y,R)$ to $D^b_c(X,R)$, is right
adjoint to integral $Rf_!$ on these categories, and has canonical
identifications

$$
G_fL\cong D_{X,R}f^*_{\mathrm{comp}}D_{Y,R}L,
\qquad (G_fL)\otimes_R^L A_n\cong Rf_n^!L_n.
$$

Here $f^*_{\mathrm{comp}}$ is completed pullback. For input
reduction Tor interval $[a,b]$, one output interval is
$[a-2\dim X,b+2\dim Y]$. The comparison identifies the
canonical units and counits; in particular the dualizing object
of [prop-coef-integral-dualizing] is $G_aR$.
This is an adjunction on the stated constructible categories.

## Proof

By [lem-coef-finite-exceptional] the displayed exceptional
tower is normalized, including its adjunction maps. Alternatively,
consider the integral object
$H=D_{X,R}f^*_{\mathrm{comp}}D_{Y,R}L$.
It exists in the integral category by
[thm-coef-integral-verdier] and
[lemma-weil-pbc-completed-pullback-reduction].
The latter gives finite reductions equal to ordinary pullback;
pullback preserves the reduction Tor interval. Applying the two
duality bounds gives $[a-2\dim X,b+2\dim Y]$.
The finite dual formula in [lem-coef-finite-exceptional]
identifies its reductions with $Rf_n^!L_n$, compatibly with
the transition maps. Reconstruction, or
[lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity], gives $H\cong G_fL$.

For $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$, use the reduction of integral compact
supports in [lem-coef-integral-compact-support] and derived
coefficient adjunction to compute

$$
\begin{aligned}
R\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_!K,L)
&\cong R\varprojlim_n R\operatorname{Hom}_{Y,A_n}(Rf_{!,n}K_n,L_n)\\
&\cong R\varprojlim_n R\operatorname{Hom}_{X,A_n}(K_n,Rf_n^!L_n)\\
&\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,G_fL).
\end{aligned}
$$

Finite units and counits commute with the transition maps by
[lem-coef-finite-exceptional]. Hence this calculation defines
the adjunction and its specified maps; the triangle identities
follow from the same identities before taking the derived limit.
For the structure morphism and $L=R$, the defining tower is
the one in [prop-coef-integral-dualizing]. This proves the
last identification with its adjunction, without an assertion about
unrestricted unbounded pro-etale inputs.

attrs.title: The integral exceptional adjoint on constructible complexes

objects.body:
Fix the finite-field datum
$p,a,q,k_0,k$, where $q=p^a$, choose a prime $\ell\neq p$, write
$\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and
choose a finite extension $E/\Ql$ contained in $\Qlb$. Let $Y_0$ be a
separated finite-type
$k_0$-scheme, put $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, and choose
$K\in D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(Y,E)$, a
Weil complex. Write $E_Y$ for the constant
Weil sheaf. Then the
$E$-coefficient abbreviations mean
$H^i(Y,E)=H^i(Y,E_Y)$ and $H_c^i(Y,E)=H_c^i(Y,E_Y)$. The
ordinary and compact-support
cohomology groups, in particular $H_c^i(Y,K)$ meaning
$H_c^i(Y,\operatorname{For}K)$, are finite-dimensional, vanish outside a
finite interval, and carry the
geometric Frobenius
automorphism. If $Y_0$ is
proper, the
canonical isomorphism

$$
H_c^i(Y,K)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^i(Y,K)
$$

is Frobenius-equivariant.
If $Y$ has dimension $e\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ and $K=E_Y$ is the
constant Weil sheaf, then

$$
H_c^i(Y,E)=0\qquad\text{for }i<0\text{ or }i>2e.
$$

For proper $Y$, the
ordinary cohomology also
satisfies $H^i(Y,E)=0$ for $i<0$ or $i>2e$. In
particular, if $X_0/\Fq$ is smooth,
proper, geometrically connected of pure dimension
$d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, and $X=X_0\times_{\Fq}k$, then

$$
H^i(X,\Ql)=0\qquad\text{for }i\notin[0,2d].
$$

Moreover, if $Y_0$ is geometrically connected (neither properness nor
smoothness is needed), then $H^0(Y,E)\cong E$, and the
geometric Frobenius acts as the
identity on this group; in particular $H^0(X,\Ql)\cong\Ql$ with
$F=\mathrm{id}$ for every smooth, separated finite-type, geometrically
connected $X_0$.

## Proof

*Step 1 (the finite level).* Work with the
finite-field datum ([def-weil-finite-field-fiber]) $p,a,q,k_0,k$ of
the statement, the
small pro-etale site ([def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]) of $Y$, and
the geometric hypotheses ([def-weil-geometric-hypotheses]) imposed on
$Y_0$. Write $a_Y:Y\to s=\Spec k$ for the
structure morphism, a
separated morphism of finite
type ([def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]) over the field
$k$ whose geometric fibres ([def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties])
have dimension at most $e$, and let
$\mathcal R$ be the amplitude interval of the Weil complex $K$. By
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] the $E$-category has the same
objects as the derived-complete integral category
$D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed];
choose an integral model $K_{\mathcal O}$ of $K$ and let
$K_n=K_{\mathcal O}\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A_{E,n})$ be its finite-level reductions, objects of the
finite-torsion
constructible category ([def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]) forming a uniformly
bounded tower with common amplitude $\mathcal R$
([def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]).

*Step 2 (compact-support finiteness at finite level).* Apply
[prop-finite-compact-support-constructibility] to $a_Y$: there
are integers $u\leq v$, depending only on $\mathcal R$ and on $e$,
such that $Ra_{Y,!,n}K_n\in D_c^{[u,v]}(s,A_{E,n})$ for every $n$.
By [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] the category
$D^b_c(s,A_{E,n})$ is $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A_{E,n})$, so each
$H^i_c(Y,K_n)$ is a finite $A_{E,n}$-module vanishing outside
$[u,v]$, and by [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] these
modules are the compact-support cohomology of $Y$ with coefficients in
$K_n$.

*Step 3 (ordinary cohomology at finite level).* By the
constructibility clause of [sbc-thm-finiteness-finite-type] the
sheaves $R^qa_{Y,*}F$ are constructible on $s_{{\mathrm{et}}}$ for
every constructible $A_{E,n}$-sheaf $F$, hence finite at the
geometric point $\bar s$
([def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]); the fibre is the cohomology
group in the proper case by
[cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-finite]. The vanishing
$H^i(Y,F)=0$ for $i>2e$ is
[fin4-lem-fibrewise-cohomological-dimension], and for $i<0$ it is
immediate from the definition of the cohomology groups.

*Step 4 (the stage $E$).* The $E$-coefficient cohomology is the
rationalization of the $\mathcal O_E$-object
([def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]); the uniform boundedness of
Step 2 makes the $\mathcal O_E$-cohomology finitely generated over the
Noetherian ring $\mathcal O_E$, and tensoring along the flat map
$\mathcal O_E\to E$ gives finite-dimensional $E$-vector spaces with
the same vanishing range. This is the asserted finiteness,
boundedness and finite-dimensionality of $H^i_c(Y,K)$ and
$H^i(Y,K)$.

*Step 5 (Frobenius).* The Weil structure of $K$ is the datum
$\varphi_K:Lg_\gamma^*K\to K$ of
[def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], natural in $K$; transported along
the functoriality of the direct image it gives the geometric-Frobenius
automorphism of [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius] on the
ordinary and on the compact-support groups, as asserted.

*Step 6 (the proper case).* If $Y_0$ is proper, then
$a_Y$ is proper and the canonical comparison
$R\Gamma_c(Y,K)\to R\Gamma(Y,K)$ of
[def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] is an isomorphism; it is
Frobenius-equivariant because both operators are those of Step 5.

*Step 7 (the constant sheaf).* For $K=E_Y$ Step 2 gives
$H^i_c(Y,E)=0$ for $i>2e$, with $e=\dim Y$, and
[fin4-lem-fibrewise-cohomological-dimension] gives
$H^i(Y,E)=0$ for $i>2e$; for $i<0$ both vanish by definition, and
in the proper case Step 6 transfers the statement to $H^i$. The
specialisation $Y=X$, $e=d$, $E=\Ql$ is the vanishing
$H^i(X,\Ql)=0$ for $i\notin[0,2d]$. Finally, if $Y_0$ is
geometrically connected then $Y$ is connected, and the constant sheaf is
the lisse sheaf of the trivial representation of the fundamental group
([thm-galois-fundamental],
[cor-galois-lisse-representations]); its space of invariants is all
of $E$, so $H^0(Y,E)\cong E$, and the geometric Frobenius acts
as the identity on this group, since the Weil structure of the constant
Weil sheaf is the identity on the constants ([def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]).
This argument uses only the connectedness of $Y$, not properness or
smoothness; the case $Y_0=X_0$, $E=\Ql$ gives $H^0(X,\Ql)\cong\Ql$.

Let $K_0$ be a field, let $X,Y$ be
finite-type $K_0$-schemes, and let
$f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type
$K_0$-morphism. Fix a prime $\ell$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and
require that its image in $K_0$ is invertible. Choose a finite extension
$E/\Ql$, an integer $n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$,
and put $A=A_{E,n}$. The coefficient $A$ is used with the
finite-torsion
constructibility condition. For objects
$c_i=(j_i,\bar f_i)\in\operatorname{Comp}(f)$ in the
compactification category
and a refinement
$u:c_1\to c_2$, the canonical transformation between the
compact-support candidates

$$
R\bar f_{1*,n}j_{1!}
\xrightarrow{\sim}
R\bar f_{2*,n}j_{2!}
$$

is the composite of the proper-composition isomorphism with the isomorphism

$$
Ru_*j_{1!}\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{2!}
$$

on the ambient derived category. These transformations are identities for
identity refinements and are transitive under composition. For any two
compactifications $c_1,c_2$, comparison through a common refinement gives
a natural isomorphism

$$
Rf_{!,n}^{c_1}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{!,n}^{c_2}.
$$

Here $R\bar f_{i*,n}$ and $j_{i!}$ are respectively the
derived direct image and
extension-by-zero functors. A common
refinement may be chosen for any finite collection of
compactifications; the resulting comparison is independent of that choice
and satisfies the cocycle condition for triples of compactifications.
The comparison is asserted on the domain declared in
[def-weil-compact-support-candidate]: the complexes of the pro-etale
site that come from the etale site with an
etale-origin witness. It is
not asserted, and not claimed anywhere in the blueprint, on the whole of
$D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$.

## Proof

We prove coherence on the full subcategory of complexes
$K=\nu_X^*L$ with $L\in D^+(X_{\Et},A)$, using the comparison
pullback of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism].
This includes bounded constructible complexes coming from the etale
site. A refinement satisfies $u j_1=j_2$
by [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Use the inverse of
the canonical isomorphism of
[lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison-proetale]:

$$
\alpha_u^{-1}:Ru_*j_{1!}\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{2!}.
$$

The composition isomorphism for derived direct images at finite level,
[lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition] (1), gives
$R\bar f_{1*,n}\simeq R\bar f_{2*,n}Ru_*$.
Composing with $R\bar f_{2*,n}(\alpha_u^{-1})$ therefore gives the
claimed map of candidates from [def-weil-compact-support-candidate].
It is the identity for an identity refinement, and the composition law
for $\alpha$ makes these maps transitive.

Finally, [prop-compactification-refinement] gives a common
refinement $d$ of any two compactifications. If
$t_i:Rf_{!,n}^{d}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{!,n}^{c_i}$ are its maps,
the comparison from $c_1$ to $c_2$ is $t_2t_1^{-1}$.
Given another choice $d'$, choose a refinement mapping to both.
The two resulting maps to each $c_i$ can be made equal by the
parallel-refinement clause; do this for the two $c_i$ successively.
Transitivity then makes the two expressions $t_2t_1^{-1}$ equal.
For three compactifications choose one common refinement, so that
$(t_3t_2^{-1})(t_2t_1^{-1})=t_3t_1^{-1}$.
This proves independence and the cocycle condition on the indicated
full subcategory.

The statement on all of $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ is no longer part of
the claim: the domain declared in
[def-weil-compact-support-candidate] is the subcategory of complexes
coming from the etale site with a witness, which is exactly the domain on
which the comparison above is proved, so the proposition is complete on its
declared domain. A comparison on complexes without an etale origin would
need proper base change for the complex itself; every proper base-change
statement of the proper-base-change chapter assumes either torsion cohomology and boundedness
below on the etale site or an etale-origin witness, so no such extension is
available, and none is used.

Let $K$ be a field, let $X,Y$ be finite-type $K$-schemes, and let
$f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type $K$-morphism. Let
$\operatorname{Comp}(f)$ be the compactification category
([def-weil-compactifications-refinements]) whose objects are factorizations
$X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y$ with $j$ an open
immersion, $\bar f$ proper, and $\bar f j=f$, and whose morphisms are proper
$Y$-morphisms $u:\overline X_1\to\overline X_2$ with $u j_1=j_2$. This
category is nonempty (Nagata's theorem, [thm-nagata-compactification]) and
cofiltered: finitely many objects admit a common refinement, and any two
parallel refinements become equal after a further refinement.

## Proof

The category $\operatorname{Comp}(f)$ of
[def-weil-compactifications-refinements] is nonempty by the
compactification clause of [thm-nagata-compactification]: every
separated finite-type morphism of finite-type schemes over a field
admits a compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X
\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y$ with $j$ an open immersion and $\bar f$
proper, exactly the objects of $\operatorname{Comp}(f)$. That the
category is cofiltered is [prop-nagata-compactification-category], applied
over the base $Y$: the scheme $Y$ is of finite type over the field $K$,
hence Noetherian, so quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and every open
immersion into the Noetherian scheme $\overline X$ is quasi-compact; so the
category of [prop-nagata-compactification-category] for $f:X\to Y$ is
$\operatorname{Comp}(f)$. Its clause (i) gives a common proper refinement of
any two compactifications, hence by induction of any finite family, and its
clause (ii) says that any two parallel refinements become equal after a
further refinement; its base-change clauses state the functoriality up to
refinement used in [def-weil-compactifications-refinements].

Let $\mathcal A=\mathrm{Mod}_\Lambda$ with $\Lambda$ a finite ring. The
full subcategory $D^b_c(\et X)$ of the bounded derived category
$D^b(\shv{\et X})$ consisting of the complexes all of whose cohomology
sheaves are constructible is a triangulated subcategory.

## Proof

For a weak Serre subcategory $\mathcal C$ of an abelian category, the
complexes with cohomology in $\mathcal C$ form a triangulated subcategory
of the derived category: the zero object and shifts are clear, and for a
distinguished triangle $K\to L\to M\to K[1]$ with $K$ and $M$ having
cohomology in $\mathcal C$, the long exact cohomology sequence
$H^{n}(K)\to H^n(L)\to H^n(M)$ exhibits $H^n(L)$ as an extension of a
subobject of $H^n(M)$ (a kernel) by a quotient of $H^n(K)$ (a cokernel),
both in $\mathcal C$, hence $H^n(L)\in\mathcal C$. Apply this to the weak
Serre subcategory of [thm-constructible-serre]. (In the formalisation the
general statement is `DerivedCategory.homologyProperty_isTriangulated`, for any
property of objects closed under isomorphisms, kernels, cokernels and extensions; it is
applied to the constructible sheaves with these closure properties, the content of
[thm-constructible-serre], as hypotheses.)

Let $X$ be a scheme and let $\mathcal F\in\shv{\et X}$ be constructible.
Then there is a dense open $U\subseteq X$ such that $\mathcal F|_U$ is
finite locally constant. (No Noetherian hypothesis on $X$ is needed.)

## Proof

Let $(\iota_k\colon Z_k\to X)_{k<n}$ be a stratification witnessing
constructibility, with strata $X_k=\iota_k(Z_k)$, and let
$U=\bigcup_kU_k$ with $U_k$ the interior of $X_k$ in $X$.

*$U$ is dense.* A locally closed subset $L$ of a topological space
with empty interior is nowhere dense: writing $L=V\cap\overline L$ with $V$
open, the open set $\operatorname{int}\overline L$ meets $V$ inside
$\operatorname{int}L=\emptyset$, and an open subset of $\overline V$
disjoint from $V$ is empty. A finite union of nowhere dense sets is
nowhere dense (if $A$ is closed with empty interior and $B$ has empty
interior, then $\operatorname{int}(A\cup B)\setminus A$ is an open subset
of $B$, hence empty, so $\operatorname{int}(A\cup B)\subseteq \operatorname{int}A=\emptyset$). Now $X_k\setminus U_k$ is locally closed
with empty interior, so $N=\bigcup_k(X_k\setminus U_k)$ is nowhere dense,
and $X\setminus N\subseteq U$ since the $X_k$ cover $X$; the complement of
a set with empty interior is dense, hence so is $U$.

*$\mathcal F|_U$ is finite locally constant.* The open subsets
$U_k$ cover $U$, and $\mathcal F|_{U_k}$ is the pullback of $\mathcal F$
along the open immersion $U_k\to X$, whose image $U_k$ is contained in
$X_k=\iota_k(Z_k)$; since $\iota_k^*\mathcal F$ is finite locally
constant, so is $\mathcal F|_{U_k}$ by
[lemma-constructible-immersion-independence] (in the form: for an
immersion $b$ and any morphism $a$ with image in the image of $b$,
$b^*\mathcal F$ finite locally constant implies $a^*\mathcal F$ finite
locally constant). Finally, a sheaf which is finite locally constant on
each member of an open cover is finite locally constant: the trivialising
étale covers of the restrictions compose to a trivialising étale
cover, and a geometric point of $U$ lifts to a member of the open cover
containing its image, where the stalk is unchanged.

A sheaf $\mathcal F\in\shv{\et X}$ is constructible if and only if
$j^*\mathcal F$ and $i^*\mathcal F$ are constructible.

## Proof

``Only if'' is [prop-constructible-pullback]. Conversely let
$(\kappa_l\colon W_l\to U)_{l<m}$ and $(\lambda_k\colon V_k\to Z)_{k<n}$ be
stratifications witnessing the constructibility of $j^*\mathcal F$ and
$i^*\mathcal F$. The family of the $j\circ\kappa_l$ and the
$i\circ\lambda_k$ is a stratification of $X$ with $m+n$ strata: each
composite is an immersion; the images $j(U_l)$ are locally closed in $X$,
being locally closed in the open $U$; the images $i(Z_k)$ are locally
closed in $X$, being locally closed in the closed $Z$; and the images are
pairwise disjoint and cover $X$ because the $U_l$ partition $U$, the $Z_k$
partition $Z$, and $X=U\sqcup Z$. Finally
$(j\circ\kappa_l)^*\mathcal F\cong\kappa_l^*j^*\mathcal F$ and
$(i\circ\lambda_k)^*\mathcal F\cong\lambda_k^*i^*\mathcal F$ are finite
locally constant by construction and [lemma-constructible-iso-invariance].

Let $g\colon Y\to X$ be a morphism and let $\mathcal F\in\shv{\et X}$ be
constructible. Then $g^*\mathcal F$ is constructible. In particular
constructibility is preserved by restriction to an open, to a closed
subscheme, and to any locally closed subscheme.

## Proof

Let $(\iota_k\colon Z_k\to X)_k$ be a stratification of $X$ with all
$\iota_k^*\mathcal F$ finite locally constant, and let
$(\iota'_k\colon Z_k\times_XY\to Y)_k$ be its pullback
([lemma-constructible-pullback-stratification]), with projections
$g_k\colon Z_k\times_XY\to Z_k$. Since $\iota_k\circ g_k=g\circ\iota'_k$
and pullback is functorial up to natural isomorphism,
$\iota_k'^*g^*\mathcal F\cong g_k^*\iota_k^*\mathcal F$, which is finite
locally constant by
[lemma-constructible-pullback-locally-constant], [lemma-constructible-pullback-finite]
and [lemma-constructible-iso-invariance].

Fix the finite-field datum
$p,a,q,k_0,k$, where $q=p^a$. Fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, write
$\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and
choose a finite extension $E/\Ql$ contained in $\Qlb$. Let $Y$ be a
finite-type $k$-scheme, where
finite type is the scheme
condition used throughout. Let
$\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$. For $\Lambda=E$, let
$D^b_c(Y,E)$ be the
rationalized
category obtained
from integral complexes whose finite-level reductions satisfy the
finite-torsion
constructibility condition; for $\Lambda=\Qlb$, use the
common finite-stage
coefficient construction. The symbols $\mathcal H^r$ denote the
cohomology sheaves of a
derived complex. Let $m,i\in\mathbf Z$.
There are truncation functors

$$
\tau^{\leq m},\tau^{\geq m}:D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)
\longrightarrow D^b_c(Y,\Lambda).
$$

At a common finite coefficient field they are the
standard truncations of the
constructible derived category; they commute with finite scalar extension and
with the transitions of the coefficient tower.
For $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, these truncations, their natural maps, and the
distinguished truncation triangles satisfy the axioms of a
bounded t-structure. For
$K\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$, define its cohomology functors by

$$
\mathcal H^i(K)=\bigl(\tau^{\geq i}\tau^{\leq i}K\bigr)[i].
$$

For every scheme automorphism $h:Y\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$, the
derived pullback $Lh^*$
commutes with the truncations and with $\mathcal H^i$.

## Proof

At a finite coefficient stage the truncation functors of the
t-structure of [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] are the
canonical truncations of complexes, computed levelwise; they are exact
triangulated on the bounded constructible derived category, because the
truncation of a bounded constructible complex has the cohomology sheaves
of the original complex in the surviving degrees, hence satisfies the
finite-torsion constructibility condition in the same finite partition.
At the derived-complete integral level, the truncations are the
levelwise ones on the reduction tower of
[thm-weil-pbc-integral-truncations] of the proper-base-change chapter, and the
standard t-structure restricts to the integral category by
[prop-weil-pbc-integral-tstructure] of the proper-base-change chapter.
The canonical truncation triangles give the axioms of a bounded
t-structure in the sense of [def-weil-t-structure]. Being
characterized by the vanishing of cohomology sheaves,
the truncations commute with finite scalar extension and with the
transitions of the coefficient tower, so they descend to the rationalized
category of
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and to the common-stage
category of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], where
the truncation triangles give the same bounded t-structure axioms; the
displayed definition of $\mathcal H^i$ is then the canonical
identification. For a scheme automorphism $h$, the derived pullback
$Lh^*$ of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] is exact
triangulated, so it commutes with the canonical truncations and hence
with $\mathcal H^i$.
