Let $p$ be prime, let $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, put $q=p^a$, and set
$k_0=\Fq$; let $k=\Fbar$ be the
fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$.
Fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and for
$P(T)=\sum_r c_rT^r\in\mathbf Z[T]$ write
$P^{(\ell)}(T)=\sum_r(c_r\cdot1_{\Ql})T^r$ for coefficientwise extension.
Let
$X_0/k_0$ be smooth,
proper, and geometrically connected of pure dimension
$d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, let $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $F$ be the
geometric Frobenius. Fix an indeterminate
$T$. For every integer $i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$, put
$V_{i,\ell}=H^i(X,\Ql)$, where $H^i(X,\Ql)$ denotes the
ordinary cohomology group,
and set $P_{i,\ell}(T)=\det(1-TF\mid V_{i,\ell})$. Let
$P_i(T)\in\mathbf Z[T]$ be the
normalized integral factor
with $P_i^{(\ell)}=P_{i,\ell}$; these determinant data are the
smooth-proper
cohomological family. Put
$b_i=\deg P_i$, and set

$$
D_i=(-1)^{b_i}[T^{b_i}]P_i(T).
$$

Let $\langle-,-\rangle_i$ be the
trace–cup-product pairing. Poincare
duality identifies
the multiset of
Frobenius eigenvalues in degree $2d-i$ with

$$
\left\{\frac{q^d}{\alpha}:\alpha
\text{ is an eigenvalue in degree }i\right\},
$$

including algebraic multiplicity. Moreover,

$$
b_i=b_{2d-i},
\qquad
D_iD_{2d-i}=q^{db_i},
$$

and the integral factors satisfy the Laurent-polynomial identity

$$
P_{2d-i}(q^{-d}T^{-1})
=(-1)^{b_i}T^{-b_i}D_i^{-1}P_i(T)
\quad\text{in }\mathbf Q[T,T^{-1}].
$$

For the middle degree $i=d$, the pairing is $(-1)^d$-symmetric. In particular,
if $d$ is odd, then $b_d$ is even.

## Proof

1. **1.** Write $V_i=H^i(X,\Ql)$, put
$n_i=\dim_{\Ql}V_i$, and let
$\alpha_{i,1},\ldots,\alpha_{i,n_i}$ denote the eigenvalues of $F$ on
$V_i$, counted with algebraic multiplicity. The perfect,
Frobenius-similitude pairing in [prop-poincare-pairing] induces
$$
V_{2d-i}\xrightarrow{\sim}V_i^\vee(-d),\qquad
y\longmapsto\bigl(x\longmapsto\langle x,y\rangle_i\bigr).
$$
Since $F$ acts on $\Ql(-d)$ by $q^d$, the operator transported to the
right-hand side is $q^d(F^{-1})^\vee$. Its eigenvalue multiset is
$$
\{\alpha_{2d-i,1},\ldots,\alpha_{2d-i,n_{2d-i}}\}
=
\{q^d/\alpha_{i,1},\ldots,q^d/\alpha_{i,n_i}\}.
$$
In particular the two multisets have the same cardinality.
1. **2.** By the Betti-number convention in
[def-weil-betti-numbers], $b_j=\dim_{\Ql}V_j=n_j$. The cardinality
comparison in Step 1 therefore gives
$$
b_{2d-i}=b_i.
$$
The determinant-constant definition in
[def-weil-determinant-constants] and the factorization
$P_i(T)=\prod_{r=1}^{b_i}(1-\alpha_{i,r}T)$ give
$$
D_i=(-1)^{b_i}[T^{b_i}]P_i(T)
=\prod_{r=1}^{b_i}\alpha_{i,r}.
$$
Using the reciprocal multiset from Step 1,
$$
D_{2d-i}
=\prod_{r=1}^{b_i}\frac{q^d}{\alpha_{i,r}}
=\frac{q^{db_i}}{D_i},
$$
and hence $D_iD_{2d-i}=q^{db_i}$.
1. **3.** The same factorization gives, as an identity in
$\mathbf Q[T,T^{-1}]$,
$$
\begin{aligned}
P_{2d-i}(q^{-d}T^{-1})
&=\prod_{r=1}^{b_i}
\left(1-\frac{1}{\alpha_{i,r}}T^{-1}\right)\\
&=(-1)^{b_i}T^{-b_i}
\left(\prod_{r=1}^{b_i}\alpha_{i,r}\right)^{-1}
\prod_{r=1}^{b_i}(1-\alpha_{i,r}T)\\
&=(-1)^{b_i}T^{-b_i}D_i^{-1}P_i(T).
\end{aligned}
$$
This is the claimed Laurent-polynomial reciprocity.
1. **4.** For $i=d$, the symmetry clause of
[prop-poincare-pairing] makes the pairing $(-1)^d$-symmetric. If
$d$ is odd, choose a nonzero $\Ql$-linear trivialization
$\Ql(-d)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Ql$; this is possible because the Tate-twist
construction in [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] makes
$\Ql(-d)$ an invertible rank-one coefficient space. Transporting the
pairing along this trivialization gives a nondegenerate alternating
$\Ql$-valued form on $V_d$. The
coefficient field is $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, of characteristic zero under
the finite-field convention of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], so its
characteristic is not $2$. Applying
[lem-weil-alternating-form-dimension] gives
$\dim_{\Ql}V_d$ even; [def-weil-betti-numbers] then gives that
$b_d$ is even.

Let $p$ be prime, let $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, put $q=p^a$, and set
$k_0=\Fq$, and let $k=\Fbar$ be the
fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$.
Fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and fix an
indeterminate $T$. For $P(T)=\sum_r c_rT^r\in\mathbf Z[T]$, write
$P^{(\ell)}(T)=\sum_r(c_r\cdot1_{\Ql})T^r$ for coefficientwise extension.
Let
$X_0/k_0$ be smooth, proper,
geometrically connected of pure dimension $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$. Set
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $F$ be the
geometric Frobenius; for every
integer $i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$ define

$$
V_{i,\ell}=H^i(X,\Ql),\qquad
F_{i,\ell}=F\vert_{V_{i,\ell}},\qquad
P_{i,\ell}(T)=\det(1-TF_{i,\ell}\mid V_{i,\ell}).
$$

The tuples $(V_{i,\ell},F_{i,\ell},P_{i,\ell})$ form the
smooth-proper
cohomological family, with
$V_{i,\ell}=H^i(X,\Ql)$, where this is the
ordinary cohomology group.
For every integer $i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$, let $P_i(T)\in\mathbf Z[T]$ be the
normalized integral factor with
coefficient extension $P_i^{(\ell)}=P_{i,\ell}$, and put
$b_i=\deg P_i$, the Betti number.
There are Frobenius-equivariant isomorphisms

$$
H^0(X,\Ql)\cong\Ql,
\qquad
H^{2d}(X,\Ql)\cong\Ql(-d),
$$

where $\Ql(-d)$ is the
Tate twist of degree $-d$.
Geometric Frobenius acts by $1$ on the first space and, by the
Frobenius-on-twists
normalization, by $q^d$ on the second. Consequently

$$
P_0(T)=1-T,
\qquad
P_{2d}(T)=1-q^dT,
\qquad
b_0=b_{2d}=1.
$$

## Proof

Apply the perfect pairing in [prop-poincare-pairing] to degree zero and
top degree. The geometric-connectedness clause of
[def-weil-geometric-hypotheses], together with the constant-sheaf
finiteness statement [prop-cohomological-finiteness], gives
$H^0(X,\Ql)\cong\Ql$. The smooth orientation and twist normalization in
[prop-poincare-pairing], [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] give
$H^{2d}(X,\Ql)\cong\Ql(-d)$. The Frobenius convention in
[def-weil-smooth-proper-cohomological-family] gives the eigenvalue $1$
on $H^0$, while the twist action in
[def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists] gives the eigenvalue $q^d$
on $\Ql(-d)$. The factor and degree identifications in
[prop-integral-recovery], [def-weil-betti-numbers] give the displayed
factors and endpoint Betti numbers.

For every finite-type $\Fq$-scheme $Y_0$ and every $n\geq1$, the
closed points of degree dividing $n$ and the geometric Frobenius orbits give

$$
\#Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})
=\sum_{r\mid n}r\,c_r,
$$

where $c_r$ is the number of closed points of degree $r$. Consequently

$$
Z(Y_0,T)
=\prod_{y\in|Y_0|}(1-T^{\deg(y)})^{-1}
\in1+T\mathbf Z[[T]].
$$

The product is coefficientwise locally finite: modulo $T^{m+1}$, only
closed points of degree at most $m$ occur.

**Status.** Both displayed identities are formalized and proved in Lean, over
$\mathbf Q$. The integrality assertion
$Z(Y_0,T)\in1+T\mathbf Z[[T]]$ is not part of either Lean statement.

Fix the finite-field datum
$p,a,q,k_0,k$, where $q=p^a$. Choose a prime $\ell\neq p$, write
$\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and
choose a finite extension $E/\Ql$ contained in $\Qlb$, and a
separated finite-type
$k_0$-scheme $Y_0$, and
$Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$. Let
$K\in D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(Y,E)$ be a
Weil complex, let
$F$ be its global
geometric-Frobenius action on
compactly supported
cohomology. For every
integer $n\geq1$ and each point $x\in Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$, choose a
geometric point
$\bar x\to Y$ over $x$. The local operators
$F_x^{(n)}$ and the stalk complexes
$K_{\bar x}=L\bar x^*\operatorname{For}(K)$, using the
derived pullback; these are the
local Frobenius and stalk
constructions; their alternating traces are independent of the choices.
The sets $Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$ and their cardinalities $N_n(Y_0)$ use the
point-count convention.
For every such $n$, one has

$$
\sum_{x\in Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})}\sum_{j\in\mathbf Z}(-1)^j
\Tr\bigl(F_x^{(n)}\mid
\mathcal H^j(\operatorname{For}K)_{\bar x}\bigr)
=\sum_{i\in\mathbf Z}(-1)^i
\Tr\bigl(F^n\mid H_c^i(Y,K)\bigr).
$$

Both sums are finite. For the constant
Weil sheaf $E_Y$, each local
alternating trace is $1$, so

$$
N_n(Y_0)=\sum_{i\in\mathbf Z}(-1)^i
\Tr\bigl(F^n\mid H_c^i(Y,E)\bigr).
$$

If $Y_0$ is proper,
compactly supported
cohomology may be replaced by
ordinary cohomology. In
particular, let $X_0/\Fq$ be
smooth, proper, geometrically
connected of pure dimension $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, put
$X=X_0\times_{\Fq}k$, let $(\Ql)_X$ be its constant
Weil sheaf, and let $F_X$ be the
global geometric Frobenius
on $H^i(X,\Ql)$ for every $i\in\mathbf Z$. Put
$V_{i,\ell}=H^i(X,\Ql)$, $F_{i,\ell}=F_X|_{V_{i,\ell}}$, using the
smooth-proper
cohomological family. Then

$$
N_n(X_0)=\sum_{i=0}^{2d}(-1)^i
\Tr(F_{i,\ell}^n\mid V_{i,\ell}).
$$

## Proof

The local alternating trace is the one defined in
[def-weil-local-frobenius-trace].
The trace identity and its constant-sheaf and proper-specialization clauses
are supplied by [thm-weil-grothendieck-lefschetz-trace]; finiteness and
the Frobenius action are [prop-cohomological-finiteness]. Thus the
displayed formulae follow.

Let

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X'&\xrightarrow{\ g'\ }&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{\ g\ }&Y
\end{array}
$$

be Cartesian with $f,f'$ separated finite type carrying the ambient
exceptional right adjoint datum of
[def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint], and let $g$ be arbitrary.
Then the right-adjoint mate of the compact-support base-change
isomorphism of [def-cbc-exchange-map],

$$
\beta^{\vee}:\ Rf^{\times}Rg_*\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rg'_*Rf'^{\times},
$$

is an isomorphism. On the blueprint's coefficient class
[def-sf-fullcd-used-class] the datum displayed as the hypothesis is the
theorem [cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge], and the mate is formed
object-wise, so on that class the isomorphism holds without hypothesis; the
datum is retained for the complexes outside it,
[rem-sf-class-adjoint-residue].

## Proof

Compact-support base change is the isomorphism
$Lg^*Rf_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_!Lg'^*$ of
[def-cbc-exchange-map]. By
[def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint] the functors $Rf_!$ and
$Rf'_!$ have the right adjoints $Rf^{\times}$ and $Rf'^{\times}$;
the right adjoint of the composite $Lg^*Rf_!$ is the composite
$Rf^{\times}Rg_*$ of the right adjoints, and the right adjoint of
$Rf'_!Lg'^*$ is $Rg'_*Rf'^{\times}$. An isomorphism of functors
induces, by uniqueness of right adjoints, a unique isomorphism of their
right adjoints compatible with the units and counits; applied to the
displayed compact-support base change this is $\beta^{\vee}$.

attrs.title: Dual base change for the ambient right adjoint is formal

objects.body:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be proper, carrying the ambient exceptional right adjoint
datum of [def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint], let
$g:Y'\hookrightarrow Y$ be an open immersion with closed complement
$i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$, and form the Cartesian squares with
$X'=f^{-1}(Y')$, $g':X'\hookrightarrow X$, $f'=f|_{X'}$ and
$i':f^{-1}(Z)\hookrightarrow X$. Then for every object $K$ the
base-change comparison

$$
\beta:\ Lg'^*Rf^{\times}K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf'^{\times}Lg^*K
$$

is an isomorphism. On the blueprint's coefficient class
[def-sf-fullcd-used-class] the ambient datum displayed as the hypothesis
is the theorem [cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge], and the argument below
is object-wise, so on that class the comparison is an isomorphism for every
$K$ of the class without hypothesis; the datum is retained for the complexes
outside it, [rem-sf-class-adjoint-residue].

## Proof

Step 1: the target triangle. The closed-support triangle of
[lem-exc-closed-support-triangle] for the pair $(i,g)$ on $Y$ is

$$
i_*Ri^!K\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow Rg_*Lg^*K\xrightarrow{+1}.
$$

Step 2: applying the exact right adjoint. The compact-support direct
image is exact by [lem-compact-support-direct-image-triangulated]; a right adjoint of an exact functor
is exact, so $Rf^{\times}$ carries the triangle into

$$
Rf^{\times}i_*Ri^!K\longrightarrow Rf^{\times}K
\longrightarrow Rf^{\times}Rg_*Lg^*K\xrightarrow{+1}.
$$

Step 3: dual base change in the two squares. The dual base-change
isomorphism [prop-exc-ambient-dual-base-change], applied to the
Cartesian squares of $i$ and of $g$ along $f$, identifies the outer
terms with

$$
i'_*Rf^{\times}_{Z}Ri^!K,
\qquad
Rg'_*Rf'^{\times}Lg^*K,
$$

where $f_Z:f^{-1}(Z)\to Z$ is the restriction of $f$.
Step 4: restriction to the open. Apply $Lg'^*$ to the resulting
triangle. By [lem-exc-open-fully-faithful] the first term is killed
($Lg'^*i'_*=0$, the images of $g'$ and $i'$ being complementary)
and the last term becomes $Rf'^{\times}Lg^*K$
($Lg'^*Rg'_*\cong\operatorname{id}$). A distinguished triangle whose
first term vanishes exhibits its second-to-third map as an isomorphism;
that map is $Lg'^*Rf^{\times}K\to Rf'^{\times}Lg^*K$, the pullback of the
restriction map of the triangle, which is the base-change comparison
$\beta$ (its adjoint under $Rf'_!\dashv Rf'^{\times}$ is the composite
with the counit). Hence $\beta$ is an isomorphism.

attrs.title: Base change for a proper morphism, against an open immersion

objects.body:
Let $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$
be a closed immersion with
quasi-compact open complement $j$. Suppose $R^qj_*$ vanishes on all module
sheaves for $q>c$, takes
constructible sheaves
to constructible sheaves in every degree. The functor $Rj_*$ is
the derived direct image.
If $K$ is bounded constructible with
Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$,
then $Ri^!K$ is bounded constructible with Tor amplitude in
$[a,b+c+1]$.

## Proof

Constructibility is [lem-exc-closed-amplitude].
The quasi-compact open immersion is quasi-separated, so
[lem-exc-direct-image-coproducts] proves coproduct compatibility
from the stated cohomological-dimension bound. Put
$\kappa=A/(\varpi_E)$. Tensor the triangle of
[lem-exc-closed-support-triangle], for the right adjoint $Ri^!$
of [lem-exc-closed-ambient], with $\kappa$ and apply
[lem-exc-constant-tensor] to its third term. Exact closed
direct image commutes with this constant derived tensor: this is checked
on etale stalks, where its value is either the original module or zero.
The triangle is therefore the closed-support triangle of
$K\otimes_A^L\kappa$. By
[lem-exc-residue-tor-test], this input has cohomology in
$[a,b]$. The amplitude computation of
[lem-exc-closed-amplitude] places the first term in
$[a,b+c+1]$. A second use of
[lem-exc-residue-tor-test] proves the asserted Tor bound.

attrs.title: Finite Tor amplitude for closed support

objects.body:
Let $A=A_{E,n}$ be a
finite coefficient ring,
and let $e:V\to X$ be
finite etale.
On the small pro-etale sites,
direct image is exact and

$$
Re_!=Re_*=e_*\dashv e^*
\quad\hbox{on }D(V_{\mathrm{proet}},A),D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A).
$$

Here $e^*$ is the
inverse image.

## Proof

By [lem-fet-locally-trivial], there is an etale covering of $X$
over which $V$ is a finite disjoint union of copies of the base.
This is also a covering for [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].
On such a member, write the sheets as $1,\ldots,r$. A sheaf on $V$
is a tuple $(M_1,\ldots,M_r)$; direct image and inverse image of
[def-weil-derived-direct-image], [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]
are respectively

$$
(M_1,\ldots,M_r)\longmapsto\bigoplus_{s=1}^r M_s,
\qquad N\longmapsto(N,\ldots,N).
$$

Finite sums of modules are exact. Moreover,
$\operatorname{Hom}(\bigoplus_s M_s,N) =\prod_s\operatorname{Hom}(M_s,N)$.
These formulas commute with permutations of the sheets; therefore the
adjunction maps glue on overlaps. Both functors are exact, so their unit,
counit, and triangular identities descend from complexes to the ordinary
derived categories. Finally $e$ is proper, so its proper
compactification is itself and $Re_!=Re_*$.

attrs.title: The right adjoint for a finite etale morphism

objects.body:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, including the
finite coefficient rings
$A_{E,n}$,
and let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be a
open immersion.
On the small pro-etale sites,
extension by zero has the
inverse image as its
right adjoint on the entire ordinary derived categories:

$$
j_!:D(U_{\mathrm{proet}},A)\rightleftarrows
D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A):j^*.
$$

In particular, the right adjoint is constructed without a constructibility
or finite-Tor hypothesis.

## Proof

The site over the open $U$ is the localization of the site of
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] at the subterminal sheaf represented by
$U$. Thus restriction $j^*$ is exact. For module sheaves $M,N$,
the extension-by-zero adjunction of
[lem-weil-extension-by-zero-adjunction] gives

$$
\operatorname{Hom}(j_!M,N)=\operatorname{Hom}(M,j^*N).
$$

Exactness of extension by zero is proved using presheaf kernels,
local lifting, and sheafification in
[lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact]. Apply the two exact
functors degree by degree to complexes.
They preserve acyclic complexes. Their sheaf-level unit and counit are
chain maps, still satisfy both triangular identities, and descend through
localization at quasi-isomorphisms. Hence they define the asserted
adjunction, with inverse image as in
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].

attrs.title: The right adjoint for an open immersion

objects.body:
In the conventions of [rem-dl-a1-conventions], let
$j:U_0\hookrightarrow A_0$ be a dense open immersion with finite
complement $S_0$, and let $\mathcal M$ be a nonzero irreducible lisse
Weil sheaf on $U_0$ which is constituent-nonexceptional in the sense of
[def-a1-constituent-nonexceptional] and punctually $\iota$-pure of
weight $w$. Let $j':U'_0\hookrightarrow A'_0$ and $\mathcal M'$ be as in
[prop-a1-fourier-middle-extension], so that
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi\bigl((j_*\mathcal M)[1]\bigr)\cong
(j'_*\mathcal M')[1]$ for the transform of [def-fd-transform], and put

$$
\mathcal B:=j_*\mathcal M/j_!\mathcal M ,
$$

with $j_*$ the middle extension of [def-wf-middle-extension]. Then there
are Weil sheaves $\mathcal G$ and $\mathcal B'$ on the dual line $A'_0$
such that

$$
\operatorname{FT}_\psi\bigl(j_!\mathcal M[1]\bigr)\cong\mathcal G[1],
\qquad
\operatorname{FT}_\psi(\mathcal B)\cong\mathcal B'[1],
\qquad
0\longrightarrow\mathcal B'\longrightarrow\mathcal G\longrightarrow
j'_*\mathcal M'\longrightarrow0 .
$$

The correction $\mathcal B'$ is lisse on the entire dual line $A'_0$, and
it has weights at most $w$: for every closed point $y$ of $A'_0$ and
every eigenvalue $\alpha$ of the local Frobenius $F_y$ on
$\mathcal B'_{\bar y}$,

$$
|\iota(\alpha)|^2\le q_y^{\,w}.
$$

In particular the transform of $j_!\mathcal M[1]$ is a sheaf shifted by
one without assuming geometric irreducibility of $\mathcal M$ or
unramifiedness at infinity.

## Proof

*Step 1: the boundary sheaf.* The map $j_!\mathcal M\to j_*\mathcal M$ is
an isomorphism over $U_0$ and $j_!\mathcal M$ has zero stalks on $S_0$,
so it is injective and $\mathcal B$ vanishes on $U_0$. Hence
$\mathcal B$ is supported on the finite reduced closed subscheme $S_0$,
and

$$
\mathcal B\cong\bigoplus_{s\in S_0}i_{s*}E_s,
\qquad E_s:=(j_*\mathcal M)_{\bar s},
$$

where $i_s:s\hookrightarrow A_0$ is the inclusion of the closed point
$s$ and $E_s$ is the boundary stalk with its Frobenius $F_s$, a
finite-dimensional Weil module of the residue field $k(s)$ of degree
$d(s)$ over $k_0$.

*Step 2: the transform of a boundary point.* Fix $s\in S_0$ and a Weil
module $E$ of $k(s)$. Put $A'_s:=s\times_{k_0}A'_0=A'_0\otimes_{k_0}k(s)$,
let $i'_s:A'_s\hookrightarrow A_0\times A'_0$ be the base change of $i_s$
along the first projection $p_1$, let $\pi_s=p_2\circ i'_s:A'_s\to A'_0$
be the base change of $\operatorname{Spec}k(s)\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$,
which is finite étale of degree $d(s)$, and let
$q_s:A'_s\to s$ be the projection. Pullback commutes with direct image
along the closed immersion $i_s$, so $p_1^*i_{s*}E\cong i'_{s*}q_s^*E$,
and the projection formula for the closed immersion $i'_s$ gives
$i'_{s*}q_s^*E\otimes\mathcal K_\psi\cong
i'_{s*}\bigl(q_s^*E\otimes i'^*_s\mathcal K_\psi\bigr)$ for the kernel
$\mathcal K_\psi$ of [def-fd-kernel]. The pairing restricted to
$A'_s$ is the linear function $f_s:\xi\mapsto s\xi$, so
$\mathcal L_s:=i'^*_s\mathcal K_\psi=f_s^*\mathcal L_\psi$ is the
Artin–Schreier sheaf of [def-fd-artin-schreier-sheaf] attached to
$s\xi$, a lisse sheaf of rank one. Since
$p_{2!}\,i'_{s*}=(p_2 i'_s)_!=\pi_{s!}=\pi_{s*}$, the last because
$\pi_s$ is finite, the definition [def-fd-transform] gives

$$
\operatorname{FT}_\psi(i_{s*}E)\cong
\pi_{s*}\bigl(q_s^*E\otimes\mathcal L_s\bigr)[1].
$$

This is the computation of the second formula of [lem-fd-first-formula]
(the case $s=0$, $E=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$) at a general closed
point. As the transform is additive, Step 1 gives
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi(\mathcal B)\cong\mathcal B'[1]$ with

$$
\mathcal B':=\bigoplus_{s\in S_0}
\pi_{s*}\bigl(q_s^*E_s\otimes\mathcal L_s\bigr).
$$

*Step 3: $\mathcal B'$ is lisse.* Each $q_s^*E_s\otimes\mathcal L_s$ is
lisse on $A'_s$. After the base change to $k$, the finite étale map
$\pi_s$ becomes the projection
$A'\times\operatorname{Hom}_{k_0}(k(s),k)\to A'$ from a disjoint union
of $d(s)$ copies of $A'$, so the direct image becomes a direct sum of
$d(s)$ lisse sheaves on $A'$. Hence each summand, and $\mathcal B'$,
is lisse on the whole dual line.

*Step 4: the weights of $\mathcal B'$.* Since $\mathcal M$ is
punctually pure of weight $w$, it is punctually of weights at most $w$ in
the sense of [def-weil-punctual-weights], and the boundary
semicontinuity [lem-wf-boundary-semicontinuity] on the curve $A_0$ with
$\beta=w$ gives $|\iota(\mu)|^2\le q_s^{\,w}$ for every eigenvalue $\mu$
of $F_s$ on $E_s$.

Fix $s\in S_0$, put $\mathcal F_s:=q_s^*E_s\otimes\mathcal L_s$, and let
$z$ be a closed point of $A'_s$ of degree $n$ over $k_0$. Its image in
$s$ gives $d(s)\mid n$, and the local Frobenius $F_z$ acts on the stalk
of $q_s^*E_s$ as $F_s^{\,n/d(s)}$, whose eigenvalues are the
$(n/d(s))$-th powers of those of $F_s$ and so have squared modulus at
most $q_s^{\,wn/d(s)}=q^{wn}$. On the rank-one stalk of
$\mathcal L_s=f_s^*\mathcal L_\psi$ the operator $F_z$ acts as
$F_u^{\,n/d(u)}$, where $u=f_s(z)$ is the image closed point of the line;
by [lem-fd-as-trace] $F_u$ acts by the $p$-th root of unity
$\psi(\operatorname{Tr}_{\kappa(u)/k_0}(u))$. Hence every
eigenvalue of $F_z$ on $(\mathcal F_s)_{\bar z}$ has squared
$\iota$-modulus at most $q^{wn}$.

Now let $y$ be a closed point of $A'_0$ with geometric point $\bar y$.
The stalk of the finite direct image is the sum over the geometric
points of $A'_s$ above $\bar y$,

$$
(\pi_{s*}\mathcal F_s)_{\bar y}=\bigoplus_{\bar z\mapsto\bar y}
(\mathcal F_s)_{\bar z},
$$

and $F_y$ permutes these summands. Its orbits correspond to the closed
points $z$ of $A'_s$ above $y$; if the orbit of $\bar z$ has length $e$,
then $z$ has degree $n=e\,d(y)$ and $F_y^{\,e}$ maps the summand at
$\bar z$ to itself, acting there as $F_z$. Let $\alpha$ be an eigenvalue
of $F_y$ with eigenvector $v=(v_{\bar z})$, and choose $\bar z$ with
$v_{\bar z}\ne0$, of orbit length $e$. Since $F_y^{\,e}$ preserves each
summand of that orbit, comparing components of $F_y^{\,e}v=\alpha^ev$
gives $F_zv_{\bar z}=\alpha^ev_{\bar z}$. By the previous paragraph
$|\iota(\alpha)|^{2e}\le q^{we\,d(y)}$, that is
$|\iota(\alpha)|^2\le q_y^{\,w}$. An eigenvalue of $F_y$ on the finite
direct sum $\mathcal B'_{\bar y}$ is an eigenvalue on one of its
summands, which proves the weight bound.

*Step 5: concentration and the exact sequence.* The short exact sequence
$0\to j_!\mathcal M\to j_*\mathcal M\to\mathcal B\to0$ of Step 1 gives a
distinguished triangle
$j_!\mathcal M[1]\to(j_*\mathcal M)[1]\to\mathcal B[1]\to$. The transform
is an exact triangulated functor by [thm-fd-transform-well-defined];
by [prop-a1-fourier-middle-extension] and Step 2, and after rotation,
this gives a distinguished triangle

$$
\mathcal B'[1]\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow(j'_*\mathcal M')[1]
\longrightarrow\mathcal B'[2],
\qquad K:=\operatorname{FT}_\psi\bigl(j_!\mathcal M[1]\bigr).
$$

Both outer terms have a single cohomology sheaf, in degree $-1$. The
long exact sequence of cohomology sheaves therefore gives
$\mathcal H^aK=0$ for $a\ne-1$, so $K\cong\mathcal G[1]$ with
$\mathcal G:=\mathcal H^{-1}K$, and in degree $-1$ it reads

$$
0=\mathcal H^{-2}\bigl((j'_*\mathcal M')[1]\bigr)\to\mathcal B'\to
\mathcal G\to j'_*\mathcal M'\to\mathcal H^{0}\bigl(\mathcal B'[1]\bigr)=0,
$$

which is the asserted exact sequence. All objects and maps carry the Weil
structure, since the transform and the triangles are formed in the Weil
category.

Let $K_0$ be a field, let $X,Y$ be
finite-type $K_0$-schemes, and let
$f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type
$K_0$-morphism. Fix a prime $\ell$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and
require that its image in $K_0$ is invertible. Choose a finite extension
$E/\Ql$, an integer $n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$,
and put $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $Rf_{!,n}$ be the coherent finite-level
compact-support direct image
functor associated to the
compactification candidates.
The comparison maps for refinements are identities and satisfy the cocycle
condition, and $D^b_c(X,A)$ uses
finite-torsion
constructibility. For $a,b\in\mathbf Z$ with $a\leq b$, write

$$
D_c^{[a,b]}(X,A)=\{K\in D^b_c(X,A):
\mathcal H^r(K)=0\text{ for }r\notin[a,b]\},
$$

where $D^b_c(X,A)$ has the
finite-torsion
constructibility condition, and $\mathcal H^r$ is the
cohomology-sheaf functor.
The ambient
derived direct-image functor
$Rf_{!,n}$ restricts to an exact triangulated functor

$$
Rf_{!,n}:D^b_c(X,A_{E,n})
\longrightarrow D^b_c(Y,A_{E,n}).
$$

For each cohomological interval
$[a,b]$ with $a,b\in\mathbf Z$ and
$a\leq b$, and each integer $e\geq0$ such that every
geometric fiber of $f$ has
dimension at most $e$, there
are integers $a'\leq b'$, independent of the compactification, such that
for every $K\in D_c^{[a,b]}(X,A_{E,n})$ one has

$$
Rf_{!,n}K\in D_c^{[a',b']}(Y,A_{E,n}).
$$

The restriction and its amplitude bound commute with finite coefficient
reduction.
(*Source: the finiteness of compact-support direct images of
constructible torsion sheaves: Stacks Project, More Étale Cohomology,
Section 63.14 (Complexes with constructible cohomology), Theorem 63.14.5,
[Tag `0GL0`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0GL0);
the fibre-dimension amplitude bounds are the finiteness bounds of the
same formalism, cf. Stacks Project, Etale Cohomology, Lemma 59.92.2,
[Tag `095U`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/095U).*)

## Proof

*Step 1 (the compactification form).* By
[def-weil-compact-support-candidate] a compactification of $f$
is a factorisation $f=\bar f\circ j$ with $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$
an open immersion ([def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]) and
$\bar f:\bar X\to Y$ proper ([def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]),
and the candidate
attached to it is $R\bar f_*\circ j_!$, formed with the
derived direct image ([def-weil-derived-direct-image]); the functor
$Rf_{!,n}$ of
[def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] is the coherent choice of a
candidate in the compactification category
[def-weil-compactifications-refinements], and by the hypothesis
recalled in the statement its comparison maps are identities satisfying
the cocycle condition. It therefore suffices to bound the candidate of
a single compactification, and the bound produced below involves only
the amplitude interval of $K$ and the fibre bound $e$, so that it is
independent of the choice.

*Step 2 (transport to the étale site).* The functor is defined on
the pro-étale categories. Under the comparison morphism of sites
$\nu$ of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] the direct images
correspond, $\nu^*Ru_{{\mathrm{et}},*}\cong Ru_{{\mathrm{proet}},*}\nu^*$
([prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image]), and constructibility on
the pro-étale site is by definition the inverse image of
constructibility on the étale site
([def-weil-pbc-constructible-direct-image-finiteness]). It is
accordingly enough to prove the assertion for the étale direct image,
which is what the two classical finiteness theorems below provide.

*Step 3 (extension by zero and the proper case).* For
$K\in D^b_c(X,A)$ the object $j_!K$ lies in $D^b_c(\bar X,A)$ with
constructible cohomology
sheaves ([def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]) in the same degrees: extension by zero
is exact and preserves
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]
([def-weil-extension-by-zero], [lem-fin-extension-by-zero]).
The geometric fibres of $\bar f$ have dimension at most $e$, so
[obl-fin-comparison] applies to $\bar f$: for every constructible
$A$-sheaf $F$ on $\bar X_{{\mathrm{et}}}$ the sheaves
$R^q\bar f_*F$ are constructible and vanish for $q>2e$. For a
complex whose cohomology sheaves lie in degrees $[a,b]$ the conclusion
holds degreewise, the constructible sheaves forming a weak Serre
subcategory ([thm-constructible-serre]), so that
$Rf_{!,n}K\in D_c^{[a,b+2e]}(Y,A)$ for the
constructible cohomological
interval ([def-weil-constructible-intervals]) $D_c^{[a,b+2e]}(Y,A)$.

*Step 4 (the finite-type form).* The same bound is available
without compactifying. By [sbc-thm-finiteness-finite-type],
applied to the finite-type morphism $f$ over the field $K_0$ whose
geometric fibres have dimension at most $e$, the sheaves $R^qf_!F$
are constructible for every $q$ and vanish for $q>2e$, for every
constructible $A$-sheaf $F$; the case of a complex follows as in
Step 3.

*Step 5 (exactness and reduction).* The restriction is a
triangulated functor, $j_!$ and $R\bar f_*$ being exact and
triangulated on the bounded constructible categories, and it commutes
with finite coefficient reduction because the finite-level direct image
does, the reduction being compatible with the comparison morphisms that
enter the definition ([def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]).

attrs.title: Finite-level bounded constructibility for proper support

objects.body:
Let $p$ be prime, let $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, put $q=p^a$, and set
$k_0=\Fq$; let $k=\Fbar$ be the
fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$.
Fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and fix an
indeterminate $T$. For $P(T)=\sum_r c_rT^r\in\mathbf Z[T]$, write
$P^{(\ell)}(T)=\sum_r(c_r\cdot1_{\Ql})T^r$ for coefficientwise extension.
Let $X_0/k_0$ be a
smooth, proper, geometrically
connected scheme of pure dimension
$d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$; put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. Let $F$ be
geometric Frobenius. For every integer $i$
with $0\leq i\leq2d$, put

$$
V_{i,\ell}=H^i(X,\Ql),
\qquad
F_{i,\ell}=F\vert_{V_{i,\ell}},
\qquad
P_{i,\ell}(T)=\det(1-TF_{i,\ell}\mid V_{i,\ell}).
$$

Here $H^i(X,\Ql)$ is the
ordinary cohomology group.
These data form the
smooth-proper
cohomological family. Let $P_i(T)\in\mathbf Z[T]$ be the
integral Frobenius factor
with $P_i(0)=1$ and $P_i^{(\ell)}=P_{i,\ell}$. Put
$b_i=\deg P_i$ and define the
determinant constant
$D_i=(-1)^{b_i}[T^{b_i}]P_i(T)$. Define

$$
\chi=\sum_{i=0}^{2d}(-1)^ib_i,
\qquad
\Delta=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}D_i^{(-1)^i},
\qquad
\varepsilon=(-1)^\chi q^{-d\chi/2}\Delta.
$$

Thus $\varepsilon$ is the
normalized functional-equation
sign. Define the point-count zeta
series by

$$
Z(X_0,T)=\exp\left(\sum_{n\geq1}
\#X_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})\frac{T^n}{n}\right).
$$

The alternating determinant scalar satisfies

$$
\Delta^2=q^{d\chi}.
$$

The normalized sign satisfies

$$
\varepsilon^2=1,\qquad \varepsilon\in\{1,-1\},
$$

and the zeta function satisfies

$$
Z(X_0,q^{-d}T^{-1})
=\varepsilon q^{d\chi/2}T^\chi Z(X_0,T)
\quad\text{in }\mathbf Q(T).
$$

Equivalently, the determinant-constant form of the functional equation is

$$
Z(X_0,q^{-d}T^{-1})
=(-1)^\chi T^\chi
\left(\prod_{i=0}^{2d}D_i^{(-1)^i}\right)Z(X_0,T).
$$

## Proof

1. **1.** The exponential series defining $Z(X_0,T)$ is the
point-count zeta series of [def-weil-point-counts-zeta]; the
trace-to-determinant calculation in
[prop-trace-determinant] identifies it with the normalized product
$$
Z(X_0,T)=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}P_i(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}.
$$
All subsequent manipulations therefore take place in the Laurent rational
function field $\mathbf Q(T)$.
1. **2.** The reciprocity relations in
[prop-duality-reciprocity] give
$$
b_i=b_{2d-i},\qquad D_iD_{2d-i}=q^{db_i},\qquad
P_i(q^{-d}T^{-1})
=(-1)^{b_i}T^{-b_i}D_{2d-i}^{-1}P_{2d-i}(T),
$$
where the last equality is the displayed relation with $i$ replaced by
$2d-i$. Reindexing the product in Step 1 by $i\mapsto2d-i$, and using
$(-1)^{2d-i}=(-1)^i$, gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
Z(X_0,q^{-d}T^{-1})
&=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}
\left((-1)^{b_i}T^{-b_i}D_{2d-i}^{-1}P_{2d-i}(T)\right)^{(-1)^{i+1}}\\
&=(-1)^\chi T^\chi
\left(\prod_{i=0}^{2d}D_i^{(-1)^i}\right)Z(X_0,T).
\end{aligned}
$$
These same reciprocity relations show that $d\chi$ is even. This is
immediate if $d$ is even. If $d$ is odd, then
[prop-duality-reciprocity] gives that $b_d$ is even, while pairing
the terms indexed by $i$ and $2d-i$ gives
$$
\chi=
2\sum_{0\leq i<d}(-1)^ib_i+(-1)^db_d,
$$
which is even. Thus the normalized sign in
[def-weil-functional-equation-sign] is defined.
The determinant-constant definition in
[def-weil-functional-equation-sign] names the product in parentheses
$\Delta$, and the same definition gives
$$
\varepsilon=(-1)^\chi q^{-d\chi/2}\Delta.
$$
The determinant relation also implies
$$
\Delta^2
=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}(D_iD_{2d-i})^{(-1)^i}
=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}q^{db_i(-1)^i}
=q^{d\chi}.
$$
1. **3.** Squaring the preceding normalization and using
[def-weil-functional-equation-sign] yields
$$
\varepsilon^2
=(-1)^{2\chi}q^{-d\chi}\Delta^2=1.
$$
Since $\varepsilon\in\mathbf Q^\times$, it follows that
$\varepsilon\in\{1,-1\}$.
1. **4.** Substituting
$(-1)^\chi\Delta=\varepsilon q^{d\chi/2}$ into the product identity of
Step 2 gives
$$
Z(X_0,q^{-d}T^{-1})
=\varepsilon q^{d\chi/2}T^\chi Z(X_0,T).
$$
Replacing $\Delta$ by its defining product from
[def-weil-functional-equation-sign] gives equivalently
$$
Z(X_0,q^{-d}T^{-1})
=(-1)^\chi T^\chi
\left(\prod_{i=0}^{2d}D_i^{(-1)^i}\right)Z(X_0,T),
$$
which proves both asserted forms.

Use the coefficient stages $A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb$, finite-type
separated schemes over the fixed algebraic closure of a finite field, and separated
finite-type morphisms of [def-fix-six-functor-datum].
Pullback, tensor and the two direct images have their proved constructible
domains. At finite stages, internal Hom preserves bounded constructible
finite-Tor complexes in both variables by
[cor-weil-finite-constructible-hom].
General internal-Hom coefficient change is [thm-coef-finite-hom].
Integral internal Hom and exceptional inverse image preserve the
specified bounded constructible category by
[cor-coef-integral-internal-hom], [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint];
their field versions are [lem-coef-rational-operations], [thm-coef-qbar-verdier].
At finite coefficients the domain remains $D^b_{ctf}$; at integral
and field coefficients it is the specified $D^b_c$.
The sharper dimension-free Hom bound and tensor-dual formulas still
require a site-perfect first
argument. Exceptional adjunction here is on these constructible
categories, without asserting an unrestricted unbounded ambient adjoint.
The following seven clauses collect the preceding results.

1. Finite coefficient-field extension is exact. Compatible finite-stage
functors and transformations descend to the idempotent-complete common-stage
$\Qlb$-category.
1. Compactification comparisons for $Rf_!=R\bar f_*j_!$ are independent
of refinement and satisfy the cocycle condition. For a derived-complete
$\mathcal O_E$-object $K$, put
$K_n=K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$. Then
$$
(Rf_*K)\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}\simeq Rf_*K_n,
\qquad
(Rf_!K)\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}\simeq Rf_!K_n.
$$
Between finite quotient rings, both direct-image coefficient comparisons
hold on the bounded finite-Tor domains. For a coherent normalized DVR
tower, the canonical reduction of its derived limit recovers its terms
by [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity]; uniform finite-level
bounds supply constructibility of the integral output. No such claim
is made for a tower whose normalization has not been proved.
1. Compact-support composition satisfies
$R(gf)_!\simeq Rg_!Rf_!$, with the identity and associativity equations.
For proper $f$, $Rf_!\simeq Rf_*$. For a closed immersion $i$
with open complement $j$, applying $Rf_!$ to the localization triangle gives
$$
R(fj)_!j^*K\longrightarrow Rf_!K\longrightarrow R(fi)_!i^*K\longrightarrow .
$$
1. In a Cartesian square, $g^*Rf_*\to Rf'_*g'^*$ is an isomorphism
if $f$ is proper or $g$ is smooth, and
$g^*Rf_!\simeq Rf'_!g'^*$ for arbitrary base change, on the stated
bounded coefficient domains: for $g^*Rf_*$ this means bounded-below
complexes with torsion cohomology at the finite stages, and
$D^b_c$ of the adic (pro-étale) categories at $\mathcal O_E$, $E$, $\Qlb$,
obtained from the finite stages by derived limits and transport; no claim is
made for discrete non-torsion coefficients on the small étale site.
1. For $K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ and $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$,
the compact-support projection map is an isomorphism:
$$
Rf_!K\otimes^L L\simeq Rf_!(K\otimes^L f^*L).
$$
1. Smooth purity for relative dimension $r$ identifies
$Rf^!L\simeq f^*L(r)[2r]$, with its normalized trace, on the
admissible domains and coefficient stages proved in the purity chapter.
1. For separated finite-type $f:X\to Y$ and structure morphisms set
$\omega_X=Ra_X^!\Lambda$ and
$D_X=R\mathcal Hom(-,\omega_X)$. For
$M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$, the formal Verdier exchange map of
[fix-cor-verdier-exchange] is a natural isomorphism
$$
D_YRf_!M\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf_*D_XM.
$$
Point biduality and smooth site-perfect biduality are proved independently.
At every finite stage $A=A_{E,n}$, the general anti-equivalence
$D_Y:D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)^{\mathrm{op}}\simeq D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$, with
$D_Y^2\simeq\operatorname{id}$, is
[thm-fix-general-biduality]. Its geometric proof also supplies the
finite-stage boundary comparison in
[cor-weil-boundary-duality-discharge].
The coefficient comparisons and uniform bounds are proved separately
in [thm-coef-integral-verdier], [thm-coef-rational-verdier], [thm-coef-qbar-verdier].
They give the same anti-equivalence and evaluation-defined biduality
on $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$, $D^b_c(Y,E)$, and $D^b_c(Y,\Qlb)$.
On these domains $Rf^!=D_Xf^*D_Y$, with its exceptional adjunction,
by [lem-coef-finite-exceptional], [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint], [lem-coef-rational-operations].

All comparisons have the coherence and equivariance proved for their
individual clauses. No clause enlarges the domain of another clause.

## Proof

The finite-stage internal-Hom preservation recorded before the clauses
is [cor-weil-finite-constructible-hom]; its coefficient comparison
is [thm-coef-finite-hom]. Integral preservation and field passage
are [cor-coef-integral-internal-hom], [lem-coef-rational-operations].
Clause (1) is [lem-weil-scalar-extension-exact-triangulated],
[prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors], and
[thm-weil-pbc-idempotent-complete-triangulation].
For (2), use [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed] and the independently
proved [lem-fix-operation-reduction], [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change].
The ordinary finite quotient comparison is [lem-coef-finite-direct-image];
normalized tower reconstruction is [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity].
Clause (3) follows from [thm-sf-comp-composition], [fix-lem-exchanges],
[cor-cbc-proper-coincidence], and the image of
[lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement] under the exact functor of
[lem-compact-support-direct-image-triangulated].
Clause (4) is [thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below], [thm-weil-pbc-qbar],
[sbc-thm-bounded-below-derived-smooth-base-change], and
[thm-cbc-finite-torsion], [thm-cbc-qbar].
Clause (5) is [fix-prop-projection-formula].
Clause (6) is [thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity],
[thm-pur-adic-reconstruction], and
[thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity].
For (7), the exchange is [fix-cor-verdier-exchange];
[lem-weil-coefficient-frobenius] proves the required point duality,
and [thm-sf-dual-perfect] reduces the smooth site-perfect
case to local perfect-complex biduality. General finite-stage biduality is
[thm-fix-general-biduality]; its proof establishes constructible
preservation first and then uses geometric generic restriction and
dimension induction. Boundary exchange is its consequence
[cor-weil-boundary-duality-discharge].
The integral and field anti-equivalences are
[thm-coef-integral-verdier], [thm-coef-rational-verdier], [thm-coef-qbar-verdier].
The exceptional adjunction and its coefficient comparisons are
[lem-coef-finite-exceptional], [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint], [lem-coef-rational-operations].
Finally apply [fix-prop-coherence].
Each ingredient has its own proof; this proposition is a terminal summary.

attrs.title: Coefficient and functor package on the proved domains

objects.body:
Fix the finite-field datum
$p$, $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\Fq$, and let
$k=\Fbar$ be the fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$, a
prime $\ell\neq p$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and choose an algebraic
closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and an
algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}$ of $\mathbf Q$. Put

$$
\overline{\mathbf Q}^{(\ell)}
=\{z\in\Qlb:z\text{ is algebraic over }\mathbf Q\}.
$$

For $\alpha\in\overline{\mathbf Q}^{\times}$ and $i\in\mathbf Z$, call
$\alpha$ a $q$-Weil number of weight $i$ when

$$
|\tau(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}
\quad\text{for every }\tau:\mathbf Q(\alpha)\hookrightarrow\mathbf C;
$$

this is the Weil-number condition, and the
algebraic-closure convention fixes
the ell-adic comparison field. Let $X_0/k_0$ be
smooth, proper, geometrically connected
of pure dimension
$d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let
$(V_{i,\ell},F_{i,\ell},P_{i,\ell})_{0\leq i\leq2d}$ be the
smooth-proper
cohomological family.
Fix indeterminates $T$ and $U$.
Let $Z(X_0,T)$ be the
point-count zeta series.
Let $A,B\in\mathbf Z[T]$ satisfy

$$
Z(X_0,T)=A(T)/B(T),\qquad A(0)=B(0)=1,\qquad
\gcd(A,B)=1\text{ in }\mathbf Q[T],
$$

the normalized integral-fraction
conditions; fix such a normalized presentation. For
$C\in\{A,B\}$, let
$r=\deg C$ and define its reciprocal polynomial

$$
C^\#(U)=U^rC(U^{-1})
$$

Its roots, with multiplicity, are the reciprocal roots in the
reciprocal-root convention;
their inverses are the corresponding ordinary roots. For every integer $i$ with
$0\leq i\leq2d$, define

$$
R_i=
\begin{cases}
\text{the submultiset of roots of \(A^\#\) that are \(q\)-Weil numbers
of weight \(i\)},& i\text{ odd},\\
\text{the submultiset of roots of \(B^\#\) that are \(q\)-Weil numbers
of weight \(i\)},& i\text{ even}.
\end{cases}
$$

Assume that every reciprocal root occurring in $A^\#$ or $B^\#$ has a
unique weight in $\{0,\ldots,2d\}$, and that the displayed $q$-Weil
condition is invariant under every embedding of its number field into
$\mathbf C$. Then for every integer $i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$ each
$R_i$ is stable, with multiplicities, under
$\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathbf Q}/\mathbf Q)$.

## Proof

The polynomials $A^\#,B^\#$ of
[def-weil-ordinary-reciprocal-roots] have rational coefficients,
so their root multisets are stable under
$\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathbf Q}/\mathbf Q)$, and by
[lem-embedding-extension] the $q$-Weil condition of weight $i$
of [def-weil-numbers] is Galois-stable. Hence, for each $i$,
the submultiset $R_i$ is stable under
$\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathbf Q}/\mathbf Q)$, with
multiplicities, which is the assertion.

attrs.title: Galois stability of the weight strata

objects.body:
In the situation of [prop-galois-weight-strata], for every integer
$i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$ the
reciprocal-root multiset of
$Q_i$, equivalently the root multiset of
$Q_i^\#(U)=U^{\deg Q_i}Q_i(U^{-1})$, is exactly the submultiset of the
roots of $A^\#$ satisfying the weight-$i$
$q$-Weil condition when $i$ is odd, and
exactly the submultiset of the roots of $B^\#$ satisfying that condition
when $i$ is even; the multiset is therefore determined by the weight
condition alone and does not depend on the ordering of the roots.

## Proof

The reciprocal-root multiset of $Q_i$ is the root multiset of the monic
polynomial

$$
Q_i^\#(U)=U^{\deg Q_i}Q_i(U^{-1})
=\prod_{\alpha\in R_i}(U-\alpha),
$$

in the convention of [def-weil-ordinary-reciprocal-roots], and by the
definition of $R_i$ – the submultiset of roots of $A^\#$ for $i$
odd and of $B^\#$ for $i$ even satisfying the weight-$i$ $q$-Weil
condition – this is exactly the asserted submultiset; since each root has
a unique weight by assumption, the submultiset does not depend on the
ordering of the roots. The normalized presentation used here is the one
of [def-weil-normalized-integral-fraction].

attrs.title: Identification of the stratum root multisets

objects.body:
In the situation of [prop-galois-weight-strata], for every integer
$i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$ the normalized stratum polynomial

$$
Q_i(T)=\prod_{\alpha\in R_i}(1-\alpha T)
$$

over the $q$-Weil numbers of weight $i$
lies in $\mathbf Z[T]$.

## Proof

Every element of $R_i$ is a root of the reciprocal polynomial
$A^\#$ or $B^\#$ of [def-weil-ordinary-reciprocal-roots], and
because $A,B\in\mathbf Z[T]$ have constant coefficient one these
reciprocal polynomials are monic with integer coefficients, so their roots
are algebraic integers; every elementary symmetric function of the elements
of $R_i$, counted with multiplicities, is therefore an algebraic integer.
These elementary symmetric functions are, up to sign, the coefficients of

$$
Q_i(T)=\prod_{\alpha\in R_i}(1-\alpha T),
$$

and by [prop-galois-weight-strata] they are fixed by
$\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathbf Q}/\mathbf Q)$, hence rational;
being rational algebraic integers, they lie in $\mathbf Z$.

attrs.title: Integrality of the normalized stratum polynomials

objects.body:
Let $p$ be prime, let $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, put $q=p^a$ and
$k_0=\Fq$, and let $k=\Fbar$ be the
fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$.
Fix an indeterminate $T$.
Let $X_0/k_0$ be
smooth, proper, and geometrically
connected of pure dimension $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, and put
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. For every prime
$\ell\neq p$, let
$\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and, for $P(T)=\sum_r c_rT^r\in\mathbf Z[T]$, write
$P^{(\ell)}(T)=\sum_r(c_r\cdot1_{\Ql})T^r$ for its coefficientwise
extension, and let
$(V_{i,\ell},F_{i,\ell},P_{i,\ell})_{0\leq i\leq2d}$ be the
smooth-proper
cohomological family. Define the
point-count zeta series by

$$
Z(X_0,T)=\exp\left(\sum_{n\geq1}
\#X_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})\frac{T^n}{n}\right),
$$

and write its
normalized reduced integral
presentation as

$$
Z(X_0,T)=\frac{A(T)}{B(T)},\qquad
A,B\in\mathbf Z[T],\quad A(0)=B(0)=1,
\quad\gcd(A,B)=1\text{ in }\mathbf Q[T].
$$

For every prime $\ell\neq p$, define the
odd and even parity products

$$
N_\ell(T)=\prod_{\substack{0\leq i\leq2d\\i\text{ odd}}}P_{i,\ell}(T),
\qquad
D_\ell(T)=\prod_{\substack{0\leq i\leq2d\\i\text{ even}}}P_{i,\ell}(T).
$$

There are unique polynomials

$$
P_i(T)\in\mathbf Z[T]
\qquad(0\leq i\leq2d)
$$

with $P_i(0)=1$ and $P_i^{(\ell)}=P_{i,\ell}$ for every
$\ell\neq p$. These are the
integral Frobenius factors.
For every $\ell\neq p$,

$$
A^{(\ell)}=N_\ell,
\qquad
B^{(\ell)}=D_\ell.
$$

The resulting factors satisfy

$$
Z(X_0,T)=
\prod_{i=0}^{2d}P_i(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}
\quad\text{in }\mathbf Q(T),
$$

and

$$
\deg P_i=\dim_{\Ql}H^i(X,\Ql)
$$

where $H^i(X,\Ql)$ denotes the
ordinary cohomology group,
for every $\ell\neq p$.

## Proof

The terminal realization-independent factor interface
[thm-weil-realization-independence] supplies, for every $i$, a unique
integral polynomial $P_i$ whose scalar extension is $P_{i,\ell}$ for every
$\ell\neq p$. Its normalization and the parity products are the
normalizations in [def-weil-integral-frobenius-factor] and
[def-weil-parity-products]; the normalized fraction is the one in
[def-weil-normalized-integral-fraction]. Thus
[def-weil-point-counts-zeta] gives

$$
Z(X_0,T)=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}P_i(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}
$$

after scalar extension, and uniqueness of the normalized fraction gives
$A^{(\ell)}=N_\ell$ and $B^{(\ell)}=D_\ell$. The degree of
$P_{i,\ell}$ is $\dim_{\Ql}H^i(X,\Ql)$ by
[def-weil-smooth-proper-cohomological-family]; scalar extension preserves
degree, so the displayed degree equality follows. All objects and
identifications used here are formed with the finite-field and geometric
hypotheses in [def-weil-finite-field-fiber],
[def-weil-geometric-hypotheses], and the ordinary cohomology convention
[def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology].

The Fourier kernel $\mathcal K_\psi$ of [def-fd-kernel] is lisse of rank one on
$V_0\times_{S_0}V_0^\vee$ and of finite Tor amplitude
([def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]), and

$$
\mathcal K_\psi\otimes\mathcal K_{\psi'}\cong\mathcal K_{\psi\psi'},
\qquad
\mathcal K_\psi^{-1}\cong\mathcal K_{\psi^{-1}} .
$$

(Blueprint def:fd-kernel with lem:fd-as-lisse; the
purity of the kernel is a weight-theoretic statement and is not used here.)

## Proof

$\mathcal K_\psi=b^*\mathcal L_\psi=\mathcal L_{\psi,b}$ is the inverse
image along the pairing $b:V_0\times_{S_0}V_0^\vee\to\mathbf A^1$ of the
Artin–Schreier sheaf $\mathcal L_\psi$ on $\mathbf A^1$, i.e. the Artin–Schreier
sheaf of the function $b$ ([def-fd-kernel]); inverse images of
lisse rank-one sheaves are lisse of rank one, so [lem-fd-as-lisse]
applies verbatim, the value of the character being additive in the defining
function. Lissity of rank one gives finite Tor amplitude, which is what the
definition of the transform needs.

Uses: [def-fd-kernel], [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], [lem-fd-as-lisse]

attrs.title: P1: the kernel is a lisse rank-one character sheaf

objects.body:
The constructed morphism $\chi_a$ is an isomorphism over
$\operatorname{Spec}(A)$.

## Proof

The ring map $\theta_a$ is bijective by the two cited lemmas. The induced
affine morphism is therefore an isomorphism. Compatibility with the
structure morphism is checked on the image of every $r\in A$.

If $I=(f_0,\ldots,f_r)$, the affine opens

$$
\operatorname{Spec}(A[I/f_i])
$$

form a finite open cover of
$\operatorname{Bl}_I(\operatorname{Spec}A)$.

## Proof

The opens $D_+(f_it)$ cover by
[lemma-nagata-rees-generators-cover-proj]. Replace each one by the
affine spectrum supplied by [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart]. The
compatibility of the open embeddings with the structure map is part of that
chart isomorphism.

The constructed morphism $r_s$ is an isomorphism over
$\operatorname{Spec}(A_s)$.

## Proof

By [prop-nagata-rees-localization], the coefficientwise localization
of the Rees algebra is the Rees algebra of $IA_s$. On the standard open
indexed by a homogeneous generator, the induced map is the isomorphism of
degree-zero chart rings from the localization equivalence. These chart
isomorphisms agree on overlaps by the localization cocycle, and therefore
glue to an inverse to $r_s$. The degree-zero piece is $A_s$ on both sides,
so the glued inverse and $r_s$ are morphisms over $\operatorname{Spec}(A_s)$.

The constructed factorization $\mathsf C_{\mathrm{aff}}(U/S)$ is a
compactification of $U\to S$. Consequently, if $U$ is a quasi-affine
scheme and $U\to S$ is quasi-compact and locally of finite type, then
$U\to S$ is compactifiable; this applies in particular when $U$ is affine.

## Proof

Since $U$ is affine, it is quasi-affine by
[lemma-nagata-affine-finite-type-is-quasi-affine]. Apply
[lemma-nagata-quasi-affine-immersion-affine-space] to obtain an
immersion $\iota_U\colon U\to\mathbb A^n_S$. Its composite with the
standard open immersion of
[lemma-nagata-relative-affine-space-open-immersion] is an immersion
$U\to\mathbb P^n_S$. By
[lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper], $\mathbb P^n_S\to S$ is proper.
The immersion-into-proper construction of
[lemma-nagata-immersion-into-proper] therefore supplies a
compactification, and this is exactly
$\mathsf C_{\mathrm{aff}}(U/S)$ by definition.

attrs.title: Property of the affine compactification construction

objects.body:
The constructed factorization $\mathsf{Closed}(i,C')$ is a compactification
of $X\to S$.

## Proof

Its ambient scheme $\overline X$ is closed in the proper scheme
$\overline X'$, hence is proper over $S$. By
[lemma-nagata-scheme-image-restrict-open], its pullback to the open
$X'\subseteq\overline X'$ is the scheme-theoretic image of
$i\colon X\hookrightarrow X'$. By
[lemma-nagata-scheme-image-of-closed-immersion], the factor map for
$i$ is an isomorphism, and compatibility with the image inclusion identifies
the pullback image with $X$. Hence

$$
X\cong\overline X\times_{\overline X'}X',
$$

so $X\to\overline X$ is identified with the base change of the
quasi-compact open immersion $X'\to\overline X'$.

attrs.title: The closed-subscheme construction is a compactification

objects.body:
Let $S$ be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated scheme and let $f\colon X\to S$
be separated and of finite type. Let $\operatorname{Comp}(f)$ be the
category whose objects are the compactifications
$c=(X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{\bar f}S)$ of $f$ in the sense of
[def-nagata-compactification] ($j$ a quasi-compact open immersion, $\bar f$
proper, $\bar f\circ j=f$; scheme-theoretic density of $j$ is *not*
required), and whose morphisms $u\colon c_1\to c_2$, the *refinements*, are
the proper $S$-morphisms $u\colon\overline X_1\to\overline X_2$ with
$u\circ j_1=j_2$. Then:

1. $\operatorname{Comp}(f)$ is nonempty.
1. **(i)** Any two objects $c_1,c_2$ admit a common refinement
$c\to c_1$, $c\to c_2$; hence every finite family of objects admits one.
One such $c$ is the scheme-theoretic image $\overline X$ of
$(j_1,j_2)\colon X\to\overline X_1\times_S\overline X_2$, and for it
$j$ is scheme-theoretically dense.
1. **(ii)** Any two parallel refinements $u,v\colon c_1\to c_2$ are
equalized by a further refinement $c'\to c_1$.

In particular $\operatorname{Comp}(f)$ is cofiltered. Moreover it is
compatible with base change: let $g\colon S'\to S$ be any morphism and
$f'\colon X'=X\times_SS'\to S'$ the base change of $f$.

1. For every object $c$ of $\operatorname{Comp}(f)$, its base change
$c_{S'}=(X'\xrightarrow{j'}\overline X\times_SS'\to S')$ is an object of
$\operatorname{Comp}(f')$, and for every refinement $u\colon c_1\to c_2$ the
base change $u'=u\times_SS'$ is a refinement $c_{1,S'}\to c_{2,S'}$,
functorially in $u$. Consequently base change carries a common refinement
$c\to c_1,\ c\to c_2$ to a common refinement
$c_{S'}\to c_{1,S'},\ c_{S'}\to c_{2,S'}$, and equalizing refinements to
equalizing refinements.
1. If $c$ is the common refinement constructed in (i) from $c_1,c_2$ and
$c'$ the one constructed from $c_{1,S'},c_{2,S'}$, then the ambient scheme
of $c'$ is a closed subscheme of that of $c_{S'}$, and the inclusion is a
refinement $c'\to c_{S'}$ over the two projections. If $g$ is flat, this
inclusion is an isomorphism, i.e. the construction of (i) commutes with
flat base change.

Scheme-theoretic density is not preserved by arbitrary base change, which
is why it is not part of the objects: $c_{S'}$ need not be
scheme-theoretically dense ([def-nagata-dense-compactification]) even if
$c$ is, but it always is when $g$ is flat.

## Proof

*Category.* Identities are refinements, and a composite of two proper
$S$-morphisms compatible with the open immersions is again one, so
$\operatorname{Comp}(f)$ is a category. Note that any $S$-morphism
$u\colon\overline X_1\to\overline X_2$ with $u\circ j_1=j_2$ is automatically
proper by [lemma-nagata-proper-to-separated-target], since $\overline X_1\to S$
is proper and $\overline X_2\to S$ is separated.

*Nonemptiness.* Since $S$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $f$ is
separated of finite type, [thm-nagata-compactification] provides a
compactification of $f$ in the sense of [def-nagata-compactification], i.e.
an object of $\operatorname{Comp}(f)$.

*(i).* Put $Y=\overline X_1\times_S\overline X_2$ and
$a=(j_1,j_2)\colon X\to Y$. The structure map $Y\to S$ is proper: it is the
base change of $\bar f_2$ along $\bar f_1$ followed by $\bar f_1$, and proper
maps are stable under base change and composition. The map $a$ is a
quasi-compact immersion: it factors as

$$
X\xrightarrow{(\mathrm{id},j_2)}X\times_S\overline X_2
\xrightarrow{j_1\times\mathrm{id}}\overline X_1\times_S\overline X_2 ,
$$

where the first map is the graph of $j_2$, a closed immersion because
$\overline X_2\to S$ is separated, and the second is the base change of the
quasi-compact open immersion $j_1$, hence a quasi-compact open immersion.
Moreover $a$ lies over $S$, the composite $X\to Y\to S$ being $f$.
Hence the factorization $\mathsf C(a)$ of [def-nagata-immersion-compactification],

$$
X\xrightarrow{a^{\mathrm{im}}}\overline X=\operatorname{SIm}(a)
\hookrightarrow Y\longrightarrow S ,
$$

with $\operatorname{SIm}(a)$ the scheme-theoretic image of
[def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image], is a compactification
$c=(j,\bar c)$ of $f$ by [lemma-nagata-immersion-into-proper], where
$j=a^{\mathrm{im}}$; by [lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image], $j$
is moreover scheme-theoretically dense. Let
$p_i\colon\overline X\hookrightarrow Y\to\overline X_i$ be the restricted
projections. They are $S$-morphisms with
$p_i\circ j=\mathrm{pr}_i\circ a=j_i$, and they are proper by
[lemma-nagata-proper-to-separated-target] since $\overline X\to S$ is proper
and $\overline X_i\to S$ is separated. So $p_i\colon c\to c_i$ are
refinements. For a family $c_1,\dots,c_n$ with $n\geq3$, take a common
refinement $c''$ of $c_1,\dots,c_{n-1}$ by induction and a common refinement
of $c''$ and $c_n$; composing refinements gives the claim.

*(ii).* Let $u,v\colon c_1\to c_2$ be parallel refinements, and let
$\overline X'\subseteq\overline X_1$ be their equalizer, i.e. the pullback of
the diagonal $\Delta\colon\overline X_2\to\overline X_2\times_S\overline X_2$
along $(u,v)\colon\overline X_1\to\overline X_2\times_S\overline X_2$. Since
$\overline X_2\to S$ is separated, $\Delta$ is a closed immersion, so
$i\colon\overline X'\hookrightarrow\overline X_1$ is a closed immersion and
$\overline X'\to\overline X_1\xrightarrow{\bar f_1}S$ is proper. Because
$u\circ j_1=j_2=v\circ j_1$, the universal property of the pullback gives
$j'\colon X\to\overline X'$ with $i\circ j'=j_1$. This $j'$ is a
quasi-compact open immersion: the closed subscheme
$\overline X'\times_{\overline X_1}X$ of $X$ receives the section induced by
$j'$, so it is all of $X$; hence
$X\cong\overline X'\times_{\overline X_1}X$ and $j'$ is the base change of
$j_1$ along $i$. Thus $c'=(j',\bar f_1\circ i)$ is an object of
$\operatorname{Comp}(f)$, the closed immersion $i$ (which is proper) is a
refinement $c'\to c_1$, and $u\circ i=v\circ i$ by construction.

A nonempty category in which any two objects have a common refinement and
any two parallel morphisms are equalized by a further morphism is cofiltered
by definition, so (i), (ii) and nonemptiness give the cofilteredness.

*Base change, first part.* By [lemma-nagata-compactification-base-change],
the construction $c_{S'}$ of [def-nagata-compactification-base-change] is a
compactification of $f'$, i.e. an object of $\operatorname{Comp}(f')$. For
a refinement $u\colon c_1\to c_2$, the map
$u'=u\times_SS'\colon\overline X_1\times_SS'\to\overline X_2\times_SS'$ is an
$S'$-morphism, it is proper as a base change of a proper morphism, and
$u'\circ j_1'=(u\circ j_1)\times_SS'=j_2'$ by functoriality of fibre
products. Functoriality $(u\circ w)'=u'\circ w'$ and $\mathrm{id}'=\mathrm{id}$
holds for the same reason; hence commuting triangles and equalities
$u\circ w=v\circ w$ are preserved, which gives the statements on common and
equalizing refinements.

*Base change, second part.* Let $Y'=Y\times_SS'
=\overline X_{1}'\times_{S'}\overline X_{2}'$ with
$\overline X_i'=\overline X_i\times_SS'$, let $q\colon Y'\to Y$ be the
projection, and let $a'=(j_1',j_2')\colon X'\to Y'$, which is the base change
of $a$ along $q$. The ambient scheme of $c_{S'}$ is
$\operatorname{SIm}(a)\times_YY'$, a closed subscheme of $Y'$ through which
$a'$ factors (via $j\times_SS'$). By [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-universal]
applied to $a'$, there is a unique closed immersion
$\operatorname{SIm}(a')\hookrightarrow\operatorname{SIm}(a)\times_YY'$
compatible with the maps to $Y'$ and hence with the maps from $X'$; it is
proper and lies over the two projections to $\overline X_i'$, so it is a
refinement $c'\to c_{S'}$ compatible with the refinements to $c_{i,S'}$.
If $g$ is flat, so is $q$. The morphism $a$ is quasi-compact, and it is
quasi-separated as an immersion; so the flat base change statement in
[lemma-nagata-dense-flat-pullback] gives
$\operatorname{SIm}(a')\cong\operatorname{SIm}(a)\times_YY'$ as closed
subschemes of $Y'$, i.e. the above inclusion is an isomorphism.

*Density.* Density is not stable under arbitrary base change: for
$S=\overline X=\operatorname{Spec}K[t]$ over a field $K$, $X=D(t)$ and $j$ the
inclusion, $c=(j,\mathrm{id})$ is scheme-theoretically dense, but its base
change to $S'=\operatorname{Spec}K$ ($t=0$) has $X'=\varnothing$ and
$\overline X'=\operatorname{Spec}K$, so it is not. For flat $g$, the
dense-pullback statement in [lemma-nagata-dense-flat-pullback], applied to
$j$ (quasi-compact, and quasi-separated as an immersion) and the flat map
$\overline X\times_SS'\to\overline X$, shows that $c_{S'}$ is again
scheme-theoretically dense whenever $c$ is. This is why
$\operatorname{Comp}(f)$ uses the notion of [def-nagata-compactification]
without density.

attrs.title: The compactification category is nonempty, cofiltered, and base-changes

objects.body:
The object $\mathsf{Dense}(C)$ is a scheme-theoretically dense
compactification of the same morphism as $C$.

## Proof

The induced map from $X$ is a quasi-compact open immersion and is
scheme-theoretically dense by
[lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image]. The new ambient scheme
is closed in $\overline X$, so it remains proper over $S$. Finally, if
$p\colon\overline X\to S$ is the original structural map, then

$$
j^{\mathrm{im}};j_{\mathrm{im}};p
=j;p=f
$$

by `Scheme.Hom.toImage_imageι`; hence the refined factorization has
the same composite as $C$.

The constructed morphism $X^{\mathrm{fp}}\to S$ is separated and of
finite presentation, and the constructed map
$i^{\mathrm{fp}}_{X/S}\colon X\to X^{\mathrm{fp}}$ is a closed immersion
over $S$.

## Proof

A finite-type morphism over a quasi-compact base has quasi-compact source,
and separatedness makes that source quasi-separated, so the model system is
available. Its property lemma makes every term finite presentation and
every structural map $i_\alpha$ a closed immersion. At the explicitly
selected stage $\alpha^{X/S}_{\mathrm{sep}}$, separatedness follows from
[lemma-nagata-fixed-base-separated-eventually]. These are exactly the
three assertions for the named envelope.

attrs.title: Properties of the separated finite-presentation envelope, [stacks-project]

objects.body:
The constructed comparison is the unique isomorphism over $X$ restricting
to the identity comparison on every common affine refinement.

## Proof

By [prop-nagata-global-blowup-cover-independent], the comparison is an
isomorphism on every member of the common refinement. The overlap cocycle
makes these local isomorphisms compatible, so they glue; the glued inverse
is obtained from the local inverses. Uniqueness follows because morphisms
of schemes are determined on an affine open cover.

## Compatibility of the local structure maps

On every overlap, the two local structure maps to $X$ agree after applying
the constructed overlap map $\omega_{ij}$.

*Proof.*
On a basic refinement, both composites are the structural map from the
blow-up of the localized ideal to $D(s)\subseteq X$; the degree-zero part of
the restriction isomorphism makes them equal. Equality on the basic cover
gives equality on the overlap.

## Global blow-up morphism

Define

$$
b_{X,\mathcal I}\colon\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)\longrightarrow X
$$

by gluing the local structure maps
$\mathsf B_{V_i}(\mathcal I)\to V_i\to X$. Their overlap equality is
[prop-nagata-global-blowup-cover-independent], so the morphism-gluing
interface applies.

## Affine-restriction comparison for the global blow-up

If $V=\operatorname{Spec}(A)\subseteq X$ and $I_V$ represents
$\mathcal I|_V$, define

$$
q_V\colon b_{X,\mathcal I}^{-1}(V)\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Bl}_{I_V}(\operatorname{Spec}A)
$$

by gluing the affine restriction maps on the basic intersections of $V$
with the chosen affine cover of $X$.

## Comparison between two affine-cover constructions

Given two affine covers of $X$, choose their intersection refinement. On
every refined affine chart use the two affine-restriction isomorphisms to
define a comparison, and glue these comparisons after transporting them to
the original charts. The overlap equalities are those of
[lemma-nagata-global-blowup-overlap-cocycle].
The refinement maps are independent of the selected basic chart by the
overlap cocycle, so the glued comparison is well-defined as a morphism of
the two gluing data.

## Affine restriction of the global blow-up

The constructed comparison $q_V$ is an isomorphism over $V$.

*Proof.*
Cover $V$ by basic opens contained in the chosen affine charts. On each,
the comparison is an isomorphism by
[prop-nagata-affine-blowup-restrict]; the overlap cocycle and local-map
compatibility show that these maps and their inverses agree. The gluing
theorem therefore produces mutually inverse global morphisms over $V$.

attrs.title: The global blow-up map, its affine restrictions, and independence of the affine cover

objects.body:
Every quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme $S$ admits a Noetherian
approximation. Concretely, the constructed system $\mathsf N(S)$ has affine
transition morphisms, every term is of finite type over $\mathbf Z$, and
$\kappa_S$ identifies $S$ with its inverse limit.

## Proof

Nonemptiness and directedness of the index type, including the transition
identities, are supplied by
[lemma-nagata-valid-refinements-directed]. By
[lemma-nagata-glue-noetherian-stage], every chart of every $S_\lambda$
is the spectrum of a finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-algebra and every
transition is affine. Such rings are Noetherian, so the glued schemes are
Noetherian. On a selected affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ of $S$,
the chart rings $A_\lambda$ form a filtered system whose colimit is $A$ by
the finite-subalgebra lemma; the affine inverse-limit calculation therefore
identifies $\varprojlim\operatorname{Spec}(A_\lambda)$ with
$\operatorname{Spec}(A)$. The identifications commute with restriction to
every recorded basic overlap because all transition maps are induced by the
same localization maps in $A$. Since the affine charts and overlaps are
finite, these local inverses glue and are inverse to the comparison
$\kappa_S$ of [def-nagata-glued-limit-comparison]. Hence $\kappa_S$ is
an isomorphism and all asserted properties hold.

Each positive-degree homogeneous $f$ determines an open subscheme
$D_+(f)\subseteq\operatorname{Proj}(R)$ and a canonical isomorphism

$$
D_+(f)\cong\operatorname{Spec}(R_{(f),0}).
$$

If homogeneous elements $(f_i)$ generate $R_+$, the $D_+(f_i)$ cover
$\operatorname{Proj}(R)$.

## Proof

The standard-open isomorphism is `Proj.basicOpenIsoSpec`.
The cover assertion is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.iSup_basicOpen_eq_top`; its hypothesis
that the chosen homogeneous family generates the irrelevant ideal is the
assumption in the statement.
Thus no independently glued affine scheme is being used.

If $I=(f_0,\ldots,f_r)$, then $\mathcal R_A(I)$ is generated as an algebra
over its degree-zero piece by $f_0t,\ldots,f_rt$. In particular it is of
finite type over $\mathcal R_A(I)_0$.

## Proof

A homogeneous coefficient in $I^n$ is a linear combination of degree-$n$
monomials in the $f_i$. Hence every homogeneous Rees element belongs to the
algebra generated by the $f_it$, and
[lemma-nagata-rees-sum-components] treats an arbitrary element.
Transport finite generation along
[lemma-nagata-rees-degree-zero].

The family $n\mapsto\mathcal R_A(I)_n$ defines an
$\mathbb N$-graded-ring structure on $\mathcal R_A(I)$.

## Proof

Use [lemma-nagata-rees-piece-mul] for graded multiplication,
[lemma-nagata-rees-sum-components] for existence of the direct-sum
decomposition, and [lemma-nagata-rees-components-unique] for
uniqueness.

attrs.title: Graded-ring structure on the Rees algebra

objects.body:
The map $\rho_s$ is a graded ring equivalence.

## Proof

For each $n$, let $\rho_{s,n}$ be the equivalence of
[lemma-nagata-localization-rees-piece]. Taking their direct sum is
legitimate because every Rees element has finite homogeneous support. On
homogeneous tensors of degrees $m,n$, both ways around the multiplication
square have coefficient $(xy)/1$ in degree $m+n$; the equality of localized
ideal powers from [lemma-nagata-localization-ideal-pow] proves
multiplicativity. The direct sum of the inverse maps is constructed in
the same way, and the two composites are identities in each degree, hence
on finite sums. This gives the claimed graded ring equivalence.

attrs.title: Graded localization of the Rees algebra

objects.body:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: no separate relative-Proj
primitive was formalized. The blow-up is glued from the affine Proj charts
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.basicOpenIsoSpec`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.iSup_basicOpen_eq_top`) with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Cover.RelativeGluingData`.

Relative Proj has the following properties.

1. Its restriction to an affine open $V$ is canonically
$\operatorname{Proj}(\Gamma(V,\mathcal A))$, compatibly on iterated
restrictions.
1. A degree-preserving equivalence of graded algebras inducing the
chosen degree-zero base identification induces an isomorphism of Proj.
1. A surjective degree-preserving morphism of graded algebras induces
a closed immersion in the opposite direction on Proj.
1. If $g\colon X'\to X$ is flat, then coefficientwise pullback gives a
canonical base-change isomorphism
$$
\operatorname{Proj}_{X'}(g^*\mathcal A)
\cong X'\times_X\operatorname{Proj}_X(\mathcal A).
$$

The same base-change construction is required for an arbitrary morphism
$X'\to X$ when the universal blow-up lift is formed; that unrestricted
comparison is recorded as a separate conditional interface below.

## Proof

For (1), use the restriction isomorphism in
[lemma-nagata-relative-proj-exists]; transitivity of coefficientwise
localization gives the iterated-restriction equality. For (2), on an affine
chart the graded equivalence carries each homogeneous denominator to a
homogeneous denominator and induces an isomorphism of the corresponding
degree-zero localizations, hence an isomorphism of standard affine opens.
These maps agree on overlaps by the localization cocycle and glue uniquely.
For (3), a surjection has surjective maps on every homogeneous localization;
the induced maps on degree-zero rings give closed immersions of all standard
affine opens, which glue to the asserted closed immersion. Finally, for
(4), on $V=\operatorname{Spec}(A)\subseteq X$, put
$C=\Gamma(V,\mathcal A)$, and on
$V'=\operatorname{Spec}(B)\subseteq X'$ over $V$, the chart at a
homogeneous $f$ is identified on both sides using

$$
(C_{(f),0})\otimes_A B
\xrightarrow{\sim}(B\otimes_A C)_{(f\otimes1),0},
\qquad (x/f^m)\otimes b\longmapsto (x\otimes b)/(f\otimes1)^m .
$$

To justify this without a hidden cancellation argument, identify the
degree-zero homogeneous localization with the filtered colimit
$\varinjlim_m C_{md}$ whose transition map is multiplication by $f$.
Tensor product commutes with this filtered colimit, giving the displayed
isomorphism (in fact without using flatness). On pure fractions its inverse
sends $(x\otimes b)/(f\otimes1)^m$ to $(x/f^m)\otimes b$. It is compatible
with further localization, so the chart isomorphisms glue, and their
structural maps identify the glued schemes over $X$. This proves all four
assertions.

**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the strict transform is
supplied by the API of
`WeilConjectures/Compactification/StrictTransform.lean` —
`AlgebraicGeometry.strictTransform`, its closed immersion
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.isClosedImmersion_pullbackLift_blowup_comap`,
and the pullback square
`AlgebraicGeometry.isPullback_strictTransformOpen` — so the
strict-transform chart rings and their cocycle are never assembled by hand.

The constructed comparison $\overline\sigma_a$ is a ring equivalence.

## Proof

The map $\sigma_a$ is surjective and its kernel is precisely the ideal by
which the source was quotiented. The first isomorphism theorem therefore
makes $\overline\sigma_a$ bijective and identifies its inverse ring
structure, so it is a ring equivalence.

**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the strict transform is
supplied by the API of
`WeilConjectures/Compactification/StrictTransform.lean` —
`AlgebraicGeometry.strictTransform`, its closed immersion
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.isClosedImmersion_pullbackLift_blowup_comap`,
and the pullback square
