strict-transform chart rings and their cocycle are never assembled by hand.

Under the data of
[def-nagata-strict-transform-closed-chart-model], the constructed chart
model $Y^{\mathrm{st}}_{\mathrm{chart}}$ is a closed
subscheme of $Y\times_XX'$ and agrees with the strict transform of
[def-nagata-strict-transform].

## Proof

The chartwise closed immersions agree on overlaps by
[lemma-nagata-strict-transform-chart-cocycle]; therefore their ideals
glue to a global quasi-coherent ideal, with localization compatibility
supplied by [lemma-nagata-strict-transform-chart-localization-data].
On each chart the quotient removes
exactly the sections supported on the exceptional divisor, so the resulting
closed subscheme is the scheme-theoretic closure of the preserved open and
hence is the strict transform.

attrs.title: Global strict transform is a closed subscheme

objects.body:
Let $i\colon Z\to X$ be a closed immersion. Then the counit

$$
\varepsilon\colon i^*i_*\Longrightarrow\mathrm{id}_{\shv{\et Z}}
$$

is an isomorphism; equivalently, $i_*$ is fully faithful.

## Proof

Fix $\mathcal H\in\shv{\et Z}$. By [lemma-openclosed-point-ulift] it is
enough to show that $\varepsilon_{\mathcal H}$ is an isomorphism on the stalk
at every geometric point $\bar z$ of $Z$. So fix $\bar z$ and write
$\Phi_{\bar z}$ for its stalk functor on $\shv{\et Z}$; recall that
$\Phi_{\bar z}$ is left adjoint to the skyscraper functor
$M\mapsto\mathrm{sky}_{\bar z}(M)$ of $\bar z$.

The stalk of $i^*i_*\mathcal H$ is never computed. Instead:

*Step 1.* A morphism is invertible as soon as precomposition with it is
bijective on morphisms into every object $M$ of $\mathcal A$. So it suffices
to show that

$$
(-)\circ\Phi_{\bar z}(\varepsilon_{\mathcal H})\colon
\Hom(\Phi_{\bar z}(\mathcal H),M)\to
\Hom(\Phi_{\bar z}(i^*i_*\mathcal H),M)
$$

is bijective for every $M$.

*Step 2.* The composite of $i^*\dashv i_*$ with
$\Phi_{\bar z}\dashv\mathrm{sky}_{\bar z}$ is an adjunction
$i^*\circ\Phi_{\bar z}\dashv\mathrm{sky}_{\bar z}\circ\,i_*$ (note
$\Phi_{\bar z}(i^*-)$ is the source of the map in Step 1 read at
$i_*\mathcal H$). Transposing along it turns precomposition with
$\Phi_{\bar z}(\varepsilon_{\mathcal H})$ into

$$
i_*\colon
\Hom(\mathcal H,\mathrm{sky}_{\bar z}(M))\to
\Hom(i_*\mathcal H,i_*\mathrm{sky}_{\bar z}(M));
$$

this is a formal identity of the two adjunctions, the triangle identity of
$i^*\dashv i_*$ read through the naturality of the unit of
$\Phi_{\bar z}\dashv\mathrm{sky}_{\bar z}$.

*Step 3.* Pushing forward a skyscraper along $i_*$ gives a skyscraper:
$i_*\mathrm{sky}_{\bar z}(M)$ is, on the nose, the skyscraper sheaf at the
point $i\circ\bar z$ of $\et X$ obtained from $\bar z$ by base change.
Therefore the map of Step 2 is, after transposing back along
$\Phi_{i\circ\bar z}\dashv\mathrm{sky}_{i\circ\bar z}$, precomposition with
the stalk comparison

$$
(i_*\mathcal H)_{i\circ\bar z}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\mathcal H_{\bar z}
$$

of [lemma-openclosed-stalk-lowerstar], which is an isomorphism.
Precomposition with an isomorphism is bijective, so the map of Step 1 is
bijective and $(\varepsilon_{\mathcal H})_{\bar z}$ is an isomorphism.

Hence $\varepsilon_{\mathcal H}$ is an isomorphism for every $\mathcal H$,
that is, $\varepsilon$ is an isomorphism and $i_*$ is fully faithful.

The only step that is not formal is Step 3, and there the only thing to check
by hand is the compatibility of the stalk comparison with the canonical maps
from the sections over a pointed étale neighbourhood; that is where the
initiality of [lemma-openclosed-stalk-lowerstar] enters.

Let $k$ be a separably closed field
and let $X$ be a smooth
projective curve over $k$ with a
$k$-rational point $\sigma$. Then:

1. $H^0(X,\mathcal{O}_X)=k$ and $f_*\mathcal{O}_X=\mathcal{O}_k$ (where $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec} k$);
1. for every field extension $K/k$, the
base change $X_K$ is a smooth
projective curve over $K$ (in particular $X_K$ is integral, and $X$ is
geometrically integral), with $H^0(X_K,\mathcal{O}_{X_K})=K$ and
$\dim_KH^1(X_K,\mathcal{O}_{X_K})=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal{O}_X)$.

## Proof

Since $X$ is a proper variety (projective $\Rightarrow$ proper,
[lem-pc-projective-proper]; a curve is a variety, hence integral,
[def-pc-curve]), the ring $k':=H^0(X,\mathcal{O}_X)$ is a finite field
extension of $k$ by [lem-pc-h0-proper-variety] (1). The section
$\sigma$ gives a $k$-algebra homomorphism $\sigma^\#:H^0(X,\mathcal{O}_X)\to H^0(\operatorname{Spec}(k),\mathcal{O}_k)=k$, and a field homomorphism $k'\to k$ over $k$ is
injective; hence $[k':k]=1$, i.e. $k'=k$; since $H^0(X,\mathcal{O}_X)=k$ the
quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_k$-module $f_*\mathcal{O}_X$ is free of rank one, so
$f_*\mathcal{O}_X=\mathcal{O}_k$. This proves (1).

For (2): let $K/k$ be a field extension and let
$g:\operatorname{Spec}(K)\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$. The base change $g$ is flat
([lem-pc-flat-field]), and $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated
(proper, [lem-pc-projective-proper]), so by
[lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom] applied to $\mathcal{F}=\mathcal{O}_X$,

$$
g^*f_*\mathcal{O}_X\;\cong\;f_{K,*}\mathcal{O}_{X_K},
$$

hence $f_{K,*}\mathcal{O}_{X_K}=\mathcal{O}_K$ and $H^0(X_K,\mathcal{O}_{X_K})=K$; likewise
$H^1(X_K,\mathcal{O}_{X_K})\cong H^1(X,\mathcal{O}_X)\otimes_kK$, whence
$\dim_K H^1(X_K,\mathcal{O}_{X_K})=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal{O}_X)$.
The morphism $X_K\to\operatorname{Spec}(K)$ is smooth (base change of smooth,
[lem-pc-proper-base-change]) and proper (base change of proper,
[lem-pc-proper-base-change]), so $X_K$ is regular
([lem-sc-smooth-regular]), hence normal ([rem-pc-regular-normal])
and reduced. Moreover $X_K$ is geometrically reduced: for every $K'/K$,
$X_{K'}$ is smooth over $K'$, hence regular, hence reduced; and $X_K$ is
proper, so [lem-pc-h0-geom-connected] (with $k$ replaced by $K$ and
$X$ by $X_K$) shows that $X_K$ is geometrically connected, in particular
connected. A Noetherian normal connected scheme is irreducible by
[rem-pc-regular-normal]: the normal scheme $X_K$ is a finite disjoint
union of normal integral schemes, and connectedness forces a single
component. Hence $X_K$ is integral. By [lem-pc-dim-base-change]
the dimension of $X_K$ is $1$, and $X_K\to\operatorname{Spec}(K)$ is of finite type and
separated (base changes of finite type and separated morphisms), so $X_K$
is a variety of dimension $1$, i.e. a curve ([def-pc-curve]).
Finally $X_K$ is projective: the closed immersion
$i:X\to\mathbf{P}^n_k$ base changes to a closed immersion
$i_K:X_K\to\mathbf{P}^n_K$ ([lem-pc-closed-imm-base-change]). This proves
(2); applying (2) to $K=k$ (and all extensions) gives geometric
integrality of $X$.

attrs.title: Base changes of $X$ are smooth projective curves

objects.body:
Let $k$ be a separably closed field
and let $C$ be a smooth projective
curve over $k$. Fix a $k$-rational point
$P\in C(k)$ (one exists by [lem-pc-rational-points-dense]), and for
$d\in\Z$ put $\mathcal{O}_C(dP):=\mathcal{O}_C(P)^{\otimes d}$ (a negative power
meaning a power of the dual), where $\mathcal{O}_C(P)$ is the module of
[def-pc-divisor-line-bundle] of the effective Cartier divisor $P$
([lem-sc-point-cartier]). Let $\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}_{C/k}$ be the group
scheme representing $\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}$
([thm-pc-picard-representable], [rem-pc-group-structure]), and let
$\deg:\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}\to\underline{\Z}$ be the degree morphism of
[def-pd-degree-morphism]. For $d\in\Z$ let
$\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}\subseteq\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}$ be the
subfunctor of classes whose
fibrewise degree function is identically $d$. Then:

1. $\deg$ is a homomorphism of sheaves of groups; in particular
$\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}=\ker(\deg)$ is a subgroup functor and
$\operatorname{Pic}^{d}_{C/k}\cdot\operatorname{Pic}^{e}_{C/k}\subseteq\operatorname{Pic}^{d+e}_{C/k}$.
1. The function $\delta:\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}_{C/k}\to\Z$, $t\mapsto\deg\mathcal{L}_t$,
is locally constant, where $\mathcal{L}$ is an invertible module on
$C\times_k\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}_{C/k}$ representing the universal class
(one exists, normalized along $P$). Hence
$$
\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}_{C/k}=\coprod_{d\in\Z}\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}^d_{C/k},
\qquad
\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}^d_{C/k}:=\delta^{-1}(d),
$$
each $\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}^d_{C/k}$ is an open and closed subscheme,
and it represents the subfunctor $\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}$.
1. $\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}^0_{C/k}$ is an open and closed subgroup scheme
of $\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}_{C/k}$.
1. For every $d\in\Z$, tensoring with $\mathcal{O}_C(dP)$, i.e. the translation
$x\mapsto x\cdot[\mathcal{O}_C(dP)]$ by the $k$-point
$[\mathcal{O}_C(dP)]\in\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}_{C/k}(k)$, which on a class
represented by an invertible module $\mathcal{M}$ on $C_T$ is
$\mathcal{M}\mapsto\mathcal{M}\otimes\operatorname{pr}_C^*\mathcal{O}_C(dP)$, restricts to an
isomorphism of schemes
$$
\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}^0_{C/k}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}^d_{C/k},
$$
with inverse the translation by $[\mathcal{O}_C(-dP)]$.

## Proof

Throughout, for a field extension $K/k$ the base change $C_K$ is a smooth
projective curve over $K$, in particular integral, with the $K$-rational
point $P_K$ ([prop-pc-xk-integral], applied with $\sigma=P$); so $C$ is
geometrically integral and [def-pd-fibrewise-degree],
[def-pd-degree-morphism] and [lem-pd-degree-locally-constant] apply.

*Step 0: additivity of the degree over a field.* Let $K/k$ be a field
extension, write $Q=P_K$, and let $\mathcal{N},\mathcal{M}$ be invertible modules
on $C_K$. We claim
$\deg(\mathcal{N}\otimes\mathcal{M})=\deg\mathcal{N}+\deg\mathcal{M}$, with $\deg$ as in
[def-pc-degree-line-bundle]. First, for every invertible $\mathcal{N}'$,
[lem-pc-degree-base-change](2) with $D=Q$ and [lem-pc-degree-agrees-sc]
($\deg\mathcal{O}_{C_K}(Q)=1$ for the $K$-rational point $Q$) give
$\deg(\mathcal{N}'\otimes\mathcal{O}_{C_K}(Q))=\deg\mathcal{N}'+1$; iterating,
$\deg(\mathcal{N}'\otimes\mathcal{O}_{C_K}(Q)^{\otimes n})=\deg\mathcal{N}'+n$ for $n\geq0$.
Now choose $n\geq0$ with $\deg\mathcal{M}+n+\chi(C_K,\mathcal{O}_{C_K})>0$ and put
$\mathcal{M}'=\mathcal{M}\otimes\mathcal{O}_{C_K}(Q)^{\otimes n}$. By
[def-pc-degree-line-bundle],
$\chi(C_K,\mathcal{M}')=\deg\mathcal{M}'+\chi(C_K,\mathcal{O}_{C_K})=\deg\mathcal{M}+n+\chi(C_K,\mathcal{O}_{C_K})>0$,
and since $H^i(C_K,\mathcal{M}')=0$ for $i\geq2$ ([lem-pc-vanishing-above-dim])
the Euler characteristic ([def-pc-euler-characteristic]) is
$\dim_KH^0-\dim_KH^1$, so $H^0(C_K,\mathcal{M}')\neq0$. Let $s$ be a nonzero
global section. As $C_K$ is integral, on an open where
$\mathcal{M}'\cong\mathcal{O}$ the section $s$ is a nonzero element of a domain, hence
a nonzerodivisor; so its zero scheme $D$ is an
effective Cartier divisor,
$s$ identifies $\mathcal{M}'^{\vee}$ with the ideal $\mathcal{I}_D$, and dualizing
gives $\mathcal{M}'\cong\mathcal{I}_D^{\vee}=\mathcal{O}_{C_K}(D)$. Applying
[lem-pc-degree-base-change](2) twice,
$$
\deg(\mathcal{N}\otimes\mathcal{M})+n=\deg(\mathcal{N}\otimes\mathcal{O}_{C_K}(D))
=\deg\mathcal{N}+\deg\mathcal{O}_{C_K}(D)=\deg\mathcal{N}+\deg\mathcal{M}+n,
$$
which is the claim. In particular $\deg\mathcal{O}_{C_K}=0$,
$\deg\mathcal{N}^{\vee}=-\deg\mathcal{N}$, and (iterating from
$\deg\mathcal{O}_C(P)=1$) $\deg\mathcal{O}_C(dP)=d$ for all $d\in\Z$.

*(1) $\deg$ is a homomorphism.* Let $x,y\in\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}(T)$. Since the
Picard functor is the fppf
sheafification of the Picard presheaf, there is an fppf covering
$\{T_i\to T\}$ (a common refinement of coverings for $x$ and for $y$)
and invertible modules $\mathcal{L}_i,\mathcal{M}_i$ on $C_{T_i}$ whose classes are
$x|_{T_i}$, $y|_{T_i}$; the map from the presheaf to its sheafification
is a homomorphism, and the group law of the presheaf is $\otimes$, so
$(xy)|_{T_i}$ is the class of $\mathcal{L}_i\otimes\mathcal{M}_i$. For $t\in T$ pick
$t_i\in T_i$ over $t$. By the construction of [def-pd-degree-morphism]
and [lem-pd-degree-locally-constant](3), $\deg(xy)(t)$ is the degree of
$(\mathcal{L}_i\otimes\mathcal{M}_i)_{t_i}=(\mathcal{L}_i)_{t_i}\otimes(\mathcal{M}_i)_{t_i}$ on
$C_{\kappa(t_i)}$, which by Step 0 equals
$\deg(x)(t)+\deg(y)(t)$. Hence $\deg(xy)=\deg(x)+\deg(y)$; the remaining
assertions of (1) follow.

*(2) Decomposition.* By [cor-pc-sigma-pic-iso] (with $\sigma=P$) the
class of the identity of $\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}_{C/k}$, the universal class
$\xi\in\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}(\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}_{C/k})$, is the class of an
invertible module $\mathcal{L}$ on $C\times_k\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}_{C/k}$ (trivial
along $P$). Computing [def-pd-degree-morphism] with the trivial covering,
$\deg(\xi)=\delta$, which is locally constant by
[lem-pd-degree-locally-constant](1). Hence the sets
$U_d:=\delta^{-1}(d)$ are open and closed, pairwise disjoint and cover
$\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}_{C/k}$, so $\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}_{C/k}$ is the scheme-theoretic
disjoint union of the open subschemes $U_d=\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}^d_{C/k}$. Let
$h:T\to\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}_{C/k}$ correspond to $x=h^*\xi$. Since $\deg$ is a
morphism of sheaves and restriction in $\underline{\Z}$ is composition,
$\deg(x)=\delta\circ h$. So $x\in\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}(T)$ iff
$h(T)\subseteq U_d$ iff $h$ factors (uniquely) through the open
subscheme $U_d$; that is, $U_d$ represents the subfunctor
$\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}$ (a subfunctor by
[lem-pd-degree-locally-constant](3)).

*(3) Subgroup scheme.* The unit $e:\operatorname{Spec}k\to\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}_{C/k}$ is the
class of $\mathcal{O}_C$, of degree $0$, so it factors through $U_0$. The
restriction of the multiplication $m$ to the open subscheme
$U_0\times_kU_0$ is the $U_0\times_kU_0$-point
$\operatorname{pr}_1^*\xi\cdot\operatorname{pr}_2^*\xi$ whose degree is $0+0=0$ by (1), so by
(2) it factors through $U_0$; likewise the inverse maps $U_0$ into $U_0$
since $\deg(x^{-1})=-\deg(x)$. Thus $U_0$ is an open and closed
subgroup scheme.

*(4) Translation.* Let $a_d\in\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}_{C/k}(k)$ be the class of
$\mathcal{O}_C(dP)$ and let
$\tau_d=m\circ(\mathrm{id},a_d\circ\pi):\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}_{C/k}\to\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}_{C/k}$,
$\pi$ the structure morphism; on $T$-points $\tau_d(x)=x\cdot(a_d)_T$, which
on a representing module is tensoring with $\operatorname{pr}_C^*\mathcal{O}_C(dP)$. Since
$a_{-d}a_d=[\mathcal{O}_C]=e$, $\tau_{-d}\circ\tau_d=\tau_d\circ\tau_{-d}=\mathrm{id}$,
so $\tau_d$ is an automorphism of the scheme $\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}_{C/k}$. The
fibre of $\operatorname{pr}_C^*\mathcal{O}_C(dP)$ at $t\in T$ is
$\mathcal{O}_C(dP)\otimes_k\kappa(t)$, of degree $d$ by
[lem-pc-degree-base-change](1) and Step 0; so $\deg((a_d)_T)\equiv d$ and,
by (1), $\deg(\tau_d(x))=\deg(x)+d$. Hence $\tau_d$ maps the subfunctor
$\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$ into $\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}$ and $\tau_{-d}$ maps
$\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}$ into $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$; by (2) they restrict to
mutually inverse morphisms $U_0\rightleftarrows U_d$, and
$\tau_d|_{U_0}:\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}^0_{C/k}\to\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}^d_{C/k}$ is an
isomorphism of schemes.

attrs.title: Degree decomposition of the Picard scheme

objects.body:
In the Poincare duality conventions of this chapter (the fixed setting),
let $C$ be a perfect point complex. The
evaluation and coevaluation give a canonical isomorphism

$$
C\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }C^{\vee\vee},
$$

and for every object $D$ of the category at the point, the canonical
tensor–internal-Hom comparison

$$
C^\vee\otimes_A^LD\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,D)
$$

is an isomorphism.

## Proof

An object of the category at the point of
[def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] is a complex of $A$-modules.
Step 1: for $P$ a single finite projective
$A$-module concentrated in degree zero, the canonical map
$P^\vee\otimes_A^LD\to\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,D)$ is an isomorphism
because $\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,-)$ is exact, so
$R\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,D)$ is represented by the termwise Hom
complex, and the map is the one of
[lem-pod-finite-projective-tensor-hom] at the base $s$, an
isomorphism since $P$ is dualizable; and $P\to P^{\vee\vee}$ is the
iso of a finite projective module with its double dual. Step 2: for a
bounded complex $P^\bullet$ of finite projective modules in a finite
range $[a,b]$, the two statements are proved by descending induction
on the number of nonzero terms: for the cone
$\operatorname{cone}(P^{b-1}\to P^b)$-decomposition, or, directly, by
writing $P^\bullet$ as the finite iterated cone of the truncation
triangles $\tau^{\leq i-1}P^\bullet\to\tau^{\leq i}P^\bullet\to P^i[-i]\xrightarrow{+1}$, and using that
$C\mapsto R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,D)$ and $C\mapsto C^\vee\otimes_A^LD$
convert distinguished triangles to distinguished triangles (in the
argument, together with the naturality of the canonical map) and the
five lemma. Step 3: the general $C$ is quasi-isomorphic to such a
$P^\bullet$ by [def-pod-perfect-point-complex]; replacing $C$
by $P^\bullet$ is legitimate because both sides are quasi-isomorphism
invariants: the derived functors of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] are independent of the
selected resolutions. The canonicality of both isomorphisms is the
naturality of the adjunction in $C$ and $D$.

In the Poincare duality conventions of this chapter (the fixed setting), mixed-support cup product is natural in $K$ and $L$, and satisfies the associativity identity on $R\Gamma _c(X,K)\otimes R\Gamma (X,L)\otimes R\Gamma (X,M)$; the unit element $1\in H^0(X,A)$ acts as the identity after the canonical identifications; and the compatibility with the iterate of the cup product and with the identification $R\Gamma _c(X,-)\cong R\Gamma (X,-)$ for a proper $X$ holds.

## Proof

The cup product is the composite of the projection transformation of
[def-exchange-projection] and the direct-image counit of
[def-weil-derived-direct-image]; both are natural.
The tensor associator and unit in [def-weil-derived-tensor],
the composite-counit identity of [fix-prop-adjunctions], and
the projection coherence of [fix-prop-projection-formula]
identify the two parenthesizations of the triple product.
The same identities with a unit factor prove the unit assertion.
If $a_X$ is proper, [cor-cbc-proper-coincidence] identifies
$Ra_{X!}$ with $Ra_{X*}$, using the identity compactification.
Under this comparison the projection map and counit are the same
maps, so the supported and ordinary cup products agree.

attrs.title: Coherence of the mixed-support cup product

objects.body:
In the Poincare duality conventions of this chapter (the fixed setting), let $\Lambda\in\{A,\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell}\}$ and let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ be perfect over $\Lambda_X$. The shift convention $H^r(C[m])=H^{r+m}(C)$ identifies the degree-zero part of the derived pairing $\beta _K$ of Definition 9.17 with the pairings

$$
\langle -,-\rangle _i:\   H_c^i(X,K)\times H^{2d-i}\bigl(X,K^\vee (d)\bigr) \longrightarrow \Lambda \qquad (i\in \mathbf Z).
$$

Before inserting the Tate twist, the same morphism is the line-valued pairing

$$
H_c^i(X,K)\times H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee ) \longrightarrow \Lambda(-d),
$$

obtained by eliminating the invertible twist $\Lambda _X(d)$ of the second factor through the canonical isomorphism $H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee (d))\cong H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee )\otimes _\Lambda \Lambda (d)$ and using the twist inverse.

## Proof

The degree of $\beta _K$ is zero: both the mixed-support cup product and the evaluation are degree-preserving, and the trace $\operatorname {Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{a_X,\Lambda }$ has degree zero on the shifted complex $R\Gamma _c(X,\Lambda _X(d))[2d]$, whose top cohomology sits in degree $2d-2d=0$. Unpacking $H^r(C[m])=H^{r+m}(C)$ in the second variable gives $H^0\bigl(R\Gamma (X,K^\vee (d))[2d]\bigr)=H^{2d}(X,K^\vee (d))$ and, more generally, decomposing into cohomological degrees, the degree-zero part of the pairing pairs $H_c^i(X,K)$ against $H^{-i}\bigl(R\Gamma (X,K^\vee (d))[2d]\bigr)=H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee (d))$. For the line-valued form, the twist $\Lambda _X(d)=\Lambda _X\otimes _\Lambda \Lambda (d)$ with $\Lambda (d)$ the invertible locally constant rank-one twist sheaf of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] is eliminated by tensoring the pairing with its twist inverse $\Lambda(-d)$ and using the canonical isomorphisms $\Lambda (d)\otimes _\Lambda \Lambda (-d)\cong \Lambda$: this is the identification of $H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee (d))$ with $H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee )\otimes _\Lambda \Lambda (d)$ (by [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], the twist of a complex commutes with the global sections), so the pairing becomes $H_c^i(X,K)\times H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee )\to \Lambda(-d)$.

In the Poincare duality conventions of this chapter (the fixed setting), strict Weil complex with $K$ perfect. The datum $\varphi _{K^\vee }$ of Definition 9.28 defines a strict Weil complex $(K^\vee ,\varphi _{K^\vee })$, the coefficient evaluation

$$
K\otimes ^L_{A_X}K^\vee \xrightarrow {\  \operatorname {ev}_K\  }A_X
$$

is a morphism of Weil objects, the twisted object $(K^\vee (r),\varphi _{K^\vee (r)})$ is a strict Weil complex, and the canonical identification $\mathbb D_XK\cong K^\vee (d)[2d]$ of Proposition 9.16 is an isomorphism of Weil objects (the compatibility of the purity isomorphism with the geometric-Frobenius data is the Weil equivariance of purity and trace, [thm-pur-weil-equivariance-of-purity-and-trace], and the duality isomorphisms are morphisms of Weil complexes by Proposition 1.48). All these objects and morphisms commute with finite reduction, adic normalization, rationalization, finite coefficient-field extension, and idempotent splitting (which exists for Weil complexes by [lem-weil-weil-complex-qbar-idempotent-complete]).

## Proof

Step 1: $\varphi _{K^\vee }$ is a genuine Weil datum, i.e. a typed isomorphism of the displayed source and target. The first arrow of the composite in [def-pod-dual-tate-datum] is the canonical isomorphism

$$
Lg_\gamma ^*R\mathcal Hom_X(K,A_X) \xrightarrow {\  \sim \  } R\mathcal Hom_X\bigl(Lg_\gamma ^*K,Lg_\gamma ^*A_X\bigr),
$$

the derived internal Hom under the pullback along the geometric-Frobenius automorphism of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius], which is an isomorphism by the exactness of the pullback along an automorphism and the functoriality of the internal Hom, recorded in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]; the second arrow is induced by the canonical datum $\varphi _A$ on the constant object, the canonical structure of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]; and the third by $\varphi _K^{-1}$. Each is an isomorphism, hence so is the composite, and it is a structure map of one object $K^\vee$, so $(K^\vee ,\varphi _{K^\vee })\in D^b_{ctf,\mathrm W}(X,A)$ by the definition of the strict Weil complex of [def-trf-strict-weil-complex], the underlying object $K^\vee$ lying in $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ by [lem-pod-coefficient-dual-perfect]. Step 2: the evaluation is equivariant. The evaluation is the counit of the tensor–internal-Hom adjunction of [def-weil-derived-tensor], whose unit–counit identity is natural; the definition of $\varphi _{K^\vee }$ is precisely the typed iso making the square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc} Lg_\gamma ^*\bigl(K\otimes ^L_{A_X}K^\vee \bigr) &  \xrightarrow {\  \sim \  } &  Lg_\gamma ^*K\otimes ^L_{A_X}Lg_\gamma ^*K^\vee \\ \big\downarrow \varphi _K\otimes \varphi _{K^\vee } &  \sim &  \quad \  \sim \quad \big\downarrow \operatorname {ev}_K\\ K\otimes ^L_{A_X}K^\vee &  \xrightarrow {\  \operatorname {ev}_K\  } &  A_X \end{array}
$$

commute, by the naturality of the tensor–internal-Hom adjunction [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] (the composite being the image of the identity under the unit–counit of the adjunction carried through the three isomorphisms), so the evaluation is a morphism of Weil objects by [lem-fix-weil-operations]. Step 3: the twisted object: $\varphi _{K^\vee (r)}=\varphi _{K^\vee }\otimes \tau _r$, the tensor of two Weil data, is a Weil datum by the compatibility of the derived tensor product with the pullback along $g_\gamma$, of [def-weil-derived-tensor] and [lem-fix-weil-operations], and $\tau _r$ is the equivariant structure of the Tate line of [def-pur-tate-datum] with normalization $q^{-r}$. Step 4: the purity identification: $\mathbb D_XK\cong K^\vee (d)[2d]$, of [thm-sf-dual-perfect], is an isomorphism of Weil objects by the Weil equivariance, [thm-pur-weil-equivariance-of-purity-and-trace], of the purity map and of the trace, together with the naturality of internal-Hom evaluation under the automorphism pullback in [lem-fix-weil-operations]. Step 5: the transport statements: all the constructions are those of the operations of the six-operations package, whose coefficient comparisons are built from the same evaluation and tensor maps and are preserved by the automorphism transport of [lem-fix-weil-operations]; and the data are built from the same operations, so they commute with these transports.

attrs.title: Compatibility of the dual and Tate data

objects.body:
In the Poincare duality conventions of this chapter (the fixed setting), $K_n=K\otimes ^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$. Derived perfectness at the $\mathcal O_E$-stage yields the universal-coefficient exact sequences for the cohomology modules

$$
0\longrightarrow H^i_c(X,K)\otimes _{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n} \longrightarrow H^i_c(X,K_n) \longrightarrow \operatorname {Tor}_1^{\mathcal O_E}\bigl(H^{i+1}_c(X,K),A_{E,n}\bigr) \longrightarrow 0,
$$

and the corresponding sequences for the second variable of the pairing and for the adjoint maps. If the relevant cohomology modules are finite projective over $\mathcal O_E$, the Tor terms vanish and the degreewise maps are perfect $\mathcal O_E$-module pairings. (Source: the universal-coefficient formalism of derived complete torsion coefficients, Milne, Lectures on Etale Cohomology, Section 19; recorded here as the coefficient-layer bookkeeping input.)

## Proof

By [thm-pod-derived-poincare-duality] at the $\mathcal O_E$-stage, the inverse adjoint $R\Gamma _c(X,K)^\vee \to R\Gamma (X,K^\vee (d))[2d]$ is an isomorphism of derived-complete perfect $\mathcal O_E$-complexes; finite reduction is the derived tensor product $-\otimes ^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$, which is computed levelwise by [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], so the derived-complete perfectness of the two complexes (the definition of the category at the point of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] at the $\mathcal O_E$-stage) gives the levelwise Tor-exact sequences of the statement: for a derived-complete complex $C$ of $\mathcal O_E$-modules of finite Tor-amplitude, the triangle

$$
C\otimes ^L_{\mathcal O_E}K_1 \longrightarrow C\otimes ^L_{\mathcal O_E}K_{n+1} \longrightarrow C\otimes ^L_{\mathcal O_E}K_n \xrightarrow {+1}
$$

of the exact coefficient sequence $0\to A_{E,1}\to A_{E,n+1}\to A_{E,n}\to 0$ yields the Tor-sequence, with the Tor term the $\varpi$-torsion of the $\mathcal O_E$-module and the reduction term the tensor product; the identification of the two terms with $H^i_c(X,K)\otimes _{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$ and $\operatorname {Tor}_1^{\mathcal O_E}(H^{i+1}_c(X,K),A_{E,n})$ is the derived-tensor computation over a principal ideal ring, in which a bounded complex of finite projective $\mathcal O_E$-modules, the perfect representative of the input (the finite-Tor condition of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] and the derived completion of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]), replaces the coefficients levelwise. The same argument applied to the second variable $K^\vee (d)$ and to the adjoint map gives the other two sequences. When the cohomology modules are finite projective over $\mathcal O_E$, the Tor terms vanish, so the sequences show that the cohomology of $K_n$ is the reduction of the cohomology of $K$; transporting the perfect derived pairing along these identifications gives $\mathcal O_E$-module perfect pairings levelwise, defining the degreewise maps of the statement.

In the Poincare duality conventions of
this chapter, let $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ be a finite ring and let $P$ be a
finite projective $\Lambda_X$-module on the
small pro-etale site of $X$.
Then $P$ is flat, so that $P$, regarded as a complex concentrated in
degree $0$, has finite $\operatorname{Tor}$-amplitude concentrated in
degree $0$ in the sense of
[def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]; and $P$ is constructible with
finite stalks in the sense of
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. Consequently a complex
that is quasi-isomorphic, locally on the small pro-etale site of $X$,
to a bounded complex of finite projective $\Lambda_X$-modules has
bounded constructible cohomology sheaves.

## Proof

A finite projective $\Lambda_X$-module $P$ is a direct summand of a
finite free module $\Lambda_X^r$, say $P=\ker(e)$ for an idempotent
endomorphism $e$ of $\Lambda_X^r$; in particular $P$ is flat, hence
$\operatorname{Tor}_i^{\Lambda_X}(P,-)=0$ for $i>0$, which is the
stated Tor-amplitude in the sense of
[def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. The constant sheaf
$\Lambda_X^r$ is a finite direct sum of copies of $\Lambda_X$, and
$\Lambda=\Lambda_{E,n}$ is a finite ring, so $\Lambda_X^r$ is locally
constant with finite stalks and therefore constructible in the sense of
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. The constructible
$\Lambda$-sheaves form a weak Serre subcategory
([thm-constructible-serre]), so the kernel of the
idempotent $e$ is constructible as well, and its stalks, being
subgroups of the finite stalks of $\Lambda_X^r$, are finite; this
proves the first two assertions. For the last one, a bounded complex of
constructible sheaves has bounded cohomology, and each cohomology sheaf
is the kernel of a morphism of constructible sheaves modulo the image of
one, hence constructible by the same weak-Serre property.

Let $p$ be prime, let $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, put $q=p^a$, and set
$k_0=\Fq$, and let $k=\Fbar$ be the
fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$.
Fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, and write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$.
Let
$X_0/k_0$ be smooth,
proper, and geometrically connected of pure dimension
$d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$; set $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. Let $F$ be the
geometric Frobenius acting on the
ordinary cohomology group
$H^i(X,\Ql)$, and let $\langle-,-\rangle_i$ be the
trace–cup-product pairing with values
in the Tate twist $\Ql(-d)$.
The trace map
$\operatorname{tr}^{(-d)}_X:H^{2d}(X,\Ql)\to\Ql(-d)$ is an isomorphism, and for every integer $i$ with
$0\leq i\leq2d$, the pairing
$\langle-,-\rangle_i$ is perfect. Equivalently, it induces a
Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism

$$
H^{2d-i}(X,\Ql)
\xrightarrow{\sim}H^i(X,\Ql)^\vee(-d).
$$

For every integer $i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$, every
$x\in H^i(X,\Ql)$, and every $y\in H^{2d-i}(X,\Ql)$, geometric
Frobenius acts on $\Ql(-d)$ by $q^d$, and

$$
\langle Fx,Fy\rangle_i=q^d\langle x,y\rangle_i.
$$

For every integer $i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$, every
$x\in H^i(X,\Ql)$, and every $y\in H^{2d-i}(X,\Ql)$, graded
commutativity gives

$$
\langle y,x\rangle_{2d-i}=(-1)^i\langle x,y\rangle_i;
$$

in middle degree the pairing is $(-1)^d$-symmetric.

## Proof

1. **1.** The orientation and coefficient multiplication in
[def-weil-poincare-trace-cup] identify the trace and pairing used here:
$$
\langle x,y\rangle_i=\operatorname{tr}^{(-d)}_X(x\smile y)
\quad\text{in }\Ql(-d),
\qquad
x\in H^i(X,\Ql),\ y\in H^{2d-i}(X,\Ql).
$$
Thus the pairing in the proposition is the one to which the duality
interface applies, rather than an auxiliary bilinear form.
1. **2.** The trace isomorphism and perfectness are supplied by
[thm-weil-poincare-duality]. For each $0\leq i\leq2d$, perfectness
means that the map
$$
\Phi_i:H^{2d-i}(X,\Ql)\longrightarrow
H^i(X,\Ql)^\vee(-d),\qquad
y\longmapsto\bigl(x\longmapsto\langle x,y\rangle_i\bigr)
$$
is an isomorphism, and the same interface gives
$\operatorname{tr}^{(-d)}_X:H^{2d}(X,\Ql)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Ql(-d)$.
This proves both the asserted perfect pairings and the displayed duality
isomorphism.
1. **3.** The Frobenius clause of
[thm-weil-poincare-duality] says that the trace target has scalar
action $q^d$ and that
$$
\langle Fx,Fy\rangle_i=q^d\langle x,y\rangle_i.
$$
Equivalently, under $\Phi_i$, the operator on the second factor is
$q^d(F^{-1})^\vee$. This is precisely the Frobenius similitude asserted
in the proposition.
1. **4.** The cup product in
[def-weil-poincare-trace-cup] is graded-commutative. Taking degrees
$i$ and $2d-i$ gives
$$
y\smile x=(-1)^{i(2d-i)}x\smile y=(-1)^i x\smile y,
$$
because $2d$ is even. Applying the trace therefore yields
$$
\langle y,x\rangle_{2d-i}=(-1)^i\langle x,y\rangle_i.
$$
For $i=d$ this is $(-1)^d$-symmetry, completing all the claims.

In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, let
$a:\mathbf A^1_Y\to Y$ be the projection, and let
$i_0,i_1:Y\to\mathbf A^1_Y$ be the sections $t=0$ and $t=1$, so that
$a\circ i_0=a\circ i_1=\operatorname{id}_Y$ and hence
$i_0^*a^*\cong\operatorname{id}\cong i_1^*a^*$. Let
$F\in D^b_{ctf}(\mathbf A^1_Y,\Lambda)$ and
$C\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$, and let
$\theta:i_1^*F\xrightarrow{\sim}C$ be an isomorphism. Suppose given an
etale covering family $\{u_\alpha:Y_\alpha\to Y\}$ by separated
finite-type schemes such that:

- *local shape.* for every $\alpha$ the restriction
$F|_{\mathbf A^1_{Y_\alpha}}$ is a shift and twist
$\mathcal L_\alpha(m_\alpha)[n_\alpha]$ of a finite locally
constant $\Lambda$-sheaf $\mathcal L_\alpha$ of rank one on
$\mathbf A^1_{Y_\alpha}$;
- *normalized local comparisons.* for every $\alpha$ there is an
isomorphism
$\kappa_\alpha:F|_{\mathbf A^1_{Y_\alpha}}\xrightarrow{\sim}
a^*C|_{\mathbf A^1_{Y_\alpha}}$ whose restriction along the section
$t=1$ is $\theta|_{Y_\alpha}$, i.e.
$i_1^*\kappa_\alpha=\theta|_{Y_\alpha}$ under
$i_1^*a^*C\cong C$.

Then:

1. *gluing.* There is a unique isomorphism
$\kappa:F\xrightarrow{\sim}a^*C$ with
$\kappa|_{\mathbf A^1_{Y_\alpha}}=\kappa_\alpha$ for every
$\alpha$.
1. *uniqueness.* $\kappa$ is the unique isomorphism
$F\xrightarrow{\sim}a^*C$ with $i_1^*\kappa=\theta$; in
particular it does not depend on the cover or on the local
comparisons $\kappa_\alpha$.
1. *constancy.* Restriction along $i_0$ and $i_1$ gives a
canonical identification
$$
i_0^*F\xrightarrow{\ i_0^*\kappa\ }i_0^*a^*C\cong C
\cong i_1^*a^*C\xleftarrow{\ i_1^*\kappa\ }i_1^*F,
$$
the right-hand map being $\theta$: the object $F$ is constant
along the $\mathbf A^1$-direction, its values at $t=0$ and
$t=1$ agreeing.

## Proof

Throughout, pullback along an etale morphism, restriction to an
open subscheme, and the pullbacks $i_0^*,i_1^*,a^*$ are the exact
derived pullbacks of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]; they
commute with the cohomology sheaves of
[def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] and with one another up to the
canonical isomorphisms, which are used without comment. The base
changes $\{\mathbf A^1_{Y_\alpha}\to\mathbf A^1_Y\}$ of the given
cover form again an etale covering family, hence a covering family
of the site of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], etale morphisms being
weakly etale ([def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]).

Step 1: reduction to one shift. For a point $y\in Y$ and an index
$\alpha$ with $y$ in the image of $u_\alpha$, the object $F$ has, at
every geometric point of $\mathbf A^1_Y$ over $y$, nonzero
cohomology in exactly the degree $-n_\alpha$, because
$\mathcal L_\alpha(m_\alpha)$ is a sheaf with nonzero stalks
(rank one, and a twist of a finite locally constant rank-one sheaf
is again one, as $\Lambda(m)$ is invertible in the conventions of
[def-pur-conventions]). Hence $n(y):=n_\alpha$ is independent of
$\alpha$, and it is constant on the image of each connected component
of $Y_\alpha$, an open subset of $Y$ since etale morphisms are open.
So $n:Y\to\mathbf Z$ is locally constant. The scheme $Y$ is Noetherian,
so it is the finite disjoint union of its connected components $Y_c$,
which are open and closed, and $n$ is constant on each of them; by
[lem-pur-a1-components](1) the connected components of
$\mathbf A^1_Y$ are the $\mathbf A^1_{Y_c}$. All data in the statement
restrict to each $Y_c$, and a morphism over $\mathbf A^1_Y$ (resp.
$Y$) is the same as a family of morphisms over the open and closed
pieces $\mathbf A^1_{Y_c}$ (resp. $Y_c$). We may therefore assume
that $n_\alpha=n$ for all $\alpha$ and a fixed integer $n$.

Step 2: reduction to sheaves. With $n$ fixed, the cohomology sheaves
$\mathcal H^q(F)$ vanish for $q\neq-n$ after restriction to every
member of a covering family, hence vanish, a sheaf which vanishes
locally being zero; and
$\mathcal L:=\mathcal H^{-n}(F)$ restricts on
$\mathbf A^1_{Y_\alpha}$ to $\mathcal L_\alpha(m_\alpha)$, so it is a
finite locally constant sheaf of rank one. The truncations of
the standard t-structure of [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]
then identify $F$ with $\mathcal L[n]$, a complex with a single
nonzero cohomology sheaf being isomorphic to that sheaf placed in its
degree. Likewise $C|_{Y_\alpha}\cong i_1^*a^*C|_{Y_\alpha}
\cong i_1^*F|_{Y_\alpha}$ via $\kappa_\alpha$ and $\theta$, so $C$
has the single nonzero cohomology sheaf
$\mathcal M:=\mathcal H^{-n}(C)$, again finite locally constant of
rank one, and $C\cong\mathcal M[n]$,
$a^*C\cong(a^*\mathcal M)[n]$. Morphisms in the derived category
between two objects concentrated in the single degree $-n$ are the
morphisms of the corresponding sheaves, the heart of the standard
t-structure being the abelian category of sheaves. Thus
$\kappa_\alpha$ and $\theta$ are, after the shift $[n]$ is removed,
isomorphisms of finite locally constant sheaves
$$
\kappa_\alpha:\mathcal L|_{\mathbf A^1_{Y_\alpha}}\xrightarrow{\sim}
a^*\mathcal M|_{\mathbf A^1_{Y_\alpha}},
\qquad
\theta:i_1^*\mathcal L\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal M,
$$
and everything to be proved is a statement about morphisms of
sheaves; no descent of objects or morphisms of a derived category
is used.

Step 3: agreement on the overlaps. Put
$Y_{\alpha\beta}=Y_\alpha\times_YY_\beta$, a separated finite-type
$k$-scheme, and restrict $\kappa_\alpha$ and $\kappa_\beta$ to
$\mathbf A^1_{Y_{\alpha\beta}}$. Their restrictions along the unit
section both equal $\theta|_{Y_{\alpha\beta}}$. By the second
assertion of [lem-pur-lisse-uniqueness], applied over the base
$Y_{\alpha\beta}$ to the restrictions of the two sheaf morphisms to
$\mathbf G_{m,Y_{\alpha\beta}}$, through which the unit section
factors, they agree on $\mathbf G_{m,Y_{\alpha\beta}}$; by the first
assertion of the same lemma they then agree on all of
$\mathbf A^1_{Y_{\alpha\beta}}$.

Step 4: gluing, and (1). Morphisms of sheaves form a sheaf
$\mathcal Hom(\mathcal L,a^*\mathcal M)$ on the site, so by Step 3
the $\kappa_\alpha$ glue to a unique morphism
$\kappa:\mathcal L\to a^*\mathcal M$ restricting to each
$\kappa_\alpha$. The inverses $\kappa_\alpha^{-1}$ agree on overlaps
as well, and glue to a two-sided inverse of $\kappa$, since the
composites restrict to identities on every member of the cover. Hence
$\kappa$ is an isomorphism; shifting back by $[n]$ gives (1).

Step 5: (2) and (3). The restriction $i_1^*\kappa$ and $\theta$ are
two morphisms $i_1^*\mathcal L\to\mathcal M$ of sheaves on $Y$ which
agree after restriction to every $Y_\alpha$, by the normalization of
$\kappa_\alpha$; hence they are equal. If
$\kappa':F\xrightarrow{\sim}a^*C$ is another isomorphism with
$i_1^*\kappa'=\theta$, then, by Step 2 applied to $\kappa'$, both are
sheaf morphisms $\mathcal L\to a^*\mathcal M$ after the shift is
removed; their restrictions to $\mathbf G_{m,Y}$ agree along the unit
section, hence agree by the second assertion of
[lem-pur-lisse-uniqueness], and then $\kappa'=\kappa$ by its first
assertion. This proves (2); in particular two covers with normalized
local comparisons produce the same $\kappa$, both having restriction
$\theta$ at $t=1$. For (3), apply $i_0^*$ and $i_1^*$ to $\kappa$
and use $a\circ i_0=a\circ i_1=\operatorname{id}_Y$; the resulting
identification $i_0^*F\cong C\cong i_1^*F$ is canonical because
$\kappa$ is, by (2).

In the situation of [thm-pur-adic-reconstruction], the same
transport statement holds for the smooth trace of
[def-pur-smooth-trace] and for the coherence statements of
[thm-pur-composition-coherence] and
[thm-pur-smooth-base-change-coherence].

## Proof

The trace of [def-pur-smooth-trace] is the counit of the realized
adjunction and its transport is
included in the same reconstruction
([lem-weil-pbc-reconstruction-uniform-tower]), as in the trace-formula
blueprint; the coherence statements are the compatible systems of the
finite-level coherence statements of
[thm-pur-composition-coherence] and
[thm-pur-smooth-base-change-coherence].

In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
$\Lambda=A$. For every morphism $v:Y'\to Y$, with $s'$ the zero
section of $\mathbf A^1_{Y'}$, the
exceptional
base-change comparison identifies $Lv^*\operatorname{pur}_s$ with the
orientation $\operatorname{pur}_{s'}$ for $\mathbf A^1_{Y'}$ of
[thm-pur-affine-line-orientation].

## Proof

Both $Lv^*\operatorname{pur}_s$ and $\operatorname{pur}_{s'}$ are morphisms
$\Lambda_{Y'}\to Rs'^!\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_{Y'}}(1)[2]$: the source and
target of the first are transported by the exceptional base-change
comparison of [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility] (the
base change of a closed immersion is a closed immersion and the
affine-line datum base-changes, by [lem-pur-gysin-structure] and
[def-pur-affine-line-datum]). Its pullback to a geometric point
$\bar y'$ of $Y'$ is the pullback of the normalization class
$1$: the Kummer class is compatible with the pullback
([lem-pur-kummer-coefficient-base-change]) and the rank-one
calculation is the one of [thm-pur-rank-one-local-calculation]
transported along $Y'\to Y$, using $s'(\bar y')=s(\bar y)$ with
$\bar y=v(\bar y')$. Hence, by the normalization of
[thm-pur-affine-line-orientation] and the uniqueness of
[prop-pur-affine-line-orientation-uniqueness], the two morphisms
coincide.

attrs.title: Base change of the global orientation

objects.body:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting), let $Y$ and $\kappa(t)$ be as in
[thm-pur-affine-line-orientation]. The restriction of the
homomorphism group to
geometric points is an
injective map

$$
\operatorname{Hom}_{D(Y,\Lambda)}
\bigl(\Lambda_Y,Rs^!\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_Y}(1)[2]\bigr)
\longrightarrow
\prod_{\bar y\to Y}H^2_{s(\bar y)}(\mathbf A^1_{\bar y},\Lambda(1)),
$$

whose image contains the family with every component $1\in\Lambda$ (by
[thm-pur-rank-one-local-calculation] and the normalization of
[thm-pur-affine-line-orientation]). Consequently
$\operatorname{pur}_s$ is the unique global morphism whose pullback to
every geometric point is the normalized class $1$.

## Proof

Step 1: reduction to sections of a sheaf. By
[lem-pur-gysin-structure], $F:=Rs^!\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_Y}(1)[2]$ is
concentrated in degree zero with

$$
\Hom_{D(Y,\Lambda)}(\Lambda_Y,F)=H^0(Y,F)=\Gamma\bigl(Y,\mathcal H^0(F)\bigr),
$$

the first equality being the definition of the global sections as
$\operatorname{Hom}$ with the unit object (the tensor–internal-Hom
adjunction of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]) and the
second the degree-zero cohomology of a complex concentrated in one
degree. Step 2: the injectivity. A section $s\in\Gamma(Y,\mathcal H^0(F))$ is determined by its stalks: if all stalks $s_{\bar y}=0$,
then $s=0$, by the stalk criterion for the equality of sheaf
sections on the (small pro-)etale site
([def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]). The map of the statement
is exactly the stalkwise evaluation of the section, hence injective.
Step 3: the image contains $(1)_{\bar y}$. By the normalization in
[thm-pur-affine-line-orientation], the pullback of
$\operatorname{pur}_s$ to $\bar y$ is the class $1$ of
[thm-pur-rank-one-local-calculation] under the canonical
identification of $(Rs^!\Lambda(1)[2])_{\bar y}$ with the support
object at the point (the exactness of the pullback along a geometric
point and [lem-pur-gysin-structure]). Step 4: the uniqueness.
If $\varphi:\Lambda_Y\to F$ is any morphism whose pullbacks are all
$1$, then its section equals the section of $\operatorname{pur}_s$
by Step 2, so $\varphi=\operatorname{pur}_s$.

In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
$A=A_{E,n}$, and let $d,e\geq1$. Under the canonical identification
$\mathbf A^{d+e}_Y\cong\mathbf A^d_{\mathbf A^e_Y}$, the equality

$$
\gamma_{p_{d+e},K}
=
c_{p_e,p_d}^{-1}\circ
\gamma_{p_d,Rp_e^!K}\circ
Lp_d^*(\gamma_{p_e,K})(d)[2d]
$$

holds after the canonical reassociation of twists and shifts, where
$c_{g,f}:R(gf)^!\cong Rf^!Rg^!$ is the composition isomorphism for the
exceptional inverse image. The Koszul sign interchanging the two
$A(1)$-tensor factors in the product of $(d)[2d]$ and $(e)[2e]$ is
$+1$, both factors being of even degree; the two orderings of the affine
coordinates give the same composite comparison.

## Proof

Step 1: unpack the definition. By [def-pur-affine-space-comparison],
$\gamma_{p_{d+e},K}$ is defined as the ordered composite of the
$d+e$ affine-line comparisons
$\gamma_{p_1,-}$ applied to the tower

$$
\mathbf A^{d+e}_Y\to\mathbf A^{d+e-1}_Y\to\cdots\to Y,
$$

with the composition isomorphisms for the exceptional inverse image of a
composite morphism and the additivity isomorphisms for the twists, and
the natural identification $Lp_{d+e}^*K\cong Lp_d^*Lp_e^*K$ of the
pullback-composition. Step 2: the reassociation. The right-hand side
of the displayed equality is the same ordered composite
$(\gamma_{p_e,K},\ \gamma_{p_d,Rp_e^!K})$ except that the regroupation
of the $d+e$ factors into the last $e$ coordinates and the first
$d$ coordinates is made explicit: both sides are the composite of
the $d+e$ affine-line comparisons ordered by the coordinate
$(x_1,\ldots,x_{d+e})$, and the two regroupings differ only by the
associativity of the composition isomorphism $c_{g,f}$ of
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] – the reassociation
pentagon for the triple $(R^!$-isomorphisms of the three stages of
the tower), the unit laws, and the compatibility of the
twist-additivity isomorphisms. Step 3: the signs. The shift of
$K(d)[2d]$ produced by $d$ factors is $2d$, and the symmetry of
the tensor product interchanging the two blocks of "degrees" $2a$ and
$2b$ (the total shifts of the two blocks, $a$ and $b$ factors
each) carries the Koszul sign $(-1)^{(2a)(2b)}=+1$; the
twist-additivity isomorphisms similarly involve only even-degree
factors, so the reorderings of the coordinates produce no sign at all.
Step 4: the conclusion. By Steps 2 and 3 the composite comparison is
invariant under the permutation $(1,\ldots,d+d')\to(d+1,\ldots,d+e,1,\ldots,d)$ of the block order, which is exactly the displayed
equality, both orderings giving the same global morphism.

In the situation of [cor-pur-affine-space-purity], the comparison
$\gamma_{p_d,K}$ is symmetric under permutation of the affine
coordinates (the Koszul sign being $+1$ by
[prop-pur-affine-space-composition-law]), compatible with the base
change of $Y$, and compatible with the products of affine-space
projections and with the composition law of
[prop-pur-affine-space-composition-law].

## Proof

The symmetry is recorded in
[prop-pur-affine-space-composition-law]; the base-change
compatibility is the base-change compatibility of the affine-line
purity [thm-pur-affine-line-purity] transported along the tower of
affine-space projections, the composition law of
[prop-pur-affine-space-composition-law] being functorial.

attrs.title: Symmetry and compatibilities of affine-space purity

objects.body:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting), in the situation of
[def-pur-dnc-section-family] with family object $F$, let
$a:\mathbf A^1_B\to B$ be the projection and let
$i_1:B\to\mathbf A^1_B$ be the section $t=1$.

1. *the family is a shift of a lisse line.* The family object
is a shift of a finite locally constant rank-one sheaf,
$$
F\simeq\mathcal L_F(d)[2d],
$$
and likewise $C(g,s)\simeq\mathcal L_1(d)[2d]$ on $B$; in
particular no descent of an object or of a morphism of a derived
category is needed below.
1. *constancy along the affine line.* There is a canonical
isomorphism
$$
\kappa:\;F\;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;a^*C(g,s).
$$
Since $i_1^*a^*C(g,s)=C(g,s)=i_1^*F$ by
[lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry](1), the family object is the
pullback of its own fibre at $t=1$: the deformation family is
constant along $\mathbf A^1_B$ over $B$.
1. *normalization and uniqueness.* $\kappa$ is the unique
isomorphism $F\to a^*C(g,s)$ which at the section $t=1$
restricts to the identity of $C(g,s)$ under the identification
$i_1^*F\simeq C(g,s)$ of
[lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry](1).
1. *locality and base change.* $\kappa$ is compatible with
etale localization on $B$ and with arbitrary base change
$B'\to B$.

## Proof

The family object is the one of [def-pur-dnc-section-family]; tensor inverses and shifts are understood as in [def-weil-derived-tensor].
Write $a:\mathbf A^1_B\to B$ and let $i_1:B\to\mathbf A^1_B$ be the
unit section.

Step 1: the family object is a shift of a lisse rank-one line. By
[lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry](2),
$\widetilde g$ is smooth, so $\omega_{\widetilde g}$ is invertible
by [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness]; by (2) and (4) it is etale-locally
$\Lambda(d)[2d]$, hence so is $F$. An etale cover of $B$ on
which the pair $(V,s)$ has standard coordinates also carries the
family to the standard model, so
[lem-pur-concentrated-complex-shift] applied to that cover gives

$$
F\;\simeq\;\mathcal L_F(d)[2d],
$$

with $\mathcal L_F$ a finite locally constant rank-one sheaf on
$\mathbf A^1_B$; the same argument gives
$C(g,s)\simeq\mathcal L_1(d)[2d]$ on $B$. This is (1), and this
reduction to actual sheaves is the point which makes the glueing at the
end of the proof the ordinary sheaf axiom.
Step 2: the local models and their normalization. Refine the etale
cover so that in addition $C(g,s)|_{B_i}$ is a shift-twist of the free
rank-one module; such a refinement exists because $C(g,s)$ is finite
locally constant by Step 1. Let $B_i\to B$ be the resulting cover,
on which there are coordinates of pairs
$(V_i,s_i)\to(\mathbf A^d_{B_i},0)$
([lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry](2)); for the standard pair the
deformation space is
$\mathbf A^d_{B_i}\times_{B_i}\mathbf A^1_{B_i}$, $x_k=tu_k$.
Exceptional pullback along the coordinate map is ordinary pullback, and
the vector-bundle Thom calculation
([cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity] as in
[lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry](4)) supplies an isomorphism

$$
\kappa_i:F|_{\mathbf A^1_{B_i}}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
a_i^*C(g,s)|_{B_i},
$$

whose restriction $\kappa_i(1)$ is an automorphism of the free
rank-one sheaf on $B_i$. Multiplying $\kappa_i$ by the pullback
of its inverse $a_i^*(\kappa_i(1)^{-1})$ normalizes it to the
identity at $t=1$, on every connected component of $B_i$.
Step 3: gluing and uniqueness, i.e. (2) and (3). Apply
[prop-pur-a1-invariance] over the base $Y=B$ with $C=C(g,s)$, with
$\theta:i_1^*F\xrightarrow{\sim}C(g,s)$ the identification of
[lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry](1), and with the cover $\{B_i\to B\}$ of
Step 2, whose members may be taken affine, hence separated of finite type
over $k$. Its hypotheses hold: the *local shape* because
$F\simeq\mathcal L_F(d)[2d]$ by Step 1, and the *normalized local
comparisons* are the $\kappa_i$ of Step 2, which restrict at $t=1$ to the
identity of $C(g,s)|_{B_i}$ under $\theta$. Its gluing assertion gives a
unique isomorphism

$$
\kappa:F\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }a^*C(g,s)
$$

restricting to every $\kappa_i$, hence to the identity at $t=1$: this is
(2), and existence in (3). Its uniqueness assertion says that $\kappa$ is
the only isomorphism $F\to a^*C(g,s)$ restricting to $\theta$, i.e. to the
identity of $C(g,s)$, at $t=1$, which is the uniqueness in (3).
Finally, the Rees-algebra description of the DNC
for the closed section, the local standard models, and the localized
Thom classes all commute with base change and etale localization, hence
so does the resulting isomorphism: this is (4).

attrs.title: The deformation family is constant along the affine line

objects.body:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}$, let $Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme,
and use the affine-line datum of [def-pur-affine-line-datum]: the
projection $p:\mathbf A^1_Y\to Y$, the zero section $s$, the open
complement $j:\mathbf G_{m,Y}\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_Y$, the composite
$\pi=pj:\mathbf G_{m,Y}\to Y$, the finite-level twist
$\Lambda(1)=\mu_{\ell^N}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^N}A$, and the Kummer class
$\kappa(t)\in H^1(\mathbf G_{m,Y},\Lambda(1))$ of the coordinate. Write
$R^m\pi_*=\mathcal H^m R\pi_*$ for the cohomology sheaves of
[def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Then:

1. *(Acyclicity of the affine line.)* The units
$\Lambda_Y\to Rp_*\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_Y}$ and
$\Lambda_Y(1)\to Rp_*\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_Y}(1)$ are isomorphisms; so
$R^mp_*\Lambda(1)=0$ for $m>0$.
1. *(The Kummer generator.)* The unit
$\Lambda_Y(1)\to R^0\pi_*\Lambda(1)$ — equivalently, restriction along $j$
composed with the pullback $p^*$ — is an isomorphism, and the map
$$
\Lambda_Y\longrightarrow R^1\pi_*\Lambda(1),\qquad 1\longmapsto\kappa(t),
$$
sending $1$ to the image of $\kappa(t)$ under the edge map
$H^1(\mathbf G_{m,Y},\Lambda(1))=H^1(Y,R\pi_*\Lambda(1))\to
\Gamma(Y,R^1\pi_*\Lambda(1))$, is an isomorphism: $R^1\pi_*\Lambda(1)$
is free of rank one on $\kappa(t)$.
1. *(Vanishing above degree one.)* $R^m\pi_*\Lambda(1)=0$ for $m\geq2$.
1. *(Base change.)* For every morphism $g:Y'\to Y$ of separated
finite-type $k$-schemes, with base changes
$p':\mathbf A^1_{Y'}\to Y'$, $\pi':\mathbf G_{m,Y'}\to Y'$ and
$g':\mathbf G_{m,Y'}\to\mathbf G_{m,Y}$, the pullback of the Kummer class
is the Kummer class, $g'^*\kappa(t)=\kappa(t')$, and the base-change
morphisms
$$
g^*Rp_*\Lambda(1)\to Rp'_*\Lambda(1),\qquad
g^*R\pi_*\Lambda(1)\to R\pi'_*\Lambda(1)
$$
are isomorphisms.

In particular, taking $Y'=\bar y$ a geometric point, (1)–(3) are
equivalent to the corresponding statements for $\mathbf A^1$ and
$\mathbf G_m$ over an algebraically closed field, which are
[thm-pur-kummer-affine-line].

## Proof

We follow the reduction to a geometric fibre by smooth base change;
nothing below uses the exceptional inverse image of the zero section.
Throughout, $\Lambda(1)_{\mathbf A^1_Y}=p^*\Lambda_Y(1)$ and
$\Lambda(1)_{\mathbf G_{m,Y}}=\pi^*\Lambda_Y(1)$, since $\mu_{\ell^N}$ and
the coefficient extension by $A$ are compatible with pullback
([lem-pur-finite-kummer-level], [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]).
Since the base field $k$ of [def-pur-conventions] is algebraically
closed, a primitive $\ell^N$-th root of unity $\zeta\in k$ trivializes
$\mu_{\ell^N}$, hence $\Lambda(1)\cong\Lambda$, on every $k$-scheme,
compatibly with pullback. We compute on the small etale site; the
comparison inverse image commutes with the derived direct images of
[def-weil-derived-direct-image] ([prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image])
and is fully faithful on bounded-below complexes
([thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]), so the units, the classes and the
isomorphisms below transport to the pro-etale site.

Step 1: clause (1). The untwisted statement is
[lem-pur-a1-direct-image] with $B=Y$. Under the trivialization by
$\zeta$ the twisted unit $\Lambda_Y(1)\to Rp_*p^*\Lambda_Y(1)$ of
[fix-prop-adjunctions] is the untwisted unit
$\Lambda_Y\to Rp_*\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_Y}$, hence an isomorphism; so
$R^mp_*\Lambda(1)=0$ for $m>0$.

Step 2: clauses (2) and (3), on stalks. Let $\bar y$ be a geometric
point of $Y$ and $S'=Y_{(\bar y)}$ the strict henselization, a
$k$-scheme. As $\pi$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and
$\mathbf G_{m,Y}\times_YS'=\mathbf G_{m,S'}$, the stalk formula
[prop-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-stalk-formula] gives
$$
(R\pi_*\Lambda(1))_{\bar y}\simeq R\Gamma(\mathbf G_{m,S'},\Lambda(1)),
$$
compatibly with the unit (on the left) and pullback of constants along
$e:\mathbf G_{m,S'}\to S'$ (on the right), and compatibly with global
classes: the stalk at $\bar y$ of the section of
$R^1\pi_*\Lambda(1)$ defined by a class in
$H^1(\mathbf G_{m,Y},\Lambda(1))$ is its restriction to
$\mathbf G_{m,S'}$.
Now $\mathbf G_{m,S'}=\mathbf G_{m,k}\times_kS'$. The smooth base change
theorem [sbc-thm-smooth-base-change], for the square with smooth side
$f:\mathbf G_{m,k}\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, affine side
$g:S'\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, projections
$h:\mathbf G_{m,S'}\to\mathbf G_{m,k}$ and $e$, and the constant sheaf
$\Lambda(1)_{S'}$ (torsion prime to $p$), gives
$f^{-1}R^qg_*\Lambda(1)\cong R^qh_*\Lambda(1)$ for all $q$. As $S'$ is
strictly henselian, $R^qg_*\Lambda(1)=H^q(S',\Lambda(1))$ is
$\Lambda(1)(k)$ for $q=0$ and $0$ for $q>0$
([sbc-lem-strict-henselian-constant-cohomology]); so
$\Lambda(1)_{\mathbf G_{m,k}}\to Rh_*\Lambda(1)_{\mathbf G_{m,S'}}$ is an
isomorphism and, by the composition of derived direct images
[lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition] (item (5)), pullback along
$h$ is an isomorphism
$$
h^*:R\Gamma(\mathbf G_{m,k},\Lambda(1))\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
R\Gamma(\mathbf G_{m,S'},\Lambda(1)).
$$
By [thm-pur-kummer-affine-line](2),(3), the left side has $H^0=A$
(the constants), $H^1$ free of rank one on the Kummer class of the
coordinate of $\mathbf G_{m,k}$, and no other cohomology. The Kummer
boundary and the coefficient extension of [def-pur-affine-line-datum]
commute with pullback, and the coordinate $t$ restricts to the
coordinate on $\mathbf G_{m,S'}$ and on $\mathbf G_{m,k}$; so the
restriction of $\kappa(t)$ to $\mathbf G_{m,S'}$ is $h^*$ of the Kummer
class of the coordinate of $\mathbf G_{m,k}$. Consequently, at every
geometric point $\bar y$ (writing $R^m\pi_*$ for the cohomology
sheaves of [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]):
$(R^m\pi_*\Lambda(1))_{\bar y}=0$ for $m\geq2$; the stalk of the unit
$\Lambda_Y(1)\to R^0\pi_*\Lambda(1)$ is an isomorphism (constants go to
constants); and the stalk of $\Lambda_Y\to R^1\pi_*\Lambda(1)$,
$1\mapsto\kappa(t)$, sends $1$ to a generator of a free rank-one
module, hence is an isomorphism. Geometric stalks being conservative
([lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]), this proves (3) and both
halves of (2). By [fix-prop-adjunctions](3) the unit of $\pi=pj$ is
the unit of $p$ followed by $Rp_*$ of the unit of $j$, i.e. by
restriction along $j$; with Step 1 this identifies the unit
$\Lambda_Y(1)\to R^0\pi_*\Lambda(1)$ with restriction along $j$
composed with $p^*$, as stated.

Step 3: clause (4). The Kummer sequence of
[def-pur-affine-line-datum], its boundary map, and the coefficient
extension by $A$ are compatible with pullback along
$g':\mathbf G_{m,Y'}\to\mathbf G_{m,Y}$, and $g'^*t=t'$ is the coordinate
of $\mathbf G_{m,Y'}$; hence $g'^*\kappa(t)=\kappa(t')$. The base-change
morphism $g^*Rf_*\to Rf'_*g'^*$ (for $f\in\{p,\pi\}$) is the mate of the
equality $f'^*g^*=g'^*f^*$ under the adjunctions of
[fix-prop-adjunctions], and it is compatible with the units, i.e. its
composite with $g^*$ of the unit $\Lambda_Y(1)\to Rf_*\Lambda(1)$ is the
unit $\Lambda_{Y'}(1)\to Rf'_*\Lambda(1)$; it is also compatible with
pullback of cohomology classes, so on $\mathcal H^1$ for $f=\pi$ it
sends $g^*$ of the section $\kappa(t)$ to the section $g'^*\kappa(t)=
\kappa(t')$. By (1)–(3) over $Y$ and over $Y'$, both sides of each
base-change morphism have cohomology sheaves only in degrees $0$ (for
$p$) resp. $0$ and $1$ (for $\pi$); in degree $0$ they are
$\Lambda_{Y'}(1)$ via the units, and in degree $1$ they are free of rank
one on $g^*\kappa(t)$ resp. $\kappa(t')$. The morphism therefore induces
isomorphisms on all cohomology sheaves ($g^*$ being exact), and is an
isomorphism. For $Y'=\bar y$ a geometric point with algebraically closed
field, $Rf'_*$ is the cohomology of $\mathbf A^1_{\bar y}$ resp.
$\mathbf G_{m,\bar y}$, and the resulting stalk statements are exactly
those of [thm-pur-kummer-affine-line].

attrs.title: The affine line and the punctured line over a base

objects.body:
The purity isomorphisms of
[thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity] commute with the smooth trace of
[def-pur-smooth-trace] and with the composition and
base-change coherence.

## Proof

The smooth trace of [def-pur-smooth-trace] and the composition and
base-change coherence statements over $E$ and $\Qlb$ – those of
[thm-pur-composition-coherence] and
[thm-pur-smooth-base-change-coherence] – are the $E$-
and $\Qlb$-reductions of the corresponding $\mathcal O_E$-level
statements of [thm-pur-adic-reconstruction] and [prop-pur-adic-reconstruction-trace-coherence], transported along
the same exact functors and restricted to the direct summands (the
trace of a summand is the summand of the trace, by naturality).

attrs.title: Trace and coherence compatibilities of rational purity

objects.body:
The purity isomorphisms of
[thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity] are transitive in coefficient
extensions, and preserve idempotent summands (via
[thm-weil-pbc-idempotent-complete-triangulation] and the descent
functors of [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors]).

## Proof

Two lattices of the same $E$-object are related by inverting a
denominator, and the two purity isomorphisms differ by the
corresponding unit ([prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport]); a finite
extension $E'\supset E$ is flat, and the transport is the tensor with
$E'$, giving the transitivity. The independence from the finite stage
and from the particular presentation is the independence of the descent
functors of [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors] and the idempotent
completeness of [thm-weil-pbc-idempotent-complete-triangulation]
(the purity isomorphism is natural in the object by [prop-pur-smooth-purity-naturality-cover], hence commutes with
the descent from a finite stage and with the extension of the
coefficient field).

attrs.title: Transitivity and summand preservation of rational purity

objects.body:
In the situation of [thm-pur-regular-immersion-purity], the purity
isomorphism is compatible with

1. *base change* along an étale morphism $X'\to X$, and more generally
along a smooth morphism $X'\to X$ of smooth $k$-schemes: then
$Z'=Z\times_XX'$ is smooth over $Z$, hence regular, and
$Z'\hookrightarrow X'$ is a regular closed immersion of the same pure
codimension $c$ (flat base change preserves regular sequences), so the
base-changed pair is again in the situation of
[thm-pur-regular-immersion-purity]. Base change along an arbitrary
morphism of pairs would leave that situation and is not claimed;
1. *transverse composition* of regular immersions: for
$i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$ and $j:Y\hookrightarrow X$ transverse regular
immersions of codimensions $b$ and $d$, the purity isomorphisms for
$i$, $j$ and $ji$ compose with the twist additivity;
1. *cup products* (the purity class of a product of pairs is
the exterior product of the classes);
1. *finite reduction* from $A_{E,n}$ to $A_{E,n-1}$.

## Proof

All four assertions reduce to the corresponding assertions about the
canonical classes of [def-pur-frame-class] together with the
canonical structure of the identification of
[thm-pur-regular-immersion-purity]: the purity isomorphism is the
composite of the smooth purity identifications of the structure
morphisms, the composition law for $(-)^!$ and the co-projection
(Steps 1–2 of [thm-pur-regular-immersion-purity]), and only the
classes carry the content (everything else is the canonical
six-functor structure).

*(a) Base change.* For $X'\to X$ smooth (in particular étale) the structure morphisms and the whole
composite identification of Steps 1–2 are stable under base change
(the structure morphisms of the base-changed pair are the base changes
of the structure morphisms; the smooth purity identification
[thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object] is compatible with base
change; the composition law and the co-projection are canonical); the
class of the pair is the Kummer boundary, whose
[lem-pur-frame-independence] and compatibility with pullback give
the assertion.

*(b) Transverse composition.* For transverse $i,j$, the frame
of $ji$ is the product of the frames of the two immersions (the ideal is generated by the ideal of $Y$ in $X$
and lifts of generators of the ideal of $Z$ in $Y$); the Kummer
class of the multiplication is the sum and the exterior product of the
classes of the two frames is the class of the composite pair by
[lem-pur-kunneth-supported]; combining with the twist additivity
of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] and the composition law for $(-)^!$
of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] gives the statement (the
dimensions add: $c=b+d$).

*(c) Cup products.* The canonical class of a product of pairs is
the exterior product of the classes, by [lem-pur-kunneth-supported]
and [lem-pur-frame-independence]; an iterated application gives
the cup-product compatibility.

*(d) Finite reduction.* The Kummer boundary of the coordinate
reduces to itself (the Kummer sequence is natural in $n$), the
localization triangles and the classes reduce compatibly by the
naturality of [lem-pur-kunneth-supported] and of the
recollement; hence every displayed step of
[thm-pur-regular-immersion-purity] is natural in $n$.

attrs.title: Compatibilities of purity for regular immersions

objects.body:
In the situation of [thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity],
the smooth purity map $\gamma_{f,K}$ of
[def-pur-smooth-purity-map] is natural in $K$, and it is
independent of the choices made in its construction.

## Proof

Naturality in $K$ is the naturality of the tensor formula
[thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness], of the twist
isomorphisms [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], and of the
identification of [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object] (in the
object and in the morphism, all steps of the construction of
[def-pur-smooth-purity-map] being canonical derived
transformations).
The independence of the choices: the construction contains no
choices at all – the identification of
[thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object] is the unique one normalized
on the standard pairs and compatible with base change and etale
localization ([thm-pur-dnc-invariance]), the tensor formula and
the twist isomorphisms are canonical, and the normalization of the
fundamental class is the single one of the Kummer boundary of the
coordinate ([thm-pur-affine-line-orientation] and
[thm-pur-rank-one-local-calculation]).

attrs.title: Naturality and independence of the smooth purity map

objects.body:
All geometric- and scheme-Frobenius equivariance squares of
[thm-pur-weil-equivariance-of-purity-and-trace] and of
[prop-pur-weil-equivariance-scheme-frobenius] commute with finite
reduction, scalar extension, composition, and base change.

## Proof

The compatibilities are those of the constituent purity, counit, and
trace statements established in
[thm-pur-weil-equivariance-of-purity-and-trace] (each being
compatible with the coefficient transport of
[thm-pur-adic-reconstruction]), transported by the scheme-Frobenius
identification of [prop-pur-weil-equivariance-scheme-frobenius].

Precomposing the vertical maps of the three squares of
[thm-pur-weil-equivariance-of-purity-and-trace] with the
corresponding $\kappa_X$ or $\kappa_Y$ of
[def-pur-scheme-geometric-frobenius] gives the same three squares
for the scheme-Frobenius maps $u_N$.

## Proof

The isomorphisms $\kappa_X,\kappa_Y$ of
[def-pur-scheme-geometric-frobenius] identify $L\Phi^*$ with
$Lg_\gamma^*$ compatibly with the pullback-composition identifications
and with $f$, so precomposing the vertical maps preserves the
commutativity of the squares.

Fix a prime $p$, $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, put $q=p^a$,
$k_0=\Fq$, and let $k=\Fbar$ be the
fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$.
Choose a prime $\ell\neq p$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and let
$d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$. Let $X_0/k_0$ be
smooth, proper, geometrically connected
of pure dimension $d$, with $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ and
$(V_{i,\ell},F_{i,\ell},P_{i,\ell})_{0\leq i\leq2d}$ the
smooth-proper
cohomological family.
Fix an indeterminate $T$. For $n\geq1$, put
$N_n(X_0)=\#X_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$ and define the
point-count zeta series

$$
Z(X_0,T)=\exp\left(\sum_{n\geq1}N_n(X_0)\frac{T^n}{n}\right).
$$

Assume the closed-point product

$$
Z(X_0,T)=\prod_{x\in|X_0|}(1-T^{\deg(x)})^{-1}
$$

and the trace-to-determinant identity

$$
Z(X_0,T)=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}P_{i,\ell}(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}
\quad\text{in }\Ql(T).
$$

Writing
$Z(X_0,T)=\sum_{n\geq0}z_nT^n$, assume that its Hankel matrix
$\mathcal H(Z)=(z_{r+s})_{r,s\geq0}$ has finite rank, in the sense of the
Hankel-matrix definition; equivalently,
the sequence $(z_n)$ satisfies a linear recurrence over $\mathbf Q$ from
some index onward. A normalized presentation is a pair
$A,B\in\mathbf Z[T]$ satisfying

$$
Z(X_0,T)=A(T)/B(T),\qquad A(0)=B(0)=1,\qquad
\gcd(A,B)=1\text{ in }\mathbf Q[T],
$$

and this is the
normalized integral-fraction
condition. Then

$$
Z(X_0,T)\in\mathbf Q(T).
$$

## Proof

The finite-rank hypothesis on $\mathcal H(Z)=(z_{r+s})_{r,s\geq0}$ in
the sense of [def-weil-hankel-matrix] is exactly the finite-rank
hypothesis of [prop-weil-rationality-criterion] with
$K=\mathbf Q$, so the equivalence of its first two items gives
$Z(X_0,T)\in\mathbf Q(T)$, which is the assertion.

attrs.title: Rational descent of the zeta series

objects.body:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$, an integer $n\in\mathbf
Z_{\geq1}$, and put $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $T$ be a Noetherian scheme on which
$\ell$ is invertible (for instance a finite-type scheme over a field in which
$\ell$ is invertible), and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with complementary
open immersion $j$, as in the open-closed recollement
[def-weil-open-closed-recollement]. Let $Ri^!$ be the right adjoint of the
direct image $i_*=Ri_*$ on the ambient ordinary derived categories of the
small pro-etale sites, as in [lem-exc-proetale-closed-support]. Then for
every $Q\in D(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ the adjunction unit is an isomorphism

$$
Q\xrightarrow{\ \eta_i^!\ }Ri^!Ri_*Q .
$$

No boundedness or constructibility of $Q$ is required. In particular, for the
constructible exceptional adjoint $Ri^!$ of
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] — which exists without the ambient datum
of [def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint], that datum being false in general —
computed with the compactification
$Z\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}Z\xrightarrow{i}T$ so that $Ri_{!,n}=Ri_*$,
for $Q\in D^b_c(Z,A)$ the unit of the adjunction
$\Hom_T(Ri_!K,L)\cong\Hom_Z(K,Ri^!L)$ of
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] is an isomorphism
$Q\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri^!Ri_*Q$.

## Proof

By [lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact], the closed direct image is exact (the
complement of $Z$ is quasi-compact because $T$ is Noetherian), so $Ri_*$ is
computed by $i_*$ on any complex, and [lem-exc-proetale-closed-support]
provides its right adjoint $Ri^!$ on the ambient derived categories.

By [prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions], $i^*\dashv Ri_*$ on the
ambient derived categories and the counit $i^*Ri_*\to\operatorname{id}$ is an
isomorphism. A right adjoint whose counit is an isomorphism is fully
faithful, so for all $P,Q\in D(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ the map
$g\mapsto Ri_*g$ is a bijection

$$
\Hom(P,Q)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Hom(Ri_*P,Ri_*Q).
$$

Now fix $Q$ and consider, for every $P$, the composite

$$
\Hom(P,Q)\xrightarrow{\ \eta^!_{i,Q}\circ-\ }\Hom(P,Ri^!Ri_*Q)
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Hom(Ri_*P,Ri_*Q),
$$

the second map being the adjunction bijection of $Ri_*\dashv Ri^!$. By the
triangle identity, the adjoint of $\eta^!_{i,Q}\circ g$ is
$\epsilon^!_{Ri_*Q}\circ Ri_*(\eta^!_{i,Q})\circ Ri_*g=Ri_*g$, so the
composite is the bijection displayed above. Hence composition with
$\eta^!_{i,Q}$ is a bijection $\Hom(P,Q)\to\Hom(P,Ri^!Ri_*Q)$, naturally in
$P$, and the Yoneda lemma shows that $\eta^!_{i,Q}$ is an isomorphism.

For the last assertion, the right adjoint $Ri_n^{\times}$ of
$Ri_{!,n}=Ri_*$ given by the datum of [def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint]
is, by uniqueness of right adjoints, identified with $Ri^!$ together with its
unit. The functor $Ri^!$ of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] is its
restriction to $D^b_c$, with the same unit, so its unit at $Q\in D^b_c(Z,A)$
is the isomorphism just proved.

Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of separated finite-type
$k$-schemes and let $\Lambda$ be one of the coefficient stages
$A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb$, with the categories $D^b_c(-,\Lambda)$ of
[def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed],
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi],
[def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] and the direct image
$i_*=Ri_*=Ri_!$ of [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. Then

$$
i_*:D^b_c(Z,\Lambda)\longrightarrow D^b_c(X,\Lambda)
$$

is fully faithful. Consequently, at every stage at which $i_*$ has a right
adjoint $Ri^!$ on these categories (the exceptional inverse image of
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]), the adjunction unit is an isomorphism

$$
Q\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Ri^!i_*Q\qquad(Q\in D^b_c(Z,\Lambda)).
$$

At $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ the right adjoint exists on the ambient categories and
this is [prop-sf-closed-immersion-unit].

## Proof

*Finite stage.* By [prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions] the
counit $i^*i_*\to\operatorname{id}$ of $i^*\dashv i_*$ is an isomorphism, so
$i_*$ is fully faithful on the ambient categories and hence on the full
subcategories $D^b_c$.

*Integral stage.* Put $R=\mathcal O_E$ and $A_n=R/\varpi_E^n$. For
$P,Q\in D^b_c(Z,R)$ one has $Q\cong R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nQ_n$
and, by [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits],
$i_*Q\cong R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_ni_*Q_n$ with
$(i_*P)_n\cong i_*P_n$. Extension and restriction of scalars give
$\operatorname{Hom}(P[m],\operatorname{Res}_nQ_n)
=\operatorname{Hom}_{A_n}(P_n[m],Q_n)$ and
$\operatorname{Hom}(i_*P[m],\operatorname{Res}_ni_*Q_n)
=\operatorname{Hom}_{A_n}(i_*P_n[m],i_*Q_n)$, and $i_*$ identifies the two by
the finite stage, compatibly with the transition maps. Apply
$\operatorname{Hom}(P[m],-)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(i_*P[m],-)$ to the two
Roos triangles of [prop-weil-pbc-roos-triangle]; the map induced by $i_*$ is
an isomorphism on the two product terms for all $m$, so by the five lemma
$\operatorname{Hom}(P,Q)\to\operatorname{Hom}(i_*P,i_*Q)$ is bijective.

*Rational stage.* Hom groups in $D^b_c(-,E)$ are the integral ones tensored
with $E$ ([def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]), and $i_*$ is the
rationalized integral functor, so bijectivity persists.

*Algebraically closed stage.* Hom groups in $D^b_c(-,\Qlb)$ are filtered
colimits over finite extensions $L$ of Hom groups at the stage $L$
([def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]), and $i_*$ commutes with
finite scalar extension ([prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]); a colimit of
bijections is a bijection.

*The unit.* Given a right adjoint $Ri^!$ at the stage $\Lambda$, fix $Q$.
For every $P$ the composite of $\eta_Q\circ-:\operatorname{Hom}(P,Q)\to
\operatorname{Hom}(P,Ri^!i_*Q)$ with the adjunction bijection onto
$\operatorname{Hom}(i_*P,i_*Q)$ is, by a triangle identity, $g\mapsto i_*g$,
which is bijective by full faithfulness. So $\eta_Q\circ-$ is bijective,
naturally in $P$, and Yoneda makes $\eta_Q$ an isomorphism, exactly as in
[prop-sf-closed-immersion-unit].

attrs.title: Closed direct image is fully faithful at every coefficient stage

objects.body:
Let $X$ be a scheme and let $\nu_X:X_{\Proet}\to X_{\Et}$ be the comparison
morphism of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], the coefficient ring
being $A$. Let $G$ be a sheaf of $A$-modules on the small étale site
$X_{\Et}$, in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]; *no*
constructibility hypothesis is imposed on $G$. Then the adjunction map

$$
G\longrightarrow\nu_{X,*}\nu_X^*G
$$

is an isomorphism, and consequently

$$
R^q\nu_{X,*}\bigl(\nu_X^*G\bigr)=0\qquad(q>0).
$$

Thus on the sheaves of étale origin – equivalently, by
[lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], on the coefficient sheaves of the
blueprint's class [def-sf-fullcd-used-class] – the vanishing degree of
the comparison direct image is bounded by $M=0$, independently of the
dimension of $X$ and of any constructibility of $G$.
[thm-sf-fullcd-etale-origin] is the form of this statement that the
chapter consumes: there the bound read off for the condition
[def-weil-full-cohomological-dimension] is $2d$, the $2d$ being the
étale direction of the Leray spectral sequence of
[thm-sp-grothendieck] and not the comparison bound, which is $0$.

## Proof

The two inputs are Bhatt–Scholze, Lemma 5.1.1 and Corollary 5.1.6 of
[arXiv:1309.1198v2](https://arxiv.org/html/1309.1198v2), quoted verbatim in
Section 16.1 of the audit ledger; both are stated for an arbitrary scheme and
an arbitrary sheaf, respectively bounded-below complex, on the small étale
site, so a sheaf of $A$-modules on $X_{\Et}$ in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] is covered verbatim. By Lemma 5.1.1, for
$G\in\Sh(X_{\Et})$ and an affine pro-étale $U=\lim_iU_i$ one has
$\nu_X^*G(U)=\colim_iG(U_i)$, the presheaf so defined being a sheaf; by
Lemma 5.1.2 the pullback $\nu_X^*$ is fully faithful, with essential image
exactly those sheaves $F$ on $X_{\Proet}$ whose values on $U=\lim_iU_i$
are the filtered colimits of their values on the $U_i$. The sheaf
$\nu_X^*G$ lies in that essential image, so
$\nu_X^*\nu_{X,*}\nu_X^*G\to\nu_X^*G$ is an isomorphism; applying the fully
faithful $\nu_X^*$ to the two maps $G\to\nu_{X,*}\nu_X^*G$ and
$\nu_{X,*}\nu_X^*G\to G$ that this isomorphism exhibits shows that the
adjunction map $G\to\nu_{X,*}\nu_X^*G$ is an isomorphism in
$\Sh(X_{\Et},A)$. Corollary 5.1.6 is the derived form of the same identity:
$K\to R\nu_{X,*}\nu_X^*K$ is an equivalence for every
$K\in D^+(X_{\Et})$. Taking $K=G$ concentrated in degree zero and passing
to cohomology sheaves gives
$R^q\nu_{X,*}\nu_X^*G=\mathcal H^q(R\nu_{X,*}\nu_X^*G)=0$ for every $q>0$,
which is the displayed vanishing. The identification of the class of étale
origin with the coefficient class [def-sf-fullcd-used-class] is
[lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], and the passage from this bound to
the bound $2d$ of [thm-sf-fullcd-etale-origin] in the form of
[def-weil-full-cohomological-dimension] is through the Leray spectral
sequence of [thm-sp-grothendieck], whose $p$-direction is bounded by
$2d$ on the étale site.

attrs.title: The comparison bound on coefficients of étale origin is $M=0$

objects.body:
In the setting of [def-sf-datum], let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ be
quasi-isomorphic, locally on the site of $X$, to a bounded complex of finite
projective $\Lambda_X$-modules. Then
$K^\vee=R\mathcal H om_X(K,\Lambda_X)$ is perfect on $X$ and the
evaluation $K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}K^\vee\to\Lambda_X$ is defined.

## Proof

Choose locally a bounded complex $P^\bullet$ of finite projective
$\Lambda_X$-modules with a quasi-isomorphism $P^\bullet\to K$. By
[lem-sf-hom-finite-projective] the dual $P^{\bullet\vee}$ is again
bounded with finite projective terms, so $K^\vee$ is quasi-isomorphic to
$P^{\bullet\vee}$ and is perfect on $X$. The evaluation
$K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}K^\vee\to\Lambda_X$ is the counit of the
tensor–internal-Hom adjunction of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], hence is defined.

In the setting of [def-sf-datum], let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ be
quasi-isomorphic, locally on the site of $X$, to a bounded complex of finite
projective $\Lambda_X$-modules. Then
$K^\vee\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}M\to R\mathcal H om_X(K,M)$ is an
isomorphism for every $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$.

## Proof

Choose locally a bounded complex $P^\bullet$ of finite projective
