$\Lambda_X$-modules with a quasi-isomorphism $P^\bullet\to K$, and let
$I(M)$ be a functorial K-injective replacement of $M$. Since the terms of
$P^\bullet$ are projective, $R\mathcal H om_X(K,M)$ is represented by
$\mathcal H om^\bullet_X(P^\bullet,I(M))$, and termwise
$\mathcal H om_X(P^j,I(M)^k)=P^{j\vee}\otimes_{\Lambda_X}I(M)^k$ by
[lem-sf-hom-finite-projective], the identification being compatible
with differentials. Hence
$R\mathcal H om_X(K,M)\cong P^{\bullet\vee}\otimes_{\Lambda_X}I(M)\cong K^\vee\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}M$, which is the displayed isomorphism, the
$K^\vee$-side of both objects being the coefficient dual of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].

attrs.title: Internal Hom through the coefficient dual

objects.body:
Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be
a closed immersion and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ the complementary open
immersion. Let $\Lambda$ be one of the coefficient stages
$A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb$, with the categories $D^b_c(-,\Lambda)$ of
[def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed],
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi],
[def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], the pullbacks of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and the direct images $i_*$, $Rj_*$
of [def-weil-derived-direct-image].

1. $Rj_*$ carries $D^b_c(U,\Lambda)$ into $D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$.
2. $i_*:D^b_c(Z,\Lambda)\to D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ has a right adjoint $Ri^!$;
   it is the exceptional inverse image of
   [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] (at $\mathcal O_E$ it is
   $R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nRi_n^!K_n$, with reductions
   $Ri_n^!K_n$).
3. For $K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ the closed exceptional counit and the open
   unit extend to a distinguished triangle
   $$
   i_*Ri^!K\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow Rj_*j^*K
   \longrightarrow i_*Ri^!K[1],
   $$
   with $\operatorname{Hom}(i_*Ri^!K[m],Rj_*j^*K)=0$ for all $m$, so the
   third arrow is unique and the triangle is functorial in $K$.
4. $Ri^!Rj_*G=0$ for $G\in D^b_c(U,\Lambda)$, and the unit
   $Q\to Ri^!i_*Q$ is an isomorphism for $Q\in D^b_c(Z,\Lambda)$.

The same holds on the finite-Tor subcategories $D^b_{ctf}(-,\Lambda)$ of
[def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Let $d=\dim U$ and assume
$c=\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(k)$ ([def-sc-etale-torsion-cd]) is finite
($c=0$ for $k$ algebraically closed).

- (1') $Rj_*$ carries $D^b_{ctf}(U,\Lambda)$ into $D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$;
   at $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ goes to Tor amplitude in
   $[a,b+2d+c]$, and at $\mathcal O_E$ the same holds for the uniform
   interval of the reductions.
- (2') $Ri^!$ carries $D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ into $D^b_{ctf}(Z,\Lambda)$,
   with Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ going to $[a,b+2d+c+1]$ (at $A_{E,n}$, and
   uniformly in the reductions at $\mathcal O_E$).
- (3') $i_*$, $i^*$ and $j^*$ preserve $D^b_{ctf}$ and Tor amplitude
   intervals; hence for $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ all three vertices of
   the triangle of (3) lie in $D^b_{ctf}$.
- (4') For $G\in D^b_{ctf}(U,\Lambda)$ and $Q\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,\Lambda)$,
   $Ri^!Rj_*G=0$ and $Q\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri^!i_*Q$ inside $D^b_{ctf}$.

At $E$ and $\Qlb$ these are (1)–(4), since there $D^b_{ctf}=D^b_c$.

If $X,Z,U$ come from $k_0$-schemes and $\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$, then $Ri^!$
carries Weil structures ([def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]) for which the
adjunction is equivariant, and for Weil complexes the three arrows of the
triangle and the unit are Weil-equivariant.

## Proof

*Vanishing.* At every stage $\operatorname{Hom}(i_*P[m],Rj_*N)=0$ for
$P\in D^b_c(Z,\Lambda)$ and $N\in D^b_c(U,\Lambda)$. At a finite stage this
is $\operatorname{Hom}(j^*i_*P[m],N)$ by $j^*\dashv Rj_*$
([def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]), and $j^*i_*=0$ by
[lem-exc-proetale-closed-essential-image] and the exactness of $i_*$
([lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact]). At $\mathcal O_E$ it follows from the
finite case by the Roos triangle of [prop-weil-pbc-roos-triangle] (as in
[prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages]), since
$Rj_*N=R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nRj_*N_n$ by
[def-weil-derived-direct-image], [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits]. At $E$
and $\Qlb$ the groups are $\otimes E$, resp. filtered colimits, of these.

*Finite stage.* Let $A=A_{E,n}$. For (1), write $G=\nu_U^*G'$ with $G'$
étale bounded constructible ([lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]); then
$Rj_*G\cong\nu_X^*Rj_*G'$ by [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image], and
$Rj_*G'$ is bounded constructible by [thm-fin-open-immersion] and dévissage
over the finitely many cohomology sheaves ([thm-constructible-serre]). The
right adjoint $Ri^!$ of $i_*$ on the ambient categories is
[lem-exc-proetale-closed-support], and the triangle of (3) is
[lem-exc-proetale-support-triangle]. Its outer vertices $K$ and
$Rj_*j^*K$ are in $D^b_c$, hence so is $i_*Ri^!K$, and
$Ri^!K\cong i^*i_*Ri^!K$ lies in $D^b_c(Z,A)$. So $Ri^!$ restricts to
$D^b_c$, and by uniqueness of right adjoints it is the finite exceptional
inverse image of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], as in
[prop-sf-closed-immersion-unit].

*Integral stage.* Put $R=\mathcal O_E$, $A_n=R/\varpi_E^n$ and
$K_n=K\otimes^L_RA_n$. For (1): $M=Rj_*G$ is derived complete with
$M_n\cong Rj_*G_n$ ([prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits]), and these are
bounded constructible by the finite stage. The triangles
$M_1\to M_n\to M_{n-1}\to$ induced by
$0\to A_1\xrightarrow{\varpi_E^{n-1}}A_n\to A_{n-1}\to0$ show inductively
that all $M_n$ lie in the cohomological interval of $M_1$ and are
constructible ([thm-constructible-serre]), so $M\in D^b_c(X,R)$.

For (2) and (3), let $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$, let $K\to Rj_*j^*K$ be the derived
limit of the finite units (its reductions are the finite units, by
[lemma-weil-pbc-completed-pullback-reduction] and
[prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits]), and let $F$ be its fibre, an object of
$D^b_c(X,R)$ by (1). By TR3 and the finite triangles, the induced map of
triangles is an isomorphism on two terms, hence on the third
([lem-sf-triangle-two-out-of-three]):
$F_n\cong i_*Ri_n^!K_n$. Put $Q=i^*F\in D^b_c(Z,R)$. The unit
$F\to i_*i^*F$, taken as the derived limit of the finite units, reduces to
the finite units, which are isomorphisms because $F_n$ lies in the image of
$i_*$ ([lem-exc-proetale-closed-essential-image]). Its cone is derived
complete with zero reductions, hence zero by [def-weil-derived-complete]; so
$F\cong i_*Q$ and $Q_n\cong Ri_n^!K_n$. For $P\in D^b_c(Z,R)$ the vanishing
above and the full faithfulness of [prop-sf-closed-unit-all-stages] give,
naturally in $P$,
$$
\operatorname{Hom}(P,Q)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(i_*P,i_*Q)
=\operatorname{Hom}(i_*P,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(i_*P,K).
$$
Thus $Ri^!K:=Q$ is right adjoint to $i_*$, with counit $F\to K$; since $Q$
is derived complete with reductions $Ri_n^!K_n$, it is the derived limit of
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. The triangle of (3) is
$F\to K\to Rj_*j^*K\to$.

*Rational stage.* The exact $R$-linear functor $Ri^!$, the adjunction data
and the maps of the triangle rationalize by
[prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport]; Hom groups become
$\operatorname{Hom}\otimes_RE$, so the adjunction persists, and triangles
remain distinguished.

*Algebraically closed stage.* Since $Ri^!K\cong i^*\operatorname{fib}(K\to
Rj_*j^*K)$ with a fibre unique up to unique isomorphism (by the vanishing),
the scalar-extension compatibilities of $i^*,j^*,Rj_*$
([prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]) induce coherent ones for $Ri^!$. So
$Ri^!$, its adjunction and the triangle descend by
[prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors], triangles remain distinguished by
[thm-weil-pbc-verdier-axioms], and the Hom bijections pass to the filtered
colimits.

*Consequences.* For (4): $\operatorname{Hom}(N[m],Ri^!Rj_*G)
=\operatorname{Hom}(i_*N[m],Rj_*G)=0$ for all $N$ and $m$, so
$Ri^!Rj_*G=0$; the unit is an isomorphism by
[prop-sf-closed-unit-all-stages].

*Finite Tor amplitude.* Let $A=A_{E,n}$ and $\kappa=A/(\varpi_E)$, the
constant sheaf on each site.

*Residue criterion.* On any of the pro-étale sites, a bounded constructible
complex $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ if and only if $K\otimes^L_A\kappa$
has cohomology in $[a,b]$, by [lem-sf-proetale-residue-tor-test], the
pro-étale form of the étale criterion [lem-exc-residue-tor-test]; it is
applied below only to bounded constructible complexes, by (1) and (2). The pullbacks
$i^*,j^*,\nu^*$ commute with $-\otimes^L_A\kappa$, being monoidal with
$\kappa$ pulling back to $\kappa$ ([def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom],
[prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]); being exact they preserve
cohomological intervals. Conversely $\nu^*$ reflects them: if
$\nu^*C$ has cohomology in $[a,b]$ for $C\in\Dplus$, then
$\nu^*\tau_{>b}C=\tau_{>b}\nu^*C=0$, hence $\tau_{>b}C=0$ by
[thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], and likewise below $a$.

*(3') for $i^*,j^*,i_*$.* For $i^*$ and $j^*$ this is the criterion and
the commutation just stated. For $P\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$ with amplitude
$[a,b]$, $j^*(i_*P\otimes^L_A\kappa)\cong j^*i_*P\otimes^L_A\kappa=0$, so
each cohomology sheaf of $i_*P\otimes^L_A\kappa$ is in the image of $i_*$
([lem-exc-proetale-closed-essential-image]) and equals
$i_*i^*\mathcal H^r(i_*P\otimes^L_A\kappa)\cong
i_*\mathcal H^r(P\otimes^L_A\kappa)$, using exactness of $i^*$ and
$i^*i_*\cong\operatorname{id}$; it vanishes outside $[a,b]$.

*(1') at the finite stage.* Let $G\in D^b_{ctf}(U,A)$ have amplitude
$[a,b]$ and write $G=\nu_U^*G'$ as in the proof of (1). Then
$\nu_U^*(G'\otimes^L_A\kappa)\cong G\otimes^L_A\kappa$ has cohomology in
$[a,b]$, hence so has $G'\otimes^L_A\kappa$. The higher direct images
$R^qj_*$ on the small étale site vanish on sheaves of $A$-modules for
$q>2d+c$: for $k$ algebraically closed this is
[lem-sf-etale-direct-image-vanishing]; in general its proof applies
verbatim, with [thm-sc-finite-type-torsion-cd] at the given $c$. By the
truncation spectral sequence [thm-sp-truncation-e2],
$Rj_*(G'\otimes^L_A\kappa)$ has cohomology in $[a,b+2d+c]$.

*Projection formula for $\kappa$.* The canonical map
$Rj_*G'\otimes^L_A\kappa\to Rj_*(G'\otimes^L_A\kappa)$ is an isomorphism.
Choose a bounded-above resolution $P\to\kappa$ by finite free $A$-modules;
tensoring with the constant complex $P$ computes $-\otimes^L_A\kappa$. For
the finite stupid truncations $\sigma_{\ge-t}P$ the comparison is an
isomorphism: it is the identity for $A$ and is preserved by finite sums,
shifts and cones. Let $G'$ and $Rj_*G'$ have cohomology in degrees $\le e$.
The quotients $\sigma_{<-t}P$ live in degrees $\le-t-1$, so
$G'\otimes\sigma_{<-t}P$ has cohomology in degrees $\le e-t-1$, and
$Rj_*$ of it in degrees $\le e-t-1+2d+c$ (the vanishing above), while
$Rj_*G'\otimes\sigma_{<-t}P$ has cohomology in degrees $\le e-t-1$.
For fixed $r$ and $t$ large, the long exact sequences of the two
triangles attached to $\sigma_{\ge-t}P\to P\to\sigma_{<-t}P$ therefore
identify both sides with the finite-free comparison in degree $r$.

Hence $Rj_*G'\otimes^L_A\kappa$ has cohomology in $[a,b+2d+c]$. Applying
$\nu_X^*$ and [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image],
$Rj_*G\otimes^L_A\kappa\cong\nu_X^*(Rj_*G'\otimes^L_A\kappa)$ has
cohomology in the same interval; with (1), the residue criterion gives
$Rj_*G\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ with amplitude $[a,b+2d+c]$.

*(2') at the finite stage.* Let $K$ have amplitude $[a,b]$. Then $j^*K$
has amplitude $[a,b]$ and $Rj_*j^*K$ amplitude $[a,b+2d+c]$. Tensoring the
triangle of (3) with $\kappa$ and taking the long exact sequence,
$\mathcal H^r(i_*Ri^!K\otimes^L_A\kappa)$ lies between
$\mathcal H^{r-1}(Rj_*j^*K\otimes^L_A\kappa)$ and
$\mathcal H^r(K\otimes^L_A\kappa)$, so it vanishes outside
$[a,b+2d+c+1]$. Since $Ri^!K\cong i^*i_*Ri^!K$, the commutation of $i^*$
with $-\otimes^L_A\kappa$ and the residue criterion give amplitude
$[a,b+2d+c+1]$ for $Ri^!K$.

*Other stages.* At $\mathcal O_E$, the reductions are
$(Rj_*G)_m\cong Rj_*G_m$ ([prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits]) and
$(Ri^!K)_m\cong Ri_m^!K_m$ (integral stage above), and similarly for
$i^*,j^*,i_*$; the finite-stage bounds hold with intervals depending only on
the uniform interval of the reductions of $G$, resp. $K$. At $E$ and $\Qlb$,
$D^b_{ctf}=D^b_c$ by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Clauses (3') and (4')
are then (3) and (4) read inside the full subcategories $D^b_{ctf}$.

*Weil structures.* The Weil structures of $i^*,j^*,Rj_*$ and the
equivariance of the open unit are those of
[prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages]. For a Weil complex $K$, the
fibre $F$ therefore carries a unique Weil structure making $F\to K$
equivariant (uniqueness from the vanishing), and $Ri^!K=i^*F$ inherits it;
under the adjunction bijection above this is the mate of the Weil structure
of $i_*$, so the adjunction, its counit and unit are equivariant. The third
arrow is equivariant by the uniqueness in (3).

attrs.title: The closed-support triangle at every coefficient stage

objects.body:
Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be
a closed immersion and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ the complementary open
immersion. Let $\Lambda$ be one of the coefficient stages
$A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb$, with the categories $D^b_c(-,\Lambda)$
([def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed],
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi],
[def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]), the pullbacks $i^*,j^*$ of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the direct image $i_*=Ri_*$ of
[def-weil-derived-direct-image] and the extension by zero $j_!=Rj_!$ of
[def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. For
$K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ the open counit and the closed unit extend to a
distinguished triangle, the open–closed recollement triangle of
[def-weil-open-closed-recollement],
$$
j_!j^*K\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow i_*i^*K
\longrightarrow j_!j^*K[1].
$$
Moreover $\operatorname{Hom}(j_!j^*K[m],i_*i^*K)=0$ for all $m$; hence the
third arrow is uniquely determined by the other two and the triangle is
functorial in $K$. If $X=X_0\otimes_{k_0}k$, $Z$, $U$ come from
$k_0$-schemes, $\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$ and $K$ is a Weil complex
([def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]), then all three arrows are
Weil-equivariant.

## Proof

*Finite stage.* Let $A=A_{E,n}$. By [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]
write $K\cong\nu_X^*G$ with $G$ a bounded constructible complex on the étale
site. The étale triangle $j_!j^{-1}G\to G\to i_*i^{-1}G\to$ is
[lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement]. Apply the exact functor $\nu_X^*$
([prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level]). The comparisons of
[lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] (for $j_!$),
[lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] (for $j^*,i^*$) and
[prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] (for the finite, hence
quasi-compact, $i$) identify its vertices with $j_!j^*K$, $K$, $i_*i^*K$.
These comparisons are those of the adjunctions of
[prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions], so the first two arrows
become the pro-étale open counit and closed unit. Hom vanishing: by
[prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions] $j_!\dashv j^*$, and
$j^*i_*=0$ (the closed fibre of an object over $U$ is empty), so
$\operatorname{Hom}(j_!N[m],i_*M)=\operatorname{Hom}(N[m],j^*i_*M)=0$. Two
completions of the first two arrows differ by an automorphism $h$ of the third
vertex with $h-\operatorname{id}$ factoring through $i_*i^*K\to
j_!j^*K[1]$, hence through a zero map; so $h=\operatorname{id}$.

*Integral stage.* Put $R=\mathcal O_E$, $A_n=R/\varpi_E^n$,
$K_n=K\otimes^L_RA_n$. The operations have the finite reductions:
$(j^*K)_n\cong j^*K_n$ and $(i^*K)_n\cong i^*K_n$ by
[lemma-weil-pbc-completed-pullback-reduction];
$(i_*M)_n\cong i_*M_n$, with $i_*M$ derived complete, by
[prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits]; and for the extension by zero,
[lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison] applied to the identity square
shows that $j_!N$ is derived complete with $(j_!N)_n\cong j_!N_n$, so it is
the derived limit $R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nj_!N_n$ of
[def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. Define the counit
$j_!j^*K\to K$ and the unit $K\to i_*i^*K$ as the derived limits of the
finite counits and units, using $K\cong R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nK_n$;
their reductions are the finite maps.

Hom vanishing. If $P$ is integral and
$M=R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nM_n$, then
$\operatorname{Hom}(P[m],\operatorname{Res}_nM_n)=
\operatorname{Hom}_{A_n}(P_n[m],M_n)$ by extension and restriction of
scalars; if these vanish for all $m,n$, the Roos triangle of
[prop-weil-pbc-roos-triangle] gives $\operatorname{Hom}(P[m],M)=0$. With
$P=j_!j^*K$, $M=i_*i^*K$ the finite vanishing gives the integral one.

Completion criterion. Let $u:A\to B$, $v:B\to C$ be maps of derived complete
objects with $A,B\in D^b_c(X,R)$, $\operatorname{Hom}(A[m],C)=0$ for all
$m$, and reductions $A_n\to B_n\to C_n$ extending to distinguished
triangles. Then $vu=0$, because $\operatorname{Hom}(A,C)=0$. Choose a
cone $B\xrightarrow{w}C'\to A[1]$ of $u$; then $v=\varphi w$ for a unique
$\varphi:C'\to C$. Modulo $\varpi_E^n$, TR3 and the finite uniqueness make
$\varphi_n$ an isomorphism, so the cone of $\varphi$ is derived complete with
zero reductions, hence zero by [def-weil-derived-complete]. Thus
$A\to B\to C\to A[1]$ is distinguished. Applied to the counit and unit this
gives the integral triangle, and $i_*i^*K\in D^b_c(X,R)$.

*Rational stage.* By [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] the objects of
$D^b_c(-,E)$ are the integral ones, and by
[prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] the exact $R$-linear functors
$i^*,j^*,i_*,j_!$ and the two maps are the rationalized integral ones. The
image of a distinguished integral triangle is distinguished, and Hom groups
become $\operatorname{Hom}\otimes_RE=0$.

*Algebraically closed stage.* An object of $D^b_c(-,\Qlb)$ is a pair
$(E,K)$ ([def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]). The operations are
the descended functors of [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors], built from the
scalar-extension compatibilities of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] (for
$j_!$, the finite-stage compact-support functor of
[def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]); the two maps descend as
compatible transformations. The finite-stage inclusions are exact by
[thm-weil-pbc-verdier-axioms], so the $E$-stage triangle gives the
$\Qlb$-triangle, and Hom groups are filtered colimits of vanishing
$E$-stage groups.

*Weil structures.* The geometric Frobenius $g_X$ of
[def-weil-frobenius-detailed] restricts to $g_U$ and $g_Z$, and the squares
formed by $j$, $i$ and these automorphisms are cartesian. The exchange maps
of [fix-lem-exchanges] for these automorphism squares are isomorphisms
(their inverses come from the inverse squares), and they give the Weil
structures on $j_!$ and $i_*$; the pullbacks use $g_U^*j^*=j^*g_X^*$ and
$g_Z^*i^*=i^*g_X^*$. The counit and unit are equivariant, since the exchange
maps are built from, and paste with, the same units and counits
([fix-lem-exchanges]). Transporting the triangle along $g_X^*$ and the Weil
isomorphisms gives a distinguished triangle with the same first two arrows;
by the uniqueness above it has the same third arrow, which is therefore
equivariant.

attrs.title: The open–closed triangle at every coefficient stage

objects.body:
In the setting of [def-sf-datum], the projection transformations
satisfy: naturality in $K$, $L$, $f$ and the coefficient ring; the identity
for $f=\operatorname{id}$; the associativity pentagon for composable
$f,g$, compatible with the composition law (A4), i.e. the isomorphism
$\alpha_{g,f}:Rg_!Rf_!\cong R(gf)_!$ of [thm-sf-comp-composition]; independence of the chosen
compactification; the identification with the direct-image projection
formula through $Rf_!\cong Rf_*$ for proper $f$; compatibility with base
change, i.e. for a Cartesian square $(f',g',f,g)$ the square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
Lg^*\bigl(Rf_!K\otimes^L_\Lambda L\bigr)&\xrightarrow{\ Lg^*\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}\ }&
Lg^*Rf_!\bigl(K\otimes^L_\Lambda Lf^*L\bigr)\\
{\scriptstyle \operatorname{Ex}_!\otimes1}\downarrow&&\downarrow{\scriptstyle \operatorname{Ex}_!}\\
Rf'_!Lg'^*K\otimes^L_\Lambda Lg^*L&\xrightarrow{\ \operatorname{PF}_{f',Lg'^*K,Lg^*L}\ }&
Rf'_!\bigl(Lg'^*K\otimes^L_\Lambda Lf'^*Lg^*L\bigr)
\end{array}
$$

commutes, with $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ the exchange of axiom (A2) and the
vertical arrows read through the monoidality isomorphisms
$Lg^*(M\otimes^LN)\cong Lg^*M\otimes^LLg^*N$ and $Lg'^*Lf^*\cong Lf'^*Lg^*$
(the projection formula commutes with base change; SGA 4, XVII, §5.2); and
compatibility with finite reduction, scalar extension and the pro-étale
realization.

## Proof

All projection transformations appearing below are those of
[def-sf-pf].
Naturality is the naturality of the mate construction, which uses only the
natural units and counits of the axioms; for $f=\operatorname{id}$ the two
adjunctions are the identity adjunction and the mate of the identity is the
identity. The pentagon: both sides are mates of the same composite of the
two component mate constructions, because the units and counits of composite
adjunctions are the pasted ones by [fix-prop-adjunctions], item (3)
(through the composition isomorphism of [thm-sf-comp-composition]),
and pasting of mates is associative; the associativity of the derived tensor
product identifies the two tensor reassociations. Independence of the
compactification is the compatibility of the refinement comparisons with
the counits and with $j_!$, together with naturality. The proper case is
(A4). Compatibility with base change: choose a compactification
$f=p\circ j$ and base change it along $g$ to $f'=p'\circ j'$, with
$\bar g':\overline X'\to\overline X$ over $g$; by (A2) and (A4),
$\operatorname{Ex}_!$ is the identification $L\bar g'^*j_!\cong j'_!Lg'^*$
followed by the proper-base-change exchange $\operatorname{Ex}_*$ for $p$.
On the $j_!$ factor both composites take values in the essential image of
$j'_!$, where a map is determined by its restriction to $X'$, and both
restrict to the identity. On the $p$ factor, for $M$ on $\overline X$:
$\operatorname{PF}_{p,M,L}$ is the transpose under $Lp^*\dashv Rp_*$ of
$\varepsilon_p\otimes1$ ($\varepsilon_p$ the counit) read through the
monoidality of $Lp^*$, and $\operatorname{Ex}_*$ is the mate of
$L\bar g'^*Lp^*\cong Lp'^*Lg^*$ under $Lp^*\dashv Rp_*$ and
$Lp'^*\dashv Rp'_*$; transposing the two composites
$Lg^*(Rp_*M\otimes^LL)\to Rp'_*(L\bar g'^*M\otimes^LLp'^*Lg^*L)$ under
$Lp'^*\dashv Rp'_*$ gives, by the pasting compatibility of mates
([lem-sf-mate]) and the triangle identity for $p$, one and the same map
$Lp'^*Lg^*(Rp_*M\otimes^LL)\to L\bar g'^*M\otimes^LLp'^*Lg^*L$, namely
$L\bar g'^*\varepsilon_p\otimes1$ read through the monoidality isomorphisms;
so the two composites are mates of the same composite. The same computation
with an arbitrary $L'$ on $Y'$ in place of $Lg^*L$ identifies
$\operatorname{PF}_{p'}\circ(\operatorname{Ex}_*\otimes1)$ with the
transpose of $L\bar g'^*\varepsilon_p\otimes1$, which is the form used for
the symmetry of the relative product. The last clause is
[prop-sf-pf-reduction], [thm-sf-pf-field] and [thm-sf-pf-proetale].

In the setting of [def-sf-datum], let $m\le n$ and let
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A_{E,n})$, $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A_{E,n})$ with reductions
$K_m,L_m$. Then the square comparing $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}$ and
$\operatorname{PF}_{f,K_m,L_m}$ through the finite-reduction
compatibilities of $Rf_!$, $-\otimes^L$ and $Lf^*$ commutes; hence
$\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}$ is an isomorphism if and only if
$\operatorname{PF}_{f,K_m,L_m}$ is.

## Proof

Use the pullback and tensor comparisons of
[lem-fix-operation-reduction] and the compact-support comparison
of [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change]. Transpose both
routes around the reduction square for the projection transformation
of [def-sf-pf]. Each route pulls back the first factor, applies
the counit, and tensors with the reductions of the remaining factors.
Associativity of derived tensor and compatibility of that counit
with coefficient change identify these composites. Thus the square
commutes as a square of the specified maps. This argument does not
infer equality of morphisms merely from equality on geometric stalks.
Both horizontal maps are isomorphisms by [thm-sf-pf-finite];
in particular the asserted equivalence of invertibility holds.

Let $K$ be a characteristic-zero field, fix an indeterminate $T$, let
$I\subset\mathbf Z$ be finite, and let
$(V_i,u_i)_{i\in I}$ be a finite graded family of finite-dimensional vector
spaces and endomorphisms over $K$. Put

$$
P_i(T)=\det(1-Tu_i\mid V_i),
\qquad
\Delta(T)=\prod_iP_i(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}.
$$

Then, for every $i\in I$,

$$
-\log P_i(T)=
\sum_{n\geq1}\Tr(u_i^n\mid V_i)\frac{T^n}{n},
$$

and, with the displayed parity signs,

$$
\log\Delta(T)=
\sum_{n\geq1}\left(\sum_{i\in I}(-1)^i\Tr(u_i^n\mid V_i)\right)
\frac{T^n}{n}.
$$

For the geometric application, let $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, take
$I=\{0,\ldots,2d\}$, and use the
finite-field datum; fix a prime
$p$, an integer $a\geq1$, put $q=p^a$, and set
$k_0=\Fq$, and let $k=\Fbar$ be the fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$.
Choose a prime $\ell\neq p$, write
$\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and let
$X_0/k_0$ be smooth, proper,
geometrically connected of pure dimension $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$. Put
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, $V_i=H^i(X,\Ql)$, and $u_i=F_{i,\ell}$, where
$(V_{i,\ell},F_{i,\ell})$ is the
smooth-proper
cohomological family. The
point-count and zeta series and the
ordinary cohomology
construction give, after coefficient extension
$\mathbf Q[[T]]\to\Ql[[T]]$, the identity

$$
Z(X_0,T)=
\prod_{i=0}^{2d}P_{i,\ell}(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}.
$$

This identity belongs to $\Ql(T)\cap\Ql[[T]]$.

## Proof

Over an algebraic closure of $K$, let
$\lambda_{i,1},\ldots,\lambda_{i,n_i}$ denote the eigenvalues of
$u_i$, counted with algebraic multiplicity, where
$n_i=\dim_KV_i$. Then $P_i(T)=\prod_j(1-\lambda_{i,j}T)$ and, in the
ring of formal power series,

$$
-\log P_i(T)
=\sum_j\sum_{n\geq1}\lambda_{i,j}^n\frac{T^n}{n}
=\sum_{n\geq1}\operatorname{Tr}_K(u_i^n\mid V_i)\frac{T^n}{n},
$$

the last equality because the trace is the sum of the eigenvalues after
scalar extension. Summing over $i$ with the parity signs in
$\Delta(T)=\prod_iP_i(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}$ gives

$$
\log\Delta(T)=\sum_{n\geq1}\Bigl(\sum_{i\in I}(-1)^i
\operatorname{Tr}_K(u_i^n\mid V_i)\Bigr)\frac{T^n}{n},
$$

which proves the linear-algebra part of the statement.

For the geometric application, $Z(X_0,T)$ is the point-count zeta
series of [def-weil-point-counts-zeta], and by
[prop-every-iterate-trace] applied to the constant Weil sheaf on
the smooth proper geometrically connected $X_0$,

$$
N_n(X_0)=\sum_{i=0}^{2d}(-1)^i
\operatorname{Tr}_{\Ql}(F_{i,\ell}^n\mid V_{i,\ell})
$$

for every $n\geq1$, where $(V_{i,\ell},F_{i,\ell})$ is the
smooth-proper cohomological family of
[def-weil-smooth-proper-cohomological-family]. Hence
$\log Z(X_0,T)$ equals the logarithm of
$\prod_{i=0}^{2d}P_{i,\ell}(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}$ after the coefficient
extension $\mathbf Q[[T]]\to\Ql[[T]]$, and exponentiating gives the
displayed identity. Both sides are Taylor expansions of rational
functions, so the identity belongs to
$\Ql(T)\cap\Ql[[T]]$.

Fix the global finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ and the coefficient
conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], with
$A_n=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$ and $k_E=A_1$. Let $X_0$ be a separated
finite-type $k_0$-scheme, $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, $\Phi$ the $q$-power scheme
Frobenius, $g_\gamma$ the geometric-Frobenius automorphism and
$\kappa^{(m)}:L\Phi^{m*}\xrightarrow{\sim}Lg_\gamma^{m*}$ the comparison of
[prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison].

Let $K_\bullet=(K_n)_{n\geq1}$ be a normalized $A_\bullet$-system of
[def-trf-adic-system], $K_n\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A_n)$, with normalization
isomorphisms $\nu_n:K_{n+1}\otimes^L_{A_{n+1}}A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}K_n$; no
Weil structure is assumed. A *compatible system of Frobenius coefficient
morphisms* on $K_\bullet$ is a family of Frobenius coefficient morphisms
$\psi_n:L\Phi^*K_n\to K_n$ of [def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism]
such that
$$
\nu_n\circ(\psi_{n+1}\otimes^L_{A_{n+1}}A_n)=\psi_n\circ L\Phi^*(\nu_n)\circ\mu_n
\qquad(n\geq1),
$$
where $\mu_n:(L\Phi^*K_{n+1})\otimes^L_{A_{n+1}}A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}
L\Phi^*(K_{n+1}\otimes^L_{A_{n+1}}A_n)$ is the monoidality of pullback
([def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]); no invertibility is assumed.
Examples: the scheme-Frobenius maps $\varphi_n\circ\kappa_{K_n}$ of a system
with a strict Weil structure at every level, and the systems
$\psi_n=u_n\circ\kappa_{K_n}$ of [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model],
item (2), attached to a lattice $K_{\mathcal O}$ and a clearing of
denominators $\varphi_E=\varpi^{-N}u$.

Put, for a geometric point $\bar y$ of $X$,
$$
P_n=R\Gamma_c(X,K_n),\qquad P_{\bar y,n}=(K_n)_{\bar y},\qquad
P_{\mathcal O}=R\!\varprojlim_nP_n,\qquad
P_{\bar y,\mathcal O}=R\!\varprojlim_nP_{\bar y,n},
$$
the derived limits of [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit] of the towers
in $D(\mathcal O_E)$ (via the point identification of
[def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]) whose transition maps are the
composites $P_{n+1}\to P_{n+1}\otimes^L_{A_{n+1}}A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}P_n$ of
item (1) below, with projections $\mathrm{pr}_n$. If $K_\bullet$ is the
reduction tower $K_n=K_{\mathcal O}\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_n$ of an integral
object $K_{\mathcal O}$ ([def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed],
[def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]), then
$P_{\mathcal O}=R\Gamma_c(X,K_{\mathcal O})$ by
[def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] and
$P_{\bar y,\mathcal O}=L\bar y^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K_{\mathcal O}=:K_{\mathcal O,\bar y}$
is the completed stalk of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback].

Call a family $f_\bullet=(f_n)$ of endomorphisms $f_n$ of $P_n$
*compatible* if $f_n$ corresponds to $f_{n+1}\otimes^L_{A_{n+1}}A_n$ under
the isomorphisms of item (1), and call an endomorphism $V$ of $P_{\mathcal O}$
in $D(\mathcal O_E)$ a *lift* of $f_\bullet$ if
$\pi_n\circ(V\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_n)=f_n\circ\pi_n$ for all $n$, where
$\pi_n:P_{\mathcal O}\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_n\to P_n$ is the
$A_n$-linear map adjoint to $\mathrm{pr}_n$; likewise for the stalks. Then:

1. *Levelwise perfectness and normalization.* Each $P_n$ and $P_{\bar y,n}$ lies
in $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A_n)$, and $\nu_n$ induces isomorphisms
$P_{n+1}\otimes^L_{A_{n+1}}A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}P_n$ and
$P_{\bar y,n+1}\otimes^L_{A_{n+1}}A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{\bar y,n}$.
1. *Integral realization and lifts.* $P_{\mathcal O}$ and
$P_{\bar y,\mathcal O}$ are represented by bounded complexes of finite free
$\mathcal O_E$-modules, and every $\pi_n$ is an isomorphism. Every
compatible family of endomorphisms has a lift, and every $V$ with
$\mathrm{pr}_n\circ V=f_n\circ\mathrm{pr}_n$ for all $n$ (for instance the
derived limit of a morphism of towers) is a lift of $f_\bullet$.
1. *Compatibility of the Frobenius operators.* For every $m\geq1$ the global
operators $F_{c,m}(\psi_n)=T_{c_m}(\psi_{n,m})$ of
[def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism] form a compatible family on
$(P_n)$, and for $y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ with geometric point $\bar y$
the stalk endomorphisms $\psi_{n,m,\bar y}=(\psi_{n,m})_{\bar y}\circ\iota_{K_n}$
(normalized as in [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model]) form a
compatible family on $(P_{\bar y,n})$.
1. *Traces.* If $V$ lifts the compatible family $f_\bullet$, then the
categorical trace $\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}(V\mid P_{\mathcal O})$
reduces modulo $\varpi^n$ to $\operatorname{tr}_{A_n}(f_n\mid P_n)$ for
every $n$; hence
$$
\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}(V\mid P_{\mathcal O})
=\bigl(\operatorname{tr}_{A_n}(f_n\mid P_n)\bigr)_n\in\varprojlim_nA_n=\mathcal O_E,
$$
independently of the lift. In particular the elements
$\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}\bigl(F_{c,m}(\psi_\bullet)\mid P_{\mathcal O}\bigr)$
and
$\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}\bigl(\psi_{\bullet,m,\bar y}\mid P_{\bar y,\mathcal O}\bigr)$,
the traces of any lifts of the families of item (3), are well defined.

Here $\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}$ is the categorical trace of
[def-trf-categorical-trace] formed over the commutative ring
$\mathcal O_E$, with the duality data of [lem-trf-chain-supertrace].

## Proof

*(1).* Each $K_n$ lies in $D^b_{ctf}(X,A_n)$, so $P_n$ and $P_{\bar y,n}$ are
perfect by [prop-trf-compact-support-perfectness]. The finite-level
coefficient change of [thm-trf-finite-coefficient-map] for
$\rho:A_{n+1}\to A_n$ and $f=a_X:X\to\Spec k$ (its compact-support
isomorphism is the coefficient comparison of
[lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change]), followed by $R\Gamma_c(X,\nu_n)$,
gives $P_{n+1}\otimes^L A_n\cong R\Gamma_c(X,K_{n+1}\otimes^LA_n)\cong P_n$;
for the stalks, its pullback isomorphism for $\bar y$ ($L\bar y^*$ is a
pullback, hence monoidal, [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]) gives
$P_{\bar y,n+1}\otimes^LA_n\cong(K_{n+1}\otimes^LA_n)_{\bar y}\cong P_{\bar y,n}$.

*(2).* We prove the assertion for an arbitrary tower $(Q_n)$ of objects
$Q_n\in D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A_n)$ with isomorphisms
$\theta_n:Q_{n+1}\otimes^L_{A_{n+1}}A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_n$, the transition
maps being $Q_{n+1}\to Q_{n+1}\otimes^LA_n\xrightarrow{\theta_n}Q_n$; by (1)
this applies to $(P_n)$ and to $(P_{\bar y,n})$.

*Minimal models.* By [def-trf-categorical-trace] each $Q_n$ is a bounded
complex $M$ of finite projective, hence free, modules over the local ring
$A_n$. If some differential satisfies $d^i\otimes k_E\neq0$, pick
$e\in M^i$ with $f=d^ie\notin\varpi M^{i+1}$; by Nakayama $f$ is part of a
basis, $M^{i+1}=A_nf\oplus D'$ with $D'$ free, and $A_ne\cong A_n$
(as $ae=0$ forces $af=0$). Put
$C=(d^i)^{-1}(D')$. Writing $d^ix=af+d'$ one has $x-ae\in C$, so
$M^i=A_ne\oplus C$; if $d^ix=0$ then $af\in D'$, so $a=0$ and
$\ker d^i\subset C$; in particular $d^{i-1}(M^{i-1})\subset C$, and $C$, a
direct summand of a free module over a local ring, is free. Since $d^{i+1}f=0$, the complex $M$ is the direct sum of
the contractible complex $A_ne\xrightarrow{\sim}A_nf$ and of the complex
$\cdots\to M^{i-1}\to C\to D'\to M^{i+2}\to\cdots$ of finite free modules.
Discarding the contractible summand lowers the total rank, so after finitely
many steps $Q_n$ is represented by a *minimal* complex, i.e. one with
$d\otimes k_E=0$. A quasi-isomorphism $\alpha:M\to M'$ between minimal
complexes is an isomorphism of complexes: $\alpha\otimes k_E$ is a
quasi-isomorphism between complexes with zero differential, hence bijective
in each degree, and by Nakayama each $\alpha^i$ is a surjection between free
modules of the same finite rank, hence bijective. Morphisms in $D(A_n)$
between bounded complexes of projectives are homotopy classes of chain maps.

*Strictification.* Choose a minimal model $\chi_1:M_1\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_1$.
Given a minimal $\chi_n:M_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_n$, choose a minimal model
$\chi':M'\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_{n+1}$. The isomorphism
$\chi_n^{-1}\circ\theta_n\circ(\chi'\otimes A_n):M'\otimes A_n\to M_n$ in
$D(A_n)$ is represented by a chain map $\alpha$ between minimal complexes,
hence by an isomorphism of complexes; so $M'^i$ and $M_n^i$ have the same
rank $r_i$. In bases, each $\alpha^i\in\mathrm{GL}_{r_i}(A_n)$; lift it to
$\beta^i\in\mathrm{GL}_{r_i}(A_{n+1})$ (a lift of an invertible matrix over
a local ring is invertible) and let $M_{n+1}$ be $M'$ with the differential
transported by $\beta$. Then $\beta:M'\to M_{n+1}$ is an isomorphism of
complexes, $M_{n+1}\otimes A_n=M_n$ as complexes because $\alpha$ is a chain
map, and $\chi_{n+1}=\chi'\circ\beta^{-1}$ satisfies
$\theta_n\circ(\chi_{n+1}\otimes A_n)=\chi_n$. Under the $\chi_n$ the
transition maps become the reduction maps $\rho_n:M_{n+1}\to M_n$, which are
surjective in each degree.

*Limit.* Put $M=\varprojlim_nM_n$ degreewise: a bounded complex with
$M^i\cong\mathcal O_E^{r_i}$ and $M/\varpi^n=M_n$. The sequence
$0\to M\to\prod_nM_n\xrightarrow{1-\rho}\prod_nM_n\to0$ is exact in each
degree (given $(y_n)$, choose $x_1$ and inductively $x_{n+1}$ lifting
$x_n-y_n$), so it gives a distinguished triangle; products in the derived
category are computed termwise ([def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit]), so this
is the Roos triangle of the tower, and $R\varprojlim_nQ_n\cong M$ compatibly
with the maps to $\prod_nQ_n$. Thus $\mathrm{pr}_n$ is $\chi_n$ composed with
the projection $M\to M_n$, and its adjoint
$\pi_n:M\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_n=M/\varpi^n\to M_n\xrightarrow{\chi_n}Q_n$
is an isomorphism.

*Lifts.* Transport a compatible family along the $\chi_n$. Then
$f_n=[g_n]\in H^0\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(M_n,M_n)$ with
$[\rho(g_{n+1})]=[g_n]$, and
$\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(M,M)=\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(M_n,M_n)$
with surjective transitions (matrices over $\mathcal O_E$ modulo $\varpi^n$).
Choose representatives inductively: if $\rho(g'_{n+1})=g_n+dh_n$, lift $h_n$
to $h'_{n+1}$ and replace $g'_{n+1}$ by $g_{n+1}=g'_{n+1}-dh'_{n+1}$, a
cocycle in the same class with $\rho(g_{n+1})=g_n$. Then $V=(g_n)_n$ is a
chain endomorphism of $M$ with $V\otimes A_n=g_n$, i.e. a lift. Finally, if
$\mathrm{pr}_n\circ V=f_n\circ\mathrm{pr}_n$, then $\pi_n\circ(V\otimes A_n)$
and $f_n\circ\pi_n$ are both adjoint to this map under the adjunction between
$-\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_n$ and restriction of scalars, so they are equal.

*(3).* The iterates are compatible: by induction on $m$, using the recursion
of [def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism], the monoidality isomorphisms
$\mu$ and their compatibility with the composition isomorphisms of pullback
([def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]), $\psi_{n+1,m}\otimes A_n$
corresponds to $\psi_{n,m}$. The comparison $\kappa^{(m)}$ is natural and
compatible with the coefficient reductions, as shown in the proof of item (2)
of [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model]; hence
$v_n=\psi_{n,m}\circ(\kappa^{(m)}_{K_n})^{-1}:Lg_\gamma^{m*}K_n\to K_n$
satisfy $v_{n+1}\otimes A_n=v_n$ under $\nu_n$. By the general clause of
[prop-trf-graph-frobenius-operator], which allows non-invertible $v$,
$$
F_{c,m}(\psi_n)=T_{c_m}(v_n\circ\kappa^{(m)}_{K_n})
=R\Gamma_c(X,v_n)\circ g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}.
$$
The coefficient comparison of [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change]
is natural in the complex and compatible with pullback, hence with the
base-change isomorphisms $g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}$; so $F_{c,m}(\psi_{n+1})\otimes A_n$
corresponds to $F_{c,m}(\psi_n)$ under the isomorphism of (1). For the stalks,
$\iota_{K_n}$ is built from composition isomorphisms of pullback for
$\Phi^m\circ\bar y=\bar y$, and $L\bar y^*$ is monoidal; hence
$\psi_{n+1,m,\bar y}\otimes A_n$ corresponds to $\psi_{n,m,\bar y}$.

*(4).* Represent $P_{\mathcal O}$ by $M$ as in (2) and $V$ by a chain map.
By [lem-trf-chain-supertrace], over $\mathcal O_E$ and over $A_n$,
$\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}(V\mid M)=\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(V^i\mid M^i)$,
whose reduction modulo $\varpi^n$ is
$\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(V^i\bmod\varpi^n\mid M_n)=\operatorname{tr}_{A_n}(V\otimes A_n\mid M_n)$
(equivalently, item (3) of [prop-trf-trace-formal-laws]). Since $\pi_n$
conjugates $V\otimes A_n$ into $f_n$, conjugacy invariance
([prop-trf-trace-formal-laws], item (1)) gives
$\operatorname{tr}_{A_n}(V\otimes A_n)=\operatorname{tr}_{A_n}(f_n\mid P_n)$.
As $\mathcal O_E$ is $\varpi$-adically complete and separated,
$\mathcal O_E\to\varprojlim_nA_n$ is an isomorphism, which gives the displayed
formula and its independence of the lift. The last sentence combines this
with (2) and (3).

attrs.title: Adic realization for systems of Frobenius coefficient morphisms

objects.body:
Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions, and let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ with structure morphism
$a_X:X\to\Spec k$ separated finite type. Then

$$
R\Gamma_c(X,K)\in D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A),
$$

and the derived geometric stalk $K_{\bar x}=L\bar x^*K$ lies in
$D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$ for every
geometric point
$\bar x$ of $X$.

## Proof

Let $C=R\Gamma_c(X,K)$, with compact support as in
[def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], [def-trf-coefficient-conventions].
The finite-level constructibility theorem
[prop-finite-compact-support-constructibility] gives a bounded
complex on $\operatorname{Spec}k$ with finite cohomology modules,
using the point identification of
[def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. This assertion alone does
not give perfectness over the finite local ring $A$.

Put $\kappa=A/(\varpi_E)$. The narrow coefficient-change result
[lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change], applied to
$A_{E,n}\to A_{E,1}=\kappa$, identifies

$$
C\otimes_A^L\kappa
\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_c(X,K\otimes_A^L\kappa).
$$

The input on the right is bounded constructible: finite Tor amplitude
gives boundedness, and its cohomology is constructible by restricting
to a finite constructible stratification and taking the derived
tensor of the finite coefficient modules, as in
[def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility].
Hence the right side is bounded by
[prop-finite-compact-support-constructibility] at the residue
coefficient stage. The residue-field criterion of
[lem-exc-residue-tor-test], applied on the point, now proves
that $C$ has finite Tor amplitude. Together with its finite
cohomology, [lem-trf-finite-tor-amplitude-perfect] shows that
$C$ is represented by a bounded complex of finite free
$A$-modules.

For $K_{\bar x}$, the exact inverse-image property
[prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact] and the finite-stalk
condition of [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] give
bounded finite cohomology. The tensor-vanishing definition
[def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] is preserved by this inverse
image, so the same module-theoretic perfectness criterion applies.
Thus both objects lie in the perfect category used for categorical
trace in [def-trf-categorical-trace].
No preservation of finite Tor amplitude by a package summary is used
in this argument.

*Recorded in advance* from chapter *The trace formula* of the source.

For $i=1,2$, let $f_i:X_i\to Y_i$ be morphisms of separated
finite-type schemes satisfying the
exceptional-adjoint admissibility of
[def-trf-admissibility], and let $L_i\in D^b_{ctf}(Y_i,A)$. The
canonical comparison of [def-sf-kv-maps] (ii), formed with the geometric operations,

$$
\alpha:f_1^!L_1\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L} f_2^!L_2
\longrightarrow
(f_1\times f_2)^!\bigl(L_1\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L} L_2\bigr)
$$

is an isomorphism, natural in the $L_i$.

## Proof

First, shriek Kunneth: by $!$-base change and the projection formula
for the exceptional adjoint pair of [def-trf-admissibility], the
comparison

$$
(f_1\times f_2)_!\bigl(f_1^!L_1\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L} f_2^!L_2\bigr)
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
(f_1)_!f_1^!L_1\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}(f_2)_!f_2^!L_2
$$

is invertible. Evaluating it on the $f_i^!L_i$ and composing with the
two exceptional counits of [def-trf-admissibility] produces a map
to $L_1\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}L_2$; the exceptional adjoint of this
composite defines $\alpha$.

It remains to see that $\alpha$ is invertible. For a constant auxiliary
coefficient, smooth maps are handled by smooth purity with compatibility
of the smooth trace under base change [thm-pur-affine-line-purity],
and closed immersions by localization together with the
open-product base change, which is the case $Q=\underline A_Z$ of
[lem-trf-ordinary-kunneth]. An affine factorization of a general
$f_i$ into a closed immersion followed by a smooth projection
therefore gives the local case. This settles constant coefficients
$L_i=\underline A_{Y_i}$, and by additivity finite free ones.

Lisse coefficients. If $L_i$ is lisse with flat stalks, invertibility of
$\alpha$ is étale-local on $Y_1\times Y_2$: for an étale $u$ one has
$u^!=u^*$, so by the composition isomorphism of exceptional inverse images
([lem-sf-mate]) $f^!$ commutes with étale pullback, compatibly with
$\alpha$. On a finite étale cover trivializing the $L_i$ they become finite
free, the case above. This is a local reduction, not a dévissage: lisse
coefficients cannot be replaced by constant ones globally
([lem-trf-devissage-generation]).

General coefficients. Argue by induction on
$\delta=\dim\operatorname{supp}L_1+\dim\operatorname{supp}L_2$; the claim is
trivial if some $L_i=0$. Both sides of $\alpha$ are exact in each $L_i$, so
the two-out-of-three property [lem-sf-triangle-two-out-of-three] applies to
distinguished triangles in either variable.

Closed pushforward. Let $g_1:Z_1\hookrightarrow Y_1$ be a closed immersion,
with $g_1':X_1\times_{Y_1}Z_1\hookrightarrow X_1$ and
$f_1':X_1\times_{Y_1}Z_1\to Z_1$ the projections. The dual base change
$f_1^!Rg_{1*}\cong Rg'_{1*}f_1'^!$ (the mate of the $!$-base change,
[lem-sf-mate]) and the identity-factor Künneth
$Rg_{1*}M_1\boxtimes L_2\cong R(g_1\times\mathrm{id})_*(M_1\boxtimes L_2)$
of [lem-trf-ordinary-kunneth] identify $\alpha_f(Rg_{1*}M_1,L_2)$ with
$R(g_1'\times\mathrm{id})_*\,\alpha_{f_1'\times f_2}(M_1,L_2)$, compatibly
with the definition of $\alpha$ as an exceptional adjoint (a mate-calculus
check); likewise in the second variable. Since $L_i\cong Rg_{i*}g_i^*L_i$
for $Z_i=\operatorname{supp}L_i$ (the open–closed triangle
[prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages], as $L_i$ vanishes on the
complement), we may assume $\dim Y_i=\dim\operatorname{supp}L_i$. Then by
the generation [lem-trf-devissage-generation] on $Y_i$ it suffices to treat
the generators $L_i=Rg_{i*}j_{i!}F_i$ with $F_i$ lisse with flat stalks on a
stratum $U_i$ dense in $\overline U_i$, $\dim\overline U_i\le\dim Y_i$, and
by the closed pushforward just described we may take $\overline U_i=Y_i$,
$L_i=j_{i!}F_i$.

Open localization. The functor $f^!$ does not commute with $j_!$, so pass
through $Rj_*$. For the open immersion $j=j_1\times j_2$ with base changes
$j'$ and $f'$, the dual base change $f^!Rj_*\cong Rj'_*f'^!$ (the mate of
the base change for $j_!$) and [lem-trf-ordinary-kunneth], which gives
$Rj_{1*}F_1\boxtimes Rj_{2*}F_2\cong Rj_*(F_1\boxtimes F_2)$ and
$Rj'_{1*}f_1'^!F_1\boxtimes Rj'_{2*}f_2'^!F_2\cong
Rj'_*(f_1'^!F_1\boxtimes f_2'^!F_2)$, identify
$\alpha_f(Rj_{1*}F_1,Rj_{2*}F_2)$ with $Rj'_*\,\alpha_{f'}(F_1,F_2)$,
compatibly with $\alpha$ as before; the latter is the lisse case already
treated, so $\alpha$ is invertible on $(Rj_{1*}F_1,Rj_{2*}F_2)$. The
open–closed triangle [prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages] for
$M=Rj_{i*}F_i$ reads $j_{i!}F_i\to Rj_{i*}F_i\to T_i\xrightarrow{+1}$ with
$T_i=i_{i*}i_i^*Rj_{i*}F_i\in D^b_{ctf}(Y_i,A)$ ([thm-sf-ctf-stability]), a
general object of $D^b_{ctf}$ supported on the boundary
$Z_i=Y_i\setminus U_i$, of dimension $<\dim Y_i$. By the induction
hypothesis $\alpha$ is invertible on $(T_1,j_{2!}F_2)$ and on
$(Rj_{1*}F_1,T_2)$, the support dimensions having dropped; two-out-of-three
in the second variable gives $(Rj_{1*}F_1,j_{2!}F_2)$, and then in the first
variable $(j_{1!}F_1,j_{2!}F_2)$. Thus $\alpha$ is an isomorphism.

For $i=1,2$, let $E_i\in D^b_{ctf}(X_i,A)$ and $L_i\in D^b_{ctf}(X_i,A)$ on separated finite-type $X_i$, with the
admissibility of [def-trf-admissibility] where $!$-pullbacks
occur. The evaluation-defined comparison of [def-sf-kv-maps] (iii)

$$
\beta:\RHom_A(E_1,L_1)\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}\RHom_A(E_2,L_2)
\longrightarrow
\RHom_A\bigl(E_1\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}E_2,\,
L_1\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}L_2\bigr)
$$

is an isomorphism, natural in all four variables.

## Proof

Both sides are exact in each $E_i$, so devissage in both $E_i$ by the
generation [lem-trf-devissage-generation] (generators $Rg_*j_!F$ with $F$ lisse with flat stalks on a
stratum) reduces to $E_i=Rh_{i!}F_i$, where $h_i=g_ij_i$ with $g_i$ finite
and $j_i$ open, and $F_i$ is lisse on $U_i$ with flat stalks. The stalks of
$F_i$ are finite flat, hence free, over the local ring $A$, so $F_i$ is
locally finite free, hence perfect, and [prop-sf-dualizable-hom] gives
$\RHom_A(F_i,-)\simeq F_i^\vee\otimes^{\mathrm L}_A-$. The tensor–Hom
and exceptional adjunctions ([lem-sf-tensor-hom]) give

$$
\RHom_A(E_i,L_i)\simeq Rh_{i*}\RHom_A(F_i,h_i^!L_i)
\simeq Rh_{i*}\bigl(F_i^\vee\otimes^{\mathrm L}_Ah_i^!L_i\bigr).
$$

Writing $h=h_1\times h_2$ and $F=F_1\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}F_2$, so that
$F^\vee\simeq F_1^\vee\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}F_2^\vee$ and
$E_1\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}E_2\simeq Rh_!F$ by the $!$-Kunneth map, the
comparison becomes

$$
Rh_{1*}\bigl(F_1^\vee\otimes h_1^!L_1\bigr)\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}
Rh_{2*}\bigl(F_2^\vee\otimes h_2^!L_2\bigr)
\xrightarrow[\text{twice}]{\mathrm{Ku}_*}
Rh_*\bigl(F^\vee\otimes(h_1^!L_1\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}h_2^!L_2)\bigr)
\xrightarrow{Rh_*(1\otimes\alpha)}
Rh_*\bigl(F^\vee\otimes h^!(L_1\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}L_2)\bigr),
$$

whose target is $\RHom_A(E_1\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}E_2,L_1\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}L_2)$
by the same identifications;
the first arrow being [lem-trf-ordinary-kunneth] applied in each
factor (after the symmetry of the tensor product), and the second the exceptional Kunneth
[prop-trf-exceptional-kunneth]. To identify this composite with the
specified $\beta$, take ordinary and then exceptional adjoints: both
paths become the tensor product of the two evaluation maps after the
projection formula. Hence $\beta$ itself is an isomorphism.

Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions, $A=A_{E,n}$, put $s=\Spec k$, and let
$c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times_sX$ be a
cohomological correspondence with
fixed scheme
$F=\operatorname{Fix}(c)$ of [def-trf-fixed-scheme] and projections
$i_F:F\to C$, $d:F\to X$. Then the square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
F & \xrightarrow{i_F} & C\\
{\scriptstyle d}\downarrow & & \downarrow{\scriptstyle c}\\
X & \xrightarrow{\Delta_X} & X\times_sX
\end{array}
$$

is Cartesian, the composites
$c_1i_F$ and $c_2i_F$ both equal $d$, and the identity
$\Delta_Xd=ci_F$ holds. Moreover the composition law for the
exceptional inverse image gives

$$
Rd^!\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Ri_F^!Rc_1^!
$$

(the adjoint form of the composition law $R(c_1i_F)_!\cong Rc_{1!}Ri_{F!}$ of [thm-sf-comp-composition],
as $d=c_1i_F$); it is the only unconditional "!"-transport of the two
legs in the fixed square, see also the remark below.

## Proof

By [def-trf-fixed-scheme], $F$ is the fiber product
$C\times_{X\times_sX,c,\Delta_X}X$, which is precisely the assertion that
the square is Cartesian. The composites $c_1i_F$ and $c_2i_F$ are the
projections $p_1,p_2:X\times_sX\to X$ applied to the identity
$\Delta_Xd=ci_F$ of [def-trf-fixed-scheme], hence both equal $d$;
the identity $\Delta_Xd=ci_F$ is part of the fiber-product data. The
last displayed isomorphism is the composition law for the exceptional
inverse image of [def-trf-admissibility] applied to the equality
$d=c_1i_F$ in the form
$R(c_1i_F)^!=Ri_F^!Rc_1^!$.

For every $m\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, the absolute $q^m$-power Frobenius
$\operatorname{Fr}^{(q^m)}_X:X\to X$, $a\otimes b\mapsto a^{q^m}\otimes b^{q^m}$, factors as

$$
\operatorname{Fr}^{(q^m)}_X=g_\sigma{}^m\Phi^m=\Phi^mg_\sigma{}^m.
$$

## Proof

By [def-trf-scheme-frobenius] all three morphisms are $k_0$-maps
of the geometric fiber whose affine incarnations are the $q^m$-th power
map on the $A_0$-factor, the $q^m$-th power map on the $\bar k$-factor, or their composition, in either order; thus both composites
equal $\operatorname{Fr}^{(q^m)}_X$.

*Recorded in advance* from chapter *The trace formula* of the source.

Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions, and let $(K,\varphi)$ be a
strict Weil complex of
[def-trf-strict-weil-complex]. For $m\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$ let
$\Phi^m$ be the $m$-fold iterate of the
scheme Frobenius of
[def-trf-scheme-frobenius] and
$u_m:L\Phi^{m*}K\to K$ the
scheme-Frobenius map of
[def-trf-iterated-weil-map], and consider the
graph correspondence
$c=(\operatorname{id}_X,\Phi^m)$ with $u_m$. Then its
global operator $T_c(u_m)$ of
[def-trf-global-operator], identified as in
[prop-trf-graph-operator], equals the $m$-th iterate of the
global geometric Frobenius:

$$
T_c(u_m)=F_{c,K}^{\,m}:
R\Gamma_c(X,K)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_c(X,K),
$$

where $F_{c,K}^{\,m}$ is the endomorphism of the
global geometric Frobenius
operator of [def-trf-frobenius-operators] (equivalently the
global geometric Frobenius action of
[def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius]). The equality is natural in
$(K,\varphi)$ and compatible with the cocycle law in $m$.

More generally, let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ carry no Weil structure and
let $v:Lg_\gamma^{m*}K\to K$ be an arbitrary morphism, not necessarily
invertible. Then the graph correspondence $c=(\operatorname{id}_X,\Phi^m)$
with coefficient map $v\circ\kappa^{(m)}_K:L\Phi^{m*}K\to K$ has

$$
T_c\bigl(v\circ\kappa^{(m)}_K\bigr)
=R\Gamma_c(X,v)\circ g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}:
R\Gamma_c(X,K)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_c(X,K),
$$

where $g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}:R\Gamma_c(X,K)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_c(X,Lg_\gamma^{m*}K)$
is the compact-support base-change isomorphism along $g_\gamma^m$; the
displayed identity $T_c(u_m)=F_{c,K}^{\,m}$ is the case $v=\varphi^{[m]}$.

## Proof

By [prop-trf-graph-operator] applied to $h=\Phi^m$ (finite,
hence proper, by [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]) and to $v=u_m$,
the operator $T_c(u_m)$ is the composite

$$
R\Gamma_c(X,K)\xrightarrow{\ \eta_{\Phi^m}\ }
R\Gamma_c(X,L\Phi^{m*}K)\xrightarrow{R\Gamma_c(X,u_m)}R\Gamma_c(X,K),
$$

where $\eta_{\Phi^m}$ is the unit of
$L\Phi^{m*}\dashv R\Phi^{m}_*$ composed with the identification
$R\Phi^{m}_*\cong R\Phi^{m}_!$ and the composition law for the
compact-support direct image ([def-trf-global-operator],
[prop-trf-graph-operator], [prop-functor-package],
item (3)).

*Step 1: the identification of the functors and of the units.*
As $L\Phi^{m*}$ and $Lg_\gamma^{m*}$ are left adjoints to
$R\Phi^{m}_*$ and $Rg_\gamma^{m,*}$, respectively, with the
adjunction data of (the derived direct image of)
[prop-functor-package], and as
[prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison] supplies the natural isomorphism

$$
\kappa^{(m)}:L\Phi^{m*}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Lg_\gamma^{m*},
$$

the mate lemma [lem-trf-adjoint-mate] supplies the canonical
natural isomorphism

$$
\beta:R\Phi^{m}_*\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rg_\gamma^{m,*}
$$

(unique subject to the unit and counit compatibilities, by (3) of
[lem-trf-adjoint-mate]), together with the unit compatibility
in the form

$$
Rg_\gamma^{m,*}\kappa^{(m)}\circ\beta L\Phi^{m*}\circ\eta_{\Phi^m}
=\eta_{\gamma^m},
$$

where $\eta_{\gamma^m}$ is the unit of
$Lg_\gamma^{m*}\dashv Rg_\gamma^{m,*}$. Hence the *transported
unit* of $T_c(u_m)$ is the geometric-Frobenius unit, and the diagram

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
R\Gamma_c(X,K) & \xrightarrow{\ \eta_{\Phi^m}\ }
& R\Gamma_c(X,L\Phi^{m*}K)\\
& & \ \ \downarrow{\scriptstyle R\Gamma_c(X,\kappa^{(m)})}\\
& & R\Gamma_c(X,Lg_\gamma^{m*}K)
\end{array}
$$

commutes with the corresponding composite starting from
$\eta_{\gamma^m}$ after the identification of the targets along
$R\Gamma_c(X,R\Phi^{m}_*L\Phi^{m*}K)\cong R\Gamma_c(X,Rg_\gamma^{m,*}Lg_\gamma^{m*}K)$ supplied by $\beta$.

*Step 2: identification with the compact-support base change.*
The composite

$$
R\Gamma_c(X,K)\xrightarrow{\ \eta_{\gamma^m}\ }
R\Gamma_c(X,Rg_\gamma^{m,*}Lg_\gamma^{m*}K)
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }R\Gamma_c(X,Lg_\gamma^{m*}K)
$$

(the identification $Rg_\gamma^{m,*}\cong Rg_\gamma^{m,!}$ for the
proper, indeed finite, automorphism $g_\gamma^m$ together with the
compact-support composition law) is, by the construction of
[def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius], the first arrow of the
compact-support base-change identification $g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}$
(the exchange $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ of
[def-exchange-projection] along the automorphism $g_\gamma^m$,
composed with the canonical identification of the compact-support
cohomology of an isomorphism-fixed scheme and the naturality of
$R\Gamma_c$); and the compatibility of this exchange with the
adjunction data and with the identifications of Step 1 is part of the
adjunction-compatibility and coherence records of the package
([def-exchange-projection] and [prop-functor-package]).
Therefore the first arrow of the composite defining $T_c(u_m)$ equals
the arrow $g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}$, and the last arrow is
$R\Gamma_c(X,\varphi^{[m]})\circ R\Gamma_c(X,\kappa^{(m)})$,
whence

$$
T_c(u_m)=R\Gamma_c(X,\varphi^{[m]})\circ g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}
=F_{c,K}^{\,m}
$$

by [lem-trf-frobenius-operator-compact-description], where
$F_{c,K}^{\,m}$ is the $m$-th iterate of the global geometric
Frobenius of [def-trf-frobenius-operators] and
$\varphi^{[m]}$ is the iterated Weil isomorphism of
[def-trf-iterated-weil-map]. Naturality in $(K,\varphi)$ is
the naturality of $\kappa^{(m)}$ of [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison]
and of the base-change identification. The compatibility with the
cocycle law in $m$: for $m,n\geq1$, the base-change identifications
along the automorphisms compose as

$$
g_{\gamma,c}^{m+n,*}
=\bigl(g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}\bigr)_{Lg_\gamma^{n*}K}\circ g_{\gamma,c}^{n,*}
$$

(transitivity of the compact-support base change, from
$g_\gamma^{m+n}=g_\gamma^m\circ g_\gamma^n$), and the base-change
identification is natural in the coefficient complex, so by the cocycle
identity $\varphi^{[m+n]}=\varphi^{[m]}\circ Lg_\gamma^{m*}\varphi^{[n]}$
of [lem-trf-iterated-weil-cocycle] one has

$$
\begin{aligned}
F_{c,K}^{\,m+n}
&=R\Gamma_c(X,\varphi^{[m+n]})\circ g_{\gamma,c}^{m+n,*}\\
&=R\Gamma_c(X,\varphi^{[m]})\circ R\Gamma_c(X,Lg_\gamma^{m*}\varphi^{[n]})
\circ\bigl(g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}\bigr)_{Lg_\gamma^{n*}K}\circ g_{\gamma,c}^{n,*}\\
&=R\Gamma_c(X,\varphi^{[m]})\circ g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}
\circ R\Gamma_c(X,\varphi^{[n]})\circ g_{\gamma,c}^{n,*}
=F_{c,K}^{\,m}\circ F_{c,K}^{\,n},
\end{aligned}
$$

which is the claimed cocycle compatibility (the third equality uses the
naturality of $g^{m,*}$ in the coefficient complex; multiplicativity of
the $\kappa^{(m)\,}$s of [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison]
transports the same identity to the scheme-Frobenius side).

*Step 3: general coefficient maps.* Steps 1 and 2 concern only the
object $K$ and the functors $L\Phi^{m*}$, $Lg_\gamma^{m*}$, $R\Gamma_c$:
neither the Weil structure $\varphi$ nor any inverse of a coefficient map
enters them. For an arbitrary $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ they give that the
composite

$$
R\Gamma_c(X,K)\xrightarrow{\ \eta_{\Phi^m}\ }R\Gamma_c(X,L\Phi^{m*}K)
\xrightarrow{R\Gamma_c(X,\kappa^{(m)}_K)}R\Gamma_c(X,Lg_\gamma^{m*}K)
$$

is $g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}$. For $v:Lg_\gamma^{m*}K\to K$ arbitrary,
[prop-trf-graph-operator] applied to $h=\Phi^m$ and to the coefficient
map $v\circ\kappa^{(m)}_K$, together with functoriality of
$R\Gamma_c(X,-)$, gives

$$
T_c\bigl(v\circ\kappa^{(m)}_K\bigr)
=R\Gamma_c(X,v)\circ R\Gamma_c(X,\kappa^{(m)}_K)\circ\eta_{\Phi^m}
=R\Gamma_c(X,v)\circ g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*},
$$

which is the general assertion; for $v=\varphi^{[m]}$ it is the identity
$T_c(u_m)=F_{c,K}^{\,m}$ proved above.

attrs.title: Graph construction of the global Frobenius operator

objects.body:
Let $(h,v)$ be a graph correspondence with $h$ proper. The global
operator $T_c(v)$ of [def-trf-global-operator] is the composite

$$
R\Gamma_c(X,K)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_c(X,Lh^*K)
\xrightarrow{R\Gamma_c(X,v)}R\Gamma_c(X,K),
$$

where the first arrow is induced by the unit
$K\to Rh_*Lh^*K$ and the canonical identification
$Rh_*\simeq Rh_!$. It is functorial in $(K,v)$, additive in
distinguished triangles, and compatible with composition of proper
endomorphisms.

## Proof

For the graph correspondence $c_1=\operatorname{id}_X$ and $c_2=h$,
the display of [def-trf-global-operator] reads

$$
\begin{aligned}
R\Gamma_c(X,K)&\xrightarrow{\eta^*_h}
R\Gamma_c(X,Rh_*Lh^*K)
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }R\Gamma_c(X,Lh^*K)\\
&\xrightarrow{R\Gamma_c(X,v)}
R\Gamma_c(X,K),
\end{aligned}
$$

where the second arrow is the identification of
[def-weil-derived-direct-image] for the proper $h$
($Rh_*\simeq Rh_!$ composed with the compact-support direct-image
identification of [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]), and the
last arrow is the counit of the identity adjunction. This is the
displayed composite. Functoriality, additivity over triangles, and
compatibility with composition are the corresponding properties of the
unit-counit calculus, of $R\Gamma_c$, and of the identifications
quoted above.

attrs.title: Graph construction of the global operator

objects.body:
Fix the global finite-field datum
and the joint conventions of [def-trf-karoubi-trace]. Let
$(E,K)$ and $(F,L)$ represent the same object of
$D^b_c(X,\Qlb)$ with $K\in D^b_c(X,E)$, $L\in D^b_c(X,F)$. After
passage to a common finite overfield $M$ of $E$ and $F$, the two
transported objects become isomorphic, and the
summand traces of compatible
endomorphisms agree; the same holds for the competing Frobenius
endomorphisms and their iterates, and the comparisons are transitive.
Consequently the trace formula of [thm-trf-trace-formula-e] is
independent of the finite field of definition and of the
representative.

## Proof

The equality of the two representatives in the common-stage category
[def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] gives, after scalar extension to a
common field, an isomorphism of the transported perfect complexes under
which compatible idempotents and endomorphisms are transported; by the
conjugacy invariance and scalar-extension law of the categorical trace
[prop-trf-trace-formal-laws], the summand traces
[def-trf-karoubi-trace] agree and depend only
on the isomorphism class of the summand. Naturality in the
endomorphism and transitivity of the comparison follow from these two
laws of [prop-trf-trace-formal-laws], applied to the transporting
isomorphism; the Frobenius endomorphisms are transported by this
isomorphism, by the definition of the objects and morphisms of the
common-stage category of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category].

attrs.title: Representative independence of the summand trace

objects.body:
Let $(C,c,u)$, $(D,d,v)$ be an opposite pair of cohomological
correspondences as in [def-trf-supported-pairing], with intersection
support $E=E(C,D)$ (the fiber product of the two supports of
[def-trf-correspondence-between-pairs]) and Borel–Moore section
$\langle u,v\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}:A_E\to\omega_{E,A}$. Suppose that
$E$ is a finite disjoint union

$$
E=\coprod_{\beta\in B}\beta
$$

of open-and-closed subschemes $j_\beta:\beta\hookrightarrow E$, each
proper over $s$. For $\beta\in B$ let
$\langle u,v\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}|_\beta:=j_\beta^*\langle u,v\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}:A_\beta\to\omega_{\beta,A}$
be the restricted pairing and

$$
\LT_\beta(u,v)=\int_\beta\bigl(\langle u,v\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}|_\beta\bigr)\in A
$$

the local term of the pair on $\beta$, both as in
[def-trf-local-term-pair]; the restricted pairing is the restriction
of [lem-trf-integration-component-sum] (both are the composite
$A_\beta\simeq Lj_\beta^*A_E\to Lj_\beta^*\omega_{E,A}\cong\omega_{\beta,A}$),
and for $v=1_K$ and $\beta\subseteq\Fix(c)$ the local term is
$\LT_\beta(u)$ of [def-trf-local-term]. Then $E$ is proper over $s$ and

$$
\int_E\langle u,v\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}
=\sum_{\beta\in B}\LT_\beta(u,v).
$$

If $E=\emptyset$ both sides are $0$. Moreover, for a perfect
$A$-complex $P$ on $s$ and an endomorphism $w:P\to P$, regarded as an
endocorrespondence with support $s$ (whose sole component is $s$),

$$
\LT_s(w)=\LT_s(w,1_P)=\tr_A(w\mid P).
$$

## Proof

Apply [lem-trf-integration-component-sum] to $T=E$, the finite
decomposition $E=\coprod_{\beta\in B}\beta$ and
$\tau=\langle u,v\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}$: it shows that $E$ is proper
over $s$, so that $\int_E$ of [def-trf-integration] is defined, and
that

$$
\int_E\langle u,v\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}
=\sum_{\beta\in B}\int_\beta\bigl(\langle u,v\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}|_\beta\bigr)
=\sum_{\beta\in B}\LT_\beta(u,v),
$$

the last equality being the definition of the local terms in
[def-trf-local-term-pair]; for
$E=\emptyset$ the lemma gives $0=0$. When $v=1_K$, so that
$\langle u,1_K\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}=\Tr_c(u)$ by
[lem-trf-trace-class-diagonal-pairing], the restriction to a component
$\beta\subseteq\Fix(c)$ is the composite used in [def-trf-local-term],
whence $\LT_\beta(u,1_K)=\LT_\beta(u)$, as also recorded in
[def-trf-local-term-pair].

For the point case, $E=s$, $B=\{s\}$, and $j_s$ and the structure map
$a_s$ are identities. Then $\omega_{s,A}=Ra_s^!A=A$ by
[def-trf-dualizing-complex], the restriction to the sole component is
the section itself, and both adjunction maps in [def-trf-integration]
(the unit of $La_s^*\dashv Ra_{s*}$ and the counit of
$Ra_{s!}\dashv Ra_s^!$) are identities, so $\int_s$ is the
identification $\Hom_{D(s,A)}(A,A)=A$. Hence
$\LT_s(w,1_P)=\langle w,1_P\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}$, which equals
$\tr_A(1_P\circ w\mid P)=\tr_A(w\mid P)$ by the point normalization
[prop-trf-pairing-point-normalization].

attrs.title: Decomposition of the pairing into local terms

objects.body:
Let $P,Q$ be perfect $A$-complexes on $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and
let $u:P\to Q$, $v:Q\to P$, both regarded as correspondences with
support $s$. The
supported pairing satisfies

$$
\langle u,v\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}=\tr_A(vu\mid P),
$$

where the right-hand side is the
ordinary categorical trace.

## Proof

The supported-class bijection of
[def-trf-correspondence], followed by the Kunneth–Verdier
isomorphism [thm-trf-kunneth-verdier], turns $u$ at a point into
$(u\otimes1)\operatorname{coev}_P:A\to Q\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}P^\vee$, and
similarly for $v$. In the recipe of
[def-trf-supported-pairing], contraction of these two classes cancels
the adjacent evaluation–coevaluation pair by a triangle identity. What
remains is precisely the composite defining the categorical trace of
[def-trf-categorical-trace], with endomorphism $vu$; the graded
signs are fixed by the formal laws [prop-trf-trace-formal-laws].
This proves the normalization.

The same adjunction calculation identifies the *diagonal
specialization* on any $X$: if $f:\Fix(c)\to X$ is the canonical map,
its exceptional adjoint is

$$
Rf_!A_{\Fix(c)}\simeq\Delta^*Rc_!A_C
\xrightarrow{\Delta^*\widetilde u}K\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}D_XK
\xrightarrow{\mathrm{ev}\circ\mathrm{sym}}\omega_X .
$$

Indeed, under the tensor–Hom adjunction and biduality ([thm-trf-verdier-biduality]) of
[def-trf-dualizing-complex], the class of the diagonal identity maps
to $1_K$, and the supported cup product reduces by the projection
formula and $!$-base change to the displayed composite. This is the
classical trace-class dictionary used by the proper-comparison input on
the specific representatives.

Fix the global finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ and the coefficient
conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], with $E$, $\mathcal O_E$,
a uniformizer $\varpi=\varpi_E$ and $A_n=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$.
Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$,
$g_\gamma$ the geometric-Frobenius automorphism and $\Phi$ the $q$-power
scheme Frobenius of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius], and $\kappa^{(m)}$ the
comparison isomorphisms of [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison].

Let $K_{\mathcal O}\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ be an integral object
([def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]) whose reductions
$K_n=K_{\mathcal O}\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_n$ lie in $D^b_{ctf}(X,A_n)$,
and let $K_E$ be the same object of the rationalized category
$D^b_c(X,E)=D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)[1/\varpi]$ of
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] (so $K_{\mathcal O}$ is a lattice of
$K_E$). Let

$$
\varphi_E:Lg_\gamma^*K_E\longrightarrow K_E
$$

be an arbitrary morphism of $D^b_c(X,E)$ (for instance the Weil
structure of an $E$-Weil complex, [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]); no
invertibility, and no invertibility on any lattice, is assumed.

*$E$-stage operators.* All functors below at the stage $E$ are the
rationalizations, by [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport], of the
integral ones: the pullbacks $Lg_\gamma^{i*}$ with their composition
isomorphisms, $R\Gamma_c(X,-)$ of
[def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], the compact-support
base-change isomorphisms $g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}$ along the automorphisms
$g_\gamma^m$, and the stalk functors with the stalk transports
$\tau_{y,m}$ of [def-trf-frobenius-operators]. Put
$\varphi_E^{[m]}=\varphi_E\circ Lg_\gamma^*\varphi_E\circ\cdots\circ
L(g_\gamma^{m-1})^*\varphi_E:Lg_\gamma^{m*}K_E\to K_E$, as in
[def-trf-iterated-weil-map], and define, by the formulas of
[def-trf-frobenius-operators] in the form of
[lem-trf-frobenius-operator-compact-description],

$$
F_{c,K_E}^{\,m}=R\Gamma_c(X,\varphi_E^{[m]})\circ g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*},
\qquad
F_{y,m}=\varphi^{[m]}_{E,\bar y}\circ\tau_{y,m}
$$

on $R\Gamma_c(X,K_E)$ and on $K_{E,\bar y}$, for $m\geq1$ and
$y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ with geometric point $\bar y$. For $m=1$ and
invertible $\varphi_E$ the first is the compactly supported operator of
[def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius].

*Stalk normalization.* For $y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ one has
$\Phi^m\circ\bar y=\bar y$ ([thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points]), whence a
natural identification $\iota_M:M_{\bar y}\cong(L\Phi^{m*}M)_{\bar y}$
for every $M$; as throughout, the stalk transport of
[def-trf-frobenius-operators] is taken in the form
$\tau_{y,m}=(\kappa^{(m)}_M)_{\bar y}\circ\iota_M$, natural in $M$ and
defined with no Weil structure on $M$, at every finite level $A_n$ (this
is the normalization under which the stalk map of the scheme-Frobenius
map $u_m$ of [def-trf-iterated-weil-map] is $F_{y,m}$). On integral
objects $\tau_{y,m}$ is the derived limit of these levelwise isomorphisms
on the reduction tower, and at the stage $E$ its rationalization. For a
Frobenius coefficient morphism $\psi$ on $K_n$ with iterates $\psi_m$,
the stalk endomorphism of $K_{n,\bar y}$ is
$\psi_{m,\bar y}=(\psi_m)_{\bar y}\circ\iota_{K_n}$, as in the
coefficient-morphism trace formula of the trace-formula chapter.

Then:

1. *Clearing denominators.* There are an integer $N\geq0$ and a morphism
$u:Lg_\gamma^*K_{\mathcal O}\to K_{\mathcal O}$ of
$D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ with $\varphi_E=\varpi^{-N}u$ in
$D^b_c(X,E)$; that is, $\varpi^N\varphi_E$ maps the lattice into itself.
1. *Integral Frobenius coefficient morphisms.* For such $(N,u)$ let
$u_n:Lg_\gamma^*K_n\to K_n$ be the reduction of $u$ modulo $\varpi^n$
and put
$$
\psi_n=u_n\circ\kappa_{K_n}:L\Phi^*K_n\longrightarrow K_n .
$$
Each $\psi_n$ is a Frobenius coefficient morphism on $K_n$ in the sense
of [def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism] (in general not
invertible), the $\psi_n$ are compatible with the transitions
$K_{n+1}\otimes^L_{A_{n+1}}A_n\cong K_n$, and the iterates are
$$
\psi_{n,m}=u_n^{[m]}\circ\kappa^{(m)}_{K_n},\qquad
u_n^{[m]}=u_n\circ Lg_\gamma^*u_n\circ\cdots\circ L(g_\gamma^{m-1})^*u_n .
$$
1. *Global operator.* For every $n,m\geq1$,
$$
F_{c,m}(\psi_n)=T_{c_m}(\psi_{n,m})
=R\Gamma_c(X,u_n^{[m]})\circ g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}
\quad\text{on }R\Gamma_c(X,K_n).
$$
Let $U_m=R\Gamma_c(X,u^{[m]})\circ g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}$ be the integral
endomorphism of $R\Gamma_c(X,K_{\mathcal O})=R\varprojlim_nR\Gamma_c(X,K_n)$;
it is the derived limit of the levelwise operators $F_{c,m}(\psi_n)$
(the realization of the graph operators $T_{c_m}(\psi_{n,m})$), and
$$
\boxed{\,F_{c,K_E}^{\,m}=\varpi^{-Nm}\,\bigl(U_m\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E\bigr)
\quad\text{on }R\Gamma_c(X,K_E)=R\Gamma_c(X,K_{\mathcal O})\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E.\,}
$$
1. *Local operators.* For $y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ the stalk
endomorphism of $\psi_{n,m}$ is $\psi_{n,m,\bar y}=u^{[m]}_{n,\bar y}\circ\tau_{y,m}$
on $K_{n,\bar y}$; the integral endomorphism
$U_{y,m}=u^{[m]}_{\bar y}\circ\tau_{y,m}$ of $K_{\mathcal O,\bar y}$
reduces modulo $\varpi^n$ to $\psi_{n,m,\bar y}$, and
$$
\boxed{\,F_{y,m}=\varpi^{-Nm}\,\bigl(U_{y,m}\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E\bigr)
\quad\text{on }K_{E,\bar y}=K_{\mathcal O,\bar y}\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E.\,}
$$

Replacing $(N,u)$ by $(N+1,\varpi u)$ multiplies $U_m,U_{y,m}$ by
$\varpi^m$ and leaves the right-hand sides unchanged. *Example:* for
$X_0=\Spec\mathbf F_q$, $K_E=E^2$ and $\varphi_E=\operatorname{diag}(1,\ell)$,
one may take $N=0$ and $u=\operatorname{diag}(1,\ell)$ on
$\mathcal O_E^2$; no rescaling $c\,\varphi_E$ ($c\in E^\times$) is invertible
on any lattice, since its eigenvalues $c,c\ell$ are not both units, but
$\psi_n=u\bmod\varpi^n$ is a (non-invertible) Frobenius coefficient
morphism.

## Proof

*(1).* By [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] the morphisms of
$D^b_c(X,E)$ are
$\operatorname{Hom}_{D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)}(Lg_\gamma^*K_{\mathcal O},K_{\mathcal O})\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$,
the rationalized pullback being that of the integral one
([prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport]). Since $E=\mathcal O_E[1/\varpi]$,
every element of $H\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E=H[1/\varpi]$, for an
$\mathcal O_E$-module $H$, has the form $u\otimes\varpi^{-N}$ with
$u\in H$ and $N\geq0$. This is $\varphi_E=\varpi^{-N}u$.

*(2).* The reduction $u_n$ is the $n$-th evaluation of the morphism of
towers attached to $u$ by the functorial reduction tower of
[def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], using
$(Lg_\gamma^*K_{\mathcal O})\otimes^L A_n\cong Lg_\gamma^*K_n$: since
$g_\gamma$ is an automorphism, $Lg_\gamma^*$ is an exact monoidal
equivalence fixing the constant coefficient sheaves
([def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]), so it commutes with the
reductions and with the transitions. Hence the $u_n$ are compatible with
the transitions. The isomorphism $\kappa$ of
[prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison] is composed of the functoriality of
pullback for $\Phi=g_\gamma F_X^{(q)}$ and the trivialization of
absolute-Frobenius pullback of [lem-trf-absolute-frobenius-site], which is
induced on the pro-etale site itself; both are natural in the object and
compatible with the monoidal reduction $-\otimes^L_{A_{n+1}}A_n$.
Therefore $\psi_n=u_n\circ\kappa_{K_n}$ is a morphism
$L\Phi^*K_n\to K_n$, i.e. a Frobenius coefficient morphism, and the
$\psi_n$ are compatible with the transitions.

For the iterates argue by induction on $m$, the case $m=1$ being the
definition. Suppressing the composition isomorphisms of pullback (they
are part of both recursive definitions), the recursion of
[def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism] and the induction hypothesis
give

$$
\psi_{n,m}=\psi_n\circ L\Phi^*\psi_{n,m-1}
=u_n\circ\kappa_{K_n}\circ L\Phi^*\bigl(u_n^{[m-1]}\bigr)\circ
L\Phi^*\bigl(\kappa^{(m-1)}_{K_n}\bigr).
$$

Naturality of $\kappa$ applied to
$u_n^{[m-1]}:Lg_\gamma^{(m-1)*}K_n\to K_n$ gives
$\kappa_{K_n}\circ L\Phi^*(u_n^{[m-1]})
=Lg_\gamma^*(u_n^{[m-1]})\circ\kappa_{Lg_\gamma^{(m-1)*}K_n}$, and the
multiplicativity of the iterates in [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison],
for $m=1+(m-1)$, gives
$\kappa_{Lg_\gamma^{(m-1)*}K_n}\circ L\Phi^*(\kappa^{(m-1)}_{K_n})
=\kappa^{(m)}_{K_n}$. Hence
$\psi_{n,m}=u_n\circ Lg_\gamma^*(u_n^{[m-1]})\circ\kappa^{(m)}_{K_n}
=u_n^{[m]}\circ\kappa^{(m)}_{K_n}$.

*(3).* The first equality is the definition of $F_{c,m}(\psi_n)$ in
[def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism]. By (2),
$\psi_{n,m}=v\circ\kappa^{(m)}_{K_n}$ with $v=u_n^{[m]}$, and the general
clause of [prop-trf-graph-frobenius-operator], which allows an arbitrary,
not necessarily invertible $v$ and no Weil structure on $K_n$, gives
$T_{c_m}(\psi_{n,m})=R\Gamma_c(X,u_n^{[m]})\circ g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}$.

By [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support],
$R\Gamma_c(X,-)$ on $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ is the derived limit of the
levelwise compact-support cohomology of the reduction tower of
[def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]; on morphisms it is the derived
limit of the levelwise maps. The integral morphism $u^{[m]}$ (formed from
$u$ by the integral pullbacks) has reductions $u_n^{[m]}$, because
$Lg_\gamma^{i*}$ commutes with the reductions as in (2); and the integral
base-change isomorphism $g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}$ is the derived limit of the
levelwise ones, the pullback $Lg_\gamma^{m*}$ carrying the reduction tower
of $K_{\mathcal O}$ to that of $Lg_\gamma^{m*}K_{\mathcal O}$. Hence
$U_m$ is the derived limit of the levelwise composites
$R\Gamma_c(X,u_n^{[m]})\circ g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}=F_{c,m}(\psi_n)$.

At the stage $E$, $R\Gamma_c(X,K_E)=R\Gamma_c(X,K_{\mathcal O})\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$
([def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]), and every
rationalized functor or natural transformation acts on
$\operatorname{Hom}\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$ by $f\otimes\lambda\mapsto
F(f)\otimes\lambda$ ([prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport]); composition in
$D^b_c(X,E)$ is $E$-bilinear. Hence
$L(g_\gamma^{i})^*\varphi_E=\varpi^{-N}\,L(g_\gamma^{i})^*u$ for each $i$,
the composition isomorphisms are those of the integral pullbacks, and

$$
\varphi_E^{[m]}=\prod_{i=0}^{m-1}\varpi^{-N}\cdot
\bigl(u\circ Lg_\gamma^*u\circ\cdots\circ L(g_\gamma^{m-1})^*u\bigr)
=\varpi^{-Nm}u^{[m]}.
$$

Applying the $E$-linear map induced by the rationalized $R\Gamma_c(X,-)$
and composing with the rationalization of the integral
$g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}$ gives
$F_{c,K_E}^{\,m}=\varpi^{-Nm}\bigl(R\Gamma_c(X,u^{[m]})\circ g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}\bigr)\otimes E
=\varpi^{-Nm}(U_m\otimes E)$.

*(4).* By the stalk normalization and (2),
$\psi_{n,m,\bar y}=(u_n^{[m]})_{\bar y}\circ(\kappa^{(m)}_{K_n})_{\bar y}\circ\iota_{K_n}
=u^{[m]}_{n,\bar y}\circ\tau_{y,m}$. The stalk functor $L\bar y^*$ is a
pullback, hence monoidal and compatible with the reductions
([def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]), and $\tau_{y,m}$ is natural and
compatible with the reductions by the same argument as for $\kappa$ in
(2), its integral form being the derived limit of the levelwise ones; so
$U_{y,m}=u^{[m]}_{\bar y}\circ\tau_{y,m}$ reduces modulo
$\varpi^n$ to $u^{[m]}_{n,\bar y}\circ\tau_{y,m}=\psi_{n,m,\bar y}$. At
the stage $E$, the stalk of $K_E$ is $K_{\mathcal O,\bar y}\otimes E$ and,
exactly as in (3), $\varphi^{[m]}_{E,\bar y}=\varpi^{-Nm}(u^{[m]}_{\bar y}\otimes E)$,
whence $F_{y,m}=\varphi^{[m]}_{E,\bar y}\circ\tau_{y,m}
=\varpi^{-Nm}(U_{y,m}\otimes E)$.

The remark on $(N+1,\varpi u)$ is $(\varpi u)^{[m]}=\varpi^mu^{[m]}$, by
$\mathcal O_E$-linearity of the pullbacks. In the example, identify the
coefficient categories of $X=\Spec k$ with complexes of modules, so that
$u=\operatorname{diag}(1,\ell)$ is an endomorphism of the lattice
$\mathcal O_E^2$. If $c\,\varphi_E$ were an automorphism of some lattice
$L\subset E^2$, then its characteristic polynomial and that of its inverse
would have coefficients in $\mathcal O_E$, so its eigenvalues $c$ and
$c\ell$ would both be units of the integral closure of $\mathcal O_E$;
then so would be their quotient $\ell$, which is absurd.

attrs.title: Integral models of rational Frobenius operators

objects.body:
Fix the global finite-field datum
$p,a,q,k_0,k$, where $q=p^a$, let $X_0$ be a
finite-type $k_0$-scheme,
put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $A$ be a finite commutative ring
annihilated by an integer invertible in $k$. The $q$-power scheme
Frobenius $\Phi$ and the
geometric-Frobenius automorphism
$g_\gamma$ of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius] induce, on the
small pro-etale site of $X$,
natural isomorphisms of derived categories

$$
\kappa:L\Phi^*\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Lg_\gamma^*,
$$

and, for every $m\geq1$, a multiplicative iterate

$$
\kappa^{(m)}:L\Phi^m{}^*\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Lg_\gamma^{m*}.
$$

The isomorphisms are compatible with the factorization of
[prop-trf-frobenius-factorization]: scheme Frobenius and geometric
Galois Frobenius differ by a universal homeomorphism, namely the
absolute $q$-power Frobenius. (Source: the comparison between
geometric and arithmetic Frobenius, via the invariance of
the etale site under universal homeomorphisms, is the terminal interface
of the trace-formula chapter.)

## Proof

Write $F_X^{(q)}$ for absolute $q$-power Frobenius.
The canonical trivialization of
[lem-trf-absolute-frobenius-site], iterated $a$ times, gives
$L(F_X^{(q)})^*\simeq\operatorname{id}$.
The factorization [prop-trf-frobenius-factorization] gives
$\Phi=g_\gamma F_X^{(q)}$, where $g_\gamma=g_\sigma^{-1}$
as in [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. Thus functoriality of pullback
and this specified trivialization give

$$
L\Phi^*=L(F_X^{(q)})^*Lg_\gamma^*
\xrightarrow{\sim}Lg_\gamma^*.
$$

This defines $\kappa$. For $\Phi^m=g_\gamma^mF_X^{(q^m)}$ the
same construction is the multiplicative iterate $\kappa^{(m)}$:
