the relative Frobenius maps compose to the corresponding power maps.
The resulting identifications therefore respect both the
factorization and addition of the exponents.

*Recorded in advance* from chapter *The trace formula* of the source.

attrs.title: Comparison of scheme and Galois pullbacks

objects.body:
Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient conventions, $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $X_0$ be a
separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, let $i_0:Z_0\hookrightarrow X_0$
be a closed immersion with complementary open immersion
$j_0:U_0\hookrightarrow X_0$, and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$,
$j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be their base changes to $k$. Let
$(K,\varphi)\in D^b_{ctf,\mathrm W}(X,A)$ be a strict Weil complex
of [def-trf-strict-weil-complex].

1. For $h\in\{i,j\}$ with source $W\in\{Z,U\}$, one has
$h\,g_W=g_X\,h$, and the composite
$$
h^*\varphi:\;
Lg_W^*Lh^*K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Lh^*Lg_X^*K
\xrightarrow{\ Lh^*\varphi\ }Lh^*K
$$
of the canonical pullback identification with $Lh^*\varphi$ makes
$(Lh^*K,h^*\varphi)$ a strict Weil complex on $W$; its iterates of
[def-trf-iterated-weil-map] are
$(h^*\varphi)^{[m]}=Lh^*\varphi^{[m]}\circ c_{h,m}$, with
$c_{h,m}:Lg_W^{m*}Lh^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh^*Lg_X^{m*}$ the canonical
identification.
1. For every $m\geq1$, with $F_{c,-}^{\,m}$ the global geometric
Frobenius operators of [def-trf-frobenius-operators] for these
Weil structures,
$$
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(F_{c,K}^{\,m}\mid R\Gamma_c(X,K)\bigr)
=
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(F_{c,j^*K}^{\,m}\mid R\Gamma_c(U,j^*K)\bigr)
+
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(F_{c,i^*K}^{\,m}\mid R\Gamma_c(Z,i^*K)\bigr)
$$
in $A$. These are categorical traces of perfect complexes in the
sense of [def-trf-categorical-trace]; no trace of an individual
cohomology module occurs.
1. *(Frobenius coefficient morphisms.)* Let instead
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ carry an arbitrary Frobenius coefficient
morphism $\psi:L\Phi_X^*K\to K$ of
[def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism], with no Weil structure and no
invertibility. For $h\in\{i,j\}$ with source $W$ one has
$h\,\Phi_W=\Phi_X\,h$, the composite
$h^*\psi:L\Phi_W^*Lh^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh^*L\Phi_X^*K
\xrightarrow{Lh^*\psi}Lh^*K$ is a Frobenius coefficient morphism on
$W$ with iterates $(h^*\psi)_m=Lh^*\psi_m\circ c'_{h,m}$, where
$c'_{h,m}:L\Phi_W^{m*}Lh^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh^*L\Phi_X^{m*}$ is the
canonical identification, and for every $m\geq1$ the global operators
$F_{c,m}$ of [def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism] satisfy
$$
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(F_{c,m}(\psi)\mid R\Gamma_c(X,K)\bigr)
=
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(F_{c,m}(j^*\psi)\mid R\Gamma_c(U,j^*K)\bigr)
+
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(F_{c,m}(i^*\psi)\mid R\Gamma_c(Z,i^*K)\bigr).
$$

The proof below uses the Weil maps only as morphisms: the
invertibility of $\varphi$ is used only to stay inside the category
$D^b_{ctf,\mathrm W}$ on which $F_{c,-}^{\,m}$ is defined.

## Proof

*Step 1: restricted Weil structures.* Write
$g_X=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ and
likewise for $U,Z$. The automorphism $g_X$ maps $U=U_0\times_{k_0}k$
and $Z=Z_0\times_{k_0}k$ onto themselves, with restrictions $g_U$ and
$g_Z$. For the open square this is
[lem-trf-frobenius-open-square]; for the closed square the same
argument applies, since the inverse image of the closed subscheme
$Z$ under the isomorphism $g_X$ is the closed subscheme
$Z_0\times_{k_0}k$ with its restricted structure sheaf. Hence
$h\,g_W=g_X\,h$ and both squares are Cartesian. The complexes
$Lh^*K$ lie in $D^b_{ctf}(W,A)$ by [thm-sf-ctf-stability](i),
and $h^*\varphi$ is a composite of two isomorphisms, so
$(Lh^*K,h^*\varphi)$ is a strict Weil complex. The iterate formula
follows by induction on $m$ from the product formula of
[def-trf-iterated-weil-map]: the inductive step is naturality of
the pullback identifications in the coefficient together with their
cocycle law for the composite $g_X^{m+1}=g_X\circ g_X^m$.

*Step 2: the triangle is Frobenius-compatible.* Fix $m\geq1$, write
$g=g_X^m$ and $\psi_K=\varphi^{[m]}:Lg^*K\to K$. For the other two
vertices of the open–closed triangle of
[prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages],

$$
j_!j^*K\xrightarrow{\ \varepsilon\ }K\xrightarrow{\ \eta\ }
i_*i^*K\xrightarrow{\ \delta\ }j_!j^*K[1],
$$

put
$\psi_U=j_!(j^*\varphi)^{[m]}\circ b_g:Lg^*j_!j^*K\to j_!j^*K$ (the $m$-th iterate of the Weil extension by zero [def-trf-weil-extension-zero] of $(j^*K,j^*\varphi)$), with
$b_g$ the open-square exchange of [lem-trf-open-square-exchange],
and $\psi_Z=i_*(i^*\varphi)^{[m]}\circ e_g:Lg^*i_*i^*K\to i_*i^*K$,
with $e_g:Lg^*i_*\xrightarrow{\sim}i_*Lg_Z^{m*}$ the proper
base-change isomorphism for the closed immersion $i$
([prop-functor-package], clause (4)).

(a) $\varepsilon\circ\psi_U=\psi_K\circ Lg^*\varepsilon$. Both sides
are maps $Lg^*j_!j^*K\cong j_!Lg_U^{m*}j^*K\to K$, the identification
being $b_g$. By the adjunction $j_!\dashv j^*$ of
[prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions] it suffices to
compare their restrictions to $U$. There $b_g$ is the identity
([lem-trf-open-square-exchange]) and $j^*\varepsilon$ is the
identity after the unit identification, so both restrictions equal
$j^*\varphi^{[m]}\circ c_{j,m}=(j^*\varphi)^{[m]}$, by Step 1.

(b) $\psi_Z\circ Lg^*\eta=\eta\circ\psi_K$. Both sides are maps
$Lg^*K\to i_*i^*K$. By the adjunction $i^*\dashv i_*$ of
[prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions] it suffices to
compare the adjoint maps $i^*Lg^*K\to i^*K$. Since $e_g$ is the
exchange of the Cartesian closed square, its adjoint is the
canonical identification $c_{i,m}$, and the counit $i^*i_*\to\mathrm{id}$
is an isomorphism; both adjoints therefore equal
$i^*\varphi^{[m]}\circ c_{i,m}=(i^*\varphi)^{[m]}$, by Step 1.

(c) $\psi_U[1]\circ Lg^*\delta=\delta\circ\psi_Z$. The functor
$Lg^*$ is exact, so the image of the triangle under $Lg^*$ is
distinguished. By (a) and (b), the pair $(\psi_U,\psi_K)$ is
compatible with the first arrows; by the axiom of morphisms of
triangles there is $\psi':Lg^*i_*i^*K\to i_*i^*K$ with
$\psi'\circ Lg^*\eta=\eta\circ\psi_K$ and
$\delta\circ\psi'=\psi_U[1]\circ Lg^*\delta$. Then
$(\psi'-\psi_Z)\circ Lg^*\eta=0$ by (b), so $\psi'-\psi_Z$ factors
as $d\circ Lg^*\delta$ with $d:Lg^*j_!j^*K[1]\to i_*i^*K$. Via
$b_g$ the source of $d$ is $j_!N[1]$ with $N=Lg_U^{m*}j^*K$, and
$\operatorname{Hom}(j_!N[1],i_*i^*K)=\operatorname{Hom}(N[1],j^*i_*i^*K)=0$
since $j^*i_*=0$ ([prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions],
as in the Hom vanishing of
[prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages]). Hence $\psi'=\psi_Z$,
proving (c). Invertibility of the $\psi$ was not used.

*Step 3: an endomorphism of a triangle of perfect complexes.* By
[lem-trf-frobenius-operator-compact-description],
$F_{c,K}^{\,m}=R\Gamma_c(X,\psi_K)\circ g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}$, where
$g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}:R\Gamma_c(X,-)\to R\Gamma_c(X,Lg^*-)$ is the
compact-support base change along the automorphism $g$ of the
Cartesian square over $g_s^m$. This exchange is a natural
transformation between exact functors, natural in the coefficient
([fix-lem-exchanges], (1)), and it commutes with the connecting
morphisms because it is built from units, counits and pullback
identifications of exact functors. Applying the exact functor
$R\Gamma_c(X,-)$ to the triangle and using Step 2, the three
endomorphisms

$$
E_V=R\Gamma_c(X,\psi_V)\circ g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*},
\qquad V\in\{j_!j^*K,\;K,\;i_*i^*K\},
$$

(with $\psi_{j_!j^*K}=\psi_U$, $\psi_{i_*i^*K}=\psi_Z$) form an
endomorphism of the distinguished triangle

$$
R\Gamma_c(X,j_!j^*K)\to R\Gamma_c(X,K)\to R\Gamma_c(X,i_*i^*K)\to .
$$

More precisely, they form an endomorphism of this triangle *of filtered
origin*: the open–closed triangle is the cofibre sequence of the inclusion
$j_!j^*K\to K$, a two-step filtered object with graded pieces $j_!j^*K$ and
$i_*i^*K$; the maps $\psi_U,\psi_K,\psi_Z$ are the components of one
endomorphism of this filtered object (Step 2 exhibits $\psi_U$ as the
restriction of $\psi_K$ to the subobject and $\psi_Z$ as the induced map on
the quotient, with the identifications $b_g$, $e_g$ natural in the
coefficient); and $R\Gamma_c(X,-)\circ g^{m,*}_{\gamma,c}$ is a natural
transformation of exact functors, so it carries this filtered endomorphism
to an endomorphism of the two-step filtered perfect complex
$R\Gamma_c(X,j_!j^*K)\subset R\Gamma_c(X,K)$ in the filtered derived
category $DF(A)$. This filtered origin is what Step 5 uses; an endomorphism
of the distinguished triangle in the plain derived category, with its three
squares commuting only up to unspecified homotopies, would not suffice
([prop-trf-trace-formal-laws], item (2)).

*Step 4: identification with the operators on $U$ and $Z$.* By the
composition law and $Ri_!=Ri_*$ for the proper $i$
([prop-functor-package], clause (3)),
$R\Gamma_c(X,j_!-)\cong R\Gamma_c(U,-)$ and
$R\Gamma_c(X,i_*-)\cong R\Gamma_c(Z,-)$. Under these identifications
the compact-support base change $g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}$ on $X$, followed
by $b_g$ resp. $e_g$, is the compact-support base change on $U$
resp. $Z$ along $g_U^m$ resp. $g_Z^m$: this is the pasting law of
[fix-lem-exchanges], (2), for the Cartesian squares
$W\to X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ over $g_W^m,g,g_s^m$, together with
its compatibility with the composition law, [fix-lem-exchanges], (4);
for $j$ the exchange of the inner square is $b_g$ by construction of
$\operatorname{Ex}_!$ via extension by zero, for $i$ it is $e_g$
because $i$ is proper. Hence, by
[lem-trf-frobenius-operator-compact-description] on $U$ and $Z$ and
Step 1, $E_{j_!j^*K}$ is conjugate to $F_{c,j^*K}^{\,m}$ and
$E_{i_*i^*K}$ to $F_{c,i^*K}^{\,m}$, and $E_K=F_{c,K}^{\,m}$.

*Step 5: traces.* All three complexes are perfect by
[prop-trf-compact-support-perfectness], applied to
$K$, $j^*K$ and $i^*K$, which lie in $D^b_{ctf}$ by Step 1.
Filtered additivity [prop-trf-trace-formal-laws](2) applied to
the filtered endomorphism of Step 3 gives
$\operatorname{tr}_A(E_K)=\operatorname{tr}_A(E_{j_!j^*K})+\operatorname{tr}_A(E_{i_*i^*K})$,
and conjugacy invariance [prop-trf-trace-formal-laws](1) together
with Step 4 converts the right-hand side to the traces on
$R\Gamma_c(U,j^*K)$ and $R\Gamma_c(Z,i^*K)$. This is the asserted
identity.

*Step 6: Frobenius coefficient morphisms (item 3).* Repeat Steps 1–5
with the automorphism $g=g_X^m$ replaced by the finite morphism
$\Phi=\Phi_X^m$ and $\psi_K=\varphi^{[m]}$ replaced by the iterate
$\psi_m$, with the following changes. In Step 1, $\Phi_X$ is the base
change of the absolute Frobenius of $X_0$ ([def-trf-scheme-frobenius]),
which commutes with every morphism, so $h\Phi_W=\Phi_Xh$; the formula
for the iterates of $h^*\psi$ follows by induction on $m$ from the
recursion of [def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism], exactly as the
iterate formula of Step 1. The open square is Cartesian by
[lem-trf-frobenius-open-square]. The closed square $i\Phi_Z^m=\Phi i$
need not be Cartesian, since $\Phi^{-1}(Z)$ may be a nilpotent
thickening of $Z$; in Step 2 replace $e_g$ by the ordinary base-change
morphism $e:L\Phi^*Ri_*\to Ri_*L\Phi_Z^{m*}$ of this commutative square
(unit of $L\Phi_Z^{m*}\dashv R\Phi^m_{Z*}$ followed by the counit of
$i^*\dashv Ri_*$, as in [def-exchange-projection]). Its adjoint is again
the canonical identification $c'_{i,m}$, and it is an isomorphism on
every geometric stalk: $\Phi$ is a universal homeomorphism with
$\Phi^{-1}(Z)=Z$ as sets, so both sides have stalk $N_{\Phi(\bar z)}$ at
$\bar z\in Z$ and stalk $0$ off $Z$. With these substitutions the
arguments (a)–(c) of Step 2 apply verbatim, and invertibility of
$\psi$ is not used.

In Steps 3 and 4, replace [lem-trf-frobenius-operator-compact-description]
by [prop-trf-graph-operator]: $F_{c,m}(\psi)=R\Gamma_c(X,\psi_m)\circ\Phi^\sharp$,
where
$\Phi^\sharp:R\Gamma_c(X,-)\to R\Gamma_c(X,L\Phi^*-)$ is induced by the
unit of $L\Phi^*\dashv R\Phi_*$, the identification
$R\Phi_*\simeq R\Phi_!$ for the finite $\Phi$ and the composition law
for $a_X\Phi=a_X$ ([prop-functor-package], clause (3)). It is a natural
transformation between exact functors, built from units and
identifications, so it commutes with the connecting morphisms and
Step 3 applies. For Step 4, the unit of the composite adjunction for
$\Phi h=h\Phi_W^m$ can be computed in either order, and $b_g$ (for $j$,
now the open-square exchange $b$ of [lem-trf-open-square-exchange]
for $\Phi$) and $e$ are the mates of the resulting equality
$h^*R\Phi_*=R\Phi^m_{W*}h^*$ on the open, respectively the
adjoint description on the closed, piece; the unit compatibility of
mates ([lem-trf-adjoint-mate], item (2)) therefore identifies
$\Phi^\sharp$ on $R\Gamma_c(X,h_!-)\cong R\Gamma_c(W,-)$, followed by
$b$ or $e$, with $(\Phi_W^m)^\sharp$ on $W$, compatibly with the
composition law ([fix-lem-exchanges], (2) and (4)). By
[prop-trf-graph-operator] on $U$ and $Z$ the three endomorphisms of
Step 3 are then conjugate to $F_{c,m}(\psi)$, $F_{c,m}(j^*\psi)$ and
$F_{c,m}(i^*\psi)$. Step 5 applies without change, the complexes being
perfect by [prop-trf-compact-support-perfectness]. This proves item 3.

attrs.title: Additivity of the Frobenius traces along an open–closed decomposition

objects.body:
1. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed subscheme with open complement
$j:U\hookrightarrow X$ which is $c$-invariant, $c_2(c_1^{-1}(Z))\subset Z$,
let
$$
K'=j_!j^*K\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow K''=Ri_*i^*K\longrightarrow K'[1]
$$
be its open–closed triangle, and let $(u',u,u'')$ be the induced morphism
of the corresponding triangles of the functors $Lc_2^*$ and $Rc_1^!$, with
$u'=[j]_!(u|_U)$ and $u''=[i]_!(u|_Z)$ the induced coefficient morphisms of
[lem-trf-trace-triangle-compatibility] (an arbitrary morphism of
distinguished triangles is not enough, see there). Then
$$
\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)=
\operatorname{Tr}_c(u')+\operatorname{Tr}_c(u'')
$$
in $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(F,A)}(A_F,\omega_{F,A})$; if $F$ is
proper over $s$ with
finitely many components in the sense of
[def-trf-fixed-scheme], the same identity holds for the
local terms.
1. *(Curve pieces.)* In the setting of [d-curve-pieces] ($m\geq1$,
$x\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$, $c=(\operatorname{id}_X,\Phi_m)$ the
graph correspondence), let $v:\Phi_m^*K\to K$ be the scheme-Frobenius
map $\varphi_m$ or an arbitrary Frobenius coefficient morphism, with
pieces $u^Z,u^U$. Then $(u^U,v,u^Z)$ is a morphism of the
open–closed triangles $K^U\to K\to K^Z\to K^U[1]$ under
$L\Phi_m^*$ and $Rc_1^!=\operatorname{id}$, and hence
$$
\operatorname{Tr}_c(v)=\operatorname{Tr}_c(u^Z)+\operatorname{Tr}_c(u^U),
\qquad
\operatorname{LT}_\beta(v)=\operatorname{LT}_\beta(u^Z)+\operatorname{LT}_\beta(u^U)
$$
for every component $\beta$ of $F=\operatorname{Fix}(\Phi_m)$.
Invertibility of $v$ is not required.

## Proof

The first assertion of (1) is exactly
[lem-trf-trace-triangle-compatibility]. For the second, suppose
$F$ proper over $s$ with finitely many open-and-closed components
$\beta\in\pi_0(F)$; the local terms of
[def-trf-local-term] are the integrals
$\operatorname{LT}_\beta(u)=\int_\beta\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)|_\beta$
of [def-trf-integration], and integration is $A$-linear by
[lem-trf-integration-linear], so
additivity of the classes gives
$\operatorname{LT}_\beta(u)=\operatorname{LT}_\beta(u')+ \operatorname{LT}_\beta(u'')$ for every $\beta$.

For (2), write $\Phi=\Phi_m$ and let
$$
K^U\xrightarrow{\ \varepsilon\ }K\xrightarrow{\ \eta\ }K^Z
\xrightarrow{\ \delta\ }K^U[1]
$$
be the open–closed triangle of [prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages],
with $\varepsilon$ the counit of $j_!\dashv j^*$ and $\eta$ the unit of
$i^*\dashv Ri_*$. The functor $L\Phi^*$ is exact, so it carries this
triangle to a distinguished triangle, and $Rc_1^!=\operatorname{id}$.
Let $b:L\Phi^*j_!\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!L\Phi_U^*$ be the open base-change
isomorphism used in $u^U$ ([prop-functor-package], clause (4)), and
$\gamma$ the ordinary half used in $u^Z$, as in [d-curve-pieces].

(a) $\varepsilon\circ u^U=v\circ L\Phi^*\varepsilon$. By the adjunction
$j_!\dashv j^*$ of [prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions] it
suffices to compare the restrictions to $U$ of the two maps
$L\Phi^*j_!j^*K\cong j_!L\Phi_U^*j^*K\to K$. There $b$ restricts to the
pullback identification and $j^*\varepsilon$ to the identity, so both
restrictions equal $j^*v$ composed with
$L\Phi_U^*j^*\cong j^*L\Phi^*$.

(b) $u^Z\circ L\Phi^*\eta=\eta\circ v$. By the adjunction $i^*\dashv Ri_*$
it suffices to compare the adjoint maps $i^*L\Phi^*K\to i^*K$. The
adjoint of $\eta\circ v$ is $i^*v$. By the construction of $\gamma$ as
unit followed by counit, the triangle identities make the adjoint of
$u^Z\circ L\Phi^*\eta=Ri_*v_{\bar x}\circ\gamma\circ L\Phi^*\eta$
equal to $v_{\bar x}$ precomposed with $i^*L\Phi^*K\cong(\Phi i)^*K=i^*K$;
this is $i^*v$, by the definition of the stalk map $v_{\bar x}$
($i^*$ being the stalk at $\bar x$).

(c) $u^U[1]\circ L\Phi^*\delta=\delta\circ u^Z$. By (a), (b) and the
axiom of morphisms of triangles there is
$w:L\Phi^*K^Z\to K^Z$ with $w\circ L\Phi^*\eta=\eta\circ v$ and
$\delta\circ w=u^U[1]\circ L\Phi^*\delta$. Then
$(w-u^Z)\circ L\Phi^*\eta=0$, so $w-u^Z$ factors through
$L\Phi^*\delta$ as $d\circ L\Phi^*\delta$ with
$d:L\Phi^*K^U[1]\to K^Z$. Via $b$ the source of $d$ is
$j_!N[1]$ with $N=L\Phi_U^*j^*K$, and
$\operatorname{Hom}(j_!N[1],Ri_*i^*K)=\operatorname{Hom}(N[1],j^*Ri_*i^*K)=0$
because $j^*Ri_*=0$ ([prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions],
as in the Hom vanishing of [prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages]).
Hence $w=u^Z$.

Thus $(u^U,v,u^Z)$ is the induced morphism of the open–closed triangles
for the closed point $Z=\{\bar x\}$, which is $c$-invariant because
$c_1=\operatorname{id}$ and $\Phi(\bar x)=\bar x$, and $u^U,u^Z$ are the
induced coefficient morphisms $[j]_!(v|_U)$, $[i]_!(v|_Z)$ of
[lem-trf-trace-triangle-compatibility]; so (1) gives the identity of trace
classes. The fixed scheme $F=\operatorname{Fix}(\Phi)$
is a finite disjoint union of copies of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ by
[thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points], hence proper over $s$ with finitely
many open-and-closed components, so (1) also gives the identity of local
terms. No step inverts $v$.

Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions, $A=A_{E,n}$, put $s=\Spec k$, let
$c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times_sX$ be an
admissible cohomological
correspondence with fixed scheme
$F=\operatorname{Fix}(c)$, and let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$. Then the
Verdier trace class
$\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)$ of [def-trf-trace-class] is defined for
every correspondence $u:Lc_2^*K\to Rc_1^!K$, under no hypothesis
beyond the admissibility of $c$ and $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$.

## Proof

By [def-trf-trace-class] the trace class is the composite

$$
A\xrightarrow{\ \widetilde u\ }
R\Gamma(C,\mathcal H_c(K))\xrightarrow{\ \mathfrak t_{c,K}\ }
R\Gamma(F,\omega_{F,A})
$$

followed by the identification of the target with
$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(F,A)}(A_F,\omega_{F,A})$, where
$A=A_{E,n}$ is the coefficient ring of
[def-trf-coefficient-conventions].
The first arrow is the mate of $u$ under the tensor–internal-Hom
adjunction of [def-trf-trace-class-source], which is defined for
every correspondence $u$ and needs no hypothesis. The second arrow
is the morphism $\mathfrak t_{c,K}$ of
[lem-trf-trace-map-from-external-duality]: its construction
applies the external duality
[thm-trf-verdier-duality] — itself a consequence of the
Kunneth–Verdier chain [thm-trf-kunneth-verdier] — to the
external product of the dualizing data of
[def-trf-dualizing-complex], and its inverse comparisons are the
ones supplied by the supported pairing of
[def-trf-supported-pairing]. Both arrows therefore exist as soon
as the correspondence $c$ is admissible in the sense of
[def-trf-correspondence] and the fixed scheme is the one of
[def-trf-fixed-scheme], which is the assertion.

attrs.title: The Verdier trace class is unconditionally defined

objects.body:
Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions. The categorical
trace has the following properties, all with $A=A_{E,n}$ and
$\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$ when infinite coefficients occur:

1. *Conjugacy invariance.* If $w:P_1\xrightarrow{\sim}P_2$ is
an isomorphism and $v_2\circ w=w\circ v_1$, then
$\operatorname{tr}_A(v_1\mid P_1)=\operatorname{tr}_A(v_2\mid P_2)$.
1. *Filtered (triangle) additivity.* Let $P'\to P\to P''\to P'[1]$ be a
distinguished triangle in $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$ and $(v',v,v'')$ an
endomorphism of it *of filtered origin*: the triangle is the cofibre
sequence of a two-step filtered object $P'\subset P$ with graded pieces
$P'$ and $P''$, and $(v',v,v'')$ is induced by an endomorphism of this
filtered object in the filtered derived category $DF(A)$ (for instance by
a chain endomorphism of a short exact sequence $0\to P'\to P\to P''\to0$
of bounded complexes of finite projective modules, strictly compatible
with the maps). Then
$$
\operatorname{tr}_A(v\mid P)=
\operatorname{tr}_A(v'\mid P')+\operatorname{tr}_A(v''\mid P'').
$$
The filtered origin cannot be dropped: for an endomorphism of a
distinguished triangle in the Verdier derived category whose squares
commute only up to unspecified homotopy, additivity fails (Ferrand's
example, cf. [Stacks, Tag 087J](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/087J):
over $R=\mathbf Z/4$, the sequence $0\to R[-1]\to[R\xrightarrow{2}R]\to R\to0$
with $(v',v,v'')=(0,(0,2),0)$, where $(0,2)$ is $0$ in degree $0$ and
$2$ in degree $1$, has $\operatorname{tr}_A(v\mid P)=-2\neq0$).
1. *Scalar extension.* For a ring homomorphism
$\rho:A\to B$, $\rho\bigl(\operatorname{tr}_A(v\mid P)\bigr) =\operatorname{tr}_B\bigl(v\otimes_A^LB\mid P\otimes_A^LB\bigr)$.
1. *Supertrace over a field.* For
$\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$ and $P\in D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(\Lambda)$,
$$
\operatorname{tr}_\Lambda(v\mid P)=
\sum_{i\in\mathbf Z}(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}
\bigl(H^i(v)\mid H^i(P)\bigr).
$$

## Proof

In this proof all traces are the categorical traces of
[def-trf-categorical-trace], computed with the explicit model
conventions of [lem-trf-chain-supertrace]; throughout, $w^\vee$
denotes the natural isomorphism
$R\operatorname{Hom}_A(w,A):P_2^\vee\xrightarrow{\sim}P_1^\vee$ induced
by an isomorphism $w:P_1\xrightarrow{\sim}P_2$ (the internal Hom is a
bifunctor of the derived category, [def-weil-derived-tensor]).

*(1) Conjugacy invariance.* The duality data
$\operatorname{coev}_{P_i},\operatorname{ev}_{P_i}$ are natural in
isomorphisms: the squares

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
A & \xrightarrow{\operatorname{coev}_{P_1}} & P_1\otimes^LP_1^\vee\\
\| & & \downarrow w\otimes^L(w^\vee)^{-1}\\
A & \xrightarrow{\operatorname{coev}_{P_2}} & P_2\otimes^LP_2^\vee
\end{array}
\qquad
\begin{array}{ccc}
P_1^\vee\otimes^LP_1 & \xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_{P_1}} & A\\
\downarrow (w^\vee)^{-1}\otimes^Lw & & \|\\
P_2^\vee\otimes^LP_2 & \xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_{P_2}} & A
\end{array}
$$

commute, and the braiding
$\operatorname{sim}$ is natural in both variables; these are the
compatibilities of the tensor–internal-Hom adjunction and of the
symmetric monoidal structure with the identification
$P^\vee=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,A)$. Hence, if
$v_2\circ w=w\circ v_1$, then with the abbreviations
$\iota_w=w\otimes^L(w^\vee)^{-1}$ and
$\iota^w=(w^\vee)^{-1}\otimes^Lw$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{tr}_A(v_2\mid P_2)
&=\operatorname{ev}_{P_2}\circ\operatorname{sym}\circ
(v_2\otimes^L1)\circ\operatorname{coev}_{P_2}\\
&=\operatorname{ev}_{P_2}\circ\operatorname{sym}\circ
\iota_w\circ(v_1\otimes^L1)\circ\operatorname{coev}_{P_1}\\
&=\operatorname{ev}_{P_1}\circ\operatorname{sym}\circ
(v_1\otimes^L1)\circ\operatorname{coev}_{P_1}
=\operatorname{tr}_A(v_1\mid P_1),
\end{aligned}
$$

where the second equality uses $v_2\otimes^L1=\iota_w\circ(v_1\otimes^L1) \circ\iota_w^{-1}$ together with the first square, and the third the
naturality of $\operatorname{sym}$ and the second square.

*(2) Filtered additivity.* This is the additivity of the trace on the
filtered derived category of perfect complexes,
[Stacks, Tag 03TJ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03TJ). Concretely,
an object of $DF(A)$ with a two-step filtration and perfect graded pieces is
represented by a filtered bounded complex of finite projective modules
$M'\subset M$ with $M'$ and $M''=M/M'$ bounded complexes of finite
projectives (the sequence $0\to M'\to M\to M''\to0$ is then degreewise
split), and a morphism in $DF(A)$ between such filtered complexes is
represented by a strict morphism of filtered complexes (filtered
quasi-isomorphisms are inverted, and a filtered map out of a filtered
complex of projectives with projective graded pieces lifts along a filtered
quasi-isomorphism). A strict endomorphism $\bar v$ of $M'\subset M$ is, in
degree $n$ and for a splitting $M^n=M'^n\oplus M''^n$, block triangular,

$$
\bar v^n=\begin{pmatrix}\beta^n & s^n\\ 0 & \alpha^n\end{pmatrix},
$$

with $\beta$ the restricted chain endomorphism of $M'$, which represents
$v'$, $\alpha$ the induced chain endomorphism of $M''$, which represents
$v''$, and $s^n:M''^n\to M'^n$ some family of maps. The trace of a
block-triangular matrix is the sum of the traces of its diagonal blocks, so
by the chain-level formula of [lem-trf-chain-supertrace]

$$
\begin{gathered}
\operatorname{tr}_A(v\mid P)
=\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(\bar v^i\mid M^i)\\
=\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(\beta^i\mid M'^i)
+\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(\alpha^i\mid M''^i)
=\operatorname{tr}_A(v'\mid P')+\operatorname{tr}_A(v''\mid P''),
\end{gathered}
$$

the traces being independent of the chosen representatives by (1) and
[lem-trf-chain-supertrace]. The flaw of the naive argument for an
arbitrary endomorphism $(v',v,v'')$ of the triangle in the plain derived
category is visible here: one then only knows that $v$ is represented by a
chain map $M\to M$ whose squares with $M'\to M$ and $M\to M''$ commute up
to homotopy, and such a map need not be block triangular with diagonal
blocks representing $v'$ and $v''$. In Ferrand's example above every chain
representative of $v$ acts on the subcomplex $M'=R[-1]$ by $2$, which
represents $2\neq v'=0$ (the square commutes only up to the homotopy
$\mathrm{id}:M'^1\to M^0$), and the supertraces differ by $-2$.

*(3) Scalar extension.* The derived scalar extension
$F=-\otimes_A^LB:D(A)\to D(B)$ is exact (it is the derived tensor
product with the $K$-flat complex $B$) and monoidal: the canonical
comparison isomorphism

$$
F(P)\otimes_B^LF(Q)=(P\otimes_A^LB)\otimes_B^L(Q\otimes_A^LB)
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }(P\otimes_A^LQ)\otimes_A^LB=F(P\otimes_A^LQ)
$$

is the associativity of the derived tensor product (no flatness of
$B$ over $A$ is needed in the derived setting, as both sides
compute the same absolute derived tensor $P\otimes_A^LQ\otimes_A^LB$),
and it is compatible with the braidings, with the shifts, and with
distinguished triangles. It also carries the duals: the canonical
isomorphism

$$
F(P)^\vee=R\operatorname{Hom}_B(P\otimes_A^LB,B)
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }R\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,A)\otimes_A^LB=F(P^\vee)
$$

(the standard base-change statement for finite projective modules,
with the derived-tensor form valid for all $P\in D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$
via the projective resolution), and it identifies
$\operatorname{coev}_{F(P)}$, $\operatorname{ev}_{F(P)}$,
and the braiding with the $F$-images of
$\operatorname{coev}_P,\operatorname{ev}_P$ and the braiding;
consequently the composite of
[def-trf-categorical-trace] for $F(P)$ is the $F$-image
of the composite for $P$, and identifying
$\operatorname{End}_{D(B)}(B)\cong B$ with the application of
$\rho:\operatorname{End}_{D(A)}(A)\cong A\to B$ gives
$\rho(\operatorname{tr}_A(v\mid P))= \operatorname{tr}_B(v\otimes_A^LB\mid P\otimes_A^LB)$.
The same argument applies to the scalar extensions
$A\to A_{E'\!,n'}$, $A\to\mathcal O_E$, $\mathcal O_E\to E$, and
$E\to\Qlb$ of the coefficient passages of Blueprints 01 and 02,
the latter two being the monoidal functors of the rationalized
([def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]) and common-stage
([def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients])
constructions.

*(4) Supertrace over a field.* Let $\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$ (for
$\Lambda=E$, $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(E)$ is the bounded derived category
of finite-dimensional $E$-vector spaces by
[def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]). Every
$P\in D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(\Lambda)$ is represented by a bounded
complex $P^\bullet$ of finite-dimensional $\Lambda$-vector spaces
together with a chain map $v^\bullet$ inducing $v$. For an integer
$i$ let $P^{\leq i}$ be the canonical truncation

$$
P^{\leq i}=\bigl(\cdots\to P^{i-2}\to P^{i-1}\to\ker d^i\to0\bigr)
$$

(a subcomplex stable under $v^\bullet$), so that
$P^{\leq i+1}/P^{\leq i}$ is the two-term complex

$$
C_i=\bigl(\operatorname{im}d^i\xrightarrow{d}\ker d^{i+1}\bigr)
\qquad\text{(degrees }i,i+1\text{)}
$$

with the induced endomorphism; it carries the induced endomorphism
and is quasi-isomorphic to
$\mathcal H^{i+1}(P)[-(i+1)]$ because the arrow
$\operatorname{im}d^i\hookrightarrow\ker d^{i+1}$ is injective with
cokernel $\mathcal H^{i+1}(P)$. Since all terms are vector spaces,
the short exact sequences

$$
0\to P^{\leq i}\to P^{\leq i+1}\to C_i\to0
$$

are degreewise split short exact sequences of complexes with strictly
compatible chain endomorphisms, hence give distinguished triangles of
$D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(\Lambda)$ with endomorphisms of filtered origin in the
sense of (2). By (2), and by the chain-level computation of
[lem-trf-chain-supertrace] applied to $C_i$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{tr}_\Lambda(v\mid P^{\leq i+1})
&=\operatorname{tr}_\Lambda(v\mid P^{\leq i})
+\operatorname{tr}_\Lambda(v\mid C_i)\\
&=\operatorname{tr}_\Lambda(v\mid P^{\leq i})
+(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(v\mid\operatorname{im}d^i\bigr)
+(-1)^{i+1}\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(v\mid\ker d^{i+1}\bigr)\\
&=\operatorname{tr}_\Lambda(v\mid P^{\leq i})
+(-1)^{i+1}\operatorname{Tr}
\bigl(\mathcal H^{i+1}(v)\mid\mathcal H^{i+1}(P)\bigr),
\end{aligned}
$$

the last equality using the split exact sequence
$0\to\operatorname{im}d^i\to\ker d^{i+1}\to\mathcal H^{i+1}(P)\to0$
of vector spaces with the induced endomorphisms, which gives
$\operatorname{Tr}(v\mid\ker d^{i+1})- \operatorname{Tr}(v\mid\operatorname{im}d^i)= \operatorname{Tr}(\mathcal H^{i+1}(v))$. Induction over the finite
cohomological range of $P^\bullet$ (starting from
$P^{\leq i}=0$ below the lowest degree) gives

$$
\operatorname{tr}_\Lambda(v\mid P)
=\sum_{i\in\mathbf Z}(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}
\bigl(\mathcal H^{i}(v)\mid\mathcal H^{i}(P)\bigr),
$$

which is the displayed formula.

attrs.title: Formal laws for the categorical trace

objects.body:
Fix the global finite-field datum
$(p,a,q,k_0,k)$, where $p$ is prime and $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$ with
$q=p^a$. Choose a prime $\ell\neq p$, an algebraic closure
$\Qlb$ of $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an isomorphism
$\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$. Interpret the $\Qlb$-objects
in the algebraically
closed coefficient category. Let
$X_0/k_0$ be smooth, proper,
geometrically connected of pure dimension
$d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, and put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. Let
$a_X:X\to\Spec k$ be the structure morphism, and let
$g_X=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{Frob}_q)$
be the geometric-Frobenius automorphism.
Let $F_\ell$ be the induced
global geometric Frobenius
on the ordinary and
compactly supported cohomology with $\Ql$-coefficients,
and let $F_{\Qlb}$ be its scalar extension to the corresponding
$\Qlb$-cohomology. Define the graded cohomology notation by

$$
H^\bullet(X,\Lambda):=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbf Z}H^i(X,\Lambda),
\qquad
H_c^\bullet(X,\Lambda):=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbf Z}H_c^i(X,\Lambda)
\quad(\Lambda=\Ql,\Qlb).
$$

Use the scalar-extension identifications

$$
H^\bullet(X,\Ql)\otimes_{\Ql}\Qlb\simeq H^\bullet(X,\Qlb),\qquad
H_c^\bullet(X,\Ql)\otimes_{\Ql}\Qlb\simeq H_c^\bullet(X,\Qlb).
$$

Assume $a_X:X\to\Spec k$ is
exceptional-adjoint
admissible at $\Qlb$, and choose a dualizing
Weil complex
$(\omega_X,\theta_{\omega_X})$ with

$$
\operatorname{For}(\omega_X)=Ra_X^!\Qlb,
$$

where $Ra_X^!$ is the
exceptional inverse image
for this admissible structure morphism, and require
$\theta_{\omega_X}$ to be the canonical functorial Weil lift induced by
geometric-Frobenius base change and the adjunction units and counits, rather
than an arbitrary lift.
These operators come from the constant
Weil sheaf $(\Qlb)_X$ on the
small pro-etale site, with the
geometric-Frobenius convention. Fix an
indeterminate $T$. For
$0\leq i\leq2d$, set

$$
H^i(X,\Qlb)=H^i\!\left(R\Gamma(X,(\Qlb)_X)\right),\qquad
H_c^i(X,\Qlb)=H^i\!\left(R\Gamma_c(X,(\Qlb)_X)\right),
\qquad
V_{i,\ell}=H^i(X,\Ql),
$$

and $F_{i,\ell}=F_\ell|_{V_{i,\ell}}$,
$P_{i,\ell}(T)=\det(1-TF_{i,\ell}\mid V_{i,\ell})$. These data are the
smooth-proper
cohomological family; reciprocal roots use the
ordinary/reciprocal-root
convention. Use the
complex-weight and
Frobenius-module weight
predicates. Then the constant
Weil sheaf $(\Qlb)_X$ is
$\iota$-pure of weight $0$.

## Proof

The interpretation of the words weight for the constant Weil complex and
its cohomology is the one fixed by [def-weil-complex-weights]: its
upper-weight predicate is checked on the cohomology-sheaf filtration while
its lower-weight predicate is obtained by applying the duality operation
and the same filtration criterion. With these conventions the constant
Weil sheaf $(\Qlb)_X$ of the statement is the constant Weil complex of
the smooth-proper purity interface, whose hypotheses are exactly the
smoothness, properness, geometric connectedness, coefficient, and
Frobenius data fixed above; clause (1) of
[thm-weil-deligne-purity] is therefore precisely the assertion that
$(\Qlb)_X$ is $\iota$-pure of weight $0$.

attrs.title: Smooth-proper purity of the constant Weil sheaf

objects.body:
In the situation of [prop-weight-purity], for every
$0\leq i\leq2d$ the
Frobenius module
$H^i(X,\Qlb)$ is $\iota$-pure of weight $i$.

## Proof

Clause (4) of [thm-weil-deligne-purity] states that the
geometric-Frobenius module $H^i(X,\Qlb)$ of the situation of
[prop-weight-purity] is $\iota$-pure of weight $i$, in the sense
of [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights].

In the situation of [prop-weight-purity], for every
$0\leq i\leq2d$ every
reciprocal root
$\alpha\in\Qlb$ of the polynomial $P_{i,\ell}$ of the
smooth-proper
cohomological family satisfies

$$
|\iota(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}.
$$

## Proof

By [def-weil-smooth-proper-cohomological-family], the polynomial
$P_{i,\ell}(T)=\det(1-TF_{i,\ell}\mid V_{i,\ell})$ records the
eigenvalues of the Frobenius operator $F_{i,\ell}$ on $V_{i,\ell}$,
and after scalar extension to $\Qlb$ that operator is the operator
$F_{\Qlb}$ on the module $H^i(X,\Qlb)$ of
[def-weil-frobenius-module-weights]. By
[prop-weight-purity-ordinary] that module is $\iota$-pure of
weight $i$, which by the same definition means that each of its
eigenvalues $\alpha$ satisfies $|\iota(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}$; by
[def-weil-ordinary-reciprocal-roots] the reciprocal roots of
$P_{i,\ell}$ are exactly these eigenvalues, counted with algebraic
multiplicity. This is the assertion, in the situation of
[prop-weight-purity].

attrs.title: Reciprocal roots have the weight-$i$ absolute value

objects.body:
Fix a prime $p$, an integer $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, put $q=p^a$,
$k_0=\Fq$, and let $k=\Fbar$ be the
fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$.
Fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic
closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and fix an isomorphism
$\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$ and an indeterminate $T$. Let
$X_0/k_0$ be
smooth, proper, geometrically
connected of pure dimension
$d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let
$(V_{i,\ell},F_{i,\ell},P_{i,\ell})_{0\leq i\leq2d}$ be the
smooth-proper
cohomological family.
Interpret ordinary and reciprocal roots by the
root convention, and use the
absolute-value weight condition. Assume
that, for every integer $i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$, every reciprocal root
$\alpha$ of $P_{i,\ell}$ satisfies

$$
|\iota(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}.
$$

Let $Z(X_0,T)$ be the
point-count zeta series. Assume the
trace-to-determinant identity

$$
Z(X_0,T)=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}P_{i,\ell}(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}
\quad\text{in }\Ql(T).
$$

For all integers $0\leq i,j\leq2d$ with
$i\neq j$, the polynomials $P_{i,\ell}$ and $P_{j,\ell}$ have no common
ordinary root in $\Qlb$ and are coprime in $\Qlb[T]$. Define the
odd and even parity products by

$$
N_\ell(T)=\prod_{\substack{0\leq i\leq2d\\ i\text{ odd}}}
P_{i,\ell}(T),
\qquad
D_\ell(T)=\prod_{\substack{0\leq i\leq2d\\ i\text{ even}}}
P_{i,\ell}(T).
$$

They are coprime, have constant coefficient $1$, and the
Hasse–Weil zeta series satisfies

$$
Z(X_0,T)=\frac{N_\ell(T)}{D_\ell(T)}
$$

after coefficient extension to $\Ql[[T]]$. More precisely, the ordinary
root multiset of each $P_{i,\ell}$ is exactly the submultiset of roots of
the appropriate parity product whose reciprocal $\alpha$ satisfies

$$
|\iota(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}
$$

for the fixed isomorphism
$\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$.

## Proof

Let $\beta\in\Qlb$ be a common ordinary root of $P_{i,\ell}$ and
$P_{j,\ell}$ with $i\ne j$. Then $\alpha=\beta^{-1}$ is a
reciprocal root of both polynomials in the sense of
[def-weil-ordinary-reciprocal-roots], so the assumed absolute
value condition gives $|\iota(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}=q^{j/2}$, hence
$i=j$, a contradiction. Thus distinct $P_{i,\ell}$ have no common
ordinary root, and since every $P_{i,\ell}$ has constant coefficient
one, they are coprime in $\Qlb[T]$; consequently the parity products
$N_\ell,D_\ell$ of [def-weil-parity-products] are coprime and
have constant coefficient one. The assumed trace-to-determinant
identity for the point-count zeta series of
[def-weil-point-counts-zeta],

$$
Z(X_0,T)=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}P_{i,\ell}(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}},
$$

groups the odd-degree factors into $N_\ell(T)$ and the even-degree
factors into $D_\ell(T)$, giving $Z(X_0,T)=N_\ell(T)/D_\ell(T)$
after coefficient extension to $\Ql[[T]]$. Every ordinary root of
$N_\ell$ is an ordinary root of exactly one $P_{j,\ell}$ with $j$
odd, and its reciprocal satisfies the assumed absolute value condition
with weight $j$; hence the submultiset of ordinary roots of $N_\ell$
whose reciprocal satisfies $|\iota(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}$ is exactly the
ordinary root multiset of $P_{i,\ell}$ for $i$ odd, and the
corresponding assertion with $D_\ell$ holds for $i$ even, which is the
asserted more precise multiset identification.

Let $p$ be prime, let $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, put $q=p^a$ and
$k_0=\Fq$, and let $k=\Fbar$ be the
fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$.
Let $X_0/k_0$ be
smooth, proper, and geometrically
connected of pure dimension $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, and put
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. Fix an indeterminate $T$. For every prime
$\ell\neq p$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and for
$P(T)=\sum_r c_rT^r\in\mathbf Z[T]$ write
$P^{(\ell)}(T)=\sum_r(c_r\cdot1_{\Ql})T^r$, and let
$(V_{i,\ell},F_{i,\ell},P_{i,\ell})_{0\leq i\leq2d}$ be the
smooth-proper
cohomological family. Let $P_i(T)\in\mathbf Z[T]$ be the
integral Frobenius factor
with $P_i(0)=1$ and $P_i^{(\ell)}=P_{i,\ell}$ for every
$\ell\neq p$, and define the Betti
numbers by $b_i=\deg P_i$ for $0\leq i\leq2d$ and $b_i=0$
otherwise. Write $H^i(X,\Ql)$ for
ordinary cohomology.
For every integer $i$ and every $\ell\neq p$,

$$
b_i=\dim_{\Ql}H^i(X,\Ql).
$$

In particular, the integers $b_i$ are independent of $\ell$, vanish
outside $0\leq i\leq2d$, and in the displayed range agree with the degrees
of the integral factors.

## Proof

For $0\leq i\leq2d$, [def-weil-betti-numbers] gives
$b_i=\deg P_i$, and [prop-integral-recovery] identifies this degree
with $\dim_{\Ql}H^i(X,\Ql)$. Outside the displayed range,
[def-weil-betti-numbers] gives $b_i=0$, while
[prop-cohomological-finiteness] gives $H^i(X,\Ql)=0$. Hence the
comparison is independent of $\ell$.

Assume that for every $E\in\mathsf{FinExt}_\ell$ the category
$\mathcal C_E(T)=\Dbc(T,E)$ of
[def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category] is idempotent complete (for
instance by [thm-weil-pbc-finite-stage-karoubian]). Then the pair category
$\mathcal P_T$ is idempotent complete: every idempotent of $\mathcal P_T$
splits, and a splitting may be represented over a single finite coefficient
field.

*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this descent: the ledger's
verified entries contain no idempotent-completion or filtered-colimit entry,
and the blueprint adds the splitting of an idempotent of the pair category
over a single finite coefficient field, given idempotent completeness of the
finite-stage categories. The nearest entries, each fetched and quoted, are
Homological Algebra, Definition 12.4.1 ([Tag
09SG](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09SG), Karoubian: every
idempotent endomorphism of an object has a kernel) and Lemma 12.4.2 ([Tag
09SH](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09SH), Karoubian iff every
idempotent has a cokernel iff $z=x\oplus y$ with $p$ the projection onto
$y$), with the Karoubianity criteria Lemma 12.4.3 ([Tag
05QV](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05QV), countable products with
kernels of maps having a right inverse) and Lemma 13.4.14 ([Tag
05QW](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05QW), a triangulated category
with countable products, or with countable coproducts, is Karoubian); the
only idempotent inside a filtered colimit in Stacks is the one of Remark
4.21.6 ([Tag 09P8](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09P8)), where the
colimit of an idempotent diagram in *Sets* is its image. Difference: those
entries test a category that is already given, and Stacks constructs no
idempotent completion (the request to add the Karoubi envelope stands as a
comment on Section 12.4, Tag 09SF); here idempotent completeness is assumed
for every finite stage and the conclusion is a splitting over one stage.

## Proof

Let $e:(E,K)\to(E,K)$ be an idempotent of the pair category
$\mathcal P_T$ of [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category] and let
$(M,u)$, with $u:T_{M/E}K\to T_{M/E}K$, be a representative of $e$. The
equality $e^2=e$ holds in $\mathcal P_T$, so by the equivalence relation and
the transport formula of [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus] there is a
finite $P\supset M$ with
$$
 u_P\circ u_P=u_P
 \qquad\text{in }\mathcal C_P(T)
$$
(the composite $e^2$ being represented by $(M,u\circ u)$). The category
$\mathcal C_P(T)=\Dbc(T,P)$ is idempotent complete by the hypothesis
(verified by [thm-weil-pbc-finite-stage-karoubian]), so there exist
$K'_P\in\mathcal C_P(T)$, $p_P:T_{P/E}K\to K'_P$, and
$i_P:K'_P\to T_{P/E}K$ with
$$
 p_P\,i_P=\operatorname{id}_{K'_P},\qquad i_P\,p_P=u_P.
$$
In $\mathcal P_T$, let $K'=(P,K'_P)$, and let
$$
 i=[P,i_P]:K'\longrightarrow(P,T_{P/E}K)\cong(E,K),
\qquad
 p=[P,p_P]:(E,K)\cong(P,T_{P/E}K)\longrightarrow K',
$$
where the displayed isomorphisms are the classes of the identity morphisms
(well defined, since $P\supset E$). Then $p\,i=[P,p_P\,i_P]$ is the class of
the identity, i.e. the identity of $K'$, and $i\,p=[P,i_P\,p_P]=[P,u_P]$ is
the class of $e$. Hence $e$ splits in $\mathcal P_T$, over the single field
$P$.

For a t-structure $(\mathcal T^{\le0},\mathcal T^{\ge0})$ on a triangulated
category, the heart $\mathcal T^{\le0}\cap\mathcal T^{\ge0}$ of
[def-weil-t-structure] is abelian. Consequently every idempotent of the heart
splits: an idempotent $e:A\to A$ of an abelian category splits as
$A\cong\ker(e)\oplus\ker(\operatorname{id}_A-e)$, with $e$ carried to the
projection onto the second summand.

(*Source: the classical theorem on t-structures and their hearts in
Beilinson--Bernstein--Deligne; the second assertion is the elementary
abelian-category argument exhibited in the proof; no Stacks Project entry
states this form: Stacks has no heart of a t-structure (it defines no
t-structure at all; see the pages listed at [def-weil-t-structure]) and no
abelian-category statement that idempotents split — the nearest is the
splitting criterion for a Karoubian preadditive category, Lemma 12.4.2 (Tag
[09SH](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09SH)) (3) with Definition 12.4.1
(Tag [09SG](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09SG)), which presupposes
Karoubianity instead of proving it for an abelian category. The blueprint
adds the explicit supplementary-kernel argument for the splitting of an
idempotent of the heart, which together with the Karoubianity theorem below
replaces any appeal to a Stacks entry.*)

## Proof

For the heart defined in [def-weil-t-structure], the abelianity assertion is
the classical theorem recorded in the source note. Its only use below is that
the heart is idempotent complete: for an idempotent $e$ in an abelian
category the kernels $\ker(e)$ and $\ker(\operatorname{id}_A-e)$ are
supplementary subobjects of $A$, the map
$\ker(e)\oplus\ker(\operatorname{id}_A-e)\to A$ is an isomorphism
($\operatorname{id}_A=e+(\operatorname{id}_A-e)$, and the two kernels have
zero intersection), and under it $e$ becomes the projection onto the second
summand with the canonical maps of the split.

Let $Z(T)\in1+T\mathbf Z[[T]]$ be rational over $\mathbf Q$.
Then $Z$ has a unique
normalized reduced
integral presentation: there are unique $A,B\in\mathbf Z[T]$
such that $A(0)=B(0)=1$, $\gcd(A,B)=1$ in $\mathbf Q[T]$,
and $BZ=A$.

## Proof

Write $Z=\sum_{n\geq0}z_nT^n$ and
$R_j=(z_{j+s})_{s\geq0}$. By
[prop-weil-rationality-criterion], their rational span $V$
is finite-dimensional. Left shift $S(v)_n=v_{n+1}$ preserves $V$,
since $S(R_j)=R_{j+1}$.
Put $L=V\cap\mathbf Z^{\mathbf Z_{\geq0}}$.
This subgroup contains every $R_j$, spans $V$ over $\mathbf Q$,
and is preserved by $S$.

Choose a finite coordinate set $J$ using
[lem-weil-finite-coordinate-detection]. Evaluation embeds $L$
in $\mathbf Z^J$. A subgroup of $\mathbf Z^r$ is finite free:
induct on $r$, project to the last coordinate, and write the image
as $d\mathbf Z$. If the image is zero, apply induction in
$\mathbf Z^{r-1}$. Otherwise choose one lift of $d$; it splits
off a copy of $\mathbf Z$, with kernel a subgroup of
$\mathbf Z^{r-1}$. This proves the assertion and supplies a finite
basis of $L$.

In this basis $S|_L$ has an integer matrix $M$, $R_0$ has an
integer coordinate column $v$, and evaluation at coordinate zero
has an integer row $e$. Thus

$$
z_n=eM^nv,\qquad
Z(T)=e(I-TM)^{-1}v
=\frac{e\,\operatorname{adj}(I-TM)v}{\det(I-TM)}.
$$

The inverse identity is a formal power series identity:
$(I-TM)\sum_{n\geq0}T^nM^n=I$ coefficient by coefficient.
Let $A_0=e\,\operatorname{adj}(I-TM)v$ and
$B_0=\det(I-TM)$. They are integer polynomials and
$B_0(0)=1$, $A_0(0)=ev=z_0=1$.

Choose a primitive integer polynomial $G$ representing the greatest
common divisor of $A_0,B_0$ over $\mathbf Q[T]$.
Gauss' lemma says that a primitive integer polynomial dividing an
integer polynomial over $\mathbf Q[T]$ already divides it over
$\mathbf Z[T]$. Hence $A_0=GA$ and $B_0=GB$ with integral
quotients. The equality $1=B_0(0)=G(0)B(0)$ forces
$G(0)=\pm1$. Choose its sign so that $G(0)=1$; then
$A(0)=B(0)=1$, and the two quotients are coprime.
They give the presentation of [def-weil-normalized-integral-fraction].

If $A/B=A'/B'$ are two such reduced fractions, $AB'=A'B$.
Coprimality implies $B\mid B'$ and $B'\mid B$ in
$\mathbf Q[T]$, so $B'=cB$ for $c\in\mathbf Q^\times$.
Their constant terms force $c=1$, and then $A'=A$.

attrs.title: Normalized integral fraction for an integral rational series

objects.body:
Let $E/\Ql$ be finite and let $\varpi$ be a uniformizer of $\mathcal O_E$.
By [prop-weil-pbc-integral-tstructure] the standard t-structure restricts to
$\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], and
the $\varpi$-power-torsion subcategory is stable under the truncation
functors; the truncations are the levelwise ones on the reduction tower
[thm-weil-pbc-integral-truncations], which is exactly the adic-model
condition of the standard t-structure (objectwise cohomological boundedness
alone is not a bounded t-structure on a derived-complete category, and the
levelwise definition shows the truncations to persist). Then the
subcategories
$$
  (\Dbc(T,E))^{\le0}:=
  \{K:K\cong L\text{ in }\Dbc(T,E),\ L\in(\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E))^{\le0}\},
$$
$$
  (\Dbc(T,E))^{\ge0}:=
  \{K:K\cong L\text{ in }\Dbc(T,E),\ L\in(\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E))^{\ge0}\},
$$
with the objects of $\Dbc(T,E)$ [def-weil-pbc-rational-category] identified
with those of $\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)$, form a bounded t-structure on
$\Dbc(T,E)$ for which the localization functor is t-exact; the truncation
functors are the levelwise canonical truncations on an integral
representative, and the heart is the essential image of the integral heart.

*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this form: Stacks has no
t-structure or heart, and its truncation entries (Homological Algebra,
Section 12.15, [Tag 0118](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0118); Remark
13.12.4, [Tag 08J5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08J5)) concern the
complexes of one fixed abelian category and are not stable under changing
the coefficient ring; the blueprint adds the bounded t-structure on the
rational category $\Dbc(T,E)$, its $t$-exactness for the localization
functor and the identification of its heart with the integral heart.

## Proof

The shift conditions hold first for the integral representatives in
$\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)$, by [prop-weil-pbc-integral-tstructure], and then for
their isomorphism closures in the rational category. For orthogonality,
choose integral representatives $A_0$ in degrees $\le0$ and $B_0$ in degrees
$\ge0$, together with rational isomorphisms $A\cong A_0$ and $B\cong B_0$.
By [def-weil-pbc-rational-category],
$$
 \Hom_{\Dbc(T,E)}(A,B[-1])
  \cong\Hom_{\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)}(A_0,B_0[-1])\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E=0,
$$
the first factor being zero by orthogonality of
[prop-weil-pbc-integral-tstructure] and the tensor product being zero. For
the truncation axiom, the truncation triangle
$$
 \tau^{\le0}K\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow\tau^{\ge1}K
 \longrightarrow\tau^{\le0}K[1]
$$
of $K$ in $\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)$ (the triangle of
[thm-weil-pbc-integral-truncations] (iii)) is carried to a distinguished
triangle of $\Dbc(T,E)$ by the exact localization functor of
[def-weil-pbc-rational-category], whose end terms lie in
$(\Dbc(T,E))^{\le0}$ and $(\Dbc(T,E))^{\ge0}$ by definition; the same
argument at every truncation level shows that the truncations are computed
levelwise on integral representatives. Boundedness, in terms of the
cohomology sheaves, is inherited: an object of $\Dbc(T,E)$ is an object of
the bounded category $\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)$. The t-exactness of the
localization functor is the identity on objects together with the displayed
definitions of the two subcategories, and the heart is the essential image
in $\Dbc(T,E)$ of the integral heart.

The source records that audit item BC-03 is resolved for this proposition:
its truncation functors are those of [thm-weil-pbc-integral-truncations],
whose proof is complete once the Tor-compatibility condition is carried as
an explicit hypothesis.

For complementary open and closed immersions $j:U\hookrightarrow X$,
$i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ as in the open-closed recollement, one has
$j_!\dashv j^*$ and $i^*\dashv Ri_*$ on the ambient ordinary derived
categories with finite constant coefficients. The open unit and the closed
counit are isomorphisms
$$
 \operatorname{id}\xrightarrow{\sim}j^*j_!,\qquad
 i^*Ri_*\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{id}.
$$
The operations are those of extension by zero, derived direct image, and
derived pullback, tensor and hom.

## Proof

The open adjunction is the extension-by-zero adjunction. Both functors are
exact, so they pass to ordinary derived categories with the same adjunction
and triangle identities. The unit is an isomorphism term by term by
[lem-exc-proetale-open-unit].

For the closed adjunction, choose a K-injective resolution $M\to J$ on $Z$.
Since $i^*$ is exact, $i_*J$ is K-injective: its Hom complex from an acyclic
complex $N$ is the Hom complex from the acyclic $i^*N$ to $J$, hence
acyclic. Thus $i_*J$ represents $Ri_*M$, and complex-level adjunction gives
$i^*\dashv Ri_*$. Exactness of $i^*$ lets us compute the derived counit by
$i^*i_*J\to J$. This is an isomorphism in every degree by
[lem-exc-proetale-closed-fully-faithful]. Hence the derived counit is an
isomorphism. This calculation does not assume exactness of $i_*$ for an
arbitrary closed immersion; the complement's quasi-compactness is needed for
the separate sheaf-exactness and recollement theorems above.

Fix the finite-field datum
$p,a,q,k_0,k$, where $q=p^a$, and fix a prime $\ell\neq p$; write
$\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and
let $E/\Ql$ be finite and contained in $\Qlb$, and let
$\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$; use the
Weil-complex category, the
bounded constructible
coefficient categories and their
finite-Tor subcategories, the
separated finite-type
morphism conditions, and the
exceptional-adjoint
admissibility condition in its constructible form (the exceptional inverse
image of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], defined for every separated
finite-type morphism; the ambient clause (1) of
[def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility] is not assumed, as it fails in
general). Use the
derived pullback, tensor, and
internal-Hom operations, the
derived direct-image and
compact-support direct image, the
exceptional inverse image, the
exchange/projection transformations, and
the standard truncation functors $\tau^{\leq m},\tau^{\geq m}$.
Let $X_0,Y_0$ be
finite-type $k_0$-schemes
and let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a
separated finite-type
$k_0$-morphism, and let
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $f:X\to Y$ be
the geometric fiber of
$f_0$. For
$K\in D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(X,\Lambda)$, and, whenever a tensor or internal
Hom is used on a scheme $W\in\{X,Y\}$, for
$M\in D^b_{ctf}(W,\Lambda)$ and $N\in D^b_c(W,\Lambda)$, the exact functors

$$
Lf^*,\quad Rf_*,\quad Rf_!,\quad -\otimes^L-,\quad R\mathcal Hom
$$

lift to Weil complexes on every one of these domains on which their
underlying bounded constructibility has been proved. In particular, the
elementary internal-Hom preservation theorem applies when its first
argument is site-perfect. Equivariance itself supplies no preservation
theorem for a larger domain. Put

$$
g_X=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{Frob}_q),
\qquad
g_Y=\operatorname{id}_{Y_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{Frob}_q),
$$

using the geometric-Frobenius convention.
The constructible exceptional inverse image $Rf^!$ of
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] — available for every separated
finite-type $f$, so that no admissibility hypothesis is needed — also has an
equivariant lift, with its Weil
isomorphism induced by the corresponding exchange and adjunction maps. For
example, the Weil isomorphism on $Rf_*K$ is

$$
Lg_Y^*Rf_*\operatorname{For}(K)
\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Ex}_*}
Rf_*Lg_X^*\operatorname{For}(K)
\xrightarrow{Rf_*(\theta_K)}Rf_*\operatorname{For}(K),
$$

and the compact-support construction uses $\operatorname{Ex}_!$.
For every $W\in\{X,Y\}$ and $m\in\mathbf Z$, let
$\tau^{\leq m},\tau^{\geq m}:D^b_c(W,\Lambda)\to D^b_c(W,\Lambda)$
be the truncation functors, characterized by vanishing of the
cohomology sheaves
$\mathcal H^r(\tau^{\leq m}K)=0$ for $r>m$ and
$\mathcal H^r(\tau^{\geq m}K)=0$ for $r<m$, together with their
standard truncation triangles. The
forgetful functor commutes with these lifted operations. Composition,
base change, projection, purity, and duality isomorphisms are morphisms of
Weil complexes and induce Frobenius-equivariant maps on
cohomology.

## Proof

The equivariant lifts of the operations, evaluations, adjunction maps,
exchanges and projection maps are [lem-fix-weil-operations].
Pullback by the Frobenius automorphism is exact, so it commutes with
the truncations of [prop-constructible-truncations].
The geometric orientation and trace are equivariant by
[thm-pur-weil-equivariance-of-purity-and-trace] and
[prop-pur-weil-equivariance-compatibilities].
The formal duality exchange of [fix-cor-verdier-exchange] is made
from the same evaluation and adjunction maps, hence is equivariant;
its smooth pairing form is
[thm-pod-equivariance-of-the-twisted-pairing].
This proves the assertion on the stated domains without appealing to
the later verification export.

Let $k\subset k'$ be algebraically closed, let $C$ be proper of dimension at
most one over $k$, and let $F$ be a torsion etale sheaf. Then

$$
 H^q(C,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(C_{k'},F|_{C_{k'}})
 \qquad(q\geq0).
$$

## Proof

The assertion is $\mathcal C_7(C,F)$ of
[def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions]. By
[lem-weil-pbc-curve-constructible-reduction] the instances for reduced curves
with constructible $\mathbf F_r$-coefficients imply $\mathcal C_7(C,F)$. A
reduced scheme of finite type over $k$ with dimension at most one is the
disjoint union of its zero-dimensional irreducible components and its
one-dimensional components: there are finitely many components, and a
zero-dimensional irreducible component is a closed point contained in no other
component, so both unions are open and closed. The zero-dimensional union
satisfies the assertion by [lem-weil-pbc-zero-dimensional-field-extension].
Cohomology and pullback over a finite disjoint union are the products of those
on its components, so it remains to treat the pure one-dimensional union. Now
the dense-open localization of [lem-weil-pbc-curve-dense-open-localization]
and the extension-by-zero comparison of
[lemma-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-extension-zero] reduce to the
sheaves $j_{a,!}\mathbf F_r$ on irreducible curves. On the normalization,
[lemma-weil-pbc-normalization-exact-sequence] transfers the assertion from the
smooth case, where [thm-sc-main] supplies it for
the constant sheaf; the locally constant reduction of
[lemma-weil-pbc-curve-locally-constant-reduction], using the filtration of
[lemma-weil-pbc-finite-l-group-filtration] and the trace splitting, passes from
the constant sheaf to finite locally constant sheaves. The short-exact
devissage of [lemma-weil-pbc-eight-curve-devissage] and the filtered cohomology
of [lemma-weil-pbc-curve-filtered-cohomology] assemble the assertion for
arbitrary torsion sheaves.

Let $\square$ be a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with
$\Lambda$-coefficient data as in the adic coefficient datum and suppose that
$\mathrm{AMP}(\square;c)$ of [def-weil-pbc-finite-level-amplification]
holds. Then for every $n\geq1$, with $P_n=A/I^n$, and all $a\leq b$,
$$
 \begin{aligned}
  Rf_*\bigl(D^b_c(X_{\Proet},P_n)^{[a,b]}\bigr)
  &\subset D^b_c(Y_{\Proet},P_n)^{[a,b+c]},\\
  Rf'_*\bigl(D^b_c(X'_{\Proet},P_n)^{[a,b]}\bigr)
  &\subset D^b_c(Y'_{\Proet},P_n)^{[a,b+c]},\\
  Lg_n^*\bigl(D^b_c(Y_{\Proet},P_n)^{[a,b]}\bigr)
  &\subset D^b_c(Y'_{\Proet},P_n)^{[a,b]},\\
  Lg_n'^*\bigl(D^b_c(X_{\Proet},P_n)^{[a,b]}\bigr)
  &\subset D^b_c(X'_{\Proet},P_n)^{[a,b]}.
 \end{aligned}
$$

*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states these four containments: they
are formal consequences of the predicate of
[def-weil-pbc-finite-level-amplification], whose etale inputs are Lemma
59.92.2 ([Tag 095U](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/095U), the
amplitude bound $R^qf_*=0$ for $q>2n$ when the fibres have dimension
$\le n$) and Theorem 63.14.5 ([Tag
0GL0](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0GL0), constructibility of
$Rf_!$), together with Definition 61.29.1 ([Tag
09C1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C1)) and Proposition 61.29.7
([Tag 09C7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C7)) for adic
constructibility; the blueprint adds the assembly of the containments for
the four functors of one square.

## Proof

By [def-weil-pbc-finite-level-amplification] the condition
$\mathrm{AMP}(\square;c)$ consists, for every $n\geq1$, of the finiteness
conditions $\mathrm{FIN}(f,P_n;c)$ and $\mathrm{FIN}(f',P_n;c)$ of
[def-weil-pbc-constructible-direct-image-finiteness] and of the restriction
of the pullbacks $Lg_n^*,Lg_n'^*$ to exact triangulated functors carrying
the class of objects with cohomology in $[a,b]$ into the same class. The
finiteness conditions supply the hypotheses of
[prop-weil-pbc-restriction-direct-image], which therefore yields the first
two displayed containments; the restriction clause is the conclusion of
[lem-weil-pbc-pullback-preserves-bounded-constructible] for the two
coordinates, which yields the last two.

Let $T$ be a scheme and let $F$ be an etale abelian sheaf on the small etale
site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] of $T$. If $F\to I^\bullet$ and $F\to
J^\bullet$ are two K-injective resolutions
[def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions] of $F$, then for every $q\geq0$ the
groups $\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(T,I^\bullet))$ and $\mathcal
H^q(\Gamma(T,J^\bullet))$ are isomorphic, so the groups $H^q(T_{\Et},F)$ of
[def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] are independent of the chosen resolution.

## Proof

By [prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist] the two K-injective
resolutions of $F$ are chain-homotopy equivalent, so there are chain maps
$I^\bullet\to J^\bullet$ and $J^\bullet\to I^\bullet$ over $F$ whose
composites are homotopic to the identities. The additive functor
$\Gamma(T,-)$ occurring in [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] carries chain maps
to chain maps and preserves homotopies and composites, so
$\Gamma(T,I^\bullet)$ and $\Gamma(T,J^\bullet)$ are chain-homotopy
equivalent complexes of abelian groups. Chain-homotopy equivalent complexes
have isomorphic cohomology in every degree, so $\mathcal
H^q(\Gamma(T,I^\bullet))\cong\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(T,J^\bullet))$ for all $q$.
These cohomology groups are the groups $H^q(T_{\Et},F)$ of
[def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], which is therefore independent of the
resolution, the resolutions being those of
[def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions].

The equivalence relation of [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category] is
reflexive, symmetric, and transitive. Transport is additive and obeys
$(u_N)_P=u_P$ for $M\subset N\subset P$. The common-stage operations are
representative-independent and make $\mathcal P_T$ an additive category.
Every finite diagram of objects, morphisms, composites, and asserted
equalities in $\mathcal P_T$ is represented over one finite field, and an
asserted equality holds exactly when it holds after passage to a further
common stage.

Define
$$
 (E,K)[1]=(E,K[1])
$$
and, for $f=[M,u]:(E,K)\to(F,L)$, define
$$
 f[1]=\left[M,
 \sigma_{M/F,L}^{-1}\circ u[1]\circ\sigma_{M/E,K}\right].
$$
This gives a well-defined additive autoequivalence $[1]$ with inverse
$[-1]$, and every finite-stage inclusion
$j_E:\mathcal C_E(T)\to\mathcal P_T$ commutes with shifts through the
specified comparison.

*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this form: the ledger's
verified entries contain no filtered-colimit category, and the blueprint
adds the common-stage calculus, in which every finite diagram and every
asserted equality in $\mathcal P_T$ is represented over one finite
coefficient field. The nearest entries, each fetched and quoted, are
Definition 4.21.1 ([Tag 00D3](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00D3),
the directed-set condition satisfied by the poset $\mathsf{FinExt}_\ell$)
and Lemma 4.21.5 ([Tag 0032](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0032))
with Remark 4.21.6 ([Tag
09P8](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09P8)). Difference: Stacks
computes the colimit of a diagram in one fixed category, whereas the colimit
here indexes a category, so addition, composition, shifts and finitely many
asserted equalities must first be transported to one common stage.

## Proof

The relation of [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category] is reflexive and
symmetric from the definitions, and transitive: if $(M,u)\sim(N,v)$ and
$(N,v)\sim(Q,w)$ with witnesses $P_1,P_2$, transport all to their compositum
$P$, where both equalities hold by the transport formula $(u_N)_P=u_P$ and
the unit/associator equations of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. The same
formula shows that transport is additive and satisfies $(u_N)_P=u_P$ for
$M\subset N\subset P$ (the associator cocycle), so addition, negatives,
identities and composition, computed after transport to one common finite
field, are independent of the representatives and of the field; the
finite-stage additive category laws transported to a common field (with
$T_{F/E}$ additive) make $\mathcal P_T$ an additive category. Every finite
diagram is represented over one finite field by transporting objects and
morphisms (via the $\gamma$-isomorphisms of
[def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]), and a finite list of asserted
equalities holds in $\mathcal P_T$ exactly when the transported equalities
hold over a further common stage, by the definition of the equivalence. For
the shift: equivalent representatives define equivalent shifted
representatives by naturality of $\sigma$ and the associator equations of
[prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], so $[1]$ and $[-1]$ are well-defined
additive endofunctors, $[1]$ has inverse $[-1]$ (the finite-stage shift
laws), and the inclusion $j_E$ commutes with the shifts through the
specified comparison.

Let $u:U\to V$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated and let
$L\in\Dplus(U_{\Et},\Lambda)$. There is a natural isomorphism

$$
 \nu_V^*Ru_{\Et,*}L
 \xrightarrow{\sim}
 Ru_{\Proet,*}\nu_U^*L.
$$

It is compatible with identities, composites, and morphisms of $L$.

## Proof

Specify the map before proving it invertible. By the pullback identification
of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], the counit for the etale adjunction
gives

$$
 u_{\Proet}^*\nu_V^*Ru_{\Et,*}L
 \simeq\nu_U^*u_{\Et}^*Ru_{\Et,*}L
 \longrightarrow\nu_U^*L.
$$

Its mate under the adjunction of the pro-etale operations is the map
$\alpha_L$ in the statement. Both sides are bounded below; inverse images are
exact and right derived direct images preserve lower bounds.

The assertion is local on $V$, so take $V$ affine. Let $W=\varprojlim_i W_i$
be an arbitrary affine ind-etale basis object, with $W_i\to V$ affine etale
of finite presentation, and put $U_i=U\times_VW_i$, $U_W=U\times_VW$. The
schemes $U_i$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated because $u$ is, and their
transition maps are affine. Pullback compatibility and
[lem-weil-pbc-comparison-global-cohomology] identify the degree-$n$ derived
sections of the source with

$$
 H^nR\Gamma\bigl(W_{\Et},(Ru_{\Et,*}L)|_W\bigr).
$$

Apply the continuity of derived cohomology first on $W=\varprojlim_iW_i$ and
then on $U_W=\varprojlim_iU_i$. They give the two outer identifications in

$$
 \begin{split}
 H^nR\Gamma\bigl(W_{\Et},(Ru_{\Et,*}L)|_W\bigr)
 &\simeq\varinjlim_i
       H^nR\Gamma\bigl(W_{i,\Et},(Ru_{\Et,*}L)|_{W_i}\bigr)\\
 &\simeq\varinjlim_i H^nR\Gamma(U_{i,\Et},L|_{U_i})\\
 &\simeq H^nR\Gamma(U_{W,\Et},L|_{U_W}).
 \end{split}
$$

The middle identification is derived evaluation of the direct image. Indeed
an injective resolution on $U_{\Et}$ restricts to an injective resolution on
$U_i$ by the etale-restriction lemma; direct image preserves injectives since
its inverse image is exact. Evaluation of that resolution gives precisely the
same section complex on the two sides.

By [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-global-cohomology], the last group is
$H^nR\Gamma(U_{W,\Proet},(\nu_U^*L)|_{U_W})$. By
[lem-weil-pbc-proetale-restriction-injectives], this in turn is

$$
 H^nR\Gamma(W_{\Proet},Ru_{\Proet,*}\nu_U^*L),
$$

the derived sections of the target. For this last equality use a pro-etale
injective resolution on $U$; its restriction to $U_W$ is injective, and its
direct image is injective because $u_{\Proet}^*$ is exact.

We check that the isomorphism just calculated is induced by $\alpha_L$.
Represent $L$ by an etale injective complex $I^\bullet$, and resolve
$\nu_U^*I^\bullet$ by a pro-etale injective complex $J^\bullet$. The mate is
represented by the map $\nu_V^*u_{\Et,*}I^\bullet\to u_{\Proet,*}J^\bullet$
adjoint to the pulled-back counit followed by $\nu_U^*I^\bullet\to
J^\bullet$. Each $u_{\Et,*}I^r$ is injective on $V_{\Et}$. Hence
[lem-weil-pbc-comparison-injective-acyclicity] makes $\nu_V^*u_{\Et,*}I^r$
acyclic for sections on every basis object $W$. Bounded-below acyclic
resolutions thus allow derived sections of the source to be computed by
evaluating this very complex; the target complex is already injective.
Moreover [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-sections] identifies its source section
complex with $\varinjlim_i\Gamma(U_i,I^\bullet)$. This justifies checking the
named map on these models. At a finite stage $W_i$, evaluation of that counit
is the identity on sections of $I^\bullet$ on $U_i$. Restricting to $W$ gives
exactly the canonical restriction from $U_i$ to $U_W$ followed by the global
cohomology comparison. The identifications above are natural in these
restriction maps. On taking the filtered colimit they therefore compute
$H^nR\Gamma(W,\alpha_L)$, not an unspecified isomorphism between the same
groups.

Thus $\alpha_L$ is an isomorphism on derived sections of every basis object,
in every degree. [lem-weil-pbc-basis-derived-detection] proves it is an
isomorphism of complexes. For identity morphisms its defining mate is the
identity. For a composite, the counit is the composite of the two counits
after the usual associativity identifications; applying the displayed mate
formula gives the composite of the two comparison maps. The triangle
identities remove the inserted unit--counit pairs. This proves the
composition law, while naturality in $L$ follows from naturality of the
counit and the coherent pullback identification. See
[Stacks Project, Section 61.19](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099R)
for the comparison's standard setting.

Let $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{h}Z$ be proper. If $\mathrm{IA}(f)$ and
$\mathrm{IA}(h)$ hold, then $\mathrm{IA}(hf)$ and hence $\mathrm{PBC}(hf)$
hold.

## Proof

After an arbitrary base change $c:Z'\to Z$, write $Y'=Y\times_ZZ'$,
$X'=X\times_ZZ'$, with projections $b:Y'\to Y$ and $a:X'\to X$, and
base-changed maps $f'$, $h'$. Let $I$ be injective in $\mathbf F_r$-module
sheaves on $X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-preserves-injectives] the sheaf
$f_*I$ is injective on $Y$. $\mathrm{IA}_r(f)$ gives $R^qf'_*a^{-1}I=0$ for
$q>0$, and the underived proper exchange identifies $f'_*a^{-1}I\cong
b^{-1}f_*I$; $\mathrm{IA}_r(h)$ applied to the injective $f_*I$ makes this
sheaf $h'_*$-acyclic. The Grothendieck spectral sequence of
[lem-weil-pbc-grothendieck-spectral-sequence] therefore vanishes in every
positive total degree, giving $\mathrm{IA}_r(hf)$, and $\mathrm{PBC}(hf)$ by
the equivalence between $\mathrm{PBC}$ and $\mathrm{IA}$ recorded with
[def-weil-pbc-property].

If $M\subset N$, exactness of $T_{N/M}$ identifies the scalar extension of a
cone triangle for $u$ with a cone triangle for $u_N$. If two representatives
define the same morphism of $\mathcal P_T$, their cone triangles become
isomorphic after passage to a field where the representatives agree. Any two
cone triangles selected for one finite-stage morphism are isomorphic by a
morphism of triangles whose first two components are identities. Thus
distinguishedness in [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones] is independent of
every representative, common field, and cone choice.

*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this independence: the
blueprint adds the proof that distinguishedness of a common-stage triangle
is independent of the representative, the common field and the chosen cone,
which is what makes the pair category a triangulated category below. The
fixed-category input is Stacks': Lemma 13.4.7 ([Tag
014B](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/014B), fetched and quoted) states
that a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of a pre-triangulated category has a
distinguished triangle $(X,Y,Z,f,g,h)$ unique up to (nonunique) isomorphism
of triangles, more precisely that a second such triangle is related to the
first by an isomorphism $(1,1,c)$ — exactly the assertion that two cone
triangles are isomorphic by a morphism of triangles with identity on source
and target — with Lemma 13.4.3 ([Tag
014A](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/014A), if two of the three
components of a morphism of distinguished triangles are isomorphisms so is
the third). Difference: 014B is internal to one pre-triangulated category,
whereas the blueprint must also compare the cone triangles of the scalar
extensions $T_{N/M}$ and of different representatives of one morphism of
$\mathcal P_T$.

## Proof

For $M\subset N$, the functor $T_{N/M}$ of
[prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] is exact and its shift comparison carries
the cone triangle for $u$ in $\mathcal C_M$ to a distinguished triangle of
$\mathcal C_N$ which is a cone triangle for $u_N$, identifying the scalar
extension of the first with a cone triangle of the second. If
$(M,u)\sim(N,v)$, then $u_P=v_P$ for some finite $P$, and transporting the
two cone triangles to $P$ via the transport of
[prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus] and the $\sigma$-comparisons of
[prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] makes them isomorphic over $P$ by the
finite-stage axiom TR3, with identity components on the common source and
target; any two cone triangles selected for one finite-stage morphism are
isomorphic by a morphism of triangles whose first two components are
identities (the finite-stage uniqueness of cones up to noncanonical
isomorphism). Combining these facts, distinguishedness in
[def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones] is independent of the representative, of
the common field and of the cone choice, in the sense of the category of
[def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category].

objects.body:
Let $\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T)$ be the tower category of
[def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and let $M_\bullet\in
D(\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T))$. If $M_\bullet\to I_\bullet$ is a K-injective
resolution [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions] of $M_\bullet$ in the
abelian category of towers, then $\varprojlim_nI_n$ represents the sequential
derived inverse limit $\Rlim M_\bullet$ of
[def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit].

(*Source note:* the model statement is Stacks Project, Derived Categories,
Lemma 13.34.6 (Tag [070M](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/070M)): for a
complex $K^\bullet$ and the inverse system $I_n^\bullet$ of bounded below
complexes of injectives produced by Lemma 13.29.3,
$I^\bullet=\lim_nI_n^\bullet$ exists, is K-injective, and represents
$R\lim_n\tau_{\ge-n}K^\bullet$; existence of the derived limit is Lemma
13.34.3 (Tag [0BK7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BK7)), and
functorial K-injective resolutions in a Grothendieck abelian category are
Theorem 19.12.6 (Tag [079P](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/079P)).
Stacks treats the truncation tower of a single complex of $D(\mathcal A)$,
whereas the form used here resolves an arbitrary object of
$\operatorname{Tow}_A(T)$ in the abelian category of towers over
$T_{\Proet}$; that general-tower form is the one already recorded in the
conventions chapter.)

## Proof

By [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit] the object $\Rlim M_\bullet$ is the
derived limit of the inverse system $(\operatorname{ev}_nM_\bullet)$ in the
triangulated category $D(T_{\Proet},A)$ attached to the tower category of
[def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], an abelian category with exact
countable products. Clause (3) of the derived-limit existence lemma of the
conventions chapter states that a K-injective representative of the system in
the abelian category of towers represents its derived limit; applying it to
the system $(\operatorname{ev}_nM_\bullet)$ and its K-injective
representative $I_\bullet$ exhibits $\varprojlim_nI_n$ as a derived limit of
the system, and clause (1) of the same lemma shows that any two derived
limits of one system are isomorphic.

attrs.title: Computation of the sequential derived inverse limit

objects.body:
Let $\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T)$ be the tower category of
[def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and let $M_\bullet\in
D(\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T))$ with a K-injective resolution
[def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions] $M_\bullet\to I_\bullet$ in the abelian
category of towers. Then the derived product $R\!\prod_nM_n$ of
[def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit] is represented by
$\prod_n\operatorname{ev}_n(I_\bullet)$.

(*Source note:* the representing complex is Stacks Project, Derived
Categories, Lemma 13.31.5 (Tag
[0BK6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BK6)): if the $I_t^\bullet$ are
K-injective complexes and $I^n=\prod_tI_t^n$ exists for all $n$, then
$I^\bullet$ is K-injective and represents the product of the $I_t^\bullet$ in
$D(\mathcal A)$; the termwise description of products is Lemma 13.34.2 (Tag
[07KC](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07KC)). Stacks states this for an
arbitrary index set in one abelian category; the form used here applies it to
the levelwise K-injective representatives of the evaluations of one tower
object, the products being taken in the tower category
$\operatorname{Tow}_A(T)$ and the result being read in $D(T_{\Proet},A)$.)

## Proof

By [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit] the derived product $R\!\prod_nM_n$
is the product of the system $(\operatorname{ev}_nM_\bullet)$ in the
triangulated category $D(T_{\Proet},A)$ attached to the tower category of
[def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Clause (2) of the derived-limit
existence lemma of the conventions chapter states that in the derived
category of an abelian category with exact countable products the countable
products exist and are represented by termwise products of any
representatives, and clause (3) of the same lemma exhibits
$\prod_n\operatorname{ev}_n(I_\bullet)$ as the termwise product of the
K-injective representatives $\operatorname{ev}_n(I_\bullet)$ of the objects
$\operatorname{ev}_nM_\bullet$; hence that product represents
$R\!\prod_nM_n$.

attrs.title: Representation of the derived product of a tower

objects.body:
Let $\Phi_E:\mathcal C_E(T)\to\mathcal C_E(S)$ be exact functors and let
$$
 \beta_{F/E}:T^S_{F/E}\Phi_E
 \xrightarrow{\sim}\Phi_FT^T_{F/E}
$$
be exact natural isomorphisms satisfying the unit, associator, and shift
equations of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. Then they induce an exact
functor $\Phi:\mathcal P_T\to\mathcal P_S$. On a representative
$u:T^T_{M/E}K\to T^T_{M/F}L$, its value is represented by
$$
 T^S_{M/E}\Phi_EK\xrightarrow{\beta_{M/E}}
 \Phi_MT^T_{M/E}K\xrightarrow{\Phi_M(u)}
 \Phi_MT^T_{M/F}L\xrightarrow{\beta_{M/F}^{-1}}
 T^S_{M/F}\Phi_FL.
$$
This functor is, by [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], already a functor on the
$\Qlb$ coefficient categories $\Dbc(T,\Qlb)=\mathcal P_T$ and
$\Dbc(S,\Qlb)=\mathcal P_S$. Compatible natural transformations and their
equations descend by the same formula.

In particular, the scalar-compatible families $(Rf_{*,E})_E$ and
$(Lg_E^*)_E$ descend to exact functors on $\Qlb$ coefficient categories, and
the finite-stage exchange maps descend to a natural transformation.

*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this descent of functors: the
ledger's verified entries contain no filtered-colimit-of-categories
statement — the nearest, the Chapter 61 coefficient entries 09BS, 09BT, 09C1
and 09C7, work with one fixed Noetherian coefficient ring — and the
blueprint adds the descent of scalar-compatible exact functors and of their
natural transformations to the $\Qlb$ coefficient categories, together with
the descended direct images, pullbacks and exchange maps. The closest
descent statements in Stacks, each fetched and quoted, are the universal
properties of a localization and of a Verdier quotient: Lemma 13.5.7 ([Tag
05R7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05R7), an exact functor out of
$\mathcal D$ that inverts the multiplicative system factors uniquely and
exactly through $S^{-1}\mathcal D$) and Lemma 13.6.8 ([Tag
05RJ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05RJ), the same for the quotient
$\mathcal D/\mathcal B$ by a full triangulated subcategory), with Definition
13.6.1 ([Tag 05RB](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05RB), saturated,
