i.e. thick, triangulated subcategory) and Definition 13.6.7 ([Tag
05RI](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05RI),
$\mathcal D/\mathcal B=S^{-1}\mathcal D$). Difference: a localization or
quotient inverts a multiplicative system inside one category and its
factorization needs no further data, whereas $\mathcal P_T$ is a filtered
colimit of categories and the functors descend with the explicit
$\beta$-isomorphisms of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension].

## Proof

Define $\Phi(E,K)=(E,\Phi_EK)$ on objects and, on a representative $(M,u)$,
by the displayed composite in $\mathcal C_M(S)$. The value is independent of
$M$: for $M\subset N$ the $\beta$-isomorphisms transport the composite for
$u$ to the composite for $u_N$, using the unit and associator equations of
[prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] which the $\beta$'s satisfy; equivalent
representatives give equal composites at the witnessing stage by those
equations, so $\Phi$ is well defined on the morphisms of
[def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]. It is additive, the composites
being exact functors and exact natural isomorphisms of exact natural
transformations, and exact (finite-stage exactness of the $\Phi_E$ and the
$T$'s makes the composite exact on distinguished triangles); natural
transformations and their equations descend by that formula by the
equivariance with the $\beta$'s. By [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] this is
already the descent to the $\Qlb$ coefficient categories
($\Dbc(T,\Qlb)=\mathcal P_T$ and $\Dbc(S,\Qlb)=\mathcal P_S$); no extension
to an envelope is needed. The families $(Rf_{*,E})_E$ and $(Lg_E^*)_E$ carry
the scalar-extension isomorphisms of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] as the
data $\beta$, so they descend to exact functors on the $\Qlb$ coefficient
categories, and the finite-stage exchange maps, being compatible with scalar
extension, descend to a natural transformation.

Levelwise direct image on tower categories has a total right derived functor

$$
 Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}:
 D(\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(X))
 \longrightarrow D(\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(Y)),
$$

with $\operatorname{ev}_nRf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}M_\bullet\simeq Rf_*M_n$.
For every $M_\bullet$ the canonical map

$$
 Rf_*\Rlim M_\bullet
 \xrightarrow{\sim}
 \Rlim\bigl(Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}M_\bullet\bigr)
$$

is an isomorphism. Under the two canonical Roos triangles associated with the
derived inverse-limit [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit] construction, it
is induced by the canonical isomorphisms

$$
 Rf_*R\!\prod_nM_n\xrightarrow{\sim}
 R\!\prod_nRf_*M_n
$$

and their commutation with $(1-s)$. If $K\in D(X_{\Proet},A)$ is derived
$I$-complete, then $Rf_*K$ is derived $I$-complete. For every $n\geq1$, the
projection-formula morphism

$$
 (Rf_*K)\otimes_A^LP_n\longrightarrow Rf_*(K\otimes_A^LP_n)
$$

is a functorial isomorphism

$$
 (Rf_*K)\otimes_A^LP_n
 \xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*(K\otimes_A^LP_n)=Rf_*K_n,
$$

and these isomorphisms commute with $P_{n+1}\to P_n$. Under them, the
completion map for $Rf_*K$ is the composite

$$
 Rf_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*\Rlim K_\bullet
 \xrightarrow{\sim}\Rlim Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}K_\bullet.
$$

The commutation $Rf_*\Rlim\xrightarrow{\sim}\Rlim Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}$
and the completeness of $Rf_*K$ for derived complete $K$ are clauses (1), (3)
and (4) of Stacks Project, Lemma 61.20.2 (Tag
[099N](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099N), Section 61.20, Tag
[099L](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099L)): the Stacks entry assumes
a Noetherian ring $\Lambda$, an ideal $I\subset\Lambda$ and a morphism of
topoi, and states that $Rf_*$ sends $D_{comp}$ into $D_{comp}$ and that
$Rf_*K=\Rlim Rf_*(K\otimes^L_\Lambda\underline{\Lambda/I^n})$; the form used
here is its tower-level refinement over $T_{\Proet}$, and the finite-level
projection-formula isomorphisms coming from
[lemma-weil-pbc-perfect-projection-formula] are not part of the Stacks
statement.

## Proof

The tower category of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] is Grothendieck
abelian with exact evaluation functors, so levelwise K-injective resolutions
(also with respect to the K-injective presentation of
[def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit]) give the total right derived functor
$Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}$ with
$\operatorname{ev}_nRf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}M_\bullet\simeq Rf_*M_n$.
Applying $Rf_*$ to the canonical Roos triangle of
[prop-weil-pbc-roos-triangle] for $M_\bullet$ and comparing with the Roos
triangle for $Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}M_\bullet$, using that the derived
products commute with $Rf_*$ (they are the products of the levelwise
K-injective resolutions and direct image is a right adjoint, hence
product-preserving) and with $(1-s)$, identifies the two triangles and gives
the displayed isomorphism $Rf_*\Rlim M_\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}
\Rlim(Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}M_\bullet)$. If $K$ is derived $I$-complete
then, applied to the tower $K_\bullet$, this shows $Rf_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}
\Rlim Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}K_\bullet$, so $Rf_*K$ is derived
$I$-complete; [lemma-weil-pbc-perfect-projection-formula] supplies the
projection-formula isomorphisms
$(Rf_*K)\otimes_A^LP_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*(K\otimes_A^LP_n)=Rf_*K_n$ of
[def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-map], commuting with $P_{n+1}\to P_n$ by the
normalization data of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]; under them the
completion map for $Rf_*K$ is the displayed composite.

attrs.title: Direct image, derived limits, and completeness

objects.body:
Every finite morphism satisfies $\mathsf{PBC}$.

## Proof

The finite exchange lemma supplies the required isomorphism for every base
change and every torsion sheaf, which is exactly Definition
[def-weil-pbc-property]. Equivalently, the vanishing in the exactness
lemma gives $\mathsf{IA}$ and Lemma [lemma-weil-pbc-property-iff-acyclicity]
gives $\mathsf{PBC}$.

## Detailed form

Every finite morphism $f$ satisfies $\mathrm{PBC}(f)$ in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-property].

## Proof

Finite morphisms and all their base changes are finite, so
[lemma-weil-pbc-finite-exchange] supplies the canonical exchange isomorphism for
every base change and every torsion sheaf, which is the definition of
$\mathrm{PBC}(f)$ by [def-weil-pbc-property].

attrs.title: Finite morphisms satisfy proper base change

objects.body:
For an affine henselian pair $(T,T_0)$ and torsion $F$,
$H^q(T,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(T_0,F_0)$ for all $q\geq0$.

## Proof

Degree zero is the etale henselian restriction lemma applied on the affine.
For $q>0$, assume comparison in all degrees below $q$. To prove injectivity,
take a nonzero $\xi\in H^q(T,F)$ and apply effacement with closed subscheme
$T$ itself, obtaining $F\hookrightarrow F'$ in which $\xi$ dies. Put
$Q=F'/F$. Exactness lifts $\xi$ from $H^{q-1}(T,Q)$. The induction
isomorphism in degree $q-1$ carries any such lift to $T_0$; if $\xi$ restricted
to zero, exactness and the commutative boundary square would force the lift
to come from $H^{q-1}(T,F')$, contradicting the choice of nonzero $\xi$.

For surjectivity, take $\eta\in H^q(T_0,F_0)$ and use effacement with closed
subscheme $T_0$ to choose $F\hookrightarrow F'$ killing $\eta$. Exactness
lifts $\eta$ from $H^{q-1}(T_0,Q_0)$. By induction this lift is the
restriction of a class in $H^{q-1}(T,Q)$, whose boundary in $H^q(T,F)$
restricts to $\eta$. Thus the comparison is separately injective and
surjective. This expands Tag `09ZI`; no statement is imported from
that tag.

## Detailed form

Let $(A,I)$ be an affine henselian pair and let $X$ be an affine scheme of
finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}A$, with closed fibre
$X_0=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$. Then for every
torsion etale sheaf $F$ on $X$,

$$
 H^q(X,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(X_0,F_0)
 \qquad(q\geq0).
$$

The case $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is the comparison for the affine henselian
pair $(T,T_0)=(\operatorname{Spec}A,\operatorname{Spec}(A/I))$ itself. The
relative form is the one used below: the affine charts of a finite-type
$A$-scheme are affine of finite type over $A$, but they are *not* themselves
henselian pairs, so the pair form alone does not apply to them.

**Status.** This is the cited Gabber input (Stacks Project, Theorem 59.82.7,
Tag [09ZI](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09ZI)); its formal
consequences are proved below in this section. The former effacement
statements of this chapter were retired, since no proof uses them.

## Proof

The statement is the input recorded in the reference: the Gabber comparison
for affine henselian pairs, i.e. that for an affine henselian pair $(T,T_0)$
and a torsion etale sheaf $F$ on $T$, the restriction map $H^q(T,F)\to
H^q(T_0,F_0)$ is an isomorphism for every $q\geq0$ (Stacks Project, Theorem
59.82.7, Tag [09ZI](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09ZI)). Its proof is
the effacement argument: by induction on $q$, classes of degree $q>0$ are
killed by the effacement step, giving injectivity, and the induction step
builds the extension of classes of degree $q-1$ from $T_0$ to $T$, giving
surjectivity. The blueprint isolates this single assertion, proves separately
its formal consequences (degree-zero comparisons over henselian pairs, and the
acyclicity bound for restricted injectives), and does not discharge it here.

For every geometric point $\bar t$ of $T$, the stalk functor $F\mapsto
F_{\bar t}$ of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]

$$
 \Ab(T_{\Et})\longrightarrow\Ab,\qquad F\longmapsto F_{\bar t}
$$

is exact (filtered colimits are exact and a stalk is a filtered colimit of
sections over pointed etale neighbourhoods).

## Proof

By [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] the stalk $F_{\bar t}$ is the filtered
colimit of the section groups over pointed etale neighbourhoods. The category
of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] on $T_{\Et}$ is Grothendieck abelian, so
filtered colimits of sheaves are exact: kernels and images of the colimit are
the colimits of the kernels and images. Applied to a short exact sequence
$0\to F\to G\to H\to0$ this gives exactness of the sequence of colimits over
the filtered index category of pointed neighbourhoods on the kernel and image
parts, and for the cokernel part a section of $H$ over a pointed
neighbourhood which lifts over an etale cover of it still represents a
section of the filtered colimit after composing the index with a pointed
etale refinement; hence the sequence of stalks is exact.

In the setting of [thm-weil-pbc-integral-truncations], set
$$
 (\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A))^{\le0}:=\{K:\mathcal H^i(K)=0\ \forall i>0\},
$$
$$
 (\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A))^{\ge0}:=\{K:\mathcal H^i(K)=0\ \forall i<0\}.
$$
These form a bounded t-structure on $\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)$, whose truncation
functors are the $\tau^{\le m},\tau^{\ge m}$ of
[thm-weil-pbc-integral-truncations] and whose heart consists of the objects
with cohomology concentrated in degree zero. The subcategory of
$\varpi$-power-torsion objects is stable under the truncation functors.

*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this form: Stacks defines no
t-structure and no heart, and what it does provide is the truncation
triangle
$\tau_{\le a}K^\bullet\to K^\bullet\to\tau_{\ge a+1}K^\bullet\to(\tau_{\le a}K^\bullet)[1]$
of a complex of an abelian category, Remark 13.12.4 ([Tag
08J5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08J5)) with Section 12.15 ([Tag
0118](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0118)). The blueprint adds the
standard t-structure on the derived complete category, its identification
with the truncations of [thm-weil-pbc-integral-truncations] and the
stability of the $\varpi$-power-torsion subcategory.

## Proof

The shift conditions and the orthogonality of a t-structure, namely
$\Hom(A,B[-1])=0$ for $A\in(\Dbc)^{\le0}$, $B\in(\Dbc)^{\ge0}$, are the
corresponding ambient statements for the standard t-structure of
$D(T_{\Proet},A)$, since $\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)$ is a full subcategory and its
objects' cohomology sheaves are the ambient ones. The truncation axiom and
the truncation triangles are [thm-weil-pbc-integral-truncations] (ii)--(iii)
with the cohomology formulas of (ii) showing the end terms to lie in the
claimed subcategories. Boundedness: by the reconstruction lemma for uniform
towers (and its use in [thm-weil-pbc-integral-truncations]), an object's
local models are supported in a finite interval $[d_0,d_1]$, so its
cohomology vanishes outside it; the interval is part of the data of
[def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]. Finally the truncation
functors are additive and $A_T$-linear, so if $\varpi^n\cdot1_K=0$ in
$\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)$, then
$\varpi^n\cdot1_{\tau^{\le m}K}=\tau^{\le m}(\varpi^n\cdot1_K)=0$, and
similarly for $\tau^{\ge m+1}$.

attrs.title: The standard t-structure on the integral category

objects.body:
For a morphism [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] $u:U\to V$ of schemes, the
inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]

$$
 u^{-1}:\Ab(V_{\Et})\longrightarrow\Ab(U_{\Et})
$$

of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] is an exact functor.

## Proof

By [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] the functor $u^{-1}$ is the left adjoint of
the direct image $u_*$ of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and is obtained by
sheafifying the presheaf inverse image along the functor $U_{\Et}\to V_{\Et}$
of [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. The presheaf inverse image is computed
sectionwise by a filtered colimit of sections of the given presheaf; it has a
left adjoint (extension by zero of presheaves) and a right adjoint (presheaf
direct image), so it preserves kernels and cokernels and is exact.
Sheafification of presheaves of abelian groups is exact (Stacks Project,
Lemma 7.10.15, Tag [00WJ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00WJ)), and a
composite of exact functors is exact, so $u^{-1}$ is exact. This is the
exactness of pullback of abelian sheaves on small etale sites (Stacks
Project, Lemma 59.36.2, Tag
[03Q1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03Q1)); the source category is
the category of sheaves of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves].

Every complex in $\mathsf{Cpx}(\Mod(T_{\Et},R))$ admits a K-injective
resolution $K\to I$, functorially up to chain homotopy; two K-injective
resolutions of one object are chain-homotopy equivalent, and a bounded-below
complex of injective objects is K-injective.

## Proof

The category of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] is Grothendieck abelian; the
existence of a K-injective resolution of every complex, functorially up to
chain homotopy, and the chain-homotopy equivalence of any two K-injective
resolutions of the same object are the theorem on K-injective complexes in
Grothendieck abelian categories (Stacks Project,
[Theorem 19.12.6, Tag 079P](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/079P)) in
the formulation of [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions]. A bounded-below
complex $I$ of injective objects is K-injective: for $A$ acyclic, the
spectral sequence of the double complex
$\operatorname{Hom}(A^\bullet,I^\bullet)$ has the
$\operatorname{Hom}(A^\bullet,I^q)$ rows acyclic, since
$\operatorname{Hom}(-,I^q)$ is exact as $I^q$ is injective and $A$ is
acyclic, so $\operatorname{Hom}(A,I)$ is acyclic.

For the strict quotient tower $K_\bullet$ of
[def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] there is a functorial isomorphism

$$
 K^{\wedge}_{\mathrm{Kos}}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Rlim K_\bullet
$$

carrying the Koszul completion map to the quotient-tower completion map
$K\to\Rlim K_\bullet$. Every derived $I$-complete object consequently
satisfies

$$
 K\xrightarrow{\sim}\Rlim K_\bullet.
$$

(*Source: the adic reconstruction, i.e. the identification of the
Koszul-derived completion with the derived limit over the Koszul tower
$K_\bullet(A,f_1^n,\dots,f_r^n)$ of the generators (not over the quotient
tower $A/I^n$, which is not quasi-isomorphic to it in general), is the
derived-completion formalism of Stacks Project, More on Algebra, Section
15.93 (Derived Completion), Tag
[091N](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/091N), with Lemma 15.93.17, Tag
[091Z](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/091Z). The same identification
over the quotient tower, in the constant Noetherian case, is Stacks Project,
Lemma 61.20.1 (Tag [099M](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099M), Section
61.20, Tag [099L](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099L)), whose proof
passes through the Koszul pro-system $K(\Lambda,f_1^n,\dots,f_r^n)$ and
concludes $K^\wedge=\Rlim(K\otimes^L_\Lambda\underline{\Lambda/I^n})$: the
Stacks entry assumes a Noetherian ring $\Lambda$ and an ideal
$I\subset\Lambda$ on an arbitrary site, while the form used here is the
reconstruction over a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with $A=\mathcal O_E$,
$I=(\varpi)$.*)

## Proof

This is the recorded classical input of the statement, the derived-completion
formalism of Stacks Project, More on Algebra, Section 15.93 (Tag
[091N](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/091N)): the Koszul-derived
completion of a complex and the derived limit over its strict quotient tower
compute the same object, and both completion maps are the canonical ones. The
blueprint uses the identification as the defining property of the adic
coefficient datum of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and gives no
separate proof.

Let the adic datum be $A=\mathcal O_E$, $I=(\varpi)$, with $P_n=A_{E,n}$,
and let $K_\bullet\in D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(T))$ be an adic tower (an
object with normalization isomorphisms
$K_{n+1}\otimes^L_{P_{n+1}}P_n\xrightarrow{\sim}K_n$ satisfying the quotient
cocycle), given by a K-flat representative $QK$ of a single object $K$ of
the underlying pro-etale complex category, $K_n=QK\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_n)_T$.
Then for every $m\in\mathbf Z$:

1. the levelwise truncations
   $$
    \tau^{\le m}K_\bullet:=(\tau^{\le m}K_n)_n,\qquad
    \tau^{\ge m+1}K_\bullet:=(\tau^{\ge m+1}K_n)_n,
   $$
   of the levelwise t-structure of $D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(T))$ (whose
   evaluations are the levelwise canonical truncations of the strict-tower
   representatives) are adic towers, with canonical normalization
   isomorphisms
   $$
    \tau^{\le m}K_{n+1}\otimes^L_{P_{n+1}}P_n
    \xrightarrow{\sim}\tau^{\le m}K_n,\qquad
    \tau^{\ge m+1}K_{n+1}\otimes^L_{P_{n+1}}P_n
    \xrightarrow{\sim}\tau^{\ge m+1}K_n
   $$
   satisfying the quotient cocycle, *provided* the following
   Tor-compatibility condition (1) holds: for every $n$ and every $q\ge m+1$
   the canonical morphism
   $$
    \mathcal H^q(K_{n+1})\otimes^L_{P_{n+1}}P_n
    \longrightarrow\mathcal H^q(K_n)
   $$
   is an isomorphism.

   By the Künneth spectral sequence of the Koszul triangle,
   $$
    E_2^{p,q}=\operatorname{Tor}_p^{P_{n+1}}
    \bigl(\mathcal H^q(K_{n+1}),P_n\bigr)\Rightarrow
    \mathcal H^{q-p}(K_n),
   $$
   condition (1) is precisely the vanishing of the higher Tor-terms
   $\operatorname{Tor}_p^{P_{n+1}}(\mathcal H^q(K_{n+1}),P_n)$, $p\ge1$, in
   the range $q\ge m+1$, i.e. the vanishing of the Künneth obstruction of
   the reduction morphism above level $m$. A sufficient condition is that
   the cohomology sheaves $\mathcal H^i(K)$ of the ambient object
   (equivalently, of the local models) be $\varpi$-torsion-free (over the
   discrete valuation ring $A_T$ equivalently flat) for all $i\ge m+1$,
   because then
   $\mathcal H^q(K_{n+1})=\mathcal H^q(K)\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_{n+1})_T$ has no
   higher $\varpi$-torsion and the morphism of (1) is the identity on
   $(\mathcal H^q(K)/\varpi^{n+1})\otimes^L_{P_{n+1}}P_n$.

   *In general the levelwise truncations are not adic towers*: the failure
   is exactly the Tor-contribution. For instance, for
   $K=(A_T/\varpi)[-(m+1)]$ (a single shift of the constant
   $\varpi$-torsion sheaf) one has
   $$
    K_n=K\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_n)_T
    =\bigl((A_T/\varpi)\oplus(A_T/\varpi)[1]\bigr)[-(m+1)]
   $$
   for every $n\ge1$ — the two-term Koszul resolution of $(P_n)_T$ over
   $A_T$ gives
   $\operatorname{Tor}_1^{A_T}(A_T/\varpi,(P_n)_T)=A_T/\varpi$ — and hence
   $\tau^{\le m}K_n=(A_T/\varpi)[-m]$ for every $n$, whereas
   $$
    (\tau^{\le m}K_{n+1})\otimes^L_{P_{n+1}}P_n
    =\bigl((A_T/\varpi)\otimes^L_{P_{n+1}}P_n\bigr)[-m],
   $$
   whose cohomology is $A_T/\varpi$ in *every* degree $\le m$ (since
   $\operatorname{Tor}_i^{P_{n+1}}(A_T/\varpi,P_n)=A_T/\varpi$ for all
   $i\ge0$, $n\ge1$); this is not $(A_T/\varpi)[-m]$, so the levelwise
   truncated tower $\tau^{\le m}K_\bullet$ fails to be an adic tower.

   Statements (i) and (ii) are therefore asserted under the
   Tor-compatibility condition (1); statement (iii) holds unconditionally,
   being a formal property of the canonical truncations. The levelwise form
   is recorded here as the natural algebraic preparation of the
   derived-limit statement for the completed category, where the condition
   is imposed as an explicit hypothesis; the sufficient condition recorded
   above is that the cohomology sheaves of the local models be flat over
   $A_T$, which is strictly stronger than finiteness of the terms of the
   models. *Local freeness of the terms of a model does not imply (1)*: for
   the two-term complex $P_{n+1}\xrightarrow{\ \varpi\ }P_{n+1}$ the terms
   are free while the first cohomology is the torsion module $P_n$, so
   freeness of the terms forces neither torsion-freeness of the cohomology
   nor the vanishing of the higher Tor terms in (1). Condition (1) is
   therefore carried as a hypothesis in (i) and (ii) and is never deduced
   from freeness;
2. if $K_\bullet$ is uniformly bounded constructible, with local models
   $L_{\alpha j}$ supported in $[d_0,d_1]$ and with the isomorphisms
   $K_n|_{U_{\alpha j}}\simeq L_{\alpha j}\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_n)_T$ for every
   $n$, then $\tau^{\le m}K_\bullet$ is uniformly bounded constructible with
   the local models $\tau^{\le m}L_{\alpha j}$ (supported in
   $[\min(d_0,m),m]$), and $\tau^{\ge m+1}K_\bullet$ is uniformly bounded
   constructible with the local models
   $$
    C_{\alpha j}:=\operatorname{Cone}\bigl(\tau^{\le m}L_{\alpha j}
    \longrightarrow L_{\alpha j}\bigr)
   $$
   (supported in $[m+1,d_1]$), the terms of both families of models being
   finite locally free and their reductions having finite lisse cohomology;
3. for every $n$ there are canonical isomorphisms
   $$
    \mathcal H^i\bigl((\tau^{\le m}K_\bullet)_n\bigr)
     \xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^i(K_n)\quad(i\le m),
    \qquad
    \mathcal H^i\bigl((\tau^{\le m}K_\bullet)_n\bigr)=0\quad(i>m),
   $$
   and analogously
   $$
    \mathcal H^i\bigl((\tau^{\ge m+1}K_\bullet)_n\bigr)
     \xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^i(K_n)\quad(i\ge m+1),
    \qquad
    \mathcal H^i\bigl((\tau^{\ge m+1}K_\bullet)_n\bigr)=0\quad(i\le m),
   $$
   compatible with the normalization maps; if the tower carries compatible
   etale-origin witnesses [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]
   $(L_n^{\mathrm{et}},\alpha_n)$, the truncated towers carry the
   compatible witnesses
   $(\tau^{\le m}L_n^{\mathrm{et}},\nu^*\tau^{\le m}\circ\alpha_n)$ and
   $(\tau^{\ge m+1}L_n^{\mathrm{et}},\nu^*\tau^{\ge m+1}\circ\alpha_n)$.

*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this levelwise form. The
truncations used are Stacks': Homological Algebra, Section 12.15 ([Tag
0118](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0118)) defines the canonical
truncations $\tau_{\le m},\tau_{\ge m}$ of a complex of an abelian category
with $H^i(\tau_{\le m}A^\bullet)=H^i(A^\bullet)$ for $i\le m$ and $0$ for
$i>m$ (and dually for $\tau_{\ge m+1}$), and Remark 13.12.4 ([Tag
08J5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08J5)) gives the canonical
truncation triangle in $D(\mathcal A)$. Difference: Stacks truncates
complexes of one fixed abelian category, whereas the statement here is about
the truncation tower of a strict tower of complexes over the varying
coefficient rings $P_n$, and it adds the Tor-compatibility condition (1),
the local models and the compatible etale-origin witnesses. The nearest
constructibility and completion entries are Definition 61.29.1 ([Tag
09C1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C1)), Proposition 61.29.7 ([Tag
09C7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C7)), Lemmas 61.20.1 and
61.20.2 ([Tag 099M](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099M), [Tag
099N](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099N)) and, for the reduction
tower of one constructible object, Lemma 61.29.2 ([Tag
09C2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C2)).

## Proof

The evaluations $\operatorname{ev}_n$ are exact and jointly conservative, so
the levelwise t-structure of $D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(T))$ has the levelwise
canonical truncations of the statement, computed on the strict-tower
representatives.

*Step 1: the normalization isomorphisms of (i).* The derived tensor functor
$-\otimes^L_{P_{n+1}}P_n$ is triangulated, being the left derived functor of
$-\otimes_{P_{n+1}}P_n$ (take a K-flat resolution of $P_n$); tensoring the
truncation triangle of $K_{n+1}$,
$$
 \tau^{\le m}K_{n+1}\longrightarrow K_{n+1}
 \longrightarrow\tau^{\ge m+1}K_{n+1}\longrightarrow
 \tau^{\le m}K_{n+1}[1],
$$
with $P_n$ and using the normalization
$K_{n+1}\otimes^L_{P_{n+1}}P_n\simeq K_n$ gives the triangle
$$
 (\tau^{\le m}K_{n+1})\otimes^L_{P_{n+1}}P_n
 \longrightarrow K_n
 \longrightarrow(\tau^{\ge m+1}K_{n+1})\otimes^L_{P_{n+1}}P_n
 \longrightarrow .
$$
Künneth spectral sequence. For a complex $M$ of $P_{n+1}$-modules there is
the Künneth spectral sequence of the derived tensor
$$
 E_2^{p,q}=\operatorname{Tor}_p^{P_{n+1}}\bigl(\mathcal H^q(M),P_n\bigr)
 \Rightarrow\mathcal H^{q-p}\bigl(M\otimes^L_{P_{n+1}}P_n\bigr).
$$
For $M=\tau^{\le m}K_{n+1}$ one has $\mathcal H^q(M)=0$ for $q>m$, so all
the $E_2$-terms of total degree $>m$ vanish and the first end term of the
triangle has no cohomology above degree $m$. For $M=\tau^{\ge m+1}K_{n+1}$,
the $E_2$-terms of total degree $\le m$ are exactly the higher Tor-terms
$$
 \operatorname{Tor}_p^{P_{n+1}}\bigl(\mathcal H^q(K_{n+1}),P_n\bigr),
 \qquad q\ge m+1,\ p\ge q-m\ge1,
$$
of the cohomology sheaves of degree $\ge m+1$; by the same spectral sequence
applied to $K_{n+1}$, the Tor-compatibility condition (1) of the statement —
whose displayed morphisms are the $p=0$ edge terms in degrees $q\ge m+1$ —
is exactly the vanishing of all these higher Tor-terms (a sufficient
condition being the $\varpi$-torsion-freeness, i.e. flatness over the
discrete valuation ring $A_T$, of the cohomology sheaves $\mathcal H^i(K)$
of the ambient object for $i\ge m+1$, as in the statement; for the towers of
the form $K_n=QK\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_n)_T$ the cohomology sheaves of the models
are then flat over the respective $P_n$ by base change along $A_T\to P_n$).
Under (1) the second end term therefore has no cohomology in degrees $\le m$,
and the triangle above is a truncation triangle of $K_n$; truncation
triangles are unique (a triangle whose end terms, endowed with the displayed
maps, lie in the full subcategories of complexes with cohomology in $\le m$
and $\ge m+1$ respectively is canonically isomorphic to the canonical
truncation triangle of the middle term), so the canonical normalization
isomorphisms of (i) follow, and the cocycle is inherited from the quotient
cocycle of $K_\bullet$. When condition (1) fails, the displayed end terms of
the triangle carry the Tor-contributions of the Künneth spectral sequence in
the wrong degrees, and the composite is in general only a canonical
morphism, not an isomorphism; the counterexample of the statement shows the
failure is real.

*Step 2: the models of (ii).* The local models here are those of the
bounded constructible tower. (Under the Tor-compatibility condition (1),
which the hypotheses of (ii) ensure throughout: the cohomology sheaves of
the local models are the ones of the ambient object.) The terms of
$\tau^{\le m}L_{\alpha j}$ are $L_{\alpha j}^i$ for $i<m$, and $\ker(d^m)$
in degree $m$: after refining the pro-etale covering so that each
$U_{\alpha j}$ is connected, $A_T|_{U_{\alpha j}}$ is the constant completed
valuation ring, over which submodules of finite free modules are finite
free, so the terms are finite locally free. The support and the finite lisse
reduction cohomology of the models follow from the isomorphisms of (iii)
(the reductions of the truncated models have the same cohomology sheaves as
the reductions of $L_{\alpha j}$ in the surviving degrees, by Step 1 applied
locally). The terms of $C_{\alpha j}$ are direct sums of terms of
$L_{\alpha j}$ and of $\tau^{\le m}L_{\alpha j}$, hence finite locally free;
its support is $[m+1,d_1]$, and, being the cone of the model truncation map,
its reductions are constant by the same local computation, since
$$
 C_{\alpha j}\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_n)_T
 \cong\operatorname{Cone}\bigl(
   \tau^{\le m}K_n|_{U_{\alpha j}}\longrightarrow K_n|_{U_{\alpha j}}\bigr)
 \cong\tau^{\ge m+1}K_n|_{U_{\alpha j}}.
$$
The intertwinings with the quotient transition maps are the local forms of
the canonical isomorphisms of (i).

*Step 3: the cohomology isomorphisms and the witnesses of (iii).* The
formulas of (iii) hold by construction of the levelwise truncations of the
strict-tower representatives. Under condition (1), for $i\le m$ the triangle
of Step 1 has end terms with zero cohomology in the relevant degrees, so the
long exact cohomology sequence of the tensored truncation triangle yields
the displayed isomorphisms of (iii) directly (compatible with the
normalization maps of (i) by their canonicality); the etale-origin witnesses
[def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness] are transported by the exactness of the
site-comparison inverse image $\nu^*$
[def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]: for a witness
$K_n\simeq\nu^*L_n^{\mathrm{et}}$ one has
$\tau^{\le m}K_n\simeq\nu^*\tau^{\le m}L_n^{\mathrm{et}}$, and the
normalization compatibility is the naturality of $\nu^*$.

The source records that audit item BC-03 was resolved for this proposition
by carrying the Tor-compatibility condition (1) as an explicit hypothesis
instead of deducing it from freeness.

attrs.title: Levelwise truncations of the adic tower

objects.body:
For an injective sheaf $I$ of $\mathbf F_r$-modules on $X=\mathbf P^1_A$ in
the setup of [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselian-setup],

$$
 H^q(X_0,I_0)=0\qquad(q>0).
$$

## Proof

For $q>1$, $X=\mathbf P^1_A$ has affine diagonal and is covered by two affine
opens, so [lemma-weil-pbc-injective-restriction-acyclicity] gives the vanishing.
Let $\xi\in H^1(X_0,I_0)$. By [lemma-weil-pbc-h1-constructible-representation],
$\xi$ is the image of a tuple of classes in
$\bigoplus_iH^1(X_0,(h_i)_*\underline{M_i}|_{X_0})$, where each $h_i:V_i\to X$
is finite and finitely presented. [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact] and
[lemma-weil-pbc-finite-exchange] identify this group with
$\bigoplus_iH^1((V_i)_0,\underline{M_i})$. Each $V_i$ is proper over $A$, so
[lemma-weil-pbc-h1-torsor-comparison] lifts every component to
$H^1(V_i,\underline{M_i})$, and finite Leray assembles their sum into a class
of $H^1(X,\bigoplus_i(h_i)_*\underline{M_i})$. Its image in $H^1(X,I)$
vanishes because $I$ is injective, and the restriction square is commutative,
so $\xi=0$.

attrs.title: Acyclicity on the closed projective line

objects.body:
For every torsion sheaf $F$ on $X$, restriction induces isomorphisms

$$
H^q(X,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(X_0,F_0)\qquad(q\geq0).
$$

## Proof

Choose an injective resolution $F\to I^\bullet$. Exactness of inverse
image along the closed immersion gives an exact complex $F_0\to I_0^\bullet$.
The preceding lemma makes each $I_0^r$ acyclic, so Leray's acyclicity lemma
identifies $R\Gamma(X_0,F_0)$ with $\Gamma(X_0,I_0^\bullet)$. Degree-zero
restriction identifies this complex with $\Gamma(X,I^\bullet)$ term by term.
Taking cohomology gives the displayed isomorphisms, and naturality follows
from the naturality of the restriction map and of injective resolutions. The
source locators are Tags `0A0C` and `0A3S`.

## Detailed form

In the setup of [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselian-setup], for every torsion
etale sheaf $F$ on $X$, restriction gives natural isomorphisms

$$
 H^q(X,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(X_0,F_0)
 \qquad(q\geq0).
$$

## Proof

Choose a K-injective resolution $F\to I^\bullet$. By the acyclicity statement
of [prop-weil-pbc-p1-acyclicity] each $I^m|_{X_0}$ is acyclic on $X_0$, so
$H^q(X_0,F_0)$ is computed by $\Gamma(X_0,I^\bullet|_{X_0})$; the degree-zero
comparison, applied termwise to the abelian sheaves $I^m$, identifies this
with $\Gamma(X,I^\bullet)$, whose cohomology is $H^q(X,F)$. Naturality in $F$
is the naturality of the two comparisons in the setup of
[def-weil-pbc-strict-henselian-setup].

Let $\square$ be the cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with
$X,Y,X',Y'$ noetherian of finite dimension, $f$ and $f'$ proper, and suppose
there is a positive integer $N$ annihilating $A/I$ which is invertible on
all four schemes. Assume that the geometric fibers of $f$ have dimension at
most $e\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$; put $c=2e$.

Then, for every $K\in\Dbc(X_{\Proet},A)$ whose reductions have a common
cohomological interval $[a,b]$, one has
$$
 \begin{aligned}
  Rf_*K&\in\Dbc(Y_{\Proet},A),&
  Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rf_*K&\in\Dbc(Y'_{\Proet},A),\\
  Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K&\in\Dbc(X'_{\Proet},A),&
  Rf'_*Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K&\in\Dbc(Y'_{\Proet},A).
 \end{aligned}
$$
The two pullbacks have reduction amplitude $[a,b]$ and the two direct images
have reduction amplitude contained in $[a,b+c]$.

*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this preservation: the
constructibility of the four outputs is the adic constructibility of
Definition 61.29.1 ([Tag 09C1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C1))
and Proposition 61.29.7 ([Tag
09C7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C7)), and the amplitude bounds
are those of Lemma 59.92.2 ([Tag
095U](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/095U)) and Theorem 63.14.5 ([Tag
0GL0](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0GL0)), each stated for a single
complex on a Noetherian scheme; the closest packaged form is Lemma 61.29.2
([Tag 09C2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C2)), which realizes one
constructible $K$ as $\Rlim K_n$ with a common interval and etale origins
but says nothing about functors. The blueprint adds the simultaneous
statement for the completed pullbacks and direct images of
$\Dbc(X_{\Proet},A)$ whose reductions share the interval $[a,b]$.

## Proof

By [thm-weil-pbc-amplification-proper] the three conditions
$$
 \mathrm{AMP}(\square;2e),\qquad\mathrm{WIT}(\square),\qquad\mathrm{TOW}(\square)
$$
of [def-weil-pbc-finite-level-amplification],
[def-weil-pbc-witness-compatibility] and [def-weil-pbc-tower-preservation]
hold for $c=2e$, so the argument below applies. Let
$K\in\Dbc(X_{\Proet},A)$ have all reductions supported in $[a,b]$, so that
its reduction tower is uniformly bounded constructible in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete] with compatible etale-origin
witnesses. By the amplification $\mathrm{AMP}(\square;c)$ and the tower
preservation $\mathrm{TOW}(\square)$, the levelwise tower functors carry
this tower to uniformly bounded constructible towers whose local models have
amplitude compatible with the containments, and by the witness compatibility
of [def-weil-pbc-witness-compatibility] the compatible etale-origin
witnesses are carried to compatible witnesses. By the reconstruction lemma
for uniform towers each of the four derived limits is then realized by its
local models, hence lies in the bounded constructible complete category, is
derived complete and has the stated reduction amplitude; and by the
direct-image-limits proposition the four limits are exactly $Rf_*K$,
$Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rf_*K$, $Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K$ and
$Rf'_*Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K$, which proves the assertions.

Let $\Lambda$ be a finite discrete ring, let $u:U\to V$ be a morphism
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] of schemes, and let the coefficient sheaves
be the constant sheaves $\Lambda_{U,\Proet},\Lambda_{V,\Proet}$ of
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Then the module inverse image $u^*$ of
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] is an exact functor on $\Lambda$-module
sheaves.

## Proof

By [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] the module inverse image is

$$
 u^*F=u^{-1}F\otimes_{u^{-1}\Lambda_{V,\Proet}}\Lambda_{U,\Proet},
$$

and [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] identifies the base ring
$u^{-1}\Lambda_{V,\Proet}$ with $\Lambda_{U,\Proet}$, so that $u^*F\cong
u^{-1}F\otimes_{\Lambda_{U,\Proet}}\Lambda_{U,\Proet}\cong u^{-1}F$,
naturally in $F$. The functor $u^{-1}$ is exact: by
[def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] the presheaf inverse image is computed
sectionwise and has both a left and a right adjoint, so it preserves kernels
and cokernels, and sheafification of presheaves of abelian groups is exact
(Stacks Project, Lemma 7.10.15, Tag
[00WJ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00WJ)); this is the argument of
[prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact] carried out on the small pro-etale site
in place of the small etale site. Hence $u^*$, being naturally isomorphic to
$u^{-1}$, is exact as well.

attrs.title: Exactness of the pro-etale inverse image for constant coefficients

objects.body:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite discrete ring and let $u:U\to V$ be a morphism
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] of schemes, with $\Lambda_{V,\Proet}$ and
$\Lambda_{U,\Proet}$ the sheaves of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] on the
small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Then the structure map

$$
 u^{-1}\Lambda_{V,\Proet}\longrightarrow\Lambda_{U,\Proet}
$$

is an isomorphism.

## Proof

By [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] the sheaf $\Lambda_{T,\Proet}$ is the
sheafification of $U\mapsto\operatorname{Cont}(\pi_0(|U|),\Lambda)$;
decomposing a pro-etale object into its clopen connected components, which
form a covering in the small pro-etale topology
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], identifies $\Lambda_{T,\Proet}$ with the free
$\Lambda$-module sheaf of rank one, so that

$$
 \operatorname{Hom}\bigl(\Lambda_{T,\Proet},G\bigr)=G(T)
$$

for every sheaf $G$ of $\Lambda$-modules on $T_{\Proet}$, naturally in $G$.
By [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] the inverse image is the sheafification of
the presheaf inverse image, hence left adjoint to the direct image, and
adjunction therefore gives a natural bijection

$$
 \operatorname{Hom}\bigl(u^{-1}\Lambda_{V,\Proet},G\bigr)
 \cong\operatorname{Hom}\bigl(\Lambda_{V,\Proet},u_*G\bigr)
 \cong(u_*G)(V)=G(U)
 \cong\operatorname{Hom}\bigl(\Lambda_{U,\Proet},G\bigr)
$$

for every sheaf $G$ of $\Lambda$-modules on $U_{\Proet}$. The composite is
the map induced by the displayed structure morphism, which is consequently an
isomorphism by the Yoneda lemma.

attrs.title: Constant coefficients on the pro-etale site

objects.body:
For every scheme $S$, the projection $\mathbf P^1_S\to S$ satisfies
$\mathsf{PBC}$.

## Proof

At every geometric $\bar t\to T$, the exchange map is the field-extension
map of the preceding lemma. The two residue fields are separably closed and
the fibre is a proper curve, so proper-curve invariance makes this map an
isomorphism. Geometric stalk conservativity gives an isomorphism of every
$R^q$ sheaf. Specializing to inverse images of injective
$\mathbf F_\ell$-module sheaves gives $\mathsf{IA}$ after every base change;
the S0 equivalence gives $\mathsf{PBC}$.

## Detailed form

For every scheme $S$, the projection $\mathbf P^1_S\to S$ satisfies
$\mathrm{PBC}$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-property].

## Proof

Let $I$ be injective in $\mathbf F_r$-module sheaves on $\mathbf P^1_S$ and
make an arbitrary base change. On every geometric stalk,
[lemma-weil-pbc-p1-exchange-geometric-stalk] identifies the exchange map with
pullback between proper curves over separably closed fields;
[prop-weil-pbc-proper-curve-sepclosed-invariance] makes it an isomorphism. Since
$R^qp_*I=0$ for $q>0$, the target stalks $R^qp'_*g'^{-1}I$ vanish for $q>0$,
and conservativity of geometric stalks gives $\mathrm{IA}_r$ for the
projection; the equivalence between $\mathrm{PBC}$ and $\mathrm{IA}$ gives
$\mathrm{PBC}$.

Let $k\subseteq k'$ be separably closed fields, $C$ a proper $k$-scheme of
dimension at most one, and $F$ a torsion etale sheaf. Then

$$
H^q(C,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(C_{k'},F|)
$$

for every $q$.

## Proof

First assume both fields algebraically closed. Apply constructible/primary
reduction. The closed immersion $C_{\mathrm{red}}\to C$ is a universal
homeomorphism, so the explicit site equivalence first replaces $C$ by its
reduction. Then apply dense-open localization, the prime-to-$\ell$ trace
splitting, the
finite-pushforward comparison, and the normalized smooth constant calculation
in that order. Every step commutes with field extension, giving the result.
For separably closed $k\subseteq k'$, apply Lemma
[lemma-weil-pbc-curve-separably-closed-passage] to the algebraically
closed result just proved. Its commutative rectangle identifies the
resulting isomorphism with the specified restriction map. This expands Tags
`03SC` and `0A5E`.

## Detailed form

Let $k\subset k'$ be separably closed, let $C$ be proper of dimension at most
one over $k$, and let $F$ be torsion. The same canonical restriction map is an
isomorphism in every degree.

## Proof

Pass to compatible algebraic closures: the isomorphism of
[prop-weil-pbc-algebraically-closed-extension] holds for the two algebraically
closed extensions, and the two purely inseparable extensions identify the
sites by invariance under universal homeomorphisms, so the separably closed
case is obtained by composing the isomorphisms.

attrs.title: Proper curve invariance over separably closed fields

objects.body:
Every exact $\mathcal O_E$-linear functor among the integral constructible
categories, and every natural transformation between such functors, extends
uniquely to the rationalization of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. In
particular $Rf_*$, completed pullback, and their exchange transformation
define exact functors and a natural transformation on $\Dbc(-,E)$.

## Proof

Localization at a central natural endomorphism (inverting the
multiplication by $\varpi$) is functorial for exact functors and natural
transformations, so every integral datum descends uniquely to the category
of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]; applying this to the direct image,
completed pullback, and the completed exchange morphism gives the displayed
structures.

attrs.title: Functorial transport to a finite field

objects.body:
If every projection $\mathbf P^1_S\to S$ satisfies $\mathsf{PBC}$ for every
base scheme $S$, then every proper morphism satisfies $\mathsf{PBC}$.

## Proof

Use target locality and the Chow factorization. The closed immersion
$X'\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_Y$ is proper and finite onto its image, so
finite base change plus composition reduces $X'\to Y$ to
$\mathbf P^n_Y\to Y$. The finite surjective map $\sigma_n$ and cancellation
reduce this projection to $(\mathbf P^1_Y)^n\to Y$. Repeated base change and
composition reduce the product projection to the one-dimensional projection.
Finally cancellation along $\pi$ transfers the property from $X'$ and
$X'\to Y$ to $X\to Y$. Every comparison used is the named exchange map of
Definition [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange].

## Detailed form

Assume that $\mathbf P^1_S\to S$ satisfies $\mathrm{PBC}$ in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-property] for every scheme $S$. Then every proper morphism of
schemes satisfies $\mathrm{PBC}$; no finite-presentation hypothesis is
needed, because the Chow factorization [lemma-weil-pbc-chow-factorization]
holds for every proper morphism over an affine base.

## Proof

By [lemma-weil-pbc-target-locality] the assertion is local on the target, so we
work over an affine $Y$, where [lemma-weil-pbc-chow-factorization] supplies $\pi$, $i_Y$, and
the two closed embeddings $i_Y$ and $i_X$ of
[lem-weil-pbc-projective-embedding]. At every use of composition or
cancellation below, first convert all $\mathrm{PBC}$ inputs to $\mathrm{IA}$,
apply the lemma, and convert back. The projective-space projections $\mathbf
P^n_S\to S$ have $\mathrm{PBC}$ by
[lem-weil-pbc-reduction-projective-space]. The Chow map factors as $\pi=q_X\circ
i_X$, where $i_X$ is finite and hence has $\mathrm{PBC}$ by
[prop-weil-pbc-finite-morphism], and $q_X:\mathbf P^n_X\to X$ has
$\mathrm{PBC}$; composition by [prop-weil-pbc-composition-stability] gives
$\mathrm{PBC}$ for $\pi$. Likewise $f\pi=q_Y\circ i_Y$ has $\mathrm{PBC}$.
Since $\pi$ is proper and surjective, [lemma-weil-pbc-cancellation] applied to
$\pi$ and $f$ gives $\mathrm{PBC}$ for $f$.

attrs.title: Reduction of proper base change to $\mathbf P^1$

objects.body:
Let $\Lambda=P_n$ be as in
[def-weil-pbc-constructible-direct-image-finiteness], let $u:S\to T$ be a
morphism of schemes, and suppose $\mathrm{FIN}(u,\Lambda;c)$. Then the
ambient functor $Ru_*$ restricts to an exact triangulated functor
$$
 Ru_*:\Dbc(S_{\Proet},\Lambda)\longrightarrow\Dbc(T_{\Proet},\Lambda),
$$
and if $K\in\Dbc(S_{\Proet},\Lambda)$ has cohomology in $[a,b]$, then
$Ru_*K$ has cohomology in $[a,b+c]$.

*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this conditional restriction.
Stacks' constructibility entries are Definition 61.29.1 ([Tag
09C1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C1)) and Proposition 61.29.7
([Tag 09C7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C7)), stated on a
Noetherian scheme for a Noetherian coefficient ring, together with Lemma
61.29.2 ([Tag 09C2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C2)), which
realizes one constructible $K$ as $\Rlim K_n$ with each $K_n$ of bounded tor
amplitude, constructible cohomology and etale origin; the finiteness and
amplitude inputs are Lemma 59.92.2 ([Tag
095U](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/095U): for $f$ proper with all
fibres of dimension $\le n$ and every abelian torsion sheaf $\mathcal F$ on
$X_{\Et}$ one has $R^qf_*\mathcal F=0$ for $q>2n$) and Theorem 63.14.5 ([Tag
0GL0](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0GL0): for $f$ separated of
finite presentation and $K\in D^+_{tors,c}(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$, $Rf_!K$ has
constructible cohomology sheaves). Difference: both are etale-site
statements about a single coefficient ring, with no amplitude shift, no
uniformity over a coefficient tower and no pro-etale site; the blueprint
adds the transport of these conditions to the small pro-etale sites as the
predicate $\mathrm{FIN}(u,\Lambda;c)$ and the amplitude shift by $c$.

## Proof

An object $K\in\Dbc(S_{\Proet},\Lambda)$ has constructible cohomology
sheaves $F_q=\mathcal H^q(K)$, zero outside the finite interval $[a,b]$. The
truncation-couple spectral sequence applied to the left exact $u_*$ gives
$$
 E_2^{p,q}=R^pu_*F_q\Longrightarrow\mathcal H^{p+q}(Ru_*K),
$$
with $E_2^{p,q}$ constructible for all $p,q$ by clause (i) of
[def-weil-pbc-constructible-direct-image-finiteness] and zero for $p>c$ by
clause (ii). For fixed $n=p+q$, the finite filtration of a convergent
spectral sequence exhibits $\mathcal H^n(Ru_*K)$ as a subquotient of a
finite extension of the constructible $E_\infty$-terms, hence constructible
by [thm-constructible-serre]; only $a\leq q\leq n$ and $p\leq c$
contribute, so $\mathcal H^n(Ru_*K)=0$ for $n\notin[a,b+c]$. Exactness is
the exactness of the ambient $Ru_*$ on the full triangulated subcategory
$\Dbc(S_{\Proet},\Lambda)$.

attrs.title: Restriction of the direct image to bounded constructibles

objects.body:
Let $\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T)$ be the tower category of
[def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], an abelian category with enough
injectives. Fixing a functorial K-injective resolution
[def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions] $M_\bullet\to I_\bullet$ of every
object of $\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T)$, the assignment

$$
 \Rlim:D(\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T))\longrightarrow D(T_{\Proet},A),
 \qquad
 M_\bullet\longmapsto\varprojlim_nI_n
$$

is a triangulated functor, and any two such choices of functorial K-injective
resolutions give isomorphic functors.

(*Source note:* functoriality of the derived limit is contained in Stacks
Project, Derived Categories, Definition 13.34.1 (Tag
[08TC](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08TC)), whose triangle is natural
in the system, and the functorial K-injective resolutions fixed here are
those of Theorem 19.12.6 (Tag
[079P](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/079P)) together with the
existence statement of Lemma 13.34.3 (Tag
[0BK7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BK7)). What Stacks does not
state, and what the blueprint adds, is the resulting assignment
$D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(T))\to D(T_{\Proet},A)$ as a triangulated functor,
together with the comparison of any two choices of functorial resolutions.)

## Proof

In a Grothendieck abelian category every complex admits a functorial
K-injective resolution, and quasi-isomorphic K-injective complexes are
chain-homotopy equivalent (Stacks Project, Theorem 19.12.6, Tag
[079P](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/079P)); applied to the tower
category of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] this supplies the
functorial resolutions fixed in the statement. By
[prop-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit-computation] the value of the assignment
at $M_\bullet$ represents the derived limit $\Rlim M_\bullet$ of
[def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit], and the derived limit is a triangulated
functor of the system, being the first term of the Roos triangle, which is
natural in the system; the assignment therefore inherits exactness on
distinguished triangles. A second choice of functorial K-injective
resolutions is related to the first by a chain-homotopy equivalence over each
object, and $\varprojlim_n(-)$ of a levelwise homotopy equivalence of towers
is a homotopy equivalence, so the two assignments agree up to a natural
isomorphism of functors. The K-injectivity used here is that of
[def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions].

attrs.title: Functoriality of the sequential derived inverse limit

objects.body:
For every $M_\bullet\in D(\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T))$, the tower category
being that of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], the transition maps
define an endomorphism $s$ of $R\!\prod_nM_n$, and the defining Roos triangle
of [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit] is the functorial distinguished
triangle

$$
 \Rlim M_\bullet\longrightarrow R\!\prod_nM_n
 \xrightarrow{1-s}R\!\prod_nM_n
 \longrightarrow(\Rlim M_\bullet)[1].
$$

If $U$ is a weakly contractible quasi-compact object of $T_{\Proet}$, then
for every $i\in\mathbf Z$ this triangle induces the functorial exact sequence

$$
 0\to\varprojlim{}^1_nH^{i-1}(U,M_n)
 \to H^i(U,\Rlim M_\bullet)
 \to\varprojlim_nH^i(U,M_n)\to0.
$$

(*Source note:* the canonical triangle is Stacks Project, More on Algebra,
Lemma 15.88.9 (Tag [07KX](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07KX)): for
$K=(K_n^\bullet)$ in $D(\textit{Ab}(\mathbf N))$ there is a canonical
distinguished triangle $R\lim K\to\prod_nK_n^\bullet\to\prod_nK_n^\bullet\to
R\lim K[1]$, so that $R\lim K$ is a derived limit in the sense of Definition
13.34.1 (Tag [08TC](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08TC)); the
associated short exact sequences are Lemma 15.88.10 (Tag
[07KY](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07KY): the long exact cohomology
sequence breaks up into $0\to R^1\lim_nH^{p-1}(K_n^\bullet)\to H^p(R\lim
K)\to\lim_nH^p(K_n^\bullet)\to0$), and the representation of $\Rlim$ by the
two-term complex $\prod A_n\to\prod A_n$, $(x_n)\mapsto(x_n-f_{n+1}(x_{n+1}))$,
in degrees $0,1$, together with $R^p\lim A_n=0$ for $p>1$, is Lemma 15.88.1
(Tag [07KW](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07KW)). The Stacks entries
are stated for towers of abelian groups; the blueprint states the same
triangle for the tower category $\operatorname{Tow}_A(T)$ over $T_{\Proet}$
with $A_T$-coefficients, where the two derived products are those of
[prop-weil-pbc-derived-product-representation], and it evaluates the Milnor
sequence at a weakly contractible quasi-compact $U\in T_{\Proet}$, which is
the form in which it is used below.)

## Proof

The triangle is the definition of $\Rlim$ in
[def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit], namely the defining Roos triangle for
the system $(\operatorname{ev}_nM_\bullet)$, with the endomorphism $1-s$
induced by the transition maps; the identification of its middle term with
$R\!\prod_nM_n$ is the representability statement of the derived-limit
existence lemma. For the exact sequence the functor $\varprojlim$ is the
kernel of $1-s$ on the product; the cokernel of $1-s$ is the *first derived
limit* $\varprojlim^1M_n$, an exact-in-general cokernel, so the ordinary
sequence

$$
 0\to\varprojlim_nM_n\to\prod_nM_n
 \xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_nM_n\to\varprojlim^1_nM_n\to0
$$

is exact (the left exactness of $\varprojlim$ with the cokernel
$\varprojlim^1$ recorded rather than zero) in the evaluation categories of
[def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. This exhibits $\varprojlim$ as the
kernel of $1-s$ and $\varprojlim^1$ as its cokernel; the *Roos resolution* is
the two-term complex

$$
 \prod_nM_n\xrightarrow{\ 1-s\ }\prod_nM_n
$$

placed in degrees $0,1$, whose cohomology is $\varprojlim$ in degree $0$ and
$\varprojlim^1$ in degree $1$ — and whose higher cohomology vanishes because,
for a tower of module sheaves, the higher derived limits $\varprojlim^i$
vanish for $i\geq2$ (the Roos/Mittag-Leffler chain: $\varprojlim^1$ of a
countable tower of modules is computed by the cokernel of $1-s$, and
$\varprojlim^i=0$ for $i\geq2$; this is the classical Milnor exact sequence
of Stacks Project, More on Algebra, Lemma 15.88.1, Tag
[07KW](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07KW), which represents $\Rlim$
by the two-term complex $\prod\to\prod$ sitting in degrees $0,1$, and the
resulting derived-limit triangle of Lemma 15.88.9, Tag
[07KX](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07KX), with the short exact
sequences of Lemma 15.88.10, Tag
[07KY](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07KY)); that triangle is exactly
the triangle displayed in the statement. For a weakly contractible
quasi-compact $U\in T_{\Proet}$, the functor $\Gamma(U,-)$ is exact on
$\Mod(T_{\Proet},A_T)$, preserves the products and limits involved and the
maps $1-s$, so the long exact cohomology sequence of the triangle is the
displayed functorial exact sequence, with $\varprojlim{}^1$ arising as the
cohomology of $1-s$ in the degree below.

attrs.title: Roos triangle and Milnor exact sequence

objects.body:
For a finite extension $E\subset E'$, derived scalar extension is an exact
functor
$$
 T_{E'/E}=E'\otimes_E^L-:
 \Dbc(T,E)\longrightarrow\Dbc(T,E').
$$
Choose $T_{E/E}=\operatorname{id}$ literally. For $E\subset E'\subset E''$,
derived tensor associativity gives a specified exact natural isomorphism
$$
 a_{E'',E',E}:T_{E''/E'}T_{E'/E}
 \xrightarrow{\sim}T_{E''/E}.
$$
These associators satisfy the unit equations and the pentagon for four
nested fields. Exactness supplies natural shift comparisons
$$
 \sigma_{E'/E,K}:T_{E'/E}(K[1])
 \xrightarrow{\sim}(T_{E'/E}K)[1]
$$
which commute with the associators.

There are coherent natural isomorphisms
$$
 E'\otimes_E^LRf_{*,E}K\xrightarrow{\sim}
 Rf_{*,E'}(E'\otimes_E^LK)
$$
and analogous isomorphisms for pullback. Under these isomorphisms, scalar
extension of the $E$-exchange map is the $E'$-exchange map.

*Source:* the coherent scalar-extension package for finite coefficient
fields, i.e. the coefficient-extension formalism of derived complete torsion
coefficients: the exactness is the flatness of a finite field extension, and
the associators, shift comparisons and the direct-image and pullback
compatibilities are the standard derived-tensor-associativity and
projection-formula identifications of the formalism, as in Milne, *Lectures
on Etale Cohomology*, Section 19 (finiteness theorems; sheaves of
$\mathbf Z_\ell$-modules); no Stacks Project tag is recorded for this
package.

## Proof

This is the recorded input of the statement, the coherent scalar-extension
package of the adic formalism (Milne, *Lectures on Étale Cohomology*,
Section 19; no Stacks Project tag is recorded for it). Its two elementary
ingredients are named in the statement itself: exactness is the flatness of
a finite field extension, and the associators, unit equations and pentagon
are the coherence of the derived tensor product, transported along the exact
functor $E'\otimes_E^-$. The blueprint uses the package as the definition of
the coefficient extension between the $E$- and $E'$-stages of
[def-weil-pbc-rational-category]; no separate proof is given.

For finite $\Lambda$, $\nu_T^*$ is exact, its unit

$$
 F\longrightarrow\nu_{T,*}\nu_T^*F
$$

is an isomorphism for every etale $\Lambda$-module sheaf, and

$$
 R^q\nu_{T,*}\nu_T^*I=0\qquad(q>0)
$$

for every injective etale $\Lambda$-module sheaf $I$.

## Proof

The inverse image of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] preserves finite
limits and is a left adjoint. On module sheaves it therefore preserves
kernels and cokernels, and is exact. Equivalently on affine charts, the
section formula in [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-sections] preserves kernels, and
an epimorphism lifts locally after an etale cover at the stage representing a
section. These covers are also pro-etale covers.

On every affine etale $W\to T$, the same section formula identifies
$(\nu_T^*F)(W)$ with $F(W)$: apply it on an affine open of $T$, then use
ordinary etale gluing. Under this identification the unit is the identity on
sections. The affine etale basis consequently proves that it is an
isomorphism of etale sheaves.

If $I$ is injective on $T_{\Et}$, its restriction to any affine etale $W$ is
injective by the etale-restriction lemma. The adjunction, or its explicit
section construction, identifies $(\nu_T^*I)|_W$ with $\nu_W^*(I|_W)$. Its
positive cohomology on $W$ vanishes by
[lem-weil-pbc-comparison-injective-acyclicity]. Finally
$R^q\nu_{T,*}(\nu_T^*I)$ is the sheafification of $W\mapsto
H^q(W_{\Proet},(\nu_T^*I)|_W)$: apply restriction to an injective resolution
and then sheafify the cohomology of the resulting section complex.
Restriction of that injective resolution computes cohomology on $W$ by
[lem-weil-pbc-proetale-restriction-injectives]. The basis detection in
[lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis], or just the affine etale basis on the target,
now gives the required zero sheaf.

attrs.title: Exactness and full faithfulness at finite level

objects.body:
For quasi-compact quasi-separated $f:X\to S$, torsion $F$, and $q\geq0$,

$$
(R^qf_*F)_{\bar s}\cong
H^q(X\times_SS_{(\bar s)},F|).
$$

For $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}})$ this lifts to

$$
(Rf_*K)_{\bar s}\xrightarrow{\sim}
R\Gamma(X\times_SS_{(\bar s)},K|)
$$

in $D^+(\mathbf{Ab})$.

## Proof

The stalk is the colimit over $\mathcal N_{\bar s}^{\mathrm{op}}$ of
$H^q(X\times_SV,F|)$. Replace the index by affine neighbourhoods, identify
their inverse limit by Lemma [lemma-weil-pbc-fibre-product-limit], and
apply cohomology continuity. For the derived statement, choose a
bounded-below injective complex $J^\bullet$ representing $K$. The chain map
from the stalk complex $(f_*J^\bullet)_{\bar s}$ to the sections complex on
the strict henselization is obtained by restricting each representative
section. Its map on every cohomology group is the preceding isomorphism, so
it is a quasi-isomorphism. This expands Tag `03Q9`.

## Detailed form

Let $f:X\to S$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let $F$ be a torsion etale sheaf
[def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], and let $\bar s\to S$ be geometric. Then

$$
 (R^qf_*F)_{\bar s}\xrightarrow{\sim}
 H^q(X\times_SS_{(\bar s)},F|)
 \qquad(q\geq0),
$$

where $S_{(\bar s)}$ is the strict henselization limit
[def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] at $\bar s$. For
$K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ with torsion cohomology, this assembles to

$$
 (Rf_*K)_{\bar s}\xrightarrow{\sim}
 \RGamma(X\times_SS_{(\bar s)},K|)
 \quad\text{in }\Dplus(\Ab).
$$

## Proof

The stalk is the colimit over pointed etale neighbourhoods, whose inverse
limit is the strict henselization by
[def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]; the fibre product
commutation of [lemma-weil-pbc-fibre-product-limit] replaces $X\times_SS_{(\bar
s)}$ by the limit of the $X\times_SV$, and
[lemma-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology-continuity] identifies the colimit of
cohomologies with the cohomology of the limit. On a bounded-below K-injective
[def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions] representative the same argument gives
the derived statement.

Let $A\to B$ be a local morphism of strictly henselian local rings inducing a
specified extension of their separably closed residue fields. For the
base-change square of $\mathbf P^1_A\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, the stalk of the
exchange morphism [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] at the closed geometric
point of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is the restriction map between the
cohomologies of the two closed projective lines. If the residue-field map is
an isomorphism, this stalk map is an isomorphism.

## Proof

On a termwise injective representative of the exchange morphism of
[def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange], the stalk at the closed geometric point is
computed by applying the comparison of
[prop-weil-pbc-p1-strict-henselian-comparison] to the two closed fibres; expanding
the unit--$\theta_\square$--counit composite shows that this is the
restriction map between the cohomologies of the two closed projective lines,
which is an isomorphism when the residue-field map is an isomorphism.

Let $u:X_0\to X$ be a universal homeomorphism. Pullback along $u$ is an
equivalence between the small etale topos of $X$ and that of $X_0$, and for
every abelian sheaf $F$ on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ and every $n$ it induces an
isomorphism

$$
H^n(X_{\mathrm{et}},F)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^n(X_{0,\mathrm{et}},u^{-1}F).
$$

This is Tag `03SI`.

## Proof

Base change is an equivalence of the underlying categories and matches the
covering families, hence is an equivalence of sites; so restriction along it
is an equivalence of the categories of sheaves, and pullback, being its left
adjoint, is a quasi-inverse. Cohomology is the $\operatorname{Ext}$-groups
out of the constant sheaf $\mathbf Z$, and an exact equivalence carrying the
constant sheaf to the constant sheaf induces an isomorphism on those groups.

attrs.title: Topological invariance of the small etale topos

objects.body:
Let

$$
\begin{CD}
X'@>{g'}>>X\\
@V{f'}VV @VV{f}V\\
Y'@>{g}>>Y
\end{CD}
$$

be Cartesian with $f$ proper. For every torsion sheaf $F$ on
$X_{\mathrm{et}}$, the canonical exchange map

$$
g^{-1}Rf_*F\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_*g'^{-1}F
$$

is an isomorphism. These isomorphisms are natural in $F$, equal the identity
for identity squares, and commute with horizontal and vertical pasting.

## Proof

The torsion assembly proves the isomorphism in every cohomological degree for
the map constructed in S0. A morphism in $D^+$ is an isomorphism exactly when
all its cohomology sheaf maps are isomorphisms. Naturality, identity, and
pasting are the corresponding S0 coherence equations and survive each
devissage step. This is the expanded endpoint whose source locator is Tag
`095T`; that tag is not used as a proof leaf.

## Detailed form

Let

$$
 \begin{array}{ccc}
 X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
 f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
 Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y
 \end{array}
$$

be cartesian [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with $f$ proper. For every
torsion sheaf $F$ on $X_{\Et}$,

$$
 \Ex_{\square,F}:g^{-1}Rf_*F
 \xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_*g'^{-1}F
$$

is an isomorphism in $\Dplus(Y'_{\Et})$, where $\Ex_{\square,F}$ is the
derived exchange morphism [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange].

## Proof

View $F$ as the complex $F[0]$; its only cohomology sheaf is the torsion sheaf
$F$, so $F[0]$ has torsion cohomology. [thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below] applied to
$K=F[0]$ makes the derived exchange morphism $\Ex_{\square,F[0]}$ an
isomorphism in $\Dplus(Y'_{\Et})$; by [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] that
morphism for a complex concentrated in degree zero is the exchange morphism
$\Ex_{\square,F}$ of the sheaf $F$, giving the assertion.

In the notation of
[def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], if $Y$ is
proper then the
compact-support direct image and the ordinary direct image agree,

$$
Ra_{Y!}\cong Ra_{Y*},
$$

so that $H_c^i(Y,K)\cong H^i(Y,K)$ for every $K$. (This is
$\Cref{def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed}$ and
[def-weil-derived-direct-image] applied to a proper structure
morphism, and the exchange criterion of the proper base-change theorem
for the identity base change.)

## Proof

If $Y$ is proper, the identity is a compactification of the structure
morphism $a_Y$, namely
$Y\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}}Y\xrightarrow{a_Y}\Spec k$
with $a_Y$ proper, so at every finite coefficient level
$Ra_{Y!,n}=Ra_{Y*,n}$ by
[def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], and the comparison maps of
that definition are identities for the identity refinement; hence the
compactification-independent functor $Ra_{Y!}$ is naturally
identified with the ordinary derived direct image $Ra_{Y*}$ of
[def-weil-derived-direct-image]. Applying the equivalence
$\operatorname{Fib}_s$ of
[def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] to both sides gives
$\RGammac(Y,K)\cong\RGamma(Y,K)$, hence
$H_c^i(Y,K)\cong H^i(Y,K)$ for every $K$, by the definitions of the
ordinary and compactly supported cohomology groups in
[def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology].

attrs.title: Proper coincidence of compact-support and ordinary cohomology

objects.body:
Let $K$ be a field and
$C(T)=\sum_{n\geq0}c_nT^n\in K[[T]]$ a
formal power series.
The following conditions are equivalent:

1. $C=P/Q$ for polynomials $P,Q\in K[T]$ with $Q(0)=1$.
1. The Hankel rank of $C$ is finite.
1. There are integers $m\geq0,d\geq1$ and
$a_0,\ldots,a_{d-1}\in K$ such that
$$
c_{n+d}+a_{d-1}c_{n+d-1}+\cdots+a_0c_n=0
\qquad(n\geq m).
$$

## Proof

Write $R_j=(c_{j+s})_{s\geq0}$ and
$V=\operatorname{span}_K\{R_j:j\geq0\}$. We first identify the
matrix rank in [def-weil-hankel-matrix] with $\dim_K V$.
If $r$ rows are independent as infinite sequences,
[lem-weil-finite-coordinate-detection] applied to their span
shows that finitely many columns still detect their independence.
A further selection of $r$ columns gives a nonzero $r$-minor.
Conversely a nonzero finite minor makes its rows independent.
Thus bounded finite matrix ranks are equivalent to finite $\dim_K V$.

Suppose (2) holds. If $R_0=0$, all $c_n$ vanish and (3) holds
with $m=0,d=1,a_0=0$. Otherwise choose the least $d\geq1$
for which $R_0,\ldots,R_d$ are dependent. The preceding rows are
independent, so the last row has coefficient nonzero in any nontrivial relation.
Dividing by that coefficient gives
$R_d+a_{d-1}R_{d-1}+\cdots+a_0R_0=0$.
Its $n$-th coordinate is (3) with $m=0$.

Suppose (3) holds. Put
$Q(T)=1+a_{d-1}T+\cdots+a_0T^d$.
For $N\geq m+d$, the coefficient of $T^N$ in $QC$ is
zero by the recurrence with $n=N-d$. Hence $QC=P$ is a
polynomial, proving (1). For later use, (3) also directly implies
(2): for every $j\geq m$ the same recurrence in every coordinate
expresses $R_{j+d}$ in the span of $R_j,\ldots,R_{j+d-1}$.
All rows therefore lie in the span of $R_0,\ldots,R_{m+d-1}$.

Finally suppose (1) holds. Write
$Q=1+b_1T+\cdots+b_dT^d$, first taking $d\geq1$.
The coefficient identity $QC=P$, in degrees $N>\deg P$
and $N\geq d$, gives (3) with $a_{d-j}=b_j$ and sufficiently
large $m$. If $Q=1$, the coefficients of $C=P$ eventually
vanish, so take $d=1,a_0=0$ and $m$ sufficiently large.
This proves all implications.

In the situation of [prop-arithmetic-roots], for every prime
$\ell\neq p$,

$$
r_i=\dim_{\Ql}H^i(X,\Ql),
$$

where $H^i(X,\Ql)$ is the
ordinary cohomology group
and $r_i=\deg P_i$; the integral Frobenius factor $P_i$ and its degree
$r_i$ are therefore independent of the chosen ell-adic realization.

## Proof

The degree equality is the degree assertion in
[def-weil-smooth-proper-cohomological-family], namely
$\deg P_{i,\ell}=\dim_{\Ql}H^i(X,\Ql)$ for the ordinary cohomology groups
of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], together with the
scalar-extension identity $P_i^{(\ell)}=P_{i,\ell}$ and the uniqueness of
$P_i$ in [prop-integral-recovery]; scalar extension preserves
degree, so $r_i=\deg P_i=\dim_{\Ql}H^i(X,\Ql)$, and the factor $P_i$ as
well as its degree $r_i$ are independent of the chosen ell-adic
realization.

attrs.title: Realization-independent degrees of the integral factors

objects.body:
For $P_{i,\ell}$ of
[def-weil-ordinary-reciprocal-roots], the
reciprocal roots are
exactly the eigenvalues of $F_{i,\ell}$ after scalar extension to
$\Qlb$ (the determinant identity $\det(1-TF)= \prod_j(1-\alpha_jT)$ over the algebraically closed field).

## Proof

After scalar extension to $\Qlb$, the operator $F_{i,\ell}$ on
$V_{i,\ell}\otimes_{\Ql}\Qlb$ has eigenvalues
$\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_m$ with $m=\dim_{\Ql}V_{i,\ell}$, counted
with algebraic multiplicity, and over the algebraically closed field

$$
\det(1-TF_{i,\ell}\mid V_{i,\ell})
=\prod_{j=1}^{m}(1-\lambda_jT).
$$

By [def-weil-ordinary-reciprocal-roots], the same factorization
displays the reciprocal roots of $P_{i,\ell}$ with algebraic
multiplicity, so the reciprocal roots are precisely the $\lambda_j$,
i.e. exactly the eigenvalues of $F_{i,\ell}$ in $\Qlb$.

In the notation of
[def-coefficient-twists-detailed], each $\Lambda(m)$ is an
invertible locally
constant rank-one sheaf, and twisting $K\mapsto K(m)$ preserves
bounded constructibility
and the finite Tor amplitude
condition (being the derived tensor product with an invertible sheaf).

## Proof

By [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], $\Lambda(1)_S$ is built from the
pro-etale sheaf $\mu_{\ell^r,S}$, which is locally constant of rank one
with finite stalks, by tensor products and scalar extension, and the
twists $\Lambda(m)$ are tensor powers and internal Homs of
$\Lambda(1)_S$. Hence each $\Lambda(m)$ is an invertible locally
constant rank-one sheaf, and such a sheaf is flat with Tor amplitude
$[0,0]$. For an invertible locally constant rank-one $L$, the spectral
sequence for the derived tensor product of [def-weil-derived-tensor]
collapses to $\mathcal H^r(K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_S}L)\cong \mathcal H^r(K)\otimes_{\Lambda_S}L$: tensoring with the locally constant
rank-one $L$ preserves the finite partitions and locally constant
finite stalks of the constructibility condition of
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] levelwise, and it
preserves the vanishing interval of the finite Tor amplitude condition of
[def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], because $L$ is flat and the
tensor products with $L$ and with the dual line are mutually inverse.
The integral and $\Qlb$-twists are obtained from the same statement
levelwise modulo $\varpi_E^n$ and at the common finite stages,
for every coefficient ring.

In the situation of [prop-rational-descent], the
point-count zeta series satisfies

$$
Z(X_0,T)\in1+T\mathbf Z[[T]]\cap\mathbf Q(T).
$$

## Proof

In the situation of [prop-rational-descent] the assumed closed-point
product is the identity of [prop-euler-product], so the
[def-weil-point-counts-zeta] series $Z(X_0,T)$ lies in
$1+T\mathbf Z[[T]]$; by [prop-rational-descent] it also lies in
$\mathbf Q(T)$. This is the assertion.

attrs.title: The zeta series is integral and rational

objects.body:
In the situation of [prop-rational-descent], the point-count zeta
series has a unique
normalized reduced
integral presentation: there are unique $A,B\in\mathbf Z[T]$ with
$A(0)=B(0)=1$, $\gcd(A,B)=1$ in $\mathbf Q[T]$, and
$Z(X_0,T)=A(T)/B(T)$.

## Proof

By [prop-weil-zeta-integral-rational] the series lies in
$1+T\mathbf Z[[T]]\cap\mathbf Q(T)$, and
[prop-weil-integral-rational-series] applied to it supplies the
existence and uniqueness of the normalized reduced integral presentation
of [def-weil-normalized-integral-fraction].

attrs.title: The normalized reduced integral presentation exists and is unique

objects.body:
Let $U_0/\mathbf F_q$ be normal, geometrically connected,
separated and of finite type,
pure of dimension one, and put
$U=U_0\times_{\mathbf F_q}\overline{\mathbf F}_q$. If
$\ell\nmid q$, then for the
geometric Frobenius

$$
\left(\varprojlim_nH^1_{\mathrm{\acute et}}
(U,\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z)\right)^{\Phi_q=1}=0.
\tag{5.4}
$$

The scheme and Frobenius conventions are those of
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], [def-tw-frobenius-action].

## Proof

Choose the smooth projective geometrically connected compactification
$j_0:U_0\hookrightarrow C_0$ and finite reduced boundary $D_0$ from
[lem-wf-curve-normal-smooth-compactification]. Let
$z=(z_n)_n$ be fixed by $\Phi_q$ in the inverse limit in (5.4).
Choose $m$ as in [lem-wf-open-curve-residue-sequence] and put
$Q=q^m$. The residues
$r_n=\operatorname{res}_n(z_n)$ form a compatible element
$r=(r_n)_n$ of the inverse-limit boundary module and are fixed by
$\Phi_Q$. The last assertion of the residue lemma gives $r=0$, hence
$r_n=0$ for every $n$.

Exactness of (5.1) gives a unique $x_n\in H^1(C,A_n)$ with
$j^*x_n=z_n$. Uniqueness shows that the $x_n$ are compatible under
reduction. Injectivity of $j^*$ and Frobenius equivariance show that
$\Phi_Qx_n=x_n$. Thus $x=(x_n)_n$ is a fixed element of
$\varprojlim_nH^1(C,A_n)$. Put
$C_{0,Q}:=C_0\times_{\mathbf F_q}\mathbf F_Q$. Its geometric fiber is
the same $C$, and its geometric Frobenius is $\Phi_q^m=\Phi_Q$.
Apply [lem-wf-proper-curve-compatible-h1-no-fixed] to
$C_{0,Q}/\mathbf F_Q$; it gives $x=0$, and then
$z_n=j^*x_n=0$ for every $n$.

attrs.title: No Frobenius-fixed compatible class on an open normal curve

objects.body:
Throughout, $C_0$ is the curve and $C$ its base
change to $k$; $P=\pi_1(C)$ is the geometric fundamental group, $W(C_0)$ the
Weil group with degree map and chosen degree-one lift $\gamma$, and
$E\subset\Qlb$ a finite coefficient field with valuation ring
$\mathcal O_E$ and maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_E$, all as in
[def-wf-weil-group]. A lisse Weil sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $C_0$ has geometric
generic stalk $\mathcal F_{\bar\eta}$.

The functor $\mathcal F\mapsto(V,\rho)=(\mathcal F_{\bar\eta}, \rho_{\mathcal F})$, the representation of [def-wf-fundamental-representation] (continuous by [lem-wf-weil-fundamental-representation]), is an exact tensor equivalence between lisse Weil sheaves
on $C_0$ and the representations of [def-wf-weil-group]: a short exact
sequence $0\to\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal F''\to0$ corresponds to
$0\to V'\to V\to V''\to0$. Subobjects, quotients and subquotients therefore
match on the two sides, in both directions.

## Proof

*Finite level.* Each $\mathcal O_E/\mathfrak m_E^n$ is a finite ring, so
[cor-galois-lisse-representations] identifies locally constant sheaves of finite free
$\mathcal O_E/\mathfrak m_E^n$-modules on $C$ with finite free modules over
that ring carrying a continuous $P$-action. Rank is a property of the stalk
and is constant because $C$ is connected.

*Integral and rational levels.* A lisse adic model has surjective
transition maps, so the stalks $M_n$ form a surjective system whose limit is
finite free over $\mathcal O_E$, with continuous action because the
$\mathfrak m_E$-adic topology is the limit of the discrete quotient
topologies; levelwise reduction inverts the construction. Morphism groups
are the limits of their finite-level counterparts,
$\Hom_{\mathcal O_E[P]}(M,N)=\varprojlim_n\Hom_P(M_n,N_n)$: a map of adic
systems is by definition a compatible family of finite-level maps, while
$\Hom_{\mathcal O_E}(M,N)$ is finite free with reductions $\Hom(M_n,N_n)$
and $P$-invariants commute with inverse limits. The transition maps of
this tower need not be surjective (for $E=\mathbf Q_3(\zeta_3)$,
$\pi=\zeta_3-1$, a trivial lattice and the lattice of a cubic Kummer
character agree modulo $\pi$, but every equivariant map between them modulo
$\pi^2$ satisfies $\pi a=0$ and reduces to zero), but each
$\Hom_P(M_n,N_n)$ is a finite group, so the tower is Mittag–Leffler and
$\varprojlim^1$ vanishes; this is all the inverse-limit argument needs: a
compatible family of finite-level maps has a unique lift, and two maps
agreeing at every level are equal. Hence the functor is fully faithful.
Inverting the uniformizer on morphisms and passing to the filtered colimit
over the finite $E\subset\Qlb$ are each given by a universal property and are
performed the same way on both sides, so the equivalence descends to the
coefficients of [d-real-setup].

*Frobenius descent.* Geometric Frobenius is an automorphism of the
scheme $C$, so $\Frob^*$ is an autoequivalence of lisse sheaves on $C$;
comparing the stalks at $\bar\eta$ and $\Frob(\bar\eta)$ along the
degree-one lift $\gamma$ turns it into a twist of $\rho$ by the conjugation
$c_\gamma(g)=\gamma g\gamma^{-1}$ of $P$, and the comparison is oriented
so that the twist is $\rho\mapsto\rho\circ c_\gamma^{-1}$,
$g\mapsto\rho(\gamma^{-1}g\gamma)$ (the opposite orientation amounts to
replacing $\gamma$ by the degree $-1$ lift $\gamma^{-1}$). A Weil
structure $\varphi:\Frob^*\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$ is therefore an
automorphism $\Phi$ of $V$ with
$\Phi\,\rho(g)\,\Phi^{-1}=\rho(\gamma g\gamma^{-1})$ for $g\in P$, which is
exactly the relation making $g\gamma^{n}\mapsto\rho(g)\Phi^{n}$
multiplicative; since every element of $W(C_0)$ is uniquely $g\gamma^{n}$
by [def-wf-weil-group], setting $\rho(\gamma)=\Phi$ extends $\rho$ to
$W(C_0)$. (With the relation written as
$\Phi\,\rho(\gamma g\gamma^{-1})\,\Phi^{-1}=\rho(g)$ one would be forced to
set $\rho(\gamma)=\Phi^{-1}$ instead.) The choice $\rho(\gamma)=\Phi$ is
the geometric Frobenius normalization of [def-wf-weil-group]: at a closed
point $x$ with $k(x)=\Fq$ the operator induced by $\varphi$ on
$\mathcal F_{\bar x}$ is the geometric Frobenius $F_x$, because $\Frob$
composed with the arithmetic Frobenius of $k$ is the absolute Frobenius of
$C$, which acts trivially on etale sheaves, and $F_x$ has degree $+1$; so
the degree-one elements $g\gamma$ of $W(C_0)$ act through $\Phi$, not
$\Phi^{-1}$, in agreement with $F=\rho(\gamma)$ and with the Tate line
$\Qlb(1)=\mathcal B_{q^{-1}}$ (geometric Frobenius acts on $\Qlb(1)$ by
$q^{-1}$), in the notation of the constant Weil twist
[def-wf-constant-weil-twist]. Another lift changes
$\Phi$ by an element of $\rho(P)$ and gives an isomorphic representation. The
morphism condition $u\varphi=\psi\,\Frob^{*}u$ says on stalks that $u$
intertwines the two operators $\Phi$, which with $P$-equivariance is exactly
$W(C_0)$-equivariance; hence full faithfulness.

*Exactness.* Exactness and tensor products are levelwise for adic
systems and survive the localization and the filtered colimit, and Weil
kernels and cokernels are computed on the underlying sheaves. The matching
of subobjects, quotients and subquotients follows.

Fix the finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$, where $q=p^a$, a prime
$\ell\neq p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$ and an
isomorphism $\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$. Let
$f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a smooth proper morphism of separated finite-type
$k_0$-schemes of pure relative dimension $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ (no
admissibility hypothesis on $f_0$ or the structure morphisms: the exceptional
inverse images are the constructible ones, defined for every separated
finite-type morphism, so the operations of [prop-weil-operations] apply), and let
$\mathcal F_0$ be a lisse $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf on $X_0$ which is punctually
$\iota$-pure of weight $w\in\mathbf R$ in the sense of
[def-weil-punctual-weights]. Then for every $i\in\mathbf Z$:

1. **(a)** the canonical map
$R^{i}f_{0!}\mathcal F_0\to R^{i}f_{0*}\mathcal F_0$ is an isomorphism of
Weil sheaves, and this sheaf is lisse;
1. **(b)** it is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w+i$: for every closed
point $y\in|Y_0|$, with $q_y=\#\kappa(y)$, every eigenvalue $\alpha$ of the
local geometric Frobenius $F_y$ on
$(R^{i}f_{0*}\mathcal F_0)_{\bar y}=H^{i}(X_{\bar y},\mathcal F)$
([cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-qbar]) satisfies
$|\iota(\alpha)|=q_y^{(w+i)/2}$.

In the absolute case $Y_0=\Spec k_0$, $\mathcal F_0=(\Qlb)_{X_0}$ ($w=0$)
clause (b) says that every eigenvalue $\alpha$ of geometric Frobenius on
$H^{i}(X,\Qlb)$ satisfies $|\iota(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}$.

## Proof

Write $f:X\to Y$ for the geometric fiber of $f_0$ and $\mathcal F$ for the
underlying sheaf of $\mathcal F_0$. The upper bound on weights is the
