direct-image theorem [cor-zl-rfshriek-sheaf]; the content here is that
relative duality supplies the matching lower bound.

*Step 1 (coincidence and local constancy).* Since $f$ is proper, the
compactification $j=\operatorname{id}$, $p=f$ gives the canonical
identification $Rf_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*$ of
[cor-cbc-proper-coincidence], and under it the exchange map
$\operatorname{Ex}_!$ defining the Weil structure on $Rf_!\mathcal F$ is the
exchange map $\operatorname{Ex}_*$ defining the Weil structure on
$Rf_*\mathcal F$ ([cor-cbc-proper-coincidence], and the description of the
Weil isomorphisms in [prop-weil-operations]). Hence
$R^{i}f_{0!}\mathcal F_0\to R^{i}f_{0*}\mathcal F_0$ is an isomorphism of
Weil sheaves for every $i$; this is the first half of (a).

For local constancy, choose a lattice for $\mathcal F$ over the ring of
integers $\mathcal O_E$ of a finite extension $E/\Ql$, with reductions
$\mathcal F_n$ modulo $\lambda^{n}$; since $\mathcal F$ is lisse, each
$\mathcal F_n$ is a finite locally constant sheaf of
$\mathcal O_E/\lambda^{n}$-modules, of $\ell$-power torsion with $\ell$
invertible on $Y$. By [thm-fin-proper-constructibility-complete] the sheaves
$R^{q}f_*\mathcal F_n$ are constructible, and a constructible sheaf all of
whose specialization maps are isomorphisms is locally constant; so it
suffices to show that for a geometric point $\bar s$ of $Y$ and a geometric
point $\bar t$ of the strict henselization $Y'=Y_{(\bar s)}$ the
specialization map
$(R^{q}f_*\mathcal F_n)_{\bar s}\to(R^{q}f_*\mathcal F_n)_{\bar t}$ is an
isomorphism. Proper base change
[prop-weil-proet-finite-proper-base-change] along $Y'\to Y$ lets us replace
$f$ by its base change $f':X'\to Y'$, which is again smooth and proper, with
closed point $\bar s$; then
$(R^{q}f'_*\mathcal F_n)_{\bar s}=H^{q}(X',\mathcal F_n)$ ($Y'$ being strictly
local), the geometric-fibre formula [cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-finite]
identifies $(R^{q}f'_*\mathcal F_n)_{\bar t}$ with
$H^{q}(X'_{\bar t},\mathcal F_n)$, and the specialization map becomes the
restriction along $h:X'_{\bar t}\to X'$. We show that
$\mathcal F_n\to Rh_*h^{-1}\mathcal F_n$ restricts to an isomorphism on the
closed fibre $X'_{\bar s}$. The question is étale local on $X'$ and
$R^{q}h_*$ commutes with étale restriction, so we may pass to an étale
$U\to X'$ on which $\mathcal F_n$ is constant, with value $M$; the composite
$U\to Y'$ is smooth, and smooth base change [sbc-thm-smooth-base-change],
applied to the cartesian square formed by $U\to Y'$ and the
quasi-compact quasi-separated $\bar t:\Spec\Omega\to Y'$ and to the
constant sheaf $M$ on $\Spec\Omega$, gives
$R^{q}h_{U*}M\cong(U\to Y')^{-1}R^{q}\bar t_*M$. As $Y'$ is strictly local,
the stalk of $R^{q}\bar t_*M$ at $\bar s$ is $H^{q}(\Spec\Omega,M)$, which is
$M$ for $q=0$ and $0$ for $q>0$ since $\Omega$ is separably closed. Thus
$(Rh_*h^{-1}\mathcal F_n)|_{X'_{\bar s}}\cong\mathcal F_n|_{X'_{\bar s}}$.
Applying [cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-finite] at the closed point
$\bar s$ of the strictly local $Y'$ twice, to
$K=Rh_*h^{-1}\mathcal F_n\in D^+(X',\mathcal O_E/\lambda^{n})$ and to
$\mathcal F_n$, we get

$$
H^{q}(X'_{\bar t},\mathcal F_n)=H^{q}(X',Rh_*h^{-1}\mathcal F_n)
\cong H^{q}\bigl(X'_{\bar s},(Rh_*h^{-1}\mathcal F_n)|_{X'_{\bar s}}\bigr)
\cong H^{q}(X'_{\bar s},\mathcal F_n)\cong H^{q}(X',\mathcal F_n),
$$

compatibly with restriction along $h$. So every specialization map is an
isomorphism, and every $R^{q}f_*\mathcal F_n$ is finite locally constant.
No separate local-acyclicity theorem is needed: the vanishing of
$R^{q}h_*$ along the closed fibre is exactly what smooth base change
supplies. The complexes $Rf_*\mathcal F_n$ form the reduction tower of
$Rf_*$ of the lattice; passing to the limit and inverting $\lambda$, with
the stalks computed by [cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-qbar], the
specialization maps of $R^{i}f_*\mathcal F$ are isomorphisms of
finite-dimensional $\Qlb$-vector spaces and $R^{i}f_*\mathcal F$ is lisse.
This completes (a).

*Step 2 (upper bound).* A punctually $\iota$-pure sheaf of weight $w$ is
$\iota$-mixed of weights at most $w$ in the sense of
[def-weil-punctual-weights] (take $m=1$, $w_1=w$). Hence
[cor-zl-rfshriek-sheaf], applied to the separated finite-type
$f_0$, shows that $R^{i}f_{0!}\mathcal F_0=R^{i}f_{0*}\mathcal F_0$ is
$\iota$-mixed of weights at most $w+i$. Taking the stalk at $\bar y$ of the
filtration in [def-weil-punctual-weights] is exact and $F_y$-equivariant,
so every eigenvalue $\alpha$ of $F_y$ on $(R^{i}f_{0*}\mathcal F_0)_{\bar y}$
is an eigenvalue on a graded piece of some weight $w_r\leq w+i$, whence
$|\iota(\alpha)|\leq q_y^{(w+i)/2}$.

*Step 3 (lower bound by relative Verdier duality).* Let
$\mathcal F_0^\vee=R\mathcal H om(\mathcal F_0,\Qlb)$ be the coefficient dual
of $\mathcal F_0$: since $\mathcal F$ is lisse, it is locally on the site a
finite free $\Qlb$-module, so by [lem-sf-hom-finite-projective]
$\mathcal F^\vee$ is concentrated in degree $0$, lisse, and a Weil sheaf by
[prop-weil-operations]; its local Frobenius at a closed point $x$ is the
contragredient of that of $\mathcal F_0$, so its eigenvalues are the
$\beta^{-1}$ with $\beta$ an eigenvalue of $F_x$ on $\mathcal F_{\bar x}$,
and as $|\iota(\beta^{-1})|=|\iota(\beta)|^{-1}=q_x^{-w/2}$ it is
punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $-w$. By
[lem-wf-tate-twist-frobenius] the local Frobenius on $\Qlb(d)_{\bar x}$
is $q_x^{-d}$, so $\mathcal F_0^\vee(d)$ is lisse and punctually
$\iota$-pure of weight $-w-2d$.

The relative duality isomorphism is assembled from three canonical
isomorphisms, each a morphism of Weil complexes by [prop-weil-operations]
(composition, purity and duality isomorphisms are Weil). First, the
tensor–Hom form of the Verdier exchange [lem-sf-tensor-hom], applied to
$f$ with $M=\mathcal F$ and $N=\Qlb_Y$, together with $Rf_!=Rf_*$
from Step 1:

$$
Rf_*R\mathcal H om_X\bigl(\mathcal F,Rf^!\Qlb_Y\bigr)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
R\mathcal H om_Y\bigl(Rf_*\mathcal F,\Qlb_Y\bigr).
$$

Second, the smooth orientation: [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity], for the
smooth separated $f$ of relative dimension $d$ and $K=\Qlb_Y$ at the
$\Qlb$-stage, gives $\Qlb_X(d)[2d]=Lf^*\Qlb_Y(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf^!\Qlb_Y$.
Third, the perfect form of duality: $\mathcal F$ is perfect over
$\Qlb_X$, so [lem-sf-twist-interchange] with $m=d$, $n=2d$ gives
$R\mathcal H om_X(\mathcal F,\Qlb_X(d)[2d])\cong\mathcal F^\vee(d)[2d]$.
Composing,

$$
R\mathcal H om_Y\bigl(Rf_*\mathcal F,\Qlb_Y\bigr)\;\cong\;
Rf_*\bigl(\mathcal F^\vee(d)\bigr)[2d]
$$

as Weil complexes on $Y$. By Step 1 the cohomology sheaves
$R^{j}f_*\mathcal F$ of $Rf_*\mathcal F$ are lisse; for a lisse sheaf
$\mathcal L$ on $Y$, [lem-sf-hom-finite-projective] (locally on the site
$\mathcal L$ is finite free) gives
$\mathcal E xt^{r}(\mathcal L,\Qlb_Y)=0$ for $r>0$ and
$\mathcal H om(\mathcal L,\Qlb_Y)=\mathcal L^\vee$ lisse, with stalks the
linear duals of those of $\mathcal L$. Induction on the truncation
triangles of the bounded complex $Rf_*\mathcal F$ therefore identifies the
cohomology sheaf in degree $-i$ of the left side with
$(R^{i}f_*\mathcal F)^\vee$. Taking $\mathcal H^{-i}$ of both sides gives the
Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism of lisse sheaves

$$
\bigl(R^{i}f_{0*}\mathcal F_0\bigr)^{\vee}
\;\cong\;
R^{2d-i}f_{0*}\bigl(\mathcal F_0^{\vee}(d)\bigr).
$$

Now fix a closed point $y\in|Y_0|$ and $\bar y$ over it. Step 2 applied to
the lisse, punctually pure $\mathcal F_0^\vee(d)$ of weight $-w-2d$ in degree
$2d-i$ bounds every eigenvalue $\gamma$ of $F_y$ on the right-hand stalk by
$|\iota(\gamma)|\leq q_y^{(-w-2d+2d-i)/2}=q_y^{(-w-i)/2}$. The left-hand
sheaf being the dual of a lisse sheaf, its stalk at $\bar y$ is the
linear dual of $(R^{i}f_{0*}\mathcal F_0)_{\bar y}$ with the contragredient
action of $F_y$, whose eigenvalues are the $\alpha^{-1}$ with $\alpha$ an
eigenvalue of $F_y$ on $(R^{i}f_{0*}\mathcal F_0)_{\bar y}$. Hence
$|\iota(\alpha)|^{-1}\leq q_y^{(-w-i)/2}$, i.e.

$$
|\iota(\alpha)|\geq q_y^{(w+i)/2}.
$$

With Step 2 this gives $|\iota(\alpha)|=q_y^{(w+i)/2}$ for every
eigenvalue of every $F_y$, which is punctual $\iota$-purity of weight $w+i$.
This proves (b).

*What the upgrade costs.* Steps 1 and 3 use only smoothness, properness and
duality; no no-cancellation argument enters, because purity is read off
eigenvalue by eigenvalue. All the arithmetic sits in
[cor-zl-rfshriek-sheaf]: without it Step 3 bounds nothing, and with it both
inequalities are automatic.

*Why the descent is needed.* The factorization of
[prop-trace-determinant] is produced by one chosen $\ell$, so it only
exhibits $Z\in\Ql(T)$. The argument above does not compare the different
$\ell$; it uses only that the coefficients $z_n$ are rational integers, so
that a rank bound over $\Ql$ propagates to $\Q$. The comparison of the
realizations (that $P_i$ is independent of $\ell$) is a separate statement,
[prop-integral-recovery].

The degree-one estimate for an irreducible factor identifies the Fourier
transform of the ordinary middle extension $(j_*\mathcal M)[1]$ with a
middle extension $(j'_*\mathcal M')[1]$ on the dual line, determines the
weight of $\mathcal M'$ through the extension by zero and Plancherel, and
reads off $H^1_c(\mathbf A^1,j_*\mathcal M)$ as the origin stalk of
$j'_*\mathcal M'$. The curve reduction then only needs finite-map
transport, geometric constituents after a constant extension, and the
surjection supplied by deleting a regular point; it performs no further
Fourier-theoretic identification.

The degree-one estimate uses the Fourier transform of extension by zero. The reduction requires finite-map transport, geometric constituents after a constant extension, and the surjection supplied by deleting a regular point. None of these steps identifies the Fourier transforms of ordinary middle extension and extension by zero.

Three things that a reader of the compiled Fourier–Deligne chapter might expect are
*not* in this file, on purpose. (i) The purity of the kernel
($\mathcal K_\psi$ punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $0$) is a weight-theoretic
statement about the same sheaf, and it is used in layer 2, not in the yoga of
layer 1. (ii) The perverse amplitude of the transform is a statement about
the perverse $t$-structure, not a consequence of the six operations; it is
layer 3. (iii) The concentration of $\FT_\psi(j_!\mathcal M)$ for a
nonexceptional $\mathcal M$, and the identification of the origin fibre with
$H^1_c$, use the geometry of affine curves (via the two affine computations of
the weight-estimate chapter) and weight theory respectively; they are layer 2
and layer 3. What remains in layer 1 is exactly what can be said about
$\FT_\psi$ before any weight is mentioned.

attrs.title: What is deliberately absent, and why

objects.body:
The purity chapter of this blueprint introduces the same notion under
its own conventions, as the relative spectrum of the symmetric algebra
of a locally free module of constant rank, together with its zero
section; that chapter states it inside its purity conventions, whereas
[def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section] above is the coordinate-free
form used here, so that the present chapter can be read before those
conventions are available. The two definitions agree on the schemes
they both treat, and neither of them assumes anything about $f^{!}$:
the purity statement itself is a theorem of the purity chapter, not part
of this definition.

attrs.title: Relation to the purity chapter's vector bundles

objects.body:
Noetherianness of $S$ is used only through the finiteness of the set of
irreducible components of $X$ and through the quasi-compactness and
quasi-separatedness assertions of the scheme conventions [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Accordingly,
[thm-chow-lemma] remains true for a quasi-compact and quasi-separated
scheme $S$ and a separated morphism $f\colon X\to S$ of finite type such that
$X$ has finitely many irreducible components; see 0203. The
proof of that variant proceeds by absolute noetherian approximation, writing
$S$ as a limit of noetherian schemes and descending the data constructed
above; it is not needed for the applications in this blueprint, where the base
is always noetherian.

The objects $\omega_{X,A_{E,n}}$, with transition maps

$$
\omega_{X,A_{E,n+1}}\longrightarrow
\omega_{X,A_{E,n+1}}\otimes^L_{A_{E,n+1}}A_{E,n}
\xrightarrow{u}\omega_{X,A_{E,n}},
$$

form a normalized system by [lem-coef-finite-dualizing].
The uniform Tor interval is $[-2\dim X,0]$, by
[lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata].
For a normalized system $K_n$ with uniform Tor interval
$[a,b]$, the maps of [cor-coef-finite-verdier] similarly
make $D_{X,A_{E,n}}K_n$ a normalized system with interval
$[-b-2\dim X,-a]$. Evaluation and double-dual maps are maps
of these coefficient systems. The normalization cocycles here
are the ones required by [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum].

To pass to the integral category of
[def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], the next argument must
still establish that a normalized system reconstructs with its
given reductions. It must also verify the uniform finite-Tor
condition for the reductions of an object of that definition:
the definition literally requires uniformly bounded constructible
reductions, rather than explicitly asserting finite Tor amplitude.
These are derived-completion and residue-test steps; neither is
proved simply by writing $R\varprojlim$. No common lisse
stratification of all finite levels is assumed in the finite
comparisons proved above.

attrs.title: Normalized towers supplied to the integral argument

objects.body:
Fix $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne \operatorname{char}(k_0)$, and $\iota:\DLAQ\simeq\mathbf C$. Write
$A_0=\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$, $A=A_0\otimes k$, and use a prime to denote the
dual affine line. All cohomology is geometric, with geometric Frobenius
([def-weil-frobenius-detailed]).
A lisse Weil sheaf is *pure of weight $w$* if every eigenvalue
$\alpha$ at a closed point $x$ satisfies
$|\iota\alpha|=q_x^{w/2}$; replace equality by $\leq$ for an upper bound
([def-weil-punctual-weights]).
The twist $(-1)$ raises weights by two ([def-wf-tate-twist]).

For a dense open $j:U_0\hookrightarrow A_0$, $j_*F$ denotes the
*ordinary* sheaf direct image. Its stalks at missing points are
inertia invariants; its curve perverse intermediate extension is
$j_{!*}(F[1])=(j_*F)[1]$ ([def-wf-middle-extension]). Unramifiedness at infinity means that inertia
at $\infty\in\mathbf P^1_k$ acts trivially on the geometric generic fiber.
A geometrically constant sheaf has trivial geometric fundamental-group
action, while its Frobenius module may be nontrivial.

Clause (1) is the classical finiteness theorem for the higher direct
images of a constructible sheaf under a morphism of finite type of
Noetherian schemes, SGA IV, Exposé XIV, Th. 1.1 (Stacks Project, Theorem 63.14.5, [Tag 0GL0](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0GL0), the proper case being $Rf_!=Rf_*$); its compact-support
form for a separated morphism of finite presentation is Stacks Project,
More Etale Cohomology, Theorem 63.14.5,
[Tag `0GL0`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0GL0). It
is proved in this blueprint as
[thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility] of the constructibility chapter, by Deligne's
finite-boundary induction: the open-immersion case is reduced to smooth
morphisms with locally constant coefficients, which are treated by duality
from the compact-support theory and not by an appeal to constructibility of
the ordinary direct image itself, and the general finite-type case is
assembled from the open-immersion and proper cases by a finite alternating
Cech resolution. The proper case is the comparison theorem
[obl-fin-comparison], and the resulting finite-type statement is
[sbc-thm-finiteness-finite-type], whose earlier circular
open-immersion argument is thereby superseded.

Clause (2) is the cohomological-dimension bound of a finite-type scheme
over a separably closed field: the affine case is Stacks Project, Etale
Cohomology, Proposition 59.95.6,
[Tag `0F0V`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F0V), and
the general case Stacks Project, Etale Cohomology, Section 59.95,
[Tag `0F0P`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F0P). It is
proved in this blueprint as [thm-sc-finite-type-torsion-cd] of
the Jacobian chapter, from the affine bound for arbitrary torsion sheaves and the
comparison of the etale and Zariski topologies, with the vanishing of the
torsion cohomological dimension of a separably closed field as the base
case ([lem-kun-cd-sep-closed-point]).

Consequently both clauses hold over every separably closed field, which is
the form used below: [thm-exc-direct-image-input-holds].

attrs.title: Sources of the direct-image input, and its proof here

objects.body:
Passing to the mate under an adjunction does *not* preserve
isomorphisms: for an adjunction $F\dashv G$ a map $FA\to B$ can be an
isomorphism while its transpose $A\to GB$ is not, and conversely, since
the unit and the counit intervening need not be isomorphisms. In
particular the base-change comparison
$\beta:Lg'^*Rf^{\times}\to Rf'^{\times}Lg^*$ cannot be tested for
isomorphy by testing its adjoint under $Rf'_!\dashv Rf'^{\times}$, and a
criterion of that shape is invalid. This is visible already for
$f=\operatorname{id}_Y$ and an open immersion $g:Y'\hookrightarrow Y$:
the comparison is the identity of $Lg^*K$, an isomorphism, while its
transpose under the adjunctions $Rf'_!\dashv Rf'^{\times}$ and
$Lg^*\dashv Rg_*$ is the composite of the counit (the identity) with the
unit of $Lg^*\dashv Rg_*$, i.e. the localization unit
$K\to Rg_*Lg^*K$, which is not an isomorphism (for $K=\Lambda$ its
cokernel is the skyscraper at the boundary).

attrs.title: The mate of the base-change comparison is not a criterion

objects.body:
The final proposition is used downstream as follows: the monodromy and
real-purity chapter uses the perfectness, the dualizing-complex
identification and the equivariance; the Fourier–Deligne chapter uses the
global duality and the equivariance; the affine-line weight estimate and
the zeta-function linear algebra use the trace isomorphism, the Frobenius
similitude and the reciprocal eigenvalues; the final Weil-conjecture
chapter uses the graded-commutativity clause for the symmetry
$b_i=b_{2d-i}$ and the sign in the functional equation.
*What remains open* splits into two lists. *Inside this spine*:
(i) the axiom verifications for the concrete operations — base change and
biduality — which are the content of the base-change chapters; and (ii) the
two still-pending master interfaces of 1, the all-stage projection
formula and Verdier biduality, on which the six-operations package is
conditional. The finiteness input is *not* among them: it is proved in
9 and assembled in 1. Global duality and the pairing
identification are cited directly as [thm-sf-global-duality] and
[thm-sf-identification]; their degreewise field consequence is
[thm-pod-degreewise-perfectness-over-a-field]. *Inside
the external interface* (the purity chapter 14, which proves
[thm-pur-adic-reconstruction]): the étale-local structure of smooth morphisms, the
étale locality of the purity map, the tensor formula, and — among the
purity nodes that this route bypasses — the projective-bundle formula, the
localized top Chern class, vector triangularity, deformation-to-the-normal-cone
invariance and the frame independence for frames of an ideal. The
$p$-primary case in characteristic $p$ is excluded throughout by
$\ell\ne p$.

attrs.title: Where this feeds, and what remains

objects.body:
The material above replaces three uncited invocations in the compiled
blueprint. (1) The definition of the geometric fundamental representation
of lisse sheaves in the monodromy chapter invokes "the standard equivalence
of lisse sheaves on a connected scheme with continuous representations of
its etale fundamental group": this is
[cor-galois-lisse-representations] together with the definition of
$\pi_1$ in [def-galois-fibre-functor]. (2) The proof of the
additive-character lemma of the monodromy chapter invokes "the defining
finite-etale fiber-functor equivalence" and the dictionary between torsors,
finite $\pi_1$-sets and homomorphisms: this is
[thm-galois-fundamental] together with [cor-galois-abelian-h1].
(3) The proof of the finite-monodromy lemma of the smooth base change
chapter invokes "open subgroups correspond to finite etale coverings": this
is [cor-galois-open-subgroups]. The two nodes of the
proper-base-change chapter that stated the torsor–$H^1$ identification
and the finite-etale correspondence as admitted classical inputs are proved
here as [thm-galois-torsor-h1] and [thm-galois-lc-etale]. Every
proof above is written out; the only facts used without proof are
elementary and named where used: Nakayama's lemma and the structure of
finite etale algebras over a separably closed field
([lem-fet-locally-trivial]), glueing of schemes along open immersions
([lem-galois-glue]), and the limit arguments spreading finitely
presented data out over an etale neighbourhood.

attrs.title: Where the compiled blueprint used this without citation

objects.body:
The Kunneth-specific arguments of this chapter are decomposed in full:
the Kunneth map and its comparison with the cup product
([def-kun-kunneth-map], *The Kunneth map via the relative cup product*,
[lem-kun-kunneth-map-agrees]), the one-proper-factor formula
([lem-kun-0f14a], [lem-kun-0f14b]), the closed-point
statements, the open-immersion base change [lem-kun-0f1h], the
field base change [lem-kun-0f1i], the projection-formula variant
[lem-kun-0f1j] and its unbounded form [lem-kun-0f1n], and
the final theorem [thm-kun-0f1p]. The statements listed below are
the *imported general inputs* that these proofs quote; each is a
decomposed statement with a Stacks reference, and each is used only
where no earlier chapter of this blueprint supplies it.

1. *Limits:* the base change along limits of cartesian squares
[lem-kun-0ezt]
(Tag [0EZT](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EZT)) and the
descent of a sheaf on an affine inverse limit
[lem-kun-descent-limit]
(Tag [0EYN](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EYN)). The
descent of a quasi-compact open in an affine limit is proved in this
chapter as [lem-kun-descent-limit-open] (the affine case of Tag
[01ZM](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01ZM)); the ambient-foundations chapter
proves the continuity
thm:weil-pbc-etale-cohomology-continuity and the smooth-base-change chapter the
higher-direct-image limit formula
[sbc-lem-higher-direct-image-limit], which are the cases quoted in
the proofs above; the two statements listed here are the limit
statements that are not among those.
1. *Constructibility:* the constructible generation
[lem-kun-03sa]
(Tag [03SA](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03SA)). The
approximation with controlled support that the proofs above quote is
proved in this chapter as [lem-kun-cp-approximation], in the case of
the set of closed points of a scheme of finite type over a separably
closed field; the weak
Serre property is lem:weil-pbc-constructible-serre of the proper-base-change chapter and the finite-pushforward statement is
[fin4-thm-finite-morphisms-constructible] of the smooth-base-change chapter, both
proved there and quoted above.
1. *Base change:* the integral-normal base produced by a failure of
base change [lem-kun-0f1d]
(Tag [0F1D](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F1D)), the base
change for flat finitely presented morphisms with geometrically reduced
fibres [lem-kun-0eys]
(Tag [0EYS](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EYS)) and the
strict henselization as a limit of smaller-dimensional finite type
algebras [lem-kun-0f0u]
(Tag [0F0U](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F0U)). The
commutation of direct images with field extensions [lem-kun-0f1c] is
*proved* in this chapter from the limit form of smooth base change
[lem-kun-0f09] and the topological invariance of etale cohomology
(thm:weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance), with the algebraic
input [lem-kun-fg-separable-smooth] (Tag [07BV](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07BV)). The
vanishing at a separably closed field [lem-kun-0ezp], the unbounded
proper base change over $\kunZn$ [lem-kun-0f0c] and the two
projection formulas [lem-kun-0f0g], [lem-kun-0f0f] are
*proved* in this chapter, their Stacks tags being
[0EZP](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EZP),
[0F0C](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F0C),
[0F0G](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F0G) and
[0F0F](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F0F). the proper-base-change chapter
proves proper base change for torsion sheaves
(thm:weil-pbc-finite-torsion,
thm:weil-pbc-bounded-below) and the smooth-base-change chapter the classical
smooth base change ([sbc-thm-smooth-base-change],
[sbc-thm-bounded-below-derived-smooth-base-change]), which are the
instances quoted in the proofs above; the projection formula at all
coefficient stages is the interface
fix-prop-projection-formula of the framework chapter, proved in the
six-functor chapter of this manuscript, which is placed *after*
the present chapter and can therefore not be quoted here.
1. *Algebra:* the algebra statement that a *finitely generated* separable field extension is a filtered colimit of finitely generated smooth subalgebras, [lem-kun-fg-separable-smooth] (Tag [07BV](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07BV)). The general separable case, and the algebraic case, are proved in this chapter as [lem-kun-separable-smooth-colimit] and [lem-kun-algebraic-separable-smooth]; the finitely generated statement is the only ingredient of the proof of [lem-kun-0f1c] that is not already available in this manuscript.
1. *Cohomological dimension:* the finite-dimensionality
statement [lem-kun-0f10]
(Tags [0F10](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F10),
[0F0P](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F0P)) and the
tensor products with a constant complex [lem-kun-0f12],
[lem-kun-0f0e]
(Tags [0F12](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F12),
[0F0E](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F0E)). The
homological algebra used by the two projection-formula variants is
*proved* in this chapter: the tor-amplitude criterion
[lem-kun-0f1m] follows from the functorial flat replacement
[lem-kun-bounded-flat-replacement], the K-flat criteria
[lem-kun-kflat-criteria], the flatness criterion
[lem-kun-tor-cokernel-flat] and the flat K-flat resolutions
[lem-kun-flat-resolution-existence], itself proved from the
truncation telescope [lem-kun-hocolim-truncations]; likewise the
direct-sum statement [lem-kun-0f11] is proved from the
filtered-colimit theorem
lem:weil-pbc-direct-image-filtered-colimit of the ambient-foundations chapter by a
hypercohomology comparison, so that no homological-algebra statement
of this chapter is imported any more. For
schemes of finite type over a separably closed field the
cohomological-dimension bounds of the Jacobian chapter
(lem:sc-cohomological-dimension) and the finiteness chain of
the constructibility chapter ([sbc-thm-finiteness-finite-type]) give the curve and
proper instances; the general dimension statement above is quoted from
the Stacks project.

The eight imported statements listed above are the residue of the reduction
performed in this chapter. For each of them the Stacks proof reduces to a
development which is not yet part of this manuscript, and the reductions are
recorded above in the source notes: the limit statements
[lem-kun-0ezt] and [lem-kun-descent-limit] need the descent of
finitely presented and etale morphisms along affine limits (Stacks Tags 0EYL
and 0EXJ, with the algebra of finitely presented descent, whose first step is proved in this chapter as [lem-kun-fp-algebra-descent]); the constructible
generation [lem-kun-03sa] needs the finitely presented presentations of
Modules on Sites, Lemma 18.30.7 (Tag 093C) together with the constructibility
of representable sheaves, Lemma 59.73.1 (Tag 03S8); the base-change statements
[lem-kun-0f1d] and [lem-kun-0eys] need the witness diagram of Tag
0F08 with Tag 0F0B, respectively the local factorization of Tag 0EZX with the
section lemma Tag 0EY5; [lem-kun-0f0u] needs the dimension theory of
quasi-finite algebras over a polynomial ring on top of Noether normalization;
and [lem-kun-0f10] needs the Mayer–Vietoris sequences (Tags 0EYK and
0A50) together with the affine bounds of Tags 0F0X and 0F0V. The purely
algebraic input [lem-kun-fg-separable-smooth] needs the theory of
separating transcendence bases and generic smoothness of finitely generated
separable extensions.
No other statement of this chapter is left without proof: the
proved-but-unquoted statements of the blueprint replace the
corresponding Stacks inputs wherever the chapter order allows.

attrs.title: Inventory of the imported inputs of this chapter

objects.body:
*Layer 1 (this file).* The transform and everything that follows from
the six operations and the classical trace formula. Nothing here mentions a
weight: there is no $L^2$-weight parameter, no punctual purity, no
mixedness, no reality, no perverse amplitude. The properties are the ones a
kernel transform always has — it is exact and triangulated (P2), its stalks
are integrals against the kernel (P3), it commutes with base change (P5) and
with the coefficient sheaves of the base (P7), it is compatible with shifts
and twists (P6), and it is invertible (P13) — together with the two
computations of the kernel's own cohomology that the definition makes
accessible (P4) and the two numerical identities that come from the classical
finite Fourier transform (P8, P9).
*Layer 2 (weight theory).* Only now does weight enter, through the
$L^2$-weight parameter of def:wf-l2-norm and its dictionary: Plancherel
P9 becomes the statement that the $L^2$-weight shifts by one under the
transform, purity and reality of the kernel and of the input give the
realified kernel, and the origin fibre of the transform is identified with
$H^1_c$ with its eigenvalue bound. Those statements cite P8, P9, P10 and P13
of this file and the weight foundations of the weight-foundations and weight-functoriality chapters; they are not
stated here.
*Layer 3 (perverse and middle-extension theory).* The perverse amplitude
of the transform (Artin–Gabber, the perverse-curve chapter) and the Fourier theory of middle
extensions: the concentration statement for a nonexceptional input, and the
stationary-phase identification at the origin.
The affine-line weight estimate then consumes layer 2 and layer 3 together.
Keeping the layers apart is what makes the estimate readable: layer 1 is pure
yoga, layer 2 is where the arithmetic enters, layer 3 is where the geometry of
the input enters.

attrs.title: The three layers, and why the order matters

objects.body:
For the proofs below we use the following consequence of the local
theory (for smooth curves this is [lem-sc-point-cartier]; in
general: Stacks Project, Varieties, Lemma 33.43.8, Tag
[0B8Y](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B8Y)): a closed point
$P$ of a smooth curve over a field has
invertible ideal sheaf, i.e. is an effective Cartier divisor, and
$\mathcal{O}_{C,P}$ is a discrete valuation ring.

attrs.title: Closed points of curves are Cartier divisors

objects.body:
In Stacks Project, Chapter 44, a *smooth projective curve over $k$*
is a variety (integral, separated, finite type, dimension $1$) which is
smooth and projective over $k$
([def-pc-smooth-projective-curve]); the proof of Proposition
44.6.6 only uses this in combination with the fact that, for $k$
separably closed, all base changes $X_K$ are again smooth projective
curves ([prop-pc-xk-integral]), which is what the geometric
arguments (the Cartier criterion, the density of rational points, the
DVR computations) need. This is the reason why the individual lemmas
of the chain are stated for separably closed $k$ —Stacks states
44.6.2–44.6.4 for arbitrary fields, but in the proof of 44.6.6 they
are only used in the separably closed case (the deeper geometric
irreducibility of $X$ is automatic then; cf. [prop-pc-xk-integral]
and the discussion in [thm-pc-picard-representable]). The proof of
[prop-pc-xk-integral] uses the ``smoothness'' route
(smooth $\Rightarrow$ regular $\Rightarrow$ normal $\Rightarrow$
decomposition into integral components, with connectedness); the
classical alternative route goes through the fact that $\bar k/k$ is
purely inseparable ([lem-pc-kbar-pure-insep]), the homeomorphism
statement [lem-pc-homeo-pure-insep], and the equivalence
$H^0=k\Leftrightarrow$ geometrically connected
([lem-pc-h0-geom-connected]) —all of which are recorded above,
even though the smoothness route is the one used in the proof.

attrs.title: The meaning of ``curve'' and the role of separably closedness

objects.body:
The theorem produces a scheme $\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}_{X/k}$ representing
$\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k}$ together with the group structure given by the group law of
the sheaf $\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k}$ —the multiplication and inversion morphisms are
induced by the corresponding natural transformations of the representable
functor (the group-valued functor structure of $\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k}$ is part of
its definition via the groups $\operatorname{Pic}(X_T)$).

We use the following two facts of the Stacks Project:

- *regular schemes are normal* (Properties of Schemes,
Lemma 28.9.4, Tag [0569](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0569);
see also Lemma 28.9.2, Tag [02IT](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02IT)),
and
- *Noetherian normal schemes decompose*: a Noetherian normal
scheme is a finite disjoint union of normal integral schemes (Properties
of Schemes, Lemma 28.7.6, Tag [033M](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/033M)).

In particular a regular, connected, Noetherian scheme is irreducible.
(These are the scheme-level regularity-normal facts, in contrast with
[rem-pc-regularity-sc] which works with smooth curves.)

attrs.title: Regular schemes are normal; the normal decomposition

objects.body:
The local regularity facts used in this blueprint are already decomposed
in file 06: [lem-sc-smooth-regular] (a smooth curve over a field has
regular, hence domain, local rings), [lem-sc-regular-dim1-dvr] (a
regular local ring of dimension $1$ is a discrete valuation ring) and
[lem-sc-point-cartier] (a closed point of a smooth connected curve is an
effective Cartier divisor with ideal generated by one non-zero-divisor).
They apply in our situation because a
smooth projective curve over a
field is in particular a *smooth connected curve* in the sense of
[def-sc-curves] (nonempty, connected, separated, of finite type, of dimension
one; see [rem-pc-relation-sc]), and every base change $X_K$ is
again such a curve ([lem-sc-base-change-curve] and
[prop-pc-xk-integral]).

attrs.title: Local regularity theory: already in file 06

objects.body:
File 06 uses a slightly coarser notion: for a field $k$, a *curve
over $k$* there is a separated scheme of finite type over $k$
of dimension at most $1$ ([def-sc-curves]). A
smooth projective curve in
our sense is in particular a smooth curve in the sense of
[def-sc-curves] ([lem-pc-curves-are-sc]); conversely, for
smooth proper connected curves the two notions coincide.

attrs.title: Relation to the curves of file 06

objects.body:
The notions of *ample* and *very ample* invertible module are
those of file 06: [def-sc-ample] (with the Stacks Project
references Properties of Schemes, Section 28.27, Tag
[01PR](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01PR), Proposition
28.27.13, Tag [01Q3](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01Q3),
and Morphisms of Schemes, Definition 29.39.1, Tag
[01VM](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01VM)). We use that
definition in its stated generality (any proper scheme over a field).

attrs.title: Ample and very ample: existing in file 06

objects.body:
For a curve $C$ over a field, the *divisors* ($D=\sum_Pn_P[P]$,
$\operatorname{Div}(C)$, principal divisors, the divisor class group
$\operatorname{Cl}(C)$ and the associated module $\mathcal{O}_C(D)$ of a
divisor, defined via $k(C)$) are those of file 06: [def-sc-divisor].
In this blueprint they are used for the curve $X$ and its base changes
$X_K$; the corresponding invertible module of an effective Cartier
divisor is the one of [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]
([lem-pc-divisor-line-bundle-agrees-sc]).

attrs.title: Divisors and the divisor class group: existing in file 06

objects.body:
The notion of a $k$-*group scheme* (and of commutative group
scheme, homomorphism and kernel) is that of file 06:
[def-sc-group-scheme].

The notions of *invertible module* (and its dual),
*tensor product of modules* and *Picard group* used below are
those already introduced in file 06:
Definition [def-sc-invertible-module]
([def-sc-invertible-module], with [lem-sc-invertible-dual])
and
Definition [def-sc-picard-group]
([def-sc-picard-group], with the group law of
[lem-sc-pic-group]). The basic properties that we will use are

- an
invertible module is closed under
duals and tensor products ([lem-pc-tensor-dual-invertible]);
- $\operatorname{Pic}(S)$ is trivial for $S=\operatorname{Spec}(k)$, $k$ a field
([lem-pc-pic-of-field]).

attrs.title: Invertible modules and Picard groups: existing in file 06

objects.body:
[thm-pd-jacobian-general-field] is the statement that
[rem-sc-jacobian-scope] of the Jacobian chapter declares to lie outside
the scope of that chapter. The route taken here is the descent route: the
theorem is proved over a separable closure by
[thm-pd-geometric-pic0] and then descended, so that neither
Grothendieck's existence theorem in the presence of a rational point nor a
choice of a base point enters. In particular the hypothesis that $k$ be
separably closed in [thm-pc-picard-representable] and in
[thm-sc-jacobian-representability] is used only to manufacture a
$k$-rational point, as the proof of [thm-pc-picard-representable]
records through [lem-pc-rational-points-dense] and
[lem-pc-rational-hyp]; over an arbitrary ground field the rational point
is unnecessary.

## Proof

The comparison of scopes is immediate from the statements:
[rem-sc-jacobian-scope] asserts that representability over a general
ground field is not proved in that chapter and would require a descent from a
finite separable extension, while
[thm-pd-jacobian-general-field] supplies exactly that descent, with the
two ingredients named in that remark replaced by
[thm-pd-effective-descent] (Stacks Project, Lemma 39.25.3, Tag
[0CCJ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CCJ)) and
[thm-pd-spreading-out] (Stacks Project, Lemma 32.10.1, Tag
[01ZM](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01ZM)). That the separable
closedness of the two cited theorems serves only to produce a rational point
is visible in the proof of [thm-pc-picard-representable], which obtains
$\sigma$ from [lem-pc-rational-points-dense] and then applies
[lem-pc-rational-hyp]; the rational point is what
[thm-pd-geometric-pic0] supplies geometrically and what the descent of
[thm-pd-jacobian-general-field] replaces, the two theorems
[thm-sc-jacobian-representability] and [thm-pd-geometric-pic0] being
the separably closed statement and its geometric consequence.

attrs.title: What changed relative to the separably closed case

objects.body:
The decomposition of Strand A and its spectral-sequence inputs into
makes the four seams visible.

1. ****$S_1$**** *Into the hypothesis check of the Hilbert
theorem* ([thm-pc-hilb-curves]): the existence of an affine open
containing finitely many points of $X$ uses the Riemann–Roch consequences
[lem-sc-positive-degree-ample] (positive degree $\Rightarrow$ ample) and
[lem-sc-ample-complement-affine] (ample effective divisor
$\Rightarrow$ affine complement), which are Riemann–Roch
consequences of [thm-sc-serre-duality-curve] and [lem-pc-projective-space-twist-cohomology].
1. ****$S_2$**** *Into the dictionary*
([lem-pc-zero-scheme-recd]): $\deg Z(s)=\deg\cL_t=g$ is exactly
[cor-picard-degree-g], i.e. [lem-sc-riemann-roch] with
$\chi(\cL_t)=h^0=1$ and $\chi(\cO)=1-g$; this is what makes the
codomain $\underline{\Hilb}^g_{X/k}$ have index $g$, the same $g$ as
the genus—the equality of the two $g$'s is Riemann–Roch.
1. ****$S_3$**** *Into the openness of $F$*
([lem-pc-f-open-subfunctor]): the openness of the locus where
$Rf_{T,*}\cL$ is finite locally free of rank $1$ in degree $0$ is
[lem-pc-perfect-locus] (perfect-locus openness, from the
semicontinuity [lem-pc-rf-perfect-base-change]), a
theorem about coherent families — the world of Strand A.
1. ****$S_4$**** *Into condition (2)(c)*
([thm-pc-criterion]): the generation condition is precisely
[lem-pc-twist] (Serre vanishing [lem-pc-serre-vanishing], Riemann–Roch
[lem-sc-riemann-roch], density of rational points
[lem-pc-rational-points-dense]); without it the criterion has no input,
and without it $F$ would only give (2)(a), (2)(b).

Conversely, Strand B never feeds Strand A: no descent or
representability statement is used in the proofs of
[lem-sc-cech-spectral]–[lem-pc-twist]. This is why the correct
dependency picture is one chain, not two parallel ones.

attrs.title: The dependencies are one-way: $\mathbf A\Rightarrow\mathbf B$ at four seams

In the notation of [def-trf-admissibility], the following holds. Of the ambient
exceptional right adjoint datum of
[def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint] — clause (1) of
[def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility] — *both halves are
theorems* for a separated finite-type morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes on
the bounded constructible and finite-Tor categories, by
[cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge].

In the notation of [def-trf-admissibility], the following holds. The two *preservation* clauses
(2) and (3) of the same definition — the typing
$Rf^!:D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)\to D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ together with the interval
bounds — are theorems there as well, for *every* separated finite-type
morphism and at every finite coefficient stage, with constants independent of
the stage: they are [thm-sf-preservation-class] of the six-functor
chapter and its corollary [lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata], proved there by
the chartwise assembly of the smooth-purity chapter, whose only hypothesis, the
open-complement condition, is the theorem
[lem-exc-open-complement-known] of the chapter on exceptional right
adjoints.

The coefficient comparisons in [def-trf-admissibility] on the
constructible coefficient categories are supplied by
[lem-coef-finite-exceptional], [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint], [lem-coef-rational-operations].
They identify the relevant units and counits. Each geometric
base-change or exchange assertion used by a trace argument still has
the scope of its own theorem; proving coefficient comparison does
not prove an arbitrary base-change assertion. The older local-model
route has the more specific hypotheses recorded in
[rem-sf-finite-level-comparison-ingredient].

In the notation of [def-trf-categorical-trace], the following holds. Localized at
quasi-isomorphisms (the model category of the Koszul conventions of
[lem-trf-chain-supertrace]).

In the notation of [def-trf-categorical-trace], the following holds. The
finite-coefficient
categories over a point of the trace-formula chapter are the bounded
complexes with finite cohomology modules; that the two descriptions
agree on the objects of finite Tor amplitude for the finite ring
$A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ is
[lem-trf-finite-tor-amplitude-perfect].

In the notation of [def-trf-categorical-trace], the following holds. The
explicit model-level formulas for $\operatorname{coev}_P$ and
$\operatorname{ev}_P$, the verification of the triangle identities,
and the Koszul sign convention of the symmetric monoidal structure
(the braiding $\operatorname{sym}_{P,Q}:P\otimes_A^LQ\xrightarrow{\sim} Q\otimes_A^LP$, $p\otimes q\mapsto(-1)^{|p||q|}q\otimes p$) are
given in [lem-trf-chain-supertrace], whose statement is the
derived-category consequence (the supertrace formula).

In the notation of [def-trf-categorical-trace], the following holds. Its $A$-linearity, naturality, and
the alternating-sum formula over a field coefficient ring are the
formal properties recorded in the trace-laws proposition proved below;
the chain-level supertrace computation justifying the name is
[lem-trf-chain-supertrace].

construction, $R\Gamma_c(X,K)\in D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$ for every
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, is
[prop-trf-compact-support-perfectness].

In the notation of [def-trf-global-operator], the following holds. I.e. $R\Gamma_c(Z,M)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{Z!}M)$,
the assertion $R\Gamma_c(Z,M)\in D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$ for
$M\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$ is
[prop-trf-compact-support-perfectness]),

In the notation of [def-trf-global-operator], the following holds. Its naturality in
$(u,K)$ and $A$-linearity in $u$ are
[lem-trf-global-operator-naturality] and
*Linearity of the global operator in the correspondence*.

$\operatorname{End}_{D(A)}(A)\cong A$; its $A$-linearity is

In the notation of [def-trf-local-term], the following holds. The identification of the
local term with the element of $A$ corresponding to
$\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)|_\beta$ in the point case $\beta\simeq\Spec k$ is [lem-trf-local-term-point]. The restricted pairing
$j_B^*\langle u,v\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}$ and the local term

[def-trf-local-term-pair].

In the notation of [def-trf-supported-pairing], for an opposite pair
between $(X,K)$ and $(Y,L)$ the recipe has three ingredients: the inverse
Künneth–Verdier maps give the supported classes

$$
\widetilde u:Rc_!A_C\longrightarrow P:=L\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}D_XK,
\qquad
\widetilde v:R\bar d_!A_D\longrightarrow Q:=D_YL\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}K;
$$

for $e:E(C,D)\to Z$ the map from the fiber product of the two
supports ([def-trf-correspondence-between-pairs]), the projection formula and $!$-base change give
$Re_!A_E\simeq Rc_!A_C\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}R\bar d_!A_D$; and the two
Verdier evaluations followed by
$\omega_Y\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}\omega_X\simeq\omega_Z$ contract

canonical, so $\langle u,v\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}$ depends only on the
two correspondences. In the diagonal case
$(Y,L)=(X,K)$, $(D,d,v)=(X,\Delta_X,1_K)$, where $E(C,D)=\Fix(c)$, the
section $\langle u,1_K\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}$ is the trace class
$\Tr_c(u)$ of [def-trf-trace-class], by
[lem-trf-trace-class-diagonal-pairing].

In the notation of [def-trf-weil-extension-zero], the following holds. $b_{g_Y}$ is the comparison isomorphism of
[lem-trf-open-square-exchange] for the Cartesian square of
[lem-trf-frobenius-open-square].

In the notation of [def-trf-weil-extension-zero], the following holds. That the pair

Of the three clauses of
[def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility] this chapter uses only
clause (1), the ambient exceptional right adjoint datum of
[def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint]: the existence of
$Rf_n^{\times}$ on the ordinary derived categories, together with the
full cohomological-dimension condition. That clause is *not a
hypothesis* of this chapter: on the bounded constructible and finite-Tor
coefficients that every statement below quantifies over — the coefficients
of the blueprint's class [def-sf-fullcd-used-class], which by
[lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] are exactly the sheaves of
étale origin — both of its halves are theorems, the vanishing half
[thm-sf-fullcd-class] with the bound $2\dim\overline X$ and the
existence half [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] with its unit, counit and
compactification comparisons, together
[cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge]. The datum remains an assumption
only for the complexes outside that class, and no statement of this chapter
applies the adjunction $Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$ to such a complex
([rem-sf-class-adjoint-residue]). The two preservation clauses are
likewise not hypotheses:

1. clause (2), the constructibility clause, is *derived* in this
chapter for the morphisms for which purity is proved:
[cor-pur-smooth-admissibility] below shows that a smooth
morphism of pure relative dimension $d$ satisfies
$Rf^{!}\cong Lf^{*}(-)(d)[2d]$, hence carries
$D_c^{[a,b]}(Y,A)$ into $D_c^{[a-2d,b-2d]}(X,A)$; for a closed
immersion it is proved without any purity input in
[lem-exc-closed-ambient], [lem-exc-closed-amplitude];
1. clause (3), the finite-Tor clause, is likewise *derived* here
for smooth morphisms, in the same corollary: the residue-field
criterion [lem-exc-residue-tor-test] reduces it to the
vanishing degrees of $Lf^{*}(K\otimes^L_A\kappa)(d)[2d]$, which
the criterion applied to $K$ controls. For a closed immersion it
is proved without purity in [prop-exc-closed-tor]. For a
general separated finite-type morphism it is derived in the assembly
of [thm-pur-general-admissibility] and
[cor-pur-general-admissibility-datum] from the ambient datum,
which on the coefficients of those two statements is the theorem
[cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge], together with the
open-complement condition supplied by
[lem-exc-open-complement-known]; no clause of
[def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility] is assumed where
the two preservation clauses are used.

In particular no statement of this chapter presupposes the admissibility
of a general separated finite-type morphism, so the present chapter and
the chapter on exceptional right adjoints do not use each other's
conclusions: that chapter records the smooth adjunction as a separate
obligation, and this chapter records the preservation clauses as
conclusions rather than hypotheses
(rem:weil-admissibility-split).

General finite-coefficient Verdier biduality on $D^b_{ctf}$ is
the independent geometric theorem [thm-fix-general-biduality].
It proves preservation before biduality by stratification, geometric
generic restriction, and dimension induction. It is not inferred
solely from existence or preservation of an ambient right adjoint.
The subsequent coefficient comparisons extend it to the specified
integral and field categories, as exported in
[thm-sf-biduality-class]. The smooth orientation constructed in
this chapter identifies the dualizing object in that separate theorem;
this navigation record is not an input to the purity proof.

The two closed-immersion statements
([lem-exc-closed-amplitude], [prop-exc-closed-tor]) are conditional on
the open-complement condition of the pair they treat, which is a statement
about the ordinary direct image and is proved in the chapter on exceptional
right adjoints from the direct-image finiteness theorems of Blueprints 06b
and 07 ([thm-sf-preservation-class]). Apart from the ambient
exceptional right adjoint datum — a theorem on the coefficients used
here, as just recorded — this chapter therefore assumes no geometric
hypothesis at all.

attrs.title: The ambient datum of this chapter is a theorem on its coefficients

objects.body:
The only hypothesis of [thm-pur-general-admissibility] is the
open-complement condition
([def-exc-open-complement-bound]) for the finitely many complements of
the affine charts inside affine space; the ambient exceptional right adjoint
datum that the theorem formerly displayed is not one, being the theorem
[cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge] on the coefficients it quantifies
over. That condition is a theorem of this
blueprint, not an assumption: [lem-exc-open-complement-known] derives
it with $c=2d$ from the two clauses of the direct-image finiteness input
[def-exc-direct-image-input], which are
[thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility] of the constructibility chapter and
[thm-sc-finite-type-torsion-cd] of the Jacobian chapter,
assembled as [thm-exc-direct-image-input-holds], and
[thm-pur-open-complement-unconditional] records the same two clauses with
a constant independent of the coefficient ring and hence of the coefficient
stage. Consequently
[thm-pur-general-admissibility] and
[cor-pur-general-admissibility-datum] prove the two preservation
clauses for an arbitrary separated finite-type morphism without further
hypotheses, on the coefficients of the blueprint's class. No
affineness of the base is needed: the passage from the affine opens of
$Y$ to $Y$ itself uses the base-change compatibility of the ambient
right adjoint along an open immersion, which is proved in the chapter on
exceptional right adjoints
([cor-exc-base-change-open-immersion-general]) and is read here on the
same coefficients, where its ambient-datum hypothesis is again the theorem
[cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge].

The five moves are the whole proof. Conveniently located: the
rank-one computation (Kummer $c_1$, excision, Gysin identification of
$Rs^{!}(1)[2]$ with $H^2_s$) — inside [thm-pur-kummer-affine-line], proved from
the Kummer sequence and the cohomological-dimension bound of §[sec-curve-estimates], with the
orientation itself derived in [lem-pur-gysin-structure]; the Künneth and
frame-independence arguments (the Thom class is the $\Aaf^1$-class written in
coordinates) — inside [cor-pur-affine-space-purity]; the geometry of the deformation of a
*section* — [lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry], used by [thm-pur-dnc-invariance] and through it
by [thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity]. Purity for regular closed immersions
([thm-pur-regular-immersion-purity]) is *not* one of the moves: it is a consequence of
[thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity] for the two structure morphisms together with the
co-projection [lem-pur-coprojection], and the deformation to the normal cone
is never applied to a general regular immersion. The formal six-functor
bookkeeping (base change, transpose composition, cup products, coefficient
transport, Frobenius equivariance, the trace normalization for the Lefschetz
formula) is all downstream of [thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity] and absent here.

attrs.title: The five moves of the purity proof

objects.body:
The independent starting point is the projective-line adjunction
[thm-amb-p1-adjunction], whose two triangles are computed from
the two integrals of the Cartier diagonal class. It gives
[cor-amb-affine-space-adjunction], and then the orientation-free
tensor and base-change statements
[thm-asd-smooth-tensor], [prop-asd-smooth-base-change] and the
vector-bundle orientation [thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity].
Their finite etale-origin transports are
[thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness], [lem-pur-smb-extraordinary], [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity].
Only after these inputs does the deformation statement
[thm-pur-dnc-invariance] identify the section invariants, leading
to [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object] and
[thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity].
The coherence of this chosen orientation is the later conclusion
[thm-pur-smooth-base-change-coherence]; it is not an input to
affine-line purity or orientation-free exceptional base change.
This dependency order does not infer any theorem from a package
summary or certify the separate proofs of the optional Thom route.

attrs.title: Monodromy data of a Weil representation

objects.body:
Four standard facts are used in the proofs above; each is either basic
mathematics, which the decomposition rules allow to be quoted, or a
theorem of this blueprint, and we record them here so that no step of the
argument is left implicit.

1. A finite morphism has exact direct image with no higher direct
images, and its direct image preserves injective sheaves because its
inverse image is exact and left adjoint to it; this is
[lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact], and it is used in the
dimension-zero case and in the reduction by Noether normalization.
1. A separably closed residue field and a polynomial with a simple root
there admit a unique lift of that root, by the Hensel lifting lemma
for a strict henselian local ring; the simplicity is supplied by the
discriminant, a nonzero element of the coefficient field and hence a
unit in the strict local ring. This is the local-algebra input of
the strict-local dimension-drop computation.
1. Vanishing of all geometric stalks of an etale sheaf forces the sheaf
to vanish; this is
[lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative], and it is what
converts the stalkwise bounds above into the stated vanishing of
$R^qj_*M$ and of $H^q(X,F)$.
1. For a finite-type algebra over a field, the transcendence degree of
the residue field at a point bounds its local dimension, and a
proper closed subset of an irreducible finite-type scheme has
strictly smaller dimension; these are the dimension statements used
when the support of $R^qf_*M$ is bounded by the transcendence
degree and when only the generic point of $\mathbf A^{d-1}_K$ has
transcendence degree $d-1$.

All four are standard, and the first and the third are proved in this
blueprint; none of them is a finiteness or constructibility statement, so
no circularity with the later direct-image theory arises.

The existence theorem of this chapter is proved in
this blueprint over a separably closed ground field, which is the maximal
generality available here: representability of the Picard functor is
[thm-pc-picard-representable] of the Picard chapter for such a field, and
that proof uses separable closedness exactly to produce a rational point. The
weight chapters use the special case of an algebraically closed ground field:
for a curve $C_0$ over an arbitrary field $k_0$ one applies the theorem to
the base change $C=C_0\times_{k_0}\overline{k}_0$ over the algebraically
closed field $\overline{k}_0$, while the
$\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{k}_0/k_0)$-action on the group
$J(\overline{k}_0)$ of points of the geometric [def-sc-jacobian] is
obtained from the functoriality of the Picard functor, not from a model of
$J$ over $k_0$. Representability over a general ground field, that is,
the existence of an abelian variety over $k$ representing
$\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$ for a geometrically integral smooth projective
curve $C$ over $k$ in the vocabulary of [def-sc-general-curve], is
*not* proved here: it requires a descent from the separable closure (the
representability over $k_s$ of [thm-pc-picard-representable], spread out to a
finite separable level and descended), and the representability criterion of the
Picard chapter cannot supply that base case over a finite extension by itself,
since its twist lemma needs the dense rational points of a separably closed
field even when the curve has a rational point. No statement of this chapter
uses the general-field form; it is supplied by the descent chapter.

attrs.title: Scope of the Jacobian existence result

objects.body:
*(i) The two lanes contradict (this is the whole proof):* a
first failure in degree $q$ produces a universal curve-test datum
with $R^qh_*(\Z/d\Z)\neq0$ ([sbc-lem-bc-universal-test], from the
counterexample chain anchored at the minimal-counterexample lemma
`0F06`), while the curve-test lane ([sbc-thm-universal-test-vanishing])
makes it zero. *(ii) The curve-estimate seam:*
[thm-sc-constant-invariance] (the algebraically closed
field-extension invariance) is Blueprint 06 /
`OBL-PBC-CURVES` — the same input that computes the
closed fibre of $\mathbb P^1$ in proper base change; it is used in
[sbc-thm-universal-test-vanishing] at $q=1$ only, together with the torsor
translation [thm-galois-torsor-h1] (proved in Ch. 02b of the
detailed blueprint and sketched here) and the spreading theorem
[sbc-thm-spreading-finite-etale-galois] (I5, tame extension), the deepest of
the lane's inputs and the one the blueprint carries only in
sketch.
*(iii) This is Stacks' second, shorter proof:* the
counterexample lemmas are Stacks `0F06`, `0F07`,
`0F08`, and the theorem is `0EYU`; the blueprint's
definitions (base-change map, smooth, allowed coefficients)
are the ones its own proof actually uses. *(iv) Local
acyclicity/Milnor tubes are later:* they are defined in the
subsequent local-acyclicity section of the chapter, and the
*smooth morphisms are universally locally acyclic* theorem
there is derived from the base-change theorem (via base change for
open immersions under local acyclicity), not the other way around.

The formal axioms of [def-sf-datum] are supplied operation by
operation. Adjunction (A1) is [fix-prop-adjunctions], with the
explicit exceptional-adjoint hypothesis of
[def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility]. Base change (A2)
is the independent base-change theorems collected in
[fix-lem-exchanges] and [cor-cbc-proper-coincidence]. Projection (A3) is the proved
[fix-prop-projection-formula]. Composition and proper coincidence
(A4) are [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed],
[prop-compactification-coherence-detailed] and
[cor-cbc-proper-coincidence].

For (A5), [lem-fix-operation-reduction] supplies the elementary
coefficient comparisons on its stated domains. The additional
constructible-tower comparisons are
*The finite-level comparison isomorphisms of the package, from uniform local models* with its explicit hypotheses,
which *The finite-level comparison isomorphisms in the two cases* verifies in the
specified cases. The exceptional comparisons remain subject to the
coefficient compatibility in admissibility. Biduality (A6) is the
separate geometric theorem [thm-fix-general-biduality], on its
actual hypotheses and coefficient domains. The aggregate package
collects these results only after their individual proofs.

Let $T$ be a scheme, let $U\to T$ be a nonempty object of the
small pro-étale site $T_{\Proet}$ of
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of
$A$-modules on $T_{\Proet}$, that is, an object of
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], and let $W\to U$ be a pro-étale
covering whose source is weakly contractible, as supplied by Stacks Project,
Pro-étale Cohomology, Lemma 61.13.5,
[Tag 0F4P](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F4P); let $K$ be the
Čech hypercover of that covering,
$K_n=W^{n+1}=W\times_U\dots\times_UW$, which is a hypercovering by Stacks
Project, Example 25.3.6, [Tag
0GMA](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0GMA). The following four facts answer, for this device, the question of what a
bound on the length of a weakly contractible hypercovering can and cannot give.

1. **(i)** *Every term of $K$ is nonempty, so this hypercover cannot be
truncated at all.* Each $W^{n+1}$ contains the diagonal copy of $W$, so no
term is empty and no truncation of $K$ is a hypercovering;
*No hypercovering of a nonempty object has an empty term* shows that this is a property of
hypercoverings and not of this construction, and
*The question of a bounded weakly contractible hypercovering has a negative answer* draws the consequence.
1. **(ii)** *If all fibre products $W^{n+1}$ are weakly contractible, the
Čech complex computes $R\Gamma(U,\mathcal F)$, and its truncation is
legitimate exactly when the vanishing holds.* This is
*Truncating the Čech complex of a single weakly contractible covering needs the vanishing as input*: the complex has a term in every degree,
by (i), and its truncation at $N$ is a quasi-isomorphism if and only if
$H^q(U,\mathcal F)=0$ for every $q>N$. The truncation therefore needs as
input exactly the vanishing it is meant to produce, and no bounded replacement
follows from pro-étale descent.
1. **(iii)** *The weak contractibility of $W$ alone does not give (ii),
and no other recorded cover does either.* The recorded sources say nothing
about the fibre products $W\times_U\dots\times_UW$, so the weak contractibility
of the terms of the Čech hypercover is a second input, distinct from the weak
contractibility of $W$; neither does the stronger cover of Stacks Project,
Pro-étale Cohomology, Proposition 61.11.3,
[Tag 0983](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0983) (for an affine $U$;
Lemma 61.13.3, [Tag 098I](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/098I), in
general), whose members are spectra of w-contractible rings, with Definition
61.11.1, [Tag 0981](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0981), and Lemma
61.11.2, [Tag 0982](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0982), and are
therefore weakly contractible, supply it: the Čech nerve of any of its
members has the same shape. What Stacks Project, Pro-étale
Cohomology, Lemma 61.14.1,
[Tag 09A1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09A1), supplies instead is a
hypercovering whose terms are weakly contractible by construction, and by
*The question of a bounded weakly contractible hypercovering has a negative answer* that hypercovering is unbounded. The
criterion that is available in place of a length bound is the vanishing of the
coefficient sheaf on the terms, *Vanishing above the degree in which the coefficient sheaf dies on the terms*.
1. **(iv)** *Neither the degeneration of the spectral sequence nor the
compact generation of the derived category bounds the degree.* If all terms are
weakly contractible, the spectral sequence of Stacks Project, Hypercoverings,
Lemma 25.5.3, [Tag 01GY](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01GY), for the
Čech hypercover degenerates at $E_2$, and for the constant coefficient
sheaf its remaining row $E_1^{p,0}=\mathcal F(W^{p+1})$ is nonzero in every
degree, its cohomology being $H^p(U,\mathcal F)$ itself; and the compact
generation of the pro-étale derived category, Stacks Project, Pro-étale
Cohomology, Lemma 61.15.1,
[Tag 0F4Q](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F4Q), exhibits generators,
namely the $j_{U!}\mathcal A_U$ at affine weakly contractible $U$, and
contains no bound on degrees.

attrs.title: The Čech complex of a single weakly contractible covering: what its truncation is missing, and what does not supply it

objects.body:
The theorem [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] constructs the finite
right adjoint relative to bounded-below objects of etale origin by
$\nu_X^*f^{\times}R\nu_{Y,*}$. It does not assert an adjunction
on every unbounded pro-etale object.

Within the constructible coefficient categories, finite exceptional
preservation is [thm-sf-preservation-class]; its coefficient
comparison is [lem-coef-finite-exceptional]. Integral
exceptional inverse image and its adjunction are
[prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint], and the rational and
common-stage identifications are
[lem-coef-rational-operations], [thm-coef-qbar-verdier].
General Verdier biduality is proved at the finite, integral, rational,
and algebraically closed coefficient stages in
[thm-fix-general-biduality], [thm-coef-integral-verdier], [thm-coef-rational-verdier], [thm-coef-qbar-verdier].
These later constructible results preserve the distinction between
the bounded comparison adjunction and an unrestricted ambient one.

Pullback, tensor, and the elementary coefficient comparisons are
[lem-fix-operation-reduction]. General finite constructible
internal Hom, duality, and exceptional inverse image have the
comparisons
[thm-coef-finite-hom], [cor-coef-finite-verdier], [lem-coef-finite-exceptional].
At integral coefficients the corresponding conclusions are
[lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction], [thm-coef-integral-verdier], [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint].
Their finite scalar-extension and rational identifications are
[lem-coef-integral-finite-extension], [lem-coef-rational-operations], [thm-coef-qbar-verdier].
These comparisons preserve the specified evaluations and adjunction
maps. The coefficient-only sharp Hom bound still requires the
site-perfect hypothesis in [thm-sf-hom-ctf]; that bound is a
different assertion from coefficient comparison.

A separately supplied DVR system reconstructs with its stated
reductions once the coherent normalization condition of
[def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower] is verified, by
[lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity]. Constructibility of the
result additionally requires the stated finite-level finiteness and
uniform bounds. Common lisse local models are an optional stronger
description, as [rem-sf-tower-shapes-occurring] explains.
The formal Weil lift [lem-fix-weil-operations] applies to these
proved operations; duality equivariance is
[cor-coef-verdier-weil-equivariance].

attrs.title: Proved coefficient transport and its domains

objects.body:
The argument tests geometric stalks and therefore proves the coherence on the
étale-origin complexes $\nu_X^*D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ — the range in which
[def-fix-six-functor-datum] (iv) asserts compactification-independence.
Extending it to arbitrary objects of $D(X_{\Proet},\Lambda)$ is not proved
here and is not used by [prop-functor-package]; ordinary geometric stalks are
not conservative on all pro-étale sheaves. What the stalk computation
consumes is the *bounded-below* form of proper base change; this document
states [thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below] for torsion sheaves, and the passage to
$D^+$ is the standard dévissage along the canonical truncations, which the
expanded blueprint records separately (thm:weil-pbc-bounded-below). The
same remark applies to [thm-sf-comp-composition] and
[cor-cbc-proper-coincidence].

If the complex $M_0$ of
*Stage-independent local models for a constant tower* is itself a bounded complex of
finite locally constant $A_T$-modules concentrated in degrees $[a,b]$,
then no construction is needed: putting $L=M_0$ exhibits the tower as the
reduction tower of one bounded complex of finite locally constant
$A_T$-modules,

$$
M_n=M_0\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}
=L\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_n)_T,
$$

which is the uniformity clause of
[def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower] verbatim, with the identity
cover. This is the ``trivial coefficient'' case: the constant local system
at every coefficient stage, and every bounded complex of finite locally
constant sheaves whose stages are its reductions; in particular a bounded
flat model of $M_0$ whose terms are finite locally constant may be taken
as the stage-independent model and base changed to every stage. The point
of *Stage-independent local models for a constant tower* is that the same conclusion
holds under the weaker hypothesis that the *stages* are lisse with one
Tor amplitude bound, no single finite locally constant model of $M_0$
being assumed.

attrs.title: The trivial coefficient case, in one line

objects.body:
The continuity statement $(\mathrm{C}_q)$ of
*Continuity for arbitrary sheaves implies the vanishing* was the single missing
input of the route that would have deduced $(\mathrm{G})$ from
[lem-sf-etale-direct-image-vanishing]. That route is now closed in the
negative: $(\mathrm{G})$ is *false*, by
*The all-sheaves, uniform-in-the-base-change form of the comparison bound is false* and
[rem-sf-fullcd-counterexample], so by the contrapositive of
*Continuity for arbitrary sheaves implies the vanishing* the statement
$(\mathrm{C}_q)$ fails at the base change $U$ of that counterexample in
every degree $q$ in which $R^q\nu_{U,*}F_G\neq0$, that is in unboundedly
many degrees. What the present remark records is why that failure is not an
accident of the construction: $(\mathrm{C}_q)$ is *not* obtained from
the étale vanishing lemma, and its
proof in the sources covers only sheaves of étale origin, so the hypothesis
is not available in the generality in which the general form needed it. A
further point is that
the resulting criterion does not go through geometric-point stalks, in
contrast with the failure of conservativity of the pro-étale geometric-point
stalks recorded in clause (4) of
[lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative]: by
[lem-sf-proetale-vanishing-detection] and
[cor-sf-fullcd-weakly-contractible-test] the vanishing is tested on the
affine weakly contractible objects, and the continuity of the values along the
pointed étale neighbourhoods, not the conservative detection of sheaves, was
what the general form needed.

1. *The étale lemma does not bound the terms of the colimit.* The
colimit in $(\mathrm{C}_q)$ runs over the pointed étale neighbourhoods
$U$ of a geometric point of $V$, the comparison morphism being the
$\nu_V$ of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], and its terms are
the *pro-étale* cohomology groups $H^q(U_{\Proet},\mathcal F|_U)$ of
those finite-type models, the cohomology of the small pro-étale site of
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].
[lem-sf-etale-direct-image-vanishing] bounds the higher direct images of a
finite-type morphism on the *étale* sites, that is the groups
$H^q(U_{\Et},-)$; it says nothing about the pro-étale cohomology of $U$,
which for the sheaves of étale origin equals the étale cohomology by
Stacks Project, Pro-étale Cohomology, Lemma 61.19.6,
[Tag 099W](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099W), but is not
controlled for the remaining sheaves. A bound on those terms uniform over the
inverse system is therefore a hypothesis about pro-étale cohomology and not
an étale statement, and *Continuity for arbitrary sheaves gives the full cohomological-dimension bound*(i) shows that the
continuity hypothesis, not the étale lemma, is what makes the terms vanish
above $2d$ for the finite-type models; so this route is not a reduction to
the étale bound. What the étale bound does give is the second factor of
the Leray spectral sequence of the comparison morphism, the $p$-direction
bounded by $2d$, as recorded in [rem-sf-fullcd-reduction].
1. *What the recorded proof of the comparison theorem uses.* The
vanishing of Stacks Project, Pro-étale Cohomology, Lemma 61.19.5,
[Tag 099V](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099V) — which is
[thm-sf-fullcd-etale-origin] with the bound $2d$ sharpened to $0$ —
is proved through Lemma 61.19.4,
[Tag 099U](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099U): for an injective
abelian sheaf $\mathcal I$ on $X_{\Et}$ and a pro-étale covering
$\lbrace U_i\to U\rbrace$ of an affine $U$ that is ind-étale over the
affine $X$, one writes each $U_i$ as a directed inverse limit of affine
étale $U_{i,a}\to U$, computes
$$
\check H^p\bigl(\mathcal U,\epsilon^{-1}\mathcal I\bigr)
=\varinjlim\check H^p\bigl(\mathcal U_{(a_1,\dots,a_n)},
\epsilon^{-1}\mathcal I\bigr)
$$
and reduces to the étale coverings $\mathcal U_{(a_1,\dots,a_n)}$ of the
*models*, where the Čech complexes are acyclic in positive degrees.
Three inputs make this work, and none of them is available for an arbitrary
pro-étale sheaf $\mathcal F$:
   1. **(a)** the degree-zero continuity of the *values* along the inverse
system, Stacks Project, Pro-étale Cohomology, Lemma 61.19.3,
[Tag 099S](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099S): for a sheaf
$\mathcal G$ on $X_{\Et}$ and a directed inverse system of quasi-compact
quasi-separated pro-étale objects with affine transition maps one has
$\epsilon^{-1}\mathcal G(\varprojlim Y_i)=\varinjlim\epsilon^{-1}\mathcal G(Y_i)$.
This is the only continuity the sources record, and it is a statement about
pulled-back étale sheaves; for a sheaf that is not of étale origin it fails
in general. The recorded witness is Stacks Project, Pro-étale Cohomology,
Section 61.18, [Tag 0991](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0991),
together with Example 61.19.12,
[Tag 0F6D](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F6D): the sheaf
$fun(-,A)/\underline A$ has zero stalk at the unique geometric point of
$\operatorname{Spec}k$, hence zero value at the strictly henselian limit
object by *The strictly henselian limit has no higher cohomology*(i), while its value at a
pro-étale model with infinitely many points is nonzero. The example is
stated for pro-étale neighbourhoods; it is the reason why no value
continuity may be assumed in $(\mathrm{C}_q)$.
   1. **(b)** the identification $\epsilon_*\epsilon^{-1}\mathcal G=\mathcal G$
of Stacks Project, Pro-étale Cohomology, Lemma 61.19.2,
[Tag 099T](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099T), which converts the
étale Čech complex of the model into the pro-étale one; and the
acyclicity criterion of Stacks Project, Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 21.10.9,
[Tag 03F9](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03F9), whose hypothesis
(3) requires the vanishing of the higher Čech cohomology of the sheaf with
respect to the chosen covers, which is what (a) and (b) supply — together
with the acyclicity of étale Čech complexes of injective étale sheaves,
Stacks Project, Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 21.10.2,
[Tag 03AW](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03AW).
   1. **(c)** the injectivity of $\mathcal I$, used to produce the resolution.
For a general $\mathcal F$ the sheaf $R^q\nu_{V,*}\mathcal F$ is the sheaf
associated to the presheaf $U\mapsto H^q(U_{\Proet},\mathcal F|_U)$ by Stacks
Project, Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 21.7.4,
[Tag 072W](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/072W), and its sections
need not lift to the terms of that presheaf over a cover of the model; the
lifting that *is* available, *Sections of an associated sheaf lift locally*,
is what *Continuity for arbitrary sheaves implies the vanishing* uses, and it
converts $(\mathrm{C}_q)$ into the vanishing of the associated sheaf only
because $(\mathrm{C}_q)$ is a statement about *every* class on
*every* pointed neighbourhood. The converse implication is not
available: the vanishing of $R^q\nu_{V,*}\mathcal F$, that is $P^{\#}=0$,
says only that every class of $P(U)$ dies on some étale *cover* of
$U$ — this is what the two-step construction of the associated sheaf
recalled in the proof of *Sections of an associated sheaf lift locally* gives,
since $P\to P^{+}$ kills exactly the classes that vanish on a covering and
$P^{+}\to P^{\#}$ is injective — whereas $(\mathrm{C}_q)$ demands death
on a single pointed refinement.
1. *What remains true, and where the residue lies.* On the
pro-étale site the only vanishing statement for *all* sheaves that the
recorded sources supply is at a weakly contractible object (Sites, Definition
7.40.2, [Tag 090L](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/090L); Pro-étale
Cohomology, Lemma 61.13.3,
[Tag 098I](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/098I) and Lemma 61.13.5,
[Tag 0F4P](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F4P)), which is the input
of [lem-sf-proetale-vanishing-detection] and of
[cor-sf-fullcd-weakly-contractible-test]; the hypercovering of Pro-étale
Cohomology, Lemma 61.14.1,
[Tag 09A1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09A1) with Lemma 61.14.2,
[Tag 09A2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09A2) carries no bound on
its length — and by *The question of a bounded weakly contractible hypercovering has a negative answer* no hypercovering of a
nonempty object is bounded at all, so that a bound on the length is
unattainable in principle and not merely absent from this construction — so
it cannot bound the vanishing degree of $R^q\nu_{V,*}$, as
[rem-sf-fullcd-general-form] records. Accordingly neither the sources
recorded here nor the acyclicity devices recalled above decide
$(\mathrm{C}_q)$ for a sheaf that is not of étale origin, and in this form
$(\mathrm{C}_q)$ is not proved here in that generality, and cannot be: by the
contrapositive of *Continuity for arbitrary sheaves implies the vanishing* the
counterexample of [rem-sf-fullcd-counterexample] refutes it at its base
change. What is now known about it is
exactly three things, recorded in the items following this remark. First, for
every sheaf of étale origin – in particular on the blueprint's coefficient
class [def-sf-fullcd-used-class] – the statement is a theorem with a
complete proof, *Continuity for sheaves of étale origin: every class dies on a single pointed refinement*: every class dies on a
single pointed étale refinement, obtained from a covering that kills it by
forming the disjoint union of its members. Second, its pro-étale form holds
for *every* sheaf and is a triviality,
*The pro-étale form of the continuity statement: every class dies on the strict henselization limit*: the strict henselization limit is
an initial object of the category of pointed pro-étale neighbourhoods, so
every class dies on that one pro-étale refinement, the target being zero by
*The strictly henselian limit has no higher cohomology*(iii); the whole content of
$(\mathrm{C}_q)$ is therefore the passage from pro-étale refinements to
étale ones. Third, that passage cannot be made by a cofinality argument,
*The pointed étale neighbourhoods are not cofinal among the pointed pro-étale ones*: an infinite separable extension
