of the residue field gives a pointed pro-étale neighbourhood that receives no
morphism from any pointed étale neighbourhood, so the two colimits are not
related by the criterion that compares them. With
$(\mathrm{C}_q)$ failing in that remaining case – the general form of
$(\mathrm{G})$ being false, by
*The all-sheaves, uniform-in-the-base-change form of the comparison bound is false* and
[rem-sf-fullcd-counterexample], and $(\mathrm{C}_q)$ failing with it at
that counterexample's base change, by
*Continuity for arbitrary sheaves implies the vanishing* – the condition
$\operatorname{FullCD}(p,A;c_{\mathrm{cd}})$ of
[open-sf-ambient-adjoint-input] is read on the blueprint's coefficient
class, where it is the theorem [thm-sf-fullcd-used-class] with the sharp
comparison bound $M=0$ of [prop-sf-comparison-bound-zero]. Nothing
here weakens the unconditional results: on the blueprint's coefficient class
[def-sf-fullcd-used-class] the vanishing is the theorem
[thm-sf-fullcd-etale-origin], with the comparison bound $0$ and
uniformly over the base changes, by
[prop-sf-comparison-bound-zero], and every conditional entry of the
matrix is conditional, on that class, on the ambient datum's assertion for the
complexes outside it, whose vanishing half there is the theorem
[thm-sf-fullcd-class] and whose existence half there is the theorem
[thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class], as
[rem-sf-class-adjoint-residue] records.

attrs.title: What the recorded proof of the comparison theorem uses, and why it does not extend to arbitrary sheaves

objects.body:
The clauses of [thm-sf-ctf-stability] may be substituted into
the formal axioms of [def-sf-datum] only on their displayed
domains. General finite-coefficient Hom comparison is
[thm-coef-finite-hom]; finite exceptional comparison is
[lem-coef-finite-exceptional]. Both use the independently
proved finite geometric duality [thm-fix-general-biduality].
The elementary coefficient-dual formula for a site-perfect complex
remains distinct from those general geometric results.

Integral duality, internal Hom and the exceptional adjunction are
[thm-coef-integral-verdier], [cor-coef-integral-internal-hom], [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint].
The rational and common-stage conclusions are
[thm-coef-rational-verdier], [lem-coef-rational-operations], [thm-coef-qbar-verdier].
These results supply the coefficient comparisons on the stated
constructible categories. They do not supply an exceptional
adjunction for arbitrary unbounded pro-etale complexes; that
separate domain remains in the existing record
[open-sf-preservation-gaps]. This summary exports the
individual proofs and is not an input to them.

attrs.title: How the verified domains enter the formal framework

objects.body:
The proof of clause (iii) of the finite-Tor preservation summary bounds
$\mathcal H^r(Rf_*K\otimes^L_AM)$ for an arbitrary module sheaf $M$ by
combining the projection formula for the constant coefficient sheaf
$M_Y$ with a bound ``produced by the proofs'' of the direct-image
finiteness theorems. Two points about that step are worth recording
exactly.

1. The projection transformation of [def-exchange-projection] and
[def-sf-pf] is the one for $Rf_!$, and its recorded forms require the
tensor factor to lie in the finite-Tor subcategory. The direct-image form
used in that step, with a constant tensor factor outside the finite-Tor
subcategory, is supplied by
[lem-sf-projection-finite-constant] for a finitely presented constant
coefficient; no projection formula with an *arbitrary* test sheaf is
recorded, and the proof below does not need one.
1. The uniform bound on $\mathcal H^r(Rf_*K\otimes^L_AM)$ that the
step needs, independent of $M$, is exactly the hypothesis
$\operatorname{UDV}$ of
[def-sf-uniform-direct-image-vanishing]. On the small étale site it
is a theorem, [lem-sf-etale-direct-image-vanishing], for every
finite-type morphism, so clause (iii) is unconditional there, by
[cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-nonproper]. On the small pro-étale site
the bound is *not* used at all in the route taken here: the cell is
reduced to the étale one. By
[lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] every object of
$D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Proet},A)$ is of étale origin, and
[lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] transfers the finite-Tor condition
across the comparison in both directions, so
[cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale] proves clause (iii) at the finite
coefficient stages for *every* object of
$D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Proet},A)$, with the amplitude $[a,b+2d]$, through
[cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-nonproper] and the comparison direct image.
The earlier corollary [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-etale-origin] remains
the special case of objects presented with an explicit étale model. In
particular the transport no longer needs a pro-étale analogue of the
residue test as an input: such a test is now a theorem,
[lem-sf-proetale-residue-tor-test], proved from the origin statement
and the transfer of the finite-Tor condition. What is still recorded in
[open-sf-preservation-gaps] is not the direct-image cell but the
internal-Hom cell and the full-cohomological-dimension interface.

The step that passes from a constant test sheaf to an arbitrary one is the
residue test [lem-exc-residue-tor-test], which is available for
bounded constructible complexes on the small étale site; the flat model
[lem-sf-flat-model] is what produces the cohomological interval of
$K$, and hence the interval of the test complex
$K\otimes^L_A\kappa_X$.

attrs.title: Status of the recorded argument for clause (iii)

objects.body:
At finite coefficients, $\omega_{X,A}=Ra_X^!A$ is finite-Tor
constructible by [lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata]. For site-perfect
$K$, the coefficient-only internal-Hom bound of
[thm-sf-hom-ctf] applies. For general constructible finite-Tor
$K$, [lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata] gives the geometric
Tor interval $[-b-2\dim X,-a]$, and
[thm-fix-general-biduality] proves biduality. The distinction
between these bounds remains the one explained in
[rem-sf-proetale-hom-status].

The finite comparisons of dualizing objects and general internal Hom
are [lem-coef-finite-dualizing], [thm-coef-finite-hom]; hence they
are available beyond the site-perfect case. Integral preservation,
coefficient comparison, and biduality are
[prop-coef-integral-dualizing], [thm-coef-integral-verdier], [cor-coef-integral-internal-hom].
The rational and common-stage conclusions are
[thm-coef-rational-verdier], [thm-coef-qbar-verdier]. These are
theorems on the stated constructible categories; they make no assertion
about an unrestricted unbounded pro-etale exceptional adjoint.

attrs.title: Geometric duality and its coefficient comparisons

objects.body:
The package [prop-functor-package] is consumed as follows. The smooth-purity
chapter needs clause (7) — the relative product theorem — as the relative
input for its affine-line orientation and its affine-space case. The duality
chapter is re-based on clauses (3) and (6): its global duality, pairing
identification, derived duality, degreewise, proper, trace and
reciprocal-eigenvalue nodes are read off from
[thm-sf-global-duality], [thm-sf-identification] and the pairing
statements. The trace-formula and final chapters use clause (8) (stability,
perfectness of compact-support cohomology), the trace-layer statements
[prop-trf-compact-support-perfectness], [lem-trf-open-ctf] and
[thm-trf-internal-hom-pullback], and — outside the package — the
Künneth–Verdier isomorphism [thm-trf-kunneth-verdier], on which their
supported pairing and local-term nodes rest. The final Weil statements cite the package through
prop:weil-operations-verified. Corresponding blueprint source:
`10b_six_functor_formalism.tex` of
`version/sketch`, whose statements carry the labels reused above.

The proof of *The finite-level comparison isomorphisms of the package, from uniform local models* uses the uniform
local models of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower].
The two sufficient criteria
*Stage-independent local models for a constant tower*, *Stage-independent local models for a lisse tower with a uniform trivializing cover*
retain all of their lisse and amplitude hypotheses, and
*The finite-level comparison isomorphisms in the two cases* applies under those
complete hypotheses. These results provide additional local-model
information; they are not necessary hypotheses for DVR reconstruction.

The separate theorem [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity]
reconstructs every coherent normalized DVR tower of
[def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower], without a common stratification
or common lisse model. With finite-level constructibility and a
uniform amplitude bound it yields an object of the integral category.
The direct-image and duality towers have their normalization maps from
[lem-coef-finite-direct-image], [cor-coef-finite-verdier]; the
exceptional tower has them from [lem-coef-finite-exceptional].
General internal-Hom reduction and the integral exceptional adjunction
are independently established in
[lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction], [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint].
For an arbitrary tower whose normalization has not been checked,
merely taking its derived limit still supplies no identification with
the proposed finite reductions.

attrs.title: The local-model proof and normalized DVR reconstruction

objects.body:
Fix an odd prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$, put
$A=A_{E,1}$ – a finite field of characteristic $\ell$ – fix a discrete set
$I$ of cardinality $\aleph_\omega$, and put

$$
S=\beta I\times\beta I,\qquad
U=\Spec\,\mathcal C_{\mathrm{lc}}(S,\mathbf C),\qquad
X_0=\Spec\mathbf C,
$$

where $\beta I$ is the Čech–Stone compactification of $I$ and
$\mathcal C_{\mathrm{lc}}(S,\mathbf C)$ is the ring of locally constant
$\mathbf C$-valued functions on $S$, so that $U$ is a scheme over
$X_0$. The seven clauses below are the construction and its computation.
The two sources used are Bhatt–Scholze,
[arXiv:1309.1198v2](https://arxiv.org/html/1309.1198v2), and
Bergfalk–Lambie-Hanson,
[arXiv:2412.19605v2](https://arxiv.org/html/2412.19605v2); their exact
statements, numbers and verbatim wording are recorded in Section 16.1 of the
audit ledger, the first at Lemmas 5.1.1 and 5.1.2, Corollary 5.1.6,
Definition 3.2.1, Example 4.1.10, Remark 4.1.11 and Proposition 4.2.8, the
second at Theorem 4.3, Lemma 4.8 and Theorem 4.11.

1. **(i)** *$U$ is an affine pro-étale object of $X_{0,\Proet}$, a
cofiltered limit of finite disjoint unions of points.* The profinite space
$S$ is the cofiltered limit of its finite quotients
$S\twoheadrightarrow S_i$, and
$\mathcal C_{\mathrm{lc}}(S,\mathbf C)=\colim_i\mathbf C^{S_i}$; hence
$$
U=\lim_i\Spec\bigl(\mathbf C^{S_i}\bigr)
=\lim_i\coprod_{S_i}\Spec\mathbf C
$$
is a cofiltered limit of finite disjoint unions of points with affine
transition maps, the structure maps $\Spec(\mathbf C^{S_i})\to X_0$ being
finite étale. Since a cofiltered limit of finite étale $X_0$-schemes is
pro-étale over $X_0$, the projection $U\to X_0$ is affine pro-étale and
$U$ is an object of the small pro-étale site
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].
1. **(ii)** *Its étale topos is the topos of sheaves on $S$, and
$\Gamma(U_{\Et},-)$ is exact.* Passing to small étale topoi along (i),
$$
\Mod(U_{\Et},A)\cong\Sh(S,A),
$$
the category of sheaves of $A$-modules on the profinite set $S$,
equivalently on the site of its finite quotients: an étale sheaf on
$\coprod_{S_i}\Spec\mathbf C$ is a family of $A$-modules indexed by the
finite set $S_i$, and the colimit of these categories along the cofiltered
system of quotients is $\Sh(S,A)$. Under this identification the global
sections of an étale sheaf on $U$ are computed on the finite quotients,
$H^q(U_{\Et},\mathcal G)=\colim_iH^q(S_i,\mathcal G_i)=0$ for $q>0$, a
finite set having no higher cohomology; so $\Gamma(U_{\Et},-)$ is an exact
functor on $\Sh(S,A)$.
1. **(iii)** *Weakly contractible objects of $U_{\Proet}$, and their
sections.* The weakly contractible objects of the pro-étale topos of
$\Spec\mathbf C$ correspond exactly to the extremally disconnected profinite
sets, evaluation on them is exact, and the topos is locally weakly
contractible (Bhatt–Scholze, Definition 3.2.1, Example 4.1.10, Remark 4.1.11
and Proposition 4.2.8); transported along the pro-étale morphism
$U\to X_0$, the objects
$$
U_T=\Spec\,\mathcal C_{\mathrm{lc}}(T,\mathbf C)\qquad
(T\ \text{extremally disconnected profinite})
$$
are weakly contractible and form a basis of $U_{\Proet}$, and on a weakly
contractible object every pro-étale cover has a section, so the global-sections
functor there is exact; this is the device of
[lem-sf-proetale-vanishing-detection], whose clause (ii) is the statement
that a complex of $A$-module sheaves on $U_{\Proet}$ is acyclic as soon as
its evaluations at the objects of such a basis are acyclic complexes.
1. **(iv)** *Unbounded $\operatorname{Ext}$ against the constant sheaf.*
By (ii) and by Bergfalk–Lambie-Hanson, Theorem 4.3, applied to the two
étale-origin factors $S=T=\beta I$ of cardinality $|I|=\aleph_\omega$ and
to the field $K=A$, the constant sheaf $A$ on the product
$\beta I\times\beta I=S$ has infinite injective dimension in
$\Sh(S,A)$:
$$
\operatorname{injdim}_{\Sh(S,A)}(A)=\infty .
$$
(For the *finite* field $A$ the first clause of the same theorem, proved
separately as Lemma 4.8, gives at the same time that the constant sheaf $A$
on an extremally disconnected compact Hausdorff space is injective.) Hence
for every integer $M$ there are a sheaf $G$ of $A$-modules on
$U_{\Et}$, that is, an object of $\Sh(S,A)$, and an integer $q>M$ with
$$
\operatorname{Ext}^q_{\Sh(S,A)}(G,A)\neq0 :
$$
otherwise $\operatorname{Ext}^q(-,A)=0$ for all $q>M$ would present $A$
as an object of injective dimension at most $M$.
1. **(v)** *The sheaf $F_G$, and the vanishing of its higher derived
Hom.* Put
$$
F_G=\mathcal H om_A\bigl(\nu_U^*G,A\bigr),
$$
a sheaf of $A$-modules on $U_{\Proet}$ in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], and outside the blueprint's coefficient
class unless $G$ is constructible. Then
$$
R\mathcal H om_A\bigl(\nu_U^*G,A\bigr)\cong
\mathcal H om_A\bigl(\nu_U^*G,A\bigr),
$$
that is, the derived Hom is concentrated in degree $0$. Indeed, at the
basis objects $U_T$ of (iii) the restriction of $\nu_U^*G$ is the constant
sheaf with value $G(T)$, sections there are exact by (iii), and the constant
sheaf $A$ is injective on $U_T$ by the injectivity clause of (iv); so
$\operatorname{Ext}^q_A\bigl(\nu_U^*G(U_T),A\bigr)=0$ for every $q>0$ and
every basis object, and therefore
$\mathcal E xt^q_A(\nu_U^*G,A)=0$ for $q>0$, by the detection criterion
[lem-sf-proetale-vanishing-detection](ii).
1. **(vi)** *$R\Gamma(U_{\Proet},F_G)=R\Hom_{\Sh(S,A)}(G,A)$, and the
failure of the bound.* From (v) and the identification of global sections of
the sheafified Hom with the derived Hom in the derived category of
$U_{\Proet}$,
$$
R\Gamma(U_{\Proet},F_G)
=R\Hom_{D(U_{\Proet},A)}\bigl(\nu_U^*G,A\bigr)
=R\Hom_{D(U_{\Et},A)}\bigl(G,R\nu_{U,*}A\bigr)
=R\Hom_{\Sh(S,A)}(G,A),
$$
the second step being the adjunction $\nu_U^*\dashv R\nu_{U,*}$ for the
comparison morphism of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] and the
third the identity $R\nu_{U,*}A=A$, which is
[prop-sf-comparison-bound-zero] applied to the constant étale sheaf
$A$. By the exactness of $\Gamma(U_{\Et},-)$ established in (ii), the
Leray spectral sequence of the composite
$\Gamma(U_{\Proet},-)=\Gamma(U_{\Et},-)\circ\nu_{U,*}$ degenerates and gives,
for every $q$,
$$
\Gamma\bigl(U_{\Et},R^q\nu_{U,*}F_G\bigr)=H^q(U_{\Proet},F_G)
=\operatorname{Ext}^q_{\Sh(S,A)}(G,A).
$$
By the choice of $G$ and $q$ in (iv) the right-hand side is nonzero for
arbitrarily large $q$, and $\Gamma$ is a functor to $A$-modules, so the
left-hand side is nonzero for those $q$; hence
$$
R^q\nu_{U,*}F_G\neq0\qquad\text{for arbitrarily large }q,
\qquad\text{that is,}\qquad
\operatorname{cd}_A(\nu_{U,*})=\infty .
$$
This is the failure proved in *The all-sheaves, uniform-in-the-base-change form of the comparison bound is false*: the
object $U$ of $X_{0,\Proet}$ is one of the pro-étale base changes over
which the bound $(\mathrm{G})$ is required, and $F_G$ is a sheaf of
$A$-modules on $U_{\Proet}$ with no constructibility hypothesis, so no
integer $M$ bounds the vanishing degree. Note that $S=\beta I\times\beta I$
is *not* extremally disconnected – the product of two infinite
extremally disconnected compact Hausdorff spaces never is – which is exactly
what allows the constant sheaf on $S$ to have infinite injective dimension
while the constant sheaf on each $U_T$ of (iii) is injective.
1. **(vii)** *What the counterexample does not affect.* On the
blueprint's coefficient class [def-sf-fullcd-used-class] – the sheaves of
étale origin, equivalently the constructible ones – the bound is $M=0$,
by [prop-sf-comparison-bound-zero], so the vanishing required by
[def-weil-full-cohomological-dimension] holds there with the bound
$2d$, which is [thm-sf-fullcd-used-class]; the counterexample uses a
sheaf $F_G$ that is not of étale origin. Two further consequences are
recorded here for the status of the neighbouring items. First, by
*The strictly henselian limit has no higher cohomology*(iii) the limit object
$\Spec\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{U,\bar u}$ of a geometric point of $U$ has
no higher cohomology for any sheaf, and by the contrapositive of
*Continuity for arbitrary sheaves implies the vanishing* the present computation
shows that the continuity statement $(\mathrm{C}_q)$ of that theorem
*fails* at $U$, in those degrees $q$ in which
$R^q\nu_{U,*}F_G\neq0$; the continuity route is therefore not a residue
"for arbitrary sheaves" but a statement about the finite-type models, which is
the form in which *Continuity for arbitrary sheaves gives the full cohomological-dimension bound* consumes it. Second,
nothing here weakens any statement of this chapter: the class form
[thm-sf-fullcd-used-class] and the sharp comparison bound
[prop-sf-comparison-bound-zero] are unconditional on that class, and the
only statement that changes status is $(\mathrm{G})$ itself, which passes
from "open" to "false".

attrs.title: The counterexample: a pro-étale base change whose comparison direct image has infinite cohomological dimension

objects.body:
The three items of the refutation ([prop-sf-comparison-bound-zero], [rem-sf-fullcd-counterexample]) leave the following picture
of the failure. The counterexample of
[rem-sf-fullcd-counterexample] is neither a phenomenon of the finite-type
world nor a phenomenon of the coefficients of étale origin: it lives at a
pro-étale limit and in the coefficients outside the blueprint's class, and
every restricted form of the statement that the manuscript uses is untouched by
it.

1. **(i)** *Where the object lives: at a pro-étale limit, not in the
finite-type world.* The object of the counterexample is
$U=\Spec\mathcal C_{\mathrm{lc}}(S,\mathbf C)$ with
$S=\beta I\times\beta I$, and by clause (i) of
[rem-sf-fullcd-counterexample] it is the cofiltered limit
$U=\varprojlim_i\Spec(\mathbf C^{S_i})$ of finite disjoint unions of points
with affine transition maps, hence an affine pro-étale object of
$X_{0,\Proet}$ for $X_0=\Spec\mathbf C$ in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Every model
$\Spec(\mathbf C^{S_i})$ is a finite-type $\mathbf C$-scheme of dimension
$0$, so the system is a cofiltered system of finite-type schemes over the
base field with affine transition maps and with bounded dimension — the
dimension is $0$ at every stage — while the limit $U$ is itself
*not* of finite type over $\mathbf C$, nor even locally of finite type:
the ring $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{lc}}(S,\mathbf C)$ is not Noetherian, the
clopen subsets $\{i\}\times\beta I\subseteq S$ for $i\in I$ being pairwise
disjoint and nonempty and giving the strictly ascending chain of ideals
generated by their indicator functions, whereas a finitely generated algebra
over a field is Noetherian. Consequently no statement of this manuscript whose
hypothesis is a finite-type
$k$-scheme applies to $U$ itself — in particular neither
[thm-sf-fullcd-used-class] nor [thm-sf-fullcd-etale-origin], whose
bound $2d$ is a bound for finite-type sources — and the counterexample is a
statement about the limit and not about the finite-type models: clauses
(iv)–(vi) of [rem-sf-fullcd-counterexample] compute exactly the failure
of the passage from the dimension-zero models to the limit, the finite-type
bound being unavailable at the limit.
1. **(ii)** *Where the sheaf lives: outside the étale origin.* The
coefficient sheaf of the counterexample is
$F_G=\mathcal H om_A(\nu_U^*G,A)$ of clause (v) of
[rem-sf-fullcd-counterexample], a sheaf of $A$-modules on $U_{\Proet}$
in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], with
$\nu_U:U_{\Proet}\to U_{\Et}$ the comparison morphism of
[def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. It is *not* of étale
origin. For if $F_G\cong\nu_U^*\mathcal H$ for a sheaf $\mathcal H$ of
$A$-modules on $U_{\Et}$, then [prop-sf-comparison-bound-zero], which
is stated for an arbitrary scheme and an arbitrary étale $A$-module sheaf
and imposes no constructibility hypothesis, would give
$R^q\nu_{U,*}F_G=R^q\nu_{U,*}\nu_U^*\mathcal H=0$ for every $q>0$; clause
(vi) of [rem-sf-fullcd-counterexample] gives
$R^q\nu_{U,*}F_G\neq0$ for arbitrarily large $q$. By
[lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], which is likewise stated for an
arbitrary scheme, $F_G$ is then also not constructible in the intrinsic
sense, so it lies outside the coefficient sheaves that
[def-sf-fullcd-used-class] describes.
1. **(iii)** *What survives, stated exactly.* Three things, and nothing
weaker.
   1. The comparison bound is $M=0$ for *every* scheme and *every*
coefficient sheaf of étale origin, with no constructibility hypothesis:
[prop-sf-comparison-bound-zero] states that the unit
$\mathcal G\to\nu_{X,*}\nu_X^*\mathcal G$ is an isomorphism for every scheme
$X$ and every sheaf $\mathcal G$ of $A$-modules on $X_{\Et}$, and hence
that $R^q\nu_{X,*}(\nu_X^*\mathcal G)=0$ for every $q>0$. That is the
sharp form of the bound, it is proved, and the counterexample does not touch
it; indeed the counterexample shows that this sharpest of bounds is confined to
the coefficients of étale origin: with the bound $0$ fixed on that class,
the only freedom left in the refuted statement is the class of coefficients,
and it is there that the general form fails.
   1. On the blueprint's coefficient class [def-sf-fullcd-used-class] —
the sheaves of étale origin, equivalently the constructible ones — the
vanishing required by [def-weil-full-cohomological-dimension] is a theorem
with the bound $2d$ *uniformly over all base changes*, for finite-type
$k$-schemes $Y$ and $\overline X$ with
$\dim\overline X\leq d$ and a proper finite-type
$p:\overline X\to Y$: this is [thm-sf-fullcd-used-class], whose
$\operatorname{FullCD}$-form is [thm-sf-fullcd-etale-origin]. On that
class the comparison bound itself is moreover $0$, by
[prop-sf-comparison-bound-zero], the residual $2d$ being the étale
direction of the Leray spectral sequence of [thm-sp-grothendieck] and not
a lower bound on $R^q\nu_{\overline X,*}$. This is the form of the condition
that the blueprint uses.
   1. For arbitrary coefficients on arbitrary pro-étale base changes the
statement is *false*: *The all-sheaves, uniform-in-the-base-change form of the comparison bound is false* refutes the
form recorded in [rem-sf-fullcd-general-form], in which the bound is asked
for every sheaf of $A$-modules and uniformly over the base changes. The
blueprint therefore restricts to the class it uses: the interface
[open-sf-ambient-adjoint-input] is read on
[def-sf-fullcd-used-class], where the vanishing half is the
class-restricted datum [def-sf-fullcd-class] supplied by
[thm-sf-fullcd-class] and the existence half of the ambient datum is now
the theorem [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class], and what it still asks
for is the adjunction for the complexes outside that class, as
[rem-sf-fullcd-reduction] and [rem-sf-class-adjoint-residue] record.
One further variant must be separated from these three, and it is *not*
addressed by any statement of this manuscript: keeping the coefficients
arbitrary while restricting the base changes themselves to be of finite type.
No item of the chain proves that restriction —
[def-weil-full-cohomological-dimension] quantifies over all objects of
$Y_{\Proet}$ — and the finite-type bounds of the chain may not be read as
such a restriction, since by clause (i) above the object of the counterexample
is itself a limit of finite-type models with affine transition maps, over which
the finite-type bound does not pass. The only statement of that shape is the
conditional *Continuity for arbitrary sheaves gives the full cohomological-dimension bound*, which derives the vanishing for
arbitrary sheaves on limits of finite-type $k$-schemes of dimension at most
$d$ from its continuity hypothesis $(\mathrm{Co})$ for arbitrary sheaves;
that hypothesis is not proved anywhere in this manuscript, and the continuity
statement $(\mathrm{C}_q)$ from which that route starts fails at the
counterexample's $U$ in the degrees of clause (vi), by the contrapositive of
*Continuity for arbitrary sheaves implies the vanishing*. The variant is therefore
neither proved nor refuted here, and no statement of this chapter rests on it:
what the manuscript proves is the class form of the preceding item, and it is
only on that class that the statements depending on the ambient datum are
conditional.

attrs.title: Where the counterexample lives, and which restricted statements survive it

objects.body:
The condition [def-weil-full-cohomological-dimension] quantifies over
*all* sheaves of $A$-modules on $\overline X_{\Proet}$, and it is by
[lem-sf-fullcd-detection-equivalence] equivalent to a uniform bound on
the cohomological dimension of the pro-étale sites of the base-changed
sources. Two forms of that condition must be distinguished.

1. *On the blueprint's coefficient class it is a theorem*, with the
bound $2\dim\overline X$ and uniformly over the base changes: this is
[thm-sf-fullcd-used-class], whose class
[def-sf-fullcd-used-class] is the class of étale origin, equivalently
– by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] – the class of
constructible pro-étale coefficient sheaves
([def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]). The comparison bound
itself is $M=0$ on that class, by
[prop-sf-comparison-bound-zero]: the residual $2\dim\overline X$ is the
étale direction of the Leray spectral sequence of
[thm-sp-grothendieck] and not a lower bound on
$R^q\nu_{\overline X,*}$. Every coefficient sheaf
that this manuscript constructs lies in it: the construction of the six
operations takes place on the bounded constructible categories, so the
coefficient sheaves occurring in the statements of the blueprint are
constructible, and by the cited origin statement they are exactly the ones
covered by [thm-sf-fullcd-etale-origin].
1. *On arbitrary pro-étale module sheaves, uniformly over the base
changes, it is FALSE.* The general form is refuted by
*The all-sheaves, uniform-in-the-base-change form of the comparison bound is false*, whose counterexample is recorded in
[rem-sf-fullcd-counterexample]: there are a scheme $X_0$, an affine
pro-étale object $U\to X_0$ of $X_{0,\Proet}$ and, for every integer
$M$, a sheaf $F_G$ of $A$-modules on $U_{\Proet}$ – not of étale
origin – with $R^q\nu_{U,*}F_G\neq0$ for some $q>M$. What the recorded
tools do and do not bound is the following. The
recorded tools do not bound it: by
[lem-sf-fullcd-detection-equivalence] the condition is the vanishing of
the pro-étale cohomology of the base-changed source
$\overline X\times_YV$, tested by
[lem-sf-proetale-vanishing-detection] at the affine weakly contractible
objects $W\to V$ — the form of the test recorded in
[cor-sf-fullcd-weakly-contractible-test] — and the object
$\overline X\times_YW$ that appears is
the base change of $W$ along the proper morphism $p$, which is *not*
pro-étale; the argument that makes every sheaf acyclic on a weakly
contractible object – every pro-étale cover of it has a section, so its
global-sections functor is exact, which is Stacks Project, Cohomology on
Sites, Lemma 21.51.1,
[Tag 0946](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0946) – therefore does
not apply to $\overline X\times_YW$, and no bound on those groups is
recorded. A search of the sources recorded in this blueprint's audit ledger
was carried out for exactly this bound, and it found no proof and no
counterexample. On the pro-étale site the only vanishing statement for
*all* sheaves is the one just named, at a weakly contractible object;
for sheaves of étale origin the sharper statement
$R^q\nu_{\overline X,*}\nu_{\overline X}^*\mathcal G=0$ for $q>0$, that
is with the bound $0$, is Stacks Project, Pro-étale Cohomology, Lemma
61.19.5,
[Tag 099V](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099V), which is
[thm-sf-fullcd-etale-origin] with the bound $2d$ replaced by the
sharper one; Stacks Project, Pro-étale Cohomology, Example 61.19.12,
[Tag 0F6D](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F6D), names a sheaf
that is not of étale origin and computes none of its cohomology; and the
pro-étale chapter 61 contains no statement about a cohomological dimension
of the pro-étale site at all. The étale analogue of the missing bound is
classical and is a definition plus a theorem: the cohomological dimension
$\operatorname{cd}(f)$ is defined by the vanishing of $R^if_*\mathcal F$,
$i>\operatorname{cd}(f)$, for *every* abelian *torsion* sheaf
$\mathcal F$ on $X_{\Et}$, Stacks Project, Étale Cohomology,
Definition 59.96.1,
[Tag 0F0Z](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F0Z), and it is finite
for a morphism of finite type over a field, Lemma 59.96.2,
[Tag 0F10](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F10); the pro-étale
counterpart of neither exists in the sources recorded here. The one
class of non-constructible coefficients for which the blueprint has a name
is the sheafified quotient of clause (4) of
[lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative], a nonzero sheaf with all
geometric-point stalks zero; the vanishing for it and its relatives is not
decided by anything in this manuscript either, no degree of its pro-étale
cohomology being computed anywhere in the chain, so this sheaf yields neither a
proof of the general form nor a counterexample to it; the counterexample that
refutes the general form is a different sheaf, the $F_G$ of
[rem-sf-fullcd-counterexample]. Consequently the
general form is not an open problem but a false statement, refuted by
*The all-sheaves, uniform-in-the-base-change form of the comparison bound is false* and
[rem-sf-fullcd-counterexample]; what survives, and what this manuscript
uses, is the class form: on the coefficient class
[def-sf-fullcd-used-class] the vanishing is the theorem
[thm-sf-fullcd-used-class], whose comparison bound is $M=0$ by
[prop-sf-comparison-bound-zero], so the statements that need only the
class form are unconditional on that class, as
[rem-sf-fullcd-reduction] states.
1. *What the search of the round of 18 September 2026 adds: the
reduction, the shape a counterexample must have, the concrete obstruction,
and the pages checked.* None of the four points below is a claim about the
truth of the general form; each is a fact about the recorded tools.
   1. **(a)** *On the source itself the étale factor is already bounded,
so only the vanishing degree of $R^q\nu_{\overline X,*}$ is missing there.*
For *every* sheaf $G$ of $A$-modules on the étale site of a
finite-type $k$-scheme $\overline X$ with $\dim\overline X\le d$ one has
$H^p(\overline X_{\Et},G)=0$ for $p>2d$: apply
[lem-sf-etale-direct-image-vanishing] to the structure morphism
$\overline X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, whose target has trivial étale
cohomology because $k$ is algebraically closed, and read off the Leray
spectral sequence of [thm-sp-grothendieck], in which every term with
$p>0$ vanishes. Hence in the Leray spectral sequence
$E_2^{p,q}=H^p(\overline X_{\Et},R^q\nu_{\overline X,*}\mathcal F) \Rightarrow H^{p+q}(\overline X_{\Proet},\mathcal F)$ of the comparison
morphism the $p$-direction is bounded by $2d$ independently of
$\mathcal F$, and unbounded degrees can enter only through $q$: if
$R^q\nu_{\overline X,*}\mathcal F=0$ for every $q>M$ and every sheaf
$\mathcal F$ of $A$-modules on $\overline X_{\Proet}$, then
$H^r(\overline X_{\Proet},\mathcal F)=0$ for every $r>M+2d$. This is the
sense in which the étale factor of the comparison is not what is missing
on the source. It is *not* a statement about the base-changed sources
of [lem-sf-fullcd-detection-equivalence]: for $V\to Y$ in
$Y_{\Proet}$ the scheme $\overline X\times_YV$ is a pro-étale limit and
not of finite type over $k$, so the cited étale bound does not apply to
it, and the same reduction there would need that bound for the limit as
well. That second gap is recorded here rather than passed over; it is
exactly the gap that the continuity statement of
*Continuity for arbitrary sheaves implies the vanishing* closes on the limit
sources, *Continuity for arbitrary sheaves gives the full cohomological-dimension bound*(ii).
   1. **(b)** *The shape a counterexample must have: a coefficient sheaf whose
Čech complex along a weakly contractible hypercovering is unbounded.* By
Stacks Project, Pro-étale Cohomology,
Lemma 61.14.2,
[Tag 09A2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09A2), for a
hypercovering $K$ of a quasi-compact and quasi-separated object $U$ of
$T_{\Proet}$ whose terms $K_n=\{U_n\to U\}$ consist of weakly
contractible objects one has
$R\Gamma(U,\mathcal E)=\operatorname{Tot}(s(\mathcal E^\bullet(K)))$, and
by Lemma 61.14.1,
[Tag 09A1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09A1), such
hypercoverings exist with every $U_n$ affine and weakly contractible. The
construction puts no bound on the number of non-empty terms. If for some
object $U$ such a hypercovering were *bounded*, $K_n=\emptyset$ for
$n>N$, then its Čech complex would be concentrated in degrees
$0,\dots,N$ and $H^q(U,\mathcal F)=0$ for every $q>N$ and
*every* sheaf $\mathcal F$ of abelian groups. That hypothesis is
however never satisfied by a nonempty $U$: by
*No hypercovering of a nonempty object has an empty term* every hypercovering of a nonempty
object has a nonempty term in every degree, so the criterion is vacuous, and
*The question of a bounded weakly contractible hypercovering has a negative answer* records the consequence for the question
whether a bound on the length of a weakly contractible hypercovering exists
at all. The vanishing for $U=\operatorname{Spec}\bar k$ with $\bar k$
separably closed, which is the case of the sheaf of clause (4) of
[lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative] referred to here, comes instead
from *The strictly henselian limit has no higher cohomology*(iii), and it is also what the criterion
*Vanishing above the degree in which the coefficient sheaf dies on the terms* gives, the constant hypercover
of $\operatorname{Spec}\bar k$ having terms that are acyclic for that sheaf and
on which that sheaf has no sections. A counterexample to the general form must
therefore exhibit a coefficient sheaf whose Čech
complex along a weakly contractible hypercovering of one of the
base-changed sources has cohomology in arbitrarily high degrees; the
unboundedness of the hypercovering is automatic by
*No hypercovering of a nonempty object has an empty term* and is no part of the obstruction, and
such a sheaf is constructed in [rem-sf-fullcd-counterexample], where the
role of the base-changed source is played by the pro-étale object $U$ and
the unbounded degrees are those of the coefficient sheaf $F_G$.
   1. **(c)** *The concrete obstruction, and why the one known
non-étale-origin sheaf cannot witness it.* The stalk of
$R^q\nu_{\overline X,*}\mathcal F$ at a geometric point $\bar x$ is the
filtered colimit of the groups $H^q(U_{\Proet},\mathcal F)$ over the étale
neighbourhoods $U$ of $\bar x$, whereas the object
$\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O^{sh}_{\overline X,\bar x}$ at the limit of
that system is a *point* of the pro-étale topos: by Stacks Project,
Pro-étale Cohomology, Section 61.18,
[Tag 0991](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0991), the functor
$\mathcal F\mapsto\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O^{sh})$ is the
geometric-point stalk functor $\mathcal F\mapsto\mathcal F_{\bar x}$ and it
is exact. Hence $H^q(\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O^{sh}_{\overline X,\bar x},\mathcal F)=0$ for every $q>0$ and every sheaf $\mathcal F$,
which is now recorded as a proved statement,
*The strictly henselian limit has no higher cohomology*(iii), so that the sheafified quotient of
clause (4) of
[lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative] — the sheaf $fun(-,A)/\underline A$ of Stacks Project, Pro-étale Cohomology, Example 61.19.12,
[Tag 0F6D](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F6D) — is acyclic on
every such object. What the two computations leave open is exactly the
comparison of the colimit of the $H^q$ over the neighbourhoods with the
$H^q$ of the object at the limit, a continuity statement which Stacks
records only for sheaves of étale origin: the values of the pullback of an
étale sheaf commute with the limit (Lemma 61.19.3,
[Tag 099S](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099S)), the Čech
complexes of Lemma 61.19.4
([Tag 099U](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099U)) are acyclic
there, and the resulting vanishing Lemma 61.19.5
([Tag 099V](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099V)) is
[thm-sf-fullcd-etale-origin] with the bound $2d$ sharpened to $0$.
A counterexample must produce a class on the étale neighbourhoods of a
geometric point that survives every refinement, that is, a failure of this
continuity, and [rem-sf-fullcd-counterexample] produces one. That
continuity statement is isolated and
analysed in [rem-sf-continuity-obstruction]: it is *not* a
consequence of [lem-sf-etale-direct-image-vanishing], whose terms are
étale and not pro-étale cohomology groups of the models, whereas it does
imply the vanishing with the sharpest bound $M=0$,
*Continuity for arbitrary sheaves implies the vanishing*, and hence
$\operatorname{FullCD}(p,A;2d)$, *Continuity for arbitrary sheaves gives the full cohomological-dimension bound*; and it is
the statement that fails at the counterexample's base change, by
*The all-sheaves, uniform-in-the-base-change form of the comparison bound is false*. The residue of the general form was
therefore exactly that statement, and it is now a residue no longer: the
general form is false, and what the chapter uses is the class form
[thm-sf-fullcd-used-class], with the sharp comparison bound $M=0$ of
[prop-sf-comparison-bound-zero].
   1. **(d)** *Why the classical transplant fails, and the pages checked.*
The classical phenomenon of unbounded cohomology of arbitrary torsion
sheaves needs a base field of infinite cohomological dimension: for
$K=\mathbf R$ the constant sheaf $\mathbf Z/2$ has
$H^q(\operatorname{Spec}K_{\Et},\mathbf Z/2) =H^q(\mathbf Z/2,\mathbf Z/2)=\mathbf Z/2$ for *all* $q$, in the
pro-étale form as well as in the étale one by Stacks Project, Pro-étale
Cohomology, Lemma 61.22.1,
[Tag 09B4](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09B4)
($H^i(\operatorname{Spec}k,\underline M^\wedge) =H^i_{\mathrm{cont}}(G,M)$). This is exactly what forces the hypothesis
$\operatorname{cd}(K)<\infty$ in Stacks Project, Étale Cohomology, Lemma
59.96.2, [Tag 0F10](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F10), whose
part (2) bounds $\operatorname{cd}(X)$ for finite-type $X/K$, the
definition being Definition 59.96.1,
[Tag 0F0Z](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F0Z), and the affine
bound being Proposition 59.95.6,
[Tag 0F0V](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F0V)
($\operatorname{cd}(X)\le\dim X+\operatorname{cd}(K)$). In the setting of
this remark $k$ is algebraically closed, so the residue field of every
point of every pro-étale base change is separably closed and no such
periodic Galois group occurs; the transplant of the $K=\mathbf R$ example,
of the skyscraper gadgets of the Zariski topology, and of the étale
cohomological-dimension theorem therefore produces no counterexample here.
Read in this round, each page fetched and compared with the claim made: the
Chapter 61 table of contents
([Tag 0965](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0965), which contains
no section on a cohomological dimension of the pro-étale site) and its
Sections 61.13
([Tag 098I](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/098I),
[Tag 0990](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0990)), 61.14
([Tag 09A1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09A1),
[Tag 09A2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09A2)), 61.15
([Tag 0994](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0994)), 61.18
([Tag 0991](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0991)), 61.19
([Tag 099R](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099R), with Lemmas
61.19.3–61.19.6 and Example 61.19.12), 61.22
([Tag 09B4](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09B4)), together with
Chapter 59's Sections 59.95
([Tag 0F0V](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F0V)) and 59.96
([Tag 0F0Z](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F0Z),
[Tag 0F10](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F10)). The full
Bhatt–Scholze paper was again not retrievable with the tools available here
(the PDF endpoints returned a network error and an unsupported content
type), so it was consulted only through the Stacks reproductions quoted
above, as Section 12 of the audit ledger records.

*The exact wording of the form that is false.* For a finite-type
$k$-scheme $\overline X$ with $\dim\overline X\leq d$, a proper
finite-type morphism $p:\overline X\to Y$ and a coefficient ring
$A=A_{E,n}$, form $(\mathrm{G})$ is the assertion that there is an integer
$M$ with

$$
(\mathrm{G})\qquad
R^q\nu_{\overline X,*}\mathcal F=0\qquad(q>M)
$$

for *every* sheaf $\mathcal F$ of $A$-modules on
$\overline X_{\Proet}$, uniformly over the base changes $V\to Y$ of
$Y_{\Proet}$; equivalently, by
[lem-sf-fullcd-detection-equivalence], the uniform bound on the
pro-étale cohomology of the base-changed sources. That assertion is
*false*: *The all-sheaves, uniform-in-the-base-change form of the comparison bound is false* exhibits an object
$U\to X_0$ of $X_{0,\Proet}$ and a sheaf $F_G$ of $A$-modules on
$U_{\Proet}$ with $R^q\nu_{U,*}F_G\neq0$ for arbitrarily large $q$, the
construction being recorded in [rem-sf-fullcd-counterexample]. It is the
quantification over *all* sheaves of $A$-modules, together with the
uniformity over the pro-étale base changes, that fails. On the blueprint's
coefficient class [def-sf-fullcd-used-class] the comparison bound holds
with $M=0$ by [prop-sf-comparison-bound-zero], and the vanishing
required by [def-weil-full-cohomological-dimension] therefore holds on
that class with the bound $2d$, which is [thm-sf-fullcd-used-class].

attrs.title: The general form of $\operatorname{FullCD}$, and the form the blueprint uses

objects.body:
The named interface [open-sf-ambient-adjoint-input] turns on the full
cohomological-dimension condition
[def-weil-full-cohomological-dimension] for the compactification of a
general separated finite-type morphism. Three things about that condition
can now be said exactly.

1. *Its torsion half is a theorem, on the étale site and
independently of the coefficient stage.* For the étale site the
vanishing required by $\operatorname{FullCD}$ holds for every sheaf of
$A$-modules, with the bound $2d$ for a source of dimension at most
$d$, by [lem-sf-etale-direct-image-vanishing]; that lemma quantifies
over all finite-type morphisms, proper or not, and its bound is the one of
[thm-sc-finite-type-torsion-cd], which depends only on the dimension
and on the torsion cohomological dimension of the ground field, hence not
on the coefficient ring $A_{E,n}$.
1. *The same bound is a theorem for every coefficient sheaf of
étale origin, and the comparison bound there is the sharp $M=0$.*
[thm-sf-fullcd-etale-origin] transfers the bound
$2d$ of clause (1) to the small pro-étale site along the comparison
direct image for every sheaf $\mathcal F\cong\nu_{\bar X}^*\mathcal G$
pulled back from an étale sheaf $\mathcal G$, uniformly over the base
changes; the comparison bound itself is $0$ on that class, by
[prop-sf-comparison-bound-zero], the residual $2d$ being the étale
direction of the Leray spectral sequence of [thm-sp-grothendieck]. The
general form, quantified over *all* pro-étale module sheaves and
uniformly over the pro-étale base changes, is *false*, by
*The all-sheaves, uniform-in-the-base-change form of the comparison bound is false* and
[rem-sf-fullcd-counterexample]: the counterexample's sheaf $F_G$ is a
sheaf of $A$-modules on a pro-étale base change $U$ of a base $X_0$,
not of étale origin, whose comparison direct images fail to vanish in
unboundedly many degrees. Constructibility is exactly the dividing line
here: [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] identifies the
constructible pro-étale coefficients with the étale ones, so the class on
which the bound holds is the blueprint's coefficient class
[def-sf-fullcd-used-class], while the sheafified quotient of clause (4)
of [lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative] and the sheaf $F_G$ of
[rem-sf-fullcd-counterexample] lie outside it.
1. *What remains can be tested without geometric-point stalks.*
Let $\nu_{\bar X}:\bar X_{\mathrm{proet}}\to\bar X_{\Et}$
be the comparison morphism and let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of $A$-modules
on $\bar X_{\mathrm{proet}}$. The Grothendieck spectral sequence of the
composite of the two section functors
$\Gamma(\bar X_{\mathrm{proet}},-)=\Gamma(\bar X_{\Et},-)\circ\nu_{\bar X,*}$
is [thm-sp-grothendieck], and it reads
$$
E_2^{p,q}=H^p\bigl(\bar X_{\Et},R^q\nu_{\bar X,*}\mathcal F\bigr)
\Longrightarrow H^{p+q}\bigl(\bar X_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal F\bigr).
$$
Each $R^q\nu_{\bar X,*}\mathcal F$ is a torsion étale sheaf of
$A$-modules, so clause (1) makes $E_2^{p,q}=0$ for
$p>2\dim\bar X$; hence a bound
$R^q\nu_{\bar X,*}\mathcal F=0$ for $q>M$, uniform in $\mathcal F$,
would give $\operatorname{FullCD}(p,A;2\dim\bar X+M)$, and the same
argument applied to the fibres of the base changes gives the relative form.
For such a bound, and for $\operatorname{FullCD}$ itself, the geometric
point stalks need not be consulted: by
[lem-sf-proetale-vanishing-detection] vanishing on the pro-étale
site is detected by evaluation at the affine weakly contractible objects,
and by [cor-sf-fullcd-weakly-contractible-test] the condition
$\operatorname{FullCD}(p,A;c)$ is therefore equivalent to the vanishing
of the finitely many evaluations recalled there, so the failure of
conservativity of the geometric-point stalks recorded in clause (4) of
[lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative] does not by itself obstruct the
test. What that test does not supply is a bound: the evaluations are
cohomology groups of the pro-étale site of the base-changed source, and
no recorded statement bounds them for the module sheaves that are not of
étale origin – clause (2) is the only case in which a bound is known, and
in general the bound fails, by
*The all-sheaves, uniform-in-the-base-change form of the comparison bound is false*. The implication that would have
supplied such a bound is recorded here, and its hypothesis is now known to
fail in general: by *Continuity for arbitrary sheaves implies the vanishing* the
continuity statement $(\mathrm{C}_q)$ recorded there — every cohomology
class on an étale neighbourhood of a geometric point dies after refinement,
equivalently the cohomology of the limit object is the colimit of the
cohomologies of its finite-type models, the limit object itself having no
higher cohomology for any sheaf by *The strictly henselian limit has no higher cohomology* — gives
$R^q\nu_{\bar X,*}\mathcal F=0$ for *every* $q\ge1$, that is, the
sharpest bound $M=0$, and then
$\operatorname{FullCD}(p,A;2\dim\bar X)$ by
*Continuity for arbitrary sheaves gives the full cohomological-dimension bound*, so that the bound of this item would improve
from $2\dim\bar X+M$ to $2\dim\bar X$. The counterexample of
[rem-sf-fullcd-counterexample] shows, through the contrapositive of that
theorem, that $(\mathrm{C}_q)$ fails at its base change $U$ in the degrees
in which $R^q\nu_{U,*}F_G\neq0$, so that continuity cannot be the residue in
that generality; its terms are pro-étale, not étale, cohomology groups of
the models, hence it is not obtained from
[lem-sf-etale-direct-image-vanishing] either, as
[rem-sf-continuity-obstruction] records, and the form in which
*Continuity for arbitrary sheaves gives the full cohomological-dimension bound* consumes it is the one for the finite-type
models.

Accordingly the general form, on all sheaves, is not merely unproved: it is
*false*, by *The all-sheaves, uniform-in-the-base-change form of the comparison bound is false* and
[rem-sf-fullcd-counterexample], so the ambient datum
[def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint] is read *on the
blueprint's coefficient class* [def-sf-fullcd-used-class], where
clause (1) of [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility] is a theorem
in *both* of its halves: the vanishing half is the class-restricted
datum [def-sf-fullcd-class], supplied with the bound $2\dim\bar X$ and
uniformly over the base changes by [thm-sf-fullcd-class], and the
existence half, with its unit, counit and compactification comparisons, is
the theorem [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class]; the interface
[open-sf-ambient-adjoint-input] therefore no longer names the existence
half on that class, and what it still names – the adjunction for the
complexes outside the class – is analysed in
[rem-sf-class-adjoint-residue].
Two consequences of the class form [thm-sf-fullcd-used-class] are worth
recording here. First, every coefficient sheaf of that class satisfies the
vanishing required by $\operatorname{FullCD}$, with the bound
$2\dim\bar X$ and uniformly over the base changes, and the comparison bound
itself is $M=0$ by [prop-sf-comparison-bound-zero], so that for the
coefficient categories this manuscript
actually uses – the bounded constructible and finite-Tor categories of
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] and
[def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], whose coefficient sheaves are
constructible by construction – the full-cohomological-dimension input of
the ambient datum is a theorem on the restricted input and not a hypothesis;
what the ambient datum still assumes on those categories is nothing beyond
that theorem and [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class]: the existence half, which
*Ambient exceptional right adjoint* derives from clause (1) for the
unrestricted input, is on the class the cited theorem. Second, the general form of the condition,
quantified over arbitrary pro-étale module sheaves and uniformly over the
base changes, is by
[lem-sf-fullcd-detection-equivalence] the uniform bound on the
pro-étale cohomology of the base-changed sources, and it is refuted by
[rem-sf-fullcd-counterexample], as
[rem-sf-fullcd-general-form] records.

attrs.title: What $\operatorname{FullCD}$ supplies, and what would discharge it

objects.body:
Given biduality [thm-sf-biduality-class], the Verdier exchange
[thm-sf-verdier-exchange] has as its adjoint
$Rf^!\cong\mathbb D_X\,Lf^*\,\mathbb D_Y$, and the internal adjunction
$\RHom(A,\mathbb D C)\cong\mathbb D(A\otimes^LC)$ then rewrites
$\RHom(p_Y^*N,Rp_X^!M)$ as $\mathbb D_{X\times Y}(\mathbb D_XM\boxtimes N)$.
So [thm-trf-kunneth-verdier] is *equivalent*, by formal manipulation
inside the package, to the statement that duality commutes with the external
product,

$$
\mathbb D_{X\times Y}(M\boxtimes N)\cong\mathbb D_XM\boxtimes\mathbb D_YN .
$$

What is not formal is that statement itself: at $M=\Lambda_X$, $N=\Lambda_Y$
it reads $\omega_{X\times Y}\cong\omega_X\boxtimes\omega_Y$, which is $\alpha$
with constant coefficients and therefore needs purity, localization and
dévissage as above. For *perfect* $M$ it is formal, by
[thm-sf-dual-perfect] and [prop-sf-dualizable]; that
perfect case is the base of the induction, not a substitute for it.

attrs.title: Künneth–Verdier is formally duality of external products

objects.body:
The dependency structure of the duality material after this chapter is as
follows. *Proved here*: the formal core (mate calculus, tensor–Hom
exchange, Verdier exchange, biduality, global duality, detection, the
pairing and its identification), the relative product theorems together with
their coherence, and the yoga of the dual added after them (dual base change,
duality against pullback, the dualizing complex of a product, the
multiplicativity of the orientation, and the relative trace with its
transitivity); the
projection formula at every coefficient stage together with its coherence,
so that axiom (A3) of [def-sf-datum] is discharged; and the duality,
trace, similitude and reciprocity corollaries [thm-sf-dual-perfect] (with the orientation of the smooth dualizing complex taken from the purity chapter), *Perfectness of the trace–cup pairing* and *The trace isomorphism* (stated conditionally on the orientation datum of
[def-sf-orientation]). *Not here*: the orientation itself, which is
constructed in the purity chapter that follows (see
[rem-sf-orientation-pointer]), where the affine-line orientation over a
base, the affine-space case, the Gysin sheaf/group identification, the frame
transformation law, purity for vector bundles and smooth purity are proved
using the relative product theorem [thm-sf-kunneth-relative] of this
chapter. *Open, and where*: (1) the étale-local structure of
smooth morphisms and the étale locality of the purity map, used in the
purity chapter's smooth-purity theorem, the tensor form of purity itself
being [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness] of that chapter; (2) the four
nodes of the purity chapter on the projective-bundle, localized-top-Chern,
vector-triangularity and deformation-to-the-normal-cone route, which the
direct route through Zariski locality, the affine-space case and the frame
transformation law bypasses, so that they are off the critical path; (3) the
$p$-primary case in characteristic $p$, excluded by the standing hypothesis
$\ell\ne p$ and requiring the Artin–Schreier sequence in place of the
Kummer sequence. The nodes of the compiled duality chapter that this
chapter supersedes are its global-duality, identification, derived-duality,
degreewise, proper, trace and reciprocal-eigenvalue nodes; they may be
replaced by citations of [thm-sf-global-duality],
[thm-sf-identification], *Poincare duality, framework form*,
[thm-sf-dual-perfect], *The trace isomorphism* and
*Frobenius similitudes for the constant sheaf*, which also removes the proof cycle between the six-operations package [thm-weil-six-operations] and the duality chapter.

attrs.title: What this chapter settles, and what remains

objects.body:
The orientation datum of [def-sf-orientation] is not assumed: it is
constructed in the purity chapter that precedes this one, where the relative
product theorem [thm-sf-kunneth-relative] proved above supplies the
relative input that the purity chapter's pending notes declare missing.
Concretely, the affine-line orientation over an arbitrary base, the
affine-space case, the Gysin sheaf/group identification, the frame
transformation law, purity for vector bundles and smooth purity are proved
there; the reader should read the purity chapter immediately after this one,
the consequences *Perfectness of the trace–cup pairing* and *The trace isomorphism* are stated
conditionally on [def-sf-orientation] precisely so that they do not
depend on the order in which the two chapters are read, while
[thm-sf-dual-perfect] takes its case $f=a_X$ directly from the smooth
dualizing-complex identification of the purity chapter.

By [thm-sf-pf-finite], [prop-sf-pf-reduction],
[thm-sf-pf-adic], [thm-sf-pf-field],
[thm-sf-pf-proetale] and [prop-sf-pf-coherence], every obligation
listed in the interface [fix-prop-projection-formula] is discharged, so that interface is an unconditional
statement of this manuscript whose proof is the sequence above, and
axiom (A3) of [def-sf-datum] is verified for the concrete
compact-support direct image. The inputs consumed are the finite-level
statement [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula], the reduction
and scalar-extension compatibilities of [lem-fix-operation-reduction],
the site and compact-support comparisons, and the uniform-tower
reconstruction of chap:ambient-foundations. No duality statement is used anywhere in this
section: the projection formula is a statement about the compatibility of
$Rf_!$ with the tensor product, and it is logically prior to Verdier
duality. The status of the remaining inputs of the framework, and of the nodes of the smooth-purity chapter that this chapter completes, is recorded in
[rem-sf-ledger].

Finite exceptional preservation and the geometric duality bound are
[thm-sf-preservation-class], [lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata].
Finite biduality and its boundary exchange are
[thm-fix-general-biduality], [cor-weil-boundary-duality-discharge].
The coefficient comparisons needed to pass further are now proved:
[thm-coef-finite-hom], [cor-coef-finite-verdier], [lem-coef-finite-exceptional]
at finite levels, and
[lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction], [thm-coef-integral-verdier], [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint]
at the integral stage. Field extension and the rationalized
operations are
[lem-coef-integral-finite-extension], [lem-coef-rational-operations], [thm-coef-qbar-verdier].

The uniform local-model conditions discussed in
[rem-sf-tower-shapes-occurring] are not additional hypotheses
for these results. The normalized DVR reconstruction theorem supplies
the required integral objects. Geometric base-change clauses in
[def-trf-admissibility], [def-pod-conventions] retain the hypotheses
of their respective exchange theorems. The unrestricted unbounded
pro-etale adjunction is outside the conclusions here, as specified
in [rem-sf-class-adjoint-residue].

attrs.title: Constructible completion and the ambient boundary

objects.body:
The finite-coefficient results used in the assembly have these scopes:

1. Pullback preserves finite Tor amplitude by
[lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude]; tensor products have the bound of
[lem-sf-tensor-ctf].
1. Ordinary direct image on the constructible comparison class has the
geometric dimension bound of [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale].
1. The internal-Hom bound $[c-b,d-a]$ requires a site-perfect first
variable in [thm-sf-hom-ctf], [cor-sf-hom-ctf-proetale-unconditional].
The former general bound is false; [rem-sf-proetale-hom-status]
records the geometric obstruction. The dimension-dependent bound in
[thm-sf-hom-ctf] proves preservation for a general finite-Tor
constructible first variable.
1. Exceptional preservation is [thm-sf-preservation-class].
The dualizing object and general finite-coefficient geometric dual bound
are [lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata]. General finite-stage biduality is
[thm-sf-biduality-class]; closed-boundary exchange follows in
[cor-weil-boundary-duality-discharge].
1. Integral Hom reduction and preservation are
[lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction], [cor-coef-integral-internal-hom];
the exceptional adjunction is [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint].
Normalized DVR towers reconstruct by [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity].
The scope for other towers is [rem-sf-tower-shapes-occurring].

This record collects results and supplies no premise to their proofs.

attrs.title: Preservation results and their actual hypotheses

objects.body:
The sharp coefficient-only bound in
[cor-sf-hom-ctf-proetale-unconditional] requires a
[def-weil-site-perfect-complex] first variable.
Stalkwise finite Tor amplitude does not give that bound. For the origin
$i:\{0\}\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1$, with constant finite coefficients,
$i_*A$ and $A$ have Tor amplitude zero, whereas
$R\mathcal Hom(i_*A,A)=i_*A(-1)[-2]$ has nonzero cohomology in degree
$2$. Thus the bound $[c-b,d-a]$ for arbitrary constructible first
variables is false. General finite-coefficient constructible preservation
is proved geometrically in [cor-weil-finite-constructible-hom],
with a dimension-dependent bound, and is recorded in
[thm-sf-hom-ctf]. Site comparison for the general finite-Tor
first variable is [thm-sf-hom-comparison-constructible].

A *six-functor formalism* on a category of schemes (here: finite-type
$k$-schemes, with the small pro-étale sites and a fixed coefficient ring)
consists of the following data.

1. **Two adjoint pairs per morphism.** For every separated
finite-type $f:X\to Y$ a pair $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$ and, when $f$ is
exceptional-adjoint
admissible, a pair $Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$; the four functors are
$Lf^*,Rf_*,Rf_!,Rf^!$ — the ``six'' operations counting the tensor
product and the internal Hom.
1. **A monoidal structure.** The derived tensor product
$-\otimes^L_\Lambda-$ is symmetric monoidal on the coefficient categories
and $Lf^*$ is monoidal.
1. **Base change.** For a Cartesian square, $Lg^*Rf_!\cong Rf'_!Lg'^*$ always, and $Lg^*Rf_*\cong Rf'_*Lg'^*$ when $f$ is proper or
$g$ is smooth.
1. **The projection formula.** $Rf_!K\otimes^L_\Lambda L\cong Rf_!(K\otimes^L_\Lambda Lf^*L)$.
1. **Proper and smooth compatibility.** $Rf_!\cong Rf_*$ for
proper $f$; and for smooth $f$ the *orientation* $Rf^!\Lambda\cong Lf^*\Lambda(d)[2d]$ (relative dimension $d$) — the one datum that is not
a formal consequence of the rest.

Items 1–4 are the axioms; item 5 splits into a formal half (properness)
and the geometric input (smoothness, i.e. purity). The tensor–adjunction form of Verdier exchange is formal from items
1–4. General Verdier biduality requires its separate geometric theorem;
after that theorem and the orientation are supplied, the trace and the
Poincare pairing follow by the stated formal constructions. What is *not* formal is (i) the verification of the
axioms for the concrete coefficient system — for this blueprint,
proper, smooth and compact-support base change, the compactification
comparison, and the coefficient transports — and (ii) the orientation of
item 5. In the compiled blueprint these are exactly where the open
obligations live: the interface [fix-prop-projection-formula] (discharged in [thm-sf-pf-finite], [prop-sf-pf-reduction], [thm-sf-pf-adic], [thm-sf-pf-field], [thm-sf-pf-proetale] and [prop-sf-pf-coherence]), the base-change chapters, and the
purity chapter. In this chapter the framework is axiomatized once, the
formal core is proved once, and the two non-formal inputs are supplied.

The statements [lem-sf-flat-model], [lem-sf-tor-sheaf-constructible], [lem-sf-tensor-ctf], [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude]
are formulated at the finite stages $A=A_{E,n}$. At the other three
stages of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] they read as follows.
*Field stages:* $D^b_{ctf}(-,\Lambda)=D^b_c(-,\Lambda)$ for
$\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$ *by definition*, so the finite-Tor cells
there are the bounded-constructible cells of
[lem-sf-tensor-ctf], [thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility] and
[lem-weil-pbc-pullback-preserves-bounded-constructible].
*Integral stage:* for $K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ the definition
asks that every reduction $K\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}^LA_{E,j}$ have finite
Tor amplitude with one interval independent of $j$; pullback commutes with
these reductions, $(Lf^*K)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}^LA_{E,j}\cong Lf^*(K\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}^LA_{E,j})$, because $Lf^*$ is monoidal and
carries the constant coefficient sheaf to the constant coefficient sheaf
([def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]), so
[lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude] gives the integral form of clause (i),
with the same interval, as soon as the reduction isomorphism
$Lf^*K\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}^LA_{E,j}\cong Lf^*(K\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}^LA_{E,j})$ and the derived completeness of
$Lf^*K$ are available; both are instances of the finite-reduction clause
proved for pullback in [lem-fix-operation-reduction]; clause (vii) of
the finite-Tor preservation summary is a later summary of this computation.

For an integral object of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed],
the reductions $K_n=K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$ form a
coherent normalized tower, and
[lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] proves a common finite Tor
interval from the residue reduction. Conversely, a separately
supplied system satisfying
[def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower] reconstructs with exactly those
reductions by [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity].
This effectivity theorem needs no common stratification or lisse
local model. Membership in the integral constructible category
then follows from finite-level constructibility and a uniform bound.

For the direct-image tower in [def-weil-derived-direct-image],
normalization is [lem-coef-finite-direct-image], and the
finite direct-image bound of
[cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale] is uniform in the coefficient
level. Thus normalized DVR effectivity supplies the canonical
finite-reduction comparison without additional local models.
The compact-support and exceptional versions are
[lem-coef-integral-compact-support], [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint].

The stronger local-model assertions
*Stage-independent local models for a constant tower*, *Stage-independent local models for a lisse tower with a uniform trivializing cover*
continue to require their displayed lisse hypotheses; the corollary
*The finite-level comparison isomorphisms in the two cases* describes those
special cases. A tower with no verified normalization or quotient
cocycle is not covered by the general effectivity theorem, and merely
forming its derived limit does not identify its purported reductions.

attrs.title: Normalized DVR systems and additional local models

objects.body:
The identity of [lem-trf-trace-map-exchange] is not a consequence of
[def-sf-datum](A1)–(A6) as they are stated there: the isomorphism
$Lg'^*f^!\cong f'^!Lg^*$ that produces it is base change for $f^!$
*against pullback*, not the adjoint form [thm-sf-dual-base-change],
which concerns $Rf^!Rg_*$ and is unconditional. The identity is nevertheless
a theorem of the blueprint, proved where the trace is constructed
([lem-trf-trace-map-exchange], [lem-trf-trace-source-exchange]); the
geometric reason is that both the exchange and the trace are mates of the same
structure maps of the compactification
([prop-compactification-coherence-detailed]). A reader who works axiomatically
from [def-sf-datum] alone must therefore import this coherence from the
trace-formula chapter. It is not an additional axiom, and no statement of
this chapter is left unproved on account of it: the framework-level form is
[lem-trf-trace-map-exchange].

attrs.title: Why this coherence is not in the axiom list

objects.body:
For each operation the second column is where it is *defined*, the third
where it is *proved* to descend, with the statement that proves it.
$\Dbc,\Dctf,D_c^{[a,b]}$ are as in [def-sf-categories]; ``ét'' and
``proét'' refer to the small étale and the small pro-étale site.

| operation | ambient definition | descent to small categories (theorem) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $Lf^*$ | $D(Y,\Lambda)\to D(X,\Lambda)$ | $\Dbc(Y)\to\Dbc(X)$ ([thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility], ét); $\Dctf(Y)\to\Dctf(X)$ ([thm-sf-ctf-stability] (i)) |
| $-\otimes^L-$ | $D(Y)^2\to D(Y)$ | $\Dctf\times\Dbc\to\Dbc$ and $\Dctf\times\Dctf\to\Dctf$ on ét and proét, with $[a,b]+[c,d]\mapsto[a+c,b+d]$ ([thm-sf-ctf-stability] (ii)) |
| $\RHom(-,-)$ | $D(Y)^{\mathrm{op}}\times D(Y)\to D(Y)$ | $\Dctf\times\Dctf\to\Dctf$ on ét for two arbitrary objects, and on proét for pulled-back pairs, with $[a,b],[c,d]\mapsto[c-b-2m,d-a+2m]$ ($\dim Y\le m$), and $[c-b,d-a]$ for a site-perfect first argument ([thm-sf-hom-ctf], [thm-sf-ctf-stability] (ii)) |
| $Rf_*$ | $D^+(X)\to D^+(Y)$ | $\Dbc(X)\to\Dbc(Y)$ for every finite-type $f$ ([thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility]); $\Dctf(X)\to\Dctf(Y)$ on ét and proét, with $[a,b]\mapsto[a,b+2\dim X]$ for $f:X\to Y$ of finite-type $k$-schemes, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ ([thm-sf-direct-image-tor-amplitude], [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale], [thm-sf-ctf-stability] (iii)) |
| $Rf_!$ | ambient, via a compactification | $\Dbc(X)\to\Dbc(Y)$ ([thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility]) and $\Dctf(X)\to\Dctf(Y)$ ([thm-sf-ctf-stability] (iv)) |
| $Rf^{\times}$ | $D(Y)\to D(X)$, right adjoint of $Rf_!$; *hypothetical*: assumed to exist under the ambient datum, which fails in general (rem:sf-ambient-counterexample in the six-functors chapter) | none, and none is needed: it is an optional ambient functor used nowhere downstream. [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] proves the adjoint exists on the étale sites unconditionally; the pro-étale ambient form is conditional on a hypothesis that is false in general |
| $Rf^!$ | *defined* on $\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$ as $\nu_X^*f^{\times}R\nu_{Y,*}$, the étale adjoint of [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] transported along the comparison ([thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class], [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]) | $\Dctf(Y)\to\Dctf(X)$ for *every* separated finite-type $f$ of finite-type $k$-schemes, with no admissibility hypothesis; shifts $[a,b]\mapsto[a-2d,b-2d]$ for $f$ smooth of pure relative dimension $d$, $[a,b]\mapsto[a,b+2d+1]$ for a closed immersion into a target of dimension $\le d$ (a target-dimension bound; no codimension-only bound is asserted), and $[a,b]\mapsto[a-2D,b+2\dim Y+1]$ in general, $D$ the maximal embedding dimension of the affine charts ([thm-exc-explicit-preservation], [thm-sf-preservation-class], [thm-sf-ctf-stability] (v)) |
| $\mathbb D_X$ | $D(X)^{\mathrm{op}}\to D(X)$, $\RHom_X(-,\omega_X)$ | $\Dctf(X)\to\Dctf(X)$, a contravariant anti-equivalence, for every separated finite-type $X$ ([thm-sf-biduality-class], [thm-sf-ctf-stability] (vi)) |

The table is an enumeration: every entry is a theorem of the blueprint, and
the conditional entries are listed in [rem-sf-ledger].

attrs.title: Typing table: ambient definition, small-category theorem

objects.body:
An operation is introduced in this section *only on the ambient
categories of [def-sf-categories]*; no preservation property is built
into a definition. ``Descent'' of an operation to a small category means one
of two things, and both are theorems: for an operation already defined on the
ambient categories, the assertion that it carries the small subcategory into
the small subcategory, so that it *restricts* to a functor there; and for
the exceptional right adjoint, whose existence is itself a hypothesis, the
assertion that this restriction to the small subcategories is a functor at all.
Every such statement is enumerated operation by operation in
[rem-sf-typing] and proved in [thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility],
[thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], [thm-exc-explicit-preservation] and
[thm-sf-ctf-stability].
Consequently every functor below is written together with its source and
target categories.

attrs.title: The typing rule of this section

objects.body:
The point of the axiomatization is the following dictionary, each entry of
which is proved, as listed in the right-hand column, from
[def-sf-datum] and [def-sf-orientation] alone.

| classical statement | in the formalism | here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Verdier duality exchange $D_YRf_!\cong Rf_*D_X$ | (A1) $+$ (A3) | [thm-sf-verdier-exchange] |
| biduality $D_XD_X\cong\operatorname{id}$ | proved in the framework chapter, [thm-fix-general-biduality] | [def-sf-datum] |
| global duality $R\Gamma_c^\vee\cong R\Gamma\mathbb D_X$ | (A1) $+$ (A3) $+$ point | [thm-sf-global-duality] |
| trace–cup pairing perfect | the above $+$ orientation | [thm-sf-identification] |
| trace isomorphism $H_c^{2d}\cong\Lambda(-d)$ ($H^{2d}$ if proper) | the above $+$ connectedness | *The trace isomorphism* |
| Künneth / product formula | (A2) $+$ (A3) $+$ (A4) | [thm-sf-kunneth-relative] |
| dual base change $Rf^!Rg_*\cong Rg'_*Rf'^!$ | (A1) $+$ (A2) | [thm-sf-dual-base-change] |
| duality against pullback $D_XLf^*\cong Rf^!D_Y$ | (A1) $+$ (A3) $+$ (A6) | [cor-sf-duality-pullback] |
| dualizing complex of a product | (A4) $+$ orientation | *The dualizing complex of a product* |
| orientations are stable under products | the above $+$ (A3) | *The orientation is multiplicative* |
| relative trace, and its transitivity | (A1) $+$ (A4) | *The relative trace, and its transitivity* |
| coherence of the Künneth isomorphism | (A2) $+$ (A3) $+$ (A4) | [lem-sf-kunneth-coherence] |
| Poincaré duality for a smooth variety | all of the above | *Poincare duality, framework form* |

Two consequences of the dictionary are worth stating explicitly. First,
none of the formal core uses the orientation, so all duality statements
are theorems about the *dualizing complex* $Ra_X^!\Lambda$ rather than
about a twisted constant sheaf; only after substituting the orientation do
they become statements about $H^i(X,\Lambda)$ with the twist $(-d)$.
Second, the proof cycle recorded in the brief blueprint between the
six-operations package [thm-weil-six-operations] and the duality chapter disappears:
the exchange is a formal consequence of the axioms, not a geometric
theorem, so it may be used in [thm-weil-six-operations] without circularity.

attrs.title: The yoga: which classical theorem is which

objects.body:
The classical statements are also recorded, with proofs, in the Stacks
Project: the Lefschetz trace formula
([Tag 03TZ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03TZ)), the
section on Lefschetz numbers, global and local
([Tag 03TW](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03TW)), the trace
formula in the form for a finite type separated scheme of dimension at
most one over a finite field
(Theorem 64.16.1, [Tag 03UG](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03UG))
and its proof in Section 64.16
([Tag 03UF](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03UF)).
These give a second independent reference for the ingredients of
[thm-trf-lefschetz-verdier], [thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points]
and [thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar]. The pro-etale (rather
than etale) and the correspondence form used here is the project's
convention; the trace-class formalism is that of Milne, Lectures on
Etale Cohomology, Sections 24–29, and $SGA5$, Expose III.

Throughout this chapter, and in every statement below, the framework is
the *classical* one of the framework chapter: ordinary categories, ordinary
triangulated categories in the sense of Verdier, sets of morphisms,
exact functors, natural transformations, and 2-categorical (bicategorical)
arguments only. No $\infty$-category, no $\infty$-operad, no
model-independent ``coherent'' higher machinery is used or assumed. The
following conventions fix what this means for every phrase that could be
read either way.

1. *The derived categories.* $D^b_c(X,A)$, $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$,
$D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$, and their integral, rational, and
algebraically closed analogues are the classical Verdier derived
categories of the small
pro-etale site (or of the point), localized at quasi-isomorphisms, with
the coefficient constructions of the framework chapter. In particular
$D^b_c(X,A)$ is a triangulated category in the strict sense of
Verdier: the distinguished triangles, the shift functor, and the
octahedral axiom are given data, and there is *no* functorial choice
of mapping cone, no mapping-cone functor, and no model of the derived
category in which cones are strict. Consequently, all arguments below
that involve a distinguished triangle do it in one of two ways:
   1. the statement is about a *functor known to be exact and
triangulated* (e.g. $Lf^*$, $Rf_!$, $Rf^!$, $R\Gamma_c(X,-)$,
$L\bar x^*$), so that the image of a distinguished triangle is
distinguished and the image of a morphism of triangles is a morphism
of triangles, *because the interface records this* (the
exactness clauses of [prop-functor-package]); or
   1. the statement is proved at the level of *explicit bounded
complexes* with the Koszul convention of
[lem-trf-chain-supertrace], i.e. one chooses a representative
(possible because every object of $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$ is
represented by a bounded complex of finitely generated projective
$A$-modules), computes there, and shows the result to be a
quasi-isomorphism invariant.
1. *The six-functor package as a 2-categorical datum.* The
six operations, the exchange and projection transformations, the units
and counits of the adjunctions, the composition laws, the smooth-purity
and Verdier-biduality isomorphisms, and the coefficient-passage maps of
the framework chapter, the six-operations
package, are used in the following precise form: they are a datum
consisting of
   - for each $f:X\to Y$ (separated finite type, under the stated
admissibility), the exact functors $Lf^*$, $Rf_*$, $Rf_!$,
$Rf^!$ between the triangulated categories;
   - for each Cartesian square, the exchange transformations
$\operatorname{Ex}_*$, $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ and, for each
$L\in D^b_{ctf}$, the projection transformation
$\operatorname{PF}$ (the framework chapter,
[def-exchange-projection]), each a *natural* transformation
of exact functors;
   - for each composable pair, the composition isomorphisms
$Rg_!\circ Rf_!\cong R(gf)_!$ and their adjoint forms, with the
identity compatibilities and the associativity pentagon;
   - for each $f$, the unit $\eta_f:\operatorname{id}\to Rf^!Rf_!$ and the counit $\varepsilon_f:Rf_!Rf^!\to \operatorname{id}$ of the adjunction $Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$;
   - the compatibility laws connecting these: the base-change
cocycle over a composite of Cartesian squares (the ``outer square''
condition), the compatibility of the composition isomorphisms with
the exchanges, the projection-formula–exchange cocycles, and the
adjunction compatibility of the exchanges; each of these is a
*stated, enumerated law of the interface*, not a consequence of
coherence in a higher structure.
Whenever this chapter writes ``the canonical map'' or ``the canonical
isomorphism'', it means: a map or isomorphism *built from the
data above* by composition, whiskering, and (where an adjoint is
uniquely determined) the mate construction of
is not one of the enumerated laws, the coherence is either proved in
this chapter by an explicit model (e.g. the Koszul computations of
[lem-trf-chain-supertrace] and the split-exact-sequence
computation of [prop-trf-trace-formal-laws]) or proved from the
results of this manuscript with its classical source recorded as
provenance. The four statements that used to be recorded as
unresolved geometric interfaces are now discharged: the étale
exceptional pullback by *Exceptional pullback along an etale morphism*
(smooth purity of the manuscript), the triangle compatibility of the
trace class by [lem-trf-trace-triangle-compatibility] (reduced to
the point normalization [prop-trf-pairing-point-normalization]),
the normal-cone reduction by *Normal-cone reduction for the trace*
(from [thm-pur-dnc-invariance] and
*Normal-cone evaluation of the trace map*), and the normal-cone
evaluation of the contracting trace map by
*Normal-cone evaluation of the trace map* (from the dualizing
and Thom statements of the smooth-purity chapter and the contracting
reduction *Contracting local model at an isolated fixed point*); the contracting
computation *Trace map of a contracting correspondence* is proved from it.
All other steps of the
trace formula are proved inside this chapter: the
proper-pushforward interface by
[thm-trf-trace-proper-compatibility], the étale pullback
compatibility by *Etale pullback compatibility of trace maps*, the
additivity by [prop-trf-trace-class-additivity] and
*Additivity of the categorical traces of the global operators*, the fixed-point
localization by [thm-trf-fixed-point-localization] with the
diagonal case *Localization in the diagonal case*, and the
comparison [thm-trf-lefschetz-verdier].
1. *The trace and the duality data.* The categorical trace of
[def-trf-categorical-trace] is a 1-categorical construction: the
