strict symmetric monoidal structure on the model category of bounded
complexes of finitely generated projective modules is made explicit in
[lem-trf-chain-supertrace] (the Koszul braiding, the explicit
coevaluation and evaluation and the verification of the triangle
identities at the level of the model), and the trace is then the
composite of four *morphisms in the model category*, followed by
the identification $\operatorname{End}_{D(A)}(A)\cong A$. No
synthetic or higher-categorical trace is used.
1. *Classical bookkeeping of limits and idempotents.*
The adic passages of [def-trf-adic-system] and below use
*literal* compatible systems of bounded perfect complexes and
*literal* derived inverse limits in the classical sense (the
construction of the proper-base-change chapter,
[lem-weil-pbc-reconstruction-uniform-tower]), and the
$\Qlb$-coefficient category is the *classical*
filtered-colimit/common-stage category of the framework chapter with its
classical idempotent completion (the framework chapter,
[def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]; note that in the
classical triangulated setting the idempotent completion is taken in
the ordinary 1-categorical sense: an object together with
$e\in\operatorname{End}(P)$, $e^2=e$, and the resulting
Karoubian category, as in
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] of the framework chapter). The
compatibility of the trace with these operations is proved step by step
(in [prop-trf-adic-coefficient-morphism-systems] and
[thm-trf-integral-adic-coefficient-morphism-trace-formula]) from the explicit
levelwise formulas, never from a general ``limits commute with
functors'' statement in a higher category.
1. *Koszul sign convention.* In every explicit computation
with complexes, the conventions of
[lem-trf-chain-supertrace] are used: the differential of the
tensor product of complexes is
$d(p\otimes q)=dp\otimes q+(-1)^{|p|}p\otimes dq$, the braiding is
$c(p\otimes q)=(-1)^{|p||q|}q\otimes p$, and the internal-Hom and
duality data are the ones displayed there. These are the conventions
of the classical references for the trace-class formalism ($SGA5$,
Exposé III; Milne, *Lectures on Étale Cohomology*, Sections
24–29), which are also written in the classical triangulated framework.

The chapter extracts the two trace-formula inputs of the Weil-conjecture
proof, the fixed-point evaluation and the Lefschetz–Verdier trace
comparison, and decomposes them into the following chain. Throughout,
the framework is the classical 1-categorical one of
[rem-trf-classical-framework] (no $\infty$-categories): the
triangulated categories of the trace-formula chapter, the six-functor package as a
2-categorical datum with the enumerated coherence laws, and the
explicit-model computations of [lem-trf-chain-supertrace].

1. the framework convention and the coefficient conventions
([rem-trf-classical-framework],
[def-trf-strict-weil-complex], [def-trf-frobenius-operators]);
1. the categorical trace and its formal laws
([def-trf-categorical-trace], the explicit Koszul conventions and
computation of [lem-trf-chain-supertrace],
[prop-trf-trace-formal-laws]);
1. the correspondence formalism: [def-trf-correspondence] and
[def-trf-global-operator], the fixed scheme
[def-trf-fixed-scheme] in the Cartesian fixed square
[prop-trf-fixed-square-cartesian], the dualizing complex and Verdier
dual of [def-trf-dualizing-complex] with
[thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition] and
[thm-trf-verdier-biduality], and the internal-Hom/pullback and
fixed-square base changes ([thm-trf-internal-hom-pullback],
[thm-trf-fixed-point-base-change]); the naive single-leg
identification is explicitly rejected in the preceding discussion,
and only the displayed valid exchanges are used;
1. the trace class, integration, and local terms
([def-trf-trace-class], [def-trf-integration],
[def-trf-local-term]) built on the fixed-point evaluation
[thm-trf-verdier-duality], whose external-duality construction is
proved in this chapter from the Kunneth–Verdier chain, and the
etale-pullback, additivity and localization statements are now
theorems of this chapter; no retired
diagram labels are used. The proper-pushforward compatibility is
discharged by [thm-trf-trace-proper-compatibility]; the precise
inventory of what remains is [rem-trf-verdier-decomposition];
1. the trace-compatibility interfaces: the proper-pushforward
compatibility is proved as [thm-trf-trace-proper-compatibility]
(so the former interface [lem-trf-proper-pushforward-trace-class]
is retired), and the etale-pullback compatibility
*Etale pullback compatibility of trace maps* and the additivity
[prop-trf-trace-class-additivity] are proved; then the
fixed-point localization
[thm-trf-fixed-point-localization] and the assembly
[thm-trf-lefschetz-verdier] of the comparison; the fixed scheme of a
base-changed correspondence is [lem-trf-fixed-map-proper];
1. the Frobenius graph: [def-trf-graph-correspondence],
[prop-trf-graph-operator], the mate lemma
[lem-trf-adjoint-mate] used in
[prop-trf-graph-frobenius-operator], the fixed-point theorem
[thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points] (with the complete affine
computation and the transversality check) and the local-term formula
[thm-trf-frobenius-local-term];
1. the coefficient descent to the finite-ring, integral, rational and
algebraically closed statements
([thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-finite-ring],
[thm-trf-integral-adic-coefficient-morphism-trace-formula], [thm-trf-trace-formula-e],
[thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar]) and the point-counting
corollary [cor-trf-point-counting]; for an arbitrary, possibly
non-invertible, Weil map at the stage $E$ the descent passes through an
integral model with non-invertible Frobenius coefficient morphisms
([prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model]), their adic assembly
([prop-trf-adic-coefficient-morphism-systems]) and the integral
coefficient-morphism trace formula
[thm-trf-integral-adic-coefficient-morphism-trace-formula].

The chapter has no imported geometric input any more. The four
statements that were carried as classical inputs are now theorems of this
manuscript, each with its classical source recorded as provenance:

1. the exceptional pullback isomorphism for an étale morphism is
proved as *Exceptional pullback along an etale morphism* from the smooth purity
of the manuscript's smooth-purity chapter
([def-pur-smooth-purity-map], [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness])
and the composition laws of the six-operations package;
1. the additivity of the Verdier trace class along distinguished
triangles [lem-trf-trace-triangle-compatibility] is proved by
reducing it to the point normalization of the supported pairing
([prop-trf-pairing-point-normalization] of the trace-formula chapter) and the
triangle additivity of the categorical trace
([prop-trf-trace-formal-laws]); its classical source is SGA 5,
Exposé III, 4.2 and
[Varshavsky, Section 5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0505564);
1. the deformation-to-the-normal-cone reduction
*Normal-cone reduction for the trace* is proved from the
deformation invariance and the dualizing-object identification of the
smooth-purity chapter of this manuscript
([thm-pur-dnc-invariance], [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object])
together with the normal-cone evaluation and the contracting computation
(*Normal-cone evaluation of the trace map*,
*Trace map of a contracting correspondence*); its classical source is SGA 5,
Exposé III, 4.3–4.4 and Varshavsky 2.1.1;
1. the normal-cone evaluation of the trace map of a contracting
correspondence *Normal-cone evaluation of the trace map* is proved
from the contracting reduction *Contracting local model at an isolated fixed point*, the
point normalization [prop-trf-pairing-point-normalization], the Thom
and affine-line normalizations of the smooth-purity chapter
([thm-pur-rank-one-thom],
*Trace normalization of the affine-line purity*,
[lem-pur-lisse-uniqueness]) and the dualizing composition
[thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition]; its classical source is
Varshavsky, Theorem 2.1.2 with SGA 5, Exposé III, 4.3–4.4.

Everything else is proved in this chapter or quoted from the trace-formula chapter
(the six-functor package, Verdier biduality, and the base-change and
projection rules). In particular the proper-pushforward trace
identity is [thm-trf-trace-proper-compatibility], the étale
pullback identity is *Etale pullback compatibility of trace maps*, the
additivity is [prop-trf-trace-class-additivity], the fixed-point
localization is [thm-trf-fixed-point-localization], the
comparison is [thm-trf-lefschetz-verdier], and the four
coefficient-level trace formulas are
[thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-finite-ring],
[thm-trf-integral-adic-coefficient-morphism-trace-formula],
[thm-trf-trace-formula-e],
[thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar] with the corollary
[cor-trf-point-counting].

The proved internal-Hom comparison
[thm-trf-internal-hom-pullback] requires a site-perfect first
variable. The resulting computation
[thm-trf-fixed-point-evaluation-finite] gives the ordinary stalk
trace $\sigma_{h,K}$; for constant coefficients its value is $1$
by [cor-trf-constant-stalk-trace].

The geometric construction has a different input:
[thm-trf-verdier-duality] asks for external Verdier duality, and
[lem-trf-trace-map-from-external-duality] constructs the genuine
fixed-point trace conditionally on that comparison. The ordinary
tensor dual $K^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_A(K,A_X)$ and the Verdier dual
$D_XK=R\mathcal Hom_A(K,\omega_{X,A})$ of
[def-trf-dualizing-complex] have different targets. In particular,
$R\mathcal Hom_A(K,K)$ must not be identified with
$K\otimes_A^LD_XK$. No identification between $\sigma_{h,K}$
and a Verdier local term has been proved here.

attrs.title: Status of the fixed-point trace construction

objects.body:
The three clauses of [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility] separate
existence of an adjoint from constructible and finite-Tor preservation. The
comparison-class construction supplies the bounded instances used here; it
does not supply the unrestricted all-object datum of
[def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint]. Smooth preservation is the smooth
admissibility corollary; the finite-stage geometric assembly and its scope
are the preservation-class theorem. General Verdier biduality at finite
coefficients is a separate geometric theorem, proved by constructible
preservation, geometric generic restriction, and dimension induction. The
finite-stage boundary comparison is then a consequence. Integral duality and
the constructible exceptional adjunction, and their field transports, are
stated in the coefficient chapter. These results concern the specified
constructible categories; the unrestricted unbounded ambient adjoint remains
a separate assertion.

The open-immersion and finite-etale cases, including uniform coefficient
comparison, are proved without admissibility; the finite closed subset of a
smooth curve is treated separately, as are the independent closed-support
construction and its site comparison. The necessary direct-image bounds for
the closed-support step are made explicit there; the general geometric
verification is not supplied by calling a morphism admissible. In particular,
the upper shift $c_f^+$ cannot be omitted: an explicit computation exhibits
positive cohomological degrees.

attrs.title: Existence, preservation and geometric duality are separate

objects.body:
The finite-stage geometric gap is closed. Constructible preservation
is proved independently in [lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata];
the generic restriction comparisons of
[lem-weil-geometric-generic-exchange] justify the dimension
induction in [thm-weil-etale-geometric-biduality].
The etale–pro-etale comparison
[lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison] gives the finite-stage
theorem [thm-fix-general-biduality]. Boundary exchange is the
subsequent consequence [cor-weil-boundary-duality-discharge],
and general finite-stage internal-Hom preservation is
[cor-weil-finite-constructible-hom].

These geometric statements concern $A_{E,n}$. The following sections
prove the required coefficient comparisons: [cor-coef-finite-verdier]
normalizes the finite duals; [thm-coef-integral-verdier] reconstructs
integral duality; [thm-coef-rational-verdier], [thm-coef-qbar-verdier]
give the field stages. The point calculation
[lem-weil-coefficient-frobenius] remains an algebraic ingredient,
while those sections supply the geometric coefficient passage.

For $R=\mathcal O_E$ and $T=R/\varpi_E R$, ordinary duality gives
$T^*=0$, whereas the resolution
$0\to R\xrightarrow{\varpi_E}R\to T\to0$ gives

$$
R\operatorname{Hom}_R(T,R)\cong T[-1],\qquad
R\operatorname{Hom}_R\bigl(R\operatorname{Hom}_R(T,R),R\bigr)\cong T.
$$

These identifications use the chosen uniformizer; the derived evaluation
is canonical and is an isomorphism by
[lem-weil-coefficient-frobenius]. Computing two ordinary Hom modules
over a non-self-injective ring does not compute two derived Homs.

For the bounded constructible finite-Tor category of
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], the algebraic point case
uses perfect derived biduality and does not need a quasi-Frobenius ring.
Self-injectivity of $A_{E,n}$ also provides ordinary duality for finite
modules that need not have finite Tor dimension; this distinction is
relevant to the stronger bounded constructible category without the
finite-Tor condition. Neither algebraic assertion alone proves geometric
Verdier biduality across the boundary of a stratum: restriction along a
closed immersion cannot be treated as restriction along an open immersion.

The strict henselian local scheme $V_{(\bar v)}$ has the property that a
finite $V$-scheme becomes a finite disjoint union of finite local schemes
after base change to $V_{(\bar v)}$. Sections of $F$ over that disjoint union
are products of the sections over the components. Passing through the
cofiltered system of etale neighbourhoods of $\bar v$ identifies the stalk
with the displayed product. Finiteness of the fibre makes product and sum
equal in the abelian category, so for an abelian sheaf the stalk of $h_*F$ is
canonically the finite direct sum of the stalks of $F$ as well. This is the stalk
calculation located at Stacks Proposition 59.55.2, Tag `03QP`; no exactness is
inferred until the next lemma.

attrs.title: The classical argument, which is not the one formalised

objects.body:
*Where this feeds.* This layer is the last one of the blueprint: its
inputs are the trace formula, Poincaré duality and the weight estimate, and
its output is the five statements [thm-weil-final-rationality]–[thm-weil-final-functional-equation]. In the
compiled blueprint the layer is carried by
`16_zeta_linear_algebra.tex` (the linear algebra:
`def-zl-frobenius-trace-series`,
`lem-zl-log-det-identity`,
`lem-zl-euler-product-identity`,
`thm-zl-lefschetz-weil-identity`,
`thm-weil-final-functional-equation`,
`sk-thm-rh`) and by
`18_final_weil_statements.tex` (the assembly:
`prop-every-iterate-trace`, `prop-trace-determinant`,
`prop-euler-product`, `prop-weil-rationality-criterion`,
`prop-rational-descent`, `prop-weight-purity-roots`,
`prop-weight-separation`, `prop-duality-reciprocity`,
`prop-functional-equation`, `prop-weil-betti-comparison`,
`thm-weil-realization-independence`,
`thm-weil-final-rationality`, `thm-weil-final-integrality`,
`thm-weil-final-rh`, `thm-weil-final-betti`,
`thm-weil-final-functional-equation`).

*The one structural point.* The coefficients of $Z$ are integral
*by the Euler product* ([prop-euler-product]; the exponential definition
alone only gives rational coefficients), while
the factorization is $\ell$-adic *by construction* (one chosen $\ell$,
[prop-trace-determinant]). The two meet exactly twice: in the
rationality descent of [prop-rational-descent], where integrality of the
coefficients propagates the Hankel rank bound from $\Ql$ to $\Q$, and in the
realization-independence of [prop-integral-recovery], where integrality of the
coefficients enters once more through Fatou's lemma, which produces the
integral presentation $Z=A/B$ and with it the integrality of the reciprocal
roots. Every step that may split
into very many statements is marked qualitatively above.

It is tempting to prove [prop-openclosed-lowerstar-fully-faithful] by
showing that the base-change functor $\et X\to\et Z$ exhibits $\et Z$ as a
dense subsite, so that pushforward along it is fully faithful for formal
reasons. The functor is indeed cover-dense — that is exactly
[lemma-openclosed-etale-lifts-locally] — but it is neither locally full
nor locally faithful, so the dense-subsite criterion does not apply. The
failure is real and not a matter of bookkeeping: two morphisms $V\to V'$ of
schemes étale over $X$ that agree after base change to $Z$ need only agree
on an open subscheme of $V$ containing the preimage of $Z$, and such an open
subscheme is not in general a covering of $V$. The route taken below
replaces the formal argument by the stalk computation
[lemma-openclosed-stalk-lowerstar], where exactly this open subscheme is
allowed to shrink, because a stalk is a colimit over neighbourhoods.

Schemes live in a universe $u$ and the coefficient category $\mathcal A$ is
large relative to it: $\mathcal A$ has morphisms in $\mathrm{Type}\,(u+1)$
and is concrete over $\mathrm{Type}\,(u+1)$, so that the forgetful functor
reflects isomorphisms and preserves filtered colimits at that universe. The
same concreteness is also what makes the second hypothesis on $\mathcal A$,
namely sheafification of $\mathcal A$-valued presheaves on the small étale
sites (`CategoryTheory.HasSmallSiteSheafify`, carried by every statement
involving $f^*$ or $j_!$), available in Lean: it implies it through Mathlib's
plus construction. The two are not the same hypothesis — sheafification is
the weaker one, and holds for every Grothendieck abelian $\mathcal A$ of size
$u+1$. For $\mathcal A=\mathrm{Mod}_\Lambda$ both are inferred. The geometric points of $\et X$, on the
other hand, have fibres in $\mathrm{Type}\,u$. These two universes do not
meet, and the standard conservativity statement for a family of points is
stated at a single universe.
[lemma-openclosed-point-ulift] is what repairs the mismatch; every
stalk argument in this section is understood to take place after that
repair. The concreteness hypotheses on $\mathcal A$ — those coming from
stalks, as opposed to the sheafification hypothesis carried throughout — are
therefore carried by [prop-openclosed-lowerstar-fully-faithful]. This is
expected rather than a defect: conservativity is a statement about
stalks, and stalks are sets.

The frozen draft represented a local section by a section on
$V_i\times_{Y'}Y$. The square only supplies $g:Y'\to Y$, not a map
$Y\to Y'$, so that fibre product is not defined. The categorical
unit–Cartesian-identification–counit construction above is the replacement
used throughout this extraction. The removed historical block has SHA-256
`E982FFC21CEAF8ABCD945A58DDFADBA4EB898F882D56A00A70BAC9F6365679A0` and is not a proof input.

attrs.title: Erratum to the historical sectionwise presentation

objects.body:
In a base-change square with $f$
smooth and $g$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and for
$E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite with ring of integers $\mathcal O_E$ and
uniformizer $\varpi$, an
*integral lattice* for $K_E\in\Dbc(T,E)$ is an object
$L\in\Dbc(T_{\Proet},\mathcal O_E)$ together with an isomorphism

$$
L[\varpi^{-1}]\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }K_E
\quad\text{in }\Dbc(T,E).
$$

(The equivalence of this presentation with the classical presentation
by pairs $(L,e)$ with $e^2=e$ in the Karoubi envelope of the
rationalized category is the corresponding statement below.) The lattice is
*finite-level etale admissible* if each reduction
$L_n=L\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_n$ lies in the essential image of
$\Dbc(T_{\Et},A_n)$; it is *square-constructibly admissible* if in
addition the finite-level systems
$Rg_{n,*}L_n$, $Lf_n^*Rg_{n,*}L_n$, $Le_n^*L_n$,
$Rh_{n,*}Le_n^*L_n$ are constructible in one common finite
cohomological interval.

For a base-change square and
$K\in D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$, the *derived base-change map* is the
morphism

$$
{\operatorname{BC}}_{f,g}(K):Lf^*Rg_*K
\longrightarrow Rh_*Le^*K
$$

of $D(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ defined as the composite

$$
\begin{array}{l}
Lf^*Rg_*K\xrightarrow{\;\eta_e\;}
Lf^*Rg_*Re_*Le^*K
\;\cong\;Lf^*R(ge)_*Le^*K
\;\cong\;Lf^*Rf_*Rh_*Le^*K\\
\hphantom{Lf^*Rg_*K\xrightarrow{\;\eta_e\;}}
\xrightarrow{\;\varepsilon_f\;}
Rh_*Le^*K,
\end{array}
$$

where $\eta_e$ is the unit of the adjunction
$Le^*\dashv Re_*$, where $ge=fh$ gives the two canonical
identifications of the composite functors, and where
$\varepsilon_f$ is the counit of $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$; it is
the derived exchange morphism of
[def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] read on the same
square with the vertical and horizontal sides exchanged. Its
naturality in $K$ is the corresponding statement below, and its
compatibility with the composition of squares and with base change
along the square is the corresponding statement below and
the corresponding statement below.
For $F\in\Ab(T_{\Et})$, the *base-change map in degree $q$* is
the $q$-th cohomology sheaf of $\operatorname{BC}_{f,g}$ applied to
$F$ (placed in degree zero):

$$
{\operatorname{BC}}^q_{f,g}(F):=H^q\bigl(\operatorname{BC}_{f,g}(F)\bigr)
:f^{-1}R^qg_*F
\longrightarrow R^qh_*e^{-1}F,
$$

the identifications of the two sides following from the exactness of
$f^{-1}$ and of $e^{-1}$ on sheaves and from the definitions of the
higher direct images of
[def-weil-pbc-direct-image]; in degree $q=0$ this is the
sheaf-level base-change map obtained by the composition

$$
h^{-1}f^{-1}g_*F\xrightarrow{\theta_\square}
e^{-1}g^{-1}g_*F\xrightarrow{e^{-1}\varepsilon_g}e^{-1}F
$$

(valid for $q=0$ because the counit
$\varepsilon_g:g^{-1}g_*\to\operatorname{id}$ is a morphism of
functors on sheaves on $T_{\Et}$), transposed under
$h^{-1}\dashv h_*$.

Let $f:X\to S$ be a
morphism of schemes (conventions of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]),
let $n\geq1$ be an integer invertible on $S$, let $q\geq0$, and put
$\Lambda=\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$ (a coefficient ring as in
[sbc-def-coefficient-conventions]).
We say that *$BC(f,n,q)$ holds*, or that *the recorded
base-change property holds for $f$, $n$ and $q$*, if for every
base-change square of
[sbc-def-base-change-square] whose horizontal side $g:T\to S$ is
quasi-compact and
quasi-separated, and every abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $T_{\Et}$
annihilated by $n$ (that is, every sheaf of
$\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$-modules on $T_{\Et}$), the base-change map
of [sbc-def-base-change-map] in degree $q$,

$$
\operatorname{BC}^q_{f,g}(\mathcal F):
f^{-1}R^qg_*\mathcal F\longrightarrow R^qh_*e^{-1}\mathcal F,
$$

is an isomorphism. This is a condition in the single degree $q$ only;
the cumulative form used in the induction on $q$ is
"$BC(f,n,q')$ for all $q'\leq q$", which says that the derived
base-change map $\operatorname{BC}_{f,g}(\mathcal F)$ of
[sbc-def-base-change-map] is an isomorphism on $q'$-th cohomology
sheaves for all $q'\leq q$. We say that *$BC(f,n,q)$ holds
universally* if $BC(f',n,q)$ holds for every base change
$f':X'=X\times_SS'\to S'$ of $f$ along every morphism of schemes
$S'\to S$ (here $n$ is invertible on $S'$ because it is invertible on
$S$); this is the form in which the property is used, since the
arguments below apply it to base changes of $f$, and to horizontal
sides $T\to S'$ whose composite with $S'\to S$ need not be
quasi-compact and quasi-separated. We write $\mathrm{UBC}^{\le q}(f,n)$
for the cumulative universal property "$BC(f,n,q')$ holds universally
for all $q'\leq q$"; it is the property $BC(f,n,q)$ of the Stacks
Project, Tag 0F02, and it is the hypothesis of the reduction lemmas of
this chapter. The fixed-base property does not imply the universal one:
there are flat, finitely presented $f$ with geometrically connected
fibres for which $BC(f,n,0)$ holds but $BC(f_{\mathbf A^1_S},n,0)$
fails, so the quantifier over $S'\to S$ cannot be dropped from the
hypotheses. The smooth-base-change theorem of
this chapter is the assertion $BC(f,n,q)$ for every $q$ and every
smooth $f$; since smoothness is stable under base change, it gives
$BC(f,n,q)$ universally for every smooth $f$ and every $q$.

A *base-change square* is a diagram of schemes

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X & \xleftarrow{\;h\;} & Y\\
f\big\downarrow & & \big\downarrow e\\
S & \xleftarrow{\;g\;} & T
\end{array}
\qquad (Y=X\times_S T)
$$

together with the chosen Cartesian identification
$Y\cong X\times_ST$ of
the Cartesian square of
the proper-base-change chapter, so that $f\circ h=g\circ e$; here $f:X\to S$ and
$g:T\to S$ are the two morphisms to the base $S$ (the vertical and the
horizontal side, respectively), and $h:Y\to X$, $e:Y\to T$ the
projections. The chosen identification gives the canonical isomorphism

$$
\theta_\square:h^{-1}f^{-1}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }e^{-1}g^{-1}
$$

of inverse-image functors, compatible with identity and pasted
squares, as in [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square].

Fix a positive integer $N$ and a finite commutative ring $\Lambda$
annihilated by $N$; throughout, schemes carrying coefficients are
schemes on which $N$ is invertible. The categories
$\operatorname{Mod}(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ of $\Lambda_T$-modules, the
sheaf-theoretic notions (torsion, lisse, constructible), and the
ambient derived categories
$D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$, $\Dplus(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ with their K-injective
resolutions are the ones of
[def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves],
[def-weil-pbc-derived-categories],
[def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions] and
[def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] of the ambient-foundations chapter; the
bounded constructible category is written $\Dbc(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ as
there.

Let $\mathcal P$ be a set of primes. Write

$$
D^b_{\mathcal P\text{-tor}}(T_{\Et}),\qquad
D^+_{\mathcal P\text{-tor}}(T_{\Et})
$$

for the full triangulated subcategories of the derived category of
abelian etale sheaves on $T$ consisting respectively of bounded and
bounded-below complexes $K$ such that every geometric stalk of every
$H^q(K)$ is a torsion group whose prime divisors belong to $\mathcal P$.

For every scheme $S$ and every $n\geq0$, the projection
$\mathbf A^n_S\to S$ of [def-sbc-affine-space] is
smooth of
relative dimension $n$.
(*Stacks Project: the ring map $R\to R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ is standard
smooth,
[Algebra, Definition
10.137.5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00T6) and
[Lemma 10.137.6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00T7), so
the projection is smooth in the sense of
[Definition 29.35.1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01V5),
hence also in the sense of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] by
[Lemma 37.11.7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02H6); and
$\Omega_{\mathbf A^n_S/S}$ is finite locally free of rank $n$, which by
[Lemma 29.35.12](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02G1) is
$\dim_x(\mathbf A^n_{\kappa(f(x))})$ at every point $x$, so that the
projection has relative dimension $n$ in the sense of
[def-sbc-smooth-morphisms].*)

## Proof

This is the recorded classical input named in the statement: the polynomial ring is standard smooth over the base (Stacks Project, Algebra, Definition 10.137.5 and Lemma 10.137.6, [Tag 00T6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00T6), [Tag 00T7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00T7)), the two notions of smoothness agree (Lemma 37.11.7, [Tag 02H6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02H6)), and the module of differentials is finite locally free of rank n, which by Lemma 29.35.12 ([Tag 02G1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02G1)) computes the relative dimension. No separate proof is given.

Consider a tower of Cartesian diagrams of schemes

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
W & \xrightarrow{j} & Z\\
i\big\downarrow & & \big\downarrow k\\
X & \xrightarrow{h} & Y\\
f\big\downarrow & & \big\downarrow e\\
S & \xrightarrow{g} & T
\end{array}
$$

and let $K\in D(T_{\Et})$. If

$$
f^{-1}Rg_*K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rh_*e^{-1}K
\quad\text{and}\quad
i^{-1}Rh_*e^{-1}K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rj_*k^{-1}e^{-1}K
$$

are isomorphisms, then
$(f\circ i)^{-1}Rg_*K\to Rj_*(e\circ k)^{-1}K$ is an isomorphism
(``the outer rectangle'') and the analogous statement holds
degreewise for an abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $T_{\Et}$ and the maps
$R^q$.
(*Stacks Project, Lemma 59.86.2, [Tag `0EZS`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EZS).*)

## Proof

The composites of the two base-change maps of
[sbc-def-base-change-map] are the mates of the same composite of
the identification isomorphisms $\theta_\square$ of the two pasted
squares; the associativity and triangle identities for the
inverse-image–direct-image adjunctions (the identity and pasting laws
recorded in [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-identity-pasting], applied with
the roles of the vertical and horizontal sides interchanged) show that
this mate is exactly the base-change map of the outer rectangle, so the
composite of the two isomorphisms is the required isomorphism.

attrs.title: Base change for a composite square

objects.body:
With $f:X\to S$ and $n$ as in [sbc-def-base-change-property] assume for
some $q\geq1$ that $\mathrm{BC}(f,n,q')$ holds universally for all
$q'\leq q-1$, but $\mathrm{BC}(f,n,q)$ does not hold universally. Then there exist a commutative diagram

$$
\begin{array}{ccccc}
X & \longleftarrow & X' & \longleftarrow & Y\\
f\big\downarrow & & \big\downarrow f' & & \big\downarrow e\\
S & \longleftarrow & S' & \longleftarrow & \operatorname{Spec}K
\end{array}
$$

where $X'=X\times_SS'$, $Y=X'\times_{S'}\operatorname{Spec}K$, $S'$ is
an affine scheme, $K$ is a
field, and $\mathcal F$ is an abelian sheaf on
$\operatorname{Spec}K$ annihilated by $n$ such that

$$
f'^{-1}R^qg_*\mathcal F\longrightarrow R^qh_*e^{-1}\mathcal F
$$

is not an isomorphism. If $S$ is separated, then moreover
$S'\to S$ is an affine morphism.
(*Stacks Project, Lemma 59.88.6, [Tag `0F07`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F07).*)

## Proof

Choose a counterexample, i.e. a morphism $S'\to S$ with base change
$f':X'=X\times_SS'\to S'$ for which $\mathrm{BC}(f',n,q)$ fails: a
quasi-compact quasi-separated $g:T\to S'$ with $Y=X'\times_{S'}T$ and
$\mathcal F$ annihilated by $n$ such that the map of
[sbc-def-base-change-map] is not an isomorphism. Being an isomorphism
is local on $X'$, and for an open $U\subset S'$ the formation of
$R^qg_*$, $R^qh_*$ and of the base-change map commutes with
restriction to $U$, $X'_U$ (restriction to an open is the pullback
along an etale morphism and the higher direct images are the
sheafified cohomology presheaves); so the map already fails to be an
isomorphism over some affine open $U\subset S'$ and we may replace
$S'$ by $U$, $T$ by $T\times_{S'}U$. Thus $S'$ is affine, and $T$,
being quasi-compact and quasi-separated over the affine $S'$, is
quasi-compact and quasi-separated. By
[sbc-lem-bc-injectivity] (for the base change $f'$ along $g$) the map
is injective, so there is a
geometric point $\bar x$ of $X'$ and an element $\xi$ of
$(R^qh_*e^{-1}\mathcal F)_{\bar x}$ not in the image of
$(f'^{-1}R^qg_*\mathcal F)_{\bar x}$. For a morphism
$\pi:T'\to T$ let $\mathcal F'=\pi^{-1}\mathcal F$ and define
$P(T')$ to be the property: the image $\xi'$ of $\xi$ in
$(R^qh'_*(e')^{-1}\mathcal F')_{\bar x}$ is not in the image of
$(f'^{-1}R^qg'_*\mathcal F')_{\bar x}$. We apply
[sbc-lem-bc-minimal-counterexample] to $P$.

- *(1) Thickenings.* By [sbc-lem-thickening-etale-site]
the etale site of a scheme and of a thickening of it are the
same, so the cohomology sheaves involved are unchanged and
$P(T'')$ iff $P(T')$.
- *(2) Limits.* For $T'=\varprojlim T_i$ with affine
transitions, $\mathcal F'$ is the colimit of the pullbacks of
$\mathcal F_i$, and
[sbc-lem-higher-direct-image-limit] gives
$\varinjlim R^qh'_{i,*}e_i^{-1}\mathcal F_i =R^qh'_*e'^{-1}\mathcal F'$ and the analogue for
$g'$-side; hence $P(T_i)$ for all $i$ implies $P(T')$.
- *(3) Closed–open split.* Let $T'$ be with $P(T')$ and
$Z\subset T'$ closed with quasi-compact complement $V$. Choose an
injection $j^{-1}\mathcal F'\to\mathcal J$ with $\mathcal J$ an
injective sheaf of $\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$-modules on $V$, where
$j:V\hookrightarrow T'$; then
$\mathcal F'\to j_*\mathcal J\oplus i_*i^{-1}\mathcal F'$ is
injective (check on stalks, with $i:Z\hookrightarrow T'$ the closed
immersion), so by
[sbc-lem-bc-injectivity] (2), for the base change $f'$ along
$g':T'\to S'$ (quasi-compact and quasi-separated since $T'$ is and $S'$
is affine), the image of $\xi'$ is nonzero in
the direct-sum cokernel for
$\mathcal G=j_*\mathcal J\oplus i_*i^{-1}\mathcal F'$. If it is
nonzero in the second summand, then, since
$i_*$ (also $i'_*$) is exact for closed immersions,
$R^qg'_*i_*i^{-1}\mathcal F'=R^q(g'\circ i)_*i^{-1}\mathcal F'$
and $R^qh'_*e'^{-1}i_*i^{-1}\mathcal F'=R^qh''_*e_Z^{-1} i^{-1}\mathcal F'$ (Grothendieck spectral sequence), so
$P(Z)$ holds. If it is nonzero in the first summand, then
applying, for every $a\leq q-1$, the property
$\mathrm{BC}(e',n,a)$ of the base change $e':Y'=X'\times_{S'}T'\to T'$
of $f$ (along $T'\to S'\to S$) to the square with horizontal side the
open immersion $j:V\to T'$ (quasi-compact as $V$ is quasi-compact and
$T'$ quasi-separated, and separated) (this is where the universal
cumulative hypothesis in all degrees $\leq q-1$ is used) gives
$e'^{-1}j_*\mathcal J=j'_*e_V^{-1}\mathcal J$ (degree $a=0$) and,
together with $R^aj_*\mathcal J=0$ for $a\geq1$ ($\mathcal J$ being
injective), the vanishing of the higher direct images
$R^aj'_*e_V^{-1}\mathcal J$ for $a=1,\dots,q-1$; the
relative Leray spectral sequence for $h'\circ j'$ shows
$$
R^qh'_*e'^{-1}j_*\mathcal J\longrightarrow
R^q(h'\circ j')_*e_V^{-1}\mathcal J
$$
is injective, and applying
[sbc-lem-bc-injectivity] (3), for the base change $f'$ along
$g'\circ j:V\to S'$, to
$j^{-1}\mathcal F'\subset\mathcal J$ gives $P(V)$.
- *(4) Empty scheme.* If $T'=\emptyset$ then $Y'=X'\times_{S'}T'=\emptyset$,
so $R^qh'_*(e')^{-1}\mathcal F'=0$; hence $\xi'=0$ lies in the image and
$P(\emptyset)$ fails.

By [sbc-lem-bc-minimal-counterexample], $P(\operatorname{Spec}K)$
holds for some field $K$ with a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}K\to T\to S'$,
which is the assertion, with $S'$ the affine scheme chosen at the start.
Finally, let $S$ be separated. Then the diagonal $S\to S\times S$ is a
closed immersion, hence affine, and any morphism from an affine
scheme to $S$ is affine: for $V\subset S$ affine open,
$S'\times_SV=(S'\times V)\times_{S\times S}S$ is affine over the affine
scheme $S'\times V$, hence affine; so $S'\to S$ is affine.

attrs.title: A failure is detected on the generic fibre

objects.body:
With $f:X\to S$ and $n$ as in [sbc-def-base-change-property], assume for
some $q\geq1$ that $\mathrm{BC}(f,n,q-1)$ holds universally (in the
single degree $q-1$; no hypothesis in the degrees $<q-1$ is needed).
Let $S'\to S$ be a morphism, $f':X'=X\times_SS'\to S'$ the base change,
$g:T\to S'$ a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism, and
$h:Y=X'\times_{S'}T\to X'$, $e:Y\to T$ the projections. Then for
every abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $T_{\Et}$ annihilated by $n$:

1. the base-change map
$f'^{-1}R^qg_*\mathcal F\to R^qh_*e^{-1}\mathcal F$ is
injective;
1. if $\mathcal F\subset\mathcal G$ with $\mathcal G$ annihilated by
$n$, then
$$
\operatorname{Coker}\bigl(f'^{-1}R^qg_*\mathcal F\to
R^qh_*e^{-1}\mathcal F\bigr)
\subset\operatorname{Coker}\bigl(f'^{-1}R^qg_*\mathcal G\to
R^qh_*e^{-1}\mathcal G\bigr);
$$
1. if in (2) the sheaf $\mathcal G$ is an injective sheaf of
$\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$-modules, then
$$
\operatorname{Coker}\bigl(f'^{-1}R^qg_*\mathcal F\to
R^qh_*e^{-1}\mathcal F\bigr)
\subset R^qh_*e^{-1}\mathcal G.
$$

(*Stacks Project, Lemma 59.88.2, [Tag `0F03`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F03).*)

## Proof

Choose a short exact sequence
$0\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal I\to\mathcal Q\to0$ with $\mathcal I$ an
injective sheaf of $\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$-modules on $T_{\Et}$. The
injective-acyclicity input of [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity]
(using the adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]) gives
$R^qg_*\mathcal I=0$ for $q>0$, so the two long exact sequences of
higher direct images of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] (in the
derived categories of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], the
distinguished triangle of the short exact sequence) and the naturality
of the base-change maps of [sbc-def-base-change-map] ([sbc-lem-bc-naturality]) give the
diagram with exact rows of the statement: the long exact sequences are
the ones of [lemma-weil-pbc-five-lemma-transfer]; the left two
vertical arrows are the degree-$(q-1)$ base-change maps for
$\mathcal I$ and $\mathcal Q$ for the base change $f'$ along $g$, hence
isomorphisms by $\mathrm{BC}(f',n,q-1)$, which is part of the
hypothesis that $\mathrm{BC}(f,n,q-1)$ holds universally (only this
single degree enters), the top
right entry $f'^{-1}R^qg_*\mathcal I$ is zero, hence the middle vertical arrow is injective,
which is (1), and the same diagram gives the inclusion of the cokernel
into $R^qh_*e^{-1}\mathcal I$, which is (3); for (2), with
$\mathcal F\subset\mathcal G\subset\mathcal I$, the same diagram
applied to $\mathcal F\subset\mathcal G$ gives the inclusion of the
cokernels.

attrs.title: Injectivity of the critical map and its cokernel

objects.body:
With $f:X\to S$ and $n$ as in [sbc-def-base-change-property] and some
$q\geq1$ (no base-change hypothesis on $f$ is needed here), consider
commutative
diagrams

$$
\begin{array}{ccccccc}
X & \xleftarrow{\;\;} & X' & \xleftarrow{\pi'} & X'' & &
Y\\
f\big\downarrow & & \big\downarrow f' & & \big\downarrow f'' & &
\big\downarrow e\\
S & \xleftarrow{\;\;} & S' & \xleftarrow{\;\pi\;} & S'' & &
T
\end{array}
$$

and the diagram with the outer
$h=h'\circ\pi''$, $g=g'\circ\pi$ (as horizontal composites), all squares
Cartesian, $g'$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and $\pi$ integral.
Let $\mathcal F$ be an abelian sheaf on $T_{\Et}$ annihilated by $n$.
If

$$
f'^{-1}R^qg_*\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }R^qh_*e^{-1}\mathcal F
$$

is an isomorphism, then
$f''^{-1}R^qg'_*\mathcal F\to R^qh'_*e^{-1}\mathcal F$ is an
isomorphism.
(*Stacks Project, Lemma 59.88.4, [Tag `0F05`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F05).*)

## Proof

Since $\pi$ and $\pi'$ are integral, $\pi_*$ and $\pi'_*$ are exact
by [sbc-lem-integral-etale-direct-image-exact] (finite case
[lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact]) and
$(f')^{-1}\pi_*=\pi'_*(f'')^{-1}$, so
$\pi'_*(f'')^{-1}R^qg'_*\mathcal F=(f')^{-1}R^qg_*\mathcal F$ and
$\pi'_*R^qh'_*e^{-1}\mathcal F=R^qh_*e^{-1}\mathcal F$; hence the
assumption says that the map for $f''$ becomes an isomorphism after
$\pi'_*$. It remains to see that the exact functor $\pi'_*$ is conservative;
apply it to the kernel and cokernel $\mathcal C$ of that map, so
$\pi'_*\mathcal C=0$. Let $\bar x''$ be a geometric point of $X''$ and
$\bar x'$ its image. The stalk $(\pi'_*\mathcal C)_{\bar x'}$ is
$\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}B,\mathcal C)$ with
$B$ the ring of
$X''\times_{X'}\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{X',\bar x'}$ over an
affine neighbourhood, an integral algebra over the strictly henselian ring
$A=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{X',\bar x'}$. Write $B=\operatorname{colim}B_\lambda$
with $B_\lambda$ finite over $A$; each $B_\lambda$ is a finite product of
strictly henselian local rings, so sections over $\operatorname{Spec}B_\lambda$
are the product of the stalks at their closed points, and the stalk
$\mathcal C_{\bar x''}$ is the colimit of the factors through which
$\bar x''$ passes. Hence $\mathcal C_{\bar x''}$ is a quotient of
$(\pi'_*\mathcal C)_{\bar x'}=0$, so $\mathcal C=0$. No surjectivity of
$\pi$ is needed, and the map for $f''$ is an isomorphism.

attrs.title: Integral base change on the source

objects.body:
With $f:X\to S$ and $n$ as in [sbc-def-base-change-property] assume for
some $q\geq1$ that $\mathrm{BC}(f,n,q-1)$ holds universally (in the
single degree $q-1$, which is all that [sbc-lem-bc-injectivity]
needs).
Consider commutative
diagrams

$$
\begin{array}{ccccccc}
X & \xleftarrow{\;\;} & X' & \xleftarrow{\;\;} & Y & \xleftarrow{\pi'} & Y'\\
f\big\downarrow & & \big\downarrow f' & & \big\downarrow e & &
\big\downarrow e'\\
S & \xleftarrow{\;\;} & S' & \xleftarrow{\;\;} & T
\xleftarrow{\;\pi\;} & T' &
\end{array}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\begin{array}{ccccc}
X' & &\xrightarrow{h'=h\circ\pi'}& &Y'\\
f'\big\downarrow & & & & \big\downarrow e'\\
S' & &\xrightarrow{g'=g\circ\pi}& &T'
\end{array}
$$

where all squares are Cartesian, $g$ is quasi-compact and
quasi-separated, and $\pi:T'\to T$ is integral surjective. Let
$\mathcal F$ be an abelian sheaf on $T_{\Et}$ annihilated by $n$ and set
$\mathcal F'=\pi^{-1}\mathcal F$. If

$$
f'^{-1}R^qg'_*\mathcal F'\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
R^qh'_*(e')^{-1}\mathcal F'
$$

is an isomorphism, then
$f'^{-1}R^qg_*\mathcal F\to R^qh_*e^{-1}\mathcal F$ is an isomorphism.
(*Stacks Project, Lemma 59.88.3, [Tag `0F04`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F04).*)

## Proof

The maps $\mathcal F\to\pi_*\pi^{-1}\mathcal F$ are injective as $\pi$
is surjective, so by [sbc-lem-bc-injectivity] (2), applied to the base
change $f'$ of $f$ along $S'\to S$ and the quasi-compact
quasi-separated $g:T\to S'$, the task reduces to
showing the base-change map for $\pi_*\mathcal F'$ is an isomorphism.
For an integral morphism $\pi$ the direct image is exact by
[sbc-lem-integral-etale-direct-image-exact] (the finite case being
the one noted in [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact]),
$R^qg_*\pi_*\mathcal F'=R^qg'_*\mathcal F'$ by the Grothendieck
spectral sequence for the composite, the Cartesian identification gives
$e^{-1}\pi_*\mathcal F'=\pi'_*(e')^{-1}\mathcal F'$, and
$R^qh_*\pi'_*(e')^{-1}\mathcal F'=R^qh'_*(e')^{-1}\mathcal F'$ by that
spectral sequence; the assumption on $\mathcal F'$ then gives the
isomorphism for $\pi_*\mathcal F'$, hence for $\mathcal F$ by the
five-lemma transfer of [lemma-weil-pbc-five-lemma-transfer].

attrs.title: Integral surjective base change on the target

objects.body:
Let $T$ be a
quasi-compact and
quasi-separated scheme and let $P$ be a property for quasi-compact
quasi-separated schemes over $T$. Assume:

1. if $T''\to T'$ is a thickening of quasi-compact quasi-separated
schemes over $T$, then $P(T'')$ if and only if $P(T')$;
1. if $T'=\varprojlim T_i$ is a limit of an inverse system of
quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes over $T$ with affine
transition morphisms and $P(T_i)$ holds for all $i$, then
$P(T')$ holds;
1. if $Z\subset T'$ is a closed subscheme with quasi-compact
complement $V\subset T'$ and $P(T')$ holds, then either $P(V)$
or $P(Z)$ holds;
1. $P(\emptyset)$ does not hold.

Then $P(T)$ implies $P(\operatorname{Spec}K)$ for some morphism
$\operatorname{Spec}K\to T$ where $K$ is a field.
(*Stacks Project, Lemma 59.88.5, [Tag `0F06`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F06).*)

## Proof

Consider the set $\mathfrak T$ of closed subschemes $T'\subset T$ such
that $P(T')$; ordered by inclusion ($T''\subset T'$ means the closed
immersion), a chain has a lower bound by (2) applied to the inverse
system of its members (their transition morphisms are closed
immersions, hence affine), so by Zorn's lemma $\mathfrak T$ has a
minimal element $T'$, and $T'\neq\emptyset$ by (4). If $T'$ is not reduced, then the reduction
$T'_{\mathrm{red}}\to T'$ is a thickening, and (1) gives
$P(T'_{\mathrm{red}})$, contradicting the minimality of $T'$ as
$T'_{\mathrm{red}}$ is a strictly smaller closed subscheme; hence $T'$
is reduced. Let $\eta\in T'$ be the generic point of an irreducible
component of $T'$; then $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$ for a field $K$
and $\eta=\varprojlim V$ over the affine open subschemes $V\subset T'$
containing $\eta$. For such a $V$, the complement $Z=T'\setminus V$ is
closed with quasi-compact complement $V$, and if $P(V)$ failed then by
(3) $P(Z)$ would hold, contradicting the minimality of $T'$ ($Z$ is
strictly smaller than $T'$ since $\eta\in V$); hence
$P(V)$ holds for all these $V$, and (2) applied to the limit gives
$P(\eta)=P(\operatorname{Spec}K)$.

attrs.title: Minimal counterexamples occur over a point

objects.body:
For a base-change square the
derived base-change maps $\operatorname{BC}_{f,g}(K)$ of
[sbc-def-base-change-map] are natural in $K$: for every morphism
$u:K\to K'$ in $D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ the square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
Lf^*Rg_*K & \xrightarrow{\ \operatorname{BC}_{f,g}(K)\ } & Rh_*Le^*K\\
\big\downarrow{\scriptstyle Lf^*Rg_*u} & & \big\downarrow{\scriptstyle Rh_*Le^*u}\\
Lf^*Rg_*K' & \xrightarrow{\ \operatorname{BC}_{f,g}(K')\ } & Rh_*Le^*K'
\end{array}
$$

is commutative.

## Proof

By [sbc-def-base-change-map] the map
$\operatorname{BC}_{f,g}$ is the composite of the unit $\eta_e$ of the
adjunction $Le^*\dashv Re_*$, the two canonical identifications of the
composite functors coming from $ge=fh$, and the counit $\varepsilon_f$
of $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$. Units and counits of adjunctions are natural
transformations, the canonical identifications of composite functors
are natural in the argument, and a composite of natural transformations
is natural; hence $\operatorname{BC}_{f,g}(-)$ is a natural
transformation of functors $D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)\to D(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$,
which is the commutativity of the displayed square.

With $f:X\to S$ and $n$ as in [sbc-def-base-change-property] assume for
some $q\geq1$ that $\mathrm{BC}(f,n,q')$ holds universally for all
$q'\leq q-1$, but $\mathrm{BC}(f,n,q)$ does not hold universally. Then there exist a commutative diagram

$$
\begin{array}{ccccc}
X & \longleftarrow & X' & \longleftarrow & Y\\
f\big\downarrow & & \big\downarrow & & \big\downarrow h\\
S & \longleftarrow & S' & \longleftarrow & \operatorname{Spec}K
\end{array}
$$

with both squares Cartesian, where

1. $S'$ is affine, integral, and normal with algebraically closed
function field;
1. $K$ is algebraically closed and $\operatorname{Spec}K\to S'$ is
dominant (in other words $K$ is an extension of the function
field of $S'$),

and there exists an integer $d\mid n$ such that
$R^qh_*(\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z)$ is nonzero.
(*Stacks Project, Lemma 59.88.7, [Tag `0F08`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F08).*)

## Proof

By [sbc-lem-bc-failure-field] there are a morphism $S'\to S$ with
$S'$ affine, the base change $f':X'\to S'$, a field $K$ with a morphism
$T=\operatorname{Spec}K\to S'$, and a sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $T$
annihilated by $n$ for which the degree-$q$ base-change map of $f'$
along $T\to S'$ is not an isomorphism. By
[sbc-lem-bc-integral-surjective] (whose hypothesis, $\mathrm{BC}(f,n,q-1)$
universally, is part of ours) applied to
the base change $\pi:\operatorname{Spec}K'\to\operatorname{Spec}K$
to an algebraic closure $K'$ of $K$ (an integral surjective morphism),
we may assume $K$ is algebraically closed. A sheaf of
$\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$-modules on a geometric point is a direct sum of
copies of $\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z$ for varying $d\mid n$, so by the
finite direct-sum and retract case of the map, we may assume
$\mathcal F$ is constant with value $\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z$ for some
$d\mid n$ (the cokernel of the base-change map
$\bigl(R^qh_*(c)\bigr)$ decomposes accordingly). Finally, by
[sbc-lem-bc-integral-base] applied to
$\pi:S''\to S'$ the normalization of $S'$ in
$\operatorname{Spec}K$ (integral: the integral closure of the normal
domain $A'$ in $K$ is integral over $A'$, commutative algebra),
with $X''=X'\times_{S'}S''$, we may replace $S'$ by $S''$, which is
affine, integral, and normal with algebraically closed function field
$K$; this is the datum of the statement.

attrs.title: Universal curve-test datum for a failure

objects.body:
Let $K\in D^+_{\mathcal P\text{-tor}}(T_{\Et})$. For fixed $n$, only
$H^q(K)$ with $q\leq n$ can contribute to $H^n(Rg_*K)$. Hence

$$
H^n(Rg_*\tau_{\leq n}K)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^n(Rg_*K),
$$

and the analogous statement holds after pullback and for $h_*$.

## Proof

The hypercohomology spectral sequence of
[def-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-filtrations] has
$E_2^{p,q}=R^pg_*H^q(K)$; for $p+q=n$ only $q\leq n$ contributes since
$g_*$ is $t$-left exact, so
$H^n(Rg_*\tau_{\leq n}K)\cong H^n(Rg_*K)$; pullback and $h$ are handled
identically.

Consider a base-change square
where $f$ is flat and locally of finite presentation with
geometrically reduced
fibres (in particular, $f$ may be smooth). Then

$$
f^{-1}g_*\mathcal F=h_*e^{-1}\mathcal F
$$

for any sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $T_{\Et}$.
(*Stacks Project, Etale Cohomology, Section 59.87 (Base change
for pushforward), [Tag `0EYS`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EYS) = Lemma 59.87.2; the proof combines
Lemma 59.87.1, [Tag `0EZX`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EZX), with More on Morphisms, Lemma
37.46.3, [Tag `0EY5`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EY5): the connected components of the fibres
correspond under the base change, and direct image is computed by the
would-be equalizer of the section descriptions.*)

## Proof

The direct image of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] is computed by the
equalizer description of sections along the fibres; for a flat
morphism of finite presentation with geometrically reduced fibres, the
(reduced) connected components of the fibres are the geometric points,
and they correspond under base change, so for $V\to T$ etale the
sections of both sides over $V$ are the same systems of sections on the
fibres of $V\times_TY\to V$: this identifies $f^{-1}g_*\mathcal F$ and
$h_*e^{-1}\mathcal F$ as sheaves, which is the displayed equality.

Consider a base-change square
and let $\{U_i\to X\}$ be an etale covering such that $U_i\to S$ factors
as $U_i\to V_i\to S$ with $V_i\to S$ etale; form the associated
Cartesian diagrams

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
U_i & \xleftarrow{h_i} & U_i\times_XY\\
f_i\big\downarrow & & \big\downarrow e_i\\
V_i & \xleftarrow{g_i} & V_i\times_ST,
\end{array}
$$

and put $\mathcal F_i=\mathcal F|_{V_i\times_ST}$ and
$K_i=K|_{V_i\times_ST}$ for a sheaf $\mathcal F$ resp. a complex $K$
on $T_{\Et}$.

1. If $f_i^{-1}g_{i,*}\mathcal F_i=h_{i,*}e_i^{-1}\mathcal F_i$ for
all $i$, then $f^{-1}g_*\mathcal F=h_*e^{-1}\mathcal F$.
1. If $f_i^{-1}Rg_{i,*}K_i=Rh_{i,*}e_i^{-1}K_i$ for all $i$, then
$f^{-1}Rg_*K=Rh_*e^{-1}K$.
1. If $\mathcal F$ is an abelian sheaf and
$f_i^{-1}R^qg_{i,*}\mathcal F_i=R^qh_{i,*}e_i^{-1}\mathcal F_i$
for all $i$, then
$f^{-1}R^qg_*\mathcal F=R^qh_*e^{-1}\mathcal F$.

(*Stacks Project, Lemma 59.86.1, [Tag `0EZR`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EZR).*)

## Proof

Restricting to $U_i$ and using the factorizations
$U_i\to V_i\to S$ gives

$$
(f^{-1}g_*\mathcal F)|_{U_i}=f_i^{-1}(g_*\mathcal F|_{V_i})
=f_i^{-1}g_{i,*}\mathcal F_i,
$$

where the first equality is the compatibility of inverse and direct
images with localization of the etale site of
[def-weil-pbc-etale-site] (Sites, Lemma 7.28.2,
[Tag `03EF`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03EF)) and the second uses
$\mathcal F|_{V_i}=\mathcal F_i$, and likewise

$$
(h_*e^{-1}\mathcal F)|_{U_i}=h_{i,*}e_i^{-1}\mathcal F_i.
$$

Since $\{U_i\to X\}$ is an etale covering, a morphism of etale sheaves
whose restrictions to all $U_i$ are isomorphisms is an isomorphism
([def-weil-pbc-etale-site]), which proves (1); the assertions (2)
and (3) are the same argument with the localization compatibility for
the higher direct images and sheafified cohomology
(Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 21.20.4, [Tag `0D6G`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0D6G)), applied
degreewise for the $R^q$'s of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and to
$R^q$ of the base-change maps of [sbc-def-base-change-map].

attrs.title: Etale locality of the base-change map

objects.body:
Let $X$ be an
integral normal scheme with
separably closed function field.

1. A separated etale morphism $U\to X$ is a disjoint union of open
immersions.
1. All local rings of $X$ are strictly henselian.

(*Stacks Project, Lemma 59.80.4, [Tag `09Z9`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09Z9).*)

## Proof

This is the recorded classical input named in the statement, Stacks Project, Lemma 59.80.4 ([Tag 09Z9](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09Z9)): over an integral normal scheme with separably closed function field, separated etale morphisms are disjoint unions of open immersions, and all local rings are strictly henselian. No separate proof is given.

attrs.title: Etale covers of a normal scheme with algebraically closed function field

objects.body:
If $H^q(K)=0$ outside $[a,b]$ and the comparison of the two
hypercohomology spectral sequences of
[def-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-filtrations] is an isomorphism on
every $E_2^{p,q}$, then it is an isomorphism on every abutment
$H^n\cong H^n$, and hence
${\operatorname{BC}}_{f,g}(K)$ is an isomorphism.

## Proof

For a fixed total degree $n$, the abutment $H^n$ of
[def-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-filtrations] has a finite filtration
with associated graded pieces the $E_\infty^{p,q}$ with $p+q=n$, of
which only those with $q\in[a,b]$ are nontrivial; if the comparison is
an isomorphism on every $E_2^{p,q}$ it is an isomorphism on every
$E_\infty^{p,q}$, hence by induction along the finite filtration on
$H^n$.

Let $S$ be a scheme and let
$X=\varprojlim_{i\in I}X_i$ be a limit of a directed system of schemes
over $S$ with affine transition morphisms, and assume the structure
morphisms $g_i:X_i\to S$ and $g:X\to S$ are
quasi-compact and
quasi-separated. Let $(\mathcal F_i)$ be a system of abelian sheaves
on $(X_i,f_{i'i})$, with $f_i:X\to X_i$ the projections, and set
$\mathcal F=\varinjlim_if_i^{-1}\mathcal F_i$. Then

$$
\varinjlim_{i\in I}R^pg_{i,*}\mathcal F_i
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }R^pg_*\mathcal F
$$

for every $p\geq0$.
(*Stacks Project, Lemma 59.51.7, [Tag `09Z1`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09Z1).*)

## Proof

By [sbc-lem-higher-direct-image-presheaf] both sides are
sheafifications of the presheaves $U\mapsto H^p(U\times_SX_i,\mathcal F_i)$ and $U\mapsto H^p(U\times_SX,\mathcal F)$ of
[def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]; for $U$ quasi-compact and
quasi-separated (e.g. affine) the colimit of the former is the latter
by continuity of etale cohomology under limits with affine transition
morphisms, and every object of $S_{\Et}$ has a covering by
quasi-compact quasi-separated objects, so the sheafifications agree.

attrs.title: Higher direct images and limits of schemes

objects.body:
Let $h:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes and $F\in\Ab(Y_{\Et})$. Then
$R^qh_*F$ is the sheaf associated with the presheaf

$$
(U\to X)\longmapsto H^q\bigl(U\times_XY,F|_{U\times_XY}\bigr)
$$

on $X_{\Et}$; more generally for $K\in D(Y_{\Et})$ the cohomology sheaf
$R^qh_*K$ is associated with $U\mapsto H^q(U\times_XY,K|_{U\times_XY})$.
(*Stacks Project, Lemma 59.51.6, [Tag `03Q8`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03Q8).*)

## Proof

The cohomology of
[def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] of the fibre products
$U\times_XY$ computes the sections of the higher direct images of
[def-weil-pbc-direct-image] on the basis of etale $U\to X$; both
the direct image and the associated sheaf have the same
sheafification, which is the statement.

attrs.title: Higher direct image as a sheafified cohomology presheaf

objects.body:
For a cartesian square of
the proper-base-change chapter with $g=\operatorname{id}_Y$, the derived exchange
morphism of [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] is the identity. If
$Y''\xrightarrow{h}Y'\xrightarrow{g}Y$, then, after the canonical
associativity identifications, the derived exchange morphism for the
composite base change $g\circ h$ is

$$
Lh^*Lg^{-1}Rf_*\xrightarrow{Lh^*\operatorname{BC}_{f,g}}
Lh^*Rf'_*Lv^{-1}\xrightarrow{\operatorname{BC}_{f',h}}
Rf''_*L(v\circ v')^{-1},
$$

where $v:X'\to X$, $v':X''\to X'$ are the top morphisms of the two
squares.

## Proof

For $g=\operatorname{id}_Y$ the identity case of the pasting laws for
the derived exchange morphism,
[lem-weil-pbc-exchange-identity-pasting], gives that the exchange
morphism of [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] is the identity. For
two successive base changes $Y''\xrightarrow{h}Y'\xrightarrow{g}Y$,
the pasting laws of [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-identity-pasting]
applied to the two vertically pasted cartesian squares identify the
derived exchange morphism for $g\circ h$ with the composite displayed,
which is the statement.

Let $\pi:T'\to T$ be an
integral morphism of
schemes. Then the
direct image
$\pi_*:\Ab(T'_{\Et})\to\Ab(T_{\Et})$ is exact; consequently
$R^q\pi_*=0$ for $q>0$ and $R\pi_*=\pi_*$ on $\Dplus(T'_{\Et})$. If
$\pi$ is finite, this is [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact]
of the proper-base-change chapter.
(*Stacks Project, Etale Cohomology, Lemma 59.43.5,
[Tag `04C2`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/04C2).*)

## Proof

This is the recorded classical input named in the statement, Stacks Project, Etale Cohomology, Lemma 59.43.5 ([Tag 04C2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/04C2)): for an integral morphism the direct image of etale abelian sheaves is exact, so the higher direct images vanish and the derived direct image is the underived one on bounded-below complexes. The finite case is [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact] of the proper-base-change chapter; no separate proof of the general case is given.

attrs.title: Etale direct image is exact for integral morphisms

objects.body:
Let $f:X\to S$ be an affine smooth morphism of relative dimension one
with $X$ affine, let $n$ be an integer invertible on $S$, and assume, for some $q\geq1$, that
$\mathrm{BC}(f,n,q')$ holds universally for all $q'\leq q-1$ in the
sense of [sbc-def-base-change-property]. Then $\mathrm{BC}(f,n,q)$
holds universally, and hence $\mathrm{BC}(f,n,q')$ holds universally
for all $q'\leq q$.

## Proof

Suppose $\mathrm{BC}(f,n,q)$ does not hold universally. By
[sbc-lem-bc-universal-test] (whose hypothesis is the universal
cumulative $\mathrm{BC}(f,n,q')$, $q'\leq q-1$, assumed here) there is
a universal curve test datum: after base
change and normalization, $X'=X\times_SS'\to S'$ is a base change of
$f$ with $S'$ affine, hence (affine smooth morphisms of relative
dimension one being stable under base change, as is immediate from
[def-sbc-smooth-morphisms])
affine smooth of relative dimension one with $X'$ affine, $S'$ is the
spectrum of a normal domain with algebraically closed fraction field
$L$, $K/L$ an extension of algebraically closed fields, and for some
$d\mid n$ the sheaf $R^qh_*(\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z)$ is nonzero. This
contradicts [sbc-thm-universal-test-vanishing], whose hypotheses
hold: $d$ is invertible on $S'$ because $d\mid n$ and $n$ is invertible
on $S$ and on all its base changes (the $\mathrm{BC}$-property
being a statement about base changes of
$f$); the normalization $S''\to S'$ in $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is
integral because the integral closure of the domain $A'$ in $K$ is
integral over $A'$ (commutative algebra). Hence $\mathrm{BC}(f,n,q)$
holds universally. (Equivalently: the hypotheses of the lemma are
inherited by every base change $f'$ of $f$ with affine source, and the
class of smooth morphisms of relative dimension $\leq1$ is stable under
base change, so the induction produces the universal form.)

attrs.title: The induction step in relative dimension one

objects.body:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a
smooth morphism of schemes. Then
there exists an etale covering $\{U_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ such that
$U_i\to S$ factors as $U_i\to V_i\to S$ where $V_i\to S$ is etale and
$U_i\to V_i$ is a smooth morphism of affine schemes, which has a
section, and has geometrically
connected fibres.
(*Stacks Project, More on Morphisms, [Tag `0EY4`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EY4) = Lemma
37.38.8.*)

## Proof

This is the recorded classical input named in the statement, Stacks Project, More on Morphisms, Lemma 37.38.8 ([Tag 0EY4](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EY4)): a smooth morphism becomes, after an etale cover of its source, a smooth morphism of affine schemes with a section and geometrically connected fibres over an etale base. No separate proof is given.

A morphism $f:X\to Y$ of schemes is
smooth if and only if it is flat,
locally of finite presentation, and every fibre $X_y$ is smooth over
$\kappa(y)$.
(*Stacks Project: a smooth morphism is locally of finite
presentation and flat by
[Lemma 29.35.8](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01VE) and
[Lemma 29.35.9](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01VF), its
fibres are smooth by base change,
[Lemma 29.35.5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01VB), and
conversely flatness, local finite presentation and smooth fibres give
smoothness by
[Lemma 29.35.3](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01V8); the two
definitions of smoothness are identified by
[Lemma 37.11.7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02H6). For
morphisms of finite type the criterion is the Jacobian criterion,
[Lemma 29.35.14](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01V9).*)

## Proof

This is the recorded classical input named in the statement: smooth morphisms are flat and locally of finite presentation (Stacks Project, Lemmas 29.35.8 and 29.35.9, [Tag 01VE](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01VE), [Tag 01VF](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01VF)), have smooth fibres by base change (Lemma 29.35.5, [Tag 01VB](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01VB)), and conversely flatness with local finite presentation and smooth fibres gives smoothness (Lemma 29.35.3, [Tag 01V8](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01V8)), the two definitions of smoothness being identified by Lemma 37.11.7 ([Tag 02H6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02H6)); for morphisms of finite type this is the Jacobian criterion, Lemma 29.35.14 ([Tag 01V9](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01V9)). The blueprint uses the criterion, which is why it is recorded here; no separate proof is given.

attrs.title: Smoothness by flatness and smooth fibres

objects.body:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a smooth
morphism of schemes. Then $f$ has
geometrically reduced
fibres.
(*Stacks Project: the fibres are smooth over their residue fields
by base change,
[Lemma 29.35.5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01VB), and a
scheme smooth over a field is geometrically reduced,
[Lemma 33.25.4](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/056T).*)

## Proof

This is the recorded classical input named in the statement, Stacks Project, Lemmas 29.35.5 and 33.25.4 ([Tag 01VB](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01VB), [Tag 056T](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/056T)): the fibres of a smooth morphism are smooth over their residue fields by base change, and a scheme smooth over a field is geometrically reduced. No separate proof is given.

attrs.title: Smooth morphisms have geometrically reduced fibres

objects.body:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a smooth
morphism of schemes. Then the function
$x\mapsto\dim_x\bigl(X_{f(x)}\bigr)$ is locally constant on $X$.
(*Stacks Project,
[Lemma 29.35.12](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02G1):
$\Omega_{X/Y}$ is finite locally free and
$\operatorname{rank}_x(\Omega_{X/Y})=\dim_x(X_{f(x)})$.*)

## Proof

This is the recorded classical input named in the statement, Stacks Project, Lemma 29.35.12 ([Tag 02G1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02G1)): for a smooth morphism the module of differentials is finite locally free and its rank at a point is the dimension of the fibre there, whence the local constancy. No separate proof is given.

attrs.title: Local constancy of the relative dimension

objects.body:
Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a strictly henselian local ring, let
$X=\operatorname{Spec}R$, and let $A$ be a finite constant sheaf of
order invertible in $R$. Then

$$
H^q(X_{\Et},A)=\begin{cases}A,&q=0,\\0,&q>0,\end{cases}
$$

for the etale cohomology of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].

## Proof

A finite etale cover of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is trivial: $R$ being
strictly henselian, every finite etale $R$-algebra is a finite product
of copies of $R$ (the Hensel property and connectedness of
$\operatorname{Spec}R$). Hence the etale site of $X$ is contractible
for finite coefficients of order invertible in $R$, and the constant
sheaf $A$ is the pullback of the constant sheaf on a point:
$H^q(X_{\Et},A)=H^q(\mathrm{pt},A)$, zero for $q>0$ and $A$ for
$q=0$ (*reference: Stacks Project, Etale Cohomology: the
cohomology of a constant sheaf on a strictly henselian local scheme*).

attrs.title: Constant-sheaf cohomology of a strictly henselian local scheme

objects.body:
If $T''\to T'$ is a thickening of schemes (a closed immersion
inducing a homeomorphism of the underlying spaces), then the
small etale site of $T''$ is the
same as that of $T'$: pullback along $T''\to T'$ induces an
isomorphism of sites, hence an equivalence of the categories of
etale sheaves identifying the
cohomology of the two schemes.
(*Stacks Project, Etale Cohomology, Proposition 59.45.4,
[Tag `03SI`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03SI).*)

## Proof

This is the recorded classical input named in the statement, Stacks Project, Etale Cohomology, Proposition 59.45.4 ([Tag 03SI](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03SI)): a thickening induces an isomorphism of small etale sites, hence an equivalence of the categories of etale sheaves identifying the cohomology of the two schemes. No separate proof is given.

attrs.title: The etale site of a thickening

objects.body:
For an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ of
schemes and a Cartesian
square with base change $a:Z'\to Z$, extension by zero
([def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]) is exact and

$$
a^{-1}j_!F\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }j'_!a_U^{-1}F
$$

for every sheaf $F$ on $U_{\Et}$, and the same holds for complexes.
(*Stacks Project, Etale Cohomology, Lemma 59.70.5, [Tag `03S6`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03S6).*)

## Proof

Extension by zero is computed sectionwise as in
[def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]: for etale $V\to Z'$ the sections
of $j'_!a_U^{-1}F$ over $V$ are the sections of $a_U^{-1}F$ over
$V\times_{Z'}U'$, i.e. over $V\times_ZU$, while
$(a^{-1}j_!F)(V)=j_!F(V\times_ZZ_V)$ has the same description; the
Cartesian identification gives the natural isomorphism, and for
complexes the same argument applies termwise.

Let $Y$ be a scheme and $M$ a finite abelian group. Then there is a
canonical bijection, natural in $(Y,M)$,

$$
\operatorname{Tor}^1(Y,M)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^1(Y_{\Et},\underline M)
$$

between the pointed set of isomorphism classes of $M$-torsors of
[def-weil-pbc-finite-torsors] and $H^1(Y_{\Et},\underline M)$, and an
$M$-torsor is the same thing as a finite etale $Y$-scheme with a simply
transitive $M$-action. Moreover, let $Y$ be connected
with geometric point $\bar y$. For an $M$-torsor $P$, viewed as a finite
etale $Y$-scheme, and $p\in|P_{\bar y}|$, let
$f_P:\pi_1(Y,\bar y)\to M$ be defined by $g\cdot p=p+f_P(g)$; it is
a continuous homomorphism independent of $p$ and of $P$ within its
isomorphism class. Then $P$ is connected — that is, a Galois cover with
group $M$ — exactly when $f_P$ is surjective (the case of the sketch is
$M=\Z/d\Z$).
(Stacks 02NE, together with the finite-etale correspondence; cf. Milne,
*Lectures on Etale Cohomology*, III.3.)

## Proof

The bijection, with its naturality, is [thm-galois-torsor-h1]. By
[thm-galois-lc-etale] the functor
$P\mapsto\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_Y(-,P)$ is an equivalence from
finite etale $Y$-schemes to finite locally constant sheaves which carries
simply transitive $M$-actions to simply transitive ones, and conversely;
since an $M$-torsor is by [def-weil-pbc-finite-torsors] a finite locally
constant sheaf with an $M$-action for which $M\times P\to P\times_YP$ is
an isomorphism, $M$-torsors are the same as finite etale $Y$-schemes with
a simply transitive $M$-action.

Now let $Y$ be connected and $P$ an $M$-torsor, viewed as a
finite etale $Y$-scheme with $M$ acting by $Y$-automorphisms. By
[thm-galois-fundamental] the fibre functor $F_{\bar y}$ of
[def-galois-fibre-functor] identifies $P$ with the finite continuous
$\pi_1(Y,\bar y)$-set $|P_{\bar y}|$, and the $M$-action with an action
of $M$ on $|P_{\bar y}|$ by $\pi_1$-equivariant maps; this action is
simply transitive because the isomorphism $M\times P\to P\times_YP$
becomes $M\times|P_{\bar y}|\cong|P_{\bar y}|\times|P_{\bar y}|$ under
the exact functor $F_{\bar y}$. In particular $|P_{\bar y}|\neq\emptyset$.

*The homomorphism.* Fix $p\in|P_{\bar y}|$. By simple transitivity there
is a unique $f_P(g)\in M$ with $g\cdot p=p+f_P(g)$. As the two actions
commute,
$gh\cdot p=g\cdot(p+f_P(h))=(g\cdot p)+f_P(h)=p+f_P(g)+f_P(h)$, so
$f_P$ is a homomorphism. It is continuous: for $m\in M$ the set
$\{g:f_P(g)=m\}$ is the stabilizer-coset $\{g:g\cdot p=p+m\}$, which
is open because the action on the finite discrete set $|P_{\bar y}|$ is
continuous (the definition of a $\pi_1(Y,\bar y)$-set in
[def-galois-fibre-functor]). Replacing $p$ by $p+a$ gives
$g\cdot(p+a)=p+a+f_P(g)$, so $f_P$ does not depend on $p$, $M$ being
abelian; and an $M$-equivariant isomorphism $P\cong P'$ carries $p$ to a
point $p'$ with the same $f$, so $f_P$ only depends on the class of $P$,
hence (by the bijection) on the class in $H^1(Y_{\Et},\underline M)$.

*Connectedness.* By [lem-fet-galois-category], $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$
with $F_{\bar y}$ is a Galois category whose connected objects are the
connected finite etale $Y$-schemes, and the equivalence of
[thm-galois-fundamental] preserves finite coproducts and initial
objects, so $P$ is connected exactly when the nonempty
$\pi_1(Y,\bar y)$-set $|P_{\bar y}|$ is not a disjoint union of two
nonempty sub-$\pi_1$-sets, i.e. exactly when $\pi_1(Y,\bar y)$ acts
transitively on it (each orbit is a sub-$\pi_1$-set with an invariant
complement). Since $p\mapsto p+m$ is a bijection $M\to|P_{\bar y}|$
and the orbit of $p$ is $p+f_P(\pi_1(Y,\bar y))$, the action is
transitive exactly when $f_P$ is surjective.

*Galois.* If $P$ is connected, $M$ acts on $P$ by
$Y$-automorphisms, faithfully and transitively on the fibre
$|P_{\bar y}|$ of cardinality $\#M$, so $\#\operatorname{Aut}(P)\ge\#M$;
by [lem-galois-axioms] (6) $\#\operatorname{Aut}(P)\le\#|P_{\bar y}|=\#M$.
Hence $\operatorname{Aut}(P)=M$ acts simply transitively on the
fibre, and $P$ is a Galois cover with group $M$. Conversely a
Galois cover is connected by definition.

In the square of
[sbc-thm-smooth-base-change], assume $f$ smooth, $g$ quasi-compact
and quasi-separated, all schemes noetherian, $\ell$ invertible on $S$,
and let $A=\mathcal O_E$ with ideal $I=(\varpi)$ such that every
$A_n=A/I^{n+1}$ is finite of order invertible on the schemes under
consideration and perfect as an $A$-module. Let
$K\in\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)$ with each reduction $K_n$ in the essential
image of $\Dbc(T_{\Et},A_n)$. Then the completed exchange map

$$
Lf^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rg_{*,\mathrm{comp}}K
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rh_{*,\mathrm{comp}}Le^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K
$$

is an isomorphism in the derived-complete category, and in
$\Dbc(S_{\Proet},A)$ whenever the four finite-level systems involved
have constructible cohomology in one common finite cohomological
interval.

## Proof

The completed actions of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] are the
derived inverse limits of their finite levels; direct image commutes
with derived limits and derived completion
([thm-weil-pbc-complete-proetale]), the perfect projection formula
of [lemma-weil-pbc-perfect-projection-formula] identifies the
finite levels of the two sides with the finite-level exchanges, and
each finite-level exchange is an isomorphism by
[sbc-thm-finite-proetale-smooth-base-change]; derived inverse
limits of isomorphisms are isomorphisms, and the constructible hypothesis
gives the indicated landing.

Let $k\subseteq k'$ be algebraically closed, let $C$ be a
smooth separated curve
over $k$, and let $d\geq1$ be prime to $\operatorname{char}k$. For
every $q\geq0$ the pullback map

$$
H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z)
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^q((C_{k'})_{\Et},\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z)
$$

is an isomorphism.
(*the Jacobian chapter, [thm-sc-constant-invariance] (= Lemma
59.83.12, [Tag `0A5E`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A5E) of Stacks Project for the corresponding
statement).*)

## Proof

This is [thm-sc-constant-invariance] of the Jacobian chapter (applied with
$n=d$), which proves the same assertion for the constant sheaf
$\mathbf F_d$; this is the displayed pullback map by the definition of
the etale cohomology of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].

attrs.title: Invariance under extension of algebraically closed fields

objects.body:
In the square of
[sbc-thm-smooth-base-change] with $f$ smooth, $g$ quasi-compact
and quasi-separated, and $\mathcal P$ the set of primes invertible on
$S$: for every $K\in D^b_{\mathcal P\text{-tor}}(T_{\Et})$, the
exchange map ${\operatorname{BC}}_{f,g}(K)$ of [sbc-def-base-change-map] is an
isomorphism in $D^b_{\mathcal P\text{-tor}}(S_{\Et})$ whenever both
sides are bounded, and is always an isomorphism in the ambient derived
category of abelian sheaves.

## Proof

Each $H^q(K)$ has geometric stalks that are torsion with prime divisors
in $\mathcal P$ ([sbc-def-derived-categories-with-allowable-torsion]);
[sbc-thm-smooth-base-change] applied to $H^q(K)$ makes the
comparison an isomorphism on every $E_2^{p,q}$ of
[def-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-filtrations]; $K$ is bounded, so
[sbc-lem-finite-range-comparison] transfers these isomorphisms to
the abutments; if both sides are bounded, this is the isomorphism in
$D^b_{\mathcal P\text{-tor}}(S_{\Et})$, and in general the detection on
cohomology sheaves of [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]
gives the isomorphism in the ambient category.

In the square of
[sbc-thm-smooth-base-change] with $f$ smooth, $g$ quasi-compact
and quasi-separated, and $\mathcal P$ the set of primes invertible on
$S$: for $K\in D^+_{\mathcal P\text{-tor}}(T_{\Et})$,

$$
{\operatorname{BC}}_{f,g}(K):Lf^*Rg_*K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rh_*Le^*K
$$

in $D^+_{\mathcal P\text{-tor}}(S_{\Et})$.

## Proof

For each $n$ apply [sbc-thm-bounded-allowable-torsion] to
$\tau_{\leq n}K$ (bounded, allowable torsion) and use
[sbc-lem-bounded-below-truncation-criterion] to identify the
abutments; detection on cohomology sheaves
([lem-weil-pbc-derived-stalk-conservative], [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]) gives the statement.

In the square of
[sbc-thm-smooth-base-change] with $f$ smooth and $g$ quasi-compact
and quasi-separated, for every $K\in\Dbc(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$,

$$
{\operatorname{BC}}_{f,g}(K):Lf^*Rg_*K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rh_*Le^*K
$$

in $D(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$, where the derived exchange is the one of
[sbc-def-base-change-map].

## Proof

Each $H^q(K)$ is constructible, hence by the finite stratification
filtration (the exact open–closed localization sequence and extension
by zero of [sbc-prop-extension-by-zero-and-arbitrary-base-change]) it is a
finite extension of extensions by zero of finite locally constant
sheaves; finite locally constant sheaves are torsion with orders
invertible on $S$ (the ring $\Lambda$ is annihilated by $N$), so
[sbc-thm-smooth-base-change] together with the compatibility of
the base-change map with short exact sequences
([lemma-weil-pbc-five-lemma-transfer]) gives the isomorphism on the
$E_2$ page of the hypercohomology spectral sequences of
[lemma-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-convergence]; since $K$ is bounded,
[sbc-lem-finite-range-comparison] transfers the isomorphisms to
the abutments and gives the displayed isomorphism in the ambient
derived category.

Let $k$ be algebraically closed, let $C$ be a
smooth affine curve over
$k$, and let $d\geq1$ be prime to $\operatorname{char}k$. Then

$$
H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z)=0\qquad(q>1)
$$

with $H^0(C_{\Et},\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z)=\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z$.
(*the Jacobian chapter, [thm-sc-affine-cohomology]; Stacks Project,
Theorem 59.83.10, [Tag `03SC`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03SC), (2).*)

## Proof

The cohomology groups of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] of the
constant sheaf $\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z$ are computed in
[thm-sc-affine-cohomology] of the Jacobian chapter (with
$n=d$), where the vanishing for $q>1$ is displayed under the
identifications of the Kummer sequence; this is the claim.

In the square of
[sbc-thm-smooth-base-change], assume $f$ smooth, $g$ quasi-compact
and quasi-separated, all schemes noetherian, $\ell$ invertible, and let
$K_E\in\Dbc(T,E)$ admit a finite-level etale admissible lattice. Then
the exchange morphism is an isomorphism in the ambient rationalized
complete category

$$
Lf^*_{\mathrm{comp},E}Rg_{*,\mathrm{comp},E}K_E
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rh_{*,\mathrm{comp},E}Le^*_{\mathrm{comp},E}K_E
\quad\text{in }D_{\mathrm{comp}}(S,E),
$$

independent of the lattice, and an isomorphism in $\Dbc(S,E)$ if the
lattice is square-constructibly admissible.

## Proof

The two-term free resolution
$[\mathcal O_E\xrightarrow{\varpi^{n+1}}\mathcal O_E]$ of $A_n$ and
the adic theorem [sbc-thm-adic-smooth-base-change] give the
statement for integral lattices; central localization (inverting
multiplication by $\varpi$) of
[def-weil-pbc-rational-category] gives
it for $K_E$, independent of the admissible lattice, and the
constructible landing is the four-system hypothesis of
[sbc-def-admissible-lattices].

Let $g:Y'\to Y$ be
smooth at $y'\in Y'$. After
replacing $Y,Y'$ by affine neighbourhoods, there are $d\geq0$ and an
etale morphism

$$
e:Y'\longrightarrow\mathbf A^d_Y
$$

such that $g$ is $e$ followed by the projection
$p_d:\mathbf A^d_Y\to Y$ of [def-sbc-affine-space].
(*Stacks Project, Morphisms, [Tag `054L`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/054L) = Lemma
29.37.21.*)

## Proof

Choose affine neighbourhoods $Y=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and
$Y'=\operatorname{Spec}C$ of the specified points, small enough
that $g$ is smooth on the latter. We use the ordinary
commutative-algebra infinitesimal criterion: a finitely presented
formally smooth algebra is smooth
([Stacks, Tag 00TN](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00TN)),
and near any prime it has a presentation

$$
C=R[x_1,\ldots,x_N]/(F_1,\ldots,F_c),\qquad
\det\left(\frac{\partial F_a}{\partial x_b}\right)_{a,b\leq c}
\in C^\times.
$$

The latter is the standard-presentation lemma of commutative
algebra ([Tag 00TA](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00TA)).
Its algebraic mechanism is to choose a basis of the projective
conormal module, then a nonzero minor of its split injection into
the free module of differentials. Localizing at that minor and
using Nakayama on the finitely generated relation ideal gives the
displayed generators; a localization is incorporated by adjoining
one variable and its inverse relation. These operations replace
the source by an affine open containing the selected point.
This is an application of the ring lifting criterion to the local
lifting condition in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms].

Put $d=N-c$ and regard the last $d$ variables as base
coordinates: let $P=R[x_{c+1},\ldots,x_N]$. The same presentation
is now a $P$-algebra presentation with $c$ variables and $c$
relations, and its square Jacobian determinant is invertible.
It is exactly a presentation of [def-exc-jacobian-presentation].
For clarity, the lifting assertion for this new base can also be
read directly from the equations. Given a square-zero ideal
$J\subset Q$, a $P$-algebra map $C\to Q/J$ determines
arbitrary lifts $q_b$ of the first $c$ variables. Its errors
$F_a(q)$ lie in $J$. A correction $v\in J^c$ must satisfy

$$
(\partial F_a/\partial x_b)(q)\,v_b=-F_a(q).
$$

There is exactly one solution because the determinant is a unit:
it is a unit modulo a nilpotent ideal and hence a unit in $Q$.
Taylor expansion has no higher correction terms since $J^2=0$.
This constructs the unique lift fixing all the base coordinates.
Successive square-zero quotients treat a general nilpotent ideal.
Consequently [lem-exc-etale-jacobian-presentation] makes
$\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}P$ etale.
By [def-sbc-affine-space], $\operatorname{Spec}P=\mathbf A^d_Y$.
The composite with its projection is induced by the original
ring homomorphism $R\to C$, and is therefore exactly $g$.
