*Theorem (sketch).*

The three maps of [sk-def-sf-kv-maps] are isomorphisms, natural in their
variables, under the hypotheses of that definition (the $Rf_i^!$ are the
constructible exceptional adjoints of [sk-def-sf-operations] (vi); no
admissibility datum of [sk-def-sf-admissible] is assumed): the
exceptional Künneth $\alpha$, the external Hom $\beta$, and
in particular, for $X,Y$ separated of finite type over $k$, with the structure
morphism $a_Y$ and the product projection $p_X=\operatorname{id}_X\times a_Y$
as in [sk-def-sf-kv-maps] (iv), and
$M\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$, $N\in\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$,

$$
\kappa_{M,N}:M\boxtimes\mathbb D_YN\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\
\RHom\bigl(p_Y^*N,Rp_X^!M\bigr).
$$

## Proof

*The map $\alpha$.* Take first a constant auxiliary coefficient. For
smooth $f_i$ of relative dimension $d_i$, [sk-thm-smooth-purity] identifies
$Rf_i^!$ with $Lf_i^*(d_i)[2d_i]$, and its compatibility with base change and
with composition identifies the smooth product comparison with the ordinary
pullback–tensor comparison and the sum of the twists; the smooth trace is the
exceptional counit under this orientation, and its base-change square is the
adjoint of the same purity comparison, using the adjunction coherence of
fix-prop-adjunctions and the mate calculus [sk-lem-sf-mate]. Closed immersions are handled by supported
localization [sk-prop-sf-localization] together with the closed-immersion unit
[sk-prop-sf-closed-unit] and the case $Q=\Lambda_Z$ of
[sk-lem-sf-kunneth-star]; the regular case carries the fundamental class of
[sk-thm-regular]. An affine factorization of a general $f_i$ into a closed
immersion followed by a smooth projection gives the map locally. This
settles constant coefficients $L_i=\Lambda_{Y_i}$, hence, by additivity,
finite free ones. For $L_i$ lisse with flat stalks the invertibility of
$\alpha$ is étale-local on $Y_1\times Y_2$ — $Rf^!$ commutes with étale
pullback (for étale $u$, $Ru^!=Lu^*$, and the composition isomorphism of
[sk-lem-sf-mate]), compatibly with $\alpha$ — and on a finite étale cover
trivializing the $L_i$ they become finite free, the case just treated; this
is a local reduction, not a dévissage (the lisse coefficients cannot be
replaced by constant ones globally, [sk-lem-sf-ctf-generation]). For
general $L_i\in\Dctf(Y_i,\Lambda)$ argue by induction on
$\delta=\dim\operatorname{supp}L_1+\dim\operatorname{supp}L_2$; the claim is
trivial if some $L_i=0$, and both sides of $\alpha$ are exact in each $L_i$,
so two-out-of-three applies to triangles in either variable.
*Closed pushforward.* For a closed immersion $g_1:Z_1\hookrightarrow
Y_1$, with $g_1':X_1\times_{Y_1}Z_1\hookrightarrow X_1$ and
$f_1':X_1\times_{Y_1}Z_1\to Z_1$ the projections, the dual base change
$Rf_1^!Rg_{1*}\cong Rg'_{1*}Rf_1'^!$ (the mate of $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ under
[sk-lem-sf-mate]) and $Rg_{1*}M_1\boxtimes L_2\cong
R(g_1\times\mathrm{id})_*(M_1\boxtimes L_2)$ ([sk-lem-sf-kunneth-star])
identify $\alpha_f(Rg_{1*}M_1,L_2)$ with
$R(g_1'\times\mathrm{id})_*\,\alpha_{f_1'\times f_2}(M_1,L_2)$, compatibly
with the definition of $\alpha$ as an exceptional adjoint (a mate-calculus
check, [sk-lem-sf-mate]); likewise in the second variable. Since
$L_i\cong Rg_{i*}g_i^*L_i$ for $Z_i=\operatorname{supp}L_i$
([sk-prop-sf-open-closed-triangle], as $L_i$ vanishes on the complement),
we may assume $\dim Y_i=\dim\operatorname{supp}L_i$. Then by the generation
[sk-lem-sf-ctf-generation] on $Y_i$ it suffices to treat the generators
$L_i=Rg_{i*}j_{i!}F_i$ with $F_i$ lisse with flat stalks on a stratum $U_i$
dense in $\overline U_i$, $\dim\overline U_i\le\dim Y_i$, and by the closed
pushforward just described we may take $\overline U_i=Y_i$, $L_i=j_{i!}F_i$.
*Open localization.* $Rf^!$ does not commute with $j_!$, so pass
through $Rj_*$: for the open immersion $j=j_1\times j_2$ with base changes
$j'$ and $f'$, the dual base change $Rf^!Rj_*\cong Rj'_*Rf'^!$ (the mate of
the base change for $j_!$) and [sk-lem-sf-kunneth-star], which gives
$Rj_{1*}F_1\boxtimes Rj_{2*}F_2\cong Rj_*(F_1\boxtimes F_2)$ and
$Rj'_{1*}Rf_1'^!F_1\boxtimes Rj'_{2*}Rf_2'^!F_2\cong
Rj'_*(Rf_1'^!F_1\boxtimes Rf_2'^!F_2)$, identify
$\alpha_f(Rj_{1*}F_1,Rj_{2*}F_2)$ with $Rj'_*\,\alpha_{f'}(F_1,F_2)$,
compatibly with $\alpha$ as before; the latter is the lisse case already
treated, so $\alpha$ is invertible on $(Rj_{1*}F_1,Rj_{2*}F_2)$. The
open–closed triangle [sk-prop-sf-open-closed-triangle] for
$M=Rj_{i*}F_i$ reads
$j_{i!}F_i\to Rj_{i*}F_i\to T_i\xrightarrow{+1}$ with
$T_i=i_{i*}i_i^*Rj_{i*}F_i\in\Dctf(Y_i,\Lambda)$
([sk-thm-sf-ctf-stability]), a general object of $\Dctf$ supported on the
boundary $Z_i=Y_i\setminus U_i$, of dimension $<\dim Y_i$. By the induction
hypothesis $\alpha$ is invertible on $(T_1,j_{2!}F_2)$ and on
$(Rj_{1*}F_1,T_2)$, the support dimensions having dropped; two-out-of-three
in the second variable gives $(Rj_{1*}F_1,j_{2!}F_2)$, and then in the first
variable $(j_{1!}F_1,j_{2!}F_2)$. Hence $\alpha$ is invertible.

*The map $\beta$.* Both sides are exact in each $E_i$, so dévissage in
both $E_i$, by [sk-lem-sf-ctf-generation], reduces to $E_i=Rh_{i!}F_i$ with
$h_i=g_ij_i$, $g_i$ finite and $j_i$ open, and $F_i$ lisse on $U_i$ with flat
stalks. Such an $F_i$ is dualizable: its stalks are finite flat, hence free,
over the local ring $\Lambda$, so $F_i$ is locally finite free and
[sk-prop-sf-dualizable-biduality] gives $\RHom(F_i,-)\simeq
F_i^\vee\otimes^L-$. Tensor–Hom and the exceptional adjunction then give
$\RHom(E_i,L_i)\simeq Rh_{i*}\RHom(F_i,Rh_i^!L_i)\simeq
Rh_{i*}\bigl(F_i^\vee\otimes^LRh_i^!L_i\bigr)$ ([sk-thm-sf-tensor-hom]).
With $h=h_1\times h_2$ and $F=F_1\boxtimes F_2$, so that
$F^\vee\simeq F_1^\vee\boxtimes F_2^\vee$ and $E_1\boxtimes E_2\simeq Rh_!F$
($\mathrm{Ku}_!$), the comparison becomes

$$
 Rh_{1*}\bigl(F_1^\vee\otimes^LRh_1^!L_1\bigr)\boxtimes
 Rh_{2*}\bigl(F_2^\vee\otimes^LRh_2^!L_2\bigr)
 \xrightarrow[\text{twice}]{\ \mathrm{Ku}_*\ }
 Rh_*\bigl(F^\vee\otimes^L(Rh_1^!L_1\boxtimes Rh_2^!L_2)\bigr)
 \xrightarrow{\ Rh_*(1\otimes\alpha)\ }
 Rh_*\bigl(F^\vee\otimes^LRh^!(L_1\boxtimes L_2)\bigr),
$$

the first arrow being [sk-lem-sf-kunneth-star] in each factor (after the
symmetry of $\otimes^L$) and the second the $\alpha$ just proved; by the same
identifications the target is $\RHom(E_1\boxtimes E_2,L_1\boxtimes L_2)$.
Taking ordinary and then exceptional adjoints identifies this composite with
the specified $\beta$: both paths become the tensor product of the two
evaluation maps after the projection formula. Hence $\beta$ is invertible.

*The map $\kappa$.* Apply $\beta$ to the pairs $(\Lambda_X,M)$ and
$(N,\omega_Y)$, then $\RHom(1,\alpha)$ for the identification
$M\boxtimes\omega_Y\simeq Rp_X^!M$, which is $\alpha$ for
$\operatorname{id}_X\times a_Y$. Their composite is $\kappa_{M,N}$ by
[sk-def-sf-kv-maps] (iv), and both factors have just been shown invertible.

and none of them uses anything proved
in this section except the definitions. The latter two are statements about
torsion sheaves; their bounded-below forms at $A_{E,n}$ are the truncation
dévissage thm:weil-pbc-bounded-below and
sbc-thm-bounded-below-derived-smooth-base-change, transported to the
pro-étale site along the comparison of [sk-prop-sf-comparison], and the
$\mathcal O_E$, $E$, $\Qlb$ forms on $\Dbc$ of the adic categories are the
derived-limit, rationalization and scalar-extension transports cited in the
clause — the same three steps as [sk-thm-sf-pf-adic] and
[sk-thm-sf-pf-field]. The coherence of $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ is
fix-lem-exchanges. Clause (3) is the projection-formula
chain of §§ *What this section proves*: the finite case [sk-thm-sf-pf-finite] reduces to
the compact-support projection formula of the framework chapter, and
[sk-prop-sf-pf-reduction], [sk-thm-sf-pf-adic], [sk-thm-sf-pf-field] and
[sk-thm-sf-pf-proetale] transport it to the remaining stages, with
[sk-prop-sf-pf-coherence] for the coherence. Clause (4) is
[sk-thm-nagata-compactification] and [sk-prop-nagata-sketch-comp-category]
for the compactifications themselves, and [sk-prop-sf-comp-coherence],
[sk-thm-sf-comp-composition], [sk-prop-sf-comp-proper] of
§§ *What this section proves* for the independence, the composition law and proper
coincidence. Clause (5) is
[sk-thm-smooth-purity] of §[sec-smooth-purity], with
[sk-prop-cohsm] for the tensor form and [sk-thm-purity-transport] for the
$\mathcal O_E$, $E$ and $\Qlb$ stages; it is what makes the orientation of
[sk-def-sf-orientation] a theorem. Its compatibility with composition and
with $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ is the composition and base-change compatibility
of [sk-thm-smooth-purity] and [sk-prop-cohsm] (c), read through
[sk-lem-sf-mate]; its compatibility with $\alpha$ is the smooth step of the
proof of [sk-thm-sf-kunneth-verdier]. Clause (6) is
[sk-prop-sf-biduality-general] (Chapter 1), [sk-thm-sf-verdier-exchange]
and [sk-thm-sf-global-duality] and [sk-thm-sf-identification]
(§§ *What this section proves*, using [sk-thm-sf-tensor-hom]), with
[sk-prop-sf-dualizable-biduality], [sk-lem-sf-twist-interchange] and
[sk-thm-sf-dual-perfect] for the perfect case; the compatibility of
$\varepsilon$ with composition is obtained by pasting the tensor–Hom chain of
[sk-thm-sf-tensor-hom] for $f$ and for $g$, using the associativity pentagon
of [sk-prop-sf-pf-coherence] and [sk-lem-sf-mate]
(fix-prop-coherence). Clause (7) is
[sk-thm-sf-kunneth-relative], whose proof uses clause (2), clause (3)
(with the base-change clause of [sk-prop-sf-pf-coherence] for its
coherence), clause (4) and, for the typing of $\operatorname{PF}_g$, clause
(8)(iv). Clause (8) is [sk-thm-sf-ctf-stability], whose proof uses
[sk-lem-sf-flat-model], [sk-thm-sf-direct-image-tor-amplitude],
[sk-cor-sf-direct-image-ctf], [sk-thm-sf-hom-ctf],
[sk-prop-sf-finiteness], [sk-prop-sf-comparison] and
[sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation]. No clause assumes a property that is
not proved in the blueprint: the *Conditional on* lines of
[sk-prop-sf-existence], [sk-prop-sf-biduality-general] and
[sk-thm-sf-ctf-stability] are the
complete list of what is conditional, and they are restated in the ledger
below.

Uses: `\Cref{sk-cor-sf-direct-image-ctf}`, `\Cref{lem-sf-flat-model}`, `\Cref{lem-sf-twist-interchange}`, `\Cref{sk-prop-cohsm}`, `\Cref{sk-prop-nagata-sketch-comp-category}`, `\Cref{sk-prop-sf-biduality-general}`, `\Cref{sk-prop-sf-cbc}`, `\Cref{sk-prop-sf-comp-coherence}`, `\Cref{sk-prop-sf-comp-proper}`, `\Cref{sk-prop-sf-comparison}`, `\Cref{sk-prop-sf-dualizable-biduality}`, `\Cref{sk-prop-sf-existence}`, `\Cref{sk-prop-sf-finiteness}`, `\Cref{sk-prop-sf-kunneth-ordinary}`, `\Cref{prop-sf-pf-coherence}`, `\Cref{prop-sf-pf-reduction}`, `\Cref{sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation}`, `\Cref{sk-rem-sf-matrix}`, `\Cref{thm-nagata-compactification}`, `\Cref{sk-thm-properbasechange}`, `\Cref{sk-thm-purity-transport}`, `\Cref{thm-sf-comp-composition}`, `\Cref{thm-sf-ctf-stability}`, `\Cref{thm-sf-direct-image-tor-amplitude}`, `\Cref{thm-sf-dual-perfect}`, `\Cref{thm-sf-global-duality}`, `\Cref{thm-sf-hom-ctf}`, `\Cref{thm-sf-identification}`, `\Cref{thm-sf-kunneth-relative}`, `\Cref{thm-sf-pf-adic}`, `\Cref{thm-sf-pf-field}`, `\Cref{thm-sf-pf-finite}`, `\Cref{thm-sf-pf-proetale}`, `\Cref{sk-thm-sf-tensor-hom}`, `\Cref{thm-sf-verdier-exchange}`, `\Cref{sk-thm-smooth-base-change}`, `\Cref{sk-thm-smooth-purity}`, `\Cref{lem-sf-mate}`, `\Cref{def-sf-kv-maps}`, `\Cref{sk-thm-sf-kunneth-verdier}`, `\Cref{sk-def-sf-admissible}`

*Theorem (sketch).*

Let $K,L$ be derived-complete $\Dctf$-objects over $\mathcal O_E$ of finite Tor
amplitude, with finite reductions $K_n,L_n$. Then the maps
$\operatorname{PF}_{f,K_n,L_n}$ form a morphism of normalized systems and
realize a canonical isomorphism $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}$ over
$\mathcal O_E$, compatible with all finite reductions.

## Proof

Each finite-level map is an isomorphism by [sk-thm-sf-pf-finite], and the
maps are compatible under reduction by [sk-prop-sf-pf-reduction], with
uniform bounds inherited from $K$ and $L$ (finite Tor amplitude of a
derived-complete object is uniform in $n$). Derived completeness and this
compatibility are exactly the hypothesis of the uniform-tower reconstruction
lem:weil-pbc-reconstruction-uniform-tower, which realizes the system as a
morphism of derived-complete complexes with the given reductions; it is an
isomorphism because its reductions are and reduction is conservative on
derived-complete complexes of finite Tor amplitude.

Uses: `\Cref{prop-sf-pf-reduction}`, `def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed`, `lem-weil-pbc-reconstruction-uniform-tower`

*Theorem (sketch).*

Let $K,L$ be obtained by rationalization from $\mathcal O_E$-objects, or
represented at a finite stage $E'/\Ql$. Then
$\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}$ is an isomorphism over $E$ and over $\Qlb$,
compatible with the extension functors and with finite reduction.

## Proof

Rationalization $-\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}E$ is exact, commutes with $Rf_!$,
$\otimes^L$ and $Lf^*$, and carries the mate-theoretic projection
transformation to the mate-theoretic projection transformation, since units
and counits are transported; an exact functor carries isomorphisms to
isomorphisms. For $\Qlb$ each object is represented over a finite stage by
def:weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients, and compatibility with scalar
extension makes the finite-stage system descend to the $2$-colimit.

Uses: `\Cref{thm-sf-pf-adic}`, `def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients`, `def-weil-rationalization-karoubi`

*Theorem (sketch).*

Let $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type, and let
$K$ and $L$ be bounded constructible complexes on the small étale sites with
$L$ of finite Tor amplitude, so that $K\in\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ and
$L\in\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$. Then $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}$ is an isomorphism in
$D^+(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$, natural in $K$ and $L$.

## Proof

Split off a compactification $f=\bar f\circ j$; the projection transformation is
then the direct-image projection map for $\bar f$ composed with the
identification $j_!K\otimes^L\bar f^*L\cong j_!(K\otimes^Lf^*L)$, which is
checked on étale stalks. For a geometric point $\bar y$ of $Y$, compact-support
base change identifies the stalk of the projection map with
$R\Gamma_c(X_{\bar y},K^{\mathrm{fib}}_{\bar y})\otimes^LP\to R\Gamma_c(X_{\bar y},K^{\mathrm{fib}}_{\bar y}\otimes^L\underline P)$. The
fibrewise map is an isomorphism for every $P$: choose a bounded complex of
finite free modules representing $P$; both sides are exact functors of $P$
agreeing on $P=\Lambda$ (the unit identification), and the class of $P$ for
which the map is an isomorphism is closed under finite sums, shifts, cones and
direct summands. Hence all geometric stalks of the cone vanish, and geometric
stalks are conservative on the étale site.

Uses: `\Cref{sk-def-sf-exchanges}`, `def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed`, `lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula`

*Theorem (sketch).*

Let $K,L$ be the pro-étale realizations of bounded constructible finite-Tor
complexes, with étale-origin witnesses, at any coefficient stage. Then
$\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}$ is an isomorphism in
$D^+(Y_{\Proet},\Lambda)$.

## Proof

The exact comparison pullback $\nu^*$ of thm:weil-pbc-site-comparison
commutes with $Lf^*$ and with $\otimes^L$, and the compact-support comparison
of thm:cbc-finite-level-proetale identifies the transported
$R\bar f_*j_!$ together with its exchange and projection maps; hence the
comparison carries the étale projection transformation to the pro-étale
one, and transporting [sk-thm-sf-pf-finite] along it gives the statement at
every stage ([sk-thm-sf-pf-field] for the non-finite stages).

Uses: `\Cref{thm-sf-pf-field}`, `def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness`, `thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale`, `thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison`

*Theorem (sketch).*

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of finite-type
$k$-schemes, with $f^!=Rf^!$ the constructible exceptional adjoint of
[sk-def-sf-operations] (vi) (no admissibility datum is assumed), and let
$M\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ and $N\in\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$. Then there is a canonical isomorphism
$$
Rf_*\RHom_X(M,f^!N)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\RHom_Y(Rf_!M,N),
$$

in the ambient category $D^+(Y,\Lambda)$, natural in $M$ and $N$ and
compatible with finite reduction, scalar extension and shifts.

## Proof

For every $L$ the adjunctions and the tensor–internal-Hom adjunction give a
chain

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_Y\bigl(L,\RHom_Y(Rf_!M,N)\bigr)
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_!M\otimes^LL,N)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y\bigl(Rf_!(M\otimes^LLf^*L),N\bigr)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X\bigl(M\otimes^LLf^*L,f^!N\bigr)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X\bigl(Lf^*L,\RHom_X(M,f^!N)\bigr)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y\bigl(L,Rf_*\RHom_X(M,f^!N)\bigr),
\end{aligned}
$$

in which the second isomorphism is the *inverse* of the projection
formula at the coefficient stage of $\Lambda$ — [sk-thm-sf-pf-finite] at
$\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, and [sk-thm-sf-pf-adic], [sk-thm-sf-pf-field],
[sk-thm-sf-pf-proetale] at the remaining stages, all stated in the ambient
$D^+$ and collected in [sk-rem-sf-pf-done] — and the third is the adjunction
$Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$ of [sk-prop-sf-existence](c), valid because
$M\otimes^LLf^*L$ is bounded below of étale origin when $L$ is. The chain
is natural in $L$ ranging over the bounded-below complexes of étale origin,
a full subcategory containing both sides (each is the comparison image of the
corresponding complex on the étale site, [sk-prop-sf-comparison]), so
the two objects represent the same functor there and Yoneda gives the
isomorphism.

Uses: `\Cref{sk-def-sf-exchanges}`, `\Cref{sk-def-sf-operations}`, `\Cref{lem-sf-mate}`, `\Cref{sk-thm-sf-pf-finite}`, `\Cref{sk-thm-sf-pf-adic}`, `\Cref{sk-thm-sf-pf-field}`, `\Cref{sk-thm-sf-pf-proetale}`, `\Cref{sk-rem-sf-pf-done}`, `def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom`

*Theorem (sketch).*

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes,
with $Rf^!$ and the dualizing complexes $\omega_X=Ra_X^!\Lambda$,
$\omega_Y=Ra_Y^!\Lambda$ formed with the constructible exceptional adjoint of
[sk-def-sf-operations](vi) (no admissibility datum is assumed).
Then $Rf^!\omega_Y\cong\omega_X$, and for $M\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
\mathbb D_Y(Rf_!M)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf_*\mathbb D_X(M),
$$

in the ambient category $D^+(Y,\Lambda)$, natural in $M$ and compatible with
finite reduction, scalar extension and shifts.

## Proof

*Step 1:* $Rf^!\omega_Y\cong\omega_X$: by the composition law and
[sk-lem-sf-mate], the mate of $R(a_Y\circ f)_!\cong Ra_{Y!}Rf_!$ is the
isomorphism $Rf^!Ra_Y^!\cong Ra_X^!$. *Step 2:* apply
[sk-thm-sf-tensor-hom] with $N=\omega_Y$ and substitute Step 1:
$\mathbb D_Y(Rf_!M)=\RHom_Y(Rf_!M,\omega_Y)\cong Rf_*\RHom_X(M,f^!\omega_Y)\cong Rf_*\RHom_X(M,\omega_X)=Rf_*\mathbb D_XM$.
Naturality and the compatibilities are those of the two ingredients. (This
proof uses only the tensor–Hom exchange and never the duality chapter, which
is what removes the proof cycle between the framework and duality chapters.)

Uses: `\Cref{sk-def-sf-operations}`, `\Cref{lem-sf-mate}`, `\Cref{sk-thm-sf-tensor-hom}`, `def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image`

*Theorem (sketch).*

(Stacks Project, Étale Cohomology, Theorem 59.89.2, Tag
`0EYU`; the chapter follows the *second, shorter proof*.)
Let

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X & \xleftarrow{\;h\;} & Y\\
f\downarrow & & \downarrow e\\
S & \xleftarrow{\;g\;} & T
\end{array}
$$

be Cartesian with $f$ smooth and $g$ quasi-compact
quasi-separated. Then for every $q$ and every abelian sheaf
$\mathcal F$ on $T_{\Et}$ all of whose geometric stalks are torsion
of orders invertible on $S$,

$$
f^{-1}R^qg_*\mathcal F\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ R^qh_*e^{-1}\mathcal F,
$$

the map being the base-change map of [sk-def-bc].

## Proof

*Degree zero*: [sk-prop-deg0] (smooth is flat, of finite
presentation, with geometrically reduced fibres).
*Filtered torsion*: $\mathcal F=\varinjlim_n\mathcal F[n]$
over $n$ invertible on $S$; inverse images are left adjoints and
$R^qg_*$, $R^qh_*$ commute with filtered colimits for qcqs $g,h$;
so it suffices to handle sheaves annihilated by a single $n$
invertible on $S$.
*Reduction to relative dimension one*: the assertion is
étale local on $X$ and $S$; by [sk-prop-normal-form] one may
assume $X$ and $S$
affine and $X\to S$ factoring through $\Aaf^d_S$; writing $X\to \Aaf^{d-1}_S\to\cdots\to\Aaf^1_S\to S$ and using the composition
compatibility of the base-change map, it suffices to prove the
assertion for affine smooth $X\to S$ of relative dimension one.
*Induction on $q$*: for $q\ge1$ with the theorem known in
degrees $<q$, that theorem applied to every base change $f_{S'}$ of
$f$ (again affine smooth of relative dimension one) and every qcqs
$T\to S'$ is exactly $\mathrm{UBC}^{\le q-1}(f,n)$, the hypothesis of
[sk-lem-induction]; the lemma gives $\mathrm{BC}(f,n,q)$ (indeed
universally); running the filtered colimit back over $n$
finishes the degree-$q$ case. Induction on $q$ concludes.

Uses: [sk-def-bc], [sk-def-smooth], [sk-lem-induction], [sk-prop-deg0], [sk-prop-input-spreading], [sk-prop-input-torsors]

*Theorem (sketch).*

In the conventions of [sk-def-purity-conv], let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth
separated of pure relative dimension $d$. Then

$$
\omega_f=Rf^{!}\Lambda_Y\ \cong\ \Lambda_X(d)[2d],
$$

canonically; for every $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ the tensor formula
[sk-prop-cohsm] (b) gives the purity isomorphism

$$
Rf^{!}K\ \cong\ Lf^{*}K(d)[2d].
$$

These isomorphisms are compatible with base change and with composition
of smooth morphisms (twist additivity). *Agreement on the model:*
for the projection $\pi$ of a vector bundle of rank $d$ (in particular for
$p_d:\Aaf^d_Y\to Y$) the isomorphism $\omega_\pi\cong\Lambda(d)[2d]$
constructed below is the $R\pi^{!}$-form $\gamma_{\pi,\Lambda}$ of
[sk-prop-an] (ii) (detailed: lem:pur-projection-purity-agreement).

## Proof

Put $W=X\times_YX$, let $p_1,p_2$ be its projections and let
$\Delta:X\hookrightarrow W$ be the diagonal.
*Step 1: the section invariant of the diagonal is $\omega_f$.* The
square with $p_1,p_2$ over $f$ is Cartesian and $p_1$ is the base change of
$f$, so $\omega_{p_1}\cong Lp_2^{*}\omega_f$ by [sk-prop-cohsm] (c). Since
$p_2\circ\Delta=\mathrm{id}_X$,

$$
\mathcal C(p_1,\Delta)=L\Delta^{*}\omega_{p_1}
\cong L\Delta^{*}Lp_2^{*}\omega_f\cong\omega_f .
$$

*Step 2: the deformation to the normal cone of that section.* $\Delta$
is a closed section of the smooth map $p_1$, with normal bundle
$N_\Delta\cong T_{X/Y}$ of rank $d$ by [sk-lem-diag-reg]. Applying
[sk-thm-dnc] to $(p_1,\Delta)$ gives

$$
\mathcal C(p_1,\Delta)\ \cong\ \mathcal C(\pi_T,0_T),\qquad
\pi_T:T_{X/Y}\to X .
$$

*Step 3: the other side is the Tate twist.* Vector-bundle purity,
the $R\pi^{!}$-form [sk-prop-an] (ii) applied to $\pi_T$, gives
$\omega_{\pi_T}=R\pi_T^{!}\Lambda_X\cong\Lambda_{T_{X/Y}}(d)[2d]$, and
pulling back along the zero section,

$$
\mathcal C(\pi_T,0_T)=L0_T^{*}\omega_{\pi_T}
\cong L0_T^{*}\Lambda_{T_{X/Y}}(d)[2d]\cong\Lambda_X(d)[2d].
$$

Combining the three steps gives $\omega_f\cong\Lambda_X(d)[2d]$. Every step
is canonical, by the uniqueness clause of [sk-thm-dnc]; base-change
compatibility follows from that of the diagonal, of [sk-thm-dnc] and of
[sk-prop-an] (ii), the normal bundle of the diagonal of a base change being the
base change of the normal bundle. Substitution into [sk-prop-cohsm] (b)
gives the purity map for every $K$. Compatibility with composition is
that of [sk-prop-cohsm] (a),(c) and of the twist.

*Agreement on the model.* Let $f=\pi:E\to Z$ be a vector bundle of
rank $d$ with zero section $0_E$. Then $p_1:W=E\times_ZE\to E$ is the
bundle $\pi^{*}E$ and $\Delta$ is the translate of its zero section by the
tautological section; translation is an automorphism of $W$ over $E$
carrying $(p_1,\Delta)$ to $(\pi^{*}E,0)$, and the trace $\int_{\pi^{*}E}$,
hence $\gamma_{\pi^{*}E,\Lambda}$, is translation invariant, because the
class of every section of a vector bundle integrates to $1$ (the integral
of the class of the universal section is a locally constant function on
$E$, equal to $1$ along the zero section by [sk-prop-an] (iii), and every
connected component of $E$ meets the zero section, the fibres of $\pi$
being connected). Under $\gamma_{\pi,\Lambda}$ and $\gamma_{\pi^{*}E,\Lambda}$
the base-change isomorphism of Step 1 is the identity (base-change
compatibility in [sk-prop-an] (ii)); on the standard pair $(\pi^{*}E,0)$
the deformation space is $\pi^{*}E\times\Aaf^1$ with constant family object
([sk-lem-geometry] (4)) and the isomorphism of [sk-thm-dnc] is the
identity on the standard section invariant (its normalization clause); and
Step 3 is $L0^{*}$ of $\gamma_{\pi_T,\Lambda}$ with
$T=N_\Delta\cong\pi^{*}E$. Hence the composite of Steps 1–3 is
$\gamma_{\pi,\Lambda}^{-1}$: the isomorphism $\omega_\pi\cong\Lambda_E(d)[2d]$
of this theorem for $\pi$ is the $R\pi^{!}$-form of [sk-prop-an] (ii)
(detailed: lem:pur-projection-purity-agreement).

Uses: [sk-def-purity-conv], [sk-lem-diag-reg], [sk-prop-an], [sk-prop-cohsm], [sk-thm-dnc]

*Proposition (sketch).*

For every Weil datum on a separated finite-type
$X_0/\mathbf F_q$ and every $m\ge1$, with
compact cohomology and ordinary traces,

$$
\boxed{\tr_A(F_{c,m}\mid R\Gamma_c(X,K))
=\sum_{x\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})}\tr_A(F_{x,m}\mid K_{\bar x}).}
$$

## Proof

First prove the formula for every closed subscheme of the affine
line, uniformly over all finite extensions. For a finite scheme,
[sk-i-topology] permits reduction, preserving the Weil maps,
compact cohomology, and geometric stalks. Being reduced of dimension
zero, its geometric base change is a finite disjoint union of spectra of
finite extensions, hence of points (06LH).
Frobenius permutes their perfect stalk complexes; the chain
supertrace in [sk-p-trace] receives contributions only from
the diagonal blocks, exactly the fixed points.

For $\mathbf A^1$, extend the [sk-d-weil] datum by zero to
the projective line of [sk-d-lines], which is proper (0FMG)
and smooth of pure dimension one (0B2P).
Open base change and composition in [sk-thm-sf-package] identify its
compact cohomology and global operator with the originals.
Apply [sk-c-proper-global] on this smooth proper curve, then
[sk-p-local] and [sk-p-frob]. The coefficient stalk at
$\infty$ is zero, so its computed local term is zero.
Finally a closed subscheme of $\mathbf A^1_F$ has coordinate ring
$F[t]/I$. If $I=0$, it is the line; otherwise a nonzero polynomial
in $I$ makes the quotient finite-dimensional over $F$, and the
finite-scheme case applies. This includes nonreduced schemes.

Now prove the formula for all affine schemes with a presentation
$F[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/I$, by induction on $n$, simultaneously over all
finite extensions and for every Weil complex and every iterate.
The cases $n\le1$ were just proved. For $n\ge2$, forget $t_n$ to
obtain $f_0:X_0\to Y_0=\mathbf A^{n-1}_F$. Use the Weil
$!$-pushforward $(L,\psi)$ of [sk-d-weil-push].
Its compact global operator is conjugate to the original one.
Induction on $Y_0$ gives

$$
\tr_A(F_{c,m},R\Gamma_c(X,K))
=\sum_{y\in Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})}\tr_A(\psi_{m,\bar y},L_{\bar y}).
$$

Base change identifies the operator at $\bar y$ with the compact
Frobenius operator on the fiber, considered over $\mathbf F_{q^m}$
with one-step Weil map $\varphi_m$. This follows by pasting the
base-change squares and relative-Frobenius units defining $\psi_m$.
The fiber is a closed subscheme of the affine line over that field,
so the base case computes its trace. Summing over the fibers gives
the rational-point sum on $X_0$.

For a general separated finite-type scheme, take a finite affine
cover $U_1,\ldots,U_N$ and the affine pieces
$U_i\setminus\bigcup_{j<i}U_j$. The successive closed complements
give a finite localization filtration. Repeated
[sk-i-global-additivity] combines their proven trace formulas;
their rational points form the same disjoint partition.

Uses: [sk-c-proper-global], [sk-d-lines], [sk-d-six], [sk-d-trace], [sk-d-weil-push], [sk-d-weil], [sk-i-global-additivity], [sk-i-topology], [sk-p-frob], [sk-p-local], [sk-p-trace], [sk-thm-sf-package]

*Theorem (sketch).*

Let the coefficient ring range over the three non-finite stages

$$
\Lambda\in\{\mathcal O_E,\ E,\ \overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\},
$$

the $\mathcal O_E$-stage being the normalized systems of
finite-level objects, the $E$-stage its
rationalization, and the $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-stage the colimit over
finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $X_0/\mathbf F_q$ be separated of finite
type and let $K$ be a Weil datum with coefficients in
$\Lambda$, that is, a Weil pair at the stage $\Lambda$ in the all-stage
sense of [sk-def-sf-weil-complexes]: at $\mathcal O_E$ a normalized system
of finite-level Weil pairs ([sk-d-weil]) whose transitions commute with the
$\varphi_n$ (a compatible tower of Weil pairs as in
[sk-prop-trace-adic](ii)), and at $E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ its
rationalization and colimit. Then:

1. **(a)** *Trace identity.* The identity of
[sk-thm-trace-formula] holds for every $m\ge1$ with $A$ replaced by
$\Lambda$, with compact cohomology and
ordinary traces taken at the stage $\Lambda$.
1. **(b)** *Euler-product form.* Let
$\Lambda\in\{E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$, write $e_x$ for the degree of
a closed point $x\in|X_0|$, and put
$$
L(X_0,K,T)=\prod_{x\in|X_0|}
\det\bigl(1-T^{e_x}F_x\mid K_{\bar x}\bigr)^{-1}
\in1+T\Lambda[[T]],
$$
a locally finite product. For a complex, the stalk determinant denotes
the alternating product of the determinants on its cohomology. Then
$$
L(X_0,K,T)=\prod_{i}
\det\bigl(1-TF\mid H_c^i(X,K)\bigr)^{(-1)^{i+1}}
$$
as formal power series, the product being finite; if $X_0$ is a curve and $K$ is a sheaf in degree zero, it
runs over $0\le i\le2$. Any field embedding
$\iota:\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\to\mathbf C$ carries the identity to one
in $\mathbf C[[T]]$.

## Proof

*Step 1 (the finite levels).* At $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, clause (a) is
[sk-thm-trace-formula]. Its coefficient-morphism variant also applies
to noninvertible maps, under the explicit curve input above; Steps 2–3
preserve this variant.

*Step 2 (compatibility with the reductions).* By [sk-p-trace-coeff], both sides commute with
$(-)\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,m}$: compact cohomology and the
geometric stalks are compatible with finite reduction of the coefficient
ring, the Frobenius structure of [sk-d-weil] reduces with them, and the
ordinary trace of [sk-d-trace] on a perfect complex is compatible with
base change of the coefficient ring. So the identities of Step 1 form a
compatible system over the tower.

*Step 3 (the adic stage).* Write $C_n=R\Gamma_c(X,K_n)$.
By [sk-thm-sf-ctf-stability], each $C_n$ is perfect, and Step 2 gives
$C_n\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,1}\simeq C_1$.
To see that the Tor-amplitudes are uniform, choose a bounded finite-free
model of $C_n$ over the Artinian local ring $A_{E,n}$. Whenever a
differential has a unit entry, split off the resulting contractible
two-term summand. The remaining minimal complex has zero differential
after reduction to the residue field $A_{E,1}$. Its ranks are therefore
the dimensions of $H^i(C_1)$, and its terms vanish outside the fixed
cohomological range of $C_1$. The same argument applies to each stalk
tower. Thus the perfect-realization input in [sk-prop-trace-adic] applies
over $\mathcal O_E$. The realized traces reduce to the finite-level
traces; completeness of $\mathcal O_E$ now gives (a) from Step 2.

*Step 4 (the field stages).* The map $\mathcal O_E\to E$ is flat and
the trace of an endomorphism of a perfect complex commutes with flat
extension of the coefficient ring, so (a) holds over $E$ for the
rationalization of a lattice. A $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-object is
represented over some finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and traces are compatible
with $E\hookrightarrow\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$; this gives (a) at the
last stage. If a field-stage Weil map is only defined after inverting
$\varpi$, clear its denominators on a finite coefficient model, as in
[sk-prop-trace-adic]. Multiplication of the one-step map by $c\ne0$
multiplies its $m$-th iterate and both traces by $c^m$. Apply the
integral formula and divide by $c^m$.

*Step 5 (from (a) to (b)).* Group the points of
$X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ by the closed points below them: a closed point $x$
of degree $e_x$ contributes $e_x$ rational points exactly when
$e_x\mid m$, each with stalk trace $\tr(F_x^{m/e_x}\mid K_{\bar x})$.
Multiply (a) by $T^m/m$, sum over $m\ge1$ and exponentiate. In
characteristic zero

$$
\exp\Bigl(\sum_{m\ge1}\tr(F^m\mid V)\,\frac{T^m}{m}\Bigr)
=\det(1-TF\mid V)^{-1}
$$

for an endomorphism of a finite-dimensional vector space; applied on the
point side it produces the local factors
$\det(1-T^{e_x}F_x\mid K_{\bar x})^{-1}$, hence $L(X_0,K,T)$, and applied
to each $H_c^i$ it produces the alternating product of determinants. The
groups $H_c^i(X,K)$ are finite dimensional and vanish outside a bounded
range by [sk-thm-sf-ctf-stability], so the product is finite; for a curve and a coefficient sheaf in degree zero,
compactification by [sk-thm-nagata-compactification], extension by zero and
[sk-prop-cd] give the range $0\le i\le2$.

*Step 6 (the embedding).* A field embedding $\iota$ is a ring
homomorphism, so it carries the identity in
$\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell[[T]]$ coefficientwise to one in
$\mathbf C[[T]]$.

Uses: [sk-d-setup], [sk-d-six], [sk-d-trace], [sk-d-weil], [sk-def-sf-weil-complexes], [sk-i-curve-zero], [sk-p-trace-coeff], [sk-prop-cd], [sk-prop-logdet], [sk-prop-trace-adic], [sk-thm-sf-ctf-stability], [sk-thm-trace-formula]

attrs.title: Transport of the trace formula to the non-finite stages

objects.body:
*Theorem (sketch).*

Let $X_0/\Fq$ be smooth, proper and geometrically connected of pure dimension
$d$, and let $(V_{i,\ell},F_{i,\ell},P_{i,\ell})$ be the family of
[sk-def-cohfamily]. Then

$$
Z(X_0,T)=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}P_{i,\ell}(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}
\qquad\text{in }\Ql(T)\cap\Ql[[T]] .
$$

## Proof

By [sk-thm-trace-transport] (a) the point counts are alternating traces,
$N_n=\sum_i(-1)^{i}\Tr(F_{i,\ell}^{n}\mid V_{i,\ell})$. Substituting into the
exponential definition of [sk-def-zeta] and exchanging the finite $i$-sum
with the power series,

$$
\log Z(X_0,T)=\sum_{n\ge1}\Bigl(\sum_i(-1)^{i}\Tr(F_{i,\ell}^{n}\mid
V_{i,\ell})\Bigr)\frac{T^{n}}{n}
=\sum_i(-1)^{i}\sum_{n\ge1}\Tr(F_{i,\ell}^{n})\frac{T^{n}}{n}.
$$

By [sk-prop-logdet] the inner series is $-\log P_{i,\ell}(T)$, so
$\log Z=\sum_i(-1)^{i+1}\log P_{i,\ell} =\log\prod_iP_{i,\ell}^{(-1)^{i+1}}$. Exponentiating gives the identity; it
lies in $\Ql(T)$ because the right side is a finite product of rational
functions with constant term $1$, and in $\Ql[[T]]$ because the left side is.

Uses: [sk-def-cohfamily], [sk-def-zeta], [sk-prop-logdet], [sk-thm-trace-formula], [sk-thm-trace-transport]

*Theorem (sketch).*

In the setting of [sk-def-pairing], the derived isomorphism of
[sk-thm-sf-identification], its degreewise form under the hypotheses of
[sk-thm-sf-identification] and [sk-thm-derived-duality], the trace isomorphism
and the Frobenius statements are
compatible with finite reduction, and they are realized over $\Oe$, over
$E$ and over $\Qlb$ by the uniform-tower reconstruction and by descent
along the common-stage construction. (Blueprint 15,
thm:pod-finite-reduction,
thm:pod-adic-reconstruction-and-scalar-extension,
thm:pod-qbar-coefficient-pairing.)

## Proof

*Step 1 (finite reduction).* The pairings at the levels $A_{E,n}$
are the reductions of one another: $\beta_K$ is built from the cup
product, the evaluation and the trace, and each of these is compatible with
finite reduction by [sk-thm-sf-package] (3) and [sk-def-ops]. The inverse adjoints
therefore form a morphism of normalized systems, and the isomorphism of
[sk-thm-sf-identification] descends level by level
(thm:pod-finite-reduction).
*Step 2 (the integral and field stages).* The uniform-tower
reconstruction realizes the system over $\Oe$ with one common amplitude;
localization $\Oe\to E$, extension of the coefficient field and the passage
to the common stage $\Qlb$ then transport the isomorphism, its degreewise
form and the trace isomorphism by flat extension of scalars, while the
Frobenius statements transport as well because the Weil data are defined
stagewise and the comparison maps are equivariant
(thm:pod-adic-reconstruction-and-scalar-extension,
thm:pod-qbar-coefficient-pairing).
*Step 3 (what is transported).* The transported data are exactly the
isomorphism, its degreewise form, the map of [sk-cor-trace] and the
equivariance and similitude of [sk-thm-frobenius] (a) at every stage,
together with its reciprocity clause (b) at the field stages $E$ and
$\Qlb$ only, where the degreewise form is perfect; each
of these is constructed from the pairing and the trace alone and no further
input enters.

Uses: [sk-cor-trace], [sk-def-ops], [sk-def-set], [sk-thm-derived-duality], [sk-thm-frobenius], [sk-thm-sf-identification], [sk-thm-sf-package]

*Theorem (sketch).*

Let $X\to S$ be affine smooth of relative dimension one with $X$
affine, $S=\Spec A$ normal with algebraically closed fraction field
$L$, $K/L$ an extension of algebraically closed fields, $d$
invertible on $S$, and

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X & \xleftarrow{\;h\;} & Y=X\times_S\Spec K\\
f\downarrow & & \downarrow e\\
S & \xleftarrow{\;g\;} & \Spec K.
\end{array}
$$

Then

$$
R^qh_*(\Z/d\Z)=0\qquad(q\ge1).
$$

## Proof

$R^qh_*(\Z/d\Z)$ is the sheaf associated with
$U\mapsto H^q(U\times_S\Spec K,\Z/d\Z)$ on $X_{\Et}$; we must kill
each $\xi$ in one of these groups on an étale cover of $U$.

- $q>1$: $U\times_S\Spec K$ is an affine smooth curve over
$K$, and [sk-prop-cd-affine] gives the vanishing.
- $q=1$: by [sk-prop-normal-form] replace $U$ by an étale
cover with $U\to V\to S$, $U\to V$ affine smooth with geometrically connected fibres
and a section $\sigma$, $V\to S$ étale; by
[sk-prop-etale-normal], $V$ is an open
of the normal $S$, so we may assume $X\to S$ affine smooth, with
geometrically connected fibres and a section $\sigma$, and
$\xi\in H^1(Y,\Z/d\Z)$. By [sk-prop-ext-invariance] the pullback
map $H^1(X_L,\Z/d\Z)\to H^1(Y,\Z/d\Z)$ is an isomorphism, so $\xi$ comes from a class on
$X_L$; by [sk-prop-input-torsors] this
class is a $\Z/d\Z$-torsor $P\to X_L$, a finite étale cover with a
free transitive $\Z/d\Z$-action. It need not be connected ($X_L$ is
connected, and $P$ is connected only when the class corresponds to a
*surjection* $\pi_1(X_L)\to\Z/d\Z$), so it need not be Galois;
let $P_0\subseteq P$ be a connected component. Then $P_0\to X_L$ is
a finite étale Galois cover whose group is the stabiliser
$G\subseteq\Z/d\Z$ of $P_0$ (the image of $\pi_1(X_L)$), $|G|$
divides $d$, and $P$ is the torsor induced from the $G$-torsor
$P_0$; in particular $P_0\to X_L$ trivializes $P$ (the diagonal
section of $P_0\times_{X_L}P_0$). Over the $L$-point $\sigma(\eta)$
the cover $P_0$ is split ($L$ algebraically closed), so $P_0$ has an
$L$-point above $\sigma(\eta)$; by [sk-prop-input-spreading] $P_0$
spreads to a finite étale Galois cover $X'\to X$ with group $G$
and $X'\times_XX_L=P_0$; then $X'\times_XY\to Y$ is the pullback of
$P_0\to X_L$, over which $P$, hence $\xi$, is trivial, so the class
of $\xi$ is killed in $H^1(X'\times_XY,\Z/d\Z)$: $\{X'\to X\}$ is
the required étale cover and the sheaf is zero.

Uses: [sk-def-smooth], [sk-prop-cd-affine], [sk-prop-etale-normal], [sk-prop-ext-invariance], [sk-prop-input-spreading], [sk-prop-input-torsors], [sk-prop-normal-form]

In Lean the two conclusions are split into
`ValuativeCriterion.universallyClosed_of_isDominant` and
`ValuativeCriterion.isSeparated_of_isDominant`; both are fully
proved. The ingredients — the valuation probe
(Tag 02JQ, `nonempty_valuationProbe`), the
composite valuation ring (`ValuationSubring.comapResidue`), the
intersection lemma (Tag 052K,
`ValuationSubring.comap_eq_of_le_comap`) and the extension lemma
(Tag 00IA, `ValuationSubring.exists_comap_eq`, via
Mathlib's Chevalley extension theorem rather than the Zorn argument) — live
in the `WeilConjectures.Mathlib` helper files. The formalized proof
deviates from the Stacks Project text in two reductions: instead of
replacing $U,X,S$ by their reductions, the morphism $h$ is factored through
its scheme-theoretic image — the factor map `Scheme.Hom.toImage` is
scheme-theoretically dominant with no reducedness hypothesis, and the
valuative data factors through the image because $\operatorname{Spec}$ of a
valuation ring or of a field is reduced
(`Scheme.IdealSheafData.le_ker_of_range_subset_support`); and the
polynomial presentation of a field-valued point is inlined via
`MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom`. The flat-pullback and reduced-density
inputs ([lemma-nagata-dense-flat-pullback],
[lemma-nagata-reduced-dense-image-schematic]) are provided by Mathlib's
`IsSchemeTheoreticallyDominant` API.

## Proof

We first verify the existence part of the valuative criterion for $f$.
Start with an arbitrary square

$$
\operatorname{Spec}(K)\longrightarrow X,
\qquad
\operatorname{Spec}(A)\longrightarrow S.
$$

Valuation rings and fields are reduced, so replacing $U,X,S$ by their
reductions does not change this lifting problem. After this replacement,
topological density of $h(U)$ says that the scheme-theoretic image of
$h$ is all of $X$ by
[lemma-nagata-reduced-dense-image-schematic]. We may also replace
$S$ by an affine open through
which $\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to S$ factors; write it as
$\operatorname{Spec}(R)$.

Choose an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}(B)\subseteq X$ through which
the generic map factors. Choose the polynomial $B$-algebra $P$ and
surjection $P\twoheadrightarrow K$ presenting the field-valued point. The map
$\operatorname{Spec}(P)\to X$ is flat. Therefore

$$
U\times_X\operatorname{Spec}(P)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}(P)
$$

is scheme-theoretically dense by
[lemma-nagata-dense-flat-pullback].

Apply [lemma-nagata-dense-valuation-probe] to the point
$\operatorname{Spec}(K)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}(P)$. We obtain a
valuation ring $A'$, with fraction field $K'$, whose generic point maps
to $U\times_X\operatorname{Spec}(P)$ and whose closed point maps to the
chosen $K$-point of $\operatorname{Spec}(P)$. If
$k'=A'/\mathfrak m_{A'}$, this gives a field embedding
$K\to k'$. Choose a valuation ring $A''\subseteq k'$ dominating the
image of $A$, with fraction field $k'$, by
[lemma-nagata-valuation-ring-extension].

Form the inverse-image ring

$$
C=\{a\in A'\mid a\bmod\mathfrak m_{A'}\in A''\}.
$$

By [lemma-nagata-composite-valuation-ring], $C$ is a valuation ring
with fraction field $K'$, and $C/\mathfrak m_{A'}=A''$. Since
$A''$ contains the image of $A$, the map $R\to A'$ factors through
$C$. Thus the generic map
$\operatorname{Spec}(K')\to U$ and the map
$\operatorname{Spec}(C)\to S$ form a diagram covered by the hypothesis.
Let $g_C\colon\operatorname{Spec}(C)\to X$ be its unique lift.

There are now two maps $\operatorname{Spec}(A')\to X$: one is obtained
from $\operatorname{Spec}(A')\to\operatorname{Spec}(P)\to X$, and the
other by composing $\operatorname{Spec}(A')\to\operatorname{Spec}(C)$
with $g_C$. They have the same generic map through $U$ and the same
composite to $S$. Applying the assumed uniqueness to the valuation ring
$A'$ shows that the two maps are equal.

Restrict $g_C$ along the closed immersion
$\operatorname{Spec}(A'')\to\operatorname{Spec}(C)$ induced by
$C/\mathfrak m_{A'}\cong A''$. Its generic point is
$\operatorname{Spec}(k')$, the residue field of the prime
$\mathfrak m_{A'}\subset C$. The preceding equality on
$\operatorname{Spec}(A')$ identifies this generic map with the closed-point
residue map of $\operatorname{Spec}(A')\to X$ and hence with the base
change of the original $\operatorname{Spec}(K)\to X$. Let $x\in X$ be the image
of the closed point. The image of the induced local homomorphism
$\mathcal O_{X,x}\to A''$ lies in the subfield $K\subseteq k'$.
By [lemma-nagata-valuation-intersection],
$K\cap A''=A$. Hence the local homomorphism factors through $A$, and
therefore defines the required lift $\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to X$.
The existence part of the valuative criterion now shows that $f$ is
universally closed.

Finally suppose $f$ is quasi-separated. Then its diagonal
$\Delta_f\colon X\to X\times_SX$ is quasi-compact. A map
$\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to X\times_SX$ is a pair of maps to $X$.
If their common generic restriction factors through $U$, the uniqueness
hypothesis for $f$ forces the pair to be equal, hence to factor uniquely
through $\Delta_f$. Applying the universally-closed part just proved to
$\Delta_f$ and $h\colon U\to X$ makes the diagonal universally closed.
Since every diagonal is an immersion, a universally closed diagonal is a
closed immersion. Thus $f$ is separated.

Only the six theorems of §§ *The six theorems* are statements; every other fact used
in the proofs is argued inline (finite morphisms, composition,
cancellation, the symmetric product, étale locality, the
degree-zero exchange). The curve-estimate theorem [prop-weil-pbc-projective-line] is
the single step carrying the split marker: it alone sits on the
critical path (Step 1 of the final theorem and the hypothesis of the
reduction), and its own decomposition is by far the largest one.
The target theorem is last, as the readme's decomposition order
prescribes. The blueprint labels:

`prop-weil-pbc-projective-line`,
`prop-weil-pbc-reduction-to-projective-line`.

*Where this feeds in.*

- **Smooth base change** ([sec-smooth-base-change],
the bad-prime computation of the eight curve assertions): clauses (a)
and (b) supply that the $p$-torsion group scheme of the Jacobian is
finite flat of order $p^{2g_{C_0}}$ (blueprint

The Kummer identification
$H^1(C,A_n(1))\cong J[\ell^n](\overline{k}_0)$ and the dual form

This is the final part of this section, used in [prop-weil-pbc-projective-line]

## Proof

$H^0(C,\Z/n)=H^0(C,\mu_n)=\mu_n(k)=\Z/n$ (algebraically closed,
primitive root). By [lem-sc-kummer-les] ($C$ is proper), $H^1(C,\Z/n)=\Pic(C)[n]$; the
degree map splits $\Pic(C)=\Pic^0(C)\times\Z$ (a base point gives a
section) and $\Z$ is torsion-free, so
$\Pic(C)[n]=\Pic^0(C)[n]=J(C)[n]$, which is $(\Z/n)^{2g}$ by
[thm-sc-jacobian-representability] and [thm-av-final](c). By
[lem-sc-second-kummer-divisors], $H^2(C,\Z/n)=\Pic(C)/n\Pic(C)=(\Z/n)\oplus J(C)/nJ(C) =\Z/n$ by [thm-av-final](d) (the $\Z/n$ is the degree part).
The vanishing is [lem-sc-arbitrary-curve-cd].

Uses: [thm-av-final], [lem-sc-arbitrary-curve-cd], [lem-sc-kummer-les], [lem-sc-second-kummer-divisors], [thm-sc-jacobian-representability]

In the split chapter of the sketch blueprint, [thm-sc-proper-cohomology]
is labeled `sk-thm-curveestimate`.

The case $U=V$ is the only one used in the applications, but the proof does
not go through if $U=V$ is imposed throughout. The extra flexibility is
needed in the general case of the proof of
[thm-nagata-conrad-elimination]: there one restricts to
$X_i=\overline{U_i}$ for a piece $U_i=f^{-1}(Y_i)$ of $U$, and even when
$U=V$ to begin with, the open $V_i=X_i\cap V$ can be strictly larger than
$U_i$. This is why
[lemma-nagata-conrad-quasi-affine-general] (Case 3) is stated for
$U\subseteq V$ and not only for $U=V$, and why
[lemma-nagata-conrad-disjointness-blowup] is needed to reduce Case 3 to
Case 2.

attrs.title: Why the theorem must allow $U\neq V$

objects.body:
[lemma-nagata-elimination-indeterminacy] (Stacks Tag 081S) is
formalized along this section, not along a module-flattening argument. The bridge is the
following argument, which uses no further input; it is carried out as the
construction [def-nagata-elimination-indeterminacy] and the proof of
[lemma-nagata-elimination-indeterminacy] at the end of this section.

Let $X$ be qcqs, let $U\subseteq X$ be a quasi-compact open and let
$q\colon Z\to X$ be separated and of finite type with a chosen isomorphism
$q^{-1}(U)\cong U$ over $U$.

1. By [lemma-nagata-conrad-schematically-dense-blowup], replace $X$
by the $U$-admissible blow-up along a finite type ideal with zero scheme
exactly $X\setminus U$, and $Z$ by its strict transform. The new $q$ is
still separated and of finite type and is still an isomorphism over $U$,
and now $U$ is scheme-theoretically dense in $X$; in particular the
density hypothesis of [thm-nagata-conrad-elimination] holds. The
final centre is recombined with this one by
[lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-comp].
1. Apply [thm-nagata-conrad-elimination] with $V=U$ and with $f$
the section $U\cong q^{-1}(U)\hookrightarrow Z$: it produces a
$U$-admissible blow-up $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$ and a
quasi-domination $(W,\widetilde f)$ of it over $Z$ extending $f$.
1. Enlarge the centre from $\mathcal I$ to $\mathcal I\cdot\mathcal I_0$
with $V(\mathcal I_0)=X\setminus U$, and let
$X'=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal I_0}(X)$. By
[cor-nagata-blowup-product-common-refinement] it dominates
$\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$, so $W$ pulls back to an open
$W'\subseteq X'$ containing $U$ and $\widetilde f$ pulls back to
$f'\colon W'\to Z$ with $\Gamma_{f'}$ closed in $X'\times_XZ$. Now
$X'\setminus V(\mathcal I\mathcal I_0)=U$, so $U$ is
scheme-theoretically dense in $X'$ and hence in $W'$.
1. The strict transform $Z'$ of $Z$ in $X'$ is, by
[lemma-nagata-strict-transform-closure-characterization], the
scheme-theoretic closure of the part of $X'\times_XZ$ lying over
$X'\setminus V(\mathcal I\mathcal I_0)=U$, that is, the
scheme-theoretic closure of $\Gamma_f$. It is therefore contained in
the closed subscheme $\Gamma_{f'}\cong W'$. So $Z'$ is a closed
subscheme of $W'$ containing $U$ as a scheme-theoretically dense open
subscheme, whence $Z'=W'$ and $Z'\to X'$ is an open immersion.

This is exactly the conclusion of
[lemma-nagata-elimination-indeterminacy]. The two external inputs are
Zariski's Main Theorem, used once in the proof of
[thm-nagata-conrad-elimination] and available in Mathlib as
`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/ZariskisMainTheorem.lean`, and the
immersion of a quasi-affine scheme into relative affine space (Stacks Tag
04II), used in [lemma-nagata-conrad-quasi-affine-affine-base] and
already formalized as
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_immersion_affineSpace_of_quasiAffine`.

attrs.title: Formalization route: Tag 081S from Theorem 2.4 and Zariski's Main Theorem

objects.body:
The dictionary of [lem-pc-zero-scheme-recd] ($\cL\mapsto D=Z(s)$)
defines an injective natural transformation
$F\hookrightarrow\Hilb^g_{X/k}$ through which the open subscheme
$W\subseteq\underline{\Hilb}^g_{X/k}$ represents $F$; the inverse is
$D\mapsto\cO(D)\otimes\operatorname{pr}_T^*\sigma_T^*\cO(D)^{-1}$
(the $\sigma$-normalization of $\cO(D)$ on $X_T$, as for the
normalized universal module in the proof of $F$'s representability). This is the precise
sense in which ``$F$ is a subsheaf of the Hilbert functor''.

attrs.title: $F$ is a subfunctor of the Hilbert functor

objects.body:
The criterion contains the complete categorical part of the
argument. It is an assertion about ordinary functors between
triangulated categories; no descent of an object or of a morphism in a
derived category is used anywhere in the chapter. The only descent
used below is ordinary descent for finite locally constant sheaves,
after all relevant complexes have been shown to be shifts of such
sheaves.

Let $C_0$ be a smooth geometrically connected affine curve and let
$\mathcal F$ be a lisse Weil sheaf that is punctually $\iota$-pure of
weight $w$. Then every
compactly supported cohomology group
$H_c^i(C,\mathcal F)$ has weights at most $w+i$. More precisely,
$H_c^0(C,\mathcal F)=0$, $H_c^2(C,\mathcal F)$ is $\iota$-pure of
weight $w+2$, and $H_c^i(C,\mathcal F)=0$ for $i\notin\{0,1,2\}$.

## Proof

The bounds in degrees zero and two are
[lem-a1-affine-hc0], [lem-a1-curve-hc2-bound]; the first is the
vanishing $H_c^0(C,\mathcal F)=0$, and the purity of weight $w+2$ in
degree two is [lem-a1-affine-hc2-pure].
There is no cohomology outside degrees zero through two, by the
cohomological range [lem-zl-affine-curve-range] of an affine curve
applied to the (constructible) lisse sheaf $\mathcal F$.

For degree one choose the finite map of
[lem-a1-finite-map-curve]. By
[lem-a1-reduction-composition], the cohomology to be bounded is
$H_c^1(\mathbf A^1,\mathcal K)$, where
$\mathcal K=g_*j_!\mathcal F$.
On the open
$W_0=\mathbf A^1\setminus(B\cup g(C'_0\setminus C_0))$
the restriction of the transported complex is lisse and pure of weight
$w$, by [lem-a1-reduction-lisse-pure].
For the inclusion $a:W_0\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1$,
the open–closed triangle of [def-weil-open-closed-recollement] (at $\Qlb$ for Weil complexes,
[prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages]) and the finite-boundary
vanishing [lem-a1-finite-boundary-cohomology] give

$$
H_c^1(W,a^*\mathcal K)\twoheadrightarrow
H_c^1(\mathbf A^1,\mathcal K).
$$

It suffices to bound the source.

Apply [lem-a1-unramified-at-infinity] to the lisse sheaf
$a^*\mathcal K$ on $W_0$. After a finite constant extension it gives a
dense open $v:V_0\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1$ and a lisse sheaf
$\mathcal E$ on $V_0$, punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$ and
unramified at infinity, with a Frobenius-equivariant surjection
$H_c^1(V,\mathcal E)\twoheadrightarrow H_c^1(W,a^*\mathcal K)$. It
suffices to bound $H_c^1(V,\mathcal E)$ by $w+1$.

Pass to the middle extension $v_*\mathcal E$, as in the sketch. Let
$i:Z_0\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1$ be the finite complement of $V_0$.
The boundary sequence [prop-a1-curve-boundary-sequence] for $v$ gives
the Frobenius-equivariant exact sequence

$$
H_c^0(Z,i^*v_*\mathcal E)\longrightarrow H_c^1(V,\mathcal E)
\longrightarrow H_c^1(\mathbf A^1,v_*\mathcal E)\longrightarrow0 .
$$

The stalks of $i^*v_*\mathcal E$ have weights at most $w$ by the
boundary semicontinuity [lem-wf-boundary-semicontinuity] (with
$\beta=w$), so $H_c^0(Z,i^*v_*\mathcal E)$, and hence its image in
$H_c^1(V,\mathcal E)$, has weights at most $w$ by
[lem-a1-finite-boundary-weights] and
[lem-a1-subquotient-extension-bounds]. The right-hand group has
weights at most $w+1$ by the affine-line estimate for the middle
extension [thm-a1-line-middle-extension-upper]; this is where the
composition filtration, the exactness of the middle extension at a
fixed pure weight, and the Fourier bound of each factor enter. By
[lem-a1-extension-bounds], $H_c^1(V,\mathcal E)$ has weights at most
$w+1$.

The successive surjections preserve this bound by
[lem-a1-subquotient-extension-bounds].
Finally finite constant extensions preserve and reflect weight
bounds, as verified in [lem-a1-weight-bound-constant-extension].
This proves the degree-one assertion over the original field and
completes the proof.

In the setting of [def-per-support-condition], let the base field $k$ be
perfect (in the applications $k=k_0=\mathbf F_q$ or its algebraic
closure) and let $X=C$ be a smooth separated $k$-scheme of pure dimension
one, for instance $C=A_0$ or a dense open of it. For $k=k_0$ the objects
may equally be Weil complexes on $C_0$, in the conventions of
[rem-dl-a1-conventions]. All conditions below concern cohomology sheaves,
and the operations used in the proof carry the Weil structure, so the
statements hold verbatim in that case. "Sheaf" means a constructible
$\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-sheaf on $C$ (a Weil sheaf in the Weil case),
that is, an object of the heart of the standard t-structure of
[prop-constructible-truncations]. A sheaf is *punctual* if its support is
a finite set of closed points. Let ${}^pD^{\le0}(C)$ and
${}^pD^{\ge0}(C)$ be the classes of [def-per-perverse-subcategories].

1. (*Description.*) For $K\in D^b_c(C,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$,
   $$
   \begin{aligned}
   K\in{}^pD^{\le0}(C)&\iff \mathcal H^aK=0\ (a>0)\ \text{and}\
   \mathcal H^0K\ \text{is punctual},\\
   K\in{}^pD^{\ge0}(C)&\iff \mathcal H^aK=0\ (a<-1)\ \text{and}\
   \mathcal H^{-1}K\ \text{has no nonzero punctual subsheaf}.
   \end{aligned}
   $$
2. (*t-structure.*) The pair $\bigl({}^pD^{\le0}(C),{}^pD^{\ge0}(C)\bigr)$
   is a bounded t-structure on $D^b_c(C,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ in the
   sense of [def-weil-t-structure]. Its heart
   $$
   \mathrm{Perv}(C):={}^pD^{\le0}(C)\cap{}^pD^{\ge0}(C)
   $$
   (the perverse heart candidate of [def-per-perverse-subcategories]) is
   an abelian category.
3. (*The heart.*) $K\in\mathrm{Perv}(C)$ if and only if
   $\mathcal H^aK=0$ for $a\notin\{-1,0\}$, $\mathcal H^0K$ is punctual,
   and $\mathcal H^{-1}K$ has no nonzero punctual subsheaf.
4. (*Basic objects.*) If $j:U\hookrightarrow C$ is a dense open immersion
   and $\mathcal N$ is a lisse sheaf on $U$, then the middle extension
   $(j_*\mathcal N)[1]$ of [def-wf-middle-extension] lies in
   $\mathrm{Perv}(C)$. If $x$ is a closed point with inclusion $i_x$ and
   $E$ is a sheaf on $x$ (a finite-dimensional continuous
   representation of the Galois group, respectively of the Weil group,
   of $k(x)$), then $i_{x*}E$, placed in degree $0$, lies in
   $\mathrm{Perv}(C)$.
5. (*Exact sequences.*) For $P\in\mathrm{Perv}(C)$ the sequence
   $0\to(\mathcal H^{-1}P)[1]\to P\to(\mathcal H^0P)[0]\to0$ is exact in
   $\mathrm{Perv}(C)$. A short exact sequence $0\to Q\to P\to R\to0$ in
   $\mathrm{Perv}(C)$ gives an exact sequence of sheaves
   $$
   0\to\mathcal H^{-1}Q\to\mathcal H^{-1}P\to\mathcal H^{-1}R
   \to\mathcal H^0Q\to\mathcal H^0P\to\mathcal H^0R\to0 .
   $$

## Proof

*Step 0: two facts about sheaves on a smooth curve.* (i) Let $V$ be a
smooth curve (every component of dimension one) and $\mathcal M$ a lisse
sheaf on $V$. Then $\mathcal M$ has no nonzero punctual subsheaf, and in
particular a punctual lisse sheaf on $V$ is zero. Indeed, let
$\mathcal G\subset\mathcal M$ be supported on a finite set $S$ and let
$s$ be a section of $\mathcal G$ over a connected étale $W\to V$ on which
$\mathcal M$ is constant. Then $s$ vanishes on the complement of the
preimage of $S$, which is dense in $W$. A section of a constant sheaf on
a connected scheme that vanishes on a nonempty open is zero, so $s=0$.
(ii) Every sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $C$ has a largest punctual subsheaf
$\mathcal F_{\mathrm p}$, and $\mathcal F/\mathcal F_{\mathrm p}$ has no
nonzero punctual subsheaf. Choose a dense open $j:U\hookrightarrow C$ on
which $\mathcal F$ is lisse. Its complement $Z$ is a finite set of closed
points, because $C$ has pure dimension one. Put
$\mathcal F_{\mathrm p}:=\ker(\mathcal F\to j_*j^*\mathcal F)$. This
kernel vanishes on $U$, so it is punctual. If $\mathcal G\subset\mathcal F$
is punctual, then $j^*\mathcal G=0$ by (i), so $\mathcal G\subset
\mathcal F_{\mathrm p}$. The quotient embeds in $j_*j^*\mathcal F$. A
section of $j_*\mathcal M$ over $W$ is a section of $\mathcal M$ over
$W\times_CU$, so a punctual subsheaf of $j_*\mathcal M$ restricts to zero
on $U$ and is therefore zero. The same argument shows that $j_*\mathcal M$
has no nonzero punctual subsheaf for any lisse $\mathcal M$ on $U$.

*Step 1: the support condition.* The supports of constructible sheaves on
$C$ have dimension $\le1$. So in [def-per-support-condition] the
inequalities for $i\ge1$ are automatic. For $i=0$ the inequality says that
$\mathcal H^0$ is punctual, and for $i<0$ it says that $\mathcal H^{-i}=0$.
This gives
$$
\operatorname{SuppCon}(N)\iff\mathcal H^aN=0\ (a>0)\ \text{and}\
\mathcal H^0N\ \text{is punctual},
$$
which is the first half of (1). Now fix a dense open $j:U\hookrightarrow C$
on which all $\mathcal H^aN$ are lisse, with finite closed complement
$i:Z\hookrightarrow C$. Stalks at the points of $U$ and of $Z$ detect
vanishing, and a lisse punctual sheaf on $U$ is zero by Step 0(i). Hence
$$
\operatorname{SuppCon}(N)\iff \mathcal H^a(j^*N)=0\ (a\ge0)\ \text{and}\
\mathcal H^a(i^*N)=0\ (a>0).\tag{$*$}
$$

*Step 2: the duals on $U$ and on $Z$.* By [cor-pur-adic-and-rational-smooth-dualizing-complexes],
$\omega_U\cong\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell(1)[2]$. Restriction to an open
commutes with internal Hom, and $j^*\omega_C=\omega_U$, so
$j^*D_C=D_Uj^*$. For a lisse sheaf $\mathcal L$ on $U$,
[lem-per-dual-lisse-tensor] with $K=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ gives
$D_U\mathcal L\cong\omega_U\otimes\mathcal L^\vee=\mathcal L^\vee(1)[2]$.
Now let $M$ have lisse cohomology sheaves on $U$. Induction on the number
of nonzero cohomology sheaves, using the truncation triangles
$\tau^{\le n-1}M\to M\to\mathcal H^nM[-n]\to$ of
[prop-constructible-truncations] and the exactness of $D_U$, gives
$$
\mathcal H^a(D_UM)\cong\bigl(\mathcal H^{-2-a}M\bigr)^\vee(1),
$$
and these sheaves are again lisse. The reduced scheme $Z$ is a finite
disjoint union of spectra of perfect fields, hence smooth of dimension
zero, so $\omega_Z=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ by
[cor-pur-adic-and-rational-smooth-dualizing-complexes]. Sheaves on $Z$ are finite-dimensional
representations, and $R\mathcal Hom(-,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ is
computed on geometric stalks by the exact linear dual. Hence
$\mathcal H^a(D_ZM)\cong(\mathcal H^{-a}M)^\vee$.

*Step 3: the cosupport condition.* Let $K\in D^b_c(C,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$,
and choose $U$ and $Z$ as in Step 1 for $K$. By Step 2 this choice also
serves for $N:=D_CK$ on $U$. By [lem-weil-closed-costalk-duality] applied
to $D_CK$, and by the biduality of [thm-coef-qbar-verdier] on $C$ and on
$Z$, we get $Ri^!K\cong Ri^!D_CD_CK\cong D_Zi^*D_CK$, hence
$i^*D_CK\cong D_ZRi^!K$. The object $Ri^!=D_Zi^*D_C$ is constructible by
[thm-coef-qbar-verdier]. By $(*)$ and Step 2,
$$
\operatorname{CosuppCon}(K)\iff
\text{(a) }\mathcal H^b(j^*K)=0\ (b\le-2)\ \text{and (b) }
\mathcal H^b(Ri^!K)=0\ (b<0).
$$
Assume (a). The closed-support triangle, [prop-sf-localization-all-stages]
(on the $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-category, with Weil-equivariant arrows in the Weil case;
at each finite stage it is [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle]), with $Rj_*j^*K$ constructible,
reads
$$
i_*Ri^!K\to K\to Rj_*j^*K\to .
$$
Since $j^*K\in D^{\ge-1}$ and $j_*$ is left exact, $Rj_*j^*K\in D^{\ge-1}$
and $\mathcal H^{-1}(Rj_*j^*K)=j_*j^*\mathcal H^{-1}K$. Apply the exact
functor $i^*$ (note $i^*i_*=\mathrm{id}$) to the long exact sequence of
cohomology sheaves. This gives $\mathcal H^b(Ri^!K)\cong i^*\mathcal H^bK$
for $b\le-2$, and
$$
0\to\mathcal H^{-1}(Ri^!K)\to i^*\mathcal H^{-1}K\to
i^*j_*j^*\mathcal H^{-1}K .
$$
The second map is $i^*$ of the unit $\mathcal H^{-1}K\to j_*j^*\mathcal
H^{-1}K$. That unit is an isomorphism on $U$, so its kernel is
$i_*\mathcal H^{-1}(Ri^!K)$, which is the largest punctual subsheaf of
$\mathcal H^{-1}K$ by Step 0(ii). So under (a), condition (b) says that
$\mathcal H^bK$ vanishes on $Z$ for $b\le-2$ and that $\mathcal H^{-1}K$
has no nonzero punctual subsheaf. Together with (a) on $U$, this is the
second half of (1).

*Step 4: t-structure.* Write ${}^pD^{\le n}$ and ${}^pD^{\ge n}$ for the
shifts of [def-per-perverse-subcategories]. By (1),
$B\in{}^pD^{\ge1}(C)$ if and only if $\mathcal H^bB=0$ for $b<0$ and
$\mathcal H^0B$ has no nonzero punctual subsheaf. Both classes are
strictly full, and the stability under shifts in axiom 1 of
[def-weil-t-structure] can be read off (1).

For axiom 2, let $A\in{}^pD^{\le0}$ and $B\in{}^pD^{\ge1}$. Then $A$ is in
standard degrees $\le0$ and $B$ in standard degrees $\ge0$. The truncation
axioms of the standard t-structure of [prop-constructible-truncations]
give $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B)=\operatorname{Hom}(\tau^{\ge0}A,B)
=\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal H^0A,\tau^{\le0}B)=
\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal H^0A,\mathcal H^0B)$, a Hom of sheaves. The
image of a map $\mathcal H^0A\to\mathcal H^0B$ is a punctual subsheaf of
$\mathcal H^0B$, hence zero.

For axiom 3, let $K$ be given, put $K'=\tau^{\le0}K$ and
$\mathcal F=\mathcal H^0K$, and let $\mathcal F_{\mathrm p}$ be as in
Step 0(ii). Complete the composite
$K'\to\mathcal F[0]\to(\mathcal F/\mathcal F_{\mathrm p})[0]$ to a
triangle $A\to K'\to(\mathcal F/\mathcal F_{\mathrm p})[0]\to$. Its long
exact sequence gives $\mathcal H^aA=\mathcal H^aK$ for $a<0$,
$\mathcal H^0A=\mathcal F_{\mathrm p}$ and $\mathcal H^aA=0$ for $a>0$.
So $A\in{}^pD^{\le0}$. The octahedral axiom applied to
$A\to K'\to K$ gives a triangle $A\to K\to B\to$, together with a triangle
$(\mathcal F/\mathcal F_{\mathrm p})[0]\to B\to\tau^{\ge1}K\to$. Then
$\mathcal H^bB=0$ for $b<0$ and
$\mathcal H^0B=\mathcal F/\mathcal F_{\mathrm p}$, which has no punctual
subsheaf by Step 0(ii). So $B\in{}^pD^{\ge1}$, which is axiom 3 with
$B=(B[1])[-1]$.

Finally, if $K$ has standard cohomology in degrees $[a,b]$, then (1)
gives $K\in{}^pD^{\le b+1}\cap{}^pD^{\ge a}$, so the t-structure is
bounded. Its heart is abelian by [prop-weil-heart-abelian]. This proves
(2), and (3) is the intersection of the two conditions in (1).

*Step 5: basic objects.* $(j_*\mathcal N)[1]$ has only
$\mathcal H^{-1}=j_*\mathcal N$, which has no nonzero punctual subsheaf
by Step 0(ii). $i_{x*}E$ has only $\mathcal H^0=i_{x*}E$, which is
punctual. By (3) both lie in the heart, which is (4).

*Step 6: exact sequences.* In the heart of a t-structure, a sequence
$0\to Q\to P\to R\to0$ is short exact exactly when it extends to a
distinguished triangle $Q\to P\to R\to Q[1]$, by part (4) of
[lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles]. For $P\in\mathrm{Perv}(C)$
the standard truncation triangle is
$(\mathcal H^{-1}P)[1]\to P\to(\mathcal H^0P)[0]\to$. Its outer terms lie
in the heart by (3), which gives the first claim of (5). For a short exact
sequence in the heart, the long exact cohomology sequence of the
corresponding triangle, together with the vanishing of $\mathcal H^a$ for
$a\notin\{-1,0\}$ on all three terms, gives the displayed six-term
sequence.

attrs.title: The perverse t-structure on a smooth curve and its heart

objects.body:
Let $C_0$ be a smooth geometrically connected curve and let
$\mathcal F$ be a lisse Weil sheaf that is punctually $\iota$-pure of
weight $w$. Then every $H_c^r(C,\mathcal F)$ has weights at most
$w+r$.

## Proof

Apply [prop-a1-middle-extension-curve-upper] to the identity open
immersion $C_0\hookrightarrow C_0$; its middle extension is
$\mathcal F$ itself, giving the bound $H_c^r(C,\mathcal F)\leq w+r$.

attrs.title: Compact-support upper bound on a curve

objects.body:
In the conventions of [rem-dl-a1-conventions], let
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi$ be the Fourier–Deligne transform of
[def-fd-transform] from the line $A_0$ to the dual line $A'_0$, and
write $\mathrm{Perv}(A_0)$, $\mathrm{Perv}(A'_0)$ for the hearts of the
perverse t-structure of [thm-a1-curve-perverse-heart], built from the
classes ${}^pD^{\le0}$, ${}^pD^{\ge0}$ of
[def-per-perverse-subcategories]. Then $\operatorname{FT}_\psi$ is
t-exact:

$$
\operatorname{FT}_\psi\bigl({}^pD^{\le0}(A_0)\bigr)\subset{}^pD^{\le0}(A'_0),
\qquad
\operatorname{FT}_\psi\bigl({}^pD^{\ge0}(A_0)\bigr)\subset{}^pD^{\ge0}(A'_0),
$$

so it sends $\mathrm{Perv}(A_0)$ into $\mathrm{Perv}(A'_0)$, and
likewise $\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}$ (from $A'_0$ to $A_0$) is
t-exact and sends $\mathrm{Perv}(A'_0)$ into $\mathrm{Perv}(A_0)$. This
sharpens the amplitude bound $[-1,1]$ of [thm-fd-fourier-perverse] to
amplitude $0$. Moreover, with the Tate twist of [def-wf-tate-twist],
the functors

$$
\operatorname{FT}_\psi:\mathrm{Perv}(A_0)\rightleftarrows\mathrm{Perv}(A'_0):
G:=\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}(-)(1)
$$

are mutually quasi-inverse exact equivalences of abelian categories.

## Proof

Throughout, a class is tested after the geometric base change to $k$:
cohomology sheaves commute with this pullback, supports and their
dimensions are unchanged, and the transform commutes with it by
[lem-fd-base-change]. By [thm-fd-transform-well-defined] the transform
is an exact triangulated functor with values in $D^b_c$.

*Step 0: the upper class on a curve.* On a curve every support has
dimension $\le1$, so the support condition of
[def-per-support-condition] says exactly: $K\in{}^pD^{\le0}$ if and
only if $\mathcal H^aK=0$ for $a>0$ and $\mathcal H^0K$ has finite
support. This class is stable under the shifts $[n]$, $n\ge0$, and under
extensions: for a triangle $K'\to K\to K''\to$ the long exact sequence
of cohomology sheaves gives
$\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal H^aK\subset
\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal H^aK'\cup\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal H^aK''$.
It is also stable under the twist $(1)$, which is the tensor with a
lisse sheaf of rank one and so preserves each cohomology sheaf's support.

*Step 1: $\operatorname{FT}_\psi$ preserves the upper class.* Let
$K\in{}^pD^{\le0}(A)$. The ordinary truncation triangles exhibit $K$ as
an iterated extension of $\mathcal H^0K$ (finite support, degree $0$)
and of objects $\mathcal G[m]$ with $\mathcal G=\mathcal H^{-m}K$ a
constructible sheaf and $m\ge1$. By Step 0 and exactness of the
transform it suffices to treat (a) $\mathcal G[1]$ for an arbitrary
constructible sheaf $\mathcal G$ (then $\mathcal G[m]=\mathcal G[1][m-1]$
follows), and (b) a sheaf $\mathcal G$ of finite support in degree $0$.

For a geometric point $\xi$ of $A'$ the stalk formula
[lem-fd-stalk-formula] (with $r=1$) gives

$$
\operatorname{FT}_\psi(\mathcal G)_{\xi}\cong
R\Gamma_c\bigl(A,\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L_{\psi(\xi x)}\bigr)[1].
$$

(b) If $\mathcal G$ has finite support, so has
$\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L_{\psi(\xi x)}$, whose compact-support
cohomology is the direct sum of its stalks, in degree $0$ (a
zero-dimensional scheme over $k$ has no higher cohomology). So every
stalk of $\operatorname{FT}_\psi(\mathcal G)$ is concentrated in degree
$-1$, and $\operatorname{FT}_\psi(\mathcal G)\in{}^pD^{\le0}(A')$ by
Step 0.

(a) For a constructible sheaf $\mathcal G$ the twisted groups
$H^i_c(A,\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L_{\psi(\xi x)})$ vanish for
$i\notin\{0,1,2\}$ by [lem-zl-affine-curve-range], so the stalks of
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi(\mathcal G[1])$ live in degrees $-2,-1,0$, and

$$
\mathcal H^0\bigl(\operatorname{FT}_\psi(\mathcal G[1])\bigr)_{\xi}
\cong H^2_c\bigl(A,\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L_{\psi(\xi x)}\bigr).
$$

It remains to see that this is nonzero for only finitely many $\xi$ (the
sheaf $\mathcal H^0$ being constructible, its support is then finite).
Let $j:U\hookrightarrow A$ be a dense open on which $\mathcal G$ is
lisse, with finite complement $Z$. In the sequence
$0\to j_!j^*\mathcal G\to\mathcal G\to i_*i^*\mathcal G\to0$, tensored
with the lisse $\mathcal L_{\psi(\xi x)}$, the third term has no
$H^1_c$ or $H^2_c$ (finite support, as in (b)), so

$$
H^2_c\bigl(A,\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L_{\psi(\xi x)}\bigr)\cong
H^2_c\bigl(U,\mathcal G|_U\otimes\mathcal L_{\psi(\xi x)}|_U\bigr)
\cong\bigl(V\otimes\chi_\xi\bigr)_{\pi_1(U)}(-1)
$$

by [lem-a1-affine-hc2], where $V=\mathcal G_{\bar\eta}$ and $\chi_\xi$ is
the rank-one character of $\mathcal L_{\psi(\xi x)}|_U$. These
coinvariants are nonzero exactly when $V$ has a quotient isomorphic to
$\chi_\xi^{-1}=\chi_{-\xi}$ ([lem-fd-as-characters]:
$\mathcal L_{\psi(\xi x)}^{-1}\cong\mathcal L_{\psi(-\xi x)}$). The
characters $\chi_a$ are pairwise distinct: if $\chi_a=\chi_b$ with
$a\neq b$, then by [lem-fd-as-characters]
$\mathcal L_{\psi((a-b)x)}$ is trivial on $U$, hence on $A$ (a rank-one
lisse sheaf on the normal connected $A$ that is trivial on a dense open
is trivial, its global section extending), contradicting
$H^0(A,\mathcal L_{\psi((a-b)x)})=0$ from
[lem-fd-cohomology-affine-line-character]. If $\chi_{a_1},\dots,\chi_{a_n}$
are pairwise distinct quotients of $V$, the combined map
$V\to\bigoplus_i\chi_{a_i}$ is surjective (its image is a submodule of a
sum of pairwise non-isomorphic simple modules projecting onto each
summand, hence the whole sum), so $n\le\dim V=\operatorname{rank}\mathcal G|_U$.
Hence $\mathcal H^0\operatorname{FT}_\psi(\mathcal G[1])$ has finite
support, and $\operatorname{FT}_\psi(\mathcal G[1])\in{}^pD^{\le0}(A')$ by
Step 0. This proves
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi({}^pD^{\le0}(A))\subset{}^pD^{\le0}(A')$. The
argument uses nothing about $\psi$ beyond its nontriviality, so it
applies equally to $\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}$ from $A'$ to $A$, and
by Step 0 also to $G=\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}(-)(1)$.

*Step 2: $\operatorname{FT}_\psi$ is an equivalence with quasi-inverse
$G$.* Fourier inversion [lem-fd-inversion] with $r=1$ gives
$\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K)\cong K(-1)$, hence
$G\circ\operatorname{FT}_\psi\cong\mathrm{id}$; applied to the character
$\psi^{-1}$ it gives
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}(M)\cong M(-1)$, and
since the twist is the pullback of a sheaf on the base, linearity over the
base [prop-base-linear] gives
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi(M(1))\cong\operatorname{FT}_\psi(M)(1)$, so
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi\circ G\cong\mathrm{id}$.

*Step 3: the lower class.* In a t-structure, as provided by
[thm-a1-curve-perverse-heart], one has
${}^pD^{\ge0}=\{K:\operatorname{Hom}(M,K)=0\ \text{for all}\ M\in{}^pD^{\le-1}\}$.
Indeed $\subset$ is the orthogonality axiom; conversely, if $K$ is
right orthogonal to ${}^pD^{\le-1}$, the map
$\tau^{\le-1}K\to K$ in the truncation triangle
$\tau^{\le-1}K\to K\to\tau^{\ge0}K\to$ vanishes, so the triangle splits
and $\tau^{\le-1}K[1]$ is a direct summand of $\tau^{\ge0}K$; it
therefore lies in ${}^pD^{\le-2}\cap{}^pD^{\ge0}$, which is zero by
orthogonality, so $K\cong\tau^{\ge0}K$. Now let $K\in{}^pD^{\ge0}(A)$
and $M\in{}^pD^{\le-1}(A')$. By Step 2,

$$
\operatorname{Hom}\bigl(M,\operatorname{FT}_\psi K\bigr)\cong
\operatorname{Hom}\bigl(GM,K\bigr),
$$

and $GM=G(M[-1])[1]\in{}^pD^{\le-1}(A)$ by Step 1 (the classes are
compatible with shifts), so the right-hand side vanishes. Hence
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi K\in{}^pD^{\ge0}(A')$. The same argument with
the roles of $\psi,\psi^{-1}$ and of the two lines exchanged (and the
twist, which preserves ${}^pD^{\ge0}$ by the same orthogonality since
$(-1)$ is its inverse) shows that $\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}$ and $G$
preserve ${}^pD^{\ge0}$.

*Step 4: the hearts.* By Steps 1 and 3, $\operatorname{FT}_\psi$ and $G$
are t-exact, hence restrict to functors between $\mathrm{Perv}(A_0)$ and
$\mathrm{Perv}(A'_0)$, which are quasi-inverse by Step 2. A t-exact
triangulated functor induces an exact functor on the abelian hearts of
[thm-a1-curve-perverse-heart], the short exact sequences of a heart
being the distinguished triangles with all three vertices in it. So
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi$ is an exact equivalence
$\mathrm{Perv}(A_0)\simeq\mathrm{Perv}(A'_0)$ with quasi-inverse $G$.
