objects.body:
In the conventions of [rem-dl-a1-conventions], let
$j:U_0\hookrightarrow A_0=\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ be a dense open immersion
and let $\mathcal F$ be a lisse Weil sheaf on $U_0$, punctually
$\iota$-pure of weight $w$ ([def-weil-punctual-weights]) and
unramified at infinity. Then, for the ordinary middle extension
$j_*\mathcal F$ of [def-wf-middle-extension] and the compactly
supported cohomology of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], for
every integer $r$

$$
H_c^r(A,j_*\mathcal F)\quad\text{has weights at most }w+r
$$

in the sense of [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights]. More precisely,
$H_c^0(A,j_*\mathcal F)=0$, $H_c^2(A,j_*\mathcal F)$ is $\iota$-pure of
weight $w+2$ (possibly zero), $H_c^r(A,j_*\mathcal F)=0$ for
$r\notin\{0,1,2\}$, and $H_c^1(A,j_*\mathcal F)$ has weights at most
$w+1$.

## Proof

*Degrees other than one.* $A_0$ is a smooth geometrically connected
affine curve, so [lem-a1-middle-extension-endpoints] applied to $j$
gives $H_c^0(A,j_*\mathcal F)=0$, the vanishing outside degrees
$0,1,2$, and the purity of weight $w+2$ of $H_c^2(A,j_*\mathcal F)$.
These are the assertions in all degrees $r\neq1$.

*Step 1: a finite constant extension is harmless.* Let
$k'_0=\mathbf F_{q^m}$ and replace $U_0\subset A_0$ and $\mathcal F$
by their base changes to $k'_0$. The geometric objects $U\subset A$,
the geometric generic stalk with its geometric monodromy, the sheaf
$j_*\mathcal F$ on $A$ and the group $H_c^1(A,j_*\mathcal F)$ do not
change; only the Weil structure is replaced by its $m$-th power, so
the Frobenius on $H_c^1$ becomes $F^m$. The base-changed sheaf is still
lisse, punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$ (a closed point over $x$
of degree $e$ over $\kappa(x)$ has local Frobenius $F_x^e$ and norm
$q_x^e$) and unramified at infinity (the inertia at $\infty$ is a
subgroup of the unchanged geometric fundamental group). By
[lem-a1-weight-bound-constant-extension] with $b=w+1$, a bound $w+1$
for $H_c^1(A,j_*\mathcal F)$ over $k'_0$ implies the bound over
$k_0$. We may therefore pass to finite constant extensions freely.

*Step 2: a composition filtration.* By
[lem-a1-geometric-constituent-reduction], after a finite constant
extension $\mathcal F$ has a finite filtration by lisse Weil subsheaves

$$
0=\mathcal F^0\subset\mathcal F^1\subset\cdots\subset\mathcal F^n=\mathcal F
$$

whose graded pieces $\mathcal M_i=\mathcal F^i/\mathcal F^{i-1}$, after
discarding repeated terms, are nonzero, geometrically irreducible and
punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$. Each $\mathcal F^i$ is
punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$ as well: at a closed point $x$
the stalk $\mathcal F^i_{\bar x}$ is an $F_x$-stable subspace of
$\mathcal F_{\bar x}$, so its eigenvalues are among those of
$\mathcal F_{\bar x}$ by [lem-a1-spectrum-exact-sequence]. Each
$\mathcal M_i$ is unramified at infinity: the inertia group at
$\infty$ acts trivially on $\mathcal F_{\bar\eta}$, hence on its
subquotient $(\mathcal M_i)_{\bar\eta}$
([def-wf-fundamental-representation]).

*Step 3: exactness of the middle extension along the filtration.* For
each $i$ the sequence $0\to\mathcal F^{i-1}\to\mathcal F^i\to
\mathcal M_i\to0$ consists of lisse Weil sheaves on $U_0$ that are all
punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$. By [p-dl-a1-exact] (with
$C_0=A_0$),

$$
0\longrightarrow j_*\mathcal F^{i-1}\longrightarrow j_*\mathcal F^i
\longrightarrow j_*\mathcal M_i\longrightarrow0
$$

is an exact sequence of Weil sheaves on $A_0$. Its long exact
sequence of compactly supported cohomology, which is
Frobenius-equivariant because it comes from a triangle of Weil
complexes, contains the exact segment

$$
H_c^1(A,j_*\mathcal F^{i-1})\longrightarrow H_c^1(A,j_*\mathcal F^{i})
\longrightarrow H_c^1(A,j_*\mathcal M_i).
$$

Hence $H_c^1(A,j_*\mathcal F^i)$ is an extension of a
Frobenius-stable subobject of $H_c^1(A,j_*\mathcal M_i)$ by a
Frobenius-stable quotient of $H_c^1(A,j_*\mathcal F^{i-1})$. By
[lem-a1-subquotient-extension-bounds] and [lem-a1-extension-bounds],
induction on $i$ (starting from $H_c^1(A,j_*\mathcal F^0)=0$) shows
that the bound $w+1$ for $H_c^1(A,j_*\mathcal F)$ follows from the
same bound for every $H_c^1(A,j_*\mathcal M_i)$. No splitting of the
filtration is used.

*Step 4: one factor.* Let $\mathcal M=\mathcal M_i$; it is a nonzero
lisse Weil sheaf on $U_0$, geometrically irreducible, punctually
$\iota$-pure of weight $w$ and unramified at infinity. A
geometrically irreducible sheaf is irreducible as a Weil sheaf, since a
Weil-stable subspace of $\mathcal M_{\bar\eta}$ is stable under the
geometric fundamental group.

(a) *$\mathcal M$ geometrically constant.* The geometric fundamental
representation is then trivial and irreducible, so $\mathcal M$ has
rank one and is a constant Weil twist in the sense of
[def-wf-constant-weil-twist]. By [lem-a1-exceptional-constituents]
(the case without Artin–Schreier factor), $H_c^1(U,\mathcal M)$ has
weights at most $w+1$. The boundary sequence
[prop-a1-curve-boundary-sequence] for $j$ gives a
Frobenius-equivariant surjection
$H_c^1(U,\mathcal M)\twoheadrightarrow H_c^1(A,j_*\mathcal M)$, so
$H_c^1(A,j_*\mathcal M)$ has weights at most $w+1$ by
[lem-a1-subquotient-extension-bounds]. (In fact $j_*\mathcal M$ is the
lisse constant twist on $A_0$ and $H_c^1(A,j_*\mathcal M)=0$, as in
Step 1 of the proof of [lem-a1-exceptional-constituents]; only the
bound is needed.)

(b) *$\mathcal M$ not geometrically constant.* Since $\mathcal M$ is
irreducible, unramified at infinity and not geometrically constant,
it is constituent-nonexceptional by
[lem-a1-unramified-nonexceptional]; by part (1) of
[lem-a1-constituent-nonexceptional-comparison] its middle extension
$j_*\mathcal M$ is Fourier-nonexceptional. Thus $\mathcal M$ is an
irreducible lisse Weil sheaf on $U_0$, unramified at infinity,
punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$, with irreducible geometric
fundamental representation and Fourier-nonexceptional middle
extension, and [cor-a1-fourier-middle-hc1] shows that
$H_c^1(A,j_*\mathcal M)$ has weights at most $w+1$.

*Conclusion.* By Step 4 every factor satisfies the bound $w+1$; by
Step 3 so does $H_c^1(A,j_*\mathcal F)$ over the extended field, and
by Step 1 over $k_0$. Together with the degrees other than one this
proves the theorem.

objects.body:
Let $f:X\to S$ admit a compactification
$X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{r}S$ between
Noetherian schemes, with $j$ open and $r$ proper of finite
type. The ambient functor $Rf_!=Rr_*j_!$ on ordinary derived
categories of etale $A$-module sheaves has a right adjoint,
denoted $f^\times$. No restriction to a constructible
subcategory is made in this assertion.
The notation refers to ordinary derived categories, and ordinary etale compact supports.

## Proof

The extension by zero in [def-amb-etale-compact-support]
is exact and commutes with coproducts, as is checked at geometric
stalks. The fibre dimensions of the fixed finite-type proper
morphism $r$ have a finite bound, so
[lem-amb-proper-coproducts] makes $Rf_!$ an
exact coproduct-preserving functor. Apply the ordinary
Brown representability theorem for the derived category of a
Grothendieck abelian category: an exact functor out of such a
derived category which preserves coproducts has a right adjoint.
Here the abelian category consists of sheaves of $A$-modules;
it is Grothendieck since filtered colimits are exact and the free
module sheaves on a small set of site objects form a generating
set. The precise homological-algebra input is
[Stacks Project,
Proposition 19.15.2, Tag 0F5Y](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F5Y) (Section 19.15, Brown representability
and Grothendieck abelian categories), about ordinary triangulated
categories.

Representability is applied to the functor
$M\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_!M,K)$, for each $K$.
Yoneda makes the representing objects functorial in $K$,
and the identity of a representing object gives the counit.
The representing bijection then gives the unit, and the two
triangle identities follow by applying that bijection to an
identity map. Finally the coherent comparisons of the left
functors in [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] give the
corresponding unique comparisons of right adjoints. Thus this
construction makes no additional assumption about $f^\times K$.

On the whole ordinary derived categories of etale $A$-modules,

$$
Rq_*\dashv q^*(1)[2]
\qquad(q:\mathbf P^1_S\to S).
$$

The counit is $\epsilon$ of [def-amb-p1-trace].
The notation refers to the projective line, and Tate twists.

## Proof

Write $F=Rq_*$, $G=q^*(1)[2]$. Use the notation
and the map $\delta$ of
[lem-amb-p1-diagonal-integrals]. For an arbitrary
complex $M$ on $P$, define

$$
\eta_M:M=R(p_2)_*\Delta_*M
\xrightarrow{R(p_2)_*(\delta\otimes p_1^*M)}
R(p_2)_*p_1^*M(1)[2]
\xrightarrow{\sim} q^*Rq_*M(1)[2]=GFM.
$$

Here $\Delta_*M\cong\Delta_*A\otimes_A^Lp_1^*M$
by the closed-immersion projection formula (or directly on
geometric stalks), and the last arrow is proper base change
[cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-finite], extended to
complexes as in [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection].
Thus $\eta$ is a natural transformation on all complexes.
Set $\epsilon$ equal to the natural transformation in
[def-amb-p1-trace].

We verify both triangles, keeping track of the coordinate
integrated in each. For the first triangle, the composite
$\epsilon_{FM}\circ F\eta_M$, after proper base change,
the projection formula and the composition
$R(qp_1)_*\cong Rq_*Rp_{1*}$ of
[lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition] (item (5)), is

$$
\begin{split}
Rq_*M
&=R(qp_1)_*\Delta_*M\\
&\longrightarrow R(qp_1)_*p_1^*M(1)[2]\\
&\cong Rq_*\bigl(M\otimes_A^LR(p_1)_*A_W(1)[2]\bigr)\\
&\xrightarrow{Rq_*(1_M\otimes t_{p_1})}Rq_*M.
\end{split}
$$

By the base-change compatibility of
[thm-amb-p1-decomposition], $t_{p_1}$ is the
pullback of $t_q$ along $q:P\to S$, under
the proper base-change identification for $p_1$.
Indeed $\eta$ first sums over the first coordinate,
whereas $\epsilon_{FM}$ then integrates the second
coordinate. The equality $qp_1=qp_2$ and the
composition isomorphism for derived direct images interchange
these two operations; the exchange map is obtained from the
same pullback counits on the Cartesian square. Naturality
of the tensor projection map identifies the resulting first
arrow with $1_M\otimes R(p_1)_*\delta$.
Consequently the whole composite is $Rq_*$ of $1_M$
tensored with
$t_{p_1}\circ R(p_1)_*\delta$. This is the identity
by [lem-amb-p1-diagonal-integrals].

For the other triangle, substitute $M=GK$ in $\eta$.
Since $p_1^*q^*K=p_2^*q^*K$, the projection formula
pulls this common coefficient out of $R(p_2)_*$.
The map $G\epsilon_K$ integrates the first coordinate
of $W$, and is therefore $t_{p_2}$ on the remaining
kernel factor. Hence

$$
G\epsilon_K\circ\eta_{GK}
=1_{q^*K(1)[2]}\otimes
\bigl(t_{p_2}\circ R(p_2)_*\delta\bigr)
=1_{GK}.
$$

The rearranged shifts are all even, so these rearrangements
introduce no Koszul sign. This proves the second triangle.
In these calculations the exchange and projection maps are
the canonical ones, not unspecified isomorphisms: their
compatibility is obtained by substituting their definitions
from pullback counits before applying derived direct image.
Both expressions use the same counit once in each coordinate.
The two verified triangles prove the stated adjunction.

Let $q:P=\mathbf P^1_S\to S$, with $S$ Noetherian.
Let $h$ be the Kummer first Chern class of $\mathcal O_P(1)$.
Then

$$
(1,h):A_S\oplus A_S(-1)[-2]\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_*A_P
$$

is an isomorphism, compatible with arbitrary change of $S$.
The notation refers to the projective line, Tate twists, ordinary derived categories, and derived direct images.

## Proof

For $\mathbf Z/n$-coefficients, the map is globally
defined by the unit and the Cartier class of infinity in
[lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map]. On a geometric fibre,
[thm-sc-proper-cohomology] gives cohomology only in
degrees $0,2$, each free of rank one; the genus is zero.
In its Kummer description, the degree-two map is
$\operatorname{Pic}(\mathbf P^1)/n\to H^2(\mathbf P^1,\mu_n)$,
and the class of $\mathcal O(1)$, of degree one, generates.
Thus $(1,h)$ is an isomorphism on every geometric fibre.
By [cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-finite], [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]
it is an isomorphism on $S$. Both defining components
commute with base change, so the isomorphism does too. For
general $A$, tensor this isomorphism over $\mathbf Z/n$
with $A$ and use
[lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection].

Let $\pi:E\to S$ be a vector bundle of rank $d$
over a Noetherian scheme. For every complex $K$ of
etale $A$-modules on $S$, the adjoint of

$$
R\pi_!(\pi^*K(d)[2d])
\cong K\otimes_A^LR\pi_!A_E(d)[2d]
\xrightarrow{1\otimes t_\pi}K
$$

is an isomorphism

$$
\pi^*K(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}\pi^\times K.
$$

The notation refers to Tate twists, and vector-bundle integration.

## Proof

The vector bundle is compactifiable by its projective
completion. Thus its actual ambient adjoint exists by
[thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. The projection
formula of [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection]
on this compactification defines the displayed
integration for every $K$, using the global map
of [def-amb-vector-integration].
Transpose it under the ambient adjunction.

Restrict to a trivializing open set of $S$.
The resulting map is the adjoint of the affine-space
counit. By
[lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality], [cor-amb-affine-space-adjunction],
this map is the identity under the affine-space
identification of the right adjoint. Hence it is an
isomorphism on the inverse image of every trivializing
open set. These opens cover $E$, so
[lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] proves
that it is an isomorphism everywhere.
The construction used only the projective-line diagonal,
compact supports, and ordinary adjunctions; it did not
use general smooth purity, a localized top Chern class,
or frame independence in codimension greater than one.

Let $f:X\to S$ be smooth, separated, compactifiable,
and of pure relative dimension $d$, with Noetherian base.
Put $\omega_f=f^\times A_S$, using the ambient right
adjoint. Then $\omega_f[-2d]$ is a locally constant
sheaf of free rank-one $A$-modules. For every complex
$K$ on $S$, the canonical tensor morphism is an
isomorphism

$$
f^*K\otimes_A^L\omega_f\xrightarrow{\sim}f^\times K.
$$

The notation refers to inverse images.

## Proof

Construct the tensor morphism by transposing

$$
Rf_!(f^*K\otimes_A^L\omega_f)
\cong K\otimes_A^LRf_!\omega_f
\longrightarrow K\otimes_A^LA_S=K
$$

under [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint].
The displayed projection formula follows from
[lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] on a compactification:
extension by zero commutes with tensoring a pulled-back
complex, as its stalk is either that complex or zero.

By [sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form], every point of
$X$ has an etale neighbourhood $u:U\to X$ such
that $fu=p_de$, where $e:U\to\mathbf A^d_S$
is etale (one may restrict the base to an open neighbourhood).
The adjunctions in
[lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality], [cor-amb-affine-space-adjunction]
identify

$$
u^*f^\times K\cong e^*p_d^*K(d)[2d],\qquad
u^*\omega_f\cong A_U(d)[2d].
$$

By its definition as the transpose of the projection formula
and counit, the tensor map restricts under these identifications
to the canonical reassociation
$(fu)^*K\otimes_A^LA_U(d)[2d]\cong(fu)^*K(d)[2d]$.
To check this assertion, transpose on $U$: both maps
become the projection formula followed by the composite of
the etale counit with the $d$ affine-line counits. The
uniqueness in the adjunction bijection therefore identifies
them. In particular it is an isomorphism locally on $X$,
hence globally by
[lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative].

The same local calculation shows that all cohomology sheaves
of $\omega_f$ except $\mathcal H^{-2d}$ vanish,
and that $\mathcal H^{-2d}(\omega_f)$ is etale locally
free of rank one. The canonical truncation isomorphism
$\omega_f\cong\mathcal H^{-2d}(\omega_f)[2d]$
gives the stated conclusion. No complexes or morphisms were
glued in a derived category: the adjoint and tensor morphism
were constructed globally, and geometric stalks only tested
their properties.

attrs.title: Smooth cohomological duality without a chosen orientation

objects.body:
Let $A$ be an abelian variety of dimension $g$ over a field $k$, let
$p=\operatorname{char}k$ and let $n\ge1$.

- **(a)** $[n]:A\to A$ is a finite flat surjective homomorphism, hence
an isogeny of degree $n^{2g}$; $A[n]=\ker[n]$ is a finite flat group
scheme over $k$ of order $n^{2g}$.
- **(b)** If $p>0$, then $A[p^e]$ is finite flat of order $p^{2ge}$ for
every $e\ge1$. If $n$ is prime to $p$ (in particular if $p=0$), then
$A[n]$ is finite étale of rank $n^{2g}$.
- **(c)** Let $k$ be algebraically closed and $n$ prime to $p$. Then
$A[n](k)\cong(\Z/n\Z)^{2g}$, and for every extension
$k\subseteq k'$ of algebraically closed fields the canonical map
$A[n](k)\to A[n](k')$ is an isomorphism.
- **(d)** Let $k$ be algebraically closed. Then $A(k)$ is a divisible
abelian group, $A(k)[n]\cong(\Z/n\Z)^{2g}$ for every $n$ prime to $p$,
and for every prime $\ell\ne p$
$$
T_\ell A\cong\Z_\ell^{2g},\qquad V_\ell A\cong\Q_\ell^{2g}.
$$

## Proof

*(a)* This is exactly [lem-sc-isogeny-facts], [lem-sc-mult-n-finite-flat]: $[n]$ is a
homomorphism ([lem-sc-mult-n-homomorphism] with [lem-sc-av-commutative]), has
finite fibres ([lem-sc-mult-n-finite-kernel]) and is surjective
([lem-sc-mult-n-isogeny]), is flat with locally free pushforward of
rank the order of its kernel ([lem-sc-isogeny-degree]), and its
degree is computed as $n^{2g}$ from
$[n]^*\cN\cong\cN^{\otimes n^2}$ ([lem-sc-mult-n-pullback],
[lem-sc-ample-tensor]) together with
$\deg_{[n]^*\cN}(A)=\deg[n]\deg_{\cN}(A)$
([lem-sc-deg-pullback-finite]).

*(b)* The first clause is (a) with $n=p^e$. For the second,
$A[n]$ is finite flat of order $n^{2g}$ by (a); write
$G=A[n]$ and let $\bar k$ be an algebraic closure of $k$. Then
$G_{\bar k}=A_{\bar k}[n]$ is a finite flat group scheme over $\bar k$
of order $n^{2g}$, prime to $p$, so it is étale over $\bar k$ by
[lem-sc-fg-order-prime-etale] (for $p>0$: the identity component
$(G_{\bar k})^0$ is a connected finite flat group scheme, so its order
is a power of $p$ by [lem-sc-connected-finite-order] and divides
$n^{2g}$, whence $(G_{\bar k})^0=\Spec\bar k$; every connected
component of $G_{\bar k}$ is a translate of $(G_{\bar k})^0$ by a
$\bar k$-point, so $G_{\bar k}$ is reduced, hence étale over the
algebraically closed $\bar k$; for $p=0$ this is Cartier's theorem).
Finally étaleness descends to $k$: $G$ is flat over $k$ and
$\Omega_{G/k}\otimes_k\bar k\cong\Omega_{G_{\bar k}/\bar k}=0$, so
$\Omega_{G/k}=0$ and $G$ is étale over $k$. (The passage to
$\bar k$ is needed: over an imperfect $k$ a finite reduced $k$-scheme
need not be étale, so one cannot conclude directly from
$G^0=\Spec k$.)

*(c)* Assume $k$ algebraically closed and $n$ prime to $p$. By
(b), $A[n]$ is finite étale of order $n^{2g}$, so
$\lvert A[n](k)\rvert=n^{2g}$ and $A[n](k)\to A[n](k')$ is bijective
by [lem-sc-finite-etale-points]. The group structure
$(\Z/n\Z)^{2g}$ is the content of [lem-sc-ntorsion-etale]: the
prime-power case follows from divisibility of $A(k)$
([lem-sc-finite-flat-surj-points], [lem-sc-finite-nonempty-point], [lem-sc-isogeny-surjective]) and the structure theorem for torsion of a
divisible group ([lem-sc-divisible-group-structure]), and the general case
from the Chinese remainder theorem applied to the coprime-order
subgroup schemes $A[\ell_i^{e_i}]$.

*(d)* Still with $k$ algebraically closed:
$A(k)$ is abelian by [lem-sc-av-commutative] and divisible by
[lem-sc-finite-flat-surj-points], [lem-sc-finite-nonempty-point], [lem-sc-isogeny-surjective]; and $A(k)[n]\cong(\Z/n\Z)^{2g}$ for $n$ prime to
$p$ is clause (c). For the Tate module, each level
$A[\ell^n](k)\cong(\Z/\ell^n\Z)^{2g}$ by (c) and the transition maps
are surjective by [lem-sc-finite-flat-surj-points], [lem-sc-finite-nonempty-point], [lem-sc-isogeny-surjective], so the inverse limit
$T_\ell A$ of [def-wf-abelian-tate-module] is $\Z_\ell^{2g}$; this is
[prop-av-tate-rank], and $V_\ell A=T_\ell A\otimes\Q_\ell$.

Uses: [def-sc-isogeny], [rem-ptr-sc-isogeny-2], [def-sc-mult-n], [def-wf-abelian-tate-module], [def-sc-abelian-variety], [rem-ptr-sc-abelian-variety-1], [lem-sc-connected-finite-order], [lem-sc-divisible-group-structure], [lem-sc-finite-flat-surj-points], [lem-sc-finite-nonempty-point], [lem-sc-isogeny-surjective], [lem-sc-isogeny-facts], [lem-sc-mult-n-finite-flat], [lem-sc-ntorsion-etale], [lem-sc-fg-order-prime-etale], [prop-av-tate-rank]

Let $(A,I)$ satisfy [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], let
$\square$ be a
compact-support
base-change square with $f$ separated of finite type and
$g:Y'\to Y$ arbitrary, and let $K\in D(X_{\Proet},A)$ be derived
$I$-complete whose reductions $K_n$ carry compatible
etale-origin witnesses.
Then

$$
\Ex^{\mathrm{comp}}_!(K):
Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rf_!K
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf'_!Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K
$$

of [def-cbc-completed-exchange-map] is an isomorphism, natural
in $K$ and coherent for identities and pasted squares.

## Proof

Choose a compactification $c=(j,p)$ of $f$ and its base change
$c'$; the composite defining
[def-cbc-completed-exchange-map] consists of two
isomorphisms: the completed proper base change
[thm-weil-pbc-complete-proetale] applied to the proper $p$
(the hypotheses hold: $j_!K$ is derived $I$-complete by the
exactness of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero], and its
reductions $j_!K_n$ carry the witnesses $j_!L_n$ if the
witnesses of $K$ are $L_n$), and the completed
extension-by-zero comparison
[lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison]. Hence
$\Ex^{\mathrm{comp}}_!(K)$ is an isomorphism, and it is
independent of the compactification and natural by the corresponding
properties of the two factors (the coherence of
[def-cbc-exchange-map] and of the completed map of
[thm-weil-pbc-complete-proetale], with the compatibility of the
comparisons of [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] with the
completed maps).

For every finite $E/\Ql$, every
compact-support
base-change square with $f$ separated of finite type and $g$
arbitrary, and every $K\in\Dbc(X,E)$ (in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-rational-category]), whose reductions satisfy the
constructibility and amplitude conditions of
[prop-finite-compact-support-constructibility],

$$
Lg^*Rf_!K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf'_!Lg'^*K
\quad\text{in }\Dbc(Y',E).
$$

This is independent of the integral lattice and natural and coherent
for identities and pasted squares.

## Proof

Choose an integral lattice for $K$. The isomorphism of
[thm-cbc-complete-proetale] is an isomorphism of
$\mathcal O_E$-linear functors on the integral constructible
categories, so by [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] it remains
an isomorphism after the rationalization of
[def-weil-pbc-rational-category]; the constructible landing is
the finite-level condition of the statement. Independence of the
lattice (both sides are lattice-independent by
[lem-weil-compact-support-representative-independence]) and
coherence are inherited from the integral level.

attrs.title: Compact-support base change over a finite extension

objects.body:
Let $\Lambda$ be finite, let $\square$ be a
compact-support
base-change square with $f$ separated of finite type and
$g:Y'\to Y$ arbitrary, and let
$K\in D^+(X_{\Proet},\Lambda)$ carry an
etale-origin witness
$(L,\alpha)$. Then the pro-etale exchange map

$$
g^{-1}Rf_!K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf'_!g'^{-1}K
$$

of [def-cbc-exchange-map] (with the compact-support functors
and exchange map of [def-cbc-exchange-map] transported to the
pro-etale site) is an isomorphism; it is independent of replacing
the witness by an isomorphic one.

## Proof

Choose a compactification $c=(j,p)$ of $f$ with base change
$c'$ as in [def-cbc-compact-support-square]. The etale
statement of [thm-cbc-finite-torsion] applies to the etale
representative $L$: the etale exchange map
$\operatorname{Ex}_!(L)$ is an isomorphism. Transporting it to
the pro-etale site: the fully faithful comparison
$\nu_T^*$ of [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] (the interface
`OBL-PBC-SITE-COMPARISON` of the proper-base-change chapter) carries the
direct-image parts by
[lem-weil-pbc-transport-identifies-exchange] (and
[prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image]), and the
extension-by-zero factors by the comparisons
[lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] (etale to
pro-etale) and [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change]
(pro-etale base change); the transported composite is the pro-etale
map of [def-cbc-exchange-map] for $K=\nu_X^*L$. Independence
of the witness follows from the functoriality of the transported map and
the notion of an etale-origin witness of
[def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness].

Let $\square$ be a
compact-support
base-change square with $f:X\to Y$ separated of finite type, let
$\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring and let $g:Y'\to Y$ be
arbitrary. For every derived category

$$
K\in D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)
$$

the exchange map

$$
\operatorname{Ex}_!(K):g^{-1}Rf_!K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
Rf'_!g'^{-1}K
$$

of [def-cbc-exchange-map] is an isomorphism in
$D^+(Y'_{\Et},\Lambda)$; it is natural in $K$, is the identity for
identity base changes, and satisfies horizontal and vertical pasting
after inserting the canonical associativity isomorphisms. It is
independent of the chosen compactification.

## Proof

Fix a compactification $c=(j,p)$ of $f$ with base change
$c'=(j',p')$ as in [def-cbc-compact-support-square]. The map
$\operatorname{Ex}_!(K)$ of [def-cbc-exchange-map] is the
composite

$$
\begin{aligned}
g^{-1}Rf_!K&=g^{-1}Rp_*j_!K
&&\text{(definitions)}\\
&\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rp'_*g^{-1}j_!K
&&\text{(\Cref{thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below} applied to the
proper \(p\))}\\
&\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rp'_*j'_!g'^{-1}K
&&\text{(\Cref{cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change})}\\
&=Rf'_!g'^{-1}K &&\text{(definitions).}
\end{aligned}
$$

The first arrow is an isomorphism by the bounded-below proper base
change of the proper-base-change chapter ([thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below]; $p$ is
proper, $g$ arbitrary, $j_!K\in D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ because
$j_!$ is exact), the second by the extension-by-zero base change of
[cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change] applied to the
open-immersion square with $g_U=g'$ (the square of
[def-cbc-compact-support-square] is cartesian, so
$X'=U\times_{\overline X}\overline X'$ and the identification
$j'_!g'^{-1}K$ is the one of
[def-cbc-exchange-map]). Hence $\operatorname{Ex}_!(K)$ is an
isomorphism for the chosen compactification. For another
compactification $c_1$ with a refinement to $c_2$, the
comparison isomorphisms of the compact-support direct image of
[def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] commute with the two displayed factors by
[prop-compactification-coherence-detailed] (the comparison of $Rf_!$
is $Ru_*j_{1!}\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{2!}$ composed with the
composition isomorphism of proper direct images, and both factors of
$\operatorname{Ex}_!$ are compatible with the refinement maps, as
the refined data are cartesian over the same base change and the maps
are mates of compatible data); hence $\operatorname{Ex}_!(K)$ is
independent of the compactification. Naturality in $K$, the
identity for identity base changes, and the pasting laws follow from
the corresponding properties of the two factors (the proper exchange
of [thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below] and the extension-by-zero
comparison of [cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change]),
which is the statement of [def-cbc-exchange-map].

attrs.title: Compact-support base change at finite coefficients

objects.body:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type, $g:Y'\to Y$ arbitrary
and $K\in\Dbc(X,\Qlb)$, with the finite-level hypotheses of
[thm-cbc-finite-extension] at every finite stage. The
descended exchange transformation of
[prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors] is an isomorphism

$$
Lg^*Rf_!K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf'_!Lg'^*K
\quad\text{in }\Dbc(Y',\Qlb).
$$

If $K$ is represented by a pair $(E,K_E)$ with
$K_E\in\Dbc(X,E)$, the map is represented
after a finite overfield $M$ by the $M$-coefficient isomorphism of
[thm-cbc-finite-extension] applied to $T_{M/E}K_E$; the result
is independent of $E$, $M$, and the representative.

## Proof

The scalar-extension compatibilities for the functors $Rf_!$ and
$Lg^*$ hold: for the direct image factor, scalar extension
commutes with $Rp_*$ of the proper $p$ by
[prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], and with $j_!$ by the
projection formula [lem-cbc-extension-zero-projection-formula]
(whose scalar-extension instance is
$F\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}j_!K\cong j_!(F\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}K)$ for a finite field $F/E$,
as $j^*$ of the constant coefficient is the restriction);
hence the family $(Rf_{!,E})_E$ with the exchange
transformations descends by
[prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors], and at every finite stage it
is an isomorphism by [thm-cbc-finite-extension]. The common
stage colimit of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], triangulated and
idempotent complete by
[thm-weil-pbc-idempotent-complete-triangulation], preserves the
isomorphism, giving the assertion, with the stated independence as
in [thm-cbc-finite-extension] and [lem-weil-compact-support-finite-field-independence].

Let $S$ be a noetherian scheme and let $f\colon X\to S$ be a separated morphism
of finite type. Then there are an integer $n\geq0$, a scheme $X'$ over $S$, a
morphism $\pi\colon X'\to X$ and an immersion $i\colon X'\to\mathbf P^n_S$ of
$S$-schemes such that

1. $\pi$ is proper and surjective, and
1. there is a dense open subscheme $U\subseteq X$ such that
$\pi^{-1}(U)\to U$ is an isomorphism.

The formalisation makes $X'$, the index set of the homogeneous coordinates of
the ambient projective space, $\pi$ and $i$ four separate definitions rather
than existentially bound data, so that a consumer gets properness, surjectivity
and the immersion property by typeclass inference; all four are read off a
single auxiliary choice, `ChowModification.data`. Following
[def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], $\mathbf P^n_S$ is
$\mathbf P(N;S)$ for a finite type $N$ of homogeneous coordinates. Finally,
[lem-chow-graph] needs the covering of Step 1 to be nonempty; this costs
nothing, since $m=0$ happens only for $X$ empty, and one may then replace the
covering by the one-element covering $\{X^{*}\}$.

## Proof

By the scheme conventions [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] (Stacks 01T6, 0BA8, 01T8, 01KV) the scheme $X$ is
noetherian and has finitely many irreducible components, and it is
quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

*Step 1: the cover.* By [lemma-nagata-dense-affine-cover-exists] there is a finite
affine open covering $X=U_1\cup\dots\cup U_m$ whose members all contain the
generic points of the irreducible components of $X$, and
$U:=U_1\cap\dots\cap U_m$ is a dense open subscheme of $X$.

*Step 2: reduction to $U$ scheme-theoretically dense.* Let
$X^{*}\subseteq X$ be the scheme-theoretic image of $U\to X$, as in
[lem-chow-scheme-theoretic-closure]. Then $X^{*}\to S$ is again separated
of finite type, $X^{*}=\bigcup_iU_i^{*}$ is a finite affine open covering with
$\bigcap_iU_i^{*}=U$, and $U$ is scheme-theoretically dense in $X^{*}$.
It suffices to produce, for $X^{*}$ with the covering $\{U_i^{*}\}$ and the
same open $U$, a proper surjective morphism $\pi^{*}\colon X'\to X^{*}$ and an
immersion $X'\to\mathbf P^n_S$ such that $(\pi^{*})^{-1}(U)\to U$ is an
isomorphism; this is exactly what Steps 3–7 below construct. Indeed,
$X^{*}\to X$ is a surjective closed immersion, hence proper and surjective, and
it is an isomorphism over $U$; so $\pi:=(X^{*}\to X)\circ\pi^{*}$ is proper and
surjective, $U$ is a dense open subscheme of $X$, and
$\pi^{-1}(U)=(\pi^{*})^{-1}(U)\to U$ is an isomorphism. We may therefore
replace $X$ by $X^{*}$ and $U_i$ by $U_i^{*}$, and assume from now on that $U$
is scheme-theoretically dense in $X$.

*Step 3: the graph.* Apply [lem-chow-graph] to obtain immersions
$j_i\colon U_i\to\mathbf P^{n_i}_S$, their closed models $Z_i$, the
scheme-theoretic image $Z$ of $j=(j_1|_U,\dots,j_m|_U)$, the proper
projections $p_i\colon Z\to Z_i$, and the closed immersion
$Z\to\mathbf P^{n_1}_S\times_S\dots\times_S\mathbf P^{n_m}_S$.

*Step 4: the modification.* Put $V_i:=p_i^{-1}(U_i)$ and
$X':=V_1\cup\dots\cup V_m$. By [lem-chow-glue] the morphisms
$p_i|_{V_i}$ glue to $\pi\colon X'\to X$ with $\pi|_U=\mathrm{id}_U$, and by
[lem-chow-preimage] we have $\pi^{-1}(U_i)=V_i$ with
$\pi^{-1}(U_i)\to U_i$ proper.

*Step 5: $\pi$ is proper and surjective.* Properness is local on the
target by 01W2, and $X=\bigcup_iU_i$ is an open covering with
$\pi^{-1}(U_i)\to U_i$ proper; hence $\pi$ is proper. In particular
$\pi(X')\subseteq X$ is closed. It contains $U$ because
$\pi|_U=\mathrm{id}_U$, and $U$ is dense in $X$; therefore $\pi(X')=X$.

*Step 6: $\pi$ is an isomorphism over $U$.* Repeat the argument of
[lem-chow-preimage] with $U_i$ replaced by $U$: the identity
$U\to U$ is proper, $\pi^{-1}(U)\to U$ is separated, so
01W6 shows that $U\to\pi^{-1}(U)$ is universally closed and
hence $U$ is closed in $\pi^{-1}(U)$; and $U$ is dense in the open subscheme
$\pi^{-1}(U)\subseteq Z$. Thus $U=\pi^{-1}(U)$ and $\pi^{-1}(U)\to U$ is the
identity.

*Step 7: the immersion.* Put $N=\prod_i(n_i+1)-1$. Composing the closed
immersion $Z\to\mathbf P^{n_1}_S\times_S\dots\times_S\mathbf P^{n_m}_S$ of
[lem-chow-graph](1) with the Segre embedding, which is a closed
immersion by [lem-chow-segre], gives a closed immersion
$Z\to\mathbf P^N_S$. The subscheme $X'\subseteq Z$ is open, so the composition
$i\colon X'\to\mathbf P^N_S$ is an immersion. Taking $n:=N$ completes the
proof.

## Detailed form

In the situation of [lem-chow-glue], the morphism
$\pi:X'\to X$ is proper and surjective, and

$$
 \pi^{-1}(U)\xrightarrow{\sim}U
$$

is an isomorphism.

## Proof

*Properness of $\pi$.* By [lem-chow-preimage] the
restrictions $\pi^{-1}(U_i)\to U_i$ are proper for every member of the finite
affine open cover $X=U_1\cup\dots\cup U_m$. Properness is local on the target
(Stacks Project, Morphisms, Lemma 29.42.3, Tag
[01W2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01W2): a morphism $g:W\to S$ is
proper as soon as there is an open cover $S=\bigcup_jS_j$ with
$g^{-1}(S_j)\to S_j$ proper for all $j$); applying this to $g=\pi$, $S=X$,
$S_j=U_j$ shows that $\pi$ is proper.

*Surjectivity of $\pi$.* A proper morphism has closed image (Stacks Project,
Morphisms, Lemma 29.42.7, Tag
[01W6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01W6)). Hence $\pi(X')\subseteq X$
is closed; it contains $U$ (since $\pi|_U=\operatorname{id}_U$ by
[lem-chow-glue]), and $U$ is dense in $X$ (it is
scheme-theoretically dense after the reduction of
[lem-chow-graph], hence topologically dense). Thus
$\pi(X')=X$, i.e. $\pi$ is surjective.

*The isomorphism over $U$.* Identify $U$ with an open subscheme of
$\pi^{-1}(U)\subseteq X'$ via the inclusion of the dense open. We apply Stacks
Project, Morphisms, Lemma 29.42.7 (Tag
[01W6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01W6)) to the diagram whose
composite $U\to\pi^{-1}(U)\to U$ is the identity (hence proper) and whose
second member $\pi^{-1}(U)\to U$ is separated over $U$ (the morphism
$\pi^{-1}(U)\to U$ is the base change of the separated morphism $\pi$, see the
first step of the proof of [lem-chow-preimage]): the
lemma yields that $U\to\pi^{-1}(U)$ is proper, hence closed, so $U$ is closed
in $\pi^{-1}(U)$. On the other hand $U$ is scheme-theoretically dense in
$\widetilde X$ by [lem-chow-graph] (i), and
$\pi^{-1}(U)\subseteq\widetilde X$ is open, so $U$ is dense in $\pi^{-1}(U)$.
A closed and dense subscheme of a scheme coincides with it: $U=\pi^{-1}(U)$
inside $X'$, and $\pi^{-1}(U)\to U$ is the isomorphism inverse to the
inclusion.

*The closed immersion $i$.* The composed morphism $i$ is an immersion:
$X'\subseteq\widetilde X$ is open ($X'=\bigcup_iV_i$ with the
$V_i\subseteq\widetilde X$ open), and the remaining factors are closed
immersions by [lem-chow-graph] (iii) and
[lem-chow-segre]; a composite of an open immersion
and closed immersions is an immersion. Its source is proper over $Y$: $\pi$ is
proper by the first paragraph and $f:X\to Y$ is proper by hypothesis, so
$f\circ\pi:X'\to Y$ is the composite of two proper morphisms, hence proper. By
Tag [01W6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01W6) once more, now with
$X=X'$, $S=Y$, $Y'=\mathbf P^N_Y$ (separated over $Y$, being projective), the
morphism $X'\to\mathbf P^N_Y=i$ is proper. A proper immersion is a closed
immersion (Stacks Project, Schemes, Lemma 26.10.4, Tag
[01IQ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01IQ): an immersion is a closed
immersion iff its image is closed; here the image is closed by properness, Tag
[01W6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01W6)). Hence $i$ is a closed
immersion.

*The factorization.* Both $f\circ\pi$ and the composite $X'\xrightarrow{i}
\mathbf P^N_Y\to Y$ are equal to the structure morphism of the $Y$-scheme
$X'$: all schemes involved are defined over $Y$ and every morphism displayed
is a morphism over $Y$ (the open immersions $V_i\subseteq\widetilde X$, the
closed immersions and the projections $p_i$ are all over $Y$, and $\pi$ is a
morphism of $Y$-schemes by [lem-chow-glue]). Hence
$f\circ\pi=p\circ i$ with $p:\mathbf P^N_Y\to Y$.

For $K,M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, the evaluation-defined map

$$
v_{K,M}:R\mathcal Hom_A(K,M)\otimes_A^LB
\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_B(K_B,M_B)
$$

is an isomorphism. It respects evaluation, tensor–Hom adjunction,
composition of internal-Hom morphisms, and successive coefficient
changes. The statement holds on both finite coefficient sites.

## Proof

Define $v_{K,M}$ by tensoring evaluation
$R\mathcal Hom_A(K,M)\otimes_A^LK\to M$ with $B$,
reassociating, and transposing over $B$.
Finite-Tor constructible preservation of its source and target
is [cor-weil-finite-constructible-hom].

Choose a finite stratification on which the cohomology of $K$
is finite locally constant. Its restrictions $P=s^*K$ are
site-perfect, by the finite-free-resolution truncation argument
of [lem-weil-bounded-finite-tor-perfect] and the notion in
[def-weil-site-perfect-complex]. The localization triangles
of [def-weil-open-closed-recollement] reduce the assertion
in the first argument to $K=Rs_!P$. On this generator
[lem-weil-stratum-ambient-hom] identifies the left side
before coefficient change with

$$
Rs_{*,A}R\mathcal Hom_A(P,Rs_A^!M).
$$

The inner complex is finite-Tor constructible: the closed
exceptional inverse images in $s^!$ have that property by
[lem-coef-finite-closed-shriek], and internal Hom from a
site-perfect complex is its finite-projective dual tensor the
second argument. Move coefficient change through $Rs_*$
by [lem-coef-finite-direct-image], through $Rs^!$ by
[lem-coef-finite-closed-shriek], and through internal Hom
from $P$ by its finite-projective model. The result is

$$
Rs_{*,B}R\mathcal Hom_B(P_B,Rs_B^!M_B)
=R\mathcal Hom_B(Rs_{!,B}P_B,M_B).
$$

Extension by zero commutes with coefficient tensor, so this is
the required target. Every comparison used is defined by the
same evaluations and adjunction counits; transposing identifies
their composite with $v_{K,M}$. Exactness in the first
argument now proves it for $K$. The comparison maps respect
evaluation by their definition; associativity of tensor product
and uniqueness of its transpose give the successive-quotient
and composition identities. Finally
[lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison] transports the
specified internal-Hom comparison to the pro-etale site.

attrs.title: General constructible internal Hom and finite coefficient change

objects.body:
Set

$$
D_{X,R}K=R\mathcal Hom_R(K,\omega_{X,R}).
$$

This is an exact contravariant anti-equivalence of
$D^b_c(X,R)=D^b_{ctf}(X,R)$. Its canonical comparisons satisfy

$$
(D_{X,R}K)\otimes_R^L A_n\cong D_{X,n}K_n,
\qquad D_{X,R}K\cong R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nD_{X,n}K_n.
$$

If $\dim X\leq d$ and the reductions of $K$ have Tor interval
$[a,b]$, those of $D_{X,R}K$ have interval
$[-b-2d,-a]$. The comparisons preserve evaluation and identify
the reduction of the actual double-dual map
$\delta_K:K\to D_{X,R}D_{X,R}K$ with $\delta_{K_n}$.
In particular $\delta_K$ is an isomorphism.

## Proof

The dualizing object and its reductions are
[prop-coef-integral-dualizing]. Apply
[lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction]; it proves both displayed
identifications and completeness of the ambient internal Hom.
By [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor], all input reductions are
finite-Tor constructible. The finite bound
[lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata] and the comparison
[lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison] prove constructibility
and the uniform interval stated for every reduction of the output.
This establishes preservation in the actual integral category.

Apply the internal-Hom comparison twice. Its evaluation
compatibility identifies the reduction of $\delta_K$, defined by
the tensor–Hom evaluation as in [lem-weil-duality-pairing],
with the canonical finite double-dual map. Those maps are
isomorphisms by [thm-fix-general-biduality].
The cone of $\delta_K$ is derived complete and all its
reductions are zero. Its reconstruction in
[def-weil-derived-complete] is therefore zero.
Thus $\delta_K$ is an isomorphism. The evaluation identity
$D_{X,R}(\delta_K)\circ\delta_{D_{X,R}K}=\operatorname{id}$
shows that these natural isomorphisms exhibit the stated
anti-equivalence. The argument proves a property of ambient
internal Hom, not a replacement definition of that functor.

The finite-field dualities and their scalar-extension comparisons
induce an exact $\Qlb$-linear anti-equivalence

$$
D_{X,\Qlb}:D^b_c(X,\Qlb)^{\mathrm{op}}
\xrightarrow{\sim}D^b_c(X,\Qlb),
\qquad (E,K)\longmapsto(E,D_{X,E}K).
$$

It is the internal Hom into $\omega_{X,\Qlb}=Ra_X^!\Qlb$
in the common-stage category. Evaluation and biduality descend,
giving a natural isomorphism
$K\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{X,\Qlb}D_{X,\Qlb}K$.
For a separated finite-type $f:X\to Y$, the same passage
gives the constructible adjunction $Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$ and
$Rf^!=D_Xf^*D_Y$. All of these maps are compatible with
finite scalar extension and with retracts.

## Proof

Apply [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors] to the opposite
categories and the comparisons of [thm-coef-rational-verdier].
For clarity, a morphism from $(E,K)$ to $(F,L)$ represented
at a common finite field $M$ by
$u:T_{M/E}K\to T_{M/F}L$ is sent to

$$
T_{M/F}D_FL\xrightarrow{\beta_{M/F}}
D_MT_{M/F}L\xrightarrow{D_Mu}
D_MT_{M/E}K\xrightarrow{\beta_{M/E}^{-1}}T_{M/E}D_EK.
$$

The unit and associator equations for $\beta$ show that this
is independent of the common field and of the representative;
these are exactly the equivalences on morphisms in
[def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Exactness
and linearity follow at a common finite stage.

The scalar-compatible evaluations and $\delta$'s descend by
the same construction. The inverse of each $\delta$ is
already present at its finite stage, so the descended map is an
isomorphism, proving the anti-equivalence. The tensor–Hom and
exceptional adjunctions of [lem-coef-rational-operations]
also descend: represent their finitely many objects and maps at
one common stage as in [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus],
apply the finite-stage adjunction, and use its coefficient
compatibility to pass to the filtered colimit of Hom groups.
For the exceptional functor this compatibility also follows
directly from $Rf^!=D_Xf^*D_Y$, since pullback is compatible
with scalar extension. This proves the asserted identification
of $\omega$, internal Hom, and $Rf^!$, including their
units and counits. Restriction to retracts is
[lem-coef-rational-retract-evaluation], performed at a
finite common stage. No tensor product with an infinite
topological coefficient extension is required by this proof.

attrs.title: Verdier biduality at algebraically closed coefficients

objects.body:
For every finite extension $E/\Ql$, integral duality induces
an exact $E$-linear anti-equivalence

$$
D_{X,E}:D^b_c(X,E)^{\mathrm{op}}\xrightarrow{\sim}D^b_c(X,E).
$$

Its evaluation and natural isomorphism
$\delta_K:K\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{X,E}D_{X,E}K$ are obtained
by rationalizing integral evaluation and biduality. The dualizing
object is the image $\omega_{X,E}$ of $\omega_{X,\mathcal O_E}$.
For $E\subset L$, the canonical comparison

$$
(D_{X,E}K)\otimes_E L\xrightarrow{\sim}
D_{X,L}(K\otimes_E L)
$$

commutes with evaluation and $\delta$, and satisfies the unit
and associator equations for scalar extension.

## Proof

Put $\mathcal C=D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$. Its actual objects,
not merely a separately chosen finite-Tor subcategory, are in the
domain of integral duality by [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor].
The exact functor $D_{X,\mathcal O_E}:\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}} \to\mathcal C$ of [thm-coef-integral-verdier] is
$\mathcal O_E$-linear. Apply
[prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] to the opposite category
as well as to $\mathcal C$. More explicitly, it sends

$$
f/\varpi_E^r:K\longrightarrow M
\quad\hbox{to}\quad
D(f)/\varpi_E^r:D(M)\longrightarrow D(K).
$$

The equality relation on fractions and their compositions is
preserved by linearity and contravariant functoriality. Thus this
is a functor on exactly the raw scalar localization
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]; there is no extra
idempotent completion or assumption about the choice of a lattice.

The integral natural transformation $\delta$ and its inverse
localize. Its naturality for fractions follows by multiplying
the integral naturality equation by the same scalar denominator.
Consequently $D_{X,E}^2\cong\operatorname{id}$, proving the
anti-equivalence. Evaluation and its transpose localize as well.
Finally localize all the comparisons and their equations in
[lem-coef-integral-finite-extension]. The scalar-extension
functor used there is exactly the one on integral representatives
in [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], so the resulting
comparison has the asserted domain and coherence.

attrs.title: Verdier biduality over a finite coefficient field

objects.body:
Let $\mathcal A=\mathrm{Mod}_\Lambda$ with $\Lambda$ a finite ring. The
kernel and the cokernel of a morphism between constructible sheaves on
$\et X$, finite direct sums of constructible sheaves, and the middle term of
a short exact sequence whose outer terms are constructible, are
constructible. Consequently the constructible sheaves form a weak Serre
subcategory of $\shv{\et X}$. (The kernel and cokernel statements are
formalised, for any ring $\Lambda$, as are the instances
`IsClosedUnderKernels` and `IsClosedUnderCokernels` of
`Etale.constructibleSheaf`; the extension statement is not.)

## Proof

Let $\varphi\colon\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$ be a morphism of constructible
sheaves. By [lemma-constructible-common-refinement] and
[lemma-constructible-of-refines] there is one stratification
$(\iota_k\colon Z_k\to X)_k$ such that all $\iota_k^*\mathcal F$ and
$\iota_k^*\mathcal F'$ are finite locally constant. Since $\iota_k^*$ is
exact, $\iota_k^*\ker\varphi=\ker(\iota_k^*\varphi)$ and
$\iota_k^*\operatorname{coker}\varphi=\operatorname{coker}(\iota_k^*\varphi)$
are finite locally constant by [lemma-constructible-flc-serre], so
$\ker\varphi$ and $\operatorname{coker}\varphi$ are constructible with
respect to the same stratification. The same argument, using exactness of
$\iota_k^*$ and the extension part of [lemma-constructible-flc-serre],
handles extensions, and [lemma-constructible-flc-biproduct] handles
finite direct sums. A full subcategory of an abelian category closed under
kernels, cokernels and extensions is a weak Serre subcategory.

## Detailed form

For a scheme $T$ and a finite ring $\Lambda$, the constructible
$\Lambda$-module sheaves on $T_{\Et}$ form a weak Serre subcategory of
$\Mod(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$: kernels, cokernels, and extensions of constructible
sheaves are constructible.

*Source:* Stacks Project, Etale Cohomology, Lemma 59.71.6, [Tag
03RZ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03RZ). The pro-etale counterpart
of the weak-Serre assertion, stated there for a Noetherian coefficient ring,
is Stacks Project, Section 61.27, [Tag
09AI](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09AI); the form used here is the
etale statement just cited, for a finite ring $\Lambda$.

## Proof

Work on an affine open of $T$, and refine the finitely many partitions of
the given constructible sheaves to one common partition, as in the
definition of a constructible complex. Inverse image to a part is exact, by
the stalkwise exactness of geometric stalks. It suffices to prove the
assertions for finite locally constant sheaves on each part, locally for the
topology of the small etale site.

For a map between two such sheaves, trivialize both near a geometric point.
The images of the finitely many elements of the first constant module are
sections of the second. After an etale refinement each is a specified
constant section. The map is then induced by a map of finite modules, whose
kernel and cokernel give the constant kernel and cokernel sheaves. These
descriptions prove the first two assertions.

Consider an extension $0\to F'\to F\to F''\to0$ with $F'$ and $F''$ finite
locally constant. Fix a geometric point $\bar t$ and trivialize both outer
sheaves on an etale neighbourhood. By the exactness of geometric stalks, the
middle stalk $B=F_{\bar t}$ is an extension of two finite modules and is
finite. Represent each of its finitely many elements by a section of $F$ on
a common pointed etale neighbourhood. All addition, zero and
scalar-multiplication relations of $B$ hold after a further common
refinement: there are only finitely many relations since $B$ and $\Lambda$
are finite, and equality in a stalk means equality on such a neighbourhood.
Also impose the finitely many equalities identifying the chosen sections of
the submodule with the constant sections of $F'$, and their images with the
constant sections of $F''$. We obtain a map from the constant exact sequence
of stalk modules to the given exact sequence, which is the identity on the
outer terms. The kernel--cokernel argument for a map of short exact
sequences makes the middle map an isomorphism; equivalently, apply the same
argument on every stalk and conservativity of geometric stalks. Thus $F$ is
finite locally constant near every point. Applying this on the common
partition proves extension closure and completes the proof.

## Detailed form

Let $X$ be a scheme and $\Lambda$ a finite ring. The category of
constructible $\Lambda$-module sheaves on $X_{\Et}$ is closed under
kernels, cokernels, and extensions inside $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$.

## Proof

This is [thm-constructible-serre] of the proper-base-change chapter,
restated in the notation of this chapter.

attrs.title: Constructible sheaves form a weak Serre subcategory

objects.body:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism between finite-type schemes over
a field $k$, and let $A$ be a finite ring annihilated by an
integer invertible in $k$. Then

$$
Rf_*:D^b_c(X,A)\longrightarrow D^b_c(Y,A)
$$

is defined on the ordinary derived categories. The morphism
$f$ need not be separated.
The notation refers to bounded constructible complexes.

## Proof

The assertion is local on $Y$. Choose a finite affine cover
of $Y$, prove it on each member, and take the finite union of
the resulting cohomological ranges. We may therefore assume
$Y$ affine. Cover $X$ by finitely many affine opens
$X_1,\ldots,X_r$. For each nonempty subset
$I\subset\{1,\ldots,r\}$, the intersection
$X_I=\bigcap_{i\in I}X_i$ is a quasi-compact open of the affine
scheme $X_i$ for any $i\in I$. It need not be affine.
The finite-type morphism $X_i\to Y$ admits a closed embedding
in $\mathbf A^m_Y$; hence $X_I$ is locally closed in
$\mathbf P^m_Y$. In its scheme-theoretic closure
$\overline X_I$, it is open and dense. We obtain a factorization

$$
f_I:X_I\xrightarrow{j_I}\overline X_I
\xrightarrow{p_I}Y
$$

with $j_I$ open and $p_I$ projective. The two preceding
results [cor-fin-deligne-open-finite-coefficients], [lem-fin-proper-bounded-constructible]
prove bounded constructibility of
$Rf_{I,*}K|_{X_I}=Rp_{I,*}Rj_{I,*}K|_{X_I}$.
Composition of the derived direct images is
[lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition] (item (5)); on cohomology
sheaves it is
[lem-weil-pbc-grothendieck-spectral-sequence].

For completeness, use the finite alternating Cech resolution
of the open cover. In degree $p$ it has the direct sum over
strictly increasing index sets $i_0<\cdots<i_p$, so
$0\leq p\leq r-1$. Its augmented rows are exact: near any
point of $X$, choose a member of the cover containing that
point and contract the augmented alternating complex by inserting
its index. Apply this to an injective resolution of $K$.
Restriction to an open preserves injectives because its left
adjoint, extension by zero in
[def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], is exact. Thus after
applying $f_*$ the double complex gives

$$
E_1^{p,q}=\bigoplus_{|I|=p+1}
\mathcal H^q(Rf_{I,*}K|_{X_I})
\ \Longrightarrow\ \mathcal H^{p+q}(Rf_*K).
$$

There are only finitely many subsets $I$, and each corresponding
direct image has a finite range already proved above. Hence this
spectral sequence lies in a bounded rectangle. Every term on
every page is constructible by kernels and cokernels, and each
abutment has a finite constructible filtration, using
[thm-constructible-serre]. Outside the finite sum
of the two ranges the abutment vanishes. This proves the theorem
without an unbounded Cech argument, an affine-intersection
assumption, or a closed-base-change identification for $Rj_*$.

attrs.title: Bounded constructibility of every finite-type direct image

objects.body:
Let $T$ be of finite type of dimension at most one over
a finite field or its algebraic closure, let
$j:U\hookrightarrow T$ be open, and let $A$ be finite
and killed by a power of a prime invertible on $T$.
For a constructible
etale $A$-module sheaf $F$, every
$R^qj_*F$ is
constructible on $T$.

## Proof

Degree zero is [thm-fin-open-degree-zero]; degrees
greater than one vanish by
[thm-exc-curve-open-dimension-general].
For degree one, the stalk calculation just used, namely
[prop-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-stalk-formula], [lem-exc-punctured-curve-branches],
reduces a stalk at a closed boundary point to the finite
product of the first cohomology groups of its branch fields.
The pullback of $F$ to each field has a finite geometric
fibre by [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes].
The equivalence in [lem-exc-field-discrete-modules]
therefore gives a finite Galois module. The finiteness
part of [lem-exc-dvr-galois] proves that each of these
degree-one stalks is finite.

The sheaf is zero on $U$, since $j^*j_*$ is the
identity, and on $T\setminus\overline U$, where the
inverse image of $U$ is empty, using
[def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. The boundary
$\overline U\setminus U$ is a finite set of closed
points: it is a closed subset of the Noetherian
one-dimensional $\overline U$ and contains none of its
generic points. At each of these closed point schemes,
a finite continuous Galois module is finite locally
constant by [lem-exc-field-discrete-modules].
These point strata together with the open complement
give the finite lisse partition required by
[def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes].

attrs.title: Open direct-image constructibility on arbitrary curves

objects.body:
Let $T$ be of finite type of dimension at most one over
a finite field or its algebraic closure, and let
$j:U\hookrightarrow T$ be any
open immersion.
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring killed by a power
of a prime $\ell$ invertible on $T$. Then
$R^qj_*M$ is zero
for $q>1$ and every etale $A$-module sheaf $M$.

## Proof

Restriction to $U$ is exact and $j^*j_*$ is the
identity by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], so all positive
direct-image stalks there vanish. Outside $U$, use the
stalk formula of
[prop-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-stalk-formula].
At a generic point belonging to the closed complement,
the strict local spectrum has dimension zero and its
pullback of $U$ is empty, giving zero.

For a closed point $t$, put
$R=\mathcal O^{\rm sh}_{T,\bar t}$.
This ring is excellent and Noetherian of dimension at
most one: finite-type field algebras are excellent, and
localization and strict henselization preserve excellence,
Noetherianness and local dimension. These are the ordinary
local-algebra permanence theorems. Its residue field is
algebraically closed, since the ground field is finite or
algebraically closed and $t$ is closed.
Replace $R$ by $R_{\rm red}$, which changes neither
the etale site nor its cohomology, by
[thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance].
If its dimension is zero, the open above $U$ is empty.
Otherwise that open is contained in the punctured spectrum
and hence, by [lem-exc-punctured-curve-branches], is a
disjoint union of a subset of the finitely many branch fields.

For every such field, [lem-exc-field-discrete-modules]
identifies etale cohomology, including for arbitrary $M$,
with continuous Galois cohomology. The DVR computation
[lem-exc-dvr-galois] makes it zero above degree one.
A finite disjoint union has the finite product of these
cohomology groups. Thus every stalk vanishes for $q>1$,
and [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] proves
the asserted sheafwise vanishing.

attrs.title: Open direct-image dimension on arbitrary curves

objects.body:
Let $k$ be a separably closed field, let $N$ be an integer prime to
$\operatorname{char}(k)$, and let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative
ring annihilated by $N$. Then both clauses of the
direct-image finiteness input of
[def-exc-direct-image-input] hold over $k$.

## Proof

Clause (1) is [thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility]: for a morphism
$u:S\to T$ of finite type between finite-type $k$-schemes and a
constructible $\Lambda$-sheaf $F$, the derived direct image $Ru_*F$ is
bounded constructible, so each of its cohomology sheaves $R^qu_*F$ is
constructible on $T_{{\mathrm{et}}}$.

For clause (2), let $K$ be a separably closed field and let $W$ be a
finite-type $K$-scheme of dimension at most $d$. A separably closed
field has torsion cohomological dimension zero
([lem-kun-cd-sep-closed-point]), so
[thm-sc-finite-type-torsion-cd] bounds the torsion cohomological
dimension of $W$ by $2d+0=2d$; by the definition of that bound this is
the vanishing of $H^q(W,M)$ for every torsion sheaf $M$ and every
$q>2d$, which is the asserted clause.

Let $A=A_{E,n}$, and let $f:V\to X$ be an
open immersion or a finite
etale morphism. Its ambient exceptional right adjoint satisfies

$$
Rf^{\times}D_c^{[a,b]}(X,A)\subseteq D_c^{[a,b]}(V,A).
$$

Here $D_c^{[a,b]}$ denotes the
constructible interval.
It also preserves the same
Tor-amplitude interval.
For every quotient $A\to B=A_{E,m}$, $m\leq n$, its
derived coefficient comparison is
an isomorphism:

$$
(Rf_A^{\times}K)\otimes_A^L B
\simeq Rf_B^{\times}(K\otimes_A^L B).
$$

For finite-Tor input the two sides are bounded constructible.
All bounds are independent of $n$.

## Proof

By [prop-exc-open-adjoint], [prop-exc-finite-etale-adjoint], the ambient
right adjoint is the exact functor $f^*$. Pull back each stratum in
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. The resulting partition
is finite and constructible; inverse image of a locally constant finite
module sheaf is locally constant with the same finite module fibres.
Exactness identifies $\mathcal H^q(f^*K)$ with
$f^*\mathcal H^q(K)$, proving the assertion about the intervals of
[def-weil-constructible-intervals].

If $K$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b]$, the usual flat-resolution
criterion for [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] represents it by a
complex of flat module sheaves in these degrees. Inverse image preserves
flatness: the relations criterion for flatness is local and is preserved
by the exact inverse-image functor and its compatibility with tensor
products. Pulling back this bounded flat complex and tensoring it with
any module sheaf on $V$ proves the same Tor bound. Finally inverse
image is an exact tensor functor and preserves flat resolutions. Applying
it to a flat resolution in the definition of the derived tensor product
in [def-weil-derived-tensor] gives the displayed coefficient
isomorphism. No assertion that $A\to B$ is flat is used.

attrs.title: Preservation in the open and finite etale cases

objects.body:
Let $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, let $V=V^\vee=\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$, let
$p_1,p_2:V\times_{k_0}V^\vee\to V,V^\vee$ be the projections of the
Fourier square, and let $\mathcal K_\psi$ be the
Fourier kernel of [def-fd-kernel]. The
Fourier–Deligne transform

$$
\operatorname{FT}_\psi=p_{2,!}\bigl(p_1^*(-)\otimes^L\mathcal K_\psi\bigr)[1]
$$

of [def-fd-transform] has perverse amplitude at most one on both
sides with respect to the perverse candidate subcategories of
[def-per-perverse-subcategories]:

$$
\operatorname{FT}_\psi\bigl({}^pD^{\le0}(V)\bigr)\subset
{}^pD^{\le1}(V^\vee),\qquad
\operatorname{FT}_\psi\bigl({}^pD^{\ge0}(V)\bigr)\subset
{}^pD^{\ge-1}(V^\vee),
$$

hence maps the perverse heart candidate of [def-per-perverse-subcategories]
into the strip ${}^pD^{\le1}(V^\vee)\cap{}^pD^{\ge-1}(V^\vee)$.

## Proof

Let $K\in{}^pD^{\le0}(V)$ (respectively $K\in{}^pD^{\ge0}(V)$),
and put $X:=V\times_{k_0}V^\vee$. The projection $p_1$ is smooth
of constant relative dimension one, so the smooth-pullback exactness
[lem-per-smooth-pullback-t-exact] of the perverse-curve chapter gives

$$
Lp_1^*K\in{}^pD^{\le1}(X),\qquad
Lp_1^*K\in{}^pD^{\ge1}(X)
$$

for the corresponding side: with the shift convention
${}^pD^{\le n}={}^pD^{\le0}[-n]$, the direct statement is
$Lp_1^*[1]K\in{}^pD^{\le0}(X)$ and
$Lp_1^*[1]K\in{}^pD^{\ge0}(X)$, and the displayed inclusions are
the same statements after the $[-1]$-shift (the shift
$[-1]$ lowers both indices by one:
${}^pD^{\le0}[-1]={}^pD^{\le1}$,
${}^pD^{\ge0}[-1]={}^pD^{\ge1}$).

The kernel $\mathcal K_\psi$ is lisse of rank one [prop-kernel-lisse] (the pullback
$b^*\mathcal L_{\psi(b(x,\xi))}$ of the rank-one lisse
Artin–Schreier sheaf of [lem-fd-as-lisse]), so the lisse-tensor
permanence [lem-per-lisse-tensor-permanence] of the perverse-curve chapter
gives the same sidewise inclusions for
$Lp_1^*K\otimes^L\mathcal K_\psi$:

$$
Lp_1^*K\otimes^L\mathcal K_\psi\in{}^pD^{\le1}(X),
\qquad
Lp_1^*K\otimes^L\mathcal K_\psi\in{}^pD^{\ge1}(X).
$$

The projection $p_2$ is affine with fibers of dimension at most
one, so the affine pushforward amplitude
[lem-per-artin-gabber-affine-curve] of the perverse-curve chapter (relative
dimension $d=1$) gives $p_{2,!}\bigl({}^pD^{\le0}(X)\bigr) \subset{}^pD^{\le1}(V^\vee)$ and
$p_{2,!}\bigl({}^pD^{\ge0}(X)\bigr)\subset {}^pD^{\ge-1}(V^\vee)$; applied to the
$[-1]$-shifted objects of the two families above (the functor
$p_{2,!}$ commutes with shifts), this yields

$$
p_{2,!}\bigl(Lp_1^*K\otimes^L\mathcal K_\psi\bigr)
\in{}^pD^{\le2}(V^\vee),\qquad
\bigl(\,\cdot\,\bigr)\in{}^pD^{\ge0}(V^\vee)
$$

sidewise (the $\le$-bound increases the index by one for the
$[-1]$-shifted input, and the $\ge$-bound respectively). The
normalization $[1]$ of [def-fd-transform] lowers both indices
by one, since
${}^pD^{\le n}[1]={}^pD^{\le n-1}$ and
${}^pD^{\ge n}[1]={}^pD^{\ge n-1}$ by the shift convention of
[def-per-perverse-subcategories], so

$$
\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K)\in{}^pD^{\le1}(V^\vee),\qquad
\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K)\in{}^pD^{\ge-1}(V^\vee)
$$

for the two sides respectively, which is the asserted amplitude.

attrs.title: Perverse amplitude of the Fourier transform

objects.body:
For $y\in\mathbf F_{q^n}$ and a Weil complex $K$ on $\mathbf A^1$,

$$
t_{\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K)}(y)
=-\sum_{x\in\mathbf F_{q^n}}t_K(x)\ \psi\Bigl(\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathbf F_{q^n}/k_0}(xy)\Bigr),
$$

where $t_K$ is the trace function of [def-fd-trace-function].

## Proof

By [lem-fd-stalk-formula], the stalk of $\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K)$ at the geometric point over $y$ is the shifted compact-support complex $H^*_c(\mathbf A^1,K\otimes^L\mathcal L_{\psi(xy)})[1]$. The Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula over $\mathbf F_{q^n}$,
[thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar] (in the point-counting form of [cor-trf-point-counting]), computes the trace of the Frobenius on that complex as the sum of the traces on the geometric points of the fibre, i.e. $-\sum_{x\in\mathbf F_{q^n}}t_{K\otimes^L\mathcal L_{\psi(xy)}}(x)$: the sign is the shift $[1]$ of [def-fd-transform]. The trace of the tensor product is the product of the traces, and the trace of the Artin–Schreier summand at $x$ is $\psi(\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathbf F_{q^n}/k_0}(xy))$ by [lem-fd-as-trace]; this gives the displayed formula.

In the conventions of [rem-dl-a1-conventions], let
$j:U_0\hookrightarrow A_0=\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ be a dense open immersion
and let $\mathcal M$ be a nonzero irreducible lisse Weil sheaf on $U_0$
which is constituent-nonexceptional in the sense of
[def-a1-constituent-nonexceptional] and punctually $\iota$-pure of
weight $w$. Let $j':U'_0\hookrightarrow A'_0$ and the nonzero irreducible
lisse Weil sheaf $\mathcal M'$ on $U'_0$ be those of
[prop-a1-fourier-middle-extension], so that

$$
\operatorname{FT}_\psi\bigl((j_*\mathcal M)[1]\bigr)\cong(j'_*\mathcal M')[1].
$$

Then $\mathcal M'$ is punctually $\iota$-pure, on all of $U'_0$, of some
real weight $v$ (in the sense of [def-weil-punctual-weights]).

## Proof

*Step 1: the real envelope after zero extension.* Put
$b=\iota^{-1}(q^w)$, $\mathcal M^\dagger=\mathcal M^\vee\otimes\mathcal B_b$,
and let $\mathcal K$ be the realified kernel on the Fourier square formed
from $j_!\mathcal M$ and $j_!\mathcal M^\dagger$ as in
[lem-fd-realified-kernel-real]. By the general form of
[lem-fd-realified-kernel-real], which needs only the purity of
$\mathcal M$, the constructible Weil sheaf $\mathcal K$ is $\iota$-real.
By [lem-fd-constituent-nonexceptional-concentration](3),
$R^\nu p_{2,!}\mathcal K=0$ for $\nu\neq1$, and the sheaf

$$
\mathcal G:=\operatorname{FT}_\psi(j_!\mathcal M)
$$

(concentrated in degree $0$) is a direct summand of
$\mathcal H:=R^1p_{2,!}\mathcal K$. By [lem-fd-realness-pushforward],
applied to $\mathcal K$ and this vanishing, $\mathcal H$ is an
$\iota$-real constructible Weil sheaf on the dual line $A'_0$. Working
with $j_!\mathcal M$ rather than $j_*\mathcal M$ is what makes the
reality available: at a missing point both summands of $\mathcal K$ have
zero stalk, while the boundary stalks of $j_*\mathcal M$ and
$j_*\mathcal M^\dagger$ need not have conjugate spectra.

*Step 2: $\mathcal G$ surjects onto the middle extension.* By the
zero-extension comparison [prop-fd-zero-extension-comparison], whose
hypotheses are exactly those of the present statement,
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi(j_!\mathcal M[1])\cong\mathcal G[1]$ and there is
a short exact sequence of Weil sheaves
$0\to\mathcal B'\to\mathcal G\to j'_*\mathcal M'\to0$ on the dual line,
with $j'_*\mathcal M'$ the middle extension of
[def-wf-middle-extension]. In particular
$\mathcal G\to j'_*\mathcal M'$ is an epimorphism of Weil sheaves.

*Step 3: purity on a dense open.* By [fin2-lem-lisse-dense-open],
applied to $\mathcal H$ and to $\mathcal G$ and intersected with
$U'_0$, there is a dense open $V'_0\subset U'_0$ on which $\mathcal H$
and $\mathcal G$ are lisse. Restriction to $V'_0$ is exact and additive,
and $(j'_*\mathcal M')|_{V'_0}=\mathcal M'|_{V'_0}$. Composing the
projection $\mathcal H\to\mathcal G$ onto the direct summand with the
epimorphism of Step 2 gives an epimorphism of lisse Weil sheaves

$$
\mathcal H|_{V'_0}\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal M'|_{V'_0}.
$$

The restriction $\mathcal M'|_{V'_0}$ is nonzero and irreducible: the
Weil group of the dense open $V'_0$ of the normal connected curve
$U'_0$ surjects onto that of $U'_0$ (the corresponding surjectivity of
étale fundamental groups for a dense open of a normal connected scheme,
SGA 1, Exp. V, 8.2), so the invariant subspaces are the same. Refining
the kernel of this epimorphism to a composition series of
$\mathcal H|_{V'_0}$ shows that $\mathcal M'|_{V'_0}$ is an irreducible
constituent of $\mathcal H|_{V'_0}$, which is lisse and $\iota$-real
([def-wf-iota-real]; reality is a pointwise condition and passes to
the open). As $V'_0$ is a dense open of the affine line, it is a smooth
geometrically connected affine curve, and
[thm-rp-real-lisse-purity-affine] shows that $\mathcal M'|_{V'_0}$ is
punctually $\iota$-pure of the real weight
$v:=\dw_\iota(\mathcal M'|_{V'_0})$, its determinantal weight of
[def-wf-determinantal-weight].

*Step 4: purity on all of $U'_0$.* The sheaf $\mathcal M'$ is lisse on
the smooth geometrically connected curve $U'_0$ and its restriction to
the dense open $V'_0$ is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $v$. At a
point $x\in U'_0\setminus V'_0$ the inertia acts trivially, $\mathcal M'$
being lisse there, and the ordinary direct image from $V'_0$ recovers the
stalk of $\mathcal M'$ (the translation step of
[lem-a1-constituent-nonexceptional-comparison]). The consequence
clause of [cor-wf-unramified-boundary-purity] therefore gives that
$\mathcal M'$ is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $v$ on all of
$U'_0$.

attrs.title: The generic Fourier sheaf is pure of some weight

objects.body:
Let $S_0$ be a separated
scheme of finite type over $k_0$, let $V_0\to S_0$ be a vector
bundle of rank $r$ with dual $V_0^\vee$, let $E/\Ql$ be a finite
extension, and let $p_1,p_2$ be the projections of
[def-fd-transform]. Then for every $K\in D^b_c(V,E)$,

$$
\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K)\in D^b_c(V^\vee,E),
$$

and $\operatorname{FT}_\psi$ is an exact triangulated functor

$$
\operatorname{FT}_\psi:
D^b_c(V,E)\longrightarrow D^b_c(V^\vee,E).
$$

## Proof

The kernel $\mathcal K_\psi$ of [def-fd-kernel] is a lisse
rank-one module, hence of finite Tor amplitude [prop-kernel-lisse] in the
coefficient conventions of the proper-base-change chapter ([def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]). By [prop-functor-package] of the framework chapter, the derived
pullback $Lp_1^*$, the derived tensor product, and the derived
compact-support direct image $p_{2,!}$ (the compact-support direct
image of the separated finite-type $p_2$)
are exact triangulated functors on their constructible and finite-Tor
domains; hence $Lp_1^*K\otimes^L_E\mathcal K_\psi$ lies in
$D^b_c(V\times_SV^\vee,E)$, and its image under $p_{2,!}$
lies in $D^b_c(V^\vee,E)$; the shift $[r]$ of
[def-fd-transform] preserves boundedness and constructibility.

Let $S$ be integral and of finite type over a field $k$, let
$\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, and let
$j:X\hookrightarrow Y$ be an open immersion of finite-type
$S$-schemes. For a constructible $\mathbf F_\ell$-sheaf $F$
on $X$, there is a nonempty open $U\subset S$ such that
$Rj_{U,*}F|_{X_U}$ belongs to $D^b_c(Y_U,\mathbf F_\ell)$
and, for every morphism $T\to U$ with Noetherian $T$, its canonical base-change morphism

$$
Rj_{U,*}F|_{X_U}\big|_{Y_T}
\longrightarrow Rj_{T,*}F|_{X_T}
$$

is an isomorphism.
The notation refers to ordinary derived categories.

## Proof

Throughout this proof all base changes have Noetherian source.
We prove the two assertions simultaneously, so that every use of
the induction includes the specific exchange map. Replace $Y$
by the scheme-theoretic closure of $X$; the original immersion
is its composite with a closed immersion. Closed direct image
is exact and preserves constructibility by
[lem-fin-closed-immersion], and it commutes with base change by
[lemma-weil-pbc-finite-exchange]. We may therefore assume
that $X$ is dense in $Y$. The same observation extends any
case already proved for a dense open immersion to an arbitrary
immersion with that bound on the generic dimension of its source.

Induct on $n=\dim X_{k(S)}$. Before starting, remove the
closures of the images of the finitely many irreducible components
of $Y$ that do not dominate $S$. For an empty generic fiber
the remaining scheme is empty. For $n=0$, the dense open
$X_{k(S)}$ contains every point of the zero-dimensional
Noetherian space $Y_{k(S)}$, so it equals that space.
The closed complement $Y\setminus X$ has empty generic fiber.
Its finite affine presentations show that it becomes empty after
inverting one nonzero element of the base: over the fraction
field each coordinate ring is zero, so a nonzero base element
kills its unit; use the product for a finite affine cover.
Thus, after shrinking, $j$ is the identity and the assertion
holds. Assume now the assertion for generic source dimension
at most $n-1$, including all immersions as above.

*First step: the good locus has finite complement.*
The question is local on $Y$, and $Y$ has a finite affine
cover. For this step suppose $Y$ projective over an affine
open of $S$, and cover it by finitely many affine schemes
$Y_\alpha\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^{m_\alpha}_S$.
For each coordinate, regard
$X\cap Y_\alpha\hookrightarrow Y_\alpha$ as an immersion
over the integral finite-type base $\mathbf A^1_S$.
Its generic source dimension is at most $n-1$ by
[lem-fin-coordinate-generic-dimension]. The induction
hypothesis supplies a dense open $V_{\alpha r}\subset\mathbf A^1_S$
over whose inverse image the direct image is bounded constructible
and commutes with all base changes. This includes every base
change induced from $T\to S$: restrict the induced morphism
$\mathbf A^1_T\to\mathbf A^1_S$ to $V_{\alpha r}$.
There are finitely many coordinate pairs. Their union $G$
therefore has both properties, with a common finite cohomological
range. By [lem-fin-projective-coordinate-boundary], shrink
$S$ so that $Z=Y\setminus G$, with reduced structure, is
finite over $S$.

*Second step: smooth source and locally constant sheaf.*
Assume $X\to S$ is smooth and $F$ locally constant.
The assertion can be checked on each member of a finite affine
cover of $Y$. For one such member, embed it in affine space
and take its projective closure. The original affine member
is open in this closure, so $X$ remains an open subscheme of
the projective closure. Replacing the closure by the closure of
$X$ makes $X$ dense. This operation changes no generic
dimension of $X$, and the desired result on the projective
closure restricts to the original member.
We can thus use the first step with $b:Y\to S$ projective.
Set $K=Rj_*F$ and $a=bj:X\to S$. The first step proves
$K|_G\in D^b_c(G)$. After one further shrinking,
[lem-asd-smooth-generic-direct-image] proves
$Ra_*F=Rb_*K\in D^b_c(S)$.
[lem-fin-finite-boundary-reconstruction] now gives
$K\in D^b_c(Y)$.

For any $T\to S$ with Noetherian $T$, let $c:K|_{Y_T}\to Rj_{T,*}F|_{X_T}$
be its exchange morphism. On $G_T$ it is an isomorphism by
the first step. After applying $Rb_{T,*}$, proper base change
[thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below] and the composition rule
[sbc-lem-base-change-composition] identify the resulting
morphism with the exchange for $a$, which is an isomorphism
by the smooth-source lemma. The base change of $Z\to S$
is finite. Hence [lem-fin-finite-boundary-comparison],
applied over $T$, says that $c$ is an isomorphism.
Notice that the target of $c$ need only start in $D^+$;
its boundedness follows from the proved isomorphism.
This proves the entire dimension-$n$ assertion whenever the
source is smooth and the coefficient sheaf is locally constant.

*Third step: arbitrary constructible sheaf.*
By [lem-fin-generic-radicial-smoothing], after shrinking and
making a finite radicial surjective base change, the reduction of
$X$ has a dense smooth open $v:V\hookrightarrow X$ on which
$F$ is locally constant. Replacing the schemes by their
reductions does not change their etale topoi, by
[thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance].
The second step, which has already been proved at dimension
$n$, applies both to $v:V\hookrightarrow X$ and to
$jv:V\hookrightarrow Y$. After intersecting the two resulting
base opens, their derived direct images are bounded constructible
and commute with every base change. Form the triangle

$$
F\longrightarrow Rv_*v^*F\longrightarrow\Delta\longrightarrow F[1].
\tag{1}
$$

The first arrow is the adjunction unit. Both first terms are
bounded constructible, so the cohomology long exact sequence and
[thm-constructible-serre] show that $\Delta$ is
bounded constructible. The unit is the identity after restriction
to $V$, hence $\Delta|_V=0$. For the reduced closed complement
$i:W\hookrightarrow X$, termwise open–closed localization from
[def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] identifies
$\Delta=i_*i^*\Delta$. The generic dimension of $W$ is less
than $n$.

Apply the induction hypothesis to the immersion $ji:W\to Y$
and to each of the finitely many constructible sheaves
$\mathcal H^q(i^*\Delta)$. Intersect the finitely many base
opens. Finite truncation triangles, or their bounded spectral
sequence [thm-sp-truncation-e2], prove that
$R(ji)_*i^*\Delta=Rj_*\Delta$ is bounded constructible and
commutes with every base change. Only a finite number of
cohomology sheaves and a bounded truncation filtration occur.
Apply $Rj_*$ to (1). The middle term is
$R(jv)_*v^*F$, already handled by the second step, and the
third term has just been handled by lower-dimensional induction.
The long exact sequence proves bounded constructibility of
$Rj_*F$. After any base change, the second-step exchange
identifies the pullback of (1) with the analogous triangle for
$v_T$. The three exchange morphisms consequently form a
morphism of triangles; the second and third are isomorphisms,
so the first is an isomorphism as well.
Finally [lem-fin-radicial-exchange-descent] descends the result
through the finite radicial base change. Its hypothesis must be checked
over the whole base to which it is applied, so we first produce an open of
$S$ whose preimage lies inside the good open. Let $U\subseteq S$ be
the open over which the preceding steps hold and let
$U'\subseteq S'_{U}=S'\times_SU$ be the nonempty open of $S'_{U}$ on
which they were verified. Since $S'\to S$ is finite, surjective and
radicial, it is a homeomorphism on underlying spaces; $S$ being
integral, $S'$ and $S'_{U}$ are therefore irreducible of dimension
$\dim S$. The complement $F=S'_{U}\setminus U'$ is closed in
$S'_{U}$, and its image $C\subseteq U$ is closed because
$S'_{U}\to U$ is finite. If $C=U$, then $F\to U$ is surjective, so
$\dim F\ge\dim U=\dim S'_{U}$, which is impossible for a proper closed
subset of the irreducible $S'_{U}$. Hence $C\neq U$, and for the
nonempty open $U_1=U\setminus C$ the preimage $S'_{U_1}$ is contained
in $U'$. Applying [lem-fin-radicial-exchange-descent] over
$U_1$, and intersecting with the finitely many opens already produced,
completes the induction.

attrs.title: Generic bounded constructibility for an open immersion

objects.body:
Let $X$ be of finite type over a field, let
$j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an
open immersion,
and let $F$ be a
constructible
module sheaf over a finite commutative ring on $U_{\Et}$.
Then $j_*F$ is
constructible on $X_{\Et}$.

## Proof

We prove the assertion for every open in $X$ by Noetherian
induction on the ambient closed subset. Reduction of the
ambient scheme causes no change, by
[thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance].
The inverse-image equivalences for reduction commute with
open restriction; adjunction then identifies their direct
images as well. Thus take $X$ reduced.
If $U$ is not dense, factor it through the proper closed
subset $\overline U$, use induction there, and use
[lem-fin-closed-immersion] to push to $X$.

Suppose $U$ is dense. There are finitely many irreducible
components $X_a$, by
[lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-components]. The finite
partition of $F$ in
[def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] contains a lisse
open near each generic point. Inside it choose a normal
nonempty open $V_a\subset X_a$, using
[lem-fin-dense-normal-open], and remove all other
components. Each $V_a$ is then open in $X$, lies in
$U$, and the $V_a$'s are disjoint. Put
$V=\coprod V_a$, $h:V\hookrightarrow U$, $k=jh$,
