and $L=h^*F$. For each component,
[lem-fin-normal-open-lisse-image] gives a constructible
direct image on $X_a$; then
[lem-fin-closed-immersion] and the finite product give
constructibility of $k_*L$ on $X$.

Let $K=\ker(F\to h_*L)$. This subsheaf of $F$ is
constructible by
[lem-weil-pbc-constructible-subobjects-noetherian],
and its restriction to $V$ is zero. Put $W=X\setminus V$,
$W_U=W\cap U$, with immersions $i:W\hookrightarrow X$,
$i':W_U\hookrightarrow U$, and $j_W:W_U\hookrightarrow W$.
The closed unit identifies $K=i'_*K'$, where
$K'=i'^*K$: this is an isomorphism on all stalks by
[lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula] and hence by
[lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative].
Direct-image composition in
[def-weil-pbc-direct-image] gives
$j_*K=i_*j_{W,*}K'$. Since $W$ is a proper closed
subset, induction and [lem-fin-closed-immersion] make
this sheaf constructible.

Left exactness identifies the kernel of
$j_*F\to j_*h_*L=k_*L$ with $j_*K$.
Its image $I$, being a subsheaf of the constructible
$k_*L$, is constructible by
[lem-weil-pbc-constructible-subobjects-noetherian].
Finally the short exact sequence

$$
0\longrightarrow j_*K\longrightarrow j_*F
\longrightarrow I\longrightarrow0
$$

and [thm-constructible-serre] prove the claim.
This argument uses only the left exactness of $j_*$.

attrs.title: Constructibility of the degree-zero open direct image

objects.body:
Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an
open immersion of
finite-type schemes over a field $k$, and let $F$ be a finite
constructible
$\Lambda$-sheaf with the prime-to-characteristic finite
coefficients of this blueprint.
Every higher direct image
$R^qj_*F$ is constructible, and they vanish for all sufficiently
large $q$. For $q>0$ their restrictions to $U$ vanish.

## Proof

The bounded constructibility assertion is
[cor-fin-deligne-open-finite-coefficients], applied to the sheaf
$F$ in degree zero. To check the support assertion, choose an
injective resolution $F\to I^\bullet$ on $U_{\rm et}$.
The section definition in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] gives
$j^*j_*I^\bullet=I^\bullet$. Exactness of the inverse image in
[def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] gives
$j^*\mathcal H^q(Rj_*F)=\mathcal H^q(F)=0$ for $q>0$.

Every projective morphism
between schemes of finite type over $k$ satisfies
$\mathcal C(f)$ of [def-finrepair-property-c].

## Proof

[thm-fin-projective-line-constructible] proves projective-line
constructibility over every finite-type base. Apply
[lem-finrepair-projective-from-line].

Let $f:X\to S$ be projective
between schemes of finite type
over a field. Assume its geometric fibres have dimension at most one,
and let $\ell$ be a prime invertible on $S$.
Every higher direct image
$R^qf_*\mathbf F_\ell$ is
constructible.

## Proof

First suppose $S$ is integral. After restriction to a nonempty open,
[lem-fin-generic-curve-model] gives a finite surjection $p:S'\to S$
and a finite comparison $Y\to T=(X_{S'})_{\mathrm{red}}$, an isomorphism
away from a closed subset finite over $S'$.
Each component of $Y$ is either a smooth projective curve family
or finite etale. Its constant-coefficient higher direct images are
constructible by
[thm-fin-projective-smooth-curve-finiteness], [lem-fin-finite-morphism].
Their finite direct sum has the same property.
Apply [lem-finrepair-constant-finite-comparison] to $Y\to T$.
The equivalence for the nilpotent closed immersion
$T\hookrightarrow X_{S'}$ in
[thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance]
identifies direct images and constant coefficients, proving
constructibility for $X_{S'}\to S'$.

Put $E_q=R^qf_*\mathbf F_\ell$.
Proper base change [cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-finite]
identifies $p^*E_q$ with the just computed sheaf.
Finite direct image preserves constructibility by
[lem-fin-finite-morphism], so $p_*p^*E_q$ is constructible.
The unit $E_q\to p_*p^*E_q$ is injective: on stalks it is the
diagonal into a nonempty finite product, by
[lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula].
Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-subobjects-noetherian]
makes $E_q$ constructible on this open of $S$.
This proves the required dense-open assertion over every integral base.

For completeness, pass from it to all of $S$ as follows.
Fix $q$ and use Noetherian induction on reduced closed subsets $Z\subset S$.
Proper base change identifies $E_q|_Z$ with the direct image for
the projective family $X_Z\to Z$, whose fibres still have dimension
at most one. If $Z$ is irreducible, it is integral; the preceding
argument gives a nonempty open where $E_q|_Z$ is constructible.
Apply induction to its proper closed complement and combine the
two finite locally closed partitions.
If $Z$ is reducible, it has finitely many components $Z_i$ by
[lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-components]; induction applies
to each, since it is a proper closed subset.
Restrict their partitions to
$Z_i\setminus\bigcup_{j<i}Z_j$ to make them disjoint.
This gives constructibility on $Z$ in the precise sense of
[def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes].
Reduction of $S$ has the same etale topos by the same invariance
theorem. Thus the argument also covers a nonreduced $S$.

attrs.title: Constant coefficients on projective families of dimension at most one

objects.body:
Let $S$ be of finite type
over $k$, and let $\Lambda$ be the finite ring killed by an
integer invertible in $k$ of [sbc-def-coefficient-conventions].
For every constructible
$\Lambda$-sheaf $F$ on $\mathbf P^1_S$, every
higher direct image
$R^q\pi_*F$, for $\pi:\mathbf P^1_S\to S$, is constructible.

## Proof

First regard $F$ as a sheaf of $\mathbf Z/N$-modules.
Apply [lem-fin-finite-type-pushforward-embedding] to embed it
into a finite sum $G^0$ of finite pushforwards of constant finite
groups killed by $N$.
The sheaf $G^0$ is constructible by [lem-fin-finite-morphism];
its cokernel $Q_1$ is constructible by
[thm-constructible-serre].
Repeat with $Q_1$, and inductively with every subsequent cokernel.
Factoring the differentials through those cokernels produces an exact
augmented complex

$$
0\to F\to G^0\to G^1\to\cdots ,
\qquad G^a=\bigoplus_i(h_{ai})_*\underline {M_{ai}},
$$

with each $h_{ai}:Y_{ai}\to\mathbf P^1_S$ finite.
By [lem-fin-finite-over-projective], $Y_{ai}\to S$ is projective.
Its geometric fibres have dimension at most one, since they are
finite over a projective line. Thus
[cor-fin-projective-curve-finite-group] applies to $M_{ai}$.
Finite exactness and the composition sequence of
[lem-fin-finite-morphism], [lem-weil-pbc-grothendieck-spectral-sequence]
give

$$
R^b\pi_*G^a
=\bigoplus_i R^b(\pi h_{ai})_*\underline {M_{ai}},
$$

which is constructible in every degree.

Now use [thm-sp-if-e1] for the ordinary bounded-below resolution:

$$
E_1^{a,b}=R^b\pi_*G^a\Longrightarrow R^{a+b}\pi_*F,
\qquad a,b\geq0.
$$

All pages are constructible by kernels and cokernels.
For any fixed total degree, first-quadrant convergence supplies
a finite filtration by stable terms of this spectral sequence.
Extensions therefore prove constructibility of the abutment by
[thm-constructible-serre].
This step establishes constructibility degree by degree.

Finally these are also the underlying abelian higher direct images
of the original $\Lambda$-sheaf. Here is an explicit simultaneous
computation. Choose a conservative family $P$ of geometric points
of $\mathbf P^1_S$, let $e^*$ take the family of stalks, and set
$e_*((M_x))=\prod_{x\in P}x_*M_x$.
Both $e_*$ and $\pi_*e_*$ are exact on families of modules:
on any etale object their sections are products of the module
coordinates, and products of surjections of modules are surjective.
Also $e_*$ preserves injectives, being right adjoint to the exact
stalk functor $e^*$.
The ordinary composition spectral sequence therefore makes every
$e_*((M_x))$ acyclic for $\pi_*$.
Iterate the injective unit $E\to e_*e^*E$ on its successive
cokernels. This is an acyclic resolution, with all maps
$\Lambda$-linear; it remains an acyclic resolution on underlying
abelian sheaves by the identical argument.
Thus it computes both higher direct images, with the same
underlying abelian cohomology.
This argument uses products of modules in an explicit section
calculation, and does not assert that arbitrary products of
epimorphisms of sheaves are epimorphisms.
On each finite locally constant abelian stratum the finitely many
scalar actions are maps of finite locally constant sheaves.
A common etale refinement makes their values constant. The given
module identities then identify the stratum with a constant finite
$\Lambda$-module, proving the module constructibility required
by [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes].

attrs.title: Constructible coefficients on the projective line

objects.body:
Let $S$ be Noetherian
and let $f:X\to S$ be
projective and
smooth, with geometric fibres
of pure dimension one. If $\ell$ is a prime invertible on $S$,
every higher direct image
$R^rf_*\mathbf F_\ell$ is
constructible.

## Proof

The morphism is proper by [lem-pc-projective-proper].
Proper base change [cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-finite]
identifies its stalks with $H^r(X_{\bar s},\mathbf F_\ell)$.
These stalks are finite and have constructible cardinalities by
[lem-fin-projective-curve-betti-cardinalities].
The fully proved criterion
[fin4-lem-stalk-constructibility-criterion] now applies to
the sheaf $R^rf_*\mathbf F_\ell$.
Proper base change was used only as an isomorphism; finiteness
of the fibre groups came from the curve calculation.

attrs.title: Constant-coefficient finiteness for projective smooth curves

objects.body:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a proper
morphism with $S$ of finite type over $k$, all
geometric fibres of $f$
of dimension at most $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, and let $F$ be a
constructible
$\Lambda$-sheaf on $X_{{\mathrm{et}}}$. Then $R^qf_*F$ of
[def-weil-pbc-direct-image] is constructible on $S_{{\mathrm{et}}}$
for every $q\geq0$, and $R^qf_*F=0$ for $q>2d$.

## Proof

Constructibility follows from
[thm-fin-proper-constructibility-complete], applied to the given
proper morphism and constructible coefficient sheaf.
For every geometric point $\bar s$, proper base change
[cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-finite] identifies

$$
(R^qf_*F)_{\bar s}=H^q(X_{\bar s},F|_{X_{\bar s}}).
$$

The right side is zero above twice the specified fibre-dimension
bound by [fin4-lem-fibrewise-cohomological-dimension].
Geometric stalk conservativity
[lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] proves the sheaf vanishing.
Each fibre group is finite because constructible sheaves have finite
stalks by [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes].
The constructibility proof uses finite resolutions and proper
modifications; the sharp bound is obtained separately from this
geometric-fibre calculation.

attrs.title: The proper case: direct images of proper morphisms

objects.body:
Every proper morphism
between schemes of finite type over $k$ satisfies
$\mathcal C(f)$ of [def-finrepair-property-c].

## Proof

The assertion is local on the target in the Zariski topology:
restriction to an open commutes with derived direct image because
open restriction has exact extension by zero as a left adjoint and
thus preserves injectives. Constructibility glues on a finite
open cover by refining finite partitions. We may assume $S$ affine.

Fix $f:X\to S$ and use Noetherian induction on closed subsets
$Z\subset X$, with their reduced structures.
For the empty set there is nothing to prove.
For nonempty $Z$, the morphism $f_Z:Z\to S$ is proper.
By [lem-fin-noetherian-chow-modification], choose
$\pi:Y\to Z$ proper, an isomorphism over a dense open $U\subset Z$,
with $Y\to S$ projective.
Its direct images are constructible by
[thm-fin-projective-constructibility-complete].
The complement $Z\setminus U$ is a proper closed subset, so its
proper map to $S$ has the desired property by induction.
Apply [lem-finrepair-modification-c].
That lemma uses $R\pi_*j'_!=j_!$, proved by proper base change,
rather than dropping the positive direct images of a general
pullback. It gives the assertion for $Z$.
This completes Noetherian induction.

The nilpotent closed immersion $X_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow X$
induces the etale equivalence of
[thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance], compatible
with direct image, so the result for $Z=X_{\mathrm{red}}$ proves
it for $X$.
The spaces used are Noetherian and have finitely many components
by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-components]; hence every
partition and target cover in this argument can be taken finite.

Let $Y$ be a separated finite-type scheme over
$k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, and let $A=A_{E,n}$.
On either the small etale site or the small pro-etale site,

$$
D_Y=R\mathcal Hom_A(-,\omega_Y),\qquad \omega_Y=Ra_Y^!A,
$$

is a contravariant exact anti-equivalence of $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$,
and the natural map $\delta_K:K\to D_YD_YK$ is an isomorphism.
No boundary duality input is a hypothesis of this theorem.

## Proof

Etale preservation and biduality are
[lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata], [thm-weil-etale-geometric-biduality].
Every pro-etale constructible finite-Tor complex descends to the etale
category by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude].
The evaluation-compatible comparison of
[lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison] transports both assertions
and the natural double-dual isomorphism to that category.

Let $(\mathcal C,F)$ be a Galois category and
$G=\operatorname{Aut}(F)$. Then $\mathcal C\to \text{finite-}G\text{-}\mathbf{Sets}$, $X\mapsto F(X)$ with the induced
$G$-action, is an equivalence of categories.

## Proof

Let $(\mathcal C,F)$ be a Galois category in the sense of
[def-galois-category] and $G=\operatorname{Aut}(F)$, profinite by
[lem-galois-aut-profinite].
The functor is well defined: each $F(X)$ is finite, and the action of
$G$ on it is continuous by [lem-galois-action-continuous], so $F(X)$ is a
finite continuous $G$-set; morphisms go to $G$-equivariant maps by
naturality.
Step 1: faithfulness is [lem-galois-axioms](1).
Step 2: full faithfulness. Let $s:F(X)\to F(Y)$ be $G$-equivariant. Its
graph $\Gamma_s\subseteq F(X)\times F(Y)=F(X\times Y)$ is a union of
connected components: $G$ acts transitively on the fibre of a connected
component by [lem-galois-transitive], so a $G$-equivariant subset is
a union of such fibres. Hence there is a union of connected components
$Z\subseteq X\times Y$ with $F(Z)=\Gamma_s$. The projection
$F(Z)\to F(X)$ is bijective, so $Z\to X$ is an isomorphism by axiom (4),
and $s=F(f)$ for the composite $f:X\to Z\to Y$. Together with Step 1
this makes $F$ fully faithful.
Step 3: essential surjectivity. It suffices to realize $G/H$ for $H$
open of finite index. By definition of the topology on $G\le \prod_X\operatorname{Aut}(F(X))$ there are finitely many objects $X_i$,
which we may take connected, with
$\ker\bigl(G\to\prod_i\operatorname{Aut}(F(X_i))\bigr)\subseteq H$.
Choose a Galois object $Y$ mapping to a connected component of
$\prod_iX_i$ ([lem-galois-object-exists]) and identify
$F(Y)=G/U$ for the open subgroup $U$ fixing a chosen element; since
$Y$ is Galois, $U$ is normal. As $F(Y)\to F(X_i)$ is surjective,
$U\subseteq H$. Let $M\subseteq\operatorname{Aut}(Y)$ correspond to
$(H/U)^{\mathrm{op}}\subseteq(G/U)^{\mathrm{op}} =\operatorname{Aut}(Y)$, and put $X=Y/M$, the coequalizer of the maps
$m:Y\to Y$, $m\in M$. Exactness of $F$ gives
$F(X)=F(Y)/M=G/H$, as required.

Let $Y$ be connected with a geometric point $\bar y\to Y$. Then the
fibre functor induces an equivalence

$$
F_{\bar y}:\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
\pi_1(Y,\bar y)\text{-}\mathbf{Set},
$$

and likewise on $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$ under the identification of
[thm-galois-lc-etale], where
$\pi_1(Y,\bar y)=\operatorname{Aut}(F_{\bar y})$ carries the profinite
topology of [def-galois-fibre-functor]. The equivalence is compatible
with finite limits and colimits, and with base change along $Y'\to Y$ for
$Y'$ connected, where it corresponds to the passage to the open subgroup
of the fundamental group.

## Proof

By [lem-fet-galois-category] the pair
$(\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y),F_{\bar y})$ is a Galois category, so
[thm-galois-abstract-equivalence] applies with
$G=\operatorname{Aut}(F_{\bar y})=\pi_1(Y,\bar y)$ as in
[def-galois-fibre-functor], which is profinite by
[lem-galois-aut-profinite]; this is the equivalence. The
identification with $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$ is [thm-galois-lc-etale], and
the compatibility with finite limits and colimits is the exactness of
$F_{\bar y}$. For base change: by [lem-galois-transitive] the
Galois covers pro-represent the fibre functor, so the pullback of the system of Galois
covers of $Y$ along $Y'\to Y$ is a cofinal system for $Y'$, and the
limit of the corresponding automorphism groups is the stabilizer of the
fibre of a cover trivializing a connected cover of $Y'$, an open subgroup
because stabilizers in a finite continuous $\pi_1$-set are open.

attrs.title: The fibre functor is an equivalence

objects.body:
In the situation of [def-galois-categories], the functor

$$
\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)\longrightarrow\mathrm{FLC}(Y),\qquad
P\longmapsto\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_Y(-,P),
$$

where $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_Y(T,P)$ is the set of
$Y$-morphisms $T\to P$, is an equivalence of categories. It is
compatible with base change and with the fibre functors, and it carries
$M$-torsors to $M$-torsors and simply transitive $M$-actions to
simply transitive ones.

## Proof

We work with the categories $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$ and
$\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$ of [def-galois-categories], and with the
$M$-torsors of [def-weil-pbc-finite-torsors].
Step 1: the sheaf is finite locally constant. By
[lem-fet-locally-trivial] there is a surjective etale $Y'\to Y$
with $P\times_YY'\cong Y'\times S$; then
$\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_Y(Y'\times S,T)= \underline S(Y'\times_YT)$ is constant of value $S$, so the sheaf is
locally constant with finite fibres.
Step 2: full faithfulness. For finite etale $P,Q$ the comparison map
$\operatorname{Hom}_Y(P,Q)\to\operatorname{Hom}( \underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(-,P),\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(-,Q))$
is injective since a morphism is determined by its graph, a closed
subscheme, hence a subsheaf; it is surjective because a morphism of sheaves
is, after applying Step 1 to $P$ and $Q$ over a common cover, given by
a map of finite sets compatible with the descent data, which descends by
[lem-galois-descent], Step 1.
Step 3: essential surjectivity. Let $\mathcal F\in\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$ and
choose a surjective etale $Y'\to Y$ with $\mathcal F|_{Y'}\cong \underline S$. Put $P'=Y'\times S$, finite etale over $Y'$. The
glueing isomorphisms of $\mathcal F$ over $Y''$, transported through
the Yoneda bijection of Step 2 over $Y''$, give a descent datum for
$P'$; by [lem-galois-descent] there is a finite etale $P\to Y$
with $P\times_YY'\cong P'$, and then
$\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(-,P)\cong\mathcal F$ because both are
locally constant with value $S$ over the cover and the sheaf condition
glues the identification.
Step 4: the compatibilities and the torsor statement are as in the
statement: the fibre of the sheaf of morphisms is
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\bar y}(\bar y,P)=|P_{\bar y}|$, and an $M$-action
on $P$ corresponds to one on the sheaf, the map
$M\times P\to P\times_YP$ being an isomorphism exactly when the action on
each fibre is simply transitive.

attrs.title: Finite locally constant sheaves and finite etale schemes

objects.body:
In the situation of [def-galois-categories], let $M$ be a finite
abelian group. Then the construction below is a canonical bijection

$$
\operatorname{Tor}^1(Y,M)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^1(Y_{\Et},\underline M),
$$

natural in $(Y,M)$. For a curve the statement is proved independently in
the smooth-curve chapter by $\operatorname{Ext}^1$ and the Baer-sum
description of torsors.

## Proof

We use the $M$-torsors of [def-weil-pbc-finite-torsors], the
cohomology $H^1(Y_{\Et},-)$ of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]
and the dictionary of [thm-galois-lc-etale] between finite locally
constant sheaves and finite etale schemes.
Step 1: the lifting torsor. Choose $0\to\underline M\to I\xrightarrow{d}J\to0$ as in [lem-galois-flasque] and let $s\in J(Y)$ represent a class in $H^1(Y_{\Et},\underline M)$. Define
$P_s(U)=\{x\in I(U):d(x)=s|_U\}$, a sheaf of sets with the translation
action of $\underline M$.
Step 2: $P_s$ is an $M$-torsor. If $x,x'\in P_s(U)$ then
$d(x-x')=0$, so $x'-x\in\ker d(U)=\underline M(U)$; hence
$M\times P_s\to P_s\times P_s$, $(m,x)\mapsto(x+m,x)$, is an
isomorphism. It is locally nonempty because $J$ is the quotient sheaf of
$I$: over a cover $\{U_i\}$ there are $x_i\in I(U_i)$ with
$d(x_i)=s|_{U_i}$, and then $P_s|_{U_i}\cong\underline M|_{U_i}$. So
$P_s$ is finite locally constant with simply transitive $M$-action,
i.e. an $M$-torsor.
Step 3: well-definedness and naturality. Translation by $x\in I(Y)$
identifies $P_{s+d(x)}\cong P_s$, so $s\mapsto[P_s]$ factors through
$\operatorname{coker}(d_Y)\cong H^1(Y_{\Et},\underline M)$; functoriality
of $I,J,d$ and of pullback gives naturality.
Step 4: injectivity. Suppose $P_s\cong P_{s'}$. Trivialize both over a
cover $\{U_i\}$ and choose $p_i\in P_s(U_i)$, $p_i'\in P_{s'}(U_i)$.
Over $U_i$ the isomorphism is translation by $a_i=p_i'-p_i\in I(U_i)$;
over $U_{ij}$ the two trivializations differ by an element of
$\underline M(U_{ij})$, and compatibility of the isomorphism with the
torsor structures says exactly that the $a_i$ agree on overlaps, so they
glue to $a\in I(Y)$ with $d(a)=s'-s$. Hence $s-s'\in \operatorname{im}(d_Y)$ and the classes agree.
Step 5: surjectivity. Let $P$ be an $M$-torsor and trivialize it over
a cover $\{U_i\to Y\}$ with sections $p_i\in P(U_i)$ (possible by
Step 2 applied to the locally constant structure); put
$c_{ij}=p_i-p_j\in\underline M(U_{ij})$. The $c_{ij}$ form a Čech
1-cocycle. The Čech complex of the Godement sheaf $I$ of
[lem-galois-flasque] with respect to any covering is acyclic in
positive degrees: at each geometric point it is the cochain complex
of the nerve of a surjection of sets, which is contractible, and
products of such complexes are again acyclic in positive degrees.
Hence $c_{ij}=a_i|_{U_{ij}}-a_j|_{U_{ij}}$ for some
$a_i\in I(U_i)$. The sections $d(a_i)\in J(U_i)$ agree on the
overlaps, because $d(c_{ij})=0$, so they glue to $s\in J(Y)$, and
$a_i\in P_s(U_i)$ are trivializations of the lifting torsor $P_s$ with
transition data $a_i-a_j=c_{ij}$. Both $P$ and $P_s$ are therefore
glued from the trivial torsors $\underline M|_{U_i}$ by the same
cocycle $(c_{ij})$, so $P\cong P_s$.
Steps 1–5 give the bijection.

Let $k$ be a separably closed
field and let $X$ and $Y$ be schemes of finite type over $k$.
Let $n\ge1$ be an integer invertible in $k$. Then for
$E\in D(X_{\Et},\kunZn)$ and $K\in D(Y_{\Et},\kunZn)$ the
Kunneth map of [def-kun-kunneth-map]

$$
\kappa_{E,K}:\RGamma(X_{\Et},E)\kunotimes{\kunZn}\RGamma(Y_{\Et},K)
\longrightarrow
\RGamma\bigl((X\times_kY)_{\Et},
\pr_1^{-1}E\kunotimes{\kunZn}\pr_2^{-1}K\bigr)
$$

is an isomorphism. (*Source:* Stacks Project, Tag
[0F1P](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F1P).)

## Proof

By [lem-kun-0f1n] applied to the diagram

$$
\begin{array}{ccccc}
X&\xleftarrow{\;=\;}&X&\xleftarrow{\;\pr_1\;}&X\times_kY\\
\Big\downarrow{}&&\Big\downarrow{}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle \pr_2}\\
\Spec(k)&\longleftarrow&\Spec(k)&\xleftarrow{\;=\;}&Y
\end{array}
$$

(all schemes of finite type over $k$, $n$ invertible in $k$) we
have the isomorphism

$$
\varphi:
E\kunotimes{\kunZn}\underline{\RGamma(Y_{\Et},K)}
\longrightarrow
R\pr_{1,*}\bigl(\pr_1^{-1}E\kunotimes{\kunZn}\pr_2^{-1}K\bigr).
$$

We conclude by [lem-kun-kunneth-via-0f1n] and the following
two identifications: first,
$\RGamma((X\times_kY)_{\Et},-)\cong\RGamma(X_{\Et},-)\circ R\pr_{1,*}$
by [lem-kun-leray-unbdd], which applies because $\pr_1$ is a
qcqs morphism of finite type schemes over $k$ and
$\kuncd(\pr_1)<\infty$ by [lem-kun-0f10](1); second,

$$
\RGamma\bigl(X_{\Et},E\kunotimes{\kunZn}\underline{\RGamma(Y_{\Et},K)}\bigr)
\cong\RGamma(X_{\Et},E)\kunotimes{\kunZn}\RGamma(Y_{\Et},K)
$$

by [lem-kun-0f12], which applies because
$\kuncd(X)<\infty$ by [lem-kun-cd-sep-closed-point] and
[lem-kun-0f10](2). Hence $\kappa_{E,K}$ (the Kunneth map of
[def-kun-kunneth-map]) is an isomorphism, as desired.

**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: blow-ups are never
base-changed along a flat morphism. Every base-change step the route takes
goes through the universal property
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.exists_lift_blowup` and
the chart pullback squares
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.isPullback_blowup$\iota$`
instead.

The constructed comparison $\operatorname{bc}_g$ is an isomorphism over
$Y$.

## Proof

Relative Proj sends the graded equivalence of
[lemma-nagata-flat-pullback-rees] to an affine-local isomorphism.
Compatibility with degree zero identifies the structure maps, and the
localization cocycle glues the local isomorphisms.

If $\mathcal I$ is a finite type quasi-coherent ideal on $X$, then on
$\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$ the extended ideal
$\mathcal I\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)}$ is locally
principal, generated locally by a non-zero-divisor, and hence is an
invertible ideal defining an effective Cartier divisor.

## Proof

Work locally on an arbitrary affine open of $X$. Finite type of
$\mathcal I$ gives finitely many generators on that affine, and the
corresponding standard charts cover its blow-up. Use
[lemma-nagata-chart-extended-ideal-principal] and
[lemma-nagata-chart-generator-regular]. The local principal ideals
glue because their generators differ by units by
[lemma-nagata-chart-generators-associated].

The constructed maps $\Phi_{\mathcal I,\mathcal J}$ and
$\Psi_{\mathcal I,\mathcal J}$ are inverse over $X$. Thus the iterated
blow-up is identified with the blow-up of $\mathcal I\mathcal J$.

## Proof

Write $p\colon X_{\mathcal I,\mathcal J}\to X$ for the composite and
$q\colon\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal J}(X)\to X$ for the
product blow-up. The construction of $\Phi_{\mathcal I,\mathcal J}$ is
the unique $X$-morphism whose pullback of the tautological invertible
quotient on the product blow-up is the product of the two tautological
quotients on $X_{\mathcal I,\mathcal J}$. Conversely, the construction of
$\Psi_{\mathcal I,\mathcal J}$ first uses the invertible quotient
$q^*\mathcal I$ and then the invertible quotient of the pullback of
$\mathcal J$; their product is the tautological quotient of
$q^*(\mathcal I\mathcal J)$. Thus both composites are $X$-morphisms
pulling back the relevant tautological quotient to itself. Apply uniqueness
in [thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property] first for the product
blow-up to obtain $\Phi\circ\Psi=\mathrm{id}$. For the other composite,
first apply uniqueness for the $\mathcal I$-blow-up to see that its
projection to $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$ is the original first
projection. It is therefore a morphism over
$\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$, and uniqueness for the second blow-up
gives $\Psi\circ\Phi=\mathrm{id}$.

Under the data of [thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property], the constructed
map $\widetilde f$ is the unique $X$-morphism from $Y$ to
$\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$ inducing the chosen invertible
quotient. Thus the blow-up is final among such $X$-schemes.

## Proof

Existence is [thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property], and uniqueness
among $X$-morphisms inducing the specified quotient is
[thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property]. Together these are exactly the
asserted final-object property.

## Graded map induced by an invertible quotient

Let $f\colon Y\to X$, let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be a
quasi-coherent ideal, and let
$\mathcal L\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_Y$ be an invertible ideal together with
a surjection $q\colon f^*\mathcal I\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal L$ such that
the composite $\mathcal L\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_Y$ after $q$ is the
canonical map whose image is the extended ideal
$\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y$ of
[def-nagata-extended-ideal]. Define $\alpha_f$ degreewise by the
tensor powers of this quotient:

$$
\alpha_f\colon
f^*\Bigl(\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal I^n\Bigr)
\longrightarrow\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal L^{\otimes n}.
$$

## The quotient construction is a graded algebra map

The degreewise map $\alpha_f$ respects the unit and multiplication and is a
graded algebra morphism.

*Proof.*
In degree $n$, tensor $q$ $n$ times. Let
$\mu_{\mathcal I}\colon(f^*\mathcal I)^{\otimes n}\to f^*(\mathcal I^n)$ be multiplication. The composite of $q^{\otimes n}$
with
multiplication isomorphism
$\mathcal L^{\otimes n}\cong\mathcal L^n$ from
[lemma-nagata-invertible-ideal-tensor-power] and the injection
$\mathcal L^n\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_Y$ is ordinary $n$-fold
multiplication. It therefore kills $\ker(\mu_{\mathcal I})$; injectivity
of $\mathcal L^n\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_Y$ shows that $q^{\otimes n}$
itself kills this kernel. Hence it factors uniquely through
$f^*(\mathcal I^n)$. These factorizations commute with multiplication by
associativity and with the degree-zero unit, giving the graded algebra map.
Associativity of tensor products and the multiplication maps for ideal
powers show that these degreewise maps preserve the unit and multiplication.

## Universal lift construction

Under the data of
[thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property], use the inverse of the canonical isomorphism in
[lemma-nagata-relative-proj-invertible-tensor-powers], apply the
contravariant relative-Proj map induced by $\alpha_f$. Then use the
arbitrary base-change comparison in
[lemma-nagata-relative-proj-base-change-arbitrary] to identify the
resulting target with $Y\times_X\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$. Here
$\operatorname{Proj}_X(\mathcal R_X(\mathcal I))$ is identified with
[def-nagata-global-blowup]: both are obtained by gluing the same affine
Rees-algebra Proj schemes, and the comparison respects the restriction
cocycles. Compose
the resulting map with the second projection
$Y\times_X\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)\to \operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$, and
define

$$
\widetilde f\colon Y\longrightarrow\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)
$$

to be the resulting composite. The affine maps and their gluing data are
part of the relative-Proj interface; no identification of $Y$ with a Proj
is left implicit.

## Uniqueness of the universal lift

Under the data of [thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property], every $X$-morphism
$h\colon Y\to\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$ inducing the chosen
invertible quotient equals the constructed map $\widetilde f$.

*Proof.*
On each affine open of $X$, let $D_+(f)$ range over the standard opens
indexed by the degree-one elements $f\in\mathcal I$; these opens cover the
blow-up Proj. The inverse image of each chart
under $h$ is determined by the degree-zero map obtained from the given
quotient $f^*\mathcal I\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal L$: on a representative
$x/f_i^n$ it is the coefficient of the corresponding quotient fraction in
$\mathcal O_Y$. The constructed lift uses exactly the same degreewise maps,
by definition of $\alpha_f$ and the tensor-power identification, so $h$ and
$\widetilde f$ agree on each inverse-image chart. These equalities are
compatible on chart overlaps because both maps send a localized fraction to
its further localization; the localization cocycle gives literal equality.
The standard charts cover the target, hence their inverse images cover $Y$,
and equality of morphisms on this cover implies $h=\widetilde f$.

## The constructed lift lies over $X$

Under the data of [thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property], the constructed
map $\widetilde f$ is an $X$-morphism: its composite with
$b_{X,\mathcal I}$ is $f$.

*Proof.*
On each standard chart, the degree-zero component of
[thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property] is the canonical map to
$\mathcal O_Y$, hence the composite with the blow-up structure map is $f$.
The chart maps agree on overlaps by functoriality of localization, and the
glued equality is therefore the specified equality over $X$.

The explicitly constructed factorization
$\mathsf C_{\mathrm{Nag}}(f)$ is a compactification of $f$. In particular,
every separated finite type morphism to a quasi-compact and
quasi-separated scheme is compactifiable.

## Proof

$\mathsf C_{\mathrm{Nag}}(f)$ is the composition of two maps $j_f$ and $p_f$. The first map is a quasi-compact open immersion by
[lemma-nagata-final-open-immersion]; the second is proper by
[lemma-nagata-final-ambient-proper]; and their composite is $f$ by
[lemma-nagata-final-factorization]. These are exactly the fields of
[def-nagata-compactification]. Hence the named construction is a
compactification, and its existence witnesses compactifiability.

With $Z=V(\mathcal I)$ as above, the two constructed comparison maps are
inverse over $X$. Hence the
composite is the blow-up of the finite-presentation center
$Y(Z')=V(\mathcal K(Z'))\hookrightarrow X$, whose support satisfies

$$
|Y(Z')|=|Z|\cup b(|Z'|).
$$

## Proof

Put $X_1=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$ and
$\mathcal J'=\mathcal J\mathcal O_{X_1}$. By the extended-ideal equality,
$\mathcal J'=\mathcal I_E^d\mathcal I_{Z'}$. The product-ideal comparison
[thm-nagata-blowup-product-ideal] therefore gives an isomorphism over
$X$

$$
\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J'}(X_1)
\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal J}(X).
$$

Since $\mathcal I_E^d$ is invertible, the invertible-factor comparison
[lemma-nagata-blowup-invertible-factor] gives a canonical isomorphism
$\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I_{Z'}}(X_1)\cong \operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J'}(X_1)$. Their composite is the map
$\Omega_{Z,Z'}$ in the definition; the reverse composite of the inverse
comparisons is the stated reverse map.

For completeness, these maps are the universal lifts for the same quotient:
on the iterated blow-up the product of the tautological invertible quotients
is the tautological quotient of $\mathcal I\mathcal J$, while on the
$\mathcal I\mathcal J$-blow-up its two factor quotients give the tautological
quotients for $\mathcal I$ and for $\mathcal J'$; multiplying by the inverse
of the local generator of $\mathcal I_E^d$ gives the quotient for
$\mathcal I_{Z'}$. Thus each composite is an $X$-morphism inducing the
original tautological quotient. Uniqueness in the blow-up universal
property, first over $X$ and then over $X_1$, makes both composites identities.
The center ideal $\mathcal K=\mathcal I\mathcal J$ is finite type, hence
defines a finite-presentation closed immersion, and
[lemma-nagata-composition-center-ideal] gives its support as
$|V(\mathcal I)|\cup b(|Z'|)$.

Let $S$ be qcqs and let $X$ and $Y$ be qcqs $S$-schemes with $Y\to S$
separated and of finite type. Let $U\subseteq V\subseteq X$ be dense open
subschemes whose open immersions into $X$ are quasi-compact, and let $(U,f)$
be a quasi-domination of $V$ over $Y$ in the sense of
[def-nagata-conrad-quasi-domination]. There exists a $V$-admissible
blow-up $\widetilde X\to X$ such that $\widetilde X$ quasi-dominates $Y$ in a
manner extending $f\colon U\to Y$.

## Proof

The morphism $f$ is automatically quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
Replacing $Y$ by $Y\times_SX$ we may assume $X=S$; thus $p\colon Y\to X$ is
separated and of finite type and $f\colon U\to Y$ is a section of $p$ over
$U$ whose image is closed in the part of $Y$ lying over $V$.

If $p$ is quasi-affine, this is
[lemma-nagata-conrad-quasi-affine-general]. In general, let
$q\colon\widetilde X\to X$ be the $V$-admissible blow-up produced by
[lemma-nagata-conrad-graph-closure-quasi-finite] and let
$\overline{F(U)}\subseteq\widetilde X\times_XY$ be the scheme-theoretic image
of $F=(\sigma,f)$. That lemma makes
$\overline{F(U)}\to\widetilde X$ quasi-finite and separated, so
[lemma-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism-of-quasi-finite] makes it
quasi-affine as a morphism to $\widetilde X$. (Note that $\widetilde X$ is a
blow-up of a qcqs scheme and is not itself quasi-affine, so the absolute form
of quasi-affineness is not available here.)

By [lemma-nagata-conrad-blowup-base-change-reduction] we may base change
along the $V$-admissible blow-up $q$ without leaving the statement of the
theorem; [lemma-nagata-conrad-dense-in-admissible-blowup] keeps $U$ and
$V$ dense. After that base change the scheme-theoretic image
$\overline{f(U)}$ of $U$ in $Y$ is quasi-affine over the base, so
[lemma-nagata-conrad-closed-target-reduction] lets us replace $Y$ by
$\overline{f(U)}$, and we are reduced to the quasi-affine case already
treated.

Let $U=X\setminus V(\mathcal I)$. The restriction

$$
b_{X,\mathcal I}^{-1}(U)\longrightarrow U
$$

is an isomorphism.

## Proof

Cover $X$ by affine opens. Under
[prop-nagata-global-blowup-cover-independent], the restriction over each
affine is the affine complement isomorphism of
[lemma-nagata-affine-blowup-complement]. These local isomorphisms glue,
and isomorphisms are local on source and target.

If $\mathcal I$ is of finite type, then
$b_{X,\mathcal I}$ is proper.

## Proof

Apply [lemma-nagata-global-blowup-proper-local] to the affine open cover
of $X$. Each restricted morphism is proper, and
[lemma-nagata-projective-target-local] is the verified target-local
properness lemma (despite its historical label). It follows that
$b_{X,\mathcal I}$ is proper. This argument does not use the unresolved
global projectivity theorem.

The recursively constructed factorization
$\mathsf C_{\mathrm{Noeth}}(X/S)$ is a compactification of $X\to S$.
Consequently $X\to S$ is compactifiable.

## Proof

The final component $h_n$ of the dependent recursive datum in
[def-nagata-noetherian-compactification] has the three fields required
by [def-nagata-compactification], and $X_n=X$. Thus
$\mathsf C_{\mathrm{Noeth}}(X/S)$ is a compactification of $X\to S$. No
later induction theorem is used to define any earlier $\mathsf C_r$.

attrs.title: Nagata compactification over a Noetherian base

objects.body:
Under the preceding hypotheses, the comparison morphism
$\psi_{f,\mathcal I}$ identifies the blow-up of $Y$ in the extended ideal
$\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y$ with the strict transform of $Y$: there is an
isomorphism
$\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y}(Y)\cong Y^{\mathrm{st}}$
compatible with the projections to $Y$ and with the structure morphisms
to $X$. No finiteness hypotheses on $\mathcal I$ are needed.

## Proof

Write $U=X\setminus V(\mathcal I)$ and let
$\Omega\subseteq Y\times_XX'$ be the open locus over $U$, whose
scheme-theoretic closure is the strict transform
([def-nagata-strict-transform]). Both $\psi_{f,\mathcal I}$ and the
inclusion of $\Omega$ are cut out by quasi-coherent kernels, and it
suffices to identify the two kernels. The blow-up of
$\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y$ is an isomorphism over the preimage of $U$
([thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement]), which identifies $\Omega$
with the preimage $\Omega'$ of $f^{-1}(U)$ in
$\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y}(Y)$, compatibly with
$\psi_{f,\mathcal I}$ — the two composites into $X'$ agree by the
uniqueness part of [thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property], since both
lie over $U$ where the pulled-back ideal is the unit ideal. The
exceptional ideal is invertible, i.e. locally generated by a
nonzerodivisor, so $\Omega'$ is schematically dense in
$\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y}(Y)$ (the blow-up part of
[lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-preserves-density]). Hence
precomposing $\psi_{f,\mathcal I}$ with the schematically dense open
$\Omega'\cong\Omega$ does not change the kernel, and the kernel of
$\psi_{f,\mathcal I}$ equals the kernel of the inclusion of $\Omega$.
Since $\psi_{f,\mathcal I}$ is a closed immersion
([def-nagata-strict-transform-blowup-comparison]), it factors as an
isomorphism onto the strict transform, and the stated compatibilities
hold by construction.

The constructed factorization $\mathsf C_{12}(U/S)$ is a compactification
of $U\to S$. Consequently $U\to S$ is compactifiable.

## Proof

By [lemma-nagata-two-open-final-modification], the first map
$j_W\colon U\to W$ is an open immersion and $W\to S$ is separated and of
finite type. It is proper by
[lemma-nagata-two-open-candidate-proper]. The open immersion $j_W$ is
quasi-compact by
[lemma-nagata-open-immersion-qc-over-separated-target], applied to the
triangle $U\to W\to S$. The defining gluing maps give the factorization
equality, so all fields of [def-nagata-compactification] are present.

(Picard Schemes of Curves, Lemma 44.5.1, Tag
[0B9Q](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B9Q).)
Let $k$ be a field and let
$G:(\mathit{Sch}/k)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\textit{Groups}$ be a functor. With the
terminology of
Definition [def-pc-subfunctor], assume:

1. **(1)** $G$ satisfies the sheaf property for the Zariski topology ([def-pc-zariski-sheaf-property]);
1. **(2)(a)** there exists a subfunctor $F\subseteq G$ such that $F$ is
representable;
1. **(2)(b)** $F\subseteq G$ is representable by open immersions ([def-pc-open-subfunctor]);
1. **(2)(c)** for every field extension $K$ of $k$ and every
$g\in G(K)$ there exists $g'\in G(k)$ such that $g'g\in F(K)$.

Then $G$ is representable by a group scheme over $k$.

## Proof

Apply [lem-pc-schemes-criterion] with $S=\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ and $I=G(k)$: for
$i=g'\in I$ let $F_i\subseteq G$ be the subfunctor

$$
F_i(T):=\{g\in G(T):g'g\in F(T)\}.
$$

Then $F_i\cong F$ via multiplication by $g'$ (a natural isomorphism
because $G$ is a functor with values in groups), so $F_i$ is
representable by (2)(a), and $F_i\subseteq G$ is representable by open
immersions: the map $F_i\to G$ is isomorphic (via multiplication by
$g'$) to the inclusion $F\to G$ of (2)(b), and the base change of a
natural isomorphism is a natural isomorphism. The family
$(F_i)_{i\in I}$ covers $G$ ([def-pc-cover]): given $g\in G(T)$, for each point $t\in T$
let $\kappa=\kappa(t)$ and let $j:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa\to T$; by (2)(c) applied to
$j^*g\in G(\kappa)$ there is $g'\in G(k)$ with
$g'j^*g\in F(\kappa)$, i.e. $j^*g\in F_{g'}(\kappa)$. By (2)(b) (the
open-immersion property for the pair $(T,\xi)$ with $\xi=g$, in the sense
of [def-pc-subfunctor]) there is an open
$U_\xi^{g'}\subseteq T$ such that a morphism $u:T'\to T$ factors through
$U_\xi^{g'}$ iff $u^*g\in F_{g'}(T')$; taking $T'=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa$ with
$j$ and noting that $j$ factors through the open $U$ iff the image point
$t$ lies in $U$, we find $t\in U_g^{g'}$ for the suitable $g'$, so the
open sets $U_g^{g'}$ ($g'\in G(k)$) cover $T$, and
$g|_{U_g^{g'}}\in F_{g'}(U_g^{g'})$ by the criterion. This verifies
(2)(c) of [lem-pc-schemes-criterion] (in the form of the covering
condition [def-pc-subfunctor]), while (2)(a), (2)(b) for the family
$(F_i)$ are what we just proved and (1) is the hypothesis; hence $G$ is
representable by a scheme. As $G$ takes values in groups and the
representing object is unique up to unique isomorphism, the group
structure on $G$ makes it a group scheme (the group-valued sheaf
structure is given; see the usual Yoneda argument, cf. [def-pc-representable-functor]).

(Picard Schemes of Curves, Lemma 44.6.4, Tag
[0B9X](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B9X).)
Let $k$ be a separably closed field,
let $X$ be a
smooth projective curve of
genus $g$ over $k$ with a
$k$-rational point $\sigma$, and let
$F$ be the subfunctor of
[lem-pc-f-open-subfunctor]. Then $F$ is representable by an open
subscheme of $\underline{\operatorname{Hilb}}^g_{X/k}$.

## Proof

Write $H:=\underline{\operatorname{Hilb}}^g_{X/k}$; it exists by [prop-pc-xk-integral]
(2) and [thm-pc-hilb-curves]. Let $D_{\mathrm{univ}}\subset H\times X$
be the universal divisor, and let

$$
\mathcal{L}_H:=\mathcal{O}(D_{\mathrm{univ}})\otimes
\mathrm{pr}_H^*\sigma_H^*\mathcal{O}(D_{\mathrm{univ}})^{\otimes-1}
$$

be the normalized universal module ($\sigma_H:H\to H\times X$ is the
section of $\mathrm{pr}_H$ induced by $\sigma$; the cancellation of the
$\sigma$-factors in
$\sigma_H^*\mathcal{L}_H=\sigma_H^*\mathcal{O}(D_{\mathrm{univ}})\otimes \sigma_H^*\mathrm{pr}_H^*\sigma_H^*\mathcal{O}(D_{\mathrm{univ}})^{-1}\cong\mathcal{O}_H$,
because $\mathrm{pr}_H\circ\sigma_H=\mathrm{id}_H$, shows
$\mathcal{L}_H\in\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}(H)$, [def-pc-pic-sigma-functor]). By the
Yoneda lemma ([def-pc-representable-functor]) the element
$\mathcal{L}_H$ defines a natural transformation $h_H\to\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}$.

Since $F\subseteq\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}$ is an open subfunctor
([lem-pc-f-open-subfunctor]), there is a maximal open $W\subseteq H$
such that $\mathcal{L}_H|_{W\times X}\in F(W)$; by
[def-pc-subfunctor] it is the open subscheme produced by
[lem-pc-flat-rf-open] (with $i=0$, $r=1$) applied to the proper
morphism of finite presentation
$p:H\times X\to H$ and the flat
invertible module
$\mathcal{O}(D_{\mathrm{univ}})$ (the twist by $\mathrm{pr}_H^*\sigma_H^*\mathcal{O}(D_{\mathrm{univ}})^{-1}$
does not affect the perfect-locus condition: by
[lem-pc-projection-formula] and [lem-pc-rf-base-change-flat-module],
$Rp_*$ commutes with tensoring by the pullback of an invertible module
from the base). Applying the Yoneda lemma again we obtain the commutative
diagram

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
h_W & \xrightarrow{\ \psi\ } & F\\[-2pt]
\downarrow & & \downarrow\\[-2pt]
h_H & \xrightarrow{\ \ } & \operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}
\end{array}
$$

and we show that the top horizontal arrow $\psi$ is an isomorphism.

*Construction of the inverse.* Let $\mathcal{L}\in F(T)$ for a scheme
$T$ over $k$; let $\mathcal{N}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_T$-module with
$Rf_{T,*}\mathcal{L}\cong\mathcal{N}[0]$, and let $s$ be the adjoint section of
$\mathcal{L}\otimes f_T^*\mathcal{N}^{-1}$ ([lem-pc-zero-scheme-recd]). By
[lem-pc-zero-scheme-recd], $D:=Z(s)$ is a relative effective Cartier
divisor on $X_T/T$ which is finite locally free of degree $g$; hence
$D\in\operatorname{Hilb}^g_{X/k}(T)$ ([def-pc-hilb-functor]) and, by the
representability of $\operatorname{Hilb}^g_{X/k}$ ([thm-pc-hilb-curves] (1)), there
is a morphism $m:T\to H$ with $D=(m\times\mathrm{id}_X)^*D_{\mathrm{univ}}$
(the universal object of [lem-pc-universal-divisor]).

*$m$ factors through $W$.* By
[lem-pc-recd-pullback] the pullback of the relative effective
Cartier divisor $D_{\mathrm{univ}}$ along $m$ is the divisor with
associated module

$$
(m\times\mathrm{id})^*\mathcal{O}(D_{\mathrm{univ}})\cong\mathcal{O}_{X_T}(D)\cong\mathcal{M}
=\mathcal{L}\otimes f_T^*\mathcal{N}^{-1}
$$

(the second isomorphism holds because the section $s$ of $\mathcal{M}$ has zero
scheme $D$, so $s$ generates the ideal sheaf $\mathcal{I}_D$ at the points where
it does not vanish and the identification $D=Z(s)$ gives
$\mathcal{O}_{X_T}(D)=\mathcal{I}_D^\vee$; write $u$ for this isomorphism). We compute:

$$
(m\times\mathrm{id})^*\mathcal{L}_H
=(m\times\mathrm{id})^*\mathcal{O}(D_{\mathrm{univ}})
\otimes\mathrm{pr}_T^*\bigl(m^*\sigma_H^*\mathcal{O}(D_{\mathrm{univ}})\bigr)^{-1}
=\mathcal{O}_{X_T}(D)\otimes\mathrm{pr}_T^*\sigma_T^*\mathcal{O}_{X_T}(D)^{-1}
$$

(using $(m\times\mathrm{id})\circ\sigma_T=\sigma_H\circ m$ and
$(m\times\mathrm{id})^*\mathrm{pr}_H^*=\mathrm{pr}_T^*m^*$). Since $\sigma_T^*\mathcal{O}_{X_T}(D)\cong\sigma_T^*\mathcal{M}$
$=\sigma_T^*\mathcal{L}\otimes\sigma_T^*f_T^*\mathcal{N}^{-1} =\mathcal{O}_T\otimes\mathcal{N}^{-1} =\mathcal{N}^{-1}$ (because $\mathcal{L}\in\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}(T)$ and
$\sigma_T^*f_T^*=\mathrm{id}$; here $\sigma_T^*\mathcal{O}_{X_T}(D)$ means the pullback of
the corresponding quotient of the ideal sheaf, equivalently the fibre of
$\mathcal{O}(D)$ along $\sigma_T$), we get

$$
(m\times\mathrm{id})^*\mathcal{L}_H\cong\mathcal{O}_{X_T}(D)\otimes f_T^*\mathcal{N}
\cong\mathcal{L}\otimes f_T^*\mathcal{N}^{-1}\otimes f_T^*\mathcal{N}\cong\mathcal{L}.
$$

Thus $(m\times\mathrm{id})^*\mathcal{L}_H\in F(T)$ (as $\mathcal{L}\in F(T)$ and $F$ is a
subfunctor, the restriction of $\mathcal{L}_H$ along the morphism $(m\times\mathrm{id})$
of schemes over $H$ is in $F(T)$ if and only if $m$ factors through the
open $W$ of [lem-pc-flat-rf-open], by the characterization in
[def-pc-subfunctor] for the pair $(H,\mathcal{L}_H)$ and the explicit
description of $W$ given above), so $m$ factors through $W$; we still
write $m:T\to W$.

*$\psi$ is bijective on points, with inverse
$\theta:\mathcal{L}\mapsto m$.* The two maps are natural in $T$ (all constructions
commute with base change: pullback of divisors and their modules along
$T'\to T$ by [lem-pc-recd-pullback] and [lem-pc-rf-base-change-flat-module];
the universal object property of [def-pc-hilb-functor] and the
uniqueness of the classifying morphism of [lem-pc-cartier-criterion]
give functoriality of $m$). The composite
$h_W(T)\to F(T)\to h_W(T)$, $m\mapsto(m\times\mathrm{id})^*\mathcal{L}_H\mapsto m'$: the
adjoint section of $(m\times\mathrm{id})^*\mathcal{L}_H$ is the pullback of the adjoint
section of $\mathcal{L}_H$ ([lem-pc-universal-adjoint-section], whose zero
scheme is $D_{\mathrm{univ}}$, and [lem-pc-zero-scheme-recd]), so the
zero scheme of the adjoint section of
$(m\times\mathrm{id})^*\mathcal{L}_H$ is $D=(m\times\mathrm{id})^{-1}(D_{\mathrm{univ}})$, and
$m'$ is exactly the morphism classifying $D$, i.e. $m'=m$ by the
uniqueness in the universal property. The other composite
$\theta\circ\psi=\mathrm{id}$ on $F(T)$ was computed above
($(m\times\mathrm{id})^*\mathcal{L}_H\cong\mathcal{L}$). Hence $\psi$ is an isomorphism of
functors $h_W\cong F$, i.e. $F$ is representable (by the open subscheme
$W$ of $H$, which is a scheme: open subschemes of schemes are schemes).

attrs.title: $F$ is representable by an open subscheme of $\underline{\operatorname{Hilb}}^g_{X/k}$

objects.body:
(Picard Schemes of Curves, Proposition 44.3.6, Tag
[0B9I](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B9I).) Let $X$ be a
geometrically irreducible smooth proper curve over a field $k$ and let
$d\geq0$. Then:

1. $\operatorname{Hilb}^d_{X/k}$ is representable by a smooth proper variety
$\underline{\operatorname{Hilb}}^d_{X/k}$ of dimension $d$ over $k$;
1. for a field extension $k'/k$ the $k'$-rational points of
$\underline{\operatorname{Hilb}}^d_{X/k}$ are in bijection with the effective Cartier
divisors of degree $d$ on $X_{k'}$;
1. for $d_1,d_2\geq0$ there is a morphism
$$
\underline{\operatorname{Hilb}}^{d_1}_{X/k}\times_k\underline{\operatorname{Hilb}}^{d_2}_{X/k}
\longrightarrow\underline{\operatorname{Hilb}}^{d_1+d_2}_{X/k}
$$
which is finite locally free of degree $\binom{d_1+d_2}{d_1}$.

## Proof

*Step 0: the affine-open hypothesis.*
We verify the hypotheses of [lem-pc-hilb-representable]: $X$ is proper,
hence separated, over $k$, and it remains to check the affine-open condition.
Given finitely many points $x_1,\ldots,x_d\in X$, choose a closed
point $Q$ different from every closed point in this list.
Such a $Q$ exists: the complement of finitely many closed points
is a nonempty open of the one-dimensional integral variety $X$;
a nonempty affine open inside it has a maximal ideal with residue
field finite over $k$ by Zariski's lemma. This point is closed in
$X$, since its residue field is finite over $k$.
The divisor $[Q]$ is effective Cartier on the smooth curve and
has positive degree $[\kappa(Q):k]$ by
[lem-pc-degree-base-change]. Therefore $\mathcal O_X(Q)$ is
ample by [lem-pc-ample-positive-degree], and
$X\setminus\{Q\}$ is affine by [lem-sc-ample-complement-affine].
It contains all the prescribed points, including the generic
point. This proves the affine-open hypothesis.

*Step 1: representability and the properties (1).* By
[lem-pc-hilb-representable] the functors
$\operatorname{Hilb}^d_{X/k}$ are representable by schemes $H_d:=\underline{\operatorname{Hilb}}^d_{X/k}$
for all $d\ge0$. The scheme $H_d$ is smooth of relative dimension $d$
over $k$ by [lem-pc-hilb-smooth]. It is separated over $k$: the
diagonal $\Delta:H_d\to H_d\times_kH_d$ is a closed immersion: let
$Z_1,Z_2\in\operatorname{Hilb}^d_{X/k}(H_d\times_kH_d)$ be the two pullbacks of the
universal object along the projections; a morphism $T\to H_d\times_kH_d$ factors through $\Delta$ iff $Z_{1,T}=Z_{2,T}$ (the
universal property: a $T$-valued point of $H_d\times H_d$ is a pair
of elements of $\operatorname{Hilb}^d(T)$; they are equal iff the pair comes from
$H_d$ via the diagonal); the locus $\{\,T:\ Z_{1,T}=Z_{2,T}\,\}$ is
closed in $H_d\times H_d$: it is the intersection of the closed loci
$\{Z_1\subseteq Z_2\}$ and $\{Z_2\subseteq Z_1\}$, each of which is
closed by the closed-immersion claim of the proof of
[lem-pc-hilb-representable] (Step 1 there: applied with
$Y=X_{H\times H}$, $X'=Z_1$ (closed in $X_{H\times H}$— yes: $Z_1$
is closed in $X_{H_d\times_kH_d}$) and $Z=Z_2$ – the locus where
$Z_{2,T}\subseteq Z_{1,T}$ is closed). Hence $\Delta$ is a closed
immersion, i.e. $H_d$ is separated over $k$ (the standard
characterization of separatedness via the diagonal,
[def-pc-morphism-conventions]). It is proper: by
[lem-pc-hilb-addition] the morphism
$H_{d-1}\times_kX\to H_d$ is finite locally free of degree $d$; the
iterated composite

$$
\pi_d:X^d=X\times_k\cdots\times_kX\;\longrightarrow\;H_d,
\qquad
(x_1,\dots,x_d)\longmapsto x_1+\cdots+x_d
$$

(the addition applied successively) is finite locally free of degree
$d!$ (composites of finite locally free morphisms of degrees
$1,2,\dots,d$: the degree multiplies, the classical multiplicativity:
the composite $H_{d-1}\times X\to H_d$ has degree $d$; the
projection $X^d\to X^{d-1}\times X$ is an isomorphism
($X^d\cong X^{d-1}\times X$), the composite
$X^d\to H_{d-1}\times X$ (the product of $\pi_{d-1}$ with
$\mathrm{id}_X$) has degree $(d-1)!$ by the multiplicativity of the
degree (the degree of a product of finite locally free morphisms is
the product of the degrees: the rank of the finite locally free
module attached to the fibre product is the tensor product of the
modules, whose rank multiplies), and the composite of $X^d\to H_{d-1}\times X$ with $H_{d-1}\times X\to H_d$ has degree
$(d-1)!\cdot d=d!$, the degree of a composite of finite locally free
morphisms being the product of the degrees (again multiplicativity,
or: the fibre of the composite over a point is the scheme of the
tensor product of the two finite locally free algebras, whose rank is
the product of the ranks). The morphism $\pi_d$ is
*surjective*: the image $I:=\pi_d(X^d)$ is closed
($X^d$ is proper, $\pi_d$ is finite hence proper, and the image of a
proper morphism is closed: the standard statement); for a closed
point $\bar t$ of $H_d\otimes_k\bar k$ the corresponding closed
subscheme $D_{\bar t}\subseteq X_{\bar k}$ is finite flat of rank
$d$ over $\bar k$, so it is a sum
$D_{\bar t}=y_1+\cdots+y_d$ of $\bar k$-points (with the
multiplicities $m_j$, $\sum_jm_j=d$: a finite flat scheme over an
algebraically closed field is a union of closed points with
Artinian structures), hence $\bar t$ lies in the image of
$X^d\otimes_k\bar k\to H_d\otimes_k\bar k$; so
$I\otimes_k\bar k$ contains every closed point of the scheme of
finite type $H_d\otimes_k\bar k$; since
$I\otimes_k\bar k$ is closed and the closed points of a scheme of
finite type over an algebraically closed field are dense,
$I\otimes_k\bar k=H_d\otimes_k\bar k$; as
$\bar k/k$ is faithfully flat, the closed subset $I$ has
$I\otimes_k\bar k=$ everything, hence $I=H_d$ (for a closed subset
$I$ with $I\otimes_k\bar k=H_d\otimes_k\bar k$: the closure
condition: if $x\in H_d\setminus I$ then the image point
$x_{\bar k}$ lies in $H_d\otimes\bar k\setminus I\otimes\bar k$,
contradiction). So $\pi_d$ is surjective.
Then $H_d$ is proper: $X^d$ is proper (finite products of proper schemes over $k$ are proper, the standard statement; and $X\to\operatorname{Spec} k$ is proper by hypothesis), $\pi_d$ is finite hence proper, so
$H_d=\pi_d(X^d)$ is the image of a proper scheme under a proper morphism, hence proper (Morphisms, Lemma 29.42.9, Tag
[03GN](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03GN): the image of a proper morphism is proper). Finally $H_d$ is irreducible: $X^d$ is irreducible (geometrically irreducible over $k$: products of geometrically irreducible schemes over $k$ are irreducible: Varieties, Lemma 33.8.4, Tag
[038F](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/038F)), and the image of an irreducible scheme under a continuous surjective map is irreducible; together with smoothness (hence reducedness: smooth over the field $k$ is reduced, the standard statement) $H_d$ is an integral separated scheme of finite type over $k$ of dimension $d$, i.e. a variety over $k$ ([def-pc-curve]: a variety is an integral separated scheme of finite type over $k$). This proves (1).

*Step 2: the points of $H_d$; part (2).* For a field extension
$k'/k$: a $k'$-rational point of $H_d$ is, by the representability of
[def-pc-hilb-functor], the same as an element
$Z\in\operatorname{Hilb}^d_{X/k}(k')$, i.e. a closed subscheme
$Z\subset X_{k'}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec} k}\operatorname{Spec} k'$ ([def-pc-base-change])
finite locally free of degree $d$ over $k'$. Since $X_{k'}\to k'$ is
smooth of relative dimension $1$ (base change of smooth), the
criteria of [lem-pc-cartier-criterion] apply with
$S=\operatorname{Spec}(k')$ and give: $Z\to k'$ is finite locally free
(i.e. (1)) iff $Z$ is a relative effective Cartier divisor on
$X_{k'}/k'$, iff $Z$ is an effective Cartier divisor on $X_{k'}$
(the relative condition being automatic over a field:
$Z\to k'$ is flat): i.e. the $k'$-points of $H_d$ are exactly the
effective Cartier divisors $D\subseteq X_{k'}$; its degree: the
effective Cartier divisor $D$ has degree $\deg(\mathcal{O}_{X_{k'}}(D))$
([def-pc-degree-line-bundle] and the divisor-degree formulas of
[lem-pc-degree-base-change](2)) and this equals the rank $d$ of
the finite locally free $Z\to k'$ (the classical: the degree of the
divisor is the length of $\mathcal{O}_D$, i.e. the rank over the field: the
computation of [lem-pc-degree-base-change](2): the fibre is
finite flat of rank $d$ over $k'$; and $\deg D=d$ iff the point has
degree $d$). This gives the bijection of (2).

*Step 3: the addition morphism; part (3).* For $d_1,d_2\ge0$ and
$T$ over $k$: an element of
$\operatorname{Hilb}^{d_1}_{X/k}(T)\times\operatorname{Hilb}^{d_2}_{X/k}(T)$ is a pair of closed
subschemes $D_1,D_2\subseteq X_T$ finite locally free of degrees
$d_1,d_2$ over $T$; by [lem-pc-cartier-criterion]
((1)$\Rightarrow$(2)) both are relative effective Cartier
divisors on $X_T/T$; the sum $D_1+D_2$ (the closed subscheme defined
locally by the product of the two defining equations: an effective
Cartier divisor, and flat over $T$: the short exact sequence
$0\to\mathcal{O}_{X_T}/(f_1)\to\mathcal{O}_{X_T}/(f_1f_2)\to\mathcal{O}_{X_T}/(f_2)\to0$
(exact because $f_1$ is a nonzerodivisor; the two ends flat over $T$)
shows $\mathcal{O}_{D_1+D_2}$ flat over $T$, and the rank is the sum
$d_1+d_2$) is again finite locally free of degree $d_1+d_2$ over
$T$: it is an element of $\operatorname{Hilb}^{d_1+d_2}_{X/k}(T)$. The assignment
$(D_1,D_2)\mapsto D_1+D_2$ is natural in $T$, so by the
representability of $\operatorname{Hilb}^{d_1+d_2}$ it is induced by a morphism

$$
\alpha:H_{d_1}\times_kH_{d_2}\longrightarrow H_{d_1+d_2} .
$$

The map $\alpha$ is proper, since its source is proper over $k$
and its target is separated over $k$, by part (1).
The surjection $u:=\pi_{d_1}\times\pi_{d_2}$ from
$X^{d_1+d_2}$ onto its source is finite locally free, and
$\alpha\circ u=\pi_{d_1+d_2}$ is finite locally free as well.
For every point of the target, the fibre of $\alpha$ is therefore
the surjective image of the finite fibre of $\pi_{d_1+d_2}$, so it
has finitely many points. Thus $\alpha$ is finite by
[thm-pqf-finite-iff-proper-finite-fibres].
It is flat by [lem-pc-flat-source-descent], since $u$ is a flat
surjection and the composite is flat. These are morphisms of
finite type schemes over a field, hence of finite presentation;
so $\alpha$ is finite locally free. We may now compute its rank
using the commutative diagram

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X^{d_1}\times_kX^{d_2}&\stackrel{\sim}{\longrightarrow}&X^{d_1+d_2}\\
\downarrow&&\downarrow\\
H_{d_1}\times_kH_{d_2}&\longrightarrow&H_{d_1+d_2}
\end{array}
$$

(the vertical left arrow is $\pi_{d_1}\times\pi_{d_2}$, the vertical
right $\pi_{d_1+d_2}$; the diagram commutes by the definition of $\alpha$
and the additivity of the sums). The left vertical arrow is finite
locally free of degree $d_1!\cdot d_2!$ (the degrees multiply), the
right vertical arrow of degree $(d_1+d_2)!$; with
$\deg(\alpha)=N$ the commutativity gives
$d_1!\,d_2!\,N=(d_1+d_2)!$ (the classical multiplicativity of the
degree of composites of finite locally free morphisms: the composite
has degree the product; the identity in the diagram is the identity of
the two schemes), so $N=\binom{d_1+d_2}{d_1}$. This proves (3).

attrs.title: Hilbert schemes of smooth projective curves

objects.body:
(Picard Schemes of Curves, Lemma 44.4.3, Tag
[0B9N](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B9N).)
Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes as in
Definition [def-pc-picard-functor].
Assume $f$ has a section $\sigma$ and that
$\mathcal{O}_T\to f_{T,*}\mathcal{O}_{X_T}$ is an isomorphism for all
$T\in\operatorname{Ob}((\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf})$. Then the sequence

$$
0\longrightarrow\operatorname{Pic}(T)\xrightarrow{\ f_T^*\ }\operatorname{Pic}(X_T)
\xrightarrow{\ }\operatorname{Pic}_{X/S}(T)\longrightarrow 0
$$

is exact and split, the splitting being given by
$\sigma_T^*:\operatorname{Pic}(X_T)\to\operatorname{Pic}(T)$ (i.e. for every $T$,
$\operatorname{Pic}(X_T)=\operatorname{Pic}(T)\oplus K(T)$ with
$K(T)=\operatorname{Ker}\sigma_T^*$, and $\operatorname{Pic}_{X/S}$ is the fppf
sheafification of the presheaf $K$).

## Proof

Since $\sigma$ is a section of $f$, we have
$\sigma_T^*\circ f_T^*=\mathrm{id}_{\operatorname{Pic}(T)}$; hence $f_T^*$ is injective and, by
the splitting lemma for abelian groups,
$\operatorname{Pic}(X_T)=f_T^*(\operatorname{Pic}(T))\oplus K(T)$ (for $\mathcal{L}\in\operatorname{Pic}(X_T)$,
$\mathcal{L}=f_T^*\sigma_T^*\mathcal{L}\otimes(\mathcal{L}\otimes f_T^*\sigma_T^*\mathcal{L}^{-1})$ with
the second factor in $K(T)$). By [lem-pc-pic-exact] the kernel of
$\operatorname{Pic}(X_T)\to\operatorname{Pic}_{X/S}(T)$ is exactly $f_T^*(\operatorname{Pic}(T))$, in particular
$K(T)\subseteq\operatorname{Pic}_{X/S}(T)$ (already as a subset, compatibly with the
restriction maps). By [lem-pc-k-sheaf] the presheaf $K$ is an fppf
sheaf, and it is clear from the construction (the sheafification of the
pointwise split presheaf $T\mapsto\operatorname{Pic}(X_T)$ is its splitting, the first
summand $T\mapsto\operatorname{Pic}(T)$ being fppf-locally trivializable exactly
through the descent condition, cf. the argument of
[lem-pc-k-sheaf]) that $\operatorname{Pic}_{X/S}$ is the sheafification of $K$.
Consequently the third map is surjective and the sequence is split.

attrs.title: The split exact sequence for the Picard functor

objects.body:
(Stacks Project, Picard Schemes of Curves, Proposition 44.6.6, Tag
[0B9Z](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B9Z).)
Let $k$ be a separably closed field.
Let $X$ be a
smooth projective curve over
$k$. Then the
Picard functor $\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k}$ is
representable, and the representing scheme
$\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}_{X/k}$ is a group scheme over $k$.

## Proof

Since $k$ is separably closed and $X$ is smooth over $k$ (hence nonempty:
$X$ is a variety), there exists a
$k$-rational point $\sigma$ of $X$ by
[lem-pc-rational-points-dense]. By [cor-pc-sigma-pic-iso] it
suffices to show that the functor
$\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}$ classifying invertible modules trivial along
$\sigma$ is representable (then $\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k}$ is representable too, and
the representing scheme carries the group structure because it represents
the group-valued functor; moreover the fact that it is a group scheme
follows from the conclusion of [thm-pc-criterion]).

We check the conditions (1), (2)(a), (2)(b), (2)(c) of
[thm-pc-criterion] (with $G=\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}$ and $F$ the
subfunctor of [lem-pc-f-open-subfunctor]):

1. **(1)** The functor $\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}$ satisfies the sheaf condition
for the fppf topology: by [lem-pc-rational-hyp] the hypotheses of
[thm-pc-pic-split] hold, and the fppf sheaf condition for
$K=\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}$ was shown in
[lem-pc-k-sheaf]. Since every Zariski covering is an fppf covering ([lem-pc-zariski-coverings-are-fppf])
(affine-locally the maps $\operatorname{Spec}(A_f)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ are flat and of finite
presentation, $A\to A_f$ being the localization), it satisfies the sheaf
property for the Zariski topology. [Condition (1); note that
[cor-pc-sigma-pic-iso] gives the same conclusion from the fact that
$\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k}$ is by definition an fppf sheaf.]
1. **(2)(a)** The subfunctor $F$ of [lem-pc-f-open-subfunctor] is
representable: [thm-pc-f-representable] represents it by the open
subscheme $W\subseteq\underline{\operatorname{Hilb}}^g_{X/k}$ (the genus $g$ is finite:
$X$ is a smooth projective curve over $k$, geometrically irreducible by
[prop-pc-xk-integral], so [def-pc-genus] applies).
1. **(2)(b)** $F\subseteq\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}$ is representable by open
immersions: [lem-pc-f-open-subfunctor].
1. **(2)(c)** Let $K/k$ be a field extension and let
$g_0\in\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}(K)$, i.e. an invertible module $\mathcal{L}$ on $X_K$
with $\sigma_K^*\mathcal{L}\cong\mathcal{O}_K$. By [lem-pc-twist] there is an
invertible sheaf $\mathcal{L}_0$ on $X$ with
$\dim_KH^0(X_K,\mathcal{L}\otimes\mathcal{L}_0|_{X_K})=1$ and
$H^1(X_K,\mathcal{L}\otimes\mathcal{L}_0|_{X_K})=0$. Since
$\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}(k)=\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ ([def-pc-pic-sigma-functor], [lem-pc-sigma-k-points]), the
module $\mathcal{L}_0$ corresponds to an element $g_0'\in G(k)$; and in
$G(K)$ the product $g_0'\cdot g_0$ is the class of
$\mathcal{L}_0|_{X_K}\otimes\mathcal{L}$. For it we have
$H^p(X_K,\cdot)=0$ for all $p\geq1$
(Serre: from [lem-pc-twist] we have $H^1=0$ and
[lem-pc-vanishing-above-dim] gives $H^p=0$ for $p\geq2$), and
$H^0$ is $1$-dimensional over $K$, so
$$
Rf_{K,*}\bigl(\mathcal{L}_0|_{X_K}\otimes\mathcal{L}\bigr)\cong\bigl(H^0(X_K,\mathcal{L}_0|_{X_K}\otimes\mathcal{L})\bigr)[0]
\cong K[0],
$$
which is an invertible $\mathcal{O}_K$-module placed in degree $0$; hence
$g_0'g_0\in F(K)$ as required.

All four conditions hold, so by [thm-pc-criterion] the functor
$\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}$ is representable by a group scheme over $k$, and
hence so is $\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k}$ by [cor-pc-sigma-pic-iso].

attrs.title: The Picard scheme of a curve is representable

objects.body:
Let $f:X\to T$ be a proper morphism of finite presentation and let
$\mathcal F$ be an $\mathcal O_X$-module of finite presentation, flat
over $T$. For $t\in T$ write $X_t=X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$
and let $\mathcal F_t$ be the pullback of $\mathcal F$ to $X_t$. Fix an
integer $q$.

1. For every $t\in T$ the space $H^q(X_t,\mathcal F_t)$ is finite
   dimensional over $\kappa(t)$, and there is a canonical base-change map
   $$
   \varphi^q(t):\;R^qf_*\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_T}\kappa(t)
   \longrightarrow H^q(X_t,\mathcal F_t).
   $$
2. The function
   $\beta^q(t)=\dim_{\kappa(t)}H^q(X_t,\mathcal F_t)$ is upper
   semicontinuous on $T$.
3. If $T$ is reduced and $\beta^q$ is locally constant on $T$, then
   $R^qf_*\mathcal F$ is a finite locally free $\mathcal O_T$-module (in
   particular it is flat over $T$), and $\varphi^q(t)$ is an isomorphism
   for every $t\in T$.

The reducedness hypothesis in (3) cannot be omitted: over a
non-reduced base, $T$ may even be a single point (so that $\beta^q$ is
trivially constant) while $R^qf_*\mathcal F$ is not flat.

## Proof

*Local model.* Put $E=Rf_*\mathcal F$, the
derived direct image. By
[lem-pc-rf-perfect-base-change], $E$ is perfect and for every
$g:T'\to T$ the canonical map $Lg^*E\to Rf_{T',*}\mathcal F_{T'}$ is an
isomorphism. Fix $t\in T$. By [def-pc-perfect-complex] there is an
affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}(A)\ni t$ on which $E|_U$ is
isomorphic to the complex associated with a bounded complex of finite
projective $A$-modules. Each of these finitely many modules is free on
some principal open neighbourhood of $t$; the intersection of these
neighbourhoods is again principal, and localisation of the complex
represents the restriction. Shrinking $U$, we may therefore assume

$$
E|_U\cong\widetilde K,\qquad
K:\;0\to K^a\xrightarrow{d^a}K^{a+1}\to\cdots\to K^b\to0,\qquad
K^i\cong A^{n_i}.
$$

Since higher direct images commute with restriction to open subsets
of the base, $R^qf_*\mathcal F|_U=\widetilde{H^q(K)}$. For
$s\in U$ let $g_s:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to T$ be the canonical
morphism. The terms of $K$ are free, hence flat, so by
[lem-pc-flat-complex-derived-pullback] the derived pullback
$Lg_s^*E$ is represented by $K\otimes_A\kappa(s)$. By the base-change
isomorphism above,
$K\otimes_A\kappa(s)\cong Rf_{s,*}\mathcal F_s$, where
$f_s:X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$. The target is a one-point
space, on which the $q$-th higher direct image is the $q$-th cohomology
group; hence

$$
H^q(X_s,\mathcal F_s)\cong H^q(K\otimes_A\kappa(s)),
$$

a finite dimensional $\kappa(s)$-vector space.

*(1).* The map $\varphi^q(t)$ is the canonical base-change map
$g_t^*R^qf_*\mathcal F\to R^qf_{t,*}\mathcal F_t$ attached to the
cartesian square with bottom arrow $g_t$. In the local model it is
the evident map

$$
H^q(K)\otimes_A\kappa(s)\longrightarrow H^q(K\otimes_A\kappa(s)),\qquad
[z]\otimes1\longmapsto[z\otimes1],
$$

which is well defined because a cycle (resp. boundary) of $K$ maps to
a cycle (resp. boundary) of $K\otimes_A\kappa(s)$.

*(2).* Write $d^i(s)=d^i\otimes_A\kappa(s)$ for the matrix of $d^i$
with entries reduced to $\kappa(s)$, and let
$\rho_i(s)=\operatorname{rank}d^i(s)$. Linear algebra over $\kappa(s)$
gives

$$
\beta^q(s)=n_q-\rho_q(s)-\rho_{q-1}(s)\qquad(s\in U).
$$

For every integer $r$, the set $\{s:\rho_i(s)\ge r\}$ is the set of
points at which some $r\times r$ minor of $d^i$ does not vanish, i.e.
the complement of the closed set $V(I_r(d^i))$ cut out by the ideal of
$r\times r$ minors. Hence each $\rho_i$ is lower semicontinuous on
$U$, so $\beta^q$ is upper semicontinuous on $U$. Such opens $U$ cover
$T$, and upper semicontinuity is local, which proves (2).

*(3).* Now let $T$ be reduced, hence $A$ reduced, and let $\beta^q$ be
locally constant. Shrinking $U$ around $t$ we may assume $\beta^q$ is
constant on $U$, so $\rho_q+\rho_{q-1}=c$ is constant. Then
$\rho_q=c-\rho_{q-1}$ is also upper semicontinuous, hence locally
constant, and likewise $\rho_{q-1}$. Shrinking $U$ once more, we may
assume $\rho_q\equiv r$ and $\rho_{q-1}\equiv r'$ on $U$.

*Claim.* Let $\phi:A^m\to A^n$ be a matrix over a reduced ring $A$
whose rank at every point of $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ equals $r$. Then
every point has a principal open neighbourhood over which, in suitable
bases, $\phi=\begin{pmatrix}I_r&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$. Indeed, every
$(r+1)\times(r+1)$ minor of $\phi$ vanishes in every residue field,
hence lies in every prime ideal, hence is nilpotent, hence is $0$ since
$A$ is reduced. At a given point some $r\times r$ minor $\delta$ is
nonzero, so $\delta$ is a unit on $D(\delta)$. After permuting bases,
$\phi=\begin{pmatrix}D&B\\C&F\end{pmatrix}$ with $D$ invertible over
$A_\delta$; invertible row and column operations bring $\phi$ to
$\begin{pmatrix}I_r&0\\0&F'\end{pmatrix}$ with $F'=F-CD^{-1}B$. The
$(r+1)\times(r+1)$ minors of the new matrix are
$A_\delta$-linear combinations of those of $\phi$ (Cauchy–Binet), so
they vanish; the minor formed by $I_r$ and one entry of $F'$ equals
that entry, so $F'=0$.

Apply the claim to $d^q$ and to $d^{q-1}$ and shrink $U$ to a principal
open neighbourhood of $t$ on which both normal forms hold (the bases
used for the two maps need not agree). Then
$Z=\ker d^q$ is a direct summand of $K^q$, free of rank $n_q-r$, with a
complement $Z'$ mapped by $d^q$ isomorphically onto a direct summand of
$K^{q+1}$; and $B=\operatorname{im}d^{q-1}$ is a direct summand of
$K^q$, free of rank $r'$, with $K^{q-1}\to B$ a split surjection.
Since $B\subseteq Z$, a retraction $K^q\to B$ restricts to a retraction
$Z\to B$, so $B$ is a direct summand of $Z$ and

$$
H^q(K)=Z/B
$$

is a finite projective $A$-module of rank $n_q-r-r'=\beta^q(t)$. Being
finite projective, it is locally free on principal opens, so
$R^qf_*\mathcal F$ is finite locally free near $t$, in particular flat.

For $s\in U$ split injections and split surjections remain so after
$\otimes_A\kappa(s)$. Thus $d^q(s)$ is injective on
$Z'\otimes\kappa(s)$ and zero on $Z\otimes\kappa(s)$, giving
$\ker d^q(s)=Z\otimes_A\kappa(s)$; and
$\operatorname{im}d^{q-1}(s)=B\otimes_A\kappa(s)$ inside
$K^q\otimes_A\kappa(s)$. The split exact sequence
$0\to B\to Z\to Z/B\to0$ stays exact after tensoring, so

$$
H^q(K\otimes_A\kappa(s))
=\frac{Z\otimes_A\kappa(s)}{B\otimes_A\kappa(s)}
=H^q(K)\otimes_A\kappa(s),
$$

and the identification is exactly the map of (1). Hence $\varphi^q(s)$
is an isomorphism for all $s\in U$. Since $t$ was arbitrary, (3)
follows.

*Why reducedness is needed.* Let $A=k[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)$ and let
$E_0$ be an elliptic curve over the field $k$. Let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible
sheaf on $E_0\times_k\operatorname{Spec}A$ that restricts to
$\mathcal O_{E_0}$ but is a nontrivial first-order deformation of it
(these are classified by the nonzero elements of
$H^1(E_0,\mathcal O_{E_0})\cong k$). A global section of $\mathcal L$
reduces to a constant on $E_0$. A nonzero constant cannot lift, since
a lift would trivialise $\mathcal L$. Hence
$H^0(\mathcal L)=\varepsilon H^0(E_0,\mathcal O_{E_0})\cong k$, a
module killed by $\varepsilon$ and so not flat over $A$. The base is a
single point, so $\beta^0$ is constant.

Let $X\to Y$ be a surjective
finite locally free morphism and let $V$
be a scheme over $X$ such that $V\to X$ is
projective. Then every
descent datum on $V$ over $X/Y$ is effective.
This is Stacks Project, Groupoid Schemes, Lemma 39.25.3, Tag
[0CCJ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CCJ).

## Proof

This is Stacks Project, Groupoid Schemes, Lemma 39.25.3, Tag
[0CCJ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CCJ). In the notation of
[def-pd-descent-datum] and [def-pc-morphism-conventions] we recall
why projectivity ([def-pc-projective-morphism]) is exactly the hypothesis
that makes the descent effective, since that is the point at which the
projectivity of $J_K$ of [cor-pd-finite-level] is used. In loc. cit. the effectiveness is deduced from Lemma 39.25.2, Tag
[0CCI](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CCI), which states that a
descent datum on $V/X/Y$ is effective as soon as every finite set of points of
$V$ lying over one point of $Y$ is contained in an affine open of $V$; that
criterion in turn is Lemma 39.25.1, Tag
[0H8K](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H8K), proved by producing a
$\varphi$-invariant affine open neighbourhood of each point (Constructions,
Lemma 27.2.1, Tag [01LH](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01LH), for
the reduction to $Y$ affine, and Lemma 39.24.1, Tag
[03JE](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03JE), for the invariant
neighbourhood) and glueing along the resulting covering. A projective $V\to X$ has an $X$-very ample invertible sheaf, and for an ample invertible sheaf
finitely many points lie in an affine open (Properties, Lemma 28.30.5, Tag
[01ZY](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01ZY)), which is the
condition of Lemma 39.25.2; this is the verification carried out in the proof
of Stacks Project, Lemma 39.25.3, Tag
[0CCJ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CCJ), cases (1), (2) and
(4). The hypothesis that $X\to Y$ be
[def-pc-finite-locally-free] is what makes the fibres of the two
projections finite and hence the orbits of Lemma 39.25.1 finite.

Let $k\subseteq K$ be a finite field extension and let $Z$ be a scheme over $k$
such that $Z_K=Z\times_kK$, the base change of
$Z$, is of finite type and smooth over
$K$, proper over $K$, and connected.
Then $Z$ is of finite type and smooth over $k$, proper over $k$, and connected.
The corresponding statements, together with the case of a faithfully flat
morphism that is merely locally of finite presentation, are Stacks Project,
Descent, Section 35.23, Tag
[02YJ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02YJ); for smoothness the
precise statement is Lemma 35.23.29, Tag
[02VL](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02VL), for local finite
presentation Lemma 35.14.3, Tag
[02KL](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02KL), and for smoothness
along a faithfully flat morphism which is locally of finite presentation
Lemma 35.14.5, Tag
[05B5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05B5).

## Proof

A finite field extension $k\subseteq K$ makes $\Spec(K)\to\Spec(k)$ a
surjective [def-pc-finite-locally-free]
morphism, in particular faithfully flat, quasi-compact, and locally of finite
presentation, so it is an fpqc covering of $\Spec(k)$ in the sense of Stacks
Project, Descent, Section 35.23, Tag
[02YJ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02YJ); the scheme $Z_K$ is the
base change of [def-pc-base-change], and smoothness and properness are the
notions of [def-pc-morphism-conventions].

*Being of finite type and smooth.* The morphism $Z_K\to\Spec(K)$ is
locally of finite presentation, and $Z_K\to Z$ is surjective flat and of finite
presentation, so $Z\to\Spec(k)$ is locally of finite presentation by Lemma
35.14.3, Tag [02KL](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02KL); since
$Z_K$ is quasi-compact over $K$ and $Z_K\to Z$ is surjective, $Z$ is
quasi-compact, hence of finite type. Smoothness of $Z\to\Spec(k)$ then follows
from smoothness of $Z_K\to\Spec(K)$ by Lemma 35.14.5, Tag
[05B5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05B5), applied to the
surjective flat locally finitely presented morphism $Z_K\to Z$; this is the
same lemma that Stacks Project, Lemma 39.9.4, Tag
[0BFC](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BFC), invokes for abelian
varieties, there in the form Lemma 35.23.29, Tag
[02VL](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02VL).

*Properness.* This is one of the properties of morphisms proved to be
local in the fpqc topology on the target in Stacks Project, Descent, Section
35.23, Tag [02YJ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02YJ):
separatedness and universal closedness are separated in the list of that
section, and properness is their conjunction together with being of finite
type, which was settled above.

*Connectedness.* The morphism $Z_K\to Z$ is the base change of the
surjective morphism $\Spec(K)\to\Spec(k)$, hence surjective. The image of a
connected space under a continuous map is connected, so $Z$ is connected
because $Z_K$ is.

attrs.title: Properties of morphisms are local in the fpqc topology on the target

objects.body:
Let $k$ be a field, let $C$ be a
smooth projective curve over $k$
which is geometrically integral,
of genus $g$ ([def-pc-genus]), and let $k_s$ be a
separable closure of $k$. Then the
degree-zero part
$\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C_{k_s}/k_s}$ is representable, and the representing
object $J_s$ is an abelian variety over
$k_s$ of dimension $g$; moreover $J_s(k_s)=\operatorname{Pic}^0(C_{k_s})$
under the canonical identification of [def-sc-pic0].

## Proof

By [lem-pd-geometric-curve] the curve $C_{k_s}$ is a smooth projective
curve over the separably closed field $k_s$ of [def-pd-separable-closure]
which is geometrically integral of genus $g$
([def-pc-genus]). [thm-sc-jacobian-representability] therefore
produces an abelian variety $J_s$ over $k_s$ of dimension $g$, whose defining
property is the isomorphism $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C_{k_s}/k_s}\cong h_{J_s}$
of [def-sc-jacobian], and it identifies $J_s(k_s)$ with the group
$\operatorname{Pic}^0(C_{k_s})$ of [def-sc-pic0]. That theorem
formulates its functor as the degree-zero part of the Picard functor, which is
