the subfunctor introduced in [def-pd-degree-morphism]; hence $J_s$
represents $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C_{k_s}/k_s}$ in the sense used here.
[thm-sc-theorem-of-the-base] supplies the same conclusion independently,
together with smoothness, properness and the dimension, which is what makes
$J_s$ an abelian variety in the sense of [def-sc-abelian-variety].

attrs.title: The degree-zero Picard functor over a separable closure

objects.body:
Let $k$ be any field and let $C$ be a
smooth projective curve over $k$
which is
geometrically connected, of genus
$g$ ([def-pc-genus]). Then there is an
abelian variety $J$ over $k$ of dimension
$g$, together with a natural isomorphism of group-valued functors

$$
h_J\;\cong\;\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k},
$$

where $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}=\ker(\deg)$ is the
degree-zero part of the
Picard functor; that is, $J$ represents the
degree-zero relative Picard fppf sheaf. Moreover for every field extension
$K/k$ the base change is the Jacobian of the
base change,

$$
J_K\;\cong\;\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C_K/K},
$$

naturally in $K$.

Let moreover $\bar k$ be an algebraic closure of $k$ and $k_s\subseteq\bar k$ the separable
closure of $k$ in it, put
$C_{\bar k}=C\times_k\bar k$, and let
$\Gamma=\operatorname{Aut}(\bar k/k)$, which restriction identifies with
$\operatorname{Gal}(k_s/k)$. For $\sigma\in\Gamma$ write
$\sigma^\sharp=\Spec(\sigma)$, a $k$-automorphism of $\Spec(\bar k)$. The
induced identification

$$
J(\bar k)\;=\;\operatorname{Pic}^0(C_{\bar k})
$$

is *$\Gamma$-equivariant* for the natural actions: on the left through the
$k$-structure of $J$, $\sigma\cdot x=x\circ\sigma^\sharp$ for
$x\in J(\bar k)=\operatorname{Hom}_k(\Spec\bar k,J)$; on the right through
the $k$-structure of $C$, $\sigma\cdot[\mathcal L]=
[(\mathrm{id}_C\times\sigma^\sharp)^*\mathcal L]$. In particular, for every
prime $\ell$ and every $n\ge1$, restricting to $\ell^n$-torsion gives a
$\Gamma$-equivariant isomorphism

$$
J[\ell^n](\bar k)\;\cong\;\operatorname{Pic}^0(C_{\bar k})[\ell^n].
$$

No $k$-rational point of $C$ is assumed.

## Proof

Fix a separable closure $k_s$ of $k$ as in [def-pd-separable-closure].
The curve is a [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve] which is
[def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], of genus $g$ in the sense of
[def-pc-genus], and its degree-zero Picard functor is the
[def-pd-degree-morphism] inside the [def-pc-picard-functor].

*Step 1 (the geometric object).* By [thm-pd-geometric-pic0] the
degree-zero part $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C_{k_s}/k_s}$ is represented by an
abelian variety $J_s$ over $k_s$ of dimension $g$. In particular the functor
$\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$ of [def-pd-degree-morphism] becomes
representable after base change to $k_s$, by
[cor-pd-pic0-base-change].

*Step 2 (the canonical descent datum).* By
[lem-pd-canonical-descent-datum] and [lem-pd-descent-cocycle] the
scheme $J_s$ carries a canonical
descent datum ([def-pd-descent-datum])
over $\Spec(k_s)/\Spec(k)$; it is canonical because it is produced by Yoneda
from the single functor $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$, so no Galois action is
chosen.

*Step 3 (reduction to a finite level).* By [cor-pd-finite-level]
there are a finite separable extension $K/k$, a projective scheme $J_K$ of
finite presentation over $K$, and a descent datum over $\Spec(K)/\Spec(k)$
which base changes to the datum of Step 2, with $J_K\times_KK_s\cong J_s$.

*Step 4 (effectivity).* The extension $k\subseteq K$ is finite, so
$\Spec(K)\to\Spec(k)$ is surjective finite locally free, and
[thm-pd-effective-descent] applies to the projective $J_K$: the descent
datum is effective, giving a scheme $J$ over $k$ with
$J\times_kK\cong J_K$ and hence $J\times_kk_s\cong J_s$.

*Step 5 (the group structure).* The group law of the abelian variety
$J_s$ is defined over $K$ at the finite level, because it is part of the
functor $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$ restricted to $K$, and it is compatible
with the descent datum by construction. [lem-pd-group-scheme-descent]
therefore descends it, so that $J$ is a $k$-group scheme in the sense of
[def-sc-group-scheme], with $J_K$ the given group scheme.

*Step 6 (the geometric properties).* The scheme $J_K=J\times_kK$ is
smooth over $K$ and proper over $K$, and it is connected, because it is the
base change of the abelian variety $J_s$ of Step 1 along
$\Spec(k_s)/\Spec(K)$ and an abelian variety is a variety, hence connected
([def-sc-abelian-variety]). By
[thm-pd-fpqc-local-properties] the scheme $J$ is therefore of finite type,
smooth and proper over $k$, and connected. By
[lem-pc-dim-base-change] applied to the flat extension $k\subseteq K$,
$\dim J=\dim J_K=\dim J_s=g$, the last equality by Step 1. By Stacks Project,
Remark 39.9.12, Tag
[0H2U](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H2U), a group scheme over a
field which is proper, connected and smooth is an abelian variety; hence $J$
is an abelian variety over $k$ of dimension $g$ in the sense of
[def-sc-abelian-variety].

*Step 7 (the functorial identification).* By Steps 1 and 4 the scheme
$J$ satisfies $J\times_kk_s\cong J_s$, and $J_s$ represents
$\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C_{k_s}/k_s}$, which by
[cor-pd-pic0-base-change] is the base change of
$\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$. The two functors
$h_J=\operatorname{Hom}_k(-,J)$ and $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$ on
$(\mathit{Sch}/k)_{fppf}$ therefore become isomorphic after base change along
the faithfully flat morphism $\Spec(k_s)\to\Spec(k)$; an fppf sheaf is
determined by its base change along a faithfully flat cover, so
$h_J\cong\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$. Concretely, the isomorphism is the one
whose base change to $k_s$ is the representing isomorphism of $J_s$; it is
canonical because the representing isomorphism is. In the vocabulary of
[def-sc-jacobian] this says that $J$ is a Jacobian of $C$ over $k$.

*Step 8 (base change of the functor).* For an arbitrary field extension
$K/k$, apply the already proved statement to the curve $C_K$ over $K$: it is
smooth projective and geometrically connected of genus $g$ as well, so its
degree-zero Picard functor is representable by an abelian variety $J'$ over
$K$. Since $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C_K/K}$ is the base change of
$\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$ by [cor-pd-pic0-base-change], and
$h_{J_K}=h_J\times_kK$, the two representing objects $J_K$ and $J'$ of the
same functor are canonically isomorphic, which is the asserted natural
isomorphism $J_K\cong\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C_K/K}$.

*Step 9 (the geometric points).* Take $T=\Spec(\bar k)$, a $k$-scheme.
The curve $C_{\bar k}$ has a $\bar k$-rational point because $\bar k$ is
algebraically closed, so by [lem-pc-rational-hyp] and [thm-pc-pic-split]
(with $\operatorname{Pic}(\Spec\bar k)=0$ by [lem-pc-pic-of-field]) the canonical map from the
Picard presheaf,
$\operatorname{Pic}(C_{\bar k})\to\operatorname{Pic}_{C_{\bar k}/\bar k}(\bar k)$,
is an isomorphism; by [lem-pd-picard-base-change] the target is
$\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}(T)$, the value of the Picard functor of $C/k$ on
the $k$-scheme $T$. For a point $T$ the fibrewise degree
([def-pd-fibrewise-degree]) of a class is the degree of the invertible
module on $C_{\bar k}$, so the degree-zero parts correspond:
$\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}(T)=\operatorname{Pic}^0(C_{\bar k})$ in the
sense of [def-sc-pic0]. Composing with the value on $T$ of the
isomorphism $h_J\cong\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$ of Step 7 gives the
identification $J(\bar k)=h_J(T)=\operatorname{Pic}^0(C_{\bar k})$.

*Step 10 (equivariance).* Let $\sigma\in\Gamma$. The map
$\sigma^\sharp:T\to T$ is a morphism in $(\mathit{Sch}/k)_{fppf}$, so every
functor on that category assigns to it an endomorphism of its value on $T$;
for $h_J$ this is $x\mapsto x\circ\sigma^\sharp$, the action through the
$k$-structure of $J$, and for the Picard presheaf of $C/k$ it is pullback
along $\mathrm{id}_C\times\sigma^\sharp:C_{\bar k}\to C_{\bar k}$, the
action through the $k$-structure of $C$ (it preserves degrees, since
$\mathrm{id}_C\times\sigma^\sharp$ is an isomorphism of schemes over the
automorphism $\sigma^\sharp$ of the base). Both the canonical map from the
Picard presheaf to its sheafification $\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}$ and the
isomorphism $h_J\cong\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$ of Step 7 are natural
transformations of functors on $(\mathit{Sch}/k)_{fppf}$, so they commute
with the endomorphisms induced by $\sigma^\sharp$. Hence every map in the
chain of Step 9 commutes with the action of $\sigma$, i.e. the
identification $J(\bar k)=\operatorname{Pic}^0(C_{\bar k})$ is
$\Gamma$-equivariant. The rules $\sigma\mapsto F(\sigma^\sharp)$ are left
actions because both $F$ and $\Spec$ are contravariant. Finally, restriction
to $\operatorname{Gal}(k_s/k)$ is an isomorphism
$\Gamma\to\operatorname{Gal}(k_s/k)$ because $\bar k/k_s$ is purely
inseparable, so every $k$-automorphism of $k_s$ extends uniquely to
$\bar k$.

*Step 11 (torsion).* The identification of Step 9 is an isomorphism of
groups, because the isomorphism of Step 7 is one of group-valued functors
and the map from the Picard presheaf is additive. The $\bar k$-points of
the kernel $J[\ell^n]$ of multiplication by $\ell^n$ on $J$ are the
$\ell^n$-torsion of the group $J(\bar k)$, since taking $T$-points commutes
with kernels. A $\Gamma$-equivariant group isomorphism maps the
$\ell^n$-torsion subgroup isomorphically and equivariantly onto the
$\ell^n$-torsion subgroup, which gives
$J[\ell^n](\bar k)\cong\operatorname{Pic}^0(C_{\bar k})[\ell^n]$
equivariantly.

Let $I$ be a directed set, let $(S_i,f_{ii'})$ be an inverse system of schemes
over $I$ with affine transition morphisms and $S_i$ quasi-compact and
quasi-separated, and put $S=\varprojlim_iS_i$. Then:

1. for every morphism of finite presentation $V\to S$ there are $i\in I$ and
a morphism of finite presentation $V_i\to S_i$ with
$V\cong V_i\times_{S_i}S$;
1. given $i$, schemes $V_i,W_i$ of finite presentation over $S_i$ and a
morphism $\psi:V_i\times_{S_i}S\to W_i\times_{S_i}S$, there are $i'\geq i$
and a morphism $\psi_{i'}:V_i\times_{S_i}S_{i'}\to W_i\times_{S_i}S_{i'}$
whose base change to $S$ is $\psi$;
1. given $i$, schemes $V_i,W_i$ of finite presentation over $S_i$ and two
morphisms $\psi_i,\chi_i:V_i\to W_i$ whose base changes to $S$ agree,
there is $i'\geq i$ with
$\psi_i\times_{S_i}S_{i'}=\chi_i\times_{S_i}S_{i'}$.

This is Stacks Project, Limits of Schemes, Lemma 32.10.1, Tag
[01ZM](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01ZM).

## Proof

This is Stacks Project, Limits of Schemes, Lemma 32.10.1, Tag
[01ZM](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01ZM); the proof is the
standard reduction to the affine case, where it is Algebra, Lemma 10.127.8,
Tag [05N9](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05N9): a finitely
presented algebra is the colimit of its finitely generated subalgebras, and
two maps out of a finitely presented algebra agree after passing to a
sufficiently large stage. The passage from the affine case to the general
case is carried out in loc. cit. by choosing finite affine open coverings and
glueing; the three assertions are proved there in the order (3), (2), (1), and
we use them in that order. The only two notions of
[def-pc-morphism-conventions], [def-pc-base-change] that the statement needs
are ``of finite presentation'' and the fibre product $V_i\times_{S_i}S$, which
are the ones appearing in its three clauses. We record the statement here
because the chapter needs exactly those clauses, and because the generality of
the cover $\Spec(k_s)\to\Spec(k)$ is what forces this detour through a filtered
limit.

attrs.title: Descent of finitely presented data at a filtered limit

objects.body:
(Hartshorne, *Algebraic Geometry*, II, Theorem 5.17.)
Let $k$ be a field, let $i:X\hookrightarrow P=\mathbf P^n_k$ be a closed
immersion, put $\mathcal O_X(m):=i^*\mathcal O_P(m)$
([def-pc-projective-space-twist]) and let $\mathcal F$ be a
coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module ([pqf-def-coherent]). Then there is
$m_0\ge0$ such that for every $m\ge m_0$ the module
$\mathcal F(m):=\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal O_X(m)$ is
*generated by its global sections*: for every $x\in X$ the stalk
$\mathcal F(m)_x$ is generated as an $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-module by the
germs of elements of $H^0(X,\mathcal F(m))$ (equivalently, the evaluation
map $\bigoplus_{s\in H^0(X,\mathcal F(m))}\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal F(m)$ is
surjective).

## Proof

*Step 1: reduction to $P$.* By
[lem-pc-closed-immersion-coherent-cohomology] the module
$\mathcal G:=i_*\mathcal F$ is coherent on $P$, and for every $m$ the
natural map $\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal O_P(m)\to i_*(\mathcal F(m))$ is an
isomorphism. Moreover $H^0(P,i_*(\mathcal F(m)))=H^0(X,\mathcal F(m))$ by
definition of $i_*$, and for $x\in X$ the stalk of $i_*(\mathcal F(m))$ at
$i(x)$ is $\mathcal F(m)_x$ (the preimages of the open neighbourhoods of
$i(x)$ are cofinal among the open neighbourhoods of $x$, $i$ being a
homeomorphism onto a closed subset), with $\mathcal O_{P,i(x)}$ acting
through the surjection $\mathcal O_{P,i(x)}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$. Hence if
the germs of global sections generate $\mathcal G(m)_{i(x)}$ over
$\mathcal O_{P,i(x)}$, the same germs generate $\mathcal F(m)_x$ over
$\mathcal O_{X,x}$. It therefore suffices to show that $\mathcal G(m)$ is
generated by its global sections on $P$ for $m\gg0$.

*Step 2: twisting modules of non-negative degree.* Let $d\ge0$ and
$0\le j\le n$. On the standard chart $U_l=D_+(x_l)$ put
$\sigma_{j,l}:=(x_j/x_l)^d e_l^{(d)}\in\Gamma(U_l,\mathcal O_P(d))$. By the
transition rule of [def-pc-projective-space-twist], on $U_l\cap U_{l'}$
we have
$(x_j/x_l)^de_l^{(d)}=(x_j/x_l)^d(x_l/x_{l'})^de_{l'}^{(d)}=(x_j/x_{l'})^de_{l'}^{(d)}$,
so the $\sigma_{j,l}$ glue to a global section $x_j^d$ of
$\mathcal O_P(d)$, whose restriction to $U_j$ is the basis $e_j^{(d)}$.
As the $U_j$ cover $P$, every stalk of $\mathcal O_P(d)$ is generated by
the germ of one of the global sections $x_0^d,\ldots,x_n^d$.

*Step 3: a quotient of such modules.* By
[lem-pc-projective-space-twist-quotient] (with $A=k$) there are
$m_1,\ldots,m_r\ge0$ and a surjection
$\varphi:\bigoplus_{a=1}^r\mathcal O_P(-m_a)\to\mathcal G$. Put
$m_0:=\max(0,m_1,\ldots,m_r)$ and let $m\ge m_0$. Tensoring with the
invertible module $\mathcal O_P(m)$ ([def-sc-invertible-module]) preserves
surjectivity, and [lem-pc-twist-tensor] identifies
$\mathcal O_P(-m_a)\otimes\mathcal O_P(m)\cong\mathcal O_P(m-m_a)$, so we get
a surjection
$\varphi(m):\bigoplus_a\mathcal O_P(m-m_a)\to\mathcal G(m)$ with all
$d_a:=m-m_a\ge0$. The images $\varphi(m)(x_j^{d_a}\text{ in the $a$-th
summand})$ are global sections of $\mathcal G(m)$. For $p\in P$ the stalk
map $\varphi(m)_p$ is surjective, and by Step 2 its source is generated
by the germs of the $x_j^{d_a}$ (in the $a$-th summand, for $j$ with
$p\in U_j$); hence $\mathcal G(m)_p$ is generated by the germs of their
images. (If $r=0$ then $\mathcal G=0$ and there is nothing to prove.)
By Step 1 this proves the theorem.

(The sketch follows the same route: the finite presentation by twisting
modules, which also drives the proof of Serre vanishing, gives the
conclusion directly.)

attrs.title: Serre's theorem A: global generation after a twist

objects.body:
Let $X/k$ be smooth and geometrically connected as in
the Poincare duality conventions, and
let $K$ be a derived-complete
site-perfect $\mathcal O_E$-complex whose reductions
$K_n=K\otimes^L A_{E,n}$ form a normalized system with common
constructible and finite-Tor bounds. Assume the admissible structure
morphism and coefficient conventions used for the Poincare pairing. The finite-level pairings $\beta _{K_n}$ of Definition 9.17 form a morphism of normalized systems in the sense of Definition 2.148 (by Theorem 9.33), and they induce the $\mathcal O_E$-valued derived Poincare pairing

$$
R\Gamma _c(X,K)\otimes ^L_{\mathcal O_E}R\Gamma \bigl(X,K^\vee (d)\bigr)[2d] \longrightarrow \mathcal O_E,
$$

perfect in the sense of the uniform-tower reconstruction of Lemma 2.156: the inverse of its adjoint is the canonical isomorphism

$$
R\Gamma _c(X,K)^\vee \xrightarrow {\  \sim \  } R\Gamma \bigl(X,K^\vee (d)\bigr)[2d]
$$

over $\mathcal O_E$. Localization at $\varpi _E$ and finite coefficient-field extension carry this pairing, its adjoint, every degree-indexing map, the relative form, and all Frobenius squares to their counterparts over the extended coefficient field.

## Proof

By [thm-pod-finite-reduction], the reduction of the inverse adjoint $\beta _{K_{n+1}}^\sharp$ along $A_{E,n+1}\to A_{E,n}$ is $\beta _{K_n}^\sharp$, so the finite-level inverse adjoints form a morphism of normalized systems with the common bounds and amplitudes inherited from $K$; the realization under the uniform-tower reconstruction of [lem-weil-pbc-reconstruction-uniform-tower] is the displayed $\mathcal O_E$-level inverse adjoint, whose levelwise perfectness is [thm-pod-derived-poincare-duality] (the perfectness and the pairing over $\mathcal O_E$ are then the corresponding statements over the realized object). Scalar extension to $E$ and to a finite coefficient field is the exactness of the extension functors, and transport along the finite-reduction and scalar-extension rectangles of [thm-pod-finite-reduction] gives the compatibility of the pairing, the adjoint, the degree-indexing maps, and the Frobenius squares.

In the Poincare duality conventions of this chapter (the fixed setting), fix the field stage $\Lambda \in \{ E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell }\}$ of the datum (with the finite coefficient groups $H^i_c(X,K)$, $H^i(X,K)$); let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda )$ be perfect over $\Lambda _X$ in the sense of Definition 9.6, and let $\langle -,-\rangle _i$ denote the degreewise pairings of Proposition 9.21,

$$
\langle -,-\rangle _i:\   H_c^i(X,K)\times H^{2d-i}\bigl(X,K^\vee (d)\bigr)\longrightarrow \Lambda ,
$$

obtained by decomposing the degree-zero part of the derived Poincare pairing $\beta _K$ of Definition 9.17. Then all cohomology spaces in the displays of Proposition 9.21 are finite-dimensional, and each map

$$
H^{2d-i}\bigl(X,K^\vee (d)\bigr) \xrightarrow {\  \sim \  }H_c^i(X,K)^\vee
$$

– the adjoint of $\langle -,-\rangle _i$, the right side being the ordinary dual of a finite-dimensional $\Lambda$-vector space, by Definition 1.50 – is an isomorphism; equivalently each bilinear pairing $\langle -,-\rangle _i$ is perfect, and the line-valued pairing $H_c^i(X,K)\times H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee )\to \Lambda (-d)$ is perfect degreewise.

## Proof

The derived duality of [thm-pod-derived-poincare-duality] is an isomorphism of perfect point complexes over the field $\Lambda$ (the field-stage case of [thm-pod-point-perfectness]). Apply $H^{-i}$ to both sides. On the right, $H^{-i}(C^\vee )\cong H^i(C)^\vee$ for $C=R\Gamma _c(X,K)$, a bounded complex of finite-dimensional vector spaces (the field-stage definition of perfectness, [def-pod-perfect-point-complex]), hence with bounded finite-dimensional cohomology by [lem-pod-perfect-point-complex-field], by [lem-pod-cohomology-of-dual-over-field]. On the left, $H^{-i}\bigl(R\Gamma (X,K^\vee (d))[2d]\bigr) =H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee (d))$ by the shift convention. Hence the isomorphism and hence the perfectness of the degreewise pairings, the derived pairing being perfect by [thm-pod-derived-poincare-duality]; the line-valued form follows from the twist elimination of [prop-pod-degree-of-the-pairing].

In the Poincare duality conventions of this chapter (the fixed setting; $X_0$ is not assumed proper), let $\Lambda \in \{ A,\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell }\}$, let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda )$ be a bounded constructible finite-Tor complex that is perfect over $\Lambda _X$, let $K^\vee =R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\Lambda _X)$ be its coefficient dual with Tate twist $K^\vee (d)$, and let $\beta _K$ be the derived Poincare pairing (the composite of the mixed-support cup product, the evaluation, and the normalized smooth trace). Then $\beta _K$ is a perfect derived pairing in the sense of Definition 9.18: the inverse of its tensor–internal-Hom adjoint is the canonical isomorphism

$$
R\Gamma _c(X,K)^\vee \xrightarrow {\  \sim \  } R\Gamma \bigl(X,K^\vee (d)\bigr)[2d].
$$

The statement is natural in $K$, compatible with finite reduction, scalar extension, shifts and truncations, and its transpose form

$$
R\Gamma _c(X,K)\otimes _\Lambda ^LR\Gamma \bigl(X,K^\vee (d)\bigr)[2d] \longrightarrow \Lambda
$$

is the pairing of Definition 9.17.

## Proof

Step 1: the two constituent isomorphisms. By [thm-pod-global-verdier-duality] there is the canonical isomorphism

$$
R\Gamma _c(X,K)^\vee \xrightarrow {\  \sim \  }R\Gamma (X,\mathbb D_XK),
$$

and by [thm-sf-dual-perfect] (its hypothesis being the perfectness of $K$ over $\Lambda _X$) there is the canonical identification

$$
R\Gamma (X,\mathbb D_XK)\xrightarrow {\  \sim \  } R\Gamma \bigl(X,K^\vee (d)\bigr)[2d].
$$

Step 2: the composite is the inverse of the adjoint of the pairing. By [thm-pod-identification-of-the-comparison], the adjoint of the derived pairing $\beta _K$ of [def-pod-derived-poincare-pairing] is the inverse of the composite of these two isomorphisms; hence the composite is an isomorphism if and only if the pairing is perfect, by the definition of [def-pod-perfect-derived-pairing]. Step 3: perfectness of the objects. By [thm-pod-point-perfectness], $R\Gamma _c(X,K)$ is a perfect point complex in the sense of [def-pod-perfect-point-complex]; its dual $R\Gamma _c(X,K)^\vee$ is perfect by [def-pod-perfect-point-complex] (the dual of a bounded complex of finite projective modules is again a bounded complex of finite projective modules), and the shift of a perfect point complex is perfect, again by [def-pod-perfect-point-complex]. Step 4: the conclusion. The composite is an isomorphism by Step 1, and its two objects are perfect by Step 3; hence the adjoint of $\beta _K$ is an isomorphism and $\beta _K$ is a perfect derived pairing according to [def-pod-perfect-derived-pairing]. Step 5: naturality and compatibility. Both constituent isomorphisms are natural in $K$ and compatible with finite reduction, scalar extension, shifts, and truncations, by the statements of [thm-pod-global-verdier-duality], [thm-sf-dual-perfect], and [thm-pod-point-perfectness], so the composite and the pairing inherit these properties; the transpose form is the pairing of [def-pod-derived-poincare-pairing] itself. Step 6: the inputs, separated. The first isomorphism of Step 1 is the abstract global duality [thm-sf-global-duality] in its concrete form (valid without properness: $Ra_{X!}$ and $Ra_{X*}$ enter as different functors and are never compared), and the second is the smooth-purity orientation [thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity] of the purity chapter; the identification consumed in Step 2 is [thm-sf-identification], and the finiteness consumed in Step 3 is [thm-pod-point-perfectness].

In the Poincare duality conventions of this chapter (the fixed setting), strict Weil complex with $K$ perfect. With $F_{c,K}$ and $F_{K^\vee (d)}$ the operators of Definition 7.7 formed from $\varphi _K$ and the datum $\varphi _{K^\vee (d)}$ of Definition 9.28, the degreewise pairings satisfy

$$
\bigl\langle F_{c,K}x,\; F_{K^\vee (d)}y\bigr\rangle _i =\langle x,y\rangle _i \qquad \bigl(x\in H_c^i(X,K),\  y\in H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee (d))\bigr),
$$

where the action on the second factor includes the scalar $q^{-d}$ on $A_X(d)$ and the pairing is the derived Poincare pairing in the form of Proposition 9.21.

## Proof

Step 1: the derived pairing $\beta _K$ of [def-pod-derived-poincare-pairing] is the composite of the mixed-support cup product, the evaluation, and the smooth trace. The mixed-support cup product is induced by the tensor product of sheaves and its $\Gamma _c$-realization, both equivariantly lifted to Weil complexes by [lem-fix-weil-operations], and the same statement applies to the global-sections functors $R\Gamma _c$ and $R\Gamma$ with the data of [def-trf-frobenius-operators]. The evaluation is a morphism of Weil objects by [prop-pod-dual-tate-data-compatibility]. The trace $\operatorname {Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{a_X,A}$ is equivariant by the trace square of [thm-pur-weil-equivariance-of-purity-and-trace], whose source datum carries the twist normalization of the Tate line, [def-pur-tate-datum], and the target datum on $A$ is the canonical datum of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Step 2: composing, the tuple

$$
\bigl(R\Gamma _c(X,K),\  R\Gamma (X,K^\vee (d))[2d],\  A\bigr)
$$

carries the Weil data $\varphi _{c,K},\  \varphi _{K^\vee (d)}$, and the canonical datum, and the pairing $\beta _K$ is a morphism of Weil objects from the tensor of the first two to the last, by Step 1 and the compatibility of the tensor product with the data in [lem-fix-weil-operations]. Step 3: on cohomology, in the degree-zero part

$$
\beta _K:\  H_c^i(X,K)\otimes H^{2d-i}\bigl(X,K^\vee (d)\bigr)\to A
$$

of the pairing (the form of [prop-pod-degree-of-the-pairing]), the induced operators are the $F$'s of [def-trf-frobenius-operators]: the operator on the first factor is $F_{c,K}$, and the operator on the second factor is $F_{K^\vee (d)}$, the datum $\varphi _{K^\vee (d)}$ containing the scalar $q^{-d}$ on $A_X(d)$ by [def-pod-dual-tate-datum] and [def-pur-tate-datum]. The morphism property of Step 2 evaluated on the tensor of two vectors gives

$$
\bigl\langle F_{c,K}x,\; F_{K^\vee (d)}y\bigr\rangle _i =F\bigl(\langle x,y\rangle _i\bigr)
$$

with $F$ the global geometric Frobenius of [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius]; but the target datum is the canonical one, so $F$ acts on $A$ as the identity, by [def-weil-frobenius-detailed] and [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], giving the displayed identity.

Use the smooth Poincare setting, with
the admissible structure morphism and normalized smooth orientation.
Let $n\geq m\geq1$, put $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and
$A_m=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m$, and let $K_n$ be a
site-perfect constructible
$A_n$-complex. Put $K_m=K_n\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m$.
The coefficient comparisons identify the reduction of the
derived Poincare pairing
for $K_n$ with the pairing for $K_m$. In particular, writing
$K_n^\vee$ for its coefficient dual,
the canonical isomorphisms make the square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
R\Gamma_c(X,K_n)^\vee\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m
&\xrightarrow{\beta_{K_n}^{\sharp,-1}\otimes1}&
R\Gamma(X,K_n^\vee(d))[2d]\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m\\
\downarrow\wr&&\downarrow\wr\\
R\Gamma_c(X,K_m)^\vee
&\xrightarrow{\beta_{K_m}^{\sharp,-1}}&
R\Gamma(X,K_m^\vee(d))[2d]
\end{array}
$$

commute. Here $\beta^{\sharp,-1}$ denotes the inverse of the
tensor–Hom adjoint of the pairing.

## Proof

The compact-support, tensor, site-perfect internal-Hom and evaluation
comparisons are [lem-fix-operation-reduction]. Thus the coefficient dual of
[def-pod-coefficient-dual-on-x], the cup product and evaluation
in [def-pod-derived-poincare-pairing], and their adjunction maps
all reduce compatibly. The remaining geometric ingredient is the
normalized trace of [def-pur-smooth-trace]; its coefficient
compatibility, together with that of the smooth orientation, is
[thm-pur-finite-reduction-of-purity].
The identification in [thm-sf-dual-perfect] uses
that orientation and the same internal-Hom operations.
Composing these commuting squares gives the square for the pairing,
using the canonical coefficient comparison on ordinary global sections;
no isomorphism assertion for that map is needed at this step.
By [thm-pod-point-perfectness] the compact-support complex is
perfect, so its coefficient dual commutes with reduction and the left
vertical map is an isomorphism. At each coefficient stage,
[thm-pod-identification-of-the-comparison] identifies the adjoint
of the pairing with the duality isomorphism. Taking adjoints in the
commuting pairing square therefore proves that the ordinary-global-section
comparison on the right is an isomorphism too. Taking inverses of the
horizontal adjoints gives exactly the displayed square.
No flatness of $A_m$ over $A_n$ is asserted: every reduction is
derived, and the coefficient-dual comparisons use the stated
perfectness hypothesis.

attrs.title: Finite reduction of the Poincare pairing

objects.body:
Use the Poincare duality conventions of [def-pod-conventions] (so $X_0$
is smooth, separated of finite type and geometrically connected of pure
dimension $d$, not necessarily proper). The statement below also
holds verbatim for a smooth, proper, geometrically connected $k$-scheme
$X$ of pure dimension $d$ not assumed to descend to $k_0$ (see
[thm-sf-global-duality]). Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$. For the admissible structure
morphism $a_X:X\to s$ there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
R\Gamma_c(X,K)^\vee\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(X,\mathbb D_XK),
$$

with the cohomology functors
of the fixed coefficient stage. It is natural in $K$ and compatible
with shifts. For a site-perfect
$K$, it is also compatible with finite coefficient reduction and
scalar extension under the smooth orientation and its coefficient
comparisons. At $K=\Lambda_X$ it identifies
$R\Gamma_c(X,\Lambda_X)^\vee$ with $R\Gamma(X,\omega_{X,\Lambda})$.

## Proof

Apply the independently proved exchange [fix-cor-verdier-exchange]
to $f=a_X$ and the coefficient object at $s$:

$$
D_sRa_{X!}K\cong Ra_{X*}D_XK.
$$

By [lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex], $D_s$ is the derived
coefficient dual. Apply the point equivalence of
[def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]; the two resulting global
functors are those of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology].
This proves the asserted isomorphism and its naturality and shift
compatibility. Its construction uses only tensor–Hom adjunction,
the compact-support projection formula, and the adjunction for
$Ra_{X!}$; it does not use global Poincare duality.
For $K$ site-perfect in the sense of
[def-weil-site-perfect-complex], the tensor, internal-Hom,
evaluation, and cohomology comparisons are
[lem-fix-operation-reduction]. The smooth dualizing object and
its counit reduce compatibly by
[thm-pur-finite-reduction-of-purity]. Each constituent of the
adjunction comparison therefore commutes with coefficient change,
so their composite does too. Finally $D_X\Lambda_X=\omega_X$
by tensor–Hom evaluation of the unit object, giving the specialization.
Properness of $X_0$ is used nowhere above: the exchange
[fix-cor-verdier-exchange] needs only that $a_X$ is exceptionally
admissible, $Ra_{X!}$ and $Ra_{X*}$ enter as different functors with no
comparison between them, and the smooth dualizing object and its finite
reduction ([thm-pur-finite-reduction-of-purity]) are stated for smooth
separated morphisms. The same argument applies word for word to a smooth
proper $X$ over $k$ that is not defined over $k_0$, which is the proper
case of [thm-sf-global-duality].

attrs.title: Global Verdier duality at the point

objects.body:
Fix $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$, the smooth
geometrically connected $k$-scheme $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ of dimension $d$
(not necessarily proper), and its
structure morphism $a_X:X\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ as in
the Poincare duality conventions.
Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ be
perfect over $\Lambda_X$, with
coefficient dual $K^\vee$.
The tensor–internal-Hom adjoint of the
derived Poincare pairing is
the canonical isomorphism

$$
b_K^\sharp:R\Gamma(X,K^\vee(d))[2d]
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(R\Gamma_c(X,K),\Lambda).
$$

Its inverse is the global Verdier-duality isomorphism followed by the
smooth-purity identification of the Verdier dual.

## Proof

Work at the chosen coefficient stage. The adjunctions, tensor–Hom
operations and projection transformation below are those at that stage
in [fix-prop-projection-formula] and the adjunction definitions cited below.
They are taken at the chosen coefficient stage.
Put $C=Ra_{X!}K$, $\omega=Ra_X^!\Lambda$, and
$D=Ra_{X*}R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\omega)$. The identification
[thm-sf-dual-perfect] identifies $D$ with the first
object of the displayed map. By
[def-pod-derived-poincare-pairing], [def-pod-coefficient-dual-on-x], [def-pur-smooth-trace],
the pairing, before this identification, is cup product followed by
evaluation into $\omega$ and the counit $Ra_{X!}\omega\to\Lambda$.

Let $T=\Lambda[-r]$ for any integer $r$. This is a perfect point
complex, so its pullback and its tensor product with $K$ are in the
stated finite-Tor domains. The adjunctions and projection
formula give natural bijections

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_s(T,D)
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(La_X^*T,R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\omega))\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(K\otimes_\Lambda^LLa_X^*T,Ra_X^!\Lambda)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_s(Ra_{X!}(K\otimes_\Lambda^LLa_X^*T),\Lambda)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_s(C\otimes_\Lambda^LT,\Lambda)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_s(T,R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(C,\Lambda)).
\end{aligned}
$$

Here the first bijection is $La_X^*\dashv Ra_{X*}$ from
[def-weil-derived-direct-image]; the second and fifth are
tensor–internal-Hom adjunction from
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]; the third is
$Ra_{X!}\dashv Ra_X^!$ from
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]; and the fourth is the
projection formula of [def-exchange-projection], [fix-prop-projection-formula].

These bijections are induced by $b_K^\sharp$, not merely abstract
bijections of groups. Indeed, a map $t:T\to D$ is first pulled back
and composed with the counit $La_X^*Ra_{X*}\to\mathrm{id}$, then
evaluated against $K$, then pushed forward and composed with
$Ra_{X!}Ra_X^!\Lambda\to\Lambda$. By
[def-pod-mixed-support-cup-product], this is precisely the map
$C\otimes T\xrightarrow{1\otimes t}C\otimes D\to\Lambda$
obtained from the specified pairing. Its tensor–Hom transpose is
$b_K^\sharp\circ t$. Thus $b_K^\sharp$ induces an isomorphism on
every $H^r=\operatorname{Hom}_s(\Lambda[-r],-)$, under the point-category
equivalences at all four coefficient stages in
[def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]; its cone has zero
cohomology and is zero by [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves].
This proves that the actual adjoint is an isomorphism. The same
adjunction and evaluation characterize the canonical global-duality
comparison of [thm-pod-global-verdier-duality]; consequently the
comparison written there in the reverse direction is its inverse. At every
step the two inputs used are separated: the adjunction, projection and
tensor–internal-Hom calculus is [lem-sf-tensor-hom], [thm-sf-verdier-exchange],
whose abstract outcome is [thm-sf-identification], and the identification
of the Verdier dual of a smooth $X$ with $K^\vee (d)[2d]$ is the
smooth-purity orientation [thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity]
consumed through [thm-sf-dual-perfect].
Properness of $X$ is used nowhere in this argument: the adjunctions,
the projection formula and the smooth-purity orientation hold for any
smooth separated finite-type $X$ with admissible $a_X$.

attrs.title: Identification of the Poincare pairing with Verdier duality

objects.body:
Fix the finite-field datum and the coefficient stages
$\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$ of the Poincare duality
conventions [def-pod-conventions], but let $X_0$ be an arbitrary
separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme: neither properness nor smoothness
of $X_0$ is assumed. Put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, let
$a_X:X\to s=\Spec k$ be the structure morphism, and let
$d\geq\dim X$. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda )$. Then the four
complexes

$$
R\Gamma (X,K),\qquad R\Gamma _c(X,K),\qquad R\Gamma (X,K)^\vee,\qquad R\Gamma _c(X,K)^\vee
$$

are perfect point complexes at every coefficient stage, in the
following sense.

1. At finite level $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}$ they are bounded with finite
cohomology modules and finite Tor amplitude, i.e. quasi-isomorphic to
bounded complexes of finite free $A$-modules
([def-pod-perfect-point-complex]). If $K$ has Tor amplitude in
$[a,b]$, then $R\Gamma(X,K)$ and $R\Gamma_c(X,K)$ have Tor amplitude
in $[a,b+2d]$ and their duals in $[-b-2d,-a]$.
1. At the stage $\mathcal O_E$ they lie in
$D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(\mathcal O_E)$ and are perfect; their reductions
modulo $\varpi_E^n$ are the corresponding finite-level complexes of the
reductions $K_n=K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$, and these are
perfect with one common amplitude independent of $n$.
1. At the stages $E$ and $\Qlb$ they are bounded with
finite-dimensional cohomology.

If $X_0$ is proper, the canonical comparison
$R\Gamma_c(X,K)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(X,K)$ of
[def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] identifies the two cases; in
particular this applies in the fixed setting of
[def-pod-conventions]. (Source: the finiteness theorems of etale
cohomology, Milne, Lectures on Etale Cohomology, Sections 19 and 29,
for the finiteness and the perfectness at the point. The finite-level
compact-support membership $R\Gamma _c(X,K)\in D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$
is recorded in [prop-trf-compact-support-perfectness].)

## Proof

*Step 1: the finite level.* Let $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}$ and let
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ have Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$
([def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility],
[def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]). At the geometric point $s$ a bounded
constructible complex is a bounded complex of $A$-modules with finite
cohomology ([def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]), and the Tor
amplitude of a complex on $s$ is the Tor amplitude of the underlying
$A$-module complex, since the sheaves of $A$-modules on $s$ are the
$A$-modules.

For ordinary cohomology, apply [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale]
to the separated finite-type morphism $a_X:X\to s$: the complex
$Ra_{X,*}K$ is bounded constructible with Tor amplitude in
$[a,b+2d]$. Hence $R\Gamma(X,K)$ is bounded, has finite cohomology
modules, and has Tor amplitude in $[a,b+2d]$. No properness is used.

For compact support, choose a compactification $a_X=\bar a\circ j$
with $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ an open immersion and $\bar a$ proper
([def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]); replacing $\bar X$ by
the scheme-theoretic closure of $X$ we may assume $\dim\bar X\leq d$.
Then $Ra_{X,!}K=R\bar a_*j_!K$. Extension by zero is exact and
commutes with derived tensor product, as one checks on stalks, so
$j_!K$ is bounded constructible with Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, and
[cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale] applied to $\bar a$ gives Tor
amplitude in $[a,b+2d]$ for $R\Gamma_c(X,K)$. The finiteness and
boundedness of its cohomology is
[prop-trf-compact-support-perfectness].

By [lem-trf-finite-tor-amplitude-perfect], a bounded complex of
$A$-modules with finite cohomology and Tor amplitude in $[a',b']$ is
quasi-isomorphic to a complex $P^\bullet$ of finite free $A$-modules
with $P^i=0$ for $i\notin[a',b']$. Hence $R\Gamma(X,K)$ and
$R\Gamma_c(X,K)$ are represented by bounded complexes of finite free
$A$-modules in degrees $[a,b+2d]$. For such a $P^\bullet$ the derived
dual $P^{\bullet\vee}=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(P^\bullet,A)$ is computed
termwise, $P^\bullet$ being a bounded complex of projectives, and is
the complex of finite free modules $\operatorname{Hom}_A(P^{-i},A)$
in degrees $[-b-2d,-a]$. Thus all four complexes are perfect point
complexes in the sense of [def-pod-perfect-point-complex], with the
stated amplitudes.

*Step 2: the stage $\mathcal O_E$.* Put $R=\mathcal O_E$,
$A_n=A_{E,n}$, $\kappa=A_1$, and let $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ be a
derived-complete integral object
([def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]) with reductions
$K_n=K\otimes^L_RA_n$. By [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] all the
$K_n$ have Tor amplitude in one interval $[a,b]$, namely the
cohomological range of $K_1$. By Step 1 every
$R\Gamma(X,K_n)$ and $R\Gamma_c(X,K_n)$ is a bounded complex of finite
free $A_n$-modules in the common interval $[a',b']=[a,b+2d]$.

For compact support, [lem-coef-integral-compact-support] applied to
$a_X$ gives $R\Gamma_c(X,K)\in D^b_c(s,R)$ with
$R\Gamma_c(X,K)\otimes^L_RA_n\cong R\Gamma_c(X,K_n)$, these
reductions having the uniform Tor interval $[a,b+2d]$; the integral
compact support is the one of
[def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support].

For ordinary cohomology, by [def-weil-derived-direct-image]
$R\Gamma(X,K)=R\varprojlim_nR\Gamma(X,K_n)$. The coefficient
comparisons of [lem-coef-finite-direct-image], applied to the
quotients $A_m\to A_n$ ($m\geq n$), are isomorphisms
$R\Gamma(X,K_m)\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(X,K_n)$
compatible with successive quotients, so
$(R\Gamma(X,K_n))_n$ is a normalized DVR tower on the point
([def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]).
[lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity] then gives
$R\Gamma(X,K)\otimes^L_RA_n\cong R\Gamma(X,K_n)$ for all $n$, and
$R\Gamma(X,K)$ is derived complete.

It remains to see that a derived-complete $R$-complex $C$ whose
reductions $C_n=C\otimes^L_RA_n$ are perfect with amplitude in
$[a',b']$ is perfect. The triangle
$C\xrightarrow{\varpi_E}C\to C_1\to$ gives exact sequences

$$
0\to H^i(C)/\varpi_EH^i(C)\to H^i(C_1)\to H^{i+1}(C)[\varpi_E]\to0 .
$$

Each $H^i(C)$ is a derived-complete $R$-module, the cohomology modules
of a derived-complete complex being derived complete. By the derived
Nakayama lemma for the ideal $(\varpi_E)$ of the Noetherian ring $R$,
a derived-complete module $M$ with $M/\varpi_EM=0$ vanishes, and one
with $M/\varpi_EM$ finitely generated is finitely generated. Hence
$H^i(C)=0$ for $i\notin[a',b']$ and every $H^i(C)$ is a finitely
generated $R$-module, i.e. $C\in D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(R)$. Since $R$ is
a discrete valuation ring, every finitely generated $R$-module has a
two-term resolution by finite free modules and every complex over $R$
is quasi-isomorphic to the sum of its shifted cohomology modules;
therefore $C$ is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite free
$R$-modules, i.e. it is perfect ([def-pod-perfect-point-complex]),
and its reductions are the perfect complexes $C_n$ of common
amplitude $[a',b']$. Applied to $C=R\Gamma(X,K)$ and
$C=R\Gamma_c(X,K)$ this proves the assertion for these two complexes.

For the duals, if $P^\bullet$ is a bounded complex of finite free
$R$-modules representing $C$, then $C^\vee$ is the termwise dual
complex, again bounded and finite free, and
$C^\vee\otimes^L_RA_n\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{A_n}(P^\bullet\otimes_RA_n,A_n)=C_n^\vee$;
by Step 1 these reductions are perfect in the common interval
$[-b',-a']$.

*Step 3: the field stages.* For $\Lambda=E$, the object is the
rationalization of an integral object $K_R$
([def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]), possibly up to a direct
summand, and the operations $R\Gamma$ and $R\Gamma_c$ at the stage $E$
are the rationalizations of the integral ones
([def-weil-derived-direct-image],
[def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]). By Step 2 they
are $C\otimes_RE$ with $C$ a perfect $R$-complex; since
$R\to E$ is flat, $H^i(C\otimes_RE)=H^i(C)\otimes_RE$ is
finite-dimensional and vanishes outside the bounded interval of $C$,
and $(C\otimes_RE)^\vee=C^\vee\otimes_RE$ has the same property. A
direct summand of a bounded complex with finite-dimensional cohomology
is again one. For $\Lambda=\Qlb$, the object is represented at a
finite stage $E'/\Ql$ ([def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]),
and all four complexes are obtained from the $E'$-stage complexes by
the exact extension of scalars $-\otimes_{E'}\Qlb$, which preserves
boundedness, finite-dimensionality and commutes with the dual of a
complex with finite-dimensional total cohomology. This proves the
field-stage assertions.

*Step 4: the proper case.* If $X_0$ is proper, then $a_X$ is proper
and the comparison $R\Gamma_c(X,K)\to R\Gamma(X,K)$ of
[def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] is an isomorphism at each
stage, compatible with the constructions above; in the setting of
[def-pod-conventions] this applies when $X_0$ is in addition proper.

In the Poincare duality conventions of this chapter (the fixed setting), assume in addition that $X_0$ is proper, let $\Lambda \in \{ A,\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell }\}$ with $A=A_{E,n}$, let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda )$ be perfect over $\Lambda _X$, let $K^\vee$ be the coefficient dual with Tate twist $K^\vee (d)$, and let $\beta _K$ be the derived Poincare pairing (mixed-support cup product, evaluation, normalized smooth trace). Since $X$ is proper, the canonical comparison $R\Gamma _c(X,K)\cong R\Gamma (X,K)$ of proper compact-support comparison (the proper case of $Rf_!\cong Rf_*$, $f=a_X$) identifies $\beta _K$ with a perfect pairing

$$
R\Gamma (X,K)\otimes _A^LR\Gamma \bigl(X,K^\vee (d)\bigr)[2d] \longrightarrow A,
$$

whose adjoint has inverse the canonical isomorphism

$$
R\Gamma (X,K)^\vee \xrightarrow {\  \sim \  } R\Gamma \bigl(X,K^\vee (d)\bigr)[2d].
$$

Over a field this gives perfect degreewise pairings

$$
H^i(X,K)\times H^{2d-i}\bigl(X,K^\vee (d)\bigr)\longrightarrow \Lambda ,
$$

and the line-valued form

$$
H^i(X,K)\times H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee )\longrightarrow \Lambda (-d).
$$

## Proof

Step 1: the comparison of the global-section functors. Since $X_0$ is proper by hypothesis, so is its base change $X$, and the structure morphism $a_X$ is proper; so by [cor-cbc-proper-coincidence] the canonical comparison $Ra_{X!}\to Ra_{X*}$ is an isomorphism, giving the canonical identification $R\Gamma _c(X,K)\cong R\Gamma (X,K)$ of [def-pod-derived-poincare-pairing] used in the construction. Step 2: transport of the pairing. The derived Poincare pairing $\beta _K$ of [thm-pod-derived-poincare-duality] is a morphism of the complex $R\Gamma _c(X,K)\otimes ^L_A R\Gamma (X,K^\vee (d))[2d]$ into $A$, so it transports along the identification of the first factor to the displayed pairing of $R\Gamma (X,K)\otimes _A^LR\Gamma (X,K^\vee (d))[2d]\to A$. Step 3: the adjoint. The adjoint of the transported pairing is the transported adjoint (the tensor–internal-Hom adjunction is functorial in both variables, and the identification of the first factor is transported back and forth by that canonical isomorphism), so the inverse of the transported adjoint

$$
R\Gamma (X,K)^\vee \xrightarrow {\  \sim \  }R\Gamma \bigl(X,K^\vee (d)\bigr)[2d]
$$

is the canonical isomorphism of [thm-pod-derived-poincare-duality] read through the identification, in particular it is a canonical isomorphism. Step 4: the degreewise forms. These are the field-stage part of [thm-pod-derived-poincare-duality], namely [thm-pod-degreewise-perfectness-over-a-field], with the twist elimination of [prop-pod-degree-of-the-pairing]; the finite dimensionality and the perfectness statements of the theorem are the ones of those two statements (for the proper $X$, $H_c^i=H^i$), so no further input is needed.

In the Poincare duality conventions of this chapter (the fixed setting), let $K\in D^b_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell })$ be perfect over the coefficient sheaf and be represented by an object over some finite $E/\mathbf Q_{\ell }$ as in Definition 1.12. The derived Poincare pairing of Definition 9.17 preserves the corresponding direct summands and is independent of every further finite extension; it defines the perfect derived and degreewise pairings over $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell }$, whose adjoint has inverse the canonical isomorphism

$$
R\Gamma _c(X,K)^\vee \xrightarrow {\  \sim \  } R\Gamma \bigl(X,K^\vee (d)\bigr)[2d]
$$

in the $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell }$-category of Definition 1.13. The degreewise pairings $H_c^i(X,K)\times H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee(d))\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell }$ over the field $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell }$ are perfect, the trace $\operatorname {tr}_X:H_c^{2d}(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell }(d))\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell }$ and its untwisted form $\operatorname {tr}^{(-d)}_X:H_c^{2d}(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell })\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell }(-d)$ are isomorphisms (on $H^{2d}$ in place of $H_c^{2d}$ if $X_0$ is proper), and the Frobenius similitude of Corollary 9.31 holds.

## Proof

Represent $K$ by an $E$-object $K_E\in D^b_{ctf}(X,E)$ over the finite $E/\mathbf Q_{\ell }$ stage of the common-stage construction. The $E$-level pairing is perfect by [thm-pod-degreewise-perfectness-over-a-field], and the equivariance by [cor-pod-untwisted-similitude]; the trace isomorphism (in its compact-support form, and on $H^{2d}$ when $X_0$ is proper) is the $E$-level case of [thm-pod-trace-isomorphism]. Finite extension of the coefficient field transports all of it by [thm-pod-adic-reconstruction-and-scalar-extension]; the descent of the pairings to the common-stage category and the independence of the further extensions are the descent functors of [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors], with the common-stage category of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] idempotent complete by the filtered-retract-descent theorem of [thm-weil-pbc-idempotent-complete-triangulation] (so its presentation by an idempotent is unnecessary), and the transport of the duality identification is the corresponding transport of the smooth purity, [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity]. The pairing and its adjoint are thus well defined and perfect; the remaining assertions are the transported degreewise and similitude statements of the $E$-level case.

9.7 The master interface

In the Poincare duality conventions of this chapter (the fixed setting; $X_0$ not necessarily proper), let the field stage be $\Lambda \in \{ E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell }\}$ of the datum, and let $\Lambda _X$ be the constant sheaf with its canonical strict Weil structure. The trace map $\operatorname {tr}_X$ of [def-weil-poincare-trace-cup], in the reading of [def-pod-trace-cup-reading], is the counit of $Ra_{X!}\dashv Ra_X^!$ read through the canonical orientation $\eta _X$ of [cor-pur-finite-stage-smooth-dualizing-complex] (the normalized smooth trace), and

$$
\operatorname {tr}_X:\   H_c^{2d}\bigl(X,\Lambda (d)\bigr)\xrightarrow {\  \sim \  }\Lambda
$$

is an isomorphism, and so is its untwisted form (the twist elimination of Definition 1.49)

$$
\operatorname {tr}^{(-d)}_X:\   H_c^{2d}(X,\Lambda )\xrightarrow {\  \sim \  }\Lambda (-d).
$$

For the constant sheaf on the geometrically connected $X$, the geometric Frobenius $F$ acts as the identity on $H^0(X,\Lambda )\cong \Lambda$ and by $q^d$ on $H_c^{2d}(X,\Lambda )\cong \Lambda (-d)$. If $X_0$ is proper, then $H_c^{2d}=H^{2d}$ and $\operatorname {tr}^{(-d)}_X:H^{2d}(X,\Lambda )\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda (-d)$ is an isomorphism, with $F$ acting by $q^d$ on $H^{2d}(X,\Lambda)$.

## Proof

By [cor-pod-constant-coefficients] (at $i=2d$, valid without properness), the pairing $H_c^{2d}(X,\Lambda(d))\times H^0(X,\Lambda)\to\Lambda$ is perfect and $H_c^{2d}(X,\Lambda (d))\cong H^0(X,\Lambda )^\vee \cong \Lambda$, the isomorphism being the map induced by the trace, i.e. the $\eta _X$-counit composite with the normalization of [def-pur-smooth-trace], which is $\operatorname {tr}_X$ of [def-weil-poincare-trace-cup]; its untwisting is $\operatorname {tr}^{(-d)}_X:H_c^{2d}(X,\Lambda)\to\Lambda(-d)$. For the Frobenius action, $H^0(X,\Lambda )\cong \Lambda$ with $F$ acting as the identity is the connectedness clause of [prop-cohomological-finiteness] (no properness needed); for the top degree, the $F$-action on $\Lambda _X(d)$ in the trace is the twist normalization $q^{-d}$, of [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists], so the untwisted form $\Lambda (-d)$ carries the $q^d$-action, again by [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists]. If $X_0$ is proper, $a_X$ is proper and [cor-cbc-proper-coincidence] identifies $Ra_{X!}$ with $Ra_{X*}$ Frobenius-compatibly, so $H_c^{2d}(X,\Lambda)=H^{2d}(X,\Lambda)$ (the proper comparison of [thm-pod-proper-poincare-duality]) and $\operatorname{tr}^{(-d)}_X$ becomes the map $H^{2d}(X,\Lambda)\to\Lambda(-d)$ of [def-weil-poincare-trace-cup], still an isomorphism with $F$ acting by $q^d$.

Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes, where $S$ is
locally Noetherian. The following are
equivalent:

1. **(1)** $f$ is
finite;
1. **(2)** $f$ is
proper with finite
fibres, in the sense of
[pqf-def-quasifinite].

(*Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 30.21.1, Tag
[02OG](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02OG).*)

## Proof

*(1) $\Rightarrow$ (2).* If $f$ is finite, then $f$ is proper by
[lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper] of the ambient-foundations chapter, and $f$ is
quasi-finite by [pqf-lem-finite-qf]. A quasi-finite morphism has
finite fibres by [pqf-lem-qf-finitefibres]. Hence $f$ is proper
with finite fibres.

*(2) $\Rightarrow$ (1).* Assume $f$ is proper with finite fibres.
It suffices to prove that $f$ is affine: if $f$ is affine, then $f$ is
universally closed by [pqf-lem-proper-basic] (it is proper), so
$f$ is integral by [pqf-lem-integral-univclosed]; since $f$ is
proper it is of finite type, hence locally of finite type, by
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]; therefore $f$ is finite by
[pqf-lem-integral-lft-finite].

To prove that $f$ is affine, by
[pqf-lem-affine-local-target] we may assume that $S$ is affine,
and our goal is to show that $X$ is affine. Since $f$ is proper, $X$
is separated and quasi-compact by [pqf-lem-proper-basic], so we
may use [pqf-lem-serre-criterion] to prove that $X$ is affine.
Let $\mathcal I\subset\mathcal O_X$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf of
ideals of finite type. First, $X$ is locally Noetherian: $f$ is of
finite type by [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and $S$ is
locally Noetherian, so [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] applies. Hence
$\mathcal I$, being quasi-coherent of finite type on the locally
Noetherian scheme $X$, is coherent by
[pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. By
[pqf-lem-fff-vanishing] applied to the coherent sheaf
$\mathcal I$ we get $(R^1f_*\mathcal I)_s=0$ for all $s\in S$
(the fibre $f^{-1}(\{s\})$ is finite by assumption), i.e. the sheaf
$R^1f_*\mathcal I$ has vanishing stalks at every point, so
$R^1f_*\mathcal I=0$ by [pqf-lem-sheaf-zero-stalks]. From the
Leray spectral sequence [pqf-lem-leray] of the morphism $f$, more
precisely from its low degree terms
[pqf-lem-leray-lowdegree], we obtain

$$
\mathrm H^1(X,\mathcal I)\cong\mathrm H^1(S,f_*\mathcal I).
$$

Now $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by
[pqf-lem-proper-basic], so $f_*\mathcal I$ is quasi-coherent by
[pqf-lem-pushforward-qcoh]. Since $S$ is affine,
[pqf-lem-affine-vanishing] gives
$\mathrm H^1(S,f_*\mathcal I)=0$. Hence
$\mathrm H^1(X,\mathcal I)=0$ for every quasi-coherent ideal of finite
type, and [pqf-lem-serre-criterion] shows that $X$ is affine.
Since $S$ is affine as well, $f$ is affine by
[pqf-def-affine-morphism], which finishes the proof.

attrs.title: Finite = proper with finite fibres; Stacks Lemma 30.21.1

objects.body:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a separated morphism of finite type which is
everywhere quasi-finite, with $S$
quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let $\nu_f:N_f\to S$ be the
relative normalization of $S$ in $X$, with $X\xrightarrow{\iota_f} N_f$ a quasi-compact open immersion, and let
$N_f=\varprojlim_\lambda T_\lambda$ be the presentation of $N_f$ as a
filtered limit of finite $S$-schemes, with affine transition maps,
supplied by the finite-approximation tail of the preceding proof. Then
there are an index $\lambda_0$ and a factorization

$$
X\xrightarrow{\ j\ }T\xrightarrow{\ i\ }T_{\lambda_0}
$$

with $j$ a quasi-compact open immersion and $i$ a closed immersion.
If moreover $S$ is
locally Noetherian — in particular if
$f$ is locally of finite presentation over a locally Noetherian
$S$ — the index $\lambda_0$ may be chosen so that
$T_{\lambda_0}$ is finite and of finite presentation over $S$.

(*Stacks Project*: the descent is the step of the proof of the
Zariski main theorem, More on Morphisms, Lemma 37.43.3,
[Tag 05K0](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05K0), that its
limit lemma
[Tag 01ZM](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01ZM) does not
supply — that lemma descends the open subscheme $\iota_f(X)$ to an
open $U\subseteq T_{\lambda_0}$, exhibiting $X$ as the fibre product
$N_f\times_{T_{\lambda_0}}U$, whose projection onto $U$ is the base
change of the integral morphism $\nu_f$, hence finite and surjective of
the same degree as $\nu_f$, and therefore not an immersion as soon as
one fibre of $\nu_f$ over $U$ has more than one point; what is
needed in addition is the spreading out of the *closed* immersion
$X\to U$, Limits of Schemes, Lemma 32.4.16,
[Tag 081B](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/081B), together with
the descent of the quasi-compact open, Limits of Schemes, Lemma 32.4.11,
[Tag 01Z4](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01Z4). The
factorization of the immersion is Morphisms of Schemes, Lemma 29.3.2,
[Tag 01QV](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01QV). The
finite-presentation refinement of the theorem,
[Tag 0F2N](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F2N), is a
statement about the factorization scheme $T$ and not about a stage of
the presentation above: its proof replaces that presentation by an
approximating directed system of finite finitely presented $S$-schemes,
Limits of Schemes, Lemma 32.9.8,
[Tag 09YY](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09YY). Hence for
$f$ locally of finite presentation over a general quasi-compact
quasi-separated $S$ the clause about a stage of the presentation of the
finite-approximation tail is not proved here: Tag 09YY does not apply to
that presentation, whose transition maps are affine and dual to the
injective algebra maps $\mathcal A_\lambda\hookrightarrow\mathcal A_\mu$ rather than closed immersions. The clause holds in the corrected
form proved in the last section of this
chapter: Tag 09YY, applied to the finite scheme $T$ of the factorization
constructed above, replaces it by a finite and finitely presented
$S$-scheme containing $X$ as a quasi-compact open subscheme. Over a
locally Noetherian $S$ the clause holds for the tail itself, because
every finite $S$-scheme is then of finite presentation.)

## Proof

*Step 1: the descended open.* By the finite-approximation tail of
the preceding proof, $N_f=\varprojlim_\lambda T_\lambda$ is a filtered
limit of $S$-schemes with affine transition morphisms, each
$T_\lambda$ being finite over $S$ by
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], hence quasi-compact and
quasi-separated; by the recorded input Tag 02LR, applied to the
everywhere quasi-finite morphism $f$ of [pqf-def-quasifinite],
the morphism $\iota_f$ is a quasi-compact open immersion, so
$V:=\iota_f(X)\subset N_f$ is a quasi-compact open subscheme. By
[pqf-lem-limit-qc-open-descends] there are an index $\lambda_1$
and a quasi-compact open $U_{\lambda_1}\subset T_{\lambda_1}$ with
$V=N_f\times_{T_{\lambda_1}}U_{\lambda_1}$; let $U_\lambda$ be the
preimage of $U_{\lambda_1}$ in $T_\lambda$ for
$\lambda\ge\lambda_1$. Clause (3) of the same lemma identifies $V$
with the filtered limit $\varprojlim_{\lambda\ge\lambda_1}U_\lambda$,
the projections being those of $N_f$.

*Step 2: the immersion spreads out.* The morphism $\iota_f$
induces an isomorphism $X\to V$, so $X$ is a closed subscheme of the
limit $\varprojlim_{\lambda\ge\lambda_1}U_\lambda$; the structure
morphism $X\to S$ is locally of finite type by
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and each $U_\lambda$ is
quasi-compact. Hence [pqf-lem-limit-immersion-descends] applies and
the composite $X\to U_\lambda$ is a closed immersion for all
sufficiently large $\lambda$. Fix such an index and call it
$\lambda_0$; enlarging it if necessary we may assume
$\lambda_0\ge\lambda_1$.

*Step 3: factoring the immersion.* The composite
$h:X\to U_{\lambda_0}\hookrightarrow T_{\lambda_0}$ is an immersion,
and it is quasi-compact: for a quasi-compact open
$W\subset T_{\lambda_0}$ the intersection
$U_{\lambda_0}\cap W$ is quasi-compact by
[pqf-lem-qs-intersection-qc], since $T_{\lambda_0}$ is
quasi-separated and both $U_{\lambda_0}$ and $W$ are quasi-compact
opens, and $h^{-1}(W)=X\times_{U_{\lambda_0}}(U_{\lambda_0}\cap W)$ is
a closed subscheme of it — the base change of the closed immersion
$X\to U_{\lambda_0}$ — hence is quasi-compact. By the recorded input
Tag 01QV a quasi-compact immersion factors as an open immersion followed
by a closed immersion: there are a scheme $T$, an open immersion
$j:X\to T$ and a closed immersion $i:T\to T_{\lambda_0}$ with
$h=i\circ j$. In that construction $T$ is the closed subscheme of
$T_{\lambda_0}$ whose sheaf of ideals is the kernel of
$\mathcal O_{T_{\lambda_0}}\to h_*\mathcal O_X$, so that $X$ is the
fibre product $T\times_{T_{\lambda_0}}U_{\lambda_0}$ and $j$ is the
base change of the open immersion
$U_{\lambda_0}\hookrightarrow T_{\lambda_0}$ along the closed immersion
$i$; that open immersion is quasi-compact for the same reason as
$h$, and quasi-compactness is stable under base change, so $j$ is a
quasi-compact open immersion, as required.

*Step 4: the finitely presented stage.* If $S$ is
[pqf-def-locnoeth], then the finite morphism
$T_{\lambda_0}\to S$ is of finite presentation by
[pqf-lem-finite-fp-locnoeth], so the index $\lambda_0$ fixed in
Step 2 satisfies the additional clause of the statement.

attrs.title: Descent of the immersion to a finite stage

objects.body:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a
separated morphism of finite
type which is everywhere
quasi-finite, with $S$
quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Then there exist a scheme $T$, a
quasi-compact open
immersion $j:X\hookrightarrow T$ and a
finite morphism
$p:T\to S$ with $f=p\circ j$.
(*Stacks Project: the Zariski main theorem, More on Morphisms,
Lemma 37.43.3, Tag [05K0](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05K0);
the
normalization-of-the-target-in-the-source constructions used in the
proof are the quasi-finite-locus theorem Tag
[03GW](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03GW) and Tag
[02LR](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02LR).*)

## Proof

*Step 1: the canonical branch (recorded input).* The
normalization of $S$ in $X$ (the relative
integral-closure construction of the recorded input Tag
03GW, cf. also the quasi-finite-locus statement OBL-PQF-06) is a
scheme $N_f$ with a morphism

$$
X\xrightarrow{\ \iota_f\ }N_f\xrightarrow{\ \nu_f\ }S,
\qquad \nu_f\circ\iota_f=f,
$$

where $\nu_f$ is *integral* and, since $f$ is everywhere
quasi-finite ([pqf-def-quasifinite]), $\iota_f$ is a
*quasi-compact open immersion*
(the classical form of the theorem, Tag 02LR). Write
$\mathcal A_f=\nu_{f*}\mathcal O_{N_f}$, an $\mathcal O_S$-algebra
whose fibres are the integral closures mentioned there; locally on an
affine $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq S$ the algebra
$\mathcal A_f(\operatorname{Spec}A)$ is the integral closure of $A$ in
$\Gamma(f^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}A),\mathcal O_X)$.

*Step 2: the finite approximation tail.* On every affine
$\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq S$, the ring $B=\mathcal A_f(A)$ is
the filtered union of its finite $A$-subalgebras: each $b\in B$ is
integral over $A$, so the subalgebra $A[b]$ is a finite $A$-module
(generated by $1,b,\dots,b^{n-1}$ for the minimal degree of a monic
equation), finite lists of integral elements generate finite
subalgebras (the same argument, iterated), and the union of the
finite subalgebras generated by finite lists of elements of $B$ is
$B$ and is filtered by inclusion of the generating lists. Globally,
since $S$ is quasi-compact, $\mathcal A_f$ is the filtered union of
its finite quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-subalgebras
$\mathcal A_\lambda$, with $T_\lambda=\operatorname{Spec}_S\mathcal A_\lambda$ finite over $S$ by
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] (affine and finite
$\mathcal O_S$-module); the transition maps of the system
$\{T_\lambda\}$ are affine, and $N_f=\varprojlim_\lambda T_\lambda$.

*Step 3: the descended stage (recorded input).* By
[thm-pqf-immersion-descent] there are an index $\lambda_0$ and a
factorization

$$
X\xrightarrow{\ j\ }T\xrightarrow{\ i\ }T_{\lambda_0}
$$

with $j$ a quasi-compact *open* immersion and $i$ a *closed*
immersion. The closed immersion $i$ is finite, hence a
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] finite morphism, and a closed
subscheme of a finite $S$-scheme is finite over it: $T\to T_{\lambda_0}$ is an affine $S$-morphism with finite module of sections
(closed immersion), and finiteness is transitive (finite over finite is
finite: the module of sections over the composite affine is generated
by the products of the two finite generating lists). Therefore
$p=T\to T_{\lambda_0}\to S$ is finite, and pasting the canonical
equality $\nu_f\circ\iota_f=f$ with the stage projections gives
$p\circ j=f$: the projections of the limit $N_f=\varprojlim_\lambda T_\lambda$ are compatible, and the interface identifies the descended
factorization with the one of Step 1.

attrs.title: Zariski's main theorem: the quasi-finite factorization

objects.body:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
$f:X\to Y$ be smooth separated of relative dimension $d$, and let
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ with finite reductions
$K_n\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A_{E,n})$. The comparisons
$\gamma_{f,K_n}$ of [thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity] form a
morphism of normalized systems in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], and they induce an isomorphism

$$
Lf^*K(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf^!K
$$

in $D^b_{ctf}(X,\mathcal O_E)$, whose reduction at every level $n$ is
exactly $\gamma_{f,K_n}$.

## Proof

By [thm-pur-finite-reduction-of-purity], the reduction of
$\gamma_{f,K_{n+1}}$ along $A_{E,n+1}\to A_{E,n}$ is
$\gamma_{f,K_n}$, i.e. the comparisons are compatible with the
transition maps of the normalized system; the common bounds and
stratifications of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower] are those
of $K$ with the same $d$-shift. Hence
$(\gamma_{f,K_n})_{n}$ is a morphism of normalized systems, whose
realization under the uniform-tower reconstruction of
[lem-weil-pbc-reconstruction-uniform-tower] is the displayed
isomorphism over $\mathcal O_E$, and the levelwise nature of the
reconstruction gives the compatibility with the reductions.

In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting), let $Y$ be the separated finite-type $k$-scheme of the
affine-line datum, and let
$\kappa(t)\in H^1(\mathbf G_{m,Y},A(1))$ be the
Kummer class of the global coordinate
$t$. The boundary of $\kappa(t)$, determined through the
identification of [lem-pur-gysin-structure] (which gives the
support object $Rs^!\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_Y}(1)[2]\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$
concentrated in degree zero), is the *global orientation* – a
morphism

$$
\operatorname{pur}_s:\Lambda_Y\longrightarrow Rs^!\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_Y}(1)[2]
$$

in $D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ with $\Lambda=A$, where $Rs^!$ is the
exceptional inverse image
of the zero section $s:Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_Y$, a closed
immersion whose ambient right adjoint exists unconditionally
([lem-exc-closed-ambient]) and preserves constructibility and
finite Tor amplitude, the open complement
$\mathbf G_{m,Y}\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_Y$ satisfying the
open-complement condition of
[lem-exc-closed-amplitude], [prop-exc-closed-tor] by
[lem-exc-open-complement-known],
with the shift $[2]$ and the twist
$(1)$. Its restriction to every geometric point $\bar y\to Y$ is
the normalized class $1\in H^2_{s(\bar y)}(\mathbf A^1_{\bar y},\Lambda(1))$ of
[thm-pur-rank-one-local-calculation]. (Source: the affine-line
case of cohomological purity, obtained from the Kummer sequence and the
fundamental class of the zero section; Milne, Lectures on Etale
Cohomology, Section 16, Theorems 16.1 and 16.7, and Proposition 16.11
(the case $r=2c-1=1$ of the Gysin sequence of the divisor), with the
acyclicity of the affine line computed in Example 16.3, for the
relative form over a base scheme $Y$.)

## Proof

The Kummer boundary defines the global morphism in the statement by
[lem-pur-gysin-structure], [def-pur-affine-line-datum].
Its target is already a sheaf in degree zero, identified there with
$\Lambda_Y$ through the boundary $\delta$ of the localization triangle
of [lem-pur-support-localization-triangle] pushed forward to $Y$:
$\delta$ carries $R^1\pi_*\Lambda(1)$, free of rank one on $\kappa(t)$
by [prop-pur-gm-relative-kummer](2), isomorphically onto
$\mathcal H^2(Rs^!\Lambda(1))$. So $\operatorname{pur}_s$, which sends
$1$ to the boundary of $\kappa(t)$, already maps $1$ to a generator of
this free rank-one sheaf.
The supported Cartier map of [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map] is natural
for the base changes of the zero section, and its geometric fibre is
the coordinate boundary. By [thm-pur-rank-one-local-calculation]
that boundary is $1$. Consequently the morphism of degree-zero
sheaves has every stalk equal to the identity, and is an isomorphism.
The etale-origin comparison of [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]
transports the assertion and its normalization to the stated site.
Uniqueness follows because a section of a sheaf is determined by its
stalks; this does not require a conservativity assertion for morphisms
of arbitrary derived objects.

In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting), let $Y$ be the scheme of the
affine-line datum and let
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ with $\Lambda=A$. The affine-line purity
comparison $\gamma_{p,K}$ of
[def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison] – the adjoint of the
projection-formula composite
$Rp_!Lp^*K(1)[2]\cong K\otimes^L Rp_!\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_Y}(1)[2]\to K$
formed with the projective-line trace and normalized by the orientation
$\operatorname{pur}_s$ of [thm-pur-affine-line-orientation] – is an isomorphism

$$
\gamma_{p,K}:Lp^*K(1)[2]\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rp^!K.
$$

It is natural in $K$ and compatible with arbitrary base change of $Y$.
(Source: the relative affine-line case of cohomological purity, as in
Milne, Lectures on Etale Cohomology, Section 16, Theorems 16.1 and
16.7 and Proposition 16.11, with the acyclicity computation of Example
16.3 and the Gysin sequence of the divisor, over an arbitrary base
scheme.)

## Proof

On the ordinary etale site, [cor-amb-affine-space-adjunction]
constructs $Rp_!\dashv p^*(1)[2]$ by composing
$j_!\dashv j^*$ with the explicit projective-line adjunction.
Its counit is exactly the composite in
[def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison], since
[def-amb-p1-trace] defines the same normalized trace.
Uniqueness of a right adjoint with its counit therefore identifies its
adjoint $\gamma_{p,K}$ with an isomorphism.
The actual-adjoint comparison of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class]
and [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] transport this statement and
the adjunction bijection to the finite etale-origin coefficients of
this chapter. Naturality follows from the defining adjunction.
For base change, [prop-asd-smooth-base-change] identifies the mate
of compact-support base change with the inverse-image and twist
identification for this explicit affine-line adjunction. Hence the
same defining counit, and therefore $\gamma_{p,K}$, commutes with
arbitrary base change. General smooth purity is not an input here.

In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
for every smooth separated morphism $f:X\to Y$ of relative dimension
$d$ put

$$
\omega_f\;=\;Rf^!\Lambda_Y.
$$

Then:

1. *Tensor formula.* For every $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ the
canonical map
$$
Lf^*K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}\omega_f\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf^!K
$$
is an isomorphism.
1. *Invertibility.* $\omega_f$ is invertible.
1. *Base change.* The formation of $\omega_f$ and of the
canonical map is compatible with arbitrary base change: for a
Cartesian square with $f'$ the base change of $f$,
$$
Lu^*\omega_f\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\omega_{f'},
$$
and the two canonical maps correspond under $Lu^*$; this holds for
*arbitrary* $v$ by [lem-pur-smb-extraordinary].
1. *Composition.* The tensor formula is compatible with
composition of smooth morphisms, through the composition isomorphism
for $R^!$ of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image].

(*Orientation-free form*: none of the four statements identifies
$\omega_f$ with a twist and a shift; that identification,
$\omega_f\cong\Lambda(d)[2d]$, is the content of
[thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object] proved below from the diagonal
argument.)

## Proof

Work at a finite coefficient stage. The earlier orientation-free
theorem [thm-asd-smooth-tensor] proves the canonical tensor
formula on the ordinary etale site and shows that
$\omega_f[-2d]$ is a locally constant free rank-one sheaf.
In particular it is tensor-invertible, and tensoring it with the
pullback of a bounded constructible finite-Tor complex stays in that
category. The actual-adjoint comparison
[thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] and
[thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] transport the tensor map and
its isomorphy to the finite etale-origin objects used here.
Because the map is obtained by transposing the projection formula
and counit on both sites, the transported map is the canonical
$\theta_{f,K}$ in [def-pur-co-smoothness].

For the third condition of that definition,
[lem-pur-smb-extraordinary] proves arbitrary base change of the
actual right adjoint, and [prop-asd-smooth-base-change] also
proves its compatibility with the tensor transformation before
transport. Thus these are all three conditions of cohomological
smoothness. For composition, [lem-pur-co-smooth-composition]
identifies $\omega_{gf}$ with
$\omega_f\otimes^LLf^*\omega_g$. The two tensor transformations
agree: transposing them gives the projection formula followed by
the same two counits, composed in their adjunction order. This
proves the fourth assertion without using an orientation of $f$.

In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
ingredients used here: the global finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$
with $q=p^a$, the prime $\ell\neq p$, the finite extension
$E/\Ql$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer
$\varpi_E$, the level $n\geq1$, and the finite coefficient ring
$A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$; let
$f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be smooth separated
morphisms of relative dimensions $d$ and $e$. Under the canonical
identification

$$
L(gf)^*(-)(d+e)[2d+2e]
\cong Lf^*Lg^*(-)(d)[2d](e)[2e],
$$

the smooth purity map $\gamma_{gf,K}$ equals the composite

$$
\begin{array}{l}
L(gf)^*K(d+e)[2d+2e]
\xrightarrow{\ Lf^*(\gamma_{g,K})(d)[2d]\ }
Lf^*Rg^!K(d)[2d]
\xrightarrow{\ \gamma_{f,Rg^!K}\ }
Rf^!Rg^!K\\
\hphantom{L(gf)^*K(d+e)[2d+2e]}
\xrightarrow{\ c_{g,f}^{-1}\ }R(gf)^!K,
\end{array}
$$

where $c_{g,f}:R(gf)^!\cong Rf^!Rg^!$ is the composition isomorphism for
the exceptional inverse image.

## Proof

Step 1: the dualizing-object version. By
[thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness] (the tensor
formula for the smooth morphisms $f,g,gf$) and the composition rule
of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], the identity

$$
\omega_{gf}\cong\omega_f\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}Lf^*\omega_g
$$

holds; and the identification of
[thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object] applied to $gf$, to $g$
and to $f$ is compatible with this identity. Indeed, both
identifications are built from the DNC invariance of the section
invariant ([thm-pur-dnc-invariance]) and the vector-bundle purity
of the relative tangent bundle ([cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity]);
the diagonal of $gf$ is the transverse composite of the diagonals of
$g$ and of $f$ through the canonical Cartesian product
identifications of the twofold fibred products, and the canonical exact
sequence of the relative tangent bundles

$$
0\longrightarrow T_{X/Y}\longrightarrow T_{X/Z}\longrightarrow
f^*T_{Y/Z}\longrightarrow0
$$

splits in the standard coordinates of the etale local normal forms
([sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form]); the direct-sum compatibility
of [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity] and, above all, the uniqueness
clause of [thm-pur-dnc-invariance] – one and the same
identification is forced by being the identity on the standard pairs
and compatible with etale localization and base change, and the two
assemblies have exactly these properties – make the two assemblies
agree after the canonical reassociation (the coherence of the package's
composition isomorphisms and the pentagon for the twofold diagonal).
The remaining constituents of [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object]
– the smooth base change ([lem-pur-diagonal-base-change]) and the
co-projection – are compatible with composition by the definition of
the canonical maps (the base-change squares of the composite and the
associativity of the derived tensor product).
Step 2: the $K$-form. The identity of Step 1 transposes to the
statement: the tensor formula is compatible with composition by its
definition (the mate of the projection formula), the twist
isomorphisms [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] are compatible with the
pullback-composition, and composing gives the composite of the
statement, the identifications being those displayed.

In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth,
separated, of pure
relative dimension $d$. Then there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
\omega_f=Rf^!\Lambda_Y\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Lambda_X(d)[2d].
$$

## Proof

The final restriction of the Tate line uses [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], with tensor identifications as in [def-weil-derived-tensor].
Step 1: the section invariant of the diagonal. Apply
[thm-pur-dnc-invariance] to the smooth map
$p_1:W\to X$ of [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change] and its closed
section $\Delta$. By [lem-pur-diagonal-regular-immersion] its
normal bundle is canonically $N_\Delta\cong T_{X/Y}$, a vector
bundle of rank $d$, so

$$
C(p_1,\Delta)\;\cong\;C(\pi_T:T_{X/Y}\to X,\,0_T).
$$

Step 2: the two sides. The left side is $\omega_f$ by
[lem-pur-diagonal-base-change]. For the right side,
[cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity] applied to $\pi_T$ gives

$$
\omega_{\pi_T}=R\pi_T^!\Lambda_X\;\cong\;\Lambda_{T_{X/Y}}(d)[2d],
$$

and pulling back by the zero section $0_T$ gives

$$
C(\pi_T,0_T)=0_T^*\omega_{\pi_T}
\;\cong\;0_T^*\Lambda_{T_{X/Y}}(d)[2d]
\;\cong\;\Lambda_X(d)[2d].
$$

Combining the two steps proves the assertion. The identification is
canonical (every displayed step is canonical, by the uniqueness clause
of [thm-pur-dnc-invariance]); compatibility with base change
follows from the base-change compatibility of the diagonal, of
[thm-pur-dnc-invariance], and of
[cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity] (the normal bundle of the diagonal
of the base change is the base change of the normal bundle).

attrs.title: The smooth dualizing object is the Tate twist

objects.body:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting), in the situation of
[def-pur-dnc-section-family], there is a unique isomorphism

$$
C(g,s)\;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;C(\pi_N,0_N)
$$

which, in coordinates carrying $(g,s)$ to
$(\mathbf A^d_B\to B,0)$, is the identity on the standard section
invariant. It is compatible with etale localization and arbitrary base
change in $B$.

## Proof

Write $a:\mathbf A^1_B\to B$, let
$i_0,i_1:B\rightrightarrows\mathbf A^1_B$ be the sections $t=0$ and
$t=1$, and let $\kappa:F\xrightarrow{\sim}a^*C(g,s)$ be the
canonical isomorphism of
[prop-pur-dnc-family-constancy](2). By
[lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry](1) the fibre of $\widetilde g$
over $t=0$ is the normal bundle $\pi_N:N_s\to B$ with its zero
section, and $i_0^*F\simeq C(\pi_N,0_N)$; hence the inverse of
$i_0^*\kappa$ is a canonical isomorphism
$C(g,s)\to C(\pi_N,0_N)$. In coordinates carrying $(g,s)$ to
$(\mathbf A^d_B\to B,0)$ it is the identity on the standard section
invariant, because there the deformation is the pulled-back standard
family and $\kappa$ restricts to the pullback identification (Step 3
of the proof of [prop-pur-dnc-family-constancy]). It is unique:
two such isomorphisms differ by a locally constant unit on $B$ by
[lem-pur-lisse-rank-one-aut](1)–(2), and that unit is trivial on
every coordinate chart $B_i$, hence trivial on $B$.
Compatibility with etale localization and base change is
[prop-pur-dnc-family-constancy](4).

attrs.title: DNC invariance of the section dualizing line

objects.body:
Fix the purity conventions with its
explicit ingredients: the global finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$,
the prime $\ell\neq p$, the finite extension $E/\Ql$ with valuation
ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, the integer
$n\geq1$, and the finite coefficient ring
$A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$; on the
small pro-etale site of a
