$\mathcal O_C(C)^\times/k^\times$ with the subgroup of the
degree-zero divisors supported on $S$ whose class in
$J_{\overline C}$ is zero. This subgroup is finitely generated free;
it is unchanged by base change $k\to k'$, because
$J_{\overline C}(k)\to J_{\overline C}(k')$ is injective, so a
degree-zero divisor supported at the same $k$-rational set $S$ is
principal over $k$ if and only if it is principal over $k'$. As
$k^\times$ and $k'^\times$ are both $n$-divisible, the natural maps

$$
\mathcal O_C(C)^\times/\mathcal O_C(C)^\times{}^{\,n}
\to\mathcal O_{C_{k'}}(C_{k'})^\times/
\mathcal O_{C_{k'}}(C_{k'})^\times{}^{\,n}
$$

are isomorphisms. The five lemma now shows that the
middle maps $H^1(C,\mu_n)\to H^1(C_{k'},\mu_n)$ are isomorphisms.
For the right-hand identification: under the quotient descriptions
of [lem-sc-pic-affine] for $C$ and
$C_{k'}$ (the compactification of $C_{k'}$ is
$\overline C_{k'}$ by [lem-sc-base-change-curve], and the
deleted set $S$ is the same finite set, since
$S_{k'}=S\otimes_kk'=S$), the pullback map is
$x+\Lambda\mapsto x+\Lambda$. This is an isomorphism on
$n$-torsion: injectivity is clear; for surjectivity, let
$y\in J_{\overline C}(k')$ with $ny\in\Lambda\subset J_{\overline C}(k)$; by divisibility of $J_{\overline C}(k)$
([thm-av-final](d)) there is $z\in J_{\overline C}(k)$ with $ny=nz$, so
$y-z\in J_{\overline C}[n](k')=J_{\overline C}[n](k)\subset J_{\overline C}(k)$ ([thm-av-final](c)), whence
$y\in J_{\overline C}(k)$. For $H^2$: both groups vanish
([lem-sc-brauer-zero] over $k$ and over $k'$), and for
$q>2$ both groups vanish by
[lem-sc-cohomological-dimension] (over $k$ and over
$k'$).

Let $K$ be a field with $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(K)\leq c$,
and let $X$ be a finite-type
$K$-scheme of dimension $d$.
Then $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(X)\leq2d+c$, in the sense of
[def-sc-etale-torsion-cd].

## Proof

Restrict etale sheaves to Zariski opens to obtain the direct
image $\epsilon_*:\operatorname{Ab}(X_{\rm et})\to \operatorname{Ab}(X_{\rm Zar})$, using [def-sc-zariski-site].
Its inverse image is exact: the geometric stalk of
$\epsilon^{-1}G$ over $x$ is the ordinary Zariski stalk
$G_x$, an exact functor. Thus $\epsilon_*$ preserves
injectives, and [thm-sp-grothendieck] gives

$$
H^p(X_{\rm Zar},R^q\epsilon_*F)
\ \Longrightarrow\ H^{p+q}(X_{\rm et},F).
$$

This is the composite of the two ordinary section functors
of [def-sc-zariski-cohomology].

The Zariski stalk of $R^q\epsilon_*F$ at $x$ is
$\varinjlim_{x\in V}H^q(V_{\rm et},F|_V)$.
To see this, restrict an injective etale resolution to
each open $V$; it remains injective because extension
by zero from an open is exact. Then take the exact
filtered colimit over $V$.
Affine opens are cofinal among neighborhoods of $x$.
They have dimension at most $d$, so
[thm-sc-affine-torsion-cd] makes the stalk zero for
$q>d+c$. Hence $R^q\epsilon_*F=0$ in these degrees.
On the other hand
[lem-sc-zariski-dimension-bound] kills the spectral
sequence for $p>d$, without needing its entries to be
constructible or torsion. All surviving total degrees
are at most $d+(d+c)=2d+c$.
This proves the ordinary etale bound for every torsion $F$;
no identification with compactly supported cohomology is used.

attrs.title: Torsion cohomological dimension of a finite-type scheme

objects.body:
Let $X$ be a scheme (for instance a curve $C$ as in
[def-sc-curves]). The set of isomorphism classes of invertible
$\mathcal O_X$-modules ([def-sc-invertible-module]) is an
abelian group under $\otimes$, and the natural maps are isomorphisms
of abelian groups

$$
\{\text{invertible }\mathcal O_X\text{-modules}\}/{\cong}
\;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;
H^1(X_{\mathrm{Zar}},\mathcal O_X^\times)\;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;
H^1(X_{\Et},\mathbf G_m),
$$

the first sending $\mathcal L$ to the Zariski torsor
$\underline{\operatorname{Isom}}(\mathcal O_X,\mathcal L)$, the second
being the comparison map induced by the morphism of sites
$\varepsilon:X_{\Et}\to X_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ and
$\varepsilon^{-1}\mathcal O_X^{\times}\to\mathbf G_m$, and the
composite sending the class of $\mathcal L$ to the class of the
$\mathbf G_m$-torsor
$\underline{\operatorname{Isom}}(\mathcal O_{X_{\Et}},\mathcal L_{\Et})$.
(*Stacks Project, Tag [03P8](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03P8)*.)

## Proof

*The two maps out of the Picard set are bijective group maps.* By
[lem-sc-torsor-h1], $H^1(X_{\Et},\mathbf G_m)$ is the group of
isomorphism classes of $\mathbf G_m$-torsors ([def-sc-gm-torsor])
under contracted product, and $H^1(X_{\mathrm{Zar}},\mathcal O_X^{\times})$
is likewise the group of Zariski $\mathcal O_X^{\times}$-torsors. By
[lem-sc-line-bundle-torsor] (etale and Zariski versions),
$\mathcal L\mapsto\underline{\operatorname{Isom}}(\mathcal O,\mathcal L)$
is in both cases a bijection from the set of isomorphism classes of
invertible modules, carrying $\otimes$ to contracted product and
$\mathcal O_X$ to the trivial torsor. Transporting the group structure,
$\otimes$ makes the Picard set an abelian group (with inverse the class
of the torsor inverse, i.e. of $\mathcal L^{\vee}$) and both maps are
group isomorphisms.

*The comparison map.* Under the torsor descriptions of
[lem-sc-torsor-h1], the comparison map
$H^1(X_{\mathrm{Zar}},\mathcal O_X^{\times})\to H^1(X_{\Et},\mathbf G_m)$
sends a Zariski torsor $T$ to the etale torsor
$\varepsilon^{-1}T\times^{\varepsilon^{-1}\mathcal O_X^{\times}}\mathbf G_m$:
indeed it is obtained from the extension
$0\to\mathcal O_X^{\times}\to E\to\mathbf Z_X\to0$ of $T$ by the exact
functor $\varepsilon^{-1}$ followed by push-out along
$\varepsilon^{-1}\mathcal O_X^{\times}\to\mathbf G_m$, and the preimage
of $1$ in the push-out is this contracted product. For
$T=\underline{\operatorname{Isom}}(\mathcal O_X,\mathcal L)$, the map
sending a Zariski-local isomorphism $\varphi:\mathcal O_U\to\mathcal L|_U$
and a unit $u$ on an etale $V\to U$ to the
$\mathcal O_{X_{\Et}}$-linear isomorphism $u\cdot\varphi_V$ of
$\mathcal O_V$ onto $\mathcal L_{\Et}|_V$ is a $\mathbf G_m$-equivariant
map from this torsor to
$\underline{\operatorname{Isom}}(\mathcal O_{X_{\Et}},\mathcal L_{\Et})$,
hence an isomorphism (an equivariant map of torsors is one, as one
checks locally). So the triangle formed by the three maps commutes;
since the two maps out of the Picard group are isomorphisms, so is the
comparison map.

Let $k$ be a separably closed field and let $C$ be a
smooth projective curve over $k$
which is geometrically integral,
of genus $g=g(C)=\dim_kH^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$ ([def-pc-genus]). There is
an abelian variety $J_C$ over
$k$, the *Jacobian* of $C$ in the sense of [def-sc-jacobian], of dimension $g$, together
with a natural isomorphism of group-valued functors

$$
\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\cong h_{J_C},
$$

where $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$ is the degree-zero part of the
Picard functor; its $k$-points are the
invertible modules of degree $0$ on $C$, and for algebraically closed
$k$ they are the $\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)$ of [def-sc-pic0], so that
$\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)=J_C(k)$ canonically in that case. Moreover $J_C$
is compatible with base change along extensions of separably closed fields:
$J_{C_{k'}}\cong(J_C)_{k'}$ for $k\subseteq k'$ separably closed.
The scope of this result, and the case of a general ground field, are
discussed in a remark below in this chapter.

## Proof

[thm-pc-picard-representable] of the Picard chapter – the Picard functor
of a smooth projective curve over a separably closed field is
representable, with the full decomposition carried out there (*reference: Stacks Project, Picard Schemes of Curves, Proposition 44.6.6, [Tag 0B9Z](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B9Z)*); cf. Mumford, Abelian Varieties; Milne, Abelian Varieties, Ch. 12. We outline the
classical construction; the existence and property statements are
theorems of the sources above.

*(1) The Picard functor.* $\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}$ and
$\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\subseteq\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}$ are
as in [def-sc-picard-functor]; for $k$ algebraically closed, $C$ is a
smooth connected curve in the sense of [def-sc-pic0] by
[lem-pc-curves-are-sc], and
$\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}(k)=\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)$ of
[def-sc-pic0].

*(2) Representability.* The theorem of Grothendieck states
that $\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}$ (which is the functor of [def-pc-picard-functor] by [lem-pc-picard-functor-agrees-sc]) is represented by a group scheme
locally of finite type over $k$ ([thm-pc-picard-representable] of the Picard chapter; *reference: Stacks Project, Picard Schemes of Curves, Proposition 44.6.6, [Tag 0B9Z](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B9Z)*). The
subfunctor $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$ is represented by an open
and closed subgroup scheme ([prop-pd-picard-degree-decomposition],
parts (2) and (3)).

*(3) Smoothness and the tangent space.* By
[lem-sc-pic-tangent-space], the tangent space of
$\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}$ at the identity is
$H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$, of dimension $g$ ([def-pc-genus]);
by [thm-sc-theorem-of-the-base],
$\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}$ is a disjoint union of smooth
varieties of dimension $g$.

*(4) Properness.* $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$ is proper by
[thm-sc-theorem-of-the-base] (the ``theorem of the base'').

*(5) Abelian variety and base change.* By (2)–(4),
$J_C:=\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$ is a proper smooth connected
group scheme, i.e. an abelian variety
([def-sc-abelian-variety]), of dimension $g$. For
$k$ algebraically closed, $J_C(k)=\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)$
([def-sc-picard-functor], [def-sc-pic0]) by
representability, and base change
compatibility $J_{C_{k'}}\cong(J_C)_{k'}$ holds because the Picard
functor commutes with base change. Finally, $J_C$ is projective
by [lem-sc-abelian-variety-projective].

The hypothesis that $k$ is separably closed enters this proof exactly as in
the Picard chapter: it is what produces a $k$-rational point of $C$, from
which the representability theorem [thm-pc-picard-representable] of that
chapter deduces the fppf sheaf property of the naive Picard presheaf and hence
representability. For a curve over a general ground field the conclusion is
not asserted in this blueprint; see [rem-sc-jacobian-scope].

attrs.title: The Jacobian over a separably closed field

objects.body:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed and let $C$ be a
smooth separated connected curve over $k$. Let
$\mathbf F_r$ be the constant sheaf
([def-sc-constant-sheaves]) and consider the assertions
$\mathcal C_1,\dots,\mathcal C_8$ of
[def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions].

1. **(a)** If $r\neq\operatorname{char}k$, then
$\mathbf F_r$ satisfies $\mathcal C_1$, $\mathcal C_4$,
$\mathcal C_6$, and $\mathcal C_8$; it satisfies $\mathcal C_2$
when $C$ is affine and $\mathcal C_5,\mathcal C_7$ when $C$
is proper. Explicitly (for $r\neq\operatorname{char}k$):
$$
H^0(C,\mathbf F_r)=\mathbf Z/r\mathbf Z,\qquad
H^2(C,\mathbf F_r)=0\ \text{if}\ C\ \text{is affine},
$$
and, after choosing the trivialization by a primitive $r$-th
root of unity, there is a short exact sequence
$$
0\longrightarrow\mathcal O_C(C)^\times/\mathcal O_C(C)^\times{}^{\,r}
\longrightarrow H^1(C,\mathbf F_r)
\longrightarrow\operatorname{Pic}(C)[r]\longrightarrow0.
$$
If $C$ is proper of genus $g$,
$$
H^0(C,\mathbf F_r)=\mathbf Z/r\mathbf Z,\quad
H^1(C,\mathbf F_r)=(\mathbf Z/r\mathbf Z)^{2g},\quad
H^2(C,\mathbf F_r)=\mathbf Z/r\mathbf Z,\quad
H^q(C,\mathbf F_r)=0\ (q>2),
$$
and all these identifications are compatible with
algebraically closed field
extension (the pullback maps are isomorphisms).
1. **(b)** If $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$, the constant sheaf
$\mathbf F_p$ satisfies $\mathcal C_1$, $\mathcal C_3$, and
$\mathcal C_8$; it satisfies $\mathcal C_2$ when $C$ is affine
and $\mathcal C_5,\mathcal C_7$ when $C$ is proper.
1. **(c)** The maps in $\mathcal C_6$, $\mathcal C_7$, and
$\mathcal C_8$ are the pullback and restriction maps fixed in
[def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions] (and in
[def-sc-field-extension]).

## Proof

Assertions (a) and (b) are the conjunctions, respectively, of
[lem-sc-c1], [lem-sc-c4], [lem-sc-c6],
[lem-sc-c8], [lem-sc-c2] (affine case) and
[lem-sc-c5], [lem-sc-c7] (proper case) for
$r\neq\operatorname{char}k$, and of [lem-sc-c1],
[lem-sc-c3], [lem-sc-c8], [lem-sc-c2] (affine) and
[lem-sc-c5], [lem-sc-c7] (proper) for
$r=\operatorname{char}k=p>0$, exactly as stated in
[def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions]. The explicit
identifications are [thm-sc-proper-cohomology] and
[thm-sc-affine-cohomology], and the compatibility with field
extension is [thm-sc-constant-invariance]. Assertion (c) is by
the definitions of the maps in [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions]
(and [def-sc-field-extension]).

Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field. For every coherent
$\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1_k}$-module $\mathcal G$, with

$$
\omega_{\mathbf P^1}:=\Omega^1_{\mathbf P^1_k/k}\cong\mathcal O(-2)
$$

([def-sc-kahler-differentials],
[lem-sc-p1-monomial](iii)), there are canonical isomorphisms

$$
H^1(\mathbf P^1_k,\mathcal G)^{\vee}\;\cong\;
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1}}\bigl(\mathcal G,
\omega_{\mathbf P^1}\bigr),
$$

$$
H^0(\mathbf P^1_k,\mathcal G)^{\vee}\;\cong\;
\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathbf P^1}\bigl(\mathcal G,
\omega_{\mathbf P^1}\bigr)
$$

(with $\operatorname{Ext}$ of [def-sc-ext-sheaf]; all groups
involved are finite-dimensional, the cohomology of coherent modules
on a proper scheme over a field being finite-dimensional: *Source:
Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Proposition 30.19.1,
[Tag 02O5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02O5)*).

## Proof

*Step 1: the twisted structure sheaves.* For
$\mathcal E=\bigoplus_j\mathcal O(d_j)$ both statements are
additive in $\mathcal E$, so it suffices to check $\mathcal O(d)$,
$d\in\mathbf Z$. For $\mathcal O(d)$, the Cech computation of
[lem-sc-p1-monomial] gives the monomial duality: with the bases

$$
H^1(\mathbf P^1_k,\mathcal O(d))=\bigoplus_{j=d+1}^{-1}k\cdot[t^{j}],
\qquad
H^0(\mathbf P^1_k,\mathcal O(-2-d))=\bigoplus_{j=d+1}^{-1}k\cdot
x_0^{j-d-1}x_1^{-1-j}
$$

(for $d\leq-2$; both are zero otherwise), the pairing
$\langle[t^{j}],x_0^{j-d-1}x_1^{-1-j}\rangle=1$ is perfect (the case $n=1$, $A=k$ of [lem-pc-projective-space-serre-pairing]), because
the product class is the basis element $[t^{-1}]$ of
$H^1(\mathbf P^1_k,\mathcal O(-2))\cong k$. Hence, for $d\leq-2$,

$$
H^1(\mathbf P^1_k,\mathcal O(d))^{\vee}\cong
H^0(\mathbf P^1_k,\mathcal O(-2-d))
\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O(d),\mathcal O(-2))
\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O(d),\omega_{\mathbf P^1}),
$$

the second isomorphism being
$\mathcal H om(\mathcal O(d),\mathcal O(-2))=\mathcal O(-2-d)$
for the line bundles of [def-sc-p1-standard], which are
invertible by [lem-sc-p1-twist-exists] (the dual of
$\mathcal O(d)$ is $\mathcal O(-d)$, from the glueing of
[def-sc-p1-standard]), and both sides are zero for $d\geq-1$.
Similarly, by
$\operatorname{Ext}^i(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)=H^i(\mathcal F^{\vee}\otimes\mathcal G)$
for finite locally free $\mathcal F$
([lem-sc-ext-locally-free], the $\operatorname{Ext}$ of
[def-sc-ext-sheaf]):

$$
H^0(\mathbf P^1_k,\mathcal O(d))^{\vee}\cong
H^1(\mathbf P^1_k,\mathcal O(-2-d))\cong
\operatorname{Ext}^1(\mathcal O(d),\omega_{\mathbf P^1})
$$

for all $d$ (for $d\leq-2$ both sides are zero, for $d\geq0$
they have dimension $d+1$ by (i), (ii) of
[lem-sc-p1-monomial]). So Step 1 holds for all $\mathcal E$.

*Step 2: the devissage.* The isomorphisms of Step 1 are
natural, and both pairings defining them (the pairing of the Cech
class with the monomial, and the Yoneda pairing
$\operatorname{Ext}^1(\mathcal G,\omega)\times H^0(\mathcal G)\to \operatorname{Ext}^1(\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1},\omega) =H^1(\mathbf P^1_k,\omega)\cong k$) are natural in the sheaf and
compatible with the connecting maps of the long exact sequences
(standard homological algebra: the pairings are induced by
compositions in the derived category of $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1}$-modules). Fix a coherent $\mathcal G$ and choose a
resolution $0\to\mathcal E_2\to\mathcal E_1\to\mathcal E_0\to \mathcal G\to0$ as in [lem-sc-p1-graded-resolution]; put
$\mathcal K:=\operatorname{coker}(\mathcal E_2\to\mathcal E_1)$,
so that

$$
0\to\mathcal E_2\to\mathcal E_1\to\mathcal K\to0,\qquad
0\to\mathcal K\to\mathcal E_0\to\mathcal G\to0
$$

are exact. For a short exact sequence
$0\to\mathcal A\to\mathcal B\to\mathcal C\to0$ of coherent
modules the cohomology sequence ends with $H^2=0$
([lem-sc-p1-hi-vanishing]), so, dualizing the six-term sequence
(finite-dimensional vector spaces, all finite-dimensional as noted
in the statement),

$$
0\to H^1(\mathcal C)^{\vee}\to H^1(\mathcal B)^{\vee}\to
H^1(\mathcal A)^{\vee}\to H^0(\mathcal C)^{\vee}\to
H^0(\mathcal B)^{\vee}\to H^0(\mathcal A)^{\vee}\to0
$$

is exact; and the long exact Ext sequence, truncated (the groups
$\operatorname{Ext}^i(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$ for coherent
$\mathcal F$ on the smooth curve $\mathbf P^1_k$ vanish for
$i\geq2$: the Exts are Zariski-local in $\mathcal F$, and the
local rings $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1,x}$ are regular of dimension
one, in which every module has projective dimension at most one –
homological algebra), gives the exact sequence

$$
0\to\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal C,\omega)\to
\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal B,\omega)\to
\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal A,\omega)\to
\operatorname{Ext}^1(\mathcal C,\omega)\to
\operatorname{Ext}^1(\mathcal B,\omega)\to
\operatorname{Ext}^1(\mathcal A,\omega)\to0,
$$

$\omega:=\omega_{\mathbf P^1}$. The maps of Step 1 and the
compatibility make the vertical maps of these two exact sequences a
morphism of exact sequences. Applying [lem-sc-four-lemma]
first with $(\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal C)= (\mathcal E_2,\mathcal E_1,\mathcal K)$ and then with
$(\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal C)= (\mathcal K,\mathcal E_0,\mathcal G)$ proves the two
isomorphisms of the statement for $\mathcal K$, then for
$\mathcal G$: in both applications the columns $2,3,5,6$ are
isomorphic (Step 1 for the $\mathcal E_i$, and for the second
application the two isomorphisms just proved for $\mathcal K$).

Let $k$ be algebraically closed, let $C$ be a
smooth proper connected curve of genus $g$ over
$k$, and let $n\geq1$ be prime to $\operatorname{char}k$.
Then, under the canonical trivialization
$\theta_\zeta$ for a primitive root $\zeta$
([def-sc-mu-trivialization], existence by
[lem-sc-primitive-root]), the constant sheaf
$\mathbf F_n$ satisfies

$$
H^0(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_n)\cong\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z,\qquad
H^1(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_n)\cong(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)^{2g},\qquad
H^2(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_n)\cong\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z,
$$

and $H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_n)=0$ for $q>2$.

## Proof

Use $\theta_\zeta$ ([def-sc-mu-trivialization], with the
primitive root of [lem-sc-primitive-root]) to replace
$\mathbf F_n$ by $\mu_n$. By [lem-sc-kummer-les]
(applied to the exact Kummer sequence
[def-sc-kummer-sequence]; the unit group of the proper connected
curve is $k^\times$, $n$-divisible since $k$ is algebraically
closed, so the exact sequence of the lemma degenerates),

$$
H^1(C,\mu_n)=\operatorname{Pic}(C)[n],\quad
H^2(C,\mu_n)=\operatorname{coker}(n:\operatorname{Pic}(C)\to
\operatorname{Pic}(C)),
$$

which by [lem-sc-pic-proper-ntorsion] are
$(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)^{2g}$ and
$\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$; $H^0(C,\mu_n)=\mu_n(k)=\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$
by [lem-sc-primitive-root]. The vanishing for $q>2$ is
[lem-sc-cohomological-dimension].

attrs.title: Kummer computation on a proper curve

objects.body:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $C$ a
proper smooth connected curve over $k$ and
$\mathcal M$ a finite locally free $\mathcal O_C$-module (a
quasi-coherent module Zariski-locally isomorphic to
$\mathcal O_C^{\oplus r}$ for some $r\ge0$), with dual
$\mathcal M^{\vee}:=\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_C}(\mathcal M,\mathcal O_C)$.
Put $n:=\dim C\in\{0,1\}$ and $\omega_C:=\Omega^n_{C/k}$, where
$\Omega^1_{C/k}$ is the sheaf of Kähler differentials of $C$
over $k$ ([def-sc-kahler-differentials]) and
$\Omega^0_{C/k}=\mathcal O_C$. Then all groups
$H^q(C,\mathcal M)$ and $H^q(C,\mathcal M^{\vee}\otimes\omega_C)$
are finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces (coherent cohomology of a
proper scheme over a field is finite-dimensional: *Source:
Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Proposition 30.19.1,
[Tag 02O5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02O5)*), and
for every $q\in\mathbf Z$ there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
H^q(C,\mathcal M)^{\vee}\;\cong\;
H^{n-q}\bigl(C,\;\mathcal M^{\vee}\otimes\omega_C\bigr)
$$

(both sides vanish unless $0\le q\le n$). In particular, for
$n=1$ and an invertible $\mathcal M$ ([def-sc-invertible-module],
so $\mathcal M^{\vee}\cong\mathcal M^{-1}$ by
[lem-sc-invertible-dual]):

$$
H^1(C,\mathcal M)^{\vee}\;\cong\;
H^0\bigl(C,\;\Omega^1_{C/k}\otimes\mathcal M^{-1}\bigr),
\qquad
H^0(C,\mathcal M)^{\vee}\;\cong\;
H^1\bigl(C,\;\Omega^1_{C/k}\otimes\mathcal M^{-1}\bigr).
$$

This is Serre duality $H^q(X,\mathcal F)^{\vee}\cong H^{n-q}(X,\mathcal F^{\vee}\otimes\omega_X)$
for a smooth proper $X$ of dimension $n\le1$ over an algebraically
closed field and a finite locally free $\mathcal F$. For a coherent
$\mathcal F$ which is not locally free the right hand side must be
replaced by $\operatorname{Ext}^{n-q}(\mathcal F,\omega_X)$, as in
[thm-sc-p1-duality]: e.g. for the skyscraper
$\mathcal F=\kappa(x)$ at a closed point $x$ of a curve,
$H^0(C,\mathcal F)^{\vee}=k$ but $\mathcal F^{\vee}=0$.

## Proof

The sheaf $\Omega^1_{C/k}$ is a line bundle
([lem-sc-canonical-sheaf]), so in both cases $\omega_C$ is a line
bundle and $\mathcal M^{\vee}\otimes\omega_C$ is again finite locally
free (on an open trivializing $\mathcal M$ and $\omega_C$ it is
$\mathcal O^{\oplus r}$). All modules below are finite locally free,
hence coherent on the Noetherian scheme $C$ ([pqf-def-coherent]),
which gives the finite-dimensionality.

*Reduction to $q=n$.* For finite locally free $\mathcal M$ the
canonical maps $\mathcal M\to\mathcal M^{\vee\vee}$ and
$\omega_C^{\vee}\otimes\omega_C\to\mathcal O_C$ are isomorphisms
(check on opens where the modules are free), so
$(\mathcal M^{\vee}\otimes\omega_C)^{\vee}\otimes\omega_C\cong\mathcal M$.
Hence, once the isomorphism
$H^n(C,\mathcal N)^{\vee}\cong H^0(C,\mathcal N^{\vee}\otimes\omega_C)$
is proved for every finite locally free $\mathcal N$, applying it to
$\mathcal N:=\mathcal M^{\vee}\otimes\omega_C$ gives
$H^n(C,\mathcal M^{\vee}\otimes\omega_C)^{\vee}\cong H^0(C,\mathcal M)$,
and dualizing (finite-dimensional spaces) gives the case $q=0$,
$H^0(C,\mathcal M)^{\vee}\cong H^n(C,\mathcal M^{\vee}\otimes\omega_C)$.
For $n=0$ the cases $q=0$ and $q=n$ coincide. It remains to show
the vanishing $H^q(C,\mathcal N)=0$ for $q\notin\{0,\dots,n\}$ and
every finite locally free $\mathcal N$ (for $q<0$ this is the
convention for derived functors), and the case $q=n$.

*Case $\dim C=0$.* The finite-type scheme $C$ has
finitely many points (it is Noetherian of dimension zero), so the
morphism $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is proper with finite fibres,
hence finite by [thm-pqf-finite-iff-proper-finite-fibres]
(the quasi-finite chapter); thus $H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)$ is a
finite-dimensional
$k$-algebra, reduced because $C$ is smooth, and connected
because $C$ is connected, hence equal to $k$ (a reduced
finite-dimensional algebra over the algebraically closed field $k$
is a product of finitely many copies of $k$, and connectedness
leaves one factor). So $C=\operatorname{Spec}k$: then
$H^q(C,\mathcal N)=0$ for $q>0$ by [pqf-lem-affine-vanishing]
($\operatorname{Spec}k$ is affine, $\mathcal N$ quasi-coherent),
and a finite locally free $\mathcal N$ is the sheaf associated with
a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space $V=H^0(C,\mathcal N)$, with
$\mathcal N^{\vee}\otimes\omega_C=\mathcal N^{\vee}$ associated with
$\operatorname{Hom}_k(V,k)=V^{\vee}$; so
$H^0(C,\mathcal N)^{\vee}=V^{\vee}=H^0(C,\mathcal N^{\vee}\otimes\omega_C)$,
the case $q=n=0$. (Also $\Omega^1_{C/k}=0$: the module of
Kähler differentials of $k$ over $k$ is zero, the universal
derivation of the identity being $d=0$; this is why the sheaf
$\omega_C=\Omega^{\dim C}_{C/k}$ is $\mathcal O_C$ here.)

*Case $\dim C=1$.* The connected smooth curve $C$ is
integral: its local rings are domains ([lem-sc-smooth-regular]),
so its irreducible components are pairwise disjoint (a point
belonging to two components would have a local ring with two minimal
primes), and connectedness leaves a single component. The function
field $k(C)$
([def-sc-function-field]) has transcendence degree one over
$k$: for an integral scheme of finite type over a field,
$\dim X=\operatorname{trdeg}_k k(X)$, by Noether normalization
(*Source: Stacks Project, Commutative Algebra,
[Tag 00OY](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00OY)*; as in the
proof of [lem-sc-deg-principal-zero]). Choose
$t\in k(C)\setminus k$ (a transcendental element, since
$k\subset k(C)$ is a field extension and $k$ is algebraically
closed), and let $f:=\pi_t:C\to\mathbf P^1_k$ be the morphism of
[lem-sc-morphism-from-function]: finite, surjective and flat,
of degree $d:=[k(C):k(t)]$.

*Transfer of the cohomology.* The morphism $f$ is proper
(finite morphisms of schemes are proper,
[lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper] of the ambient-foundations chapter), and its fibres
are finite ([pqf-lem-finite-qf] and
[pqf-lem-qf-finitefibres] of the quasi-finite chapter); $\mathbf P^1_k$
is locally Noetherian (of finite type over the field $k$). Let
$\mathcal M$ be finite locally free. It is coherent (on the locally
Noetherian scheme $C$, a locally free module of finite type is
coherent: [pqf-def-coherent]), so [pqf-lem-fff-vanishing] gives
$(R^p f_*\mathcal M)_y=0$ for all $p>0$ and all
$y\in\mathbf P^1_k$, i.e. $R^pf_*\mathcal M=0$ for $p>0$
([pqf-lem-sheaf-zero-stalks]). The Leray spectral sequence
$E_2^{p,q}=H^p(\mathbf P^1_k,R^qf_*\mathcal M)\Rightarrow H^{p+q}(C,\mathcal M)$
([pqf-lem-leray]) is therefore concentrated on the row $q=0$ and
degenerates, giving $H^p(C,\mathcal M)\cong H^p(\mathbf P^1_k,f_*\mathcal M)$
for all $p$; in degree one this is the low-degree exact sequence of
[pqf-lem-leray-lowdegree]:

$$
H^1(C,\mathcal M)\cong H^1(\mathbf P^1_k,f_*\mathcal M),
\qquad
H^p(C,\mathcal M)\cong H^p(\mathbf P^1_k,f_*\mathcal M)=0\quad(p\ge2),
$$

the vanishing by [lem-sc-p1-hi-vanishing]. This is the vanishing
outside $\{0,1\}$ required in the reduction step.

Moreover $f_*\mathcal M$ is a finite locally free
$\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1_k}$-module (of rank $d$): over an affine
open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset\mathbf P^1_k$ the preimage
$f^{-1}(U)=\operatorname{Spec}B$ is affine with $B$ a finite
locally free $R$-algebra (finite flat), and
$f_*\mathcal M|_U$ is the finite locally free $R$-module
$\Gamma(f^{-1}(U),\mathcal M)$: the sections of a finite locally
free module on the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}B$ form a
finitely generated projective $B$-module, which is a finitely
generated projective $R$-module because $B$ is one (a direct summand
of $B^{\oplus m}$, and $B^{\oplus m}$ is finite projective over $R$);
if $\mathcal M$ has rank $r$, the generic rank is
$rd$, $d= \dim_{k(t)}k(C)$.

*Duality.* Since $f_*\mathcal M$ is finite locally free,
hence coherent, [thm-sc-p1-duality] gives

$$
H^1(\mathbf P^1_k,f_*\mathcal M)^{\vee}
\cong
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1}}
\bigl(f_*\mathcal M,\omega_{\mathbf P^1}\bigr),
$$

and since $f$ is finite flat, [lem-sc-finite-duality] gives

$$
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1}}
\bigl(f_*\mathcal M,\omega_{\mathbf P^1}\bigr)
\cong
H^0\bigl(C,\omega_C\otimes\mathcal M^{\vee}\bigr).
$$

Composing (the three isomorphisms are compatible with the
identification $\omega_C=\Omega^1_{C/k}$):

$$
H^1(C,\mathcal M)^{\vee}
\cong H^1(\mathbf P^1_k,f_*\mathcal M)^{\vee}
\cong \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1}}
\bigl(f_*\mathcal M,\omega_{\mathbf P^1}\bigr)
\cong H^0\bigl(C,\mathcal M^{\vee}\otimes\Omega^1_{C/k}\bigr),
$$

which is the case $q=n=1$; by the reduction step this proves the
theorem. For invertible $\mathcal M$, [lem-sc-invertible-dual]
identifies $\mathcal M^{\vee}$ with $\mathcal M^{-1}$, which gives
the two displayed particular cases.

attrs.title: Serre duality for smooth proper curves

objects.body:
Let $A$ be an abelian variety
over a field $k$, and let $\mathcal L$ be an
invertible $\mathcal O_A$-module. For $1\leq i_1<\cdots<i_t\leq3$ let
$m_{i_1,\dots,i_t}:A\times_kA\times_kA\to A$ be the partial sum
map $(x_1,x_2,x_3)\mapsto x_{i_1}+\cdots+x_{i_t}$. Then

$$
m_{123}^*\mathcal L\otimes m_1^*\mathcal L\otimes m_2^*\mathcal L
\otimes m_3^*\mathcal L
\cong m_{12}^*\mathcal L\otimes m_{13}^*\mathcal L\otimes
m_{23}^*\mathcal L
$$

on $A\times_kA\times_kA$.

## Proof

*Reference: Stacks Project, Groupoid Schemes, Lemma 39.9.6,
[Tag 0BFE](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BFE).* Apply
the general theorem of the cube (More on Morphisms, Theorem
37.33.8, [Tag 0BF4](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BF4)) to the difference

$$
\mathcal M=m_{123}^*\mathcal L\otimes m_1^*\mathcal L\otimes
m_2^*\mathcal L\otimes m_3^*\mathcal L\otimes
m_{12}^*\mathcal L^{-1}\otimes m_{13}^*\mathcal L^{-1}\otimes
m_{23}^*\mathcal L^{-1}
$$

with $X=Y=Z=A$ over $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and the unit
sections $x=y=e$. The hypotheses of [Tag 0BF4](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BF4) hold:
$A\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is flat, proper and of finite
presentation with geometrically integral fibres ($A$ is smooth,
proper and connected, hence geometrically integral by [lem-sc-abelian-variety-characterization] and Groupoid
Schemes, Remark 39.9.12,
[Tag 0H2U](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H2U)), and
$A$ is connected, so it has a $k$-point (the unit). On
$A\times A\times e$ the restriction of $\mathcal M$ is

$$
n_{12}^*\mathcal L\otimes n_1^*\mathcal L\otimes n_2^*\mathcal
L\otimes e^*\mathcal L\otimes n_{12}^*\mathcal L^{-1}\otimes
n_1^*\mathcal L^{-1}\otimes n_2^*\mathcal L^{-1}\cong\mathcal O,
$$

where $n_{i_1,\dots,i_t}(x_1,x_2)=x_{i_1}+\cdots+x_{i_t}$ and
$e^*\mathcal L\cong\mathcal O$ (an invertible module on the
point); the same computation on $A\times e\times A$ and
$e\times A\times A$ shows $\mathcal M$ trivial on the slices
required by [Tag 0BF4](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BF4), and $\mathcal M$ is trivial on the fibre
$A\times A\times e$. Hence $\mathcal M\cong\mathcal O$, which
is the displayed relation.

Let $k$ be a separably closed field and let $C$ be a
smooth projective curve over $k$
which is geometrically integral,
of genus $g=g(C)=\dim_kH^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$ ([def-pc-genus]). Then the
Picard functor $\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}$ of
[def-sc-picard-functor] is a disjoint union over $d\in\mathbf Z$ of smooth proper $g$-dimensional $k$-varieties
$\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}$, whose $k$-points are the
degree-$d$ invertible modules, and
$\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$ is an open and closed subgroup
scheme; in particular $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$ is a proper
smooth group scheme of dimension $g$.

## Proof

*Reference: Stacks Project, Picard Schemes of Curves, Lemma
44.6.7, [Tag 0BA0](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BA0).* The argument of loc. cit. is the following. By Derived
Categories of Schemes, Lemma 36.32.2,
[Tag 0B9T](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B9T), the
Picard functor decomposes as a disjoint union over $d\in\mathbf Z$ of open and closed subfunctors $\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}$,
classified by the fibrewise Euler characteristic
$\chi(X_t,\mathcal L_t)=d+1-g$. Smoothness and dimension: the
Hilbert scheme $\underline{\mathrm{Hilb}}^g_{C/k}$ is smooth of
dimension $g$ (Proposition 44.3.6,
[Tag 0B9I](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B9I)); the
morphism $\gamma_g:\underline{\mathrm{Hilb}}^g\to \operatorname{Pic}^g$, $D\mapsto\mathcal O_C(D)$, is an open
immersion on a nonempty open (as the proof of representability of
[thm-pc-picard-representable] shows), and the translates of this open by $k$-points of the
group scheme form an open covering, so
$\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}$ is smooth of dimension $g$.
Properness: for $d\geq g$ the map
$\gamma_d:\underline{\mathrm{Hilb}}^d_{C/k}\to\operatorname{Pic}^d$,
$D\mapsto\mathcal O_C(D)$, given by the universal divisor (Remark
44.3.7, [Tag 0B9J](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B9J)), is surjective: for $\mathcal L\in\operatorname{Pic}^d(K)$
one has $\chi(C_K,\mathcal L)=d+1-g>0$ ([lem-sc-riemann-roch]), so
$\mathcal L$ has a nonzero global section, which yields
$\mathcal L\cong\mathcal O_C(D)$ for an effective divisor $D$
of degree $d$. The Hilbert scheme is proper over $k$ (it is
projective), and the image of a proper scheme in a separated target
is proper (Morphisms of Schemes, Lemma 29.42.10,
[Tag 0AH6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AH6)), so
$\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}$ is proper for $d\geq g$; every
other component is isomorphic to one of these by a translation under
the group law ([prop-pd-picard-degree-decomposition](4): translation by
$\mathcal O_C(eP)$ maps $\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}$ isomorphically onto
$\operatorname{Pic}^{d+e}_{C/k}$), hence proper. Therefore the open and closed subgroup scheme
$\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$ is proper and smooth of dimension
$g$.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type over $\Fbar$, with a
compactification of dimension at most $d$, and let $A=A_{E,n}$.
Then the following statements hold:

1. The class-restricted dimension datum
[def-sf-fullcd-class] holds with bound $2d$.
1. Let $f^\times$ be the right adjoint of the étale
compact-support functor. On bounded-below pro-étale coefficients put
$$
Rf_n^\times L=\nu_X^* f^\times R\nu_{Y,*}L.
$$
For every bounded-below $K$ of étale origin and every bounded-below
$L$, there is a natural bijection
$$
\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_{!,n}K,L)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}(K,Rf_n^\times L).
$$
Thus this formula is the right adjoint relative to the bounded-below
comparison class. It applies in particular to the bounded constructible
inputs used here.
1. Compactification comparisons of these functors are canonical and
satisfy the cocycle condition.

No adjunction on arbitrary unbounded pro-étale objects is asserted.

## Proof

Clause (1) is [thm-sf-fullcd-class]. Write $K=\nu_X^*G$ with
$G$ bounded below. The finite cohomological dimension of compact
support implies that its right adjoint $f^\times$ takes bounded-below
objects to bounded-below objects: a bound
$Rf_!D^{\leq0}\subseteq D^{\leq N}$ gives
$f^\times D^{\geq0}\subseteq D^{\geq-N}$ by adjunction and
orthogonality. Hence all étale objects in the following comparison
are in the domain of the fully faithful functor of
[thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]. Using
[lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] and the adjoint of
[thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] gives

$$
\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_{!,n}\nu_X^*G,L)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_!^{\Et}G,R\nu_{Y,*}L)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}(G,f^\times R\nu_{Y,*}L)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\nu_X^*G,\nu_X^*f^\times R\nu_{Y,*}L).
$$

The last step is full faithfulness, not an adjunction with a second
$R\nu_{X,*}$; the latter would have the wrong source category.
The bijection is natural and independent of the witness. The coherent
compactification comparisons follow by applying the fixed functors
$\nu_X^*$ and $R\nu_{Y,*}$ to the étale comparisons of
[lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] and using uniqueness of the
étale right adjoints. This proves (2) and (3).

attrs.title: The exceptional adjoint on the bounded comparison class

objects.body:
Let $X$ be separated of finite type over $\Fbar$, and let
$\Lambda=A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E$, or $\Qlb$.
Use the constructible coefficient categories of the blueprint and put
$\omega_{X,\Lambda}=Ra_X^!\Lambda$,
$D_{X,\Lambda}=R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(-,\omega_{X,\Lambda})$.
Then $D_{X,\Lambda}$ is an exact contravariant anti-equivalence
of $D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$, and the evaluation-defined map

$$
K\longrightarrow D_{X,\Lambda}D_{X,\Lambda}K
$$

is a natural isomorphism. At the integral and field stages this is
the whole specified category $D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$.

At finite coefficients, an input Tor interval $[a,b]$ gives
$[-b-2\dim X,-a]$ for its dual. At integral coefficients the
same assertion holds for the uniform Tor intervals of the finite
reductions. In particular the finite or integral dualizing object
has interval $[-2\dim X,0]$. Field objects may be computed from
any integral representative and then localized.

## Proof

The finite-stage anti-equivalence is [thm-fix-general-biduality],
with its independent bound from
[lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata]. The normalized-tower
argument and the integral evaluation comparison give
[thm-coef-integral-verdier], including the same reduction bounds.
Its domain is the whole integral constructible category by
[lem-coef-integral-residue-tor].
The exact scalar localization and the common finite coefficient
stage give respectively [thm-coef-rational-verdier] and
[thm-coef-qbar-verdier]. Those proofs transport the evaluation
map itself, so the resulting isomorphism is the stated double-dual
map at every coefficient stage.

attrs.title: Verdier biduality on the coefficient class

objects.body:
Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to S$ be separated of finite type between finite-type
$k$-schemes. There is a canonical isomorphism

$$
\alpha_{g,f}:\ Rg_!Rf_!\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ R(g\circ f)_!
$$

of functors $D^+(X,\Lambda)\to D^+(S,\Lambda)$ on étale-origin complexes,
where $Rf_!$ is the compact-support direct image of
[def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed],
independent of all compactification choices by [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed],
equal to the identity when $f$ or $g$ is an identity, and associative:
for a third $h:S\to T$ the two composites
$Rh_!Rg_!Rf_!\to R(hgf)_!$ agree.

## Proof

*Construction.* Compactify $g$ as $Y\xrightarrow{v}\overline Y \xrightarrow{\bar g}S$, and compactify $v\circ f$ as
$X\xrightarrow{a}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}\overline Y$, using
Nagata's theorem [thm-nagata-compactification]. Put $V=\overline X\times_{\overline Y}Y$,
with its open immersion $b:V\to\overline X$ and proper projection
$p_Y:V\to Y$. Since $p\circ a=v\circ f$, the morphism $a$ factors as
$a=b\circ c$ through an open immersion $c:X\to V$, so
$X\xrightarrow{c}V\xrightarrow{p_Y}Y$ is a compactification of $f$ and
$Rf_!=Rp_{Y*}c_!$ on that model. For every
étale-origin $N$ on $V$ the map

$$
v_!Rp_{Y*}N\ \longrightarrow\ Rp_*b_!N
$$

is an isomorphism: over $Y$ it is proper base change for the Cartesian square
defining $V$ ([thm-weil-pbc-finite-level-proetale]), and at a geometric point of
$\overline Y$ outside $Y$ both sides vanish, because the corresponding fibre of
$p$ misses $V$ ([cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-finite]). Apply this to the extension by zero of a complex on $X$ and
then push by $R\bar g_*$: extension by zero along opens composes termwise and
proper derived direct image composes
([lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition]), giving $\alpha_{g,f}$.

*Independence and associativity.* Any two choices are compared by
[prop-compactification-coherence-detailed], which also makes $\alpha_{g,f}$ natural. For
three morphisms choose, by
[def-weil-compactifications-refinements], [prop-compactification-refinement] (i), a single common refinement of all
the compactifications involved; the two composites then restrict to the same
identity over the source and use the same proper base-change maps on each
Cartesian rectangle, so their pasting identity together with the refinement
transitivity of [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed] gives associativity.

Uses: [cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-finite], [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition], [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed], [prop-compactification-refinement], [thm-nagata-compactification], [thm-weil-pbc-finite-level-proetale]

Fix the finite-field datum,
$A=A_{E,n}$, and separated finite-type morphisms between separated finite-type
$k$-schemes. Use the bounded
constructible categories and their
finite-Tor subcategories.
At this finite coefficient stage the following hold:

1. **(i)** $Lf^*$ carries $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ into
$D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$.
1. **(ii)** Derived tensor carries
$D^b_{ctf}\times D^b_{ctf}$ into $D^b_{ctf}$; if the two inputs have
Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ and $[c,d]$, the output has Tor amplitude in
$[a+c,b+d]$.
For $K,L\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, internal Hom has this same conclusion.
If $K,L$ have Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ and $[c,d]$ and
$\dim X\leq m$, then $R\mathcal Hom(K,L)$ has Tor amplitude in
$[c-b-2m,d-a+2m]$; if moreover $K$ is site-perfect, it has Tor
amplitude in the sharper interval $[c-b,d-a]$.
The elementary formula $R\mathcal Hom(K,L)=K^\vee\otimes^L L$
with coefficient dual $K^\vee=R\mathcal Hom(K,A_X)$, and the
dimension-free interval $[c-b,d-a]$, still require
a site-perfect first argument (for the origin
$i:\{0\}\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1$, both $i_*A$ and $A$ have Tor
amplitude $[0,0]$, while $R\mathcal Hom(i_*A,A)=i_*A(-1)[-2]$ has
cohomology in degree $2$);
the general preservation assertion uses geometric Verdier duality.
1. **(iii)** $Rf_*$ carries $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ into
$D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$; for input Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ and
$\dim X\leq d$, the output has Tor amplitude in $[a,b+2d]$.
1. **(iv)** $Rf_!$ carries $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ into
$D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$.
1. **(v)** The exceptional adjoint on the constructible
coefficient category satisfies $Rf^!=D_Xf^*D_Y$ and carries
$D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ into $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$.
For input Tor interval $[a,b]$, one output interval is
$[a-2\dim X,b+2\dim Y]$.
1. **(vi)** For every separated finite-type $X/k$,
$D_X=R\mathcal Hom_X(-,Ra_X^!A)$ is a contravariant exact
anti-equivalence with $K\simeq D_XD_XK$, by the geometric
Verdier-biduality theorem on this domain.
1. **(vii)** On the finite-Tor constructible domains,
finite coefficient quotients commute with pullback, tensor, both
direct images, general internal Hom, Verdier duality and the
exceptional adjoint, preserving their evaluation and adjunction maps.
For derived-complete
integral objects, $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)=D^b_{ctf}(X,\mathcal O_E)$.
General internal Hom and the exceptional adjoint preserve this
category; Verdier duality is an anti-equivalence on it, with the
canonical finite reductions of these operations. These conclusions
pass to the bounded constructible categories at $E$ and
$\Qlb$, with their specified coefficient-passage operations.
The elementary site-perfect formula in (ii) retains its stated
hypothesis. No unrestricted unbounded pro-etale exceptional
adjunction is asserted here.

## Proof

For (i), bounded constructibility is
[lem-weil-pbc-pullback-preserves-bounded-constructible], and
flat inverse image in [lem-exc-constant-inverse-image-flat]
preserves the Tor interval of
[def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].
For (ii), the Tor intervals add under derived tensor: with bounded
flat models of $K$ in $[a,b]$ and of $L$ in $[c,d]$, the total tensor
complex is a bounded flat model in $[a+c,b+d]$. Refine the
finite constructible stratifications for the two complexes; the
bounded tensor complexes on each stratum have finite locally constant
cohomology, which gives constructibility. If $K$ is site-perfect
in [def-weil-site-perfect-complex], a bounded finite-projective
local model $P$ in $[a,b]$ computes its dual and identifies
$R\mathcal Hom(K,L)=K^\vee\otimes^L L$ by
[prop-sf-dualizable-hom]. The tensor argument proves Hom
preservation in that case, and since $P^\vee$ is a bounded
finite-projective complex in $[-b,-a]$, the tensor bound gives the
interval $[c-b,d-a]$; this is the sharper assertion of
[thm-sf-hom-ctf], whose argument is local on the site and so applies
on either site; on the pro-étale site this is [cor-sf-hom-ctf-proetale-unconditional]. For a general constructible finite-Tor
first argument, use [cor-weil-finite-constructible-hom], whose
proof uses geometric Verdier biduality and gives the
dimension-dependent interval $[c-b-2m,d-a+2m]$. The displayed
example shows the dimension-free interval fails without
site-perfectness: $R\mathcal Hom(i_*A,A)=i_*Ri^!A$ by adjunction, and
$Ri^!A=A(-1)[-2]$ by purity for the point in the smooth curve.

Clause (iii) is [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale]: its etale
calculation is [thm-sf-direct-image-tor-amplitude], with the
uniform all-sheaf cohomological bound supplied by
[lem-sf-etale-direct-image-vanishing]. That calculation uses a
bounded-above free resolution of a finite constant coefficient and
the cohomological bound; it does not use a projection formula for an
arbitrary sheaf on the target. For (iv), choose a compactification
$f=pj$ and use [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed].
Extension by zero $j_!$ is exact and commutes with tensor, as is
seen on stalks, so preserves the Tor interval and constructibility.
Apply (iii) to the proper factor $p$.

Clause (v) is the preservation result for the exceptional inverse
image, assembled from the closed and smooth cases. For a closed immersion
$i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ with $\dim T\leq d$, the open complement satisfies
the open-complement condition with $c=2d$ by
[thm-pur-open-complement-unconditional], so [prop-exc-closed-tor]
carries bounded constructible input of Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ to bounded
constructible output of Tor amplitude $[a,b+2d+1]$. For $f$ smooth of pure
relative dimension $d$, purity identifies $Rf^!$ with $Lf^*(-)(d)[2d]$ and
[cor-pur-smooth-admissibility] gives the shift $-2d$ on both intervals.
A general $f$ is, on affine charts $U\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$, a closed
immersion $U\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^{d_U}_V$ followed by the smooth
projection, and composing the two cases along the charts is
[thm-pur-general-admissibility]; its open-complement hypothesis on the
charts is discharged by [cor-pur-general-admissibility-datum], so it is a
theorem and not an assumption. At the finite stage $A=A_{E,n}$ and for every
separated finite-type $f$ of the statement this is
[thm-sf-preservation-class](2): $Rf^!$ carries $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ into
$D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, with no ambient datum assumed on that category. With this
preservation, the finite dual formula and adjunction of
[lem-coef-finite-exceptional] identify $Rf^!$ with $D_Xf^*D_Y$ on this
domain; applying the finite duality bound on $Y$, ordinary pullback, and
the finite duality bound on $X$ gives the displayed output interval. Clause (vi) is
[thm-fix-general-biduality] at finite coefficients;
its geometric proof supplies the
anti-equivalence and is not replaced by the site-perfect calculation
in (ii).

For (vii), use [lem-fix-operation-reduction] for pullback,
tensor and compact supports, and [lem-coef-finite-direct-image]
for ordinary direct image. General finite internal-Hom and duality
comparisons are [thm-coef-finite-hom], [cor-coef-finite-verdier];
the exceptional comparison is [lem-coef-finite-exceptional].
Their proofs compare the specified evaluations and adjunction maps.

At integral coefficients, [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor]
identifies the two constructible categories. General internal Hom
and its finite reductions are
[cor-coef-integral-internal-hom], [lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction].
The anti-equivalence and exceptional adjunction are
[thm-coef-integral-verdier], [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint].
These proofs establish normalized-tower effectivity and the finite
reductions with uniform bounds; they do not infer a common integral
local model merely from levelwise constructibility.
Finally [thm-coef-rational-verdier], [lem-coef-rational-operations]
identify the operations after rationalization, and
[thm-coef-qbar-verdier] transports them to the common-stage
category, including its retracts. Their adjunctions have precisely
the bounded constructible domains stated in those results.

attrs.title: Preservation on the proved finite-Tor domains

objects.body:
Fix an algebraically closed field $k$, a prime
$\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, $n\geq1$,
$A=A_{E,n}$, finite-type
$k$-schemes $X,Y$ and a separated finite-type morphism $f:X\to Y$.
Assume $\operatorname{UDV}(f,A;N)$ for an integer $N\geq0$, in the sense
of [def-sf-uniform-direct-image-vanishing]. Let $K$ be a bounded
constructible complex of $A$-modules on the small étale site $X_{\Et}$
with finite Tor amplitude in
$[a,b]$, the finite-Tor condition being the one of the étale clause of
[lem-sf-flat-model]. Then $Rf_*K$ is bounded constructible on
$Y_{\Et}$ and has finite Tor amplitude in $[a,b+N]$.

## Proof

Let $P$ be the bounded flat model of $K$ given by the étale clause of
[lem-sf-flat-model]: $P\cong K$ is a bounded complex of flat
$A_X$-module sheaves with $P^q=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$. Its terms
vanish outside $[a,b]$, so $\mathcal H^q(K)=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$.
Put $\kappa=A/(\varpi_E)$, the residue field of the local ring $A$. The
constant sheaf $\kappa_X$ is a sheaf of $A$-modules placed in degree
zero, so the definition of finite Tor amplitude gives

$$
\mathcal H^q\bigl(K\otimes^L_A\kappa_X\bigr)=0\qquad(q\notin[a,b]).
$$

Apply the truncation spectral sequence of [thm-sp-truncation-e2] to
the left exact direct image functor and to the complex
$K\otimes^L_A\kappa_X$:

$$
E_2^{p,q}=R^pf_*\bigl(\mathcal H^q(K\otimes^L_A\kappa_X)\bigr)
\ \Longrightarrow\ \mathcal H^{p+q}\bigl(Rf_*(K\otimes^L_A\kappa_X)\bigr).
$$

Only $q\in[a,b]$ occurs, and only $p\leq N$ occurs by
$\operatorname{UDV}(f,A;N)$; hence
$\mathcal H^n(Rf_*(K\otimes^L_A\kappa_X))=0$ for $n\notin[a,b+N]$.

The coefficient ring $A$ is finite and annihilated by the integer
$\ell^n$, which is invertible in $k$ by the stated characteristic
assumption; so
[thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility] makes $Rf_*K$ a bounded
constructible complex on $Y_{\Et}$, with constructible cohomology
sheaves.

The module $\kappa$ is finitely presented over the Noetherian ring $A$,
so the projection formula of [lem-sf-projection-finite-constant]
identifies

$$
(Rf_*K)\otimes^L_A\kappa_Y\cong Rf_*\bigl(K\otimes^L_A\kappa_X\bigr),
$$

and by the spectral-sequence computation this complex has cohomology only
in $[a,b+N]$. The residue test [lem-exc-residue-tor-test] applies to
the bounded complex $Rf_*K$, whose cohomology sheaves are constructible,
and to the residue field $\kappa=A/(\varpi_E)$; it converts the
concentration just proved into finite Tor amplitude of $Rf_*K$ in
$[a,b+N]$, which is the assertion.

attrs.title: Direct image and finite Tor amplitude

objects.body:
In the setting of [def-sf-datum], let

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X' & \xrightarrow{g'} & X\\
f'\downarrow && \downarrow f\\
Y' & \xrightarrow{g} & Y
\end{array}
$$

be a Cartesian square of separated finite-type $S$-schemes. Then there is a
canonical isomorphism, natural in the square and compatible with the pasting
of squares,

$$
Rf^!Rg_*\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rg'_*Rf'^!,
$$

the right adjoint of the base-change isomorphism
$\operatorname{Ex}_!:Lg^*Rf_!\cong Rf'_!Lg'^*$. If $g$ is proper, so that
$g'$ is proper as well and $Rg_!=Rg_*$, $Rg'_!=Rg'_*$ by [fix-prop-adjunctions],
the same isomorphism reads

$$
Rf^!Rg_!\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rg'_!Rf'^!.
$$

## Proof

The map $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ is the canonical exchange of
[def-exchange-projection]; that it is an isomorphism is axiom (A2), and
in the concrete setting it is the assertion of the compact-support
base-change theorem of the compact-support chapter
([thm-cbc-qbar], with the finite-coefficient, pro-étale and finite-extension forms [thm-cbc-finite-torsion], [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale], [thm-cbc-complete-proetale], [thm-cbc-finite-extension]) at the coefficient stage
$\Lambda$, with the proper case and the finite-type case supplied by the
proper-base-change theorems of the proper-base-change chapter
([lemma-weil-pbc-prime-proper-base-change], [thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below], [thm-weil-pbc-finite-level-proetale], [thm-weil-pbc-complete-proetale], [thm-weil-pbc-qbar]) and the smooth case by the
smooth-base-change theorems of the smooth-base-change chapter
([sbc-thm-smooth-base-change]). The right adjoint of the composite
$Lg^*Rf_!$ is the composite of the right adjoints in the reverse order,
$Rf^!Rg_*$, and the right adjoint of $Rf'_!Lg'^*$ is $Rg'_*Rf'^!$: both
adjunctions are the ones of [def-sf-datum](A1), and they are the
adjunctions proved in [fix-prop-adjunctions]. An isomorphism of
functors induces an isomorphism between their right adjoints by the
uniqueness of adjoints, and the induced map is the mate of
$\operatorname{Ex}_!$ along the two pasted adjunctions, hence natural and
compatible with pasting by [lem-sf-mate]. The second assertion
substitutes the properness identification $Rg_!=Rg_*$ of
[fix-prop-adjunctions], which is stable under base change because
properness is ([lemma-weil-pbc-prime-proper-base-change] for the square).

In the Poincare duality conventions of [def-pod-conventions] (an
instance of the setting of [def-sf-datum], with $X$ smooth,
separated of finite type and of pure dimension $d$), let
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ be perfect over $\Lambda_X$, at any
coefficient stage $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$.
The smooth dualizing-complex identification
$\eta_X:\omega_{X,\Lambda}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Lambda_X(d)[2d]$ of the
purity chapter (the orientation of [def-sf-orientation] for $f=a_X$)
and the twist interchange give a canonical isomorphism

$$
\mathbb D_XK\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }K^\vee(d)[2d],
$$

natural in $K$, compatible with finite reduction, scalar extension,
shifts, and the canonical evaluation. Moreover $K^\vee$ is perfect, the
canonical map $K\to K^{\vee\vee}$ is an isomorphism, and consequently
$\mathbb D_X$ restricts to an anti-equivalence on the perfect objects,
the biduality $K\to\mathbb D_X\mathbb D_XK$ being, under this
identification, the coefficient-dual biduality $K\to K^{\vee\vee}$.

*Relative form.* The same holds for a smooth separated finite-type
$f:X\to Y$ of pure relative dimension $d$ over an arbitrary base $Y$ of the
setting: with the orientation $\gamma_f:\Lambda_X(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}
Rf^!\Lambda_Y$ of [def-sf-orientation] and
$\mathbb D_{X/Y}K=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,Rf^!\Lambda_Y)$, the composite of
$R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\gamma_f^{-1})$ with the twist interchange is a natural
isomorphism $\mathbb D_{X/Y}K\xrightarrow{\sim}K^\vee(d)[2d]$ for perfect
$K$, with the same biduality statement; the absolute case is $f=a_X$. The
proof below uses nothing about the base beyond the orientation.

## Proof

Step 1: the definition. By [def-pod-conventions],
$\mathbb D_XK=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\omega_{X,\Lambda})$ with
$\omega_{X,\Lambda}=Ra_X^!\Lambda$, and
$K^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\Lambda_X)$.

Step 2: the smooth purity input. The smooth dualizing-complex
identification of [cor-pur-finite-stage-smooth-dualizing-complex]
(at the finite stage $A=A_{E,n}$) and its transport
[cor-pur-adic-and-rational-smooth-dualizing-complexes] (at the
$\mathcal O_E$-, $E$- and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-stages) provide the
canonical orientation

$$
\eta_X:\omega_{X,\Lambda}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Lambda_X(d)[2d],
$$

which is the case $f=a_X$ of an orientation datum as in
[def-sf-orientation], compatible with finite reduction, scalar
extension, and shifts.

Step 3: substitution and interchange. Substituting $\eta_X$ into the
internal Hom and using the shift of the second variable,

$$
\mathbb D_XK\cong R\mathcal Hom_X\bigl(K,\Lambda_X(d)[2d]\bigr)
\cong\bigl(R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\Lambda_X(d))\bigr)[2d]
\cong K^\vee(d)[2d],
$$

the second isomorphism being the shift axiom of the derived internal Hom
of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the third being
[lem-sf-twist-interchange] with $m=d$ (its hypothesis is the
perfectness of $K$ over $\Lambda_X$).

Step 4: canonicality and compatibilities. The composite is canonical
because its ingredients are: the orientation is the canonical one of the
purity chapter, and the twist interchange and the shift identification
are canonical maps of the tensor–internal-Hom adjunction (natural in
$K$; on the generators $K=\Lambda_X^r$ they are the coordinate
isomorphisms; the shift index is the constant $2d$). Naturality in $K$
and compatibility with finite reduction, scalar extension and shifts
follow from the corresponding properties of $\eta_X$ recorded in
[cor-pur-finite-stage-smooth-dualizing-complex] and
[cor-pur-adic-and-rational-smooth-dualizing-complexes], and of the
derived tensor and internal Hom recorded in
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. The compatibility with the
canonical evaluation is the compatibility of the twist interchange with
the tensor–internal-Hom adjunction of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]: the evaluation is the counit,
and the interchange carries the counit for $K\otimes^L\Lambda_X(d)$ to
the counit for $K$ tensored with the identity of $\Lambda_X(d)$, after
unwinding $K^\vee(d)\otimes\Lambda_X(d)$ through the associativity and
commutativity coherence of the derived tensor product.

Step 5: biduality and the anti-equivalence. By [prop-sf-dualizable],
$K^\vee$ is perfect and the evaluation $K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}K^\vee\to\Lambda_X$
is defined. Choose locally a bounded complex $P^\bullet$ of finite
projective $\Lambda_X$-modules with a quasi-isomorphism $P^\bullet\to K$.
By [prop-sf-dualizable-hom] (with $M=\Lambda_X$) the dual $K^\vee$ is
represented by $P^{\bullet\vee}$, again bounded with finite projective
terms, and applying this once more $K^{\vee\vee}$ is represented by
$P^{\bullet\vee\vee}$; the canonical map $K\to K^{\vee\vee}$ is then
termwise the double-dual map $P^j\to P^{j\vee\vee}$, an isomorphism by
[lem-sf-hom-finite-projective], compatible with the differentials,
so $K\to K^{\vee\vee}$ is an isomorphism (the statement being local on
the site). Applying Step 3 twice,
$\mathbb D_X\mathbb D_XK\cong\bigl(K^\vee(d)[2d]\bigr)^\vee(d)[2d]\cong K^{\vee\vee}$,
where $\bigl(K^\vee(d)[2d]\bigr)^\vee\cong R\mathcal Hom_X(K^\vee,\Lambda_X(-d)[-2d])\cong K^{\vee\vee}(-d)[-2d]$
by the tensor–internal-Hom adjunction of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] (moving the invertible twist
$\Lambda_X(d)$ of the first variable to $\Lambda_X(-d)$ in the second)
and [lem-sf-twist-interchange] with $m=-d$ applied to the perfect
complex $K^\vee$; and
under this identification the biduality map is $K\to K^{\vee\vee}$.
Hence $K\mapsto\mathbb D_XK\cong K^\vee(d)[2d]$ preserves perfect
objects and is its own quasi-inverse on them, i.e. an anti-equivalence of
the perfect objects.

attrs.title: The dual of a perfect complex

objects.body:
In the setting of [thm-sf-fullcd-used-class] — $k=\Fbar$,
finite-type $k$-schemes $Y$ and $\overline X$ with
$\dim\overline X\leq d$, and a
proper finite-type morphism
$p:\overline X\to Y$ — the class-restricted datum of
[def-sf-fullcd-class] holds for $p$ with the bound $2d$:

$$
\operatorname{FullCD}_{\mathrm{cls}}(p,A;2d).
$$

The bound is $2\dim\overline X\leq2d$ and it is uniform over all base
changes $V\to Y$ of $Y_{\Proet}$; the comparison bound on the class is
moreover the sharp $M=0$ of [prop-sf-comparison-bound-zero], so that
the residual $2\dim\overline X$ is the étale direction of the Leray
spectral sequence of [thm-sp-grothendieck] and not a lower bound on
$R^q\nu_{\overline X,*}$.

## Proof

The two clauses of [def-sf-fullcd-class] are the two clauses of
[def-weil-full-cohomological-dimension] read on the blueprint's
coefficient class, and [thm-sf-fullcd-used-class] is exactly their
assertion with the coefficient sheaves of that class. Indeed the class
quantified over in that theorem is
[def-sf-fullcd-used-class], which is by its definition the class of
étale origin on the finite-type source $\overline X$, the same class that
[def-sf-fullcd-class] quantifies over; the identification of that class
with the constructible one, used only for reading the statement, is
[lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]. The absolute clause is
therefore the first clause of [thm-sf-fullcd-used-class], whose bound
$2\dim\overline X$ is the one of [thm-sf-fullcd-etale-origin]. The
relative clause is the second clause of [thm-sf-fullcd-used-class],
which asserts the vanishing of the base-changed direct images for every base
change $V\to Y$ and every coefficient sheaf of the class; the restriction
of such a sheaf to the base-changed source is again a coefficient sheaf of
the class there, by [lem-sf-fullcd-class-restriction], so the two
statements quantify over the same base-changed coefficients, and the second
clause of [def-sf-fullcd-class] is exactly that relative clause. The
last sentence of the statement is [prop-sf-comparison-bound-zero], the
residual $2\dim\overline X$ being the étale direction of the Leray
spectral sequence of [thm-sp-grothendieck]; the comparison morphism
that appears there is the one of
[def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism].

attrs.title: The blueprint's coefficient class supplies the restricted datum, with $c=2\dim\overline X$

objects.body:
Fix the global finite-field datum, a prime $\ell\ne p$, an integer
$n\geq1$, $A=A_{E,n}$, the algebraically closed field
$k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, finite-type $k$-schemes $Y$ and
$\overline X$ with $\dim\overline X\leq d$, and a
proper finite-type morphism
$p:\overline X\to Y$. Let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of $A$-modules on
$\overline X_{\Proet}$ that is of étale origin:
$\mathcal F\cong\nu_{\overline X}^*\mathcal G$ for a sheaf
$\mathcal G$ of $A$-modules on $\overline X_{\Et}$. Then the vanishing
required by [def-weil-full-cohomological-dimension] holds for
$\mathcal F$ with the bound $2d$: for every $r>2d$ one has
$\mathcal H^r(Rp_*\mathcal F)=0$, and the same holds for every base change
$V\to Y$ whose source has dimension at most $d$, in particular for
every base change by an étale $Y$-scheme.

## Proof

The morphism $p$ is proper and of finite type, in particular quasi-compact
and quasi-separated, and $\mathcal G$ lies in
$D^+(\overline X_{\Et},A)$, so the comparison direct image of
[prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] gives

$$
Rp_*\nu_{\overline X}^*\mathcal G\cong\nu_Y^*Rp_{\Et,*}\mathcal G .
$$

By [lem-sf-etale-direct-image-vanishing] the higher direct images of
$p$ on the étale sites vanish above $2d$ for *every* sheaf of
$A$-modules, because $k$ is algebraically closed and
$\dim\overline X\leq d$; that lemma needs no separatedness and no
properness. Hence $\mathcal H^r(Rp_*\mathcal F)=0$ for $r>2d$, which is
the absolute clause of [def-weil-full-cohomological-dimension].
For a base change $V\to Y$ whose source has dimension at most $d$, the
object $V$ of $Y_{\Proet}$ is a weakly étale $Y$-scheme, hence a
scheme, and $p_V:\overline X\times_YV\to V$ is again proper of finite type;
moreover the restriction of $\mathcal F$ to $\overline X\times_YV$ is
the pullback of the étale sheaf
$\mathcal G|_{\overline X\times_YV}$ along the comparison morphism of
$\overline X\times_YV$, by the compatibility of the comparison pullback
with scheme pullback, [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. The same
computation therefore applies to $p_V$, with the same bound $2d$, which
is the relative clause.

attrs.title: FullCD for coefficients of étale origin

objects.body:
Fix the global finite-field datum, a prime $\ell\ne p$, $n\geq1$,
$A=A_{E,n}$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, finite-type $k$-schemes $Y$
and $\overline X$ with $\dim\overline X\leq d$
([def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]) and a proper finite-type
morphism $p:\overline X\to Y$. Then the vanishing required by
[def-weil-full-cohomological-dimension] holds for every coefficient
sheaf of the blueprint's class [def-sf-fullcd-used-class], with the
bound $c=2d$ and uniformly over all base changes $V\to Y$ of
$Y_{\Proet}$; that is,

$$
\mathcal H^r\bigl(R(p_V)_*(\mathcal F|_{\overline X\times_YV})\bigr)=0
\qquad(r>2d)
$$

for every base change $V\to Y$ and every $\mathcal F$ of that class.
Moreover that class is closed under inverse image along morphisms of
finite-type $k$-schemes, under extensions and under colimits, and it
contains the constant coefficient sheaf and every sheaf of étale origin.

## Proof

The vanishing is [thm-sf-fullcd-etale-origin], whose two clauses are
the absolute one and the relative one over every base change and whose bound
is $2\dim\overline X\leq2d$; equivalently, by
[lem-sf-fullcd-detection-equivalence], it is the vanishing of the
pro-étale cohomology of the base-changed source for those coefficients.
The class is stable under inverse image because the comparison pullback
$\nu^*$ of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] is exact and
commutes with the scheme pullbacks of the comparison sites, so the inverse
image of an étale-origin sheaf is étale-origin; it is stable under
extensions and colimits because $\nu^*$, being a left adjoint and exact,
preserves them; and the constructible description of the class is clause (i)
of [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]. The constant coefficient
sheaf is the pullback of the constant étale sheaf, hence lies in the class.

attrs.title: The full cohomological-dimension condition on the blueprint's coefficient class

objects.body:
In the setting of [def-sf-datum], let $X$ be smooth, separated of finite
type and geometrically connected of pure dimension $d$ over $k$, with
structure morphism $a_X$ (no admissibility hypothesis: $Ra_X^!$ is the
constructible exceptional inverse image of
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and $a_X$ is exceptionally admissible
in the sense of [def-trf-admissibility] as every separated finite-type
morphism is). Assume either
that $X$ is proper, or that $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ for a smooth, separated
finite-type, geometrically connected $k_0$-scheme $X_0$; in the latter
case no properness is required. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$. Then
there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
R\Gamma_c(X,K)^\vee\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }R\Gamma\bigl(X,\mathbb D_XK\bigr)
$$

in the point category $D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$ of
[def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], natural in $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$
and compatible with finite reduction, scalar extension, and shifts. For
$K=\Lambda_X$ it specializes to
$R\Gamma_c(X,\Lambda)^\vee\cong R\Gamma(X,\omega_X)$.

## Proof

Apply [thm-sf-verdier-exchange] with $Y=s$, $f=a_X$ and $M=K$:
$D_s(Ra_{X!}K)\cong Ra_{X*}D_XK$. Apply $\Fib_s$ and the point
identifications of [lem-sf-point]: the left-hand side becomes
$R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(R\Gamma_c(X,K),\Lambda)=R\Gamma_c(X,K)^\vee$
and the right-hand side becomes
$\Fib_s(Ra_{X*}D_XK)=R\Gamma(X,\mathbb D_XK)$. Since $\Fib_s$ is an
equivalence onto the point category by [lem-sf-point], the resulting
composite is an isomorphism in $D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$, and it is the displayed
isomorphism; naturality and the compatibilities are those of
the two ingredients. The argument uses only the exceptional adjunction for $a_X$ (so that
[thm-sf-verdier-exchange] applies to $f=a_X$, $Y=s$), which is available
for every separated finite-type morphism, never that $a_X$ is proper: the compact-support image
$Ra_{X!}$ and the ordinary image $Ra_{X*}$ enter as two different
functors, and no comparison $Ra_{X!}\cong Ra_{X*}$ is invoked. Hence the
same proof covers both cases of the hypothesis, the proper one and the
nonproper one $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. The constant case is
$\mathbb D_X\Lambda_X=R\mathcal H om_X(\Lambda_X,Ra_X^!\Lambda)=\omega_X$
by [def-sf-pf].

Let $X$ be a finite-type $\overline{\mathbf F}_q$-scheme,
let $\nu_X:X_{\Proet}\to X_{\Et}$ be the site comparison,
let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Et},A_{E,n})$, and let
$M\in D^b_c(X_{\Et},A_{E,n})$. Then

$$
\nu_X^*R\mathcal Hom_A(K,M)\longrightarrow
R\mathcal Hom_A(\nu_X^*K,\nu_X^*M)
$$

is an isomorphism.

## Proof

The assertion is local on $X$, since internal Hom and site
comparison restrict to open subschemes. A finite affine cover
therefore reduces to separated $X$. This is then the internal-Hom assertion of
[lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison]. Its proof uses
extension by zero from site-perfect strata and the closed-support
triangle to compare exceptional restriction, so it applies to a
general finite-Tor constructible first argument.

attrs.title: Internal-Hom comparison for finite-Tor constructible inputs

objects.body:
Let $A=A_{E,n}$, let $X$ be a finite-type $\overline{\mathbf F}_q$-scheme,
and let $K,M\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Et},A)$ have Tor amplitude in
$[a,b]$ and $[c,d]$, and suppose $\dim X\leq m$.
Then $R\mathcal Hom_A(K,M)$ belongs to $D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Et},A)$,
with Tor amplitude in $[c-b-2m,d-a+2m]$.
If $K$ is site-perfect, the sharper interval $[c-b,d-a]$ holds.

## Proof

The assertion is local on $X$; a finite affine cover reduces to
the separated case without increasing the dimension bound.
The general assertion and its dimension-dependent interval are
[cor-weil-finite-constructible-hom], proved from geometric
Verdier biduality and tensor preservation.
For the sharper assertion, locally on the site choose a finite projective model $P$ of $K$
in $[a,b]$, as in [def-weil-site-perfect-complex]. By
[lem-sf-hom-finite-projective], internal Hom is
$P^\vee\otimes_A^LM$. A bounded flat model of $M$, supplied by
[lem-sf-flat-model], makes this a bounded flat complex in
$[c-b,d-a]$. This proves the Tor bound; bounded constructibility is
[lem-sf-ext-sheaf-constructible]. Both assertions are local on the site.

attrs.title: Derived internal Hom at finite coefficients

objects.body:
In the setting of [def-sf-pairing] — so $X$ satisfies the hypotheses of
[thm-sf-global-duality]: $X$ is proper, or $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ with $X_0$
smooth, separated of finite type and geometrically connected, and no
properness is required in the latter case — suppose in addition that $K$ is
perfect over $\Lambda_X$ and that the orientation of
[def-sf-orientation] is fixed. Then the tensor–internal-Hom adjoint of
$\beta_K$ is the canonical isomorphism

$$
b_K^\sharp:\ R\Gamma\bigl(X,K^\vee(d)\bigr)[2d]\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda\bigl(R\Gamma_c(X,K),\Lambda\bigr)
$$

in the point category $D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$, and its inverse is the global
duality isomorphism of [thm-sf-global-duality] followed by the
identification $\mathbb D_XK\cong K^\vee(d)[2d]$ induced by the orientation.
In particular $\beta_K$ is perfect. If $X$ is proper and
$\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$, its degreewise form
gives perfect pairings

$$
\langle-,-\rangle_i:H_c^i(X,K)\times H^{2d-i}\bigl(X,K^\vee(d)\bigr)
\longrightarrow\Lambda\qquad(i\in\mathbf Z),
$$

the line-valued form being $H_c^i(X,K)\times H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee)\to \Lambda(-d)$.
For nonproper $X$ the degreewise assertion over field coefficients is
recorded separately in the Poincare duality chapter
(thm-pod-degreewise-perfectness-over-a-field).

## Proof

The cup product, the pairing and the orientation used below are those of
[def-sf-cup], [def-sf-pairing] and [def-sf-orientation],
the projection transformation is [def-sf-pf], and the interchange
law is [lem-sf-twist-interchange].
Steps 1–3 use properness of $X$ nowhere: they use only the global duality
isomorphism of [thm-sf-global-duality], which holds under either of its two
hypotheses, the orientation of [def-sf-orientation] for the smooth
morphism $a_X$, and the formal adjunction calculus of the six-functor
datum; so they prove the derived assertion for proper $X$ and for
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ alike.
Step 1: the two maps. By [thm-sf-global-duality] there is a canonical
isomorphism $R\Gamma_c(X,K)^\vee\to R\Gamma(X,\mathbb D_XK)$, and by the
orientation $\mathbb D_XK=R\mathcal H om_X(K,Ra_X^!\Lambda)\cong R\mathcal H om_X(K,\Lambda_X(d)[2d])\cong K^\vee(d)[2d]$; composing gives a
canonical isomorphism
$R\Gamma_c(X,K)^\vee\to R\Gamma(X,K^\vee(d))[2d]$, whose inverse is the map
displayed in the statement. Step 2: the adjoint of the pairing is that
map. The chain of [lem-sf-tensor-hom] with $M=K$, $N=\Lambda$ and
$f=a_X$ is, by [lem-sf-mate] and the definition of the pairing, the
transpose of the composite of cup product, evaluation and trace: taking
$\operatorname{Hom}_s(T,-)$ for $T=\Lambda[-r]$ converts a map $t:T\to R\Gamma(X,K^\vee(d))[2d]$ into $b_K^\sharp\circ t$ after the identifications
of [def-sf-pf]. Step 3: conclude by [lem-sf-detection]: the two
maps agree after applying $\operatorname{Hom}_s(\Lambda[-r],-)$ for all $r$,
hence they are equal. Step 4: the degreewise form (for proper $X$) is the
shift convention $H^r(C[m])=H^{r+m}(C)$ together with the identification
$H^{-i}(C^\vee)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(H^i(C),\Lambda)$ for a
point complex $C$, applied to $C=R\Gamma_c(X,K)$. This identification holds
because $\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(-,\Lambda)$ is exact on
$\Lambda$-modules, so that $R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(C,\Lambda)$ is
computed termwise and commutes with taking cohomology: for
$\Lambda=E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ this is clear, and
$\Lambda=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ is self-injective by Baer's
criterion — its ideals are the $\varpi_E^jA_{E,n}$, a homomorphism
$\varphi:\varpi_E^jA_{E,n}\to A_{E,n}$ sends $\varpi_E^j$ to an element
killed by $\varpi_E^{n-j}$, hence to some $\varpi_E^ja$, and
$\varphi$ extends to multiplication by $a$. The adjoint
$H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee(d))\to\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(H^i_c(X,K),\Lambda)$ of
$\langle-,-\rangle_i$ is then $H^{-i}(b_K^\sharp)$, an isomorphism. (For
$\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ the degreewise statement is false in general: a
torsion class in $H^i_c(X,K)$ pairs to zero with everything, and
$H^{-i}(C^\vee)$ acquires an $\operatorname{Ext}^1$-contribution from the
torsion of $H^{i+1}(C)$.) The line-valued form is obtained by
eliminating the invertible twist $\Lambda_X(d)$ through
$\Lambda(d)\otimes_\Lambda\Lambda(-d)\cong\Lambda$.

attrs.title: The pairing is the duality isomorphism

objects.body:
In the setting of [def-sf-datum], let $B$ be a separated finite-type
$k$-scheme, $f:X\to B$, $g:Y\to B$ separated finite type, $p,q$ the
projections of $X\times_BY$ (so $f\times_Bg=g\circ q$), and put $K\boxtimes L=p^*K\otimes^L_\Lambda q^*L$ for $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$, $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$.
Define the canonical map as the composite of the inverse of the
composition isomorphism $Rg_!Rq_!\cong R(f\times_Bg)_!$ of (A4), the inverse
of the projection transformation of [def-sf-pf] for $q$ at $(p^*K,L)$, the
inverse of the base-change exchange
$\operatorname{Ex}_!:Lg^*Rf_!K\to Rq_!Lp^*K$ of (A2), the symmetry of
$\otimes^L_\Lambda$, and the inverse of the projection transformation for $g$
at $(L,Rf_!K)$ followed by the symmetry, i.e. of the four steps of the proof
below (its coherence — symmetry, triple products, base change, projection
formula — is the separate coherence lemma for the relative product). Then this
canonical map

$$
R(f\times_Bg)_!\bigl(K\boxtimes L\bigr)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
Rf_!K\otimes^L_\Lambda Rg_!L
$$

is an isomorphism, natural in $K$ and $L$, compatible with base change
$B'\to B$, finite reduction, scalar extension, and with the
identifications $Rf_!\cong Rf_*$ for proper $f$. For $B=\operatorname{Spec}k$
and closed immersions $i_Z:Z\hookrightarrow X$, $i_W:W\hookrightarrow Y$,
it gives the compact-support product on the closed subschemes:

$$
R\Gamma_c(Z,i_Z^*K)\otimes^L_\Lambda R\Gamma_c(W,i_W^*L)
\cong R\Gamma_c(Z\times_kW,(i_Z\times i_W)^*(K\boxtimes L)).
$$

This is cohomology of the restrictions to the closed subschemes.
Cohomology with supports $R\Gamma_Z(X,K)=R\Gamma(Z,Ri_Z^!K)$ is a different
object from $R\Gamma_c(Z,i_Z^*K)$; its product formula over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is
[lem-pur-kunneth-supported], proved directly for smooth purity, and is
deduced again from the display above by Verdier duality later in the
Poincaré duality chapter. Over a general base $B$ the supports version
fails, so only the compact-support form is stated relatively.

## Proof

The operations are those of [def-sf-datum] and [def-sf-pf],
cohomology with supports has its separate meaning in
[def-pur-support-cohomology].
Step 1: by (A4), $R(f\times_Bg)_!=Rg_!\circ Rq_!$, so
$R(f\times_Bg)_!(K\boxtimes L)=Rg_!\bigl(Rq_!(q^*L\otimes^L_\Lambda p^*K)\bigr)$. Step 2: the projection formula (A3) for $q$, whose target is
$Y$, gives $Rq_!(q^*L\otimes^L p^*K)\cong L\otimes^L_\Lambda Rq_!(p^*K)$.
Step 3: base change (A2) for the Cartesian square with $p,q,f,g$ gives
$Rq_!(p^*K)\cong Lg^*Rf_!K$. Step 4: applying the projection formula to
$g$ with first variable $L$ and second variable $Rf_!K$ gives
$Rg_!\bigl(L\otimes^L_\Lambda Lg^*Rf_!K\bigr)\cong Rg_!L\otimes^L_\Lambda Rf_!K$, which is the displayed isomorphism. Step 5:
apply the same formula to the separated finite-type morphisms
$Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, $W\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and the
pullbacks $i_Z^*K,i_W^*L$. Pullback preserves their finite-Tor
hypotheses, and the exterior product is the pullback of $K\boxtimes L$.
This proves the claimed compact-support formula on the closed subschemes.

In the setting of [def-sf-datum], let $K,L$ be derived-complete
$D^b_{ctf}$-objects over $\mathcal O_E$ of finite Tor amplitude with finite
reductions $K_n,L_n$. Then the maps $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K_n,L_n}$ form a
morphism of normalized systems and realize a canonical isomorphism
$\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}$ over $\mathcal O_E$, compatible with all finite
reductions.

## Proof

The projection transformation is that of [def-sf-pf] and derived
completeness is that of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed].
By [thm-sf-pf-finite] each finite-level map is an isomorphism, and by
[prop-sf-pf-reduction] the maps are mutually compatible under
reduction, with uniform bounds and amplitudes inherited from $K$ and $L$
(finite Tor amplitude of a derived-complete object is uniform in $n$).
Derived completeness of the four complexes in the square together with this
compatibility is the hypothesis of the uniform-tower reconstruction of
[lem-weil-pbc-reconstruction-uniform-tower], which realizes the system
as a morphism of derived-complete $\mathcal O_E$-complexes with the given
reductions; it is an isomorphism because its reductions are isomorphisms
and the reduction functors are conservative on derived-complete complexes
of finite Tor amplitude. Finally, the realized map agrees with the
mate-theoretic projection transformation, since both reduce levelwise to
$\operatorname{PF}_{f,K_n,L_n}$ and reductions are conservative.

In the setting of [def-sf-datum], let $K,L$ be obtained by
rationalization from $\mathcal O_E$-objects, or represented at a finite
stage $E'/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Then $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}$ is an
isomorphism over $E$ and over $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, compatible with
the extension functors and with finite reduction.

## Proof

The projection transformation is that of [def-sf-pf]; rationalization
is [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi].
The rationalization functor $-\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}E$ is exact,
commutes with $Rf_!$, $-\otimes^L$ and $Lf^*$, and carries the
mate-theoretic projection transformation to the mate-theoretic projection
transformation (the units and counits are transported, being those of the
axioms); an exact functor carries isomorphisms to isomorphisms, so
[thm-sf-pf-adic] gives the $E$-statement. For
$\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, each object is represented over a finite stage
$E'/\mathbf Q_\ell$ by [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients],
the $E'$-statement is the previous paragraph, and compatibility with
scalar extension makes the finite-stage system descend to the
$2$-colimit.

In the setting of [def-sf-datum], let $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, let
$f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type, and let $K$ and $L$ be bounded
constructible complexes on the étale sites with $L$ of finite Tor
amplitude. Then $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}$ is an isomorphism, natural in
$K$ and $L$. ([lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula]; its proof is complete
and is the base case of the passage to all stages below.)

## Proof

The projection transformation used below is [def-sf-pf], and the
finite compact-support case is
[lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula].
Step 1: split off a compactification $f=\bar f\circ j$; then
$Rf_!=R\bar f_*j_!$ and the projection transformation is the composite of
