the direct-image projection map for $\bar f$ with the identification
$j_!K\otimes^L\bar f^*L\cong j_!(K\otimes^Lf^*L)$, which is checked on
étale stalks (on the open $X$ both sides have stalk
$K_{\bar x}\otimes L_{\bar x}$, and off $X$ both are zero). Step 2: for a
geometric point $\bar y\to Y$ with fibre $X_{\bar y}$, compact-support base
change identifies the stalk of the projection map with
$R\Gamma_c(X_{\bar y},K^{\mathrm{fib}}_{\bar y})\otimes^L P\to R\Gamma_c(X_{\bar y},K^{\mathrm{fib}}_{\bar y}\otimes^L\underline P)$,
where $P=L_{\bar y}$ and $\underline P$ is the pullback of the complex of
$A_{E,n}$-modules $P$. Step 3: the fibrewise map is an isomorphism for
every $P$: choosing a bounded complex of finite free modules representing
$P$, both sides are exact functors of $P$ agreeing on $P=A_{E,n}$ (the unit
identification), and the class of $P$ for which the map is an isomorphism
is closed under finite sums, shifts, cones and direct summands. Step 4:
all geometric stalks of the cone vanish, and geometric stalks are
conservative on the étale site, so the cone is zero.

attrs.title: Finite coefficients on the étale site

objects.body:
In the setting of [def-sf-datum], let $K,L$ be the pro-étale
realizations of bounded constructible finite-Tor complexes, with
étale-origin witnesses or with witnesses supplied by the site comparison,
at any coefficient stage. Then $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}$ is an
isomorphism on the pro-étale site.

## Proof

The projection transformation used below is [def-sf-pf], and the
field case is [thm-sf-pf-field].
The exact comparison inverse image of [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]
commutes with $Lf^*$ and with $-\otimes^L$, and the compact-support
comparison of [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale] identifies the
transported $R\bar f_*j_!$ together with its exchange and projection maps;
hence the comparison carries the étale projection transformation to the
pro-étale one. Transporting [thm-sf-pf-finite] along the comparison
gives the finite-coefficient statement; [thm-sf-pf-adic] gives the
integral stage and [thm-sf-pf-field] gives the field stages.
For objects presented without witnesses, the site
comparison supplies them by [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness].

Fix the global finite-field datum, a prime $\ell\ne p$, the algebraic
closure $k=\Fbar$ of the finite field $k_0$ of that datum, a
separated finite-type
$k$-scheme $Y$, a finite-type $k$-scheme $X$
([def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]), and a
separated finite-type
$k$-morphism $f:X\to Y$; the source $X$ is then a separated finite-type
$k$-scheme as well, $f$ being separated and $Y$ separated over $k$.
Cover $Y$ by finitely many affine opens
$V\subseteq Y$, and for each $V$ cover $f^{-1}(V)$ by finitely many
affine opens $U\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$; each $U\to V$ is affine of finite
type, hence exhibits $U$ as a closed subscheme of the affine space
$\mathbf A^{d_U}_V$ of [def-sbc-affine-space] for some integer
$d_U\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$. Put $D=\max_U d_U$. Let $A=A_{E,n}$ be a
finite coefficient stage, let $Rf_{!,n}$ be the pro-étale
compact-support direct image
attached to a
compactification of
$f$, and let

$$
Rf_n^{\times}=\nu_X^*f^{\times}R\nu_{Y,*},
$$

with $\nu_X,\nu_Y$ the comparison morphisms of
[def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], be the right adjoint of
$Rf_{!,n}$ that [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] constructs on the
blueprint's coefficient class [def-sf-fullcd-used-class]; that the
bounded constructible and finite-Tor objects of
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] and
[def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] are exactly the complexes of étale
origin is [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], and that both halves
of the ambient datum are theorems on them is
[cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge]. Read the
exceptional inverse image
$Rf^!$ as the restriction of $Rf_n^{\times}$ to $D^b_c(Y,A)$ and to its
finite-Tor objects, and use the
constructible intervals
$D_c^{[a,b]}$ and the
finite-Tor condition. Then:

1. for all integers $a\leq b$,
$$
L\in D_c^{[a,b]}(Y,A)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
Rf^!L\in D_c^{[a-2D,\,b+2\dim Y+1]}(X,A);
$$
1. if $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ has finite Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, then
$Rf^!K$ has finite Tor amplitude in $[a-2D,b+2\dim Y+1]$; in particular
$Rf^!$ carries $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ into $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$;
1. the two constants $2D$ and $2\dim Y+1$ depend on $f$ and $Y$
alone and not on the coefficient stage $n$, so that the two clauses hold at
every finite coefficient stage $A_{E,n}$, $n\geq1$, with the same
constants;
1. consequently $f$ satisfies clauses (2) and (3) of
[def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility] at every finite coefficient
stage, with the signed constants $c_f^-=-2D$ and $c_f^+=2\dim Y+1$ of
that definition, *without* assuming clause (1) of that definition and
*without* assuming the ambient exceptional right adjoint datum of
[def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint]: on the two categories
$D^b_c$ and $D^b_{ctf}$ that datum is the theorem
[cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge]. In particular clause (v) of
the finite-Tor preservation summary holds at the stage $\Lambda=A$ for
*every* separated finite-type morphism $f$ with separated finite-type
target, the ambient datum
displayed there being redundant on that category.

This theorem concerns the finite coefficient stage and objects of
étale origin. The integral and field stages are established separately
in the subsequent coefficient-comparison sections; they are not premises
of this finite preservation argument.

## Proof

*Step 1: which functor is bounded.* By
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] the functor $Rf^!$ is, on the
bounded constructible category $D^b_c(Y,A_{E,n})$, the restriction of the
ambient right adjoint $Rf_n^{\times}$ of $Rf_{!,n}$, and its restriction
to finite-Tor objects is the corresponding restriction of the same functor.
On the blueprint's coefficient class [def-sf-fullcd-used-class] that
right adjoint exists and is the explicit composite
$\nu_X^*f^{\times}R\nu_{Y,*}$ of
[thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class](2), which also supplies its unit, its
counit and the compactification comparisons; the comparison morphisms
$\nu_X,\nu_Y$ are those of
[def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. That the bounded constructible
and finite-Tor objects are exactly the complexes coming from the étale site
is [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], and that both halves of the
ambient datum are theorems on that class is
[cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge]. The bounds proved below are
therefore bounds on that explicitly constructed functor, and no clause of
[def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint] is used in stating them.

*Step 2: the two bounds are the assembly of the purity chapter.* The
setting of [def-pur-conventions] is the present one: the same global
finite-field datum, the same $k=\Fbar$, the same separated finite-type
morphism $f:X\to Y$ between finite-type $k$-schemes and the same
coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$. [thm-pur-general-admissibility] proves
that a separated finite-type morphism satisfies the two preservation clauses
of [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility] as soon as the
open-complement condition of [def-exc-open-complement-bound] holds for
the finitely many pairs $(W_U,\mathbf A^{d_U}_V)$ formed by the affine
charts of the statement, $W_U$ being the complement of $U$ in the affine
space $\mathbf A^{d_U}_V$ of [def-sbc-affine-space]; and
[cor-pur-general-admissibility-datum] removes that hypothesis by
[lem-exc-open-complement-known]. Indeed $\mathbf A^{d_U}_V$ is of
finite type over $k$ of dimension $d_U+\dim V\leq d_U+\dim Y$, the
complement $W_U$ is a quasi-compact open subscheme of it, and $A=A_{E,n}$
is a finite ring annihilated by the power $\varpi_E^n$ of the prime
$\ell\neq\operatorname{char}(k)$, so the pair satisfies the
open-complement condition with $c_U=2(d_U+\dim Y)$. The conclusion of
[cor-pur-general-admissibility-datum] is, in the notation of
[def-weil-constructible-intervals] and
[def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], that $Rf^!$ carries
$D_c^{[a,b]}(Y,A)$ into $D_c^{[a-2D,b-2D+c]}(X,A)$ and finite Tor
amplitude in $[a,b]$ to finite Tor amplitude in $[a-2D,b-2D+c]$, where
$D=\max_Ud_U$ and $c=\max_U(c_U+1+2(D-d_U))$. For every chart $U$,

$$
c_U+1+2(D-d_U)=2d_U+2\dim Y+1+2D-2d_U=2D+2\dim Y+1,
$$

so the maximum is $c=2D+2\dim Y+1$, the lower end is $a-2D$, and the two
bounds become $[a-2D,b+2\dim Y+1]$: these are clauses (1) and (2) of the
statement. No clause of [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility] is
used: [cor-pur-general-admissibility-datum] displays the ambient datum
only to record that on the coefficients it quantifies over — the bounded
constructible and finite-Tor objects, of étale origin by
[lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] — that datum is the theorem
[cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge], whose vanishing half is the
class-restricted datum [def-sf-fullcd-class] supplied by
[thm-sf-fullcd-class] with the sharp comparison bound $M=0$ of
[prop-sf-comparison-bound-zero].

*Step 3: independence of the coefficient stage.* The charts
$U\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$, the integers $d_U$ and the number
$\dim V\leq\dim Y$ come from the presentation of the coordinate rings
$\mathcal O(U)$ over $\mathcal O(V)$, an operation on the schemes alone,
and do not depend on the coefficient ring; and the hypotheses under which
[lem-exc-open-complement-known] was applied in Step 2 are the same at
every finite stage, $A_{E,n}$ being a finite ring annihilated by the power
$\varpi_E^n$ of $\ell$. Hence both the open-complement condition with
the constants $c_U$ and the constants $D$, $c$ of
[thm-pur-general-admissibility] and
[cor-pur-general-admissibility-datum] are the same integers at every
stage, and instantiating that corollary at each $n\geq1$ gives clauses (1)
and (2) at $A_{E,n}$ with these constants and with no hypothesis; this is
clause (3). It is the stage-uniform form of the open-complement condition
recorded in [thm-pur-open-complement-unconditional].

*Step 4: reading the bounds in the definitions.* Clause (2) of
[def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility] asks for signed integers
$c_f^-,c_f^+\in\mathbf Z$ with
$Rf_n^{\times}L\in D_c^{[a+c_f^-,b+c_f^+]}(X,A)$ for every
$L\in D_c^{[a,b]}(Y,A)$, and clause (3) asks that $Rf_n^{\times}$ carry
$D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ into $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$; by clauses (1) and (2) these hold
with $c_f^-=-2D$ and $c_f^+=2\dim Y+1$, and by Step 1 the functor these
two clauses bound is $Rf^!$ on the two categories they concern. Clause (1)
of the same definition is not assumed: the existence of $Rf_n^{\times}$ on
those categories, with its unit, counit and compactification comparisons, is
Step 1, that is [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] read through
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] and
[cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge]. Finally clause (v) of
the finite-Tor preservation summary is the same two assertions at the coefficient
stage $\Lambda=A$, with the membership
$Rf^!D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)\subseteq D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ as its conclusion and the
ambient exceptional right adjoint datum as its displayed hypothesis; by
Step 1 that hypothesis is, on that category and at that stage, the theorem
[cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge], so the clause holds for every
separated finite-type morphism $f$ without it. The assertions of the
statement for the remaining coefficient stages are exactly the assertions
that this proof does not make, as the last paragraph of the statement
records.

attrs.title: The preservation clauses of exceptional-adjoint admissibility are theorems on the coefficient class

objects.body:
In the setting of [def-sf-datum], let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated
finite-type morphism, with $Rf^!$ and the dualizing complexes
$\omega_X=Ra_X^!\Lambda$, $\omega_Y=Ra_Y^!\Lambda$ formed with the
constructible exceptional inverse image of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]
(no admissibility datum is assumed; every separated finite-type morphism is
exceptionally admissible in the sense of [def-trf-admissibility]). Then for
$M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
D_Y(Rf_!M)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf_*D_X(M),
$$

natural in $M$, compatible with finite reduction, scalar extension, and
shifts. ([fix-cor-verdier-exchange]; the difference from
the compiled chapter is that the proof below uses only
[lem-sf-tensor-hom] and never the duality chapter, which removes the
cycle recorded in [rem-sf-yoga].)

## Proof

The operations are those of the six-functor datum of [def-sf-datum],
its projection transformation is [def-sf-pf], and the mate calculus
is that of [lem-sf-mate]; the formal core is
[fix-cor-verdier-exchange].
Step 1: $Rf^!\omega_Y\cong\omega_X$. By axiom (A4) and
[lem-sf-mate], the mate of the composition law [thm-sf-comp-composition]
$R(a_Y\circ f)_!\cong Ra_{Y!}Rf_!$ is the isomorphism
$Rf^!Ra_Y^!\cong Ra_X^!$, i.e. $Rf^!\omega_Y\cong\omega_X$. Step 2: apply
[lem-sf-tensor-hom] with $N=\omega_Y$ (an object of
$D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$) and substitute Step 1:

$$
D_Y(Rf_!M)=R\mathcal H om_Y(Rf_!M,\omega_Y)
\cong Rf_*R\mathcal H om_X(M,f^!\omega_Y)
\cong Rf_*R\mathcal H om_X(M,\omega_X)=Rf_*D_X(M).
$$

Step 3: naturality and the compatibilities are those of
[lem-sf-tensor-hom] and of the mate construction of
[lem-sf-mate].

Let $D^{\bullet,\bullet}$ be a first-quadrant double complex in an abelian
category, with total complex $\operatorname{Tot}(D)$ and first and second
filtrations ${}'F$, ${}''F$ as in [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Each
filtration determines, through its bigraded exact couple and the derived
couples, a first-quadrant spectral sequence:

- (I) the *first spectral sequence* ${}'E$, of the filtration ${}'F$, with
  $$
   {}'E_1^{p,q}=H^q_{II}(D^{p,\bullet}),\qquad
   {}'E_2^{p,q}=H^p_IH^q_{II}(D),
  $$
  $d_1$ being induced by $d_I$;
- (II) the *second spectral sequence* ${}''E$, of the filtration ${}''F$,
  indexed by the filtration degree $q$ first, with
  $$
   {}''E_1^{q,p}=H^p_{I}(D^{\bullet,q}),\qquad
   {}''E_2^{q,p}=H^q_{II}H^p_I(D),
  $$
  $d_1$ being induced by $d_{II}$.

Both abut to $H^\bullet(\operatorname{Tot}D)$: for $F$ either of the two
filtrations, the image filtration [def-sp-image-filtration]

$$
 F^pH^n=\operatorname{im}\bigl(H^n(F^p\operatorname{Tot}D)
 \longrightarrow H^n(\operatorname{Tot}D)\bigr)
$$

satisfies $F^0H^n=H^n(\operatorname{Tot}D)$ and $F^{n+1}H^n=0$, so it is
finite in each degree, and $E_\infty^{p,q}\cong
\operatorname{gr}^pH^{p+q}(\operatorname{Tot}D)$ in the sense of
[def-sp-convergence]; moreover each entry stabilizes, $E_r^{p,q}=
E_\infty^{p,q}$ for $r>\max(p,q+1)$. Convergence is thus automatic. Both
spectral sequences are functorial for morphisms of double complexes.

## Proof

By [def-sp-double-complex-total], ${}'F$ and ${}''F$ are decreasing
filtrations of $\operatorname{Tot}(D)$ by subcomplexes with
$F^0\operatorname{Tot}(D)^n=\operatorname{Tot}(D)^n$ and
$F^{n+1}\operatorname{Tot}(D)^n=0$, hence bounded in each degree. So
[thm-sp-spectral-object-yields] applies to each of them: it builds the
bigraded exact couple of the filtration from the long exact cohomology
sequences of $0\to F^{p+1}\to F^p\to\operatorname{gr}^p\to0$, and its
derived couples give a spectral sequence with
$E_1^{p,q}=H^{p+q}(\operatorname{gr}^p\operatorname{Tot}D)$, $d_1$ the
boundary map of $0\to\operatorname{gr}^{p+1}\to F^p/F^{p+2}\to
\operatorname{gr}^p\to0$, and $E_{r+1}\cong\mathcal H(E_r,d_r)$; item (b) of
that theorem gives convergence to $H^\bullet(\operatorname{Tot}D)$ with the
displayed image filtration, which is finite and separated, and item (c)
gives functoriality in the filtered complex, hence in $D$ (a morphism of
double complexes preserves both filtrations).

*The first sequence.* The graded piece $\operatorname{gr}^p_{'F}$ is the
column $D^{p,\bullet}$ placed in total degrees $p+\bullet$, with
differential $(-1)^pd_{II}$; a sign does not change kernels or images, so
${}'E_1^{p,q}=H^{p+q}(\operatorname{gr}^p_{'F})=H^q_{II}(D^{p,\bullet})$.
For $d_1$: a class in ${}'E_1^{p,q}$ is represented by $x\in D^{p,q}$ with
$d_{II}x=0$; viewed in $F^p/F^{p+2}$ its total differential is
$dx=d_Ix+(-1)^pd_{II}x=d_Ix\in D^{p+1,q}=\operatorname{gr}^{p+1}$, so the
boundary map sends $[x]$ to $[d_Ix]$. Hence $d_1$ is the map induced by
$d_I$ on $H^q_{II}$, and ${}'E_2^{p,q}=\mathcal H({}'E_1,d_1)^{p,q}=
H^p_IH^q_{II}(D)$.

*The second sequence.* The graded piece $\operatorname{gr}^q_{''F}$ is the
row $D^{\bullet,q}$ placed in total degrees $\bullet+q$, with differential
$d_I$, so ${}''E_1^{q,p}=H^{p+q}(\operatorname{gr}^q_{''F})=
H^p_I(D^{\bullet,q})$. A class is represented by $y\in D^{p,q}$ with
$d_Iy=0$; in ${}''F^q/{}''F^{q+2}$ one has $dy=(-1)^pd_{II}y\in
D^{p,q+1}=\operatorname{gr}^{q+1}$, so $d_1[y]=(-1)^p[d_{II}y]$. The sign
depends only on $p$, which is constant along the complex
$\bigl(H^p_I(D^{\bullet,q})\bigr)_q$ being formed, so it changes neither
kernels nor images, and ${}''E_2^{q,p}=H^q_{II}H^p_I(D)$.

*Bounds.* In both cases the $E_1$-terms vanish outside the first quadrant
(${}'E_1^{p,q}$ is a subquotient of $D^{p,q}$, ${}''E_1^{q,p}$ one of
$D^{p,q}$), and so do all later pages, which are subquotients of $E_1$. On
page $r$ the differential leaving $(p,q)$ lands in $(p+r,q-r+1)$, outside
the quadrant once $r>q+1$, and the one arriving comes from $(p-r,q+r-1)$,
outside once $r>p$; for $r>\max(p,q+1)$ the page identification
$E_{r+1}\cong\mathcal H(E_r)$ is therefore the identity on the entry
$(p,q)$, which is the stated stabilization. Finally $F^0H^n=H^n$ and
$F^{n+1}H^n=0$ because $F^0\operatorname{Tot}(D)=\operatorname{Tot}(D)$ and
$F^{n+1}\operatorname{Tot}(D)^m=0$ for $m\leq n$, so that
$H^n(F^{n+1}\operatorname{Tot}D)$ is the cohomology of a complex whose
degree-$n$ term vanishes.

(*References: Stacks Project, Homological Algebra, the spectral sequences of
a double complex; Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, 5.6.*)

attrs.title: The two spectral sequences of a first-quadrant double complex

objects.body:
Let $(F,G)$ be a composable pair [def-sp-composite-acyclicity] with $F$
sending injectives to $G$-acyclics. For every $X\in\mathcal A$ there is a
functorial first-quadrant spectral sequence whose $E_2$-page is

$$
 E_2^{p,q}=R^pG\bigl(R^qF(X)\bigr)
$$

and which converges to $R^{p+q}(G\circ F)(X)$; its edge maps in degree $n$
have directions $R^nG(F(X))\to R^n(G\circ F)(X)\to G(R^nF(X))$, and the
spectral sequence depends functorially on $X$.

## Proof

Choose an injective resolution $X\to I^\bullet$
([def-sp-injective-resolutions]) and put $C^\bullet=F(I^\bullet)$ in
$\mathcal B$, so that $R^qF(X)=\mathcal H^q(C^\bullet)$. Let
$C^{\bullet,\bullet}$ be a Cartan--Eilenberg resolution of $C^\bullet$
([thm-sp-if-e1]) and put $D^{p,q}=G(C^{p,q})$; since $G$ is left exact,
$R^qG(C^p)=\mathcal H^q(G(C^{p,\bullet}))$. Filtering the total complex of
$D$ ([def-sp-double-complex-total]) by the second degree, the $E_1$-page is

$$
 E_1^{p,q}=R^qG\bigl(F(I^p)\bigr),
$$

which vanishes for $q>0$ precisely because every $F(I^p)$ is $G$-acyclic
([def-sp-composite-acyclicity]). By the bottom-edge collapse, i.e.
[lem-sp-edge-collapse] applied to the bidegree transposition
$(p,q)\mapsto(q,p)$ (which preserves the [def-sp-exact-couple]-structure and
the first-quadrant convergence of [def-sp-convergence]), this sequence
degenerates at $E_2$: $E_2^{p,q}=0$ for $q>0$, no differential begins at
$E_2$, and

$$
 E_2^{n,0}\cong R^n(G\circ F)(X),
$$

via the edge isomorphisms and $E_2^{n,0}=H^n\bigl(GF(I^\bullet)\bigr)$
([def-sp-left-exact-additive]); this is the convergence computation. The
stated $E_2$-page $R^pG(R^qF(X))$ is the page of the first-degree filtration
of the same double complex, whose identification with the horizontal
cohomology of the $C^{\bullet,q}$-columns is the Cartan--Eilenberg
computation of [thm-sp-if-e1]; the two spectral sequences of the double
complex ([thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences]) converge to the same abutment, so the stated sequence converges to
$R^{p+q}(G\circ F)(X)$ as claimed. The induced filtration on the abutment is
the image filtration of [def-sp-image-filtration], convergence is the
half-plane case of [def-sp-convergence], and everything is functorial in
$X$.

(*References: Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Theorem 5.8.3;
Stacks Project, Lemma 13.22.1 (Tag
[015M](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/015M)) identifies the acyclicity
condition with the canonical map $R(G\circ F)\to RG\circ RF$ being an
isomorphism, and Lemma 13.22.2 (Tag
[015N](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/015N)) is the bounded, converging
spectral sequence with finite induced filtration. The relative Leray form
$E_2^{p,q}=R^pg_*(R^qf_*\mathcal F)\Rightarrow R^{p+q}(g\circ f)_*\mathcal
F$, functorial in $\mathcal F$ and available for bounded-below complexes, is
Lemma 20.13.8 (Tag [01F6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01F6)); the
topoi (site) form is Lemma 21.14.6, see the dictionary
[def-sp-etale-dictionary] for the specialization.*)

Let $(F,G)$ and $(F',G')$ be composable pairs
[def-sp-composite-acyclicity] in Grothendieck abelian categories $\mathcal
A,\mathcal B,\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal A',\mathcal B',\mathcal C'$, and let

$$
 \alpha:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A',\qquad
 \beta:\mathcal B\to\mathcal B',\qquad
 \gamma:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C'
$$

be additive *exact* functors making the squares

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
\mathcal A&\xrightarrow{F}&\mathcal B\\
\downarrow\alpha&&\downarrow\beta\\
\mathcal A'&\xrightarrow{F'}&\mathcal B'
\end{array}
\qquad
\begin{array}{ccc}
\mathcal B&\xrightarrow{G}&\mathcal C\\
\downarrow\beta&&\downarrow\gamma\\
\mathcal B'&\xrightarrow{G'}&\mathcal C'
\end{array}
$$

commute up to fixed natural isomorphisms, and suppose that $F$ sends
injectives to $G$-acyclics and $F'$ sends injectives to $G'$-acyclics. Then
the Grothendieck spectral sequences of [thm-sp-grothendieck] for $(F,G)$ and
$(F',G')$ are related by a morphism of spectral sequences natural in all the
data. In the base-change situation of the proper-base-change chapter, where
the functors are inverse images along the maps of a cartesian square, this
says that the spectral sequence is compatible with inverse image along a base
change.

**Status.** The vertical maps were formerly called "natural transformations
$\alpha:A\to A'$", a type the proof cannot use; they are now specified as
additive exact functors, and their exactness is exactly what transports
resolutions. The proof is written out through the double complexes of
[thm-sp-grothendieck] and the couple morphisms of
[lem-sp-couple-morphism].

## Proof

*Step 1: the map of double complexes.* By the proof of
[thm-sp-grothendieck] the two spectral sequences are those of the double
complexes $C^{\bullet,\bullet}$ and $C'^{\bullet,\bullet}$ obtained from
injective resolutions $X\to I^\bullet$, $X'\to I'^\bullet$ and
Cartan--Eilenberg resolutions of $F(I^\bullet)$ and $F'(I'^\bullet)$.
Exactness of $\alpha$ and of $\beta$ carries an injective resolution of $X$
to a resolution of $\alpha X$ with acyclic terms, and the commutativity of
the squares identifies $\beta F(I^\bullet)$ with $F'\alpha(I^\bullet)$ up to
the fixed natural isomorphism; applying $\beta$ termwise to the
Cartan--Eilenberg resolution and using exactness and the acyclicity
hypotheses therefore produces a morphism of double complexes
$C^{\bullet,\bullet}\to C'^{\bullet,\bullet}$ over $X\to\alpha X$. Exactness
of $\gamma$ is used in the same way to compare the total complexes after
applying the two functors.

*Step 2: the map of spectral sequences.* A morphism of double complexes
induces a morphism of the filtered total complexes and hence, by
[thm-sp-spectral-object-yields], a morphism of the associated exact couples;
by [lem-sp-couple-morphism] it induces a morphism of the spectral sequences,
commuting with the differentials and with the page identifications, and
natural in the resolutions and hence in $X\to\alpha X$. The acyclicity
hypotheses of [def-sp-composite-acyclicity] are what identify the
$E_2$-pages of the two sequences with $R^pG(R^qF(X))$ and
$R^pG'(R^qF'(\alpha X))$, and they are preserved by exactness of the vertical
functors.

*Step 3: base change.* In the base-change situation of the
proper-base-change chapter the vertical functors are the inverse images
$g'^{-1}$, $g'^{-1}$, $g^{-1}$ along the maps of a cartesian square; these
are exact, since inverse image of sheaves is exact, and the two squares
commute by the base-change identification of the inverse images in a
cartesian square. Step 1 and Step 2 therefore apply and give the
compatibility of the Grothendieck spectral sequence with inverse image along
a base change.

attrs.title: Base-change naturality of the Grothendieck spectral sequence

objects.body:
Let $(D,E_2,\alpha,f,g)$ be the exact couple of
[def-sp-exact-couple]. Assume $D^{p,q}=0$ for $q<a$, and $E_2^{p,q}=0$ unless
$p\geq0$ and $q\geq a$. Put $A^n=D^{0,n}$. Then total degree $n$ contains
only $a\leq q\leq n$, and each entry $E_r^{p,q}$ has stabilized when

$$
 r>\max(q-a+1,\,p),
$$

with the canonical identification $E_r^{p,q}=E_{r+1}^{p,q}$ supplied by page
cohomology. For $q\leq n$, set
$G_qA^n=\operatorname{im}(D^{n-q,q}\xrightarrow{\alpha^{n-q}}A^n)$, and set
$G_qA^n=A^n$ for $q\geq n$. The decreasing filtration
[def-sp-filtration] $F^pA^n=G_{n-p}A^n$ is finite, exhaustive and separated,
and $E_\infty^{p,q}\cong F^pA^{p+q}/F^{p+1}A^{p+q}$. The couple is regular
and complete in the sense of [def-sp-convergence].

## Proof

The page region gives $p\geq0$ and $q\geq a$; on $p+q=n$ these inequalities
give the finite interval $a\leq q\leq n$, so each total degree contains
finitely many entries. For an entry $(p,q)$, the incoming differentials at
page $r$ are

$$
  d_r:E_r^{p-r,q+r-1}\longrightarrow E_r^{p,q},
$$

whose source has first index $p-r<0$, hence vanishes when $r>p$; the outgoing
differentials are

$$
  d_r:E_r^{p,q}\longrightarrow E_r^{p+r,q-r+1},
$$

whose target has second index $q-r+1<a$, hence vanishes when $r>q-a+1$. The
degrees are those of [def-sp-exact-couple]. For $r>\max(q-a+1,p)$, taking
page cohomology identifies the two successive entries. The recursive
subobjects of [def-sp-convergence] therefore stabilize, giving regularity.
For completeness,

$$
 \operatorname{im}(\alpha^r)^{p,q}
 =\operatorname{im}\bigl(\alpha^r:D^{p+r,q-r}\to D^{p,q}\bigr)=0
$$

for $r>q-a$, by the stated hypothesis on $D$. Exactness of the original
couple shows that $\alpha:D^{n-q+1,q-1}\to D^{n-q,q}$ is an isomorphism for
$q>n$: both adjacent $E_2$-terms have negative first index. Thus $A^n$ is the
stable value of this system. Its image filtration has $G_q=0$ for $q<a$ and
$G_q=A^n$ for $q\geq n$.

For completeness, the associated graded calculation can be read directly in
the iterated exact couple. At page $r$, its $D_r$ term at $(u,v)$ is
$\operatorname{im}(D^{u+r-2,v-r+2}\to D^{u,v})$. For $r$ sufficiently large,
the term which maps to $E_r^{p,q}$ is consequently $G_qA^{p+q}$; the image of
the preceding $\alpha_r$-map is $G_{q-1}A^{p+q}$. The following $D_r$-term is
zero, since its source has second index $q-r+1<a$. Exactness therefore gives
$E_r^{p,q}=G_qA^{p+q}/G_{q-1}A^{p+q}$. This is the asserted associated graded
of [def-sp-filtration], and proves convergence in the sense of
[def-sp-convergence].

(Stacks Project: Lemma 12.21.4 (Tag
[011T](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/011T): $Z_r$, $B_r$ and the rule
for $d_{r+1}$); Lemma 12.23.5 (Tag
[012F](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/012F): $E_\infty$ and the
associated graded of the cohomology).)

Let $v$ be as in [def-sp-truncation-couple] and let $A^{\bullet,\bullet}$ be
a Cartan--Eilenberg resolution of a bounded-below complex $K^\bullet$: the
row $A^{\bullet,s}$ is an injective resolution
[def-sp-injective-resolutions] of $K^s$, and the column cohomologies are the
$\mathcal H^s(K^\bullet)$. Then the filtration of the total complex by the
*second* degree gives the spectral sequence

$$
 E_1^{r,s}=R^rv(K^s)\Longrightarrow
 \mathcal H^{r+s}(RvK^\bullet),
$$

$d_1:E_1^{r,s}\to E_1^{r,s+1}$, induced by the differential of $K^\bullet$,
and the abutment is the cohomology of the derived functor of $K^\bullet$,
independent of the resolution.

**Status.** The proof formerly invoked Stacks Tags 0130/0131 for the whole
bicomplex spectral sequence without constructing it. It is now an application
of [thm-sp-spectral-object-yields] to the total complex of the double complex
with its second-degree filtration ([def-sp-double-complex-total],
[thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences] (II)), together with the standard identification
of the row cohomology with the derived functors.

It also formerly asserted that a Cartan--Eilenberg resolution computes the
derived functor of a complex, attributing that to
[def-sp-left-exact-additive], which defines derived functors only on objects,
and then took independence of the resolution from
[lem-sp-kinjective-computes], whose own proof appealed back to this theorem.
$Rv$ on complexes is now defined once, in [def-sp-kinjective-bridge], and both
steps are readings of that definition. The dependence runs one way: this
theorem uses the lemma, the lemma does not use this theorem.

## Proof

Each row $A^{\bullet,s}$ is an injective resolution of $K^s$, so the entries
$R^rv(K^s)$ are the $r$-th cohomology of $v(A^{\bullet,s})$ by
[def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Apply [thm-sp-spectral-object-yields] to the
total complex
$K^\bullet:=\operatorname{Tot}\bigl(v(A^{\bullet,\bullet})\bigr)$ with its
decreasing filtration by the second degree,
$F^sK^\bullet:=\bigoplus_{s'\geq s}v(A^{\bullet,s'})$. This is a filtration
by subcomplexes: the total differential preserves the second degree in its
first summand and raises it in its second, so $\bigoplus_{s'\geq s}$ is
stable. It is bounded in each degree, because a total degree receives only
finitely many rows, the complex $K^\bullet$ being bounded below. The graded
pieces are $\operatorname{gr}^sK^\bullet=\operatorname{Tot}
\bigl(v(A^{\bullet,s})\bigr)$, so item (a) of that theorem gives

$$
 E_1^{r,s}=H^{r+s}\bigl(\operatorname{Tot}(v(A^{\bullet,s}))\bigr)
 =H^r\bigl(v(A^{\bullet,s})\bigr)=R^rv(K^s),
$$

the middle identification being the standard one for a complex concentrated
in a single degree of the second index, and the differential $d_1$ being the
boundary homomorphism of the filtration, which is induced by the differential
of $K^\bullet$ because the rows are resolutions of the $K^s$ and the maps
between them come from $K^\bullet$. Item (b) of the same theorem identifies
the abutment with the cohomology of the total complex, $\mathcal
H^{r+s}(\operatorname{Tot}(v(A^{\bullet,\bullet})))$.

It remains to identify that with $\mathcal H^{r+s}(RvK^\bullet)$, for the
derived functor on $\operatorname{Ch}^+$ of [def-sp-kinjective-bridge]. In
total degree $n$,

$$
 \operatorname{Tot}(A^{\bullet,\bullet})^n=
 \bigoplus_{r+s=n}A^{r,s},
$$

a *finite* direct sum: the rows are resolutions, so $A^{r,s}=0$ for $r<0$, and
$K^\bullet$ is bounded below, so $A^{r,s}=0$ for $s$ below some $s_0$. A
finite direct sum of injectives is injective, so
$\operatorname{Tot}(A^{\bullet,\bullet})$ is a bounded-below complex of
injectives, hence K-injective by part (2) of [lem-sp-kinjective-computes]. The
augmentation $K^\bullet\to\operatorname{Tot}(A^{\bullet,\bullet})$ of a
Cartan--Eilenberg resolution of a bounded-below complex is a
quasi-isomorphism, so it is a K-injective resolution of $K^\bullet$ and

$$
 RvK^\bullet\cong v\bigl(\operatorname{Tot}(A^{\bullet,\bullet})\bigr)
 =\operatorname{Tot}\bigl(v(A^{\bullet,\bullet})\bigr),
$$

the second equality because $v$ is additive
[def-sp-left-exact-additive] and the total complex is a finite direct sum in
each degree. Independence of the chosen Cartan--Eilenberg resolution is part
(1) of [lem-sp-kinjective-computes]: any two K-injective resolutions of
$K^\bullet$ give canonically isomorphic values.

attrs.title: Hypercohomology spectral sequence via a Cartan--Eilenberg resolution

objects.body:
Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category and let $K^\bullet$ be a complex in
$\mathcal A$ equipped with a decreasing filtration
[def-sp-filtration] $F^\bullet K^\bullet$ by subcomplexes which is *bounded*:
for every degree $n$ one has $F^pK^n=K^n$ for $p\ll0$ and $F^pK^n=0$ for
$p\gg0$. For $p\leq q$ put

$$
 X^{[p,q]}:=F^pK^\bullet/F^qK^\bullet ,
$$

so that $0\to X^{[q,r]}\to X^{[p,r]}\to X^{[p,q]}\to0$ is a short exact
sequence of complexes for $p\leq q\leq r$. Then:

- (a) there is a cohomological spectral sequence [def-sp-spectral-sequence]
  $\bigl(E_r^{p,q},d_r\bigr)_{r\geq1}$ with
  $$
   E_1^{p,q}=H^{p+q}\bigl(X^{[p,p+1]}\bigr)
   =H^{p+q}\bigl(\operatorname{gr}^pK^\bullet\bigr),
   \qquad
   d_r:E_r^{p,q}\longrightarrow E_r^{p+r,q-r+1},
  $$
  the differential $d_1$ being the boundary homomorphism of the long exact
  cohomology sequence of the displayed short exact sequence with $(p,q,r)$
  replaced by $(p,p+1,p+2)$, and with, for every $r\geq1$ and every $N\geq
  r$, $E_r^{p,q}\cong Z_r^{p,q}/B_r^{p,q}$, where
  $$
  \begin{gathered}
  Z_r^{p,q}=\operatorname{im}\bigl(H^{p+q}(X^{[p,p+N]})\to
   H^{p+q}(X^{[p,p+r]})\bigr),\\
   B_r^{p,q}=\operatorname{im}\bigl(H^{p+q}(X^{[p-r+1,p+N]})\to
   H^{p+q}(X^{[p,p+r]})\bigr),
  \end{gathered}
  $$
  and with the identification $\mathcal H(E_r)\cong E_{r+1}$ natural;
- (b) the induced filtration
  $F^pH^n(K^\bullet):=\operatorname{im}\bigl(H^n(F^pK^\bullet)\to
  H^n(K^\bullet)\bigr)$ is finite and separated on each $H^n(K^\bullet)$, and
  there are natural isomorphisms
  $E_\infty^{p,q}\cong\operatorname{gr}^pH^{p+q}(K^\bullet)$ in the sense of
  [def-sp-convergence]: the spectral sequence converges to the cohomology of
  $K^\bullet$;
- (c) the construction is functorial in the pair
  $(K^\bullet,F^\bullet K^\bullet)$;
- (d) first-quadrant variant: if in addition $F^pK^\bullet=K^\bullet$ for
  $p\leq0$ and the graded pieces $\operatorname{gr}^pK^\bullet$ have
  cohomology concentrated in degrees $[p,p+1]$, then $E_r^{p,q}=0$ unless
  $p\geq0$ and $q\geq0$, and the entries stabilize for $r>\max(p,q)+1$.

**Status.** This is the standard spectral sequence of a bounded filtered
complex, proved from the chapter's own exact-couple machinery; the user of an
earlier page formula, [thm-sp-if-e1], has been rewired accordingly.

## Proof

Step 1: the exact couple. The short exact sequences $0\to F^{p+1}K^\bullet\to
F^pK^\bullet\to\operatorname{gr}^pK^\bullet\to0$ have long exact cohomology
sequences, exact by the long exact sequence of a short exact sequence of
complexes ([lem-sp-long-exact-of-triangle]), namely

$$
 \cdots\to H^{p+q}(F^{p+1}K^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\ \alpha\ }
 H^{p+q}(F^pK^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\ g\ }
 H^{p+q}(\operatorname{gr}^pK^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\ f\ }
 H^{p+q+1}(F^{p+1}K^\bullet)\to\cdots .
$$

They assemble into a bigraded exact couple [def-sp-exact-couple] with
$D_1^{p,q}=H^{p+q}(F^pK^\bullet)$ and
$E_1^{p,q}=H^{p+q}(\operatorname{gr}^pK^\bullet)$, the maps $\alpha,g,f$
having bidegrees $(-1,+1)$, $(0,0)$, $(+1,0)$; the exactness required of a
couple is exactly the exactness of these sequences.

Step 2: the pages. The derived couples of [def-sp-exact-couple] produce a
spectral sequence [def-sp-spectral-sequence] whose differentials $d_r=g_r\circ
f_r$ have bidegree $(+r,1-r)$, that is $d_r:E_r^{p,q}\to E_r^{p+r,q-r+1}$,
and whose page identification $\mathcal H(E_r)\cong E_{r+1}$ is the one
recorded in [lem-sp-page-induction]. The identification
$E_1^{p,q}=H^{p+q}(\operatorname{gr}^pK^\bullet)$ is the definition of the
first derived couple, and the differential $d_1$ is by the same definition
the composite $g_1f_1$, i.e. the boundary homomorphism of the long exact
sequence displayed in Step 1 with $(p,q,r)$ replaced by $(p,p+1,p+2)$.

Step 3: the $Z/B$ description. Induction on $r$ shows that $D_r^{p,q}$ is the
image of $H^{p+q}(F^{p+r-1}K^\bullet)$ in $H^{p+q}(X^{[p,p+N]})$ and that
$E_r^{p,q}=g_r(D_r^{p,q})$; unwinding the two maps of the couple gives the
displayed descriptions of $Z_r^{p,q}$ and $B_r^{p,q}$. Here $N\geq r$ may be
taken arbitrarily large: the filtration is bounded, so on the finitely many
degrees that contribute to a fixed total degree $p+q$ one has $F^{p+N}K^n=0$
for $N$ large, and there $F^pK^\bullet=X^{[p,p+N]}$.

Step 4: convergence. Boundedness gives
$F^pH^n(K^\bullet)=H^n(K^\bullet)$ for $p\ll0$ and $F^pH^n(K^\bullet)=0$ for
$p\gg0$, so the induced filtration is finite and separated; for $r>2N$ the
pages $E_r^{p,q}$ stabilize, and the description of Step 3 identifies the
stable value with
$F^pH^{p+q}(K^\bullet)/F^{p+1}H^{p+q}(K^\bullet)$. This is the convergence
statement of [def-sp-convergence], and it is (b).

Step 5: functoriality and the first-quadrant variant. A morphism of filtered
complexes induces a morphism of the exact couples of Step 1, hence a morphism
of spectral sequences by [lem-sp-couple-morphism]; the construction is
natural in the pair $(K^\bullet,F^\bullet K^\bullet)$, which is (c). If
$F^pK^\bullet=K^\bullet$ for $p\leq0$ and $\operatorname{gr}^pK^\bullet$ has
cohomology concentrated in degrees $[p,p+1]$, then
$E_1^{p,q}=H^{p+q}(\operatorname{gr}^pK^\bullet)=0$ unless $p\geq0$ and
$0\leq q\leq1$; the differentials have bidegree $(+r,1-r)$, so the entries
outside the first quadrant stay zero on every page, the page identification
being a passage to subquotients, and no differential enters or leaves a fixed
entry once $r>\max(p,q)+1$, since $p+r>p$ or $q-r+1<q$ forces the target out
of the quadrant. This is (d).

attrs.title: The spectral sequence of a filtered complex

objects.body:
Let $K$ be as in [def-sp-truncation-couple]. The spectral sequence of the
truncation couple [def-sp-truncation-couple] has

$$
 E_2^{p,q}=R^pv\bigl(\mathcal H^q(K)\bigr)
 \Longrightarrow\mathcal H^{p+q}(RvK),
$$

the abutment $\mathcal H^n(RvK)$ carrying the image filtration
[def-sp-image-filtration] of the maps $\mathcal H^n(Rv\,\tau_{\leq q}K)\to
\mathcal H^n(RvK)$; in each degree $n$ only $a\leq q\leq n$ occurs, so the
couple is regular and complete and the convergence is unconditional
([def-sp-convergence]).

## Proof

The exact couple of [def-sp-truncation-couple] is an exact couple by
[lem-sp-truncation-couple-exact], and it is the couple of a t-structure
("heart") filtration, so by the spectral sequence of
[def-sp-exact-couple] the $E_2$-page is $E_2^{p,q}=R^pv(\mathcal H^qK)$, the
identification of the shifted cohomology being the shift rule
[lem-sp-shift-identification]. The abutment is $\mathcal H^{p+q}(RvK)$ with
the image filtration of [def-sp-image-filtration]. The $D$-terms vanish for
$q<a$ because $\tau_{\leq q}K=0$. The functor $Rv$ is left t-exact: an object
with no cohomology below $b$ has an injective resolution in the sense of
[def-sp-injective-resolutions] starting in degree $b$, and applying the left
exact functor does not introduce lower terms. Applied to $\tau_{>n}K$, this
shows $D^{0,n}=H^n(Rv\tau_{\leq n}K)=H^n(RvK)$. The hypotheses and the
abutment identification of [thm-sp-half-plane-convergence] therefore hold. In
particular the entries stabilize for $r>\max(q-a+1,p)$, and the stated finite
filtration is the one constructed there.

Fix the global finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$, where $q=p^a$, and
the coefficient conventions, $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $X_0$ be a separated
finite-type $k_0$-scheme, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, let
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ have an explicit etale-origin witness, and let
$\psi:L\Phi^*K\to K$ be a Frobenius coefficient morphism of
[def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism], with iterates $\psi_m$ and
global operators $F_{c,m}(\psi)$; no invertibility of $\psi$ is
assumed. Assume the exceptional-adjoint admissibility hypotheses of
[def-trf-admissibility] for the graph correspondences and fixed-point
base changes on a chosen compactification defined over $k_0$, as in
the Grothendieck–Lefschetz formula over a finite ring below (at the
finite stage these hold automatically, and the proof does not use
them). For
$y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ with geometric point $\bar y$ one has
$\Phi^m\bar y=\bar y$ (the fixed points of
[thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points]), and $\psi_m$ induces a stalk
endomorphism
$\psi_{m,\bar y}:K_{\bar y}\cong(L\Phi^{m*}K)_{\bar y}\to K_{\bar y}$.
Then for every $m\geq1$

$$
\boxed{
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(F_{c,m}(\psi)\mid R\Gamma_c(X,K)\bigr)
=\sum_{y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})}
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(\psi_{m,\bar y}\mid K_{\bar y}\bigr)
}
$$

in $A$, both sides being categorical traces of endomorphisms of
perfect complexes. This is the coefficient-morphism variant of the
finite-coefficient trace formula; for the scheme-Frobenius map
$\psi=u_1$ of a strict Weil complex it gives the
Grothendieck–Lefschetz formula over a finite ring, which is deduced from
it below. It is the form needed
when an integral lift of a field-stage Weil isomorphism is not itself
invertible.

## Proof

The traces are defined: $R\Gamma_c(X,K)$ is perfect and
$F_{c,m}(\psi)$ is a morphism of $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$ by
[lem-trf-global-operator-perfect], and the stalks are perfect by
[fix-lem-finite-tor-perfect].

The proof reduces to curves, as in the sketch: closed subschemes of
the affine line first, then affine schemes by fibring over an affine
space with the Weil $!$-pushforward, then general schemes by
localization. No compactification of $X_0$ is used, and the
admissibility hypothesis of the statement is not needed.

*Step 0: conventions.* For $r\geq1$ the finite-field datum
$(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ may be replaced by $(p,ar,q^r,\mathbf F_{q^r},k)$
([def-weil-finite-field-fiber]); every result cited below is stated for
an arbitrary datum. For a finite field $F$ of characteristic $p$, a
separated finite-type $F$-scheme $S_0$ with $S=S_0\times_Fk$, a complex
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(S,A)$ and a Frobenius coefficient morphism $\psi$ on
$K$ for the $|F|$-power scheme Frobenius $\Phi_S$, and $m\geq1$, write
$\mathrm{TF}(S_0,K,\psi,m)$ for the identity
$$
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(F_{c,m}(\psi)\mid R\Gamma_c(S,K)\bigr)
=\sum_{s\in S_0(F_m)}\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(\psi_{m,\bar s}\mid K_{\bar s}\bigr),
$$
where $F_m\subseteq k$ is the extension of degree $m$ of $F$. Every
complex in $D^b_{ctf}$ has an explicit étale-origin witness
([lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]), and every separated
finite-type morphism between separated finite-type $k$-schemes is
exceptionally admissible at the finite stage
([rem-ptr-trf-admissibility-12], [thm-sf-preservation-class]). We prove
$\mathrm{TF}$ for all such data; the theorem is the case
$(F,S_0)=(k_0,X_0)$.

*Step 1: finite schemes.* Let $S_0$ be finite over $F$. Then $S$ is
finite over $k$, hence a finite disjoint union
$S=\coprod_{\bar s\in S(k)}S_{\bar s}$ of spectra of local Artinian
$k$-algebras with residue field $k$. The inclusion
$\iota_{\bar s}:\operatorname{Spec}k\to S_{\bar s}$ is a finite
universal homeomorphism, so by [i-topology]
$K|_{S_{\bar s}}\simeq R\iota_{\bar s*}K_{\bar s}$ and
$R\Gamma_c(S,K)=R\Gamma(S,K)\simeq\bigoplus_{\bar s}K_{\bar s}$, a finite
sum of perfect complexes ([fix-lem-finite-tor-perfect]). Put
$\Phi=\Phi_S^m$; it is a universal homeomorphism, so it permutes the
points $\bar s$, and $(L\Phi^*K)_{\bar s}=K_{\Phi(\bar s)}$. By
[prop-trf-graph-operator],
$F_{c,m}(\psi)=R\Gamma(S,\psi_m)\circ\Phi^\sharp$, where $\Phi^\sharp$ is
induced by the unit of $L\Phi^*\dashv R\Phi_*$; on these decompositions
$\Phi^\sharp$ maps the summand $K_{\Phi(\bar s)}$ identically onto the
summand $(L\Phi^*K)_{\bar s}$, and $R\Gamma(S,\psi_m)$ is the sum of
the stalk maps. Hence $F_{c,m}(\psi)$ is the block matrix whose only
nonzero blocks are $\psi_{m,\bar s}:K_{\Phi(\bar s)}\to K_{\bar s}$. Choosing
bounded complexes of finite projective $A$-modules for the $K_{\bar s}$
and chain representatives of the blocks, the chain-level supertrace of
[lem-trf-chain-supertrace] only sees the diagonal blocks, those with
$\Phi(\bar s)=\bar s$. By [thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points] these are the
geometric points of $S_0(F_m)$, and there the block is the stalk map
$\psi_{m,\bar s}$. This is $\mathrm{TF}(S_0,K,\psi,m)$.

*Step 2: the affine line.* Let $S_0=\mathbf A^1_F$ and let
$j_0:\mathbf A^1_F\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^1_F$ be the compactification of
[d-lines], proper ([Stacks, Tag 0FMG](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FMG))
and smooth of pure dimension one
([Stacks, Tag 0B2P](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B2P)), with complement
the rational point $\infty$. Let $\bar\psi$ be the extension of $\psi$ to
$j_!K$ of [lem-trf-compactification-graph-operator], with iterates
$\bar\psi_m=\overline{\psi_m}$ (item (1)). By item (3) of that lemma the
isomorphism $C_{j,K}$ of [lem-trf-compactification-cohomology] conjugates
$F_{c,m}(\psi)$ into $T_{\bar c}(\bar\psi_m)$ on
$R\Gamma(\mathbf P^1,j_!K)$, where $\bar c=(\operatorname{id},\bar\Phi^m)$ is the
graph on $\mathbf P^1$, so the traces agree by conjugacy invariance
([prop-trf-trace-formal-laws], item (1)). On the proper curve
$\mathbf P^1$ the ordinary leg $\bar\Phi^m$ is finite and, by
[thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points], the fixed scheme is finite over $k$
with one reduced point component for each point of
$\mathbf P^1_F(F_m)$. The Lefschetz–Verdier comparison
[thm-trf-lefschetz-verdier], which assembles the proper global
comparison and the decomposition into local terms, gives
$$
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(T_{\bar c}(\bar\psi_m)\mid R\Gamma(\mathbf P^1,j_!K)\bigr)
=\sum_{y\in\mathbf P^1_F(F_m)}\operatorname{LT}_y(\bar\psi_m).
$$
By the coefficient-morphism form of [thm-trf-frobenius-local-term] on the
smooth curve $\mathbf P^1$ (proved there through the curve pieces),
$\operatorname{LT}_y(\bar\psi_m)=\operatorname{tr}_A(\bar\psi_{m,\bar y}\mid(j_!K)_{\bar y})$.
By [lem-trf-compactification-graph-operator], item (2), the stalk at
$\infty$ is zero, so its local term is zero, and for
$y\in\mathbf A^1_F(F_m)$ one has $(j_!K)_{\bar y}=K_{\bar y}$ and
$\bar\psi_{m,\bar y}=\psi_{m,\bar y}$. This is
$\mathrm{TF}(\mathbf A^1_F,K,\psi,m)$.

*Step 3: closed subschemes of the affine line.* A closed subscheme of
$\mathbf A^1_F$ is $\operatorname{Spec}F[t]/I$. If $I=0$ it is the line,
Step 2. Otherwise a nonzero polynomial in $I$ makes $F[t]/I$
finite-dimensional over $F$, and Step 1 applies. This includes
nonreduced schemes.

*Step 4: affine schemes.* We prove $\mathrm{TF}$ for all closed
subschemes $S_0\subseteq\mathbf A^d_F$, by induction on $d$,
simultaneously for all finite fields $F$, all $K$, all $\psi$ and all
$m$. The cases $d\leq1$ are Steps 1 and 3. Let $d\geq2$ and let
$f_0:S_0\to Y_0=\mathbf A^{d-1}_F$ forget the last coordinate, a
separated morphism. Let $(L,\psi')=(Rf_!K,Rf_!\psi\circ\theta_{f,1})$
be the Weil $!$-pushforward of [def-trf-weil-shriek-pushforward]; its
comparison $\theta_{f,1}$ is built from the relative Frobenius
factorization [d-relative-frob] and is invertible because $r_1$ is a
finite universal homeomorphism ([i-relative-frob], [i-topology]), and
$L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$. By [lem-trf-weil-shriek-operator-fibres],
item (1), the compact global operator $F_{c,m}(\psi')$ is conjugate to
$F_{c,m}(\psi)$, and the induction hypothesis for $Y_0$ gives
$$
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(F_{c,m}(\psi)\mid R\Gamma_c(S,K)\bigr)
=\sum_{y\in Y_0(F_m)}\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(\psi'_{m,\bar y}\mid L_{\bar y}\bigr).
$$
By item (2) of that lemma, $\psi'_{m,\bar y}$ is conjugate to the
degree-one compact Frobenius operator $F_{c,1}(\psi_m|_{\bar y})$ of the
fibre $S_{0,y}$, considered over $F_m$ with the one-step coefficient
morphism $\psi_m|_{\bar y}$. The fibre is a closed subscheme of
$\mathbf A^1_{F_m}$, so Step 3 over $F_m$ gives
$$
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(\psi'_{m,\bar y}\mid L_{\bar y}\bigr)
=\sum_{s\in S_{0,y}(F_m)}\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(\psi_{m,\bar s}\mid K_{\bar s}\bigr),
$$
using item (3) for the stalk maps. Summing over $y$ and using the
disjoint union of item (3) gives $\mathrm{TF}(S_0,K,\psi,m)$.

*Step 5: general schemes.* Let $S_0$ be separated of finite type over
$F$, choose a finite affine open cover $U_1,\ldots,U_N$, and put
$W_i=U_1\cup\cdots\cup U_i$, $V_i=W_i\setminus W_{i-1}$. Each $V_i$ is
closed in the affine $U_i$, hence affine of finite type and a closed
subscheme of some $\mathbf A^d_F$, and $V_i$ is the closed complement of
the open $W_{i-1}$ in $W_i$. By item (3) of
[prop-trf-trace-additivity-open-closed], applied to
$W_{i-1}\subseteq W_i$ with the restricted coefficient morphisms, whose
iterates and stalk maps are the restrictions of those of $\psi$,
$$
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(F_{c,m}\mid R\Gamma_c(W_i)\bigr)
=\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(F_{c,m}\mid R\Gamma_c(W_{i-1})\bigr)
+\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(F_{c,m}\mid R\Gamma_c(V_i)\bigr).
$$
By induction on $i$ and Step 4 for the $V_i$, the trace on
$R\Gamma_c(S,K)$ is the sum over $i$ of the point sums over
$V_i(F_m)$. These sets partition $S_0(F_m)$, which gives
$\mathrm{TF}(S_0,K,\psi,m)$ and proves the theorem.

attrs.title: Trace formula for Frobenius coefficient morphisms over a finite ring

objects.body:
Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions, $A=A_{E,n}$, put $s=\Spec k$, and let
$d:F\to X$ be a
separated finite-type
morphism with $a_X$ and $a_F=a_X\circ d$
exceptionally admissible. Then there is a
canonical isomorphism

$$
Rd^!\omega_{X,A}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\omega_{F,A},
$$

functorial in $d$, where $\omega_{X,A}$, $\omega_{F,A}$ are the
dualizing complexes of
[def-trf-dualizing-complex] and $Rd^!$ is the
exceptional inverse image of
$d$.

## Proof

The composition and base-change exchange data for the exceptional inverse
image of [def-trf-admissibility], together with the composition law
$R(a_X\circ d)_!\cong Ra_{X!}Rd_!$ of the six-operations package
[prop-functor-package] (item (3)), give the adjoint composition
isomorphism

$$
Rd^!Ra_X^!\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }R(a_X\circ d)^!=Ra_F^!.
$$

Applying it to the constant complex $A_s$ and using
$\omega_{X,A}=Ra_X^!A_s$, $\omega_{F,A}=Ra_F^!A_s$ of
[def-trf-dualizing-complex] gives the displayed canonical
isomorphism; its compatibility with further compositions is the coherence
of the exchange data of [def-trf-admissibility]. (The types of
$Rd^!$ are those of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image].)

Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions, and let $\rho:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of finite
commutative rings annihilated by integers invertible in $k$. Derived
scalar extension $-\otimes_A^LB:D(X,A)\to D(X,B)$ preserves bounded
constructibility and finite Tor amplitude, there are natural
isomorphisms

$$
(Rf_!K)\otimes_A^LB\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf_!\bigl(K\otimes_A^LB\bigr),
\qquad
(Lf^*L)\otimes_A^LB\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Lf^*\bigl(L\otimes_A^LB\bigr)
$$

for $f:X\to Y$ separated finite type and admissible, and the
scalar-extension law of the
categorical trace identifies

$$
\rho\bigl(\operatorname{tr}_A(v\mid P)\bigr)
=\operatorname{tr}_B\bigl(v\otimes_A^LB\mid P\otimes_A^LB\bigr).
$$

Consequently the finite-ring trace formula over $A$ maps to the
finite-ring trace formula over $B$; in particular, for a strict Weil
complex $(K_A,\varphi_A)$, its scalar extension $(K_B,\varphi_B)$
has $R\Gamma_c(X,K_A)\otimes_A^LB\simeq R\Gamma_c(X,K_B)$ and
$(K_A)_{\bar y}\otimes_A^LB\simeq(K_B)_{\bar y}$ with matching
Frobenius operators, and

$$
\rho\bigl(\operatorname{tr}_A(F_{y,m}\mid K_{A,\bar y})\bigr)
=\operatorname{tr}_B\bigl(F_{y,m}\mid K_{B,\bar y}\bigr).
$$

## Proof

Derived scalar extension for the small pro-etale site is the exact
monoidal functor $-\otimes_A^LB$ of [def-weil-derived-tensor];
the first displayed natural isomorphism is the projection
transformation of [def-exchange-projection] for the constant
$B$-module, and the second is the monoidality of the exact functor
$Lf^*$ applied to $-\otimes_A^LB$; both are natural in the
coefficient ring and compatible with the finite-level structures of
[def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. The trace identity is item
(3) of [prop-trf-trace-formal-laws], and the compatibility of
the Frobenius operators with scalar extension is the definition of
the Weil structure on the extension in
[def-trf-coefficient-conventions]
([def-trf-frobenius-operators] applied to the extension), all
the constructions being natural in the coefficient ring.

attrs.title: Compatibility with a finite coefficient map

objects.body:
Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions, $A=A_{E,n}$, and let
$c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times_sX$ be an
admissible
cohomological correspondence with
fixed scheme
$F=\operatorname{Fix}(c)$, so that the
fixed square of
[prop-trf-fixed-square-cartesian] is Cartesian.

1. *Pullback along the ordinary leg.* For
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$,
$$
Li_F^*Lc_2^*K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Ld^*K,
$$
the functoriality of the
derived pullback along
the equality $c_2i_F=d$.
1. *Base change for the total correspondence.* For
$M\in D^b_{ctf}(C,A)$,
$$
L\Delta_X^*Rc_!M\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rd_!Li_F^*M,
$$
the
compact-support base change of the
six-operations package in the Cartesian fixed square. For
$N\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, its right-adjoint form (from the
compatibility of the exchange with the adjunction data of
[def-trf-admissibility]) is
$$
Rc^!R\Delta_{X*}N\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Ri_{F*}Rd^!N.
$$

## Proof

The first identification is the functoriality of the derived pullback
along the equality $c_2i_F=d$ of
[prop-trf-fixed-square-cartesian]:

$$
Li_F^*Lc_2^*K=L(c_2i_F)^*K=Ld^*K.
$$

The second is the compact-support exchange
$Lg^*Rf_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_!Lg'^*$ of
[def-exchange-projection] (and of the six-operations package
[prop-functor-package], item (4)) applied to the Cartesian fixed
square of [prop-trf-fixed-square-cartesian] with $f=c$,
$g=\Delta_X$, $f'=d$, $g'=i_F$. The right-adjoint form is
obtained by taking right adjoints of the two sides and using the
compatibility of the exchange with the units and counits of the
adjunctions of [def-trf-admissibility]: the right adjoint of
$L\Delta_X^*Rc_!$ is $Rc^!R\Delta_{X*}$, and that of $Rd_!Li_F^*$
is $Ri_{F*}Rd^!$. (The derived pullbacks of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] used in the first
identification are the ones defined by exact inverse image followed by
the flat extension along the constant coefficient sheaf; no analogue of
these statements for the single exceptional leg $c_1$ is asserted
(the naive version $Li_F^*Rc_1^!K\cong Rd^!K$ is false).

attrs.title: Base change in the fixed-point square

objects.body:
Use the finite coefficient ring
$A=A_{E,n}$. Let $h:X\to X$ be an endomorphism of a
separated finite-type
$k$-scheme and let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ be a
site-perfect complex.
Suppose its fixed scheme
$j:F=\operatorname{Fix}(h)\to X$ is finite etale over $k$.
For the derived internal Hom
there is a natural morphism

$$
\sigma_{h,K}:Lj^*R\mathcal Hom_A(Lh^*K,K)\longrightarrow A_F.
$$

If $u:Lh^*K\to K$ has internal-Hom mate
$\widetilde u:A_X\to R\mathcal Hom_A(Lh^*K,K)$, the value at
$y\in F(k)$ of $\sigma_{h,K}\circ Lj^*\widetilde u$ is

$$
\operatorname{tr}_A(u_y\mid K_y),
$$

the categorical trace of the
endomorphism obtained from $hj=j$. This is a statement about stalk
traces; it does not identify them with Verdier local terms.

## Proof

Put $W=Lj^*K$. A local bounded finite-free representative, as in
[def-weil-site-perfect-complex], pulls back to such a representative
of $W$, so $W$ is site-perfect. The fixed-scheme identity $hj=j$
of [def-trf-fixed-scheme] and
[thm-trf-internal-hom-pullback], applied with first variable
$Lh^*K$, give

$$
Lj^*R\mathcal Hom_A(Lh^*K,K)\simeq R\mathcal Hom_A(W,W).
$$

Since $k$ is algebraically closed, a finite etale $k$-scheme is a
finite disjoint union of copies of $\Spec k$; its sheaf category is
the product of their sheaf categories. On each such component set
$W_y^\vee=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(W_y,A)$.
The tensor–Hom adjunction of [def-weil-derived-tensor] identifies
$R\operatorname{Hom}_A(W_y,W_y)$ with
$W_y\otimes_A^LW_y^\vee$. Compose this identification with the
Koszul symmetry and evaluation to obtain a morphism to $A$.
Their finite product defines $\sigma_{h,K}$.

The mate of $u$, after restriction to $y$, is the mate of $u_y$
by the naturality of the internal-Hom comparison. Under the preceding
tensor–Hom identification it is coevaluation followed by
$u_y\otimes1$. The composite with symmetry and evaluation is
exactly the categorical trace of [def-trf-categorical-trace].
More explicitly, on a bounded finite-projective representative $P$
and a chain representative $v$ of $u_y$, it is
$\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{tr}_A(v^i\mid P^i)$, by
[lem-trf-chain-supertrace]. This also proves independence of the
representative and the asserted naturality.

attrs.title: Stalk traces on a finite etale fixed scheme

objects.body:
Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions, $A=A_{E,n}$, put $s=\Spec k$, and let $X$ be a
proper finite-type scheme.
Let $c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times_sX$ be an
admissible
cohomological correspondence with
$c_2$ proper and with
fixed scheme
$F=\operatorname{Fix}(c)$ proper over $s$. For
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, the
categorical trace of the
global operator equals the integral of
the trace class:

$$
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(T_c(u)\mid R\Gamma_c(X,K)\bigr)
=\int_F\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)
\quad\text{in }A,
$$

where $T_c(u)$ is the global operator of
[def-trf-global-operator], $\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)$ the trace class
of [def-trf-trace-class], and $\int_F$ the integration of
[def-trf-integration].

## Proof

All morphisms below are separated and of finite type between separated
finite-type $k$-schemes, hence exceptionally admissible at the finite
stage ([thm-sf-preservation-class]).

*The pushforward to the point.* Since $a_C=a_Xc_2$ with $a_X$ and $c_2$
proper, $C$ is proper over $s$, and $a_C=a_Xc_1$ as well. Let
$b=(\operatorname{id}_s,\operatorname{id}_s):s\to s\times_ss$ be the
point correspondence. Then $(f,g)=(a_X,a_C):(C,c)\to(s,b)$ is a proper
pushforward diagram of [def-trf-coefficient-pushforward]
($b_ig=a_C=a_Xc_i$). Its fixed scheme is $\operatorname{Fix}(b)=s$, and
the induced map of fixed schemes is the structure morphism
$h=a_F:F\to s$. Put $K'=Ra_{X*}K$; since $a_X$ is proper,
$Ra_{X*}=Ra_{X!}$ ([prop-functor-package], clause (3)), so
$K'=R\Gamma_c(X,K)$, a perfect $A$-complex by
[prop-trf-compact-support-perfectness].

*The pushed coefficient map is the global operator.* In
[def-trf-coefficient-pushforward], the ordinary half $\gamma$ is the unit
$\eta_{a_C}$ followed by $Ra_{C*}c_2^*\varepsilon_{a_X}$. Because
$a_C=a_Xc_2$, the unit $\eta_{a_C}$ is $\eta_{a_X}$ followed by
$Ra_{X*}\eta_{c_2}a_X^*$, and the triangle identity
$(Ra_{X*}\varepsilon_{a_X})\circ(\eta_{a_X}Ra_{X*})=\operatorname{id}$ of
[fix-prop-adjunctions] cancels the counit; hence
$\gamma=Ra_{X*}\eta_{c_2}$, followed by $Ra_{X*}Rc_{2*}=Ra_{C*}$ and
$Rc_{2*}=Rc_{2!}$. These are the first two arrows of
[def-trf-global-operator]. For $b_1=\operatorname{id}_s$ the exceptional
adjoint in the exceptional half is the identity, so $\delta$ is the
composition isomorphism $\Xi_1$ of [thm-sf-comp-composition] followed by
$Ra_{X!}\varepsilon_{c_1}$, which are the last two arrows of
[def-trf-global-operator]. Therefore

$$
[a_X,a_C]_!u=T_c(u):R\Gamma_c(X,K)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_c(X,K)
$$

as an endocorrespondence of $K'$ with support $s$.

*Proper pushforward compatibility.* By
[thm-trf-trace-proper-compatibility],

$$
(a_F)_*\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)=\operatorname{Tr}_b\bigl(T_c(u)\bigr)
\qquad\text{in }\operatorname{Hom}(A_s,\omega_s)=A .
$$

Since $F$ is proper over $s$, the left side is the integral
$\int_F\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)$ by [lem-trf-integration-as-pushforward].

*Point normalization.* The correspondence $b$ is the diagonal of $s$, so
by [lem-trf-trace-class-diagonal-pairing] the trace class
$\operatorname{Tr}_b(T_c(u))$ is the supported pairing
$\langle T_c(u),1_{K'}\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}$, and by
[prop-trf-pairing-point-normalization], applied to the perfect complex
$P=K'$ with $u=T_c(u)$ and $v=1_{K'}$, this pairing is
$\operatorname{tr}_A(T_c(u)\mid R\Gamma_c(X,K))$. Combining the three
displays gives

$$
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(T_c(u)\mid R\Gamma_c(X,K)\bigr)
=\int_F\operatorname{Tr}_c(u).
$$

Fix the global finite-field datum
$p,a,q,k_0,k$, where $q=p^a$, let $X_0$ be a
finite-type
$k_0$-scheme, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let
$\Phi:X\to X$ be the $q$-power scheme Frobenius of
[def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. For every $m\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$,

$$
\operatorname{Fix}(\Phi^m)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
\coprod_{y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})}\Spec k,
$$

a canonical isomorphism of the
fixed scheme with the disjoint union of
one copy of $\Spec k$ for each $\mathbf F_{q^m}$-point of $X_0$.
In particular $\operatorname{Fix}(\Phi^m)$ is finite and etale over
$k$, so every fixed point is simple, and the
graph $\Gamma_{\Phi^m}$ and
the diagonal meet transversally with local multiplicity one: on the
smooth locus the differential $d\Phi^m=0$, so
$1-d\Phi^m$ is the identity.

## Proof

*Step 0: description of the fixed scheme.* By
[def-trf-fixed-scheme] (and [def-trf-graph-correspondence]),
$\operatorname{Fix}(\Phi^m)$ is the equalizer of the two
$k$-morphisms $\Phi^m,\operatorname{id}_X:X\rightrightarrows X$, a
closed $k$-subscheme of $X$, where $\Phi^m$ is the $m$-fold
iterate of the scheme Frobenius of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]:
concretely, it is the closed subscheme of $X$ cut out by the
quasi-coherent ideal sheaf

$$
\mathcal I=\operatorname{Im}\bigl(\mathcal O_X
\xrightarrow{\ \Phi^{m\#}-\operatorname{id}\ }
\mathcal O_X\bigr),
$$

the ideal sheaf generated by the differences
$\Phi^{m\#}(a)-a$, $a\in\mathcal O_X$ (note: the map
$\Phi^{m\#}-\operatorname{id}$ is not a ring homomorphism and its
kernel is not an ideal – the fixed locus is instead cut out by the
ideal generated by its image; this is the equalizer description on
every affine open, and the Zariski-sheafification of the affine
description below). Both the
construction of [def-trf-fixed-scheme] (a fiber product) and this
description are Zariski-local on $X_0$, and the resulting closed
subscheme is compatible with open restriction: the isomorphisms
constructed on the members of an affine open cover glue, because each
is the canonical isomorphism induced by the same sheaf-theoretic
construction. Hence take $X_0=\Spec A_0$ affine, with
$A_0=k_0[t_1,\ldots,t_r]/\mathfrak a$ and
$X=\Spec B$ where $B=A_0\otimes_{k_0}k$.

*Step 1: the affine computation.* By the description of Step 0,
$\operatorname{Fix}(\Phi^m)$ is the closed subscheme of $X$ on
which the iterated scheme Frobenius and the identity agree, i.e. the
closed subscheme $V(\mathfrak b)$ with

$$
\mathfrak b=\bigl(a^{q^m}\otimes1-a\otimes1:a\in A_0\bigr)
\subset B=A_0\otimes_{k_0}k.
$$

Writing $B=k[t_1,\ldots,t_r]/\mathfrak a_B$, with
$\mathfrak a_B=\mathfrak a\,k[t]$ the base change of $\mathfrak a$,
the ideal $\mathfrak b$ of the display has image, in
$B$, equal to the image of

$$
(t_i^{q^m}-t_i:i=1,\ldots,r)+\mathfrak a_B:
$$

indeed, for $a\in k_0[t]$ one has

$$
a^{q^m}-a=\sum_J c_J^{q^m}t^{q^mJ}-\sum_J c_Jt^J
=\sum_J c_J\bigl(t^{q^mJ}-t^J\bigr)
\in(t_i^{q^m}-t_i:i=1,\ldots,r),
$$

because the coefficients $c_J$ of $a$ lie in $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, so
that $c_J^{q^m}=c_J$. The monomial difference belongs to the
displayed ideal by the telescoping identity

$$
\prod_i u_i-\prod_i v_i
=\sum_i\Bigl(\prod_{h<i}u_h\Bigr)(u_i-v_i)
\Bigl(\prod_{h>i}v_h\Bigr),
\qquad u_i=t_i^{q^mJ_i},\quad v_i=t_i^{J_i}.
$$

Each $u_i-v_i=(t_i^{q^m})^{J_i}-t_i^{J_i}$ is divisible by
$t_i^{q^m}-t_i$. Conversely each generator is
$t_i^{q^m}\otimes1-t_i\otimes1\in\mathfrak b$, so the
two ideals have the same image in $B$.

*Step 2: the factorization of the coordinate ring.* Each
polynomial $t_i^{q^m}-t_i=\prod_{\lambda\in\mathbf F_{q^m}}(t_i-\lambda)$
is a product of distinct linear factors over $\mathbf F_{q^m}$, and
$k= \overline{\mathbf F_q}=\overline{\mathbf F_{q^m}}$ is
algebraically closed, so

$$
k[t]/(t_i^{q^m}-t_i:i=1,\ldots,r)
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\prod_{\lambda\in\mathbf F_{q^m}^r}k
=(k[t]/(t^{q^m}-t))\otimes_{k}\cdots,
$$

the isomorphism of the Chinese remainder theorem (canonical: the
idempotents $e_\lambda=\prod_{i}\frac{t_i^{q^m}-t_i}{t_i-\lambda_i}$
times the inverses, and the projection onto the $\lambda$-factor is
$t\mapsto\lambda$); it is the product of $q^{mr}$ copies of $k$,
one for each element of $\mathbf F_{q^m}^r$, i.e. one for
each $\mathbf F_{q^m}$-point of $\mathbf A^r_{k_0}$. In this
product the image of $\mathfrak a_B$ is the tuple of the ideals

$$
\mathfrak a_\lambda=\bigl(f(\lambda):f\in\mathfrak a\bigr)
\qquad(\lambda\in\mathbf F_{q^m}^r),
$$

because the projection $k[t]/\mathfrak a_B\to k$ at the
$\lambda$-factor is the evaluation $f\mapsto f(\lambda)$, and
$f(\lambda)=0$ for all $f\in\mathfrak a$ if and only if
$\lambda\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ (the $\mathbf F_{q^m}$-points of
the closed subscheme of $\mathbf A^r_{k_0}$ cut out by
$\mathfrak a$: $\lambda$ lies in $X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ iff the
face map $\Spec\mathbf F_{q^m}\to\mathbf A^r_{k_0}$ given by
$\lambda$ factors through $\Spec A_0$). Hence the coordinate ring
of the fixed scheme is the product

$$
\prod_{y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})}k,
$$

indexed by the $\mathbf F_{q^m}$-points of $X_0$, and the inverse
image of the unit element of the $\lambda$-factor is the
idempotent $e_\lambda$ of the CRT, so the identification is
canonical, functorial in $X_0$, and compatible with open restriction
(Zariski-descent: the factors of an open subscheme $U_0\subset X_0$
are the $U_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})\subset X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$), which
is the displayed canonical identification

$$
\operatorname{Fix}(\Phi^m)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
\coprod_{y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})}\Spec k.
$$

*Step 3: finiteness, etaleness, and multiplicity one.* The
right-hand side is a disjoint union of copies of $k$, so
$\operatorname{Fix}(\Phi^m)$ is finite and etale over $k$
(each component $\Spec k\to\Spec k$ is an isomorphism, hence finite
etale, and a finite disjoint union of finite etale schemes is finite
etale); each component is the geometric point of $X$ above the
corresponding rational point, and the local ring of the fixed scheme at
that component is $k$ itself, which is to say: the scheme
$\operatorname{Fix}(\Phi^m)\hookrightarrow X$ is a closed immersion
of a zero-dimensional reduced scheme – every fixed point is simple,
with intersection multiplicity one. On the smooth locus at a fixed
point $\bar y$, the differential $d\Phi^m:T_{\bar y}\to T_{\bar y}$
vanishes (in characteristic $p$ the derivative of the $q^m$-power
map is zero: on a chart with coordinates $z_1,\ldots,z_n$, the map is
$z_i\mapsto z_i^{q^m}$, whose Jacobian matrix is
$\operatorname{diag}(q^mz_i^{q^m-1})=0$ as $q^m=0$ in $k$); hence
$1-d\Phi^m$ is the identity of $T_{\bar y}$, the tangent spaces of
the graph $\Gamma_{\Phi^m}=\{(v,d\Phi^mv)\}=\{(v,0)\}$ and of the
diagonal $\{(v,v)\}$ intersect in $0$ (transversality), and the
Beilinson-type multiplicity datum
$\det(1-d\Phi^m)=1\neq0$ is the same conclusion: the graph meets the
diagonal transversally with local multiplicity one, as asserted.

*Recorded in advance* from chapter *The trace formula* of the source.

Fix the global finite-field datum
$p,a,q,k_0,k$, where $q=p^a$, and the
coefficient conventions,
$A=A_{E,n}$, let $X_0$ be
separated of finite type
over $k_0$, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let
$(K,\varphi)\in D^b_{ctf,\mathrm W}(X,A)$ be a strict Weil complex.
Let $u_m:L\Phi^m{}^*K\to K$ be the scheme-Frobenius map of
[def-trf-iterated-weil-map], and consider the graph correspondence
$c=(\operatorname{id}_X,\Phi^m)$ with $u_m$. For each
$y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$, viewed via
[thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points] as a closed-and-open component of
$\operatorname{Fix}(\Phi^m)$, the local
term is

$$
\operatorname{LT}_y(u_m)
=
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(F_{y,m}\mid K_{\bar y}\bigr)
$$

in $A$, where $F_{y,m}$ is the
local geometric Frobenius
operator of [def-trf-frobenius-operators] and $K_{\bar y}$ is the
stalk complex. The degree-dependence of the right-hand side is
[lem-trf-frobenius-degree-formula].

More generally, let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ carry no Weil structure and
let $v:L\Phi^{m*}K\to K$ be an arbitrary, not necessarily invertible,
morphism, for instance the iterate $\psi_m$ of a Frobenius coefficient
morphism $\psi$ of [def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism]. Then for
the graph correspondence $(\operatorname{id}_X,\Phi^m)$ with $v$

$$
\operatorname{LT}_y(v)=\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(v_{\bar y}\mid K_{\bar y}\bigr),
$$

where $v_{\bar y}:K_{\bar y}\cong(L\Phi^{m*}K)_{\bar y}\to K_{\bar y}$
is the stalk map at the fixed point $\bar y$. The first formula is the
case $v=u_m$, whose stalk map at $\bar y$ is $F_{y,m}$
([def-trf-frobenius-operators]). The case needed for the trace formula
is $X_0$ smooth of pure dimension one.

## Proof

The proof follows the curve pieces of [d-curve-pieces]. Fix
$y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$, put $x=y$, $\Phi=\Phi^m$, and let $v$ be
$u_m$ or an arbitrary morphism $L\Phi^*K\to K$ as in the statement. All
morphisms below are separated and of finite type between separated
finite-type $k$-schemes, hence exceptionally admissible at the finite
stage ([rem-ptr-trf-admissibility-12], [thm-sf-preservation-class]).

*Step 0: the fixed point.* By [thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points] the
fixed scheme $\operatorname{Fix}(\Phi)$ is a finite disjoint union of
copies of $\operatorname{Spec}k$, one for each point of
$X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$. So it is proper over $s$ with finitely many
open-and-closed components, the geometric point $\bar x$ is one of them,
a reduced point component, and $\operatorname{LT}_{\bar x}$ is the local
term of [def-trf-local-term] computed as in [lem-trf-local-term-point].

*Step 1: the pieces.* Let $i:\{\bar x\}\hookrightarrow X$,
$j:U=X\setminus\{\bar x\}\hookrightarrow X$, and let
$K^Z=Ri_*i^*K$, $K^U=j_!j^*K$ with the induced maps $u^Z,u^U$ of
[d-curve-pieces] for the coefficient morphism $v$. By
[prop-trf-trace-class-additivity], item (2),

$$
\operatorname{LT}_{\bar x}(v)=\operatorname{LT}_{\bar x}(u^Z)
+\operatorname{LT}_{\bar x}(u^U).
$$

*Step 2: the open piece.* The stalk of the extension by zero at the
point $\bar x\notin U$ vanishes, $(K^U)_{\bar x}=(j_!j^*K)_{\bar x}=0$
([def-weil-extension-by-zero]). The map
$u^U:L\Phi^*K^U\to K^U$ is a Frobenius coefficient morphism for
$\Phi=\Phi^m$ on $K^U$, and it is not required to be invertible.
Hence $\operatorname{LT}_{\bar x}(u^U)=0$ by the zero-stalk vanishing
of [lem-trf-local-term-locality]: item (3) in the smooth-curve setting
of [d-curve-pieces], and item (2) for general $X_0$, the graph of $\Phi$
being contracting at $\bar x$ because
$\Phi^{\cdot}(\mathcal I_{\bar x})\mathcal O_X\subset\mathcal I_{\bar x}^{\,q^m}$
(verified in the proof of item (3) there). This is the only step of the
proof that is not formal: it rests on Varshavsky's
contracting-correspondence theorem, quoted in that lemma.

*Step 3: the closed piece.* By [d-curve-pieces],
$u^Z=[i,i]_!(v_{\bar x})$ is the coefficient pushforward of
[def-trf-coefficient-pushforward] along the proper pushforward diagram
$(i,i)$ from the point correspondence
$c_{\mathrm{pt}}=(\operatorname{id},\operatorname{id})$ on
$\operatorname{Spec}k$, with coefficient $v_{\bar x}$ on $K_{\bar x}$, to
the graph $c=(\operatorname{id}_X,\Phi)$; the closed immersion $i$ is
proper. The fixed scheme of $c_{\mathrm{pt}}$ is $\operatorname{Spec}k$,
and the induced map of fixed schemes
$h:\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Fix}(\Phi)$ is the inclusion of
the component $\bar x$. The proper pushforward compatibility
[thm-trf-trace-proper-compatibility] gives

$$
\operatorname{Tr}_c(u^Z)=h_*\operatorname{Tr}_{c_{\mathrm{pt}}}(v_{\bar x})
$$

with $h_*$ the Borel–Moore pushforward of
[def-trf-borel-moore-pushforward]. Since $h$ is an open-and-closed
immersion, $Lh^*Rh_*\cong\operatorname{id}$ and, by the triangle
identities, the unit $\eta_h$ and the counit $\varepsilon_h$ in the
definition of $h_*$ restrict to identities along $h$. Hence
$\operatorname{Tr}_c(u^Z)|_{\bar x}=\operatorname{Tr}_{c_{\mathrm{pt}}}(v_{\bar x})$
and

$$
\operatorname{LT}_{\bar x}(u^Z)
=\int_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Tr}_{c_{\mathrm{pt}}}(v_{\bar x})
=\operatorname{LT}_s(v_{\bar x})
=\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(v_{\bar x}\mid K_{\bar x}\bigr)
$$

by the point normalization of [prop-trf-pairing-local-decomposition],
the stalk $K_{\bar x}$ being perfect by [fix-lem-finite-tor-perfect].

*Step 4: conclusion.* Steps 1–3 give
$\operatorname{LT}_{\bar x}(v)=\operatorname{tr}_A(v_{\bar x}\mid K_{\bar x})$.
For $v=u_m$ the stalk map $u_{m,\bar x}$ is the local geometric
Frobenius $F_{x,m}$ of [def-trf-frobenius-operators], as recorded in
[d-curve-pieces], which proves the first formula. No step inverts $v$.

attrs.title: Local term of the Frobenius correspondence

objects.body:
Fix the global finite-field datum
$p,a,q,k_0,k$, where $q=p^a$, and the
coefficient conventions,
$A=A_{E,n}$. Let $X_0$ be a
separated finite-type
$k_0$-scheme, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, let
$(K,\varphi)\in D^b_{ctf,\mathrm W}(X,A)$ be a
strict Weil complex whose
underlying $K$ has an
explicit etale-origin
witness, and assume
the exceptional-adjoint admissibility
hypotheses of [def-trf-admissibility] for the structure morphism
and the fixed-point base changes, including those on a chosen
compactification
defined over $k_0$. For every integer $m\geq1$,

$$
\boxed{
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(F_{c,K}^{\,m}\mid R\Gamma_c(X,K)\bigr)
=
\sum_{y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})}
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(F_{y,m}\mid K_{\bar y}\bigr).}
$$

Equivalently, in the closed-point form,

$$
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(F_{c,K}^{\,m}\mid R\Gamma_c(X,K)\bigr)
=
\sum_{\substack{x\in|X_0|\\d_x\mid m}}
d_x\,\operatorname{tr}_A
\bigl(F_x^{\,m/d_x}\mid K_{\bar x}\bigr).
$$

Both sides lie in $A$, and both sums are finite.

## Proof

This is the case $\psi=u_1$ of the coefficient-morphism trace formula
[thm-trf-coefficient-morphism-trace-formula], whose hypotheses are
among those assumed here; that theorem is proved by reduction to curves
(closed subschemes of the affine line, the Weil $!$-pushforward along
the relative Frobenius factorization, and localization), and it uses
no compactification of $X_0$.

The scheme-Frobenius map $u_1=\varphi\circ\kappa_K$ of
[def-trf-iterated-weil-map] is an invertible Frobenius coefficient
morphism of [def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism] (the example there),
and its iterates are the scheme-Frobenius maps $u_m$: both are built by
the same recursion, using the cocycle identity
[lem-trf-iterated-weil-cocycle] for $\varphi^{[m]}$ and the
multiplicativity of $\kappa^{(m)}$ in
[prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison]. By
[prop-trf-graph-frobenius-operator],
$F_{c,m}(u_1)=T_c(u_m)=F_{c,K}^{\,m}$. For
$y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ the geometric point $\bar y$ is fixed by
$\Phi^m$ ([thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points]), and the stalk map
$u_{m,\bar y}=\varphi^{[m]}_{\bar y}\circ\kappa^{(m)}_{K,\bar y}$ is the
local geometric Frobenius $F_{y,m}=\varphi^{[m]}_{\bar y}\circ\tau_{y,m}$
of [def-trf-frobenius-operators], since at the fixed point $\kappa^{(m)}$
induces the stalk transport $\tau_{y,m}$
([prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison]). Substituting into
[thm-trf-coefficient-morphism-trace-formula] gives the boxed formula.
Grouping the rational points above a closed point and applying
[lem-trf-frobenius-degree-formula] and
[lem-trf-local-frobenius-conjugacy] gives the second formula.

attrs.title: Grothendieck–Lefschetz formula over a finite ring

objects.body:
Fix the global finite-field datum
$p,a,q,k_0,k$, where $q=p^a$, and the
coefficient conventions.
Let $X_0$ be a
separated finite-type
$k_0$-scheme, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, let
$K\in D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(X,\Qlb)$ be a
Weil complex, represented by
$(E,K_E)$ with $E/\Ql$ finite in $\Qlb$ and
$K_E\in D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(X,E)$, as in the
common-stage
coefficient construction, with underlying Weil map
$\varphi_E:Lg_\gamma^*K_E\to K_E$ in $D^b_c(X,E)$. The Frobenius operators
$F^{\,m}_{c,K}$ on $R\Gamma_c(X,K)=R\Gamma_c(X,K_E)\otimes_E\Qlb$ and
$F_{y,m}$ on $K_{\bar y}=K_{E,\bar y}\otimes_E\Qlb$ are the scalar
extensions of the $E$-stage operators of $(K_E,\varphi_E)$ of
[prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model]; at the finite levels these
are the operators of [def-trf-frobenius-operators]. No integral Weil
presentation of $\varphi_E$, or of any rescaling of it, is assumed.
Assume only the finite-level hypotheses of [thm-trf-trace-formula-e] for
some lattice of $K_E$: at every level $A_{E,n}$, an explicit etale-origin
witness for its reduction and compactification admissibility.
For every integer $m\geq1$,

$$
\boxed{
\sum_{i\in\mathbf Z}(-1)^i
\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(F_{c,K}^{\,m}\mid H_c^i(X,K)\bigr)
=
\sum_{y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})}
\sum_{j\in\mathbf Z}(-1)^j
\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(F_{y,m}\mid H^j(K_{\bar y})\bigr).}
$$

All vector spaces are finite-dimensional over $\Qlb$, only finitely
many degrees occur, every trace is the image of an $E$-valued trace
along $E\hookrightarrow\Qlb$, and the equality is independent of the
finite field, the representative, and the common overfield.

## Proof

Apply [thm-trf-trace-formula-e] to
$K_E\in D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(X,E)$ with its Weil map $\varphi_E$; that
theorem needs no integral Weil presentation and only the finite-level
hypotheses assumed here. It gives finite-dimensional $E$-cohomology in
finitely many degrees, and the identity holds in $E$ for the
categorical traces and, by the supertrace law
[prop-trf-trace-formal-laws], for the alternating sums of the
traces on compact-support and stalk cohomology. The object $K$ is
represented by $K_E$, so the global cohomology and each local stalk
are the scalar extensions along $E\hookrightarrow\Qlb$ of the
$E$-level ones, and the traces are the images of the $E$-traces, by
the scalar-extension law of [prop-trf-trace-formal-laws] applied
to the summand traces of [def-trf-karoubi-trace] (at the identity
idempotent the summand trace is the ordinary categorical trace); hence
applying the summand trace to both sides of the $E$-identity gives
the displayed identity after scalar extension $E\hookrightarrow\Qlb$.
Independence is [prop-trf-karoubi-independence].

Fix the global finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ and the coefficient
conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], with
$A_n=A_{E,n}$. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme,
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, let $K_\bullet$ be a normalized $A_\bullet$-system on
$X$ and $\psi_\bullet$ a compatible system of Frobenius coefficient
morphisms on it, in the sense of [prop-trf-adic-coefficient-morphism-systems],
with $P_n$, $P_{\bar y,n}$, $P_{\mathcal O}$, $P_{\bar y,\mathcal O}$ as
there; no invertibility of the $\psi_n$ is assumed. At every finite level
$n$ assume the hypotheses of [thm-trf-coefficient-morphism-trace-formula]
for $(K_n,\psi_n)$: an explicit etale-origin witness for $K_n$
([def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]) and the exceptional-adjoint
admissibility of [def-trf-admissibility] for the graph correspondences and
fixed-point base changes on a chosen compactification defined over $k_0$.

1. For every $m\geq1$,
$$
\boxed{\,
\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}\bigl(F_{c,m}(\psi_\bullet)\mid P_{\mathcal O}\bigr)
=\sum_{y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})}
\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}\bigl(\psi_{\bullet,m,\bar y}\mid P_{\bar y,\mathcal O}\bigr)
\,}
$$
in $\mathcal O_E$; that is, $\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}(V_m)=\sum_y
\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}(V_{y,m})$ for any lifts $V_m$ of
$(F_{c,m}(\psi_n))_n$ and $V_{y,m}$ of $(\psi_{n,m,\bar y})_n$.
1. *Lattice form.* Let $K_{\mathcal O}$, $\varphi_E=\varpi^{-N}u$, $\psi_n=u_n\circ\kappa_{K_n}$,
$U_m$ and $U_{y,m}$ be as in [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model]
(so $K_\bullet$ is the reduction tower of $K_{\mathcal O}$), and assume the
finite-level hypotheses above. Then for every $m\geq1$
$$
\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}\bigl(U_m\mid R\Gamma_c(X,K_{\mathcal O})\bigr)
=\sum_{y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})}
