\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}\bigl(U_{y,m}\mid K_{\mathcal O,\bar y}\bigr)
\quad\text{in }\mathcal O_E .
$$

## Proof

*(1).* By [prop-trf-adic-coefficient-morphism-systems], items (1) and (3),
each $P_n$ and $P_{\bar y,n}$ is perfect and the families
$(F_{c,m}(\psi_n))_n$ and $(\psi_{n,m,\bar y})_n$ are compatible; by its
item (2) they have lifts, and by its item (4) the traces of any lifts are
the compatible systems
$$
\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}(V_m)=\bigl(\operatorname{tr}_{A_n}(F_{c,m}(\psi_n)\mid P_n)\bigr)_n,
\qquad
\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}(V_{y,m})=\bigl(\operatorname{tr}_{A_n}(\psi_{n,m,\bar y}\mid P_{\bar y,n})\bigr)_n .
$$
At each level $n$, [thm-trf-coefficient-morphism-trace-formula], applied to
$(K_n,\psi_n)$ under the assumed hypotheses (it requires no invertibility of
$\psi_n$), gives
$$
\operatorname{tr}_{A_n}\bigl(F_{c,m}(\psi_n)\mid P_n\bigr)
=\sum_{y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})}\operatorname{tr}_{A_n}\bigl(\psi_{n,m,\bar y}\mid P_{\bar y,n}\bigr)
\quad\text{in }A_n,
$$
with the stalk endomorphism normalized as there and in
[prop-trf-adic-coefficient-morphism-systems]. The index set
$X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ is finite ($X_0$ is of finite type over $k_0$) and the
same for all $n$, and the reduction $\mathcal O_E\to A_n$ is additive. Hence
$\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}(V_m)$ and $\sum_y\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}(V_{y,m})$
have the same image in every $A_n$, and they are equal because
$\mathcal O_E\to\varprojlim_nA_n$ is injective.

*(2).* By [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model], item (2), the
$\psi_n$ form a compatible system of Frobenius coefficient morphisms on the
reduction tower of $K_{\mathcal O}$; this tower, with the associativity
isomorphisms $K_{n+1}\otimes^L_{A_{n+1}}A_n\cong
K_{\mathcal O}\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_n=K_n$ as $\nu_n$, is a normalized
$A_\bullet$-system of [def-trf-adic-system], its levels lying in
$D^b_{ctf}(X,A_n)$ by hypothesis. For it
$P_{\mathcal O}=R\Gamma_c(X,K_{\mathcal O})$ and
$P_{\bar y,\mathcal O}=K_{\mathcal O,\bar y}$
([prop-trf-adic-coefficient-morphism-systems]). By items (3) and (4) of
[prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model], $U_m$ is the derived limit of
the levelwise operators $F_{c,m}(\psi_n)$ and $U_{y,m}$ that of the
$\psi_{n,m,\bar y}$, i.e. $\mathrm{pr}_n\circ U_m=F_{c,m}(\psi_n)\circ\mathrm{pr}_n$
and likewise for the stalks; so by item (2) of
[prop-trf-adic-coefficient-morphism-systems] they are lifts of the two
compatible families, and (1) gives the identity.

attrs.title: Integral adic trace formula for Frobenius coefficient morphisms

objects.body:
Use the finite coefficient ring
$A=A_{E,n}$. Let $g:Y'\to X$ be a
morphism of finite-type schemes,
let $M$ be a site-perfect complex
in $D(X,A)$, and let $N\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ belong to the
finite-Tor constructible category.
The canonical comparison for
derived pullback and internal Hom
is an isomorphism

$$
Lg^*R\mathcal Hom_A(M,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}
R\mathcal Hom_A(Lg^*M,Lg^*N).
$$

It is natural in both variables and compatible with shifts and
distinguished triangles in $N$.

## Proof

By [def-weil-site-perfect-complex], locally on the site $M$ is
represented by a bounded complex $P$ of finite free $A$-modules.
Writing $M^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_A(M,A_X)$, the termwise finite-free
identity $\operatorname{Hom}_A(P^i,N^j)=(P^i)^\vee\otimes_A N^j$,
with the usual total-complex signs, gives

$$
M^\vee\otimes_A^L N\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_A(M,N).
$$

There are finitely many summands in each total degree. Thus the same
identity computes the derived functors, and it is independent of the
chosen representative: the map is the adjoint of evaluation under the
tensor–Hom adjunction of [def-weil-derived-tensor]. These local
identifications therefore glue. The same argument identifies
$Lg^*M^\vee$ with $(Lg^*M)^\vee$: pull back the finite free complex
and its evaluation map. Monoidality of derived pullback, as in
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], now gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
Lg^*R\mathcal Hom_A(M,N)
&\cong Lg^*M^\vee\otimes_A^L Lg^*N\\
&\cong (Lg^*M)^\vee\otimes_A^L Lg^*N\\
&\cong R\mathcal Hom_A(Lg^*M,Lg^*N).
\end{aligned}
$$

The composite is the canonical comparison, since both have as adjoint
the pullback of evaluation. Evaluation is natural, and tensoring with
a fixed complex is exact; this proves the claimed compatibilities.

attrs.title: Internal Hom versus pullback for a site-perfect first variable

objects.body:
Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type schemes with dualizing complexes as
in [def-trf-dualizing-complex] (so the structure morphism $a_Y$ satisfies
the exceptional-adjoint admissibility of [def-trf-admissibility]), assume
that the product projection $p_X=\operatorname{id}_X\times a_Y:X\times Y\to X$
satisfies it as well, so that $p_X^!$ and the map
$\alpha_{\operatorname{id}_X,a_Y}$ of [def-sf-kv-maps] (ii) are defined, and
let $p_X,p_Y$ be the projections of $X\times Y$. For
$M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, $N\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$, the canonical
comparison of [def-sf-kv-maps] (iv), formed with the geometric operations, is an isomorphism:

$$
\kappa_{M,N}:M\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}D_YN
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
\RHom_A\bigl(p_Y^*N,\,p_X^!M\bigr),
$$

where $D_YN=\RHom_A(N,\omega_Y)$ is the dualizing functor of
[def-trf-dualizing-complex].

## Proof

Apply the external Hom [prop-trf-external-hom] to the pairs
$(A_X,M)$ and $(N,\omega_Y)$, followed by
$\RHom(1,\alpha)$ from [prop-trf-exceptional-kunneth] for the
identification $M\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}\omega_Y\simeq p_X^!M$ of
[def-trf-dualizing-complex]. Their composite is exactly
$\kappa_{M,N}$, and both factors are isomorphisms, so $\kappa_{M,N}$
is an isomorphism.

Fix the global finite-field datum
$p,a,q,k_0,k$, where $q=p^a$, let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type
$k_0$-scheme, and put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. Let
$\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$ and let $K$ be a Weil complex with
coefficients in $\Lambda$ satisfying the hypotheses of
[thm-trf-trace-formula-e] (if $\Lambda=E$) or of
[thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar] (if $\Lambda=\Qlb$). These are
only the finite-level hypotheses (explicit etale-origin witnesses and
compactification admissibility for the reductions of a lattice of an
$E$-representative $K_E$). The Weil map $\varphi_E$ of $K_E$ is an
isomorphism of $D^b_c(X,E)$, but it need not be integral, or invertible
on any lattice after any rescaling. Write
$F=F^{\,1}_{c,K}$ for the global geometric Frobenius on
$H_c^i(X,K)$, and for a closed point $x\in|X_0|$ of degree
$e_x=[\kappa(x):\Fq]$ write $F_x$ for the one-circuit local Frobenius
on the stalk $K_{\bar x}$ (well defined up to conjugation). Put

$$
\det\bigl(1-T^{e_x}F_x\mid K_{\bar x}\bigr)
:=\prod_{j\in\mathbf Z}
\det\bigl(1-T^{e_x}F_x\mid H^j(K_{\bar x})\bigr)^{(-1)^j},
\qquad
L(X_0,K,T)=\prod_{x\in|X_0|}
\det\bigl(1-T^{e_x}F_x\mid K_{\bar x}\bigr)^{-1}.
$$

Then:

1. The product defining $L(X_0,K,T)$ is locally finite for the
$T$-adic topology, and $L(X_0,K,T)\in1+T\Lambda[[T]]$.
1. As formal power series in $\Lambda[[T]]$,
$$
L(X_0,K,T)=\prod_{i\in\mathbf Z}
\det\bigl(1-TF\mid H_c^i(X,K)\bigr)^{(-1)^{i+1}},
$$
the product being finite.
1. If $\dim X_0\leq1$ and $K$ is a sheaf placed in degree zero, then
$H_c^i(X,K)=0$ for $i\notin\{0,1,2\}$, so the product in (2) runs
over $0\leq i\leq2$:
$$
L(X_0,K,T)=
\frac{\det(1-TF\mid H_c^1(X,K))}
{\det(1-TF\mid H_c^0(X,K))\,\det(1-TF\mid H_c^2(X,K))}.
$$
1. For every field embedding $\iota:\Qlb\to\mathbf C$, applying
$\iota$ coefficientwise carries the identity (2) (for $\Lambda=\Qlb$)
to the corresponding identity in $\mathbf C[[T]]$.

## Proof

*Step 0: the determinant–trace identity.* For an endomorphism $G$ of a
finite-dimensional $\Lambda$-vector space $V$,

$$
\det(1-TG\mid V)^{-1}
=\exp\Bigl(\sum_{r\geq1}\operatorname{Tr}(G^r\mid V)\frac{T^r}{r}\Bigr),
$$

by [lem-zl-euler-product-identity] (after extending scalars to
$\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\supseteq\Lambda$, which changes neither side; $\exp$ and
$\log$ are mutually inverse bijections $T\Lambda[[T]]\leftrightarrows1+T\Lambda[[T]]$
carrying sums, including $T$-adically convergent infinite sums, to products). Substituting $T^e$ for
$T$ gives the same identity with $T^{er}$ in place of $T^r$. For a
graded endomorphism of a bounded complex with finite-dimensional
cohomology, taking the alternating product over the degrees gives

$$
\prod_j\det\bigl(1-TG\mid H^j\bigr)^{(-1)^{j+1}}
=\exp\Bigl(\sum_{r\geq1}\Bigl(\sum_j(-1)^j
\operatorname{Tr}(G^r\mid H^j)\Bigr)\frac{T^r}{r}\Bigr).
\tag{$*$}
$$

*Step 1: powers and finiteness.* We argue at the stage $E$, for the
$E$-representative $(K_E,\varphi_E)$ and its operators of
[prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model]. The $\Qlb$-operators are
their scalar extensions ([thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar]), and scalar
extension preserves composition and conjugacy. No integrality of
$\varphi_E$ is used in this step.

*Global powers.* By definition
$\varphi_E^{[m]}=\varphi_E\circ Lg_\gamma^*\varphi_E^{[m-1]}$ after the
composition isomorphisms of the rationalized pullbacks. This is the
cocycle identity of [lem-trf-iterated-weil-cocycle], whose proof uses only
associativity of composition and naturality of the pullback
identifications, so it holds in $D^b_c(X,E)$. The base-change
isomorphisms at the stage $E$ are rationalizations of the integral ones
([prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport]). They are therefore natural,
$g^{*}_{\gamma,c}\circ R\Gamma_c(X,f)=R\Gamma_c(X,Lg_\gamma^*f)\circ g^{*}_{\gamma,c}$,
and compatible with composition,
$g^{*}_{\gamma,c}\circ g^{m-1,*}_{\gamma,c}=g^{m,*}_{\gamma,c}$. Hence

$$
F^1_{c,K_E}\circ F^{\,m-1}_{c,K_E}
=R\Gamma_c(X,\varphi_E)\circ R\Gamma_c(X,Lg_\gamma^*\varphi_E^{[m-1]})\circ
g^{*}_{\gamma,c}\circ g^{m-1,*}_{\gamma,c}
=R\Gamma_c(X,\varphi_E^{[m]})\circ g^{m,*}_{\gamma,c}=F^{\,m}_{c,K_E},
$$

and by induction $F^m_{c,K}=(F^1_{c,K})^m$.

*Local powers.* Consider the proofs of the conjugacy lemma
[lem-trf-local-frobenius-conjugacy] and the degree formula
[lem-trf-frobenius-degree-formula]. They use only four inputs:
(a) the cocycle identity;
(b) the canonical stalk identifications
$(Lf^*M)_{\bar z}\cong M_{f\bar z}$ and the fixed-point identifications
entering $\tau$, natural in $M$ and compatible with composition;
(c) invertibility of the Weil map, for the inverse transports $T_i^{-1}$;
(d) conjugacy invariance of traces.

All four hold at the stage $E$:
(a) as just shown;
(b) the $E$-stage identifications are rationalizations of the integral
ones ([prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport]), hence natural and compatible;
(c) $\varphi_E$ is an isomorphism of $D^b_c(X,E)$ because $K$ is a Weil
complex;
(d) is [prop-trf-trace-formal-laws], item (1), over $E$.

So those proofs apply verbatim to $(K_E,\varphi_E)$. The one-circuit local
Frobenius $F_x=F_{x_{e_x},e_x}$ is well defined up to conjugation by
$E$-linear isomorphisms of stalk complexes. Moreover, for every
$y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ above $x$ ($e_x\mid m$), the operator $F_{y,m}$
on $K_{\bar y}$ is conjugate to $F_x^{\,m/e_x}$ on $K_{\bar x}$ by such an
isomorphism.

*Finiteness.* By the finiteness clause of [thm-trf-trace-formula-e] (and,
for $\Lambda=\Qlb$, scalar extension), the spaces $H_c^i(X,K)$ and
$H^j(K_{\bar x})$ are finite-dimensional over $\Lambda$ and nonzero for only
finitely many $i$, $j$. Hence each local factor lies in
$1+T^{e_x}\Lambda[[T]]$, its determinant being invariant under
conjugation of $F_x$, and the product in (2) is finite.

*Step 2: local finiteness.* A closed point of degree $e$ has
exactly $e$ points of $X_0(\mathbf F_{q^e})$ above it, and
$X_0(\mathbf F_{q^e})$ is finite because $X_0$ is of finite type
([def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]); so for each $N$ only
finitely many $x\in|X_0|$ have $e_x\leq N$. As the factor at $x$ is
$\equiv1\bmod T^{e_x}$, the product $L(X_0,K,T)$ converges
$T$-adically, lies in $1+T\Lambda[[T]]$, and
$\log L(X_0,K,T)=\sum_x\log\det(1-T^{e_x}F_x\mid K_{\bar x})^{-1}$ is
a convergent sum. This is (1).

*Step 3: grouping by closed points.* Let $m\geq1$. The points of
$X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ lie over the closed points $x$ with
$e_x\mid m$, exactly $e_x$ of them over each such $x$. By Step 1,
$F_{y,m}$ on $K_{\bar y}$ is conjugate to $F_x^{\,m/e_x}$ on $K_{\bar x}$
by an isomorphism of complexes of $\Lambda$-vector spaces, for every $y$
above $x$. The induced maps on each $H^j$ are therefore conjugate, and
their ordinary traces agree. Hence the right-hand side of the trace
formula of
[thm-trf-trace-formula-e] (for $\Lambda=E$) or
[thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar] (for $\Lambda=\Qlb$) is

$$
\sum_{y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})}\sum_j(-1)^j
\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(F_{y,m}\mid H^j(K_{\bar y})\bigr)
=\sum_{\substack{x\in|X_0|\\e_x\mid m}}e_x
\sum_j(-1)^j\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(F_x^{\,m/e_x}\mid H^j(K_{\bar x})\bigr).
$$

*Step 4: the identity (2).* Multiply the trace formula by $T^m/m$ and
sum over $m\geq1$. On the cohomology side, $(*)$ applied to
$G=F$ on the complex with cohomology $H_c^i(X,K)$ (Step 1:
$F^m_{c,K}=F^m$) gives the logarithm of the right-hand side of (2).
On the point side, writing $m=re_x$,

$$
\sum_{m\geq1}\frac{T^m}{m}\sum_{e_x\mid m}e_x\,t_x(m/e_x)
=\sum_{x\in|X_0|}\sum_{r\geq1}t_x(r)\frac{T^{e_xr}}{r},
\qquad
t_x(r)=\sum_j(-1)^j\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(F_x^{\,r}\mid H^j(K_{\bar x})\bigr),
$$

the rearrangement being legitimate because only finitely many
$x$ contribute to each coefficient (Step 2); by $(*)$ with $T^{e_x}$ in
place of $T$, the inner sum is
$\log\det(1-T^{e_x}F_x\mid K_{\bar x})^{-1}$, so the total is
$\log L(X_0,K,T)$ (Step 2). Applying $\exp$ gives (2).

*Step 5: curves.* Let $\dim X_0\leq1$ and $K$ a sheaf in degree zero;
the groups $H_c^i(X,K)$ depend only on $K$, so for $\Lambda=\Qlb$ we
may compute them from the $E$-representative, and we may take
$\Lambda=E$. Let $K_{\mathcal O_E}$ be a lattice of $K$ (one exists by
[thm-trf-trace-formula-e]). In
the rational category [def-weil-pbc-rational-category] a morphism
whose cone has cohomology sheaves killed by a power of $\varpi$ is an
isomorphism (on a bounded cone with cohomology killed by $\varpi^N$ in
$b-a+1$ degrees, $\varpi^{N(b-a+1)}$ kills the identity, by the
truncation triangles). The cohomology sheaves $\mathcal H^j$ of
$K_{\mathcal O_E}$ for $j\neq0$ and the $\varpi$-power torsion of
$\mathcal H^0$ vanish after inverting $\varpi$ and, being
constructible, are killed by a power of $\varpi$; so
$K\cong M[1/\varpi]$ for the $\varpi$-torsion-free constructible
$\mathcal O_E$-sheaf $M=\mathcal H^0(K_{\mathcal O_E})/(\text{torsion})$,
and $H_c^i(X,K)=H^i(R\Gamma_c(X,M))\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$. The
levels $M\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_n=M/\varpi^nM$ of the reduction tower of
$M$ are constructible sheaves in degree zero, since $M$ is torsion-free. By
the argument of Step 0 of [thm-trf-trace-formula-e] they lie in
$D^b_{ctf}(X,A_n)$ and form a normalized $A_\bullet$-system. Items (1) and
(2) of [prop-trf-adic-coefficient-morphism-systems] need no Weil
structure, and they give that $P=R\Gamma_c(X,M)$ is represented by a
bounded complex of finite free $\mathcal O_E$-modules with
$P\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_1\cong R\Gamma_c(X,M/\varpi M)$. For a perfect
complex over the discrete valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, the universal
coefficient sequence gives
$\dim_E H^i(P)\otimes E=\operatorname{rank}H^i(P)
\leq\dim_{A_1}H^i(P\otimes^LA_1)$. Finally choose a compactification
$j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ over $k_0$ by [thm-nagata-compactification];
then $\dim\bar X\leq1$ after replacing $\bar X$ by the closure of $X$,
and $R\Gamma_c(X,M/\varpi M)\cong R\Gamma(\bar X,j_!(M/\varpi M))$ by
[lem-trf-compactification-cohomology]. The cohomology of the sheaf
$j_!(M/\varpi M)$ vanishes in negative degrees, and in degrees $>2$ by
[thm-sc-finite-type-torsion-cd] applied over the algebraically closed
field $k$, whose torsion cohomological dimension is $0$ by
[lem-sf-separably-closed-torsion-cd]. Hence $H_c^i(X,K)=0$ for
$i\notin\{0,1,2\}$, which is (3).

*Step 6: the embedding.* A field embedding $\iota$ is a ring
homomorphism; applied coefficientwise it is a ring homomorphism
$\Qlb[[T]]\to\mathbf C[[T]]$, continuous for the $T$-adic topologies,
so it carries the finite product in (2), each determinant (a
polynomial in the matrix entries) and the convergent product
$L(X_0,K,T)$ to the corresponding expressions for the matrices
$\iota(F)$, $\iota(F_x)$. This is (4).

attrs.title: Euler-product form of the trace formula

objects.body:
Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions, $A=A_{E,n}$, $s=\Spec k$, and let $X$ be a
proper finite-type scheme.
Let $c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times_sX$ be an
admissible
cohomological correspondence with
$c_2$ proper and with
fixed scheme
$F=\operatorname{Fix}(c)$ proper over $s$ and with finitely many
open-and-closed components. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$. Then

$$
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(T_c(u)\mid R\Gamma_c(X,K)\bigr)
=
\sum_{\beta\in\pi_0(F)}
\operatorname{LT}_\beta(u)
\quad\text{in }A,
$$

where $T_c(u)$ is the
global operator of
[def-trf-global-operator],
$\operatorname{tr}_A$ the
categorical trace, and the
$\operatorname{LT}_\beta(u)$ are the
local terms. Equivalently, the
categorical trace of the global operator equals the sum of the local
terms over the fixed points. (Source: the Lefschetz–Verdier trace
formula for cohomological correspondences; see Milne, Lectures on Etale
Cohomology, Section 29 (the Lefschetz fixed-point formula for
nonconstant sheaves), with Section 25 for the constant-sheaf case, and
$SGA5$, Expose III. The comparison is assembled here from the
trace-class machinery, the fixed-point localization theorem and the
perfectness of the global operator; see the proof.)

## Proof

The categorical trace on the left is defined because the global
operator $T_c(u)$ of [def-trf-global-operator] is a morphism of
$D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$, hence an endomorphism of a perfect complex,
by [lem-trf-global-operator-perfect]. With this, the
localization theorem [thm-trf-fixed-point-localization] gives

$$
\operatorname{tr}_A(T_c(u)\mid R\Gamma_c(X,K))
=\int_F\operatorname{Tr}_c(u).
$$

The component integration formula
[lem-trf-integration-component-sum] (applicable since each component
$\beta$, being closed in the proper $F$, is proper over $s$) rewrites
the right side as

$$
\sum_{\beta\in\pi_0(F)}
\int_\beta\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)|_\beta\bigr).
$$

Each summand is $\operatorname{LT}_\beta(u)$ by
[def-trf-local-term], which proves the comparison.

Fix the global finite-field datum
$p,a,q,k_0,k$, where $q=p^a$, and the
coefficient conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], with
$A_n=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$. Let $X_0$ be
separated finite-type
over $k_0$ ([def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]), put
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, let
$K_E\in D^b_c(X,E)$ be an object of the
rationalized
$E$-coefficient category ([def-weil-rationalization-karoubi],
[def-weil-pbc-rational-category]), and let

$$
\varphi_E:Lg_\gamma^*K_E\longrightarrow K_E
$$

be an arbitrary morphism of $D^b_c(X,E)$, for instance the Weil
structure of an $E$-Weil complex. No invertibility of $\varphi_E$, no
invertibility of a rescaling $c\,\varphi_E$ on a lattice, and no
integral Weil presentation is assumed. Let $F^{\,m}_{c,K_E}$ on
$R\Gamma_c(X,K_E)$ and $F_{y,m}$ on $K_{E,\bar y}$ be the $E$-stage
Frobenius operators of $(K_E,\varphi_E)$ defined in
[prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model] (the stalk being
$K_{\mathcal O,\bar y}\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$ for a lattice
$K_{\mathcal O}$, as there).

*Lattice and finite-level hypotheses.* Let $K_{\mathcal O}\in
D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ ([def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed])
together with an isomorphism $\alpha:K_{\mathcal O}\xrightarrow{\sim}K_E$
of $D^b_c(X,E)$ be a lattice of $K_E$. One always exists: the objects of
$D^b_c(X,E)$ are those of $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$, so one may take
$K_{\mathcal O}=K_E$ and $\alpha=\operatorname{id}$. Put
$K_n=K_{\mathcal O}\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_n$. Assume at every finite
level $n$ the finite-level hypotheses of
[thm-trf-coefficient-morphism-trace-formula] for $K_n$. These are an
explicit etale-origin witness for $K_n$
([def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]) and the exceptional-adjoint
admissibility of [def-trf-admissibility] for the graph correspondences of
the iterates $\Phi^m$ and the fixed-point base changes on a chosen
compactification defined over $k_0$. They concern $K_n$ and the geometry
of $X_0$ only, not $\varphi_E$; they are the data "assumed at each
finite level" in the source and are not proved here.

Then the $E$-vector spaces $H_c^i(X,K_E)$ and $H^j(K_{E,\bar y})$ are
finite-dimensional and nonzero for only finitely many $i$, $j$, and for
every $m\geq1$,

$$
\sum_{i\in\mathbf Z}(-1)^i
\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(F_{c,K_E}^m\mid H_c^i(X,K_E)\bigr)
=
\sum_{y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})}
\sum_{j\in\mathbf Z}(-1)^j
\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(F_{y,m}\mid H^j(K_{E,\bar y})\bigr)
$$

in $E$. For any clearing of denominators $\varphi_E=\varpi^{-N}u$ on the
lattice, the two sides are $\varpi^{-Nm}$ times the images under
$\mathcal O_E\to E$ of the two sides of the integral identity of
[thm-trf-integral-adic-coefficient-morphism-trace-formula], item (2), and
they agree with the corresponding $E$-valued categorical traces by the
supertrace law over the field $E$ of [prop-trf-trace-formal-laws].

This covers the Weil structure of every $E$-Weil complex. It also covers
Weil maps that are not invertible after any rescaling on any lattice, such
as $\varphi_E=\operatorname{diag}(1,\ell)$ on $E^2$ over
$X_0=\Spec\mathbf F_q$ (the example of
[prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model]). The earlier hypothesis of a
strict integral Weil presentation of some rescaling $c\,\varphi_E$ is a
special case and is no longer needed.

## Proof

*Step 0: the reduction tower.* By
[def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] each $K_n$ lies in
$D^b_c(X,A_n)$, and the cohomological supports
([def-weil-cohomological-support]) of all $K_n$ lie in one interval
$[r,s]$. Each $K_n$ has Tor amplitude in $[r,s]$, hence lies in
$D^b_{ctf}(X,A_n)$. Indeed, let $N$ be an $A_n$-module. The subquotients
$N'$ of the finite filtration $\varpi^iN$ are $A_1$-modules, and
$K_n\otimes^L_{A_n}N'\cong(K_n\otimes^L_{A_n}A_1)\otimes^L_{A_1}N'
\cong K_1\otimes_{A_1}N'$ by associativity of the derived tensor product
($K_n\otimes^L_{A_n}A_1\cong K_{\mathcal O}\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_1=K_1$).
Since $A_1$ is a field, $N'$ is free, so this is a direct sum of copies of
$K_1$, with cohomology sheaves in degrees $[r,s]$. The distinguished
triangles of the filtration give the same bound for
$K_n\otimes^L_{A_n}N$. The associativity isomorphisms
$K_{n}\otimes^L_{A_{n}}A_j\cong K_j$ ($j\leq n$) and the transitions of the
functorial reduction tower of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] make
$K_\bullet$ a normalized $A_\bullet$-system of [def-trf-adic-system]. In
particular $K_{\mathcal O}$ satisfies the hypotheses of
[prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model].

*Step 1: reduction to $\alpha=\operatorname{id}$.* Put
$\varphi_{\mathcal O}=\alpha^{-1}\circ\varphi_E\circ Lg_\gamma^*\alpha:
Lg_\gamma^*K_{\mathcal O}\to K_{\mathcal O}$ in $D^b_c(X,E)$. By induction
on $m$ and functoriality of the rationalized pullbacks,
$\varphi_{\mathcal O}^{[m]}=\alpha^{-1}\circ\varphi_E^{[m]}\circ
Lg_\gamma^{m*}\alpha$. The base-change isomorphisms $g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}$ and
the stalk transports $\tau_{y,m}$ at the stage $E$ are rationalizations of
natural integral transformations ([prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport]),
hence natural. So the operators of
[prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model] for
$(K_{\mathcal O},\varphi_{\mathcal O})$ are
$R\Gamma_c(X,\alpha)^{-1}\circ F^{\,m}_{c,K_E}\circ R\Gamma_c(X,\alpha)$ and
$\alpha_{\bar y}^{-1}\circ F_{y,m}\circ\alpha_{\bar y}$. Passing to
cohomology, these are conjugate to the operators for
$(K_E,\varphi_E)$ by $E$-linear isomorphisms, which changes neither the
dimensions nor the traces. We may therefore assume $K_E=K_{\mathcal O}$
(viewed in $D^b_c(X,E)$) and $\alpha=\operatorname{id}$.

*Step 2: the integral model.* By
[prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model], item (1), choose $N\geq0$ and
an integral $u:Lg_\gamma^*K_{\mathcal O}\to K_{\mathcal O}$ with
$\varphi_E=\varpi^{-N}u$. By its item (2), $\psi_n=u_n\circ\kappa_{K_n}$ is a
compatible system of Frobenius coefficient morphisms on $K_\bullet$, not
necessarily invertible. By its items (3) and (4), the integral operators
$U_m$ on $R\Gamma_c(X,K_{\mathcal O})$ and $U_{y,m}$ on
$K_{\mathcal O,\bar y}$ satisfy

$$
F^{\,m}_{c,K_E}=\varpi^{-Nm}\bigl(U_m\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E\bigr),
\qquad
F_{y,m}=\varpi^{-Nm}\bigl(U_{y,m}\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E\bigr).
$$

By item (2) of [prop-trf-adic-coefficient-morphism-systems], applied to
the reduction tower $K_\bullet$ (for which
$P_{\mathcal O}=R\Gamma_c(X,K_{\mathcal O})$ and
$P_{\bar y,\mathcal O}=K_{\mathcal O,\bar y}$), both complexes are
represented by bounded complexes of finite free $\mathcal O_E$-modules.
Hence $R\Gamma_c(X,K_E)=R\Gamma_c(X,K_{\mathcal O})\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$
([def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]) and
$K_{E,\bar y}=K_{\mathcal O,\bar y}\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$ are bounded
complexes of finite-dimensional $E$-vector spaces, which is the finiteness
assertion.

*Step 3: the integral identity.* The finite-level hypotheses assumed in the
statement are those of
[thm-trf-integral-adic-coefficient-morphism-trace-formula] for
$(K_\bullet,\psi_\bullet)$: they do not involve $\psi_n$. Its item (2)
gives

$$
\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}\bigl(U_m\mid R\Gamma_c(X,K_{\mathcal O})\bigr)
=\sum_{y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})}
\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}\bigl(U_{y,m}\mid K_{\mathcal O,\bar y}\bigr)
\quad\text{in }\mathcal O_E .
$$

*Step 4: rationalization.* Let $\rho:\mathcal O_E\to E$ be the inclusion.
Since $E$ is flat over $\mathcal O_E$, $P\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}E=P\otimes
_{\mathcal O_E}E$ for the complexes of Step 2, and the scalar-extension law
of [prop-trf-trace-formal-laws], item (3), gives
$\rho\bigl(\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}(U_m)\bigr)
=\operatorname{tr}_E\bigl(U_m\otimes E\mid R\Gamma_c(X,K_E)\bigr)$, and
likewise for each $U_{y,m}$ (directly: by the chain-level computation of
[lem-trf-chain-supertrace] over $\mathcal O_E$ and over $E$, both sides
equal $\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(U_m^i\mid M^i)$ for a finite free
model $M$ of Step 2 and a chain representative of $U_m$). By the
supertrace law over the field $E$,
item (4) of the same proposition,
$\operatorname{tr}_E(U_m\otimes E)=\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}
\bigl(H^i(U_m\otimes E)\mid H_c^i(X,K_E)\bigr)$, and likewise for the stalks.
The cohomology functors $H^i$ are $E$-linear on morphisms and the ordinary
trace is $E$-linear, so by Step 2

$$
\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(F^{\,m}_{c,K_E}\mid H_c^i(X,K_E)\bigr)
=\varpi^{-Nm}\rho\Bigl(\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}\bigl(U_m\mid
R\Gamma_c(X,K_{\mathcal O})\bigr)\Bigr),
$$

and likewise
$\sum_j(-1)^j\operatorname{Tr}(F_{y,m}\mid H^j(K_{E,\bar y}))
=\varpi^{-Nm}\rho\bigl(\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}(U_{y,m}\mid
K_{\mathcal O,\bar y})\bigr)$. The set $X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ is finite
($X_0$ is of finite type over $k_0$) and $\rho$ is additive. Applying $\rho$
to the identity of Step 3 and multiplying by $\varpi^{-Nm}$ gives the
displayed identity. The result does not depend on the choice of $(N,u)$:
replacing it by $(N+1,\varpi u)$ multiplies $U_m$, $U_{y,m}$ by $\varpi^m$
and leaves $\varpi^{-Nm}(U_m\otimes E)$ unchanged
([prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model]).

attrs.title: Trace formula over a finite extension

objects.body:
Let $(C,c,u)$ be an admissible correspondence on $(X,K)$, with
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, and let $(f,g):(C,c)\to(D,b)$ be a proper pushforward
diagram of [def-trf-coefficient-pushforward]: $f:X\to Y$ and $g:C\to D$ are
proper and $b_ig=fc_i$ for $i=1,2$. Assume the exceptional admissibility of
[def-trf-kernel-pushforward-maps]. Let
$h:F_c=\operatorname{Fix}(c)\to F_b=\operatorname{Fix}(b)$ be the induced
map, proper by [lem-trf-fixed-map-proper]. Then

$$
h_*\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)
=
\operatorname{Tr}_b\bigl([f,g]_!u\bigr)
\qquad\text{in }\operatorname{Hom}(A_{F_b},\omega_{F_b}),
$$

where $\operatorname{Tr}$ is the trace class of [def-trf-trace-class] and
$h_*$ is the Borel–Moore pushforward of [def-trf-borel-moore-pushforward].
No properness over $s$ of $X,Y,C,D$ and no Cartesian leg square is
required.

## Proof

Write $u'=[f,g]_!u$ and use the notation of
[def-trf-kernel-pushforward-maps].

*Step 1: the trace class in adjoint form.* By [def-trf-trace-class] and the
construction of $\mathfrak t_{c,K}$ in
[lem-trf-trace-map-from-external-duality] (recalled at the end of
[def-trf-kernel-pushforward-maps]), $\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)$ is the
$i_c^*\dashv Ri_{c*}$ adjoint of

$$
T_c:A_C\xrightarrow{\widetilde u}\mathcal H_c(K)\cong Rc^!P_X
\xrightarrow{Rc^!\delta_K}Rc^!R\Delta_{X*}\omega_X
\xrightarrow{\zeta_c^{-1}}Ri_{c*}\omega_{F_c},
$$

that is, $T_c=Ri_{c*}\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)\circ\eta_{i_c}$; similarly
$T_b=Ri_{b*}\operatorname{Tr}_b(u')\circ\eta_{i_b}$. By the definition of the
kernel class, the exceptional adjoint of $\zeta_cT_c$ is
$\delta_K\circ[u]_P:Rc_!A_C\to R\Delta_{X*}\omega_X$, and that of $\zeta_bT_b$
is $\delta_{K'}\circ[u']_P$. (This is the diagonal dictionary of
[prop-trf-pairing-point-normalization], read before restriction to the
diagonal.)

*Step 2: transport along $g$.* For any $\varphi:A_C\to Rc^!M$ with
exceptional adjoint $\varphi^\flat$, the exceptional adjoint of
$\mathsf E\circ Rg_*\varphi\circ\eta_g:A_D\to Rb^!Rq_*M$ is
$Rq_*\varphi^\flat\circ\Xi\circ Rb_!\eta_g$: indeed
$\varepsilon_b\circ Rb_!\mathsf E=Rq_*\varepsilon_c\circ\Xi$ by the definition
of $\mathsf E$, and $\Xi$ is natural. Moreover postcomposition with $Rb^!\psi$
corresponds to postcomposition with $\psi$.

*Step 3: the kernel calculations.* By [lem-trf-trace-source-exchange] and
part (1) of [lem-trf-trace-map-exchange],

$$
\delta_{K'}[u']_P=\delta_{K'}\rho_f\,Rq_*[u]_P\,\Xi\,Rb_!\eta_g
=R\Delta_{Y*}\tau_f\circ Rq_*\bigl(\delta_K[u]_P\bigr)\circ\Xi\circ Rb_!\eta_g .
$$

By Step 1 and Step 2 (with $\varphi=\zeta_cT_c$, $M=R\Delta_{X*}\omega_X$,
$\psi=R\Delta_{Y*}\tau_f$), the right side is the exceptional adjoint of
$Rb^!(R\Delta_{Y*}\tau_f)\circ\mathsf E\circ Rg_*(\zeta_cT_c)\circ\eta_g$, while
the left side is the exceptional adjoint of $\zeta_bT_b$. Hence, using part
(2) of [lem-trf-trace-map-exchange],

$$
\zeta_bT_b
=Rb^!(R\Delta_{Y*}\tau_f)\,\mathsf E\,Rg_*\zeta_c\circ Rg_*T_c\circ\eta_g
=\zeta_b\circ Ri_{b*}\tau_h\circ Rg_*T_c\circ\eta_g ,
$$

and cancelling the isomorphism $\zeta_b$,
$T_b=Ri_{b*}\tau_h\circ Rg_*T_c\circ\eta_g$.

*Step 4: the unit identities.* The units of composite adjunctions are the
composite units ([fix-prop-adjunctions], item 3), and
$gi_c=i_bh$ ([def-trf-coefficient-pushforward]), so, with the composition
isomorphisms of [thm-sf-comp-composition],

$$
Rg_*\eta_{i_c}\circ\eta_g=\eta_{gi_c}=\eta_{i_bh}=Ri_{b*}\eta_h\circ\eta_{i_b}.
$$

Substituting $T_c=Ri_{c*}\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)\circ\eta_{i_c}$ and using the
naturality of $\eta$,

$$
T_b=Ri_{b*}\bigl(\tau_h\circ Rh_*\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)\circ\eta_h\bigr)\circ\eta_{i_b}.
$$

Comparing with $T_b=Ri_{b*}\operatorname{Tr}_b(u')\circ\eta_{i_b}$ and taking
$i_b^*\dashv Ri_{b*}$ adjoints,

$$
\operatorname{Tr}_b([f,g]_!u)=\tau_h\circ Rh_*\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)\circ\eta_h .
$$

The right side is the composite defining $h_*\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)$ in
[def-trf-borel-moore-pushforward] ($\eta_h$, then $Rh_*$ of the section, then
$Rh_*\omega_{F_c}\cong Rh_!Rh^!\omega_{F_b}\to\omega_{F_b}$, which is
$\tau_h$). This proves the theorem. Throughout, $Rc_!$ and $Rb_!$ are
retained, so the proper-support hypothesis of SGA 5, III, Theorem 4.4 is not
imposed.

Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions, $A=A_{E,n}$, and let $Y$ be a
separated finite-type
$k$-scheme with
exceptionally admissible structure
morphism $a_Y$. For the dualizing
complex $\omega_{Y,A}$ and Verdier dual $D_Y$ of
[def-trf-dualizing-complex], let $M\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$.
Then there is a functorial isomorphism

$$
M\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }D_YD_YM,
$$

and the evaluation $\operatorname{ev}_M$ of
[def-trf-dualizing-complex] is the map

$$
\operatorname{ev}_M:D_YM\otimes_A^LM\to\omega_{Y,A}.
$$

## Proof

Finite-stage geometric biduality, [thm-fix-general-biduality],
supplies the double-dual isomorphism on the stated constructible
finite-Tor category, with no additional boundary hypothesis.
Its dualizing object is the one in [def-trf-dualizing-complex],
by uniqueness of the exceptional right adjoint.
The double-dual morphism is the adjoint of evaluation
by [lem-weil-duality-pairing], so its evaluation is the map of
[def-trf-dualizing-complex] displayed in the statement.

attrs.title: Verdier biduality for the dualizing complex

objects.body:
Use the finite coefficient ring
$A=A_{E,n}$, an admissible
correspondence
$c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times_sX$, and
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ in the
finite-Tor constructible category.
Assume also that the total map $c$ and the two projections from
$X\times_sX$ are exceptionally admissible. There is a natural
external-duality isomorphism

$$
R\mathcal Hom_A(p_2^*K,p_1^!K)
\simeq K\boxtimes_A^L D_XK,
$$

where $p_i$ are the projections,
$D_XK=R\mathcal Hom_A(K,\omega_{X,A})$ is the
Verdier dual, and the
external product has this order.
It is compatible with evaluation and with the exceptional
tensor–Hom adjunction, and it yields the comparison

$$
\mathcal H_c(K)\simeq Rc^!(K\boxtimes_A^L D_XK),
$$

where $\mathcal H_c(K)$ is the
trace-class source and
$Rc^!$ is the exceptional
inverse image.

## Proof

Step 1 (the first comparison). Apply the Kunneth–Verdier isomorphism
[thm-trf-kunneth-verdier] of the trace-formula chapter to the case
$X=Y$, $M=N=K$. With the projections $p_1,p_2:X\times_sX\to X$,
its source $M\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}D_YN$ becomes
$K\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}D_XK$ and its target
$\RHom_A(p_Y^*N,p_X^!M)$ becomes
$\RHom_A(p_2^*K,p_1^!K)$, so

$$
\kappa_{K,K}:K\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}D_XK
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
\RHom_A(p_2^*K,p_1^!K)
$$

is the first display, read in the inverse direction.

Step 2 (the second comparison). By [def-trf-trace-class-source],

$$
\mathcal H_c(K)=R\mathcal Hom_A\bigl(Lc_2^*K,Rc_1^!K\bigr) .
$$

Since $Lc_2^*=c^*p_2^*$ and $Rc_1^!=(p_1c)^!=c^!p_1^!$ by the
composition identities of the six-operation package, the exceptional
internal-Hom exchange [lem-trf-exceptional-internal-hom-exchange],
applied to the admissible $c$ with $M=p_2^*K$ and $N=p_1^!K$, gives

$$
R\mathcal Hom_A\bigl(c^*p_2^*K,c^!p_1^!K\bigr)
\cong
c^!R\mathcal Hom_A(p_2^*K,p_1^!K).
$$

Composing with the inverse of Step 1 under $c^!$ yields the second
display.

Step 3 (compatibilities). The isomorphism of Step 1 is $\kappa_{K,K}$,
which by its construction in [thm-trf-kunneth-verdier] is the
adjoint-canonical comparison, hence compatible with evaluation and with
the tensor–Hom adjunction; the exchange of Step 2 is likewise
adjoint-canonical by [def-trf-admissibility]. Both compatibilities
therefore hold.

attrs.title: External duality for the fixed-point trace

objects.body:
Fix a prime $p$, an integer $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, put $q=p^a$,
$k_0=\Fq$, and let $k=\Fbar$ be the
fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$.
Choose a prime $\ell\neq p$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an
algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and
an isomorphism $\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$. Let
$X_0/k_0$ be smooth, proper,
geometrically connected of pure dimension
$d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, and put
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. Let
$a_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the structure morphism, and let
$\gamma=\operatorname{Frob}_q$ and $g_X=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times \operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ be the
geometric Frobenius; let $F$ be the induced
global geometric-Frobenius
operator. Let
$(\Qlb)_X$ be the constant object in the
Weil-complex category on the
small pro-etale site. For each $0\leq i\leq2d$, let

$$
H_c^i(X,\Qlb)=H^i\!\left(Ra_{X!}(\Qlb)_X\right),\qquad
H^i(X,\Qlb)=H^i\!\left(Ra_{X*}(\Qlb)_X\right),
$$

using the ordinary and
compactly supported cohomology functors. Assume
$a_X:X\to\Spec k$ is exceptional-adjoint
admissible at $\Qlb$, and choose a dualizing
Weil complex
$(\omega_X,\theta_{\omega_X})$ with

$$
\operatorname{For}(\omega_X)=Ra_X^!\Qlb,
$$

where $Ra_X^!$ is the
exceptional inverse image
for this admissible structure morphism, and require
$\theta_{\omega_X}$ to be the canonical functorial Weil lift induced by
geometric-Frobenius base change and the adjunction units and counits, rather
than an arbitrary lift. Assume directly that all displayed
cohomology groups are finite-dimensional $\Qlb$-vector spaces equipped with the
induced $F$-actions. Weight predicates for
$(\Qlb)_X$ and for these complexes use the
Weil-complex weight definition; weights for the resulting vector spaces use
finite-dimensional
Frobenius-module weights. Then,
for every $0\leq i\leq2d$, the following five assertions hold:

1. the constant Weil sheaf
$(\Qlb)_X$ is $\iota$-pure of weight $0$;
1. $H_c^i(X,\Qlb)$ is $\iota$-mixed of weights at most $i$;
1. the canonical comparison
$$
H_c^i(X,\Qlb)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^i(X,\Qlb)
$$
is Frobenius-equivariant;
1. the geometric-Frobenius
module $H^i(X,\Qlb)$ is $\iota$-pure of weight $i$;
1. every eigenvalue $\alpha$ of
geometric Frobenius on
$H^i(X,\Qlb)$ satisfies $|\iota(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}$.

## Proof

*Step 1: the main-route purity input.* The constant
$\Qlb$-Weil sheaf $(\Qlb)_X$ is the constant $\Qlb$-sheaf of
[cor-zl-purity-smooth-proper] of the zeta chapter on the smooth,
proper, geometrically connected $X_0$ of pure dimension $d$: the
smoothness, properness, geometric connectedness, coefficient, and
Frobenius data of that corollary are among those fixed in the
statement, and the cohomological family is extended to $\Qlb$ with
the Frobenius operator $F_{\Qlb}$ as in the constant-sheaf setting
there. Hence, for every $0\leq i\leq2d$,
$(H^i(X,\Qlb),F_{\Qlb})$ is $\iota$-pure of weight $i$ in the sense of
[def-weil-frobenius-module-weights] – this is assertion (4).

For assertion (2), apply the general $Rf_!$ weight theorem
[thm-zl-wme-deligne-estimate] to the structure morphism
$a_{X_0}:X_0\to\Spec k_0$ and to $K=(\Qlb)_{X_0}$, viewed as a
complex concentrated in degree $0$. Its only cohomology sheaf is the
constant sheaf, punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $0$ by
[lem-zl-constant-sheaf-weight-zero], so $K\in D_{\le0}(X_0)$ in the
sense of [def-weil-complex-weights]. Hence
$Ra_{X_0!}K\in D_{\le0}(\Spec k_0)$: its degree-$i$ cohomology sheaf,
whose stalk at the unique closed point (with $q_y=q$) is
$H_c^i(X,\Qlb)$ with its geometric Frobenius, is $\iota$-mixed of
weights at most $i$. This is assertion (2); it is the absolute case of
the relative estimate, which bounds $Rf_!$ on every bounded
constructible Weil complex.

In addition, the proper coincidence
$H_c^i(X,\Qlb)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^i(X,\Qlb)$ in the form of
[prop-weil-proper-compact-coincidence] is Frobenius-equivariant,
which is assertion (3), and it transfers the mixed bound of assertion
(2) from $H_c^i$ to $H^i$.

*Step 2: the eigenvalue bound – assertion (5).* By
[def-weil-frobenius-module-weights], $\iota$-purity of weight
$i$ of the Frobenius module $(H^i(X,\Qlb),F_{\Qlb})$ means
precisely that every eigenvalue $\alpha$ of $F_{\Qlb}$ on
$H^i(X,\Qlb)$ satisfies $|\iota(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}$, which is
assertion (5).

*Step 3: the constant Weil sheaf is pure of weight $0$ –
assertion (1).* Let $K=(\Qlb)_X$, with the canonical Weil
structure, and use the two predicates of [def-weil-complex-weights].
The cohomology sheaves of
$\operatorname{For}K$ are $(\Qlb)_X$ in degree $0$ and $0$
elsewhere. The constant sheaf is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight
$0$: its local Frobenius operators are the identities on the
one-dimensional stalks ([def-trf-frobenius-operators]), so every
local eigenvalue is $1$, with $|\iota(1)|=1=q_y^{0/2}$ for the
residue-field base $q_y$, which is the definition of
[def-weil-punctual-weights] (this is [lem-zl-constant-sheaf-weight-zero]). Hence
$\Wt_{\iota,\leq0}(K)$ holds. For the lower predicate, the dual
complex $D_XK$ of [def-weil-complex-weights] is

$$
D_XK=R\mathcal Hom_{\Qlb}\bigl(K,\omega_X\bigr),
\qquad \operatorname{For}(\omega_X)=Ra_X^!\Qlb,
$$

by the choice made in the statement and
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]; the smooth-dualizing
identification [thm-sf-dual-perfect] gives

$$
D_XK\cong(\Qlb)_X^{\vee}(d)[2d]\cong(\Qlb(d))_X[2d],
$$

the coefficient dual $(\Qlb)_X^{\vee}$ of the constant rank-one sheaf
being the constant rank-one sheaf
([def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]), and the twist
$(\Qlb(d))_X$ carrying the canonical Weil structure. Its only
cohomology sheaf, in degree $-2d$, is $((\Qlb(d))_X)$, punctually
$\iota$-pure of weight $-2d$: the local geometric Frobenius acts on
$\Qlb(d)$ by the scalar $q^{-d}$
([def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists]), so every local
eigenvalue is $q^{-d}$ with
$|\iota(q^{-d})|=q^{-d}=q^{(-2d)/2}$, by
[def-weil-punctual-weights]. The weight $0+j$ required at
$j=-2d$ by [def-weil-complex-weights] is therefore available:
$-2d=0+(-2d)$. Thus $\Wt_{\iota,\leq0}(D_XK)$ holds, i.e.
$\Wt_{\iota,\geq0}(K)$, and with $\Wt_{\iota,\leq0}(K)$ the
constant Weil sheaf $(\Qlb)_X$ is $\iota$-pure of weight $0$.
This is assertion (1), and all five assertions of the statement are
established.

For every separated finite-type $X/k$, the natural map

$$
\delta_K:K\longrightarrow D_XD_XK
\qquad(K\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Et},A))
$$

is an isomorphism. Consequently $D_X$ is an exact contravariant
anti-equivalence of $D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Et},A)$.

## Proof

Induct on $d=\dim X$, simultaneously for all algebraically closed
fields of characteristic different from $\ell$. Dimension zero
reduces to finitely many geometric points, since nilpotent thickenings
do not change the etale site. There the assertion is perfect derived
coefficient biduality, [lem-weil-coefficient-frobenius].

By [lem-weil-delta-restriction] the assertion is local on $X$.
We may first choose an affine open and then a proper compactification
$j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$, using
[thm-nagata-compactification], and replace $\overline X$ by the
scheme-theoretic closure of $X$. Its dimension is $d$. Extension by zero
$j_!K$ is bounded constructible with the same Tor interval, as is
checked on stalks. Restriction of its double-dual map is the original
map. It therefore suffices to prove the assertion for proper $X$
of dimension $d$.

Set $\Delta=\operatorname{Cone}(\delta_K)$. Preservation from
[lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata] makes $\Delta$ bounded
constructible. We show that every cohomology sheaf of $\Delta$
vanishes at every nonclosed point $x$. Choose an affine open
$V\ni x$. Since $x$ is nonclosed, $\kappa(x)/k$ has positive
transcendence degree. Among a finite set of algebra generators of
$\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$, some $t$ has transcendental image in
$\kappa(x)$. The resulting map $V\to\mathbf A^1_k$ sends
$x$ to the generic point. Its generic fibre has dimension at most
$d-1$, by the dimension argument of
[lem-fin-coordinate-generic-dimension]: components with constant
$t$ disappear, and a dominant component loses one dimension.
Algebraic field extension preserves this dimension bound.

The induction hypothesis over $\overline{k(t)}$, together with
[lem-weil-geometric-generic-duality], says that the restriction of
$\delta_{K|_V}$ to the geometric generic fibre is an isomorphism.
Every geometric point above $x$ factors through such a fibre after
choosing an algebraic closure of $k(t)$ in its algebraically closed
residue field. Hence $\Delta$ has zero stalk at $x$.
Each of its finitely many cohomology sheaves has constructible support,
and a constructible subset of a Noetherian finite-type $k$-scheme
containing only closed points is finite: in a finite locally closed
decomposition, a positive-dimensional piece would contain a nonclosed
generic point. Thus all the cohomology of $\Delta$ is supported
on one finite set of closed points.

Write $a:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. The direct-image preservation
in [thm-sf-direct-image-tor-amplitude], with
[lem-sf-etale-direct-image-vanishing], makes $Ra_*K$ a perfect
coefficient complex. Its double-dual map is an isomorphism by
[lem-weil-coefficient-frobenius]. Proper compatibility of
evaluation, [lem-weil-delta-proper-pushforward], therefore gives
$Ra_*\Delta=0$. For a sheaf supported on finitely many closed
points over the algebraically closed field $k$, global sections are
the finite direct sum of its stalks and higher cohomology vanishes.
The truncation spectral sequence of [thm-sp-truncation-e2] thus
identifies

$$
H^qRa_*\Delta=\Gamma(X,\mathcal H^q\Delta)
=\bigoplus_x(\mathcal H^q\Delta)_{\bar x}.
$$

Every summand vanishes, so $\Delta=0$. This completes the induction.
Preservation was proved before the induction; together with the natural
evaluation of [lem-weil-duality-pairing], $D_X^2\cong\mathrm{id}$
therefore gives the claimed anti-equivalence.

Let $X_0$ be a smooth, proper, geometrically connected scheme of pure
dimension $d$ over $\Fq$. Put $X=X_0\times_{\Fq}k$, let
$\mathscr X$ be the resulting smooth-proper datum, and let
$P_i=P_i(\mathscr X)$ be the canonical factors of
Definition *Canonical integral cohomological factors*. Then the following
statements hold.

1. The zeta series has both point-counting descriptions
$$
Z(X_0,T)=
\exp\left(\sum_{n\geq1}
\#X_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})\frac{T^n}{n}\right)
=\prod_{x\in|X_0|}(1-T^{\deg(x)})^{-1},
$$
and belongs to $1+T\mathbf Z[[T]]\cap\mathbf Q(T)$.
1. The polynomials $P_i$ are the unique polynomials
$$
P_i(T)\in\mathbf Z[T]
\qquad(0\leq i\leq2d)
$$
with $P_i(0)=1$ such that, for every prime $\ell\neq p$,
$$
\bigl((\mathbf Z[T]\longrightarrow\Ql[T])(P_i)\bigr)(T)=
\det(1-TF\mid H^i(X,\Ql)).
$$
They give the rational factorization
$$
Z(X_0,T)=
\prod_{i=0}^{2d}P_i(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}.
$$
1. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}$ of $\mathbf Q$
and regard $P_i\in\mathbf Z[T]$ inside
$\overline{\mathbf Q}[T]$. For every $0\leq i\leq2d$, every
reciprocal root $\alpha\in\overline{\mathbf Q}$ of $P_i$ is an
algebraic integer
and a $q$-Weil number of weight $i$:
$$
|\tau(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}
$$
for every embedding
$\tau:\mathbf Q(\alpha)\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$. For every ordinary
root $\beta\in\overline{\mathbf Q}$ of $P_i$ and every embedding
$\tau:\mathbf Q(\beta)\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$, one has
$|\tau(\beta)|=q^{-i/2}$.
1. For every $0\leq i\leq2d$, with $b_i=\deg P_i$, and every
prime $\ell\neq p$,
$$
b_i=\dim_{\Ql}H^i(X,\Ql),
\qquad b_i=b_{2d-i},
\qquad b_0=b_{2d}=1,
$$
independently of $\ell$. Moreover
$$
P_0(T)=1-T,
\qquad
P_{2d}(T)=1-q^dT.
$$
In particular $Z(X_0,T)$ has a pole of order exactly $1$ at $T=1$
and, if $d\geq1$, a pole of order exactly $1$ at $T=q^{-d}$.
1. If
$$
D_i=(-1)^{b_i}[T^{b_i}]P_i(T),
\qquad
\chi=\sum_{i=0}^{2d}(-1)^ib_i,
$$
then $d\chi$ is even and, for every $0\leq i\leq2d$,
$$
P_{2d-i}(q^{-d}T^{-1})
=(-1)^{b_i}T^{-b_i}D_i^{-1}P_i(T),
$$
and
$$
Z(X_0,q^{-d}T^{-1})
=\varepsilon q^{d\chi/2}T^\chi Z(X_0,T)
$$
for the sign
$$
\varepsilon=
(-1)^\chi q^{-d\chi/2}
\prod_{i=0}^{2d}D_i^{(-1)^i}
\in\{1,-1\}.
$$

**Status.** Both Lean statements exist and both proofs are `sorry`.
`weil_conjectures` states clauses (ii), (iii) and
(v) for a smooth, proper, geometrically integral $X_0$, phrased
through the three predicates `IsWeilFactorization`,
`WeilFunctionalEquation` and `WeilRiemannHypothesis`, which are
complete definitions; `zetaSeries_rational` states the rationality
assertion of clause (i) for an arbitrary scheme of finite type over
$\Fq$.

## Proof

The hypotheses make $\mathscr X=(X_0,d,X)$ a smooth-proper datum, so all
degreewise factors and Frobenius operators in Definitions
`[def-weil-smooth-proper-cohomological-family]` and
*Frobenius characteristic factors* are available.

*Clause (i).*
Definition [def-weil-point-counts-zeta] is the exponential point-counting
description. Proposition [prop-euler-product] gives the closed-point
Euler product and membership in $1+T\mathbf Z[[T]]$. Proposition
`prop-integral-recovery` gives the factorization by integral
polynomials and hence $Z(X_0,T)\in\mathbf Q(T)$.
This proves exactly the two displayed descriptions and both coefficient
claims in (i).

*Clause (ii).*
Proposition `prop-integral-recovery` applies to the fixed datum and says
that the canonical $P_i\in\mathbf Z[T]$ have constant term one, satisfy

$$
\bigl((\mathbf Z[T]\longrightarrow\Ql[T])(P_i)\bigr)(T)=P_{i,\ell}(T)
=\det(1-TF\mid H^i(X,\Ql))
$$

for every prime $\ell\neq p$, are the unique integral family with those
realizations, and obey

$$
Z(X_0,T)=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}P_i(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}
\quad\text{in }\mathbf Q(T).
$$

These are precisely all assertions of (ii).

*Clause (iii).*
Fix $0\leq i\leq2d$. Proposition
`prop-arithmetic-roots` applies to the polynomial $P_i$ in the fixed
algebraic closure. It states that every reciprocal root is an algebraic
integer and a $q$-Weil number of weight $i$, with the displayed equality
for every complex embedding. The same proposition identifies an ordinary
root $\beta$ with the inverse of a reciprocal root of this same
polynomial $P_i$, and gives $|\tau(\beta)|=q^{-i/2}$. This proves
(iii) without changing the root terminology.

*Clause (iv).*
Fix an integer $0\leq i\leq2d$. For every prime $\ell\neq p$,
Proposition `prop-integral-recovery` gives

$$
b_i=\deg P_i=\dim_{\Ql}H^i(X,\Ql),
$$

so the left-hand side is independent of $\ell$. Proposition
`prop-duality-reciprocity` gives $b_i=b_{2d-i}$, and Proposition
`prop-endpoints` gives

$$
b_0=b_{2d}=1,\qquad P_0(T)=1-T,\qquad P_{2d}(T)=1-q^dT.
$$

Theorem [thm-weil-final-betti] states all of these equalities for the
same datum and, in addition, that $Z(X_0,T)$ has a pole of order exactly
$1$ at $T=1$ and, when $d\geq1$, at $T=q^{-d}$. This is exactly (iv).

*Clause (v).*
The definitions of $D_i,\chi,\varepsilon$ are respectively
Definitions `def-weil-determinant-constants`,
*Euler characteristic*,
and `def-weil-functional-equation-sign`. Proposition
`prop-duality-reciprocity` supplies, for every $i$, the asserted
degreewise Laurent reciprocity. Proposition
*Parity of the functional-equation exponent* verifies that $d\chi/2$ is an
integer. Finally Proposition `prop-functional-equation` proves

$$
\varepsilon\in\{1,-1\},\qquad
Z(X_0,q^{-d}T^{-1})
=\varepsilon q^{d\chi/2}T^\chi Z(X_0,T)
$$

in $\mathbf Q(T)$. Hence all assertions of (v) follow.

The five independently verified clauses are exactly the conjunction stated
in the theorem.

attrs.title: Weil conjectures for a smooth proper variety

objects.body:
Fix a finite field
$k_0=\mathbf F_q$ of characteristic $p$, with algebraic closure
$k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$.
Let $X_0/k_0$ be
smooth, proper and geometrically
connected of pure dimension $d\geq0$, and put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$.
Let $P_i\in\mathbf Z[T]$, $0\leq i\leq2d$, be the
integral Frobenius factors
provided by [thm-weil-final-integrality]: $P_i(0)=1$, and for
every $\ell\neq p$,

$$
P_i^{(\ell)}(T)=\det(1-TF_{i,\ell}\mid H^i(X,\mathbf Q_\ell)),
$$

where $F_{i,\ell}$ is
geometric Frobenius
on ordinary cohomology,
and $P_i^{(\ell)}$ means coefficientwise extension
$\mathbf Z\to\mathbf Q_\ell$.
For every integer $i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$, set
$b_i=\deg P_i$; these are the
Betti numbers. Then

$$
b_i=\dim_{\Ql}H^i(X,\Ql)
\quad\text{for every prime }\ell\neq p,
\qquad b_i=b_{2d-i},
\qquad b_0=b_{2d}=1,
$$

where $H^i(X,\Ql)$ is the
ordinary cohomology group;
so the first dimension is independent of $\ell$. Moreover

$$
P_0(T)=1-T,
\qquad
P_{2d}(T)=1-q^dT.
$$

In particular, the rational function
$Z(X_0,T)=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}P_i(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}\in\mathbf Q(T)$ of
[thm-weil-final-integrality] has a pole of order exactly $1$ at $T=1$
and, if $d\geq1$, a pole of order exactly $1$ at $T=q^{-d}$.

## Proof

The definition of the common Betti numbers is
[def-weil-betti-numbers]. The comparison in
[prop-weil-betti-comparison] gives
$b_i=\dim_{\Ql}H^i(X,\Ql)$, independently of $\ell$. The perfect pairing
has its canonical exceptional-inverse-image orientation supplied by
[thm-weil-six-operations] for the smooth proper structure morphism;
the duality interface [thm-weil-poincare-duality] and the pairing assembled in
[prop-poincare-pairing] together give $b_i=b_{2d-i}$; the endpoint calculation
[prop-endpoints] gives $b_0=b_{2d}=1$ and the two endpoint factors,
identified with $P_0,P_{2d}$ by [prop-integral-recovery].

For the poles, use the factorization
$Z(X_0,T)=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}P_i(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}$ of
[thm-weil-final-integrality]. Over $\overline{\mathbf Q}$ write
$P_i(T)=\prod_{r=1}^{b_i}(1-\alpha_{i,r}T)$, the $\alpha_{i,r}$ being the
reciprocal roots. For $c\in\overline{\mathbf Q}^\times$, the order of
vanishing of $P_i$ at $T=c^{-1}$ is the number of $r$ with
$\alpha_{i,r}=c$. By [thm-weil-final-rh], every $\alpha_{i,r}$ satisfies
$|\tau(\alpha_{i,r})|=q^{i/2}$ for every complex embedding $\tau$.

Take $c=1$. Since $q>1$, $q^{i/2}=1$ only for $i=0$, so
$P_i(1)\neq0$ for $1\leq i\leq2d$, while $P_0(T)=1-T$ vanishes to
order exactly $1$ at $T=1$. As $P_0$ occurs with exponent $(-1)^{0+1}=-1$,
$Z(X_0,T)$ has a pole of order exactly $1$ at $T=1$.

Take $c=q^d$ with $d\geq1$. Since $|\tau(q^d)|=q^d=q^{i/2}$ only for
$i=2d$, one has $P_i(q^{-d})\neq0$ for $0\leq i<2d$ (for $i=0$ this is
also visible from $P_0(q^{-d})=1-q^{-d}\neq0$), while
$P_{2d}(T)=1-q^dT$ vanishes to order exactly $1$ at $T=q^{-d}$. As
$2d$ is even, $P_{2d}$ occurs with exponent $-1$, so $Z(X_0,T)$ has a
pole of order exactly $1$ at $T=q^{-d}$. (For $d=0$ the two points
coincide and $Z(X_0,T)=(1-T)^{-1}$.)

Fix a finite field
$k_0=\mathbf F_q$ of characteristic $p$, with algebraic closure
$k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$.
Let $X_0/k_0$ be
smooth, proper and geometrically
connected of pure dimension $d\geq0$, and put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$.
Let $P_i\in\mathbf Z[T]$, $0\leq i\leq2d$, be the
integral Frobenius factors
provided by [thm-weil-final-integrality]: $P_i(0)=1$, and for
every $\ell\neq p$,

$$
P_i^{(\ell)}(T)=\det(1-TF_{i,\ell}\mid H^i(X,\mathbf Q_\ell)),
$$

where $F_{i,\ell}$ is
geometric Frobenius
on ordinary cohomology,
and $P_i^{(\ell)}$ means coefficientwise extension
$\mathbf Z\to\mathbf Q_\ell$.
Let $Z(X_0,T)$ denote the
point-count zeta series.
If
$P(T)=\sum_{m\geq0}c_mT^m$, write
$[T^m]P(T)=c_m$. For every integer $i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$, define the
determinant constants

$$
D_i=(-1)^{b_i}[T^{b_i}]P_i(T),
$$

with $b_i=\deg P_i$ as in [thm-weil-final-betti], and set the Euler
characteristic

$$
\chi=\sum_{i=0}^{2d}(-1)^ib_i.
$$

Then $d\chi$ is even and, for every integer $i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$,

$$
P_{2d-i}(q^{-d}T^{-1})
=(-1)^{b_i}T^{-b_i}D_i^{-1}P_i(T),
$$

and

$$
Z(X_0,q^{-d}T^{-1})
=\varepsilon q^{d\chi/2}T^\chi Z(X_0,T)
$$

for the sign

$$
\varepsilon=
(-1)^\chi q^{-d\chi/2}
\prod_{i=0}^{2d}D_i^{(-1)^i}
\in\{1,-1\}.
$$

The sign $\varepsilon$ is the
normalized functional-equation
sign.

## Proof

Use the determinant definitions in [def-weil-determinant-constants].
The reciprocity calculation [prop-duality-reciprocity], whose duality
input is [prop-poincare-pairing], gives

$$
P_{2d-i}(q^{-d}T^{-1})
=(-1)^{b_i}T^{-b_i}D_i^{-1}P_i(T),
\qquad D_iD_{2d-i}=q^{db_i}.
$$

Pairing $i$ with $2d-i$, and using the middle-degree alternating-form
case in [prop-duality-reciprocity], shows that $d\chi$ is even. Thus
the sign is defined by [def-weil-functional-equation-sign]. Finally,
substitution into the rational factorization of the
[def-weil-point-counts-zeta] zeta series and reindexing gives exactly
the functional-equation identity in [prop-functional-equation],
with $\chi$ and $b_i$ as in [def-weil-betti-numbers].

Fix a finite field
$k_0=\mathbf F_q$ of characteristic $p$, with algebraic closure
$k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$.
Let $X_0/k_0$ be
smooth, proper and geometrically
connected of pure dimension $d\geq0$, and put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$.
For every prime $\ell\neq p$, let $F_{i,\ell}$ be the
geometric Frobenius
on the cohomology
$H^i(X,\mathbf Q_\ell)$.
Let $Z(X_0,T)$ be the
point-count zeta series.
Then, for every integer $i$ with
$0\leq i\leq2d$, there is a
unique polynomial

$$
P_i(T)\in\mathbf Z[T]
$$

with $P_i(0)=1$ such that, for every prime $\ell\neq p$, its
coefficientwise extension $P_i^{(\ell)}(T)\in\Ql[T]$ satisfies

$$
P_i^{(\ell)}(T)=
\det(1-TF_{i,\ell}\mid H^i(X,\Ql)).
$$

Call these the
integral Frobenius factors and
retain this
coefficientwise-extension notation.
They give the rational factorization

$$
Z(X_0,T)=
\prod_{i=0}^{2d}P_i(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}},
$$

and this factorization is independent of the chosen $\ell$.

## Proof

For each $\ell$, [prop-weight-purity-roots] fixes the absolute
value of every reciprocal root of the $P_{i,\ell}$, so that the
reciprocal roots are separated by their weights, and
[prop-weight-separation] separates the odd and
even parity products. The terminal realization-independence interface
[thm-weil-realization-independence] supplies the integral factors and
their scalar identities, while [thm-weil-realization-independence] supplies
the unique intrinsic
$q$-Weil weight of every reciprocal root and the Galois-stability of the
resulting root multisets; these are therefore supplied facts rather than
additional hypotheses. Thus the hypotheses of the stratum statements
[prop-galois-weight-strata-integrality] and
[prop-galois-weight-strata-identification] are met. Applying
[prop-weil-zeta-normalized-presentation] to the fixed normalized
fraction and then these two statements to each weight stratum produces
integral polynomials. The common realization and uniqueness are exactly
[prop-integral-recovery]; its scalar-extension statement is the
displayed determinant formula, so the product identity follows.

attrs.title: Weil conjectures II: integral Frobenius factors

objects.body:
Fix a finite field
$k_0=\mathbf F_q$ of characteristic $p$, with algebraic closure
$k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$.
Let $X_0/k_0$ be
smooth, proper and geometrically
connected of pure dimension $d\geq0$, and put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$.
For an indeterminate $T$, use the
point-count zeta series

$$
Z(X_0,T)=\exp\left(\sum_{n\geq1}
\#X_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})\frac{T^n}{n}\right).
$$

Here $|X_0|$ is the set of closed points and
$\deg(x)=[\kappa(x):k_0]$. Then

$$
Z(X_0,T)\in1+T\mathbf Z[[T]]\cap\mathbf Q(T),
\qquad
Z(X_0,T)=\prod_{x\in|X_0|}(1-T^{\deg(x)})^{-1}.
$$

## Proof

The exponential definition and the closed-point product are
[def-weil-point-counts-zeta], [prop-euler-product]. The trace calculation
[prop-every-iterate-trace], together with the determinant identity
[prop-trace-determinant], gives a factorization over $\Ql(T)$. By
[prop-weil-rationality-criterion], this rational expression gives finite Hankel
rank over $\Ql$; every finite Hankel minor has integral entries, so the
same rank bound holds over $\mathbf Q$. Thus the finite-rank hypothesis of
[prop-rational-descent] is verified, and its rationality statement
descends the factorization to $\mathbf Q(T)$; the integrality of the
point-count coefficients is the exponential definition above, so the two
asserted forms hold.

attrs.title: Weil conjectures I: rationality and Euler product

objects.body:
Fix a finite field
$k_0=\mathbf F_q$ of characteristic $p$, with algebraic closure
$k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$.
Let $X_0/k_0$ be
smooth, proper and geometrically
connected of pure dimension $d\geq0$, and put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$.
Let $P_i\in\mathbf Z[T]$, $0\leq i\leq2d$, be the
integral Frobenius factors
provided by [thm-weil-final-integrality]: $P_i(0)=1$, and for
every $\ell\neq p$,

$$
P_i^{(\ell)}(T)=\det(1-TF_{i,\ell}\mid H^i(X,\mathbf Q_\ell)),
$$

where $F_{i,\ell}$ is
geometric Frobenius
on ordinary cohomology,
and $P_i^{(\ell)}$ means coefficientwise extension
$\mathbf Z\to\mathbf Q_\ell$.
For every integer $i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$, put
$r_i=\deg P_i$ and $P_i^\#(U)=U^{r_i}P_i(U^{-1})$. A
reciprocal root
$\alpha\in\overline{\mathbf Q}$ means a root of $P_i^\#$; put
$\beta=\alpha^{-1}$, the corresponding
ordinary root. Every
reciprocal root $\alpha$ is a
algebraic integer and a
Weil number for $q$ of weight $i$:

$$
|\tau(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}
$$

for every embedding $\tau:\mathbf Q(\alpha)\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$. Then
$|\tau(\beta)|=q^{-i/2}$ for every embedding
$\tau:\mathbf Q(\beta)\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$.

## Proof

The reversed polynomial is monic because the constant coefficient is one and
the coefficients are integral by [prop-integral-recovery]; hence its
roots are algebraic integers. The root/eigenvalue identification is
[def-weil-ordinary-reciprocal-roots]. For a root $\alpha$,
[lem-embedding-extension] extends every embedding of
$\mathbf Q(\alpha)$ to an isomorphism $\Qlb\simeq\mathbf C$, and
[prop-weight-purity-roots] gives
$|\tau(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}$. In the terminology of
[def-weil-numbers], this is precisely the $q$-Weil condition; taking
inverses gives the ordinary-root bound. The arithmetic formulation and the
degree independence are also recorded in [prop-arithmetic-roots] and
[prop-weil-realization-independent-degrees]; the
underlying purity interface is the boundary statement
[thm-weil-deligne-purity].

Fix the finite-field datum
$p,a,q,k_0,k$, where $q=p^a$, and choose a prime $\ell\neq p$;
write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of
$\Ql$, and let $Y_0$ be a
separated finite-type
$k_0$-scheme and put $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$. Let
$K\in D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(Y,\Qlb)$ be a
Weil complex; choose a finite
extension $E/\Ql$ contained in $\Qlb$ and a model
$K_E\in D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(Y,E)$ with scalar extension
$K_E\otimes_E\Qlb=K$. These coefficients are formed on the
small pro-etale site, and the
common-stage
coefficient construction supplies the scalar extension. Use the
geometric Frobenius convention; the induced
cohomological action $F$ is the
global geometric-Frobenius
action. Use the
local Frobenius operators and the
compact-support cohomology
defined for this complex.
For every integer $n\geq1$ and each point
$x\in Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$, choose a
geometric point
$\bar x\to Y$ over $x$, iterate its local Weil isomorphism $n$ times,
and write $K_{E,\bar x}= L\bar x^*\operatorname{For}(K_E)$, using the
derived pullback. The trace
identity is
understood after mapping the left-hand $E$-valued traces to $\Qlb$ along
the chosen inclusion $E\hookrightarrow\Qlb$, and is explicitly

$$
\sum_{x\in Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})}\sum_{j\in\mathbf Z}(-1)^j
\Tr\bigl(F_x^{(n)}\mid
\mathcal H^j(\operatorname{For}K_E)_{\bar x}\bigr)
=
\sum_{i\in\mathbf Z}(-1)^i\Tr(F^n\mid H_c^i(Y,K)).
$$

For $K_E=E_Y$, so that $K=(\Qlb)_Y$, and
proper $Y_0$, the
point-count convention specializes to

$$
\#Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})
=\sum_{i\in\mathbf Z}(-1)^i\Tr(F^n\mid H^i(Y,\Qlb)).
$$

Here $F_x^{(n)}$ and $K_{\bar x}$ are the
local Frobenius and stalk
constructions, and $H_c^i$ is
compact-support cohomology.

## Proof

*Step 1: the identity.* The local data of the interface are the
local Frobenius operators $F_x^{(n)}$ and the stalk complexes
$K_{\bar x}=L\bar x^*\operatorname{For}(K_E)$ of
[def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], computed with the derived
pullback of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and traced
alternately over the cohomology sheaves of
[def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]; the
global side is the compact-support cohomology of
[def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] with the geometric-Frobenius
operator of [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius]. The identity
is the trace formula of the trace-formula chapter: at the finite coefficient stage
it is [thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-finite-ring] (whose finite
ring, finite field, and trace-class hypotheses are the ones recorded in
the interface), the $E$-valued form is [thm-trf-trace-formula-e],
and the $\Qlb$-form over the common-stage coefficients of
[def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] is
[thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar]; the local terms are the
fixed-point and local-term computations of
[thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points] and
[thm-trf-frobenius-local-term] through the
[thm-trf-lefschetz-verdier] comparison on the projective line, in the
trace-formula chapter's reduction to curves (affine line, Weil
$!$-pushforward along the relative Frobenius, localization),
with the trace classes of
[def-trf-karoubi-trace] and the independence of
[prop-trf-karoubi-independence]. This step inherits the inputs of
the finite-ring trace formula, the construction of the Verdier local trace
and its compatibility with extension by zero to the projective line, both
of which are proved in the trace-formula chapter.
The properness hypothesis in the Lefschetz–Verdier comparison cannot be
dropped for an arbitrary correspondence on a non-proper scheme.
The displayed identity,
understood after the mapping of the $E$-valued traces along
$E\hookrightarrow\Qlb$, is exactly the one of
[thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar] transcribed to the
interface's notation, and the induced Frobenius operators on the
geometric stalks are those of the local Frobenius construction
[def-trf-frobenius-operators].

*Step 2: the point-count specialization.* For
$K_E=E_Y$, $K=(\Qlb)_Y$, and proper $Y_0$, the
interface's constant-sheaf clause is [cor-trf-point-counting],
whose second form replaces compact-support by ordinary cohomology via
the proper coincidence of [prop-weil-proper-compact-coincidence];
the point-count convention is the one of
[def-weil-point-counts-zeta].

*Step 3: the determinant form.* In the smooth-proper
geometrically connected case the same trace formula is the input of
the trace-to-determinant identity [thm-zl-lefschetz-weil-identity]
of the zeta chapter, which converts the per-iterate point counts into the
determinant factorization of the zeta series; this is the form used
in the final theorem's trace-to-determinant step.

If a triangulated category $\mathcal T$ has a bounded t-structure, then
$\mathcal T$ is idempotent complete: every idempotent $e:K\to K$ of $\mathcal
T$ splits, and the canonical fully faithful functor $\mathcal T\to\Kar(\mathcal
T)$ of [def-weil-karoubi-envelope] is an exact equivalence.

(*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this form: Stacks has no
t-structure (hence no bounded t-structure and no heart) and no idempotent
completion of a triangulated category; its Karoubianity entries are the
definition of the Karoubian property (Definition 12.4.1, Tag
[09SG](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09SG)), the splitting criterion
of Lemma 12.4.2 (Tag [09SH](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09SH)) and
the criteria of Lemma 12.4.3 (Tag
[05QV](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05QV): countable products and
kernels of maps which have a right inverse, or dually countable coproducts
and cokernels of maps which have a left inverse), which are sufficient
conditions of a different kind and are not stated for triangulated
categories. The blueprint adds the Karoubianity of a triangulated category
carrying a bounded t-structure, the input used for the finite-stage and
$\Qlb$ coefficient categories of this manuscript.*)

## Proof

By [lem-weil-karoubi-envelope-triangulated] the envelope $\mathcal
T^\natural=\Kar(\mathcal T)$ of [def-weil-karoubi-envelope] is triangulated
and, by [lem-weil-envelope-tstructure], carries the extended t-structure
$((\mathcal T^\natural)^{\le0},(\mathcal T^\natural)^{\ge0})$, which is
bounded because every object of $\mathcal T^\natural$ is a retract of an
object of $\mathcal T$, of finite t-amplitude in the bounded t-structure of
$\mathcal T$. We show that every $Y\in\mathcal T^\natural$ is isomorphic to
an object of $\mathcal T$; full faithfulness of $\mathcal T\to\mathcal
T^\natural$, which is [lem-weil-karoubi-envelope-fully-faithful], then makes
it an equivalence, and every idempotent of $\mathcal T$ splits because its
image in $\mathcal T^\natural$ splits in the envelope that is idempotent
complete by [lem-weil-karoubi-envelope-idempotent-complete], and a splitting
transported back through the equivalence splits it in $\mathcal T$.

Since the extended t-structure is bounded, replacing $Y$ by a shift (which
preserves the property of being isomorphic to an object of $\mathcal T$), we
may assume $Y\in(\mathcal T^\natural)^{\ge0}$. Let $n\ge0$ be minimal with
$Y\in(\mathcal T^\natural)^{\le n}$, and argue by induction on $n$.

If $n=0$, then $Y$ lies in the heart of $\mathcal T^\natural$, which by
[lem-weil-envelope-tstructure] is equivalent to $\Kar(\mathcal H(\mathcal
T))$; by [prop-weil-heart-abelian] the heart $\mathcal H(\mathcal T)$ is
abelian and hence idempotent complete, so $\Kar(\mathcal H(\mathcal
T))=\mathcal H(\mathcal T)$ via the canonical functor, and $Y$ is isomorphic
to an object of $\mathcal H(\mathcal T)\subset\mathcal T$.

Assume $n>0$. The top truncation triangle of [def-weil-t-structure] in
$\mathcal T^\natural$ is

$$
 A:=\tau^{\le n-1}Y\longrightarrow Y\longrightarrow
 B:=\mathcal H^n(Y)[-n]\longrightarrow A[1],
$$

with $A\in(\mathcal T^\natural)^{\ge0}\cap(\mathcal T^\natural)^{\le n-1}$
(the truncation triangle and $\mathcal T^\natural$'s $\ge0$-part being closed
under kernels in the triangulated sense: $Y,B\in(\mathcal T^\natural)^{\ge0}$
and the connecting morphism argument gives $A\in(\mathcal
T^\natural)^{\ge0}$). By the induction hypothesis $A$ is isomorphic to an
object of $\mathcal T$. By [lem-weil-envelope-tstructure] the object $\mathcal
H^n(Y)$ lies in the heart of $\mathcal T^\natural$, which is equivalent to
$\mathcal H(\mathcal T)$ by the $n=0$ case; hence $B$ is isomorphic to an
object of $\mathcal T$. Since $\mathcal T\to\mathcal T^\natural$ is fully
faithful, the connecting morphism $\delta:B\to A[1]$ is the image of a
morphism of $\mathcal T$. Complete $\delta$ to a distinguished triangle in
$\mathcal T$ and rotate it to obtain

$$
 A\longrightarrow C\longrightarrow B\overset{\delta}{\longrightarrow}A[1]
$$

with the displayed connecting morphism $\delta$. This triangle is
distinguished in $\mathcal T^\natural$ as well. It and the truncation
triangle are cone triangles for the same morphism $\delta$ in $\mathcal
T^\natural$, so by uniqueness of cones (any two cone triangles of a morphism
are isomorphic by a morphism of triangles whose first two components are
identities) there is an isomorphism of triangles fixing $A$ and $B$; in
particular $Y\cong C$ in $\mathcal T^\natural$, with $C\in\mathcal T$. This
completes the induction and the proof.

Let $\square$ be the cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with
$X,Y,X',Y'$ noetherian of finite dimension, $f$ and $f'$ proper, and suppose
there is a positive integer $N$ annihilating $A/I$ which is invertible on
all four schemes. Assume that the geometric fibers of $f$ have dimension at
most $e\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$. Then
$$
 \mathrm{AMP}(\square;2e),\qquad\mathrm{WIT}(\square),\qquad\mathrm{TOW}(\square)
$$
of [def-weil-pbc-finite-level-amplification],
[def-weil-pbc-witness-compatibility] and [def-weil-pbc-tower-preservation]
all hold.

*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this assembly: the ingredients
are the proper finiteness theorem of SGA 4 1/2, whose Stacks amplitude form
is Lemma 59.92.2 ([Tag 095U](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/095U):
$R^qf_*=0$ for $q>2n$ and abelian torsion coefficients, all fibres of
dimension $\le n$) and whose compact-support form is Theorem 63.14.5 ([Tag
0GL0](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0GL0): constructibility of
$Rf_!K$ for $K\in D^+_{tors,c}$), together with Definition 61.29.1 ([Tag
09C1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C1)), Proposition 61.29.7 ([Tag
09C7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C7)) and the reduction-tower
bounds of Lemma 61.29.2 ([Tag
09C2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C2)); the blueprint adds the
simultaneous assertion of $\mathrm{AMP}$, $\mathrm{WIT}$ and $\mathrm{TOW}$
for a proper square with fibres of dimension at most $e$.

## Proof

*step (a), AMP.* In the quotient datum of the adic coefficient datum, the
condition $N(A/I)=0$ means $N\in I$. Hence $N^nP_n=0$, and $N^n$ is
invertible on the four schemes for every $n\geq1$. The geometric fibers of
$f'$ are base changes of those of $f$, hence of dimension at most $e$, so
[thm-weil-pbc-direct-image-finiteness-proper] gives
$\mathrm{FIN}(f,P_n;2e)$ and $\mathrm{FIN}(f',P_n;2e)$ for every $n\geq1$,
i.e. clause (i) of [def-weil-pbc-finite-level-amplification]; clause (ii) is
[lem-weil-pbc-pullback-preserves-bounded-constructible] for the two
pullbacks.

*step (b), WIT.* The finite-level functors commute with the normalization
isomorphisms for $P_{n+1}\to P_n$: for the direct images this is the
projection-formula compatibility of the reduction maps (the tensor with the
perfect $P_n$ commuting with $Rf_{*,n+1}$), and for the pullbacks it is the
tensor compatibility of inverse image with the quotient maps. A compatible
etale-origin witness [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]
$K_n\cong\nu_X^*L_n$ is transported: for the direct images by
$$
 Rf_{*,n}K_n\cong Rf_{*,n}\nu_X^*L_n\cong\nu_Y^*Rf_{\Et,*}L_n
$$
of [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] (the quotient tower being built
from the same $L_n$), and for the pullbacks by
[lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]; the compatibility of the transported
witnesses is the above commutation with the normalizations. Hence
$\mathrm{WIT}(\square)$.

*step (c), TOW.* A uniformly bounded constructible tower is compatibly
witnessed on the local models $L_{\alpha j}$ supported in $[d_0,d_1]$ with
finite lisse cohomology reductions, and step (b) transports the witnesses.
The levelwise direct images are therefore etale-origin; their reduction
cohomology is bounded constructible by
[thm-weil-pbc-direct-image-finiteness-proper] with the amplitude containment
of [prop-weil-pbc-amplification-consequences], and the local models are
obtained from the etale-origin descriptions: a finite lisse module is finite
locally constant, which is exactly what the tower condition requires, while
no freeness is needed or available, a finite module over a finite local ring
being possibly non-free (for instance $\mathbf Z/2$ over $\mathbf Z/4$). The
pullback side is [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-preserves-bounded-constructible].
The output tower is hence uniformly bounded constructible, i.e.
$\mathrm{TOW}(\square)$.

The source text records that audit item BC-07 was resolved by correcting the
definition rather than the proof: the bounded constructible tower and the
tower-preservation condition formerly required the local models to have
finite locally *free* terms, which a general constructible complex does not
have. The requirement is now finite local constancy, which is exactly what
finite lissity gives.

For a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with $f$ proper and
every $K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ with torsion cohomology,

$$
 \Ex_{\square,K}:g^{-1}Rf_*K
 \xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_*g'^{-1}K
$$

is an isomorphism in $\Dplus(Y'_{\Et})$.

## Proof

The exchange morphism of [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] induces the morphism
of hypercohomology spectral sequences whose $E_2$ map is the exchange map for
the torsion cohomology sheaf $\mathcal H^q(K)$, an isomorphism by
[lemma-weil-pbc-torsion-assembly]; the differential compatibility is
[lem-weil-pbc-exact-couple-differential]. If $\mathcal H^q(K)=0$ for $q<a$,
then in fixed total degree $n$ only $a\leq q\leq n$ occurs by
[lemma-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-convergence], so both filtrations are finite,
exhaustive, and separated. Page induction gives an isomorphism on $E_\infty$,
and induction on the finite filtration gives an isomorphism on each abutment;
the abutment identification [lemma-weil-pbc-exact-couple-abutment] identifies
that abutment map with the cohomology map of the named mate, which is
therefore an isomorphism.

Let $A$ and $I$ satisfy the adic coefficient datum, let $f:X\to Y$ be
proper, and let $g:Y'\to Y$ be arbitrary. Suppose $K\in D(X_{\Proet},A)$ is
derived $I$-complete and, for every $n$, $K_n$ is equipped with an
etale-origin witness [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]
$$
 L_n\in\Dplus(X_{\Et},P_n),
 \qquad \nu_X^*L_n\xrightarrow{\sim}K_n,
$$
compatible with transition maps. Then
$$
 \Ex^{\mathrm{comp}}_{\square,K}:
 Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rf_*K
 \xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_*Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K
$$
is an isomorphism.

*Source note:* for proper base change on the pro-etale site, see Stacks
Project, Pro-etale Cohomology, Section 61.30
([Tag 09C8](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C8)). This statement is
Theorem 61.30.1 there
([Tag 09C9](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C9)): for $f:X\to Y$
proper, a Noetherian ring $\Lambda$ with an ideal $I$ such that $\Lambda/I$
is torsion, and $K\in D(X_{\Proet})$ derived complete with
$K\otimes^L_\Lambda\underline{\Lambda/I^n}$ bounded below with cohomology
sheaves coming from $X_{\Et}$ and $\Lambda/I^n$ a perfect $\Lambda$-module,
the base change map $Lg^*_{comp}Rf_*K\to Rf'_*L(g')^*_{comp}K$ is an
isomorphism. Hypothesis comparison: the blueprint's etale-origin witness is
exactly Stacks' condition that $K\otimes^L_\Lambda\underline{\Lambda/I^n}$
be bounded below and of etale origin, and the perfectness of $P_n=A/I^n$ is
required in the adic coefficient datum; what the blueprint adds is the
tower-level form, in which the witnesses are required to be compatible over
$n$ and the completed pullback is the one defined in
[def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] from Lemma 61.20.2 ([Tag
099N](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099N)), the proof running through
the finite-level rectangle and the completed-map reduction rather than
through Stacks' reduction to etale cohomology.

## Proof

By the finite-level theorem [thm-weil-pbc-finite-level-proetale], each
finite-level exchange map $\Ex_{\square,K_n}$ is an isomorphism. By
[lemma-weil-pbc-completed-map-reduction], the evaluations of the tower
morphism $V'$ are exactly these isomorphisms, so the levelwise-isomorphism
criterion for cones makes $V'$, and hence the composite defining
$\Ex^{\mathrm{comp}}_{\square,K}$ in
[def-weil-pbc-completed-base-change-map], an isomorphism; the
direct-image/limit commutation used there is the direct-image-limits
proposition. Naturality and coherence are
[lemma-weil-pbc-completed-exchange-coherence].

Let $\Lambda=P_n$ be as in
[def-weil-pbc-constructible-direct-image-finiteness], let $X,Y$ be
noetherian of finite dimension with the torsion orders invertible, and let
$f:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism whose geometric fibers have dimension at
most $e\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$. Then
$$
 \mathrm{FIN}(f,\Lambda;2e)
$$
holds.

*Source:* the finiteness theorem for higher direct images of constructible
sheaves under proper morphisms — Deligne, SGA 4 1/2, Theoreme de finitude,
Th. 1.1, for constructibility, together with the amplitude bound of Stacks
Project, Etale Cohomology, Lemma 59.92.2, [Tag
095U](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/095U)
($R^qf_*\mathcal F=0$ for $q>2n$ when all fibers have dimension at most $n$
and $\mathcal F$ is an abelian torsion sheaf on $X_{\Et}$); a
compact-support form of the constructibility input is Stacks Project, More
Etale Cohomology, Theorem 63.14.5, [Tag
0GL0](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0GL0) (for $f$ separated of
finite presentation and $K\in D^+_{tors,c}(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$, $Rf_!K$ has
constructible cohomology sheaves; for $f$ proper $Rf_!=Rf_*$), and the
etale-to-pro-etale transfer below is the comparison of
[prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image]; difference: both are etale-site
statements for a single Noetherian coefficient ring, neither tracks an
amplitude shift, only 0GL0 uses constructibility of the coefficient, and
neither mentions a coefficient tower or a pro-etale site. No Stacks Project
entry states this form for the pro-etale site, the blueprint adding the
pro-etale form of the finiteness statement with the tracked bound $2e$, the
etale-origin witnesses and the amplitude bookkeeping used by the
amplification conditions below.

## Proof
