Let $F$ be constructible on $X_{\Proet}$, so $F\cong\nu_X^*F_{\Et}$ with
$F_{\Et}$ a constructible $\Lambda$-module sheaf on $X_{\Et}$. Since the
finite ring $\Lambda=P_n$ is annihilated by an integer, $F_{\Et}$ is a
torsion abelian sheaf, so the classical input of the source note (Th. 1.1 of
SGA 4 1/2 and [Tag 095U](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/095U)) applies
to $f_{\Et}$: the sheaves $R^qf_{\Et,*}F_{\Et}$ are constructible and zero
for $q>2e$. By [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image],
$$
 R^qf_{\Proet,*}F\cong R^qf_{\Proet,*}\nu_X^*F_{\Et}
 \cong\nu_Y^*R^qf_{\Et,*}F_{\Et}\qquad(q\geq0),
$$
which is constructible on $Y_{\Proet}$ and vanishes for $q>2e$. This is the
two clauses of [def-weil-pbc-constructible-direct-image-finiteness] for
$u=f$, $c=2e$.

Let $(A,I)$ be henselian, let $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be proper, and let
$Y_0=Y\times_AA/I$. Restriction is an equivalence

$$
 \mathsf{FEt}(Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathsf{FEt}(Y_0).
$$

It lifts morphisms and finite group actions uniquely.

**Status.** The former proof invoked the torsion degree-zero comparison for
the map $H^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)\to H^0(Z_0,\mathcal O_{Z_0})$ on structure
sheaves; that citation applies in neither reading, since the structure sheaf
is not torsion and the two sheaves are different objects. The needed statement
is the idempotent lifting interface
[thm-weil-pbc-henselian-idempotent-lifting], which the proof now cites. The
rest of the proof — properness of $Z$ over $S$, the dictionary between
$Y$-morphisms $Y\to Z$ and rank-one idempotents, the Hom-computation, and
uniqueness of the lifted group action — is proved here and depends on no
further input.

## Proof

Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$, so
$Y_0=Y\times_SS_0$. For a finite etale $Z\to Y$ the composite $Z\to S$ is
proper: $Z\to Y$ is finite, hence proper, and $Y\to S$ is proper by
hypothesis, so composition applies. Let $\pi:Z\to Y$ be finite etale. The
$Y$-morphisms $Y\to Z$ are the inclusions of a member of a decomposition
$Z=Z_e\amalg Z_{1-e}$ into open and closed $Y$-subschemes, i.e. the
idempotents $e$ of $H^0(Z,O_Z)$ whose piece $Z_e$ has rank one (an affine
finite etale algebra is a product of finite etale pieces, and a piece of rank
one is $Y$-isomorphic to $Y$); here $O_Z$ is the structure sheaf of $Z$, an
etale abelian ring sheaf, and $H^0(Z,O_Z)=\Gamma(Y,\pi_*O_Z)$. By
[thm-weil-pbc-henselian-idempotent-lifting], the idempotent-lifting interface
for the structure sheaf of a proper scheme over a henselian pair applied to
the proper $Z\to S$, restriction induces a bijection between the idempotents
of $H^0(Z,O_Z)$ and those of $H^0(Z_0,O_{Z_0})$, and it matches the open and
closed subschemes of $Z$ with those of $Z_0$: an idempotent $e$ cuts out the
clopen $Z_e\subseteq Z$, and its image cuts out $Z_{0,e_0}=(Z_e)_0$. The
condition that $Z_e$ have rank one over $Y$ is therefore equivalent to the
same condition for $(Z_e)_0$ over $Y_0$: the rank of the finite locally free
$\mathcal O_Y$-module $\pi_*O_{Z_e}$ is locally constant on $Y$, and $Y_0\to
Y$ is surjective, so it is determined by its values on the image of $Y_0$,
which are the ranks of $(Z_e)_0$. This is not the torsion-sheaf comparison,
whose hypothesis of torsion coefficients the structure sheaf does not satisfy,
and it is the object-level half of the finite-etale lifting recorded as Tags
0A0C and 0A3S; the map on idempotents is restriction, hence multiplicative,
and it transports the decompositions, so

$$
 Z(Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}Z_0(Y_0),
$$

natural in $Z$. For finite etale $X,W\to Y$, the set
$\operatorname{Hom}_Y(X,W)$ is $(W\times_YX)(X)$, and
$(W\times_YX)_0=W_0\times_{Y_0}X_0$, the former scheme being finite etale and
proper over $S$; therefore

$$
 \operatorname{Hom}_Y(X,W)\xrightarrow{\sim}
 \operatorname{Hom}_{Y_0}(X_0,W_0),
$$

by restriction. The restriction functor $\mathsf{FEt}(Y)\to\mathsf{FEt}(Y_0)$
is thus fully faithful and lifts morphisms uniquely: a morphism $f_0:V_0\to
W_0$ is the restriction of a unique $f:V\to W$, and a finite group action on
$W_0$ lifts by lifting the automorphisms of its generating set and using
uniqueness for the group relations. Every finite etale $Y_0$-scheme is the
restriction of a finite etale $Y$-scheme, the lifting input of the
henselian-pair proper-base-change package (Stacks Project, Section 59.91: Tag
[0A0C](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A0C) and Tag
[0A3S](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A3S)), so restriction is onto the
object set and the three assertions hold.

attrs.title: Finite-etale lifting over a proper henselian pair

objects.body:
For every finite $E/\Ql$, every cartesian square
[def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with $f$ proper, and every
$K\in\Dbc(X,E)$,
$$
 Lg^*Rf_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_*Lg'^*K
 \quad\text{in }\Dbc(Y',E).
$$

## Proof

Choose an integral lattice for $K$: the isomorphism of
[cor-weil-pbc-constructible-complete] is an isomorphism of
$\mathcal O_E$-linear functors on the integral constructible categories, so
by [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] it remains an isomorphism after
rationalization. The independence and coherence assertions are inherited
from the integral level.

attrs.title: Proper base change over a finite extension

objects.body:
Let $\Lambda$ be finite, let $f$ be proper, and let
$K\in\Dplus(X_{\Proet},\Lambda)$ carry an etale-origin witness
[def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness] $(L,\alpha)$. Then the pro-etale exchange
map

$$
 g^{-1}Rf_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_*g'^{-1}K
$$

is an isomorphism. It is independent of replacing the witness by an
isomorphic witness.

*Source note:* for proper base change on the pro-etale site, see Stacks
Project, Pro-etale Cohomology, Section 61.30
([Tag 09C8](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C8)).

## Proof

The bounded-below theorem of the proper-base-change chapter makes the etale
exchange map for $L$ an isomorphism; the fully faithful comparison of
[thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] transports it to the pro-etale site, where
[lem-weil-pbc-transport-identifies-exchange] identifies the transported map
with the pro-etale exchange map for $\nu_X^*L$, which is $K$ under the
witness of [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]. Independence of the witness
follows from the functoriality of the transported map.

For $E/\Ql$ finite, the category $\Dbc(T,E)$
[def-weil-pbc-rational-category] is idempotent complete, and the canonical
functor $\Dbc(T,E)\to\Kar(\Dbc(T,E))$ is an exact equivalence.

*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this form: Stacks has no
idempotent completion (Homological Algebra, Section 12.4, [Tag
09SF](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09SF), states only the Karoubian
property, Definition 12.4.1, [Tag
09SG](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09SG), with the splitting
criterion of Lemma 12.4.2, [Tag
09SH](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09SH), and the criteria of Lemma
12.4.3, [Tag 05QV](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05QV)) and no
t-structure, so the Karoubianity of a triangulated category carrying a
bounded t-structure is not available; the blueprint adds the Karoubianity of
the finite-stage rational categories, deduced from the bounded t-structure
of [prop-weil-localized-tstructure] and the Karoubianity theorem for bounded
t-structures proved in this manuscript.

## Proof

By [prop-weil-localized-tstructure] the category $\Dbc(T,E)$
[def-weil-pbc-rational-category] carries a bounded t-structure, so the
Karoubianity theorem for bounded t-structures applies.

Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair and let $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be proper,
with closed fibre $Z_0=Z\times_AA/I$. Then every idempotent of
$H^0(Z_0,\mathcal O_{Z_0})$ lifts uniquely to an idempotent of $H^0(Z,\mathcal
O_Z)$; equivalently, restriction induces a bijection on idempotents, and the
open and closed subschemes of $Z_0$ are exactly the closed fibres of the open
and closed subschemes of $Z$. This statement is not proved in this blueprint;
it is the interface used by the finite-etale lifting theorem below.

(*The restriction map itself is **not** an isomorphism, and no such claim is
made:* for $A=k[[t]]$, $I=(t)$ and $Z=\mathbf P^1_A$ the map is $k[[t]]\to k$,
surjective but not injective. Only the idempotents are compared, and they
correspond to the open and closed subschemes of the two schemes. The statement
is the structure-sheaf counterpart of input (iii) of the Stein inputs: the
locally constant form of the Zariski restriction criterion does not apply to
the structure sheaf, which is not a torsion sheaf, so this idempotent
correspondence has to be supplied separately. Classically it is the
object-level half of the henselian-pair proper-base-change package, Stacks
Project, Etale Cohomology, Section 59.91, Tag
[0A0B](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A0B) (every connected component
of $Z$ meets $Z_0$, which gives the surjectivity on components, hence on
idempotents, while uniqueness follows because distinct clopens of $Z$ have
distinct traces on $Z_0$); the finite-etale forms are Tag
[0A0C](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A0C) and Tag
[0A3S](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A3S).)

attrs.title: Idempotent lifting for the structure sheaf over a henselian pair

objects.body:
For a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme $X$, an abelian etale sheaf $F$,
and $q\geq0$, there is a natural isomorphism

$$
 \varinjlim_{U}H^q(C^\bullet(U,F))
 \xrightarrow{\sim} H^q(X_{\Et},F).
$$

The limit is over refinements, modulo simplicial homotopy, of the hypercovers
finite in each degree [def-weil-pbc-finite-split-hypercover]. The right side
is the derived cohomology of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. A
representative, and a relation between representatives, use only finitely
many degrees. The same assertion holds for sheaves of modules over a fixed
constant ring, with cohomology derived in that module category.

## Proof

Choose an injective resolution $F\to I^\bullet$, in degrees $r\geq0$, to
compute the cohomology of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. For each $U$, form
the first-quadrant double complex $D^{p,r}=I^r(U_p)$ with total differential
$\delta+(-1)^p d_I$. By [lem-weil-pbc-hypercover-free-resolution], its
augmented rows are exact. Taking horizontal cohomology first therefore shows
that

$$
 \Gamma(X,I^\bullet)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Tot}D
$$

is a quasi-isomorphism. This uses only finite sums in each total degree. The
inclusion $F\to I^\bullet$ now gives the asserted map from hypercover
cohomology to derived cohomology.

We prove its surjectivity without declaring a single hypercover acyclic for
$F$. Represent a degree-$q$ class by a total cocycle. Its component in
bidegree $(0,q)$, if $q>0$, is $d_I$-closed. Exactness of the resolution as a
complex of sheaves makes it locally a $d_I$-boundary. By
[lem-weil-pbc-hypercover-refinement], refine to choose a primitive, and
subtract its total coboundary. The component $(0,q)$ is now zero. The cocycle
equation makes the component $(1,q-1)$ vertically closed. If $q-1>0$, repeat,
with the sign $(-1)^1$ in its primitive. After the finitely many positions
$(p,q-p)$ with $q-p>0$, only $(q,0)$ remains. It is vertically closed, hence
lies in $F(U_q)$, and its horizontal differential is zero. It is the required
representative in $C^\bullet(U,F)$.

For injectivity, suppose a degree-$q$ cocycle in this last complex is a total
boundary. Choose a total primitive of degree $q-1$. Its positive
vertical-degree components are vertically closed in the same successive
order, because its differential has only vertical degree zero. After
refinement subtract total coboundaries from the primitive to remove these
components. The remaining primitive lies in $F(U_{q-1})$. Thus the original
cocycle is already a boundary after refinement. For $q=0$, injectivity
instead follows directly from the injectivity of $F\to I^0$. For two
representatives first take a common refinement and apply this argument to
their difference. Homotopic refinements induce equal cohomology maps by the
prism identity in [lem-weil-pbc-hypercover-refinement]. This proves the
displayed isomorphism and its naturality. All operations used only a finite
truncation as defined in [def-weil-pbc-finite-split-hypercover]; the cocycle
condition uses degree $q+1$. This gives the finite-cover version of
[Stacks Project, Tag 01H0](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01H0). The
colimit here is taken on cohomology groups; no colimit of complexes indexed
by the homotopy category is used. For module coefficients, take an injective
resolution in the module category and use the free-module version of
[lem-weil-pbc-hypercover-free-resolution]; every subsequent local lifting and
double-complex calculation is unchanged.

attrs.title: Cohomology is computed after hypercover refinement

objects.body:
The scalar operation of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] is independent of $N$
and of the representative of $f$ and makes $\mathcal P_T=\Dbc(T,\Qlb)$
$\Qlb$-linear. The shift and distinguished triangles of
[def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] give $\Dbc(T,\Qlb)$ the structure of an
idempotent-complete ordinary triangulated category, and the canonical
functor $\Dbc(T,\Qlb)\to\Kar(\Dbc(T,\Qlb))$ is an exact equivalence. For
every finite $E$ the composite
$$
 \Dbc(T,E)\xrightarrow{j_E}\mathcal P_T=\Dbc(T,\Qlb)
$$
is exact and $E$-linear.

*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this form: the ledger's
verified entries contain no statement making a filtered colimit of
triangulated categories triangulated, and the blueprint adds the
$\Qlb$-linearity, the idempotent-complete triangulation and the exactness of
the finite-stage inclusions $j_E$. What Stacks does provide, each page
fetched and quoted, is the definition of the structure asserted here —
Definition 13.3.2 ([Tag 0145](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0145),
TR1--TR4 with the octahedral axiom) with Definition 13.3.3 ([Tag
014V](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/014V), exact functor) — the
verification of the axioms for a localization, Proposition 13.5.6 ([Tag
05R6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05R6)), and the Karoubianity
criterion Lemma 13.4.14 ([Tag
05QW](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05QW)). Difference: all of these
live in one additive category over one fixed coefficient ring, whereas the
statement here concerns the filtered colimit $\mathcal P_T$ with its
$\Qlb$-scalar action.

## Proof

The scalar operation of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] is independent of $N$:
for two finite fields $N,N'$ containing $\Ql(\alpha)$ and the stage $M$, the
representatives $\alpha u_N$ and $\alpha u_{N'}$ transport to their
compositum and agree there, since $T_{P/N}$ and $T_{P/N'}$ are linear over
$N$ and $N'$ (hence over $N\cap N'$ containing $\Ql(\alpha)$); independence
of the representative of $f$ holds through the representative equivalence
relation of [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]: transport an equality
$u_P=v_P$, which survives scalar multiplication. The field laws and
bilinearity hold at a common stage by
[prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus], so $\mathcal P_T$ is $\Qlb$-linear.
By [thm-weil-pbc-verdier-axioms], $\mathcal P_T=\Dbc(T,\Qlb)$ is
triangulated, and it is idempotent complete by
[thm-weil-pbc-qbar-idempotent-complete], so the canonical fully faithful
functor into the Karoubi envelope is an equivalence by that theorem, hence
exact. The composite $j_E$ is exact by [thm-weil-pbc-verdier-axioms], and
$E$-linear and $\Qlb$-linear by the displayed scalar definition.

Let the adic datum be $A=\mathcal O_E$, $I=(\varpi)$, $P_n=A_{E,n}$, and let
$T$ be noetherian of finite dimension with the torsion orders invertible.
For $K\in\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete],
with its canonical reduction tower $K_\bullet$ (uniformly bounded
constructible with compatible etale-origin witnesses). *Assume that the
Tor-compatibility condition (1) of [prop-weil-pbc-levelwise-truncations]
holds for $K_\bullet$ above every level, equivalently that the cohomology
sheaves of the local models are flat over $A_T$*, and define
$$
 \tau^{\le m}K:=\Rlim\tau^{\le m}K_\bullet,\qquad
 \tau^{\ge m+1}K:=\Rlim\tau^{\ge m+1}K_\bullet,
$$
the derived limits of the towers of
[prop-weil-pbc-levelwise-truncations]. Then
$\tau^{\le m}K,\tau^{\ge m+1}K\in\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)$, and:

1. *reductions:* there are canonical isomorphisms
   $$
    (\tau^{\le m}K)\otimes^L_AP_n\xrightarrow{\sim}\tau^{\le m}K_n,
    \qquad
    (\tau^{\ge m+1}K)\otimes^L_AP_n\xrightarrow{\sim}\tau^{\ge m+1}K_n,
   $$
   compatible with the normalization maps;
2. *cohomology and universality:*
   $$
    \mathcal H^i(\tau^{\le m}K)=\mathcal H^i(K)\ (i\le m),\qquad
    \mathcal H^i(\tau^{\le m}K)=0\ (i>m),
   $$
   $$
    \mathcal H^i(\tau^{\ge m+1}K)=\mathcal H^i(K)\ (i\ge m+1),\qquad
    \mathcal H^i(\tau^{\ge m+1}K)=0\ (i\le m),
   $$
   so that $\tau^{\le m},\tau^{\ge m+1}$ are additive endofunctors of
   $\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)$ characterized by the vanishing of these cohomology
   sheaves; they coincide with the canonical truncations of the ambient
   derived category;
3. *truncation triangles:* the levelwise triangles assemble into
   distinguished triangles
   $$
    \tau^{\le m}K\longrightarrow K
    \longrightarrow\tau^{\ge m+1}K
    \longrightarrow\tau^{\le m}K[1],
   $$
   functorial in $K$.

*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this form: the truncation
functors of the derived complete category are built from the canonical
truncations of complexes, Homological Algebra, Section 12.15 ([Tag
0118](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0118)), and their triangle,
Remark 13.12.4 ([Tag 08J5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08J5)),
neither of which knows a coefficient tower or a completeness condition on
the middle term; the blueprint adds the construction of $\tau^{\le m}K$ and
$\tau^{\ge m+1}K$ as derived limits of the levelwise truncation towers,
together with their reductions, their cohomology and their truncation
triangles.

## Proof

Take the reduction tower and its local models. By
[prop-weil-pbc-levelwise-truncations] (whose Tor-compatibility condition (1)
holds here by the hypothesis of the statement, namely that the cohomology
sheaves of the local models are flat over the discrete valuation ring $A_T$,
equivalently $\varpi$-torsion-free, which is exactly the sufficient
condition of that proposition), $\tau^{\le m}K_\bullet$ is an adic tower
which is uniformly bounded constructible and has compatible etale-origin
witnesses, so by the reconstruction lemma for uniform towers its derived
limit $\tau^{\le m}K$ is derived $I$-complete, has no cohomology outside the
model interval, and satisfies the reduction isomorphisms of (i) by the
finite-reduction reconstruction lemma; the same holds for
$\tau^{\ge m+1}K$. Hence both objects lie in $\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)$ of
[def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]. The cohomology formulas of
(ii) follow from (i) and the cohomology formulas of
[prop-weil-pbc-levelwise-truncations] (iii) at the reduction level, together
with the long exact cohomology sequence of the triangle of (iii) (the end
terms of the triangle are the two objects just constructed, with the
vanishing cohomology of (ii)); the functoriality and additivity are those of
the levelwise truncations and of the functor $\Rlim$. Since a truncation
triangle is characterized by the vanishing properties of its end terms, the
constructed truncations are the canonical truncations of the ambient
category. For (iii), the levelwise truncation triangles form a compatible
family under the normalization isomorphisms of
[prop-weil-pbc-levelwise-truncations] (i) (both the triangles and the
isomorphisms being canonical), hence a triangle in
$D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(T))$, whose image under the triangulated functor
$\Rlim$ is the displayed triangle; its functoriality is inherited from the
levelwise functoriality.

The source records that audit item BC-03 was resolved for this theorem by
defining $\tau^{\le m}K$ as the derived limit of the truncated tower and
obtaining the reduction isomorphisms of (i) from the two reconstruction
lemmas, rather than asserting that the ambient truncation commutes with
reduction.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be proper, let $g:Y'\to Y$ be arbitrary, and let
$K\in\Dbc(X,\Qlb)$. The descended exchange transformation of
[prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors] is an isomorphism
$$
 Lg^*Rf_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_*Lg'^*K
 \quad\text{in }\Dbc(Y',\Qlb).
$$
If $K$ is represented by a pair $(E,K_E)$ with $K_E\in\Dbc(X,E)$, this map
is represented after a finite overfield $M$ by the $M$-coefficient exchange
isomorphism of [thm-weil-pbc-finite-extension] applied to $T_{M/E}K_E$. The
result is independent of $E$, $M$, and the representative.

*Source note:* at each finite stage this is Stacks Project, Pro-etale
Cohomology, Theorem 61.30.1 ([Tag
09C9](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C9)), applied with
$\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$: a proper base-change isomorphism for a derived
complete $K$ whose reductions are bounded below and of etale origin. What
the blueprint adds is the statement on the $\Qlb$ coefficient category
$\Dbc(Y',\Qlb)$, obtained by descent from the finite-stage isomorphisms
along the scalar extensions $T_{F/E}$, together with the independence of the
stage and of the representative.

## Proof

The scalar-compatible family of finite-extension exchange maps descends to a
natural transformation by [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors]; at every finite
stage it is an isomorphism by [thm-weil-pbc-finite-extension], and the
descent formula preserves this property through the common-stage colimit of
[def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]. Independence of the representatives is the
independence statement of [thm-weil-pbc-finite-extension] together with the
equivalence relation of [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category].

The category $\Dbc(T,\Qlb)=\mathcal P_T$ of
[def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] is idempotent complete, and the canonical fully
faithful functor $\Dbc(T,\Qlb)\to\Kar(\Dbc(T,\Qlb))$ is an exact
equivalence.

*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this form: the ledger's
verified entries contain no idempotent-completion entry, and the blueprint
adds the idempotent completeness of the $\Qlb$ category together with the
equivalence of its Karoubi envelope, deduced from the filtered retract
descent and the Karoubianity of the finite-stage categories. The nearest
entries, each fetched and quoted, are the Karoubianity criteria Lemma 12.4.2
([Tag 09SH](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09SH)) and Lemma 12.4.3
([Tag 05QV](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05QV)) with Lemma 13.4.14
([Tag 05QW](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05QW), a triangulated
category with countable products, or with countable coproducts, is
Karoubian); Stacks defines no Karoubi envelope and no idempotent completion,
and the request to add the envelope stands as a comment on Homological
Algebra, Section 12.4 ([Tag
09SF](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09SF)). Difference: the
hypothesis here is not countable products or coproducts but idempotent
completeness of every finite stage, and the conclusion concerns a filtered
colimit of coefficient categories.

## Proof

By [thm-weil-pbc-finite-stage-karoubian] every finite-stage category
$\Dbc(T,E)$ is idempotent complete, so [prop-weil-filtered-retract-descent]
applies with $\mathcal P_T=\Dbc(T,\Qlb)$, as defined in
[def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]: every idempotent of $\Dbc(T,\Qlb)$ splits. The
canonical functor into the Karoubi envelope is fully faithful, and it is
essentially surjective: an object $((E,K),e)$ of the envelope is split by
the splitting of $e$ in $\mathcal P_T$ (the idempotent completeness just
proved), say by $K'\in\mathcal P_T$, $i:K'\to(E,K)$, $p:(E,K)\to K'$ with
$p\,i=\operatorname{id}$ and $i\,p=e$, and then $i$ and $p$ exhibit the
isomorphism $((E,K),e)\cong(K',\operatorname{id}_{K'})$ of the envelope (the
Karoubi-morphism conditions $p=p\circ e$ and $i=e\circ i$ follow from
$p\,i=\operatorname{id}$ and $i\,p=e$). Hence the functor is essentially
surjective, and exact because the envelope of a triangulated category is
triangulated with the canonical functor exact.

attrs.title: The Qbar-l category is idempotent complete

objects.body:
For finite $\Lambda$, the inverse image of the comparison morphism of
[def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] is fully faithful on bounded-below
complexes of finite-coefficient module sheaves:

$$
 \nu_T^*:\Dplus(T_{\Et},\Lambda)
 \longrightarrow\Dplus(T_{\Proet},\Lambda),
 \qquad \operatorname{id}\xrightarrow{\sim}R\nu_{T,*}\nu_T^*.
$$

## Proof

Represent $K$ by a bounded-below complex $I^\bullet$ of injective module
sheaves. The exactness assertion of
[prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level] shows that $\nu_T^*I^\bullet$
represents $\nu_T^*K$. Each of its terms is acyclic for $\nu_{T,*}$ by the
same proposition. The bounded-below acyclic-resolution calculation in
ordinary homological algebra therefore gives

$$
 R\nu_{T,*}(\nu_T^*K)\simeq
 \nu_{T,*}(\nu_T^*I^\bullet).
$$

More explicitly, resolve $\nu_T^*I^\bullet$ by a Cartan--Eilenberg injective
double complex before applying $\nu_{T,*}$. Its column spectral sequence has
$E_1^{p,q}=R^q\nu_{T,*}(\nu_T^*I^p)$; only $q=0$ survives, and its $d_1$
differential is the differential of $\nu_{T,*}\nu_T^*I^\bullet$. Its next
page is thus the cohomology of that complex, not the individual terms $I^p$.
Boundedness below makes each total degree finite in this calculation.

The underived unit is an isomorphism on every $I^p$, by
[prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level], and commutes with its
differentials by naturality. It identifies $I^\bullet$ with
$\nu_{T,*}\nu_T^*I^\bullet$. Under the displayed acyclic-resolution
identification, this map is the derived unit for
[def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Hence $K\to R\nu_{T,*}\nu_T^*K$ is a
natural isomorphism. For bounded-below $K,L$, derived adjunction now gives

$$
 \operatorname{Hom}\bigl(\nu_T^*K,\nu_T^*L\bigr)
 \cong\operatorname{Hom}\bigl(K,R\nu_{T,*}\nu_T^*L\bigr)
 \cong\operatorname{Hom}(K,L),
$$

with the second identification induced by that unit. This proves full
faithfulness. The finite-level proposition used here has already established
its geometric acyclicity input by the two finite-cover limits above.

Let $(A,I)$ be an affine henselian pair with $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and in
the Stein factorization $p=s\circ q$ of
[def-weil-pbc-stein-factorization] of a proper $p:Y\to S$ let
$S'=\operatorname{Spec}B$. The two inputs are:

- (i) *finiteness.* $A\to B$ is finite, equivalently $p_*\mathcal O_Y$ is a
  coherent, hence finitely generated, $\mathcal O_S$-algebra. For $A$
  Noetherian this is Stacks Project, More on Morphisms, Section 37.53 (Tag
  [03GX](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03GX)); for a general affine
  base it is not proved in this blueprint. The route available here is the
  approximation chain of this chapter: descend $Y\to S$ to a finitely
  presented model over a Noetherian base
  ([lem-weil-pbc-etale-finite-data-descent]), apply the Noetherian statement
  there, and use the affine limit formula of
  [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-continuity] for the structure sheaf to identify
  $H^0(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ with the base change of the model. That chain is not
  written out.
- (ii) *connectedness.* Every irreducible closed subset of $Y$ meets
  $Y_0=Y\times_SS_0$ in a nonempty connected subset. This is the
  henselian-pair proper-base-change input, Stacks Project, Etale Cohomology,
  Lemma 59.91.1 (Tag [0A0B](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A0B), the
  comparison $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)=\Gamma(Z,\mathcal F|_Z)$ for sheaves on
  the underlying topological space of a henselian pair; the connectedness
  consequence used here is the Stein-factorization step of its proof, Theorem
  37.53.5, Tag [03H2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03H2)); it is a
  classical theorem about henselian pairs and is not proved in this
  blueprint.

A third input, used by Stage 1 of the degree-zero comparison, is the Zariski
comparison $\Gamma(Y,G)\cong\Gamma(Y_0,G|_{Y_0})$ for the *constructible*
torsion sheaf $G$ that occurs there. The locally constant form proved in
[lemma-weil-pbc-spectral-restriction] does not give it, its statement carrying
a counterexample for sheaves that are not locally constant, so that
comparison is an obligation as well.

attrs.title: The two classical inputs of Stein connectedness

objects.body:
If $u:X'\to X$ is a universal homeomorphism
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], then the morphisms of small etale sites
[def-weil-pbc-etale-site] induced by $u$ give an equivalence of small etale
topoi, i.e. an equivalence of the categories of etale sheaves

$$
 \operatorname{Sh}(X_{\Et})\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\operatorname{Sh}(X'_{\Et}),
$$

compatible with the inverse and direct image functors and with cohomology.
The equivalence preserves and reflects covering families and is compatible
with identities, composition, and pullback of sheaves and cohomology.

## Proof

The input is the topological invariance of the small etale site
[def-weil-pbc-etale-site]: for a universal homeomorphism
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] $u:X'\to X$, base change $V\mapsto
V\times_XX'$ is an equivalence of the small etale categories, naturally in
the schemes and compatible with identities and composites, and it preserves
and reflects jointly surjective families, because the underlying topological
map of $u$ and of every base change of $u$ is a homeomorphism (Stacks
Project, Section 59.45, Tag
[04DY](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/04DY), Theorem
[04DZ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/04DZ)). The inverse functors of
the equivalence are the inverse image $u^{-1}$ and the direct image $u_*$ of
[def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]: the equivalence of sites makes $u^{-1}$ exact
and $u_*$ its quasi-inverse, so the categories of
[def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] are equivalent,

$$
 \operatorname{Sh}(X_{\Et})\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
 \operatorname{Sh}(X'_{\Et}),
$$

and covering families are preserved and reflected by the site-equivalence
input. For the compatibility with cohomology, let $F\to I$ be a resolution by
a bounded-below complex of injective sheaves (K-injective by
[prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist], so the model of
[def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions] computes $H^q(X_{\Et},F)$). Exactness
of $u^{-1}$ sends the resolution to a resolution of $u^{-1}F$ with injective
entries: for an injective $I^m$ the right adjoint criterion applied to the
adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] gives that
$\operatorname{Hom}(u^{-1}I^m,-)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(I^m,u_*-)$ is exact.
The unit and counit of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] are the isomorphisms of
the equivalence, so
$\Gamma(X',u^{-1}I)=\Gamma(X,u_*u^{-1}I)=\Gamma(X,I)$ and hence

$$
 H^q(X_{\Et},F)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(X'_{\Et},u^{-1}F)
 \qquad(q\geq0),
$$

the compatibilities with identities, composition, and pullback of sheaves
being the functoriality of the site equivalence: the equivalence of a
composite is the composite of the equivalences, and for a base change $u'$ of
$u$ — itself a universal homeomorphism by
[lem-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-base-change] — the equivalences of $u$
and $u'$ form a commutative square with the inverse-image functors of
[def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], which is the compatibility with pullback.

The shift and distinguished triangles of [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones]
satisfy the four Verdier axioms:

1. every morphism has a distinguished cone triangle, the identity triangle
   is distinguished, and distinguishedness is closed under isomorphism;
2. a triangle is distinguished if and only if its signed rotation is
   distinguished;
3. every commutative square between the first arrows of two distinguished
   triangles extends to a morphism of triangles;
4. cone triangles for composable maps can be placed in an octahedral diagram
   whose required faces commute and whose remaining cone triangle is
   distinguished.

Consequently $\mathcal P_T$ is an ordinary triangulated category. Every
finite-stage inclusion $j_E:\mathcal C_E(T)\to\mathcal P_T$ is exact, and
the identifications $j_FT_{F/E}\simeq j_E$ are exact natural isomorphisms.

*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this verification: the four
axioms verified here are exactly Stacks Project, Derived Categories,
Definition 13.3.2 ([Tag 0145](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0145),
fetched and quoted: "the definition of a triangulated category as given in
Verdier's thesis", an additive category with an additive auto-equivalence
$[1]$ and a set of distinguished triangles subject to TR1--TR4, TR4 being
the octahedral axiom); the triangles and their morphisms are Definition
13.3.1 ([Tag 0144](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0144)) and the exact
functors of the last sentence are Definition 13.3.3 ([Tag
014V](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/014V)). The closest verification
of the axioms in Stacks for a category that is constructed rather than
assumed is Proposition 13.5.6 ([Tag
05R6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05R6)), which proves TR1--TR4 for
a localization $S^{-1}\mathcal D$ whose distinguished triangles are by
definition the images of distinguished triangles of $\mathcal D$, and Lemma
13.4.15 ([Tag 014C](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/014C)) is the
normal form for TR4. The blueprint adds the verification for the triangles
of [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones] together with the exactness of the
finite-stage inclusions $j_E$.

## Proof

TR1: every morphism has a cone triangle by
[def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones]; the identity triangle is the cone
triangle of an identity (cone zero), and distinguishedness is closed under
isomorphism by the definition. TR2: by
[prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus] a distinguished triangle and its
signed rotation may be represented over one common finite field, so the
finite-stage TR2 axiom makes the signed rotation distinguished (the shift in
the signed rotation being the $\sigma$-comparison of the definition). TR3:
given a commutative square between the first arrows of two distinguished
triangles, represent the two triangles over one common finite field (using
the transport isomorphisms of
[def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]) and apply the finite-stage TR3
axiom; the resulting vertical arrow transports back to $\mathcal P_T$. TR4:
the same common-stage representation of two composable morphisms, together
with the cone independence of [prop-weil-pbc-cone-independence], and the
finite-stage TR4 axiom produce the octahedral diagram whose remaining cone
triangle is distinguished. Hence $\mathcal P_T$ is an ordinary triangulated
category; $j_E$ is exact because cone triangles of $j_E(f)$ are the
corresponding common-stage cone triangles, and the identifications
$j_FT_{F/E}\simeq j_E$ are exact natural isomorphisms by
[prop-weil-pbc-cone-independence].

For the construction of [def-weil-pbc-weak-etale-refinement], the map $B\to
B'$ is faithfully flat and ind-etale, and $A\to B'$ is ind-etale.

## Proof

Use $C,J,D_0$ from [def-weil-pbc-weak-etale-refinement]. By
[lem-weil-pbc-strict-w-cover], $C/A$ is faithfully flat and ind-etale, and
its maximal local rings are strictly henselian. The fibres of $D_0/C$ are
algebraic over their base fields by
[lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-field]. Thus $T=V(JD_0)$ consists of closed points
of $D_0$. [lem-weil-pbc-retained-localization] makes $B'$ w-local with closed
points $T$, unchanged local rings there, and $D_0\to B'$ ind-Zariski.

At every maximal ideal $n\subset B'$, its contraction $m\subset C$ is
maximal. The local map $C_m\to B'_n$ is weakly etale by
[lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability], so is an isomorphism by
[thm-weil-pbc-weak-etale-strict-local]. Every prime of $B'$ lies under a
maximal ideal. Localizing this isomorphism again shows that $C\to B'$
identifies all local rings. It is therefore ind-Zariski by
[lem-weil-pbc-local-rings-ind-zariski]. Composition with $A\to C$ proves that
$A\to B'$ is ind-etale.

The map $B\to D_0$ is ind-etale by base change from $A\to C$; composition
makes $B\to B'$ ind-etale and flat as well. The closed point set $V(J)$
surjects onto $\operatorname{Spec}A$ by
[lem-weil-pbc-strict-w-cover]. Its base change $T$ therefore surjects onto
$\operatorname{Spec}B$, and all these points are retained in
$\operatorname{Spec}B'$. This proves faithful flatness. The construction
gives the refinement theorem commonly formulated in
[Stacks Project, Tag 097Z](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/097Z); its
covering and local-ring steps have been proved above.

attrs.title: Ind-etale refinement of a weakly etale map

objects.body:
Let $A\to B$ be a local map of local rings. If $A$ is strictly henselian
[def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] and the map is weakly etale
[def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], it is an isomorphism.

## Proof

The local flat map $A\to B$ is faithfully flat. For each prime $\mathfrak
p\subset A$, its fibre is ind-etale over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, by
[lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability] and [lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-field]. If
that fibre has two primes, its finite etale subalgebras separate them by an
idempotent. If instead it has a residue extension larger than
$\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, a finite separable subextension splits into at least
two factors after a finite separable field extension. In either case there is
an algebraic field extension $L/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ such that $B\otimes_AL$
has a nontrivial idempotent.

Let $A'$ be the integral closure of $A/\mathfrak p$ in $L$. Its fraction
field is $L$, by clearing denominators in a monic algebraic equation. It is a
henselian local ring: each finite domain subalgebra over the henselian local
ring $A/\mathfrak p$ is local, since the idempotents of its finite residue
algebra lift and a domain cannot split. These local finite algebras form a
filtered union; the finite equations for henselian lifting descend to a
member of that union. Its residue extension over the separably closed residue
field of $A$ is purely inseparable. This also shows that $A'$ is strictly
henselian in [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology].

The integral extension $B\to B\otimes_AA'$ has exactly one maximal ideal.
Indeed, maximal ideals lie above the maximal ideal of $B$; its fibre, after
removing nilpotents, is the tensor product of its residue field with a purely
inseparable field extension, which has one prime. Thus $B\otimes_AA'$ is
local. By [lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-integral-closure] it is integrally closed
in $B\otimes_AL$. Every idempotent of the latter ring is integral and hence
belongs to this local ring, where it must be zero or one. This contradicts
the preceding paragraph. Therefore every fibre of $\operatorname{Spec}B\to
\operatorname{Spec}A$ is a single point with unchanged residue field.

The diagonal is now surjective on points after every field extension. Its
defining ideal $J$ in $B\otimes_AB$ is therefore nil, and its quotient is
flat by weak etaleness. The flat-quotient criterion says that for each $z\in
J$ there is $e\in J$ with $z=ze$; it follows by tensoring the inclusion
$(z)\subset B\otimes_AB$ with the quotient. Since $e$ is nilpotent, $1-e$ is
invertible, so $z=0$. Thus $B\otimes_AB\to B$ is an isomorphism. Faithfully
flat descent, in its equalizer form for modules, finally gives $A=B$. This is
the local calculation of Olivier; see
[Stacks Project, Tag 092Z](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/092Z) for its
customary formulation.

attrs.title: A weakly etale local map over a strict henselian ring

objects.body:
Let $p$ be prime, let $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, put $q=p^a$, and set
$k_0=\Fq$, and let $k=\Fbar$ be the
fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$.
Fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and choose an
algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$. Let $X_0/k_0$
be smooth, proper, geometrically
connected of pure dimension $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, and put
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. Let $a_X:X\to\Spec k$ be the structure
morphism and assume it is
exceptional-adjoint
admissible at $\Ql$. Let $Ra_X^!$ denote the
exceptional inverse image, and
choose an orientation isomorphism

$$
\eta_X:Ra_X^!\Ql\xrightarrow{\sim}(\Ql)_X(d)[2d]
$$

and let $K_X=(\Ql)_X$ with its
canonical Weil structure. Let $F$ be
the endomorphism of $R\Gamma(X,K_X)$ induced by the
global geometric Frobenius
with the normalization in the geometric
Frobenius convention; write $F$ for its induced automorphisms on every
$H^i(X,\Ql)$. Here $H^i$ and $H_c^i$ denote the
ordinary and compactly
supported cohomology groups, $\Ql(m)$ denotes the
Tate twist, and geometric Frobenius acts on
it by the specified twist
normalization. Then the Poincare duality interface holds: the trace
map

$$
\operatorname{tr}^{(-d)}_X:H^{2d}(X,\Ql)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Ql(-d)
$$

is an isomorphism, the groups $H^i(X,\Ql)$ are finite-dimensional
and vanish for $i\notin[0,2d]$, the
trace–cup-product pairings
$\langle-,-\rangle_i$ with values in $\Ql(-d)$ are perfect for
every $0\leq i\leq2d$ and satisfy

$$
\langle Fx,Fy\rangle_i=q^d\langle x,y\rangle_i
\qquad
(x\in H^i(X,\Ql),\ y\in H^{2d-i}(X,\Ql)),
$$

there is a Frobenius-equivariant duality isomorphism
$H^{2d-i}(X,\Ql)\simeq H^i(X,\Ql)^\vee(-d)$, under which the
eigenvalues of $F$ on $H^{2d-i}(X,\Ql)$ are the $q^d/\alpha$, with
multiplicity, for the eigenvalues $\alpha$ of $F$ on $H^i(X,\Ql)$, and
the base-change clause holds: for every finite extension $k_0'/k_0$
contained in $k$, with $r=[k_0':k_0]$ (so $\#k_0'=q^r$), the geometric
Frobenius of $k_0'$ acting on $H^i(X,\Ql)$, via the canonical
identification of $X_0\times_{k_0}k_0'$ base-changed to $k$ with $X$,
is $F^r$, the pairings $\langle-,-\rangle_i$ remain perfect, and

$$
\langle F^rx,F^ry\rangle_i=(q^r)^d\langle x,y\rangle_i
\qquad
(x\in H^i(X,\Ql),\ y\in H^{2d-i}(X,\Ql)).
$$

These six clauses are the items (Trace), (Finiteness), (Pairing),
(Frobenius similitudine), (Reciprocity) and (Base change) of the
detailed form below, read in the conventions fixed here; the
graded-commutativity part of (Pairing) is deduced from this theorem
in the following proposition on the Poincare pairing.

## Proof

The interface statement is the smooth-proper-geometrically-connected
case of the Poincare duality theorem of the Poincare-duality chapter,
[thm-weil-poincare-duality], whose six items (trace
isomorphism, finiteness, perfect pairings, Frobenius similitudine,
reciprocity, and base change) are the six clauses of the interface:
the trace map is the trace of [def-weil-poincare-trace-cup], the
finiteness item is the constant-sheaf case of
[prop-cohomological-finiteness], the Frobenius items use the
global operator of [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius] with the
twist normalization of [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists]
and the untwisted Frobenius similitude of
[cor-pod-untwisted-similitude], and the reciprocity and base
change are [cor-pod-reciprocal-eigenvalues] and the
Frobenius-operator convention of [def-trf-frobenius-operators]
together with $\operatorname{Frob}_{q^r}=\operatorname{Frob}_q^r$ from
[def-weil-frobenius-detailed]: the Frobenius of $k_0'$ is $F^r$, the
pairings are unchanged under the canonical identification of geometric
fibres (hence still perfect), and iterating the similitude $r$ times gives
$\langle F^rx,F^ry\rangle_i=q^{rd}\langle x,y\rangle_i=(q^r)^d\langle x,y\rangle_i$.
Both the
interface and [thm-weil-poincare-duality] are expressed in the
ordinary and compact-support conventions of
[def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] and the Tate twist
conventions of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], with the orientation
datum specified in the interface statement entering only through the
identification $\eta_X$ recorded there; the two statements therefore
agree clause by clause.

## Detailed form

Let $p$ be prime, let $a\in \mathbf Z_{\geq 1}$, put $q=p^a$, and set $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, and let $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ be the fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$. Fix a prime $\ell \neq p$, write $\mathbf Q_{\ell }=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and choose an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell }$ of $\mathbf Q_{\ell }$. Let $X_0/k_0$ be smooth, proper, geometrically connected of pure dimension $d\in \mathbf Z_{\geq 0}$, and put $X=X_0\times _{k_0}k$. Let $a_X:X\to \operatorname{Spec}k$ be the structure morphism; no admissibility hypothesis is imposed on it, its exceptional inverse image $Ra_X^!$ being the constructible one of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], which exists for every separated finite-type morphism (the ambient datum of [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility], which fails for smooth proper curves, is not used). Let $K_X=(\mathbf Q_{\ell })_X$ be the constant Weil sheaf with its canonical structure, and let $F$ be the global geometric Frobenius endomorphism of $R\Gamma (X,K_X)$ in the geometric-Frobenius convention; write $F$ also for its automorphisms of the cohomology groups, and let $\langle -,-\rangle _i$ be the trace–cup-product pairing with values in the Tate twist $\mathbf Q_{\ell }(-d)$. Then:

*Trace.* The trace map

$$
\operatorname {tr}^{(-d)}_X:H^{2d}(X,\mathbf Q_{\ell })\xrightarrow {\  \sim \  }\mathbf Q_{\ell }(-d)
$$

is an isomorphism (Theorem 9.27).

*Finiteness.* For every integer $i$, $H^i(X,\mathbf Q_{\ell })$ is finite-dimensional, and it is zero for $i\notin [0,2d]$ (Proposition 1.58).

*Pairing.* The pairing

$$
H^i(X,\mathbf Q_{\ell })\times H^{2d-i}(X,\mathbf Q_{\ell })\longrightarrow \mathbf Q_{\ell }(-d)
$$

is perfect for every $0\leq i\leq 2d$ (Theorem 9.26 with $K=(\mathbf Q_{\ell })_X$, $\Lambda =\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell }$, via Theorem 9.35 for the $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell }$-stage).

*Frobenius similitudine.* Geometric Frobenius acts on $\mathbf Q_{\ell }(-d)$ by $q^d$, and

$$
\langle Fx,Fy\rangle _i=q^d\langle x,y\rangle _i \qquad (x\in H^i(X,\mathbf Q_{\ell }),\  y\in H^{2d-i}(X,\mathbf Q_{\ell })),
$$

for every $0\leq i\leq 2d$ (Corollary 9.31 for the constant sheaf).

*Reciprocity.* For every finite-dimensional $\mathbf Q_{\ell }$-vector space $V$, write $V^\vee =\operatorname {Hom}_{\mathbf Q_{\ell }}(V,\mathbf Q_{\ell })$; then

$$
H^{2d-i}(X,\mathbf Q_{\ell })\simeq H^i(X,\mathbf Q_{\ell })^\vee (-d),
$$

Frobenius-equivariantly, and the eigenvalues of $F$ on $H^{2d-i}(X,\mathbf Q_{\ell })$ are the $q^d/\alpha$, with multiplicity, for the eigenvalues $\alpha$ of $F$ on $H^i(X,\mathbf Q_{\ell })$ (Theorem 9.26 and Corollary 9.32).

*Base change.* For every finite extension $k_0'/k_0$ contained in $k$, put

$$
r=[k_0':k_0],\qquad q'=\# k_0'=q^r,\qquad X_0'=X_0\times _{k_0}k_0', \qquad X'=X_0'\times _{k_0'}k,
$$

and identify $X'$ with $X$ by the canonical geometric-fiber identification; the base-change map is the pullback induced by $X'\to X$ on the complexes $R\Gamma (X,(\mathbf Q_{\ell })_X)$ and $R\Gamma (X',(\mathbf Q_{\ell })_{X'})$. Under this identification the geometric Frobenius for $k_0'$ is $F'=F^r$ (Definition 7.7), the pairings remain perfect, and

$$
\langle F^r x,F^r y\rangle _i=(q^r)^d\langle x,y\rangle _i
$$

for $x\in H^i(X,\mathbf Q_{\ell })$ and $y\in H^{2d-i}(X,\mathbf Q_{\ell })$.

## Proof

The coefficient stage is $\Lambda =\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell }$, the common-stage coefficients of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], with the canonical datum. Item (1) is the proper clause of [thm-pod-trace-isomorphism] at $\Lambda =\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell }$ ($X_0$ being proper by hypothesis, so $H_c^{2d}=H^{2d}$); item (2) is [prop-cohomological-finiteness], whose statement in the smooth-proper-geometrically-connected case gives the vanishing outside $[0,2d]$ and the finite-dimensionality. Item (3): by [thm-pod-proper-poincare-duality] (applicable since $X_0$ is proper) with $K=(\mathbf Q_{\ell })_X$ and the $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell }$-transport of [thm-pod-qbar-coefficient-pairing], the degreewise pairings $H^i(X,\mathbf Q_{\ell })\times H^{2d-i}(X,\mathbf Q_{\ell }(d))\to \mathbf Q_{\ell }$ are perfect, and eliminating the twist gives the line-valued perfect pairings with values in $\mathbf Q_{\ell }(-d)$, the definition of $\langle -,-\rangle _i$ in [def-weil-poincare-trace-cup] (the cup product of the master is the mixed-support cup product on a proper scheme, and the trace is the normalized smooth trace of the purity chapter restricted to the constant coefficients). Item (4): the constant sheaf $K_X$ with its canonical datum is self-dual in the canonical way; the datum on the dual is the canonical datum, and the Frobenius similitude $\langle Fx,Fy\rangle _i=q^d\langle x,y\rangle _i$ is the untwisted similitude of [cor-pod-untwisted-similitude] for $K=K_X$. Item (5): the duality isomorphism of [thm-pod-proper-poincare-duality] together with the degreewise isomorphism of [thm-pod-degreewise-perfectness-over-a-field] gives (transported to $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell }$ via [thm-pod-qbar-coefficient-pairing]) $H^{2d-i}(X,\mathbf Q_{\ell })\cong H^i(X,\mathbf Q_{\ell })^\vee (-d)$, the equivariance being the duality-isomorphism compatibility of [def-pod-dual-tate-datum] and of [lem-fix-weil-operations], and the eigenvalue reciprocity is [cor-pod-reciprocal-eigenvalues]. Item (6): the base change consists in the identification of the geometric Frobenius $\operatorname {Frob}_{q'}=\operatorname {Frob}_q^r$ (the definition of the geometric-Frobenius convention, [def-weil-frobenius-detailed], and its incarnation on the geometric fiber via the canonical identification $X'=X$), the associated operator being the $r$-th iterate $F^r$ of [def-trf-frobenius-operators]; the pairings are the ones transported along the canonical identification of $X'$ with $X$, hence perfect, and the similitude is the $r$-fold iteration of item (4), whose $r$-th power acts by $q^{rd}=(q^r)^d$.

attrs.title: Poincare duality for smooth proper schemes

objects.body:
Fix a prime $p$, an integer $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, put
$q=p^a$, $k_0=\Fq$, and let $k=\Fbar$ be the
fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$.
Let
$X_0/k_0$ be smooth, proper,
geometrically connected of pure dimension $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, and
put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. Fix an indeterminate $T$. For every prime
$\ell\neq p$, let
$(V_{i,\ell},F_{i,\ell},P_{i,\ell})_{0\leq i\leq2d}$ be the
smooth-proper
cohomological family. The reciprocal-root multiset is interpreted using the
ordinary and reciprocal-root
convention, and each $P_{i,\ell}$ is the determinant factor in that
cohomological family, explicitly

$$
P_{i,\ell}(T)=\det(1-TF_{i,\ell}\mid V_{i,\ell}).
$$

Let $Z(X_0,T)$ be the
point-count zeta series, and write
$Z(X_0,T)=A(T)/B(T)$ with $A,B\in\mathbf Z[T]$, $A(0)=B(0)=1$,
$\gcd(A,B)=1$ in $\mathbf Q[T]$; this is a chosen presentation satisfying
the normalized integral-fraction
conditions. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}$. For each
$\ell\neq p$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic closure
$\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, set
$\overline{\mathbf Q}^{(\ell)} =\{\alpha\in\Qlb:\alpha\text{ is algebraic over }\mathbf Q\}$, the
algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q$
inside $\Qlb$, and choose an isomorphism
$\jmath_\ell:\overline{\mathbf Q}\xrightarrow{\sim} \overline{\mathbf Q}^{(\ell)}$.
For $C\in\{A,B\}$, put
$r_C=\deg C$ and define its reciprocal polynomial by

$$
C^\#(U)=U^{r_C}C(U^{-1}).
$$

For each $0\leq i\leq2d$, form the multiset
ordinary roots $R_i$ of
$A^\#$ when $i$ is odd and of $B^\#$ when $i$ is even whose elements
are $q$-Weil numbers of weight $i$; the
intrinsic weights and the Galois stability of these multisets are
proved in *Intrinsic weights of the reciprocal roots* below. Put

$$
Q_i(T)=\prod_{\alpha\in R_i}(1-\alpha T)\in\mathbf Z[T].
$$

These $Q_i$ are candidate normalized integral factors.
For every
prime $\ell\neq p$, every ell-adic realization
$\jmath_\ell:\overline{\mathbf Q}\xrightarrow{\sim}\overline{\mathbf Q}^{(\ell)}$,
and every $0\leq i\leq2d$, write
$Q_i^{(\ell,\jmath_\ell)}$ for the scalar extension of $Q_i$ along
$\jmath_\ell$.
Then scalar extension identifies the reciprocal-root multiset of $Q_i$ with
that of $P_{i,\ell}$:

$$
Q_i^{(\ell,\jmath_\ell)}(T)=P_{i,\ell}(T).
$$

Here $Q_i^{(\ell,\jmath_\ell)}$ means coefficientwise extension along
$\jmath_\ell:\overline{\mathbf Q}\xrightarrow{\sim} \overline{\mathbf Q}^{(\ell)}$, so the displayed equality is an equality in
the chosen algebraic closure of $\Ql$ (with $P_{i,\ell}$ viewed through
$\Ql\subset\Qlb$).
Consequently, after these scalar identities are established, each $Q_i$ is
the normalized
integral Frobenius factor
for the common realization.
These scalar identities are independent of the chosen realization and
preserve the normalization $Q_i(0)=1$. If
$N_\ell(T)=\prod_{\substack{0\leq i\leq2d\\i\ {\rm odd}}}P_{i,\ell}(T)$ and
$D_\ell(T)=\prod_{\substack{0\leq i\leq2d\\i\ {\rm even}}}P_{i,\ell}(T)$, the
parity-product construction gives
$A^{(\ell)}=N_\ell$ and $B^{(\ell)}=D_\ell$. No additional assertion
about Frobenius operators is made by this scalar comparison.
The scalar-extension notation is coefficientwise extension of integral
polynomials.

## Proof

*Step 1: the point counts are independent of $\ell$.* The
setting is the smooth, proper, geometrically connected $X_0/k_0$ of
pure dimension $d$ of [def-weil-geometric-hypotheses], in the
datums of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], and the
integer point counts $N_n(X_0)=\#X_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$ do not
involve $\ell$, by the point-count convention of
[def-weil-point-counts-zeta]; hence the zeta series
$Z(X_0,T)$ lies in $1+T\mathbf Z[[T]]$, and by the closed-point
product of [prop-euler-product] it is the Taylor series of the
closed-point product. For each $\ell\neq p$, the point-count trace
formula of [cor-trf-point-counting] and the
[lem-zl-log-det-identity] log-determinant identity yield the
[thm-zl-lefschetz-weil-identity] trace-to-determinant identity

$$
Z(X_0,T)=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}P_{i,\ell}(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}
\quad\text{in }\Ql[[T]],
$$

after the scalar extension to the $\Ql$-coefficients of
[def-weil-smooth-proper-cohomological-family], with the root
convention of [def-weil-ordinary-reciprocal-roots]. Since the
right-hand side is rational over $\Ql$, its Taylor coefficients
satisfy a linear recurrence over $\Ql$, and its
[def-weil-hankel-matrix] has some finite rank $r$ over $\Ql$.
Every finite minor of order $r+1$ has integer entries and
vanishes in $\Ql$, hence already in $\mathbf Q$.
Thus its rank over $\mathbf Q$ is at most $r$, and by the
rationality criterion of
[prop-weil-rationality-criterion] the series lies in
$\mathbf Q(T)$; the normalized reduced integral presentation of
[def-weil-normalized-integral-fraction] is then the unique one
supplied by [prop-weil-zeta-normalized-presentation].

*Step 2: weight separation.* By [prop-weil-reciprocal-roots-eigenvalues]
the reciprocal roots of $P_{i,\ell}$ are the eigenvalues of
$F_{i,\ell}$, and [thm-weil-deligne-purity] gives
$|\iota(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}$ for every such eigenvalue, for the fixed
isomorphism $\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$ used there.
The hypotheses of [prop-weight-separation] therefore hold:
every reciprocal root of $P_{i,\ell}$ satisfies
$|\iota(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}$, and the trace-to-determinant identity of
Step 1 holds. Concretely, the polynomials $P_{i,\ell}$,
$P_{j,\ell}$ are coprime for $i\neq j$, the parity products
$N_\ell,D_\ell$ of [def-weil-parity-products]
are coprime with constant coefficient $1$,
$Z(X_0,T)=N_\ell(T)/D_\ell(T)$, and the ordinary root multiset of
each $P_{i,\ell}$ is exactly the submultiset of roots of the
appropriate parity product with the weight-$i$ absolute-value
condition.

*Step 3: the parity products are the normalized presentation.*
Both $A^{(\ell)}/B^{(\ell)}$ and $N_\ell/D_\ell$ are reduced
fractions —$\gcd(A,B)=1$ in $\mathbf Q[T]$ by
[def-weil-normalized-integral-fraction], $\gcd(N_\ell,D_\ell)=1$
by Step 2 —with constant coefficients $1$, and both equal the
Taylor series $Z(X_0,T)$ in $\Ql[[T]]$. Cross multiplication
and coprimality over $\Ql[T]$ show that the numerators and
denominators differ by the same scalar. Their constant terms
are $1$, so that scalar is $1$. Consequently
$A^{(\ell)}=N_\ell$ and $B^{(\ell)}=D_\ell$ coefficientwise in
$\Ql$, after extension along the [def-weil-algebraic-closure-q]
identification $\jmath_\ell$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]'s
datum. This is the parity-product clause.

*Step 4: the weight strata and the stratum polynomials.* By
*Intrinsic weights of the reciprocal roots* below, every root of $A^\#$ or $B^\#$ has a
unique weight in $\{0,\ldots,2d\}$, and the resulting root multisets
$R_i$ are Galois-stable. Hence
[prop-galois-weight-strata-integrality] and
[prop-galois-weight-strata-identification] apply and return that the
normalized stratum polynomials

$$
Q_i(T)=\prod_{\alpha\in R_i}(1-\alpha T)
$$

lie in $\mathbf Z[T]$ and that the reciprocal-root multiset of $Q_i$
is the weight-$i$ submultiset of the roots of $A^\#$
($i$ odd) or of $B^\#$ ($i$ even). This is the integrality clause
for the stratum polynomials.

*Step 5: the scalar identities.* For fixed
$\ell\neq p$ and $\jmath_\ell$, the scalar extension
$Q_i^{(\ell,\jmath_\ell)}$ is the product over the identified
weight-$i$ submultiset of roots of $A^{(\ell)\#}=N_\ell^\#$
($i$ odd) or of $B^{(\ell)\#}=D_\ell^\#$ ($i$ even), which by
the multiset identification of Step 2 is exactly the reciprocal-root
multiset of $P_{i,\ell}$; both polynomials have constant
coefficient $1$, so

$$
Q_i^{(\ell,\jmath_\ell)}(T)=P_{i,\ell}(T),
$$

the identity of the interface statement. The independence of the
identity from the chosen realization and realization isomorphism is
the uniqueness in Step 4, and $Q_i(0)=1$ is the normalization
$Q_i(0)=\prod_{\alpha\in R_i}1=1$. With Step 3 this establishes
the assertion, and $Q_i$ is the integral Frobenius factor of
[def-weil-integral-frobenius-factor]
in degree $i$: its scalar extension along $\jmath_\ell$ is
$P_{i,\ell}$ for every $\ell\neq p$.

## Intrinsic weights of the reciprocal roots

In the situation of [thm-weil-realization-independence], every root of
$A^\#$ or $B^\#$ has a unique weight in $\{0,\ldots,2d\}$, and the
resulting multisets $R_i$ of
ordinary roots that are
$q$-Weil numbers of weight $i$ are stable
under $\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathbf Q}/\mathbf Q)$.

*Proof.*
In the situation of [thm-weil-realization-independence] the fraction
$A^{(\ell)}/B^{(\ell)}$ and the parity products $N_\ell/D_\ell$ of
[prop-weight-separation] both equal the series $Z(X_0,T)$ in
$\Ql[[T]]$; here $\gcd(A,B)=1$ in $\mathbf Q[T]$ by
[def-weil-normalized-integral-fraction], while $\gcd(N_\ell,D_\ell)=1$
and $N_\ell(0)=D_\ell(0)=1$ by [prop-weight-separation]. Cross
multiplication over $\Ql[T]$ and coprimality therefore give
$A^{(\ell)}=N_\ell$ and $B^{(\ell)}=D_\ell$. Hence every root of
$A^\#$ or $B^\#$ maps under $\jmath_\ell$ to a root of $N_\ell^\#$
or $D_\ell^\#$ in the [def-weil-ordinary-reciprocal-roots]
convention, that is, to a reciprocal root of exactly one of the factors
$P_{i,\ell}$ (distinct $P_{i,\ell}$ being coprime by
[prop-weight-separation]); the weight of that factor is a weight of
the root, because every root of $P_{i,\ell}$ has absolute value
$q^{i/2}$ by [prop-weight-purity-roots] and an arbitrary complex
embedding of the number field generated by the root extends to an
isomorphism of algebraic closures by [lem-embedding-extension]. For
the same reason the weight is independent of the chosen $\ell$ and
realization, the $q$-Weil condition of [def-weil-numbers] being
stable under $\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathbf Q}/\mathbf Q)$ and
under every embedding of its number field into $\mathbf C$; the
conditions of distinct weights are mutually exclusive because
$q^{i/2}\neq q^{j/2}$ for $i\neq j$. Each root of $A^\#$ or $B^\#$
therefore has a unique weight in $\{0,\ldots,2d\}$, and the multisets
$R_i$ of [thm-weil-realization-independence] are stable under
$\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathbf Q}/\mathbf Q)$.

The seven clauses of [prop-functor-package] apply to the global
finite-field datum. Their domains and hypotheses are retained verbatim:
the dimension-free internal-Hom bound uses a site-perfect first
variable. General Hom coefficient comparison and exceptional adjunction
hold on the constructible domains proved in the package. General
Verdier biduality at all four coefficient stages is
[thm-sf-biduality-class]; finite coefficients use $D^b_{ctf}$,
and the integral and field stages use the specified $D^b_c$.

## Proof

Apply the terminal assembly [prop-functor-package]. This theorem is
an export of its seven clauses and is not an input to their proofs.

attrs.title: The assembled operations on their proved domains

objects.body:
Let $X_0$ be a smooth geometrically connected affine curve over
$k_0=\mathbf F_q$, and let $\mathcal G$ be a nonzero lisse
$\iota$-real Weil sheaf, punctually
$\iota$-pure of weight $w$. Then

$$
\|\mathcal G\|=w
$$

in the $L^2$-weight parameter of [def-wf-l2-norm].

## Proof

Put $\mathcal T=\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal G$.
At every point over every finite extension, the trace of $\mathcal G$
is real by [def-wf-iota-real]. Hence the trace of $\mathcal T$
is its square, equal to the squared absolute value of that trace.
The logarithm of the Frobenius determinant
[lem-zl-log-det-identity] (applied to each local factor, with
$T\mapsto t^{d(x)}$, and transported to $\mathbf C[[t]]$ by the field
isomorphism $\iota$, exactly as in the proof of
[lem-wf-conjugate-tensor-traces]) and the Euler product
[cor-rp-euler-product] therefore give

$$
\varphi_{\mathcal G}(t)=L'(t)/L(t),\qquad
L(t)=\frac{\iota\det(1-Ft,H_c^1(X,\mathcal T))}
{\iota\det(1-Ft,H_c^2(X,\mathcal T))}.
$$

Here $\varphi_{\mathcal G}$ is the series of
[def-wf-l2-series].

The tensor $\mathcal T$ is lisse and punctually pure of weight $2w$:
its local eigenvalues are products of two eigenvalues of weight $w$ ([p-linear-spectra]).
The endpoint lemma [lem-a1-middle-extension-endpoints], applied with
$j$ the identity of $X_0$ (so that $j_*\mathcal T=\mathcal T$), shows
that $H_c^2(X,\mathcal T)$ is $\iota$-pure of weight $2w+2$ in the
sense of [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights]: its Frobenius
eigenvalues $\alpha$ have $\iota$-modulus $q^{w+1}$. Hence every
denominator root $\alpha^{-1}$ of $L$, if there are any, has modulus

$$
R=q^{-w-1}.
$$

At least one of these roots remains a pole after cancellation.
Indeed [lem-rp-even-tensor-positivity], applied to
$\mathcal G$ with tensor exponent two, says that every local Euler
factor of $L$ has nonnegative real Taylor coefficients and constant
term one. Thus the coefficients of $L$ dominate those of any one
local factor. Choose a closed point $x$ of the nonempty curve.
Since $\mathcal G$ is nonzero lisse, its rank at $x$ is positive,
and the local factor for $\mathcal T$ is the reciprocal of a
nonconstant polynomial with nonzero leading coefficient.
Such a reciprocal has infinitely many nonzero Taylor coefficients:
if it were a polynomial, its product with the denominator would be
one, contradicting degrees. It follows that $L$ cannot be a
polynomial. As its denominator has all its roots on $|t|=R$,
its reduced rational expression has a pole on that circle.

The logarithmic derivative has a pole at every pole of $L$:
locally $L=(t-t_0)^{-a}u$, $a>0$, $u(t_0)\neq0$, gives
$L'/L=-a/(t-t_0)+u'/u$.
Consequently the Taylor radius of $\varphi_{\mathcal G}$ is at most
$R$. On the other hand [lem-wf-l2-upper], applied to the
punctually pure sheaf, bounds that radius below by $R$.
It is therefore exactly $q^{-w-1}$, and
[def-wf-l2-series], [def-wf-l2-norm], [lem-wf-l2-radius] gives
$\|\mathcal G\|=w$.

attrs.title: The Fourier-analytic weight of a pure real sheaf equals its weight

objects.body:
Let $U_0/\mathbf F_q$ be normal, geometrically connected,
separated and of finite type,
pure of dimension one. Put
$U=U_0\times_{\mathbf F_q}\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and
$\Pi=\pi_1(U,\bar u)$. Let $\ell\nmid q$, let
$E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite, and let

$$
\chi:\hyperref[def-wf-weil-group]{W(U_0,\bar u)}\longrightarrow E^\times
$$

be a continuous character. Then $\chi(\Pi)$ is finite. Equivalently,
there is $N\geq1$ such that $\chi(g)^N=1$ for every $g\in\Pi$.
The scheme and Weil-group conventions are those of
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], [def-wf-weil-group].

## Proof

Choose $s\in W(U_0,\bar u)$ of degree one. By
[lem-wf-compact-character-logarithm], there are $N,r\geq1$ and a
continuous additive character

$$
\lambda(g)=\log(\chi(g)^N):\Pi\longrightarrow E
$$

which is invariant under $g\mapsto s^{-1}gs$. The Frobenius-equivariant
isomorphism of [lem-wf-additive-characters-h1] is applied after
choosing a $\mathbf Q_\ell$-basis $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ of $E$ and its
dual coordinate maps $t_i:E\to\mathbf Q_\ell$. Each
$f_i=t_i\circ\lambda$ is a continuous additive character invariant under
$g\mapsto s^{-1}gs$. Its image is compact, hence bounded; choose one
integer $a$ such that
$\ell^a f_i(\Pi)\subseteq\mathbf Z_\ell$ for every $i$. Put
$f_i'=\ell^a f_i$. The lemma gives compatible reductions

$$
[f'_{i,n}]\in H^1_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(U,\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z)
\qquad(n\geq1).
\tag{6.1}
$$

Their Frobenius invariance follows from the invariance of $\lambda$ and
the equivariance in [lem-wf-additive-characters-h1]. Hence (6.1) is a
fixed element of the inverse limit, and it is zero by
[prop-wf-open-curve-h1-no-frobenius-fixed]. The isomorphism in
[lem-wf-additive-characters-h1] then gives $f_i'=0$, for every
$i$. Since the $t_i$ separate points of $E$, $\lambda=0$ on
$\Pi$.

The logarithm is injective on $1+\mathfrak m_E^r$ by
[lem-wf-deep-principal-unit-log]. It follows that

$$
\chi(g)^N=1\qquad(g\in\Pi).
$$

Thus $\chi(\Pi)$ is contained in the set of roots of the polynomial
$T^N-1$, and is finite. Conversely, if $\chi(\Pi)$ is finite, its
exponent supplies such an $N$.

attrs.title: Finite geometric image of a rank-one Weil character on a curve

objects.body:
Fix the finite-field datum
$(p,a,q,k_0,k)$, where $q=p^a$, and a prime $\ell\neq p$; write
$\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$,
and interpret the $\Qlb$-objects in the
algebraically closed
coefficient category. Let $X_0/k_0$ be
smooth, proper, geometrically
connected of pure dimension $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, put
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $(\Qlb)_X$ be the constant
Weil sheaf with its canonical Weil
structure. Let $F$ be the
global geometric Frobenius
on the ordinary and
compact-support cohomology of $(\Qlb)_X$, in the
geometric-Frobenius convention. For every
$0\leq i\leq2d$, put

$$
V_i=H^i(X,\Qlb),\qquad F_i=F\vert_{V_i},\qquad
P_{i,\ell}(T)=\det(1-TF_i\mid V_i)\in\Qlb[T],
$$

the data obtained from the
smooth-proper
cohomological family by scalar extension. Let $Z(X_0,T)$ be the
point-count zeta series, and assume
the point-counting trace formula
[cor-trf-point-counting] of the trace-formula chapter for the constant Weil
sheaf. Then

$$
\boxed{
Z(X_0,T)=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}P_{i,\ell}(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}}
\quad\text{in }\Qlb[[T]].
$$

## Proof

Step 1: the point-count identity. The scheme $X_0$ is proper, so by
[cor-trf-point-counting] applied to the constant Weil sheaf
$(\Qlb)_X$, for every $n\geq1$,

$$
N_n:=\#X_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})
=\sum_{i\in\mathbf Z}(-1)^i\Tr\bigl(F^n\mid H^i(X,\Qlb)\bigr)
=\sum_{i=0}^{2d}(-1)^i\Tr(F_i^n\mid V_i),
$$

the second identity being the finite-dimensionality, the vanishing
outside $0\leq i\leq2d$, and the identification
$V_i=H^i(X,\Qlb)$, $F_i=F|_{V_i}$, supplied by
[def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] (compactly supported
cohomology being the ordinary one for proper $X_0$, per that
definition) and by [def-weil-smooth-proper-cohomological-family]
after scalar extension to $\Qlb$.

Step 2: the logarithm of the zeta series. By
[def-weil-point-counts-zeta],

$$
Z(X_0,T)=\exp\left(\sum_{n\geq1}N_n\frac{T^n}{n}\right),
$$

so that, the formal logarithm and the exponential being mutually
inverse on $T\Qlb[[T]]$ and $1+T\Qlb[[T]]$,

$$
\log Z(X_0,T)=\sum_{n\geq1}N_n\frac{T^n}{n}.
$$

Step 3: substitution and interchange. Inserting Step 1 and using that
the sum over $i=0,\ldots,2d$ is finite while the coefficientwise sums
over $n$ are formal,

$$
\log Z(X_0,T)
=\sum_{n\geq1}\sum_{i=0}^{2d}(-1)^i\Tr(F_i^n\mid V_i)\frac{T^n}{n}
=\sum_{i=0}^{2d}(-1)^i
\left(\sum_{n\geq1}\Tr(F_i^n\mid V_i)\frac{T^n}{n}\right).
$$

Step 4: the per-degree logarithm. For every $i$, the pair
$(V_i,F_i)$ is a Frobenius module, so [lem-zl-log-det-identity]
gives

$$
\sum_{n\geq1}\Tr(F_i^n\mid V_i)\frac{T^n}{n}
=-\log P_{i,\ell}(T).
$$

Hence, by the additivity of the formal logarithm on finite products of
series with constant coefficient $1$,

$$
\log Z(X_0,T)
=\sum_{i=0}^{2d}(-1)^{i+1}\log P_{i,\ell}(T)
=\log\left(\prod_{i=0}^{2d}P_{i,\ell}(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}\right).
$$

Step 5: exponentiation. Both sides of the identity of Step 4 have the
same logarithm and lie in $1+T\Qlb[[T]]$, so applying the formal
exponential, which is inverse to the logarithm on that set, gives the
displayed identity.

Every constructible $\iota$-real $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf on a separated
finite-type scheme over a finite field is $\iota$-mixed, with a
finite filtration in the sense of [def-weil-punctual-weights].

## Proof

First suppose $X_0$ is smooth geometrically connected affine of
positive dimension and $\mathcal G$ is lisse in
[def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] and real in
[def-wf-iota-real]. We construct the finite Weil filtration
required by [def-weil-punctual-weights]. By
[lem-zl-geometric-constituents-any-base], after one finite
constant extension its Weil filtration has geometrically irreducible
quotients $\mathcal S_1,\ldots,\mathcal S_r$.
The extension preserves reality: local Frobenius becomes a positive
integral power of the old one, and powering preserves conjugation-stable
spectra. Work over this new finite field.

Fix a closed point $x_*\in X_0$. For any other closed point
$x$, apply [lem-zl-curve-testing-irreducibility] through chosen
geometric points above $x_*$ and $x$. On the resulting smooth
geometrically connected affine curve, over a further finite field,
$\mathcal G$ is real and each $\mathcal S_j$ remains geometrically,
hence arithmetically, irreducible. Pullback is exact, so it is an
irreducible constituent of the restricted real sheaf. The already
proved curve theorem [thm-rp-real-lisse-purity-affine] makes it
punctually pure there.

The weight obtained on this curve is independent of the curve.
Indeed, if its point over $x_*$ has residue degree $e$ over
$\kappa(x_*)$, its Frobenius eigenvalues are $\alpha^e$, where
$\alpha$ runs through the eigenvalues of $\mathcal S_j$ at
$x_*$; its residue cardinality is $q_{x_*}^e$. Thus curve purity
forces all those $\alpha$ to have one common modulus and fixes the
weight as

$$
w_j=2\log_{q_{x_*}}|\iota(\alpha)|.
$$

The same power calculation at $x$ proves that every eigenvalue
there has modulus $q_x^{w_j/2}$. As $x$ was arbitrary,
$\mathcal S_j$ is pure of weight $w_j$ on all of $X_0$.
The actual Weil filtration, rather than separately chosen stalk
filtrations, now proves that $\mathcal G$ is mixed.

To descend the initial constant extension $g:X'_0\to X_0$, push
this filtration forward. Finite pushforward is exact and preserves
pure weights by [lem-zl-finite-pushforward]. The diagonal unit
$\eta:\mathcal G\to g_*g^*\mathcal G$ is split as follows.
Write $d=\deg(g)$. Etale-locally the finite etale map $g$ is a
disjoint union of $d$ copies of the base, so summation on the copies
defines a map $\operatorname{Tr}:g_*g^*\mathcal G\to\mathcal G$.
Summation is unchanged by permuting the copies; hence these local maps
glue and commute with Frobenius. They satisfy
$\operatorname{Tr}\circ\eta=d\operatorname{id}$.
Since $d$ is invertible in $\Qlb$,
$d^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}$ is a Weil-equivariant retraction. Thus
[lem-a1-mixed-direct-summand] descends mixedness.

For a general constructible sheaf, pass by [i-topology] to the reduction of the
geometric scheme and form a finite chain of reduced closed subschemes

$$
X=Z_0\supset Z_1\supset\cdots\supset Z_t=\varnothing
$$

such that $U_a=Z_a\setminus Z_{a+1}$ is a disjoint union of smooth
connected affine pieces on which the sheaf is lisse. To construct a
step, take in each irreducible component of $Z_a$ a dense smooth
affine open inside the lisse locus, avoiding all the other components.
Their disjoint union is open in $Z_a$; its closed complement has
smaller dimension. Constructibility and Noetherian induction give
the finite chain. This also arranges the frontier condition needed
for successive open–closed gluing.

All these finitely many subschemes, affine pieces, and inclusions are
of finite presentation over $\overline{\mathbf F}_q$. Their
defining equations therefore descend to one finite constant-field
extension. Choose that extension large enough to define each
geometric component individually. Its Frobenius is a power of the
original Frobenius and preserves every piece, so restriction of the
original Weil structure supplies the required Weil structures there.
The pieces are geometrically connected over this field. The preceding
argument applies to those of positive dimension; in dimension zero a
Jordan filtration of each invertible Frobenius operator gives pure
factors of weights $2\log_{q_x}|\iota(\alpha)|$. On a finite disjoint
union, extend the filtrations of its components by zero and concatenate
them; this gives a mixed filtration even if their weights differ.

Mixed filtrations glue across a closed complement: for an open
$j:U_0\hookrightarrow X_0$ and closed complement $i:Z_0\hookrightarrow X_0$, use the exact sequence

$$
0\longrightarrow j_!j^*\mathcal G\longrightarrow\mathcal G
\longrightarrow i_*i^*\mathcal G\longrightarrow0.
$$

Both $j_!$ and $i_*$ are exact and preserve purity of a sheaf
already pure on its support, since their other stalks are zero.
Splice the resulting finite filtrations using inverse images under
the quotient map. Apply this to each pair
$U_a\subset Z_a$, with closed complement $Z_{a+1}$, starting
at the last nonempty member of the chain. All inclusions are defined
over the chosen finite field, so every extension and inverse image is
Weil-equivariant. The finite induction gives a global finite Weil
filtration. Finally descend the common constant extension as above.

attrs.title: Mixedness of real sheaves by reduction to the proved curve case

objects.body:
Fix the coefficient and weight conventions of
[def-weil-punctual-weights]. Let $h:U_0\to Y_0$ be a
smooth separated morphism
between separated finite-type
$k_0$-schemes, with every nonempty geometric fiber a smooth affine
curve. Let $\mathcal F$ be a
lisse
$\Qlb$-Weil sheaf that is
punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$.
Then for every $i$, $R^ih_!\mathcal F$ is $\iota$-mixed of weights
at most $w+i$.

## Proof

By [lem-zl-relative-curve-punctual], all local Frobenius
eigenvalues on $R^ih_!\mathcal F$ have absolute value at most
$q_y^{(w+i)/2}$. The curve-reduction lemma [lem-zl-relative-curve-mixedness]
supplies a finite mixed filtration of this sheaf. Apply
[lem-zl-mixed-punctual-cutoff] with $v=w+i$.
This proves the bound without assuming that unrelated filtrations
of the individual stalks glue to Weil subsheaves.

For the projection $p:\mathbf A^1_{Y_0}\to Y_0$ and every
$K\in D_{\le w}(\mathbf A^1_{Y_0})$, one has
$Rp_!K\in D_{\le w}(Y_0)$.

## Proof

By [lem-zl-sheaves-to-complexes], it suffices to treat a mixed
sheaf of weights at most $w$. Its finite weight filtration and the
extension bounds of [lem-a1-extension-bounds]
(propagated through the long exact sequences) reduce to a pure graded
piece. Apply [thm-zl-relative-line-stratification]: on a
relative-curve stratum the assertion is
[thm-zl-relative-affine-curve-core] (which gives the sheaf-level
bound $R^ap_!\mathcal F$ mixed of weights at most $w+a$, for pure
$\mathcal F$); on a quasi-finite stratum it is
[lem-zl-quasi-finite]. The composition constraint
[lem-zl-shriek-composition] identifies these stratumwise direct
images with the corresponding pieces of $Rp_!$. Noetherian induction,
using the one-way localization gluing rule [lem-zl-open-closed-weight]
for an open–closed decomposition of the strata, in the morphism-level
form [lem-zl-morphism-open-closed-reduction], reassembles the source
and target strata.

Let $Y_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme and let $\mathcal F$
be a constructible Weil sheaf on $\mathbf A^1_{Y_0}$ (in the
constructible conventions of [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]).
There are finite stratifications of source and target such that
$\mathcal F$ is lisse on every source stratum and each induced map is
either separated quasi-finite or smooth with one-dimensional affine
geometric fibers.

## Proof

We work with reduced strata; by [i-topology], nilpotent thickenings do not change the
etale coefficient categories. We induct on closed subsets of the
Noetherian target, and first explain the step on an integral affine
target $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$. The scheme
$\mathbf A^1_Y$ is integral. Constructibility in
[def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] gives a nonempty open
$U\subset\mathbf A^1_Y$ on which $\mathcal F$ is lisse.
Let $Z=\mathbf A^1_Y\setminus U$, with its reduced closed structure.
If $Z$ is empty there is nothing to remove. Otherwise its ideal
$I\subset B[T]$ contains a nonzero polynomial $g$.
This is also nonzero over $\operatorname{Frac}B$, since $B$ is a
domain. Let $b\in B\setminus\{0\}$ be its leading coefficient.
Over $V=D(b)$, the polynomial $b^{-1}g$ is monic. Consequently

$$
B_b[T]/I B_b[T]
$$

is a finite $B_b$-module: it is a quotient of the module generated
by $1,T,\ldots,T^{\deg(g)-1}$ using that monic relation.
When $g$ has degree zero the quotient is zero. Thus $Z_V\to V$
is finite, including the empty case.

The open complement $U_V=\mathbf A^1_V\setminus Z_V$ still has
$\mathcal F$ lisse. It is an open subscheme of the smooth projection
of [def-sbc-affine-space], so $U_V\to V$ is smooth of relative
dimension one. Its geometric fibers are affine lines with finitely many
points removed. Such a fiber is affine: over the geometric residue
field it is a principal open defined by the product of the finitely
many linear factors of the removed points. It is nonempty and connected.
Choose a finite lissity stratification of $\mathcal F|_{Z_V}$.
Every resulting locally closed source stratum has finite geometric
fibers over $V$, and hence is separated quasi-finite by
[pqf-def-quasifinite]. We have obtained exactly the two asserted
types over the nonempty target open $V$.

For an arbitrary nonempty reduced target, choose in each of its finitely
many irreducible components an affine open avoiding all other components.
These disjoint integral opens contain all generic points. The affine
refinement can also be made using [lem-zl-affine-partition].
Perform the preceding construction on each, and take the union of the
resulting nonempty opens $V$. Its complement is a proper closed
subset of the target. Apply the induction hypothesis to the relative
affine line and the restricted sheaf over that complement. This gives
finitely many further strata. Noetherian induction terminates, so the
combined source and target partitions are finite. Refining the lissity
partitions of the quasi-finite pieces to open–closed filtrations does
not change their quasi-finiteness, and makes all gluing steps compatible
with localization.

All lissity loci can be chosen over the finite-field model: lissity is
preserved by the Weil isomorphism. Equivalently, descend the finitely
many constructible strata to a common finite constant extension and
intersect their finitely many Frobenius conjugate dense opens; this
retains the lisse open used above. The closed complements and their
successive strata are then Weil-stable. Thus the filtration is a
filtration by Weil sheaves, not just by unrelated geometric sheaves.
At no point is smoothness deduced merely from the set of points of a
fiber; it comes from restricting the known smooth affine-line projection.
