attrs.title: Stratification of a sheaf on a relative line

objects.body:
Let $f:X_0\to Y_0$ be a
separated finite-type
morphism of separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes.
There are finite partitions of source and target by locally closed
reduced subschemes such that each source piece $X'_0$, mapping to
a target piece $Y'_0$, has
coordinates inducing a
factorization

$$
X'_0\xrightarrow{\nu}\mathbf A^d_{Y'_0}
\longrightarrow\mathbf A^{d-1}_{Y'_0}\longrightarrow\cdots
\longrightarrow\mathbf A^1_{Y'_0}\longrightarrow Y'_0
$$

with $\nu$ finite and all subsequent arrows the coordinate
projections of relative affine space.
For $d=0$, the factorization consists just of the finite map
$X'_0\to Y'_0=\mathbf A^0_{Y'_0}$.

## Proof

All schemes under consideration are Noetherian. We use induction
on closed subsets of the target, with their reduced structures.
This induction terminates because a Noetherian space has no infinite
strictly descending chain of closed subsets.

For a nonempty reduced target $Y$, take the finitely many
irreducible components. In each component choose a nonempty
affine open avoiding all the other components. These give disjoint
integral affine opens $V_j=\operatorname{Spec}A_j$ of $Y$;
their union contains every generic point of $Y$.
For each $j$, apply [lem-zl-affine-partition] to
$X_0\times_{Y_0}V_j$. The resulting finitely many reduced affine
pieces are $\operatorname{Spec}B_{ji}$, with $B_{ji}$
a finitely generated $A_j$-algebra.

Apply [lem-zl-spread-normalization] to every $A_j\to B_{ji}$.
For fixed $j$, multiply the finitely many nonzero denominators
to obtain $s_j$. Localizing the resulting finite module
generators once more preserves their generation, so all pieces
over $D(s_j)\subset V_j$ simultaneously have finite maps to
relative affine spaces. These maps are the explicit
[def-zl-localized-coordinates] maps.
The open subset $V=\bigcup_jD(s_j)$ still contains every generic
point of $Y$, and its pieces and their inverse images give the
required finite partitions over $V$.

The complement $Y\setminus V$ is a proper closed subset.
Apply the induction hypothesis to the restriction of $f$ over
this complement. Reduced source pieces factor through the reduced
target, since a nilpotent section maps to zero in a reduced ring.
Combining those partitions with the pieces over $V$ gives finite
partitions of source and target by locally closed reduced
subschemes, as in [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions].
Finally the standard coordinate projections factor each
$\mathbf A^d_{Y'_0}\to Y'_0$ into the $d$ relative affine-line
projections of [def-sbc-affine-space].

For every separated finite-type morphism $f:X_0\to Y_0$ of separated
finite-type $k_0$-schemes and every constructible $\Qlb$-Weil complex
$K$ (in the coefficient categories of
[def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]),

$$
K\in D_{\le w}(X_0)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad Rf_!K\in D_{\le w}(Y_0),
$$

where $D_{\le w}$ is the complex-weight predicate of
[def-weil-complex-weights].

## Proof

By [cor-zl-rfshriek-sheaf], every mixed Weil sheaf $\mathcal F$ of
weights at most $v$ has $R^af_!\mathcal F$ mixed of weights at most
$v+a$, for every $a$. This is the hypothesis of
[lem-zl-sheaves-to-complexes], which gives $Rf_!K\in D_{\le w}(Y_0)$.

The formal proof (`exists_lift_blowup` together with
`hom_ext_of_isInvertible_comap`) takes the
Stacks-style hypothesis that the inverse image ideal sheaf of the center is
effective Cartier, and is entirely chart-local: existence is glued from the
universal property of the chart ring $A[\mathcal I/a]$
(`AffineBlowup.chartRingLift`) on affine probes, and uniqueness
follows from chart-ring extensionality
(`chartRingHom_ext`) together with the chart-overlap localization.
The graded-map and tensor-power scaffolding
([thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property],
[lemma-nagata-invertible-ideal-tensor-power],
[lemma-nagata-relative-proj-invertible-tensor-powers],
[thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property]) is not formalized.

shiftSpan.signature: def shiftSpan.{u_1} (R : Type u_1) [Semiring R] (a : ℕ → R) : Submodule R (ℕ → R)
shiftSpan.doc: The `R`-span of all iterated left shifts of a sequence `a : ℕ → R`.

ringKrullDim_quotient_lt_of_finiteType.signature:
theorem ringKrullDim_quotient_lt_of_finiteType.{u_1, u_2} (k : Type u_1) (A : Type u_2) [Field k]
  [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [Algebra k A] [Algebra.FiniteType k A] (P : Ideal A) [P.IsPrime]
  (hP : P ≠ ⊥) : ringKrullDim (A ⧸ P) < ringKrullDim A
ringKrullDim_quotient_lt_of_finiteType.doc:
A proper closed subset of an irreducible affine variety has strictly smaller dimension: for a
finitely generated domain `A` over a field and a nonzero prime `P` of `A`,
`dim (A ⧸ P) < dim A`. (blueprint: `sk-i-geometry`)

reesAlgebra.signature: def reesAlgebra.{u} {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) : Subalgebra R (Polynomial R)
reesAlgebra.doc:
The Rees algebra of an ideal `I`, defined as the subalgebra of `R[X]` whose `i`-th coefficient
falls in `I ^ i`.

killingForm.signature:
def killingForm.{u_1, u_3} (R : Type u_1) (L : Type u_3) [CommRing R] [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra R L] :
  LinearMap.BilinForm R L
killingForm.doc:
A finite, free (as an `R`-module) Lie algebra `L` carries a bilinear form on `L`.

This is a specialisation of `LieModule.traceForm` to the adjoint representation of `L`.

isZero_Ext_succ_of_projective.signature:
theorem isZero_Ext_succ_of_projective.{u_1, v_1, u_2} {R : Type u_1} [Ring R] {C : Type u_2}
  [CategoryTheory.Category.{v_1, u_2} C] [CategoryTheory.Abelian C] [CategoryTheory.Linear R C]
  [CategoryTheory.EnoughProjectives C] (X Y : C) [CategoryTheory.Projective X] (n : ℕ) :
  CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero (((Ext R C (n + 1)).obj (Opposite.op X)).obj Y)
isZero_Ext_succ_of_projective.doc: If `X : C` is projective and `n : ℕ`, then `Ext^(n + 1) X Y ≅ 0` for any `Y`.

isReduced_tensorProduct_of_perfectField.signature:
theorem isReduced_tensorProduct_of_perfectField.{u_1, u_2, u_3} (k : Type u_1) (A : Type u_2) (B : Type u_3)
  [Field k] [PerfectField k] [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra k A] [Algebra k B] [IsReduced A]
  [IsReduced B] : IsReduced (TensorProduct k A B)
isReduced_tensorProduct_of_perfectField.doc:
Over a perfect field `k`, the tensor product of two reduced `k`-algebras is reduced.
(blueprint: `sk-i-geometry`)

By `isReduced_tensorProduct_of_forall_residueField`, applied in both factors, this reduces to the
tensor product of two field extensions, `isReduced_tensorProduct_of_field`.

iInf_ker_algHom_eq_nilradical.signature:
theorem iInf_ker_algHom_eq_nilradical.{u_1, u_2} (k : Type u_1) (A : Type u_2) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
  [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [Algebra.FiniteType k A] : ⨅ φ, RingHom.ker φ = nilradical A
iInf_ker_algHom_eq_nilradical.doc:
The vanishing principle: over an algebraically closed field `k`, an element of a finitely
generated `k`-algebra vanishing at every `k`-point is nilpotent.
(blueprint: `sk-i-geometry`)

exteriorPower.map.doc: The linear map between `n`th exterior powers induced by a linear map between the modules.

exists_isOpen_inter_subset_of_isConstruc.signature:
theorem exists_isOpen_inter_subset_of_isConstructible.{u_1} {X : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace X]
  [TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace X] {s t : Set X} (hs : Topology.IsConstructible s)
  (_ht : IsClosed t) (hirr : IsIrreducible t) (hst : closure s = t) :
  ∃ u, IsOpen u ∧ (u ∩ t).Nonempty ∧ u ∩ t ⊆ s
exists_isOpen_inter_subset_of_isConstruc.doc:
A constructible set `s` dense in an irreducible closed set `t` contains a nonempty open subset
of `t`. (blueprint: `sk-i-geometry`)

The Noetherian hypothesis is not needed for the proof.

exists_finite_inj_algHom_polynomial_of_r.signature:
theorem exists_finite_inj_algHom_polynomial_of_ringKrullDim_eq_one.{u_1, u_2} (K : Type u_1) (B : Type u_2)
  [Field K] [CommRing B] [Algebra K B] [Algebra.FiniteType K B] (hB : ringKrullDim B = 1) :
  ∃ g, Function.Injective ⇑g ∧ g.Finite
exists_finite_inj_algHom_polynomial_of_r.doc:
Blueprint `sk-i-real-normalization`: One-dimensional Noether normalization.

A finitely generated algebra `B` of Krull dimension one over a field `K` admits an injective
`K`-algebra map from the polynomial ring `K[T]` making `B` a finite module.

Nontriviality of `B` is automatic: the zero ring has `ringKrullDim = ⊥`. This is the case
`n = 1` of `exists_finite_inj_algHom_mvPolynomial_of_ringKrullDim_eq`, along the isomorphism
`MvPolynomial (Fin 1) K ≃ₐ[K] K[T]`.

exists_finite_inj_algHom_of_fg.signature:
theorem exists_finite_inj_algHom_of_fg.{u_2, u_3} (k : Type u_2) (R : Type u_3) [Field k] [CommRing R]
  [Nontrivial R] [a : Algebra k R] [fin : Algebra.FiniteType k R] :
  ∃ s g, Function.Injective ⇑g ∧ g.Finite
exists_finite_inj_algHom_of_fg.doc:
For a finitely generated algebra `A` over a field `k`,
there exists a natural number `s` and an injective homomorphism
from `k[X_0, X_1, ..., X_(s-1)]` to `A` such that `A` is finite over `k[X_0, X_1, ..., X_(s-1)]`.

exists_algHom_ker_eq_of_isMaximal.signature:
theorem exists_algHom_ker_eq_of_isMaximal.{u_1, u_2} (k : Type u_1) (A : Type u_2) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
  [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [Algebra.FiniteType k A] (𝔪 : Ideal A) [𝔪.IsMaximal] :
  ∃ φ, RingHom.ker φ = 𝔪
exists_algHom_ker_eq_of_isMaximal.doc:
Over an algebraically closed field `k`, every maximal ideal of a finitely generated
`k`-algebra is the kernel of a `k`-algebra map to `k`: closed points have residue field `k`.
(blueprint: `sk-i-geometry`)

dense_iInf_of_genericPoints_subset.doc:
The intersection of a finite family of open sets each of which contains all the generic
points of the irreducible components is dense.

cyclotomicTateModule.signature:
def cyclotomicTateModule.{u_1} (K : Type u_1) [CommMonoid K] (l : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime l)] :
  AddSubgroup (ℕ → Additive Kˣ)
cyclotomicTateModule.doc:
The cyclotomic Tate module `ℤ_ℓ(1)` of a field `K` (only the multiplicative monoid of `K` is
used). The group
`μ_{ℓ^n}(K) = {u ∈ Kˣ : u ^ ℓ ^ n = 1}` of `ℓ^n`-th roots of unity forms an inverse system under
the `ℓ`-th power maps, and `ℤ_ℓ(1)` is the group of compatible systems `(u n)` with
`u n ∈ μ_{ℓ^n}(K)` and `u (n + 1) ^ ℓ = u n`: that is, the Tate module of the abelian group
`Kˣ`, written additively. The rational cyclotomic Tate module `ℚ_ℓ(1)` is the localisation
`ℤ_ℓ(1)[1/ℓ]`; it is not defined separately here.
(blueprint: `sk-d-ab-cyclotomic`)

cyclotomicCharacter_frobeniusEquiv_pow_i.signature:
theorem cyclotomicCharacter_frobeniusEquiv_pow_inv_mul.{u_1} (K : Type u_1) [Field K] [IsAlgClosed K]
  (p : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] [CharP K p] (a l : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime l)] (hl : l ≠ p) :
  ↑((cyclotomicCharacter K l) (frobeniusEquiv K p ^ a)⁻¹) * ↑p ^ a = 1
cyclotomicCharacter_frobeniusEquiv_pow_i.doc:
The geometric Frobenius `F = σ⁻¹`, the inverse of the `q = p ^ a` power Frobenius, acts on the
cyclotomic Tate module `ℤ_ℓ(1)` as multiplication by `q⁻¹`; in particular `q` is a unit of `ℤ_ℓ`,
which holds because `ℓ ≠ p`.
(blueprint: `sk-p-cyclotomic`)

cyclotomicCharacter_frobeniusEquiv_pow.signature:
theorem cyclotomicCharacter_frobeniusEquiv_pow.{u_1} (K : Type u_1) [Field K] [IsAlgClosed K] (p : ℕ)
  [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] [CharP K p] (a l : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime l)] (hl : l ≠ p) :
  ↑((cyclotomicCharacter K l) (frobeniusEquiv K p ^ a)) = ↑p ^ a
cyclotomicCharacter_frobeniusEquiv_pow.doc:
The `q = p ^ a` power arithmetic Frobenius acts on the cyclotomic Tate module `ℤ_ℓ(1)` as
multiplication by `q`.
(blueprint: `sk-p-cyclotomic`)

ValuationSubring.exists_comap_eq.signature:
theorem ValuationSubring.exists_comap_eq.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} [Field K] [Field L]
  (f : K →+* L) (A : ValuationSubring K) : ∃ B, B.comap f = A
ValuationSubring.exists_comap_eq.doc:
**Extension of a valuation ring to a field extension** (Stacks Project Tag 00IA):
for every field extension `f : K →+* L` and every valuation subring `A ⊆ K` there is a
valuation subring `B ⊆ L` with `K ∩ B = A`; its fraction field is `L`, as for every
valuation subring of `L`.

ValuationSubring.comap_eq_of_toLocalSubr.doc:
**Intersection with a dominating valuation ring** (consequence of Stacks Project
Tag 052K): if a valuation subring `B` of a field extension `L` of `K` dominates a
valuation subring `A ⊆ K` — that is, `A ≤ B.comap f` in the domination order of local
subrings of `K` — then `K ∩ B = A`, i.e. `B.comap f = A`.
(Blueprint: `lemma:nagata-valuation-intersection`.)

ValuationSubring.comapResidue.signature:
def ValuationSubring.comapResidue.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] (A : ValuationSubring K)
  (A'' : ValuationSubring (IsLocalRing.ResidueField ↥A)) : ValuationSubring K
ValuationSubring.comapResidue.doc:
**The composite of two valuation rings**: the preimage in a valuation subring
`A ⊆ K` of a valuation subring `A''` of the residue field of `A` is a valuation subring
of `K`. (Blueprint: `lemma:nagata-composite-valuation-ring`.)

TraceDatum.zeta_mul_prod_even_eq_prod_od.signature:
theorem TraceDatum.zeta_mul_prod_even_eq_prod_odd.{u, v} {K : Type u} [Field K] {r : ℕ} (D : TraceDatum K r)
  [CharZero K] : D.zeta * ∏ i with Even ↑i, ↑(D.P i) = ∏ i with Odd ↑i, ↑(D.P i)
TraceDatum.zeta_mul_prod_even_eq_prod_od.doc:
**The cohomological determinant factorisation**: the counting series of a trace datum is
the alternating product of the reciprocal characteristic polynomials of its endomorphisms,
`Z * ∏_{i even} det (1 - t F i) = ∏_{i odd} det (1 - t F i)`.

TraceDatum.norm_eq_of_mem_roots_charpoly.signature:
theorem TraceDatum.norm_eq_of_mem_roots_charpoly_map_of_pairing.{u, v} {K : Type u} [Field K] [CharZero K]
  {q d : ℕ} (D : TraceDatum K (2 * d)) {p : (i : Fin (2 * d + 1)) → D.V i →ₗ[K] D.V i.rev →ₗ[K] K}
  (hq : 1 < q) (ι : K →+* ℂ) (hp : ∀ (i : Fin (2 * d + 1)), (p i).IsPerfPair)
  (hFG :
    ∀ (i : Fin (2 * d + 1)) (v : D.V i) (w : D.V i.rev),
      ((p i) ((D.F i) v)) ((D.F i.rev) w) = ↑q ^ d * ((p i) v) w)
  (hmixed : ∀ (i : Fin (2 * d + 1)), Polynomial.IsMixedOfWeightLE q (↑i) (Polynomial.map ι (D.P i)))
  (i : Fin (2 * d + 1)) {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ (Polynomial.map ι (LinearMap.charpoly (D.F i))).roots) :
  ‖z‖ = ↑q ^ (↑↑i / 2)
TraceDatum.norm_eq_of_mem_roots_charpoly.doc:
**The weight estimate in eigenvalue form, for a self-dual trace datum.** Under Deligne's
upper bound and the duality of `TraceDatum.isPureOfWeight_map_P_of_pairing`, every complex
eigenvalue of the `i`-th endomorphism of a self-dual trace datum has absolute
value `q ^ (i / 2)`.

TraceDatum.isPureOfWeight_map_P_of_pairi.signature:
theorem TraceDatum.isPureOfWeight_map_P_of_pairing.{u, v} {K : Type u} [Field K] [CharZero K] {q d : ℕ}
  (D : TraceDatum K (2 * d)) {p : (i : Fin (2 * d + 1)) → D.V i →ₗ[K] D.V i.rev →ₗ[K] K}
  (hq : 1 < q) (ι : K →+* ℂ) (hp : ∀ (i : Fin (2 * d + 1)), (p i).IsPerfPair)
  (hFG :
    ∀ (i : Fin (2 * d + 1)) (v : D.V i) (w : D.V i.rev),
      ((p i) ((D.F i) v)) ((D.F i.rev) w) = ↑q ^ d * ((p i) v) w)
  (hmixed : ∀ (i : Fin (2 * d + 1)), Polynomial.IsMixedOfWeightLE q (↑i) (Polynomial.map ι (D.P i)))
  (i : Fin (2 * d + 1)) : Polynomial.IsPureOfWeight q (↑i) (Polynomial.map ι (D.P i))
TraceDatum.isPureOfWeight_map_P_of_pairi.doc:
**Smooth-proper purity.** Duality supplies the lower bound missing from Deligne's estimate.
If the reciprocal characteristic polynomials of a trace datum of length `2 * d` are mixed of
weight at most `i` in degree `i`, and Frobenius acts on a perfect pairing between `D.V i` and
`D.V (2 * d - i)` by the similitude factor `qᵈ`, then the estimate in degree `2 * d - i` bounds
the reciprocal roots in degree `i` from above by `q ^ (i / 2)`, so `D.P i` is pure of
weight `i`.

TraceDatum.exists_isWeilFactorization.signature:
theorem TraceDatum.exists_isWeilFactorization.{u, v} {K : Type u} [Field K] [CharZero K] {q d : ℕ}
  (D : TraceDatum K (2 * d)) (hq : 1 < q) (ι : K →+* ℂ)
  (hpure :
    ∀ (i : Fin (2 * d + 1)), Polynomial.IsUniversallyPureOfWeight q (↑i) (Polynomial.map ι (D.P i)))
  (hzero : Polynomial.map ι (D.P 0) = 1 - Polynomial.X)
  (hlast : Polynomial.map ι (D.P (Fin.last (2 * d))) = 1 - Polynomial.C (↑q ^ d) * Polynomial.X)
  {Z : PowerSeries ℚ} (hZ : (PowerSeries.map (Algebra.algebraMap ℚ K)) Z = D.zeta)
  (hint : ∃ Z', (PowerSeries.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ)) Z' = Z) :
  ∃ P,
    AlgebraicGeometry.IsWeilFactorization q d Z P ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.WeilRiemannHypothesis q d P ∧
        ∀ (i : Fin (2 * d + 1)), Polynomial.map (Int.castRingHom ℂ) (P i) = Polynomial.map ι (D.P i)
TraceDatum.exists_isWeilFactorization.doc:
**The Weil factorisation and the Riemann hypothesis from a trace datum.** Let `D` be a
trace datum of length `2 * d` over a field of characteristic zero, embedded in `ℂ` by `ι`, such
that `(D.P i).map ι` is universally pure of weight `i` for every `i`, that `(D.P 0).map ι` is
`1 - t` and that `(D.P (2 * d)).map ι` is `1 - qᵈ t`. If the counting series `Z` of `D` has
integer coefficients, then there are integer polynomials `P 0, …, P (2 * d)` complexifying to
the `(D.P i).map ι` which give a Weil factorisation of `Z` and satisfy the Riemann hypothesis:
every complex root of `P i` has absolute value `q ^ (-i / 2)`.

TraceDatum.det_mul_det_rev_of_pairing.signature:
theorem TraceDatum.det_mul_det_rev_of_pairing.{u, v} {K : Type u} [Field K] {q d : ℕ}
  (D : TraceDatum K (2 * d)) {p : (i : Fin (2 * d + 1)) → D.V i →ₗ[K] D.V i.rev →ₗ[K] K}
  (hp : ∀ (i : Fin (2 * d + 1)), (p i).IsPerfPair)
  (hFG :
    ∀ (i : Fin (2 * d + 1)) (v : D.V i) (w : D.V i.rev),
      ((p i) ((D.F i) v)) ((D.F i.rev) w) = ↑q ^ d * ((p i) v) w)
  (i : Fin (2 * d + 1)) :
  LinearMap.det (D.F i) * LinearMap.det (D.F i.rev) = ↑q ^ (d * Module.finrank K (D.V i))
TraceDatum.det_mul_det_rev_of_pairing.doc:
**The determinant product rule.** For a trace datum that is self-dual for the similitude
factor `qᵈ`, the determinant constants `Dᵢ = det (D.F i)` satisfy
`Dᵢ · D_{2d-i} = q ^ (d · b i)`, where `b i = dim (D.V i)`.

TraceDatum.signature: structure TraceDatum.{u, v} (K : Type u) [Field K] (r : ℕ) : Type (max u (v + 1))
TraceDatum.doc:
A trace datum over a field `K`: finitely many finite dimensional `K`-vector spaces
`V 0, …, V r` with endomorphisms `F i`, together with integers `N n` computing the
alternating traces `∑ i, (-1) ^ i * tr (F i ^ n)`. This is the linear algebra shadow of a
Lefschetz trace formula.

Representation.exists_multiset_le_and_de.signature:
theorem Representation.exists_multiset_le_and_detWeight_eq_sum_of_exteriorPower.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4}
  {k : Type u_1} [Field k] {W : Type u_2} [Group W] [IsAlgClosed k] [CharZero k]
  (χ : Representation.RealCharacter k) (deg : W →* Multiplicative ℤ) (γ : W) {V : Type u_3}
  [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] [FiniteDimensional k V] [Nontrivial V] (rV : Representation k W V)
  (s : ℕ) {ι : Type u_4} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (Vs : ι → Subrepresentation rV)
  (hsimpleVs : ∀ (j : ι), (Vs j).toRepresentation.IsIrreducible)
  (hdetVs : ∀ (j : ι), Representation.HasFiniteGeometricDet deg (Vs j).toRepresentation)
  (hdirect : DirectSum.IsInternal fun j => (Vs j).toSubmodule)
  {U S : Subrepresentation (rV.exteriorPower s)} (hUS : U < S)
  (hsimple : (S.subquotient U).IsIrreducible)
  (hdet : Representation.HasFiniteGeometricDet deg (S.subquotient U)) :
  ∃ T ≤ Representation.weightMultiset χ γ Vs,
    T.card = s ∧ Representation.detWeight χ γ (S.subquotient U) = T.sum
Representation.exists_multiset_le_and_de.doc:
Let `V` be a nonzero semisimple representation of a degree datum over an algebraically closed
field of characteristic zero, written as an internal direct sum of simple subrepresentations
`Vs j`, with rank-counted weight multiset `Representation.weightMultiset χ γ Vs`: the multiset in
which the determinant weight of `Vs j` occurs `dim Vs j` times.  If the summands `Vs j` and the
simple constituent `Q = S / U` of `⋀^s V` all have finite geometric determinant, then `dw_χ(Q)` is
the sum of a sub-multiset of the weight multiset of size `s`, that is, `a_{i₁} + ⋯ + a_{i_s}` for
indices `i₁ < ⋯ < i_s` in the rank-counted weight list.

The degree map need not be surjective and `γ` need not have degree one: the degrees are the
multiples of some `a`, dividing by `a` gives a degree datum, and every weight at `γ` is the same
multiple of the corresponding weight at a degree-one element.  If all degrees vanish, all the
weights vanish.
(blueprint: `sk-p-exterior`)

Representation.exists_detWeight_eq_add_o.signature:
theorem Representation.exists_detWeight_eq_add_of_subquotient_tprod.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {k : Type u_1}
  [Field k] {W : Type u_2} [Group W] [IsAlgClosed k] [CharZero k]
  (χ : Representation.RealCharacter k) (deg : W →* Multiplicative ℤ) (γ : W) {V : Type u_3}
  {E : Type u_4} [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] [FiniteDimensional k V] [AddCommGroup E] [Module k E]
  [FiniteDimensional k E] (rV : Representation k W V) (rE : Representation k W E)
  (hdetV :
    ∀ (UV SV : Subrepresentation rV),
      (SV.subquotient UV).IsIrreducible →
        Representation.HasFiniteGeometricDet deg (SV.subquotient UV))
  (hdetE :
    ∀ (UE SE : Subrepresentation rE),
      (SE.subquotient UE).IsIrreducible →
        Representation.HasFiniteGeometricDet deg (SE.subquotient UE))
  {U S : Subrepresentation (rV.tprod rE)} (hsimple : (S.subquotient U).IsIrreducible)
  (hdet : Representation.HasFiniteGeometricDet deg (S.subquotient U)) :
  ∃ UV SV UE SE,
    UV < SV ∧
      UE < SE ∧
        (SV.subquotient UV).IsIrreducible ∧
          (SE.subquotient UE).IsIrreducible ∧
            Representation.HasFiniteGeometricDet deg (SV.subquotient UV) ∧
              Representation.HasFiniteGeometricDet deg (SE.subquotient UE) ∧
                Representation.detWeight χ γ (S.subquotient U) =
                  Representation.detWeight χ γ (SV.subquotient UV) +
                    Representation.detWeight χ γ (SE.subquotient UE)
Representation.exists_detWeight_eq_add_o.doc:
Let `V` and `E` be finite-dimensional representations of one and the same degree datum over an
algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, and let `Q` be a simple constituent of `V ⊗ E`,
presented as a subquotient `S / U` for subrepresentations `U < S` of `V ⊗ E`.  If `Q` and all
simple constituents of `V` and of `E` have finite geometric determinant, then
`dw_χ(Q) = dw_χ(V_i) + dw_χ(E_j)` for a simple constituent `V_i = SV / UV` of `V` and a simple
constituent `E_j = SE / UE` of `E`.  Neither `V`, nor `E`, nor `V ⊗ E` is assumed semisimple.

The proof follows the blueprint: `Q` is a subquotient of some `V_i ⊗ E_j`
(`Subrepresentation.exists_subquotient_tprod_equiv`), on which a positive central pair for the
semisimple representation `V_i ⊕ E_j` acts by the product of its scalars on `V_i` and on `E_j`
(`detWeight_subquotient_tprod_eq_add`).  The converse is
`exists_isIrreducible_subquotient_tprod_detWeight_eq_add`.
(blueprint: `sk-p-tensor`, `prop-ag-det-weight-two-factor-tensor`)

def Representation.detWeight.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {k : Type u_1} [Field k] {W : Type u_2} [Group W]

The *determinant weight* of a representation with respect to a real character `χ` and
a degree-one element `γ` is `dw_χ(ρ) = χ(δ(γ)) / dim V`.
(blueprint: `sk-d-weights`)

Representation.detCharacter.signature:
def Representation.detCharacter.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {k : Type u_1} [Field k] {W : Type u_2} [Group W]

Representation.detCharacter.doc:
The *determinant character* of a representation `ρ` is the homomorphism `δ(w) = det ρ(w)`,
valued in the units of `k` because `ρ(w)` is invertible.
(blueprint: `sk-d-weights`)

Representation.RealCharacter.signature: def Representation.RealCharacter.{u_4} (k : Type u_4) [Field k] : Type u_4
Representation.RealCharacter.doc:
A *real character* of the field `k` is a group homomorphism `λ : kˣ → (ℝ, +)` from the units
of `k` to the reals under addition, `λ(ab) = λ(a) + λ(b)`. The weights of this file are read off
through such a character, from the determinants of representations (`detWeight`); for
`k = ℚ̄_ℓ` the relevant one is `log |ι(·)|` for a field embedding `ι : k → ℂ`.
(blueprint: `sk-d-weights`)

Representation.IsSemisimpleRepresentatio.doc: A representation is semisimple when every subrepresentation has a complement.

Representation.IsIrreducible.signature:

  [Field k] [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] (ρ : Representation k G V) : Prop
Representation.IsIrreducible.doc:
A representation `ρ` is irreducible if it is non-trivial and has no proper non-trivial
subrepresentations.

Representation.IsConstituent.doc:
Blueprint `sk-d-real-operations`: Operations, constituents and coinvariants.

`σ.IsConstituent ρ` says that `σ` is a *constituent* of `ρ`: it is irreducible and isomorphic
to a subquotient of `ρ`. By Jordan-Hölder these are exactly the irreducible successive
quotients of a composition series of `ρ`.

Representation.HasFiniteGeometricDet.doc:
A representation has *finite geometric determinant* for a degree homomorphism `deg` when its
determinant character takes only finitely many values on the degree-zero subgroup `P = ker deg`.
(blueprint: `sk-d-weights`)

Rep.IsFiniteContinuous.signature:
def Rep.IsFiniteContinuous.{v, w} {Λ : Type v} [CommRing Λ] {G : Type w} [Group G]
  [TopologicalSpace G] : CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty (Rep.{v, v, w} Λ G)
Rep.IsFiniteContinuous.doc:
Blueprint `sk-i-real-galois`: Galois correspondence for finite local systems.

A representation of a topological group `G` on a `Λ`-module is *finite continuous* if the
underlying module is finite and every stabilizer is open, i.e. the action is continuous for
the discrete topology on the module. For a profinite `G` this is exactly the condition
appearing in the Galois correspondence: a finite `Λ`-module with a continuous `G`-action.

PrespectralSpace.exists_isCompact_isOpen.signature:
theorem PrespectralSpace.exists_isCompact_isOpen_disjoint_union_eq_univ.{u_1} {X : Type u_1}
  [TopologicalSpace X] [CompactSpace X] [PrespectralSpace X] {T₁ T₂ : Set X} (h₁ : IsClosed T₁)
  (h₂ : IsClosed T₂) (hd : Disjoint T₁ T₂) :
  ∃ O₁ O₂,
    IsOpen O₁ ∧
      IsOpen O₂ ∧ IsCompact O₁ ∧ IsCompact O₂ ∧ Disjoint O₁ T₁ ∧ Disjoint O₂ T₂ ∧ O₁ ∪ O₂ = Set.univ
PrespectralSpace.exists_isCompact_isOpen.doc:
**Separation by compact opens**: in a compact prespectral space, for two disjoint
closed subsets `T₁`, `T₂` there are compact opens `O₁`, `O₂` covering the space such
that `O₁` avoids `T₁` and `O₂` avoids `T₂`. Equivalently, the closed sets `O₁ᶜ ⊇ T₁`
and `O₂ᶜ ⊇ T₂` are disjoint and have quasi-compact complements.
(Constructible approximation step in the proof of Stacks Project Tag 0F3W.)

PowerSeries.radius.signature: def PowerSeries.radius.{u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] (f : PowerSeries 𝕜) : ENNReal
PowerSeries.radius.doc:
Blueprint `sk-d-real-series`: Radius of a formal series.

The radius of convergence `R(f) ∈ ℝ≥0∞` of a formal power series `f = ∑ aₙ Tⁿ ∈ 𝕜⟦X⟧` over a
nontrivially normed field `𝕜`.

This is defined as the radius of convergence of the associated formal multilinear series
`FormalMultilinearSeries.ofScalars 𝕜 (fun n ↦ coeff n f)`, whose `n`-th coefficient is `aₙ` by
`FormalMultilinearSeries.coeff_ofScalars`. It agrees with the description in the blueprint as
the supremum of the `r ≥ 0` for which `∑ₙ ‖aₙ‖ tⁿ` converges for all `0 ≤ t < r`: by
`FormalMultilinearSeries.radius` it is the supremum of the `r ≥ 0` for which `‖aₙ‖ rⁿ` is
bounded, and boundedness of `‖aₙ‖ rⁿ` for one `r` is equivalent to summability of
`∑ₙ ‖aₙ‖ tⁿ` for all `t < r` (`FormalMultilinearSeries.summable_norm_mul_pow` and
`FormalMultilinearSeries.le_radius_of_summable_norm`).

PowerSeries.exists_normalized_fraction_i.signature:
theorem PowerSeries.exists_normalized_fraction_iff_finiteDimensional_shiftSpan.{u_1} {K : Type u_1}
  [Field K] (f : PowerSeries K) :
  (∃ A B, B.coeff 0 = 1 ∧ f * ↑B = ↑A) ↔
    FiniteDimensional K ↥(shiftSpan K fun n => (PowerSeries.coeff n) f)
PowerSeries.exists_normalized_fraction_i.doc:
**Rationality criterion**: a power series over a field admits a normalized fraction
`f * B = A` with `B.coeff 0 = 1` if and only if the span of the shifts of its coefficient
sequence is finite-dimensional.

PowerSeries.HasNonnegCoeffs.doc:
Blueprint `sk-d-real-series`: Radius of a formal series.

A formal power series `f = ∑ aₙ Tⁿ ∈ ℂ⟦X⟧` has nonnegative coefficients if every `aₙ` is a
nonnegative real number. These are the series for which the coefficientwise comparison
arguments of the real-sheaves chapter apply: a coefficientwise bound between them is preserved
by products and gives a bound on the radius of convergence.

Polynomial.prod_odd_eq_map_and_prod_even.signature:
theorem Polynomial.prod_odd_eq_map_and_prod_even_eq_map {q r : ℕ} (hq : 1 < q)
  {P : Fin (r + 1) → Polynomial ℂ}
  (hP : ∀ (i : Fin (r + 1)), Polynomial.IsPureOfWeight q (↑i) (P i)) {A B : Polynomial ℚ}
  (hAB : IsCoprime A B) (hA : A.coeff 0 = 1)
  (h :
    (∏ i with Odd ↑i, P i) * Polynomial.map (Algebra.algebraMap ℚ ℂ) B =
      (∏ i with Even ↑i, P i) * Polynomial.map (Algebra.algebraMap ℚ ℂ) A) :
  ∏ i with Odd ↑i, P i = Polynomial.map (Algebra.algebraMap ℚ ℂ) A ∧
    ∏ i with Even ↑i, P i = Polynomial.map (Algebra.algebraMap ℚ ℂ) B
Polynomial.prod_odd_eq_map_and_prod_even.doc:
**Identification of the two parity factors**. If the parity products of a family of pure
polynomials of distinct weights cross-multiply against a coprime normalized rational fraction
`A / B`, then the odd-indexed product is `A` and the even-indexed product is `B`: no reciprocal
root cancels between odd and even indices.

Polynomial.isCoprime_prod_odd_prod_even.doc:
For a family `P i` with `P i` pure of weight `i`, the product of the odd-indexed factors and
the product of the even-indexed factors are coprime.

Polynomial.alternatingNatDegreeSum.signature:
def Polynomial.alternatingNatDegreeSum.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [Semiring R] {n : ℕ}
  (P : Fin (n + 1) → Polynomial R) : ℤ
Polynomial.alternatingNatDegreeSum.doc:
The alternating sum `∑ᵢ (-1)ⁱ deg (P i)` of the degrees of a finite family of polynomials.
For a family of Weil factors of a zeta function this is the Euler characteristic `χ`.

Polynomial.IsUniversallyPureOfWeight.signature: def Polynomial.IsUniversallyPureOfWeight (q w : ℕ) (P : Polynomial ℂ) : Prop
Polynomial.IsUniversallyPureOfWeight.doc: Every reciprocal root of `P` is universally pure of weight `w`.

Polynomial.IsPureOfWeight.signature: def Polynomial.IsPureOfWeight (q w : ℕ) (P : Polynomial ℂ) : Prop
Polynomial.IsPureOfWeight.doc:
`P` is pure of weight `w` for `q` if `P (0) = 1` and every complex root `z` of `P`
satisfies `‖z‖ = q ^ (-w / 2)`; equivalently every reciprocal root has absolute value
`q ^ (w / 2)`.

Polynomial.IsMixedOfWeightLE.signature: def Polynomial.IsMixedOfWeightLE (q w : ℕ) (P : Polynomial ℂ) : Prop
Polynomial.IsMixedOfWeightLE.doc:
`P` is *mixed of weight at most `w`* for `q` if `P (0) = 1` and every complex root `z` of
`P` satisfies `q ^ (-w / 2) ≤ ‖z‖`; equivalently every reciprocal root of `P` has absolute
value at most `q ^ (w / 2)`. This is the `≤` half of `Polynomial.IsPureOfWeight` and the
conclusion of Deligne's weight estimate.

PadicAlgCl.smallUnits.signature:
def PadicAlgCl.smallUnits.{w} (l : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime l)] (E : Type w) [Field E]
  [Algebra E (PadicAlgCl l)] : Subgroup Eˣ
PadicAlgCl.smallUnits.doc:
Blueprint `sk-d-real-log`: Small logarithm.

The subgroup `U_E = 1 + ℓ² 𝒪_E` of `Eˣ`, where `𝒪_E = PadicAlgCl.integers l E` is the ring of
integers of `E`.

PadicAlgCl.smallLog.signature:
def PadicAlgCl.smallLog.{w} (l : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime l)] (E : Type w) [Field E]
  [Algebra E (PadicAlgCl l)] (x : E) : E
PadicAlgCl.smallLog.doc:
Blueprint `sk-d-real-log`: Small logarithm.

`smallLog l E x` is the sum of the series `log (1 + x) = ∑_{n ≥ 1} (-1)^(n+1) x ^ n / n`,
formed in the topology restricted from `ℚ̄_ℓ`. It converges for `x ∈ ℓ² 𝒪_E`
(`PadicAlgCl.summable_logSeries`), and `u ↦ smallLog l E (u - 1)` is then an injective
homomorphism from `PadicAlgCl.smallUnits` to the additive group of `E`.

Module.End.hasEigenvalue_of_subquotient.signature:
theorem Module.End.hasEigenvalue_of_subquotient.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {V : Type u_2} [Field K]
  [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V] (f : Module.End K V) {U S : Submodule K V}
  (hUS : U < S) (hU : U ≤ Submodule.comap f U) (hS : S ≤ Submodule.comap f S) (c : K)
  (hc : ∀ x ∈ S, f x - c • x ∈ U) : f.HasEigenvalue c
Module.End.hasEigenvalue_of_subquotient.doc:
If a scalar `c` acts on a nonzero invariant subquotient `S ⧸ U` of `V`, then `c` is an
eigenvalue of the endomorphism on all of `V`.
(blueprint: `sk-p-linear-filtration`)

Module.End.exists_complete_invariant_fla.signature:
theorem Module.End.exists_complete_invariant_flag.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {V : Type u_2} [Field K]
  [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [IsAlgClosed K] [FiniteDimensional K V] (f : Module.End K V) :
  ∃ F,
    Monotone F ∧
      (∀ (i : Fin (Module.finrank K V + 1)), Submodule.map f (F i) ≤ F i) ∧
        ∀ (i : Fin (Module.finrank K V + 1)), Module.finrank K ↥(F i) = ↑i
Module.End.exists_complete_invariant_fla.doc:
An endomorphism `f` of a finite dimensional vector space `V` over an algebraically
closed field `K` admits a complete flag of invariant subspaces: a monotone family
`F : Fin (finrank K V + 1) → Submodule K V` with each `F i` mapped into itself by `f` and
`finrank K (F i) = i`. A basis adapted to such a flag puts `f` in upper triangular form,
with the eigenvalues of `f` on the diagonal (blueprint: `sk-p-linear-triangular`).

Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.zeroLocus.signature:
def Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.zeroLocus.{u_1, u_2, u_4} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {k : Type u_2} [CommRing k] (I : Ideal (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.CoordinateRing n k))
  [Ideal.IsHopfIdeal k I] (R : Type u_4) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R] : Subgroup (GL n R)
Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.zeroLocus.doc:
The `R`-points of the closed subgroup scheme `V(I)` of `GL_n` cut out by a Hopf ideal `I`: the
invertible matrices over `R` on which every equation in `I` vanishes.
(blueprint: `sk-d-geometry`)

Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.toPrimeSpectru.doc:
The connected components of a closed subgroup `G = V(I)` of `GL_n` are the cosets of the
identity component: a point `x` of `G` lies in the connected component of `g ∈ G` if and only if
`g⁻¹ * x ∈ G°`. (blueprint: `sk-p-geometry`)

Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.normal_zeroLoc.signature:
theorem Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.normal_zeroLocus_identityComponent.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {n : Type u_1}
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {k : Type u_2} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
  (I : Ideal (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.CoordinateRing n k)) [Ideal.IsHopfIdeal k I]
  (hI : I.IsRadical) (R : Type u_3) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R] :
  ((Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.zeroLocus (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.identityComponent I)
          R).subgroupOf
      (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.zeroLocus I R)).Normal
Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.normal_zeroLoc.doc:
The identity component `G°` of a closed reduced subgroup `G = V(I)` of `GL_n` is a normal
subgroup scheme: `G°(R)` is normal in `G(R)` for every `k`-algebra `R`.

The conjugation map `G × G° → G` sends `k`-points into `G°`, and `G × G°` is reduced, so it
factors through `G°`. (blueprint: `sk-p-geometry`)

Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.isPrime_identi.signature:
theorem Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.isPrime_identityComponent.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] {k : Type u_2} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
  (I : Ideal (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.CoordinateRing n k)) [Ideal.IsHopfIdeal k I] :
  (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.identityComponent I).IsPrime
Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.isPrime_identi.doc:
The identity component `G°` of a closed subgroup `G = V(I)` of `GL_n` is irreducible: its
ideal is prime. (blueprint: `sk-p-geometry`)

Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.identityCompon.signature:
def Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.identityComponent.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {k : Type u_2} [Field k] (I : Ideal (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.CoordinateRing n k)) :
  Ideal (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.CoordinateRing n k)
Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.identityCompon.doc:
The ideal of the reduced identity component `G°` of the closed subscheme `V(I)` of `GL_n`: the
functions vanishing on the connected component of `V(I)` containing the identity matrix.
(blueprint: `sk-d-geometry`)

Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.finiteIndex_ze.signature:
theorem Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.finiteIndex_zeroLocus_identityComponent.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1}
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {k : Type u_2} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
  (I : Ideal (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.CoordinateRing n k)) [Ideal.IsHopfIdeal k I] :
  ((Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.zeroLocus (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.identityComponent I)
          k).subgroupOf
      (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.zeroLocus I k)).FiniteIndex
Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.finiteIndex_ze.doc:
The identity component `G°` of a closed subgroup `G = V(I)` of `GL_n` has finite index in `G`.
(blueprint: `sk-p-geometry`)

Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.center.signature:
def Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.center.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {k : Type u_2} [Field k] (I : Ideal (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.CoordinateRing n k))
  [Ideal.IsHopfIdeal k I] : Ideal (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.CoordinateRing n k)
Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.center.doc:
The ideal of the reduced centre `Z(G)` of the closed subgroup scheme `G = V(I)` of `GL_n`: the
Zariski closure of the matrices of `G(k)` commuting with all of `G(k)`.
(blueprint: `sk-d-geometry`)

Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.CoordinateRing.signature:
def Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.CoordinateRing.{u_1, u_2} (n : Type u_1) [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  (k : Type u_2) [CommRing k] : Type (max u_1 u_2)
Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.CoordinateRing.doc:
The coordinate ring `k[x_ij, det⁻¹]` of the general linear group `GL_n` over `k`: the
polynomial ring in the matrix entries, localized away from the determinant.
(blueprint: `sk-d-geometry`)

LocalSubring.exists_le_valuationSubring.signature:
theorem LocalSubring.exists_le_valuationSubring.{u_3} {K : Type u_3} [Field K] (A : LocalSubring K) :
  ∃ B, A ≤ B.toLocalSubring

LinearMap.traceSeries.signature:
def LinearMap.traceSeries.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {V : Type u_2} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V]
  [Module K V] (F : Module.End K V) : PowerSeries K
LinearMap.traceSeries.doc:
The *trace series*

`tr_F(T) = ∑_{n ≥ 1} tr (F ^ n ∣ V) T ^ n / n`

of an endomorphism `F` of a finite dimensional vector space. Its companion identity
`exp (tr_F(T)) = det (1 - T F)⁻¹` is `LinearMap.inv_charpolyRev_eq_exp`, proved above
(blueprint: `sk-def-frobmod`).

LinearMap.inv_charpolyRev_eq_exp.signature:
theorem LinearMap.inv_charpolyRev_eq_exp.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {V : Type u_2} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V]
  [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V] [CharZero K] (F : Module.End K V) :
  (↑(LinearMap.charpolyRev F))⁻¹ =
    PowerSeries.subst
      (PowerSeries.mk fun n => if n = 0 then 0 else (LinearMap.trace K V) (F ^ n) / ↑n)
      (PowerSeries.exp K)
LinearMap.inv_charpolyRev_eq_exp.doc:
**The determinant-trace identity**, exponential form:
`det (1 - t F)⁻¹ = exp (∑_{n ≥ 1} tr (F ^ n) t ^ n / n)` for an endomorphism `F` of a finite
dimensional vector space over a field of characteristic zero.

LinearMap.charpoly_roots_tensorProduct.signature:
theorem LinearMap.charpoly_roots_tensorProduct.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {K : Type u_1} {V : Type u_2} {W : Type u_3}
  [Field K] [IsAlgClosed K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V] [AddCommGroup W]
  [Module K W] [FiniteDimensional K W] (f : V →ₗ[K] V) (g : W →ₗ[K] W) :
  (TensorProduct.map f g).charpoly.roots =
    Multiset.map (fun p => p.1 * p.2) (f.charpoly.roots ×ˢ g.charpoly.roots)
LinearMap.charpoly_roots_tensorProduct.doc:
The eigenvalues of the tensor product of two endomorphisms are the pairwise products of their
eigenvalues, with multiplicity.
(blueprint: `sk-p-linear-spectra`)

LinearMap.charpoly_roots_exteriorPower.signature:
theorem LinearMap.charpoly_roots_exteriorPower.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {V : Type u_2} [Field K]
  [IsAlgClosed K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V] (f : V →ₗ[K] V) (s : ℕ) :
  (exteriorPower.map s f).charpoly.roots =
    Multiset.map Multiset.prod (Multiset.powersetCard s f.charpoly.roots)
LinearMap.charpoly_roots_exteriorPower.doc:
The eigenvalues of the `s`-th exterior power of an endomorphism are the products of the
`s`-element sub-multisets of its eigenvalues.
(blueprint: `sk-p-linear-spectra`)

LinearMap.charpoly_roots_dualMap_symm.signature:
theorem LinearMap.charpoly_roots_dualMap_symm.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {V : Type u_2} [Field K]
  [IsAlgClosed K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V] (f : V ≃ₗ[K] V) :
  (↑f.symm).dualMap.charpoly.roots = Multiset.map (fun a => a⁻¹) (↑f).charpoly.roots
LinearMap.charpoly_roots_dualMap_symm.doc:
The eigenvalues of the contragredient of a linear automorphism, that is the dual of its
inverse, are the inverses of its eigenvalues.
(blueprint: `sk-p-linear-spectra`)

LinearMap.charpoly_eq_charpoly_restrict_.signature:
theorem LinearMap.charpoly_eq_charpoly_restrict_mul_charpoly_mapQ.{u_1, u_2} {R : Type u_1} {V : Type u_2}
  [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup V] [Module R V] [Module.Free R V] [Module.Finite R V] (f : V →ₗ[R] V)
  (W : Submodule R V) [Module.Free R ↥W] [Module.Finite R ↥W] [Module.Free R (V ⧸ W)]
  [Module.Finite R (V ⧸ W)] (hW : W ≤ Submodule.comap f W) :
  f.charpoly = (f.restrict hW).charpoly * (W.mapQ W f hW).charpoly
LinearMap.charpoly_eq_charpoly_restrict_.doc:
If an endomorphism preserves a submodule `W` with `W` and `V ⧸ W` finite free, its
characteristic polynomial is the product of the characteristic polynomials of the induced
endomorphisms of `W` and of `V ⧸ W`.
(blueprint: `sk-p-linear-filtration`)

LinearMap.alternatingTraceSeries.doc:
The alternating trace series

`str_F(T) = ∑_{n ≥ 1} (∑_i (-1) ^ i tr (F i ^ n ∣ W i)) T ^ n / n`

of a finite graded family `(W i, F i)` of Frobenius modules, indexed by a finite set `s` of
integers: the alternating sum of the individual trace series `LinearMap.traceSeries (F i)`,
the sign being the parity of the degree `i` via `Int.negOnePow`
(blueprint: `sk-def-frobmod`).

LinearMap.Frobenius.surjective_sub_id.signature:
theorem LinearMap.Frobenius.surjective_sub_id.{u_1, u_2} {k : Type u_1} {V : Type u_2} {p : ℕ} [Field k]
  [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] [CharP k p] [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] [IsAlgClosed k]
  [FiniteDimensional k V] (F : V →ₛₗ[frobenius k p] V) : Function.Surjective fun v => F v - v
LinearMap.Frobenius.surjective_sub_id.doc:
Blueprint `sk-prop-av-lang-steinberg`: Lang–Steinberg for `p`-linear maps.

Let `k` be an algebraically closed field of characteristic `p > 0`, let `V` be a
finite-dimensional `k`-vector space and let `F : V →ₛₗ[frobenius k p] V` be `p`-linear. Then
`v ↦ F v - v` is surjective.

LinearMap.Frobenius.natCard_fixedPoints_.signature:
theorem LinearMap.Frobenius.natCard_fixedPoints_le.{u_1, u_2} {k : Type u_1} {V : Type u_2} {p : ℕ}
  [Field k] [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] [CharP k p] [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] [FiniteDimensional k V]
  (F : V →ₛₗ[frobenius k p] V) :
  Nat.card ↥(LinearMap.Frobenius.fixedPoints F) ≤ p ^ Module.finrank k V
LinearMap.Frobenius.natCard_fixedPoints_.doc:
Blueprint `sk-prop-av-fixed-points`: Fixed points of `p`-linear maps are finite.

The `𝔽_p`-subspace of fixed points of a `p`-linear endomorphism `F` of a finite-dimensional
`k`-vector space `V` has `𝔽_p`-dimension at most `Module.finrank k V`; equivalently, it has at
most `p ^ Module.finrank k V` elements. This is the dimension bound of blueprint
`lem-sc-fixed-points-finite`.

LinearMap.Frobenius.finite_fixedPoints.signature:
theorem LinearMap.Frobenius.finite_fixedPoints.{u_1, u_2} {k : Type u_1} {V : Type u_2} {p : ℕ} [Field k]
  [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] [CharP k p] [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] [FiniteDimensional k V]
  (F : V →ₛₗ[frobenius k p] V) : Finite ↥(LinearMap.Frobenius.fixedPoints F)
LinearMap.Frobenius.finite_fixedPoints.doc:
Blueprint `sk-prop-av-fixed-points`: Fixed points of `p`-linear maps are finite.

Let `k` be a field of characteristic `p > 0`, let `V` be a finite-dimensional `k`-vector space
and let `F : V →ₛₗ[frobenius k p] V` be `p`-linear. Then the fixed points of `F` form a finite
`𝔽_p`-subspace of `V`. This is the finiteness part of blueprint `lem-sc-fixed-points-finite`.

LinearMap.Frobenius.bijective_tmul_fixed.doc:
Blueprint `sk-prop-av-fixed-base-change` (proved as `lem-sc-frobenius-fixed-invariance`):
Fixed points are unchanged by algebraically closed base change.

Let `k ⊆ k'` be an extension of algebraically closed fields of characteristic `p > 0`, let `V`
be a finite-dimensional `k`-vector space and let `F : V →ₛₗ[frobenius k p] V` be `p`-linear. If
`F'` is a `p`-linear endomorphism of the base change `k' ⊗[k] V` with `F' (1 ⊗ₜ v) = 1 ⊗ₜ F v`
for all `v` — that is, the base change of `F` of `existsUnique_baseChange` — then `v ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ v`
is a bijection from the fixed points of `F` onto the fixed points of `F'`.

LinearMap.C_det_mul_charpolyRev_of_simil.signature:
theorem LinearMap.C_det_mul_charpolyRev_of_similitude.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {L : Type u_1} {V : Type u_2}
  {W : Type u_3} [Field L] [AddCommGroup V] [Module L V] [AddCommGroup W] [Module L W]
  [FiniteDimensional L V] [FiniteDimensional L W] {p : V →ₗ[L] W →ₗ[L] L} [p.IsPerfPair]
  {F : Module.End L V} {G : Module.End L W} {c : L}
  (hFG : ∀ (v : V) (w : W), (p (F v)) (G w) = c * (p v) w) :
  Polynomial.C (LinearMap.det F) * LinearMap.charpolyRev G =
    Polynomial.C ((-1) ^ Module.finrank L V) *
      (LinearMap.charpoly F).comp (Polynomial.C c * Polynomial.X)
LinearMap.C_det_mul_charpolyRev_of_simil.doc:
The reverse characteristic polynomial of `G` is determined by the characteristic polynomial
of `F`: it is `det (1 - t • G) = (-1) ^ dim V * det (c * t - F) / det F`.

LieAlgebra.radical.signature:
def LieAlgebra.radical.{u, v} (R : Type u) (L : Type v) [CommRing R] [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra R L] :
  LieIdeal R L
LieAlgebra.radical.doc: The (solvable) radical of Lie algebra is the `sSup` of all solvable ideals.

LieAlgebra.hasCentralRadical_of_isFaithf.signature:
theorem LieAlgebra.hasCentralRadical_of_isFaithful.{u_1, u_2, u_3} (k : Type u_1) (L : Type u_2)
  (M : Type u_3) [Field k] [CharZero k] [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra k L] [Module.Finite k L]
  [AddCommGroup M] [Module k M] [LieRingModule L M] [LieModule k L M] [Module.Finite k M]
  [LieModule.IsFaithful k L M] [LieModule.IsTriangularizable k L M] [LieModule.IsSemisimple k L M] :
  LieAlgebra.HasCentralRadical k L
LieAlgebra.hasCentralRadical_of_isFaithf.doc:
A finite-dimensional Lie algebra over a field of characteristic zero admitting a faithful
semisimple finite-dimensional representation `M` has central radical: on each irreducible
summand of `M` the bracket `⁅L, rad L⁆` acts as zero, so it vanishes by faithfulness.
(blueprint: `sk-p-lie`, `lem-ag-faithful-semisimple-lie-central-radical`)

A finite-dimensional Lie algebra over a field of characteristic zero whose radical is central
is *reductive*: it is the sum of its centre `Z(L)` and its derived subalgebra `[L, L]`.
The quotient `L ⧸ Z(L)` has trivial radical, so its Killing form is non-degenerate and it is
perfect; lifting brackets gives the decomposition.
(blueprint: `sk-p-lie`, `lem-ag-central-radical-quotient`)

The center of a Lie algebra is the set of elements that commute with everything. It can
be viewed as the maximal trivial submodule of the Lie algebra as a Lie module over itself via the

A Lie algebra *has central radical* if its radical coincides with its center. Such Lie algebras
are called *reductive*, if the coefficients are a field of characteristic zero.

Note that there is absolutely [no agreement](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/284713/) on what
the label 'reductive' should mean when the coefficients are not a field of characteristic zero.

For a commutative ring `R`, a bounded complex `P` of finitely generated free `R`-modules
and a chain endomorphism `v : P ⟶ P`, the categorical trace of `v` on the object of `D(R)`
represented by `P` is the alternating sum of the ordinary `R`-module traces of the
components of `v`:

`tr_R (v ∣ P) = ∑ i, (-1) ^ i * Tr_R (v ^ i ∣ P ^ i)`.

Boundedness of `P` is rendered by a `Finset ℤ` containing its support, which also makes the
right hand sum finite. The sign `(-1) ^ i` of an integer exponent is `Int.negOnePow i`,
acting on `R` by `zsmul`. The braiding is the Koszul one in the sense that the braiding of
`R[1]` with itself is `-1` (blueprint: `sk-p-trace`).

sets `U` and `V` whose union is open, then `U ∩ V` is dense in the subspace `U ∪ V`.

CompositionSeries.doc:
A `CompositionSeries X` is a finite nonempty series of elements of a
`JordanHolderLattice` such that each element is maximal inside the next. The length of a
`CompositionSeries X` is one less than the number of elements in the series.
Note that there is no stipulation that a series start from the bottom of the lattice and finish at
the top. For a composition series `s`, `s.last` is the largest element of the series,
and `s.head` is the least element.

  [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective (ModuleCat Λ)] {T : C} (M N : ModuleCat Λ) [Finite ↑M]
  (φ :

      (CategoryTheory.constantSheaf J (ModuleCat Λ)).obj N) :
  ∃ S ∈ J T,
    ∀ ⦃U : C⦄ (g : U ⟶ T),
      S.arrows g →
        ⊥ ∉ J U →
          ∃ f,
            ∀ (m : ↑M),
              (CategoryTheory.ConcreteCategory.hom (φ.hom.app (Opposite.op U)))
                  ((CategoryTheory.ConcreteCategory.hom
                      ((CategoryTheory.toSheafify J ((CategoryTheory.Functor.const Cᵒᵖ).obj M)).app
                        (Opposite.op U)))
                    m) =
                (CategoryTheory.ConcreteCategory.hom

**A morphism between constant sheaves of modules is locally induced by a linear map**,
in the form of sections: for `φ : M_C ⟶ N_C` with `M` finite and any object `T`, there is a
covering sieve `S` of `T` such that over every member `U` of `S` not covered by the empty
sieve, `φ` sends the constant section `m` over `U` to the constant section `f m`, for a
`Λ`-linear map `f : M ⟶ N`. The map `f` is obtained by lifting the finitely many
sections `φ♭(m)`, `m : M`, to elements of `N` on a common cover; it is linear since
`N ⟶ N_C(U)` is injective.

image filtration on the total complex of a first quadrant double complex produces.

CategoryTheory.Functor.exists_grothendie.doc:
**The Grothendieck spectral sequence.** If `F : A ⥤ B` and `G : B ⥤ C` are left exact
additive functors forming a composable pair with acyclicity

```
    A ───── F ─────▶ B ───── G ─────▶ C
     ╲                                ▲
      ╲───────────── F ⋙ G ──────────╱
```

then for every `X : A` there is a first quadrant cohomological spectral sequence with
`E₂^{p, q} ≅ R^p G (R^q F X)` abutting to `R^{p + q} (F ⋙ G) X`.

For `A` the abelian sheaves on a site `X`, `F = f_*` and `G = h_*` along morphisms of sites
`X ⥤ Y ⥤ Z`, the acyclicity hypothesis holds because `f_*` is right adjoint to the exact functor
`f^{-1}` and hence preserves injectives, and the statement specializes to
`R^p h_* R^q f_* F ⟹ R^{p + q} (h ∘ f)_* F`. Taking `Z` to be the punctual site, so that
`h_* = Γ(Y, -)`, it specializes further to the Leray spectral sequence
`H^p(Y, R^q f_* F) ⟹ H^{p + q}(X, F)`.

(blueprint: `sk-thm-groth-ss`)

CategoryTheory.Functor.IsAcyclicComposab.doc:
The pair of additive functors `A ⥤ B ⥤ C` is a *composable pair with acyclicity* if `F` sends
every injective object `I` of `A` to a `G`-acyclic object of `B`, that is, one at which all the
higher right derived functors `R^q G` for `q > 0` vanish. This is what makes an injective
resolution of `X : A` compute `R^n (F ⋙ G) X` after applying `F`, and hence what makes the
Grothendieck spectral sequence of `Functor.exists_grothendieckSpectralSequence` exist.

(blueprint: `sk-def-groth-ss`)

The normalized functional-equation sign `ε = (-1)^χ q^{-m} ∏ᵢ (Dᵢ)^{(-1)ⁱ}` of a family of
Weil factors (blueprint `def-weil-functional-equation-sign`), where `χ` is
`Polynomial.alternatingNatDegreeSum P`, `Dᵢ = (-1)^{deg (P i)} · [T^{deg (P i)}] P i`, and `m` is

no junk value; that `d χ` is even is `TraceDatum.even_mul_alternatingNatDegreeSum_of_pairing`.

AlgebraicGeometry.surjective_npow_id.doc:
Blueprint `sk-prop-av-mult-surjective`: Surjectivity of the multiplication map.

Let `A` be an abelian variety over `K` and `0 < n`. Then `[n] : A ⟶ A` is surjective, so `A` is
a divisible group scheme.

This is also blueprint `lem-sc-mult-n-isogeny`, whose finiteness half is
`AlgebraicGeometry.isFinite_torsionSubgroupScheme`. The scheme-theoretic image `Z` of `[n]` is a
closed subscheme of `A` onto which `[n]` maps surjectively
(`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isMonHom_imageι`). As `A ⟶ Z` is finite and surjective,
`dim Z = dim A`; a closed subset of the irreducible finite-dimensional `A` of full dimension is
all of `A`.

AlgebraicGeometry.picardFunctorNormalize.doc:
The `σ`-normalized relative Picard functor `Pic_{X/S,σ}` of a morphism of schemes
`f : X ⟶ S` equipped with a section `σ`: the subfunctor of the Picard presheaf `T ↦ Pic (X_T)`
consisting of the classes `ℒ` that are trivial along the base-changed section, `σ_T^* ℒ ≅ 𝒪_T`.

This is a subfunctor because the base-changed sections are compatible: for `i : V ⟶ U` in
`Over S`, the square

```
          σ_V
     V ─────────▶ X ×[S] V
     │                │
   i.left      baseChangeMap f i
     │                │
     ▼                ▼
     U ─────────▶ X ×[S] U
          σ_U
```

commutes, so pulling a normalized class back along `baseChangeMap f i` keeps it normalized.

(blueprint: `sk-def-picard-pic`)

smooth projective curve of genus `g` with a `k`-rational point `σ`, and let `G = Pic_{X/k,σ}`
be the `σ`-normalized Picard functor.  The subfunctor `F ⊆ G` is
`F(T) = {ℒ ∈ G(T) | Rf_{T,*} ℒ is an invertible 𝒪_T-module placed in degree 0}`,
where `f_T : X_T ⟶ T` is the base change of `f`.

Being a `CategoryTheory.Subfunctor`, `F` comes with the inclusion natural transformation
`(picardFunctorInvertibleDirectImage f σ hσ).ι` into
`(picardFunctorNormalized f σ hσ).toFunctor`.

(blueprint: `sk-def-picard-f`)

**Step 3 of the proof of Chow's lemma.** An affine scheme `V` locally of finite type over a
Noetherian scheme `S` admits a proper closed model: a closed subscheme `Z` of some projective
space `ℙ(n; S)` with `n` finite, containing `V` as a scheme-theoretically dense open subscheme
and proper over `S`.

Indeed, `V` immerses into some `ℙ(n; S)` over `S` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isImmersion_projectiveSpace`, and this immersion is quasi-compact
since `V` is Noetherian; so its scheme-theoretic image does the job.

AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_iso_overPullb.doc:
Blueprint `sk-prop-av-mult-n-pullback`: Pullback of symmetric modules under multiplication
by `n`.

Let `A` be an abelian variety over `K` and let `N` be an invertible `𝒪_A`-module which is
*symmetric*, that is `[-1]^* N ≅ N`. Then `[n]^* N ≅ N^{⊗ n²}` for every `n`.

This is also blueprint `lem-sc-mult-n-pullback`. The proof compares isomorphism classes in the
commutative monoid `Skeleton A.left.Modules`, in which the class of `N` is a unit since `N` is
invertible. Pulling back the theorem of the cube `AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_iso_cube` along
`x ↦ (x, x, -x)` gives `[2]^* N ≅ N^{⊗ 4}`, and along `x ↦ (x, x, [n] x)` gives
`[n + 2]^* N ⊗ N^{⊗ 2} ⊗ [n]^* N ≅ [2]^* N ⊗ ([n + 1]^* N)^{⊗ 2}`, from which the claim follows
by induction on `n`.

AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_iso_cube.doc:
Blueprint `sk-prop-av-cube`: The theorem of the cube.

Let `A` be an abelian variety over a field `K` and let `L` be an invertible `𝒪_A`-module. For
`1 ≤ i₁ < ⋯ < i_t ≤ 3` let `m_{i₁…i_t} : A × A × A ⟶ A` be the partial sum map
`(x₁, x₂, x₃) ↦ x_{i₁} + ⋯ + x_{i_t}`. Then
`m₁₂₃^* L ⊗ m₁^* L ⊗ m₂^* L ⊗ m₃^* L ≅ m₁₂^* L ⊗ m₁₃^* L ⊗ m₂₃^* L`.

This is also blueprint `thm-sc-theorem-of-cube`. The proof applies the general theorem of the
cube `AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_iso_of_nonempty_iso_overPullback_slices` with `X = Y = Z = A`
and the unit as rational point: on each of the slices `{e} × A × A`, `A × {e} × A` and
`A × A × {e}` both sides restrict to `n₁₂^* L ⊗ n₁^* L ⊗ n₂^* L`, since `e^* L` is trivial.

AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_equiv_compact.doc:
In degree two, global Verdier duality on the smooth nonproper curve `U` identifies
`H_c^2(C, j_*F)` with the geometric coinvariants `V_{π₁(U)}` of `F`, Tate-twisted by `(-1)`:
the Frobenius of the cohomology is `q` times the Frobenius of the coinvariants.

```
  H_c²(C, j_*F) ──e──▶ V_{π₁(U)}
        │                 │
   Frob │                 │ q · Frob
        ▼                 ▼
  H_c²(C, j_*F) ──e──▶ V_{π₁(U)}
```
(blueprint: `sk-l-dl-a1-endpoints`)

  AlgebraicGeometry.Compactification

AlgebraicGeometry.noetherianCompactifica.doc:
**The recursive Noetherian compactification construction**: given a finite family of
affine opens `U` of `X` with dense total intersection, a compactification of every partial
union `X_r = U 0 ∪ ⋯ ∪ U (r - 1)` over `S`, constructed by recursion on `r`.

`X_0` is empty, hence proper over `S`; `X_1 = U 0` is affine, so the affine case applies;
and `X_{r+1} = X_r ∪ U r` is obtained from `X_r` and `U r` by the two-open theorem, whose
density hypothesis holds because the total intersection of the cover is contained in both
`X_r` and `U r`.
(blueprint: `def:nagata-noetherian-compactification`)

AlgebraicGeometry.nagataCompactification.doc:
**Nagata compactification for a morphism of finite presentation** (blueprint:
`lemma:nagata-final-basechanged-compactification`).

The base is written as a cofiltered limit of Noetherian stages by absolute Noetherian
approximation, `f` is descended to one of the stages, compactified there by
`AlgebraicGeometry.nagataCompactification_of_isNoetherian` and the compactification is base
changed back to `S`.

AlgebraicGeometry.nagataCompactification.doc:

The last stage `X_n = X` of the recursion
`AlgebraicGeometry.noetherianCompactificationConstruction` over the selected dense affine
cover of `X` is a compactification of `f`.

**The `σ`-normalized Picard functor is an fppf sheaf.** The relative Picard functor
`Pic_{X/S}` is an fppf sheaf, hence a Zariski sheaf, simply because it is defined as an fppf
sheafification: this is `(AlgebraicGeometry.picardFunctor f).cond`, so only the second half of
the corollary carries content. Namely, if `f` has a section `σ` and the canonical map
`𝒪_T ⟶ f_{T,*} 𝒪_{X_T}` is an isomorphism for every `T` in `(Sch/S)_fppf`, then
`Pic_{X/S,σ}(T) = ker σ_T^*` is an fppf sheaf as well.

(blueprint: `sk-cor-picard-pic-sheaf`)

**Fpqc descent for finite locally free closed subschemes.** Let `f : X ⟶ T` be a morphism
of schemes, let `{g i : T i ⟶ T}` be an fpqc covering and let `p i : X i ⟶ X`,
`q i : X i ⟶ T i` exhibit `X i` as the base change `X ×_T T i`:

```
   X' i ──── p i ────▶ X
     │                 │
   q i                 f
     │                 │
     ▼                 ▼
   T' i ──── g i ────▶ T
```

Given closed subschemes `Z i ⊆ X i`, described by ideal sheaves `I i`, which are finite
locally free of degree `d` over `T i` and whose pullbacks agree over `X i ×_X X j`, there
is a unique closed subscheme `Z ⊆ X` with `Z ×_T T i = Z i`, and `Z` is finite locally
free of degree `d` over `T`.

(blueprint: `lem-pc-descent-finite-flat-closed-subschemes`; `sk-thm-picard-descent`,
part (D2))

AlgebraicGeometry.isRepresentable_picard.doc:
**`F` is representable** by an open subscheme of `Hilb^g_{X/k}`: given a `k`-scheme `H`
representing `Hilb^g_{X/k}`, there are a scheme `W` and an open immersion `j : W ⟶ H` such that
`W`, viewed as a `k`-scheme through `j`, represents `F`.

Let `D_univ ⊆ X_H` be the universal divisor and `ℒ_H = 𝒪(D_univ) ⊗ f_H^* σ_H^* 𝒪(D_univ)^{-1}`
the normalized universal module, a point of `Pic_{X/k,σ}(H)`. Since `F ⊆ Pic_{X/k,σ}` is open
(`AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_picardFunctorInvertibleDirectImage_ι`), there is an open
`W ⊆ H` such that `a^* ℒ_H ∈ F(T)` exactly for the `a : T ⟶ H` factoring through `W`. The map
`a ↦ a^* ℒ_H` from `h_W` to `F` is inverse to the zero-scheme dictionary `ℒ ↦ Z(φ_ℒ)` followed
by the classifying map of `Hilb^g_{X/k}`: one composite is the identity by
`AlgebraicGeometry.zeroLocus_directImageCounit_eq_of_iso`, the other one because `ℒ` and
`m^* ℒ_H` are both of the form `𝒪(D) ⊗ f_T^* 𝒩` and normalized
(`AlgebraicGeometry.picardFunctorNormalized_eq_of_iso_tensorObj`).

(blueprint: `sk-thm-picard-f-representable`, `thm-pc-f-representable`)

**The Picard functor of a smooth projective curve over a separably closed field is
representable.** Let `k` be a separably closed field and let `f : X ⟶ Spec k` be a smooth
projective curve.  Then the Picard functor `Pic_{X/k} = AlgebraicGeometry.picardFunctor f` is
represented by a group scheme over `k`, i.e. by an object of `Over (Spec k)` carrying a
`CategoryTheory.GrpObj` structure.

The group structure is the one induced by the group law of the Picard functor
(`AlgebraicGeometry.picardFunctorNormalizedGrp`, blueprint `rem-pc-group-structure`).

(blueprint: `sk-thm-picard-main`, `thm-pc-picard-representable`)

AlgebraicGeometry.isRepresentable_of_rep.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.isRepresentable_of_representable_open_subfunctor.{u} {k : Type u} [Field k]
  (G :
    CategoryTheory.Functor (CategoryTheory.Over (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))ᵒᵖ
      GrpCat)
  (F : CategoryTheory.Subfunctor (G.comp (CategoryTheory.forget GrpCat)))
  (hsmall :
    ∀ (T : (CategoryTheory.Over (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))ᵒᵖ),
      Small.{u, u + 1} ((G.comp (CategoryTheory.forget GrpCat)).obj T))
  (hG :
    CategoryTheory.Presheaf.IsSheaf
      (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.zariskiTopology.over (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
      (G.comp (CategoryTheory.forget GrpCat)))
  (hFrep : F.toFunctor.IsRepresentable)
  (hFopen :
    CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.relative CategoryTheory.uliftYoneda.{u + 1, u, u + 1}
      (AlgebraicGeometry.IsOpenImmersion.inverseImage
        (CategoryTheory.Over.forget (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k))))
      F.ι)
  (hgen :
    ∀ (K : Type u) [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : Algebra k K]
      (g :
        ↑(G.obj
            (Opposite.op
              (CategoryTheory.Over.mk
                (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Algebra.algebraMap k K))))))),
      ∃ g',
        (GrpCat.Hom.hom
                (G.map
                  (CategoryTheory.Over.homMk
                      (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Algebra.algebraMap k K)))
                      ⋯).op))
              g' *
            g ∈
          F.obj
            (Opposite.op
              (CategoryTheory.Over.mk
                (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Algebra.algebraMap k K)))))) :
  ∃ A x, Nonempty ((G.comp (CategoryTheory.forget GrpCat)).RepresentableBy A)
AlgebraicGeometry.isRepresentable_of_rep.doc:
**The criterion: a functor generated by a representable open subfunctor.** Let
`G : (Sch/k)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Grp` be a presheaf of groups on the category of `k`-schemes such that

1. `G` is a Zariski sheaf, with `u`-small values;
2. there is a subfunctor `F ⊆ G` with
   (a) `F` representable,
   (b) the inclusion `F ⊆ G` representable by open immersions,
   (c) *generation*: for every field extension `K/k` and every `g ∈ G(K)` there is a
       `g' ∈ G(k)` with `g' g ∈ F(K)`.

Then `G` is representable by a group scheme over `k`.

The group-valued formulation `(Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat` is the one used here: it is what makes
the product `g' g` in (2)(c) available, and it is the shape expected by
`CategoryTheory.GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`.  The underlying presheaf of sets is
`G ⋙ forget GrpCat`, and `F` is a `CategoryTheory.Subfunctor` of it.  As in
`AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_picardFunctorInvertibleDirectImage_ι`, representability by
open immersions is `CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.relative` for
`CategoryTheory.uliftYoneda`.

The values of `G` lie in `Type (u + 1)`, while a `k`-scheme has a `u`-small set of `T`-points, so
`G(T)` has to be assumed `u`-small: without this the statement fails, for instance for the
sheaf of locally constant functions to a group which is not `u`-small, with `F` the trivial
subgroup. For the Picard functor the values are small.

The proof follows Stacks, Lemma 0B9Q: the translates `F_{g'} = g'⁻¹ F` for `g' ∈ G(k)` are
open subfunctors represented by the representing scheme of `F`, and they cover `G` by (2)(c)
applied at the residue fields of the points; the gluing criterion
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalRepresentability.isRepresentable_of_isSheaf_over` gives the
representing scheme, which is a group object by `CategoryTheory.GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`.

(blueprint: `sk-thm-picard-criterion`, `thm-pc-criterion`)

AlgebraicGeometry.isRepresentable_hilber.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.isRepresentable_hilbertPresheaf.{u} {X S : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ S)
  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated f] (d : ℕ)
  (hf :
    ∀ (s : ↥S) (t : Finset ↥(AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.fiber f s)),
      t.card ≤ d → ∃ U, ∀ x ∈ t, (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.fiberι f s) x ∈ ↑U) :
  (AlgebraicGeometry.hilbertPresheaf f d).IsRepresentable
AlgebraicGeometry.isRepresentable_hilber.doc:
**Representability of `Hilb^d`, general case.** Assume that for every point `s` of `S` and
every finite set of at most `d` points of the fibre `X_s` there is an affine open of `X`
containing all of them; this holds for instance when `X ⟶ S` is quasi-projective, or when `X`
carries an ample invertible module. If moreover `X ⟶ S` is separated, then `Hilb^d_{X/S}` is
representable by a scheme.

Separatedness cannot be dropped: for the line with doubled origin over a field and `d = 1`,
every finite set of at most one point lies in an affine open, but `Hilb^1_{X/S}` is not
representable.

The proof glues the Hilbert schemes of the morphisms of affine schemes `U ⟶ V`, for affine opens
`V ⊆ S` and `U ⊆ f⁻¹ V`, using the gluing criterion
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalRepresentability.isRepresentable_of_isSheaf_over`.

(blueprint: `sk-thm-picard-hilb-general`, `lem-pc-hilb-representable`)

theorem AlgebraicGeometry.isRegularImmersion_diagonal.{u} {X Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (d : ℕ)
  (f : X ⟶ Y) [AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated f] [AlgebraicGeometry.SmoothOfRelativeDimension d f] :
  AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegularImmersion d (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.diagonal f)
AlgebraicGeometry.isRegularImmersion_dia.doc:
Blueprint `sk-lem-diag-reg`: The diagonal is a regular immersion

Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be smooth and separated of pure relative dimension `d`, let `W = X ×_Y X` and
let `Δ : X ⟶ W` be the diagonal. Then `Δ` is a regular closed immersion of pure codimension
`d`.

Étale-locally `f` is the projection `𝔸^d_Y → Y`, on which `Δ` is the zero section of `𝔸^d`;
regularity and the codimension are étale local, whence the statement. The blueprint also
identifies the normal bundle of `Δ` with the relative tangent bundle `T_{X/Y}`; Mathlib has no
sheaf of relative differentials, and nothing downstream uses that identification, so it is not
stated here.

in its structure sheaf, i.e. it is reduced: its base change to an algebraic closure is reduced by
`isReduced_of_grpObj_of_isAlgClosed`, and reducedness descends along the faithfully flat
morphism `G_K̄ ⟶ G`. (blueprint: `sk-i-cartier`, `lem-ag-cartier-reduced`)

infinity and not geometrically constant is nonexceptional: the nonzero linear characters are
excluded by their ramification at infinity, and a geometric constant constituent of an
irreducible Weil representation forces geometric constancy. Only arithmetic irreducibility is
used. (blueprint: `sk-p-dl-a1-middle`, `lem-a1-unramified-nonexceptional`)

AlgebraicGeometry.isMonHom_npow_id.doc:
Blueprint `sk-prop-av-mult-hom`: The `n`-fold sum is a homomorphism.

Let `G` be a commutative group scheme over `K`. Then the `n`-fold sum map `[n] : G ⟶ G` is a
homomorphism of group schemes: it is the `n`-th power of the homomorphism `𝟙 G` in the
commutative monoid `G ⟶ G`, and such powers are homomorphisms
(`CategoryTheory.MonObj.isMonHom_pow`, blueprint `lem-sc-mult-n-homomorphism`).

Let `Y` be a separated `k₀`-scheme of finite type, let `U` be an open subscheme of the relative
affine line `𝔸¹_Y` whose projection `h` to `Y` is surjective, and let `F` be a lisse Weil sheaf on

```
U --- u ---> 𝔸¹_Y
  \            |
   \ h         | ↘
    `--------> Y
```

(blueprint: `sk-p-dl-general-relative-line`).

surjective homomorphism, hence an isogeny.

`AlgebraicGeometry.surjective_npow_id`, and its kernel `A[n]` is finite by
`AlgebraicGeometry.isFinite_torsionSubgroupScheme`.

AlgebraicGeometry.isFinite_npow_id.doc:
Blueprint `sk-prop-av-mult-finite`: Finiteness of the fibres of the multiplication map.

Let `A` be an abelian variety over `K` and `0 < n`. Then `[n] : A ⟶ A` is finite.

This is also blueprint `lem-sc-mult-n-finite-kernel`. Since `[n]` is proper, it suffices that it
is locally quasi-finite. Its base change to an algebraic closure `K̄` of `K` is multiplication by
`n` on the abelian variety `A_K̄`, which is locally quasi-finite by
`AlgebraicGeometry.locallyQuasiFinite_npow_id_of_isAlgClosed`, and local quasi-finiteness
descends along the surjection `A_K̄ ⟶ A`.

AlgebraicGeometry.isEffectiveCartierCent.doc:
**A closed immersion is an effective Cartier centre exactly when its kernel is
invertible.** Unfolding `Scheme.IdealSheafData.IsInvertible`, the right-hand side is the
affine-local assertion that the defining ideal of `Z` is generated by one non-zerodivisor, so
this is the promised description of (MLCI1) under the correspondence between closed
immersions and quasi-coherent ideals.

The forward direction holds because the kernel does not change under precomposition with an
isomorphism, and the kernel of `J.subschemeι` is `J`. The backward direction produces the
isomorphism from the universal property of closed immersions: `z` and `z.ker.subschemeι` are
two closed immersions with the same kernel, hence canonically isomorphic over `X`.
(blueprint: final assertion of `lemma:nagata-invertible-ideal-effective-cartier`)
