The Fourier–Deligne transform along a nontrivial additive character is exact for the curve
perverse t-structures of the two dual affine lines: a Weil complex is curve perverse exactly
when its transform is.

```
  Dᵇ(A₀) ──────FT_ψ──────▶ Dᵇ(A'₀)
     ∪                        ∪
  Perv(A₀) ────≃ exact───▶ Perv(A'₀)
```
(blueprint: `sk-p-dl-a1-perverse`)

AlgebraicGeometry.isClosed_setOf_subsing.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.isClosed_setOf_subsingleton_image.{u} {K : Type u} [Field K]
  {X Y Z : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (fX : X ⟶ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
  (fY : Y ⟶ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
  (fZ : Z ⟶ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) [AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper fX]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated fZ] (g : CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback fX fY ⟶ Z)
  (hg :
    CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp g fZ =
      CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.fst fX fY) fX) :
  IsClosed
    {y |
      (Set.range
          ⇑(AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.fiberMap
              (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.lift g (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.snd fX fY) ⋯) ⋯
              (Y.fromSpecAlgebraicClosureResidueField y))).Subsingleton}
AlgebraicGeometry.isClosed_setOf_subsing.doc:
Blueprint `sk-prop-av-const-locus`: The locus of constant fibres is closed

Let `X` be a `K`-scheme proper over `K`, let `Z` be separated over `K`, let `Y` be any
`K`-scheme and let `g : X ×_K Y ⟶ Z` be a morphism of `K`-schemes. For `y : Y` let
`g_ȳ : X_{κ(y)‾} ⟶ Z_{κ(y)‾}` be the base change of `(g, pr₂) : X ×_K Y ⟶ Z ×_K Y` along the
geometric point `ȳ` over `y`. Then the locus `L = {y ∈ Y | g_ȳ(X_{κ(y)‾}) is a subsingleton}` is
closed in `Y`. For nonempty `X` the image of `g_ȳ` is a subsingleton exactly when it is a single
point.

Constancy must be tested on the geometric fibre, not on the set-theoretic image of
`X ×_K {y}` in `Z`: for `K` algebraically closed of characteristic `≠ 2`,
`X = Spec K ⊔ Spec K`, `Y = Z = 𝔸¹_K` and `g = (t ↦ t, t ↦ -t)`, that image is one point
exactly for `y` the generic point or `y = 0`, which is not a closed set.

AlgebraicGeometry.isClosed_range_of_isMo.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.isClosed_range_of_isMonHom.{u} {k : Type u} [Field k]
  {G K : CategoryTheory.Over (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} [CategoryTheory.GrpObj G]
  [CategoryTheory.GrpObj K] [AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact G.hom] [AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType K.hom] (f : G ⟶ K)
  [CategoryTheory.IsMonHom f] : IsClosed (Set.range ⇑(CategoryTheory.Over.Hom.left f))
AlgebraicGeometry.isClosed_range_of_isMo.doc:
The image of a homomorphism from a group scheme of finite type to a group scheme locally of
finite type over a field is closed (SGA 3, VI_B, Proposition 1.2).

The source must be quasi-compact: the homomorphism `ℤ ⟶ 𝔾ₐ` from the constant group scheme,
`n ↦ n`, over `ℚ` has image the infinite non-closed set of closed points `n ∈ 𝔸¹_ℚ`.

Proof sketch (not formalized): after base change to an algebraic closure the image is
constructible (Chevalley), hence contains a dense open subset of its closure; translating it by
rational points shows the image is open in its closure, hence closed. Closedness descends along
the closed surjection from the base change. The matrix-group case over an algebraically closed
field is `AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.RationalHom.mem_range_points_iff` (blueprint
`lem-ag-homomorphism-image-closed`). (blueprint: `sk-p-geometry`)

AlgebraicGeometry.injective_pic_map_snd.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.injective_pic_map_snd.{u} {X S : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ S)
  (hf :
    ∀ (T : CategoryTheory.Over S),
      CategoryTheory.IsIso
        (AlgebraicGeometry.pushforwardUnitMap (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.snd f T.hom)))
  (T : CategoryTheory.Over S) :
  Function.Injective (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic.map (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.snd f T.hom))
AlgebraicGeometry.injective_pic_map_snd.doc:
**The pullback map `Pic T → Pic (X_T)` is injective.** This is the left-exactness half of
the split exact sequence `0 → Pic T → Pic (X_T) → Pic_{X/S}(T) → 0`, under the hypothesis that
the canonical map `𝒪_T ⟶ f_{T,*} 𝒪_{X_T}` is an isomorphism for every `T` in `(Sch/S)_fppf`
(for `X ⟶ Spec k` a smooth projective curve with a `k`-point this is `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = k` together
with flat base change).

(blueprint: `sk-prop-picard-pic-split`)

AlgebraicGeometry.hilbertPresheaf_curve_.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.hilbertPresheaf_curve_representable.{u} {k : Type u} [Field k]
  {X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
  [AlgebraicGeometry.SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f] [AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper f]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.GeometricallyIntegral f] (d : ℕ) :
  ∃ H p,
    AlgebraicGeometry.SmoothOfRelativeDimension d p ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper p ∧
        AlgebraicGeometry.GeometricallyIntegral p ∧
          ∃ e D,
            AlgebraicGeometry.IsEffectiveCartierCenter D.subschemeι ∧
              ∀ (T : CategoryTheory.Over (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
                (h : T.left ⟶ H) (hh : CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp h p = T.hom),
                D.comap
                    (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.lift
                      (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp
                        (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.snd f T.hom) h)
                      (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.fst f T.hom) ⋯) =
                  ↑(e.homEquiv (CategoryTheory.Over.homMk h hh))
AlgebraicGeometry.hilbertPresheaf_curve_.doc:
**The Hilbert scheme of a smooth projective curve.** For a geometrically integral smooth
proper curve `X` over `k` and `d : ℕ`, the functor `Hilb^d_{X/k}` is represented by a smooth
proper geometrically integral `k`-scheme `H` of dimension `d`, and `H ×[k] X` carries an
effective Cartier divisor `D` which is universal, in the sense that the point of `Hilb^d_{X/k}`
classified by a `k`-morphism `h : T ⟶ H` is the pullback of `D` along the induced morphism
`X_T ⟶ H ×[k] X`:

```
        X_T ──────────────▶ H ×[k] X ─────▶ X
         │  ⟨pr_T ≫ h, pr_X⟩    │            │
         │                      │            f
         ▼                      ▼            ▼
         T ─────── h ─────────▶ H ─── p ──▶ Spec k
```

(blueprint: `sk-thm-picard-hilb-curves`, parts (1) and (3))

AlgebraicGeometry.hilbertPresheaf_curve_.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.hilbertPresheaf_curve_points.{u} {k : Type u} [Field k]
  {X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
  [AlgebraicGeometry.SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f] [AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper f]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.GeometricallyIntegral f] (d : ℕ) (k' : Type u) [Field k'] [Algebra k k']
  (T : CategoryTheory.Over (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
  (hT :
    T =
      CategoryTheory.Over.mk
        (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Algebra.algebraMap k k'))))
  (I : (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback f T.hom).IdealSheafData) :
  (∃ Z, ↑Z = I) ↔
    AlgebraicGeometry.IsEffectiveCartierCenter I.subschemeι ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite
          (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp I.subschemeι
            (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.snd f T.hom)) ∧
        AlgebraicGeometry.Flat
            (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp I.subschemeι
              (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.snd f T.hom)) ∧
          ∀ (t : ↥T.left),
            AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.finrank
                (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp I.subschemeι
                  (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.snd f T.hom))
                t =
              d
AlgebraicGeometry.hilbertPresheaf_curve_.doc:
**The points of the Hilbert scheme of a curve.** For a field extension `k'` of `k`, the
`k'`-points of `Hilb^d_{X/k}` are exactly the effective Cartier divisors of degree `d` on
`X_{k'}`. Since both sides are described by ideal sheaves on `X_{k'}`, the bijection is the
identity on underlying ideal sheaves, which is the naturality in `k'`.

`Scheme.Hom.finrank` is junk-valued away from the finite flat case, so the right-hand side
carries the finiteness and flatness of the projection explicitly.

(blueprint: `sk-thm-picard-hilb-curves`, part (2))

AlgebraicGeometry.hilbertPresheaf_curve_.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.hilbertPresheaf_curve_add.{u} {k : Type u} [Field k]
  {X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
  [AlgebraicGeometry.SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f] [AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper f]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.GeometricallyIntegral f] (d₁ d₂ : ℕ)
  (H₁ H₂ H : CategoryTheory.Over (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
  (e₁ : (AlgebraicGeometry.hilbertPresheaf f d₁).RepresentableBy H₁)
  (e₂ : (AlgebraicGeometry.hilbertPresheaf f d₂).RepresentableBy H₂)
  (e : (AlgebraicGeometry.hilbertPresheaf f (d₁ + d₂)).RepresentableBy H) :
  ∃ α,
    CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp α H.hom =
        CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.fst H₁.hom H₂.hom)
          H₁.hom ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite α ∧
        AlgebraicGeometry.Flat α ∧
          AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFinitePresentation α ∧
            (∀ (t : ↥H.left), AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.finrank α t = (d₁ + d₂).choose d₁) ∧
              ∀ (T : CategoryTheory.Over (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (t₁ : T ⟶ H₁)
                (t₂ : T ⟶ H₂) (t : T ⟶ H),
                CategoryTheory.Over.Hom.left t =
                    CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp
                      (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.lift (CategoryTheory.Over.Hom.left t₁)
                        (CategoryTheory.Over.Hom.left t₂) ⋯)
                      α →
                  ↑(e.homEquiv t) = ↑(e₁.homEquiv t₁) * ↑(e₂.homEquiv t₂)
AlgebraicGeometry.hilbertPresheaf_curve_.doc:
**The addition morphism of the Hilbert schemes of a curve.** If `H₁`, `H₂` and `H`
represent `Hilb^{d₁}_{X/k}`, `Hilb^{d₂}_{X/k}` and `Hilb^{d₁ + d₂}_{X/k}`, then there is a
`k`-morphism `H₁ ×[k] H₂ ⟶ H`, which on points is addition of effective Cartier divisors —
i.e. the product of the corresponding ideal sheaves — and which is finite, flat and locally of
finite presentation of degree `(d₁ + d₂).choose d₁`.

The last clause is what identifies `α`: without it any finite flat morphism of the right degree
would do, and the descent argument of the blueprint needs to know which morphism it is.

(blueprint: `sk-thm-picard-hilb-curves`, part (3))

AlgebraicGeometry.hilbertPresheaf.signature:
def AlgebraicGeometry.hilbertPresheaf.{u} {X S : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ S) (d : ℕ) :
  CategoryTheory.Functor (CategoryTheory.Over S)ᵒᵖ (Type u)
AlgebraicGeometry.hilbertPresheaf.doc:
The Hilbert functor. For `f : X ⟶ S` and `d : ℕ`, `Hilb^d_{X/S}` sends an `S`-scheme `T` to
the set of closed subschemes `Z ⊆ X_T = X ×[S] T`, encoded as quasi-coherent ideal sheaves `I`
on `X_T`, such that the projection `Z ⟶ T` is finite, flat, locally of finite presentation and
of degree `d`, the last condition meaning that its rank function `Scheme.Hom.finrank` is
constantly `d`.

An `S`-morphism `φ : T' ⟶ T` acts by pulling back the ideal sheaf along the base-change map
`X_{T'} ⟶ X_T`.

(blueprint: `sk-the-hilbert-functor--definition-1`)

If `M` is irreducible, nonexceptional for a nontrivial `ψ` and punctually `ι`-pure of
weight `w` on a dense open `U₀` of the affine line, then `H_c^1(A, j_*M)` has weights at most

theorem AlgebraicGeometry.hasWeightsAtMost_compactlySupportedCohomology_of_projectiveLine.{u} {k₀ : Type u}
  [Field k₀] [Finite k₀] {l : ℕ} [Fact (Nat.Prime l)] [Fact (ringChar k₀ ≠ l)]
  (ι : PadicAlgCl l →+* ℂ) {C : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} [Nonempty ↥C]
  [C.Over (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
  (c :
    C ⟶
      AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpace (ULift.{u, 0} (Fin 2))
        (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀)))
  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsOpenImmersion c]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.IsOver c (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact (C ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]

AlgebraicGeometry.hasWeightsAtMost_compa.doc:
Let `C` be a nonempty open subscheme of the projective line `ℙ¹_{k₀}` and let `F` be a lisse
Weil sheaf on `C`, punctually `ι`-pure of weight `w`. Then the compactly supported cohomology
`H_c^r(C, F)` of the structure morphism

```
C --- c ---> ℙ¹_{k₀}
  \            |
   \           | ↘
    `--------> Spec k₀
```

has weights at most `w + r`, with no ramification restriction at the point at infinity
(blueprint: `sk-l-dl-general-open-line`).

AlgebraicGeometry.hasDirectImageWeightBo.doc:
For a separated finite-type morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of schemes of finite type over `k₀ = 𝔽_q` and
a constructible Weil sheaf `F` on `X` mixed of weights at most `w`, the sheaf `Rʳf₀!F` is mixed of
weights at most `w + r`, for every `r` (blueprint: `sk-thm-dl-general-sheaf`,
`cor-zl-rfshriek-sheaf`).

Noetherian induction on the closed subsets of `X`: for a reduced closed subscheme `T` of `X`, the
assertion holds for `T ⟶ Y` over a nonempty open `U` of `T`
(`exists_hasDirectImageWeightBound_opensι_comp`) and, by induction, over the reduced complement of
`U`; the open–closed reduction `sk-l-dl-general-excision` glues the two.

AlgebraicGeometry.ext_of_isSchemeTheoret.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.ext_of_isSchemeTheoreticallyDominant_of_isSeparated'.{u}
  (S : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme) {T Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} [T.Over S] [Y.Over S]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated (Y ↘ S)] {f g : T ⟶ Y} [AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.IsOver f S]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.IsOver g S] {W : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (ι : W ⟶ T)
  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsSchemeTheoreticallyDominant ι]
  (hU : CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp ι f = CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp ι g) : f = g
AlgebraicGeometry.ext_of_isSchemeTheoret.doc:
**Morphisms of `S`-schemes into a separated `S`-scheme agreeing on a
scheme-theoretically dominant subscheme are equal.** For `S`-morphisms `f g : T ⟶ Y`
into a separated `S`-scheme `Y`, `f = g` as soon as `ι ≫ f = ι ≫ g` for some
scheme-theoretically dominant `ι : W ⟶ T`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.ext_of_isDominant_of_isSeparated'` with dominance of `ι`
strengthened to scheme-theoretic dominance and, in exchange, the reducedness assumption
on `T` dropped.

AlgebraicGeometry.ext_of_isSchemeTheoret.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.ext_of_isSchemeTheoreticallyDominant_of_isSeparated.{u}
  {W T Y Z : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} {f g : T ⟶ Y} (s : Y ⟶ Z) [AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated s]
  (h : CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp f s = CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp g s) (ι : W ⟶ T)
  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsSchemeTheoreticallyDominant ι]
  (hU : CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp ι f = CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp ι g) : f = g
AlgebraicGeometry.ext_of_isSchemeTheoret.doc:
**Morphisms into a separated target agreeing on a scheme-theoretically dominant
subscheme are equal.** Suppose `f g : T ⟶ Y` agree over some separated `s : Y ⟶ Z`.
Then `f = g` as soon as `ι ≫ f = ι ≫ g` for some scheme-theoretically dominant
`ι : W ⟶ T`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.ext_of_isDominant_of_isSeparated` with dominance of `ι`
strengthened to scheme-theoretic dominance and, in exchange, the reducedness assumption
on `T` dropped.

**Rigidity of morphisms into a separated scheme**: if `Y` is separated over `S`, then
two `S`-morphisms `a b : T ⟶ Y` that agree after composing with a scheme-theoretically
dominant morphism `v : V ⟶ T` are equal. The classical case is `v = V.ι` for a
scheme-theoretically dense open subscheme `V ⊆ T`.

The equaliser of `a` and `b` is the base change of the diagonal `Y ⟶ Y ×[S] Y` along
`(a, b) : T ⟶ Y ×[S] Y`, hence a *closed* subscheme of `T` because `Y ⟶ S` is separated.
As `v` factors through it, its kernel ideal sheaf is contained in the kernel of `v`, which
is trivial; so the closed immersion is an isomorphism, in particular an epimorphism, and
`a = b`. (blueprint: `lem:chow-agree-on-dense-open`)

AlgebraicGeometry.exists_smooth_properCo.doc:
Blueprint `sk-i-real-compactification`: Smooth proper completion.

Every smooth geometrically connected curve `U₀` over a finite field `K` admits a smooth proper
completion: a compactification `c : Compactification p` of the structure morphism
`p : U₀ ⟶ Spec K` whose ambient scheme `c.Z = C₀` is again a smooth geometrically connected
curve over `K`, and whose boundary `C₀ \ U₀` is a finite set of closed points of `C₀`.

The open immersion `U₀ ⟶ C₀` and the properness of `C₀ ⟶ Spec K` are part of the data of a
`Compactification`, so they do not appear among the conclusions.

AlgebraicGeometry.exists_middleExtension.doc:
**The transform of an irreducible nonexceptional middle extension.** If `M` is a nonzero
irreducible lisse Weil sheaf on a dense open `U₀` of the affine line and is nonexceptional for a
nontrivial `ψ`, then there are a dense open `j' : U'₀ ↪ A'₀` of the dual line and an irreducible
lisse Weil sheaf `M'` on it whose middle extension is the transform:

```
    U₀ ──j──▶ 𝔸¹              U'₀ ──j'──▶ 𝔸'¹
     M                          M'

               FT_ψ
    (j_*M)[1] ──────≃──────▶ (j'_*M')[1]
```
Irreducibility is meant among lisse sheaves (`AlgebraicGeometry.WeilSheaf.IsIrreducibleLisse`),
not simplicity in the category of all Weil sheaves: a nonzero lisse sheaf on a curve is never
simple there. A lisse `M` with `[Simple M]` is irreducible lisse by
`AlgebraicGeometry.WeilSheaf.IsLisse.isIrreducibleLisse`.

The object `(j_*M)[1]` is simple in the curve perverse heart, hence so is its transform; a simple
perverse object is punctual or a middle extension, and the punctual case is excluded by
nonexceptionality. (blueprint: `sk-p-dl-a1-middle`, `prop-a1-fourier-middle-extension`)

  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsOpenImmersion j] [AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact j]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.IsOver j (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsDominant j]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
  (F : AlgebraicGeometry.WeilSheaf k₀ l U) (hF : F.IsLisse) (s : ↑C.finitePoints)

    ∀ (a : (((AlgebraicGeometry.WeilSheaf.directImage j).obj F.dual).stalk s).carrier)

      (e ((((AlgebraicGeometry.WeilSheaf.directImage j).obj F.dual).stalk s).frobenius a))

AlgebraicGeometry.exists_linearEquiv_dua.doc:
For a dense open immersion `j : U₀ ↪ C₀` of smooth curves, a lisse Weil sheaf `F` on `U₀` and a
closed point `s` of `C₀` outside `U₀`, there is a Frobenius-equivariant perfect pairing
`(j_*F^∨)_s̄ ⊗ (R¹j_*F)_s̄ → ℚ̄_ℓ(-1)`:

```
  (j_*F^∨)_s̄ ⊗ (R¹j_*F)_s̄ ──────▶ ℚ̄_ℓ(-1)
       │           │                  │
  Frob │      Frob │                  │ q_s
       ▼           ▼                  ▼
  (j_*F^∨)_s̄ ⊗ (R¹j_*F)_s̄ ──────▶ ℚ̄_ℓ(-1)
```

It is exhibited as a linear isomorphism of `(j_*F^∨)_s̄` onto the `ℚ̄_ℓ`-dual of `(R¹j_*F)_s̄`
which intertwines the two local Frobenius actions up to the factor `q_s` coming from the Tate
twist. (blueprint: `sk-i-dl-a1-local`)

theorem AlgebraicGeometry.exists_jacobian_descent.{u} (k₀ ks K : Type u) [Field k₀] [Field ks] [Field K]
  [Algebra k₀ ks] [Algebra k₀ K] [Algebra ks K] [IsScalarTower k₀ ks K] [IsSepClosure k₀ ks]

  [AlgebraicGeometry.GeometricallyConnected (C₀ ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]

  [C.Over (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] (p : C ⟶ C₀)
  (hC :
    CategoryTheory.IsPullback p (C ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
      (C₀ ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))
      (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Algebra.algebraMap k₀ K)))) :
  ∃ J₀ x,
    AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper J₀.hom ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.SmoothOfRelativeDimension g J₀.hom ∧
        AlgebraicGeometry.GeometricallyIntegral J₀.hom ∧
          Nonempty
              ((AlgebraicGeometry.picardFunctorDegree
                      (C ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) 0).obj.RepresentableBy

                  (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.snd J₀.hom
                    (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Algebra.algebraMap k₀ K)))))) ∧
            ∃ e,
              ∀ (σ : Gal(K/k₀)),
                ∃ γ,
                  CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp γ p = p ∧
                    CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp γ
                          (C ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) =
                        CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp

                      ∃ act,
                        (∀ (L : AlgebraicGeometry.picardZero K C),
                            ↑(act L) = AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic.map γ ↑L) ∧

AlgebraicGeometry.exists_jacobian_descen.doc:
**The Jacobian over a general base field, by Galois descent.** Let `k₀` be any field, `k_s` a
separable closure of `k₀`, `k̄₀` an algebraic closure of `k₀` containing `k_s`, and let `C₀` be a
proper smooth geometrically connected curve of genus `g` over `k₀`.  Let `C` be the base change
`C₀ ×_{k₀} k̄₀`, presented by a cartesian square.  Then the Jacobian of `C` descends to `k₀`:
there is a `k₀`-scheme `J₀` carrying a commutative group scheme structure, proper, smooth of
relative dimension `g` and geometrically integral over `k₀`, whose base change `J₀ ×_{k₀} k̄₀`
represents `Pic^0_{C/k̄₀}`, and whose `k̄₀`-points are in bijection with `Pic^0(C)`.  The
bijection is equivariant: every `k₀`-algebra automorphism `σ` of `k̄₀` induces the automorphism
`γ` of `C` over `C₀` lying over `Spec σ`, base change along `γ` preserves `Pic^0(C)`, and the
bijection intertwines that action with the action on `k̄₀`-points by precomposition with
`AlgebraicGeometry.specAlgEquivOver σ`.

No rational point of `C₀` is assumed.

(blueprint: `sk-prop-jacobian-descent`)

AlgebraicGeometry.exists_jacobian.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.exists_jacobian.{u} {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme}
  [X.Over (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] [IsSepClosed k]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper (X ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.GeometricallyIntegral (X ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] :
  ∃ J x,
    AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper J.hom ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.SmoothOfRelativeDimension (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.arithmeticGenus k X)
          J.hom ∧
        AlgebraicGeometry.GeometricallyIntegral J.hom ∧
          Nonempty
              ((AlgebraicGeometry.picardFunctorDegree
                      (X ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) 0).obj.RepresentableBy
                J) ∧
            Nonempty
              (AlgebraicGeometry.picardZero k X ≃
                (CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategoryStruct.tensorUnit
                    (CategoryTheory.Over (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) ⟶
                  J))
AlgebraicGeometry.exists_jacobian.doc:
**The Jacobian is an abelian variety.** Let `X` be a smooth projective curve of genus `g`
over a separably closed field `k`.  Then there is a `k`-scheme `J` carrying a commutative group
scheme structure which is proper, smooth of relative dimension `g` and geometrically integral
over `k`, which represents the degree-zero part `Pic^0_{X/k}` of the Picard functor, and whose
set of `k`-rational points is in bijection with `Pic^0(X)`.

The tangent space clause `T_e J ≅ H^1(X, 𝒪_X)` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_tangentSpaceAt_linearEquiv_H_one` and is not repeated here; the
base-change clause `J(X_{k'}) = J(X) ×_k k'` for `k ⊆ k'` algebraically closed is omitted, the
corresponding compatibility over a general base field being part of
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_jacobian_descent`.

(blueprint: `sk-prop-jacobian`)

AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isEffectiveCart.doc:
**The zero-scheme dictionary.** Let `ℒ ∈ F(T)`, let `𝒩` be the invertible `𝒪_T`-module with
`Rf_{T,*} ℒ ≅ 𝒩[0]` provided by the definition of `F`, and let
`s ∈ H⁰(X_T, ℒ ⊗ f_T^* 𝒩^{-1})` be the section adjoint to that isomorphism.  Then the zero
scheme `D = Z(s) ⊆ X_T` is a relative effective Cartier divisor on `X_T/T`, finite locally free
of degree `g` over `T`, where `g` is the genus of the curve.

There is no definition of a relative effective Cartier divisor, so the conclusion is stated
as the existence of the divisor: there is a point `D` of the Hilbert functor `Hilb^g_{X/k}(T)`
whose closed subscheme is moreover an effective Cartier centre in `X_T`.

The witness is the zero scheme of the adjunction morphism, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.isInvertible_zeroLocus_directImageCounit`.

(blueprint: `sk-lem-picard-zero-dictionary`)

AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isCompact_opens.doc:
**A quasi-compact open meeting `V` exactly in `U`.** If `U ≤ V` are opens of a scheme
`X` with `U` quasi-compact and `S` is a quasi-compact subset of `X` disjoint from
`closure (V ∖ U)`, then there is a quasi-compact open `X₀` containing `S` and `U` with
`X₀ ⊓ V = U`.
(Blueprint: `lemma:nagata-conrad-case3-smaller-base`.)

AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAffineOpen_pa.doc:
**Disjoint affine neighbourhoods of generic points.** Let `X` be a quasi-separated scheme
and let `s` be a finite set of generic points of irreducible components of `X`. Then there is a
family of pairwise disjoint affine opens `U x`, for `x ∈ s`, with `x ∈ U x`.

AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAffineOpen_of.doc:
A finite set of generic points of irreducible components of a quasi-separated scheme is
contained in an affine open: the disjoint union of the affine opens provided by
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAffineOpen_pairwise_disjoint` is affine.

AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAffineOpen_me.doc:
**An affine open containing a point and all generic points.** Let `X` be a quasi-separated
scheme, let `s` be a finite set of generic points of irreducible components of `X` and let
`x : X`. Then there is an affine open of `X` containing `x` and all points of `s`.

**Affine cover through the generic points.** A quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme with
finitely many irreducible components admits a finite affine open cover each member of which

**A `U`-admissible blow-up in which `U` becomes scheme-theoretically dense**
(blueprint: `lemma:nagata-conrad-schematically-dense-blowup`, absolute form).

inverse image of the complement of the center

is the assertion.

**Conrad's Theorem 2.4, Case 1: a quasi-affine target over an affine base**
(blueprint: `lemma:nagata-conrad-quasi-affine-affine-base`).

Over an affine base, the quasi-affineness of `Y` as a scheme is the same as the
quasi-affineness of `p` as a morphism, so this is the absolute form of the hypothesis.

The proof embeds `Y` into a relative affine space over `X`
(`exists_immersion_affineSpace_of_quasiAffine'`, Stacks Tag 04II), extends `f` there by
`exists_isAdmissible_extend_affineSpace`, makes the preimage of `U` scheme-theoretically
dense by one further blow-up
(`IsAdmissible.exists_comp_isSchemeTheoreticallyDominant_preimage`), and descends the
extension back to `Y` along the closed-immersion part of the immersion, using that a
morphism agreeing on a scheme-theoretically dense open with one factoring through a closed
subscheme factors through it as well.

AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAdmissible_di.doc:
**Conrad's Theorem 2.4, Case 3, Step 1**: the disjointness blow-up.

Let `X` be qcqs, let `U ≤ V` be quasi-compact opens of `X`, let `p : Y ⟶ X` be a morphism
from a qcqs scheme and let `f : U ⟶ Y` be a section of `p` over `U` whose image is closed
in `p ⁻¹ V`. There is a `V`-admissible blow-up of `X` after which the closure of the image
of the base change of `f` is disjoint from the part lying over the closure of `V ∖ U`.

The base change is left flexible: `Z'` is an arbitrary scheme over `Y` and over
`(I₁ ⊔ I₂).blowup`, and `Y'` an arbitrary scheme over `U` and over `Z'`, fitting into the two
commuting squares, exactly as in `AlgebraicGeometry.disjoint_closure_range_of_blowupMap_sup`.
(Blueprint: `lemma:nagata-conrad-case3-disjointness-reduction`.)

**`F` is a subfunctor of the Hilbert functor.** The dictionary `ℒ ↦ D = Z(s)` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isEffectiveCartierCenter_hilbertPresheaf` is natural in `T` and
injective, so it exhibits `F` as a subfunctor of `Hilb^g_{X/k}`; the inverse on the image is

`W ⊆ Hilb^g_{X/k}` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.isRepresentable_picardFunctorInvertibleDirectImage` represents `F`.

with `CategoryTheory.uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u}`; being fully faithful, this changes neither the
functor nor the injectivity of the components.

(`AlgebraicGeometry.isInvertible_zeroLocus_directImageCounit`); it is natural by
`AlgebraicGeometry.comap_zeroLocus_directImageCounit` and injective by
`AlgebraicGeometry.eq_of_zeroLocus_directImageCounit_eq`.

Let `f : X ⟶ S` be flat, locally of finite presentation and with geometrically reduced
fibres. Then there is an étale covering `p i : U i ⟶ X` of `X`, that is, a family of étale
morphisms whose images cover `X`, such that each composite `p i ≫ f` factors as `q i ≫ r i`
with `r i : V i ⟶ S` étale and `q i : U i ⟶ V i` flat, locally of finite presentation and
affine, with geometrically connected fibres, and admitting a section:

```
U i --q i--> V i
 |            |
p i          r i
 v            v
 X ----f----> S
```

A smooth morphism satisfies the hypotheses, by `AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth.geometricallyReduced`
and the instances `Smooth → Flat` and `Smooth → LocallyOfFinitePresentation`; that special
case is Stacks `0EY4`, in which the first leg `q i` is moreover smooth.

AlgebraicGeometry.exists_eq_snd_comp.doc:
Blueprint `sk-prop-av-rigidity`: The rigidity lemma

Let `X`, `Y`, `Z` be `K`-schemes with `X` proper, geometrically connected and geometrically
reduced over `K`, with `Y` connected and with `Z` separated over `K`, and let
`g : X ×_K Y ⟶ Z` be a morphism of `K`-schemes. If `g (X ×_K {y₀})` is a single point for some
point `y₀ ∈ Y`, then `g` factors through the second projection: `g = pr₂ ≫ h` for some
`h : Y ⟶ Z`, that is, the triangle

```
  pullback fX fY ─── pullback.snd ──▶ Y
             ╲                        │
              ╲  g                    │ h
               ╲                      ▼
                ╲──────────────────▶ Z
```

commutes. The set `g (X ×_K {y₀})` is spelled as the range of the restriction of `g` to the
scheme-theoretic fibre of `pr₂` over `y₀`; the point `y₀` need not be `K`-rational.

Neither geometric hypothesis on `X` can be dropped on its own. For `K = ℝ`, `X = Spec ℂ`,
`Y = 𝔸¹_ℝ`, `Z = 𝔸¹_ℂ` and `g` the identity of `X ×_K Y = 𝔸¹_ℂ`, `X` is connected and
geometrically reduced but not geometrically connected, and `g` does not factor. For `K`
imperfect of characteristic `p`, `a ∈ K ∖ K^p`, `K' = K(a^{1/p})`, `X = Spec K'`, `Y = 𝔸¹_K`,
`Z = 𝔸¹_{K'}` and `g` the identity of `X ×_K Y = 𝔸¹_{K'}`, `X` is geometrically connected and
reduced but not geometrically reduced, and `g` does not factor since `pr₂ : 𝔸¹_{K'} ⟶ 𝔸¹_K` is
not a monomorphism. In both examples `Γ(X, 𝒪_X) ≠ K`.

This is also blueprint `lem-sc-rigidity`. The proof follows the blueprint with one change: `L`
is the set of `y` near which `g` factors through `pr₂`. It is open by definition and contains
`y₀` by `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_mem_and_comp_eq_of_subsingleton_image` (Step 4). The same
lemma shows that `L` is the locus of `AlgebraicGeometry.isClosed_setOf_subsingleton_image`, so
it is closed, hence `L = Y` as `Y` is connected. The local factorizations glue because `pr₂` is
flat, surjective and quasi-compact, hence an effective epimorphism. This route needs neither
Step 2 (`AlgebraicGeometry.eventually_finite_image`) nor `Z` locally of finite type, nor `y₀`
`K`-rational.

AlgebraicGeometry.exists_dense_isFinite_.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a dominant affine morphism of finite type between integral schemes whose
generic fibre has dimension `r`. Then there is a dense open `V ⊆ Y` over which `f` factors as a
finite surjective morphism `ν` to the `r`-fold relative affine line over `V` followed by its
projection to `V`:

```
f ⁻¹ᵁ V ----- ν -----> iteratedAffineLine V r
      \                        |
       \                       | iteratedAffineLineProj V r
    f ∣_ V                     |
         \                     v
          `----------------->  V
```

(blueprint: `sk-l-dl-general-normalization`).

AlgebraicGeometry.exists_decomposition_p.doc:
**The degree decomposition of the Picard scheme.** Let `X` be a smooth projective curve over
a separably closed field `k` and let `P` represent the Picard functor `Pic_{X/k}`.  Then `P` is
the disjoint union `∐_{d ∈ ℤ} P^d` of a family of open and closed subschemes indexed by `ℤ`,
and `P^d` represents the degree-`d` part `Pic^d_{X/k}`.

(blueprint: `sk-prop-picard-degree-decomposition`)

AlgebraicGeometry.exists_admissibleBlowu.doc:
**Elimination of indeterminacy** (Stacks Project Tag 081S; blueprint:
`def:nagata-elimination-indeterminacy`, `lemma:nagata-elimination-indeterminacy`;
proof order item 30).

The proof follows the Conrad/Zariski's-Main-Theorem route: prepare a Cartier boundary
(`exists_admissibleBlowup_cartierBoundary`, Stacks Project Tag 080Y) so that `U` becomes
scheme-theoretically dense, extend the inverse of `q` over `U` to a section over an open
`W` of a second admissible blow-up (`exists_admissibleBlowup_extend_section`, Conrad's
Remark 2.5), compose the two blow-ups (`Scheme.IdealSheafData.exists_blowup_comp`, Stacks
Project Tag 080B, whose support formula shows that the composite centre is still supported
exactly on the complement of `U`), and identify the strict transform with `W`: the graph
of the extension is closed and contains the scheme-theoretically dense `U`-graph, so it
cuts out the strict transform.

  (hU : IsCompact ↑U) (q : Z ⟶ X) [AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper q] {T : Set ↥X} (hTU : T ⊆ ↑U)
  (hT : IsClosed (⇑U.ι ⁻¹' T)) {N : X.Opens} (hTN : T ⊆ ↑N) (hN : CategoryTheory.IsIso (q ∣_ N)) :
  ∃ B N',
    closure (⇑B.I.blowupMap ⁻¹' T) ⊆ ↑N' ∧
      CategoryTheory.IsIso
        (AlgebraicGeometry.strictTransformMap q B.I.blowupMap B.preservedOpen ∣_ N')
AlgebraicGeometry.exists_admissibleBlowu.doc:
**Isomorphism near the closure of a boundary piece** (Stacks Project Tag 0F3W;
blueprint: `def:nagata-isomorphism-near-closure`,
`lemma:nagata-isomorphism-near-closure`; used for the improved comparison projection of
the two-open compactification theorem).

The proof runs as follows. Inside `U`, constructible separation
(`PrespectralSpace.exists_isCompact_isOpen_disjoint_union_eq_univ`) separates `T` from
the complement of the maximal isomorphism open `M` of `q`, producing a quasi-compact
open `V₂` of `X` with `T ⊆ V₂ ⊆ U ⊓ M` and a constructible closed decomposition of `U`.
The boundary-separation blow-up `X₁ ⟶ X` (`exists_admissibleBlowup_disjoint_closures`,
Tag 0F3V) then separates the closure of the inverse image of `T` from the closure of
the inverse image of `U \ V₂`, and a second constructible separation, now in `X₁`,
produces a **quasi-compact** open `A ⊆ X₁` containing the first closure and missing the
second; consequently every point of `A` over `U` lies over `V₂`.

Over `X₁` the canonical lift of `q` is an isomorphism above `V₂`, so eliminating its
indeterminacy (`exists_admissibleBlowup_isOpenImmersion_strictTransformMap`, Tag 081S)
gives a finite-type centre whose support misses the locus above `V₂`, hence also
`A ∩ π₁⁻¹(U)`. Gluing that centre across `A` and the locus above `U`
(`Scheme.IdealSheafData.exists_finiteType_comap_eq_of_disjoint`, Tag 080M) and composing
with the first blow-up (`Scheme.IdealSheafData.exists_blowup_comp_base_change`, Tag 080B)
produces a single `U`-admissible centre `K` on `X`, together with identifications of
both `K.blowup` and `(K.comap q).blowup` with their counterparts upstairs.

Finally Tag 080E (`Scheme.IdealSheafData.exists_blowup_comap_iso_strictTransform`)
turns the strict transform of `q` along `K.blowupMap` into the canonical lift
`(K.comap q).blowup ⟶ K.blowup`, and the localization of canonical lifts
(`Scheme.IdealSheafData.exists_comm_lift_blowup_comap_opens`) identifies that lift over
the copy of `A` with the open immersion produced by Tag 081S. The neighbourhood `N'` is
the range of the resulting partial section; it contains the closure of the inverse
image of `T` because that closure lies over `A` and inside the (closed, since `q` is
proper) range of the strict transform. No scheme-theoretic density argument is used.

**Conrad's Theorem 2.4, reduced to the base `X`** (blueprint:
`thm:nagata-conrad-elimination`, in the form reduced to the base `X`;
`def:nagata-conrad-quasi-domination`).

Conrad's Theorem 2.4 is stated for a rational map over an auxiliary base `S`; the first
step of his proof replaces `Y` by `Y ×_S X`, which is the reduction to the form stated
here. In the vocabulary of the blueprint the hypothesis says that `(U, f)` is a
quasi-domination of `V` over `Y`, and the conclusion that `(W, g)` is a
quasi-domination of the blow-up over `Y` extending `f`.

Elimination of indeterminacy (Stacks Project Tag 081S,
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_admissibleBlowup_isOpenImmersion_strictTransformMap`) is
deduced from this statement.

Density of `U` is not used: neither Conrad's Case 3 nor the quasi-finiteness of the graph
needs it. The hypothesis is kept because it is part of the interface consumed
downstream.

AlgebraicGeometry.exists_admissibleBlowu.doc:
Blueprint `sk-cor-nagata-sketch-proper-extension`: Extension to a proper target.

Let `X` be quasi-compact and quasi-separated over `S`, let `U ⊆ X` be a dense quasi-compact
open and let `y : Y ⟶ S` be proper. Then every `S`-morphism `f : U ⟶ Y` extends to a
morphism `g` defined on all of a `U`-admissible blow-up `π : X' ⟶ X` of `X`.

```text
   π⁻¹(U) ──π∣_U──→ U ──f──→ Y
      │                      │
    ι │                      │ y
      ↓                      ↓
      X' ───π───→ X ───x───→ S
```

with `g : X' ⟶ Y` satisfying `g ≫ y = π ≫ x` and `ι ≫ g = (π ∣_ U) ≫ f`.

**The constructible-boundary separation blow-up** (Stacks Project Tags 080P and
0F3V; blueprint: `def:nagata-separate-constructible-closed`,
`lemma:nagata-separate-constructible-closed`,
`def:nagata-two-open-prepared-boundaries`, `lemma:nagata-prepared-boundaries`;
proof order item 36).

The blow-up is the boundary-separation blow-up of the sum of two finite-type ideals
`I₁`, `I₂` extending the vanishing ideals of `T₁`, `T₂` from `U` (Stacks Tags 01PH
and 01PF, `Scheme.IdealSheafData.exists_finiteType_preimage_coe_support_eq`); the
closure of the inverse image of `Tᵢ` is contained in the strict transform of `V(Iᵢ)`
(`IsAdmissible.closure_preimage_subset_range_strictTransformMap`), and these strict
transforms are disjoint by `disjoint_range_strictTransformMap_sup`.

AlgebraicGeometry.eventually_finite_imag.doc:
Blueprint `sk-prop-av-image-open`: Finiteness of the image is open in the parameter

Let `X` be proper over `K`, let `Z` be separated and locally of finite type over `K`, let
`g : X ×_K Y ⟶ Z` be a morphism of `K`-schemes and let `y₀ ∈ Y`. For `y : Y` let
`g_y : X_{κ(y)} ⟶ Z_{κ(y)}` be the fibre of `(g, pr₂) : X ×_K Y ⟶ Z ×_K Y` over `y`. If the
image of `g_{y₀}` is finite, then the image of `g_y` is finite for every `y` in some open
neighbourhood of `y₀`. This is also blueprint `lem-sc-finite-image-locus-open`.

Following the blueprint, apply Stacks Tag 0AH8
(`exists_finite_imageι_comp_morphismRestrict_of_finite_image_preimage`) to `h = (g, pr₂)` over
`Y`: as `h ≫ pr₂ = pr₂` is proper and `pr₂ : Z ×_K Y ⟶ Y` is separated and locally of finite type,
the image of `h` is finite over an open neighbourhood `U` of `y₀`, so its fibres over the points of
`U` are finite. The image of `g_y` is identified with `h (pr₂⁻¹ {y})` by
`Scheme.Hom.finite_range_fiberMap_iff`.

The rigidity lemma `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_eq_snd_comp` does not depend on this result.

AlgebraicGeometry.etale_torsionSubgroupS.doc:
Blueprint `sk-prop-av-ntorsion-etale`: The `n`-torsion of an abelian variety is étale.

Let `A` be an abelian variety over a field `K` of characteristic `p` and let `n` be prime to
`p`. Then `A[n]` is an étale group scheme over `K`. This is also the first part of blueprint
`lem-sc-ntorsion-etale`.

`A[n]` is a finite group scheme of order `n ^ (2 * g)`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.finrankΓ_torsionSubgroupScheme`), which is prime to `p`, so it is étale by
`AlgebraicGeometry.etale_of_not_dvd_finrankΓ`.

AlgebraicGeometry.etale_of_not_dvd_finra.doc:
Blueprint `sk-prop-av-prime-p-etale`: Group schemes of order prime to `p` are étale

Let `G` be a finite group scheme over a field `K` of characteristic `p`, of order `m`. If
`p ∤ m` — which for `p = 0` just says `m ≠ 0` — then `G` is étale over `K`.

**Boundary separation** (Stacks Project Tag 0F3V; revised blueprint
`lemma:nagata-separate-closed-subschemes`).

The proof is the chart argument of the revised blueprint: the charts of
`Bl_{I₁ ⊔ I₂}(X)` at degree-one elements coming from local sections of `I₁` or of `I₂`
cover the blow-up (`exists_mem_range_chart_sup`), and the strict transform of `V(Iᵢ)`
misses every `Iᵢ`-chart, because on such a chart the extension of the center is
generated by a section of `Iᵢ` (`disjoint_range_strictTransformMap_of_probe`); so the
two strict transforms have no common point.

**Disjointness of boundary closures persists along strict transforms**
(blueprint: `lemma:nagata-boundary-disjoint-persists`; proof order item 37).

Each strict transform is contained in the full inverse image of the corresponding closed
subscheme.

  (G : CategoryTheory.Over (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of K))) [CategoryTheory.GrpObj G]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite G.hom] [AlgebraicGeometry.Etale G.hom] :
  Nat.card
      (CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategoryStruct.tensorUnit

    AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.finrankΓ G.hom
AlgebraicGeometry.card_points_eq_finrank.doc:
Blueprint `sk-prop-av-finite-etale-points`: Points of finite étale group schemes

A finite étale group scheme `G` of order `m` over an algebraically closed field `K` has exactly
`m` points with values in `K`. This is the first half of blueprint `lem-sc-finite-etale-points`.

The proof identifies the points with `K`-algebra homomorphisms `Γ(G, ⊤) →ₐ[K] K`; as `Γ(G, ⊤)`
is an étale `K`-algebra it is a product of `m` copies of `K`, so there are `m` of them.

theorem AlgebraicGeometry.bijective_toUnit_comp.{u} {K : Type u} [Field K] [IsAlgClosed K] {K' : Type u}
  [Field K'] [Algebra K K'] [IsAlgClosed K']
  (G : CategoryTheory.Over (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of K))) [CategoryTheory.GrpObj G]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite G.hom] [AlgebraicGeometry.Etale G.hom] :
  Function.Bijective fun s =>
    CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp
      (CategoryTheory.SemiCartesianMonoidalCategory.toUnit
        (CategoryTheory.Over.mk
          (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Algebra.algebraMap K K')))))
      s
AlgebraicGeometry.bijective_toUnit_comp.doc:
Blueprint `sk-prop-av-finite-etale-points`: Points of finite étale group schemes

Let `G` be a finite étale group scheme over an algebraically closed field `K` and let `K'` be an
algebraically closed extension of `K`. Then base change along `K ⊆ K'`, that is precomposition
with the structure morphism of `Spec K'` over `K`, is a bijection `G(K) ≃ G(K')`. This is the
second half of blueprint `lem-sc-finite-etale-points`.

Under the identification of points with `K`-algebra homomorphisms out of `Γ(G, ⊤)`, the map is
composition with `K → K'`: it is injective, and both sides have `|G|` elements.

theorem AlgebraicGeometry.bijective_pic_split.{u} {X S : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ S) (σ : S ⟶ X)
  (hσ : CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp σ f = CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.id S)
  (hf :
    ∀ (T : CategoryTheory.Over S),
      CategoryTheory.IsIso
        (AlgebraicGeometry.pushforwardUnitMap (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.snd f T.hom)))
  (T : CategoryTheory.Over S) :

    (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic.map (AlgebraicGeometry.sectionBaseChange f σ hσ T) L,

AlgebraicGeometry.bijective_pic_split.doc:
**The splitting of the sequence**: `ℒ ↦ (σ_T^* ℒ, [ℒ])` is a bijection
`Pic (X_T) ≃ Pic T × Pic_{X/S}(T)`, i.e. `Pic (X_T) = Pic T ⊕ Pic_{X/S,σ}(T)`.

```
                          f_T^*                       [-]
     0 ──────▶ Pic T ───────────────▶ Pic (X_T) ───────────────▶ Pic_{X/S}(T) ──────▶ 0
                   ◀───────────────
                        σ_T^*
```

(blueprint: `sk-prop-picard-pic-split`)

AlgebraicGeometry.abelianVariety_estimat.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.abelianVariety_estimate.{u} {K : Type u} [Field K] (p : ℕ) [CharP K p]
  (A : CategoryTheory.Over (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of K))) [CategoryTheory.GrpObj A]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsAbelianVariety A] :
  (∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < n → AlgebraicGeometry.IsIsogeny (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.id A ^ n)) ∧
    (∀ (n : ℕ),
        0 < n →
          AlgebraicGeometry.isogenyDegree (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.id A ^ n) =
            n ^ (2 * AlgebraicGeometry.IsAbelianVariety.dim A)) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ),
          0 < n → AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite (AlgebraicGeometry.torsionSubgroupScheme A n).hom) ∧
        (∀ (n : ℕ),
            0 < n → AlgebraicGeometry.Flat (AlgebraicGeometry.torsionSubgroupScheme A n).hom) ∧
          (∀ (n : ℕ),
              0 < n →
                AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.finrankΓ
                    (AlgebraicGeometry.torsionSubgroupScheme A n).hom =
                  n ^ (2 * AlgebraicGeometry.IsAbelianVariety.dim A)) ∧
            ∀ (n : ℕ),
              0 < n →
                ¬p ∣ n → AlgebraicGeometry.Etale (AlgebraicGeometry.torsionSubgroupScheme A n).hom
AlgebraicGeometry.abelianVariety_estimat.doc:
Blueprint `sk-thm-av-final`: Abelian-variety estimate, clauses (a) and (b).

Let `A` be an abelian variety of dimension `g` over a field `K`, let `p = char K` and let
`0 < n`.

* **(a)** `[n] : A ⟶ A` is a finite flat surjective homomorphism, hence an isogeny of degree
  `n ^ (2 * g)`; `A[n] = ker [n]` is a finite flat group scheme over `K` of order `n ^ (2 * g)`.
* **(b)** If `n` is prime to `p` (in particular if `p = 0`), then `A[n]` is étale of rank
  `n ^ (2 * g)`; for `p > 0` and `n = p ^ e` clause (a) already gives that `A[p ^ e]` is finite
  flat of order `p ^ (2 * g * e)`.

  [Finite k₀] [Fact (ringChar k₀ ≠ l)] {X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme}
  [X.Over (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))] (F : AlgebraicGeometry.WeilSheaf k₀ l X)

AlgebraicGeometry.WeilSheaf.traceFunctio.doc:
The trace function `t_{F,n}` of a Weil sheaf: the trace `Tr(F_x^{(n)} | F_x̄)` of the
Frobenius relative to `𝔽_{qⁿ}` on the stalk at an `𝔽_{qⁿ}`-rational point `x`, taken at the
geometric point over `x` for an embedding `𝔽_{qⁿ} ↪ k̄` chosen by `IsAlgClosed.lift`.

For `n = 0` the field `FiniteField.galoisExtension k₀ 0` is a junk value, and the trace is that
of the identity, the dimension of the stalk.

AlgebraicGeometry.WeilSheaf.traceEnergy.doc:
The trace energy `S_n(X₀, F) = ∑_{x ∈ X₀(𝔽_{qⁿ})} |ι t_{F,n}(x)|²` of a Weil sheaf at
level `n`, the squared `L²`-norm of its trace function on the `𝔽_{qⁿ}`-points, with junk value
`0` if `X₀` has infinitely many `𝔽_{qⁿ}`-points. The intended situation is that of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.finite_fieldPoints`, where `X₀` is of finite type over the finite
field `k₀` and the index type is finite. (blueprint: `sk-l-dl-a1-energy`)

AlgebraicGeometry.WeilSheaf.le_sub_one_o.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.WeilSheaf.le_sub_one_of_traceEnergy_le.{u} {k₀ : Type u} [Field k₀] [Finite k₀]
  {l : ℕ} [Fact (Nat.Prime l)] [Fact (ringChar k₀ ≠ l)] (ι : PadicAlgCl l →+* ℂ)
  {V : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} [V.Over (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffine V]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType (V ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (V ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.GeometricallyConnected (V ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
  (N : AlgebraicGeometry.WeilSheaf k₀ l V) (hN : ¬CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero N)
  (hlisse : N.IsLisse) {v : ℝ} (hpure : AlgebraicGeometry.WeilSheaf.IsPunctuallyPureOfWeight ι N v)
  {C B : ℝ} (hC : 0 < C)
  (hS :
    ∀ (n : ℕ),
      1 ≤ n → AlgebraicGeometry.WeilSheaf.traceEnergy ι N n ≤ C * ↑(Nat.card k₀) ^ (↑n * B)) :
  v ≤ B - 1
AlgebraicGeometry.WeilSheaf.le_sub_one_o.doc:
Let `N ≠ 0` be lisse on a smooth geometrically connected affine curve `V₀` of finite type
over `k₀` and punctually `ι`-pure of weight `v`. If the trace energies satisfy
`S_n(V₀, N) ≤ C q^{nB}` for every `n ≥ 1`, with `0 < C` independent of `n`, then `v ≤ B - 1`.

The energy bound bounds the `L²`-weight parameter `‖N‖` by `B - 1`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.WeilSheaf.l2Weight_le_of_traceEnergy_le`), and `‖N‖ = v` by the
`L²`-rigidity `AlgebraicGeometry.WeilSheaf.l2Weight_eq_of_isPunctuallyPureOfWeight`.
(blueprint: `sk-l-dl-a1-energy`)

In degree zero the compactly supported cohomology of `j_*F` on the line vanishes.
(blueprint: `sk-thm-dl-a1-upper`)

AlgebraicGeometry.WeilSheaf.LisseOnDense.doc:
For an irreducible nonexceptional `M` and a Fourier partner `D'` of `D`, the zero-extension
comparison datum exists. (blueprint: `sk-p-dl-a1-correction`)

In degree two the compactly supported cohomology of `j_*F` on the line is pure of weight
`w + 2`, not merely of weights at most `w + 2`. (blueprint: `sk-thm-dl-a1-upper`)

Let `j : U₀ ↪ 𝔸¹_{k₀}` be a dense open immersion and let `F` be a lisse Weil sheaf on `U₀`,
punctually `ι`-pure of weight `w` and unramified at infinity. Then `H_c^r(𝔸¹, j_*F)` has
weights at most `w + r` for every integer `r`. (blueprint: `sk-thm-dl-a1-upper`)

AlgebraicGeometry.WeilSheaf.LisseOnDense.doc:
`D'` is a *Fourier partner* of `D` if the Fourier transform of the curve perverse middle
extension `(j_*M)[1]` of `D` is the middle extension `(j'_*M')[1]` of `D'`.
(blueprint: `sk-p-dl-a1-middle`)

theorem AlgebraicGeometry.WeilSheaf.LisseOnDenseOpen.FourierCorrection.isLisse.{u} {k₀ : Type u} [Field k₀]
  [Finite k₀] {l : ℕ} [Fact (Nat.Prime l)] [Fact (ringChar k₀ ≠ l)] (ψ : AddChar k₀ (PadicAlgCl l))

AlgebraicGeometry.WeilSheaf.LisseOnDense.doc:
The correction sheaf `B'` is lisse on the entire dual line: it is a sum of Artin–Schreier
kernels. (blueprint: `sk-p-dl-a1-correction`)

The correction sheaf `B'` has weights at most `w` when `M` is punctually `ι`-pure of weight
`w`: semicontinuity of weights at the boundary points, together with the weight zero of the
Artin–Schreier kernel. (blueprint: `sk-p-dl-a1-correction`)

AlgebraicGeometry.WeilSheaf.LisseOnDense.signature:
structure AlgebraicGeometry.WeilSheaf.LisseOnDenseOpen.FourierCorrection.{u} {k₀ : Type u} [Field k₀]
  [Finite k₀] {l : ℕ} [Fact (Nat.Prime l)] [Fact (ringChar k₀ ≠ l)] (ψ : AddChar k₀ (PadicAlgCl l))

AlgebraicGeometry.WeilSheaf.LisseOnDense.doc:
The zero-extension comparison datum for `D` and a Fourier partner `D'`: a short exact sequence
`0 → B' → G → j'_*M' → 0` of Weil sheaves on the dual line together with the two isomorphisms
that identify `G[1]` with `FT_ψ(j_!M[1])` and `B'[1]` with `FT_ψ(B)`, where `B = j_*M / j_!M`
is the boundary sheaf of `D`.

```
  FT_ψ(B) ≃ B'[1]        FT_ψ(j_!M[1]) ≃ G[1]

  0 ──▶ B' ──▶ G ──▶ j'_*M' ──▶ 0
```
(blueprint: `sk-p-dl-a1-correction`)

AlgebraicGeometry.WeilSheaf.IsUnramified.doc:
A lisse Weil sheaf `F` on an open `U₀` of the affine line, embedded by `j : U₀ ↪ 𝔸¹`, is
*unramified at infinity* if it extends to a lisse Weil sheaf on `U₀ ∪ {∞} ⊆ ℙ¹`. Here `𝔸¹`
sits in `ℙ¹` through the standard chart `ι = ProjectiveLine.affineChart`, whose complement is
the point `∞`, and the extension is a lisse Weil sheaf `G` on an open `W ⊆ ℙ¹` with
`ι.opensRange ⊔ W = ⊤` (that is, `∞ ∈ W`) and `ι⁻¹(W) = U₀`, together with an isomorphism
`j'^* G ≅ F` along the factorization `j'` of `j ≫ ι` through `W`:
```
  U₀ ──j'──▶ W
  │          │
  j          W.ι
  ▼          ▼
  𝔸¹ ──ι───▶ ℙ¹
```
The choice of chart does not matter: two open immersions `𝔸¹ ↪ ℙ¹` of `k₀`-schemes differ by
a `k₀`-automorphism of `ℙ¹`. This condition is equivalent to the inertia group at `∞` acting
trivially on the geometric generic fiber of `F`.
(blueprint: `sk-d-dl-a1-setup`)

AlgebraicGeometry.WeilSheaf.IsReal.isMix.doc:
Every constructible `ι`-real Weil sheaf on a separated finite-type `k₀`-scheme is `ι`-mixed
(blueprint: `sk-i-dl-general-real`, `thm-zl-real-mixed-by-curves`).

With the present scaffold every Weil sheaf is zero (`AlgebraicGeometry.WeilSheaf.isZero`), and
the filtration of length zero exhibits `F` as mixed; the reduction of the blueprint to lisse
sheaves on curves through `Representation.exists_filtration_isIrreducible_restrict` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.WeilSheaf.exists_isClosedImmersion_isIrreducibleLocalSystem_upperStar` is
not needed.

AlgebraicGeometry.WeilSheaf.IsNonexcepti.doc:
A lisse Weil sheaf `M` on `U₀` is *nonexceptional* if none of its geometric irreducible
constituents is a linear Artin–Schreier sheaf `ℒ_{ψ(a x)}|_U`, for any `a` in the algebraic
closure of `k₀`, the value `a = 0` included; for `a = 0` the excluded constituent is the trivial
rank-one sheaf. (blueprint: `sk-p-dl-a1-middle`, `def-a1-constituent-nonexceptional`)

  [AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]

AlgebraicGeometry.WeilSheaf.IsMixedOfWei.doc:
For a separated quasi-finite morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of `k₀`-schemes the exact functor `f₀!`
preserves mixed upper weight bounds (blueprint: `sk-l-dl-general-quasifinite`).

`F` is `ι`-mixed of weights at most `w` if it admits a finite filtration

```
0 = G 0 ↪--- G 1 ↪--- ⋯ ↪--- G n ≅ F
         |        |            |
         v        v            v
      coker φ 0   ⋯      coker φ (n-1)
```

whose successive quotients `coker φᵢ` are punctually `ι`-pure of some weight at most `w`
(blueprint: `sk-d-dl-general-weights`, `def-weil-punctual-weights`).

AlgebraicGeometry.WeilSheaf.IsGeometrica.doc:
A Weil sheaf `F` on `U` is *geometrically constant* if its underlying étale sheaf is
constant on every connected open `V` of the geometric fiber `Ū = U ⊗ k̄`, where `k̄` is an
algebraic closure of `k₀`; its Frobenius module may still be nontrivial. When the connected
components of `Ū` are open, for instance when `U` is of finite type over `k₀`, this says that
`F` is constant on each connected component of `Ū`. For `Ū` connected, as for `U` an open of
`𝔸¹_{k₀}`, it is the constancy of `F` on `Ū`, which motivates the definition: the geometric
fundamental group `π₁(Ū)` acts trivially on the stalks of `F`.
(blueprint: `sk-d-dl-a1-setup`)

AlgebraicGeometry.WeilGroup.isPunctually.doc:
Blueprint `sk-p-real-purity`: Purity of real lisse sheaves on curves.

The main theorem of the block. Let `C₀ / 𝔽_q` be a smooth geometrically connected curve and
`ℱ` an `ι`-real lisse Weil sheaf on it. Then every irreducible constituent `V` of `ℱ` is
punctually `ι`-pure of weight `dw_ι (V)`, its own determinant weight.

Replacing `ℱ` by its semisimplification, which has the same local polynomials and is again
real, and restricting to a nonempty affine open `U₀`, fix a nonzero weight block `𝒮 (γ)` and
let `N = N_γ` and `B = B_γ` be the rank and the weight sum of the blocks strictly above `γ`.
The exterior power `⋀ ^ (N + 1) 𝒮` is nonzero, real, and its constituents have determinant
weight at most `B + γ`. At a point of degree `e`, multiplying one eigenvalue `α` of the
`γ`-block by all eigenvalues of all higher blocks produces an eigenvalue of that exterior
power, so the Rankin–Selberg bound gives `|ι α| q ^ (e B / 2) ≤ q ^ (e (B + γ) / 2)`, that is
`|ι α| ≤ q ^ (e γ / 2)`. Since the determinant of the block is pure of weight `r γ`, the
product of the `r` ratios `|ι α_i| / q ^ (e γ / 2)` is `1` while each is at most `1`, so each
is `1`. That is purity on `U₀`, and semi-continuity of weights extends it over the finitely
many missing points of `C₀`.

  S.ShortExact ↔
    (S.map
        (CategoryTheory.forget₂ (Rep.{u, 0, u} (PadicAlgCl l) W.carrier)
          (ModuleCat (PadicAlgCl l)))).ShortExact
AlgebraicGeometry.WeilGroup.isLisseRep_s.doc:
Blueprint `sk-i-real-sheaves`, node `prop-wf-weil-sheaf-representation-equivalence`:
The lisse sheaf–representation equivalence.

A short complex of lisse Weil representations is short exact exactly when its geometric
generic stalk, i.e. its image under the forgetful functor to `ModuleCat ℚ̄_ℓ`, is short exact.
This is the form in which the exactness of the geometric-generic-stalk equivalence of
`sk-i-real-sheaves` is used, lisse `ℚ̄_ℓ`-sheaves themselves being unavailable.

The forgetful functor is faithful and exact, since kernels and cokernels of representations
are computed on the underlying vector spaces, so it preserves and reflects short exactness;
the lisse hypotheses are not needed.

underlying `ℚ̄_ℓ`-vector space is finite dimensional and the geometric subgroup `π₁(C)`

AlgebraicGeometry.WeilGroup.hasWeightsAt.doc:
Blueprint `sk-p-real-rankin`: Rankin–Selberg upper bound.

Let `U₀` be an affine smooth geometrically connected curve over `𝔽_q` and let `ℱ ≠ 0` be an
`ι`-real lisse Weil sheaf on it all of whose irreducible constituents have determinant weight
at most `d`. Then every local Frobenius eigenvalue of `ℱ` has `ι`-weight at most `d`.

The proof runs the Rankin–Selberg trick on the even tensor powers `ℋ_m = ℱ ^ ⊗ (2 m)`. Their
constituents have determinant weight at most `2 m d`, so the top compactly supported
cohomology `H_c² (U, ℋ_m)`, a coinvariant Tate twist, has eigenvalues of modulus at most
`q ^ (m d + 1)`; the Grothendieck trace formula therefore bounds the radius of convergence of
`L_ι (U₀, ℋ_m, T)` below by `q ^ (-(m d + 1))`. Reality of `ℱ` makes every coefficient of
every inverse local factor nonnegative, so each individual factor inherits that radius bound
from the product, and a zero of the local denominator at `|ι α| ^ (-2 m / e)` gives
`wt (α) ≤ d + 1 / m` for every `m`.

AlgebraicGeometry.WeilGroup.globalSectio.doc:
Blueprint `sk-p-real-sections`, node `p-real-sections`: Global sections as invariants.

For a lisse Weil representation `(V, ρ)` and a restriction `R` of Weil groups along a nonempty
open `U₀ ⊆ C₀`, the global sections `H⁰(U, F|_U) = Hom_{π₁(U)}(𝟙, V)` are the invariants
`V ^ (π₁(U))`, by evaluation at `1`: an equivariant map `ℚ̄_ℓ → V` is determined by the
image of `1`, which is fixed by `π₁(U)`, and every fixed vector arises this way. The finiteness
and lisse hypotheses are not needed for this.

Both sides carry a residual action of the geometric Frobenius `F = ρ (res γ)`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.WeilGroup.comp_mem_globalSections` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.WeilGroup.frobeniusLift_mem_invariants`), and the identification is
equivariant for it:

```
    H⁰(U, F|_U) ──── e ────▶ V^{π₁(U)}
          │                      │
    F ∘ ─ │                      │ F
          ▼                      ▼
    H⁰(U, F|_U) ──── e ────▶ V^{π₁(U)}
```

rank-one sheaf, i.e. a `π₁(U)`-equivariant `ℚ̄_ℓ`-linear map `ℚ̄_ℓ → V`, where `π₁(U)` acts

Blueprint `sk-d-real-cohom`: Cohomology and the Euler series.

The Euler series `L_ι(C₀, ρ, T) = ∏_{x ∈ |C₀|} ι P_x(ρ, T ^ e_x)⁻¹` of a Weil representation
`ρ`, the locally finite product over the closed points `x` of the curve of the inverses of the
local polynomials `P_x(ρ, T)` of `AlgebraicGeometry.WeilGroup.localPolynomial`, transported to
`ℂ` along `ι` and substituted into `T ^ e_x` for the residue degree `e_x = p.degreeOver x`.

Each factor is a formal power series with constant term `1`, so the product lies in
`1 + T ℂ⟦X⟧` (`AlgebraicGeometry.WeilGroup.constantCoeff_eulerSeries`); it is taken in the
product topology on `ℂ⟦X⟧`, in which it converges by
`AlgebraicGeometry.WeilGroup.multipliable_eulerFactors`.

Blueprint `sk-p-real-rankone`: Purity of rank-one Weil sheaves.

A rank-one lisse Weil sheaf `L` on a smooth geometrically connected curve `U₀ / 𝔽_q`, with
character `χ : W (U₀) → ℚ̄_ℓ ˣ`, is punctually `ι`-pure of weight
`w = 2 log |ι c| / log q`, where `c = χ γ` is the value at the chosen degree-one lift; here
`ℓ ≠ p` and the Weil group is linked to the étale fundamental group
(`AlgebraicGeometry.WeilGroup.IsEtaleQuotient`).

Once the geometric image is finite (`AlgebraicGeometry.WeilGroup.IsLisse.finite_geometric_image`),
`χ` is a root of unity times the constant character `c ^ deg`, so the local scalar at a point
of degree `e` has complex modulus `|ι c| ^ e = q ^ (e * w / 2)`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.WeilGroup.frobeniusWeight_eq_of_continuous`).

Blueprint `sk-p-real-rankone`: Purity of rank-one Weil sheaves.

The geometric image `χ (π₁ U)` of a rank-one lisse Weil sheaf on a smooth geometrically
connected curve `U₀ / 𝔽_q` is finite, for `ℓ ≠ p` and a Weil group linked to the étale
fundamental group (`AlgebraicGeometry.WeilGroup.IsEtaleQuotient`).

This is the heart of the matter: the `ℓ`-adic logarithm turns an `N`-th power of `χ`
restricted to `π₁ U` into a continuous additive map invariant under conjugation by `γ`, and
such a map is a Frobenius-fixed class in `H¹ (U, ℚ̄_ℓ)`, which vanishes because on a proper
curve `H¹` is dual to a Tate module with no Frobenius-fixed vector, and the boundary
contribution for an open curve is a nonzero power of `q`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.WeilGroup.finite_range_of_continuous`, applied to `χ = det ρ`).

    FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] ↥E ∧
      ∃ L,
        Module.Free ↥(PadicAlgCl.integers l ↥E) ↥L ∧

AlgebraicGeometry.WeilGroup.IsLisse.exis.doc:
Blueprint `sk-p-real-integral`: Integral models.

Let `ρ` be a lisse Weil representation on `V` over `ℚ̄_ℓ` and let `R` be a restriction of Weil
groups along a nonempty open subscheme `j : U₀ ⊆ C₀`. Then, after replacing the coefficient
field by a finite extension `E/ℚ_ℓ` — here a finite-dimensional intermediate field of
`ℚ_ℓ ⊆ ℚ̄_ℓ` — there is an `𝒪_E`-lattice `L ⊂ V`, that is a free `𝒪_E`-submodule of rank
`dim V` whose `ℚ̄_ℓ`-span is all of `V`, which is stable under `ρ (π₁(U))` and whose
reduction modulo `𝔪_E ^ n` has finite `π₁(U)`-image for every `n`.

The finiteness of the image in `Aut (L / 𝔪_E ^ n L)` is expressed as the finiteness of the
set of maps `L → V / 𝔪_E ^ n L` induced by the elements of `π₁(U)`; since `L` is stable and
`L / 𝔪_E ^ n L → V / 𝔪_E ^ n L` is injective, this is the same condition, and it avoids
having to restrict `ρ g` to `L` before the lattice is known to be stable.

AlgebraicGeometry.WeilGroup.IsLisse.signature:

AlgebraicGeometry.WeilGroup.IsLisse.doc:
Blueprint `sk-d-real-weil`: Weil sheaves and their representations.

A `ℚ̄_ℓ`-representation of the Weil group is *lisse* if the geometric subgroup `π₁(C)` acts
continuously, i.e. the matrix coefficients of the restricted representation are continuous in
every basis. By `sk-p-real-integral` this is equivalent, for a finite-dimensional `V`, to the
existence of a model over a finite extension `E/ℚ_ℓ` carrying a `π₁(C)`-stable `𝒪_E`-lattice.

Finite-dimensionality of `V` is not part of this predicate: it is an independent condition,
imposed where it is needed (see `AlgebraicGeometry.WeilGroup.isLisseRep`).

AlgebraicGeometry.WeilGroup.HasWeightsAt.doc:
Blueprint `sk-d-real-weights`: Local weights and reality.

`ρ` has weights at most `w` if every local Frobenius eigenvalue at every closed point has
`ι`-weight at most `w`.

AlgebraicGeometry.WeilGroup.HasDetWeight.doc:
Blueprint `sk-d-real-detweights`: Determinant weights and weight blocks.

`ρ` has determinant weight `γ`, written `dw_ι(ρ) = γ`, if the determinant character is
punctually `ι`-pure of weight `rank ρ * γ`. By `sk-p-real-rankone` a nonzero irreducible `ρ`
has exactly one determinant weight.

structure AlgebraicGeometry.WeilGroup.{u} {K : Type u} [Field K] {C : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} [Finite K]

AlgebraicGeometry.WeilGroup.doc:
Blueprint `sk-d-real-weil`: Weil sheaves and their representations.

The Weil group of a curve `p : C₀ ⟶ Spec 𝔽_q`. It is the preimage of the integer powers of
the geometric Frobenius under `π₁(C₀) → Gal(k / 𝔽_q)`, and comes with the exact degree
sequence `1 → π₁(C) → W(C₀) → ℤ → 0` whose kernel is the profinite geometric fundamental
group `π₁(C)`.

Since the étale fundamental group of a scheme is not available, this is recorded as data:
a topological group `W` with a surjective degree homomorphism to `ℤ` whose kernel is open and
profinite, a chosen degree-one lift `frobeniusLift`, and for every closed point `x` of `C₀` a
local Frobenius element `frobenius x`, well defined up to conjugacy, of degree
`e_x = [k(x) : 𝔽_q]`.

AlgebraicGeometry.WeilFunctionalEquation.doc:
**Betti symmetry.** The functional equation matches the reciprocal roots in degree `i` with
those in degree `2 * d - i`, so the two root multisets have the same cardinality; over `ℂ` that
cardinality is the degree, so the Betti numbers `b i = deg (P i)` satisfy
`b i = b (2 * d - i)`.

AlgebraicGeometry.WeilFunctionalEquation.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.WeilFunctionalEquation.alternatingProdEval_eq {q d : ℕ} (hq : 1 < q) {m : ℤ}
  {P : Fin (2 * d + 1) → Polynomial ℤ} (h0 : ∀ (i : Fin (2 * d + 1)), (P i).coeff 0 = 1)
  (hfe : AlgebraicGeometry.WeilFunctionalEquation q d P)
  (_hm : ↑d * Polynomial.alternatingNatDegreeSum P = 2 * m) (t : ℂ) (ht : t ≠ 0)
  (_hne :
    ∀ (i : Fin (2 * d + 1)), Polynomial.eval t (Polynomial.map (Int.castRingHom ℂ) (P i)) ≠ 0) :
  Polynomial.alternatingProdEval (fun i => Polynomial.map (Int.castRingHom ℂ) (P i))
      (↑q ^ (-↑d) * t⁻¹) =
    ↑(AlgebraicGeometry.weilSign q m P) * ↑q ^ m * t ^ Polynomial.alternatingNatDegreeSum P *
      Polynomial.alternatingProdEval (fun i => Polynomial.map (Int.castRingHom ℂ) (P i)) t
AlgebraicGeometry.WeilFunctionalEquation.doc:
**The classical functional equation** (blueprint `sk-thm-fe`, and the main claim of
`prop-functional-equation`). The alternating product of the values of a family of normalized
Weil factors satisfying the functional equation obeys `Z (q^{-d} t⁻¹) = ε q^{m} t^χ Z (t)` at
every nonzero `t` at which no factor vanishes, where `2 m = d χ`.

Substituting the reciprocity relation of each factor and reindexing by `i ↦ 2 d - i` gives the
determinant-constant form `WeilFunctionalEquation.alternatingProdEval_eq_prod_determinant`, and
`(-1)^χ ∏ᵢ Dᵢ^{(-1)ⁱ} = ε q^m` by definition of `ε`. Neither the evenness `2 m = d χ` nor the
nonvanishing of the factors at `t` is needed for the identity itself.

AlgebraicGeometry.WeilFunctionalEquation.signature: def AlgebraicGeometry.WeilFunctionalEquation (q d : ℕ) (P : Fin (2 * d + 1) → Polynomial ℤ) : Prop
AlgebraicGeometry.WeilFunctionalEquation.doc:
The functional equation part of the Weil conjectures: `α ↦ qᵈ / α` maps the inverse
roots of `Pᵢ` bijectively (with multiplicity) to the inverse roots of `P_{2d - i}`.
In terms of the complex roots `z = 1 / α` this says that `z ↦ 1 / (qᵈ z)` identifies the
root multisets of `Pᵢ` and `P_{2d - i}`. It implies the classical functional equation
`Z(X, 1 / (qᵈ t)) = ± q^{dχ/2} tᵡ Z(X, t)` for the associated rational function.

AlgebraicGeometry.WeilComplex.IsMixedOfW.doc:
If `K` is a bounded constructible Weil complex on `X` mixed of weights at most `w`, then
`Rf₀!K` is mixed of weights at most `w` (blueprint: `sk-cor-dl-general-complex`,
`thm-zl-wme-deligne-estimate`).

def AlgebraicGeometry.WeilComplex.IsMixedOfWeightsAtMost.{u} {k₀ : Type u} [Field k₀] [Finite k₀]

AlgebraicGeometry.WeilComplex.IsMixedOfW.doc:
A bounded constructible Weil complex `K` is `ι`-*mixed of weights at most* `w` if its `b`-th
cohomology sheaf `𝓗ᵇK` is mixed of weights at most `w + b`, for every `b`; equivalently, the
bound in total degree `n` is `w + n` (blueprint: `sk-d-dl-general-weights`).

AlgebraicGeometry.WeilComplex.IsCurvePer.doc:
The upper truncation class of the perverse t-structure on a smooth curve: `𝓗ᵃK = 0` for
`a > 0`, and `𝓗⁰K` has finite support. (blueprint: `sk-p-dl-a1-perverse`)

The lower truncation class of the perverse t-structure on a smooth curve: `𝓗ᵃK = 0` for
`a < -1`, and `𝓗⁻¹K` has no nonzero subsheaf of finite support.
(blueprint: `sk-p-dl-a1-perverse`)

A Weil complex on a smooth curve is *curve perverse* if it lies in both truncation classes.
(blueprint: `sk-p-dl-a1-perverse`)

AlgebraicGeometry.ValuativeCommSqWithPt..doc:
**A valuative commutative square through a dense source** (Stacks Project Tag 02JQ):
every point of the target of a quasi-compact dominant morphism is the centre of a valuative
commutative square.
(Blueprint: `lemma:nagata-dense-valuation-probe`.)

AlgebraicGeometry.ValuativeCommSqWithPt.doc:
A **valuative commutative square centred at a point** `z ∈ P` of a morphism
`h : T ⟶ P`: a valuative commutative square for `h` whose valuation-ring leg takes the
closed point of `Spec R` to `z`. It is the *valuation probe* of Stacks Project Tag 02JQ.
(Blueprint: `def:nagata-dense-valuation-probe`.)

AlgebraicGeometry.UniversallyClosed.of_v.doc:
**The dense-source valuative criterion, universal closedness** (Stacks Project
Tag 0894): a quasi-compact morphism satisfying the valuative criterion relative to a
quasi-compact dominant `h : U ⟶ X` is universally closed.
(Blueprint: `lemma:nagata-dense-source-valuative`.)

AlgebraicGeometry.UniversallyClosed.eq_v.doc: The **valuative criterion** for universally closed morphisms.

AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide.isSeparate.doc:
**Separatedness of the intermediate scheme** (Stacks Project Tag 0F3U; blueprint:
`lemma:nagata-intermediate-separated`): the two charts of `Wᵢ ⟶ S` are separated and
their overlap is a closed immersion.

AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide.isProper_g.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide.isProper_graph.{u} {U S : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} {u : U ⟶ S}
  {O : U.Opens} (σ : AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide u O) : AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper σ.graph
AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide.isProper_g.doc:
The graph of the proper extension is proper; in particular its range is closed.
(Blueprint: `lemma:nagata-proper-extension-graph-closed`.)

AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide.isProper_c.doc:
**Properness of the comparison projections** (blueprint:
`lemma:nagata-comparison-projections-proper`): the projection `X₁₂ ⟶ X₁` is a closed
immersion followed by a base change of the proper structure morphism of `X₂`.

AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide.isClosedIm.doc:
**The overlap of the two charts of the intermediate scheme is a closed immersion**
(blueprint: `lemma:nagata-intermediate-overlap-constructible` through
`lemma:nagata-intermediate-overlap-closed`).

The range of the overlap map is the preimage of the closed range of the proper graph
`V ⟶ U ×_S X`, because over the complement of the forbidden boundary the graph passes
through the embedded copy of `O` exactly over `O` (`TwoOpenSide.range_υ`).

AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide.interior.doc:
The complement of the forbidden boundary, i.e. the locus `Xᵢ°` of the blueprint.
(Blueprint: `def:nagata-two-open-intermediate-schemes`.)

AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide.forbiddenB.doc:
The **forbidden boundary** of a side: the closure in the ambient scheme of the
inverse image under `ψ` of the closed complement `U ∖ O` of its own open. Removing it
yields the intermediate locus `Xᵢ°` of the blueprint.
(Blueprint: `Z̄_{i,j}` in `def:nagata-two-open-prepared-boundaries`.)

AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide.dense_rang.doc:
**The copy of `U` is dense in the intermediate scheme**: the second chart is the
complement of the forbidden boundary, in which the embedded copy of `O` is dense.
(Blueprint: part of `lemma:nagata-two-open-density-transport`.)

AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide.comparison.doc:
The **comparison space** `X₁₂`: the scheme-theoretic image of `V₁ ×_U V₂` in
`X₁ ×_S X₂`. (Blueprint: `def:nagata-two-open-comparison-space`.)

AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide.closure_im.doc:
The image in the ambient scheme of a closed boundary locus of `V` meets `V` in
exactly itself: boundary loci are closed in `V`.

AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide.admissible.doc:
**Transport of a side along a `V`-admissible blow-up** of the ambient scheme
(blueprint: `def:nagata-two-open-prepared-boundaries`,
`def:nagata-two-open-improved-comparison`).

The open `V`, the proper extension `ψ` and the embedded copy of `O` transport along the
isomorphism over `V`; density transports because the complement of the center is dense in
the blow-up.

AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide.Prepared.doc:
A side is **prepared** relative to the other open `O'` if its two boundary closures
are disjoint. (Blueprint: `lemma:nagata-prepared-boundaries`.)

**One valuation extension avoids its forbidden boundary** (blueprint:
`lemma:nagata-valuation-pair-factors-comparison`,
`lemma:nagata-valuation-open-closed-point`,
`lemma:nagata-one-valuation-avoids-boundary`).

The **key boundary disjointness** (blueprint:
`lemma:nagata-key-boundary-disjointness`): no point of the comparison space projects
into the forbidden boundary on both sides, i.e.
`X₁₂ ∩ (Z̄₁,₂ ×_S Z̄₂,₁) = ∅` inside `X₁ ×_S X₂`.

structure AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide.{u} {U S : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (u : U ⟶ S) (O : U.Opens) :
  Type (u + 1)
AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide.doc:
The data of one **side of the two-open compactification theorem** for a morphism
`u : U ⟶ S` and an open `O` of `U` (blueprint:
`def:nagata-two-open-graph-extensions`, `def:nagata-two-open-boundary-loci`).

The second open of the two-open construction plays no role in this data; it enters only
as a parameter of the boundary loci `TwoOpenSide.selfBoundary` and of the preparedness
predicate `TwoOpenSide.Prepared`.

    ∃ (_ : AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineOpen U) (_ : AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineOpen V) (_ : g x ∈ U) (_

AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth.exists_etale_to.doc:
The étale-local normal form (blueprint `sk-prop-normal-form`).
Let `g : X ⟶ Y` be smooth of relative dimension `d` and let `x : X`. After replacing
`X` and `Y` by affine open neighbourhoods `V ∋ x` and `U ∋ g.base x` with `V ≤ g ⁻¹ᵁ U`,
the morphism `g` factors as an étale morphism `e : V ⟶ 𝔸(d; U)` followed by the projection
`𝔸(d; U) ↘ U`:

```
V --e--> 𝔸(d; U)
 \          |
  \         ↓
g.resLE     U
```

theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.zetaSeries_rational.{u} {k : Type u} [Field k] [Finite k]

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.zetaSeries_rati.doc:
**Dwork's theorem**: the zeta function of a scheme of finite type over a finite field
is a rational function with integer coefficients. This is the first Weil conjecture, which
holds without any smoothness or properness hypotheses.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.weil_conjecture.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.weil_conjectures.{u} {k : Type u} [Field k] [Finite k]
  {X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (d : ℕ)
  [AlgebraicGeometry.SmoothOfRelativeDimension d f] [AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper f]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.GeometricallyIntegral f] :
  ∃ P,
    AlgebraicGeometry.IsWeilFactorization (Nat.card k) d (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.zetaSeries f)
        P ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.WeilFunctionalEquation (Nat.card k) d P ∧
        AlgebraicGeometry.WeilRiemannHypothesis (Nat.card k) d P
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.weil_conjecture.doc:
**The Weil conjectures** (Dwork, Grothendieck, Deligne): the zeta function of a
smooth, proper, geometrically integral scheme `X` of dimension `d` over a finite field
`k` with `q` elements factors as `Z(X, t) = (P₁ ⋯ P_{2d-1}) / (P₀ ⋯ P_{2d})` with
`Pᵢ ∈ ℤ[t]`, `Pᵢ(0) = 1`, `P₀ = 1 - t`, `P_{2d} = 1 - qᵈ t`, satisfying the functional
equation and the Riemann hypothesis: all inverse roots of `Pᵢ` have absolute value
`q^{i/2}`, and `α ↦ qᵈ / α` matches the inverse roots of `Pᵢ` with those of `P_{2d-i}`.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.upperStarConsta.doc:
The pullback of étale sheaves along `f : X ⟶ Y` sends constant sheaves to constant
sheaves: `constantSheaf ⋙ f^*` and `constantSheaf` are both left adjoint to global
sections of the pushforward, since base change preserves the terminal object of the
small étale site (`X ×_Y Y ≅ X`).

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.subsingleton_co.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.subsingleton_cohomologicalPicardGroup_of_field.{u} (K : Type u) [Field K] :
  Subsingleton (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of K)).CohomologicalPicardGroup
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.subsingleton_co.doc:
**Hilbert 90** for a field: the cohomological Picard group `H¹(Spec K_ét, 𝔾ₘ)` of the
spectrum of a field vanishes.

The blueprint deduces this from the comparison
`{invertible 𝒪_X-modules}/≅ ≃ H¹(X_Zar, 𝒪_Xˣ) ≃ H¹(X_ét, 𝔾ₘ)` for `X = Spec K` and the
triviality of invertible modules over a field. Here the two steps are done at once and only in
the direction needed: a class in `H¹ = Ext¹(ℤ, 𝔾ₘ)` vanishes when the global sections of every
quotient `E/𝔾ₘ` lift (`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.subsingleton_H_one_of_surjective`), and they lift
because every `𝔾ₘ`-torsor on `Spec K` is trivial
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.surjective_app_of_shortExact_gmSheaf`).
(blueprint: `cor-sc-hilbert-90-field`)

theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.serreDuality.{u} {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme}
  [X.Over (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper (X ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] (p q : ℕ)
  (hpq : p + q = 1) :
  Nonempty
    ((SheafOfModules.isFiniteLocallyFree X.ringCatSheaf).ι.op.comp
        ((AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.cohomologyFunctor k q).op.comp
          (ModuleCat.dualFunctor k)) ≅
      (SheafOfModules.isFiniteLocallyFree X.ringCatSheaf).ι.op.comp
        ((AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.dualFunctor X).comp
          ((CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorRight
                (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials
                  (X ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))).comp
            (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.cohomologyFunctor k p))))
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.serreDuality.doc:
**Serre duality for curves.** Let `X` be a smooth proper curve over `k` with canonical module
`ω_X = Ω¹_{X/k}`, and let `p + q = 1`. Then `ℱ ↦ H^q(X, ℱ)^∨` and `ℱ ↦ H^p(X, ℱᵛ ⊗ Ω¹_{X/k})`
are naturally isomorphic as contravariant functors on finite locally free `ℱ`. That is, there are
`k`-linear isomorphisms `e ℱ : H^q(X, ℱ)^∨ ≅ H^p(X, ℱᵛ ⊗ Ω¹_{X/k})` such that for every
morphism `φ : ℱ ⟶ 𝒢` of finite locally free modules the square
```
  H^q(𝒢)^∨ ───── e 𝒢 ─────▶ H^p(𝒢ᵛ ⊗ Ω¹)
     │                           │
 H^q(φ)^∨                   H^p(φᵛ ▷ Ω¹)
     ▼                           ▼
  H^q(ℱ)^∨ ───── e ℱ ─────▶ H^p(ℱᵛ ⊗ Ω¹)
```
commutes. No hypothesis `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = k` is needed.

The case `q = 1` is `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.nonempty_dual_H_one_iso`, obtained from a finite flat
morphism `X ⟶ ℙ¹_k` and duality on `ℙ¹_k`; the case `q = 0` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.nonempty_dual_H_zero_iso`, deduced from it by biduality.

(blueprint: `sk-thm-picard-duality`, `thm-sc-serre-duality-curve`)
