  (U : Fin n → X.Opens) (r : ℕ) : X.Opens
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.partialAffineOp.doc:
**The partial unions of a finite family of opens**: `X_r = U 0 ∪ ⋯ ∪ U (r - 1)`, so that
`X_0 = ∅` and `X_n` is the union of the whole family.
(blueprint: `def:nagata-partial-affine-unions`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.nonempty_noethe.doc:
**Absolute Noetherian approximation** (Stacks Project Tag 01ZA): every quasi-compact
quasi-separated scheme is the limit of a cofiltered system of schemes of finite type over
`ℤ` with affine transition morphisms.

The affine case is `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.NoetherianApproximation.ofIsAffine`. The
general case follows by induction over a finite affine cover: each step extends an
approximation of a quasi-compact open across one more affine open, see
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.NoetherianApproximation.ExtensionData.approximation`.
(Blueprint: `prop:nagata-noetherian-inverse-system`.)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.kummerSequence_.doc:
**Exactness of the Kummer sequence.** Let `X` be a scheme and let `n ≥ 1` be invertible on
`X`. Then the Kummer sequence `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.kummerSequence` is a short exact
sequence of sheaves on `X_ét`.

The first map is a kernel of the second by definition of `μₙ`. The second map, `ω ↦ ωⁿ`, is
an epimorphism because it is locally surjective
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isLocallySurjective_nsmul_gmSheaf`): a unit `t` acquires an `n`-th
root on the finite étale surjective cover `Spec 𝒪[T]/(Tⁿ - t)`. The hypothesis is necessary: in
characteristic `p` the `p`-th power map is not an epimorphism of étale sheaves, and the correct
replacement is the Artin–Schreier sequence.
(blueprint: `lem-sc-kummer-exact`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.kummerSequence.signature:
def AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.kummerSequence.{u} (X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme) (n : ℕ) :
  CategoryTheory.ShortComplex (CategoryTheory.Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat)
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.kummerSequence.doc:
The *Kummer sequence* of a scheme `X` and an integer `n`: the sequence of étale sheaves

```
  0 ──▶ μₙ ──kernel.ι──▶ 𝔾ₘ ──n • 𝟙──▶ 𝔾ₘ ──▶ 0
```

on `X`, the second map being `ω ↦ ωⁿ` and `μₙ = ker(n)` the sheaf of `n`-th roots of unity.
Its exactness is `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.kummerSequence_shortExact` and is *not* part of
the definition.
(blueprint: `def-sc-kummer-sequence`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isIso_unit_uppe.doc:
Blueprint `sk-i-real-boundary`: Boundary stalks and restriction to an open.
Also `lem-a1-lisse-middle-extension`.

A finite locally constant sheaf `𝒢` on a smooth curve `C₀` is the direct image of its
restriction to a dense open `U₀`: the unit of the adjunction `j^* ⊣ j_*` is an isomorphism
at `𝒢`,

```
    𝒢 ──────▶ j_* j^* 𝒢
```

It suffices to check this on the stalks at all geometric points. At a point of `U₀` the stalk
of the unit is that of `j^*` of the unit, which is inverse to the counit `j^* j_* j^* 𝒢 ≅ j^* 𝒢`;
at a removed point this is `isIso_sheafFiber_map_unit_upperStarLowerStarAdjunction`.

`a^* F` is finite locally constant if and only if `b^* F` is.
(blueprint: `lemma:constructible-immersion-independence`)

immersion is.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isConstructible.doc:
Blueprint `sk-i-real-boundary`: Boundary stalks and restriction to an open.
Also `lem-wf-dense-open-pi1-surjective`, part (5).

The direct image `j_* ℱ` of a finite locally constant sheaf along an open immersion into a
curve `C₀` with finite complement is constructible. The complement consists of closed points,
since `C₀` is a Jacobson space, so the range of `j` and the boundary points stratify `C₀`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Stratification.ofOpenImmersion`). On `U₀` the restriction of
`j_* ℱ` is `ℱ`, and at a boundary point it is finite locally constant by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isFiniteLocallyConstantSheaf_upperStar_middleExtension`.

**A sheaf is constructible if and only if its restrictions to the members of a
complementary pair `(j, i)` are.** (blueprint: `prop:constructible-open-closed`)

constant if and only if the pullback of `F` to `U.left` is constant.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isConservativeF.doc: **The universe-lifted geometric points of `S` form a conservative family.**

**Positive degree implies ample.** An invertible sheaf of positive degree on a smooth
proper curve over `k` with `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = k` is ample: after base change to an algebraic closure
`k̄`, where the degree is unchanged (`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.degree_pullback`), some
power `ℒ_{k̄}^{⊗ m}` is very ample
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isAmple_of_degree_pos_of_isAlgClosed`), and very ampleness
descends (`AlgebraicGeometry.IsVeryAmple.of_pullback`).

(blueprint: `sk-thm-picard-rr`, part (G))

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isAffine_compl_.doc:
**Affine complement.** Let `D` be an effective Cartier divisor on a smooth proper curve `X`,
with invertible ideal sheaf `J = 𝒪_X(-D)`, whose line bundle `𝒪_X(D) = J.toModulesᵛ` is ample.
Then `X \ Supp D` is affine. The open complement of the support of `D` is presented by an open
immersion `j` whose range is the complement of the support of `J`. This is the case of curves of
`AlgebraicGeometry.isAffine_compl_of_isAmple_dual_toModules`.

(blueprint: `sk-thm-picard-rr`, part (H))

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.injective_cohom.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.injective_cohomologyMap_gmSheaf_two.{u} (X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme)
  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsIntegral X] [AlgebraicGeometry.IsNoetherian X]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegular X] :
  Function.Injective ⇑(AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.cohomologyMap X.fromSpecFunctionField X.gmSheaf 2)
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.injective_cohom.doc:
**Grothendieck's residue injection for the Brauer group.** Let `X` be an integral regular
noetherian scheme with function field `k(X)`. Then the pullback along the generic point
`i : Spec k(X) ⟶ X`

```
   Spec k(X) ──── i ────▶ X            H²(X_ét, 𝔾ₘ)
                                            │ cohomologyMap i 𝔾ₘ 2
                                            ▼
                                       H²(Spec k(X)_ét, i^* 𝔾ₘ)
```

is injective, that is, `Br(X) = H²(X, 𝔾ₘ) ↪ H²(Spec k(X), 𝔾ₘ) = Br(k(X))`; the target is
identified with the cohomological Brauer group of `k(X)` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isIso_upperStarGmSheafToGmSheaf_fromSpecFunctionField`. In particular
this holds for a smooth curve.

The map factors as `H²(X, 𝔾ₘ) ⟶ H²(X, i_* i^* 𝔾ₘ) ⟶ H²(Spec k(X), i^* 𝔾ₘ)`, the unit of
`i^* ⊣ i_*` followed by the edge map of the Leray spectral sequence of `i`. The first map is
injective by the long exact cohomology sequence of the divisor sequence, since
`H¹(X, ⨁_x i_{x*} ℤ) = 0`; the second is injective since `R¹i_*(i^* 𝔾ₘ) = 0`.
(blueprint: `lem-sc-brauer-injectivity`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.initial_pointSm.doc:
**Base change along a closed immersion is initial on pointed étale neighbourhoods.** For
a closed immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` and a geometric point `s` of `Z`, every pointed étale
neighbourhood of `s` in `Z` is dominated by one of the form `V ×_X Z`, and two maps out of
such a `V ×_X Z` are equalised after shrinking `V`; the categories of pointed étale
neighbourhoods being cofiltered, this is initiality by
`CategoryTheory.Functor.initial_of_exists_of_isCofiltered`.

  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper (X ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.GlobalSectionsBijective k X] (ℒ : X.Modules) [ℒ.IsInvertible]
  (hd :
    2 * ↑(AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.arithmeticGenus k X) - 1 ≤
      AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.degree k ℒ) :
  ↑(AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.finrankH k ℒ 0) =
    AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.degree k ℒ + 1 -
      ↑(AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.arithmeticGenus k X)
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.finrankH_zero_e.doc:
**Riemann–Roch for curves, `h⁰` of a line bundle of large degree.** A line bundle `ℒ` of
degree `d ≥ 2g - 1` on a smooth proper curve with `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = k` of genus `g` has
`h^0(ℒ) = d + 1 - g`; equivalently `h^1(ℒ) = 0`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.finrankH_one_eq_zero_of_degree`).

(blueprint: `sk-thm-picard-rr`, `lem-sc-riemann-roch-large-degree`)

**Properties of the selected dense affine cover**: the selected family consists of affine
opens, covers `X`, and its total intersection is dense in `X`.
(blueprint: `lemma:nagata-dense-affine-cover`)

**The selected dense affine cover**: a chosen finite affine open cover of a quasi-compact
scheme `X` with finitely many irreducible components whose total intersection is dense, given
as the pair of its length and the family itself. Its defining properties are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.finiteAffineOpenCoverDenseIInter_spec`.
(blueprint: `def:nagata-dense-affine-cover`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_shortExa.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_shortExact_divisorSequence.{u} (X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme)
  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsIntegral X] [AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyNoetherian X]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegular X] (c : CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofan fun x => X.pointConstantInt ↑x)
  (hc : CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit c) :

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_shortExa.doc:
**The divisor sequence.** Let `X` be an integral regular locally noetherian scheme with
generic point `i : Spec k(X) ⟶ X`, and let `X⁽¹⁾` be its set of coheight-one points. Then
there is a divisor map `div` making

```
  0 ──▶ 𝔾ₘ ──unit──▶ i_* i^* 𝔾ₘ ──div──▶ ∐_{x ∈ X⁽¹⁾} i_{x*} ℤ ──▶ 0
```

a short exact sequence of étale sheaves on `X`, where the third term is the vertex of any
colimit cocone `c` on the family `x ↦ i_{x*} ℤ`. The first map is pinned down as the unit
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.toGenericGm`, which is the form the residue argument of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.injective_cohomologyMap_gmSheaf_two` uses; `div` itself is only
asserted to exist, see the TODO in the module docstring. The unit is a monomorphism by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.mono_toGenericGm`, and its cokernel is `c.pt` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.nonempty_cokernel_toGenericGm_iso`.
(blueprint: `lem-sc-divisor-sequence-general`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_isSepara.doc:
**A finite-presentation model of a separated morphism is separated at a later stage.**

If `X ⟶ lim Dⱼ` is separated and `p : Y ⟶ D_k` is a finite presentation model of it at the
stage `k`, then the base change of the model to some later stage `k' ⟶ k` is separated.
(Blueprint: `lemma:nagata-separated-descent-stage-exists`.)

**Separatedness descends to a finite stage.**

Let `{Dᵢ}` be a cofiltered inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes with affine
transition maps. If `lim Dᵢ` is separated, then `Dᵢ` is separated for every `i` past some stage.
(Blueprint: `lemma:nagata-fixed-base-separated-stage-exists`.)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_isSepara.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_isSeparated_app_of_isLimit.{u} {I : Type u}
  [CategoryTheory.Category.{u, u} I] {D : CategoryTheory.Functor I AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme}
  {c : CategoryTheory.Limits.Cone D} (hc : CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit c)
  [CategoryTheory.IsCofiltered I] [∀ {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j), AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineHom (D.map f)]

**Separatedness over a fixed base descends to a finite stage.**

Let `{Dᵢ}` be a cofiltered inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes over a base
`S`, with affine transition maps and quasi-compact structure morphisms. If `lim Dᵢ ⟶ S` is
separated, then `Dᵢ ⟶ S` is separated for every `i` past some stage.
(Blueprint: `lemma:nagata-fixed-base-separated-eventually`.)

**A separated morphism of finite presentation over the limit descends to a finite stage**
(Stacks 01ZQ).

Let `{Dⱼ}` be a cofiltered inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes with affine
transition maps and let `X` be separated and of finite presentation over `lim Dⱼ`. Then `X` is
the base change of a scheme that is separated and of finite presentation over one of the
stages. (Blueprint: `lemma:nagata-separated-eventually`.)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_isPullba.doc:
**Schemes of finite presentation over a cofiltered limit of quasi-compact quasi-separated
schemes descend to a finite stage** (Stacks Project Tag 01ZM). Let `{Dⱼ}` be a cofiltered
inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes with affine transition maps and let
`X` be of finite presentation over `lim Dⱼ`. Then `X` is the base change of a scheme `Y` of
finite presentation over one of the `Dⱼ`.

The affine case is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_isPullback_of_locallyOfFinitePresentation_of_isAffine`; the
general case follows by induction over a finite cover of `X` by affine opens each of which
lies over an affine open of a fixed stage, gluing the descended charts over a common stage.
(Blueprint: `lemma:nagata-finite-presentation-descends`.)

theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_isInvertible_twist.{u} {k : Type u} [Field k]

  [AlgebraicGeometry.SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper (X ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] (K : Type u)
  [Field K] [Algebra k K] [IsSepClosed k] [ConnectedSpace ↥X]
  (ℒ :
    (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback (X ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
        (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Algebra.algebraMap k K)))).Modules)
  [ℒ.IsInvertible] :
  ∃ ℒ₀,
    ℒ₀.IsInvertible ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.finrankH K
            (CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategoryStruct.tensorObj ℒ
              ((AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.pullback
                    (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.fst
                      (X ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
                      (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map
                        (CommRingCat.ofHom (Algebra.algebraMap k K))))).obj
                ℒ₀))
            0 =
          1 ∧
        AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.finrankH K
            (CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategoryStruct.tensorObj ℒ
              ((AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.pullback
                    (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.fst
                      (X ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k))

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_isInvert.doc:
**The twist lemma.** Let `k` be separably closed, let `X` be a smooth projective connected
curve over `k`, let `K/k` be a field extension and let `ℒ` be a line bundle on the base change
`X_K = X ×_{Spec k} Spec K`. Then there is a line bundle `ℒ₀` on `X` whose restriction to `X_K`
twists `ℒ` into the situation of `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.degree_eq_genus`:
`h^0(X_K, ℒ ⊗ ℒ₀|_{X_K}) = 1` and `h^1(X_K, ℒ ⊗ ℒ₀|_{X_K}) = 0`.

The proof has three steps. Step 1: a `k`-rational point `x` gives the line bundle `𝒪_X(x)` of
degree one. Step 2: by Riemann–Roch on the smooth proper curve `X_K`, which has
`H⁰(X_K, 𝒪) = K`, the twist `ℒ ⊗ 𝒪_X(n x)_K` has `h⁰ ≥ 1` and `h¹ = 0` once its degree is at
least `2g`. Step 3: remove `h⁰ - 1` rational points
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_isInvertible_twist_of_finrankH_zero_eq`).

(blueprint: `sk-thm-picard-twist`, `lem-pc-twist`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_isClosed.doc:
**A finitely presented morphism whose base change to the limit is a closed immersion is a
closed immersion at a finite stage.**

Let `γ` be a morphism of finite presentation between schemes over a stage `D_k`, with
quasi-compact quasi-separated target. If the base change of `γ` to the limit `lim Dⱼ` is a
closed immersion, then so is its base change to some stage `k' ⟶ k` and to every stage after
that. (Blueprint: `lemma:nagata-closed-immersion-stage-exists`.)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_finiteTy.doc:
**A quasi-compact open is the complement of the support of a finite-type ideal**
(Stacks Project Tag 01PH; blueprint: `lemma:nagata-qc-open-complement-ideal-exists`).

The ideal is the finite-type approximation of the vanishing ideal of the reduced
boundary, obtained by extending finitely generated pieces over a finite affine cover.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_equivale.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_equivalence_isFiniteLocallyConstantSheaf.{u}
  (Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme) [ConnectedSpace ↥Y] {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsSepClosed Ω]
  (s : AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of Ω) ⟶ Y) (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] [Finite Λ] :
  ∃ G e,
    Nonempty
      (e.functor.comp
          (Rep.IsFiniteContinuous.ι.comp
            (CategoryTheory.forget₂ (Rep.{u + 1, u + 1, u} Λ ↑G.toProfinite.toTop) (ModuleCat Λ))) ≅
        (CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.ι fun F =>
              AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IsFiniteLocallyConstantSheaf F).comp
          (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.pointSmallEtale s).sheafFiber)
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_equivale.doc:
Blueprint `sk-i-real-galois`: Galois correspondence for finite local systems.

Let `Y` be a connected scheme, `s : Spec Ω ⟶ Y` a geometric point and `Λ` a finite ring.
Then there is a profinite group `G` — the étale fundamental group `π₁(Y, s)`, a fundamental
group of `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.FiniteEtale.fiber s`, here existentially quantified as a
`ProfiniteGrp` — together with an equivalence between the category of finite locally
constant sheaves of `Λ`-modules on `Y_ét` and the category of finite `Λ`-modules with a
continuous `G`-action, compatible with the geometric stalk at `s`: the triangle

```
    FLC(Y_ét)  ──e.functor──▶  Rep^{fin,cont}_Λ(G)
         │                            │
         │ sheafFiber s               │ forget₂
         ▼                            ▼
     ModuleCat Λ  ══════════════  ModuleCat Λ
```

commutes up to isomorphism.

Exactness and compatibility with `⊗_Λ` are automatic consequences of the equivalence being
an equivalence of abelian (monoidal) categories; the compatibility with base change along a
map `Λ → Λ'` of finite rings is not restated here, see the module implementation notes and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_equivalence_isFiniteLocallyConstantSheaf_of_isFundamentalGroup`
for the version with `π₁(Y, s)` named.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_comp_eq_.doc:
Field-valued points lift along a surjective morphism which is surjective on stalks, for
instance along a surjective closed immersion.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.eulerChar_unit_.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.eulerChar_unit_eq.{u} {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme}
  [X.Over (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper (X ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.GlobalSectionsBijective k X] :
  AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.eulerChar k (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) =
    1 - ↑(AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.arithmeticGenus k X)
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.eulerChar_unit_.doc:
**Riemann–Roch for curves, structure sheaf.** `χ(𝒪_X) = 1 - g` on a smooth proper curve `X`
over `k` with `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = k`, of genus `g`: `χ(𝒪_X) = h⁰(𝒪_X) - h¹(𝒪_X)` with
`h⁰(𝒪_X) = 1`.

Without the hypothesis `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = k` the statement fails, as for `ℙ¹_ℂ` over `ℝ`, where
`χ(𝒪) = 2`.

(blueprint: `sk-thm-picard-rr`, `lem-sc-riemann-roch`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.eulerChar_free_.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.eulerChar_free_eq.{u} {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme}
  [X.Over (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper (X ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.GlobalSectionsBijective k X] (r : ℕ) :
  AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.eulerChar k (SheafOfModules.free (ULift.{u, 0} (Fin r))) =
    ↑r * (1 - ↑(AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.arithmeticGenus k X))
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.eulerChar_free_.doc:
**Riemann–Roch for curves, free case.** The Euler characteristic of the free sheaf of rank
`r` on a smooth proper curve `X` over `k` with `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = k`, of genus `g`, is
`χ(𝒪_X^{⊕ r}) = r (1 - g)`: cohomology commutes with finite direct sums
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.finrankH_of_isBilimit`).

Together with `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.degree`, which measures the degree of a
rank-`r` sheaf against `𝒪_X^{⊕ r}`, this is the content of the Riemann–Roch identity
`χ(ℱ) = deg ℱ + r (1 - g)`.

(blueprint: `sk-thm-picard-rr`, `lem-sc-riemann-roch`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.degree_eq_genus.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.degree_eq_genus.{u} {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme}
  [X.Over (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper (X ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] (K : Type u)
  [Field K] [Algebra k K] [AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.GlobalSectionsBijective k X]
  (ℒ :
    (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback (X ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
        (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Algebra.algebraMap k K)))).Modules)
  [ℒ.IsInvertible] (h0 : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.finrankH K ℒ 0 = 1)
  (hq : ∀ (q : ℕ), 0 < q → Subsingleton (ℒ.H q)) :
  AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.degree K ℒ = ↑(AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.arithmeticGenus k X)
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.degree_eq_genus.doc:
**The degree of the dictionary.** Let `X` be a smooth projective curve of genus `g` over
`k` with `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = k`, let `K/k` be a field extension and let `ℒ` be a line bundle on the
base change `X_K = X ×_{Spec k} Spec K` with `h^0(X_K, ℒ) = 1` and `H^q(X_K, ℒ) = 0` for
`q > 0`. Then `deg ℒ = χ(ℒ) - χ(𝒪_{X_K}) = 1 - (1 - g) = g`.

Of the hypothesis `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = k`, only `h⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = 1` is used, through
`χ(𝒪_{X_K}) = χ(𝒪_X) = h⁰(X, 𝒪_X) - g = 1 - g`. Without it the statement fails: for
`X = ℙ¹_ℂ` over `k = ℝ` and `K = ℂ`, the base change `X_ℂ` is two copies of `ℙ¹_ℂ`, so
`χ(𝒪_{X_ℂ}) = 2` rather than `1 - g = 1`, and the line bundle that is `𝒪(-1)` on one copy and
`𝒪` on the other has `χ(ℒ) = 1`, hence `deg ℒ = 1 - 2 = -1 ≠ g = 0`.

(blueprint: `sk-cor-picard-degree-g`)

The pullback of a stratification of `X` along `g : Y ⟶ X`: the strata are the preimages
of the strata, with the base changes of the immersions.
(blueprint: `lemma:constructible-pullback-stratification`)

Stratifications of the members of a complementary pair `(j, i)` concatenate to a
stratification of `X`: the strata are the images of the strata of `U` and of `Z`.

**Constructibility passes to refinements**: if the pullbacks of `F` to the strata of `S`
are finite locally constant and `T` refines `S`, the pullbacks of `F` to the strata of `T` are
finite locally constant. (blueprint: `lemma:constructible-of-refines`)

A stratification `T` *refines* a stratification `S` if every stratum of `T` is contained
in a stratum of `S`. (blueprint: `def:constructible-refines`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Stratification.doc:
A *stratification* of a scheme `X`: a stratification of the underlying topological
space of `X` (`Topology.Stratification`: a finite partition into locally closed subsets
following [Stacks 09XZ]) together with, for each stratum, a scheme immersed in `X` with
set-theoretic image the stratum. A sheaf on the small étale site of `X` is constructible
if its pullbacks to the strata of some stratification are finite locally constant, see
`IsConstructibleSheaf`.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic.doc:
The Picard group of a scheme `Y`: the set of isomorphism classes of invertible sheaves
of `𝒪_Y`-modules, realized as the invertible classes inside the skeleton of `Y.Modules`.

This lives in `Type (u + 1)` rather than `Type u`; see the implementation notes of this
module.

of the copy of `U` in `X*` is scheme-theoretically dominant.

The scheme-theoretic closure `X* ⟶ X` of an open `U ⊆ X` is an isomorphism over `U`.

The traces on `X*` of an open covering of `X` cover `X*`.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.NoetherianAppro.doc:
**Noetherian approximation of an affine scheme**: the spectra of the finitely
generated `ℤ`-subalgebras of `Γ(S, ⊤)` form a cofiltered system of schemes of finite type
over `ℤ` with affine transition maps whose limit is `S`. This is the affine case of Stacks
Project Tag 01ZA.

For `A ≤ B` the transition morphism `Spec ↥B ⟶ Spec ↥A` is `Spec.map` of the inclusion:

```
              S
    π.app B  ↙         ↘  π.app A
  Spec ↥B  ─────────⟶  Spec ↥A
```

A **Noetherian approximation** of a scheme `S`: a cofiltered system of schemes of finite
type over `ℤ` with affine transition morphisms, exhibiting `S` as the limit of the system.
The stages are automatically Noetherian, see
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.NoetherianApproximation.isNoetherian_obj`.

```
              S
    π.app i  ↙         ↘  π.app j
  D.obj i  ─────────⟶  D.obj j
                D.map f
```

By absolute Noetherian approximation (Stacks Project Tag 01ZA,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.nonempty_noetherianApproximation`), every quasi-compact
quasi-separated scheme admits one.
(Blueprint: `def:nagata-noetherian-inverse-system`.)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.upperSe.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.upperSemicontinuous_hFiber.{u} {X T : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme}
  (f : X ⟶ T) (ℱ : X.Modules) [AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper f]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact f]
  [CategoryTheory.HasInjectiveResolutions X.Modules] [SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation ℱ]
  (hℱ : ℱ.IsFlatOver f) (q : ℕ) : UpperSemicontinuous (ℱ.hFiber f q)
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.upperSe.doc:
**Semicontinuity of the fibre dimension.** With `f : X ⟶ T` proper of finite presentation
and `ℱ` an `𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation which is flat over `T`, the fibre dimension
`t ↦ dim_{κ(t)} H^q(X_t, ℱ_t)` is upper semicontinuous on `T`.

Locally on `T` the fibre dimension is `dim_{κ(t)} H^q(P ⊗ κ(t))` for the bounded complex `P` of
finite free modules of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.exists_isFiniteFreeComplex_higherDirectImage`: the pullback of
`P` to `Spec κ(t)` computes the higher direct images of the fibre `ℱ_t` to the point, whose global
sections are `H^q(X_t, ℱ_t)`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.hFiber_eq_finrank_sections_higherDirectImage`). The dimension
of the cohomology of a complex of finite free modules is upper semicontinuous in the point, by the
lower semicontinuity of the ranks of its differentials
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.exists_finrank_homology_pullback_le`).

(blueprint: `sk-thm-picard-semicon`, `thm-pc-semicontinuity-base-change`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.subsing.doc:
**Vanishing of cohomology on affine schemes.** Let `X = Spec A` be affine. For every
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `ℱ` and every `q > 0` we have `H^q(X, ℱ) = 0`; the vanishing of the
abelian group `ℱ.H (q + 1)` is expressed as it being a subsingleton.

This is the Čech criterion `TopCat.Sheaf.subsingleton_H_succ_of_exactAt_cechComplex` applied to the
affine opens and their standard coverings by basic opens, on which the Čech complex of `ℱ` is
exact in positive degrees by `exactAt_cechComplex_basicOpen`.

(blueprint: `sk-lem-picard-affine`, `lem-pc-affine-vanishing`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isZero_.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isZero_higherDirectImage_restrict.{u}
  {X T : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ T) (ℱ : X.Modules) [AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper f]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact f]
  [CategoryTheory.HasInjectiveResolutions X.Modules] [SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation ℱ]
  (hℱ : ℱ.IsFlatOver f) (i r : ℕ) (U : T.Opens)
  (hU : ↑U ⊆ {t | (∀ (q : ℕ), q ≠ i → ℱ.hFiber f q t = 0) ∧ ℱ.hFiber f i t = r}) (q : ℕ)
  (hq : q ≠ i) :
  CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero
    (((AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.higherDirectImage f q).obj ℱ).restrict U.ι)
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isZero_.doc:
**The higher direct images vanish off degree `i` over the perfect locus.** Over an open
subscheme `U` of `T` contained in the rank-`r` perfect locus `U_{i,r}`, the higher direct images
`R^q f_* ℱ|_U` vanish for `q ≠ i`. This is the case of the inclusion of `U` in
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isZero_higherDirectImage_of_isPullback`.

(blueprint: `sk-thm-picard-perfect`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isOpen_.doc:
**Openness of the bounded perfect locus.** With `f : X ⟶ T` proper of finite presentation and
`ℱ` an `𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation which is flat over `T`, the locus `U_{i,≤r}` of points
`t` of the perfect locus `U_i` at which `H^i(X_t, ℱ_t)` has dimension at most `r` is open in `T`.

Near a point `t`, the fibre cohomology vanishes in degrees `q > d`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.exists_forall_hFiber_eq_zero`), so there `U_{i,≤r}` is cut out
by the finitely many conditions `h^q < 1` for `q ≤ d`, `q ≠ i`, and `h^i < r + 1`, each of which is
open by upper semicontinuity (`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.upperSemicontinuous_hFiber`).

(blueprint: `sk-thm-picard-perfect`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isFinit.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isFinitePresentation_higherDirectImage.{u}
  {X T : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ T) (ℱ : X.Modules) [AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper f]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact f]
  [CategoryTheory.HasInjectiveResolutions X.Modules] [SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation ℱ]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyNoetherian T] [SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent ℱ] (q : ℕ) :
  SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation
    ((AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.higherDirectImage f q).obj ℱ)
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isFinit.doc:
**Coherence of the higher direct images over a locally Noetherian base.** With
`f : X ⟶ T` proper, `T` locally Noetherian and `ℱ` a coherent `𝒪_X`-module, the higher direct
image `R^q f_* ℱ` is a coherent `𝒪_T`-module for every `q` [EGA III₁, 3.2.1],
[Stacks, Tag 02O5]. Coherence is spelled as quasi-coherence together with finite presentation;
quasi-coherence of `R^q f_* ℱ` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isQuasicoherent_higherDirectImage`, so only finite
presentation is stated here.

The Noetherian hypothesis cannot be dropped, even for `ℱ` flat over `T`. Let `k` be a field,
`V` an infinite-dimensional `k`-vector space, `T = Spec (k ⊕ V)` with `V` a square-zero ideal,
`E` an elliptic curve over `k` and `f : E × T ⟶ T` the projection. Line bundles on `E × T`
which are trivial on `E` are classified by `H¹(E, 𝒪_E) ⊗_k V ≅ V`; let `ℒ` be the one with class
a nonzero `v ∈ V`. The sequence `0 ⟶ 𝒪_E ⊗_k V ⟶ ℒ ⟶ 𝒪_E ⟶ 0` has connecting map
`k ⟶ H¹(E, 𝒪_E) ⊗_k V` sending `1` to `v`, so `f_* ℒ` corresponds to the module `V`, which is
killed by `V` and infinite-dimensional over `k`, hence not of finite type over `k ⊕ V`.

(blueprint: `sk-thm-picard-coherence`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isFinit.doc:
**The `i`-th higher direct image is finite locally free over the perfect locus.** Over an
open subscheme `U` of `T` contained in the rank-`r` perfect locus `U_{i,r}`, the higher direct
image `R^i f_* ℱ|_U` is finite locally free of rank `r`. This is the case of the inclusion of
`U` in
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_higherDirectImage_of_isPullback`.

(blueprint: `sk-thm-picard-perfect`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.exists_.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.exists_subsingleton_H_tensor_twist.{u} {n : Type u}
  {X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (k : Type u) [Field k] [Finite n]
  (i : X ⟶ AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpace n (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion i] (F : X.Modules) [SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent F]
  [SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation F] :
  ∃ m₀,
    ∀ m ≥ m₀,
      ∀ (q : ℕ),
        0 < q →
          Subsingleton ((F.tensorObj (AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpace.twistRestrict i m)).H q)
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.exists_.doc:
**Serre's theorem B: vanishing after a twist.** Let `X ⊆ ℙᵈ_k` be a closed subscheme, i.e. a
closed immersion `i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; Spec k)`, and let `ℱ` be a coherent sheaf on `X`. Then
`H^q(X, ℱ ⊗ 𝒪_X(m)) = 0` for all `q > 0` and all `m ≫ 0`, where `𝒪_X(m)` is the pullback along
`i` of the twisting sheaf `𝒪(m)`.

Mathlib has no `IsCoherent` predicate, so "coherent" is spelled as
`SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation` together with `SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent`; on the
noetherian scheme `X` these two conditions together are coherence.

The pushforward `i_* ℱ` is coherent
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isFinitePresentation_pushforward_of_isClosedImmersion`), with
`i_* (ℱ ⊗ 𝒪_X(m)) ≅ (i_* ℱ)(m)` by the projection formula and
`H^q(X, ℱ ⊗ 𝒪_X(m)) ≅ H^q(ℙᵈ_k, i_* (ℱ ⊗ 𝒪_X(m)))` since a closed immersion is affine
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.nonempty_cohomologyFunctor_iso_pushforward_of_isAffineHom`),
so this is Serre vanishing on `ℙᵈ_k`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpace.exists_subsingleton_H_tensor_twist`, for `i_* ℱ`.

(blueprint: `sk-thm-picard-serre-b`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.exists_.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.exists_generatingSections_tensor_twist.{u} {n : Type u}
  {X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (k : Type u) [Field k] [Finite n]
  (i : X ⟶ AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpace n (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion i] (F : X.Modules) [SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent F]
  [SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation F] :
  ∃ m₀,
    ∀ m ≥ m₀,
      Nonempty
        (SheafOfModules.GeneratingSections
          (F.tensorObj (AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpace.twistRestrict i m)))
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.exists_.doc:
**Serre's theorem A: global generation after a twist.** Let `X ⊆ ℙᵈ_k` be a closed
subscheme, i.e. a closed immersion `i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; Spec k)`, and let `ℱ` be a coherent sheaf on
`X`. Then `ℱ ⊗ 𝒪_X(m)` is generated by its global sections for all `m ≫ 0`.

"Generated by its global sections" is `Nonempty (SheafOfModules.GeneratingSections _)`: the
sections `σ.s : σ.I → M.sections` of a `GeneratingSections` are by construction global
sections of `M`, and `σ.π : free σ.I ⟶ M` being an epimorphism is exactly the statement that
the map from the free module on those global sections is surjective as a map of sheaves.

As for theorem B, "coherent" is `SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation` together with
`SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent`.

The proof follows Hartshorne: `𝒢 = i_* ℱ` is coherent on `P = ℙ(n; Spec k)`, and is a
quotient `⊕ₐ 𝒪(-mₐ) ⟶ 𝒢` of a finite sum of twists (`ProjectiveSpace.exists_epi_sigma_twist`).
For `m ≥ max mₐ`, tensoring with the invertible module `𝒪(m)` gives a surjection
`⊕ₐ 𝒪(m - mₐ) ⟶ 𝒢(m)` from a sum of twists of non-negative degree, each generated by global
sections (`ProjectiveSpace.generatingSectionsTwist`). Finally `𝒢(m) ≅ i_* (ℱ(m))` by the
projection formula, and global generation descends along `i` because `i_*` is faithful
(`Scheme.Modules.GeneratingSections.ofPushforward`).

(blueprint: `sk-thm-picard-serre-a`, `thm-picard-serre-a`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.IsInver.doc:
An `𝒪_X`-module is *invertible* if every point has an open neighbourhood on which it
restricts to the structure sheaf.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocallyConstant.signature:
structure AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocallyConstantDatum.{u, u'} {X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} {A : Type u'}
  [CategoryTheory.Category.{u + 1, u'} A] [CategoryTheory.Abelian A]
  [CategoryTheory.IsGrothendieckAbelian.{u + 1, u + 1, u'} A]
  (F : CategoryTheory.Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology A) : Type (u + 1)
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocallyConstant.doc:
The datum of a trivialization of a sheaf `F` on the small étale site of `X`: an étale
cover of `X` — a jointly surjective family of étale maps, a cover in
`Scheme.etalePrecoverage` — such that the restriction of `F` to the site localized at
each member of the cover is constant in the sense of `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.IsConstant`.
`F` is locally constant if such a datum exists, see `IsLocallyConstantSheaf`.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalRepresenta.doc:
Suppose
* F is a `Type u`-valued sheaf on `Sch` with respect to the Zariski topology
* X : ι → Sch is a family of schemes
* f : Π i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ F is a family of relatively representable open immersions
* f is jointly surjective

Then `F` is representable.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IsTorsionSheafO.doc:
A sheaf `F` of `Λ`-modules on the small étale site of `T` is *torsion of orders
invertible on `S`*, for a second scheme `S`, if every element of every geometric stalk of
`F` is killed by a positive integer which is invertible on `S`, i.e. which is a unit of
`Γ(S, ⊤)`.

This strengthening of `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IsTorsionSheaf` is the coefficient
condition of the smooth base change theorem, where `T` lies over `S` along the morphism
`g : T ⟶ S` of the Cartesian square and the smooth morphism is the one with target `S`.
For `Λ = ℤ/nℤ` with `n` invertible on `S` every sheaf of `Λ`-modules satisfies it, and a
general such sheaf is the filtered union of its `n`-torsion subsheaves over the integers
`n` invertible on `S`.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IsQuasiAffine.o.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IsQuasiAffine.of_locallyQuasiFinite.{u} {X Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme}
  (f : X ⟶ Y) [Y.IsQuasiAffine] [AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyQuasiFinite f]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType f] [AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated f]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact f] : X.IsQuasiAffine
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IsQuasiAffine.o.doc:
If `f : X ⟶ Y` is separated, quasi-compact and locally quasi-finite of finite type and `Y` is
quasi-affine, then `X` is quasi-affine. Indeed, by Zariski's Main Theorem `f` factors as an open
immersion `X ⟶ f.normalization` followed by an affine morphism onto `Y`, so `f.normalization` is
quasi-affine, and `X` is a quasi-compact locally closed subscheme of it.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IsQcqsLocalProp.signature:
structure AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IsQcqsLocalProperty.{u} (T : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme)
  (P : ⦃T' : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme⦄ → (T' ⟶ T) → Prop) : Prop
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IsQcqsLocalProp.doc:
A property `P` of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes over a quasi-compact
quasi-separated base `T`, that is, a predicate on morphisms `T' ⟶ T` with `T'` qcqs, is
*qcqs-local* when it satisfies the three stability conditions of Stacks `0F06` and fails for
the empty scheme.

**Pullback of a locally constant sheaf is locally constant**: the pullback of a
trivialising cover is a trivialising cover.
(blueprint: `lemma:constructible-pullback-locally-constant`)

theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IsLocallyConstantSheaf.of_upperStar.{u, u'} {A : Type u'}

**Local constancy descends along a universal homeomorphism** `u : X ⟶ Y`: every member
`V' ⟶ X` of a trivialising cover of `u^* G` is the base change of an étale `V ⟶ Y`
(Stacks 04DZ), the `V` cover `Y` since `u` is surjective, and `V ×_Y X ⟶ V` is again a
universal homeomorphism, along which the constancy of the pullback of `G` to `V ×_Y X`
descends to `V`. (blueprint: `lemma:constructible-universal-homeomorphism-invariance`)

fibre product of trivialising covers. (blueprint: `lemma:constructible-flc-biproduct`)

A sheaf `F` on the small étale site of `X` is *locally constant* if there is an étale
cover of `X` trivializing `F`, i.e. a `LocallyConstantDatum`. Applies to sheaves of
abelian groups (`A = Ab.{u + 1}`), of `Λ`-modules (`A = ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ`), etc.

**Pullback of a finite sheaf is finite**: the stalks of `g^* F` are stalks of `F`.
(blueprint: `lemma:constructible-pullback-finite`)

The direct sum of two finite sheaves is finite: the stalk of `F ⊞ G` is the product of the
stalks. (blueprint: `lemma:constructible-flc-biproduct`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IsFiniteSheaf.doc:
A sheaf `F` on the small étale site of `X` with values in a concrete category is
*finite* if the stalk of `F` at every geometric point of `X` is finite. A geometric
point `Spec Ω ⟶ X`, with `Ω` a separably closed field, induces a point of the small
étale site (`Scheme.pointSmallEtale`), and the stalk of `F` is its fiber
`CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Point.sheafFiber` at this point.

**Generic constancy**: a constructible sheaf is finite locally constant on a dense open
subscheme, the union of the interiors of the strata of a witnessing stratification.
(blueprint: `prop:constructible-generic-constancy`)

**The cokernel of a morphism between constructible sheaves of modules is constructible.**
(blueprint: `thm:constructible-serre`)

A sheaf `F` on the small étale site of `X` with values in a concrete category is
*constructible* if there is a stratification of `X` such that the pullback of `F` to each
stratum is finite locally constant.

The stratification records a choice of scheme structure on each stratum via the immersion
`S.immersion i : S.domain i ⟶ X`; by topological invariance of the small étale site the
condition does not depend on this choice.

The left Kan extensions along base change needed by the pullback `Etale.upperStar` are
provided by the instance
`CategoryTheory.Functor.hasPointwiseLeftKanExtension_of_hasColimitsOfSize` of
`WeilConjectures.Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Functor.KanExtension.Pointwise`. Stating
`IsFiniteLocallyConstantSheaf` needs sheafification for the localizations of the small
étale sites of the strata; since the stratification is existentially quantified, this has
to be available for all schemes, which is what the hypothesis
`CategoryTheory.HasSmallSiteSheafify A` provides (see the module implementation notes).

For `X` quasi-compact and quasi-separated this global definition agrees with the
affine-local one of [Stacks 03RW]. In the `ℓ`-adic formalism it is applied with
`A = ModuleCat Λ` for the finite ring `Λ = ℤ/ℓⁿℤ`.

(blueprint: `def:nagata-global-blowup-overlap-basic-map`,
`lemma:nagata-global-blowup-overlap-basic`)

**Local properness of the global blow-up**: the blow-up map is proper over an affine
open on which the ideal is finitely generated.
(blueprint: `lemma:nagata-global-blowup-proper-local`)

**Properness of the global blow-up**: if the ideal is finitely generated on every affine
open, the blow-up map `Bl_I(X) ⟶ X` is proper.
(blueprint: `thm:nagata-global-blowup-proper`)

**A closed subscheme of a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme is the cofiltered limit of
the closed subschemes cut out by the subideal sheaves of finite type of its ideal sheaf.**
(Blueprint: `lemma:nagata-closed-subscheme-fp-system`.)

**The blow-up is an isomorphism away from the center**: the blow-up map is an
isomorphism over the complement of the support of the ideal.
(blueprint: `thm:nagata-global-blowup-complement`)

The blow-up map is an isomorphism over any affine open on which the ideal is the unit
ideal. (blueprint: `lemma:nagata-affine-blowup-complement`)

**Blowing up an already-invertible centre is an isomorphism.** If the quasi-coherent
ideal `I` is locally generated by a single non-zerodivisor, then the blow-up map
`Bl_I(X) ⟶ X` is an isomorphism. (blueprint: `cor:nagata-blowup-cartier-iso`)

`I`, the extended ideal `I · 𝒪_{Bl_I(X)}` is invertible: locally it is generated by a single
non-zerodivisor. (blueprint: `thm:nagata-blowup-principalizes-center`)

blow-up** (Stacks Project Tag 080E, closed-immersion half; blueprint:
`thm:nagata-strict-transform-is-blowup`): for `f : Y ⟶ X`, an ideal sheaf `I` on `X`
and a lift `ρ` of `(I.comap f).blowupMap ≫ f` along `I.blowupMap` — provided by the

`I.comap f` is the invertible exceptional ideal — the induced morphism

**The extended ideal on an affine chart.** If a morphism `Spec R ⟶ X` factors as `Spec ψ`
followed by the canonical morphism of an affine open `U`, then the pullback of an ideal sheaf
`J` along it is the extension of `J.ideal U` along `ψ`.

On an affine open disjoint from the support, the ideal is the unit ideal.
(blueprint: `lemma:nagata-ideal-unit-off-support`)

The chart embeddings of the affine opens of `X` cover the blow-up.
(blueprint: `prop:nagata-affine-blowup-chart-cover`, global form)

**Uniqueness of lifts along the blow-up map** (Stacks Project Tag 0806,
uniqueness): two morphisms to the blow-up of `I` over the same base morphism `t` with
`I.comap t` invertible agree.

subschemes cut out by the subideal sheaves of finite type of `I`.

**A finite-type ideal sheaf has a power inside any ideal sheaf whose support it
contains.** If `X` is quasi-compact, `B` is of finite type and `V(A) ⊆ V(B)`, then
`B ^ n ≤ A` for some `n`.

**The "for large `α`" step**: on a qcqs scheme, a finite-type quasi-coherent subsheaf of
an ideal sheaf `H` restricting to the unit ideal on a quasi-compact open `U` is contained in
a finite-type quasi-coherent subsheaf of `H` which still restricts to the unit ideal on `U`.
(Blueprint: `lemma:nagata-ideal-directed-union-finite-type`.)

form of a supremum over a directed set of ideal sheaves.

**Existence of lifts along the blow-up map** (Stacks Project Tag 0806, existence):
a morphism `t : T ⟶ X` with `I.comap t` invertible lifts to the blow-up of `I`.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData..doc:
**A finite-type ideal sheaf on a quasi-compact scheme is a compact element**
(blueprint: `lemma:nagata-finite-type-ideal-compact`).

Affine-locally this is the compactness of a finitely generated ideal in a directed supremum
of ideals; quasi-compactness of `X` provides a finite affine cover, and directedness picks
a common index above the finitely many local ones.

**Every section of an ideal sheaf on a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme lies in a
subideal sheaf of finite type.** (Blueprint: `lemma:nagata-closed-subscheme-fp-system`.)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData..signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.exists_finiteType_le_comap_eq.{u}
  {X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} [QuasiSeparatedSpace ↥X] [CompactSpace ↥X] (H₀ : X.IdealSheafData)
  (W : X.Opens) (hW : IsCompact ↑W) (hJ : H₀.ofFiniteTypeOn W) :
  ∃ I ≤ H₀, I.ofFiniteType ∧ I.comap W.ι = H₀.comap W.ι
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData..doc:
Existence of a finite-type ideal sheaf with prescribed restriction (Stacks Project
Tag 01PF, order-theoretic form): on a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme, every ideal
sheaf `H₀` whose restriction to a quasi-compact open `W` is of finite type contains a
finite-type ideal sheaf with the same restriction to `W`.
(Blueprint: `lemma:nagata-extend-finite-type-ideal`.)

**Gluing a finite-type centre across two overlapping quasi-compact opens** (Stacks
Project Tag 080M): let `A`, `B` be quasi-compact opens of a quasi-compact
quasi-separated scheme `X` and let `J` be a finite-type ideal sheaf on `A` whose
support avoids `B`. Then `J` extends to a finite-type ideal sheaf on `X` whose support
still avoids `B`.

Unlike `AlgebraicGeometry.IsAdmissible.exists_extend`, no containment between `A` and
`B` is assumed; this is what makes the extension usable when the open to be avoided is
not contained in the open carrying the centre. The extension is built in two steps:
the naive extension `J.map A.ι` already avoids `B`, because `B` is open and misses the
image of the support of `J`, and it is of finite type on `A ⊔ B` (equal to `J` on `A`
and to the unit ideal on `B`); the finite-type extension theorem (Stacks Project
Tag 01PF) then produces a finite-type ideal sheaf on all of `X` with the same
restriction to `A ⊔ B`.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData..signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.exists_finiteType_comap_eq.{u}
  {X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} [QuasiSeparatedSpace ↥X] [CompactSpace ↥X] (W : X.Opens)
  (hW : IsCompact ↑W) (J : (↑W).IdealSheafData) (hJ : J.ofFiniteType) :
  ∃ I, I.ofFiniteType ∧ I.comap W.ι = J
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData..doc:
Extension of a finite-type ideal sheaf from a quasi-compact open (Stacks Project
Tag 01PF): on a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme, every finite-type ideal sheaf on a
quasi-compact open extends to a finite-type ideal sheaf on the whole scheme.
(Blueprint: `lemma:nagata-extend-finite-type-ideal`.)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData..signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.exists_finiteDegree_center_le_blowup.{u}
  {X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} [CompactSpace ↥X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace ↥X] (I : X.IdealSheafData)
  (hI : I.ofFiniteType) (J : I.blowup.IdealSheafData) (hJ : J.ofFiniteType) :
  ∃ d L, 0 < d ∧ L.ofFiniteType ∧ L ≤ I ^ d ∧ L.comap I.blowupMap = I.comap I.blowupMap ^ d * J
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData..doc:
**Finite-degree approximation on the blow-up itself** (Stacks Project Tag 0803;
blueprint: `lemma:nagata-proj-closed-center-finite-degree-exists`).

The candidate for `L` at degree `d` is a finite-type subsheaf of
`(I^d) ⊓ ((I_E^d * J).map I.blowupMap)` through the finitely many chart numerators of
`AffineBlowup.exists_uniform_numerator_finset`, which generate `I_E^d · J` chart by
chart for `d` large.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData..signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.exists_finiteDegree_center.{u}
  {X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} [CompactSpace ↥X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace ↥X] (I : X.IdealSheafData)
  (hI : I.ofFiniteType) (J : I.blowup.IdealSheafData) (hJ : J.ofFiniteType) :
  ∃ d L,
    0 < d ∧
      L.ofFiniteType ∧
        L ≤ I ^ d ∧
          ↑L.support = ↑I.support ∪ ⇑I.blowupMap '' ↑J.support ∧
            L.comap I.blowupMap = I.comap I.blowupMap ^ d * J
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData..doc:
**Finite-degree descent of a second blow-up center** (Stacks Project Tag 0803
together with the support computation of the proof of Tag 080B; blueprint
`lemma:nagata-proj-closed-center-finite-degree-exists`,
`lemma:nagata-composition-center-ideal`): given a finite-type center `I` on a qcqs
scheme `X` with blow-up `π = I.blowupMap` and a finite-type center `J` on `I.blowup`,
there are a positive degree `d` and a finite-type ideal `L ≤ I ^ d` on `X` such that
the support of `L` is `supp I ∪ π(supp J)` and the inverse image ideal of `L` on the
blow-up is `I_E^d · J`.

This combines the finite-degree approximation `exists_finiteDegree_center_le_blowup`
(Tag 0803) with the support computation `coe_support_eq_of_comap_pow_mul`.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData..signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.exists_blowup_mul_iso.{u} {X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme}
  (I L : X.IdealSheafData) :
  ∃ e,
    CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp e.hom
        (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (L.comap I.blowupMap).blowupMap I.blowupMap) =
      (I * L).blowupMap
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData..doc:
**Blow-up of a product ideal** (Stacks Project Tag 080A; blueprint
`thm:nagata-blowup-product-ideal`, `cor:nagata-blowup-product-common-refinement`).

The proof follows the comparison strategy of `def:nagata-blowup-product-comparison`
and `thm:nagata-blowup-product-ideal` of the revised blueprint and runs entirely
through the universal property of blowing up
(`Scheme.IdealSheafData.exists_lift_blowup` and
`Scheme.IdealSheafData.hom_ext_of_isInvertible_comap`, Stacks Project Tag 0806): on the
iterated blow-up the pullback of `I * L` is invertible, giving `α`; on the blow-up of
`I * L` the pullbacks of `I` and of `L` are invertible by the factor lemma
(`IsInvertible.of_mul_left/right`), giving the lift `β` to `I.blowup` and then
`γ` to the iterated blow-up; the two composites are identities by the uniqueness of
lifts.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData..signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.exists_blowup_mul_isInvertible_iso.{u}
  {Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} {C : Y.IdealSheafData} (hC : C.IsInvertible)
  (M : Y.IdealSheafData) :
  ∃ e, CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp e.hom M.blowupMap = (C * M).blowupMap
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData..doc:
**Multiplying a center by an invertible ideal does not change the blow-up**
(consequence of Stacks Project Tags 0807 and 080A; blueprint
`lemma:nagata-blowup-invertible-factor`).

The proof runs through the universal property of blowing up
(`Scheme.IdealSheafData.exists_lift_blowup` and
`Scheme.IdealSheafData.hom_ext_of_isInvertible_comap`, Stacks Project Tag 0806): the
pullback of `C * M` to the blow-up of `M` is a product of invertible ideals,
giving a lift `α : M.blowup ⟶ (C * M).blowup`; conversely the pullback of `M` to the
blow-up of `C * M` is invertible by the factor lemma
(`IsInvertible.of_mul_right`), giving `β` in the other direction; the two
composites are identities by the uniqueness of lifts.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData..signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.exists_blowup_comp.{u} {X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme}
  [CompactSpace ↥X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace ↥X] (I : X.IdealSheafData) (hI : I.ofFiniteType)
  (J : I.blowup.IdealSheafData) (hJ : J.ofFiniteType) :
  ∃ K,
    K.ofFiniteType ∧
      ↑K.support = ↑I.support ∪ ⇑I.blowupMap '' ↑J.support ∧
        ∃ e,
          CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp e.hom
              (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp J.blowupMap I.blowupMap) =
            K.blowupMap
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData..doc:
**Composition of blow-ups** (Stacks Project Tag 080B), interface form; blueprint
`thm:nagata-composition-of-blowups`.

This is the base-change-free part of
`Scheme.IdealSheafData.exists_blowup_comp_base_change`, obtained by discarding its
final clause rather than by instantiating `f`: the composite center is
`K = I * L` with `L` the finite-degree descent of `J`
(`Scheme.IdealSheafData.exists_finiteDegree_center`, Stacks Tag 0803).

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData..signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.exists_blowup_comap_iso_strictTransform.{u}
  {X Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (I : X.IdealSheafData) (f : Y ⟶ X) :
  ∃ e,
    CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp e.hom
          (AlgebraicGeometry.strictTransformToSource f I.blowupMap I.support.compl) =
        (I.comap f).blowupMap ∧
      CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp
          (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp e.hom
            (AlgebraicGeometry.strictTransformMap f I.blowupMap I.support.compl))
          I.blowupMap =
        CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (I.comap f).blowupMap f
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData..doc:
**The strict transform is the blow-up of the pulled-back ideal** (Stacks Project
Tag 080E; blueprint: `thm:nagata-strict-transform-is-blowup`).

The finite-type quasi-coherent subsheaves of a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf are directed:
the family is closed under `⊔`.

Tag 080A).

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData..signature:

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData..doc: Products of invertible ideals are invertible.

The closed subscheme cut out by an invertible ideal is an effective Cartier centre. This
is the direction used in practice: an invertibility statement about an ideal upgrades for
free to a statement about the closed immersion it defines.
(blueprint: part of `lemma:nagata-invertible-ideal-effective-cartier`)

**The pullback of an invertible ideal along a blow-up map is invertible**: on the
`a`-chart of the blow-up, a local equation of the pulled-back ideal is the image of a
local equation downstairs, which stays a nonzerodivisor by
`AffineBlowup.awayAlgebraMap_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_mem`. The chart rings of the
blow-up are large `HomogeneousLocalization` types, whence the raised heartbeat
limit.

A quasi-coherent ideal is **invertible** if every point has an affine open neighbourhood
on which the ideal is generated by a single non-zerodivisor. Its vanishing locus is an
*effective Cartier divisor*.
(blueprint: `def:nagata-invertible-ideal-effective-cartier`, (MLCI0),
`def-sc-effective-cartier-divisor`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.zetaSeries_.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.zetaSeries_eq_tprod.{u} {X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} {k : Type u}
  [Field k] [Finite k] (f : X ⟶ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
  [AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact f] [AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType f] :
  AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.zetaSeries f =
    ∏' (x : ↑X.finitePoints), (1 - PowerSeries.X ^ AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.degreeOver f ↑x)⁻¹
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.zetaSeries_.doc:
**The Euler product expansion** of the zeta function of a scheme of finite type over
a finite field: `Z(X, t) = ∏ (1 - t ^ deg x)⁻¹`, the product running over the closed
points of `X` and converging coefficientwise.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.zetaSeries.signature:
def AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.zetaSeries.{u} {X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} {k : Type u} [Field k]
  (f : X.Hom (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) : PowerSeries ℚ
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.zetaSeries.doc:
The zeta function of a scheme `X` over a finite field `k` with `q` elements, given by
a structure morphism `f : X ⟶ Spec k`, as a formal power series:
`Z(X, t) = exp (∑ N_n * t ^ n / n)` where `N_n = #X(𝔽_(q ^ n))`.

It is related to the zeta function `ζ_X` of `X` as an abstract scheme by the formal
identity `ζ_X(s) = Z(X, q ^ (-s))`.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.pointCount_.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.pointCount_eq_sum.{u} {X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} {k : Type u}
  [Field k] [Finite k] (f : X.Hom (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
  [AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact f] [AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType f] {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0)
  {T : Finset ↑X.finitePoints} (hT : ∀ (x : ↑X.finitePoints), f.degreeOver ↑x ∣ n → x ∈ T) :
  f.pointCount n = ∑ x ∈ T with f.degreeOver ↑x ∣ n, f.degreeOver ↑x
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.pointCount_.doc:
**The point counting formula**: the number of points of a scheme `X` of finite type
over a finite field `k` which are rational over the degree `n` extension of `k` is
`∑ deg x`, the sum running over the (finitely many) points of `X` whose degree divides
`n`.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.pointCount.signature:
def AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.pointCount.{u} {X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} {k : Type u} [Field k]
  (f : X.Hom (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (n : ℕ) : ℕ
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.pointCount.doc:
`f.pointCount n` is the number `N_n` of points of `X` which are rational over the
degree `n` extension of `k`, with junk value `0` if this number is infinite.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.picZero.signature:
def AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.picZero.{u} {K : Type u} [Field K] {C : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme}
  (f : C ⟶ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) : Set C.Pic
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.picZero.doc:
Blueprint `sk-def-av-pic`: Pic, degree, Pic⁰

Let `C` be a smooth projective geometrically integral curve over a field `K`. Its Picard group
`Pic(C) = H¹(C_ét, 𝔾ₘ)` is the group of invertible `𝒪_C`-modules up to isomorphism; it is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic`. The degree homomorphism `deg : Pic(C) → ℤ` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.picDegree`, and `Pic⁰(C) := ker(deg)` is the subgroup of classes
of degree zero, recorded here as the subset `f.picZero` of `C.Pic`.

The degree is not yet a bundled group homomorphism: the group structure on
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic` is the tensor product `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.tensorObj`
of invertible modules, which is not yet defined on `Pic` because the tensor product of
invertible modules is not yet known to be invertible.

TODO: once it is, upgrade `picDegree` to a `MonoidHom` and `picZero` to its kernel, a subgroup
of `Pic(C)`.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.nonempty_fi.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.nonempty_finitePresentationApproximation.{u}
  {X S : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ S) [CompactSpace ↥X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace ↥X]
  [CompactSpace ↥S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace ↥S] [AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType f]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact f] :
  Nonempty (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.FinitePresentationApproximation f)
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.nonempty_fi.doc:
**The finite presentation model system of a morphism of finite type** (Stacks Project
Tag 09ZQ): a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme `X` that is locally of finite type over a
quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme `S` is the cofiltered limit of a system of schemes of
finite presentation over `S` whose transition morphisms and whose morphisms from `X` are all
closed immersions.

The system is that of the closed subschemes of a finite presentation model `Y` of `X` over `S`
cut out by the subideal sheaves of finite type of the kernel of the closed immersion `X ⟶ Y`.
(Blueprint: `lemma:nagata-finite-type-fp-model-system`.)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.nonempty_de.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.nonempty_deformationToNormalConeData.{u}
  {V B : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (d : ℕ) (g : V ⟶ B)
  [AlgebraicGeometry.SmoothOfRelativeDimension d g] (s : B ⟶ V)
  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion s]
  (hs : CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp s g = CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.id B)
  (N : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.NormalConeData d s) :
  Nonempty (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.DeformationToNormalConeData d g s N)
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.nonempty_de.doc:
Blueprint `sk-lem-geometry`: Geometry of the deformation of a section

**Existence of the deformation to the normal cone.** Let `g : V ⟶ B` be smooth of pure
relative dimension `d` with a closed section `s`, and let `N_s ⟶ B` be the normal cone of `s`
with its zero section. Then the deformation datum of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.DeformationToNormalConeData` exists: étale-locally there are
relative coordinates `x₁, …, x_d` on `V` in which `s` is `x_i = 0`, and on the deformation
chart `u_i = x_i / t` the deformation is `𝔸^d × 𝔸¹` over the base, which gives both the
smoothness of `g̃` and the two cartesian squares.

All of this commutes with base change in `B` and with étale localization.

def AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.maximalIsomorphismOpen.{u} {Z X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme}
  (q : Z ⟶ X) : X.Opens
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.maximalIsom.doc:
The **maximal isomorphism open** of a morphism `q : Z ⟶ X`: the union of all opens
`W ⊆ X` such that `q` restricts to an isomorphism over `W`.
(Blueprint: `def:nagata-maximal-isomorphism-open`.)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.ker_pullbac.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.ker_pullback_snd.{u} {T Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (g : T ⟶ Y)
  [AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact g] {Y' : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (q : Y' ⟶ Y)
  [AlgebraicGeometry.Flat q] :
  AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.ker (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.snd g q) =
    (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.ker g).comap q
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.ker_pullbac.doc:
Flat base change for scheme-theoretic images, in kernel ideal sheaf form: for a
quasi-compact morphism `g : T ⟶ Y` and a flat morphism `q : Y' ⟶ Y`, the kernel of the
base change `T ×_Y Y' ⟶ Y'` is the pullback of the kernel of `g`.
(blueprint: `lemma:nagata-scheme-image-flat-base-change`; Stacks Project Tag 081I. The
blueprint and the Stacks Project assume `g` quasi-separated as well, but Mathlib's
kernel ideal sheaf theory only needs quasi-compactness.)

theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.ker_morphismRestrict.{u} {T Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (g : T ⟶ Y)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.ker_morphis.doc:
Restriction of a scheme-theoretic image to an open subscheme of the target: the
kernel of `g ∣_ U` is the restriction of the kernel of `g`. This is the special case of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.ker_of_isPullback` for the open immersion `U.ι`, which is
flat. (blueprint: `lemma:nagata-scheme-image-restrict-open`)

theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.ker_lift_admissibleBlowup.{u} {S X Y V : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme}
  {x : X ⟶ S} {y : Y ⟶ S} {U : X.Opens} (B : AlgebraicGeometry.IsAdmissible X U)
  (h : V ⟶ CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback x y) [AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact h]
  (hfac :
    Set.range ⇑(CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp h (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.fst x y)) ⊆ ↑U)
  (h' : V ⟶ CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp B.I.blowupMap x) y)
  (hlift :
    CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp h'
        (AlgebraicGeometry.partialSectionOpenι x y B.I.blowupMap) =
      h)
  [AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact
      (AlgebraicGeometry.strictTransformOpen (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.imageι h)
          (AlgebraicGeometry.partialSectionOpenι x y B.I.blowupMap)
          ((TopologicalSpace.Opens.map (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.fst x y).base).obj
            B.preservedOpen)).ι] :
  AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.ker h' =
    AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.ker
      (AlgebraicGeometry.strictTransformMap (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.imageι h)
        (AlgebraicGeometry.partialSectionOpenι x y B.I.blowupMap)
        ((TopologicalSpace.Opens.map (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.fst x y).base).obj
          B.preservedOpen))
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.ker_lift_ad.doc:
**Scheme-theoretic images and admissible blow-ups** (Stacks Project Tag 0F3Y;
blueprint: `lemma:nagata-scheme-image-strict-transform`,
`lemma:nagata-scheme-image-transport-strict-transform`; proof order item 31).

Differences from the informal statement. The two closed subschemes of `X' ×_S Y` are
recorded by the kernels of the corresponding closed immersions, so the statement is in
kernel ideal sheaf form. The Stacks Project and the blueprint also assume `h`
quasi-separated; Mathlib's kernel ideal sheaf theory only needs quasi-compactness, so that
hypothesis is dropped here.

The right-hand side is a strict transform, so the theorem carries the standing
quasi-compactness assumption of `WeilConjectures.Compactification.StrictTransform`: the
inclusion of the open locus over the preserved open must be a quasi-compact morphism. It
is not implied by the remaining hypotheses — nothing here makes `U`, `B.preservedOpen` or
`X` quasi-compact — and is discharged from finiteness data by
`AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCompact_strictTransformOpen_ι_of_isCompact`. (The
specialization `AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCompact_strictTransformOpen_ι` does *not* apply:
it is stated for a blow-up map of an ideal sheaf, not for the base-changed blow-up
occurring here.)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isIso_restr.doc:
**The maximal isomorphism open is an isomorphism locus**: `q` restricts to an
isomorphism over `q.maximalIsomorphismOpen`. This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.restrict_maximalOpen` for the isomorphisms.
(Blueprint: `lemma:nagata-maximal-isomorphism-open`.)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isEquivalen.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isEquivalence_etale.{u} {X Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ Y)
  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsUniversalHomeomorphism f] :
  (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.Etale f).IsEquivalence
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isEquivalen.doc:
**Topological invariance of the small étale site**: base change along a universal
homeomorphism `f : X ⟶ Y` is an equivalence between the category of schemes étale over `Y`
and the category of schemes étale over `X`.

(blueprint: `lemma:weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-site-equivalence`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.image.signature:
def AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.image.{u} {X Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
  AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.image.doc: The scheme-theoretic image of a morphism.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.genus.signature:
def AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.genus.{u} {K : Type u} [Field K] {C : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme}
  (f : C ⟶ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) : ℕ
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.genus.doc:
Blueprint `sk-def-curve`: Curves and genus

The *genus* of a smooth proper connected curve `C` over `K` is
`g = dim_K H⁰(C, Ω¹_{C/K})`, the `K`-dimension of the space of global sections of the sheaf of
relative differentials. Since `C` is proper the global sections form a finite-dimensional
`K`-vector space; the `K`-module structure on `Γ(Ω¹_{C/K}, ⊤)` comes from the `Γ(C, ⊤)`-module
structure by restriction of scalars along the `K`-algebra structure of `Γ(C, ⊤)`.

This definition makes sense for an arbitrary morphism `f : C ⟶ Spec K`, but is only the genus
in the intended sense when `f` is a smooth proper connected curve.

For a smooth proper curve, Serre duality identifies this with the arithmetic genus
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.arithmeticGenus K C = dim_K H¹(C, 𝒪_C)`; see
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.genus_eq_arithmeticGenus`.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.functorPush.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.functorPushforward_mem_smallEtaleTopology_iff.{u}
  {X Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ Y) [AlgebraicGeometry.UniversallyInjective f]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.Surjective f] {U : Y.Etale} (S : CategoryTheory.Sieve U) :
  CategoryTheory.Sieve.functorPushforward (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.Etale f) S ∈
      X.smallEtaleTopology ((AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.Etale f).obj U) ↔
    S ∈ Y.smallEtaleTopology U
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.functorPush.doc:
**Covering compatibility for universal homeomorphisms**: a sieve on an étale `Y`-scheme
`U` is a covering for the small étale topology of `Y` if and only if its base change along
`f` is a covering for the small étale topology of `X`.

Equivalently, a family of étale morphisms to `U` is jointly surjective if and only if its
base change along `f` is: the projection `U ×_Y X ⟶ U` is a base change of `f`, hence
bijective on points, and it matches the images of the arrows of the sieve with the images of
their base changes.
(blueprint: `lemma:weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-coverings`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.finrankΓ.signature:
def AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.finrankΓ.{u} {Z : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} {R : CommRingCat}
  (h : Z ⟶ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec R) : ℕ
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.finrankΓ.doc:
The `R`-dimension of the ring of global sections of a scheme over `Spec R`.

For a finite group scheme `G` over a field `K` this is its *order* `|G| = dim_K Γ(G, 𝒪_G)`.

theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.exists_isOpenImmersion_isAffineHom_of_locallyQuasiFinite.{u}

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.exists_isOp.doc:
**Zariski's Main Theorem**, in factorization form: a separated, quasi-compact, locally
quasi-finite morphism of finite type factors as an open immersion followed by an affine
morphism. The factorization is through the relative normalization `f.normalization`.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.exists_isIm.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.exists_isImmersion_locallyOfFinitePresentation.{u}

  [CompactSpace ↥S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace ↥S] [AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType f]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact f] :
  ∃ Y p i,
    AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFinitePresentation p ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact p ∧
        AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiSeparated p ∧
          AlgebraicGeometry.IsImmersion i ∧ CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp i p = f
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.exists_isIm.doc:
**Immersion into a scheme of finite presentation** (Stacks Project Tag 01ZE): a
quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme `X` that is locally of finite type over a quasi-compact
quasi-separated scheme `S` admits an immersion over `S` into a scheme of finite presentation
over `S`. (Blueprint: `lemma:nagata-immersion-into-fp-model`.)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.exists_isCo.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.exists_isCompact_isClosedImmersion.{u} {X Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme}
  (f : X ⟶ Y) [AlgebraicGeometry.IsImmersion f] [CompactSpace ↥X] :
  ∃ W g,
    IsCompact ↑W ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion g ∧ CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp g W.ι = f
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.exists_isCo.doc:
**Shrinking an immersion to a closed immersion.** An immersion `f : X ⟶ Y` with `X`
quasi-compact factors as a closed immersion `g : X ⟶ W` into a quasi-compact open `W` of `Y`,
followed by the inclusion of `W`.

This is the shrinking step of [Stacks, Tag 01ZG](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01ZG);
no quasi-separatedness assumption on `Y` is needed.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.exists_isCl.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.exists_isClosedImmersion_locallyOfFinitePresentation.{u}

  [CompactSpace ↥S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace ↥S] [AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType f]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact f] :
  ∃ Y p i,
    AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFinitePresentation p ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact p ∧
        AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiSeparated p ∧
          AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion i ∧ CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp i p = f
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.exists_isCl.doc:
**Closed immersion into a scheme of finite presentation**: a quasi-compact quasi-separated
scheme `X` that is locally of finite type over a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme `S`
admits a closed immersion over `S` into a scheme of finite presentation over `S`.

This is Stacks Project Tag 01ZE followed by the shrinking step of Tag 01ZG.
(Blueprint: `lemma:nagata-finite-type-fp-model-system`.)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.exists_isCl.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.exists_isClosedImmersion_isSeparated_locallyOfFinitePresentation.{u}
  {X S : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ S) [CompactSpace ↥X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace ↥X]
  [CompactSpace ↥S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace ↥S] [AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType f]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact f] [AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated f] :
  ∃ X' i f',
    AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion i ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFinitePresentation f' ∧
        AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact f' ∧
          AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated f' ∧ CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp i f' = f
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.exists_isCl.doc:
**The separated finite presentation envelope of a morphism of finite type** (Stacks Project
Tag 01ZJ): a separated morphism `f : X ⟶ S` locally of finite type between quasi-compact
quasi-separated schemes factors as a closed immersion `i : X ⟶ X'` followed by a separated,
quasi-compact morphism `f' : X' ⟶ S` locally of finite presentation.

Take a finite presentation approximation of `f` (Stacks Project Tag 09ZQ) and descend the
separatedness of `f` to a stage of the system (Stacks Project Tag 01ZH); that stage is the
required envelope. (Blueprint: `prop:nagata-finite-type-closed-in-fp`.)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.exists_int_.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.exists_int_zetaSeries.{u} {X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} {k : Type u}
  [Field k] [Finite k] (f : X ⟶ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
