  ∃ Z, (PowerSeries.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ)) Z = AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.zetaSeries f
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.exists_int_.doc:
**The zeta series has integer coefficients**: the zeta series of a scheme of finite
type over a finite field is the image of a power series over `ℤ`.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.etaleEquiva.signature:
def AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.etaleEquivalence.{u} {X Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ Y)
  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsUniversalHomeomorphism f] : Y.Etale ≌ X.Etale
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.etaleEquiva.doc:
**Topological invariance of the small étale site**, [Stacks 04DZ]: for a universal
homeomorphism `f : X ⟶ Y`, the functor `V ↦ V ×_Y X` is an equivalence of categories
between schemes étale over `Y` and schemes étale over `X`.

This bundled form is what `CategoryTheory.Equivalence.sheafCongr` consumes, see
`AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.sheafEquivalence`.
(blueprint: `lemma:weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-site-equivalence`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.diagonal_fi.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.diagonal_finitePresentation.{u} {X S : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme}
  (f : X ⟶ S) [AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiSeparated f] :
  AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFinitePresentation (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.diagonal f) ∧
    AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.diagonal f) ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiSeparated (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.diagonal f)
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.diagonal_fi.doc:
**The diagonal of a morphism of finite presentation is of finite presentation.**

Mathlib has no bundled class for "of finite presentation"; a morphism is of finite presentation
if it is locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Note that `f` itself
need not be quasi-compact for this.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.denseRange_.doc:
**Zariski density of rational points.** Let `X` be a smooth scheme over a separably closed
field `k`, given by its structure morphism `f : X ⟶ Spec k`. Then the image in `X` of the set
`X(k)` of `k`-rational points is Zariski dense.

(blueprint: `sk-prop-picard-dense-points`, `lem-pc-rational-points-dense`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.degree_pull.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.degree_pullback.{u} {K : Type u} [Field K]
  {X Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} [AlgebraicGeometry.IsIntegral X] [AlgebraicGeometry.IsIntegral Y]
  (fX : X ⟶ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
  (fY : Y ⟶ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) [AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper fX]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper fY] (g : X ⟶ Y) (hg : CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp g fY = fX)
  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite g] [AlgebraicGeometry.Surjective g] (M : Y.Modules) [M.IsInvertible]
  (hample : AlgebraicGeometry.IsAmple fY M) :
  AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.degree fX ((AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj M) =
    ↑(AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.finrank g (genericPoint ↥Y)) *
      AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.degree fY M
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.degree_pull.doc:
Blueprint `sk-prop-av-deg-pullback`: Degree of a pullback under a finite morphism.

Let `g : X ⟶ Y` be a finite surjective morphism of proper `K`-varieties of the same dimension,
let `M` be an ample invertible `𝒪_Y`-module and let `d = [k(X) : k(Y)]` be the degree of `g`.
Then `deg_{g^*M}(X) = d * deg_M(Y)`.

This is also blueprint `lem-sc-deg-pullback-finite` (Stacks 0BEX). Both sides are `g`-th forward
differences at `0`, where `dim X = dim Y` since `g` is finite surjective
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.topologicalKrullDim_eq_of_surjective`). By the projection formula
`χ(X, (g^* M)^{⊗ m}) = χ(X, g^* M^{⊗ m}) = χ(Y, g_* g^* M^{⊗ m}) = χ(Y, g_* 𝒪_X ⊗ M^{⊗ m})`, and
`g_* 𝒪_X` is a coherent module of generic rank `d`, so the leading coefficients compare by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.fwdDiff_iter_eulerChar_tensorObj_tensorPow`.

```
  X ────────── g ─────────▶ Y
    ╲                       │
     ╲  fX                  │ fY
      ╲                     ▼
       ╲───────────▶ Spec K
```

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.degree_pos_.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.degree_pos_of_isAmple.{u} {K : Type u} [Field K]
  {X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} [IsAlgClosed K] (f : X ⟶ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper f] (hdim : topologicalKrullDim ↥X = 1) (L : X.Modules)
  [L.IsInvertible] (hample : AlgebraicGeometry.IsAmple f L) :
  0 < AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.degree f L
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.degree_pos_.doc:
Blueprint `sk-prop-av-ample-positive`: Ample modules on proper curves have positive degree.

Let `K` be algebraically closed, `C` a proper curve over `K` of dimension one (possibly
disconnected) and `L` an ample invertible `𝒪_C`-module. Then `deg L > 0`.

This is also blueprint `lem-sc-ample-positive-degree`. The proof decomposes `C` into its
finitely many connected components `C_i`, which are open and closed. The degree is additive
over them (`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.degree_eq_sum_of_pairwise_disjoint`); a component
of dimension `0` is a single point, so contributes `0`; a component of dimension `1` contributes
a positive degree by the connected case
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.degree_pos_of_isAmple_of_connectedSpace`, since `L|_{C_i}` is
ample (`AlgebraicGeometry.IsAmple.pullback`). If all components had dimension `0`,
`C` would be discrete, so at least one has dimension `1`.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.degreeOver.signature:
def AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.degreeOver.{u} {X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} {k : Type u} [Field k]
  (f : X.Hom (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (x : ↥X) : ℕ
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.degreeOver.doc:
The degree `[κ(x) : k]` of a point `x` of a scheme `X` over a field `k`, with junk
value `0` if the residue field extension is infinite.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.degree.signature:
def AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.degree.{u} {K : Type u} [Field K] {X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme}
  (f : X ⟶ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) (M : X.Modules) : ℤ
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.degree.doc:
Blueprint `sk-def-av-ample-degree`: Ample modules and the Hilbert degree.

The degree of a `K`-scheme `X` of dimension `g` with respect to an `𝒪_X`-module `M`: the `g`-th
forward difference at `0` of the Hilbert function `m ↦ χ(X, M^{⊗ m})`. When the Hilbert
function is a numerical polynomial of degree at most `g`, as it is for `X` proper and `M` ample
invertible, this equals `g!` times its coefficient of `m^g`. Here `g` is the topological Krull
dimension of `X`, read as `0` if `X` is empty or infinite-dimensional.

The value is meaningful only for `f` proper and `M` coherent: otherwise the Euler
characteristics involved may be junk values.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.abs_pointCo.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.abs_pointCount_one_sub_le.{u} {k : Type u} [Field k] [Finite k]
  {X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (f : X.Hom (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) {q d : ℕ}
  (hq : q = Nat.card k) (hd : 1 ≤ d) {P : Fin (2 * d + 1) → Polynomial ℤ}
  (hfact : AlgebraicGeometry.IsWeilFactorization q d f.zetaSeries P)
  (hrh : AlgebraicGeometry.WeilRiemannHypothesis q d P) :
  |↑(f.pointCount 1) - (↑q ^ d + 1)| ≤
    ∑ i with 0 < ↑i ∧ ↑i < 2 * d, ↑(P i).natDegree * ↑q ^ (↑↑i / 2)
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.abs_pointCo.doc:
**The Hasse–Weil bound.** If the zeta function of `X` has integral Frobenius factors `P i`
satisfying the Riemann hypothesis, then the number `N₁` of `k`-rational points of `X` differs
from `qᵈ + 1` by at most `∑_{0 < i < 2d} deg (P i) · q^{i/2}`.
(blueprint: `sk-cor-hasse`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.X_mul_deriv.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.X_mul_derivative_zetaSeries.{u} {X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme}
  {k : Type u} [Field k] (f : X ⟶ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :
  PowerSeries.X * (PowerSeries.derivative ℚ) (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.zetaSeries f) =
    (PowerSeries.mk fun n => if n = 0 then 0 else ↑(AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.pointCount f n)) *
      AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.zetaSeries f
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.X_mul_deriv.doc:
The logarithmic derivative of the zeta function of `X` over `k` is the generating
function of the point counts of `X`: `t * Z'(X, t) = (∑ N_n * t ^ n) * Z(X, t)`.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.NormalConeD.signature:
structure AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.NormalConeData.{u} {X Z : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (c : ℕ)
  (i : Z ⟶ X) : Type (u + 1)
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.NormalConeD.doc:
The normal cone `N_{Z/X} = Spec_Z (⨁_{r ≥ 0} I^r/I^{r+1})` of a regular closed immersion
`i : Z ⟶ X` of pure codimension `c`, as data: the scheme `N`, its projection to `Z`, its zero
section, and the two properties the purity chapter uses — that the zero section really is a
closed section, and that `N ⟶ Z` is a vector bundle of rank `c`, of which only smoothness of
relative dimension `c` is expressible in the pinned Mathlib.

Mathlib has no relative `Spec` of a quasi-coherent graded `𝒪_Z`-algebra, so this datum cannot
yet be constructed; it is taken as a hypothesis wherever a normal cone is needed.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.GeometricFi.signature:
def AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.GeometricFiber.{u} {X Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ Y)
  {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] (y : AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of Ω) ⟶ Y) : Type u
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.GeometricFi.doc:
The geometric fibre of `f : X ⟶ Y` over the geometric point `y : Spec Ω ⟶ Y`: the geometric
points `x : Spec Ω ⟶ X` with `x ≫ f = y`. This is a reducible definition so that the
coercion `t.1` is transparent to tactics.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.FinitePrese.signature:
structure AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.FinitePresentationApproximation.{u} {X S : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme}
  (f : X ⟶ S) : Type (u + 1)
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.FinitePrese.doc:
A **finite presentation approximation** of a morphism `f : X ⟶ S` is a cofiltered system
`D` of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes of finite presentation over `S`, whose transition
morphisms are closed immersions, together with a limit cone with point `X` whose projections
are closed immersions compatible with `f`:

```
              X
    π.app i  ↙    ↓    ↘  π.app j
  D.obj i  ────────────⟶  D.obj j
                D.map g            ↘ p.app j
                                       S
```

Every morphism locally of finite type between quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes admits one
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.nonempty_finitePresentationApproximation`, Stacks Project
Tag 09ZQ). (Blueprint: `def:nagata-finite-type-fp-model-system`.)

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.Deformation.doc:
Blueprint `sk-lem-geometry`: Geometry of the deformation of a section

The deformation to the normal cone of a closed section `s` of a morphism `g : V ⟶ B` smooth of
pure relative dimension `d`, as data. Writing `𝔸¹_B = 𝔸(Fin 1; B)` with its zero and unit
sections `i₀`, `i₁`, the datum consists of the deformation space `𝒟_s V`, a morphism
`g̃ : 𝒟_s V ⟶ 𝔸¹_B` again smooth of relative dimension `d`, a section `s̃` of `g̃`, and the
identification of the two fibres:

```
  V ---ι₁---> 𝒟_s V <---ι₀--- N_s          B ---s---> V
  |             |              |           |          |
  g             g̃             π_N          ‖          g
  v             v              v           v          v
  B ---i₁---> 𝔸¹_B <---i₀---- B           B ---𝟙----> B
```

both squares cartesian, with `ι₁` carrying `s` to `s̃` and `ι₀` carrying `0_N` to `s̃`.

Mathlib has neither the relative `Spec` of the extended Rees algebra nor a blow-up along an
arbitrary closed subscheme, so the datum cannot be constructed here; existence is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.nonempty_deformationToNormalConeData`.

theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.EtaleTorsor.exists_quotientEquivSheafH.{u} (M : Type (u + 1))

  ∃ c,

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.EtaleTorsor.exi.doc:
Blueprint `sk-prop-input-torsors`: Torsors and étale H^1

For a scheme `Y` and a finite abelian group `M` the isomorphism classes of `M`-torsors on
the small étale site of `Y` are in canonical bijection with the first sheaf cohomology
group `H^1(Y_ét, M)` of the constant sheaf with value `M`, under which the class of a
torsor vanishes exactly when its structure morphism admits a section, that is, exactly
when the torsor is trivial.

An `M`-torsor is, by `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.EtaleTorsor`, the same thing as a finite
étale surjective `Y`-scheme with a simply transitive `M`-action; the naturality of the
bijection in `(Y, M)` and the connectedness criterion of the sketch are not part of this
statement, see the implementation notes of this file.

The proof combines the classification of torsors under an abelian sheaf by `H¹`
(`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.Torsor.exists_quotientEquiv_H_one`, blueprint `thm-galois-torsor-h1`)
with the comparison of étale torsors and sheaf torsors
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.EtaleTorsor.exists_sheafTorsor`, blueprint `sbc-prop-torsors-h1`).

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.EtaleTorsor.exi.doc:
Blueprint `sk-prop-input-spreading`: Spreading a finite étale Galois cover

Let `S` be a qcqs integral normal scheme with generic point `η` and function field
`κ(η) = S.functionField`, let `c : C ⟶ S` be a qcqs smooth morphism with geometrically
connected fibres, and let `σ` be a section of `c`. Let `M` be a finite abelian group whose
order is invertible on `S`, let `Cη` be the generic fibre of `c`, that is, the left column of
the cartesian square

```
Cη ---j---> C
|           |
q           c
v           v
Spec κ(η) -> S
```

and let `Z` be an `M`-torsor on `Cη` — a finite étale Galois cover of `Cη` with group `M` —
carrying a `κ(η)`-rational point above the generic point `sη` of the section. Then `Z`
extends to an `M`-torsor on `C`: there is an `M`-torsor `T` on `C` and an `M`-equivariant
morphism `ψ : Z.P ⟶ T.P` making the square

```
Z.P --ψ--> T.P
 |          |
Z.π        T.π
 v          v
 Cη --j---> C
```

cartesian, so that the restriction of `T` to the generic fibre is `Z`.

This is [Stacks 0EZJ]: it is the case `G = Multiplicative M` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.GaloisCover.exists_isPullback_of_genericFibre`.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.EtaleTorsor.signature:
structure AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.EtaleTorsor.{u} (M : Type (u + 1)) [AddCommGroup M] [Finite M]
  (Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme) : Type (u + 1)
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.EtaleTorsor.doc:
An `M`-torsor over a scheme `Y`: a finite étale surjective `Y`-scheme with a simply
transitive action of the finite abelian group `M`.

Simple transitivity is expressed by the isomorphism `M × P ≅ P ×_Y P`, in the form that the
morphism `∐_{m ∈ M} P ⟶ P ×_Y P` whose `m`-th component is `(m +ᵥ -, id)` is an isomorphism:

```
∐_{m ∈ M} P --≅--> P ×_Y P --pr₁--> P
                                    |
                                    π
                                    v
                                    Y
```

The coproduct exists because `M` is finite, hence small.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Etale.overEquiv.signature:
def AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Etale.overEquiv.{u} {X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (U : X.Etale) :

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Etale.overEquiv.doc: **The small étale site of `X` localized at `U` is the small étale site of `U.left`.**

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CohomologicalPi.doc:
The *cohomological Picard group* `H¹(X_ét, 𝔾ₘ)` of a scheme.

It is called cohomological because the Picard group proper, the group of invertible
`𝒪_X`-modules up to isomorphism, is a different definition; that the two are in bijection is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.nonempty_equiv_cohomologicalPicardGroup`
(blueprint: `lem-sc-h1-gm-pic`), and the invertible-module definition together with the degree
homomorphism and `Pic⁰` belong to the blueprint block `sk-def-av-pic`. Its vanishing for the
spectrum of a field (Hilbert 90) is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.subsingleton_cohomologicalPicardGroup_of_field`, in
`WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.Hilbert90`.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CohomologicalBr.doc:
The *cohomological Brauer group* `H²(X_ét, 𝔾ₘ)` of a scheme.

It is called cohomological because the Brauer group proper, the group of Azumaya algebras up
to Morita equivalence — Mathlib's `BrauerGroup K` for a field `K` — is a different definition;
the two agree for a quasi-compact separated scheme with an ample family of line bundles
(Gabber), which is not stated here.
(blueprint: `def-br`)

structure AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiDomination.{u} {S X Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (x : X ⟶ S) (y : Y ⟶ S)

AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiDomination.doc:
Blueprint `sk-def-nagata-sketch-quasidomination`: Quasi-domination.

A quasi-domination of `x : X ⟶ S` over a separated `y : Y ⟶ S` is a morphism `hom : U ⟶ Y`
over `S`, defined on a dense open `U ⊆ X`, whose graph `U ⟶ Y ×ₛ X` has closed range.

```text
    U ──hom──→ Y
    │          │
U.ι │          │ y
    ↓          ↓
    X ───x───→ S
```

The graph is the morphism `U ⟶ Y ×ₛ X` induced by this square, and the condition is that
its range be closed.

AlgebraicGeometry.ProperClosedModel.doc:
A **proper closed model** of `g : V ⟶ S`: a closed subscheme `Z` of a projective space
`ℙ(n; S)` with `n` finite, in which `V` sits as a scheme-theoretically dense open subscheme,
compatibly with `g`.

Since a closed immersion is proper and `ℙ(n; S)` is proper over `S` for finite `n`, the
structure morphism `Z ⟶ S` is proper; see the `IsProper` instance below.

AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpace.isPull.doc:
**Projective space commutes with base change**: for a morphism `g : X ⟶ S`, the square

```
            map n g
  ℙ(n; X) ----------> ℙ(n; S)
     |                   |
     | ↘                 | ↘
     ↓                   ↓
     X ------- g ------> S
```

is cartesian, i.e. `ℙ(n; X)` is the base change of `ℙ(n; S)` along `g`. Indeed, both squares in

```
            map n g          toProjInt n S
  ℙ(n; X) ----------> ℙ(n; S) -------------> ℙⁿ_ℤ
     |                   |                     |
     | ↘                 | ↘                   |
     ↓                   ↓                     ↓
     X ------- g ------> S --------------> Spec ℤ
```

are cartesian, and so is the outer rectangle.
(blueprint: `lemma:nagata-projective-space-base-change-pullback`)

Compact trace additivity: for a closed immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` and its open complement
`j : U ⟶ X`, the Frobenius coefficient morphisms induced on the functorial compact
localization triangle satisfy

`tr_A(F_{c,m}, RΓ_c(X, K)) = tr_A(F_{c,m}, RΓ_c(U, j^* K)) + tr_A(F_{c,m}, RΓ_c(Z, i^* K))`.

Invertibility of the coefficient morphism is unnecessary, so the statement is for plain
`WeilComplex`es (blueprint: `sk-i-global-additivity`).

**The finite-coefficient Lefschetz trace formula.** For every Weil datum on the
geometric base change `X = X₀ ×_{𝐅_q} Ω` of a separated finite type `X₀/𝐅_q`, `Ω`
algebraically closed, whose Frobenius is the base change of the `q`-power Frobenius of `X₀`,
and every `m ≥ 1`,

`tr_A(F_{c,m} ∣ RΓ_c(X, K)) = ∑_{x ∈ X₀(𝐅_{q^m})} tr_A(F_{x,m} ∣ K_x̄)`,

the sum running over the sections `x` of `a_X` fixed by `Φ_m`
(blueprint: `sk-thm-trace-formula`).

AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.relativeFrobe.doc:
The *relative Frobenius* `r_m = (f, Φ_{X,m}) : X ⟶ X'_m` of a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y`
compatible with Frobenius morphisms `Φ_X`, `Φ_Y`, where `X'_m = Y ×_{Φ_Y, Y, f} X`:

```
   X'_m ──f'_m──→ Y           r_m ≫ p_m = Φ_X
     │            │           r_m ≫ f'_m = f
  p_m│            │Φ_Y
     ↓            ↓
     X ────f────→ Y
```

Here `X'_m` is `CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback Φ_Y f`, with `f'_m = pullback.fst` and
`p_m = pullback.snd` (blueprint: `sk-d-relative-frob`).

Blueprint `sk-prop-sf-comparison`: The pro-étale comparison

**The comparison direct image.** For `u : U ⟶ V` quasi-compact and quasi-separated the
comparison commutes with direct images:

```
  D⁺(U_ét) --R u_{ét,*}--> D⁺(V_ét)
      |                        |
   ν_U^*                    ν_V^*
      |                        |
      v                        v
  D⁺(U_proét) -R u_{proét,*}-> D⁺(V_proét)
```

commutes up to isomorphism, `ν_V^* ∘ R u_{ét,*} ≅ R u_{proét,*} ∘ ν_U^*`. Exactness of `ν^*`,
which is what allows it to be applied degreewise to complexes, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.preservesFiniteLimits_comparisonUpperStar`.

AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.isZero_homolo.doc:
Blueprint `sk-prop-sf-fullcd-etale-origin`: `FullCD` on the étale-origin class

**The cohomological-dimension bound on the étale-origin class.** Let `k` be separably closed,
let `p : X' ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism of finite-type `k`-schemes with `dim X' ≤ d`, and let
`Λ` be a finite coefficient ring whose exponent is invertible on `X'` — so that every sheaf of
`Λ`-modules is torsion, which is the first line of the blueprint proof. Then for every étale
sheaf `F` of `Λ`-modules on any base change `X''` of `X'`,

`H^r(Rp'_{proét,*} ν_{X''}^* F) = 0` for `r > 2d`.

Quantifying over the base changes is what turns the statement into the bound
`HasUniformCohomologicalDimensionLE` restricted to the essential image of `ν^*`. This is *not*
clause (1) of `HasAmbientExceptionalRightAdjoint`, which quantifies over all pro-étale sheaves
and fails in general (see `sk-rem-sf-fullcd-scope` and the module docstring); what it supports
is the constructible `Rf^!` on the étale-origin class.

compactly supported cohomology over a field `Λ` of characteristic zero,

A *Weil complex* on a geometric scheme `a_X : X ⟶ s`: a geometric `q`-power Frobenius
`Φ₁ : X ⟶ X` over `s`, a complex `K` and a *Frobenius coefficient morphism*
`φ : Φ₁^* K ⟶ K`. A *Weil datum* in the strict sense of the blueprint is a `WeilComplex`
with `IsIso W.coeff` (blueprint: `sk-d-weil`).

AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.ProperPushfor.doc:
A *proper pushforward diagram* on an endocorrespondence `(C, c, u)` on `(X, K)`: a
geometric scheme `a_Y : Y ⟶ s`, a proper morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` over `s`, a
correspondence-shaped target `b = (b₁, b₂) : D ⟶ Y × Y` over `s`, and a morphism
`g : C ⟶ D` of supports with `bᵢ ∘ g = f ∘ cᵢ`:

```
        c₁         c₂
    X ←──── C ────→ X
    │       │       │
   f│      g│       │f
    ↓       ↓       ↓
    Y ←──── D ────→ Y
        b₁         b₂
```

The morphism `g` is proper, as the blueprint requires, and `g ≫ b₁` admits a
compactification. No Cartesian condition on either leg square is imposed, and nothing is
assumed proper over `s` (blueprint: `sk-d-proper-pushforward`).

AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.HasUniformCoh.doc:
Blueprint `sk-def-sf-admissible`: the bound `FullCD(p, A; c)`.

`p : X ⟶ Y` *has uniform cohomological dimension at most `c` at `A`* if the higher direct
images of `p`, and of all its base changes along objects of `Y_proét`, vanish above `c` on
*every* pro-étale sheaf of `A`-modules:

```
  X' --g'--> X
  |          |          R^r p'_* F = 0 for r > c, all F on X'_proét
  p'         p
  |          |
  v          v
  V.left --V.hom--> Y        V an object of Y_proét
```

This is the uniform bound that makes `Rp_*` preserve coproducts on the unbounded derived
category. The base changes are taken along the pro-étale site of `Y`, as in the blueprint, and
not along arbitrary morphisms of schemes: the latter is a strictly stronger hypothesis than
`sk-prop-sf-fullcd-etale-origin` can deliver.

Not satisfied in general, even for proper smooth `p`; see `sk-rem-sf-fullcd-scope` and the
module docstring.

categorical trace of the global operator `T_c(u)` on compactly supported cohomology

and `g = a_C = a_X ∘ c₂`, followed by the point normalisation of blueprint `sk-p-pairing`

Localization trace additivity: for a closed immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` and the complementary
open immersion `j : U ⟶ X`, both stable under `Φ_m`, the three coefficient morphisms `φ_m`,
`u^Z` and `u^U` form a morphism of the distinguished triangle of the open-closed
decomposition, compatibly with `Lc₂^*` and `Rc₁^!`, so triangle compatibility of the Verdier
trace class gives

`Tr_{(1, Φ_m)}(φ_m) = Tr_{(1, Φ_m)}(u^Z) + Tr_{(1, Φ_m)}(u^U)`

and `Φ_U` of `Φ_m` are data because the project cannot construct restrictions of `Φ_m` to
a closed or open subscheme (blueprint: `sk-i-additivity`).

The *trace class* `Tr_c(u) : A_F ⟶ ω_F` of an endocorrespondence `(C, c, u)` on
`(X, K)`, a Borel-Moore section on the fixed scheme `F = Fix(c)`: the contraction
`GeometricOperations.pairingOfSquare` of the supported class of `u` against the supported
class of the diagonal identity `1_K`, over the Cartesian square `F = C ×_{X × X} X` of
`Correspondence.isPullback_fixι_toProd` (blueprint: `sk-d-trace-class`). It is the
construction of the Lefschetz-Verdier pairing `⟨u, 1_K⟩_LV` with the fixed scheme `F` in
place of the intersection `E(C, X)`; the comparison with `supportedPairing` along
`F ≅ E(C, X)` is not formalised.

The *Lefschetz-Verdier pairing* of an opposite pair of correspondences: the inverse
Künneth-Verdier maps turn the supported classes of `u` and `v` into

`ũ : Rc_! A_C ⟶ L ⊠ D_X K` and `ṽ : Rd̄_! A_D ⟶ K ⊠ D_Y L`

`!`-base change, the two Verdier evaluations and `ω_Y ⊠ ω_X ⟶ ω_Z`, to a Borel-Moore

AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.GeometricOper.doc:
Zero-stalk vanishing on a smooth curve: a geometric point `x̄` fixed by `Φ_m` is an
isolated, hence open-and-closed, component `B` of the fixed scheme `Fix(c_m)` of the graph
correspondence `c_m = (1, Φ_m)`; purity in relative dimension zero computes the trace class
there from the pair `(K_x̄, u_x̄)` alone, so if the geometric stalk `K_x̄` vanishes then so
does the local term `LT_x̄(φ_m)` (blueprint: `sk-i-curve-zero`).

The *local term* `LT_B(α) ∈ A` of a Borel-Moore section `α : A_E ⟶ ω_E` along a clopen
immersion `j_B : B ⟶ E`, for `E` proper over `s`: the integral `∫_E e_B · α` of `α` cut down

Point normalization of the pairing: for a perfect `A`-complex `P` on the base point `s`
and an endomorphism `v : P ⟶ P`, regarded as an endocorrespondence with support `s` and
identity legs, the supported pairing against the diagonal identity is the ordinary
categorical trace, `⟨v, 𝟙 P⟩_LV = tr_A(v ∣ P)`.

The same adjunction calculation identifies the trace class of an endocorrespondence on an
arbitrary `X`, which is what the proper compatibility theorem uses
(blueprint: `sk-p-pairing`).

disjoint union `E = ∐_{β ∈ B} β` of clopen subschemes and `E` is proper over `s`, then the

empty sum `0` (blueprint: `sk-p-local`).

Proper pushforward compatibility: for an endocorrespondence `(C, c, u)` on `(X, K)` and
a proper pushforward diagram `(f, g) : (C, c) ⟶ (D, b)` with `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : C ⟶ D`

`u` to the trace class of the pushed coefficient map,

`h_* Tr_c(u) = Tr_b([f, g]_! u)` in `Hom(A_{Fix b}, ω_{Fix b})`.

No properness over `s` of `X`, `Y`, `C` or `D` is required, and neither leg square is
assumed Cartesian (blueprint: `sk-p-proper`).

AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.GeometricOper.doc:
The pushforward of a Borel-Moore section `α : A_T ⟶ ω_T` along a proper `h : T ⟶ T'`
over `s`: the composite

```
  A_{T'} ──η──▶ Rh_* Lh^* A_{T'} ≅ Rh_* A_T ──α──▶ Rh_* ω_T ≅ Rh_! ω_T ≅ Rh_! h^! ω_{T'}
         ──ε──▶ ω_{T'}
```

of the unit of `h^* ⊣ Rh_*`, the proper identification `Rh_* = Rh_!`, the dualizing
composition `h^! ω_{T'} ≃ ω_T` and the counit of `Rh_! ⊣ h^!`
(blueprint: `sk-d-integral`).

  [AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.DerivedBraiding A] (s : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme) :
  Type (max (u + 1) u')
AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.GeometricOper.doc:
The geometric operation package over a base `s`: the comparison data of the six
operations that the blueprint fixes, namely the dualizing complex `ω_X = a_X^! A` with its
composition `f^! ω_Y ≃ ω_X`, the identification `Rf_* = Rf_!` for proper `f`, composition
of exceptional direct images, `!`-base change, the projection formula, the monoidal
structure of the pullback `Lf^*`, braided for `DerivedBraiding`, and the invertibility of
two canonical maps: the biduality map `K ⟶ D_X D_X K` on `Dᵇctf`, and the Künneth-Verdier
map `kunnethVerdierMapOf`. The
identity isomorphism `R(𝟙 X)_! ≃ 𝟭` is tied to `lowerShriekComp` by unit axioms;
`properComparison`, `dualizingBase`, `dualizingComp` and the unit of `Lf^*` are tied to the
identity isomorphisms at `f = 𝟙`; `properComparison` and `dualizingComp`
are compatible with composition, and `baseChange` with vertical pasting.

The functors and the two adjunctions are *not* fields: they are the pro-étale functors of
`WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.ProEtale`, listed in the module docstring
(blueprint: `sk-d-six`).

AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.GeometricCoef.doc:
Coefficients and geometric categories: a choice, for every scheme `X`, of the
subcategory `Dᵇctf(X, A) ⊆ D(X, A)` of bounded constructible objects of finite Tor
amplitude, triangulated and stable under `Lf^*` and `Rf_!`
(blueprint: `sk-d-setup`).

The global operator of an endocorrespondence `(C, c, u)` on `(X, K)` whose ordinary leg
`c₂` is proper: the composite

```
  RΓ_c(X, K) ──η──▶ RΓ_c(X, Rc₂_* c₂^* K) ≅ RΓ_c(C, c₂^* K) ──u──▶ RΓ_c(C, c₁^! K)
             ≅ RΓ_c(X, Rc₁_! c₁^! K) ──ε──▶ RΓ_c(X, K)
```

of the unit of `c₂^* ⊣ Rc₂_*`, the proper identification `Rc₂_* = Rc₂_!` and the counit of
`Rc₁_! ⊣ c₁^!`, acting on compactly supported cohomology `RΓ_c(X, K) = Ra_{X!} K`
(blueprint: `sk-d-operator`).

  (K : DerivedCategory (CategoryTheory.Sheaf (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt.topology X) A))
  (L : DerivedCategory (CategoryTheory.Sheaf (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt.topology Y) A)) :
  Type (u + 1)
AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.Correspondenc.doc:
A correspondence from `(X, K)` to `(Y, L)`: a geometric scheme `C` over the base `s`,
two legs `c₁ : C ⟶ Y`, `c₂ : C ⟶ X` over `s` — the blueprint's `c = (c₁, c₂) : C ⟶ Y × X`,
`c₂` being the *ordinary-pullback* leg — and a coefficient map `u : c₂^* K ⟶ c₁^! L`:

```
            C
          ↙   ↘
       c₁       c₂
      ↙           ↘
     Y             X          u : Lc₂^* K ⟶ c₁^! L
      ↘     ↓a_C  ↙
       a_Y  ↓  a_X
          ↘ ↓ ↙
            s
```

A class supported on `i : T ⟶ Z` is an element of `Hom(Ri_! A_T, P)`; tensor-hom, the
projection formula and exceptional adjunction identify such classes with coefficient maps,
so the supported class `[u]` carries the same information as `u` and is not separate data
(blueprint: `sk-d-corr`).

AlgebraicGeometry.PoincareDualitySetting.signature: structure AlgebraicGeometry.PoincareDualitySetting.{u} (k₀ : Type u) [Field k₀] (d : ℕ) : Type (u + 1)
AlgebraicGeometry.PoincareDualitySetting.doc:
Blueprint `sk-def-set`: The fixed setting.

The geometric datum of the Poincaré duality chapter over the finite field `k₀`: a scheme `X₀`
over `k₀` which is smooth of relative dimension `d`, separated of finite type and
geometrically connected. The algebraic closure `k` of `k₀`, along which `X₀` is base changed,
is an argument of `PoincareDualitySetting.geometricFiber` rather than a field of the
datum.

AlgebraicGeometry.NagataCompactification.doc:
**Nagata compactification** (blueprint: `def:nagata-final-compactification`,
`thm:nagata-compactification`).

The morphism `f` is written as a closed immersion followed by a morphism of finite
presentation by the finite-presentation envelope (Stacks Tag 01ZJ), the latter is compactified
by `AlgebraicGeometry.nagataCompactification_of_locallyOfFinitePresentation` and the
compactification is cut back to the closed subscheme.

theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedDegreeDatum.surjective_mul_center_geometricMonodromy.{u, u_4}
  {W : Type u_4} [Group W] {n k : Type u} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Field k]

        (AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.mulCenterIdentityComponent ⋯))
AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedD.doc:
For a semisimple represented degree datum the identity component of the arithmetic monodromy
group is the central–geometric product `G° = Z(G°)° H°`: the multiplication morphism
`Z(G°)° ×ₖ H° ⟶ G°` of group schemes is surjective. This is the general
`AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.surjective_mulCenterIdentityComponent` for the pair
`H ⊆ G`, which contains the commutators of `G` and acts semisimply on `kⁿ`.
(blueprint: `sk-p-product`)

      (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.zeroLocus D.arithmeticMonodromy R)).Normal
AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedD.doc:
The geometric monodromy group is a normal subgroup scheme of the arithmetic one: for every
`k`-algebra `R`, the `R`-points of `H` form a normal subgroup of the `R`-points of `G`. This is the
closure of the normality of `ρ(P)` in `ρ(W)`.
(blueprint: `sk-i-restriction`, `lem-ag-closure-commutators`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedD.doc:
The derived algebra of `Lie G°` lies in `Lie H°`, over an algebraically closed field of
characteristic zero. (blueprint: `sk-i-restriction`, `lem-ag-closure-commutators`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedD.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedDegreeDatum.lie_mem_lieAlgebra_geometricMonodromy.{u, u_4}

  ∃ Z, (AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.lieAlgebraMap ⋯) Z = ⁅X, Y⁆

The derived algebra of `Lie G` lies in `Lie H`, over any field, where `Lie H → Lie G` is the
differential `lieAlgebraMap` of the closed immersion `H ⟶ G`.
(blueprint: `sk-i-restriction`, `lem-ag-closure-commutators`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedD.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedDegreeDatum.isSemisimpleRepresentation_standardRepresentation_identityComponent.{u,
    u_4}
  {W : Type u_4} [Group W] {n k : Type u} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Field k]
  (D : AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedDegreeDatum W n k) [IsAlgClosed k] [CharZero k]
  (hD : D.IsSemisimple) :
  (AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.standardRepresentation
      (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.identityComponent
        D.arithmeticMonodromy)).IsSemisimpleRepresentation
AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedD.doc:
A semisimple datum acts semisimply through the identity component of its arithmetic monodromy
group: the standard representation of `G°(k)` on `kⁿ` is semisimple.

Proof sketch (not formalised): `kⁿ` is a semisimple `W`-module, hence a semisimple module for the
Zariski closure `G(k)` of `ρ(W)`, since the stabilizer of a subspace is closed; `G°(k)` has finite
index in `G(k)`, so by Clifford's theorem (`Representation.isSemisimpleRepresentation_comp_subtype`)
`kⁿ` is a semisimple `G°(k)`-module. (blueprint: `sk-i-restriction`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedD.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedDegreeDatum.geometricMonodromy_le_derivedIdeal_arithmeticMonodromy.{u,

  {W : Type u_4} [Group W] {n k : Type u} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Field k]

AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedD.doc:
The geometric monodromy group contains the derived subgroup `[G, G]` of the arithmetic one, as
closed subgroup schemes of `GL_n`: `J ≤ derivedIdeal I`. (blueprint: `sk-i-restriction`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedD.signature:
def AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedDegreeDatum.geometricMonodromy.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {W : Type u_1}
  [Group W] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {k : Type u_3} [Field k]
  (D : AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedDegreeDatum W n k) :
  Ideal (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.CoordinateRing n k)
AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedD.doc:
The geometric monodromy group `H = closure ρ(P)`, as a closed subgroup scheme of `GL_n`: the
Hopf ideal of equations vanishing on `ρ(P)`, which cuts out the reduced Zariski closure.
(blueprint: `sk-d-monodromy`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedD.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedDegreeDatum.exists_mem_center_mul_mem_geometricMonodromy_eq.{u,
    u_4}
  {W : Type u_4} [Group W] {n k : Type u} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Field k]
  (D : AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedDegreeDatum W n k) [IsAlgClosed k] [CharZero k]
  (hD : D.IsSemisimple) {g : GL n k}
  (hg :
    g ∈
      Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.zeroLocus
        (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.identityComponent D.arithmeticMonodromy) k) :
  ∃
    c ∈
      Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.zeroLocus
        (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.identityComponent
          (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.center
            (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.identityComponent D.arithmeticMonodromy)))
        k,
    ∃
      h ∈
        Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.zeroLocus
          (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.identityComponent D.geometricMonodromy) k,
      c * h = g
AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedD.doc:
The central–geometric product on `k`-points, in the form used to construct admissible choices:
every matrix of `G°(k)` is a product `c h` with `c ∈ Z(G°)°(k)` and `h ∈ H°(k)`. This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.exists_mul_eq_of_containsCommutators` on the `k`-points,
read as matrices through `zeroLocusMulEquiv`; it supplies the factorization `Fᵐ = c h` of
`exists_isPositiveCentralPair`. (blueprint: `sk-p-product`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedD.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedDegreeDatum.exists_isPositiveCentralPair.{u, u_4}
  {W : Type u_4} [Group W] {n k : Type u} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Field k]
  (D : AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedDegreeDatum W n k) [IsAlgClosed k] [CharZero k]
  (hD : D.IsSemisimple) : ∃ N z, D.IsPositiveCentralPair N z
AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedD.doc:
Every semisimple represented degree datum admits a positive central pair `(N, z)`.

Proof sketch (not formalised): the component group `G(k) ⧸ G°(k)` is finite
(`AlgebraicGeometry.GrpObj.finiteIndex_range_identityComponentι`), so some `m > 0` has
`Fᵐ ∈ G°`; factor `Fᵐ = c h` with `c ∈ Z(G°)°` and `h ∈ H°` by
`exists_mem_center_mul_mem_geometricMonodromy_eq`, and choose representatives `g₁, …, gᵣ` of the
cosets of `G°` in `G`. Then `N = m r` and `z = ∏ gᵢ c gᵢ⁻¹` form a positive central pair: the
factors `gᵢ c gᵢ⁻¹` lie in the abelian group `Z(G°)` and do not depend on the choice of
representatives, so conjugation by `G`, which permutes the cosets, fixes `z`; and each factor lies
in the coset `H Fᵐ` of `c` because the commutators of `G` lie in `H`, so `z ∈ H Fᵐʳ`.
(blueprint: `sk-p-central`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedD.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedDegreeDatum.detWeight_eq_of_isPositiveCentralPair.{u_1, u_2,
    u_3}
  {W : Type u_1} [Group W] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {k : Type u_3} [Field k]
  (D : AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedDegreeDatum W n k)
  (χ : Representation.RealCharacter k) {N : ℕ} {z : GL n k} (hz : D.IsPositiveCentralPair N z)
  {U S : Subrepresentation D.asRepresentation} (hUS : U < S)
  (hdet : Representation.HasFiniteGeometricDet D.deg (S.subquotient U)) (c : kˣ)
  (hc : ∀ x ∈ S, (Matrix.toLinAlgEquiv' ↑z) x - ↑c • x ∈ U) :
  Representation.detWeight χ D.degreeOneElement (S.subquotient U) = Multiplicative.toAdd (χ c) / ↑N
AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedD.doc:
Fix a real character `χ` and a positive central pair `(N, z)` for a represented degree
datum.  If a nonzero `W`-subquotient `Q = S / U` of the defining representation has finite
geometric determinant and `z` acts on `Q` as the scalar `c`, then `dw_χ(Q) = χ(c) / N`.  The
scalar hypothesis is automatic when `Q` is simple, by Schur's lemma.
(blueprint: `sk-p-readout`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedD.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedDegreeDatum.containsCommutators_subgroupSchemeHom_arithmeticMonodromy_le_geometricMonodromy.{u,
    u_4}

  AlgebraicGeometry.IsMonHom.ContainsCommutators
    (AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.subgroupSchemeHom ⋯)
AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedD.doc:
The geometric monodromy group contains the commutators of the arithmetic one, as closed
subgroup schemes of `GL_n`: this is `commutator_zeroLocus_le_zeroLocus_geometricMonodromy` on the
`R`-points for all `k`-algebras `R`, transported to the schemes. In particular `H` is a normal
subgroup scheme of `G` (`AlgebraicGeometry.IsMonHom.Normal.of_containsCommutators`), and the
general results on such pairs of closed subgroups apply to `H ⊆ G`.
(blueprint: `sk-i-restriction`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedD.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedDegreeDatum.commutator_zeroLocus_le_zeroLocus_geometricMonodromy.{u_1,
    u_2, u_3, u_4}
  {W : Type u_1} [Group W] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {k : Type u_3} [Field k]
  (D : AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedDegreeDatum W n k) (R : Type u_4) [CommRing R]
  [Algebra k R] :
  ⁅Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.zeroLocus D.arithmeticMonodromy R,
      Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.zeroLocus D.arithmeticMonodromy R⁆ ≤
    Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.zeroLocus D.geometricMonodromy R
AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedD.doc:
Every commutator of the arithmetic monodromy group lies in the geometric one: for every
`k`-algebra `R`, `⁅G(R), G(R)⁆ ⊆ H(R)`. This is the closure of `⁅ρ(W), ρ(W)⁆ ⊆ ρ(P)`, which holds
because `W ⧸ P ≅ ℤ` is abelian.
(blueprint: `sk-i-restriction`, `lem-ag-closure-commutators`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedD.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedDegreeDatum.arithmeticMonodromy_le_geometricMonodromy.{u_1,
    u_2, u_3}
  {W : Type u_1} [Group W] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {k : Type u_3} [Field k]
  (D : AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedDegreeDatum W n k) :
  D.arithmeticMonodromy ≤ D.geometricMonodromy
AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedD.doc:
The ideal of `G` is contained in the ideal of `H`; that is, `H ⊆ G` as closed subschemes of
`GL_n`.
(blueprint: `sk-i-restriction`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedD.signature:
def AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedDegreeDatum.arithmeticMonodromy.{u_1, u_2, u_3}
  {W : Type u_1} [Group W] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {k : Type u_3} [Field k]
  (D : AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedDegreeDatum W n k) :
  Ideal (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.CoordinateRing n k)
AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedD.doc:
The arithmetic monodromy group `G = closure ρ(W)`, as a closed subgroup scheme of `GL_n`: the
Hopf ideal of equations vanishing on `ρ(W)`, which cuts out the reduced Zariski closure.
(blueprint: `sk-d-monodromy`)

A datum is *semisimple* when `n → k` is a semisimple `W`-representation.  This is an `abbrev`
so that the underlying class `Representation.IsSemisimpleRepresentation` stays visible to
instance search.
(blueprint: `sk-d-monodromy`)

A *positive central pair* for the datum is a pair `(N, z)` with `N > 0` and
`z ∈ Z(G) ∩ H Fᴺ`, where `H Fᴺ` is the right coset `H(k) · Fᴺ`, written as the pointwise product
of the set `H(k)` with the singleton `{Fᴺ}`.
(blueprint: `sk-d-central`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedD.signature:
structure AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedDegreeDatum.{u_1, u_2, u_3} (W : Type u_1) [Group W]

AlgebraicGeometry.Monodromy.RepresentedD.doc:

AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianTorsionDatum.t.doc:
Blueprint `sk-d-real-jacobian`: Jacobian torsion data and Kummer coefficients.

The Tate module `T_l J = lim_n J[lⁿ]` of a Jacobian torsion datum, realised concretely as the
subgroup of the product `∀ n, J[lⁿ]` consisting of the compatible systems, i.e. those families
`f` with `transition n (f (n + 1)) = f n` for all `n`.

Inverting `l` gives `V_l J = T_l J ⊗ ℚ_l`, the `l`-adic homology of the curve.

AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianTorsionDatum.doc:
Blueprint `sk-d-real-jacobian`: Jacobian torsion data and Kummer coefficients.

A Jacobian torsion datum for a proper smooth geometrically integral curve `p : C ⟶ Spec K`
over a finite field, a prime `l`, a group `Γ` (the Galois group of `k / K`) and a `Γ`-module
`Pic` (the Picard group of the geometric curve `C`, written additively) consists of an abelian
variety `J₀ = J` over `K` together with a compatible system of `Γ`-equivariant isomorphisms

`J[lⁿ] ≃ Pic[lⁿ] = ker (l ^ n • · : Pic → Pic)`

carrying multiplication by `l` on `J[l ^ (n + 1)] → J[lⁿ]` to the `l`-th tensor power on line
bundles, i.e. to multiplication by `l` on the additively written `Pic`.

theorem AlgebraicGeometry.IsWeilFactorization.unique {q d : ℕ} (hq : 1 < q) {Z : PowerSeries ℚ}

  (h' : AlgebraicGeometry.IsWeilFactorization q d Z P')

AlgebraicGeometry.IsWeilFactorization.un.doc:
**Uniqueness of the integral Frobenius factors.** If two families of integer polynomials
are Weil factorizations of the same power series and both satisfy the Riemann hypothesis, then
they are equal: a reciprocal root of absolute value `q^{i/2}` can only come from the degree-`i`
member of either family.

AlgebraicGeometry.IsWeilFactorization.signature:
structure AlgebraicGeometry.IsWeilFactorization (q d : ℕ) (Z : PowerSeries ℚ)
  (P : Fin (2 * d + 1) → Polynomial ℤ) : Prop
AlgebraicGeometry.IsWeilFactorization.doc:
`IsWeilFactorization q d Z P` says that the polynomials `P₀, …, P_{2d} ∈ ℤ[t]`
factor the power series `Z` as `Z = (P₁ ⋯ P_{2d-1}) / (P₀ ⋯ P_{2d})`, normalized by
`Pᵢ(0) = 1`, with `P₀ = 1 - t` and `P_{2d} = 1 - qᵈ t`. This is the shape of the zeta
function of a smooth, proper, geometrically integral scheme of dimension `d` over a field
with `q` elements predicted by the Weil conjectures.

blueprint: `lemma:nagata-dense-source-valuative`).

The uniqueness half of the hypothesis makes the diagonal satisfy the dense-source criterion
for universal closedness, and a universally closed immersion is a closed immersion.

`lemma:nagata-separated-two-open-cover`): let `W = T₁ ∪ T₂` be a union of two open

Blueprint `sk-lem-regular-smooth`: A regular immersion of smooth schemes over a perfect
field

**Smoothness of the sub-scheme.** Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a regular closed immersion of pure
codimension `c` with `X` smooth over a perfect field `k` and `Z` regular. Then the structure
morphism of `Z` is smooth too: a regular scheme of finite type over a perfect field is smooth
over it.

AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegularImmersion.rin.doc:
Blueprint `sk-lem-regular-smooth`: A regular immersion of smooth schemes over a perfect
field

**The dimension count.** With the hypotheses of `AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegularImmersion.smooth_comp`,
a component of `X` of dimension `n` meets `Z` in pure dimension `n - c`. Stated stalkwise, so
that it is insensitive to the components of `X` that `Z` misses: at every point `z` of `Z` the
local ring of `X` at `i(z)` has Krull dimension `c` more than the local ring of `Z` at `z`.

AlgebraicGeometry.IsQuasiAffineHom.doc:
A morphism of schemes is quasi-affine if the preimage of every affine open of the target is a
quasi-affine scheme.

AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper.doc: A morphism is proper if it is separated, universally closed and locally of finite type.

AlgebraicGeometry.IsMonHom.Normal.of_con.doc: A subgroup scheme containing the commutators is normal: `g h g⁻¹ = (g h g⁻¹ h⁻¹) h`.

AlgebraicGeometry.IsMonHom.ContainsCommu.doc:
A homomorphism of group schemes `f : H ⟶ G` over `S` *contains the commutators* of `G` when
every commutator `a b a⁻¹ b⁻¹` of two points `a b : X ⟶ G` of `G`, with values in an arbitrary
`S`-scheme `X`, factors through `f`. For a subgroup scheme `H ⊆ G` this is the scheme-theoretic
form of `⁅G, G⁆ ⊆ H`, that is, of the commutativity of the quotient `G ⧸ H`.
(blueprint: `sk-i-restriction`)

structure AlgebraicGeometry.IsJacobian.{u} {K : Type u} [Field K] {C : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme}
  (f : C ⟶ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) [AlgebraicGeometry.IsCurve f]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth f] [AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper f]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.GeometricallyIntegral f]
  (P :
    CategoryTheory.Functor (CategoryTheory.Over (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of K)))ᵒᵖ
      GrpCat)
  (J : CategoryTheory.Over (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of K))) [CategoryTheory.GrpObj J] :
  Prop
AlgebraicGeometry.IsJacobian.doc:
Blueprint `sk-def-av-jacobian`: The Jacobian

Let `C` be a smooth projective geometrically integral curve over a field `K`, of genus `g`. A
*Jacobian of `C`* is a pair `(J, φ)` consisting of an abelian variety `J` over `K` of dimension
`g` together with an isomorphism of group-valued functors `φ : Pic⁰_{C/K} ≅ h_J` on `(Sch/K)`;
that is, `J` represents the degree-zero relative Picard functor.

The relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/K}` enters as the parameter
`P : (Over (Spec (.of K)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat`, which the definition does not relate to `C`; see the
implementation notes of this file. The functor of points of `J` as a group-valued functor is
`CategoryTheory.yonedaGrpObj J`.

Representability is stated as `Nonempty (P ≅ yonedaGrpObj J)` rather than as a chosen
isomorphism, so that `IsJacobian` is a `Prop`; the data of `φ` is recovered by choice.

AlgebraicGeometry.IsIsogeny.isFinite.doc:
Blueprint `sk-prop-av-isogeny-degree`: The degree of an isogeny is the degree of the kernel.

An isogeny of abelian varieties is a finite morphism: it is proper, `A` being proper, and has
finite fibres (`AlgebraicGeometry.IsIsogeny.finite_preimage_singleton`).

AlgebraicGeometry.IsIsogeny.flat.doc:
Blueprint `sk-prop-av-isogeny-degree`: The degree of an isogeny is the degree of the kernel.

An isogeny of abelian varieties is a flat morphism: it is finite onto the reduced scheme `B`
with all fibres of the same degree (`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.flat_of_fiberDegree_eq`).

AlgebraicGeometry.IsIsogeny.finrank_eq.doc:
Blueprint `sk-prop-av-isogeny-degree`: The degree of an isogeny is the degree of the kernel.

For an isogeny `f : A ⟶ B` of abelian varieties with kernel of order `d`, the sheaf `f_* 𝒪_A` is
locally free of rank `d`: the degree of the finite flat morphism `f` equals the order of its
kernel.

AlgebraicGeometry.IsIsogeny.signature:
structure AlgebraicGeometry.IsIsogeny.{u} {K : Type u} [Field K]
  {A B : CategoryTheory.Over (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of K))} [CategoryTheory.GrpObj A]
  [CategoryTheory.GrpObj B] (f : A ⟶ B) : Prop
AlgebraicGeometry.IsIsogeny.doc:
Blueprint `sk-def-av-isogeny`: Isogenies and their degree.

An *isogeny* `f : A ⟶ B` of group schemes over `K` is a surjective homomorphism with finite
kernel. The blueprint defines isogenies between abelian varieties; the definition makes sense
for arbitrary group schemes, but it is only for abelian varieties that
`AlgebraicGeometry.isogenyDegree` is the degree of `f` as a finite flat morphism (see
`AlgebraicGeometry.IsIsogeny.finrank_eq`).

AlgebraicGeometry.IsImmersion.signature: structure AlgebraicGeometry.IsImmersion.{u} {X Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop
AlgebraicGeometry.IsImmersion.doc:
A morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ Y` is an immersion if
1. the underlying map of topological spaces is an embedding
2. the range of the map is locally closed
3. the induced morphisms of stalks are all surjective.

AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite.signature: structure AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite.{u_1} {X Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop
AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite.doc:
A morphism of schemes `X ⟶ Y` is finite if
the preimage of any affine open subset of `Y` is affine and the induced ring
hom is finite.

AlgebraicGeometry.IsCurve.signature:
structure AlgebraicGeometry.IsCurve.{u} {K : Type u} [Field K] {C : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme}
  (f : C ⟶ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) : Prop
AlgebraicGeometry.IsCurve.doc:
Blueprint `sk-def-curve`: Curves and genus

Let `K` be a field (in the blueprint, algebraically closed). A *curve* over `K` is a separated
scheme of finite type over `K` of dimension at most one. Smoothness and properness of a curve
are the corresponding properties `Smooth` and `IsProper` of its structure morphism, so they are
not part of this class; the dimension condition is phrased with `topologicalKrullDim`, which is
valued in `WithBot ℕ∞` and is `⊥` exactly on the empty scheme.

AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion.lift.doc:
The universal property of closed immersions:
For a closed immersion `f : X ⟶ Z`, given any morphism of schemes `g : Y ⟶ Z` whose kernel
contains the kernel of `X` in `Z`, we can lift this morphism to a unique `Y ⟶ X` that
commutes with these maps.

**Factorization through a closed subscheme over the spectrum of a domain**
(blueprint: `lemma:nagata-valuation-factor-closed`): let `A` be a domain with fraction
field `K`, let `ι : Z ⟶ Y` be a closed immersion and `γ : Spec A ⟶ Y` a morphism whose
restriction to the generic point `Spec K` factors through `Z`. Then `γ` factors
through `Z`.

AlgebraicGeometry.IsAmple.doc:

An invertible `𝒪_X`-module is *ample* if some positive tensor power of it is very ample.

**The product of two `U`-admissible centers is `U`-admissible** (bookkeeping for
blueprint `lemma:nagata-product-ideal-common-blowup`): finite-typeness is stable under
products, and the support of a product is the union of the supports.

**Scheme-theoretic density is preserved by admissible blow-ups** (blueprint:
`lemma:nagata-admissible-blowup-preserves-density`; proof order item 20): if `U` is a
quasi-compact scheme-theoretically dense open of `X`, then the inverse image of `U`
under any `U`-admissible blow-up is scheme-theoretically dense in the total space.

theorem (`thm:nagata-global-blowup-complement`) applied to the disjointness of the
center from `U`.
(Blueprint: `lemma:nagata-admissible-blowup-over-open`.)

AlgebraicGeometry.IsAdmissible.exists_ex.doc:
**Extension of an admissible blow-up center across a second quasi-compact open**
(Stacks Project Tag 080M, blueprint `lemma:nagata-extend-admissible-blowup`): a
finite-type center `J` on a quasi-compact open `A` of a quasi-compact quasi-separated
scheme `X`, whose support avoids the overlap `A ⊓ B` with a quasi-compact open `B`,
extends to a `B`-admissible center on `X` whose blow-up restricts over `A` to the
blow-up of `J`. This is `AlgebraicGeometry.IsAdmissible.exists_extend` with the
inclusion `B ≤ A` of the preserved open in the ambient open dropped; the center is
produced by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.exists_finiteType_comap_eq_of_disjoint`.

AlgebraicGeometry.IsAdmissible.exists_ex.doc:
**Extension of admissible blow-up centers across a quasi-compact open** (in the
style of Stacks Project Tag 080M; blueprint `def:nagata-extended-admissible-blowup`,
`lemma:nagata-extend-admissible-blowup`).

The extended center is the product of a finite-type extension of `J` (Stacks Project
Tag 01PF) with a finite-type ideal cutting out the boundary of `W` (Stacks Project
Tag 01PH).

theorem AlgebraicGeometry.IsAdmissible.exists_comp_isSchemeTheoreticallyDominant_preimage.{u}
  {X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} [CompactSpace ↥X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace ↥X] {U : X.Opens}
  (hU : IsCompact ↑U) (B : AlgebraicGeometry.IsAdmissible X U) :
  ∃ B' h,
    CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp h B.I.blowupMap = B'.I.blowupMap ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsSchemeTheoreticallyDominant
        ((TopologicalSpace.Opens.map B'.I.blowupMap.base).obj U).ι
AlgebraicGeometry.IsAdmissible.exists_co.doc:
**A further `U`-admissible blow-up in which `U` becomes scheme-theoretically dense**
(blueprint: `lemma:nagata-conrad-schematically-dense-blowup`, relative form).

The total space of `B` is again qcqs and `B.I.blowupMap ⁻¹ᵁ U` is again quasi-compact
(`IsAdmissible.isProper_blowupMap`), so the absolute form
`exists_isAdmissible_isSchemeTheoreticallyDominant_preimage` applies to it; composing the
two blow-ups (`IsAdmissible.exists_comp`, Stacks Tag 080L) gives a `U`-admissible center
`K` on `X` together with an identification of the two total spaces over `X`, along which
the density transports.

AlgebraicGeometry.IsAdmissible.exists_co.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.IsAdmissible.exists_comp.{u} {X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} {U : X.Opens}
  [CompactSpace ↥X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace ↥X] (B₁ : AlgebraicGeometry.IsAdmissible X U)
  (B₂ :
    AlgebraicGeometry.IsAdmissible B₁.I.blowup
      ((TopologicalSpace.Opens.map B₁.I.blowupMap.base).obj U)) :
  ∃ K,
    K.ofFiniteType ∧
      Disjoint ↑U ↑K.support ∧
        ∃ iso,
          CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp iso.hom K.blowupMap =
            CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp B₂.I.blowupMap B₁.I.blowupMap
AlgebraicGeometry.IsAdmissible.exists_co.doc:
**Composition of admissible blow-ups** (Stacks Project Tag 080L; blueprint
`lemma:nagata-admissible-blowup-comp`).

Difference from the informal statement: Stacks Tag 080L assumes `U` quasi-compact; the
formal proof needs no such hypothesis.

The proof applies the composition theorem for arbitrary blow-ups
(`Scheme.IdealSheafData.exists_blowup_comp`, Stacks Tag 080B): the composite center
`K` has support `|Z| ∪ π₁(|Z'|)`; the first part misses `U` by admissibility of `B₁`,
and the second part misses `U` because a point of `π₁(|Z'|) ∩ U` would lift to a point
of `|Z'| ∩ π₁⁻¹(U)`, contradicting admissibility of `B₂`.

AlgebraicGeometry.IsAdmissible.dense_pre.doc:
**Topological density transports through an admissible blow-up** (blueprint:
`lemma:nagata-conrad-dense-in-admissible-blowup`).

The preimage of the complement of the center is dense
(`IsAdmissible.dense_coe_preimage_preservedOpen`) and the blow-up is an isomorphism
there, so every nonempty open of the blow-up maps onto a nonempty open of the preserved
open, which meets the dense set.

AlgebraicGeometry.IsAdmissible.dense_coe.doc:
**Topological density transports through an admissible blow-up**, in the form
consumed by the Conrad case lemmas: the inverse image open of a dense open of a
quasi-compact, quasi-separated scheme is dense in any admissible blow-up.

Let `j : U ⟶ X` be an open immersion whose closed complement is `i : Z ⟶ X`. If the
direct-image weight assertion holds for `j ≫ f` and for `i ≫ f`, then it holds for `f`:

```
U --- j ---> X <--- i --- Z
  \          |          /
   `- j ≫ f  | f   i ≫ f -'
       \     v     /
        `--> Y <--'
```

(blueprint: `sk-l-dl-general-excision`; this is part 1 of
`lem-zl-morphism-open-closed-reduction`, sheaf form).

AlgebraicGeometry.HasCompactification.of.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.HasCompactification.of_two_open_cover.{u} {U S : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme}
  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsNoetherian S] (u : U ⟶ S) [AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated u]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType u] [AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact u] (O₁ O₂ : U.Opens)
  (hcov : O₁ ⊔ O₂ = ⊤) (hdense : Dense ↑(O₁ ⊓ O₂))
  [AlgebraicGeometry.HasCompactification (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp O₁.ι u)]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.HasCompactification (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp O₂.ι u)] :
  AlgebraicGeometry.HasCompactification u
AlgebraicGeometry.HasCompactification.of.doc:
**The two-open compactification theorem** (Stacks Project Tag 0F40; blueprint:
`def:nagata-two-open-final-modification` through `thm:nagata-two-open`; proof order
items 43–48).

The compactification is the common modification `W` (Stacks Project Tag 0F3X) of the
two intermediate schemes `Wᵢ = U ⊔_{Oᵢ} Xᵢ°`; the intersection `O₁ ∩ O₂` is dense in
`W` because density transports through the finite modification diagram, every
valuative square through it lifts uniquely — extend the generic point to the proper
sides, pass to the side avoiding its forbidden boundary, and lift along the proper
admissible blow-up — and the dense-source valuative criterion (Stacks Project
Tag 0894) then proves that `W ⟶ S` is universally closed, hence proper.

**A quasi-affine scheme of finite type over `S` is compactifiable over `S`**
(blueprint: `prop:nagata-affine-compactification`).

Since an affine scheme is quasi-affine, this covers the case of an affine `X` used in the
induction of Nagata's theorem.

**Compactifiability is stable under base change**: if `p : Y ⟶ T` admits a
compactification and `IsPullback h u p t`, then the base change `u : X ⟶ S` of `p` along
`t` admits one too.
(blueprint: `lemma:nagata-compactification-base-change`)

A quasi-compact morphism that factors as an immersion into a scheme proper over the
base admits a compactification.
(blueprint: `lemma:nagata-immersion-into-proper`)

**Compactifiability is inherited by closed subschemes**: if a quasi-compact morphism
`f' : X' ⟶ S` admits a compactification, then so does its restriction `i ≫ f'` to a closed
subscheme `i : X ⟶ X'`.
(blueprint: `prop:nagata-closed-subscheme-compactifiable`)

A morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` has a compactification if it factors as an open
immersion followed by a proper morphism.

AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.sur.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.surjective_mulCenterIdentityComponent.{u} {n : Type u}
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {k : Type u} [Field k]
  {I J : Ideal (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.CoordinateRing n k)} [Ideal.IsHopfIdeal k I]
  [Ideal.IsHopfIdeal k J] [IsAlgClosed k] [CharZero k] (h : I ≤ J)
  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsMonHom.ContainsCommutators
      (AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.subgroupSchemeHom h)]
  [(AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.standardRepresentation
        (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.identityComponent I)).IsSemisimpleRepresentation] :
  Function.Surjective
    ⇑(CategoryTheory.Over.Hom.left
        (AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.mulCenterIdentityComponent h))
AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.sur.doc:
**The central–geometric product.** Let `H = V(J) ⊆ G = V(I)` be closed subgroups of `GL_n` over
an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero such that `H` contains the commutators of `G`
and `G°` acts semisimply on `kⁿ`. Then `G° = Z(G°)° H°`: the multiplication morphism
`Z(G°)° × H° ⟶ G°` is surjective.

Proof sketch (not formalised): the Lie algebra `𝔤 = Lie G° ⊆ 𝔤𝔩_n` is a faithful semisimple Lie
representation, so `𝔤 = 𝔷(𝔤) + [𝔤, 𝔤]`; the brackets lie in `Lie H°`
(`lie_mem_range_lieAlgebraMap_identityComponent`) and `𝔷(𝔤) = Lie Z(G°)°`
(`range_lieAlgebraMap_identityComponent_center`), so `𝔤 = Lie Z(G°)° + Lie H°`. The multiplication
morphism is a homomorphism because `Z(G°)°` is central, so its image is closed
(`AlgebraicGeometry.isClosed_range_of_isMonHom`) and connected, and its Lie algebra is `𝔤`; by
Cartier's theorem it has the dimension of `G°`, hence is all of `G°`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_left_of_topologicalKrullDim_eq`). (blueprint: `sk-p-product`)

  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {k : Type u} [Field k]
  {I J : Ideal (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.CoordinateRing n k)} [Ideal.IsHopfIdeal k I]
  [Ideal.IsHopfIdeal k J] [IsAlgClosed k] [CharZero k] (h : I ≤ J)
  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsMonHom.ContainsCommutators
      (AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.subgroupSchemeHom h)]
  (X Y :
    AlgebraicGeometry.GrpObj.Lie
      (AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.subgroupScheme
        (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.identityComponent I))) :
  ⁅X, Y⁆ ∈ (AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.lieAlgebraMap ⋯).range
AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.lie.doc:
The brackets of the Lie algebra of `G° = V(identityComponent I)` lie in the Lie algebra of
`H° = V(identityComponent J)`, when `H = V(J) ⊆ G = V(I)` contains the commutators of `G`: in
characteristic zero the identity components have the same Lie algebras as `G` and `H`
(`lieAlgebraEquivIdentityComponent`), and the differentials of `H° ⟶ G° ⟶ G` and `H° ⟶ H ⟶ G`
agree. (blueprint: `sk-i-restriction`)

AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.lie.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.lie_mem_range_lieAlgebraMap.{u} {n : Type u} [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] {k : Type u} [CommRing k]
  {I J : Ideal (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.CoordinateRing n k)} [Ideal.IsHopfIdeal k I]
  [Ideal.IsHopfIdeal k J] (h : I ≤ J)
  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsMonHom.ContainsCommutators
      (AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.subgroupSchemeHom h)]
  (X Y : AlgebraicGeometry.GrpObj.Lie (AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.subgroupScheme I)) :
  ⁅X, Y⁆ ∈ (AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.lieAlgebraMap h).range
AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.lie.doc:
If the closed subgroup `V(J) ⊆ V(I)` contains the commutators of `V(I)`, then the bracket of two
tangent vectors of `V(I)` is a tangent vector of `V(J)`: the bracket is the mixed term of the
commutator of the points `1 + εX` and `1 + δY` over `k[ε, δ]/(ε², δ²)`.
(blueprint: `sk-i-restriction`)

AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.exi.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.exists_mul_eq_of_containsCommutators.{u} {n : Type u}
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {k : Type u} [Field k]
  {I J : Ideal (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.CoordinateRing n k)} [Ideal.IsHopfIdeal k I]
  [Ideal.IsHopfIdeal k J] [IsAlgClosed k] [CharZero k] (h : I ≤ J)

  (g :
    AlgebraicGeometry.points
      (AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.subgroupScheme

AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.exi.doc:
The central–geometric product on `k`-points: every point of `G°` is a product `t h` of a point
`t` of `Z(G°)°` and a point `h` of `H°`. Proof sketch (not formalised): a `k`-point of `G°` lifts
along the surjective multiplication morphism to a `k`-point of `Z(G°)° × H°`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_points_comp_eq_of_surjective`), whose two projections are `t` and `h`.
(blueprint: `sk-p-product`)

AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.der.signature:
def AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.derivedIdeal.{u} {n : Type u} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {k : Type u} [CommRing k] (I : Ideal (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.CoordinateRing n k))
  [Ideal.IsHopfIdeal k I] : Ideal (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.CoordinateRing n k)
AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.der.doc:
The Hopf ideal of the derived subgroup `[V(I), V(I)]`: the sum of all Hopf ideals `J ≥ I` such
that `V(J) ⟶ V(I)` contains the commutators of `V(I)`. (blueprint: `sk-i-restriction`)

AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.con.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.containsCommutators_subgroupSchemeHom.{u} {n : Type u}
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {k : Type u} [CommRing k]
  {I J : Ideal (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.CoordinateRing n k)} [Ideal.IsHopfIdeal k I]
  [Ideal.IsHopfIdeal k J] (h : I ≤ J)
  (hIJ :
    ∀ (R : Type u) [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : Algebra k R],
      ⁅Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.zeroLocus I R, Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.zeroLocus I R⁆ ≤
        Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.zeroLocus J R) :
  AlgebraicGeometry.IsMonHom.ContainsCommutators
    (AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.subgroupSchemeHom h)
AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.con.doc:
If `V(I)(R)` has its commutators in `V(J)(R)` for every `k`-algebra `R`, then the closed
immersion `V(J) ⟶ V(I)` contains the commutators scheme-theoretically
(`AlgebraicGeometry.IsMonHom.ContainsCommutators`).

Proof sketch (not formalised): it suffices to factor the universal commutator, that of the two
projections of `V(I) × V(I)`, through `V(J)`; every other commutator is obtained from it by
precomposition. The product `V(I) × V(I)` is affine, the spectrum of
`(k[GL_n] ⧸ I) ⊗[k] (k[GL_n] ⧸ I)`, so its identity is a point of `V(I) × V(I)` with values in this
algebra, and the hypothesis for this algebra, transported through `zeroLocusMulEquiv`, factors the
universal commutator. (blueprint: `sk-i-restriction`)

AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.con.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.containsCommutators_iff_le_derivedIdeal.{u} {n : Type u}
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {k : Type u} [CommRing k]
  {I : Ideal (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.CoordinateRing n k)} [Ideal.IsHopfIdeal k I]
  {J : Ideal (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.CoordinateRing n k)} [Ideal.IsHopfIdeal k J] (h : I ≤ J) :
  AlgebraicGeometry.IsMonHom.ContainsCommutators
      (AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.subgroupSchemeHom h) ↔
    J ≤ AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.derivedIdeal I
AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup.con.doc:
A closed subgroup `V(J) ⊆ V(I)` contains the commutators of `V(I)` if and only if it contains
the derived subgroup `[V(I), V(I)]`, that is, `J ≤ derivedIdeal I`.
(blueprint: `sk-i-restriction`)

theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.upperStar_map_baseChangeMap_app_counit.{u', u} (A : Type u')
  [CategoryTheory.Category.{u + 1, u'} A] [CategoryTheory.Abelian A]
  [CategoryTheory.IsGrothendieckAbelian.{u + 1, u + 1, u'} A] {X' X Y' Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme}
  {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y} (sq : CategoryTheory.CommSq g' f' f g)

  CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp
      ((AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.upperStar A f').map
        ((AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.baseChangeMap A sq).app F))
      ((AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.upperStarLowerStarAdjunction A f').counit.app
        ((AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.upperStar A g').obj F)) =
    CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp
      ((AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.squareUpperStarIso A sq).hom.app
        ((AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.lowerStar A f).obj F))

        ((AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.upperStarLowerStarAdjunction A f).counit.app F))
AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.upperStar_map_ba.doc:
**The adjoint of the base change map** is the square isomorphism followed by the counit:
for a sheaf `F` on `X`,
`f'^* (baseChangeMap F) ≫ ε_{f'} = squareUpperStarIso (f_* F) ≫ g'^* (ε_f F)`.
(blueprint: `def:weil-pbc-underived-exchange`)

stalk of `f^* F` at the geometric point `s`, taken at the universe of the coefficients, is
the stalk of `F` at `s ≫ f`. This is the form in which the comparison is used, since the
coefficient categories of the six functor formalism are concrete over `Type (u + 1)` and the
fibre functor of `pointSmallEtale s` takes values in `Type u`.

The stalk of a pullback of étale sheaves is the stalk at the image point: for a morphism
of schemes `f : X ⟶ Y` and a geometric point `s : Spec Ω ⟶ X`, the stalk of `f^* F` at `s`
is the stalk of `F` at `s ≫ f`, naturally in the sheaf `F`.

The three steps are the comparison
`CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullbackIso` between `(f)^*[A]` and
the abstract sheaf pullback along base change, the isomorphism
`CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Point.sheafFiberComapIso` of the sheaf pullback with
the fibre functor of the point obtained from `s` by `Point.comap`, and the identification
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.pointSmallEtaleComapIso` of that point with `s ≫ f`.

étale sites: left Kan extension on presheaves followed by sheafification, left adjoint to
`Etale.lowerStar`. The Kan extensions are provided by
`CategoryTheory.Functor.hasPointwiseLeftKanExtension_of_hasColimitsOfSize` of
`WeilConjectures.Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Functor.KanExtension.Pointwise`, and the sheafification by
`CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.hasSheafify_smallEtaleTopology` of
`WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.GrothendieckAbelian.HasSheafify`, which is still sorried
through `CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.hasSheafify_of_essentiallySmall`. For `g` étale
the Kan extension hypothesis is automatic by
`Etale.hasPointwiseLeftKanExtension_op_overPullback`, and `g^*` is computed by restriction,
see `Etale.upperStarIsoOpenImmersionRestriction`.

**The open–closed short complex is short exact**: for an open immersion `j : U ⟶ X`, a
closed immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` whose range is the complement of the range of `j`, and a sheaf
`F` on the small étale site of `X`, the sequence

`0 ⟶ j_! j^* F ⟶ F ⟶ i_* i^* F ⟶ 0`

this follows from

`AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.shortExact_map_upperStar_openClosedShortComplex_closed`.
(blueprint: `thm:openclosed-exact`)

**Topological invariance of the small étale topos**, [Stacks 03SI]: for a universal
homeomorphism `f : X ⟶ Y`, restriction along base change is an equivalence between the
category of `A`-valued sheaves on the small étale site of `X` and that of `Y`.

This is the sheaf-level form of the equivalence of sites
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isDenseSubsite_etale`.
(blueprint: `prop:weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-topos`)

Blueprint `sk-def-purity-conv`: Purity conventions and the rank-one datum

The *section invariant* `𝒞(g, s) = Ls^* ω_g = Ls^* Rg^! Λ_B` of a morphism `g : V ⟶ B`
together with a section `s : B ⟶ V`. For `g` smooth of pure relative dimension `d` with `s` a
closed section, smooth purity identifies it with `Λ_B(d)[2d]`; the deformation to the normal
cone of the section reduces the general case to the standard pair `(𝔸^d_B → B, 0)`.

admitting a compactification, on the unbounded derived categories of étale sheaves: *by
definition* a chosen right adjoint of the derived lower shriek `R(f)_![A]`.

of the composite is reversed. (blueprint: `BA43-RHO`)

The comparison `Rf_!(d)[A]+ ⟶ Rf_!(c)[A]+` of the bounded below derived lower shrieks
attached to two compactifications `c`, `d` of `f : X ⟶ Y` linked by a refinement
`r : c.Refinement d` whose square over `X` is cartesian.

It is the composite of the unit of the derived adjunction
`D(r.hom)^* ⊣ R(r.hom)_*`, the inverse of the base change isomorphism
`D(c.i)_! ≅ D(d.i)_! ⋙ D(r.hom)^*`, and the composition isomorphism
`R(r.hom)_* ⋙ R(d.g)_* ≅ R(c.g)_*`. Note that it goes from the coarser compactification `d`
to the finer one `c`. (blueprint: `BA43-RHO`)

The derived lower shriek `Rf_! : D(X_ét) ⥤ D(Y_ét)` attached to a compactification
`c = (X ⟶[i] Z ⟶[g] Y)` of `f`, on the unbounded derived categories of étale sheaves: the
functor `Di_!` induced on derived categories by the *exact* extension by zero `i_!`, followed
by the total right derived pushforward `Rg_*`.

Warning: It is deliberately *not* the total right derived functor of the composite
`i_! ⋙ g_* = Etale.lowerShriek`. In general, `i_!` does not sends injective sheaves to
`g_*`-acyclic ones, and `Rf_!` is not the derived functor of `f_!`, through its zeroth
homology is `f_!`. Deligne made explicit calculations on $A^1$, see SGA.

`f : X ⟶ Y` admitting a compactification: the projection map

AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.preservesFiniteC.doc:
**The direct image along a finite morphism is exact** (blueprint:
`lemma:weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact`): it preserves finite colimits, and it preserves
finite limits by `AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.preservesFiniteLimits_lowerStar`.

AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.openImmersionLow.doc:
The lower shriek `j_!` along an open immersion `j : U ⟶ X` on sheaves for the small
étale sites.

AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.openClosedShortC.doc:
**The open–closed short complex** `j_! j^* F ⟶ F ⟶ i_* i^* F` attached to an open
immersion `j` and a morphism `i` whose range is disjoint from the range of `j`.

The first map is the counit of `j_! ⊣ j^*` at `F` and the second is the unit of `i^* ⊣ i_*` at
`F`. Their composite is zero because `Hom(j_! j^* F, i_* i^* F) ≃ Hom(j^* F, j^* i_* i^* F)` is
a singleton, `j^* i_* i^* F` being zero by
`Etale.isZero_upperStar_lowerStar_of_disjoint_range`.

Both maps are components of natural transformations, so the whole complex is natural in `F`;
that is `Etale.openClosedShortComplexFunctor` below.

Blueprint `sk-thm-dnc`: DNC invariance of the section dualizing line

Let `g : V ⟶ B` be smooth of pure relative dimension `d` with a closed section `s`, and let
`N_s ⟶ B` be its normal cone with zero section `0_N`. There is an isomorphism

`𝒞(g, s) ≅ 𝒞(π_N, 0_N)`

between the two section invariants which, in coordinates carrying `(g, s)` to
`(𝔸^d_B → B, 0)`, is the identity on the standard section invariant.

The proof runs the family object `ℱ = Ls̃^* ω_{g̃}` on the deformation space of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.DeformationToNormalConeData`: its fibres at `t = 1` and `t = 0`
are the two section invariants by base change, it is trivialized over `𝔾_{m,B}`, and weak
`𝔸¹`-invariance (`sk-prop-a1-inv`) identifies the two fibres.

*Clause (b), the tensor formula.* For `f` smooth separated of pure relative dimension `d` and
`K ∈ D^b_{ctf}(Y, Λ)`,

`Rf^! K ≅ Lf^* K ⊗^L ω_f`.

blueprint statement is that the mate `φ_K` of the projection formula is this isomorphism.

First half. If `f : X ⟶ Y`, the structure morphism `a_Y : Y ⟶ S` and `a_X = f ≫ a_Y` all
admit a compactification (the last is assumed separately, there being no composition instance
for `HasCompactification`), then the exceptional inverse image along `f` of the dualizing
complex of `Y` is the dualizing complex of `X`:

`Rf^! ω_Y ≅ ω_X`.

`R(a_Y ∘ f)_! ≅ R a_{Y!} ∘ Rf_!`, evaluated at the monoidal unit `Λ_S`.

Blueprint `sk-lem-coprojection`: Co-projection for a closed immersion

For a closed immersion `i : Z ⟶ X`, a complex `K ∈ D^b_{ctf}(X, Λ)` and an object `L` of
`D^b_{ctf}(X, Λ)` that is *invertible*, the canonical co-projection

`Ri^! (K ⊗^L L) ≅ Ri^! K ⊗^L Li^* L`

is an isomorphism: an invertible tensor factor passes through `i^!` at the cost of restricting
it. Testing against an arbitrary `A ∈ D^b_{ctf}(Z, Λ)` and using `Ri_! = Ri_*`, the projection
formula for `Ri_*` and invertibility of `L`, the two Hom-functors agree naturally in `A`, so
Yoneda gives the isomorphism.

Taking `L = Λ_X(m)[2m]`, whose restriction is `Λ_Z(m)[2m]`, this reads
`Ri^!(K(m)[2m]) ≅ (Ri^! K)(m)[2m]`; taking `L = Lf^* B` for `B` invertible on `Y` and
`f' = f ∘ i` it reads `Ri^!(K ⊗ Lf^* B) ≅ Ri^! K ⊗ Lf'^* B`.

AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.nonempty_iso_rig.doc:
Blueprint `sk-lem-sf-mate`: Mate calculus for a pasted adjunction

**The mate of the composition isomorphism.** For composable `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ S`,

```
  R(f ≫ g)_! ≅ Rf_! ⋙ Rg_!           (left adjoints, sk-thm-sf-comp-composition)
        ⊣              ⊣
  R(f ≫ g)^! ≅ Rg^! ⋙ Rf^!           (right adjoints, the mate)
```

the mate of the composition isomorphism is an isomorphism `R(g ∘ f)^! ≅ Rf^! ∘ Rg^!`: the
functoriality of the mate construction turns an isomorphism of left adjoints into one of right
adjoints, and the triangle identities of a composite adjunction are the composites of the
component ones.

This is clause (b) of `sk-lem-sf-mate` in its étale form, for morphisms admitting a
compactification (`sk-prop-sf-existence`(a)). Clause (a), the pro-étale ambient form, is not
formalised. The hypothesis `HasCompactification (f ≫ g)` is redundant over a quasi-compact
quasi-separated base, by Nagata's theorem; it is kept because no composition instance for
`HasCompactification` is available in general.

Blueprint `sk-prop-a1`: Rank-one orientation: the fundamental class of the zero section

For the zero section `s : Y ↪ 𝔸¹_Y` the complex `Rs^! Λ(1)[2]` is concentrated in degree zero
with lisse rank-one `H⁰`; the *fundamental class* `pur_s : Λ_Y ⟶ Rs^! Λ(1)[2]` normalized to
`1` at every geometric point is therefore an isomorphism, and it is the boundary of the
Kummer class `κ(t)`. Since `κ(t)` is not available (see the implementation notes), only the
resulting isomorphism is recorded.

The proof applies `Rp_*` to the localization triangle of the closed–open pair `(s, j)` and
reads off the long exact sequence with `sk-prop-a1-kummer`.

isomorphism.

pairing `β_K`, and concludes that `β_K` is perfect; see the module docstring.

Blueprint `sk-prop-a1-kummer`: The affine line and `𝔾ₘ` with `Λ(1)`-coefficients

*Acyclicity of the affine line*: for the projection `p : 𝔸¹_Y → Y` one has
`Rp_* Λ ≅ Λ_Y`, equivalently `R^m p_* Λ = 0` for `m > 0` and `R⁰p_*Λ = Λ_Y`. Being an
instance of smooth base change, it is compatible with base change on `Y`; on a geometric
fibre it is the vanishing `H^q(𝔸¹_k, μ_{ℓ^N}) = 0` for `q > 0`, which follows from the
Kummer sequence, the divisibility of `k^×` and `Pic(𝔸¹_k) = 0`.

Blueprint `sk-prop-sf-comp-proper`: Proper coincidence

**Proper coincidence.** For `f : X ⟶ Y` proper the identity is a compactification of `f`, and
the resulting canonical identification

`Rf_! ≅ Rf_*`

is independent of the compactification.

At the level of sheaves this is `AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.isIso_lowerShriekToLowerStar`, which
states that the *canonical comparison* `f_! ⟶ f_*` is an isomorphism; the derived comparison
map has not been constructed, so only the existence of the derived isomorphism is recorded
here.

Blueprint `sk-thm-sf-kunneth-relative`: Relative product theorem.

Let `f : X ⟶ B` and `g : Y ⟶ B` be separated of finite type over a base scheme `B`, and let
`K` be in `Dctf(X, A)` and `M` in `Dctf(Y, A)`. Writing `K ⊠ M = Lp^* K ⊗ᴸ Lq^* M` for the
external product over `B` and `f ×_B g : X ×_B Y ⟶ B` for the structure morphism

`R(f ×_B g)_! (K ⊠ M) ⟶ Rf_! K ⊗ᴸ Rg_! M`

in `D(B_ét)` is an isomorphism.
