Blueprint `sk-prop-sf-pf-reduction`: Projection formula: compatibility with finite
reduction

**`Rf_!` commutes with finite reduction.** For an ideal `J` of `Λ`,

`Rf_!(K ⊗^L (Λ/J)_X) ≅ (Rf_! K) ⊗^L (Λ/J)_Y`.

This is one of the three compatibilities out of which the comparison square of
`sk-prop-sf-pf-reduction` is built, and the only one that is not formal; it is what reduces
the projection formula at level `n` to the projection formula at level `m ≤ n`.

Blueprint `sk-prop-sf-pf-reduction`: Projection formula: compatibility with finite
reduction

**`Lf^*` commutes with finite reduction.** For an ideal `J` of `Λ`,

`Lf^*(L ⊗^L (Λ/J)_Y) ≅ (Lf^* L) ⊗^L (Λ/J)_X`,

because `Lf^*` is monoidal and carries the constant complex on `Λ/J` to the constant complex
on `Λ/J`. Together with the associativity of `⊗^L` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.nonempty_iso_reductionModIdeal_rightDerivedLowerShriek` this is what
makes the comparison square of the blueprint commute.

Blueprint `sk-prop-cohsm`: Cohomological smoothness

*Clause (c), smooth base change for `R^!`.* In the cartesian square

```
  X' --g'--> X          Rf^! ⋙ Lg'^*  ≅  Lg^* ⋙ Rf'^!
  |          |
  f'         f          as functors D(Y_ét, Λ) ⥤ D(X'_ét, Λ)
  |          |
  v          v
  Y' --g---> Y
```

with `f` smooth and `f'` its base change along `g`, the formation of `Rf^!` commutes with base
change. Applied to the diagonal square `W = X ×_Y X` this gives `ω_{p₁} ≅ Lp₂^* ω_f` and
`ω_{p₂} ≅ Lp₁^* ω_f`, which is what makes the diagonal computation of the purity theorem
possible.

Blueprint `sk-prop-sf-kunneth-ordinary`: Künneth and the projection formula in ordinary
étale cohomology

**Künneth.** Let `k` be separably closed, let the exponent of `Λ` be invertible on `X` and `Y`
and let `X`, `Y` be finite-type `k`-schemes. For the cartesian square

```
  W --p₂--> Y
  |         |
  p₁        a_Y
  |         |
  v         v
  X --a_X-> Spec k
```

exhibiting `W = X ×_k Y`, the exterior-product map

`RΓ(X, E) ⊗^L RΓ(Y, K) ≅ RΓ(X ×_k Y, Lp₁^* E ⊗^L Lp₂^* K)`

is an isomorphism for all `E ∈ D(X_ét, Λ)` and `K ∈ D(Y_ét, Λ)` — unbounded, and with no
properness hypothesis. Without the cartesian hypothesis the statement is false: for `W = ∅`
and `X = Y = Spec k` the right-hand side is `0` and the left-hand side is `Λ`.

Blueprint `sk-lem-sf-kunneth-star`: Ordinary Künneth with an identity factor.

Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be separated of finite type between schemes over a base `S`, where `X` is
viewed over `S` through `f ≫ b`, and let `c : Z ⟶ S` be a further such scheme, so that `f`
induces `f × 𝟙_Z` across the square

```
  X ×_S Z --f × 𝟙--> Y ×_S Z --pr--> Y
     |                  |            |
     |                  |            f
     v                  v            v
     Z ------c------->  S <----b---- Y
```

`Rf_* M ⊠ Q ⟶ R(f × id_Z)_* (M ⊠ Q)`

is an isomorphism. Here both external products are taken over `S`.

Blueprint `sk-thm-smooth-purity`: Finite-coefficient smooth purity

**Smooth purity, finite coefficients.** For `f : X ⟶ Y` smooth separated of pure relative
dimension `d` and a finite coefficient ring `Λ` whose exponent is invertible on `X`,

`ω_f = Rf^! Λ_Y ≅ Λ_X(d)[2d]`,

canonically, compatibly with base change and additively in the twist under composition of
smooth morphisms.

The proof is the blueprint's five moves: the rank-one computation on `𝔸¹`
(`sk-prop-a1-kummer`, `sk-prop-a1`), its Künneth iteration to `𝔸ⁿ` (`sk-prop-an`), the
deformation to the normal cone of a section (`sk-lem-geometry`, `sk-thm-dnc`), the regularity
of the diagonal (`sk-lem-diag-reg`), and `𝔸¹`-invariance (`sk-prop-a1-inv`).

Blueprint `sk-thm-regular`: Purity for regular closed immersions

**Purity for a regular closed immersion.** Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a regular closed immersion of
pure codimension `c`, with `X` smooth of relative dimension `n` over a perfect field `k` and
`Z` regular — hence, by `AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegularImmersion.smooth_comp`, smooth of relative
dimension `m` where `m + c = n`. There is a canonical isomorphism

`Ri^! Λ_X ≅ Λ_Z(-c)[-2c]`,

the inverse of `cl_i(-c)[-2c]`, where `cl_i : Λ_Z ≅ Ri^! (Λ_X(c)[2c])`, `1 ↦ [Z ⊂ X]`, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.fundamentalClassMap` (an isomorphism by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.isIso_fundamentalClassMap`); it is compatible with étale base change
and with exterior products (`AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.restrictSupportedClass_fundamentalClass`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.fundamentalClass_eq_cupWithSupportsTateObject`).

Smooth purity computes `ω_{a_X}` and `ω_{a_Z}`, and the co-projection formula lets one divide
the former into the latter. The relative dimension of `a_Z` is carried as `m` with
`hm : m + c = n` rather than as `n - c`: truncated subtraction would silently read `0` when
`c > n`.

Blueprint `sk-thm-sf-pf-finite`: Projection formula, finite coefficients

**The projection formula at finite coefficients.** For `Λ` a finite coefficient ring whose
exponent is invertible on `Y`, `f : X ⟶ Y` separated of finite type, `K` bounded constructible
on `X` and `L` bounded constructible *of finite Tor amplitude* on `Y`, the projection map

`PF : Rf_! K ⊗^L L ⟶ Rf_!(K ⊗^L Lf^* L)`

is an isomorphism, naturally in `K` and `L`. The finite Tor amplitude of `L` is essential: the
fibrewise argument represents the stalks of `L` by bounded complexes of finite free modules.

For a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` admitting a compactification, so that `Rf_!` and its right adjoint
`Rf^!` exist, and for `M` in `Dctf(X, A)` and `N` in `Dctf(Y, A)`, the direct image of the
internal hom from `M` into `Rf^! N` agrees with the internal hom on `Y` from `Rf_! M` into `N`:

`Lf^* ⊣ Rf_*` and `- ⊗ᴸ - ⊣ RHom`, together with the projection formula.

Blueprint `sk-thm-sf-global-duality`: Global Verdier duality.

For `X` smooth, proper and geometrically connected of pure relative dimension `d` over `S`,
and `K` an object of `Dctf(X, A)`, the coefficient dual of the compactly supported cohomology
of `K` is the cohomology of the Verdier dual of `K`:

`RΓ_c(X, K)^∨ ≅ RΓ(X, 𝔻_X K)`.

It is stated here for `Ra_{X!} K` and `Ra_{X*} (𝔻_X K)` in `D(S_ét)`; applying `RΓ(S, -)`
gives the displayed form, since `RΓ_c(X/S, -) = RΓ(S, Ra_{X!} -)`.

AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.nonempty_fieldFa.doc:
Blueprint `sk-lem-failure-field`: A failure is detected on the generic fibre.

If the base-change property `BC(p, Λ, q')` holds universally for all `q' < q` while
`BC(p, Λ, q)` fails for some `q ≥ 1`, there is a counterexample over a field, that is, an
`AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.FieldFailure`. Blueprint `sbc-lem-bc-failure-field` only assumes that
`BC(p, Λ, q)` does not hold universally; that form is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.nonempty_fieldFailure_of_not_universalBaseChangeProperty`.

After restricting to an affine open of `S` the base of the failing square is quasi-compact
and quasi-separated. The base-change map is injective there
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.mono_baseChangeHomologyMap`), so some geometric stalk of its target
contains an element `ξ` outside its image, and the minimal-counterexample lemma applied to the
survival of `ξ` produces the field.

higher direct image of an injective sheaf.

subsheaf of an injective sheaf `G`, then the map `R^q h_* e⁻¹ F ⟶ R^q h_* e⁻¹ G` kills the

Blueprint `sk-prop-injectivity` (1): Injectivity of the critical map.

Let `q ≥ 1` and assume `BC(p, Λ, q - 1)`. Then for every Cartesian square

```
Y --e--> T
|        |
h        g
v        v
X --p--> S
```

with `g` quasi-compact quasi-separated and every sheaf `F` of `Λ`-modules on `T_ét`, the
degree-`q` base-change map `p⁻¹ R^q g_* F ⟶ R^q h_* e⁻¹ F` is injective.

Blueprint `sk-prop-sf-trace-perfectness`: Perfectness of compact cohomology and of
geometric stalks

**Boundedness of compactly supported cohomology.** Let `Λ` be a finite coefficient ring, `k`
separably closed, `X` separated of finite type over `k` with structure morphism `a_X`, and
`K ∈ D^b_{ctf}(X, Λ)`. Then `RΓ_c(X, K) = Ra_{X!} K` vanishes in all but finitely many

`H¹_c(Spec ℚ, ℤ/n) = Hom(G_ℚ, ℤ/n)` is infinite.

For a closed immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` and `Q ∈ D^b_{ctf}(Z, Λ)` the unit

`Q ⟶ Ri^! Ri_! Q`

of the exceptional adjunction `AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.rightDerivedUpperShriekAdjunction` is
an isomorphism; since a closed immersion is proper, `Ri_!` is `Ri_*`, so this says that `Ri_*`
is fully faithful on the exceptional side. It is the derived counterpart of the full
faithfulness of `i_*` recorded in `AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.fullyFaithfulLowerStar`.

Blueprint `sk-prop-sf-cbc`: Compact-support base change

**Compact-support base change.** For `f : X ⟶ Y` admitting a compactification, `g : Y' ⟶ Y`
arbitrary, a cartesian square

```
  X' --g'--> X
  |          |
  f'         f
  ↓          ↓
  Y' --g---> Y
```

with `f'` quasi-compact and admitting a compactification, and `Λ` finite, the exchange
transformation `Ex_! : Lg^* Rf_! ⟶ Rf'_! Lg'^*` of `sk-def-sf-exchanges` is an isomorphism of
functors `D(X_ét, Λ) ⥤ D(Y'_ét, Λ)`.

`Ex_!` is `Ex_!(c)` for the chosen compactification `c` of `f`, followed by the comparison
isomorphism `AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.rightDerivedLowerShriekIso` for `f'`, so this follows from
`AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.isIso_rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationBaseChangeMap_of_finite`.
That comparison isomorphism rests on the unproved instance
`AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.isIso_rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationComparison`, which is not
expected to hold on unbounded derived categories in this generality; the blueprint states this
theorem on `D⁺`. If `f` is quasi-compact, `[QuasiCompact f']` is obtained from `sq` by
`MorphismProperty.of_isPullback`.

**The proper base change theorem** in étale cohomology: for a cartesian square of
schemes

```
X' --g'--> X
|          |
f'         f
v          v
Y' --g---> Y
```

with `f` proper and every bounded below complex `K ∈ D⁺(X_ét, Λ)` all of whose
cohomology sheaves are torsion, the derived base change map

`BC_sq(K) : g^*(Rf_* K) ⟶ Rf'_*(g'^* K)`

is an isomorphism in `D⁺(Y'_ét, Λ)`. No hypothesis is imposed on `g`. For `Λ = ℤ` this
is [SGA 4, Exp. XII, Thm 5.1] and Stacks Project, Tag 0DDE; the case of a general
coefficient ring follows by restriction of scalars.

**The smooth base change theorem** in étale cohomology: for a Cartesian square

```

|        |
h        g
```

**The projective line satisfies base change**: for every scheme `S`, the projection
`ℙ¹_S ⟶ S` satisfies `AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.HasTorsionBaseChange`, that is, for every
cartesian square

```
ℙ¹_T --g'--> ℙ¹_S
  |            |
  p'           p
  v            v
  T ---g-----> S
```

the derived base change map is an isomorphism on every bounded below complex with torsion
cohomology. This is the geometric half of the proof of proper base change; see the module
docstring, and Stacks Project, Tag 095T, whose proof it is.
(blueprint: `prop:weil-pbc-projective-line`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.hasTorsionBaseCh.doc:
**Reduction of proper base change to the projective line**: if the projection
`ℙ¹_S ⟶ S` satisfies `AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.HasTorsionBaseChange` for every scheme `S`,
then so does every proper morphism of schemes.

The proof is Chow's lemma: a proper `f : X ⟶ Y` is dominated by a projective one,

```
       X̃ ------------> ℙⁿ_Y
       |                |
     π |                | pₙ
       v                v
       X ------ f ----> Y
```

with `π` proper surjective and the horizontal arrow a closed immersion over `Y`; the base
change property for `pₙ` comes from that of `ℙ¹` by the symmetric-product morphism, and
transfers to `f` because it composes and cancels along proper surjections. See the module
docstring for the steps, and for the noetherian-freeness of the Chow factorisation the
statement uses.
(blueprint: `prop:weil-pbc-reduction-to-projective-line`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.hasTorsionBaseCh.doc:
**The base change property is injective acyclicity**: for a proper morphism `f : X ⟶ Y`
and a coefficient ring `Λ` which is torsion as an additive group, the two properties of the
preceding definitions agree. That is, for every cartesian square

```
X' --g'--> X
|          |
f'         f
v          v
Y' --g---> Y
```

the derived base change map is an isomorphism on every bounded below complex if and only if
`Rᵠf'_*(g'^{-1} I) = 0` for `q > 0` and every injective sheaf `I` on `X_ét`.

For `PBC ⇒ IA`, apply `PBC` to the complex `I[0]` concentrated in degree `0`: its source
`g^*(Rf_* I[0]) = g^*(f_* I)[0]` is again concentrated in degree `0` because `I` is
injective, hence so is the target `Rf'_*(g'^{-1} I)`, which is the required vanishing. The
converse resolves a torsion sheaf by injectives, uses `IA` to see that the resolution stays
`f'_*`-acyclic after base change, and compares the two complexes termwise by the underived
exchange morphism, which is an isomorphism because at a geometric point of `Y'` both sides
are sections over the same proper geometric fibre.
(blueprint: `sk-thm-iff`, `lemma-weil-pbc-property-iff-acyclicity`)

**Finite Tor amplitude means a bounded flat model.** For `K ∈ D^b_c(X, Λ)` and integers
`a ≤ b` the following are equivalent: `K` has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]`; and `K` is isomorphic
to a bounded flat complex `P` in degrees `[a, b]`.

bounded-above free resolution and checks that the truncation is flat by the Tor criterion.

Blueprint `sk-thm-sf-kunneth-verdier`: Künneth–Verdier isomorphism.

The four product comparison maps of `AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.HasKunnethComparisons` are
isomorphisms: besides the `!`-Künneth map `Ku_!`, which is an isomorphism by construction,
this asserts the invertibility of the exceptional Künneth map `α`, of the external Hom map
`β`, and of the Künneth–Verdier map `κ`.

The headline case is `kunnethVerdier`: for `X` and `Y` separated of finite type over `S`,
with projections `p_X : X ×_S Y ⟶ X` and `p_Y : X ×_S Y ⟶ Y`, and for `M` in `Dctf(X, A)`
and `N` in `Dctf(Y, A)`,

`κ : M ⊠ 𝔻_Y N ≅ RHom(p_Y^* N, Rp_X^! M)`

on `X ×_S Y`, where `𝔻_Y = RHom(-, ω_Y)` is the Verdier dual relative to `b : Y ⟶ S`.

AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.fourierTransform.doc:
For a pairing `b ∈ Γ(V ×_S V', 𝒪)` between two `S`-schemes and a relative dimension `r`,
the *Fourier–Deligne transform* is

`FT_ψ(K) = Rp₂,!(p₁^* K ⊗ᴸ 𝒦_ψ)[r]`,

the kernel transform of the Fourier kernel `𝒦_ψ` with shift `r`. The shift is part of the
definition: it is Laumon's normalization, for which the inversion theorem holds up to the
Tate twist `(-r)` and no further shift. The transform attached to the inverse character is
the same construction with `Ψ⁻¹` in place of `Ψ`; its kernel is the inverse of `𝒦_ψ` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.nonempty_iso_artinSchreierSheafOf_inv`. Like the kernel, it is
defined for every commutative ring `Λ` in which `p` is invertible; torsion coefficients are
only assumed by the theorems that need them.
(sketch blueprint: `sk-def-ft`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.fourierKernel.doc:
For a pairing `b ∈ Γ(V ×_S V', 𝒪)` between two `S`-schemes, the *Fourier kernel* `𝒦_ψ`
is the Artin–Schreier sheaf `ℒ_{Ψ, b} = b^* ℒ_Ψ` of the pairing, the pullback of the
Artin–Schreier sheaf of `𝔸¹` along `b : V ×_S V' ⟶ 𝔸¹`. On the affine line over a field, with
`V = V' = 𝔸¹` and the pairing the product `x ξ`, this is the sheaf usually written
`ℒ_{ψ(xξ)}`.

Being an Artin–Schreier sheaf, it is lisse of rank one
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.isLocallyConstantSheaf_artinSchreierSheafOf`) and multiplicative in
the character (`AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.nonempty_iso_artinSchreierSheafOf_mul`), with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.nonempty_iso_artinSchreierSheafOf_inv` identifying `𝒦_ψ⁻¹` with
`𝒦_{ψ⁻¹}`. It is defined for every commutative ring `Λ` in which `p` is invertible.
(sketch blueprint: `sk-def-kernel`, `sk-prop-kernel-lisse`)

Blueprint `sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation`: Preservation for the exceptional inverse
image.

Clause (iv), dimension-free form with the shift forgotten: every separated finite-type `f`
admitting a compactification, over a Noetherian `Y`, preserves the constructible intervals up
to a single shift `c`, depending only on `f`, widening every interval `[a, b]` to
`[a - c, b + c]`. When `dim Y ≤ d` this follows from the preceding theorem, with
`c = max(2D, 2d + 1)`. Under the blueprint's standing hypothesis (finite type over a
field) `dim Y` is always finite, but this repository cannot yet prove that, so no dimension
hypothesis is imposed here: clause (v) of `sk-thm-sf-ctf-stability`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.constructibleFiniteTor_rightDerivedUpperShriek`) is proved from it.

integral normal scheme — normality being spelled out as the hypothesis `hS` that every stalk of
`S` is integrally closed — whose function field `S.functionField` is separably closed, and let
`p : V ⟶ S` be separated and étale. Then `V` is the disjoint union of a family of opens `U i`
each of which maps isomorphically onto an open of `S`.

AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.exists_isPullbac.doc:
**Étale morphisms lift locally along a closed immersion.** If `i : Z ⟶ X` is a closed
immersion and `p : W ⟶ Z` is étale, then every point `w` of `W` has an open neighbourhood `W₀`
which is the base change along `i` of a scheme `V` étale over `X`, in a way compatible with `p`:
the square
```
W₀ ------- a -------> V
|                     |
W₀.ι ≫ p              q
↓                     ↓
Z ------- i --------> X
```
is cartesian.

Blueprint `sk-lem-universal-datum`: Universal curve-test datum for a failure.

Let `p : X ⟶ S` be an affine smooth relative curve with `X` affine, and let `n` be invertible
on `S` and annihilate `Λ`. If `BC(p, Λ, q')` holds universally for all `q' < q` but
`BC(p, Λ, q)` fails for some `q ≥ 1`, there is a curve-test datum `D` which is a base change of
`p`, whose torsion order `D.d` divides `n`, and on whose geometric generic fibre the higher
direct image `R^q h_* (Λ/D.d Λ)` of the constant sheaf does not vanish.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.exists_isPullback_not_isZero_higherDirectImage`: affine
smooth morphisms of relative dimension one are stable under base change, and `d` is invertible
on the new base since it divides `n`.

AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.eq_of_leftDerive.doc:
Blueprint `sk-prop-a1-inv`: Weak `𝔸¹`-invariance

*Invariance along the line.* A comparison between an invertible complex `F` on `𝔸¹_Y` and a
pullback from `Y` is determined by its restriction to the unit section `t = 1`: two
isomorphisms `α, β : F ≅ Lp^* C` with `Li₁^* α = Li₁^* β` are equal. Consequently the
identifications `Li₀^* F ≅ C ≅ Li₁^* F` obtained from such a comparison are canonical, and the
invariant is *constant* along the `𝔸¹`-direction: its values at `t = 0` and at `t = 1` agree.

Invertibility of `F` is what puts the comparison inside the lisse rank-one world in which the
uniqueness statements above apply; it is the hypothesis `sk-prop-a1-inv` (ii) imposes, in the
weaker form available here (the blueprint asks that `F` be étale-locally a shift and twist of
a lisse rank-one sheaf).

**`Rf^!` preserves derived completeness.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be smooth separated of pure
relative dimension `d` and let `Λ = 𝒪_E` be the integral coefficient stage. Then `Rf^!`
carries derived-complete objects of `D(Y_ét, 𝒪_E)` to derived-complete objects of
`D(X_ét, 𝒪_E)`, so that it restricts to the adic categories `D_comp(−, 𝒪_E)` in which the

`sk-thm-smooth-purity` read at `Λ = 𝒪_E`, and applying
`AlgebraicGeometry.DerivedCategoryDerivedCompleteRational.fromIntegral` gives it over `E`.

on the unbounded derived categories of étale sheaves, as a natural transformation
`Rf_* ⋙ Lg^* ⟶ Lg'^* ⋙ Rf'_*`: the mate of the derived square isomorphism
`AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.derivedSquareUpperStarIso` with respect to the derived adjunctions
`Lf^* ⊣ Rf_*` and `Lf'^* ⊣ Rf'_*`. This is the exchange map `Ex_*` of `sk-def-sf-exchanges`.

```
  D(X) --Lg'^*--> D(X')
   |               |
  Rf_*   ⇓ Ex_*   Rf'_*
   ↓               ↓
  D(Y) --Lg^*---> D(Y')
```

(blueprint: `def:weil-pbc-derived-exchange-unbounded`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.ctf_generated_by.doc:
Blueprint `sk-lem-sf-ctf-generation`: Finite/open generation of `Dctf`.

Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme and `Λ` a finite ring. Then `Dctf(X, Λ)` is generated as a
thick subcategory by the objects `Rg_* Rj_! L`, where `U` is a stratum of a stratification of
`X`, `j : U ⟶ Ū` is the open immersion of `U` into its closure, `g : Ū ⟶ X` is the closed
immersion of that closure, and `L` is a lisse (finite locally constant) flat sheaf of
`Λ`-modules on `U`. Note the order: lower-star outside lower-shriek.

"Thick subcategory generated by" is unwound here: any property `P` of objects of `D(X_ét, Λ)`
that is triangulated, stable under retracts and closed under isomorphisms, and that holds for
all the generators above, holds for every object of `Dctf(X, Λ)`.

The lisse coefficients cannot be replaced by constant ones `Λ_U`: for `X = 𝔾_m`, `p ≠ 2` and
`Λ = 𝔽₃`, the complexes whose generic-stalk cohomology has only trivial `π₁`-composition factors
form a thick subcategory containing every `Rg_* Rj_! Λ_U` but not the order-`2` Kummer sheaf.

The proof resolves `K` by a bounded complex of flat constructible sheaves
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.hasTorAmplitudeIn_iff_exists_flatConstructibleModel`), reduces to one
flat constructible sheaf `F` by the stupid-truncation triangles, and then uses the open–closed
sequence `0 ⟶ j_!(F|_U) ⟶ F ⟶ i_* i^* F ⟶ 0` for a dense open `U` on which `F` is lisse,
together with Noetherian induction on the closed subsets of `X`.

Blueprint `sk-prop-deg0`: Degree-zero flat base change.

For a Cartesian square

```
Y --e--> T
|        |
h        g
v        v
X --p--> S
```

with `g` quasi-compact quasi-separated and `p` flat, locally of finite presentation and with
geometrically reduced fibres, the degree-zero base-change map `p⁻¹ g_* F ⟶ h_* e⁻¹ F` is an
isomorphism for *every* sheaf `F` of `Λ`-modules on `T_ét`: no torsion hypothesis is needed in
degree zero. This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.isIso_baseChangeMap_app_of_flat`, transferred
to the derived base-change map by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.nonempty_arrowIso_baseChangeHomologyMap_zero`.

AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.baseChange.doc:
The *derived base-change morphism* `BC_sq : Lg^* ∘ Rf_* ⟶ Rf'_* ∘ Lg'^*` of a
commutative square `g' ≫ f = f' ≫ g` of schemes on the bounded below derived
categories, assembled as the composite of the unit insertion, the square transport, and
the counit contraction.

Proper base change and smooth base change assert that this single morphism is an
isomorphism under two different sets of geometric hypotheses; no such hypothesis is
built into the definition.

`(AS_q)_* Λ`, that is, the `Ψ`-isotypic component of the pushforward of the constant sheaf
along the Artin–Schreier map `AS_q : 𝔸¹_k ⟶ 𝔸¹_k`.
(sketch blueprint: `sk-def-as`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.WeilComplex.doc:
Blueprint `sk-def-sf-weil-complexes`: Strict Weil complexes.

A *strict Weil complex* at `Λ` on `X` is a pair `(K, φ)` consisting of an object `K` of
`Dctf(X, Λ)` — a bounded constructible complex of finite Tor amplitude — together with an
isomorphism `φ : Lg^* K ≅ K`, where `g` is the geometric-Frobenius automorphism of
`X = X₀ ×_{k₀} k`.

The automorphism `g` is a parameter here: its construction from a model `X₀` over a finite
field `k₀` and a Frobenius `γ` of `k` over `k₀` belongs to a different blueprint block.

Strict Weil complexes form a category `D^b_{ctf,W}(X, Λ)`, whose morphisms are the morphisms
of the underlying complexes commuting with the two `φ`s, with a forgetful functor
`AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.WeilComplex.forget` to `Dctf(X, Λ)`.

AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.SixOperationsPac.doc:
Blueprint `sk-thm-sf-package`: The six-operations package.

Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a separated finite-type morphism of schemes over a base `S`, with
`a_Y : Y ⟶ S` the structure morphism of `Y` and `a_X = f ≫ a_Y` that of `X`, all three
admitting compactifications. The eight clauses of the blueprint, one group of fields each:

1. **Adjunctions.** `Lf^* ⊣ Rf_*` and `Rf_! ⊣ Rf^!`.
2. **Base change.** For a Cartesian square

   ```
     X' --g'--> X
     |          |
     f'         f
     v          v
     Y' --g---> Y
   ```

   one has `Lg^* Rf_! ≅ Rf'_! Lg'^*`; and `Lg^* Rf_* ≅ Rf'_* Lg'^*` for proper `f` and for
   smooth `g`.
3. **Projection formula.** `Rf_!(K ⊗ᴸ Lf^* L) ≅ Rf_! K ⊗ᴸ L` at every `K` and `L`.
4. **Compactifications and proper coincidence.** `Rf_!` is independent of the compactification,
   `R(f ≫ h)_! ≅ Rh_! Rf_!`, and `Rf_! ≅ Rf_*` for proper `f`.
5. **Orientation.** A smooth `f` of pure relative dimension `d` carries an orientation
   `Rf^! Λ_Y ≅ Lf^* Λ_Y (d)[2d]`.
6. **Duality.** `𝔻_X 𝔻_X ≅ id` on `Dctf(X, A)`, and the Verdier exchange
   `𝔻_Y Rf_! ≅ Rf_* 𝔻_X`.
7. **Relative product.** The four Künneth comparisons over `S` are isomorphisms.
8. **Stability.** `Lf^*`, `- ⊗ᴸ -`, `Rf_*`, `Rf_!`, `Rf^!` and `𝔻_X` carry `Dctf` into
   `Dctf`.

See the module docstring for the clauses that are deliberately not carried here.

Blueprint `sk-thm-sf-dual-perfect`: The dual of a perfect complex.

Let `a : X ⟶ S` be a structure morphism admitting a compactification, let `o` be an
orientation of `a` of relative dimension `d`, and let `K` be perfect over `Λ_X`, i.e.
dualizable. Substituting `ω_X ≅ Λ_X(d)[2d]` into `𝔻_X K = RHom_X(K, ω_X)` and interchanging
the twist with the internal hom identifies the Verdier dual of `K` with the twisted, shifted
coefficient dual: `𝔻_X K ≅ K^∨(d)[2d]`.

Blueprint `sk-def-sf-orientation`: Orientation: an interface record.

The special case of the orientation at the structure morphism `a : X ⟶ S`. There
`La^* Λ_S ≅ Λ_X` is the monoidal unit
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.nonempty_iso_leftDerivedUpperStar_unit`) and `Ra^! Λ_S` is by
definition the dualizing complex, so the purity isomorphism reads
```
ω_X ═══ Ra^! Λ_S ≅ T[2d]
```
for the twist `T` of `o` (`Λ_X(d)` for a Tate twist): the dualizing complex of a smooth `X` of
pure relative dimension `d` over `S` is a shifted Tate twist.

AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.Orientation.doc:
Blueprint `sk-def-sf-orientation`: Orientation: an interface record.

An *orientation* of relative dimension `d` for a smooth separated morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of
finite type is a Tate twist `Λ_X(d)` — an invertible object of `D(X_ét)` — together with an
isomorphism `γ : Lf^* Λ_Y (d)[2d] ≅ Rf^! Λ_Y`.

In the blueprint an orientation is **not** an assumption: it is the smooth purity theorem
`sk-thm-smooth-purity`, which lives in a different blueprint block and is not formalised here.
This structure therefore records only the interface that purity produces and that the six
operations consume; the blueprint's naturality in `Y` and its compatibilities with composition,
étale base change, finite reduction, scalar extension and the pro-étale realization quantify
over data that this block does not have and are not among its fields.

For the structure morphism `f = a_X` the isomorphism reads `ω_X ≅ Λ_X(d)[2d]`; see
`AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.Orientation.nonempty_iso_dualizingComplex`.

AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.IsBaseChangeIso.doc:
**The proper base change property** for the coefficients `A`: for every cartesian square
```
  X' --g'--> X
  |          |
  f'         f
  ↓          ↓
  Y' --g---> Y
```
the derived base change map `g^* Rf_* ⟶ Rf'_* g'^*` on `D⁺` is an isomorphism.
(blueprint: `def:weil-pbc-property`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.HasTorsionBaseCh.doc:
**The base change property** `PBC(f)` of a morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ Y`, for torsion
coefficients: for every cartesian square

```
X' --g'--> X
|          |
f'         f
v          v
Y' --g---> Y
```

and every object `K` of `D⁺(X_ét, Λ)` whose cohomology sheaves are all torsion, the derived
base change map `BC_sq(K) : g^*(Rf_* K) ⟶ Rf'_*(g'^* K)` is an isomorphism. No hypothesis is
imposed on `g`, and none on `f`: the proper base change theorem says that `PBC(f)` holds
whenever `f` is proper.

This is the restriction to torsion cohomology of `AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.IsBaseChangeIso`,
which is the declaration realising the blueprint's `def:weil-pbc-property`; see the module
docstring.

AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.HasKunnethCompar.doc:
Blueprint `sk-def-sf-kv-maps`: The product comparison maps.

The four product comparison maps of the six-functor formalism over a base scheme `S`, each
recorded as the assertion that it is an isomorphism. All external products are taken over
`S`.

* `kunnethShriek` is the `!`-Künneth map
  `Ku_! : Rf_! (M₁ ⊠ M₂) ⟶ Rf_{1!} M₁ ⊠ Rf_{2!} M₂` for `f = f₁ × f₂`, which is
  `AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.nonempty_iso_rightDerivedLowerShriek_externalProduct` for the base
  `Y₁ ×_S Y₂`, using `X₁ ×_S X₂ = (X₁ ×_S Y₂) ×_{Y₁ ×_S Y₂} (Y₁ ×_S X₂)`; it is an
  isomorphism *by construction*, being built out of isomorphisms;
* `exceptional` is the exceptional Künneth map
  `α : Rf₁^! N₁ ⊠ Rf₂^! N₂ ⟶ Rf^! (N₁ ⊠ N₂)`, the exceptional adjoint of `Ku_!` followed by
  the two counits of `Rf_{i!} ⊣ Rf_i^!`;
* `externalHom` is the external Hom map
  `β : RHom(E₁, N₁) ⊠ RHom(E₂, N₂) ⟶ RHom(E₁ ⊠ E₂, N₁ ⊠ N₂)`, the tensor–Hom transpose of
  the two evaluation maps;
* `kunnethVerdier` is the Künneth–Verdier map
  `κ : M ⊠ 𝔻_Y N ⟶ RHom(p_Y^* N, Rp_X^! M)` on `X ×_S Y`, the composite of `β` applied to the
  pairs `(Λ_X, M)` and `(N, ω_Y)` with `RHom(1, α)` for `id_X × a_Y`, using the unit
  identifications `RHom(Λ_X, M) = M` and `Λ_X ⊠ N = p_Y^* N`.

Only `Ku_!` is built from isomorphisms; that `α`, `β` and `κ` are invertible is the content of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.hasKunnethComparisons`, i.e. of `sk-thm-sf-kunneth-verdier`.

AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.HasInjectiveAcyc.doc:
**Injective acyclicity** `IA(f)` of a morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ Y`: for every
cartesian square

```
X' --g'--> X
|          |
f'         f
v          v
Y' --g---> Y
```

and every *injective torsion* sheaf `I` of `Λ`-modules on `X_ét`, the higher direct images
of its pullback vanish: `Rᵠf'_*(g'^{-1} I) = 0` for `q > 0`. Here `Rᵠf'_* G` is the `q`-th
cohomology sheaf of `Rf'_*` applied to `G` placed in degree `0`.

The restriction to torsion `I` is what makes `PBC(f) ⇒ IA(f)` correct over a coefficient
ring which is not itself torsion: `PBC(f)` constrains only objects with torsion cohomology.
For a torsion `Λ` — the case in which the two properties are compared below — every sheaf of
`Λ`-modules is torsion and the restriction is vacuous.

This is the form in which the proper base change theorem is actually proved: it is a
vanishing statement about a single sheaf, it composes, it cancels along proper surjections,
and it can be checked on geometric stalks.
(blueprint: `def:weil-pbc-injective-acyclicity-property`)

AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.FieldFailure.doc:
A counterexample to `BC(p, Λ, q)` living over a field: an affine scheme `S'` over `S`,
the base change `p' : X' ⟶ S'` of `p` along it, a field `K` over `S'`, and a sheaf `F`
of `Λ`-modules on `(Spec K)_ét` for which the degree-`q` base-change map of the geometric
fibre square is not an isomorphism. The two squares are stacked:

```
Y' -----e-----> Spec K
|                 |
h                 g
v                 v
X' -----p'-----> S'
|                 |
b                 a
v                 v
X ------p------>  S
```

When `S` is separated the base change `a : S' ⟶ S` is affine, see
`AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.FieldFailure.isAffineHom_a`.

AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.CurveTestDatum.i.doc:
Blueprint `sk-thm-vanishing`: Vanishing in the universal curve test.

For a curve-test datum `D` — an affine smooth relative curve `f₀ : X₀ ⟶ S₀` over an affine
integral normal base with algebraically closed function field, together with the fibre

```
Y₀ ---e---> Spec K
|              |
h              |
v              v
X₀ ---f₀----> S₀
```

over a geometric generic point and an integer `d` invertible on `S₀` — the higher direct
images `R^q h_* (Λ/dΛ)` of the constant sheaf vanish for every `q ≥ 1`.

This is also blueprint `sbc-thm-universal-test-vanishing`. It is a recombination of the lemmas
of Stacks, Étale Cohomology, Section 59.88 rather than a single tagged one. By
`AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.isZero_higherDirectImage_constantModSheaf_of_forall_exists` it
suffices to kill every class of `H^q(Y₀ ×_{X₀} U, ℤ/e)`, `e ∣ d`, on an étale cover of the
affine étale `U ⟶ X₀`. For `q ≥ 2` these groups vanish, `Y₀ ×_{X₀} U` being a smooth affine
curve over `K`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_sheafH_constantZMod_and_nonempty_addEquiv_sheafH_zero`,
blueprint `sbc-thm-cohomological-dimension-of-an-affine-curve`); the case `q = 1` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.CurveTestDatum.exists_cover_cohomologyMap_eq_zero`.

AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.CurveTestDatum.doc:
A *curve-test datum*: an affine smooth relative curve `f₀ : X₀ ⟶ S₀` over an affine,
integral, normal base with algebraically closed function field, together with its fibre over
a geometric generic point `Spec K ⟶ S₀` and an integer `d` invertible on `S₀`:

```
Y₀ ---e---> Spec K
|              |
h              |
v              v
X₀ ---f₀----> S₀
```

the right-hand column being `Spec` of an extension `i` of the function field of `S₀`
followed by the inclusion of the generic point. Normality of `S₀` is spelled out as integral
closedness of all its stalks, there being no `IsNormal` predicate on schemes.

Blueprint `sk-def-bc`: The recorded base-change property.

`BC(p, Λ, q)` holds when, for every quasi-compact quasi-separated `g : T ⟶ S`, every sheaf
`F` of `Λ`-modules on `T_ét` and every Cartesian square

```
Y --e--> T
|        |
h        g
v        v
X --p--> S
```

the base-change map `p⁻¹ R^q g_* F ⟶ R^q h_* e⁻¹ F` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.baseChangeHomologyMap` is an isomorphism. The coefficient ring `Λ`
plays the role of `ℤ/nℤ` in the blueprint; the hypothesis that `n` be invertible on `S` is
not part of the property and is carried separately by the statements that need it.

AlgebraicGeometry.ChowModification.nonem.doc:
**Chow's lemma**: a separated morphism of finite type over a Noetherian scheme admits a
Chow modification.

Steps 1 and 2 of Stacks' proof produce a reduction `R` of `f` (`AlgebraicGeometry.ChowReduction`)
with a nonempty finite affine open cover `R.U`, step 3 a proper closed model `M i` of each
member of the cover, step 4 the graph `ChowGraph M` of the family, and step 5 the modification
`ChowGraph.modificationMap M` obtained by gluing the projections of the graph. It remains to
check that the latter is proper (it is proper over each `R.U i`, which cover), surjective (it
is universally closed and dominant, the dense open `U∞` mapping isomorphically onto
`⋂ i, R.U i`) and an isomorphism over `⋂ i, R.U i` (the open `U∞` of `X'` is dense in the
preimage of `⋂ i, R.U i` and proper over it, hence all of it); step 7 is the closed immersion
of the graph into a single projective space over `S`.
(blueprint: `thm:chow-lemma`)

**Chow's lemma for proper morphisms**: if `f : X ⟶ S` is proper, the immersion of its Chow
modification into projective space is a *closed* immersion. Together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.ChowModification.isProper_modificationMap` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.ChowModification.surjective_modificationMap` this says that a proper scheme
over a Noetherian base is dominated by a projective one.

Indeed, `toProjectiveSpace f` composed with the structure morphism of `ℙ(index f; S)` is the
proper morphism `modificationMap f ≫ f`, and the structure morphism is separated, so
`toProjectiveSpace f` is itself proper, hence universally closed.
(blueprint: `cor:chow-lemma-proper`)

The **Chow modification** `X'` of a separated morphism of finite type `f : X ⟶ S` over a
Noetherian scheme `S`: a scheme with a proper surjective morphism to `X` which is an
isomorphism over a dense open subset of `X`, and an immersion into a projective space over

```
                     toProjectiveSpace
  ChowModification f -----------------> ℙ(index f; S)
          |                                   |
          | modificationMap                   | ↘
          ↓                                   ↓
          X ------------- f ----------------> S
```

commute.

AlgebraicGeometry.ChowGraph.proj.doc:
**The projection of the graph onto the `i`-th closed model.** It is the unique morphism
`pᵢ : Z ⟶ Mᵢ.Z` compatible with the `i`-th projection `∏_S ℙ(Mⱼ.n; S) ⟶ ℙ(Mᵢ.n; S)`; it exists
by the universal property of the closed immersion `Mᵢ.Z ⟶ ℙ(Mᵢ.n; S)`, because the composition
of the tuple morphism with the `i`-th projection factors through `Mᵢ.Z` by construction and
`U∞` is scheme-theoretically dense in `Z`.

  (TopologicalSpace.Opens.map (AlgebraicGeometry.ChowGraph.modificationMap M).base).obj (U i) =

AlgebraicGeometry.ChowGraph.preimage_mod.doc:
**The fibre of the modification over `Uᵢ` is `Vᵢ`.**

The inclusion `Vᵢ ⊆ π⁻¹(Uᵢ)` is proper over `Uᵢ`, hence universally closed since `π⁻¹(Uᵢ)`
is separated over `Uᵢ`; and `Vᵢ` contains `U∞`, which is dense in `X'`. So `Vᵢ` is a closed
dense open subscheme of `π⁻¹(Uᵢ)`, hence all of it.
(blueprint: `lem:chow-preimage`)

**The modification `π : X' ⟶ X`** obtained by gluing the restrictions
`pᵢ|_{Vᵢ} : Vᵢ ⟶ Uᵢ ⊆ X` of the projections of the graph over the open
`X' = ⋃ i, Vᵢ` of the graph.

The morphisms being glued agree on the scheme-theoretically dense open `U∞`, where they are
all the inclusion of `U∞` in `X`, and `X` is separated over `S`; this is enough by rigidity
of morphisms into a separated scheme.
(blueprint: `lem:chow-glue`)

AlgebraicGeometry.ChowGraph.isProper_mor.doc: **The modification is proper over each member of the family.**

  ∃ N,
    ∃ (_ : Finite N),

AlgebraicGeometry.ChowGraph.exists_isClo.doc:
**The graph is a closed subscheme of a single projective space over `S`.** Composing the
closed immersion `Z ⟶ ∏_S ℙ(Mᵢ.n; S)` of `AlgebraicGeometry.ChowGraph.emb` with the `m`-fold
Segre embedding `AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpace.exists_isClosedImmersion_pi` yields a closed
immersion of `Z` into a projective space `ℙ(N; S)` with `N` finite, compatible with the
structure morphisms over `S`.

The index type `ι` of the cover lives in an arbitrary universe, while the Segre embedding is
stated for an index type in the universe of the schemes; the two are matched up by reindexing
the product along an equivalence `ι ≃ ULift.{u} (Fin k)`.

AlgebraicGeometry.ChowGraph.emb.doc: The closed immersion of the graph into the product `∏_S ℙ(Mᵢ.n; S)`.

AlgebraicGeometry.ChowGraph.doc:
**The graph of a finite open cover**: the scheme-theoretic image `Z` of the tuple
morphism `U∞ = ⋂ i, Uᵢ ⟶ ∏_S ℙ(Mᵢ.n; S)` assembled from the closed models `Mᵢ` of the members
of the cover.

It is a closed subscheme of `∏_S ℙ(Mᵢ.n; S)` (`AlgebraicGeometry.ChowGraph.emb`), hence proper
over `S` (`AlgebraicGeometry.ChowGraph.isProper_over`), it contains `U∞` as a
scheme-theoretically dense open subscheme (`AlgebraicGeometry.ChowGraph.toGraph`) and it maps
properly to each closed model (`AlgebraicGeometry.ChowGraph.proj`).

AlgebraicGeometry.BoundaryDatum.isPunctu.doc:
Blueprint `sk-p-real-semi`: Semi-continuity of weights.

The consequence of the weight bound for `j_* ℱ`: a lisse Weil sheaf `𝒢` on a smooth
geometrically connected curve `C₀` whose restriction to the open `U₀` is punctually `ι`-pure of
weight `w` is punctually `ι`-pure of weight `w` on all of `C₀`.

At a closed point of `U₀` this is the hypothesis, the local Frobenius of `C₀` being conjugate to
the image of that of `U₀`. At a boundary point `s`, inertia acts trivially on `𝒢`, which is lisse
on `C₀`, so its stalk is the whole local representation, with Frobenius the restriction of the
residue Frobenius lift; the bound for `j_* ℱ`, applied to `𝒢` and to its dual `𝒢 ^ ∨`, whose
eigenvalues are the inverses of those of `𝒢`, gives an upper bound `w` and a lower bound `w`
(`cor-wf-unramified-boundary-purity`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.BoundaryDatum.frobeniusWeight_eq_of_isPunctuallyPure`). As there, the
Euler-product form of the trace formula is the hypothesis `hD`, without which the statement is
false.

AlgebraicGeometry.BoundaryDatum.frobeniu.doc:
Blueprint `sk-p-real-semi`: Semi-continuity of weights.

For a boundary datum `D` on a smooth geometrically connected curve `C₀`, if the lisse Weil sheaf
`ℱ` on `U₀` has weights at most `w`, then `j_* ℱ` has weights at most `w` on `C₀`. Concretely:
at a boundary point `s`, the residue Frobenius acts on the boundary stalk `V ^ (I_s)`, and every
one of its eigenvalues `α`, witnessed by a nonzero invariant eigenvector `v`, has `ι`-weight at
most `w` relative to the residue cardinality `q_s`.

Shrinking to an affine neighbourhood, the counting bound `N_e ≤ A q ^ e` for closed points of
degree `e` shows that `L_ι (U₀, ℱ, T)⁻¹` has radius at least `q ^ (-(w + 2) / 2)`, while the
open–closed sequence identifies `H_c² (C, j_* ℱ)` with a coinvariant Tate twist whose
eigenvalues are bounded by `q ^ ((w + 2) / 2)`. The trace formula then confines the zeros of
the boundary factor, giving the preliminary bound `|ι α| ≤ q_s ^ ((w + 2) / 2)`; applying it
to the tensor powers `ℱ ^ ⊗ n`, whose boundary stalks receive `(V ^ (I_s)) ^ ⊗ n`, improves it
to `|ι α| ≤ q_s ^ (w / 2 + 1 / n)` for every `n`, and `n → ∞` finishes
(`AlgebraicGeometry.BoundaryDatum.frobeniusWeight_le_of_hasEigenvalue_boundaryFrobenius`).

The curve `C₀` is smooth and geometrically connected and `ℓ ≠ char 𝔽_q`, as in the setting
`sk-d-real-setup` of the block, and `ℱ` is lisse. The trace formula used in the proof, in its
Euler-product form for middle extensions (`lem-wf-euler-product-middle-extension`), is the
hypothesis `hD`: it does not follow from the fields of a `BoundaryDatum`, and without it the
statement is false (see `AlgebraicGeometry.BoundaryDatum.HasMiddleExtensionEulerProduct`).

AlgebraicGeometry.BoundaryDatum.boundary.doc:
Blueprint `sk-d-real-boundary`: Boundary extension and inertia.

The boundary stalk of `J = j_* ℱ` at a geometric point over a boundary point `s`: the inertia
invariants `V^{I_s}` of the local generic stalk `V`. The residue Frobenius lift
`AlgebraicGeometry.BoundaryDatum.residueFrobenius` normalises `I_s`, hence acts on it
unambiguously.

AlgebraicGeometry.BoundaryDatum.doc:
Blueprint `sk-d-real-boundary`: Boundary extension and inertia.

A *boundary datum* for a nonempty open `j : U₀ ↪ C₀` of a curve: a restriction
`AlgebraicGeometry.WeilGroup.Restriction` of Weil groups along `j`, the finiteness of the
boundary `S₀ = C₀ \ U₀`, and, at every boundary point `s`, the inertia subgroup
`I_s = ker (Gal(K̄_s / K_s) → Gal(k(s)‾ / k(s)))` inside the geometric fundamental group of `U`,
together with a residue Frobenius lift of degree `e_s` normalising it and lying, after
restriction to `W(C₀)`, in the Frobenius conjugacy class at `s`.

The henselization `𝒪_{C₀, s}^h`, its fraction field `K_s` and the inertia subgroup are not
available in Mathlib, so they are recorded as data here.

AddSubgroup.nonempty_addEquiv_torsionBy_.doc:
Blueprint `sk-prop-av-divisible-structure`: The torsion of a divisible group.

This is also the blueprint lemma `lem-sc-divisible-group-structure`.

Let `D` be a divisible abelian group, let `ℓ` be a prime and suppose that the `ℓ`-torsion of
`D` is finite of order `ℓ ^ r`. Then for every `n` the `ℓ ^ n`-torsion of `D` is isomorphic
to `(ℤ / ℓ ^ n) ^ r`.

AddCommGroup.tateModule.signature: def AddCommGroup.tateModule.{u} (ℓ : ℕ) (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] : AddSubgroup (ℕ → M)
AddCommGroup.tateModule.doc:
Blueprint `sk-d-ab-tate`: Integral and rational Tate modules.

The *Tate module* `T_ℓ M` of an abelian group `M` at a prime `ℓ` is the subgroup of the product
`∀ n : ℕ, M` consisting of the compatible systems `t` of `ℓ ^ n`-torsion points, that is, those
`t` with `ℓ ^ n • t n = 0` for all `n` and `ℓ • t (n + 1) = t n` for all `n`.

AddCommGroup.rationalTateModule.signature:
def AddCommGroup.rationalTateModule.{u} (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime ℓ)] (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] :
  Type u
AddCommGroup.rationalTateModule.doc:
Blueprint `sk-d-ab-tate`: Integral and rational Tate modules.

The *rational Tate module* `V_ℓ M = ℚ_[ℓ] ⊗_{ℤ_[ℓ]} T_ℓ M`.

AddCommGroup.eq_zero_of_mem_tateModule_o.doc:
An automorphism of an abelian group whose fixed subgroup is finite fixes no nonzero element
of the Tate module.

This is the group-theoretic content of the statement that the geometric Frobenius `F` of an
abelian variety `A₀` over a finite field `k₀` has no nonzero fixed vector on the rational Tate
module `V_ℓ A`. It is equivalent to that statement: `T_ℓ M` is torsion-free, so it embeds into
`V_ℓ M = T_ℓ M[1/ℓ]`, and a `σ`-fixed vector of `V_ℓ M` becomes a `σ`-fixed vector of `T_ℓ M`
after clearing denominators. Moreover an automorphism and its inverse have the same fixed
vectors, so the arithmetic and the geometric Frobenius give the same statement. For
`M = A₀(k)` with `σ` the arithmetic Frobenius, the hypothesis `hfin` says that the fixed subgroup
`A^σ = A₀(k₀)` is finite, which is the only input the geometric proof uses.

Proof (blueprint `lem-tate-module-no-fixed`): all `t n` lie in the finite group `M^σ`, of order
`N` say; the order of `t (n + N)` is a power `ℓ ^ j` of `ℓ` dividing `N`, so `j ≤ N` and
`t n = ℓ ^ N • t (n + N) = 0`.
(blueprint: `sk-p-tate`, `lem-tate-module-no-fixed`)

AddChar.sum_mulShift.signature:
theorem AddChar.sum_mulShift.{u_1, u_2} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] [Fintype R] [DecidableEq R]
  {R' : Type u_2} [CommRing R'] [IsDomain R'] {ψ : AddChar R R'} (b : R) (hψ : ψ.IsPrimitive) :
  ∑ x, ψ (x * b) = ↑(if b = 0 then Fintype.card R else 0)
AddChar.sum_mulShift.doc:
The sum over the values of `mulShift ψ b` for `ψ` primitive is zero when `b ≠ 0`
and `#R` otherwise.

AddChar.sum_eq_ite.signature:
theorem AddChar.sum_eq_ite.{u_1, u_2} {A : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [AddGroup A] [Fintype A]
  [CommSemiring R] [IsDomain R] (ψ : AddChar A R) [Decidable (ψ = 0)] :
  ∑ a, ψ a = if ψ = 0 then ↑(Fintype.card A) else 0

AddChar.FiniteField.primitiveChar.signature:
def AddChar.FiniteField.primitiveChar.{u_1, u_2} (F : Type u_1) (F' : Type u_2) [Field F] [Finite F]
  [Field F'] (h : ringChar F' ≠ ringChar F) : AddChar.PrimitiveAddChar F F'
AddChar.FiniteField.primitiveChar.doc:
There is a primitive additive character on the finite field `F` if the characteristic
of the target is different from that of `F`.

We obtain it as the composition of the trace from `F` to `ZMod p` with a primitive
additive character on `ZMod p`, where `p` is the characteristic of `F`.
